description: Subshrubs 0.5-1 m tall, the stems roughly stellate-pubescent, the hairs somewhat antrorse. Leaf blades elliptic to oblanceolate, mostly 5-12 x 2-5 cm, basally rounded, truncate, or subcuneate, serrate, acuminate, scabridulous beneath (the hairs often bifurcate), nearly glabrous above except on midrib, or with appressed simple hairs, the margin often prominently short-ciliate or -setose; petioles 3-15(-40) mm long, with antrorse pubescence; stipules 8-12 mm long, subulate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-11 cm long, antrorsely pubescent; involucellar bracts 7-9, linear, 5-9 mm long (of variable length), connate below, ciliate; calyx 3-5 mm long, ciliate; corolla white, 8-12 mm long, minutely pubescent externally. Fruits 8-10 mm diam., glabrous, subglobose, the mericarp body 5 mm high, smooth, 3-spined, the spines 4-5 mm long, retrorsely barbed, more or less erect, the lateral spines 3.5 mm apart at base.

description: Shrubs 2 m tall, the stems densely stellate- and minutely glandular-pubescent (sometimes also with large 3-4-armed stellate spicules). Leaf blades ovate or somewhat palmately 3-lobed, mostly 6-10 x 3-7 cm, basally cordate, crenate-serrate, acute or acuminate, palmately 5-7-nerved, discolorous, the upper surface with minute glandular hairs, the lower surface densely stellate- and glandular-pubescent, both surfaces with scattered large (2 mm diam.) 3-4-armed stellate spicules, at least on younger leaves; petioles 3-8 cm long; stipules subulate, 5 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1.5-7 cm long, articulated 3-8 mm below the flower; involucellar bracts 6, ligulate, 10-12 x 1-1.5 mm, briefly connate basally (essentially distinct), glandular pubescent; calyx 11-16 mm long, glandular-pubescent, the lobes 3-ribbed; corolla 3.5-5 cm long, red, externally pubescent (the petals reflexed according to photograph on Liogier 16524, NY); staminal column slightly exserted (or clearly so by reflexion of petals), glabrous, purplish, the filaments 3-5 mm long along upper half of column; styles emergent from the column, pubescent. Fruits ca. 1 cm diam., minutely pubescent; mericarps with a dorsal crest or wing prolonged apically into an acute or scimitar-shaped structure, reticulately veined, with 2 or 3 excrescences on each side, the mericarp body 6 mm high (8-9 mm high including the wing); seeds 3.5 mm long.

description: Subshrubs 1 m tall, the stems densely viscid and sparsely pilose, with scattered simple hairs 2-2.5 mm long, or these lacking. Leaf blades mostly 4-8(-13) x 2-5(-9) cm, ovate, cordate, prominently to obscurely serrate, acuminate, palmately 5-7-nerved, minutely and softly stellate-tomentose (the hairs 0.2-0.5 mm long beneath, smaller above), also pilose on the veins, discolorous; petioles 1-2.5(-7) cm long; stipules 2-5 mm long, subulate, Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or forming a terminal panicle, the pedicels 2.5-10 cm long, equaling or exceeding the subtending leaves; involucellar bracts 6-7, 10-15 x ca. 1 mm, viscid, pilose only toward the base; calyx 6-7 mm long, ciliate, often whitish in intercostal areas; corolla 2.5-3 cm long, white, glabrous on margins of claw; staminal column 15-17 mm long, pallid, glabrous, the filaments 0.5-1 mm long, often in 3 or 4 whorls; styles exceeding the column, the stigmas villous. Fruits oblate, 7-9 mm diam., 4.5 mm high, obscurely scabridulous on suture, otherwise glabrous.

description: Shrubs 1-2 m tall, the stems with dense longitudinal rows of twisted hairs ca. 1 mm long and with scattered to dense spreading simple hairs (slightly longer), also with glandular hairs on very youngest growth. Leaf blades subhastate to ovate, mostly 4-12 x 1-8 cm (progressively reduced upward), cordate to truncate, crenate, acute, palmately 5-9-nerved, minutely pubescent; petioles 1-6.5 cm long; stipules falcate, 3-7 x 1-1.8 mm, often recurved. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or forming a terminal panicle, the pedicels 1-3 cm long, scabridulous; involucellar bracts 6, narrowly ligulate, 10-12 x 0.5 mm, ciliate (hairs 1.5-2 mm long); calyx 3-5 mm long, sparsely ciliate; corolla 8-10 mm long, pale yellow, pubescent on claw; staminal column 1-2 mm long, the erect filaments 3-6 mm long; styles exserted from androecium, united below, free for distal 1-2 mm. Fruits oblate, ca. 4 mm diam., subglabrous; mericarps 3.5 mm high, reticulately veined.

description: Shrubs 1-2 m tall, the stems stellate-pubescent, the hairs 0.5-2(-3) mm long. Leaf blades mostly 6-12 x 9 cm, ovate or weakly trilobulate, basally cordate, crenate-serrate to subentire, the lateral lobes acutish, the apex long-acuminate, palmately 7-9-nerved, discolorous, softly stellate-pubescent, densely so beneath; petioles ca. half the length of the blade or less; stipules 2-5 mm long, hirsute, subulate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-5 cm long, prominently hirsute; involucellar bracts 5, lanceolate or lance-elliptic, 10-20 x 2-4 mm, densely pubescent and marginally ciliate (cilia 1-2 mm long); calyx 8-12 mm long, densely pubescent and ciliate; corolla 3-4 cm long, white, ciliate on claw, densely pubescent externally; staminal column ca. 2 cm long, white, glabrous, declined, the filaments 3-5 mm long, the pollen white; styles exceeding the column, sparsely pubescent, white, the stigmas villous. Fruits 8-9 mm diam., minutely pubescent, the mericarps 5 mm long, prominently carinate and reticulate-veined, often with 3 or 4 excrescences on each side.

description: Shrubs 1.5 m tall, freely branched, the stems covered with minute arachnoid pubescence and with scattered larger stellate hairs. Leaf blades ovate, truncate, crenate-serrate, acute, mostly 3-9(-12) x 2-6(-10) cm, palmately 5-nerved, stellate-pubescent, more densely so beneath, sparsely so to glabrate (in age) above; petioles 0.5-2 cm long; stipules 3-8 mm long, linear-lanceolate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-4 cm long; involucellar bracts 6, linear-lanceolate, 5-9 mm long, minutely pubescent and sometimes ciliate; calyx 4-7 mm long, pubescent and sometimes ciliate; corolla 1.5-2 cm long, yellow; androecium 5-8 mm long; styles emergent from column, sparsely pubescent, the stigmas capitate, 0.6-0.8 mm diam., villous. Fruits ca. 6 mm diam., longitudinally ridged (retrorsely scabridulous on ridge) and rugose, the mericarp body 5 mm high, 3-spined, the spines erect, 2-3 mm long, retrorsely barbed.

description: Shrubs to 2 m tall, the stems stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades mostly 5-9 cm long, almost twice as long as wide, ovate, truncate to subcordate, finely serrate, acute, discolorous, stellate-pubescent; petioles ¼ the length of the blade or less; stipules 2-3 mm long, subulate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, often crowded apically, the pedicels 1-4 cm long, pubescent; involucellar bracts ca. 15, filiform, 20-30 mm long, arcuate, copiously ciliate (hairs 2-3 mm); calyx 10-18 mm long, pubescent; corolla yellow, 1.5-2.5 cm long, densely pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column 15-20 mm long, pallid, glabrous, the filaments 3-5 mm long; styles glabrous, slightly exceeding the androecium, the stigmas minutely pubescent. Fruits 8-10 mm diam., glabrous; mericarps smooth, with 1 apical and 2 lateral points (rudimentary spines), these sometimes retrorsely barbed.

description: Shrubs to 2 m tall, the stems densely glandular-pubescent. Leaf blades mostly 8-12 cm long, ca. half as wide, narrowly ovate, cordate, crenate-serrate, acuminate, discolorous, stellate-pubescent, with denser coarser pubescence beneath and with intermixture of glandular hairs above; petioles ½-¾ the length of the blades; stipules 5-12 mm long, linear, glandular-pubescent. Flowers solitary or paired in the leaf axils, the pedicels to 5.5 cm long, viscid, articulate 7-13 mm below the flower; involucellar bracts 8, linear, 8-15 mm long, viscid; calyx 6-8 mm long, ciliate, whitish (except for green veins); corolla 10-12 mm long, yellow, densely bearded on margins of claw, forming a cushion at juncture with staminal column; staminal column 6-10 mm long, glabrous, the filaments 1-3 mm long; styles glabrous, slightly exserted. Fruits oblate or somewhat obovate, 6 mm diam., obscurely scabridulous on margin, otherwise glabrous, smooth or weakly reticulate, the mericarps 5 mm high, narrowly winged laterally, with a small subapical cusp; seeds glabrous, striate.

description: Shrubs ca. 1 m tall, the stems densely to sparsely stellate-pubescent, sometimes dark-pigmented. Leaf blades mostly 2-5 cm long, slightly longer than wide, ovate, cordate, coarsely dentate, acute, discolorous, stellate-pubescent, more densely and coarsely so beneath; petioles ½-l times the length of the blade; stipules 2-5 mm long, subulate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-5 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, linear-lanceolate (or narrowly oblanceolate), shorter than to subequal to calyx, 1-2 mm wide, hirsute; calyx 9-12 mm long, hirsute, whitish with green veins; corolla 1.5-2.5 cm long, rose-lavender, ciliate on margins of claw; staminal column 7-13 mm long, glabrous, pallid, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles exceeding the column, the stigmas usually villous. Fruits 8-9 mm diam., oblate, essentially glabrous, the mericarps 3.5-4 mm long, smoothly rounded or obscurely carinate.

description: Subshrubs to 2 m tall, the stems more or less setose (hairs 1-2 mm long) and with an understory of minute glandular hairs, often with narrow longitudinal lines of recurved hairs. Leaf blades narrowly hastate, basally truncate or subcordate, crenate-serrate, acute, mostly 4-10 x l-2(-3.5) cm, both surfaces with erect simple hairs (some glandular) 0.2-0.5 mm long; petioles 0.5-4 cm long; stipules falcate, 4-6 mm long, reflexed. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-4.5 cm long; involucellar bracts 13-15, linear, 10-14 mm long, ciliate; calyx 8-11 mm long, ciliate; corolla 15-20 mm long, yellow, bearded on margins of claw; staminal column 5 mm long, glabrous, pallid, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles exserted from the column. Fruits 6-7 mm diam., glabrous or obscurely puberulent, the mericarps 4 mm high, rugose.

description: Small tree to 4 m tall, the branches with grayish bark, the young stems densely stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades elliptic, mostly 10-17 x 4-6.5 cm, basally cuneate, entire, acuminate, penninerved, the midrib raised above and beneath, with 6-8 secondary nerves on each side, glabrous above, sparsely stellate-pubescent beneath (primarily on nerves); petioles 1-3 cm long, evenly stellate-pubescent; stipules ligulate, 9-12 x 1.5 mm, erect, stellate-pubescent and ciliate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 5-9 cm long; involucellar bracts 9-11, ligulate, ca. 16 x 1.5 mm, densely stellate-pubescent and ciliate (cilia 1.5-2 mm long); calyx 10 mm long, with pubescence like involucel; corolla barely exceeding calyx, yellowish green. description: Subshrubs 0.5 m tall, the stems minutely glandular-pubescent. Leaf blades ovate, sometimes 3-lobulate, mostly 4-8 x 3-4(-8) cm, shallowly to deeply cordate, crenate-serrate, acuminate, palmately 5-7-nerved, discolorous, the upper surface with minute (0.2-0.3 mm) simple and bifurcate hairs and minute glandular hairs, the lower surface with minute stellate hairs and minute glandular hairs, and with scattered larger (1.5 mm diam.) 2-3-armed stellate spicules; petioles 3-6 cm long; stipules 3-4 mm long, subulate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 3.5-6.5 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, lanceolate, 9-11 x 2.5-4 mm, minutely stellate-pubescent (hairs 0.2 mm long); calyx 7-8 mm long, minutely stellate-pubescent; corolla white, 2-3 cm long, glabrous on claw; staminal column more or less declined, 2.5 cm long, glabrous, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles exserted. Fruits 8-9 mm diam., glabrous; mericarps 4-5 mm high, reticulate-veined, with erose apical excrescences.

description: Shrubs 1 m tall, the stems densely and finely stellate-puberulent and with scattered (longer) glandular hairs. Leaf blades broadly ovate, up to 6 x 4-6 cm, deeply cordate at base, crenate-serrate, acute or somewhat acuminate, palmately 7-nerved, somewhat discolorous, densely and softly stellate-tomentose on both surfaces; petioles 3-5.5 cm long; stipules subulate, 2-4 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels erect in flower, geniculate in fruit, up to 3.5 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, ligulate, 14-18 x 1.5-3 mm, densely stellate-tomentose and with scattered glandular hairs; calyx 14-18 mm long, whitish at base, deeply divided, with pubescence like involucel, the lobes many-veined; corolla yellow, 3.5-4 cm long. Fruits 11-12 mm diam., sparsely puberulent; mericarps 5 mm high, carinate, with prominently raised rugosities.

description: Subshrubs 0.2-0.5 m tall, the stems densely stellate-hirsute, the hairs ferruginous, 2-3 mm long. Leaf blades sagittate, mostly 3-5 x 1.5-3.5 cm, basally sagittate (the lobes 1-1.5 cm long), coarsely serrate, acute, palmately 5-7-nerved, discolorous, coarsely stellate-pubescent on both surfaces (the hairs 1-2 mm long), the blades geniculate with the petioles and more or less parallel to stem; petioles 1.5-2 cm long; stipules subulate, 3-4 mm long (obscured by pubescence of stem and petiole). Flowers solitary in the upper axils, the pedicels 1-1.8 cm long, ferruginous-hirsute; in-volucellar bracts 5, spatulate, 7-9 x 4 mm, coarsely hirsute; calyx 12-14 mm long, with stellate ferruginous hairs 1-2 mm long; corolla 15-21 mm long, red, pubescent on margins of claw, otherwise essentially glabrous; staminal column 8-9 mm long, glabrous or with pubescence at base, reddish, the filaments 2-5 mm long; styles emergent from the column, glabrous. Fruits 8-9 mm diam., minutely puberulent; mericarps 6-7 mm high, acute apically, carinate and with 3 or 4 raised excrescences on each side.

description: Shrubs 1-3 m (or more) tall, the stems stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades mostly 6-14 x 2-5 cm, lance-oblong, truncate, remotely and obscurely denticulate to subentire, acuminate, palmately 3-nerved, sparsely and minutely stellate-pubescent (especially on veins) to glabrate; petioles 1-4 cm long; stipules inconspicuous, caducous. Inflorescence an elongated terminal leafless raceme; pedicels 0.5-1.5 cm long; involucellar bracts 6-8, linear-lanceolate, 6-10 x 1-2 mm; calyx 11-13 mm long, minutely stellate-pubescent; corolla 1.5-2 cm long, yellowish green; externally pubescent; staminal column ca. 15 mm long, the filaments 1-2 mm long. Fruits ca. 1 cm diam., subequal to calyx, obscurely 10-ribbed, beaked, 10-11 mm long (including beak), retrorsely scabridulous to glabrate, the mericarps ligneous.

description: Decumbent to ascending perennial herbs or subshrubs, the stems minutely stellate-puberulent and with glandular hairs on younger stems. Leaf blades sagittate (except juvenile leaves subrotund), up to 4.5 (excluding the lobes) x 1-2 cm, basally sagittately lobed (the lobes 8-20 mm long), crenate-dentate to subentire, acute, the blade geniculate with the petiole and thus more or less parallel to the stem, the margin prominently ciliate (hairs 1 mm long) or rarely eciliate (Hatschbach 43047), both surfaces sparsely pubescent (with some glandular hairs) to subglabrous; petioles 6-10 mm long; stipules subulate, 1-5 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, often apically crowded, the pedicels 0.5-1 cm long, distally pilose; involucellar bracts 5, lance-ovate, 11-15 x 3-7 mm, ciliate-pilose (hairs 1-2 mm long); calyx 8-9 mm long, ciliate and with minute glandular hairs; corolla 1.5 cm long, rose with red center, pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column 2-3 mm long, the filaments 1-1.5 mm long; styles emergent from the column, purple. Fruits 7-8 mm diam., minutely puberulent; mericarps 4 mm high, carinate, reticulately veined.

description: Subshrubs 0.5-1.5 m tall, the stems minutely puberulent, the hairs 0.1 mm long. Leaf blades ovate to subhastate or subsagittate, mostly 2-3.5 x 2-3 cm, basally deeply cordate or sagittately lobed (lobes 8-12 mm long), shallowly crenate-serrate, acute, palmately 3-5-nerved, markedly discolorous, both surfaces minutely stellate-pubescent (hairs 0.2-0.3 mm diam.), the lower surface more densely so, the blades more or less geniculate with the petioles and parallel to the stem; petioles 2-3 cm long, with pubescence like stem but distally with longer hairs (to 0.5 mm); stipules subulate to filiform, 2-6 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 5-20 mm long; involucellar bracts 5-7, narrowly lanceolate, 10 x 1-2(-5) mm, minutely puberulent (some of the hairs glandular); calyx 10-16 mm long, minutely puberulent and viscid, the lobes 6-8(-12) mm wide; corolla 2.5-4 cm long, white or rose with a red center, pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column 7-8 mm long, glabrous, reddish, the filaments 2 mm long. Fruits 8-9 mm diam.; mericarps minutely pubescent, strongly carinate and reticulate, 7 mm high.

description: Subshrubs 20 cm tall, the stems minutely puberulent. Leaf blades elliptic to oblanceolate, up to 16 x 7 cm, narrowly cordate basally, coarsely crenate, acute, penninerved, discolorous, the upper surface subglabrous, the lower surface densely pubescent with minute stellate hairs; petioles 2-4 cm long, minutely puberulent; stipules lanceolate, erect, 7 x 1 mm, obscurely pubescent. Inflorescences on axillary peduncles, racemose or paniculate to subcapituliform; peduncles antrorsely pubescent with rigid simple hairs 1 mm long; pedicels to 5 mm long, densely antrorsely hispid; involucel of 10-12 bractlets, connate in basal half, 7-8 mm long, antrorsely hispid; calyx subequal to involucel, antrorsely hispid; corolla rose, ca. 8 mm long. Fruits glabrous, reddish; mericarps carinate and reticulate-veined, the body ca. 6 mm long, with 3 widely spaced spines, the central spine 4-5 mm long, erect, the lateral spines 3-4 mm apart at the base, somewhat divaricate.

description: Suberect to trailing or Subscandent subshrubs to 1-2 m tall, the stems glandular-pubescent, sometimes also sparsely setose. Leaf blades ovate (to triangular in distal leaves, rarely subhastate; Woolston 1150), mostly 2-7 x 1.5-6 cm, cordate, crenate-serrate, acute or acuminate, discolorous, sparsely to densely soft-puberulent, with scattered 3-armed spicules beneath or these absent; petioles 1-4.5 cm long; stipules subulate, 2-3 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-5 cm long, slender; involucellar bracts 6-8, lanceolate, 6-10 x 0.5-2 mm, puberulent, sometimes viscid; calyx 4-5 mm long, pubescent; corolla 1.5-2.5 cm long, yellow with a dark red center, densely wooly on margins of claw; staminal column ca. 5 mm long, purplish, the filaments 1 mm long. Fruits oblate, 6 mm diam., 4.7 mm high, often retrorsely scabridulous on central ridge, otherwise obscurely pubescent to subglabrous, more or less reticulate-veined, with vestigial subapical protruber-ance, or this suppressed.

description: Shrubs 2 m tall, the stems densely stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades ovate, mostly 2-4 cm x 1.5-3.5 cm, basally cordate, coarsely crenate, obtuse or acute, palmately 5-7-nerved, discolorous, minutely stellate-tomentose above and beneath; petioles 8-20 mm long; stipules subulate, 3-4 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-2 cm long, obscurely articulated 2 mm below the flower; involucellar bracts 5, ligulate, 6-8 x 1-1.5 mm, stellate-pubescent; calyx 6-7 mm long, stellate-pubescent; corolla ca. 1 cm long, red; androecium exserted (1.5-2 times length of corolla), the column glabrous, the filaments 5-8 mm long, mostly distal; styles exserted from column by 5-6 mm. description: Subshrubs 0.5-1.5 m tall, the stems with glandular hairs and sometimes a few stellate hairs. Leaf blades ovate (sometimes 3-5-lobulate), cordate, crenate, acute or acuminate, palmately 7-9-nerved, discolorous, mostly 3-7 x 2-5 cm, softly puberulent above and beneath; petioles 1-5.5 cm long; stipules subulate, 3-4 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils (sometimes geminate, rarely umbellate), the pedicels 2-5 cm long; involucellar bracts 5(-6), lanceolate, 5-9 x 1-2 mm, densely glandular-pubescent and sometimes with a few large stellate hairs; calyx subequal to involucel and with similar pubescence; corolla white, 1.5-2.5 cm long, externally covered with coarse 3-4-armed stellate hairs, the petals bearded on margins of claw; staminal column glabrous, exserted at anthesis, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles emergent from the column, glabrous, with capitate stigmas. Fruits 5-7 mm diam., subglabrous, the mericarps verruculose, dehiscent, basally minutely winged; seeds 3 mm long, glabrous, striate.

description: Shrubs 2-2.5 m tall, the stems densely covered with appressed 6-12-armed stellate hairs. Leaf blades subrotund to ovate, sometimes weakly lobed, truncate to cordate, denticulate to subentire, acute to obtuse, more or less discolorous, palmately (sometimes pedately) 7-9-nerved, stellate-pubescent above and beneath, mostly 3-8 x 3-7 cm; petioles 2-4.5 cm long; stipules 3-4 mm long. Fruits ovoid, 10 mm diam., 13 mm long, beaked, stellate-pubescent; mericarps basally winged.

description: Subshrubs, decumbent and rooting at the nodes, the stems with narrow lines of fine simple hairs 0.3-0.4 mm long, otherwise glabrous. Leaf blades mostly 2-6 x 1-3 cm, elliptic, truncate to cuneate (somewhat asymmetrical at base), serrate, acute, palmately 5-nerved, very sparsely and minutely pubescent to nearly glabrous; petioles 2-7(-15) mm long, densely pubescent on adaxial side; stipules 4-7 mm long, lance-linear. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 0.5-2 cm long, slender; involucellar bracts 5, linear, 5-6 mm long (shorter than calyx), subglabrous; calyx 7-8 mm long, marginally ciliate but otherwise sparsely pubescent to nearly glabrous, divided nearly to the base; corolla 9-10 mm long, yellow; staminal column ca. 4 mm long, the filaments 1 mm; styles and stigmas exserted from the staminal column by 5 mm. Fruits 7 mm diam. (excluding spines), ascending-setose, rugose; mericarp body 5 mm tall, each mericarp 3-spined, the central spine erect, the lateral spines spreading, the spines stout, 5-9 mm long, with minute obscure barbs at tip.

description: Shrubs 1.5-2 m tall, the stems pubescent with minute appressed stellate hairs 0.5 mm long or less. Fruits ca. 7 mm diam., minutely pubescent; mericarps carinate, apically acute, reticulately rugose, with 2 or 3 excrescences on each side, 4-4.5 mm high.

Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels up to 6 cm long, slender; involucellar bracts 8-10, linear, 20-38 x 1-2 mm, reddish, stellate-pubescent and sometimes also ciliate; calyx 10-19 mm long, densely pubescent, the lobes 4-7 mm long; corolla 2.5-3 cm long; androecium exserted by 1-2 cm, the column purplish, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles slender, minutely and sparsely pubescent, purplish. description: Shrubs ca. 1 m tall (?), the stems densely yellowish-puberulent, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long. Leaf blades ovate to 3(-5)-lobed, 1.5-2 x 1-1.5 cm, cordate, crenate-serrate, acute or subobtuse, discolorous, densely and softly puberulent above and beneath (the hairs very small), prominently reticulate-veined beneath; petioles 1-1.5 cm long; stipules subulate, 1-2 mm long, deciduous. description: Shrubs 2-2.5 m tall, the stems densely pubescent with glandular hairs, sometimes also stellate hairs, and occasionally with long setae. Leaf blades ovate-cordate, crenate-serrate, acuminate, markedly discolorous, softly tomentulose beneath, with predominantly glandular hairs above, mostly 5-11 x 2.5-7 cm, palmately 7-9-nerved; petioles 1-4 cm long, with pubescence like that of stem; stipules subulate, 5-6 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 4-8 cm long, with pubescence like that of stem, commonly bearing two flowers (or flowers solitary); involucellar bracts (4-)5-6, ovate to lanceolate, 1014 x 5-7 mm, puberulent; calyx subequal to involucel, densely ciliate; corolla 3-5.5 cm long, pink with red center, glabrous on margins of claw; staminal column 2 cm long, glabrous, the filaments 1 mm long; styles emergent from column, with capitate, villous stigmas. Fruits oblate, 7 mm diam., 4-5 mm high, nearly glabrous, each mericarp with a triangular subapical protrusion.

description: Subshrubs to 0.5 m tall, erect to decumbent, the stems densely stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades hastately or sagittately oblong-triangular, mostly 2-5 x 1-2 cm, basally sagittately lobed, the sinus narrowly to broadly acute, serrate, acute to obtuse, palmately 3-5-veined, strongly discolorous, with scattered stellate hairs above, canescent to tomentulose beneath; petioles 1-2.5 cm long (longer than lobes of blade); stipules subulate, 1-3 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 0.5-2.5 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, broadly ovate or suborbicular, 4 x 4 mm, reflexed; calyx 8-9 mm long, pubescent, the lobes broadly cordate, 7-9 mm wide, plicate-pentangular in bud; corolla 1.5-2 cm long, lavender with dark red center, pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column 5-7 mm long, glabrous. description: Trees, to 20 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.9-3.8 mm in diam., ± flattened towards the nodes, somewhat longitudinally furrowed, initially covered with a dense, reddish or brownish indument of very short, ± ascending hairs and longer (up to ca. 0.5 mm), ± erect, curled hairs, the latter ± quickly lost, twigs becoming grayish, then glabrescent; terminal buds elongate, till mm long, 1.2-2 mm thick, densely covered with moderately long, ascending, reddish-brown hairs. Petioles 9-22 mm long, 1-2.5 mm thick, irregularly roundish below, usually longitudinally ridged, canaliculate above, often flattened towards the lamina, indument ± as on twigs. Leaves subopposite to opposite, lanceolate to lanceolate elliptic, widest 1/3 from the base to (mostly) at the middle, (7-)10-20 cm long, (1.8-) 3-6(-7) cm wide, 2.4-4.4 times longer than wide, tip (mostly long and narrowly) acuminate, base varying from narrowly cuneate to obtuse, the very base sometimes attenuate, margin flat or nearly so, midrib and secondary veins (very) slightly impressed (the latter occasionally level) above, prominent below, secondary veins 5-8 (-9) pairs, diverging at 30-50(-65)°, in midlamina running at an angle of 15-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, level or very slightly impressed above, usually raised below, finer venation mostly inconspicuous. Indument in young leaves variable above, dense and feltlike to moderately sparse and inconspicuous, consisting of ± curled hairs which may be rather short and tawny and/or slightly longer and reddish, older leaves glabrescent; indument below consisting of both short, ± parallel, appressed, pale hairs in the intercostal area and longer, erect, curled, reddish hairs mainly but not exclusively on the veins, the former very dense in young leaves, in older leaves either staying dense or becoming very sparse, the latter initially regular to sparse, sometimes crowded in the axils of the secondary veins, in older leaves becoming sparser or lost. Gland dots not apparent. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, basically thyrsoids but frequently reduced to corymbiform dichasia, 1-1.3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-3 mm diam., 2.7-8.5 cm long, reaching 1/4-3/4 the length of the subtending leaf (mostly ca. 1/3); peduncle 1-3.5 cm long, i.e., 1/3 to 3/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-2 below terminal cyme, branched (2-)3-4 times, indument dense, similar to that on twigs but hairs mostly somewhat longer and more reddish. Pedicels up to 2 mm long, 0.8-1 mm thick. Flowers 7-10.5 mm in diam., tepals elliptic to oblong-elliptic, ca. 3-4 mm long and ca 1.7-3 mm wide, papillosity ± dense on the inside surface. Stamens ca 1.3-2.5 mm long including a short but distinct filament, anthers papillose, in the outer whorls narrowly trullate to rhombic, with a well developed acute sterile tip, in the third whorl acute to obtuse at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3 the length of the stamens, thickish and papillose, distinctly united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 2-3 mm long, ovary broadly ellipsoid, glabrous, style almost as long as the ovary, papillose. Receptacle deeply urceolate (to almost spherical), glabrous inside. Berry (after Schultes & Cabrera 16601) elongate, 2227 mm long, 8-12 mm in diam., slightly apiculate, cupule deep, almost campanulate, ca. 10 mm in diam. and ca. 8 mm deep, with a slightly widened entire margin.

description: Trees, to 20 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 4-6.5 mm in diam., longitudinally furrowed, initially densely covered with ± long (ca. 0.2-1.2 mm), ± erect, ± straight, reddish or light brownish hairs, on older twigs becoming gray and matted, often broken; terminal buds ± ovoid, 4-10 mm long, 2.5-6 mm thick, densely covered with ± straight, appressed to ascending, reddish to pale brown hairs. Petioles 7-15 mm long, 2.54 mm thick, roundish below, distinctly canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs. Leaves alternate, elliptic to lanceolate elliptic, widest ± at the middle, 12-27 cm long, 6-10 cm wide, 1.6-2.7 times longer than wide, tip short acuminate, cuneate to obtuse towards the base, the base itself attenuate, due to the broadly and conspicuously reflexed or revolute margin, midrib and secondary veins distinctly impressed above, but at least the midrib sometimes convex in its impression, very prominent below, secondary veins (6-)8-13 pairs, diverging at 40-70°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-50° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, (slightly) impressed above, distinctly raised to prominent below. Indument on both surfaces consisting of ± straight, long (ca. 0.3-0.8 mm), erect hairs, initially sparse to moderately dense above, denser on veins, moderately dense to intermediate below, mature leaves quickly glabrescent above except for the midrib and the secondaries, indument becoming intermediate to sparse on the lamina below, on midrib and secondaries often denser, shorter, and less erect. Gland dots not visible to moderately distinct. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, ca. 1.5-2.5 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2-6 mm diam., (6-)10-13 cm long, reaching ca. 3/5-4/5 the length of the subtending leaf (larger in fruiting specimens); peduncle (l-)4.5-6.5 cm long, i.e., ca. (1/6-) 2/5-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, its indument either as on twigs or much shorter and paler, lateral branches (the lower ones not entirely cymose) 6-12 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched once or twice. Pedicels ca. 1.5-4 mm long, ca. 0.3-0.5 mm thick. Flowers ca. 3.34 mm in diam., tepals ± elongate-ovate, ca. 1.4-1.7 mm long and 0.8-1.2 mm wide, covered with long, fine papillae on the inside surface, also with some hairs near the base. Stamens ca. 0.50.8 mm long including a distinct (or sometimes very short?) filament of 0.2-0.3 mm, anthers apically and on back side densely covered with long papillae, in the outer whorls transverse-elliptic, broadly rounded at the tip, in the third whorl ± roundish-rectangular, ± truncate at the tip. Staminodes slightly clavate-capitate, reaching ca. 2/3-3/4 the length of the stamens, with long papillae-hairs on abaxial side, possibly slightly glandular on adaxial side, free or united with the inner stamens at the very base. Pistil ca. 1-1.3 mm long, glabrous, ovary ± pear-shaped, style extremely short. Receptacle shallow, bowlshaped, glabrous inside, almost open above. Berry subglobose, ca. 11-15 mm long and ca. 11-14 mm in diam., cupule almost obconical to funnel-shaped, ca. 8-9 mm in diam., shallow inside, only 0.5-2 mm deep, ± gradually merging into the distinctly thickened pedicel.

description: Trees, to ca. 20 m tall. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 1.5-2 mm in diam., at first angular and with some short (to ca. 0.2 mm), appressed to somewhat ascending hairs, soon becoming roundish, glabrescent; terminal bud ± ovoid, the only one in the present material ca. 2 mm long and ca. 1.3 mm thick, densely covered with straight, appressed, light brown hairs. Petioles 6-11 mm long, 0.9-2 mm thick, roundish below, only slightly irregular, ± canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs. Leaves alternate, elliptic, widest ± at the middle, 7.5-12 cm long, 3-5 cm wide, 2.3-3.1 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base ± obtuse (in young leaves sometimes broadly attenuate), margin flat to slightly bent down, midrib convex in a slight impression above, prominent below, secondary veins very slightly impressed above, prominent below, 5-8 pairs, diverging at 50-65°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-40° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed, mainly ± scalariform to percurrent but ± irregular, level to very slightly impressed above, slightly raised below. Indument consisting of short ± appressed hairs, even in young leaves only a few hairs on base of midrib if any above, indument sparse and rather inconspicuous below on a finely papillose epidermis, slowly becoming sparser. Gland dots sometimes visible on upper surface of young leaves, rather inconspicuous. Inflorescences in the axils of young foliage leaves and in the axils of cataphylls at the base of the new growth, 0.7-1.7 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.3-2.8 mm diam., 2-11 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4 to almost the length of the closest foliage leaf; peduncle 0.8-3.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/4-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (2-)4-8 below terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, branched 0-3 times, indument sparse to moderately dense, consisting of mixed very short and longer (up to 0.4 mm), ± ascending, reddish-brown hairs. Pedicels ca. 0.7-2 mm long, ca. 0.3-0.4 mm thick. Flowers ca. 3.4-4.3 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic to oblong, ca. 1.3-1.8 mm long and ca. 0.9-1.4 mm wide, covered with ± fine but distinct papillae on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.7 mm long including a short but distinct filament of ca. 0.1-0.2 mm, anthers papillose apically and on back side, in the first whorl transversely roundish-rectangular, in the second whorl ± squarish with latrorse lower pollen sacs, in the third whorl ± rectangular, in all three ± truncate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. half the length of the stamens, almost terete, slightly papillose, for ca. half their length united with the inner stamens. Pistil ca. 1.4-1.7 mm long, glabrous, ovary ± ellipsoid, style ± as long as the ovary. Receptacle almost urceolate, glabrous inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Small trees. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 2-3.7 mm in diam., at first distinctly angular, with a (moderately) dense cover of very short and (fewer) slightly longer (up to ca. 0.3 mm) hairs, ± straight, appressed to somewhat ascending, older twigs more roundish but still with longitudinal ridges, indument slowly becoming sparser; terminal buds (only two seen) ± ovoid, ca. 3.5-5.5 mm long, ca. 2 mm thick, densely covered with hairs similar to the longer ones on twigs. Petioles 3-7 mm long, 1.5-2.3 mm thick, irregularly roundish below with broad ridges, ± flat above, with narrowly decurrent margin, indument ± as on twigs. Leaves alternate, elliptic, widest ± at the middle, 7.5-13 cm long, 3.6-6.6 cm wide, 1.9-2.6 times longer than wide, tip obtuse to very indistinctly acuminate, the very tip rounded, base ± obtuse to almost acute, margin flat to slightly bent down, midrib and secondary veins distinctly impressed and usually slightly convex above, prominent below, secondary veins 5-9 pairs, diverging at 45-65°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-50° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed, mainly percurrent, ± level and often scarcely visible above, raised below, intercostal areas slightly bullate, distinctly glaucous below (Fig. 4E, F). Indument on both surfaces consisting of ± appressed hairs, slightly longer and finer above than below, on both sides initially ± moderately sparse, subglabrescent above, slowly becoming sparser below. Gland dots in young leaves ± distinct above, later inconspicuous. Inflorescences in the axils of foliage leaves, 0.9-1.4 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2.3-5 mm diam., 2.5-7.5 cm long, reaching ca. 1/3 the length to almost the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 1.54 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/2-2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-6 below terminal cyme, branched once or twice, indument dense, ± as on twigs. Pedicels extremely short or up to ca. 1 mm long, ca. 0.7-0.9 mm thick. Flowers ca. 4-4.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, ca. 1.5-1.8 mm long and ca. 1-1.2 mm wide, with fine papillae on the inside surface, dense near the tip, much sparser at the base, the distal part usually also with some hairs. Stamens ca. 0.9 mm long including a distinct filament of ca. 0.3 mm, anthers without papillae, in all three whorls ± rounded-squarish to rounded-rectangular, ± truncate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. half the length of the stamens, slightly clavate, slightly glandular at the tip on adaxial side, their filaments with some hairs. Pistil ca. 1.8 mm long, glabrous, ovary ± ellipsoid, style reaching ca. 2/3 the length of the ovary. Receptacular tube deeply paraboloidal, almost as deep as the stamens are long, covered with short appressed hairs inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Trees (type specimen from an 8 m tree). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 2.5-6.5 mm in diam., ± distinctly angular (thinner ones only slightly compressed, thicker ones almost winged), with a moderately dense cover of short, appressed hairs immediately below the terminal bud, quickly becoming sparser or glabrescent; terminal buds narrow, ca. 3.5-5.5 mm long, ca. 1-2 mm thick, densely covered with short, appressed hairs. Petioles 3.5-9 mm long, 1.34 mm thick, almost completely hidden by the leaf base, irregularly roundish below, convex to shallowly canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs. Leaves alternate, ± lanceolate-oblong, widest ca. 2/5-3/5 from the base (in larger leaves usually above the middle), (13.5-)20-32 cm long, (4.5-)6.5-12.5 cm wide, 2.3-3.4 times longer than wide, tip ± tapering towards a distinct acumen, base distinctly cordate, margin flat to slightly bent down, midrib above distinctly impressed and especially in apical part usually slightly convex, very prominent below, secondary veins 7-11 pairs, diverging at 40-60°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-35° to the midrib, ± slightly impressed and sometimes slightly convex above, distinctly prominent below, tertiary venation scalariform, slightly raised to slightly impressed above, slightly raised to almost prominent below. Indument on both surfaces consisting of inconspicuous, short, appressed hairs, even in young leaves sparse on both sides but sometimes slightly denser on and along veins, soon becoming glabrous or nearly so. Gland dots only visible in young leaves, like pinpricks (see p. 14). Inflorescences in the axils of uppermost foliage leaves or occasionally some of them in the axils of cataphylls below a vegetative bud, less often apparently terminal, ca. 13 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2.3-6 mm diam., 7.5-20 cm long, reaching ca. 2/5 to almost the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 27 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/6-2/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (6-)8-14 below terminal cyme (the lower branches not always entirely cymose), branched 2-4 times, indument consisting of short, appressed hairs, sparse on peduncle, sparse to moderately dense on flowers. Pedicels ca. 1.2-3 mm long, ca. 0.3-0.5 mm thick. Flowers ca. 3.5-4.2 mm in diam., tepals ± (ovate-)elliptic, ca. 1.4-1.7 mm long and ca. 0.9-1.2 mm wide, with fine papillae on the inside surface, dense at the tip, much sparser to glabrous at the base. Stamens ca. 0.6-0.8 mm long including a distinct filament (0.3-0.4 mm), anthers with minute apical papillae, the outer ones transverse elliptic, broadly rounded to almost obtuse at the tip, the inner ones ± roundish-obtrapeziform, ± truncate to broadly rounded at the tip. Staminodes ca. half as long as the stamens, very slightly clavate, slightly papillose on adaxial side, probably slightly glandular on adaxial side, free. Pistil ca. 1.2 mm long, glabrous, ovary ± ellipsoid, style ± as long as the ovary. Receptacle cup-shaped, only slightly closed above by stamens and staminodes, with some appressed hairs inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Trees to 30 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 3-4.5 mm in diam., slightly longitudinally angular/furrowed, with short and longer (up to ca. 0.4 mm), appressed to slightly ascending, white hairs, initially dense, becoming sparser, slowly glabrescent; terminal buds elongate, 913 mm long, ca. 2 mm thick, densely white-sericeous. Petioles 11-22 mm long, 1.5-3.5 mm thick, somewhat flattened, irregularly roundish below, with an indument ± as on twigs but often sparser, ± flat above, indument denser, ± sericeous. Leaves alternate, ± oblong, widest ± slightly below the middle, 12-37 cm long, 4-12.5 cm wide, 2.5-4 times longer than wide, tip short acuminate, base broadly attenuate to acute, rarely obtuse, margin flat to slightly recurved at the base, midrib with the center impressed and the sides slightly raised above, very prominent below, secondary veins prominent on both sides, 6-12 pairs, diverging at 30-55°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-40° to the midrib, tertiary venation predominantly scalariform to percurrent but finer reticulation almost equally distinct, raised to almost prominent on both sides. Indument consisting of rather straight, white, appressed hairs, ca. 0.2-0.4 mm long, intermediate to sparse in young leaves above, later glabrescent, initially moderately dense to moderately sparse below, with additional shorter hairs, slowly becoming sparser, the axils of lower lateral veins with long erect hairs (sometimes these also along midrib). Leaves often distinctly glaucous below. Gland dots ± distinct above. Inflorescences axillary, apparently not only to distal leaves, ca. 1.5-2.3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2.2-4.5 mm diam., 11-21 cm long, slightly shorter to slightly longer than their subtending leaf; peduncle 5-10 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/2 the length of the inflorescence, with a moderate cover of white hairs to subglabrous, lateral branches 4-6 below terminal cluster of cymes, branched 2-3(-4) times, with a ± dense white indument on their terminal branches and the flowers. Pedicels 2.5-4.5 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm thick. Flowers 912 mm in diam., tepals broadly elliptic, ca. 3.5-4.3mm long and ca. 3-3.8 mm wide, densely papillose on the inside surface but also hairy at the base. Stamens ca. 2 mm long including the hairy filament of 0.2-0.6 mm, anthers in dried material red, in all three whorls roundish-rectangular to trapeziform, at the tip ± truncate, scarcely papillose but on abaxial side and at the tip covered with short, white, thickish hairs (some of them papillae-like). Staminodes very large, reaching ca. 3/4 the length of the stamens, with a broad hairy filament and a large, sagittate, glandular head. Pistil ca. 2 mm long, glabrous or with very few hairs, ovary thick, ± ellipsoid to (obovoid, style reaching 1/2 to 2/3 the length of the ovary. Receptacle shallow, cup-shaped, glabrous or with a few hairs inside. Berry elongate-ellipsoid, ca. 28 mm long and 15 mm in diam., cupule cup-shaped, distinctly longitudinally ridged, ca. 12 mm in diam. and ca. 8 mm deep.

description: Shrubs or small trees. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 1-2 mm in diam., initially slightly angular/ridged or roundish from the beginning, with a ± dense cover of ± short (few reaching ca. 0.3 mm), ± appressed, cupreous to light brown hairs, subpersistent or quickly becoming sparser; terminal buds elongate, ca. 2.55 mm long, ca. 0.7-1.5 mm thick, densely covered with ± short, ± appressed, ± cupreous hairs. Petioles 3.5-12 mm long, 0.8-1.5 mm thick, ± roundish below, flat above, with a central ridge, or broadly canaliculate, indument consisting of ± short (or rarely up to 0.4 mm long) appressed to ascending hairs, initially dense above, ± moderately dense below, glabrescent. Leaves alternate, lanceolate to lanceolate-elliptic or ovate-lanceolate, widest ca. 1/3—1/2 from the base, 3.5-10 cm long, 0.8-3.6 cm wide, 2.2-4.3 times longer than wide, tip tapering towards a ± distinct acumen or rarely almost acute, base acute to attenuate, margin flat to very narrowly recurved, midrib above ± convex, at the base often flat, level or in a slight impression, prominent below, secondary veins raised to (almost) level above, rarely slightly convex in a very slight impression, slightly raised to prominent below, (3-)4-6(-7) pairs, diverging at 45-65°, in midlamina running at an angle of (15-)30-50(-60)° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed, often almost lineate, finer reticulation almost equally distinct, clearly raised to level above, raised to almost level below. Indument consisting of very fine, inconspicuous, ± short (rarely reaching ca. 0.4 mm), appressed hairs, in young leaves on both sides moderately sparse to sparse, denser on veins, mature leaves glabrescent above except for the base of the midrib, indument becoming sparser below, axils of secondary veins on lower leaf surface often ± sunken (i.e., slightly bullate above), nearly always with relatively long (up to ca. 0.8 mm), pale, ± erect hairs, surrounding a glabrous spot or mostly forming a conspicuous tuft. Gland dots in mature leaves not visible to moderately distinct above. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, ca. 0.4-40.9 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1-1.6 mm diam., 1-6.5 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4-2/3 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 0.6-3.8 cm long, i.e., ca. 2/5-3/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-4 below the terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, branched once or twice, indument consisting of short, ± appressed hairs, sparse to (moderately) dense but not very conspicuous. Pedicels extremely short or up to 2.5 mm long, 0.2-0.4 mm thick. Flowers (the bisexual ones, see discussion) 3.1-4.7 mm in diam., tepals elliptic to elongate, ca. 1.4-1.8 mm long and ca. 0.8-1.2 mm wide, on the inside surface with a moderately dense to sparse cover of fine, short papillae and a few hairs. Stamens ca. 0.9-1.1 mm long including a hairy filament of 0.2-0.4 mm, anthers glabrous or very slightly papillose at the tip, in the two outer whorls ± roundish-trapeziform to -rectangular, very broadly rounded to slightly emarginate at the tip, in the third whorl ± roundish-rectangular, truncate to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 3/5-3/4 the length of the stamens, with a distinct glandular head. Pistil ca. 1.3-1.5 mm long, glabrous, ovary ellipsoid, style reaching ca. 2/3 of the length to ± the length of the ovary. Receptacle very small, glabrous inside or with a few hairs at the margin. Berry ellipsoid, ca. 12-15 mm long and 7-8 mm in diam., cupule bowl-shaped to almost funnel-shaped and ± gradually merging into the thickened pedicel, the cup itself shallow, ca. 4-5 mm in diam. and ca. 1-1.5 mm high.

description: Tall trees, to 50 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 3-6.2 mm in diam., strongly angular, initially densely covered with very short, ± appressed, brown hairs, on older twigs becoming greyish but very slowly wearing off; terminal buds elongate, ca. 10-22 mm long, 3.3-5 mm thick, densely covered with very short, tap-pressed, light brown hairs. Petioles 7-20 mm long but often appearing longer because of the revolute leaf base, 2.5-5.5 mm thick, broadly roundish to triangular below, slightly longitudinally ridged, broadly and sometimes deeply canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs. Leaves alternate, ± elliptic, widest at the middle or slightly above, (10.5-)13-22 cm long, (5-)6-12 cm wide, 1.4-2.2 times longer than wide, tip ± obtuse but usually with a very short, indistinct acumen, base attenuate due to the broadly and conspicuously inrolled margin, midrib broadly impressed above and often slightly convex, at least at the base with a distinct central furrow, very prominent below, secondary veins convex above in a ± distinct impression, prominent below, 9-11 pairs, diverging at 40-50°, often almost straight, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 30-50° to the midrib, tertiary venation densely and regularly percurrent, sometimes almost scalariform, distinctly raised on both sides. Indument on both surfaces consisting of very short, + appressed hairs, even in young leaves sparse or initially up to moderately dense below, usually much denser on veins, quickly glabrescent above except for the base of the midrib, ± slowly becoming sparser below. Gland dots not seen. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, 1.8-3.3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2.2-4.7 mm diam., 3.5-14 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4 to slightly more than the length of its subtending leaf; peduncle 0.2-2.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/8-1/4 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 6-14 below the terminal cyme, branched (0-)2-3 times, the lower ones not entirely cymose, indument dense, brownish, similar to that on twigs (only slightly longer and more spreading). Pedicels ca. 1.5-3.5 mm long, ca. 0.5-0.9 mm thick. Flowers ca. 4.2-5.5 mm in diam., tepals rarely fully spreading, ± elliptic, ca. 2 mm long and ca. 1-1.5 mm wide, distinctly papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.8 mm long including a filament of ca. 0.3 mm, anthers scarcely if at all papillose, in all three whorls ± roundish-trapeziform, broadly rounded to slightly emarginate at the tip, in the first whorl wider than long, in the third longer than wide. Staminodes reaching ca. half the length of the stamens or slightly more, distinctly capitate (glandular?), with a few hairs at the filament, free. Pistil ca. 1.9 mm long, ovary ± ellipsoid or (inversely) pear-shaped, glabrous, style slightly shorter than the ovary, glabrous or with a few hairs near the tip. Receptacle broadly hemispherical, glabrous inside, relatively open above. Berry ellipsoid, 22-28 mm long and 12-14 mm in diam., cupule ± funnel-shaped, or bowl-shaped and merging into a ± distinctly thickened pedicel, 15-18 mm in diam., 6-9 mm deep, with six thick ridges corresponding to the midveins of the tepals, forming six thick, ± indistinct lobes at the margin.

description: Trees, to 30 m tall. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 2-6 mm in diam., at first distinctly longitudinally angular and/or furrowed, ± quickly becoming roundish, with very short, appressed hairs at the tip, moderately dense or sparser immediately below the terminal bud, quickly glabrescent, at least the internodes of larger twigs hollow; terminal buds conical to elongate, minute or up to 5 mm long and 3 mm thick, at least their tip densely covered with short, appressed hairs. Petioles 11-25 mm long, 1.5-3.5 mm thick, roundish below, ± flat above, shallowly canaliculate, or with a central ridge, at first with short, appressed hairs, quickly glabrescent. Leaves alternate, elliptic to lanceolate, widest ± at the middle, (11-)17-38 cm long, (4-)6-15 cm wide, 2.3-3.4 times longer than wide, tip ± long acuminate, acute to obtuse towards the base, the base itself attenuate, margin flat to narrowly revolute, midrib and secondary veins ± slightly convex in a slight impression above, occasionally almost flat, prominent below, secondary veins 5-8 pairs, diverging at 30-55°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 15-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation predominantly ± scalariform but often slightly irregular, occasionally with distinct intersecondaries, level or very slightly raised above, (slightly) raised below, finer venation mostly inconspicuous. Indument consisting of very short, appressed hairs (but see below), in young leaves only a few hairs on base of midrib above, ± sparse below, rather inconspicuous, quickly glabrescent on both sides, except for some stiff, erect hairs of ca. 0.2-0.3 mm length which are usually present in the axils of the lateral veins on lower leaf surface. Gland dots usually visible only in young leaves on both sides. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves and of cataphylls below the terminal bud, often also pseudoterminal, 1.2-4 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2-7 mm diam., 2.5-14 cm long, reaching less than 1/10 to ca. 2/3 the length of the closest foliage leaf; peduncle often extremely short (inflorescences branched from the base), or sometimes up to 6 cm long, i.e., reaching up to almost half the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-14 below terminal cyme (the lower ones often like independent inflorescences), branched 2-3 times, indument consisting of short, ± appressed hairs, sparse to intermediate. Pedicels ca 2-5.5 mm long, 0.4-1 mm thick. Flowers 8-12 mm in diam., tepals elliptic to oblong-elliptic, ca. 3.3-5 mm long and ca. 2-3.5 mm wide, papillosity ± moderately dense on the inside surface, relatively fine (for the size of the flowers). Stamens ca. 1.2-1.5 mm long including the short but distinct filament of 0.2-0.4 mm, anthers distinctly papillose at the tip, in the first whorl broadly pentagonal with an obtuse sterile tip, in the second whorl slightly narrower with an obtuse to parabolic sterile tip, in the third whorl elongate-pentagonal to roundish-obtrapeziform with an obtuse to broadly rounded tip. Staminodes rather large and thick, reaching ca. 1/2-2/3 the length of the stamens, slightly clavate, glandular on adaxial side, papillose on abaxial side, free or nearly so. Pistil ca. 1.6-2.2 mm long, glabrous, ovary spherical to ellipsoid or pear-shaped, style short, reaching ca. 1/3 the length of the ovary. Receptacle broadly urceolate, glabrous or with a few appressed hairs inside. Berry (immature?) depressed spheroidal, ca. 10 mm in diam., almost completely enclosed in a large, thick-walled, broadly urceolate cupule of ca. 12-15 m diam. and ca. 10-14 mm height on a distinctly thickened pedicel.

description: Trees, to 10 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 2-4.5 mm in diam., initially irregularly ± angular, at the tip with a moderately dense to sparse indument of short and sometimes a few longer (to 0.5 mm), straight, appressed hairs, quickly becoming sparser; terminal buds ± elongate (to ovate), 3-8 mm long, 1.3-2 mm thick, densely covered with short and moderately short (up to 0.3 mm), ± straight, ± appressed, pale copper-colored hairs. Petioles 9-22 mm long, 1.4-2.6 mm thick, roundish below, ± flat or shallowly canaliculate at the lamina above, indument below ± as on twigs, ± sparse, (slightly) denser above, glabrescent Leaves alternate, lanceolate to oblong-elliptic, widest 2/5 from the base to ± at the middle, 13-30 cm long, 5.5-9 cm wide, 2.6-3.8 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base acute to obtuse, margin flat or narrowly recurved, midrib convex in an impression above, very prominent below, secondary veins impressed and sometimes very slightly convex above, prominent below, 6-11 pairs, diverging at 45-55°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation ± scalariform, ± level above or often slightly impressed near the secondaries and slightly raised in between, distinctly raised below. Indument consisting of short, ± appressed hairs, mostly also some longer (to 0.5 mm), ± ascending hairs on veins, initially moderately sparse to sparse on both sides, older leaves glabrescent above (sometimes except for the base of the midrib), slowly subglabrescent below. Gland dots initially distinct on both sides, in mature leaves very inconspicuous. Inflorescences in the axils of just expanding leaves, sometimes pseudoterminal (thus often a whole lateral branch looking like a large frondose inflorescence), 1-2 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-4.5 mm diam., 5-13.5 cm long, reaching ca. half to slightly more than the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 2-6.5 cm long, i.e., 2/5-3/5 the length of the inflorescence, indument ± as on twigs, ± moderately sparse, lateral branches 2-8 below the terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, branched 3-5 times (or possibly more, last bracteoles often bear further undeveloped buds), cymules and especially flowers densely covered with short, appressed to ascending, ± greyish hairs. Pedicels 0.5-2.5 mm long, 0.30.5 mm thick. Flowers ca. 4-5 mm in diam., tepals elliptic, 1.6-2.6 mm long and 1.2-1.8 mm wide, on the inside surface covered with papillae which are so fine and short that even at 25x they are discernable only with difficulty. Stamens ca. 0.8-1.1 mm long including a short but distinct filament of 0.1-0.2 mm, anthers minutely papillose, in the first whorl very broadly ovate with an obtuse tip, in the second whorl broadly trullate to almost triangular with a ± parabolic tip, in the third whorl roundish-obtrapeziform with a broadly obtuse to almost truncate tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3 to almost half the length of the stamens, slightly club-shaped, papillose and sometimes with a few hairs on abaxial side, sometimes indistinctly glandular on adaxial side, united with the inner stamens at the very base. Pistil ca. 1.7 mm long, ovary ellipsoid, glabrous, style ca. as long as the ovary, covered with fine papillae. Receptacle urceolate, glabrous or with a few appressed hairs inside, in older flowers developing ridges below the (outer) tepals. Fruit unknown.

description: Trees, to 20 m (30 m ?). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 2.2-4 mm in diam., ± distinctly angular, initially with a dense, yellow- or reddish-brown cover of ± short hairs and ± ascending long hairs (ca. 0.3-1 mm), many of the long ones ± straight, older twigs becoming roundish, their indument becoming grey and felted, or only the short hairs persistent, very slowly wearing off; terminal buds ovoid to elongate, ca. 5-9 mm long, ca. 2.5-3.8 mm thick, densely covered with long, appressed to ascending, yellowish to reddish hairs. Petioles 6-16 mm long, 1-3 mm thick, especially in young leaves often rather flat, roundish to almost triangular below, ± longitudinally ridged, ± broadly canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs. Leaves alternate, lanceolate to oblong or elliptic, rarely ovate, widest 1/3 from the base to ca. at the middle, (7-)12-25 cm long, (3-)4.5-8.5 cm wide, (1.8-)2.4-3.6(-4) times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base at least in larger leaves usually ± obtuse, less often acute or broadly attenuate, margin with ± distinct recurved or revolute lobes, midrib ± distinctly impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins (4-)5-8 pairs, diverging at 40-50°, in midlamina running at an angle of 10-30° to the midrib, slightly impressed and sometimes very slightly convex above, prominent below, tertiary venation scalariform, often inconspicuous, level to very slightly impressed above, almost level to slightly raised below. Indument on both surfaces consisting of both short, appressed and — especially on veins and at the base — long, ± ascending hairs (usually to 0.6 mm, rarely to ca. 1 mm), initially sparse to intermediate on both sides, often much denser on veins, usually denser below than above, becoming sparse above or finally glabrescent, slowly becoming sparser below. Gland dots visible only in still membraneous young leaves. Inflorescences in the axils of young foliage leaves or rarely pseudoterminal, 0.82 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.6-4.8 mm diam., (2.8-)4-13 cm long (rarely frondose and longer), reaching ca. 1/5 to slightly more than the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle (1.4-)2-6 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/3-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-10 below terminal cyme, branched 2-3 times, indument dense, consisting of mainly ± long (0.30.7 mm), yellowish-grey hairs, usually both curled and straight, + ascending. Pedicels ca. 14 mm long, ca. 0.3-0.6 mm thick. Flowers ca. 4.5-5.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic to obovate, ca. 1.5-2.3 mm long and ca. 1-1.5 mm wide, with long papillae on the inside surface, not covering the entire surface, on inner tepals mainly at the tip, on outer ones mainly in basal triangle. Stamens ca. 0.8-1 mm long including a distinct filament of 0.3-0.5 mm, anthers distinctly papillose, in the first whorl ± transverse-elliptic to broadly trapeziform, very broadly rounded or often slightly three-pointed at the tip, in the second whorl slightly narrower than in the first, very broadly ovate to roundish-trapeziform, rounded to truncate at the tip, in the third whorl ± roundish-rectangular to obtrapeziform, ± truncate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. half (2/5-3/5) the length of the stamens, slightly clavate, papillose at the tip, free. Pistil ca. 1.8-2.2 mm long, ovary ± ellipsoid, glabrous, style ca. as long as the ovary or slightly shorter, glabrous or somewhat papillose and with a few hairs. Receptacle almost urceolate, glabrous inside. Berry ellipsoid, ca. 13-22 mm long, ca. 8-10 mm in diam., cupule bowl-shaped to cup-shaped, always shallow inside, ca. 2-5 mm high and ca. 7-9 mm in diam., usually with minute lenticels, pedicel relatively slightly thickened to distinctly incrassate.

description: Trees to 25 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 2-4.5 mm in diam., initially distinctly longitudinally angular/flattened, with a dense grayish or sometimes very light brown cover of ± straight, short to long (up to ca. 0.5 mm), appressed or p.p. ascending hairs, older twigs roundish, with the short hairs ± persistent as a grey cover, terminal buds elongate-ovoid, ca. 4-7.5 mm long and 1.5-3 mm thick, densely covered with short to moderately long, straight, appressed hairs. Petioles 6-17 mm long, 1.2-3 mm thick, ± roundish below, shallowly canaliculate above, often with ridges along the central furrow, indument ± as on twigs, denser above than below. Leaves alternate, elliptic, ovate-oblong, or lanceolate-oblong, widest 1/3-1/2 from the base, 7-20 cm long, 3.5-9.5 cm wide, 2-3.1 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base varying between attenuate and almost truncate, with a narrowly but distinctly reflexed to revolute margin. Midrib and secondary veins (distinctly) impressed above, (very) prominent below, secondary veins (5-)6-8 pairs, diverging at 40-55°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 15-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation ± scalariform, level to very slightly raised above, usually inconspicuous, ± raised below. Indument consisting of relatively coarse hairs, short and longer (up to 0.5 mm), appressed or p.p. ascending, initially sparse to moderately dense on the lamina, much denser on midrib and secondary veins above and sometimes also below, older leaves slowly glabrescent above, indument becoming much sparser and often inconspicuous below. Gland dots rarely visible above, only in youngest leaves. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, 1.2-2.8 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2.2-5.2 mm diam., ca. 1.5-11 cm long, reaching ca. 1/10 to almost the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 0.7-4.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/10-2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-10 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched once or twice (rarely three times, but then buds of the last order apparently staying undeveloped), indument ± as on twigs. Pedicels extremely short or up to 3 mm long, ca. 0.8-1.1 mm thick. Flowers ca. 6-7.5 mm in diam., tepals elongate-elliptic, ca. 2.2-3.5 mm long and ca. 1.5-2 mm wide, with fine, short papillae on the inside surface, sparse to intermediate at the base, moderately dense to dense at the tip. Stamens ca. 1.1-1.4 mm long, filament in the two outer whorls ca. 0.30.4 mm long, anthers moderately papillose at the tip, in the first whorl pentagonal to almost transverse-elliptic, with a ± obtuse tip, in the second whorl ovate to pentagonal, with an acute to obtuse tip, in the third whorl roundish-pentagonal to -obtrapeziform with an obtuse to broadly rounded tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3-2/5 of the stamen length, clavate, very slightly papillose on abaxial side, inconspicuously glandular on adaxial side, free. Pistil ca. 2.2 mm long, glabrous, ovary ellipsoid, style rather thick, ca. as long as the ovary or somewhat shorter. Receptacle deeply bowl-shaped, almost hemispherical, glabrous or with a few tightly appressed hairs inside. Berry ellipsoid, ca. 1826 mm long, ca. 12-18 mm in diam., cupule ± campanulate in very young fruit, becoming disklike in mature fruit, undulate, ca. 8 mm in diam., on a distinctly thickened, lenticellate pedicel.

description: Trees to 25 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.3-2 mm in diam., initially slightly angular and ± densely covered with pale, short, appressed hairs, becoming roundish and slowly glabrescent; terminal buds ovate to elongate, ca. 3-5 mm long and ca. 1 mm thick, with a dense cover of ± short, ± appressed hairs. Petioles 5-13 mm long, 0.6-1.6 mm thick, irregularly roundish below, canaliculate above, with short, appressed hairs, denser above than below, quickly becoming sparse. Leaves alternate, (narrowly) lanceolate to rarely ovate-elliptic, widest ca. 2/5 from the base to ca. at the middle, 5-15 cm long, 1.6-4.8 cm wide, 2.7-4.7 times longer than wide, the tip with a very long and fine acumen, base acute to attenuate, margin flat to very narrowly recurved, midrib and secondary veins ± impressed above (the latter often only slightly), prominent below, secondary veins (2-)3-5(-6) pairs, diverging at 30-50°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 10-30° or occasionally almost parallel to the midrib, tertiary venation finely scalariform, often relatively inconspicuous, very slightly raised to very slightly impressed above, ± raised below. Indument consisting of short, appressed hairs, ± sparse from the beginning above, denser on midrib, subglabrescent, initially sparse to moderately dense below, becoming (moderately) sparse and inconspicuous, axils of secondary veins below usually with some longer (up to 0.3 mm), erect hairs surrounding a glabrous spot. Gland dots not visible or very inconspicuous. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, 0.5-0.9 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 0.8-2.7 mm diam., 3.510 cm long, reaching ca. half the length to ca. the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 1.5-5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/2 to (rarely) 2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-4(-7) below terminal cyme, branched 2-3(-4) times, indument consisting of short, appressed to ascending hairs, sparse to intermediate on peduncle, denser on receptacle. Pedicels 3.5-9 mm long, 0.30.5 mm thick. Flowers ca. 7-9 mm in diam., tepals ± spatulate to elongate-elliptic, ca. 3-4.2 mm long and ca. 1.7-2.4 mm wide, densely covered with ± fine papillae on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.7-1.1 mm long including a distinct filament of 0.2-0.4 mm, anthers papillose at the tip, in all three whorls ± roundish-pentagonal or occasionally almost transverse-elliptic, with a short but distinct, obtuse to rounded sterile tip. Staminodes roundish or slightly club-shaped, reaching 1/2-2/3 the length of the stamens, ± papillose and with a few hairs on abaxial side, often with a small, inconspicuous glandular patch near the tip on adaxial side, ± free. Pistil ca. 1-1.2 mm long, ovary spheroidal to ellipsoid, glabrous, style extremely short, glabrous or with a few papillae. Receptacle broadly hemispherical, with a few very inconspicuous, tightly appressed hairs inside. Mature fruit unknown, possibly with a slightly lobed cupule (very young cupule slightly lobed).

description: Trees, to 20 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 2 mm in diam., ± angular, initially with a (moderately) dense cover of very short and some longer (up to ca. 0.3 mm) hairs, ± straight, ± erect to p.p. ascending, on older twigs (especially the shorter hairs) ± slowly becoming sparser, finally glabrescent; terminal buds elongate, ca. 4-5 mm long, ca. 1.5 mm thick, densely covered with appressed to ascending, pale hairs. Petioles 712 mm long, 1-2 mm thick, roundish below, slightly longitudinally ridged, shallowly canaliculate above, often with ridges along the central furrow, indument ± as on twigs, denser above than below. Leaves alternate, lanceolate to lanceolate-elliptic, widest at the middle or slightly below, 9-20 cm long, 3-6 cm wide, 2.7-3.8 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base acute to attenuate, margin flat or very narrowly bent down, midrib and secondary veins slightly impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins 6-9 pairs, diverging at 35-50°, in midlamina running at an angle of 10-40° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, ± level above, raised below. Indument on both surfaces consisting of relatively inconspicuous ± erect hairs, in intercostal area relatively short (0.1-0.2 mm) above, initially sparse to intermediate, and quickly subglabrescent, on midrib and secondaries denser, longer and ± ascending, persistent for a long time but finally glabrescent, hairs slightly longer (0.2-0.4 mm) below, density initially intermediate, slowly becoming sparser. Gland dots ± distinct above, like pinpricks (see p. 14). Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves or apparently terminal, 0.8-1.7 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.2-2.8 mm diam., (3-)6-11 cm long, reaching ca. 3/5 to 4/5 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle (1-) 1.5-3 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/8-1/3(-1/2) the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (2-)4-8(-14) below terminal cyme (the lower branches not always entirely cymose), branched 2-3 times, indument intermediate to moderately dense, on peduncles ± as on twigs, becoming shorter closer to the flowers. Pedicels ca. 1-4 mm long, ca. 0.3 mm thick. Flowers ca. 3-3.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elongate-ovate, ca. 1.2-1.5 mm long and ca. 0.8 mm wide, with fine papillae on the inside surface, dense near the tip, much sparser at the base. Stamens ca. 0.4-0.7 mm long including the distinct filament (0.2-0.3 mm), anthers with minute papillae, the outer ones transverse elliptic, broadly rounded at the tip, the inner ones ± roundish-rectangular to obtrapeziform, ± truncate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/2 to 2/3 the length of the stamens, slender, slightly clavate, papillose on abaxial side, glandular on adaxial side. Pistil ca. 1.2 mm long, glabrous, ovary ± ellipsoid, style reaching about 2/3 the length of the ovary. Receptacular tube paraboloidal, almost as deep as the stamens are long, glabrous or with very few hairs inside. Only very immature fruit known, still completely enclosed in the lenticellate cupule.

description: Trees (type specimen from a4 m tree). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.5-2.8 mm in diam., slightly angular, with a dense, pale grey cover of short, tightly appressed hairs, older twigs roundish, indument subpersistent; terminal buds narrowly lanceolate, densely covered with ± short, tightly appressed hairs. Petioles 612 mm long, 1.2-2 mm thick, apparently rolled, i.e., ± round but deeply canaliculate above, indument as on twigs. Leaves alternate, oblong, widest ca. 1/2-3/5 from the base, 10-24 cm long, 2.5-6 cm wide, 3.3-4 2 times longer than wide, relatively abruptly acuminate at the tip, base acute to obtuse, or rounded immediately at the petiole, margin flat, abruptly curved upwards at the petiole, midrib distinctly impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins ± impressed above, clearly raised below, (8-)10-13 pairs, diverging at 50-75°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 45-65° to the midrib, distinctly loop-connected near the margin, tertiary venation mixed, with only a few percurrent veinlets, inconspicuous, ± level above, very slightly raised below. Indument consisting of short, tightly appressed hairs only, initially dense on midrib above, subpersistent, the lamina glabrous, initially ± sparse below, subglabrescent, very inconspicuous. Gland dots usually not visible. Inflorescences in the axils of leaves on young growth, 0.4-0.8 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-2 mm diam., ca. 4-5 cm long, reaching 1/5-1/3 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 2-3 cm long, i.e., 1/2 to 2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (0-)2 below terminal cluster of cymes, branched once or twice, indument consisting of very short, tightly appressed, pale hairs, ± dense on peduncle, becoming intermediate to moderately sparse closer to the flowers. Pedicels 3-6 mm long, 0.30.5 mm thick. Flowers ca. 4.5 mm in diam., tepals ± triangular, ca. 1.4-1.7 mm long and ca. 1 mm wide, covered with relatively long, fine papillae on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.81 mm long including a short but distinct filament of ca. 0.2 mm, anthers papillose at the tip, ± broadly rhombic in the two outer whorls, with an obtuse or less frequently acute tip, in the third whorl ± spatulate with a broadly obtuse tip. Staminodes relatively large, reaching 1/2-2/3 the length of the stamens, ± lanceolate, with a few hairs at the filament Pistil ca. 0.8 mm long, glabrous, pear-shaped, stigma almost sessile. Receptacle broadly hemispherical, glabrous inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Shrubs or small trees, to 6 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 3 mm in diam., somewhat longitudinally furrowed, at least in dried material densely dotted with prominent idioblasts, initially with some ± ascending hairs of up to 0.5 mm length, quickly glabrescent and becoming more roundish; terminal buds densely hairy; seen only aborted or sprouting. Petioles (9-) 13-21 mm long, 1.5-3.8 mm thick, roundish below, only slightly irregular, indistinctly canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs. Leaves alternate, ovate to broadly elliptic, widest at the middle or slightly below, 10.5-31 cm long, 6-21 cm wide, 1.2-2 times longer than wide, tip obtuse with a very short and often indistinct acumen, rarely acute, base broadly rounded to slightly cordate, margin flat to minutely recurved at the base, midrib and secondary veins ± slightly convex above, sometimes in a slight impression, prominent below, secondary veins 6-8 pairs, diverging at 50-65°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-45° to the midrib, tertiary venation percurrent (to scalariform), level to very slightly raised above, (very) slightly raised below. Indument consisting mainly of short, ± appressed hairs, plus some slightly longer (to 0.4 mm), ± ascending hairs on veins, initially (moderately) sparse on both sides, quickly glabrescent above, more slowly (sub)glabrescent below, axils of secondary veins sometimes with some slightly thicker, ± erect hairs. Gland dots slightly prominent, usually distinct on the midrib and some larger secondary veins above, also visible on the lamina below, less distinct. Inflorescences apparently in the axils of foliage leaves and in the axils of cataphylls (judged from the size of the subtending scars; their size and structure being a matter of interpretation, see below), 1.5-3.2 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of ca. 2-4 mm diam., 8-24 long; peduncle 4-6.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/4-2/3 the length of the inflorescence, with a rather sparse indument of relatively long (to ca. 0.7 mm), erect, reddish hairs, lateral branches 0-7 below terminal cluster of cymes, branched 2-3 times, their indument becoming progressively denser closer to the flowers. Pedicels 1.52 mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm thick. Flowers ca. 8-10 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, densely papillose on the inside surface, ca. 3-5 mm long and ca. 2-3 mm wide, the outer ones slightly larger than the inner ones. Stamens ca. 1.4-1.6 mm long including a distinct filament of 0.2-0.4 mm, anthers distinctly papillose, in the first whorl ± quadrato-rhombic, with a well developed, obtuse sterile tip, in the second whorl narrower, trullate, with an acute tip, in the third whorl almost ob-trapeziform, truncate to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes reaching almost half the length of the stamens, thick, slightly clavate, papillose on abaxial side, glandular on adaxial side, united with the inner stamens for ca. 1/3 of their length. Pistil ca. 1.8-2 mm long, glabrous, ovary almost pear-shaped, style slightly shorter than the ovary. Receptacle cup-shaped, almost closed by the united bases of stamens and staminodes above, with some appressed hairs inside. Berry elongate, ca. 16-22 mm long, ca. 8-10 mm in diam., cupule cup-shaped to almost obconical or almost hemispherical, ca. 6-7 mm high and ca. 10 mm in diam., slightly irregular and still ± hairy outside.
