description: Trees, to 30 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 2.2-4.8 mm in diam., initially irregularly angular with mostly rounded ridges and relatively distinct furrows, with a ± moderately dense indument at the tip, consisting of both short, ± curled hairs and a variable number of longer (rarely up to 0.8 mm long), ascending to erect, somewhat curled to rather straight hairs, quickly becoming moderately sparse, then very slowly glabrescent; terminal buds ± elongate(-ovate), 5-10 mm long, 1.4-2.5 mm thick, densely covered with short, ± curled and longer (up to 0.7 mm), ± straight, appressed to ascending, slightly reddish hairs. Petioles 10-17 mm long, 1.5-3 mm thick, roundish below, only slightly irregular, ± flat above, usually slightly convex at the base and shallowly canaliculate at the lamina, indument below ± as on twigs, much denser above, slowly subglabrescent Leaves alternate, ± lanceolate, widest ± at the middle or often slightly above, (10-)14-26 cm long, (2.7-)3.3-8(-9) cm wide, (2.6-)3-4.5 times longer than wide, tip acuminate (acumen often rather long and fine), ± acute towards the base, the base itself attenuate due to the revolute margin running parallel to the petiole for ca. 6-16 mm (in mature leaves), midrib (slightly) convex in a slight impression above, very prominent below, secondary veins ± impressed and often slightly convex above, prominent below, 6-10 pairs, diverging at (30-)35-50°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 15-30(-35)° to the midrib, the distal ones often loop-connected, tertiary venation finely and regularly scalariform, ± level above and sometimes inconspicuous, raised below, often lighter than the lamina (as with the finer venation). Indument consisting of fine and mostly short (rarely up to 0.3 mm), ± curled, pale yellowish hairs above and longer (up to 0.7 mm), straight or curled, ± ascending, reddish hairs mainly on midrib and largest veins but also scattered on intercostal area, initially usually the entire surface covered with the fine hairs (rarely only moderately sparse), often very quickly becoming sparser, indument below consisting of short, appressed to ascending hairs, initially ± moderately sparse and often rather inconspicuous, and longer, straight to ± curled, ascending to erect, reddish hairs, the latter mainly on veins, crowded in the axils of secondary veins, there up to 0.5 mm long, ± erect and ± curled, mature leaves above glabrescent or sometimes indument p.p. persistent on midrib, becoming ± sparse below. Gland dots initially distinct on both sides but often concealed by the indument above, in mature leaves less distinct but usually still visible. Inflorescences in the axils of distal foliage leaves, rarely pseudoterminal, 0.92 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-5 mm diam., 3-13.5 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4-1/2 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 1-5 (-8) cm long, i.e., 1/4-3/5 the length of the inflorescence, indument ± as on twigs, moderately dense to (moderately) sparse, lateral branches 2-6(-8) below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched (0-)2-3(-4) times, cymules and especially flowers densely covered with ± short, ± ascending, whitish hairs. Pedicels 1.2-5 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mm thick. Flowers (5-)6-8(-9) mm in diam., tepals oblong elliptic to elongate ovate, (2.2-)2.7-3.6(-4) mm long and 2.2-2.5 mm wide, distinctly papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.7-0.9 mm long including a short but distinct filament of 0.1-0.3 mm, anthers papillose, in the first whorl transverse-elliptic to suborbicular, with a broadly rounded to almost obtuse tip, in the second whorl quadrato-rhombic to trullate, with a parabolic to acute tip, in the third whorl roundish-obtrapeziform to roundish-rectangular, with a ± truncate tip (slightly emarginate to broadly obtuse). Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3 to almost half the length of the stamens, slightly club-shaped, papillose, not glandular, united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 1.6-1.8 mm long, ovary ellipsoid to pearshaped, glabrous, style ca. as long as the ovary, densely covered with long, hair-like papillae. Receptacle urceolate, glabrous inside. Only immature fruit known, cupule ± hemispherical but towards the margin developing six rather large and thick ± obtuse lobes, the cup ca. 7-9 mm high and ca. 12-15 mm in diam., pedicel slightly but increasingly thickened, berry ± ovate, the largest ca. 10 mm long and 7.5 mm in diam.

description: Trees, to ca. 10 m tall. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 2-3 mm in diam., initially slightly ridged, the new growth densely covered with ± short (to 0.3 mm), ± appressed, light brown hairs, older twigs ± roundish, indument quickly becoming felted, quickly glabrescent; termini buds ovoid, 2-4 mm long, ca. 1-1.5 mm thick, densely covered with ± short, tightly appressed, brown hairs. Petioles 3-5.5 mm long, 1-2 mm thick, roundish below, usually ± gutter-shaped above due to the erect margin, indument above initially ± as on twigs, (much) sparser below, glabrescent Leaves alternate (or the last pair of a growing season nearly opposite), elliptic or sometimes suborbicular, widest ± at the middle, 3-6.5 cm long, 1.5-4 cm wide, 1.3-2.2 times longer than wide, tip mostly obtuse with a very short and indistinct acumen, sometimes rounded, rarely slightly emarginate, base acute or mostly obtuse, margin flat to minutely recurved, midrib above ± convex in a slight impression, prominent below, secondary veins (slightly) convex above, often in a very slight impression, raised to prominent below, 3-5 pairs, diverging at 45-50(-65)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 40-50(-75)° to the midrib (i.e., sometimes slightly curved backwards), tertiary venation mixed to almost lineate, reticulate, ± raised on both sides. Indument consisting of short (sometimes reaching ca. 0.3 mm below), appressed hairs, in young leaves ± sparse on both sides, slightly denser on midrib and largest veins, axils of secondary veins with short to moderately long (ca. 0.6 mm), erect hairs below, surrounding a glabrous spot or forming a dense tuft, mature leaves glabrescent on both sides (often except for the base of the midrib) or remaining sparsely hairy below. Gland dots visible only in still membraneous leaves. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, ca. 0.8-1.4 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.3-2.3 mm diam., 5-8.5 cm long, teaching ca. 1-2 times the length of their subtending leaf; peduncle 0.6-3.5 cm long, i.e., less than 1/10 to ca. 2/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 4-6 below the terminal cyme, branched once or twice, indument consisting of ± short, appressed to ascending hairs, moderately sparse to moderately dense but still inconspicuous. Pedicels 1.55 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm thick. Flowers 4.5-6.2 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, ca. 1.7-2.5 mm long and ca. 1.1-1.5 mm wide, ± papillose on the inside surface (sometimes sparsely), also hairy towards the base. Stamens ca. 0.8-0.9 mm long including a hairy filament of ca. 0.3 mm, anthers glabrous, in the two outer whorls transversely ± elliptic to roundish-rectangular, broadly rounded to truncate at the tip, in the third whorl ± roundish-squarish, truncate to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes ± large, slightly clavate, reaching ca. 3/5-3/4 the length of the stamens, with a hairy filament, probably glandular at the tip on adaxial side. Pistil ca. 1-1.2 mm long, glabrous, ovary ± spheroidal, style ca. as long as the ovary or ca. 1/3 shorter. Receptacle shallow, bowl-shaped, with a few hairs inside. Berry elongate ellipsoid, ca. 18 mm long and 8 mm in diam., cupule almost obconical, ca. 7 mm in diam. and ca. 4.5 mm high outside, much shallower inside, pedicel distinctly thickened, gradually merging into the cupule.

description: Trees, to 20 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.5-3.5(-4.5) mm in diam., initially ± longitudinally angular/furrowed or somewhat flattened, covered with a dense, yellowish- or greyish-brown indument of short, appressed hairs, older twigs becoming roundish, their indument becoming grey, persistent for a long time; terminal buds elongate or rarely ovoid, 4-11 mm long, 1.2-3.5 mm thick, densely covered with mostly ± straight, appressed, brownish hairs. Petioles 7—17 mm long, 0.9-2.5 mm thick, irregularly roundish below, canaliculate above, indument initially ± as on twigs, denser above than below, subglabrescent. Leaves alternate, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate or rarely almost elliptic, widest 1/3 from the base to ± at the middle, (8-)13-22(-27) cm tong, (2-)4-8(-10) cm wide, (2.2-)2.8-4.1(-5) times longer than wide, tip tapering towards a mostly long and fine acumen, base acute to obtuse or less often broadly attenuate, margin narrowly recurved, midrib impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins (4-)5-8 pairs, diverging at (25-)35-50 (-60)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 10-35° to the midrib, slightly impressed or rarely ± level above, prominent below, tertiary venation finely scalariform, ± level above, slightly raised below. Indument in young leaves dense on both sides, consisting of short, appressed hairs, also with small, dense tufts of (often reddish) erect hairs below in the axils of at least the lower lateral veins, older leaves glabrescent above, indument for a long time ± persistent below but finally becoming very sparse. Gland dots usually not apparent, occasionally becoming visible on upper leaf surface when the indument is tost relatively early. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, 0.8-2 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.7-4 mm diam., (2-)4-10(-16) cm long, reaching ca. 1/4 to almost the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle (l-)2.5-5(-8) cm long, i.e., ca. 2/5 to 3/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (0-)2-4(-5) below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched (l-)3(-4) times, indument dense, ± as on twigs. Pedicels 0.5-2(-4.5) mm long, 0.4-0.9 mm thick. Flowers 5.5-9 mm in diam., tepals oblong-elliptic to (ob)ovate-elliptic, ca. (2.4-)2.7-3.5(-4) mm long and ca. 1.8-3 mm wide, papillosity ± dense on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.9-1.2 mm long including a distinct filament of 0.2-0.4 mm, anthers papillose, in all three whorls ± pentagonal, with a distinct, obtuse sterile tip (in the second whorl slightly narrower than in the first whorl, their tip sometimes acute). Staminodes reaching ± half the length of the stamens, slightly thickened at the tip, papillose on abaxial side, glandular on adaxial side, united with the inner stamens for almost 2/3 of their length. Pistil ca. 2-2.4 mm long, ovary ellipsoid, glabrous, style ± as long as the ovary, usually glabrous, rarely with a few papillae. Receptacle deeply urceolate, with a few inconspicuous, tightly appressed hairs inside, rarely glabrous. Berry short elliptic to ovate, ca. 10-13 mm long, 8-9 mm in diam., cupule deep, ± hemispherical, ca. 11-14 mm in diam. and ca. 7-8 mm deep, rough on outside, with small lenticels, pedicel ± slightly thickened.

description: Trees, to 15 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.8-3.5 mm in diam., ± longitudinally angular, from the beginning with only relatively few, straight, ± appressed hairs, both short and long (up to 1.2 mm), quickly glabrescent; terminal buds rather narrow, 3.5-10 mm long, 0.7-2 mm thick, densely covered with relatively long (0.41 mm), straight, appressed hairs. Petioles 6-10 (-15) mm long, 1-2.2 mm thick, roundish below, only slightly irregular, flattened above, sometimes slightly canaliculate, indument as on twigs below, only short hairs or glabrous above. Leaves alternate, lanceolate to elliptic, widest at the middle or slightly below, (7-)9-17(-21) cm long, (2.2-)3-5(-6.5) cm wide, 2.4-4.3 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base acute to rarely obtuse, margin flat or nearly so, midrib and secondary veins (very) slightly impressed above but at least the midrib convex, prominent below, secondary veins 5-7 pairs, diverging at 45-60°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, rarely with a few small intersecondaries, like the finer reticulation almost level or slightly raised above, (slightly) raised below. Indument in young leaves (moderately) dense above, inconspicuous or forming a distinct yellowish to whitish cover, consisting of rather short, ± appressed to ascending hairs, quickly wearing off but usually more persistent near the veins, indument rather sparse below, consisting of very short, appressed hairs in the intercostal area and short as well as longer, straight, appressed hairs (as on twigs) on midrib and secondaries, older leaves glabrescent on both sides, usually a few hairs on veins persistent below. Gland dots usually distinct in younger leaves. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, 0.8-1.5 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-3.5 mm diam., (3-)4-13 cm long, reaching ca. half the length to ± the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle (1.5-)2-6.5 cm long, i.e., ca. half the length of the inflorescence, with a (moderately) sparse indument of mainly short hairs, lateral branches 2-4(-6) below terminal cyme, branched 1-3 times, with a pale, short, (moderately) dense indument. Pedicels 2.5-7.5 mm long, 0.3-0.6 mm thick. Flowers 7.5-9 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, ca. 3.2-4 mm long and ca. 2.1-2.8 mm wide, densely papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 1.5 mm long including the very short filament, anthers papillose, in the first whorl variable between trullate and suborbicular, with a well developed acute to almost rounded sterile tip which occupies at least half the length of the anther, in the second whorl narrower, trullate, its tip acute to parabolic, in the third whorl roundish-rectangular to almost obtrapeziform, with a broadly ± rounded tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3 the length of the stamens, thickish and papillose, ± united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 2.2-2.5 mm long, ovary ellipsoid, glabrous, style slightly longer than the ovary, papillose. Receptacle urceolate, glabrous inside. Berry (of only fruit seen, Vásquez 10205) 19 mm long and ca. 10 mm in diam., cupule subhemispherical, lenticellate, ca. 7 mm high and probably ca. 12 mm in diam. (pressed nearly flat).

description: Trees to shrubs: branches basitonic, in axils of cataphylls; twigs angular and remaining so for at least two flushes, ca. 3 mm diam.; epidermis brownish; terminal bud plump, ca. 5 X 3 mm; cataphylls caducous; indument tomentose, caducous by next flush, the hairs dense, to 0.8 mm long, curved, erect, brownish. Leaves: petioles robust, 0.6-1.7 cm X 1.2-1.8 mm, adaxially flattened; blades chartaceous, flat, broadly elliptic to obovate, (4-)7-9(-11) X (2-)3-6 cm; base obtuse to rounded, 70-110°; apex obtuse to rounded, 90-140°, (mucronate); margin plane; primary vein above flat to slightly raised, below prominent; secondary veins (3-)4(-5) pairs, equidistant, eucamptodromous, above flat, below raised, diverging at 5055°, abruptly arching near margin (forked), chordal angle 20-25°, the angle uniform along blade length; tertiary veins above flat, below slightly raised, random-reticulate; higher-order veins above flat, below slightly raised; surface above olive-green to greenish brown, below light green to brown, conspicuously glaucous; indument above absent, the primary vein puberulous, below puberulous, the hairs sparse to isolated, to 0.3 mm long, straight to curved, erect, yellowish, caducous after one flush. Staminate inflorescences: mesotonic to acrotonic, erect, peduncles 7-13 cm long, the hypopodia 3-7 cm X ca. 1 mm, branch orders 4-5, the second-order branches 4-6, dispersed, lowest branch to 4(-7) cm long, all axes dark brown, puberulous to glabrous; bracts and bracteoles caducous (not seen). Staminate flowers: pedicels 7-12 X ca. 0.8 mm, the diameter gradually increasing apically; receptacle obconical, ca. 2 X 2.2 mm; tepals chartaceous, ovate, ca. 2.5 X 2 mm, at anthesis erect to spreading, yellowish brown, translucent, adaxially puberulous; stamens of whorls I and II spathulate, the anthers oblong inflexed, ca. 1.6 X 0.8 mm, glabrous, the locelli 4, apical, in a shallow arch, introrse, the glands absent; whorl III filiform, ca. 2.4 X 0.8 mm, glabrous, the anthers oblong, the locelli 4, the upper pair latrorse, the lower pair extrorse, the glands globular, ca. 1.5 mm diam.; whorl IV absent; all stamens reddish; pistillode filiform, ca. 1.5 x 0.3 mm, glabrous. Pistillate flowers: pistil ca. 2.5 x 1.2 mm; ovary ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous. Fruits: pedicels to 15 X 3 mm, gradually enlarging to form the cupule; cupule trumpet-shaped, to 13 X 20 mm, smooth, the margin straight, tepals caducous; berry elliptic, to 25 X 20 mm.

description: Trees: branching unknown; twigs angular, soon becoming terete, ca. 8 mm diam.; epidermis black, barely visible due to indument cover; terminal bud plump, ca. 1 x 1 mm; cataphylls caducous; indument puberulous, caducous after one flush, the hairs dense, to 1 mm long, straight to curved, erect, golden. Leaves: petioles robust, 2.5-4.2 cm x 0.3-0.6 mm, adaxially flattened; blades chartaceous, flat, broadly obovate to elliptic or oblong, 16-29(-39) x 6-11 (-17) cm; base acute to obtuse, 80-130°; apex acute to obtuse, 80-120°,  ultimately acuminate for up to 1.5(-2.5) cm; margin plane; primary vein above slightly impressed to flat, below prominent; secondary veins (12-) 14-17 pairs, equidistant, brochidodromous, above flat, below prominent, diverging at 45-60°, abruptly arching near margin, chordal angle 45-60°, the angle uniform along blade length; tertiary veins above slightly raised, below raised, conspicuously scalariform; higher-order veins above slightly raised, below raised; surface above shiny brown, below dull creamy brown; indument above absent, the primary vein puberulous, below tomentose, the hairs dense, to 0.4 mm long, straight to curved, erect, yellowish, denser on the veins, persisting for at least two flushes. Staminate inflorescences: along whole length of flush to acrotonic, pendulous, peduncles 10-20 cm long, the hypopodia 3-6 cm x ca. 3.5 mm, branch orders 3, the second-order branches 13-18, dispersed, lowest branch to 3.5 cm long, color and indument of all axes as on twigs; bracts caducous (not seen); brac-teoles persistent or caducous, to 2 mm long, adaxially glabrous. Staminate flowers: pedicels ca. 1.2 x 1.4 mm, the diameter even throughout; receptacle globose, ca. 4 x 3.6 mm, constricted at the place of tepal inception; tepals coriaceous, ovate, ca. 2.2 x 1.8 mm, at anthesis spreading, yellowish brown, adaxially pu-berulous; stamens of whorls I and II loriform, the anthers oblong, ca. 1.6 x 0.6 mm, puberulous, the locelli 4, apical, in a shallow arch, the upper pair introrse, the lower pair latrorse, the glands absent; whorls II and III fused for two thirds of their lengths into a tube; whorl III loriform, ca. 2.4 x 0.8 mm, puberulous, the locelli 4, the upper pair latrorse, the lower pair extrorse, the glands minute, ca. 0.4 mm diam.; whorl IV absent; all stamens reddish brown; pistillode filiform, ca. 1 x 0.3 mm, glabrous. Pistillate flowers: pistil ca. 4 x 1.6 mm; ovary globose, ca. 2.8 mm long, glabrous. Fruits: pedicels to 10 x 5 mm, abruptly enlarging to form the cupule; cupule hemispherical, to 15 x 25 mm, smooth, the margin straight, tepals caducous; berry elliptic, to 40 x 22 mm.

description: Trees to 25 m tall. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 2-4.5 mm in diam., initially ± angular, with a very dense cover of very short, ± appressed hairs and longer (to ca. 0.5 mm), ± erect hairs, the short hairs long persistent, gradually changing into a continuous grey cover; terminal buds elongate, ca. 6-22 mm long and 2-5 mm thick, densely covered with ± ascending hairs up to 0.5 mm long. Petioles 9-23 mm long (sometimes appearing longer when leaf base revolute), 1-3.5 mm thick, broadly irregularly roundish below, flat to canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs but often less dense below, slowly becoming sparser. Leaves alternate, narrowly lanceolate to sometimes almost linear, widest 1/3 from the base to ca. at the middle, (12-)20-28(-34) cm long, (2.5-)3-5.5(-7.5) cm wide, (3.4-}4.7-6.8 times longer than wide, tip tapering towards an often long and narrow acumen, base acute to attenuate, margin distinctly recurved to narrowly revolute, midrib ± impressed but sometimes with convex margins above, very prominent below, secondary veins level to slightly raised above, prominent below, (7-)8-ll(-14) pairs, diverging at (25-)35-45(-55)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of (10-) 20-30(-3S)° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, sometimes inconspicuous, ± raised on both sides. Indument consisting of ± short (0.1-0.3 mm), appressed hairs above, in young leaves sparse to intermediate, denser on veins, consisting of short, appressed hairs and fewer longer hairs (to ca. 0.5 mm) below, in young leaves (at least during anthesis) very dense, often slightly sparser on veins, mature leaves glabrous or nearly so above (often except for the base of the midrib), indument little changed or becoming moderately sparse below. Axils of secondary veins on lower leaf surface bearded with ± erect hairs of variable length. Gland dots visible only in the youngest leaves above. Inflorescences in the axils of (younger) foliage leaves, sometimes some of the distal ones apparently also in the axils of cataphylls, 1-2.3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.8-4 mm diam., (3.5-)5-20 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4 of the length to ca. the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle (1-)2-8 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/6-1/2 of the inflorescence length, lateral branches (4-)8-14 below the terminal cyme, branched (3-) 4-5 times, the distal 2-3 internodes staying very short, therefore flowers ± glomerate, indument ± dense, consisting of very short and ca. 0.3 mm long, somewhat curled, ± erect hairs. Pedicels extremely short or up to 1 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm thick. Flowers ca. 4-5.6 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, ca. 1.8-2.6 mm long and ca. 1-1.4 mm wide, with a moderately dense to moderately sparse cover of minute papillae on the inside surface, sometimes absent from the margin on outer tepals. Stamens ca. 1-1.4 mm long including a distinct filament of ca. 0.2-0.4 mm, anthers papillose at the tip, in the two outer whorls broadly ovate to roundish-trapeziform, distinctly apiculate to obtuse or truncate at the tip, in the third whorl ± rectangular, obtuse to truncate at the tip. Staminodes distinctly clavate, reaching ca. half the length of the stamens, glandular on adaxial side, for ca. half their length united with the inner stamens. Pistil ca. 1.8 mm long, glabrous, ovary elongate-ellipsoid, style ca. as long as the ovary or slightly shorter. Receptacle (incl. stamen and staminode bases) urceolate, glabrous or with a few appressed hairs inside. Only immature fruit known, apparently like that of N. longifolia (see above), but tepals falling off relatively late.

description: Trees to 15 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.8-3.8 mm in diam., initially ± distinctly ridged, indument consisting of very short, almost papillae-like, ± appressed, brown hairs, and slightly longer (up to 0.3 mm), thickish, appressed to erect, brown hairs, (moderately) dense below terminal bud, epidermis quickly becoming visible between the hairs, then ± slowly glabrescent; terminal buds ovoid to elongate, ca. 1.53 mm long and 1-1.6 mm thick, densely covered with (moderately) short, appressed to ascending, brown hairs. Petioles (6-) 10-22 mm long, 1-2.3 mm thick, ± roundish below, ± canaliculate above, indument initially ± similar to that on twigs, quickly glabrescent or some of the shortest hairs persistent below. Leaves alternate, elliptic to lanceolate-elliptic, widest ± at the middle, (7.5-)11-22(-28) cm long, (2.2-)4.5-9(-10.5) cm wide, 2.2-3.5 times longer than wide, tip with a relatively long and fine acumen, base cuneate to obtuse, margin flat or nearly so, midrib ± slightly impressed to almost level above, changing from concave at the base to convex higher up, very prominent below, secondary veins slightly impressed to level above, often slightly convex, prominent below, 5-7(-8) pairs, diverging at 4565°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of (15-) 25-40(-45)° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed, proportion of the percurrent to scalariform part variable, widely spaced, often rather inconspicuous above, ± level, ± raised below. Indument consisting of very short, appressed, pale brown hairs, plus some slightly longer (to ca. 0.3 mm), appressed to ascending hairs on veins, (almost) exclusively on veins or glabrous from die beginning above, initially sparse to moderately dense but very inconspicuous below, slowly glabrescent, lower leaf surface microscopically papillose. Axils of secondary veins nearly always bearded with stiff, erect, brown hairs of up to 0.4 mm length. Gland dots in mature leaves not visible below, not visible to distinct above, like minute, black, pinpricks (see p. 14), not very dense. Inflorescences most frequently in the axils of cataphylls on new growth or below the terminal bud, but also in the axils of (younger) foliage leaves or apparently terminal, 0.7-2 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.3-4.5 mm diam., 2.5-18 cm long (terminal inflorescences sometimes larger), reaching ca. 1/3 of the length to almost the length of the closest foliage leaf; peduncle extremely short (especially the larger inflorescences often branched from the base) or up to 5.5 cm long, i.e., up to half the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (2-)4-8(-16) below the terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, branched 2-3 times, indument ± as on twigs, moderately dense to sparse on peduncle, usually becoming denser on the inflorescence branches, with an increasing proportion of the longer hairs, sometimes again sparse on the flowers. Pedicels 1.5-5 mm long, 0.2-0.5 mm thick. Flowers ca. 3.5-5.5 mm in diam., tepals elliptic to oblong, ca. 1.6-2.3 mm long and ca. 0.8-1.3(-l.6) mm wide, densely covered with ± fine papillae on the inside surface, on outer tepals sometimes sparser and shorter towards the margins. Stamens minutely papillose throughout, ca. 0.6-0.9 mm long including a distinct, broad filament of ca. 0.20.3 mm length, anthers in the two outer whorls ± transverse-elliptic to broadly trapeziform, in the third whorl ± roundish-squarish, in all three very broadly rounded to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes slightly clavate, reaching ca. half die length of the stamens, slightly papillose and with a few hairs, for ca. half of their length united with the inner stamens. Pistil ca. 1.2-1.6 mm long, ovary ± ellipsoid, glabrous, style ca. as long as the ovary, slightly papillose. Receptacle cup-shaped, glabrous or with some tightly appressed hairs inside. Berry depressed ellipsoid, ca 17-20 mm long, ca. 9-11 mm in diam., cupule very shallowly bowl-shaped, almost flat or up to 2 mm high, ca. 7-9 mm in diam., pedicel ± slightly but increasingly thickened.

description: Small trees, to ca. 8 m tall (or taller?). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 1.3-2 mm in diam., roundish from the beginning (with very slight longitudinal ridges), initially with some inconspicuous, short, appressed hairs, but soon glabrescent; terminal buds elongate, ca. 1.83 mm long and ca. 0.5-1 mm thick, with a (moderately) dense cover of very short, tightly appressed hairs. Petioles 10-25 mm long, 0.92 mm thick, roundish below, ± canaliculate above, glabrous from the beginning or initially with a few very inconspicuous hairs. Leaves alternate, ± elliptic (to slightly ovate- or lanceolate-elliptic), widest at the middle or slightly below (to ca. 2/5 from the base), (7.5-)9-17 cm long, (3-)5-8 cm wide, 1.5-2.9 times longer than wide, tip ± short acuminate, base mostly obtuse, occasionally acute or broadly attenuate, margin flat to minutely bent down, midrib above impressed at the base, distinctly raised near the tip, prominent below, secondary veins on both sides distinctly raised to prominent, 5-8 pairs, diverging at 50-65°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 40-55° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed, ± reticulate, on both sides raised (almost as much as the secondary veins). Indument absent above from the beginning, consisting of a few (if any) inconspicuous, short, appressed hairs below, axils of secondary veins often with a few longer (to ca. 0.5 mm), ± erect hairs. Gland dots in mature leaves scarcely if at all visible. Inflorescences in the axils of cataphylls below the terminal bud or at the base of the new growth, ca. 0.6-0.8 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 0.8-1.2 mm diam., 3.5-5 cm long, reaching ca. 1/3-2/5 the length of closest foliage leaf; peduncle 1.4-2.6 cm long, i.e., ca. 2/5-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-4 below the terminal cyme, branched 1-3 times, indument consisting of very short (<0.1 mm), ± appressed hairs, (almost) absent on peduncle, (moderately) sparse on the flowers, occasionally denser, but then almost papillae-like. Pedicels ca. 1.7-2.3 mm long, 0.3-0.6 mm thick. Flowers (3.5-) 4.8-5.7 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, ca. (1.6-) 2-2.6 mm long and ca. 0.9-1.4 mm wide, with a moderately dense cover of fine papillae on the inside surface, especially near the base also with some hairs. Stamens ca. 0.7-1 mm long including a hairy filament of 0.2-0.3 mm, anthers finely papillose at the tip, usually with a few hairs on back side, in the outer whorls ± transverse-elliptic to (transversely) roundish-rectangular, broadly rounded to almost truncate at the tip, in the third whorl (longitudinally) ± roundish-rectangular, broadly rounded to very slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 3/5-2/3 the length of the stamens, with a ± hairy filament and a distinct glandular head. Pistil ca. 1.2-1.4 mm long, ovary ± ellipsoid, with a few minute, very inconspicuous papillae, style very short (reaching ca. 1/4 the length of the ovary), slightly papillose. Receptacle shallowly bowl-shaped, glabrous inside. Berry ± ellipsoid, puberulous, in the most mature fruit ca. 19 mm long and ca. 10 mm in diam., cupule almost trumpet-shaped, becoming shallower at maturity, ca. 1.5-4 mm high and ca. 6-7 mm in diam., pedicel thickened towards the cupule, sometimes gradually merging into it.

description: Trees: branches basitonic, in axils of cataphylls or basal foliage leaves, often pseudo-verticillate; twigs angular, soon becoming terete, 3-6 mm diam.; epidermis brownish to black, barely visible due to indument cover; terminal bud plump, 3-7 x 2-3 mm; cataphylls caducous; indument pubescent, persisting for at least two flushes, the hairs dense, to 0.3(-0.9) mm long, straight to curved, erect, yellowish. Leaves: petioles robust, 0.5-1.3 cm x 1-3 mm, adaxially flattened; blades chartaceous, flat, narrowly (broadly) elliptic, (5-) 10-14 (-18) x (2-) 3-5 (-7) cm; base acute to obtuse, ca. 100°; apex acute, 70-120°, ultimately acuminate for up to 0.5 cm; margin plane; primary vein above slightly raised, below prominent; secondary veins (6-) 7 (-9) pairs, equidistant, eucamptodromous, above slightly raised, below prominent, diverging at ca. 70°, straight to evenly arching (forked), chordal angle 40-50°, the angle uniform along blade length; tertiary veins above and below raised, random-reticulate; higher-order veins above and below slightly raised; surface above shiny yellowish brown in young leaves, opaque brown in older leaves, the veins slightly lighter, below dull yellowish brown in young leaves, faintly reddish brown in older leaves, the veins lighter; indument above puberulous to absent, the primary and secondary veins tomentose, caducous by next flush to persisting for at least two flushes, below puberulous to velutinous, the hairs dense to sparse, to 1 mm long, straight to curved, erect, yellowish, denser on the veins, persisting for at least two flushes. Staminate inflorescences: along whole length of flush, pendulous, peduncles 3-11 cm long, the hypopodia 2-6 cm X 1-1.5 mm, branch orders 4, the second-order branches 4-7, dispersed, lowest branch to 1.5(-4) cm long, color and indument of all axes as on twigs; bracts and bracteoles caducous (not seen). Staminate flowers: pedicels ca. 5.6 X 1.2 mm, the diameter gradually increasing apically; receptacle obconical, ca. 3.2 X 3.5 mm; tepals coriaceous, ovate, ca. 5 X 4 mm, at anthesis erect to spreading, black, adaxially glabrous; stamens of whorls I and II, the anthers sessile, chubby, trapezoid, ca. 1.4 X 1.2 mm, with a few hairs at base, the locelli 4, apical, in a shallow arch, introrse, the glands absent; whorl III columnar, ca. 1.6 X 0.8 mm, with a few hairs at base, the locelli 4, the upper pair latrorse, the lower pair extrorse, the glands fused, forming a continuous ring protruding between the anthers of the outer whorls; whorl IV absent; all stamens blackish; pistillode filiform, ca. 1.7 X 1 mm, glabrous. Pistillate flowers: pistil ca. 3 X 1.5 mm; ovary ovoid to globose, ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous. Fruits: pedicels to 45 X 5 mm, gradually enlarging to form the cupule; cupule hemispherical, to 7 X 19 mm, smooth, the margin undulate, tepals persisting; berry elliptic, to 35 X 21 mm.

description: Shrubs or mostly small trees, rarely (fide Williams) 30 m tall. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 2.2-4 mm in diam., initially ± distinctly angular, with ± short, appressed, whitish hairs, moderately dense to intermediate below terminal bud, usually ± quickly becoming sparser, older twigs glabrous, usually longitudinally ridged and ± lenticellate; terminal buds ovoid to elongate, 4-6 mm long, ca. 0.9-2.2 mm thick, densely covered with short, appressed, white hairs. Petioles 7-18 mm long, 1.4-3 mm thick, ± roundish to almost triangular below, ± flat to broadly canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs, denser or sparser above, glabrescent. Leaves alternate, ± elliptic, widest at the middle or slightly above, 10-23 cm long, 5-9.5 cm wide, 1.9-3(-3.5) times longer than wide, tip with a usually short and relatively blunt acumen, base acute to obtuse, margin flat to minutely recurved, midrib above level to slightly impressed, gradually changing from flat or concave at the base to convex at the tip, very prominent below, secondary veins ± slightly convex above, often in a slight impression, (very) prominent below, 6-9(-10) pairs, diverging at (35-)40-55(-60)° in mid-lamina running at an angle of 30-40(-50)°to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed to largely percurrent or scalariform, widely spaced, finer reticulation almost equally distinct, level to slightly raised above, rarely very slightly impressed, distinctly raised to prominent below. Indument consisting of ± short (rarely reaching ca. 0.3 mm), straight, white, appressed hairs, in young leaves sparse to only on midrib and largest veins above,+quickly glabrescent, initially ± sparse below, subglabrescent, axils of secondary veins nearly always bearded with rather long (up to ca. 0.8 mm), ± erect hairs. Gland dots in mature leaves usually not visible, in young leaves sometimes moderately distinct Inflorescences mainly in the axils of cataphylls at the base of the new growth or below the terminal bud, often also in the axils of younger leaves, ca. 1-2.3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.8-4 mm diam., 4-13.5(-17.5) cm long, reaching ca. 1/3-3/4 the length of the closest foliage leaf; peduncle 2-5.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/3-2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-6 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched (0-)l-2(-3) times, indument short to moderately long (up to 0.5 mm), on peduncle ± appressed and sparse to moderately dense, becoming more ascending to erect, ± curled, dense, and conspicuously white closer to the flowers. Pedicels 1.5-3.5 mm long, 0.5-0.8 (-1) mm thick. Flowers (6.5-)7.5-9(-9.6) mm in diam., tepals elliptic to elongate (the outer ones wider than the inner ones), ca. (2.4-)3-3.8 mm long and ca. 1.7-3.1 mm wide, densely covered with long papillae on the inside surface, also with hairs, especially towards the base. Stamens ca. 0.8-1.2 mm long including a hairy filament of 0.1-0.2 mm, anthers papillose apically and on abaxial side (often also with some hairs), in the two outer whorls transverse-elliptic to roundish-squarish, broadly rounded to very slightly emarginate at the tip, usually ± truncate, rarely slightly apiculate, in the third whorl ± roundish-rectangular, truncate to slighdy emarginate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 3/5 the length of the stamens, with a conspicuous glandular head, not rarely also with one or two small lateral glands, united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous, ovary subglobose to pyriform, style usually very short, rarely (abnormally) reaching ca. 2/3 the length of the ovary. Receptacle bowl-shaped but somewhat closed by the bases of stamens and staminodes above, glabrous or with a few appressed hairs inside. Berry ellipsoid, ca. 20-22 mm long and 15-18 mm in diam., cupule almost disk-like to broadly obconical and gradually merging into the swollen pedicel, ca. 7-8 mm in diam., up to 4 mm high outside but very shallow inside.

description: Shrubs or trees, up to 20 m tall (but usually collected from much smaller individuals). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.3-3.5 mm in diam., only the youngest part slightly angular, soon becoming roundish, with ± short, appressed hairs, usually sparse, rarely at the tip up to moderately dense, ± quickly glabrescent; terminal buds ± ovoid, up to 5 mm long and 2 mm thick but mostly minute, densely covered with ± short, appressed hairs. Petioles 7-21 mm long, 1.3-3.2 mm thick, roundish, usually rather smooth below, flattened to slightly canaliculate above, with a few appressed hairs only in young leaves, later glabrous. Leaves alternate, ± elliptic to (oblanceolate, widest ± at the middle (more frequently slightly above the middle than below), (8.5-)10-30 cm long, (3-)4-8.5 cm wide, (2-)2.3-4(-4.5) times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base acute to cuneate, the very base often attenuate, margin ± flat, midrib ± convex above, smooth, sometimes in a slight impression, prominent below, secondary veins flat to slightly convex above, sometimes slightly impressed, distinctly raised to almost prominent below, 4-6(-8) pairs, diverging at 30-65°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of (10-)20-35(-45)° to the midrib, tertiary venation predominantly ± scalariform, sometimes with ± distinct intersecondaries, ± level above, (very) slightly raised below, usually rather inconspicuous. Indument consisting of ± short, appressed hairs (occasionally up to 0.3 mm long), even in youngest leaves (very) sparse on both sides, glabrescent Gland dots in young leaves usually ± distinct above, in mature leaves usually not visible. Inflorescences most frequently in the axils of cataphylls below the terminal bud (or at the base of the new growth when the bud grows through), less often on an axillary brachyblast, or some of the inflorescences in the axils of foliage leaves, 0.8-1.8 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.2-3.5 mm diam., (2.5-)3.5-13 cm long, reaching ca. 1/8-3/5 the length of the foliage leaves; peduncle extremely short or up to 8 cm long, i.e., branched almost from the base or reaching up to ca 3/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (0-) 2-6(-10) below the terminal cluster of cymes (or the terminal flower, see below), mostly branched 1-2(-3) times, sometimes unbranched (inflorescences botryoid), indument consisting of short, appressed hairs, moderately sparse to sparse, sometimes up to moderately dense on receptacle. Pedicels 2-6 mm long, 0.3-0.8 mm thick. Flowers 7-12 mm in diam., tepals mostly ± elongate, varying towards elliptic or spatulate, 2.5-5 mm long and 1.7-3.5 mm wide, papillosity ± dense on the inside surface, moderately fine to thick. Stamens ca. 0.9-2 mm long including the very short filament, anthers ± heavily papillose, in the first whorl ± pentagonal to suborbicular or tongue-shaped, with an obtuse to broadly rounded tip, in the second whorl narrowly ± pentagonal, with an acute to parabolic tip, in the third whorl roundish-rectangular to almost obovate, rounded to truncate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/2-2/3 the length of the stamens, ± clavate to almost capitate, papillose on abaxial side, usually with a distinct glandular patch at the tip on adaxial side, free or nearly so. Pistil ca. 1.2-2.3 mm long, glabrous, ovary ± ellipsoid to pyriform, style reaching ca. 2/5-2/3 the length of the ovary. Receptacle ± hemispherical or somewhat closed above by the bases of stamens and staminodes, glabrous or with a few tightly appressed hairs inside. Berry ellipsoid, ca. 1517 mm long, ca. 9-10 mm in diam., cupule a very shallow bowl, often slightly radially ribbed, ca. 2-3 mm high and ca. 7-8 mm in diam., pedicel only very slightly thickened.

description: Trees to 10 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.3-2.5 mm in diam., slightly irregularly angular, quickly becoming roundish, with extremely short («0.1 mm), appressed hairs, ± dense immediately below terminal bud but very quickly becoming sparse to glabrous; terminal buds elongate, 3.5-8 mm long and ca. 1 mm thick, densely covered with short, appressed, pale copper-colored hairs. Petioles 6-15 mm long, 0.8-2 mm thick, ± roundish or higher than wide, distinctly canaliculate above, indument as on twigs. Leaves alternate, lanceolate to lanceolate-elliptic, widest ca. 2/5 from the base (occasionally at die middle), 6-16 cm long, (1.5-)2-5 cm wide, 2.7-4 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base acute to broadly attenuate, the very base usually attenuate to acute, margin flat to narrowly recurved, midrib distinctly impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins ± slightly impressed above, prominent below, (4-)5-7 pairs, diverging at 2545°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 15-25° to the midrib, tertiary venation ± scalariform, ± level above (slightly raised to slightly impressed), slightly raised to ± level below. Indument consisting of short, appressed hairs (but see below), in young leaves sparse to glabrous above from the beginning, ± sparse below, subglabrescent except for slighdy longer hairs (0.2-0.3 mm) in the axils of lateral veins, most of them spreading from midrib and veins. Gland dots occasionally visible, indistinct. Inflorescences basically inserted in the axils of cataphylls on lateral brachyblasts or immediately below the terminal bud, occasionlly the distal ones in the axils of very young leaves when bud growing through, 0.5-1.2 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 0.8-3 mm diam., 2.5-10 cm long, reaching ca. 1/3 to slighdy more than the length of foliage leaves; peduncle very short or up to 4 cm long, reaching up to half the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-8 below terminal cluster of cymes, branched 0-2 times, indument consisting of ± short, ± appressed hairs, ± sparse but often slightly denser on receptacle. Pedicels 3-7 mm long, 0.3-0.8 mm thick. Flowers 5.58 mm in diam., tepals ± elongate-elliptic, 23 mm long and 1.4-2 mm wide, papillosity ± fine and short on the inside surface, ± moderately dense or only in basal triangle on outer tepals. Stamens ca. 0.9-1.3 mm long including the short filament, anthers distinctly papillose, in the first whorl suborbicular to broadly pentagonal with an obtuse to rounded dp, in the second whorl pentagonal to trullate with an acute to parabolic dp, in the third whorl roundish-obtrapeziform with a rounded to truncate dp. Staminodes thickish, papillose on abaxial side, often with a small glandular patch on adaxial side, free or nearly so. Pistil ca. 1.7-1.9 mm long, ovary ± ellipsoid, glabrous, style ca. as long as the ovary or slightly shorter, glabrous or with a few papillae. Receptacle relatively open, shallowly bowl-shaped to cup-shaped, glabrous or with some tightly appressed, short hairs inside. Berry (after Richter 47, see discussion) ellipsoid, ca. 14 mm long, ca. 10 mm in diam., cupule almost funnel-shaped, i.e., shallowly bowl-shaped on a slightly but increasingly thickened pedicel, ca. 1.5-2.5 mm high, ca. 6-7 mm in diam.

description: Trees to 15 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.3-2.8 mm in diam., initially irregularly angular/flattened, with a dense, light brown cover of short, appressed and erect hairs, older twigs becoming roundish, the shortest hairs ± persistent as a grey-brown cover; terminal buds ovoid to narrowly lanceolate, ca. 4-7 mm long and 13 mm thick, densely covered with short, ascending to erect, brown hairs. Petioles 6-13 mm long, 0.9-2 mm thick, often distinctly longitudinally ridged below, shallowly canaliculate above, with decurrent margin, indument initially very dense, ± as on twigs. Leaves alternate, lanceolate (rarely lanceolate-elliptic), widest at the middle or slightly below, 5-17 cm long, 1.1-4.5 cm wide, 2.5-4.8 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base acute to attenuate, margin at the base slightly bent down to narrowly recurved, midrib and secondary veins ± distinctly impressed above, (very) prominent below, secondary veins 4-5 pairs, diverging at 25-40°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 5-20° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, level to slightly raised above, rather inconspicuous,! raised below. Indument consisting (almost) exclusively of short hairs, initially ± dense on both sides, ± ascending to erect above, ± curled, later becoming much sparser and more appressed, finally glabrescent, more regularly appressed and more persistent below, hairs ± pointing towards the leaf tip, slowly becoming moderately sparse, the axils of the lower secondary veins usually filled with slightly longer hairs spreading from the veins. Gland dots rarely visible on upper surface. Inflorescences in the axils of foliage leaves, 0.8-2 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.2-3.2 mm diam., 2-8 cm long, reaching ca. 1/3-5/3 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 0.7-4.5 cm long, reaching ca. 1/3-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-4(-6) below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched 1-3 times (often only 3-flow-ered), indument ± as on twigs, dense. Pedicels 2.5-6 mm long, 0.4-0.7 mm thick. Flowers 69 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic to obovate, 24 mm long and 1.4-3 mm wide, heavily papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.7-1.1 mm long including a filament of 0.1-0.3 mm, anthers heavily papillose, in the two outer whorls broadly pentagonal with an obtuse tip, in the third whorl obtrapeziform (almost triangular) with a ± truncate tip. Staminodes ca. half as long as the stamens, capitate, distinctly papillose on abaxial side, often with a glandular patch at the tip on adaxial side, for more than half of their length united with the inner stamens. Pistil ca. 1.7-2.1 mm long, ovary elongate-ellipsoid, glabrous, style slightly shorter than the ovary, papillose. Receptacle deeply urceolate, ± densely covered with appressed hairs inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Trees, to ca. 15 m (?). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 3-5.5 mm in diam., initially distinctly irregularly angular and/or furrowed, with a dense indument of short (<0.1 mm), appressed to ascending, ± brown hairs, very slowly becoming sparser; terminal buds ovoid to elongate, ca. 3.5- 11 mm long and 1.5-3.5 mm thick, with an extremely dense cover of short, ± appressed hairs. Petioles 6-13 mm long, 1.3-4 mm thick, irregularly roundish and ± ridged below, distinctly canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs, sometimes soon (sub)glabrescent above. Leaves alternate, elliptic to oblong-elliptic or lanceolate-elliptic, widest ± at the middle (2/5— 3/5 from the base), (12-) 14.5-36 cm long, (4.5-)6.5-13 cm wide, 2.1-3.2 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, obtuse to attenuate towards the base, the base itself attenuate due to the (except in the type) distinctly revolute margin, midrib ± deeply impressed above, very prominent below, secondary veins ± impressed above, prominent below, (5-)7-10(-11) pairs, diverging at 35-45°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, sometimes inconspicuous, level to slightly raised above, ± raised below. Indument consisting of short, appressed hairs, in young leaves moderately sparse above to only on veins, intermediate to very sparse below, much denser on veins, in mature leaves sparse to glabrous above, moderately sparse to subglabrous below but still moderately dense on veins. Gland dots only rarely visible above, usually visible on veins below, like a string of pearls, but mostly not very distinct. Inflorescences in the axils of (younger) foliage leaves, sometimes apparently also in the axils of cataphylls below the terminal bud, ca. 1-3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2-5.5 mm diam., 3-15 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4-2/3 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 0.5-6.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/8-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 4-12 below the terminal cyme, branched 2-4 times (lower branches often not entirely cymose), indument consisting of ± short, appressed to ascending hairs, moderately dense to dense. Pedicels ca. 1-4 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm thick. Flowers ca. 34 mm in diam., tepals ± oblong to elliptic, ca. 1.3-1.6 mm long and ca. 0.7-1.2 mm wide, with fine papillae on the inside surface, papillae absent from the margin on outer tepals. Stamens ca. 0.4-0.7 mm long including a distinct filament of ca. 0.15-0.4 mm, anthers minutely papillose at the tip, in the two outer whorls ± transverse-elliptic,-in the third whorl ± roundish-rectangular, in all three whorls broadly rounded to truncate at the tip. Staminodes ± terete to slightly clavate, reaching ca. half the length of the stamens, slightly papillose at the tip, sometimes with some hairs at the filament, ± free. Pistil ca. 0.9-1.3 mm long, glabrous, ovary ± ellipsoid, style ca. as long as the ovary or slightly shorter. Receptacular tube slightly more than half-ellipsoid, with some tightly appressed short hairs inside. Only very immature (or monstrous) fruit known, at that stage cupule ± funnel-shaped, almost gradually merging into the (still slightly) thickened, minutely lenticellate pedicel.

description: Shrubs or trees to 10 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 2-3.2 mm in diam., ± irregularly angular, with (moderately) dense cover of very short and fewer longer (up to 0.3 mm), appressed hairs, older twigs becoming roundish, die indument becoming grey and felted, very slowly glabrescent; terminal buds sprouting at anthesis, densely covered with appressed, light brown hairs. Petioles 5-9(-13) mm long, 1-2.2 mm thick, irregularly roundish to almost triangular below, often higher than wide, canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs. Leaves alternate, oblanceolate to lanceolate-elliptic, widest ca. at the middle to 3/5 from the base, 5-11.5 cm long, 1.4-4.5 cm wide, 2.5-3.5(-4.6) times longer than wide, tip short acuminate or occasionally acute, base cuneate to attenuate, margin narrowly recurved to narrowly revolute, midrib ± impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins slightly impressed to ± level above, prominent below, 5-7 pairs, diverging at 30-45(-60)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 15-30(-40)° to the midrib, tertiary venation mainly percurrent to scalariform, occasionally with small laterally oriented intersecondaries, usually rather inconspicuous, ± level above, (very) slightly raised below. Indument consisting of ± moderately short (ca. 0.1-0.3 mm), appressed to ascending hairs (but see below), initially moderately sparse on both sides, soon glabrescent above, subglabrescent below except for the barbellate axils of lateral veins. Gland dots rarely visible, only in youngest leaves. Inflorescences for the most part inserted in the axils of cataphylls on the basal part of the young growth, but usually also some of them in the axils of young leaves, 0.7-2 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.3-4 mm diam., 4-13.5 cm long, reaching ca. 2/3 to 1½ the length of foliage leaves, (frondose inflorescences occasionally much larger); peduncle 1.8-4.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/3 to almost 1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-6 below terminal cluster of cymes, usually branched twice (in Gibbs 6668 botryoid except for the terminal cluster), indument consisting of ± short (ca. 0.10.3 mm), appressed to ascending hairs, moderately sparse to moderately dense on peduncle, + dense on receptacle. Pedicels (1.5-)2.5-5.5(-8) mm long, 0.3-0.8 mm thick. Flowers 5-6.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, 1.9-2.8 mm long and 1.5-2 mm wide, papillosity ± fine and short on the inside surface, ± moderately dense. Stamens ca. 1-1.3 mm long including a distinct filament of 0.2-0.4 mm, anthers ± papillose (often weakly) at the tip, in the first whorl broadly pentagonal with a ± obtuse tip, in the second whorl pentagonal to ovate with an obtuse to narrowly parabolic tip, in the third whorl roundish-obtrapeziform with a broadly obtuse to truncate tip. Staminodes slightly clavate, reaching ca. 1/3 to 1/2 the length of the stamens, papillose-hairy on abaxial side, glandular on adaxial side, free or nearly so. Pistil ca. 1.6-2.2 mm long, glabrous, ovary ± ellipsoid, style ca. as long as the ovary or somewhat shorter. Receptacle relatively open, shallowly bowl-shaped, glabrous inside. Berry (after Guillemin 1339) ellipsoid, ca. 13 m long, ca. 9 mm in diam., cupule deeply bowl-shaped, ca. 4 mm high and 7 mm in diam., pedicel slightly but increasingly thickened towards the cupule.

description: Shrubs or usually small trees, rarely reaching 20 m (already flowering when only 1.5 m tall). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud (1.3-) 1.8-3(-3.8) mm in diam., only very slightly angular or roundish from the beginning, initially with a ± dense cover of ± pale, short, and longer, brownish hairs (up to 0.8 mm) in variable proportion, usually ± erect (occasionally appressed), the longer hairs often quickly lost, the shorter ones ± slowly wearing off; terminal buds ± ovoid, ca. 2-6 mm long, 1.3-3(-4) mm thick, densely covered with reddish-brown, ± ascending hairs. Petioles 3.5-11(-17) mm long, 1.3-2.2(-2.8) mm thick, roundish below, flat or rarely slightly canaliculate above, thicker than the midrib of the leaf, indument ± as on twigs, slowly glabrescent. Leaves alternate, elliptic, obovate-elliptic or oblanceolate, widest usually ca. 3/5 from the base, rarely at the middle or slightly below, 7-25 cm long, 2.5-11.5 cm wide, 1.8-3.6 times longer than wide, tip ± acuminate (often obtuse with a short acumen), lower half of leaf ± cuneately narrowed towards the base, the base itself abruptly obtuse to cordate, or lower half of leaf ± rounded towards the base and the base itself ± cordate, margin ± flat, rarely very slightly recurved, midrib ± flat or slightly convex in a slight impression above, very prominent below, secondary veins slightly impressed above, very prominent below, 6-10 pairs, diverging at 4070°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-45° to the midrib, sometimes loop-connected ca. 35 mm from the margin, tertiary venation scalariform or sometimes mixed, ± level or rarely slightly impressed above, raised to prominent below. Indument rather variable, above consisting of short and/or long (up to 1 mm), ± appressed or ± erect hairs, in young leaves moderately sparse to subglabrous, denser on veins, glabrescent but on veins sometimes ± persistent, below either consisting of short or long, erect hairs, or of short, appressed hairs and some longer, ± ascending hairs on veins, in young leaves intermediate to very sparse, subpersistent or subglabrescent. Gland dots usually visible on upper surface of young leaves, but not always distinct. Inflorescences most frequently in the axils of cataphylls, often both below the terminal bud and at the base of the young growth, some also in the axils of young leaves, 0.6-1.5 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1-3.8 mm diam., 2.5-14 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4 to 4/5 the length of closest foliage leaves; peduncle 0.7-7 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/4 to 2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (2-)4-8 below terminal cyme (or cluster of cymes), branched 0-3(-4) times (very rarely whole inflorescence botryoid), indument consisting of short and long, straight or twisted hairs, ascending to erect on peduncle, moderately sparse to moderately dense, closer to the flowers becoming denser and more appressed. Pedicels 1-4.5 mm long, 0.3-0.7 mm thick. Flowers 5.5-7.5(-9) mm in diam., tepals ± elongate-elliptic, 2.2-3.2(-3.5) mm long, 1.5-2(-2.5) mm wide, papillosity ± weakly developed, sometimes restricted to the margin on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 1.1-1.5 mm long including a distinct filament of 0.2-0.5 mm, anthers weakly to moderately papillose, in the two outer whorls transverse-rhombic to trullate, with an obtuse to acute tip, in the third ± broadly pentagonal to obtrapeziform, at the apex often much broader than at the base, with an obtuse to truncate tip. Staminodes slightly clavate, reaching ca. 2/5 the length of the stamens, often slightly glandular on adaxial side, free or basally united with the stamens of the third whorl. Pistil ca. 1.1-1.4 mm long, ovary ± pyriform or spheroidal, glabrous, style ca. half as long as the ovary, glabrous or rarely with a few papillae. Receptacle ± shallowly bowl-shaped, usually almost closed by the bases of stamens and staminodes above, with at least some appressed hairs inside. Berry ellipsoid, ca. 10-13 mm long, ca. 6-7 mm in diam., cupule (immature?) funnel-shaped or a shallow bowl on a slightly thickened pedicel, ca. 2 mm high and ca. 5 mm in diam.

description: Shrubs or trees, (up to?) 10 m tall. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.2-2.2 mm in diam., slightly irregularly angular and/or longitudinally ridged, the youngest part with a moderately dense to sparse cover of short and sometimes longer (up to 0.3 mm), appressed hairs, quickly becoming sparse or glabrescent; terminal buds ovoid to elongate, 3-6 mm long and 1-2.5 mm in diam., with a dense cover of ± short, appressed hairs. Petioles 4.5-12 mm long, 0.6-1.4 mm thick, often higher than wide, roundish, deeply canaliculate above, initially with short to moderately long (rarely up to 0.4 mm), appressed hairs below, quickly glabrescent Leaves alternate, ± elliptic, varying towards (ob)ovate or rarely (oblanceolate, widest ca. 2/5-2/3 from the base, 4.5-11.5 cm long, 1.7-5 cm wide, 1.8-2.7(-3.5) times longer than wide, tip short acuminate, obtuse to cuneate towards the base but the very base always attenuate, margin flat, midrib ± convex in a slight impression above, raised to prominent below, secondary veins level to very slightly impressed above, often scarcely visible, level to slightly raised below, 5-8 pairs, diverging at 40-60°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 30-50° to the midrib, tertiary venation reticulate, without any distinct orientation if visible at all, level on both sides. Indument consisting of short and sometimes longer (up to 0.3 mm), appressed hairs, glabrous from the beginning above, initially sparse or only near the midrib and the margin below, soon glabrescent. Gland dots visible only in very young leaves. Inflorescences mostly in the axils of cataphylls on axillary brachyblasts or below the terminal bud, or— when the bud grows through—at the base of the young twig and in the axils of newly developed leaves, 0.4-0.6 mm in diam. at the base, 1.1-7.5 cm long, reaching ca. 1/6-2/3 the length of the closest foliage leaf; peduncle 0.7-4 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/2-2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-4 below terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, unbranched or branched once (inflorescences rarely entirely botryoid), indument similar to that on young twigs but usually more erect closer to the flowers, on peduncle ± moderately sparse, slightly denser on receptacle. Pedicels 2-7 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm thick. Flowers ca. 4-7.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic to spatulate, ca. 1.5-3 mm long and ca. 1-1.9 mm wide, distinctly papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.6-0.8 mm long including the very short filament (up to 0.2 mm), with a short sterile tip (0.2-0.3 mm), anthers distinctly papillose at the tip, in all three whorls ± broadly pentagonal or in the first whorl sometimes transverse-elliptic, at the tip obtuse or rarely rounded. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3 of the length to almost the length of the stamens, slightly clavate, papillose on abaxial side. Pistil ca. 1.1-1.3 mm long, ovary broadly ellipsoid, glabrous, style short, reaching ca. 1/4 the length of the ovary, glabrous or slightly papillose. Receptacle ± hemispherical, glabrous or with a few appressed hairs inside. Berry (immature?) ± elongate-elliptic, ca. 12-13 mm long and 5-6 mm in diam., cupule a thin-walled shallow bowl, ca. 5 mm in diam. and 2 mm deep, pedicel only very slightly thickened.

description: Perennial herbs, 50-85 cm tall. Rhizome horizontal, short-creeping, 4-9 mm diam., scales scari-ose, usually covering the rhizome or sometimes slightly spaced, internodes 0.5-1 cm. Culms erect, 1.2-2.5 mm diam., terete, smooth. Cataphylls 2-3 to each culm, 1-15 cm long, green, stramineous or brown, often unfolding and not sheathing the mature culm densely; rudimentary blade acicular, 2-5 mm long. Foliar leaves 2-3 to each culm, all cauline and none inserted at the base, lower leaf 20-80 cm long, sheath 5-13 cm long, with scariose margins terminating in 2 rounded 1-2 mm long auricles, blade terete (0.8-) 1-1.5 mm diam., hollow with septa 2-8 mm apart but not always nodulated externally, upper leaf often inserted above the middle of the culm, usually short, the blade sometimes only 5 cm long. Inflorescence compound, anthelate, up to 7 x 4 cm but usually smaller and sometimes only 2.5 x 2 cm, flower heads 5-12, globose, 6-10 mm diam., 30-50-flowered, stramineous or rarely light reddish brown, the principal branches up to 6 cm long and 1.2 mm diam. Lower inflorescence bract 2.5-6.5 cm long with 0.5-4 cm long rudimentary blade, distal bracts shorter, floral bracts scariose, shorter than the flowers. Tepals equal or outer tepals sometimes slightly longer than inner tepals, 2.3-2.9 mm long, linear-lanceolate, subulate, rigid, outer tepals concave, inner tepals flat. Stamens 3, 1-1.5 mm long; filaments filiform; anthers oblong, 0.30.5 mm, much shorter than the filaments. Capsule ovoid, beaked, 3-lobed, 2.2-2.9 mm (incl. beak) x 0.7-0.9 mm, usually as long as or longer than the tepals, light brown, unilocular, dehiscing laterally, the valves remaining connate at the beak. Seeds ellipsoid, apiculate, 0.3-0.4 x 0.15-0.2 mm, reticulate, yellowish brown.

description: Trees. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.8-3.2 mm in diam., initially distinctly irregularly angular, with a dense, yellowish to light brown indument of mixed short to long (up to ca. 0.7 mm), almost straight to curled, ± erect hairs, the shorter hairs completely covering the epidermis, more persistent than the longer ones, on older twigs matted and greyish, very slowly wearing off; terminal buds ± ovoid to elongate, 2-11 mm long, 1-4 mm thick, densely covered with ± straight, long, ± ascending hairs. Petioles 5-11 mm long, 1.2-2.2 mm thick, roundish below, ± canaliculate above, indument above ± as on twigs, usually shorter and slightly less dense below, subpersistent. Leaves alternate, elliptic to obovate-oblong or (oblanceolate-elliptic, widest 1/2 to 2/3 from the base, mostly just above the middle, 7-13 cm long, (2-)2.7-4 cm wide, 2.4-3.6 times longer than wide, tip acute to obtuse with a very short and indistinct acumen, base attenuate to acute, margin slightly bent down to (mostly) narrowly recurved, midrib and secondary veins (in mature leaves) distinctly impressed above, very prominent below, secondary veins 5-8 pairs, diverging at 25-40°, in midlamina running at an angle of 20-30° to the midrib, tertiary venation predominantly or entirely scalariform, almost level to ± impressed above, ± raised below. Indument consisting of ± appressed to ascending, almost straight to curled hairs of variable length (ca. 0.1-0.5 mm), the longer hairs more frequent on veins, initially dense (almost completely concealing the epidermis) to moderately sparse above but much denser on veins, (moderately) dense below, the short hairs ± pointing towards the leaf tip, the longer hairs denser in the axils of the secondary veins, older leaves glabrescentabove, indument becoming moderately sparse and ± appressed below. Gland dots visible only on upper surface of youngest leaves (if not concealed by the indument). Inflorescences in the axils of young leaves, 0.7-1.5 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-5 mm diam., (3.5-)7.5-15 cm long, usually much longer than their subtending leaf; peduncle (0.7-)3.5-5.5 cm long, i.e., 1/5 to 2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (0-)2-6 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched once or twice, indument similar to that on twigs but often lighter. Pedicels 3-5.5 mm long, 0.4-0.7 mm thick. Flowers 6-9.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic to elongate, 2.8-4.2 mm long and 1.7-2.5 mm wide, heavily papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 1.1-1.4 mm long including a short filament of ca. 0.2 mm, anthers distinctly papillose, in the first whorl broadly rhombic to roundish-pentagonal, with a ± obtuse or rarely almost rounded tip, in the second whorl pentagonal to trullate with a ± acute tip, in the third whorl roundish-obtrapeziform to elongate-pentagonal with an obtuse to ± truncate tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3 the length of the stamens, slightly capitate, papillose and sometimes hairy on abaxial side, glandular on adaxial side, united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 1.7-2 mm long, glabrous, ovary spheroidal, style ca. 2/3 as long as the ovary. Receptacle shallowly cup-shaped to deeply urceolate, almost closed by the bases of stamens and staminodes above, glabrous or with a few hairs inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Trees to 10 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.7-3 mm in diam., initially irregularly an-gular/flattened, with a (moderately) dense cover of very short to moderately short (< 0.2 mm), appressed and ± erect, often ± curled hairs, later becoming roundish, the shortest hairs persistent for some time as an inconspicuous, grey cover, finally glabrescent; terminal buds ± elongate, ca. 3.5-8 mm long and 1-1.7 mm thick, densely covered with ± short, straight to curled, ± ascending, light brown hairs. Petioles 8-18 mm long, 1-2 mm thick, ± roundish below, slightly to distinctly irregular, shallowly canaliculate above, indument below ± as on twigs, slightly longer and denser above. Leaves alternate, lanceolate, widest ± at the middle or more frequently slightly below the middle, 7-22 cm long, 2.2-7 cm wide, (2.3-)2.8-3.6(-4.9) times longer than wide, tip tapering towards a short acumen, base attenuate, rarely acute, margin narrowly revolute, ending parallel to the petiole, midrib above usually distinctly impressed, rarely slightly convex in its impression, prominent below, secondary veins level to impressed above, prominent below, 6-9(-10) pairs, diverging at 30-45°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-40° to the midrib, tertiary venation ± scalariform, slightly impressed to slightly raised above, very slightly to distinctly raised below, sometimes rather inconspicuous on both sides. Indument consisting of short, appressed to ascending, straight to curled hairs in the intercostal area below, and usually slightly longer and more spreading hairs the on veins, in young leaves sparse to moderately dense but rather inconspicuous, later becoming ± sparse, hairs usually more curled and (especially on the veins) often longer (up to 0.4 mm) above, initially very sparse to intermediate, inconspicuous, glabrescent, axils of secondary veins on lower leaf surface with longer (0.2-0.7 mm), often reddish hairs spreading from the veins. Gland dots in youngest leaves sometimes distinct, later not visible. Inflorescences in the axils of younger foliage leaves, 0.6-1.5 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.3-3.5 mm diam., 3.5-13.5 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4-4/5 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 1.5-7.5 cm long, i.e., 1/4-2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-6 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched 1-3 times, indument consisting of short, ± curled, ascending to erect hairs, on peduncle moderately sparse to moderately dense, becoming denser closer to the flowers. Pedicels 2-4.5 mm long, 0.4-1.1 mm thick. Flowers 6 9.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, 2.6-4.2 mm long and 1.6-2.6 mm wide, papillosity ± thick and dense on the inside surface but on outer tepals p.p. easily lost. Stamens ca. 1-1.5 mm long including the short (0.2-0.3 mm) and broad filament, anthers heavily papillose, roundish-pentagonal to (ob)ovate or tongue-shaped in the first whorl, with an obtuse to parabolic tip, ± trullate in the second whorl, with an acute to parabolic tip, ± clavate to elongate-pentagonal in the third whorl, with an obtuse to rounded tip. Staminodes thick, slightly clavate, reaching ca. 2/5-1/2 the length of the stamens, usually with a glandular patch near the tip on adaxial side, free or united with the inner stamens at the very base. Pistil ca. 1.1-1.7 mm long, ovary ellipsoid to depressed spheroidal, glabrous, style reaching ca. 1/4-1/2 the length of the ovary, glabrous or with some papillae. Receptacle hemispherical to cupshaped, glabrous or covered with short, appressed hairs inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Shrubs or trees to 25 m tall. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.8-3.3 mm in diam., initially irregularly angular, mostly with sharp ridges, with a dense, light (brownish-)grey cover of short, appressed hairs (rarely a few of them reaching 0.3 mm), older twigs becoming roundish, the indument long persistent; terminal buds elongate to ovoid, 3-8 mm long and 1-3 mm thick, densely covered with straight, (moderately) short, appressed hairs. Petioles 7-23 mm long, 1.2-2.2 mm thick, ± roundish below, often ± ridged, deeply canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs. Leaves alternate, ± elliptic, widest ± at the middle, 8-15(-18) cm long, 3.5-6(-8) cm wide, 1.8-3 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base obtuse to broadly attenuate, margin flat or rarely slightly recurved, midrib deeply impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins ± impressed above (sometimes very slightly), occasionally very slightly convex, distinctly raised to prominent below, (4-)5-8(-9) pairs, diverging at40-65°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of (10-)20-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation predominantly or entirely scalariform, often rather inconspicuous, ± level above, level to slightly raised below. Indument consisting of ± short (occasionally up to 0.3 mm), straight, appressed hairs, moderately sparse to subglabrous from the beginning on both sides but, especially above, usually much denser on veins, in mature leaves still sparser to absent. Gland dots sometimes distinct on upper surface of young leaves, otherwise inconspicuous to invisible. Inflorescences in the axils of foliage leaves and/or in the axils of cataphylls, at the base of the new growth or below the terminal bud, 0.5-1.5 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.3-3.2 mm diam., (2.5-)5-12 cm long, reaching ca. 1/3 to almost the length of the closest foliage leaves (rarely slightly more); peduncle (1-)2-5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/3-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-12 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched (1-)2-3 times, the lower branchlets often not entirely cymose, indument on peduncle usually ± as on twigs, sometimes sparser, closer to the flowers usually becoming sparser and sometimes more erect. Pedicels 1.1-3.5(-4.5) mm long, 0.2-0.4 mm thick. Flowers 2.8-4(-5) mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic to broadly obovate, 1-1.8 mm long and 0.7-1.5 mm wide, covered with rather long, fine, hair-like papillae on the inside surface, on outer tepals mainly in a central line and a basal triangle, on inner ones covering the entire surface. Stamens ca. 0.4-0.6 mm long including a short filament of up to 0.2 mm length, anthers apically and on abaxial side covered with long papillae, in the two outer whorls ± transverse elliptic to obtrapeziform, in the third whorl ± obtrapeziform, in all three broadly rounded to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/2-3/4 the length of the stamens, slightly clavate, with long papillae on abaxial side, possibly slightly glandular on adaxial side, free. Pistil ca. 0.7-1.1 mm long, glabrous, ovary pear shaped to ellipsoid, style very short to absent. Receptacle almost flat, glabrous inside. Mature fruit unknown.

description: Trees, to 30 m, rarely shrubs. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud (2.3-)3.2-5(-6.5) mm in diam., initially (often very pronounced) irregularly angular but sometimes quickly becoming terete, with short, ± appressed hairs, moderately dense or sparser immediately below the terminal bud, quickly becoming sparse to glabrous, at the very tip occasionally with a few longer (up to 0.8 mm), ± ascending hairs; terminal buds ± elongate, (3-)6-12 mm long, 1.2-2.5 mm thick, not rarely sprouting at anthesis, densely covered with short to long (up to 0.8 mm), appressed hairs. Petioles 9-24(-30) mm long, 1.5-3.5 mm thick, ± roundish below, slightly convex to shallowly canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs but sometimes clearly denser above, (sub) glabrescent. Leaves alternate, usually (oblanceolate to oblong, rarely elliptic, widest 2/5-2/3 from the base, (12-)15-32(-44) cm long, (3.5-)4-12 (-16) cm wide, 2.4-4.7(-5.5) times longer than wide, tip ± acuminate (acumen short to long and narrow), base acute to attenuate, rarely obtuse, margin flat to bent down, rarely slightly recurved, midrib ± distinctly convex above, usually in a slight impression, very prominent below, secondary veins (7-)9-11(-13) pairs, diverging at (35-)40-70°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of (20-)25-45(-50)° to the midrib, the distal ones often loop-connected near the margin, level to impressed above, sometimes convex, prominent below, tertiary venation scalariform, rarely with a few, short intersecondaries, levello very slightly raised above, ± raised below. Indument consisting of short, appressed hairs, plus sometimes a few longer hairs (up to 0.6 mm) on veins, in young leaves sparse to subglabrous above, often slightly denser on veins, ± sparse below, often slightly denser along the veins, sometimes with tufts of often slightly reddish, ± erect hairs (up to 0.6 mm) in the axils of the secondary veins, older leaves glabrescent above, indument scarcely changed to subglabrous below. Gland dots at least in young leaves usually visible to distinct on both sides, in mature leaves often scarcely to not at all visible. Inflorescences in the axils of distal foliage leaves, occasionally pseudoterminal (terminal bud displaced to a lateral position), (0.9-)1.3-3(-3.4) mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of (2-)2.5-5(-6.5) mm diam., (3.5-)7-18(-22) cm long, reaching ca. 1/5-3/4 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle (2-)3.5-9.5(-11) cm long, i.e., ca. 1/2-3/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-5(-6) below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched (1-)2-5 times, indument on peduncle ± as on twigs, ± sparse, closer to the flowers changing into a dense, ± whitish indument of short, appressed to ± ascending hairs. Pedicels (1.5-)2.3-9(-14) mm long, 0.4-0.9 mm thick. Flowers (6.5-)7.5-12(-14) mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic to elongate-obovate, ca. (3-)3.3-5(-7) mm long and ca. (1.7-)2.2-3 (-4) mm wide, heavily papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 1.4-2.2 mm long including a filament of up to 0.3 mm length, anthers papillose, rather elongate, in the first whorl ± ovate with a ± parabolic sterile tip, in the second whorl ovate to trullate with an acute to parabolic tip, in the third whorl elongate pentagonal, obovate, or almost rectangular, with an obtuse to truncate tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3-3/5 the length of the stamens, triangular to slightly clavate, papillose, occasionally very indistinctly glandular on adaxial side, united with the inner stamens only at the very base. Pistil ca. 1.9-3.2 mm long, ovary ± ellipsoid, glabrous or rarely with a few hairs, style ca. as long as the ovary to clearly longer (by ca. 1/2), glabrous to papillose. Receptacle cupshaped (or ellipsoid inch bases of stamens and staminodes), glabrous or with some tightly appressed hairs inside. Berry ellipsoid, ca. 1317 mm long, 10-11 mm in diam., cupule deeply bowl-shaped, ca. 10-14 mm in diam. and ca. 4-7.5 mm high, pedicel ± slightly thickened.

description: Shrubs or small trees, up to 5 m tall. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.6-2.1 mm in diam., irregularly angular, with pale, short, appressed hairs, initially sparse to intermediate, quickly glabrescent, bark usually becoming light greyish; terminal buds narrow, 4-7 mm long and 0.9-1.2  mm in diam., with a dense whitish cover of (moderately) short, appressed hairs. Petioles 2.57 mm long, 0.6-1.3 mm thick, irregularly roundish below, canaliculate above, with short, appressed hairs, quickly glabrescent. Leaves alternate, almost linear, widest ca. 2/5 from the base to ca. at the middle, (5-)7-16 cm long, (0.6-)1-1.8 cm wide, (5-)6.5-10(-13) times longer than wide (in Callejas 4514 up to ca. 20 times), the tip tapering towards a very long and fine acumen, base narrowly acute to attenuate, margin flat to very slightly bent down, midrib irregularly convex or raised above, prominent below, secondary veins and finer veinlets ± raised on both surfaces (in Callejas 4514 ± level above), major secondary veins 4-8(-10) pairs (but closer to the tip not distinct from higher order venation), diverging at 30-55°, in midlamina running at an angle of 20-35(-45)°, tertiary venation ± reticulate, intersecondaries frequent. Indument consisting of ± short, appressed hairs, sparse from the beginning on both sides but sometimes slightly denser along the midrib, slowly glabrescent. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, 0.7-1.1 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.3-3.1 mm diam., 2.3-8 cm long, reaching ca. 1/6-2/3 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 1-4 cm long, i.e., 1/5 to 1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-8 below the terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, branched 0-2 times, indument consisting of short, ± appressed hairs, (moderately) sparse on all parts (in Callejas4514 up to moderately dense). Berry ovate-elliptic, ca. 9 mm long and 5 mm in diam., distinctly apiculate, cupule bowlshaped, very shallow, ca. 5 mm in diam. and up to 2 mm deep, margin especially in younger fruits usually with remnants of perianth and stamens.
