description: Tree; young shoots densely ferruginous-tomentose with rather stiff often crisped hairs, eventually glabrous, greyish-brown, often shallowly longitudinally ribbed, cracked and scaly, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 10.2-15.5 × 4.3-8 cm, elliptic or oblanceolate, apex obtusely cuspidate to narrowly attenuate, base obtuse or rounded, thinly coriaceous, glabrous above, tomentose below at first but indumentum persisting only on the midrib and veins as sparse stiff simple and branched hairs, venation brochidodromous with a marginal vein, midrib flat or slightly prominent on the upper surface, submarginal vein raised on the lower surface, secondary veins 40-50 pairs, shallowly ascending, parallel, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries extending to the margin; tertiaries parallel to the secondaries. Petiole 0.8-1.3 cm long, channelled, stiff-tomentose. Fascicles 1-10-flowered, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves. Flowers sessile, unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, ca. 4 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse, densely ferruginous-tomentose outside, appressed puberulous inside, slightly accrescent in fruit. Corolla ca. 3.5 mm long, tubular, tube ca. 2.5 mm long, lobes five, ca. 1 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, included, reduced to vestigial filaments in female. Staminodes five, ca. 0.75 mm long, oblong, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary pyramidal, five-locular, densely strigose; style ca. 3 mm long after anthesis, exserted, strigose almost to the apex; style-head lobed. Male flowers not seen. Fruit 2.5-3 cm long, narrowly ellipsoid, apex acute, base broadly tapered, smooth, tomentose near the base, sparser indumentum above. Seed not seen (according to Baehni, solitary, with long scar). Field characters. Tree to 30 m high with white latex.

description: Epiphytic shrub (branches pendent to 2 m long) or terrestrial and 4-5 m tall; mature branches terete, glabrous, bark grayish-brown; twigs subterete, striate to muricate, hispid or glabrate, reddish-brown; vegetative bracts persistent, subcoriaceous, striate, ovate to oblanceolate, to 2 cm long, long-ciliate. Leaves drying thick coriaceous, oblong to oblong-lanceolate or elliptic to lance-elliptic, (4.5-)8-17 X (1.2-)2-7 cm, basally rounded, obtuse or cuneate, apically long-acuminate, margins of proximal ¼ blade revolute, essentially glabrous on both surfaces (weakly hispid at very base of midrib), or glabrous above and densely hispid beneath with hairs to 1.5 mm long, often glaucous above when dry; 3-5-plinerved from at or near base with nerves impressed above and raised beneath, reticulate veinlets obscure; petiole terete, rugose, hispid, 5-8 mm long and 2-3 mm in diam. Inflorescence ca. 20-25-flowered, the flowers restricted to distal ¼ of inflorescence, lower nodes widely spaced and sterile, encircled at base by numerous, persistent, striate, ovate to oblanceolate bracts to 2 cm long; rachis 3-4 cm long and 2.5-3 mm in basal diam. but becoming 5-6 mm in diam. distally, glabrous or pilose, provided at nodes with minute sessile spherical glands 0.1-0.2 mm in diam.; floral bracts conspicuously reticulately veined, concave, obovate, oblanceolate, (20-)25-40 X (12-)23-30 mm, apically rounded, emarginate with tip usually curved inwardly and often split or bifid, glabrous but dorsally bearing minute sessile spherical or globular glands ca. 0.1 mm in diam.; pedicels terete, glabrous, 3-7 mm long and 1-1.5 mm in diam., ebracteolate or with bracteoles which are oblong, obtuse, (2-)8-10.5 X (1-)2—2.5 mm with margins bearing spherical globular glands. Flowers: calyx glabrous, 10-12 mm long; hypanthium cylindric, truncate or with a slight basal rim, 2.5-3.5 mm long, pale green when fresh; limb submembranaceous, smooth, cylindric-campanulate, 6.5-9 mm long, translucent cream-colored when fresh; lobes triangular, acute, 1.5-4 mm long, rarely sparsely ciliate, margins bearing few to numerous sessile spherical globular glands which may rarely fuse into oblong glands; sinus obtuse or rounded; corolla cylindric, glabrous, 22-32 mm long and ca. 6-8 mm in diam., upper ¼ becoming bright red after anthesis, lobes triangular, reflexed at anthesis, 2 mm long; stamens 11.5-18 mm long; filaments alternately 2.8-4.5 mm and 5-8.5 mm long, the short ones pilose distally, the long ones pilose medially; anthers alternately 9.5-12 mm and 8.2-11 mm long; thecae slightly granular, ca. 3.5-5 mm long; tubules dehiscing by clefts 3-3.5 mm long; style ca. 26-30 mm long. Berry not seen.

description: Small to medium sized trees, 3-15 m tall. Leaf blades usually elliptic to narrowly elliptic, infrequently lanceolate, 13-27 x 5-11 cm, glabrous, punctate abaxially, with 12-17 pairs of lateral veins; apex acuminate to very long acuminate or attenuate; base acute, obtuse, or rounded; margins entire; petiole 5-11 mm long. Inflorescences usually cauline, often from woody outgrowth on trunk, less frequently in axils of uppermost leaves, simple racemes, often with several arising from same place, the rachis, 3.5-20 cm long, often very slender, flowers usually widely spaced, the pedicel bases persisting as woody knobs, the pedicels 7-12 mm long, glabrous, without conspicuous lenticels. Flowers 5-7 cm diam.; calyx with six lobes, the lobes very widely to widely ovate, 35 x 4-5.5 mm, spreading, not imbricate, convex abaxially, concave adaxially; petals six, widely obovate, 24-44 x 17-31 mm, purple; hood of androecium 19-28 x 20-25 mm, forming double coil, purple; staminal ring with 170-326 stamens, the filaments 2-3 mm long, clavate, purple at base, white at apex or completely white, the anthers 0.5-1.0 mm long, yellow; hypanthium cuneate, glabrous, not conspicuously lenticellate but sometimes minutely papillate; ovary 2(-3)-locular, each locule with 5-11 ovules attached to placenta on floor of locule, the style 4-6 mm long. Immature fruits turbinate; operculum with conspicuous umbo. Immature seeds with well-developed lateral aril.

description: On soil, soil covered rocks and rotten log in open places below and above the tree line in elevations between 2200 and 3600 m in Mexico, Venezuela, Colombia, Peru and Bolivia.Plants to 5 cm high, yellowish-green, in loose tufts. Stems erect, appressed foliate below, ending in a comal tuft with erect spreading leaves, slightly radiculose at base. Leaves ca. 6-7 mm long, the lower stem leaves narrow lanceolate, the comal leaves with broad sheathing base abruptly narrowed into a long, narrow awn. Costa filling 1/3 of the leaf base in the appressed stem leaves (narrower in comal leaves), excurrent in a serrate awn, in transverse section with ventral hyalocysts and dorsal groups of stereids, smooth at back. Alar cells reddish. Basal laminal cells thick-walled, rectangular, sometimes slightly pitted, 5-8:1, 6-13 × 26-67 µm, those of the comal leave thin-walled, narrower and smaller at margins. Upper laminal cells subquadrate to short rectangular or oblique, 5-10 × 13-26 µm. Vegetative propagation (rarely) by deciduous comal leaves. Seta 4-8 mm long, pale. Capsule 1.5 mm long, light brown. Calyptra fringed or entire at base.

description: Plants in green, loose, soft tufts to 3 cm high. Stems erect, densely foliate, sometimes branched, tomentose, with several buds of deciduous brood-leaves. Leaves to 3 mm long, lanceolate, contracted to a subtubulose, serrate tip, erect patent when wet, rugose and appressed when dry. Costa filling 16 of the leaf width, vanishing in the leaf tip, smooth at back. Alar cells thin-walled, hyaline, isodiametric. Basal laminal cells short rectangular, incrassate, 10-13 × 16-29 µm, at margins shorter and narrower. Upper laminal cells small, quadrate, incrassate, 13-16 × 13-22 µm. Sporophyte not known.

description: Trees to 40 m tall, to 170 cm dbh, bole irregular, much-branched at crown, fluted trunk, with buttresses to 3 m tall and extending several meters from trunk; bark deeply sulcate, lamellate, grayish white; wood yellow, very hard. Leafy branchlets (4-)7-11 mm thick, semi-succulent to woody, quadrangular to decussately compressed, terminal 2-3 nodes sparsely puberulent to densely pubescent; older branches glabrate, exfoliating in narrow strips, showing the red-brown bark just below; lenticels not found. Stipules free to connate at base, more or less contorted in bud, often adnate to petioles, deltoid to narrowly triangular, strongly acuminate, golden-pubescent outside, often with ciliate margins, glabrous with sparse small colleters at base inside, 9-20 × 6-8 mm, subcaducous, reddish green, leaving a scar encircling the stem, adnate to the petiole scar 1-3 mm wide. Leaves 9-19 (-33) × 6-10.5(-16) cm, L/W = 1.5:1 to 2:1, oblong to elliptic to obovate, acute (rarely decurrent) to obtuse at base, obtuse to shallowly acute at apex, acumen usually absent; dark green, often shiny above, pale green-yellowish below, thick-chartaceous to semi-coriaceous; drying olive-green above, rust-brown below, thick-chartaceous to leathery; glabrous above, glabrous to puberulent (rarely pubescent) below; primary and secondary veins glabrous to puberulent (rarely pubescent), prominent below; secondary veins 8-12(-16) each side; tertiary veins alternatively subparallel and reticulate, quaternary veins finely reticulate, very distinctive from other species; petioles 4-15(-22) mm long, 1-2.5 mm thick, terete to adaxially flattened or concave, (glabrous-) puberulent to pubescent; domatia absent or present, usually a tuft of sparse yellow hairs, puberulent to pubescent (Fig. 57L). Inflorescences 2 per node, corymbose, laxly branched, with opposite to subopposite decussate branches, cymules lax to fairly compacted at distal end of each branchlet, (8.5-)11-13.5(-32) × 5-10(-18) cm, lateral branches 1-2(-4) pairs, basal portion of axis not branched 5-8(-15) cm long; L/A = 2:1 to 2.8:1; rachis basally terete, distally decussately compressed, rachis and branches sparsely to densely yellow-puberulent; distal bracts from reduced deltoid scales 0.2-0.3 mm long to linear bracts to 7 × 1-2 mm, sometimes leaf-like, to 7 × 2.7 cm, glabrous to puberulent, the margin sometimes ciliate; bracteoles subtending flowers absent. Flowers sessile to short-pedicellate; pedicels to 1.5 mm long, densely puberulent; hypanthium obovoid-turbinate, 1.5-2.5 × 1-1.6 mm, densely puberulent. Calyx extremely reduced, truncate to short-lobed, 0.4-0.7 × 1-1.6 mm, glabrous to sparsely puberulent; lobes shallowly triangular, to 0.2 mm long; rarely in some flowers one of the calyx lobes enlarged into a pale-green calycophyll, to 1.5 cm long. Corolla narrowly funnelform, deeply lobed, the lobes reflexed at anthesis, 3.5-6 mm long, white to yellowish white; tube long-cylindrical, 1.5-3 × 0.7-1 mm, glabrous outside and inside; lobes (4-)5, 2.5-3.5 × ca. 0.5 mm, oblong with acute apex and round tip, glabrous outside, with a basal area pilose to tomentose (ca. 1 mm wide), with distal zone glabrous inside. Stamens 5, exserted well above the corolla, equal, attached 1-2.5 mm from the base of the tube; filaments 3.5-5.5 mm long, terete, minutely costate, basally flattened, connate to throat, sparsely white long-pilose at base, the hairs decreasing in length toward medial zone; anthers elliptic, 0.8-1.5 × 0.3-0.5 mm, dorsifixed near medial zone, base rounded, apex rounded or minutely mucronate. Pollen exine foveolate-reticulate. Style exserted, 4-6 mm long, as long as the corolla, terete, densely antrorse-strigose; style branches extruding as two lips above the corolla before anthesis, oblate to oblong, 0.3-0.5 mm long, stigmatic surface microscopically (40×) papillose; ovaries often infested by insect, causing production of pyriform fruit-galls. Capsules turbinate, acute at base, rounded at apex, 3.5-6 × 2.5-3.3 mm, rust-brown, without lenticels, sparsely to densely puberulent below the disk; disk densely white-pilose, not exceeding the calyx; disk loculicidal dehiscence present in old capsules. Seeds 0.75-1.95 × 0.75-1.25 mm.

description: Trees to 30 m tall, 40-50(-60) cm dbh, with clear bole to 10 m, with small buttresses or flutes; bark soft, pale brown; wood yellow to golden-yellow, very brittle. Leafy branchlets 1.5-4 mm thick, terete to compressed, ochraceous, glabrous to appressed puberulent; older branches glabrate, terete, grayish to pale brown. Stipules free at base, contorted in bud, narrowly triangular, acuminate, appressed puberulent to gray-sericeous outside, glabrous with basal colleters inside, 6-25(-30) × 2-4 mm, reddish with a grayish tinge, readily caducous, leaving a white scar encircling the stem, 0.5-1 mm wide. Leaves 6-17(-22) × 4-7.5 cm, LAV = 2:1 to 2.5:1, elliptic to oblong-obovate, acute-decurrent (ca. 25°) at base, obtuse and mucronate at apex, the deltoid acumen 0.7-1 cm long; dark green above, pale green below, foliaceous; drying olive-green to brown, stiff-chartaceous; glabrous above, glabrous to sparsely appressed puberulent below, hairs whitish to yellowish; primary, secondary, and tertiary veins appressed puberulent below; secondary veins (5-)8-14 each side; tertiary veins starting subparallel and reticulate in the center; petioles 10-23 mm long, 1-2 mm thick, terete, glabrescent to appressed minute-puberulent; domatia absent. Inflorescences usually 2 (rarely 3-4) per node, corymbose with opposite to subopposite decussate branches, densely cymose at distal end of each branchlet, 4.5-12 × 3-7 cm; lateral branches 1-2 pairs, basal portion of axis not branched 2-7 cm long; rachis decussately compressed to subterete, reddish brown; L/A = 1.6-2.1; rachis and branches densely curled to appressed gray-puberulent; distal bracts (when present) deltoid, ca. 0.5 mm long; bracteoles subtending flowers absent. Flowers pedicellate; pedicels 0.5-2 mm long, glabrous to minute puberulent; hypanthium turbinate, 1-1.5 mm long, glabrous. Calyx extremely reduced with wavy margin or barely distinguishable lobes, to 0.5 mm long; lobes to 0.4 mm long, ovate to deltoid, ciliolate at apex. Corolla funnelform, deeply lobed, 2-4 mm long, white to cream-white; tube short cylindrical, 1-1.5 × 1-1.5 mm, glabrous outside and inside; lobes (4-)5, 1.5-2 × 1-1.5 mm, narrowly ovate, truncate at apex, glabrous outside, densely villous at medio-basal zone. Stamens (4-)5, exserted well above the corolla, equal, attached 1-1.5 mm from the base of the tube; filaments 3-4 mm long, terete, basally flattened, connate to throat, densely villous at base; anthers elliptic, 0.6-0.7 × 0.20.4 mm, dorsifixed at medial zone, reversed at maturity, base rounded. Pollen exine irregularly foveolate-reticulate. Style exserted, 2-4 mm long, as long as the corolla, glabrous, minutely costate; style branches extruding as two lips above corolla before anthesis, widely ovate to widely oblong, 0.3-0.4 mm long, stigmatic surface microscopically (40x) papillose; ovaries often infested by insects, developing into globose galls containing minute yellow larvae. Capsules obovoid to turbinate, acute at base, apex rounded, 1.5-2.5 × ca. 1.5 mm, dark brown without lenticels, glabrous throughout; disk loculicidal dehiscence present in old capsules. Seeds 0.5-0.88 × 0.38-0.5 mm.

description: Trees to 40 m tall, 100 cm or more dbh, canopy trees with lobed bole, small spreading crown, with buttresses to 3.35 m high; bark fissured, grayish brown; wood yellow, very hard. Leafy branchlets 2.5-5(-6) mm thick, subterete to decussately compressed, green to brown, glabrous; older branches terete, grayish to pale brown; lenticels not found. Stipules free at base, contorted in bud, narrowly triangular, acuminate, sparsely appressed-puberulent (rarely glabrous) outside, glabrous with basal colleters inside, (20-)25-35 × (4-)5-7 mm, reddish brown, membranous, with many parallel veins departing from base, readily caducous, leaving a scar encircling the stem ca. 1 mm wide. Leaves (10-) 16-22 × (5-)6.5-9.5 cm, L/W = ca. 2:1, elliptic to obovate, acute-de-current at base, acute to obtuse and mucronate at apex, the deltoid acumen 0.5-1.8 cm long; dark green above, pale green below, thick-foliaceous; drying brown to olive-green, stiff chartaceous; glabrous above, glabrous to sparsely appressed-puberulent below; primary and secondary veins glabrous to appressed-puberulent, secondary veins 8-11 each side; tertiary veins subparallel, laterally jointed in the center; petioles (13-)18-31 mm long, 1-1.5(-2) mm thick, adaxially flattened to concave, glabrous; tuft-domatia always present, tuft of hairs departing from the veins and converging toward the center of the axil (Fig. 58E), only at the axils of primary with secondary veins, hairs 0.7-1 mm long, white to golden. Inflorescences 2 per node, corymbose with opposite to subopposite decussate branches, cymose, very compacted at distal end of each branchlet, forming a continuous flowering plane, (8-)10-12(-15) × (4-)5-7 (-9) cm, lateral branches 2(-3) pairs, basal portion of axis not branched (5-)6.5-10.5 cm long; L/A = ca. 3.1; rachis terete to decussately compressed, rachis and branches short puberulent; distal bracts usually absent or narrowly triangular, to 4 × 3 mm; bracteoles subtending flowers absent. Flowers sessile to short-pedicellate; pedicels to 1 mm long, glabrous to sparsely puberulent; hypanthium obconical, 0.8-1 × 0.8-1.2 mm, glabrous, reddish brown. Calyx extremely reduced, truncate to faintly undulate margin, 0.3-0.6 × 1-1.4 mm, glabrous. Corolla funnelform, deeply lobed, 4-5 mm long, cream-white to greenish white (turning pale yellow at maturity); tube short cylindrical, 0.9-1.5 × 0.6-1.1 mm, glabrous outside and inside; lobes 5, 1.8-3.2 × 0.4-0.6 mm, narrowly oblong, acute (rarely rounded) at apex, glabrous outside, sparsely white-villous at basal zone, with medial and distal zones glabrous inside. Stamens 5, exserted well above the corolla, equal, attached 1-1.7 mm from the base of the tube; filaments 3.5-5.5 mm long, terete, basally flattened, connate to throat, with a tuft of densely white-pilose hairs at base; anthers elliptic, 0.6-0.7 × 0.3-0.4 mm, dorsifixed at medial zone, reversed at maturity, base rounded, apex shortly apiculate, truncate to rounded, dehiscing by longitudinal slit. Pollen exine foveolate-reticulate. Style exserted, 3-5 mm long, as long as the corolla, glabrous, minutely costate to minutely winged; style branches extruding as two lips above corolla before anthesis, rounded to oblate, ca. 0.3 mm long, stigmatic surface microscopically (40×) papillose; ovary-galls not found. Capsules subglobose, obtuse at base, rounded at apex, 1.9-2.5 × 1.3-1.7 mm, dark brown without lenticels, glabrous throughout; disk black, exceeding the calyx; disk loculicidal dehiscence present in old capsules. Seeds 0.68-73 × 0.53-0.7 mm.

description: Trees to 30 m tall, 30 cm or more dbh, canopy trees with long buttresses; wood yellow, heavy, very brittle. Leafy branchlets 4-9 mm thick, subterete to compressed, ochraceous, glabrous; older branches terete, grayish to pale brown. Stipules free at base, contorted in bud, narrowly triangular, acuminate, glabrous with ciliate margins outside, glabrous with basal colleters inside, 20-35 × 5-13 mm, reddish brown, readily caducous, leaving a dark-brown scar encircling the stem, 0.5-1 mm wide. Leaves (13-)16-28 × (5-)7-11 cm, L/W = 1.5:1 to 2:1; broadly elliptic to elliptic-obovate, acute-decurrent at base, obtuse and mucronate at apex, the deltoid acumen 0.5-1 cm long; dark green above, pale green below, foliaceous; drying brown above, olive-green below, chartaceous; glabrous above and below; primary and secondary veins glabrous, secondary veins 7-12 each side; tertiary veins starting subparallel and reticulate in the center; petioles 20-45 mm long, 1.3-1.8 mm thick, terete to adaxially concave, glabrous; domatia absent or rarely a few hairs at the axil. Inflorescences 2 per node, corymbose with opposite to subopposite decussate branches, densely cymose at distal end of each branchlet; 8-15 × 8-13 cm, lateral branches l(-2) pairs, basal portion of axis not branched 2.5-7 cm long; rachis decussately compressed to subterete, reddish brown, rachis and branches glabrous to sparsely minute puberulent; distal bracts usually absent or deltoid, 1-2 mm long, ciliolate; bracteoles subtending flowers absent. Flowers sessile to short-pedicellate; pedicels (when present) to 3 mm long, minute puberulent; hypanthium turbinate, 1.5-3 mm long, glabrous, reddish brown. Calyx extremely reduced with wavy margin or barely distinguishable lobes, 0.5-1 × 2-2.5 mm; lobes (when present) to 2 mm long, shallow-ovate to shallow-triangular. Corolla funnelform, deeply lobed, 4-5 mm long, white to greenish white; tube short cylindrical, 1-2 × ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous outside and inside; lobes 5, 2.5-3.5 × 1-1.5 mm, oblong and rounded to truncate at apex, glabrous outside, densely villous at medio-basal zone. Stamens 5, exserted well above the corolla, equal, attached 2.54 mm from the base of the tube; filaments 4-5 mm long, terete, basally flattened, connate to throat, densely white-villous at base; anthers elliptic, 0.7-1 × 0.3-0.4 mm; dorsifixed at medial zone, reversed at maturity, base rounded. Pollen exine reticulate-foveolate. Style exserted, 3.5-5 mm long, as long as the corolla, glabrous, minutely costate; style branches extruding as two lips above corolla before anthesis, rounded, ca. 1 mm long, stigmatic surface microscopically (40x) papillose; ovary-galls not found. Capsules obovoid to oblong, acute at base, apex rounded to subtruncate, 4-5 × 3-3.5 mm, dark brown without lenticels, glabrous below the disk; disk black, densely minute-puberulent; disk loculicidal dehiscence present in old capsules. Seeds 0.49-0.78 × 0.33-0.58 mm.

description: Trees to 35 m tall, 50 cm or more dbh (exceptionally 50 m tall, 1 m dbh, Baker et al. 6000), much branched at crown, with tall buttresses; bark fissured, white-grayish, peeling off in long fibrous strips exposing the reddish bark underneath; wood yellow, very hard. Leafy branchlets 3-4(-5) mm thick, woody (not succulent), subterete to decussately compressed, youngest 2-3 nodes densely appressed-canescent; older branches glabrate, terete, grayish to pale brown; lenticels not found. Stipules free at base, contorted in bud, narrowly triangular, acuminate, densely canescent (rarely puberulent or rarely glabrous) outside, glabrous with sparse small colleters at base inside, 12-18(-30) × 3-5 mm, gray-canescent, with many parallel veins departing from base, readily caducous, leaving a white scar encircling the stem, 0.5-1 mm wide. Leaves 6-16(-20) × 3-6.5(-9) cm, LAV = 2:1, elliptic to elliptic-obovate, acute at base, obtuse at apex, sometimes with a deltoid acumen 0.5 cm long; dark green above, pale green below, semi-coriaceous; drying dark brown above, olive-green below, stiff-chartaceous; juvenile leaves with blade, primary and secondary veins sparsely appressed pubescent above, mature leaves glabrous above, appressed pubescent below; primary and secondary veins ascending-pubescent to canescent (rarely glabrous), secondary veins 8-9 each side; tertiary veins starting subparallel and reticulate in the middle; petioles 8-20 mm long, 1-1.5 mm thick, terete to adaxially flattened, glabrous to puberulent to canescent; domatia represented by a few hairs surrounding a round slightly depressed glabrous area and converging toward its center (Fig. 57G), hairs 0.4-0.7 mm long. Inflorescences 2 (rarely 4) per node; corymbose with opposite to subopposite decussate branches, cymules fairly compacted at distal end of each branchlet, forming a continuous flowering plane, 8-10(-12) × (4-)5.5-7.5 cm, lateral branches 2(-3) pairs, basal portion of axis not branched 4-5.5(-8) cm long; L/A = 2.5:1 to 2.7:1 (rarely 3:1); rachis decussately compressed, rachis and branches sparsely yellow-puberulent; distal bracts reduced to scales or linear, 1-3 × 0.3-0.5 mm; bracteoles subtending flowers absent. Flowers sessile to short-pedicellate; pedicels to 1 mm long, glabrous to sparsely pubescent (to short-villous); hypanthium obovate, 0.9-1.2 × 0.8-1.1 mm, glabrous, reddish brown. Calyx extremely reduced, truncate to short-lobed, 0.3-0.5 × 1-1.5 mm, glabrous; lobes shallowly triangular, connected by a membrane, 0.1-0.6 mm long, often ciliate. Corolla funnelform, deeply lobed, 2.5-3.5 mm long, cream-white to yellowish white (turning pale yellow at maturity); tube short cylindrical, 1-1.5 × 0.7-1 mm, glabrous outside and inside; lobes 5, 1.5-2 × 0.5-0.7 mm, oblong, rounded at apex, glabrous outside, with a tuft of white thin-sericeous hairs at basal zone with medial and distal zones glabrous inside. Stamens 5, exserted well above the corolla, equal, attached 1-1.5 mm from the base of the tube; filaments 2-2.5 mm long, terete, basally flattened, connate to throat, with a dense tuft of white-sericeous hairs for half the length at base; anthers elliptic, 0.5-0.7 × 0.4-0.5 mm, dorsifixed at medial zone, base rounded, apex rounded, not mucronate. Pollen exine foveolate-reticulate. Style exserted, 2.5-3.5 mm long, as long as the corolla, terete to square (not costate), often with few sparse hairs on distal portion; style branches extruding as two lips above corolla before anthesis, rounded, ca. 0.5 mm wide, stigmatic surface microscopically (40 ×) papillose; ovary-galls not found. Capsules subglobose to obovoid, obtuse at base, shallowly hemispherical at apex, 2-2.5 × 1.5-2 mm, capsule dark brown, without lenticels; disk black, sparsely to densely pubescent, not exceeding the calyx; disk loculicidal dehiscence present in old capsules. Seeds 0.5-0.63 × 0.35-0.5 mm.

description: Tree to 15.0 m tall, usually smaller, or shrub, the young branches pilose-tomentellous to puberulous, becoming glabrous with age. Leaves oblong to elliptic, subcoriaceous to membraneous, 4.0-14.5 cm long, 2.0-5.5 cm broad, acuminate (very rarely acute) at apex, with acumen 1.0-18.0 mm long, rounded to cuneate at base, papillose beneath, with a few stiff appressed hairs, the palisade glands few; primary veins 5-13 pairs, plane or prominulous above; midrib prominulous above, prominent and hirsute beneath; petioles 1.0-3.0 mm long, terete, eglandular, tomentellous to puberulous. Stipules linear, 2.0-6.0 mm long, tomentellous, persistent, eglandular. Inflorescences terminal and axillary panicles, 3.5-17.0 cm long, with most branches bearing more than one flower and more than one pair of bracts, the rachis and branches usually short-tomentellous, less frequently short-pilose-hispid. Bracts and bracteoles 1.0-3.5 mm long, lanceolate to ovate, acute, persistent, eglandular, sometimes with numerous bracts along inflorescence branches. Receptacle campanulate, tomentellous on exterior, glabrous within except at throat; pedicels 1.0-3.0 mm long. Calyx lobes acute, puberulous on both surfaces. Petals 5, glabrous. Stamens 3, unilateral with teeth or short filamentous staminodes opposite them, the filaments glabrous, far exceeding calyx lobes. Style hirsute up to half its length. Ovary inserted at mouth of receptacle, pilose-tomentose. Fruit ellipsoid; epicarp glabrescent or puberulous, less frequently tomentose, slightly longitudinally canaliculate when dry; mesocarp thin, fleshy; endocarp thin, hard, bony, hirsute within.

description: Medium-sized tree, the young branches sparsely pubescent, soon glabrous and lenticellate. Leaves coriaceous, oblong, 10.0-15.0 cm long, 3.0-5.5 cm broad, acuminate at apex, with acumen 8.0-12.0 mm long, cuneate at base, the lower surface with several palisade glands towards base, glabrous; primary veins 9-12 pairs, prominulous on both surfaces; midrib prominulous and glabrous on both surfaces; petioles 4.0-5.0 mm long, glabrescent, terete, eglandular. Stipules linear, to 5.0 mm long, glabrescent, subpersistent, eglandular. Inflorescences terminal and axillary panicles 7.0-12.0 cm long, the rachis and branches with sparse appressed pubescence. Bracts and bracteoles oblong-lanceolate, 2.5-3.5 mm long, membraneous, persistent, sparsely puberulous, the margins with both sessile and short-stipitate glands. Flowers 5.0-6.0 mm long. Receptacle campanulate, glabrescent on exterior, glabrous within except for hairs at throat; pedicels 1.0-3.0 mm long. Calyx lobes acute, glabrescent on exterior, gray-pubescent within, the margins glandular. Petals 5, white, glabrous. Stamens 3, unilateral, with 3 short filamentous staminodes opposite them, the filaments far exceeding calyx lobes. Style hirsute up to one third its length. Ovary inserted at mouth of receptacle, pilose. Fruit not seen.

description: Tree to 20.0 m tall, the young branches tomentellous, becoming glabrous and lenticellate with age. Leaves elliptic to oblong-elliptic, coriaceous, 7.0-24.0 cm long, 3.5-10.5 cm broad, acuminate at apex, with acumen 2.0-10.5 mm long, rounded at base, with impressed venation above, hirsute beneath, with a few palisade glands towards base; primary veins 10-13 pairs, impressed above, prominent beneath; midrib plane above, prominent and hirsute beneath; petioles 3.0-8.0 mm long, tomentellous, caducous, eglandular. Stipules 2.0-3.0 mm long, ovate, tomentose, persistent. Inflorescences densely-flowered terminal and axillary panicles 6.0-25.0 cm long, the rachis and branches tomentellous to puberulous. Bracts and bracteoles 1.0-6.0 mm long, oblong to lanceolate; glands numerous, long-stalked, stipitate, arising from pedicels and axils of flowers, on stalks up to 8.0 mm long. Flowers 4.0-6.0 mm long. Receptacle campanulate, puberulous on exterior, glabrous within except at throat. Calyx lobes rounded to acute, puberulous on exterior, gray-pubescent within, the margins eglandular. Petals 5, glabrous. Stamens 3-5, unilateral, with short filamentous staminodes opposite them; filaments glabrous, far exceeding calyx lobes. Style hirsute up to one third its length. Ovary inserted at mouth of receptacle, pilose. Fruit ellipsoid; epicarp smooth, glabrous; mesocarp thin, fleshy; endocarp thin, hard, bony, hirsute within.

description: Shrub, often with trailing branches, the young stems sparsely hispid, soon becoming glabrous. Leaves oblong, thick-coriaceous, 7.0-12.0 cm long, 2.1-4.9 cm broad, acuminate at apex, with acumen 4.0-10.0 mm long, cordate at base, glabrous beneath, the palisade glands rare; primary veins 10-14 pairs, prominulous above, prominent beneath; midrib prominulous above, prominent and glabrous beneath; petioles 1.0-2.0 mm long, terete, eglandular, hispid when young. Stipules ca 4.0 mm long, linear, tomentellous, subpersistent, eglandular. Inflorescences terminal and axillary racemes 17.0-25.0 cm long, the rachis puberulous above, hispid towards base. Bracts and bracteoles 1.0-3.0 mm long, oblong to lanceolate, persistent, puberulous, with stipitate glands. Flowers 5.0-6.0 mm long. Receptacle campanulate, puberulous on exterior, glabrous within except at throat; pedicels 7.0-11.0 mm long. Calyx lobes rounded to acute, glabrescent on exterior, gray-puberulous within. Petals 5, pink, glabrous. Stamens 6-7, unilateral with toothed staminodes opposite them, the filaments far exceeding calyx lobes, glabrous. Style hirsute at base only. Ovary inserted at mouth of receptacle, tomentose. Fruit not seen.

description: Small tree, the young branches hispid, soon becoming glabrous. Leaves oblong to oblong-lanceolate, coriaceous, 8.0-17.0 cm long, 2.2-5.0 cm broad, acuminate at apex, with acumen 5.0-18.0 cm long, subcordate at base, glabrous beneath, the palisade glands rare; primary veins 8-10 pairs, prominulous and glabrous on both surfaces; midrib prominulous above, prominent and glabrous beneath; petioles 2.0-3.5 mm long, terete, eglandular, glabrous or hispid when young. Stipules 4.0-7.0 mm long, linear-filamentous, hispid to glabrous, eglandular, persistent. Inflorescences terminal and axillary racemes 12.0-27.0 cm long, the rachis hispid or glabrous. Bracts and bracteoles 1.5-3.0 mm long, oblong to lanceolate, hispid, eglandular, persistent. Flowers 4.0-5.o mm long. description: Small tree, the young branches puberulous, soon becoming glabrous. Leaves ovate-lanceolate, coriaceous, broadest below midpoint, 6.0-12.0 cm long, 1.6-4.2 cm broad, gradually tapering to an acute or acuminate apex, rounded to subcordate at base, glabrous beneath except on midrib, with palisade glands towards base; primary veins 6-9 pairs, prominulous and glabrous on both surfaces; midrib prominulous above, prominent and puberulous beneath; petioles 2.0-4.0 mm long, terete, eglandular, glabrous or with a few stiff erect hairs. Stipules ca 2.0 mm long, linear, subpersistent, glabrescent, with stipitate glands. Inflorescences terminal and axillary racemes 6.0-12.0 cm long, the rachis sparsely puberulous. Bracts and bracteoles 1.5-2.5 mm long, oblong, peristent, puberulous, with stipitate glands on apex and margins. Flowers 5.0-6.0 mm long. Receptacle campanulate, sparsely puberulous on exterior, glabrous within except at throat; pedicels 3.0-5.0 mm long, eglandular. Petals 5, pink, glabrous. Calyx lobes acute, sparsely puberulous on exterior, gray-puberulous within, Stamens 5-6, unilateral with toothed staminodes opposite them, the filaments glabrous, far exceeding calyx lobes. Style hirsute on lower portion. Ovary inserted at mouth of receptacle, pilose. Fruit ellipsoid; epicarp smooth, glabrous when mature, puberulous when young; mesocarp thin, fleshy; endocarp hard, bony, hirsute within.

description: Tree, medium to large, height to 20-40(-45) m, dbh to 80-100 cm. Trunk monopodial, erect, terete, the bole usually for 1/3-½ of the total height free of branches. Bark thick, scaly, with elongated plates and deep, longitudinal fissures, dark brown to grey-brown, on young trees and branches smooth, reddish brown or grey-brown. Branches of first order long, spreading or ascending, the lower branches curved down, often distinctly whorled; branches of higher orders slender, spreading, curved down and then upwards, or ascending. Shoots slender, smooth, with (short) decurrent pulvini, glaucous or pruinose. Cataphylls 10-15 mm long, subulate-caudate, .soon recurved, with ciliate margins, reddish brown to dark brown, falling shortly after the fascicles. Vegetative buds ovoid-conical, acute, the terminal buds 15-20 X 10-15 mm, the laterals smaller, not resinous; the scales imbricate, with free, spreading apices, subulate-linear, with ciliate margins, reddish brown. Fascicle sheaths (15-)20-30(-35) mm long, persistent, consisting of ca. 10 initially distinct, imbricate, subulate scales, lustrous red-brown, weathering grey-brown. Leaves in fascicles of 5, rarely 4 or 6, in lax tufts at the ends of upturned branches, persisting 23 years, slender, straight, spreading or drooping, rarely more or less rigid, (18-)20-30(-35) cm X 0.8-1.3 mm, with serrulate margins, acute, (light) green or glaucous-green. Stomata on all faces of leaves, in (2-)3-7 lines on the convex abaxial face and 2-4(-5) lines on each adaxial face. Leaf anatomy: Cross section triangular; hypodermis multilayered, not or scarcely intruding into the mesophyll; resin ducts (2-)3-4(-6), the 3 marginal ducts usually present, medial, rarely 1-2 internal or external; stele more or less terete; the outer cell walls of the endodermis thickened; vascular bundles 2, distinct, the xylem strands connate. Pollen cones crowded near the proximal end of a new shoot, numerous, spreading, ovoid-oblong to cylindrical, 20-35 X 5-7 mm, purplish or pinkish yellow, turning brown. Seed cones subterminal, solitary or in pairs, more rarely in whorls of 3-4 on very short, stout peduncles which remain with a few cone scales on the branch when the cone has fallen. Immature cones ovoid, 15-20 X 10-12 mm, with small, spreading spines, purplish, soon pinkish brown, sometimes glaucous, maturing in two seasons. Mature cones ovoid-oblong to obliquely ovoid when closed, sometimes ovoid-attenuate, more or less asymmetrical, often curved at base, ovoid-oblong to broadly ovoid when opened, then 7-16 X 6-13 cm. Seed scales ca. 140-190, parting to release the seeds except the proximal infertile scales, usually thick woody, oblong, straight or slightly curved, somewhat larger and more curved on one side of the cone, reddish brown to dark purplish brown, with light brown marks of seed wings on the adaxial side. Apophysis extremely variable, from nearly flat to elongated, more so on one side of the cone and toward the base, transversely keeled, tapering to an obtuse umbo (or umbo mucronate), rhombic or pentagonal in outline, upper margin angular, irregularly undulate, or rounded, colour in various hues of brown. Umbo dorsal, variable, from obtuse to prominent, 3-15 mm long, 5-10 mm wide at base, without a prickle or prickle deciduous, usually darker than the apophysis. Seeds obliquely ovoid, slightly flattened, 5-7 X 3-4.5 mm, ochraceous to grey-brown, with or without dark spots. Seed wings articulate, effective, held to the seed by two claws, thinly covering part of the seed on one side, obliquely-ovate, with a straight side, 20-25 X 7-10 mm, yellowish brown, translucent, with darker tinge distally. Seedlings: The hypocotyl of this species is consistently longer (mean 31.8 mm) than that of P montezumae (mean 17.5 mm), according to a study by Caballero (1967). Cotyledons (7-)8-12(-13), but given as a mean of 7.2 by Caballero (1967).

description: Tree, small to medium, height to 20-25 m, dbh to 70-80 cm. Trunk monopodial, usually straight, terete. Bark thick, with deep, longitudinal fissures and rough, elongated plates, on the upper part of the trunk and branches smooth to finally scaly, smooth on young trees, greyish brown. Branches long, slender, spreading or curved downward, not pendulous, forming a rounded, dense or more open crown. Shoots often multinodal, smooth, ridged with decurrent bases of pulvini, reddish brown to grey-brown. Cataphylls lanceolate to subulate, straight, erose-ciliate at margins, dark brown, soon deciduous. Vegetative buds ovoid-conical to oval-oblong, the terminal bud 10-15 mm long, the laterals more ovoid and smaller, not resinous; the scales free or spreading at apex, subulate, ciliate at margins, brown. Fascicle sheaths initially ca. 10 mm long, with chartaceous, yellowish brown to whitish brown scales, persistent but reduced in mature fascicles to 3-5 mm, scaly, exfoliating, dark brown, weathering blackish brown. Leaves in fascicles of 3, in usually rigid, spreading tufts on the ultimate branches, persisting up to 4 years, stiff and straight, (7-)9-13(-15) cm X 11.2 mm, serrulate along the margins, acute-pungent, bright, lustrous green. Stomata on all faces of the leaves, in 6-8 lines on the convex abaxial face and 3-4 lines on each adaxial face. Leaf anatomy: Cross section transverse-triangular, with a convex abaxial side; hypodermis uniform, with a double layer of cells; resin ducts 2-4(-6), medial, the two laterals always present; stele transverse-obovate to transverse-triangular in cross section; walls of endodermal cells uniformly thin; vascular bundles 2, the xylem strands connate. Pollen cones crowded near the proximal end of a new shoot, subtended by broad, scarious bracts, spreading, ovoid-oblong to cylindrical, 15-20 X 5-6 mm, yellowish, turning yellowish brown. Seed cones appearing on very young trees, subterminal or lateral, in whorls of 3-8, sometimes more, on short, stout, tenacious peduncles, at maturity appearing sessile, long persistent, serotinous. Immature cones on ca. 10 mm long, recurved peduncles, ovoid, light purplish, soon light brown, maturing in two seasons. Mature cones serotinous, narrowly and obliquely ovoid to ovoid-attenuate, slightly curved or straight when closed, with an oblique base often deformed by compression of the expanding branch and scales, (6-)8-13(-15) X (4-)5-7 cm when open (width 3.5-5 cm when closed). Seed scales ca. 80-120, remaining closed several to many years, parting eventually or not, oblong, straight or recurved when parted, the proximal scales remaining connate, purplish brown, with light brown marks of seed scales adaxially. Apophysis flat or slightly raised, rhombic to obtrullate in outline, with an undulate or crenate upper margin, (weakly) transversely keeled, sometimes gibbous on one side toward the base of the cone, lustrous ochraceous or light brown, weathering grey. Umbo dorsal, depressed or flat, rhombic in outline, 3-4 mm wide, with a minute, deciduous prickle, light brown to grey. Seeds obliquely obovoid to ellipsoid, slightly flattened, 5-8 X 3-4 mm, grey-brown to blackish brown. Seed wings articulate, effective, held to the seed by two claws and a thin layer of tissue covering the seed on one side, oblong, with a straight and a curved side, 15-20 X 6-8 mm, yellowish to grey-brown. Number of cotyledons not observed.

description: Hierbas de gran porte, rizomatosas; rizoma craso hasta de 4.5 cm diám. Lepidofilos lineares, 2.6-4.5 x 1 cm, inciso-laciniados, ápice atenuado, filiforme o acuminado, glabros por ambas caras o con la vena media (costa) pilosa, costa prominente, membrano-sos, atropurpúreos. Pecíolo ca. 1 cm diám, basal y 7 mm diám, distal, canaliculado, densamente piloso, lámina orbicular-reniforme, cordada, profundamente  5-lobulada, lóbulos 2-3-sublobulados, todos los lóbulos de ápice agudo, lóbulos terciarios dentiformes, p fundidad de los senos mayores ca. 3/4 de la longitud u laminar, senos obtusos a redondeados, margen enteo diminutamente dentado, dientes espinosos, hojas jóvenes densamente pilosas por ambas caras, cuan maduras con la haz lisa (nunca escabrosa), pilosa a largo de las venas, areolada, a veces cada areola coronada por una proyección espiniforme, y con el envés densamente piloso, especialmente a lo largo e as venas. Brácteas de la inflorescencia lineares, 6-7 x 1.5 mm, carinadas, rígidas, envés y margen densamente hirsutos, margen entero. Base de los sépalos a de 0.25 mm largo; pétalos desconocidos, estambres 2, anteras en pre-antesis orbiculares, en antesis y post-antesis elipsoides, hasta de 1.3 x 1 mm, ligeramente asimétricas, levemente apiculadas; ovario desconocido. Infructescencia hasta de 75 cm largo, sobre un escap0 hasta de 10 cm largo, pubescente; ramificaciones de la Infructescencia 10-14 cm largo. Frutos pedicelados, globosos, ca. 1.5 mm diám., fuertemente constrictos en el ápice.

description: Shrubs or small trees 1-5(-7) m tall, the stems densely stellate-pubescent (hairs 0.5 mm long or less). Leaf blades ovate, sometimes weakly angulate or lobulate, mostly 8-25 x 7-19 cm, basally cordate, serrate, acute, palmately 7-nerved, discolorous, minutely stellate-pubescent above and beneath, more densely so on nerves; petioles mostly 8-19 cm long (shorter upward); stipules erect, 1-2.5 cm long, narrowly lanceolate. Flowers in crowded terminal nearly leafless panicles; pedicels 1-3 cm long, usually several per axil; involucellar bracts 11-13, valvate in bud, externally stellate-pubescent, internally ciliate-hirsute, narrowly lanceolate, 15-20 x 2-4 mm; calyx 3-4 mm long, wholly concealed by involucel; corolla 3-4.5 cm long, rose-pink (or sometimes white), funnelform, externally stellate-pubescent; androecium subequal to corolla or slightly exserted, the filaments 5-10 mm long; styles slender, purplish. Fruits oblate, ca. 1 cm diam., blackish and viscid at maturity; mericarps 6 mm high, carinate and reticulately veined.

description: Shrubs 0.5-1 m tall, the stems densely setose (hairs 2-5 mm long) and with understory of scabrid stellate hairs (e.g., Heringer 15554) or minute glandular hairs. Leaf blades ovate, deeply cordate, serrate, acuminate, slightly discolorous, roughly pubescent on both surfaces, palmately 7-nerved, mostly 3-6 x 2.5-6 cm; petioles 1.5-6 cm long; stipules subulate, 2-6 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils (the flowers sometimes aggregated apically), the pedicels 1.5-5 cm long, with pubescence like stem; involucellar bracts 11-13, linear, 18-26 mm long, viscid and setose; calyx 15-25(-30) mm long, pubescent and ciliate; corolla 3.5-5 cm long, pink with red center; staminal column half length of corolla, glabrous; styles strongly exserted from column, subequal to corolla, united below, free for distal 1-3 mm. Fruits 8 mm diam., retuse, glabrous, the mericarps unomamented.

description: Subshrubs or decumbent herbs 0.5-1 (-2) m tall, with a deep spreading perennial root system, the stems pilose (hairs 2-4 mm long) or rarely glabrous. Leaf blades broadly ovate to subrotund (rarely narrower), deeply cordate, crenate-serrate, acute or acuminate, ciliate on margin, with minute stellate hairs to subglabrous on both surfaces or sometimes the upper surface with appressed simple hairs 1-2 mm long; mostly 2.5-4 x 2.5-5 cm; petioles 1.5-3 cm long; stipules subulate, 2 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 0.5-1.5 cm long, slender; involucellar bracts 10-12, linear-lanceolate, 12-16 x 1.5-2 mm, externally glandular-puberulent, internally hirsute; calyx 4 mm long, glandular-puberulent, mostly concealed by involucel; corolla red, 1.5-2.5 cm long, glabrous throughout, the claw scarcely discernible; staminal column 5 mm long, glabrous, the filaments 2 mm long; styles exserted from column. Fruits 1 cm diam., stellate-pubescent, the mericarps 10 mm high, keeled and coarsely rugose, apically pointed.

description: Hierbas de porte pequeño a mediano; rizoma craso, hasta de 2 cm diám. Lepidofilos lineares, 2-3 x 0.4-0.5 cm, haz esparcidamente pilosa, envés piloso, costa patente, margen entero, ápice laciniado, coriaceos, atrocarmín. Pecíolo hasta de 35 cm largo, ca. 8 mm diám, basal, ca. 5 mm diám, distal, surcado, con proyecciones espinosas diminutas en el ápice, hirsuto por lo menos en el extremo distal; lámina reniforme, anchamente cordada, 5-7-lobulada, 2-sublobulada, todos los lóbulos de ápice redondeado, senos obtusos, con una profundidad de 1/4-1/2 de la longitud laminar, cuando joven repando-ondulada y con margen diminutamente dentado, coriáceo; haz verde-opaca, pilosa, especialmente a lo largo de las venas, escabrosa, areolada, tuberculada, tubérculos usualmente blancos, envés densamente hirsuto a lo largo de la venación prominente. Inflorescencia hasta de 40 cm largo, sésil, oblongo-lanceolada, raquis pubérulo, con proyecciones espinosas cortas; brácteas de la inflorescencia angosto-ovadas a lanceoladas, (5-)20-25 x (1—)2—2.5 mm, con el apice acuminado, glabras o esparcidamente puberulas, margen ligeramente laciniado; ramificaciones de la inflorescencia 3-6 cm largo. Base de los sepalos angosta, ca. 0.25 mm largo; petalos de tamano variable, usualmente ca. 1.5 mm largo, fuertemente cuculados, crasos, base linear, apice laciniado, pilosos por la superficie dorsal; estambres 2, anteras elipsoides, 1-1.8 x 1.3(-1.5) mm, muy cortamente apiculadas; ovario subgloboso, ca. 1 x 0.9 mm, rojizo. Infructescencia con ramificaciones de 4-7 cm largo. Frutos ancho-elipsoidales, sésiles, base no atenuada, hasta de 1.5 x 1.7 mm, levemente constrictos hacia el ápice, coronado por la base diminuta de los sépalos.
bibliographicCitation: Mora-Osejo, Luis E., et al. 2011. Gunneraceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 109: i--v, 1--166.

description: Hierbas de gran porte; rizoma desconocido. Lepidofilos 7-9 x 2-4 cm, lobulados, todos los lóbulos con base engrosada, margen laciniado y ápice atenuado, filiforme. Pecíolo hasta de 20 cm largo, 5-6 mm diám, basal y 3-4 mm diám, distal, levemente canaliculado, pubescente o esparcidamente piloso, sin proyecciones espiniformes; lámina orbicular-reniforme, levemente lobulada o sublobulada, cartácea, base cordada, lóbulos <1/6 de la longitud laminar, senos obtusos, los proximales agudos, todos los lóbulos de ápice agudo-dentado, haz lisa (no escabrosa), glabra, verde-olivo, envés con venas primarias y secundarias hirsutas, verde-pálido opaco, margen irregularmente dentado (dientes de tamaño diferente). Inflorescencia subsésil, 30-50 cm largo, ca. 5 mm diám, basal, raquis hirsuto-piloso; bracteas de la inflorescencia 2-4.5 x 0.2-0.4 cm, atenuadas hacia el ápice, margen membranoso, a veces fraccionado, costa escasamente visible, haz glabra o, a veces, pilosa, envés piloso, con tricomas rígidos, adpresos; ramificaciones de la inflorescencia 7-10(-20) cm largo, 0.8-1.2 mm diam., hirsuto-pilosas. Sépalos con base hasta de 0.5 mm largo, triangulares, y ápice membranoso, laciniado, caduco; pétalos ligeramente cuculados, ca. 2 mm largo, base atenuada, margen ligeramente ciliado; estambres 2, anteras orbiculares a elipsoides, 1.5-2.2 x 1.6-1.8 mm, ápice por lo general apiculado; ovario globoso, eramente constricto hacia el ápice, ca. 1.5 mm diám. Infructescencia con ramificaciones hasta de 12 cm largo, sinuosas, no engrosadas, pilosas, hirsutas. Fru-tos laxamente dispuestos, elipsoides, subglobosos, 2 x 1.5 mm, a veces comprimidos o angulosos, corona-dos por la base de los sépalos.

description: Hierbas de porte mediano a grande, rara vez pequenas; rizoma craso, 4-5 cm diam. Lepidofilos numerosos, rfgidos, enteros o inciso-laciniados especialmente hacia la mitad distal del margen, angosto-lineares a angosto-obovados, 1-4.5 x 0.3-0.4 cm, glabros, de color atrocarmm. Peciolo 60-80 cm largo, 1-2 cm diam, basal, 5-8 mm diam, distal, levemente canaliculado, glabro, con proyecciones espinosas en toda la superficie; lamina reniforme, 50-125 cm diam., 9-lobulada, base cordada, no peltada, lobulos de apice agudo, 2-3-sublobulados, senos ca. 1/3 de la longitud laminar, margen generalmente con dientes agudos (rara vez entera), haz escabrosa, a veces en algunos sectores lisa, areolada, areolas coronadas por proyecciones espinosas, verde opaca, enves con venacion prominente, espinosa y pilosa, verde claro. Inflorescencia hasta de 80 cm largo, inclufdo un escapo de ca. 15 cm largo, 5-11 mm diam, basal, usualmente espi-noso, canaliculado, al igual que el raquis; bracteas de la inflorescencia rigidas o tenues, lineares a muy an-gostamente espatuladas, hasta de 4 x 1 mm, margen entero o muy levemente laciniado; ramificaciones de la inflorescencia 2-7 cm largo, pubescentes. Sepalos 2, triangulares, crasos, con la base persistente hasta de 0-75 mm largo; petalos espatulados, ligeramente cucu-ados, ovados, base atenuada, apice caudado, margenentero; estambres 2, filamentos 0.2 mm largo, anteras suborbiculares, ca. 1 x 0.75 mm, ligeramente apiculadas, ovario subcónico, truncado. Infructescencia hasta de 1.2 m de largo; ramificaciones pediceladas, hasta de 11 cm largo, ligeramente engrosadas. Frutos densamente dispuestos, sésiles, subglobosos, constrictos hacia el ápice, hasta de 2.5 mm diam, incluida la base de los sépalos de ca. 1 mm largo.
bibliographicCitation: Mora-Osejo, Luis E., et al. 2011. Gunneraceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 109: i--v, 1--166.

description: Hierbas de porte gigante, rizomatosas, rizoma de-cumbente, 1-3 m largo, 20-30(-40) cm diám. Lepidofilos numerosos, reverdecidos por la haz y hacia el ápice, lineares, (10-)20-39 x 4-7.5 cm, atenuados hacia el ápice, levemente areolados, margen cartáceo, profundamente laciniado, vena media prominente, engrosada, pilosa. Pecíolo hasta 2.7 m largo, piloso, provisto de proyecciones espinosas rígidas de 2-4 mm largo; lámina suborbicular, 92-115 x 170-184 cm, base profundamente cordada, 11-13-lobulada, lobulos apice águdo, longitud de los senos primarios ca. 1/5 de la longitud laminar, agudos, haz escabrosa Y con venatión hirsuta, envés con venación prominente, inerme, hirsuta, margen con dientes tamaño variable, espiniscentes. Inflorescencia juvenil ca. 50 cm largo, cuando madura hasta 1.5 m largo; brácteas lineares, 2-4 x 0.1-0.2 cm, pubescentes, pardorojizas, margen con lacinias caducas; ramificaciones de la inflorescencia subsésiles, (2-)12.5-19 cm largo, 4-6 mm diám., hirsutas. Sépalos 1.5-1.8 mm largo, carinados, base crasa, caduca, ca. 1 mm largo, ápice distalmente ensanchado, fimbriado; pétalos 2, fuertemente cuculados, elípticos a obovados, 1.8-2 x 1.5-2 mm, base atenuada, costa engrosada, margen tenue, ciliado, ápice hirsuto; estambres 2, anteras subsésiles, ovoides a oblongas, 0.8-1.7 mm largo, no apiculadas; ovario globoso, ca. 1 mm diam. Infructescencia con escapo hasta de 40 cm largo, raquis 2-2.3 m largo y ramificaciones 10-30 cm largo, hirsutas. Frutos sésiles, subglobosos, 2-2.3 x 1.8-2 mm, cuando maduros desprovistos de las bases caducas de los sepalos. De acuerdo con Saint-John (1957) los individuos de esta especie, probablemente los de mayor tamaño del género en el mundo, alcanzan alturas hasta de 4.7 m, con rizomas de 3 m de largo y 40 cm de espesor. Ejemplares cultivados en el Jardín Botánico de Bogotá desde junio de 1978 por el autor principal de esta monografía, no alcanzaron, doce años después de la siembra, tales dimensiones.

description: Hierbas rizomatosas estolomferas, con rizomas hasta de 4 mm diam, y estolones hasta de 3 mm diam. Lepidofilos ocreiformes, con la haz glabra, el enves a veces estrigoso o esparcidamente estrigoso, y el margen entero, glabro, membranosos, pardo-oscuros a translucidos, con venas visibles. Peciolo (2-)5-22 cm largo, 2-3 mm diam., estrigoso, surcado; lamina en-tera, reniforme, 2-6(-12) x 1.5—6(—11) cm, profunda-mente cordada, haz lisa, glabra, enves glabro excepto la venation que es pilosa o estrigosa, margen crenado. Inflorescencias masculinas en tirsos paniculados, 3-4 cm largo, 1-1.6 cm ancho, con escapo de 5-6 cm largo, 1-2 mm diam., estrigoso, raquis y ramificaciones de la inflorescencia pilosas. Flores masculinas pediceladas, pedicelo hasta de 2.5 mm largo; base de los sepalos linear, ca. 0.5 x 0.2 mm ancho; estambres 2, con filamentos cortos, 0.2-0.6 mm largo, y anteras oblongo-elipsoides, 1.5-1.6 x 0.75-1.2 mm, ligeramente apiculadas, atropurpureas o pardo-oscuras. Inflorescencias femeninas moradas, densifloras a lo largo de esta-quioides (es decir, inflorescencias espiciformes pero con flor terminal), a veces ramificadas hacia la base, hasta de 2.5 cm largo, 1.5 cm diam., con escapo hasta de 1 cm largo, 2 mm diam., raquis y escapo estrigosos. description: Erect shrub 0.3-1.5 m tall; mature stems terete to subterete, often conspicuously striate or ridged, glabrous or sometimes with stout, gland-tipped, basally swollen setae to 0.3 mm long (or also moderately to densely hirsute with spreading to ascending, basally swollen, straight to crisped, ferruginous, eglandular hairs to 3.5 mm long), glabrate but then scabrous (± punctate) due to remnant hair bases; bark thin, cracking longitudinally, reddish-brown; twigs terete to subterete, striate, glabrous to densely white puberulent (also hirsute as on stems); buds ovate, complanate, ca. 2 mm long, scales striate, ciliolate. description: Shrub or small tree. Stipules to 3.0 mm long, linear, caducous. Inflorescences terminal and axillary panicles, the rachis and branches densely brown-villous. Bracts and bracteoles ovate, to 15.0 mm long, persistent. Receptacle cylindrical, 15.0-18.0 mm long, densely ferrugineous-villous on exterior, glabrous within except for deflexed hairs at throat. Calyx lobes rounded, sericeous. Petals 5, white, pubescent, ciliate on margins. Stamens ca 40, inserted in a complete circle. Ovary densely villous. Style pubescent for three fourths its length. Fruit (immature) long and narrow, with smooth glabrous epicarp.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1972. Chrysobalanaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 9: 1-410.

description: Large tree. Leaves ovate 4.0-7.0 cm long, 2.5-3.0 cm broad, obtuse to subcuneate at base, caudately acuminate at apex, with acumen 6.0-9.0 mm long, glabrous above, prominently reticulate beneath with silver-gray pubescence between reticulations; midrib impressed above, pubescent on lower portion; primary veins 6-8 pairs, prominent beneath; petioles 4.0-6.0 mm long, shortly pubescent. Stipules minute. Inflorescences terminal and axillary few-flowered lax racemes, with short gray-pubescence. Bracts and bracteoles minute, caducous. Receptacle obconical-turbinate, 4.0-5.0 mm long, sparsely pubescent on exterior, glabrous within except for deflexed hairs at throat; pedicels 2.5-3.5 mm long. Calyx lobes acute. Petals 5, white, glabrous on margins, deciduous. Stamens 35-40, inserted in half a circle, with a row of short-toothed staminodes opposite them. Ovary densely villous. Style glabrous except at base. Fruit globose, 5.0-6.0 cm diameter; epicarp densely verrucose; mesocarp thick; endocarp fragile, thick, granular.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1972. Chrysobalanaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 9: 1-410.

description: Tree to 30 m tall, the young branches completely glabrous. Leaf lamina elliptic, coriaceous, 9-11.5 × 3.8-5.3 cm, cuneate at base, acuminate at apex, the acumen 10-15 mm long, glabrous on both surfaces; midrib prominulous on both surfaces, glabrous; primary veins 6-8 pairs, almost plane on both surfaces; petioles 10-12 mm long, glabrous, shallowly canaliculate. Stipules not seen. Inflorescences of pendulous panicles on long peduncles up to 75 cm, the rachis and branches glabrous, branches small and numerous. Bracts and bracteoles 0.5-1.5 mm long, acute, glabrous except for the sparsely ciliate margins, subpersistent. Receptacle campanulate, the tube 4-6 mm long when mature, contracted into pedicels 10-15 mm long, glabrous within and without. Calyx lobes five, rounded, unequal, two considerably longer than the other three, sparsely puberulous when young, the margins ciliate, the exterior with two sessile conspicuous glands. Petals five, glabrous, caducous, red. Stamens 16-21, unilateral, with ca. eight tooth-like staminodes opposite to them. Ovary sparsely villous. Style glabrous. Fruit obpyriform, 4.5 cm long, 3.5 cm wide at broadest point which is well below mid-point, exocarp smooth, glabrous; mesocarp thick, hard, fibrous; endocarp thin and bony. Habitat. Forest on terra firme.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1989. Chrysobalanaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 9S: 1-267.

description: Tree to 8.0 m tall or shrub. Leaves ovate-elliptic, 4.0-8.5 cm long, 2.0-3.8 cm broad, short-acuminate at apex, with acumen 1.0-5.0 mm long, rounded to cordate at base, glabrous when young above, densely reddish-brown-pubescent beneath; primary veins 9-12 pairs, prominent beneath; midrib pubescent on both surfaces; petioles 2.0-4.0 mm long, short-pubescent, terete. Stipules linear, 1.0-2.0 mm long, caducous. Inflorescences compact little-branched terminal panicles, the rachis and branches with short brown pubescence. Bracts and bracteoles to 3.0 mm long, ovate, caducous. Receptacle subcylindrical, 8.0-10.0 mm long, with short brown pubescence on exterior, glabrous within except for deflexed hairs at throat; pedicels 3.0 mm long. Calyx lobes rounded. Petals 5, white, sparsely pubescent on exterior, ciliate on margins. Stamens ca 65, inserted in a complete circle, the filaments far exserted. Ovary pilose. Style densely pubescent for two thirds its length. Fruit (in single specimen examined) ellipsoid, 4.0 cm long, 1.8 cm broad; epicarp verrucose; pericarp undifferentiated, hard, thick.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1972. Chrysobalanaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 9: 1-410.

description: Treelet 8-10 m tall, the young branches tomentose. Leaf lamina oblong-lanceolate, coriaceous, 15-26 × 7-9.5 cm broad, subcordate at base, acuminate at apex, the acumen 7-10 mm long, glabrous above, densely gray short-lanate beneath with contrasting brown-tomentose venation; midrib prominulous above, tomentellous when young; primary veins 26-35 pairs, lightly impressed above, prominent and tomentose beneath, anastomosing ca. 3 mm from margin to form a conspicuous marginal vein; secondary veins more or less parallel, prominulous; petioles 5-7 mm long, terete, eglandular, densely tomentose. Stipules linear, membranous, 2-2.5 cm long, persistent. Inflorescences few-flowered racemes, the rachis tomentose. Bracts and bracteoles persistent, 2-3.6 cm long, tomentose on exterior, glabrous within, ovate, acuminate. Flowers 60-75 mm long. Receptacle cylindrical, 3-4 cm long, densely velutinous-tomentellous on exterior, tomentose within to base, sessile. Calyx lobes five, triangular, acute, tomentose on exterior, tomentose within except for glabrous lower portion, 10-13 mm long, petals five, white, glabrous on exterior, the margins ciliate. Stamens ca. 165, inserted around a complete circle, fused at base to form a ring ca. 5 mm tall, the stamens inserted in several rows on exterior of ring, the interior of ring densely tomentose. Ovary inserted near mouth of tube, densely villous. Style sparsely hirsute pubescent on lower third. Fruit not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1989. Chrysobalanaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 9S: 1-267.

description: Shrub or small tree. Leaves oblong, 4.0-10.0 cm long, 1.5-5.0 cm broad, rounded to subcordate at base, rounded to obtuse at apex, glabrous above, densely gray-arachnoid beneath, usually becoming glabrous with age; primary veins 10-15 pairs, rather inconspicuous beneath; midrib prominent beneath, glabrous above except at base; petioles 3.0-5.0 mm long, sparsely pubescent, canaliculate above. Stipules linear, to 1.5 mm long, membraneous, deciduous. Inflorescences terminal and axillary panicles, the rachis and branches with short dense gray pubescence. Bracts and bracteoles 1.5-5.0 mm long, ovate, deciduous. Receptacle 5.0-7.0 mm long, subcampanulate-turbinate, often slightly curved anteriorly, short gray-pubescent on exterior, glabrous within except for deflexed hairs at throat; pedicels slender, 6.0-13.0 mm long. Calyx lobes rounded. Petals 5, white, pubescent, ciliate on margins. Stamens 60-90, inserted in a complete circle, the filaments very far exserted. Ovary pilose. Style pubescent for three fourths its length. Fruit ovoid, with a verrucose epicarp; mesocarp thin; endocarp thin, fragile, granular, sparsely pubescent within.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1972. Chrysobalanaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 9: 1-410.

description: Tree to 25.0 m tall. Leaves oblong-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 10.0-21.0 cm long, 4.0-7.5 cm broad, rounded at base, acuminate at apex, with acumen 4.0-10.0 mm long, glabrous above, densely gray-brown-arachnoid beneath; primary veins 17-25 pairs, prominent beneath; midrib glabrous above; petioles 7.0-9.0 mm long, canaliculate above, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Stipules ca 2.0 mm long, caducous. Inflorescences dense terminal or axillary panicles 4.0-6.o cm long, the rachis and branches densely gray-pubescent. Bracts and bracteoles ovate, to 8.0 mm long, early caducous. Receptacle subcylindrical 5.0-7.0 mm long, longitudinally ridged when dry, with short gray pubescence on exterior, interior lined by dense reflexed hairs to base; pedicels 1.0-3.0 mm long. Calyx lobes rounded, ovate, 3.0-4.0 mm long. Petals 5, white, ciliate on margins. Stamens 22-35, inserted in a semicircle, with a toothed ridge of staminodes opposite them. Ovary villous. Style pubescent almost to apex. Fruit round to oval; epicarp smooth, glabrous; mesocarp thin, fleshy; endocarp granular, fragile, glabrous within.

description: Tree to 20.0 m tall, usually smaller. Leaves ovate-elliptic, 8.0-22.0 cm long, 4.0-9.5 cm broad, subcordate at base, short-acuminate at apex, glabrous above, gray to brown-lanate beneath; primary veins 12-25 pairs, prominent beneath; petioles 8.0-18.0 mm long, sparsely pubescent, shallowly canaliculate. Stipules 1.5-3.5 mm long, subulate, deciduous. Inflorescences terminal panicles with short silver-gray pubescence. Bracts ovate, often exceeding the receptacle tube, enclosing small groups of buds, 7.0-12.0 mm long, persistent. Receptacle subsessile, cylindrical, 7.0-12.5 mm long, densely brown-pubescent on exterior, glabrous within except for deflexed hairs at throat. Calyx lobes acute. Petals 5, white, sparsely ciliate on margins. Stamens 25-40, connate at base of filaments, inserted in an arc of 270°, with a few short filamentous staminodes opposite them. Ovary densely villous. Style pubescent. Fruit globose, 8.0 cm long, 7.0 cm broad; epicarp verrucose or smooth; mesocarp thick and fleshy; endocarp thin and rather fragile, granular, glabrous within.

description: Tree, the young branches puberulous, soon becoming glabrous. Leaf lamina elliptic, chartaceous, 9-16 × 3.5-6.5 cm, rounded to subcuneate at base, apiculate at apex, the acumen 2-8 mm long, glabrous above, with a short appressed-lanate caducous pubescence beneath, midrib prominent on both surfaces, primary veins 12-14 pairs, plane above, prominent beneath, secondary venation prominulous, more or less parallel and 90° to primary veins; petioles 4-7 mm long, tomentellous, becoming glabrous with age, rugulose, canaliculate above, eglandular. Stipules linear-lanceolate, tomentellous, to 6 mm long, caducous. Inflorescences of terminal and axillary little-branched panicles with central rachis and short 2-3 flowered branches, or of racemes, the rachis and branches puberulous. Receptacle cylindrical, 7-8 mm long, sparsely gray-puberulous externally, glabrous within except for deflexed hairs at throat; pedicels ca. 1 mm long. Calyx lobes five, rounded, 2.5 mm long, puberulous externally. Petals five, white, the margins ciliate. Stamens 20-23, unilateral, the arc of the circle opposite to them toothed. Ovary tomentose. Style pubescent on lower portion only. Fruit ovoid, ca. 5 cm long, 4 cm broad; exocarp hard and smooth or crustaceous when dry, glabrous; mesocarp woody, 6-10 mm thick when dry; endocarp thin and bony, glabrous within.

description: Shrub or small tree to 5 m tall, the branches glabrous and lenticellate. Leaves orbicular to ovate-elliptic, 2.0-8.0 cm long, 1.2-6.0 cm broad, retuse or rounded or with a short blunt acumen not exceeding 2.0 mm at apex, subcuneate at base, glabrous on both surfaces; primary veins inconspicuous; petioles 2.0-4.0 mm long. Stipules deciduous, 1.0-3.0 mm long. Inflorescences small terminal and axillary, cymules with gray-brown tomentum. Receptacle cupuliform, tomentose on interior and exterior. Calyx lobes 5, rounded to acute. Petals exceeding calyx lobes, white, glabrous. Stamens 12-26; filaments joined for part of their length in small groups, densely hairy. Ovary pilose. Fruit ovate to obovate, 1.8-5.0 cm long; epicarp smooth with longitudinal ridges; mesocarp thin and fleshy; endocarp thin and hard with smooth, ridged exterior.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1972. Chrysobalanaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 9: 1-410.

description: Arbor usque 20 m alta trunco 10 cm diametro, praeter inflorescentiam glabra; ramuli juvenes canaliculati vel teretes. Petioli 3.0-6.0 mm longi; laminae 4.9-11.0 cm longae, 1.6-3.3 cm latae, lanceolatae usque elliptico-lanceolatae, apice abrupte acuminato vel interdum acuto in foliis parvis, basi acuta angulo incluso 45-70°, attenuata vel abrupte attenuata in petiolo; superficies leviter nitida in sicco; superficies costae mediae canaliculata, pagina inferior rotundata; nervi laterales desuper invisibiles vel obscurissime visibiles, desubter invisibiles vel parum visibiles in sicco. Cryptae stomatatae nullae; epidermis indivisa; hypodermis praesens; sclerides terminales foliariae plerumque stellatae, brachiis brevibus vel interdum nullis. Inflorescentiae 1-2 ad axillas foliorum, singulae 1-7-florae, 6.5-16.7 mm longae secus axes cum internodiis 3-5 ad bases florum; bracteae 0.6-2.0 mm longae, ovato-triangulares usque triangulares, acutae, leviter connato-perfoliatae ad bases, persistentes sub anthesi; flores sessiles, pedicellis 0-0.4 mm longis. Superficies axium inflorescentiae et interdum bractearum et basis ovarii plus minusve minute puberulae. Calyx ovarium inferior includens viridis, 4.0-5.0 mm longus; hypanthium liberum 1.7-2.0 mm longum; lobi calycis 0.9-1.4 mm longi, 1.8-2.2 mm lati, late rotundati et apiculati usque late ovato-triangulares et acuti, 1.6-1.8 mm longi ab staminibus. Petala aurea, 6.0-7.0 mm longa, 2.6-3.0 mm lata, elliptica, acuta, truncata ad basim. Stamina luteola; antherae 3.6-4.8 mm longae; thecae 2.0-2.5 mm longae, rimis apicalibus dehiscentes; glandula 0.4-0.6 mm longa cum centro 2.1-3.1 mm ab apice antherae; cauda 0.8-1.2 mm longa, 1.2-1.5 mm longa ab centro glandulae; filamenta antesepala ca. 4.5-5.0 mm longa, filamenta antepetala ca. 6.0-6.5 mm longa; basis filamenti staminum antepetalorum leviter ad basim petali adhaerens. Ovarium (l-)2-loculare, placentatione centrali libera; ovula omnino 6 vel 7, ad eandem altitudinem affixa; stylus 10-12 mm longus. Fructus ignotus.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1976. Melastomataceae tribe Memecyleae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 15: 1-295.

description: Xylem of lateral veins open above; cells of upper epidermis grouped into blocks, the blocks roughly polygonal, the individual cells 8-21 µ wide, with rounded corners; mucilaginous walls none; cells of the hypodermis 20-51 µ wide, the hypodermis double above the larger veins; crystals occasional in palisade and spongy parenchyma; free stone cells present only near base of petiole; central bodies of the foliar terminal sclereids roundish to rectangular or sometimes rather triangular or irregular, 1-2 times as long as wide, usually with 1-6 short rather blunt lateral arms, these sometimes branched, and with 1-2 vertical arms below and 1-3 above, occasionally the whole sclereid columnar.

description: Arbor parva exilis glabra cortice rubra; ramuli juvenes canaliculata, cito teretes. Petioli 0.8-2.0 mm longi; laminae 11.5-16.8 cm longae, 5.1-6.8 cm latae, ellipticae usque ovato-vel oblongo-ellipticae, ápice abrupte caudato, basi acuta vel acuta et truncata usque subcordata incisura 1.0 mm profunda; superficies costae mediae plana usque leviter canaliculata, pagina inferior prominens, rotundata ad basem, 2-angulata vel peranguste 2-alata ca 1/3 distantiae versus apicem; nervi laterales manifesti obscure in sicco. Cryptae stomatatae 75-155 judiametris, 30-37 µ altae, 15-20 in mm2; sclerides terminales foliariae columnares. Pedunculi 1-flori, 1-3 in quoque later ad nodos aphyllos ramulorum usque 4.0 mm crassorum, plerumque intra zonam foliorum, probabiliter ad axillas aliquando, singuli 0.6-2.0 mm longi cum internodio 1; bracteae 1.5-2.6 mm longae, ovatae vel ovato-triangulares, acutae, persistentes sub anthesi; pedicelli 2.6-4.0 mm longi. Flores tetrameri, viridi-flavi. Calyx ovarium inferior includens 5.0-6.5 mm longus, obconicus; calyx omnino clausus usque ad anthesem, turn ad lineas conjunctionis loborum rumpens; lobi sub anthesi 3.4-3.9 mm longi, 2.8-2.9 mm lati, triangulares, acuti, 3.5-4.0 mm longi ab staminibus; hypanthium liberum 0.5-1.0 mm longum. Petala ignota. Antherae 1.9 mm longae; thecae 1.1 mm longae; glandula 0.7 mm longa cum centro 0.8 mm ab apice antherae; cauda 0.7-1.0 mm longa. Ovarium 3-loculare, placentation axiali-basilari; ovula 3 in quoque loculo. Fructus ignotus.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1976. Melastomataceae tribe Memecyleae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 15: 1-295.

description: Midrib xylem tubular; stomatal crypts a modified Type II, large and shallow, averaging in a leaf ca 115 µ diam, 33 µ high, 17 per sq. mm (extremes given above); upper epidermis mostly one cell thick, occasionally two cells thick in scattered places in the same leaf, mucilaginous walls present in most of the cells, from 1/2-2/3 of the cell depth; hypodermis none; free stone cells scattered along midrib to within ca 2 cm of the tip; terminal sclereids columnar but often slanting, branching near both epidermises, especially the upper.

description: The epithet refers to the anther, which lacks the usual gland. Midrib xylem tubular; stomatal crypts Type I, their extreme dimensions and frequencies given above; upper epidermis one cell thick, all cells with mucilaginous walls 2/3-3/4 the depth of the cell; hypodermis none; palisade cells very short, the layer below the upper epidermis without tannin in sharp contrast to the succeeding layers; free stone cells present only near base of midvein; terminal sclereids rectangular to round to elliptic as seen through the leaf surface, from this view with few rather short and blunt arms or these sometimes of medium length, often also with columnar arms, the central bodies mostly 1-2 times as long as wide, rarely more; crystals occasional in the mesophyll. The single seed is brown, smooth, and shiny but bears a deposit of low irregular bony ridges, apparently from the inner layer of the fruit, making the seed gray-brown and low-rugose until the deposit is scraped off.

description: Arbor glabra 4.5-6.0 m alta; ramuli juvenes 4-alati. Petioli 0.5-2.0 mm longi; laminae 4.3-12.0 cm longae, 1.9-4.0 cm latae, ovato- usque oblongo-ellipticae vel ovatae vel oblongo-ovatae, plerumque angustae, ápice acuminato, basi acuta vel abrupte rotundata et abrupte attenuata in petiolo; superficies costae mediae plana vel leviter elevata, pagina inferior rotundata; nervi laterales manifesti sed inconspicui in sicco. Cryptae stomatatae 50-100 µ diametris, 10-12 µ altae, ca 7-12 in mm2; sclerides terminales foliariae stellatae branchiis brevibus. Flores tetrameri, sessiles vel subsessiles, axillares, solitarii; pedunculi 0-0.5 mm longi, 1-2 paribus bractearum 1.2-2.0 mm longarum triangularium vel ovato-triangularium acutarum; pedicelli 0-0.5 mm longi. Calyx ovarium inferior includens 3.7-5.0 mm longus; hypanthium liberum 1.5-1.8 mm longum; lobi calycis 0.9-1.0 mm longi, 1.1-1.2 mm lati, triangulares, acuti, 1.2-1.5 mm longi ab staminibus; calyx 0.5-0.9 mm findens inter lobos calycis sub anthesi. Pétala immatura 1.2 mm longa, late triangularía, acuta. Antherae 1.5-2.2 mm longae; thecae 1.4-1.8 mm longae, rimis apicalibus dehiscentes; glandula nulla; cauda 0.2-0.4 mm longa. Ovarium 1-loculare, placentatione centrali libera; ovula 5, ad eandem altitudinem affixa. Fructus roseus dives, subglobosus, calyce coronatus, ca 6.8 mm altus calyce excluso et 5.4-5.9 mm diametro in sicco, probabiliter ca 8.5 mm altus et 6.5-7.5 mm diametro in vivo, 1-spermus. Semen 6.0 mm longum, 5.9 mm latum, 5.5 mm crassum, deposito aspero irregulari crustáceo; hilum rotundum, basale, ca 2.1 mm diametro.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1976. Melastomataceae tribe Memecyleae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 15: 1-295.

description: Trees (type specimen from a 10 m tree). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.5-2 mm in diam., initially slightly angular and with ± moderately sparse cover of very short, appressed and a few longer (up to 0.4 mm), p.p. ascending, copper-colored hairs, older twigs roundish, subglabrescent; terminal buds very narrow, ca. 5 mm long and 0.8 mm thick, covered with ± appressed hairs. Petioles 8-18 mm long, 0.9-2 mm thick, roundish and only slightly irregular below, ± flat or shallowly canaliculate above, indument as on twigs. Leaves alternate, oblong-(ob)lanceolate, widest slightly below the middle to 2/3 from the base, 11-18 cm long, 3.7-5.6 cm wide, 3.0-3.3 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base cuneate to acute, margin ± flat, midrib and secondary veins very slightly impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins 5-7 pairs, diverging at 40-60°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed but predominantly scalariform, ± inconspicuous, level above, slightly raised below. Indument consisting of short, ± appressed hairs, only on midrib above, ± sparse from the beginning below, very inconspicuous. Gland dots visible on both sides as raised idioblasts, or above like pinpricks (see p. 14). Inflorescences mostly in the axils of caducous cataphylls at the base of the young growth, but also occasionally in the axil of a leaf, strictly botryoid, 0.4-0.8 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-2 mm diam., 7.5-10 cm long, reaching ca. 2/5-3/4 the length of the closest foliage leaf; peduncle 3-4.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 2/5-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral flowers 3-5 below a terminal cluster of 2-5 flowers, indument consisting of moderately short, appressed to ascending hairs, ± moderately sparse. Pedicels 10-19 mm long but only 0.2-0.3 mm thick. Flowers ca. 9-11.5 mm in diam., tepals elliptic to elongate-obovate, ca. 3-5 mm long and ca. 2-3.5 mm wide, with a ± moderately dense cover of thick, short papillae on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 1.6 mm long including the very short filament, anthers papillose, in the first whorl ± suborbicular with a ± rounded tip, in the second whorl trullate with an acute to parabolic tip, in the third whorl obtrapeziform with a ± truncate tip. Staminodes thickish, papillose, reaching 1/3-1/2 the length of the stamens. Pistil ca. 1.8 mm long, glabrous, ovary ± pear-shaped, style ca. half as long as the ovary. Receptacle broadly urceolate, glabrous inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Trees (type specimen from a 5 m tree). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.4-2.3 mm in diam., slightly angular, soon becoming terete, with ± short hairs (a few almost reaching 0.3 mm), straight, tightly appressed, below terminal bud moderately dense, quickly becoming moderately sparse, then slowly glabrescent; terminal buds (2 seen) elongate, ca. 6 mm long and 1.5- 2 mm thick, densely covered with ± short, tightly appressed hairs. Petioles (5-)6.5-13 mm long, 1.1-1.8 mm thick, ± round below, canaliculate above, indument below ± as on twigs, initially moderately sparse, glabrescent, glabrous above. Leaves alternate, elliptic, widest ± at the middle, (5-)9.5-13 cm long, (2-)4.5-6 cm wide, 1.9-2.6 times longer than wide, tip with a mostly short acumen, base acute to attenuate, or obtuse towards the base and the base itself broadly attenuate, margin flat or very narrowly bent down, at the petiole running to the upper side, midrib and secondary veins ± convex and often slightly impressed above, (slightly) prominent below, secondary veins (5-)6-8 pairs, diverging at 35-55°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-40° to the midrib, tertiary venation mainly ± scalariform but not very regular, level to slightly raised above, raised below. Indument on lower surface consisting of short and a few slightly longer (up to 0.3 mm), appressed hairs, initially moderately sparse, ± slowly subglabrescent, upper surface glabrous from the beginning. Gland dots only discernible in still membraneous leaves. Inflorescences in the axils of leaves on young growth (the lowermost perhaps in the axils of cataphylls?), 0.5-0.9 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-3 mm diam., ca. 4-10 cm long, reaching ca. 1/2-4/5 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 3-5.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/2 to 3/4 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-4 below terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, all of them three-flowered, indument! as on twigs, very sparse to intermediate on peduncle, becoming moderately dense to dense closer to the flowers, but on tepals again much sparser than on receptacle. Pedicels 2.5-4 mm long, 0.4-0.7 mm thick. Flowers ca. 4.5- 6 mm in diam., tepals elliptic, ca. 2.1-2.6 mm long and ca. 1.5-1.8 mm wide, only at the tip somewhat papillose on the inside surface, or almost glabrous. Stamens ca. 1.2-1.4 mm long including a long filament of ca. 0.5-0.6 mm, anthers papillose at the tip, in the two outer whorls ± pentagonal to heptagonal, with a small, obtuse to acute, or often slightly apiculate tip, in the third whorl ± rectangular, slightly emarginate to minutely apiculate at the tip. Staminodes slightly shorter than the filaments of the third whorl, subulate, with a few hairs. Pistil ca. 2 mm long, glabrous, elongate ellipsoid, the thick style reaching ca 2/3 the length of the ovary. Receptacle cup-shaped, small, enclosing only the lower half of the ovary, with very few appressed hairs inside. Fruit unknown (but see below).

description: Tree 25 m tall, the trunk slightly buttressed to 0.5 m, the young branches glabrous.
