description: Trees to 30 m tall. Twigs rimose, glabrous, with vertically oriented lenticels. Bark grayish-brown, with shallow vertical fissures. Leaf blades elliptic to oblong, infrequently narrowly obovate, 10-22 x 6-11 cm, glabrous above, with white papillae below, coriaceous, with 14-18 pairs of lateral veins; apex short acuminate; base obtuse; margins entire; petiole 15-20 mm long, minutely puberulous. Inflorescences racemose, terminal, simple or once-branched, the branches paniculately arranged, the principal rachises 5-10 cm long, with 10-30 flowers, puberulous; pedicels jointed, 1-2 mm long below articulation, the bract and bracteoles caducous. Flowers ca. 6 cm diam.; calyx with six very widely ovate, carinate, green lobes, 5-9 x 5-8 mm, without ducts; petals six, subequal, often asymmetrical, widely oblong, widely elliptic, or widely obovate, 20-30 x 15-20 mm, pale yellow or cream; hood of androecium ca. 16 x 20 mm, yellow, curved inwards, the curved portion thick, the appendages fused, free only at apices, antherless; staminal ring with ca. 190 stamens, the filaments 4-5 mm long, dilated at apex, often geniculate towards apex, the anthers 0.5 mm long; hypanthium puberulous, cuneate at base; ovary (3-)4-locular, with seven ovules in each locule, these basally attached, the summit truncate, the style 4 mm long. description: Small to medium-sized trees, 4-20 m tall. Leaf blades elliptic, 8.5-12.5 x 4-7 cm, glabrous, chartaceous, with 7-10 pairs of lateral veins; apex acuminate; base obtuse; margins serrate; petiole 6-10 mm long, narrowly decurrent. description: Trees, to 35 m tall. Twigs glabrous, smooth, angled, especially below leaf attachment, with vertically oriented lenticels, 4.5-7 mm thick. Leaf blades elliptic or oblong, 16-22 x 6-9.5 cm, glabrous, coriaceous, with 14-18 pairs of lateral veins; apex acute to acuminate; base obtuse; margins entire, slightly revolute, with reddish-brown scars; petiole 12-22 mm long, glabrous, canaliculate. Inflorescences racemose, unbranched, terminal or in axils of uppermost leaves, the rachis 3.5-16 cm long, with 4-15 flowers, glabrous, rimose, angled; pedicels short, ca. 1 mm long, the bract and bracteoles caducous. Flowers 4 cm diam.; calyx with six widely ovate to ovate, green lobes, 9-14 x 6.5-10 mm, ± keeled; with longitudinally oriented mucilagebearing ducts; petals six, the posterior ones larger than others, usually yellow, less frequently cream-colored; hood of androecium, 20 x 15 mm, pale yellow, the appendages antherless, coiled inwards, yellow; staminal ring with 170-260 stamens, the filaments yellow, dilated at apex, 2.83 mm long, the anthers 0.5 mm long; hypanthium glabrous, cuneate at base; ovary 4-locular, with 3-6 ovules in each locule, the ovules inserted on lower part of septum, the summit truncate, the style bent toward anterior end of flower, 5-8 mm long. description: Trees, to 15 m tall, buttressed, with knee-like pneumatophores. Leaf blades elliptic, 13-20 x 6-8 cm, glabrous, without punctae, chartaceous, usually drying a characteristic reddish-brown, with 12-14 pairs of lateral veins, the tertiary veins salient on both sides; apex acute, attenuate, or acuminate; base acute to rounded; margins entire; petiole 10-15 mm long. Inflorescences axillary or infrequently terminal, unbranched, sometimes several clustered in same axil, racemose, the rachis 3-10 cm long, with ferrugineous pubescence, the pedicel rugose, ca. 13 mm long. Flowers 2.5 cm diam.; calyx with six, erect, not imbricate, abaxially carinate, adaxially slightly concave, narrowly ovate, lobes 5-5.5 x 2-2.5 mm; petals widely obovate, 17-22 x 12-19 mm, white; hood of androecium flat, 20 x 15 mm, antherless or with a few vestigial anthers, pink with appendages white; staminal ring with 170 dimorphic stamens, the filaments of outermost thick, curved, ca. 5 mm long, the filaments of innermost slender, nearly straight, 2 mm long, the anthers 1.2 mm long; hypanthium rugose; ovary 4-locular, the summit umbonate, surmounted by long style. Fruits globose, the calycine ring inserted near middle, the infracalycine zone and operculum covered with white dot-like lenticels, the supracalycine zone free of them, the pericarp 2 mm thick; operculum flat, with slight umbo. description: Trees, to 20 m tall. Twigs thick, 6-9 mm diam. below uppermost leaf, rust-colored, rimose, with horizontally oriented scales. Leaf blades narrowly obovate, 35-40 x 15-19 cm, glabrous, with papillate abaxial surface, chartaceous, with 3034 pairs of lateral veins; apex abruptly acuminate; base obtuse; margins entire to minutely crenulate; petiole 12-20 mm long, glabrous, canaliculate. Inflorescences racemose, terminal, the rachis 10-30 cm long, with 3-4 widely spaced flowers, the lower 3/t without flowers, with horizontally elongated lenticels; pedicels jointed, sessile below joint, 5 mm long above joint, with caducous, cucullate bract, 35-50 x 20-25 mm and two caducous, cucullate bracteoles, 15-17 x 10-12 mm, the margins fimbriate. Flowers large, ca. 11 cm diam.; calyx with six very widely oblong to widely ovate pink lobes, 12-14 x 9-11 mm, the margins erose; petals six, widely obovate, white adaxially, pink to red abaxially, 45 x 30 mm; hood of androecium flat, white, the proximal appendages with anthers, the distal appendages antherless; staminal ring with ca. 1000 densely packed stamens, the filaments ca. 3 mm long, not markedly dilated at apex, white, the anthers 1 mm long, yellow; hypanthium glabrous; ovary 4(-5)-locular, each locule with 4-9 ovules attached at base of septum, the summit truncate, the style 7 mm long. Fruits depressed globose, 4.5-7 (without operculum) x 9-11 cm, the base truncate, the pedicle attachment prolonged into woody knob 1 x 2 cm, the calycine ring with persistent, thickened, downwardly oriented sepals, situated near base of fruit, the supracalycine zone erect, the pericarp 10-15 mm thick; operculum slightly convex, umbonate, the umbo ca. 15 mm long. description: Large trees, to 60 m tall, with straight, non-buttressed boles. Twigs glabrous. Bark of young trees with vertical fissures, these not so pronounced in older trees, the outer bark of older trees shedding in rectangular plates. Leaf blades oblong to narrowly oblong, infrequently elliptic, 23- 37 x 11-16 cm, glabrous, coriaceous, with 24- 25 pairs of lateral veins; apex short acuminate to acuminate; base obtuse to rounded; margins entire to crenulate; petiole 9-22 mm long, canaliculate, glabrous. Inflorescences spicate, terminal or in axils of uppermost leaves, unbranched, once-branched, or infrequently 3-branched, the rachises with rust-colored pubescence when young, glabrous with age, each flower subtended by a cucullate ovate bract, 9-10x10 mm and 2 cucullate, keeled, ovate bracteoles, 6-19 x 6-7 mm, with fimbriate margins. Flowers 4-6 cm diam.; calyx with six ovate to widely ovate, keeled, erect, green lobes, 8-15 x 7-12 mm, rounded at apices, imbricate at bases, the margins early fimbriate, later entire; petals six, widely to narrowly obovate, 20-40 x 12-22 mm, yellow; hood of androecium dorsiventrally expanded at apex, yellow, 15-22 x 16-27 mm, the appendages curved inwards at apex, antherless or with vestigial anthers; staminal ring with 299-360 stamens, the filaments 1.2-2 mm long, clavate, the anthers 0.5-0.7 mm long; hypanthium glabrous to puberulous; ovary 4-locular, with 2-7 ovules in each locule, the ovules inserted on floor of locule at juncture with septum, the summit umbonate, not well differentiated from style, the style 1.5-2 mm long. Fruits subglobose, the supracalycine zone erect, the infracalycine zone gradually tapered from calycine ring to base or abruptly constricted directly below calycine ring, 9.5-14.5 x 10-17.5 cm, the exocarp verrucose, dark brown, the pericarp 1.5 2.5 cm thick; opercular opening 8-12.5 cm diam., its rim usually muricate. description: Trees, to 35 m tall, with straight unbuttressed boles, often swollen at base. Twigs inconspicuously puberulous. Bark brown, with vertical fissures, peeling in rectangular plates, the outer bark laminated, the slash reddish yellow, with maroon colored layer between outer and inner barks. Leaf blades narrowly to widely elliptic or narrowly to widely oblong, 6.5-11.5(-2) x 2-6(-9) cm, glabrous, sometimes puberulous on abaxial surface of midrib, chartaceous, or less frequently coriaceous, with 9-14(-16) pairs of lateral veins; apex usually acuminate, sometimes acute or attenuate; base obtuse to less frequently rounded, narrowly decurrent onto petiole; margins entire to crenulate; petiole 6-12 (-15) mm long, puberulous. Inflorescences racemose, terminal, or in axils of uppermost leaves, unbranched or once-branched, when branched the branches paniculately arranged, the rachises 2.5-9 cm long, with up to 20 flowers, usually pubescent; pedicels 3.5-4.5 mm long, subtended by an ovate caducous bract 2.2 x 1.5 mm and with two oblong cucullate bracteoles 3 x 2 mm inserted below middle. Flowers ca. 2.5 cm diam.; calyx with six ovate to widely ovate or widely to very widely oblong, green lobes, 3-6 x 2.5-4 mm, their longitudinally oriented veins often conspicuous, without ducts; petals six, widely oblong to widely obovate, 11-16 x 7-10 mm, usually white, infrequently yellow; hood of androecium, 8-11 x 8-11 mm, white on outside, with antherless, swept inwards, yellow appendages; ligule of androecium, 7-10.5 x 6-9 mm, abruptly tapered from distal to proximal end; staminal ring with 63-125 stamens, the filaments 1.3-2.8 mm long, white or yellow, longer on ligular side of staminal ring, slender, not dilated at apices, the anthers 0.4-0.5 mm long, yellow or orangish; hypanthium puberulous to pubescent, cuneate at base; ovary 4(-5)-locular, with 2-11 ovules in each locule, the ovules inserted at base of septum, the summit truncate, the style 2-3.5 mm long. Fruits turbinate, light brown, 4-5 x 4 cm, the pericarp 5 mm thick, oozing a viscid orangish sap when immature fruits are cut. Seeds reddish-brown, elliptic, ± terete in cross section, 23-26 x 8-20 mm, the raphe splitting into five vascular bundles at chalazal end, these run length of seed and reunite at micropylar end, the bundles salient, with short horizontal extensions along length; aril basal, white, 15-17 x 6 mm.

description: Trees, to 35 m tall, usually unbuttressed. Twigs gray, nearly smooth to slightly rimose, with vertically oriented lenticels, 2-5 mm diam. Bark brown or grayish brown, with poorly developed, vertical fissures, the slash pink or salmon colored. Sapwood yellowish white, the heartwood maroon. Leaf blades oblong, elliptic, or infrequently oblanceolate, 8-25 x 4-10 cm, glabrous except for infrequently puberulous midrib on abaxial surface, chartaceous to coriaceous, with 11-23 pairs of lateral veins; apex acute to obtuse; base acute, obtuse or rounded; margins entire, slightly revolute, with scars left by caducous hairs; petiole 10-25 mm long, glabrous or puberulous. Inflorescences simple racemes or once-branched paniculate arrangements of racemes, terminal or axillary, the principal rachis 4-15(-25) cm long, puberulous; pedicels jointed, 1-3 mm long below joint, 1-5 mm long above joint, rugose, green. Flowers 2.5-3 cm diam.; calyx with six ovate to widely ovate lobes, 2-8 x 2-5 mm; petals six, widely obovate, 11-19 x 8-14 mm, pink, red, violet or purple, often with tinges of white on margins; hood of androecium flat, pink or reddish, dorsiventrally expanded, 10-14 x 6-12 mm, the appendages nearly entirely fused, antherless; ligule sometimes white; staminal ring with 150-190 stamens, the filaments white, not dilated at apex, 1-2 mm long, the anthers on ligular side of ring white, otherwise yellow, ca. 0.5 mm long; hypanthium rugose, puberulous, obtuse or truncate at base; ovary 4-locular, each locule with 4-8 ovules attached on lower part of septum, the summit truncate or convex, the style geniculate or slanted toward anterior end of flower, 3-5 mm long. description: Trees to 35 m tall, unbuttressed. Twigs slender, 1.5-2.5 mm diam. below uppermost leaf, glabrous, often but not always drying black, inconspicuously angled. Bark with shallow vertical fissures, the inner bark bright yellow. Leaves deciduous, flushed just before flowers appear; leaf blades narrowly elliptic to elliptic or infrequently oblong, 13-26 x 5-10 cm, glabrous, with glaucous abaxial surface, usually with rugose papillae as seen with SEM, chartaceous during flowering period, more coriaceous with maturity, with 19-26 pairs of lateral veins; apex acuminate; base obtuse, narrowly decurrent onto petiole; margins crenulate, with scars left by caducous hairs; petiole 8-13 mm long, glabrous, canaliculate. Inflorescences racemose, terminal or in axils of uppermost leaves, the rachis 12-20 cm long, with 2-7 widely spaced flowers, the lower ½ without flowers, glabrous, with conspicuous horizontally elongated lenticels; pedicels jointed, sessile below joint, 4-6 mm long above joint, the bract and bracteoles caducous, not seen. Flowers large, ca. 11 cm diam.; calyx with six very widely ovate to ovate green lobes, 10-14 x 6-11 mm, the margins erose; petals six, very widely ovate, the margins coiled under at anthesis, white, greenish white, or green, 40 x 35 mm; hood of androecium flat, white, the proximal appendages white with dark yellow anthers, the distal appendages antherless, white; staminal ring with ca. 1000 densely packed stamens, the filaments 3.5-4 mm long, white, not dilated at apex, the anthers ca. 1 mm long, yellow; hypanthium glabrous, cuneate at base, sometimes sulcate; ovary (3-) 4(-5)-locular, each locule with 14-28 ovules. description: Large trees, to 50 m tall, with or without buttresses. Twigs glabrous or puberulous when young. description: Tree to 15 m tall, the young branches glabrous. Receptacle conical with a circular accrescent calyx, crenate margin, glabrous. Pseudo-corolla (outer row of staminodes) a single united radiate unit with 24-28 conspicuous veins from center to margin, the margins ciliate, colored yellow. Stamens numerous with thin free filaments to 7 mm long, arranged in several rows around the interior rim of the pseudo-corolla; anthers small. Style to 5 mm long, glabrous. Fruit to 2 cm long, the persistent calyx expanding and forming a circular rim around the fruit, smooth below rim, deeply costate above rim, the costae coming to a pointed apex. The single seed obconical-pyriform with swollen base and pointed apex filling the interior of the loculus, the other loculi abort and are not apparent in the mature fruit.

description: Rhizomes present; erect stems terete, without spots, to 135 cm long. Leaves both submersed and floating, petiolate, ± spirally arranged; submersed leaves coarse, dark green, the blades entire, noncrisped, elliptic, nonarcuate, 15-21-veined, 11.5-14 x 2.5-3.5 cm, lacunae absent each side of midrib, the apex noncucullate, acute, the base attentuate, often decurrent on petiole, the petiole flattened, 0.5-2.5 cm long, the ligules inconspicuous, free from blade, light green, nonfibrous, not shredding at tip, persistent, convolute, 4.8-6.4 cm, apex acute; floating leaves dark green above, the blades ovate, 21-23-veined, 5-6.5 x 2.5-3 cm, the apex acuminate, the base cordate, the petiole continuous in color to apex, 1.5-13 cm long. Turions absent. Inflorescences unbranched; peduncles all similar, cylindric, terminal or axillary, erect, 5-15.5 cm long; spikes similar, cylindric, 2.5-2.8 cm long. Fruits sessile, obovate, compressed, pale green, abaxially keeled, without lateral keels or ridges, 3.8-4.2 x 2.6-2.9 mm; beak erect, ventral, ca. 0.2 mm long; sides without basal tubercles; embryo with less than one spiral.

description: Shrub 0.4-1 m tall, young shoots puberulous. Leaf blade narrowly elliptic to narrowly oblanceolate, 15-20 x 3.5-5 cm, subcoriaceous, ca. 0.2 mm thick, glabrous, base attenuate, apex narrowly acuminate or acute, margins entire with a rather conspicuous, pallid border, lateral veins rather inconspicuous, surfaces between veinlets smooth or very sparsely striate above; extraxylary sclerenchyma sparsely present adaxially as laterally compressed bundles of 2-6 cells, hypoderm lacking; petiole 1.5-2.5 cm long, 1-1.5 mm thick, puberulous at base. Racemes in bisexual plants to 7 cm long with 8-12 flowers, plants with male or female flowers not seen; rachis ca. 0.4 mm thick, puberulous; pedicels 1-1.5 mm long; bracts 0.5-0.7 mm long, inserted at nodes. Flowers 5-merous; calyx lobes 1.5 x 1.7-2 mm, glabrous; corolla orange, tube 1.5 mm long, lobes 2.7 x 2.7-3 mm. Stamen filaments glabrous, fused into a tube 1 mm long. Pistil narrowly ovoid, 1-1.5 mm long; stigma punctate; ovules 1-3. Fruits not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Ståhl, Bertil. 2010. Theophrastaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 105: 1-160.

description: Shrub or treelet to 4 m tall, young shoots puberulous, often sparsely so. Leaf blade oblanceolate, 50-86 x 12-21 cm, coriaceous, 0.15-0.2 mm thick, glabrous, base attenuate, apex short-acuminate or acute, rarely obtuse, margins serrate with 50-65 teeth per side, rarely subentire, lateral veins rather conspicuous, prominulous beneath, surfaces between veinlets striate; extraxylary sclerenchyma adjacent to epidermis on both sides, abaxially arranged in bundles 5-15 cells thick, adaxially in bundles 2-8(-10) cells thick, empty hypodermal cells sometimes present adaxially, but without forming a continuous layer; petiole 5-15(-20) cm long, 4-5 mm thick, glabrous throughout or puberulous at base. Racemes in male plants to 27 cm long with up to 40 flowers, in female plants to 2.5 cm long with 6-10 flowers, plants with bisexual flowers not seen; rachis 1.5-2.5 mm thick, puberulous; pedicels 2-3 mm long; bracts 1.2 mm long, inserted at nodes. Flowers 5-merous; calyx lobes very broadly ovate, 2 x 2-2.5 mm, glabrous; corolla orange, tube 3 mm long, lobes 3.5-4 x 4 mm. Stamen filaments glabrous, in male flowers fused into a tube 1-1.2 mm long, in female flowers united at base only, free parts ca. 0.5 mm long. Pistil in male flowers sublinear, lacking ovules, in female flowers broadly ovoid with 10-12 ovules in 2 rows; stigma in female flowers truncate. Fruits orange, to 3.5 cm diam., pericarp ca. 0.5 mm thick, surface papillose; seeds 3-8, 8-12 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Ståhl, Bertil. 2010. Theophrastaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 105: 1-160.

description: Stems 6-20 cm high, 0.3-1.5 mm wide. Rhizomes short. Roots many, to 7 cm long, glabrous to sparsely hairy. Leaves absent. Bracts triangular, 1.5-4 mm long. Pedicels 2-20 mm long, erect or ascending. Inflorescence ca. 5 cm long, flowers 1-3. Staminate flowers with a basal connate basal part of 2-2.5 mm long. Tepals three, deltate to shallowly triangular, 3-4 mm long, 3.5-6 mm wide, upper side near base keeled to winged, margins revolute, ciliate, tails 5-54 mm long. Androphore deltoid, fleshy, broadly winged, 3-4 mm long and wide, stamens implanted in basal slits at the base of the androphore. Tepals of the pistillate flowers approximately similar to those of the staminate flowers. Ovaries ellipsoid to obovoid, 0.5-0.7 x 0.3 mm, glabrous. Style glabrous, 0.4-0.5 mm long. Achenes unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Maas, Paulus J. M. & Rübsamen, T. 1986. Triuridaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 40: 1-55.

description: Stems white, 8-20 cm high, 0.9-1.5 cm diam., with slightly prominent ribs. Rhizomes cylindrical, to 10 mm long. Roots numerous, terete, 1-15 cm long, 0.4-0.7 mm diam., glabrous to sparsely hairy (hairs ca. 0.2 mm long). Leaves absent. Inflorescence 1-2(-5) cm long, flowers 1-3(-5). Bracts brownish (in herbarium material), membranous, quickly withering, triangular, 2.5-4 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide. Pedicels white, erect, 5-15(-20) mm long. Staminate flowers with a connate basal part of 1-1.2 mm long. Tepals three, white to creamy, triangular to deltate, 3.5-4.5 mm long, 2.5-3 mm (to 5 mm at the base) wide (when spread out), margins strongly revolute and the tepals as seen from above, only 0.8-1 mm wide, apex with a tail-like appendage of 20-30 mm long, tepals as well as tails patent or directed downwards. Androphore white to creamy, soon turning brownish, fleshy, conical to deltoid, 2.6-3 x 1.8-2.3 mm; stamens attached to the base of the androphore, sessile, anthers 0.5-0.6 x 0.4-0.5 mm, thecae widely separate. Tepals of the pistillate flowers approximately similar to those of the staminate flowers. Ovaries brownish, oblong-obovoid, 0.5-0.7 x 0.2-0.3 mm, glabrous, crowned by the style. Style regularly to obliquely deltoid, to 0.1 mm long. Achenes oblong-obovoid, shortly apiculate by the style, 0.8-1 x 0.3-0.4 mm, glabrous. Seeds ellipsoid, 0.4-0.5 x 0.2-0.3 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Maas, Paulus J. M. & Rübsamen, T. 1986. Triuridaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 40: 1-55.

description: Lianas; adquirindo cor avermelhada quando secas, quase totalmente glabras, tricomas raros esparsos nas axilas dos ramos das inflorescências, não ramificados; ramos cilíndricos, estriados. Gavinhas não vistas. Folhas trifolioladas; pecíolos 5,8-5,9 cm compr., canaliculados; estípulas intactas não vistas, persistentes na parte basal; peciólulos centrais 11-16 mm compr., laterais 8-10 mm compr., canaliculados; lâminas dos folíolos centrais 11,5-13,2 x 4,7-6,1 cm, laterais 7,4-9,3 x 2,7-4,6 cm, elípticas, truladas, subelípticas, ou sub-ovais, ápice agudo, margem denticulada, base cuneada ou atenuada, nervuras marrom-escuras na face abaxial, papiráceas, folíolos laterais desiguais em tamanho na mesma folha. Inflorescências 12,1-15 cm compr. x 7,3-9,3 cm larg., umbeliformes, de ápice aplanado; pedúnculos 6,3-7,5 cm compr., verdes; brácteas 0,51 mm compr., deltoides, glabras; pedicelos 2,5-3 mm compr., verde-amarelados; botões conoidais; cálice 1-1,5 mm compr. x 2-2,5 mm diâm., verde-amarelado, carnoso, truncado, base truncada e irregularmente lobada; corola em botão 1 mm compr. x 1,5-2 mm diâm.; pétalas verde-amareladas, papilosas; anteras extrorsas, conectivo triangular, giboso, granuloso, seco marrom-escuro; disco de ápice côncavo; estilete cilíndrico, estigma pontual. Fruto e semente não vistos.
bibliographicCitation: Lombardi, Julio A. 2000. Vitaceae: Géneros Ampelocissus, Ampelopsis e Cissus.. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 80: 1-250.

description: Arbor usque ad 8 m alta. Rami ex coll, cortice brunneo squamoso. Folia oblonga, iis C. rubricaulis similia, apice breviter acuminata, ipso apice subacuta, basi late attenuata usque subrotundata, saepius paullo inaequilatera, in sicco brunnea, semper supra lucidula, subtus opaca, in vivo supra viridia, subtus pallidiora, firme chartacea vel subcoriacea, flexilia, laevia, minutissime vel haud tuberculata, margine vix revoluta, 8-12 x 2.5-3.5 cm, costa supra fere plana, subtus parum ele-vata, nervis lateralibus 5-6-paribus arcuatis supra vix, subtus parum elevatis, reticulo venarum subtus tantum leviter prominulo, illo venularum subinconspi-cuo; petioli 4-6 mm longi, ca. 1 mm crassi. Flores desunt. Fructus maturus pyriformi-obovoideus, 2.5-3 cm longus, 1.7-2.1 cm diam., disco accrescente 0.3 mm crasso camoso-coriaceo in vivo rubescenti-lutescente per ¾-4/5 long, obtectus, apice ipso drupae rotundato 3-5 mm alto a disco liber ibidem in vivo viridis, in sicco lutescens denseque minute tuberculatus, basi calyce late cupuliformi undulata 2-3 mm alto et 3-4 mm diam. instructus, ultro ad calycis basem prophyllo annulari crenulato vix 1 mm alto praeditus; pedunculus 2-3 mm longus, ca. 2 mm crassus.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Frutex volubilis vel liana. Rami teretes, appresso-sericei, demum glabrati. Stip-ulae minutae, usque 0.5 mm longae, triangulares, sericeae. Folia opposita, lamina 4.7-14.0 cm longa, 2.5-8.3 cm lata, late elliptica vel ovata, basi obtusa et parum asymmetrica, apice apiculata caudatave, margine plana, subtus in nervis late-ralibus 2-4(-8) glandes stipitatas gerenti, supra sparsim appresso-sericea vel glabrata, subtus dense candida appresso-sericea vel glabrata, pilis T-formibus, pede 0.04-0.09 mm longo, trabecula 0.9-2.0 mm longa, venis venulisque supra parum prominentibus et subtus prominentibus, petiolo 10-25 mm longo, appresso-seri-ceo, apice 2 glandes stipitatas gerenti. Inflorescentia floribus in umbellis 4-floriferis fasciculatis, umbellis in cymis dispositis, appresso-sericea; bracteis brac-teolisque 1.6-2.5 mm longis, lanceolatis, abaxialiter appresso-sericeis, adaxialiter glabris, per vel post anthesin caducis; pedunculis 0-2 mm longis, pedicellis (8-) 12-17 mm longis, 0.9-1.2 mm diametro, 0.6-0.8 mm sine indumento, appresso-sericeis. Sepala 5, abaxialiter sericea, adaxialiter omnino minute tomentosa, oblonga, apice rotunda et interdum revoluta; sepalum anticum 4.5-5.0 mm lon-gum, 2.0-2.5 mm latum, 4 lateralia 4.5-5.8 mm longa, 2.5-2.8 mm lata, glandes 2.0-3.0 mm longas et 0.8-1.4 mm latas gerentia et 2.5-3.0 mm superantia. Petala 5, rosea, aetate albicantia, fimbriata, 4 lateralia inter sepala patentia, ungue 1.0-2.5 mm longo, 0.4-0.5 mm lato, limbo 7.5-11.0 mm longo, 7.0-10.5 mm lato, orbiculari, eglanduloso, 2 anterioribus quam 2 posterioribus concavioribus; petalum posticum ungue erecto 3.5-4.2 mm longo, usque 1.4 mm diametro, apice constricta, limbo 7.0-9.0 mm longo, 6.0-8.0 mm lata, oblongo, retroflexo, piano convexove, fimbriis basalibus dilatatis glandulosisque. Stamina 10, filamentis 2.0-5.0 mm longis, proximaliter connatis et inter stylos posticos inflexis; antherae loculis 0.8-1.6 mm longis, sparsim pilosis, interdum solum basi et apice, connec-tivis canarinis, petalis oppositis 0.6-1.4 mm longis, 0.4-1.0 mm latis, 0.1-0.7 mm profundis, solum 2 petalis anterioribus oppositis glandulosis, illis sepalis oppositis 0.6-2.2 mm longis, 0.4-1.6 mm latis, 0.3-1.2 mm profundis, omnibus glandulosis, solum 3 sepalis anterioribus oppositis multum dilatatis, loculis 2 sepalis antero-lateralibus 0.2-1.4 mm supra superantibus. Ovarium 1.0-1.4 mm altum carpellis 3, uniovulatis, liberis, toro pyramidali adnatis, candido-sericeis; styli 3, stylo antico rectum, 2.8-4.0 mm longo, 0.4 mm lato, stylis posticis 3.5-5.0 mm longis, divergentibus, basi lyratis, stigmatibus capitatis. Fructus ex 3 samaris (vel abortu 1-2) constans; samara carpophoro usque 3.5 mm longo, 0.8-1.0 mm lato, nuce ovoidea 7-10 mm alta, 6-8 mm longa, appresso-pubescenti, viridi, tuberculata vel manifeste alulata, alulis usque 6 mm altis, ala 19-33 mm longa, 8-15 mm lata, oblonga obovatave, viridi, appresso-sericea, pilis sessilibus T-formibus, trabecula recta gracilis 0.4-0.5 mm longa, alis posterioribus parum parallelis ad alam ante-riorem, loculis interius glabris.

description: Stems simple, or basally branched (rarely branched in the upper part), pinkish to purplish, 9-30 cm high, 0.5-1 mm diam. Rhizomes long-creeping, 0.5-1 mm diam. Roots to 2 cm long and 0.3 mm thick, densely covered with white, patent hairs (to 0.5 mm long). Leaves 3-8, narrowly triangular, 3-4 mm long, apex acuminate, base slightly saccate, apical margins slightly papillate. Inflorescence an all-sided raceme 2-7(-10) cm long, 1.0-2(-2.5) cm wide, flowers 15-50. Bracts narrowly triangular, 2-3 mm long, base slightly saccate, apex brownish, slightly papillate. Pedicels mostly slightly ascending, 4-10 mm long, fruiting heads often deflexed at maturity. Flowers unisexual, monoecious, white, fragrant, the lower 4-9 pistillate, the upper 10-50 staminate. Staminate flowers 3-4 mm diam., with a connate basal part of 0.2-0.6 mm long. Tepals 4-6, narrowly ovate, soon partly reflexed, 1-1.5 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm wide, margins densely papillate, particularly towards the apex. Stamens 2-3, filaments 0.3-0.5 mm long, 0.2-0.7 mm wide, anthers 0.4 x 0.7-1.0 mm. Pistillate flowers 3-4 mm diam., with a connate basal part of ca. 0.2 mm long. Tepals 4-6, triangular, soon partly reflexed, 1.2-2 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, margins, particularly towards the apex, densely papillate. Ovaries 30-40, obovoid, 0.6 x 0.4 mm, basally glabrous, apically papillate. Style far exceeding the ovary, 0.9-1.2 mm long, stigmatic part densely penicillate-papillate. Follicles obovoid, 1.2-1.7 x 0.6-0.8 mm, upper part papillate, longitudinally dehiscent. Seeds more or less ellipsoid, 1.2-1.4 x 0.5-0.6 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Maas, Paulus J. M. & Rübsamen, T. 1986. Triuridaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 40: 1-55.

description: Stems unbranched, purplish, 10-30 cm high, 0.5-2.5 mm diam. Rhizomes long-creeping, ca. 1 mm diam. Roots to 9 cm long, 0.7-0.8 mm diam., densely covered with white, patent hairs (0.5-1.5 mm long). Leaves 4-8, narrowly ovate, 2.5-4 mm long, obtuse, slightly saccate at the base. Inflorescence a corymb-like raceme 0.5-2(-3.5) cm long, (1-) 1.5-2.5 cm wide, flowers 7-15. Bracts narrowly obovate, 3-8 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide, apex often mucronate, apical margins sometimes slightly brownish-dotted. Pedicels 5-12 mm long, patent or ascending when young, becoming strongly deflexed in older stages. Flowers whitish outside, inner side purplish, unisexual, monoecious, the lower 2-5 pistillate, the upper 210 staminate. Staminate flowers ca. 5 mm diam., with a tubular connate basal part of 0.5 mm long. Tepals six, narrowly triangular, patent to partly reflexed, 1.8-2 mm long, 0.8-0.9 mm wide, inner side densely papillate when young, becoming glabrous with age. Stamens three, filaments ca. 0.5 mm long, anthers (3?-)4-locular, ca. 1 mm long. Pistillate flowers ca. 8 mm diam., with a connate basal part of 0.5-0.6 mm long. Tepals six, narrowly ovate-triangular, patent to partly reflexed, 1.8-3.5 mm long, 0.9-1 mm wide, acute to rounded, inner side densely papillate when young, becoming glabrous with age. Ovaries ca. 50, broadly obovoid, 0.4-0.5 x 0.3-0.4 mm, densely papillate throughout. Style equalling the ovary, 0.3-0.5 mm long, stigma obdeltoid, ca. 0.1 mm long, densely papillate. Follicles obovoid, 2-2.7 x 1.4-1.5 mm, sparsely papillate to glabrous, dehiscing with two valves. Seeds obovoid, 1.8-2.5 x 0.8-1.2 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Maas, Paulus J. M. & Rübsamen, T. 1986. Triuridaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 40: 1-55.

description: Stems unbranched, reddish, 5-10 cm high, 1.2 mm diam. Rhizomes short, vertical, to ca. 1 mm diam. Roots filiform, to 12 cm long and ca. 0.5 mm diam., densely covered with patent, white hairs (to 1 mm long). Leaves 10-15(-36), narrowly triangular, 3.5-5 mm long, saccate at the base. Inflorescence an all-sided raceme 1.7-2.5 cm long, 0.5-0.7 cm wide, flowers 10-17. Bracts narrowly triangular, implanted at the top of the pedicel, to 5 mm long, striped dark brownish, saccate at the base, inflexed over the bud. Pedicels 0.5-1 mm long, more or less patent. Flowers bisexual, red, 5-6 mm diam., with a connate basal part of ca. 0.5 mm long. Tepals four, deltate(-ovate), horizontally patent, 1.7-2.2 mm long. 1.71.8 mm wide, with an irregular pattern of brownish and white longitudinal lines (easily observed in alcohol-preserved material), glabrous, outer side somewhat papillate. Stamens two, filaments 0.8 mm long, 0.2 mm wide, anther 0.3-0.5 mm long. Ovaries 10-25, obovoid to broadly obovoid, 0.3-0.5 mm long, 0.4 mm wide, densely covered with brownish papillae placed in longitudinal rows. Style 0.4-0.5 mm long, glabrous, stigma not distinct. Follicles obovoid, 1.0-1.6 x 0.51 mm, densely papillate, only towards the apex, dehiscing longitudinally with two valves. Seeds pale brown, ovoid, 1.2-1.4 x 0.6-0.8 mm.

description: Stems simple or basally branched, reddish, 9-25 cm high, 0.5-1 mm diam. Rhizomes long-creeping, 0.7-1 mm diam. Roots coral-shaped, glabrous, to 1 mm diam. Leaves 1-4, partly or completely amplexicaul, broadly ovate, 2-3.5 mm long. Inflorescence an all-sided raceme 4-17 cm long, 0.4-0.8 cm wide, flowers 10-60. Bracts ovate-triangular, 1.5-2 mm long, the younger and lower ones most often partly or completely amplexicaul, sometimes brownish punctate. Pedicels 1-4 mm long, very soon reflexed. Flowers bisexual, dark red, 1-2.5 mm diam., with a connate basal part of 0.4 mm long. Tepals six, triangular to ovate or deltate, soon reflexed, 0.9-1.8 mm long, 0.6-1 mm wide, inner side slightly papillose, apical part densely bearded with reddish, curly hairs (to 10 mm long). Stamens six, sessile, anthers 0.4-0.5 mm long. Ovaries 10-25, obovoid to broadly obovoid, ca. 0.8-0.9 mm long, 0.5-0.6 mm wide, slightly papillate throughout. Style ca. 0.2 mm long, glabrous; stigmatic zone elongate, 0.2-0.3 mm long, densely papillate, distinctly exceeding the ovary. Follicles (broadly) obovoid, 1-1.1 x 0.70.9 mm, glabrous. Seeds obovoid, dark brown, ca. 0.8 x 0.5 mm.

description: Stems simple or basally branched, purplish, 8-20 cm high, 0.7-1.5 mm diam. Rhizomes long-creeping, 0.5-1 mm diam. Roots up to 15 cm long, 0.4-0.6 mm diam., densely covered with white, patent hairs (to 1.5 mm long). Leaves 3-7, triangular-ovate, 2.5-4 mm long, the lower ones broadly ovate-deltate, 1-2.5 mm long. Inflorescence a one- to all-sided raceme 1.5-10 cm long, 1-2.5 cm wide, flowers ca. 20. Bracts triangular-ovate, 2.5-4.5 mm long, apex acute, becoming obtuse in age. Pedicels ascending or reflexed in fruit, (2-)5-15(-18) mm long. Flowers unisexual, monoecious, the lower 3-5 pistillate, the ca. 15 upper ones staminate; tepals ending in a 1-2 mm long tail-like and apically bearded appendage. Staminate flowers 4-6 mm diam. (excluding tails), with a connate basal part of 0.3-0.5 mm long. Tepals (5-)6, narrowly triangular, horizontally patent, 1.4-3 mm long, 0.5-1.3 mm wide, inner side densely papillate. Stamens three, sessile, anthers 0.3-0.6 x 0.7-1 mm. Pistillate flowers ca. 5 mm diam. (excluding tails), with a connate basal part of 0.3-0.5 mm long. Tepals six, soon reflexed, narrowly triangular, 2-4.5 mm long, 0.5-1.5 mm wide. Ovaries (15-)50-80, obovoid, 0.7-0.9 x 0.4-0.6 mm, apical part densely papillate, brownish, basal part glabrous, yellowish. Style 0.2-0.4 mm long, glabrous, shorter than the ovary, or slightly longer in Hoehne s.n. (SP 24245); stigma obconical, 0.1-0.2 mm long, densely papillate. Follicles narrowly obovoid to obovoid, 1.7-2 x 0.9 mm, slightly papillate towards the apex, dorso-ventrally dehiscing from apex to base. Seeds obovoid, 1.2-1.7 x 0.7-0.8 mm, dorsally hyaline, ventrally brownish.

description: Stems simple, or in the upper part often repeatedly branched, 30-140 cm high, 1-4 mm diam., red to purplish, longitudinally grooved (when dry). Rhizomes almost vertical, 1.5-4(-5) mm diam. Roots to 5 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm diam., glabrous. Leaves 6-15, triangular, 2-7 mm long. Inflorescence a terminal raceme (sometimes branched at the base) 5-25 cm long, 1.5-3 cm wide, flowers 20-50. Bracts narrowly triangular to triangular, 2-7 mm long. Pedicels purplish, (6-) 13— 25(-40) mm long, ascending to patent, sometimes apically reflexed. Flowers unisexual, monoecious, purplish, the lower 3-34 flowers pistillate, the upper 2-32 staminate. Staminate flowers 3-5 mm diam., with a connate basal part of 0.5 mm long. Tepals six, narrowly triangular, soon completely reflexed, 1.7-2.3 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, inner side densely papillate, apical part densely bearded with hair-tufts (hairs 1-2 mm long) when young. Stamens three, inserted at the apex of a 0.7-1 mm long and 0.7-0.8 mm wide, rather densely papillate, cylindric androphore. Pistillate flowers 3-5 mm diam., with a connate basal part of 0.3 mm long. Tepals six, narrowly triangular, soon completely reflexed, 2.5-4 mm long, 0.5-1.2 mm wide, inner side densely papillate, apical part of young tepals densely bearded with hair-tufts (hairs ca. 1 mm long). Ovaries oo, obovoid, 0.50.8 x 0.3-0.6 mm, ventrally incurved, papillate at the apex. Style about equalling the ovary, 0.3 mm long, glabrous or slightly papillate; stigma elongate or irregularly obdeltoid, 0.1-0.2 mm long and wide, densely papillate. Fruiting heads 5-10 mm diam., brown to purplish, receptacle globose, to 2.5 mm diam. Follicles obovoid, brown to purplish, 1.9-3 x 0.7-1.2 mm, papillate towards the apex, its base sunken in the receptacle. Seeds blackish, more or less bean-shaped, (1.5-) 1.8- 2.4 x 0.6-0.9 mm, very finely longitudinally striate. After dehiscence of the fruit all seeds remain long attached to the fruit.

description: Stems white, 8-30 cm high, to 1 mm diam. Rhizomes long-creeping, 0.5-1.2 mm diam. Roots up to 10 cm long, 0.5-0.6 mm diam., densely covered with white, patent hairs (0.5-1.5 mm long). Leaves 4-10, narrowly triangular, 2-4 mm long, base slightly saccate, apex acute, sometimes acuminate. Inflorescence a raceme 3.5-12 cm long, 0.5-1 cm wide, flowers 10-50. Bracts narrowly triangular, 2-3.5 mm long, densely covered with brownish stripes and points, somewhat saccate at the base. Pedicels horizontally patent, about equalling the bracts, 1-4 mm long. Flowers cream-colored, fragrant (Raynal-Roques 19788), the lower 37 pistillate, the upper 7-43 staminate. Staminate flowers 3-4.5 mm diam., with a connate basal part of ca. 0.4 mm long. Tepals four, broadly ovate-deltate, 1-veined, horizontally patent, 1.3-1.5 mm long, 1.0-1.3 mm wide, inner side and margins slightly papillate, margins revolute (in older flowers). Stamens 2(-3), filaments very short, 0.1-0.2 mm long, 0.4 mm thick, anthers 2-locular, 0.6-0.7 x 0.4 mm. Pistillate flowers 4-5.5 mm diam., with a connate basal part of ca. 0.5 mm long. Tepals four, broadly ovate-deltate, 1-veined, horizontally patent, slightly reflexed in fruit, 1.7-2 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, inner side and margins slightly papillate. Ovaries 25-40, broadly obovoid, 0.4-0.5 mm long, strongly papillate throughout. Style ca. 0.2 mm long, glabrous; stigmatic part 0.1-0.2 mm long, densely penicillate-papillate, not exceeding the ovary. Achenes obovoid, 1.3-1.5 x 0.8-1 mm, densely papillate throughout, wall to 0.2 mm thick. Seeds globose to obovoid, 0.7-1.0 x 0.5-0.7 mm, dark brown with a ventral pale brown line and a pale brown rounded tip.

description: Stems unbranched, 16-17 cm high, 0.1-0.5 mm diam. Rhizomes and roots not seen. Leaves 1-5, to 1.5 mm long. description: Stems unbranched, white (?), 15-25 cm high, 0.5-1 mm diam. Rhizomes long-creeping, to 1 mm diam. description: Terrestrial shrubs, scandent, prostrate and decumbent, or erect, 0.5–3 m tall. description: Stems yellowish to brownish yellow, 3-11 cm high, 0.5-1 mm wide. Rhizomes weakly developed, more or less vertical. Roots many, to 2 cm long. Leaves 0-2, ovate-triangular, ca. 2 mm long. Inflorescence a raceme, in most specimens arising from near the base of the plant, flowers 6-10. Bracts ovate-triangular to broadly ovate-triangular, 1.5-2.5 mm long. Pedicels 5-15 mm long, ascending or apically slightly reflexed. Staminate flowers yellowish white, 4-6 mm diam. (including tails 8-15 mm), basal connate part 0.7-1.2 mm long. Tepals (three) or six, deltate to triangular, glabrous (?), 1.2-2.0 mm long, 0.9-1.5 mm wide, with an apical tail 1-5 mm long. Stamens three, united into a very small androphore, anthers, 0.40.7 x 0.3 mm, filaments 0.2-0.3 mm long. Pistillate flowers yellowish white, (3.5-)5 mm diam. (including tails 7-9 mm), basal, tubular part 0.6-1.0 mm long. Tepals 6(-8), deltate, 1.3-1.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, caudate like the staminate flowers. Ovaries obovoid, 0.6-0.7 x 0.3-0.4 mm, apex rather densely papillate. Style far exceeding the ovary, 1-1.2 mm long, without distinct stigmatic zone. Achenes obovoid, 0.7-0.8 x 0.3 mm, far exceeded by the style-remnant (0.5-0.8 mm), apical part spongy, hyaline, middle part brownish, basal part hyaline. Seeds ellipsoid, very pale brown, 0.4-0.5 x 0.3 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Maas, Paulus J. M. & Rübsamen, T. 1986. Triuridaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 40: 1-55.

description: Rhizomes present; erect stems terete, without spots, to 40 cm x 0.5-1 mm. Leaves both submersed and floating or floating leaves absent, ± spirally arranged; submersed leaves sessile, lax, entire, noncrisped, light to dark green, linear, often arcuate, 1-veined, 1.1-3 cm x 0.6-1 mm, the lacunae 5-6 rows each side of midrib, the apex acute, the base not clasping, without basal lobes, glands absent; ligules inconspicuous, adnate to blade ca. 1/2 of ligule length, dark green, nonfibrous, not shredding at tip, persistent to deliquescent, convolute, 2.1-3.2 mm long, the apex obtuse; floating leaves petiolate, yellow-green to dark green, the blades oval to elliptic, 7—11-veined, 1.9-2.3 x 0.5-1.2 cm, the apex round to round-acute, the base cuneate to rounded; petiole continuous in color to apex, 0.6-1.7 cm x 0.7-1 mm. Turions absent. Inflorescences unbranched; peduncles dimorphic, the submersed clavate, ca. 2 x ca. 0.6 mm, the emersed cylindric, 0.7-1.6 cm long. Fruits sessile, circular, compressed, greenish brown, abaxially and laterally winged, 1.2-1.5 x 1.1-1.5 mm, the lateral wings without sharp points, the beak erect, ca. 0.1 mm long, the sides without basal tubercles; embryo with more than one full spiral.
bibliographicCitation: Haynes, Robert R. & Holm-Nielsen, Lauritz B. 2003. Potamogetonaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 85: 1-52.

description: Dioecious or monoecious trees up to 25 m tall. Leafy twigs 2.5-6.5 mm thick, yellow tomentose. Leaves oblong to lanceolate, broadest near the upper end, hardly inequilateral, 6-25 cm long, 3-12.5 cm broad, subcoriaceous, acuminate, obtuse or emarginate at the base, denticulate to dentate towards the apex; except for the tomentose costa glabrescent above, yellow tometose beneath; veins nearly plane above, prominent, beneath, 8-17 pairs of secondary veins, most tertiary veins parallel; petioles 6-15 mm long; stipules 3-6 mm long, subsericeous. Staminate inflorescences 6-8 mm in diameter; peduncle 10-15 mm long, puberulous to tomentellous; involucre with reniform to ovate, acute, tomentellous bracts in 5-7 series, the inner bracts involute; flowers basally connate; perianth ca 2 mm high, 4-lobed, tomentellous at the upper end; filaments 2.2-2.7 mm long, anthers 0.4-0.6 mm long, o.3-0.5 mm broad, apiculate or not, connectives broad, stamens about equal, or the outer ones sometimes staminodial. Pistillate inflorescences solitary or accompanied by up to 6 staminate ones, broadly turbinate, 7-8 mm in diameter; peduncle 2-6 mm long, puberulous to tomentellous; involucre with reniform to deltoid to ovate, acuminate to acute, tomentellous bracts in ca 8 series; flowers 5-12; perianth ca 2 mm high, 4-fid to 4-parted, tomentellous at the upper end; ovary hairy at the tip, style subterminal, o.8-1.0 mm long, hairy, stigmas vittiform, ca 1.5 mm long. Flowering from November to December.

description: Dioecious, medium-sized to rather large trees. Leafy twigs 3.5-9 mm thick, light yellow tomentose, hairs partly in tufts. Leaves oblong, sometimes broadest near the upper end, hardly inequilateral, 26-43 cm long, 10-18 cm broad, coriaceous, acuminate, obtuse or emarginate, at the base, entire to faintly repand, except for the tomentose costa glabrescent above, tomentose beneath, hairs on the costa and the secondary veins beneath partly in tufts; veins nearly plane to somewhat impressed above, prominent beneath, 17-21 pairs of secondary veins, most tertiary veins parallel; petioles 10-26 mm long; stipules 10-20 mm long, subsericeous to hirsute. Staminate inflorescences up to 15 together, 7-12 mm in diameter; peduncle 10-15 mm long, tomentellous to densely puberulous; involucre with reniform to deltoid, acute, tomentellous bracts in 3-4 series; perianth 1.8-2.0 mm high, 4-lobed to 4-parted, tomentellous at the upper end; filaments 2.3-3.0 mm long, anthers 0.3-0.4 mm long, ca 0.3 mm broad, connectives broad and shortly apiculate, or less broad and more long-apiculate. Flowering from August to November.

description: Tree, to 18 m tall. Leafy twigs 1-2.5 mm thick, minutely puberulous and with sparse to rather dense, longer, uncinate hairs. Lamina elliptic to lanceolate, 5.5-17.5 × 3.5-6 cm, broadest in or above the middle, (sub)equilateral, subcoriaceous to coriaceous; apex acute to acuminate or to obtuse; base (sub)acute; margin (sub)entire; both surfaces glabrous or a few uncinate hairs on the main veins and margin; venation slightly prominent above, prominent beneath; lateral veins 6-10 pairs, the lower ones departing from the midrib at acute angles, 40°-60o(-80°); tertiary venation partly scalariform; petiole 0.3-0.7 cm long, minutely puberulous and with longer uncinate hairs; stipules 0.3-0.6 cm long, appressed-puberulous and with or without uncinate hairs. Inflorescences bisexual, ovoid, ca. 1 cm diam.; peduncle 0.5-0.7 cm long, puberulous; receptacle densely and minutely puberulous and with longer uncinate hairs; staminate flowers ca. 50, mostly on the lower part of the receptacle; pedicel ca. 1 mm long; perianth ca. 2 mm long, 3-fid, minutely puberulous; stamens 3; filaments 2-2.5 mm long, the upper part deflexed at and after anthesis; anthers 0.3-0.4 × 0.2-0.3 mm, the connective rather broad; pistillode ca. 1.5-2 mm long, branched or unbranched; pistillate flower one, almost completely immersed in the center of the receptacle; stigmas ca. 2 mm long, sparsely hairy; bracts at the base of the receptacle basally attached, (sub)ovate, passing gradually into numerous subulate to (sub)peltate interfloral ones. Infructescences globose, 2-2.5 cm diam., covered with rather dense uncinate hairs and scattered, but towards the base with ± crowded, persistent staminate flowers.

description: Shrubs or trees up to 15m tall; latex white to yellow (or brown). Leafy twigs 1-3 mm thick, white to brown puberulous to strigulose. Leaves (elliptic to) oblong to lanceolate, sometimes broadest above the middle, not or slightly inequilateral, 3-17 cm long, 1.5-6.5 cm broad, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, acuminate to caudate, at the base acute to obtuse; margin entire; above glabrous; beneath puberulous to strigulose, often also uncinate hairs; costa more or less impressed above, prominent beneath, other veins plane or nearly so above, prominent beneath, 5-12 pairs of secondary veins, without parallel tertiary veins; petioles 2-9 mm long, often with uncinate hairs; stipules 3-7 mm long, puberulous to strigulose, or subsericeous. Staminate inflorescences hemispherical to subglobose, 3-7 mm in diameter; peduncle 3-11 mm long, puberulous to short-velutinous, with or without uncinate hairs; staminate flowers numerous, often in groups of 2-5 together, sessile or short-pedicellate; perianth o.8-2.0 mm high, (3-)4-lobed to (3-)4-fid, puberulous, sometimes with a few uncinate hairs; stamens mostly 4, sometimes 3 or 5, filaments 1.0-2.2 mm long, anthers 0.4-0.5 mm long and o.3-0.4 mm broad, connectives rather broad, apiculate or not; pistillode (style) 0.5-20 mm long, unbranched or with 2 mostly unequal branches, puberulous: bracts at the base reniform to ovate, up to 2 mm long, otherwise oblong to linear, oblanceolate, subpeltate or peltate, 0.5-1.5 mm long, puberulous, often with uncinate hairs. Bisexual inflorescences subglobose to turbinate, 4-5 mm in diameter; peduncle 3-11 mm long, puberulous to short-velutinous, with or without uncinate hairs; receptacle brown puberulous with uncinate hairs or brown short-velutinous; pistillate flower one, style ca i mm long, stigmas up to 20 mm long, with irregularly shaped papillae on the lower end; staminate flowers few to several on the upper end of the receptacle; perianth 3-4-lobed; stamens 3-4; pistillode (style) up to 20 mm long, on the lower end often with short more or less irregularly shaped papillae, unbranched or with unequal branches; bracts several, scattered, oblong, subpeltate, or peltate. Infructescences globose, ca 2 cm in diameter, velutinous or hispid with dense uncinate hairs. Flowering probably throughout the year.

description: Glabrous shrub or tree, 2-10(-15) m tall; trunk 4-15(-20) cm diam.; branches spreading. Branchlets slender, subangular, dark, striate lengthwise and a little rugulose by numerous small lenticels. Leaves ovate-lanceolate or -oblong, rarely almost lanceolate, apex usually gradually attenuate, or subacuminate, sometimes subfalcate, tip acute or bluntish, base broadly cuneate to rounded, not rarely subinequilateral, thin-chartaceous to subcoriaceous, pale olive-green or yellowish-green in dry specimens, somewhat shiny above only or rather dull on both surfaces, edge hardly revolute, laticifers poorly visible beneath, usually finely tuberculate and wrinkled on both surfaces, though sometimes less distinctly or hardly so, 9-12(-15, -25) x 4.5-6(-7, -10) cm, sometimes in part microphyllous 6x2cm) in the same specimen, midrib plane or slightly immersed above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves 1 basal steeply ascendent pair and 5-7 upper curved-ascending pairs, visibly looping before the edge beneath only, plane or subimpressed above, raised beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather inconspicuous above, faintly though distinctly raised beneath; petiole longitudinally striate and more or less distinctly transversely rugulose, 5-10(-12) x 2 mm. Flowers 5-10 per axillary bracteolate usually small glomerules; pedicels stoutish, 1-2(-3) mm long. Calyx spreadingly cup-shaped, 5-lobed halfway, lobes subacute, 1 mm long. Petals ovate-acuminate, acute, cream or white, subdensely hairy inside, 2 mm long. Stamens 10, subequal; filaments filiform. Ovary subglobose. Drupe (sub)globose, whitish or pale yellowish, turning gray, slightly striate lengthwise, (0.7-)1-1.3 cm diam. Fruit-calyx membranaceous, deep red, 5-lobed about halfway, cupuliform, 3(-3.5) cm diam. when expanded, lobes erect, ovate, obtuse, plicate, accumbent to the drupe and hiding it, (1-)1.5(-1.8) cm long; peduncle 3-5(-7) mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: (Subscandent shrub, or usually liana, 1 -4 m tall, with slender flexuous branches, glabrous. Branchlets very slender, subterete, slightly striate lengthwise, not rugulose, subdistichously and remotely (1.5-3 cm) foliate. Leaves ovate or usually ovate-oblong or -elliptic, sometimes narrowly so and almost lanceolate-ovate, apex acuminate, not rarely subfalcate, tip subacute or bluntish, base broadly cuneate to obtuse or rounded, rarely subcordate, maybe subinequilateral, thinly to firmly chartaceous, shiny above, usually rather dull beneath, olive-green above, more brownish beneath in dry specimens, edge hardly revolute, neither wrinkled nor tuberculate, the laticifers well visible beneath, (4-)6-10(-13) x (2.5-)3-5(-6.5) cm, midrib plane or a little impressed above, bold beneath, lateral nerves 1 (or rarely 2) basal pair(s), curved-ascending to almost half the length of the lamina, and 3-4(-5) upper shorter pairs, curved-ascending and looping with each other and the basal pair(s) before the edge, slightly prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather lax, slightly though distinctly raised on both surfaces, rarely rather inconspicuous beneath; petiole slender, deflexed, a little thickened and rugulose in the upper ½, 7-13 x 1 mm. Fascicles of 8-20 (rarely -50) flowers from axillary small multibracteolate cushions; pedicels slender, often almost filiform, (3-)6-8 mm long. Calyx minute (1 mm long), 5-dentate halfway, lobes acuminate, each lobe with a minute apical fuscous gland. Petals 5, ovate-lanceolate, acute, laxly hairy or subglabrous inside, (1,5-)2(-2.5) mm long, ca. 1 mm broad at base. Stamens 10, unequal; filaments liguliform. Ovary conical, its base thickened and 10-sulcate. Drupe (subglobose, or obovoidly so, sometimes a little depressed, slightly 10-sulcate, shiny, smooth, finally bright orange or cherry red, 9-12 mm diam. Fruit-calyx subentire or very shallowly or undulately lobed, thin, green, strongly reflexed, (0.8-)1.2-1.4 cm diam. when expanded, on slender peduncle 1.2-1,5(-2) cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Glabrous shrub or tree, (2.5-)6-20(-25) m tall; stem or trunk (4-)10-40 cm diam. Branchlets subangular, striate, dark red or purplish in dry specimens, slender, flexuous or somewhat geniculate, older parts densely lenticellate and covered with a peeling brown cork. Leaves variable in shape and size (sometimes in the same specimen), ovate, ovate-oblong, elliptic-oblong, or occasionally ovate-lanceolate, apex shortly-, rarely more elongately-attenuate or subacuminate, tip subacute or blunt, base attenuate to obtuse or rounded, very base often contracted to the petiole, subinequilateral, subcoriaceous, flexible, or sometimes stiffly so, brown to dark red-brown when dry, remarkably shiny and seemingly smooth, though in fact irregularly wrinkled (through hand lens) above, less distinctly and usually minutely (i.e. not properly or maybe faintly) tuberculate beneath, laticifers usually a little though distinctly raised in dry specimens beneath, (5-)6-12(-15, -19) x 2.5-6(-8) cm, edge slightly revolute, midrib plane or a little impressed above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves (5-)6-8(-10, -12) pairs rather straight below, otherwise moderately curved-ascending, inconspicuously looping before the edge, plane above, slightly prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets plane or not rarely very slightly immersed above, rather dense and finely raised beneath; petiole somewhat transversely rugulose, (4-)6-10(-17) x 1-1.5 (-2) mm. Flowers few to rather numerous (-20) per axillary fascicle from small multibracteolate cushions; pedicels slender, (2-)3(-5) mm long. Calyx cup-shaped, ca. 1 mm long, acutely 5-lobed halfway. Petals ovate-lanceolate, white, yellowish, or greenish, acute, hairy at middle inside, 1.5(-2) mm long. Stamens 10. Drupe relatively small, subovoid-ellipsoid to ellipsoid-oblongoid, sometimes broadly so and practically subglobose, apiculate, finally turning yellowish or pale reddish, slightly striate lengthwise, (6-)8-10 x (4-)5-7 mm. Fruit-calyx chartaceous to subcoriaceous, red to pale crimson, erect or mostly spreading, expanded (0.8-) 1-2(-2.5, very rarely -3) cm diam., 5-lobed about halfway, lobes ovate-deltoid, obtuse; peduncle slender, 4-6(-10, -15) mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Tree, (6-)12-20(-25) m tall; trunk 10-30(-75) cm diam.; bark brown mottled with gray or white. Branchlets reddish-brownish, rugulose, striate lengthwise. Leaves elliptic- to lanceolate-oblong, rarely subovately so, or even elliptic, apex short-acuminate, tip acutish by the prominent midrib, base more or less broadly cuneate to attenuate, subinequilateral, firmly subcoriaceous, flexible, greenish-olivaceous and slightly shiny above, densely tuberculate on both surfaces, but not properly wrinkled in dry specimens, laticifers inconspicuous, edge somewhat revolute, variable in size, (7-)10-15(-18) x (3-)4.5-7(-9) cm, midrib plane or shallowly impressed above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves 6-8 pairs rather straight curved-ascending, not properly looping, very slightly immersed or inconspicuous above, a little raised beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets hardly visible beneath; petiole rugulose, 8-15 x 1.5-2 mm. Flowers numerous from multi-bracteolate globose axillary cushions (2-3 mm diam.); pedicels stoutish, (2-)3(-4) mm long. Calyx cup-shaped, 5-dentate halfway, ca. 1 mm long, lobes gland-apiculate. Petals lanceolate, acutish, white, hairy in the upper ½ inside, 2.5 mm long. Drupe subovoid-globose, apiculate, creamy white, 1.3-1.5 cm diam. Fruit-calyx thick-membranaceous to subcoriaceous, lobed about halfway, expanded (3-)3.5(-4) cm diam., red to purplish, suberect or spreading, more or less enveloping the drupe in its lower 2/3, lobes obtusely ovate-deltoid; peduncle slender, ca. 1 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Glabrous tree 3-7 m tall. Branchlets slender, subterete, rugulose by numerous linear longitudinally arranged lenticel-like tubercles, reddish-purplish when dry. Leaves elliptic, oblong, or oblong-lanceolate, apex broadly attenuate, tip subacute or usually blunt, sometimes rounded or even slightly emarginate, base cuneate, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, shiny, greenish-yellowish above, paler (glaucescent) and dull beneath both in the fresh and dry state, not wrinkled or tuberculate, edge a little revolute, laticifers hardly or not visible beneath, 6-10(-11.5) x (2.5-)3-4 cm, midrib plane or slightly immersed above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves 8-10 pairs with a few less obvious shorter ones beneath, all nerves slightly raised or obscure above, a little prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets faint above, or usually inconspicuous on both surfaces; petiole longitidinally striate and more or less distinctly transversely rugulose, (4-)5-8 x 1.5 mm. Flowers (Wurdack & Adderley 43017) few per axillary multibracteolate cluster; pedicels 1-1.5 mm long. Calyx deeply 5-lobed, lobes ovate-lanceolate, with a distinct apical gland, 1.5 mm long. Petals lanceolate-oblong, white, hairy inside, 2.5 mm long. Stamens 10; filaments filiform. Ovary thickened at base, 10-sulcate. Drupe globular, smooth, pale yellow-green, 7(-9) mm diam. Fruit-calyx cup-like, thin-chartaceous, red, plicately 5-lobed halfway, erect and hiding the drupe, expanded 1.2-1.5 cm diam., lobes deltoid, (sub)acute; peduncle ca. 3 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Glabrous shrub or small tree, (1.5-)2-4(rarely-12) m tall; trunk to 15 cm diam.; bark light. Branchlets terete to subangular, striate. Leaves narrowly to broadly oblong, or oblong-lanceolate, apex acuminate for 4-8 cm, tip blunt, base cuneate, very base acute or mostly obtuse, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, olive-green and rather dull in dry state, neither tuberculate nor wrinkled, laticifers well visible beneath, variable in size even in the same specimen (forms with smaller leaves similar to those of H. acuminata, which however, has a different fruit), (8-) 10— 20(-30) x (3-)6-8(-11) cm, edge a little revolute, midrib plane or somewhat raised above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves 8-10(-12, -16) pairs curved-ascending, obscurely inarching before the edge, plane above, raised beneath, reticulation of the oblique veins and veinlets rather dense, a little prominent on both surfaces, or often less so beneath; petiole striate lengthwise, more or less rugulose, (6-)10-15(-30) mm long. Flowers few per bracteolate axillary glomerule; pedicels 1-2 mm long. Petals 4(-5), deltoid-oblong, practically glabrous inside, 2.5 mm long. Stamens 10; filaments liguliform. Drupe (sub)globose, vertically many-ribbed, dark blue to blackish at full maturity, (6-)8-10 mm diam. Fruit-calyx subquadrate-orbicular, spreading or finally more or less reflexed, subcoriaceous, bright red, shallowly or hardly lobed, 2(-3) cm diam. when expanded; peduncle 8-12 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Glabrous shrub or tree, 3-8 m tall; trunk to 4 cm diam. Branchlets subterete, striate. Leaves broadly oblong, elliptic-oblong, or oblong-elliptic, sometimes more narrowly so, apex attenuate or subacuminate for 1.5-2.5 cm, tip subacute to obtuse, base broadly cuneate to rounded, subinequilateral, firmly chartaceous to subcoriaceous, olive-green and dull in dry specimens, paler beneath, neither tuberculate nor wrinkled, laticifers usually well visible beneath, edge cartilaginous, hardly revolute, (15-)24-34 x (7-) 10-14(-16) cm, midrib slightly raised above, much more so beneath, lateral nerves (8-) 10-12 pairs with a few less distinct and shorter ones between, curved-ascending, obscurely inarching before the edge, hardly raised or slightly impressed above, prominent beneath, reticulation of the oblique veins with the veinlets dense and finely raised mainly above, often rather inconspicuous beneath; petiole stout, lengthwise and transversely rugulose, 1.5-2(-2.5) cm x (1.5-)2-3 mm. Flowers several to numerous from multibracteolate axes (1 -2 mm long) in defoliate axils of the branchlets, or from thick protuberances (3-8 x 2-3 mm, which bear short multibracteolate axes) on trunk and/or branches; pedicels slender, 3-5 mm long. Calyx cup-shaped, flattish, small, obscurely 5-lobed. Petals ovate-acuminate, cream or yellowish, glabrous on both surfaces, 2-2.5 mm long. Stamens 10; filaments subequal, flattish, 1 mm long. Ovary conical. Drupe oblongoid to ellipsoid, finally turning blackish, (9-) 10-13 x 6-8 mm. Fruit-calyx orbicular, subentire, spreading, scarlet, subcoriaceous, expanded 2(-2.5) cm diam.; peduncle 1-1.5 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Glabrous shrub, treelet, or tree, 2-7 m tall; trunk to 20 cm diam. Branchlets stout, subterete or slightly angular, finely rugulose. Leaves elliptic-oblong, apex acuminate, not rarely subcaudately so for 2.5-3.5 cm, base cuneate, (sub)coriaceous, firm, green-olivaceous and a little shiny above, more yellowish and dull beneath in the dry state, edge slightly revolute, densely wrinkled and tuberculate on both surfaces, 20-27(-35) x 5-9(-10) cm, midrib impressed above, much prominent beneath, lateral nerves 12-15 pairs rather straight in a wide angle from the midrib and subparallel to each other, markedly inarching and forming there a distinct intramarginal nerve, more or less deeply impressed above, raised beneath, a few intercalary lateral nerves shorter and less obvious, the transverse or oblique veins slightly impressed above, hardly or not raised beneath; petiole stout, rugulose and wrinkled all length, (10-) 12—20 x 2-3 mm. Rowers subsessile from a globular cushion formed by numerous bracts, only known in bud stage. Drupe ellipsoid-oblongoid, whitish or grayish, smooth, ca. 1.7 x 0.9 cm. Fruit-calyx fleshy, purple-red, 5-lobed to almost the base, when expanded (4-)4.5-6(-7) cm diam., lobes narrowly ovate, obtuse to subacute, erect, including the drupe.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Glabrous tree, 6-20(-35) m tall; trunk to 25 cm diam. Branchlets dark, red-brown, angular or subalate, striate lengthwise. Leaves elliptic to oblong-elliptic, sometimes narrowly or obovately so, apex abruptly acuminate for 3-5(-10) mm, tip subacute or bluntish, base cuneate to broadly attenuate, or almost rounded, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, more or less flexible, olivaceous to brown and often shiny (sometimes almost lacquered) above, paler and less shiny or usually dull beneath, smooth or seemingly so, in fact often sparsely and shallowly sometimes densely tuberculate on both surfaces, not properly wrinkled, laticifers plane or a little raised, discolorous and well visible in dry specimens beneath, edge subrevolute, 5.5-10(-13) x 3-5(-7) cm, midrib slightly to faintly raised above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves 7-8(-10) pairs (including a basal pair) rather straight from the midrib, moderately curved-ascending and looping before the edge, plane or a little impressed above, slightly raised beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets very slightly raised or immersed, or usually inconspicuous on both surfaces; petiole dark, more or less markedly transversely rugulose, 0.6-1 (-1.6) cm x 1.5-2 mm. Flowers in dense clusters from multibracteolate axillary cushions; pedicels slender, (3-)4-5(-6) mm long. Calyx 5-lobed to almost the base, lobes narrowly ovate, minutely gland-apiculate, 2 mm long. Petals lanceolate, acute, minutely papillose-ciliolate, whitish-cream or greenish, hairy inside, 3-4 x 1.5 mm. Drupe ellipsoid, smooth, whitish, or finally pale bluish, 1.5-1.8 x (0.8-) 1 cm. Fruit-calyx deeply 5-lobed, reddish, thin-fleshy, firmly membranaceous to subcoriaceous in dry state, expanded 4-6(-7) cm diam., lobes ovate, subacute, erect, plicate, (1.5-) 2-3(-3.5) x (1.3-) 1.5-2(-2.5) cm; peduncle 1-1.5 cm x 1-1.5 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Glabrous, Subscandent shrub, treelet, or tree 3-10(-16) m tall; trunk to 15 cm diam.; bark rugulose, greenish to grayish. Branchlets finely striate, subterete. Leaves ovate to elliptic or oblong, sometimes broadly so, apex more or less abruptly acuminate for 0.5-1.5 cm, tip blunt, base cuneate to the petiole, thin-chartaceous to subcoriaceous, rarely firmly so, shiny or dull, remaining usually green in the dry state and subdensely wrinkled and/or tuberculate on both surfaces, the latic-ifers not or not much visible in general, edge a little revolute, (4-, 6-) 10-18(-25) x 3-5(-6, -9) cm, midrib slightly prominent above, more distinctly so beneath, lateral nerves 6-9 pairs arcuately ascending and rather distinctly looping before the edge, usually slightly impressed above, raised beneath as are a number of shorter nerves between, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather dense, distinct to subinconspicuous; petiole 5-10(-15) mm long. Flowers (1-)3-6 in a fascicle per foliate or defoliate axil, arising from a small cushion formed by numerous thin small bracts; pedicels 1-2 mm long. Calyx patently cup-shaped, shortly 5(-6)-dentate, green, ca. 1 mm high, 2 mm diam. Petals 5(-6), ovate-lanceolate, coherent below, sometimes so to the middle, white, densely hispidulous-hairy inside, 4-5(-6) mm long, 1.5(-2) mm broad at base. Stamens 10(-12); filaments slender, 1 mm; anthers subglobose, 0.4 mm. Ovary depressedly globose, 10-sulcate; style thickish, short. Drupe ellipsoid-oblongoid, sometimes subobovoid, apex mucronulate by the remaining style-base, first green, then pale yellow to orange at maturity, 10-11 (-14) x 6-8 mm, the subtending fruit-calyx becoming thickish, but only slightly accrescent, including only the base of the drupe, greenish to dull red, 2-3(-5, -7) mm diam., 1.5-2(-3) mm high; peduncle stoutish, 1.5-4 mm long; pericarp thin, brittle, smooth or a little wrinkled in the dry state.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Tree, 6-9(-18) m tall, with dense rounded crown; trunk to 10 cm diam.; bark smooth, whitish. Branchlets slender, olive-green to brownish-red, subterete or subangular at tips. Leaves elliptic to ovate-oblong, sometimes ovate, apex rather abruptly acuminate for 0.5-1.5 cm, often subfalcate, tip blunt, base attenuate to obtuse, often somewhat oblique, subcoriaceous or thinly coriaceous, flexible, green-olivaceous and shiny mainly above in dry specimens, finely and more or less densely tuberculate above only, not wrinkled, laticifera obscure, edge a little revolute, variable in size, 6-13 x 3-6 cm, on sprout-shoots to 20 x 10 cm, midrib plane or somewhat immersed, strongly raised beneath, lateral nerves rather irregular, 6-8 pairs (the lowest pair from base of the lamina) rather straight from midrib, looping before the edge, faintly raised above, slightly so beneath, veins and veinlets forming a dense network which is finely though very distinctly prominent on both surfaces; petiole dark, rugulose, (7-)10-15(-18) x l-2mm. Flowers 6-10 per fascicle from bracteolate axillary glomerules; pedicels slender, 5-7 mm long. Calyx crateriform, 1 mm long, acutely 5-lobed halfway. Petals elliptic-oblong, edge seemingly ciliolate, hairy in the upper ½ inside, white or greenish, fragrant, 2-2.5 mm long. Stamens 10. Drupe broadly ellipsoid to subglobose, white or pale yellow-green at maturity, 10-15 x 8-10 mm. Fruit-calyx subcoriaceous, 1.5—2.5 cm diam. when expanded, pinkish to red, obtusely 5-lobed in the upper 1/3 to ½, finally spreading or reflexed.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Treelet or tree 3-6 m tall; trunk to 10 cm diam. Branches elongate, often almost horizontally spreading. Branchlets slender, subterete. Leaves ovate-oblong or elliptic, apex attenuate or short-acuminate, tip blunt, often subfalcate, base broadly attenuate, subcoriaceous, flexible, dull olive-brown on both surfaces when dry, rather smooth, i.e. not properly wrinkled or tuberculate, laticifers hardly or not visible beneath, 7-14(-20) x (2.5-)3-6(-8) cm, midrib plane above, strongly raised beneath, lateral nerves 6-9 pairs, somewhat irregularly curved-ascendent and looping, flat or faintly impressed above, slightly prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets inconspicuous on both surfaces; petiole rugulose, (5-)7-10(-13) x 1-2 mm. Flowers few from very short axillary multibracteolate glomerules or axes (1-2 mm long); pedicels slender, 2-3 mm long. Calyx deeply 5-lobed, hardly 1 mm long. Petals ovate-lanceolate, practically glabrous within, white, 1.5 mm long. Stamens 10, alternately slightly unequal. Ovary thickened at base by the adnate disk. Drupe broadly oblongoid or barrel-shaped at full maturity, markedly flattened or truncate on top, densely tuberculate in the dry state, at first shiny green, finally black, 1.2-1.4 x 0.7-1.2 cm, exceeding the fruit-calyx for ca. 3 mm. Fruit-calyx cup-shaped below, expanded in the upper stiffly membranaceous, vermillion-red, 2(-2.5) cm diam. when expanded, lobed to 1/3-½, lobes erect or finally slightly spreading, not plicate, obtuse; peduncle 1-1.5 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Glabrous shrubby treelet or tree, to 3 m tall; stem to 8 cm diam. Branchlets robust, dark red-brown when dry, subterete, striate lengthwise, densely foliate. Leaves ovate or ovate-oblong, sometimes so in the same specimen, apex very shortly and broadly attenuate or subacuminate, tip obtuse, base more or less rounded, slightly unequal, coriaceous, stiff, in general dull and greenish-yellowish on both surfaces, or more brownish beneath when dry, sparsely rather faintly tuberculate above only, sometimes very sparsely or not tuberculate at all, not properly wrinkled, laticifers markedly raised beneath in dry specimens as is the case in H. ovata and its allies, edge somewhat revolute, (5-)7-10 x 3-5(-6) cm, midrib plane above, strongly raised beneath, lateral nerves rather straight from the midrib and subparallel to each other in 10-12 pairs, with more irregular and less obvious ones between, slightly raised on both surfaces, or less so above, reticulation of veins and veinlets finely though distinctly prominent on both surfaces; petiole stoutish, more or less distinctly transversely rugulose, (3-)5(-7) x 2-2.5 mm. Flowers numerous from small axillary multibracteolate cushions; pedicels ca. 2 mm long. Calyx deeply 5-lobed, lobes triangular, minutely gland-apiculate, papillate-ciliolate, 1.5 mm long. Petals ovate-lanceolate, greenish to cream, hairy inside, sparsely papillate dorsally and papillate-ciliolate along edge, 2 mm long. Stamens 10. Ovary ovoid, base thickened and 10-sulcate. Drupe (Glaziou 15201) oblongoid, color unknown, ca. 8 x 5 mm. Fruit-calyx thick-membranaceous, deeply 5-lobed, expanded ca. 2.5 cm diam., red, lobes ovate, remaining erect, plicate, including the drupe.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Glabrous tree, 3-12(-20, -30) m tall; trunk (5-) 15-40(-80) cm diam. Branchlets subterete, striate, dark red-brown in dry specimens. Leaves ovate-elliptic to elliptic or oblong, apex abruptly acuminate for 1-1.5 cm, tip obtuse and often curved, base broadly attenuate to rounded, subinequilateral, firmly chartaceous to subcoriaceous, dark reddish to olive-brown above, paler beneath when dry, shiny on both surfaces though more obviously so above, smooth, not tuberculate or wrinkled, laticifers usually sparse, sometimes hardly visible beneath, edge a little or not revolute, 6-12(-15) x (2-)3.5-5(-6) cm, midrib somewhat prominent above, more strongly so beneath, lateral nerves 6-8 pairs curved-ascending and subparallel to each other, looping before the edge, a little raised above, more distinctly so beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets dense, equally finely raised on both surfaces; petiole somewhat swollen and rugulose in the upper ½, slender, deeply grooved, 4-7(-10) x 1-1.5 mm. Flowers (3-)8-12(-15) per axillary fascicle on foliate or already defoliate branchlets from multibracteolate small glomerules; pedicels slender to filiform, 3-4 mm long. Calyx cup-shaped, flattish, shortly 5-lobed, 1 mm long. Petals oblong-acuminate, greenish-yellowish, hirsute only in the middle inside, 2 mm long, stamens 10; filaments 2 mm long. Ovary adnate below to a thickish 10-sulcate disk. Drupe subglobular to broadly ellipsoid, apex rounded, dark green, becoming blue-green to purplish-blackish when dry, shiny, a little wrinkled in dry specimens, 0.8-1 x 0.6-0.8 cm. Fruit-calyx suborbicular, shallowly lobed, thin-coriaceous, green in fresh, brownish in dry specimens, spreading or finally reflexed, 1.5(-2) cm diam. when expanded; peduncle slender, 1-2 cm long.

description: Young branches stout, golden tomentose at first becoming suberous, fissured longitudinally. Leaves pinnate with a terminal bud showing intermittent growth, to 30(-140) cm long; petiole semiterete, rhachis terete or channelled above, tomentose, becoming lenticellate when older; petiolule 2-4 mm long. Leaflets to 13 pairs (not more than 7 present at any given time), elliptic to broadly oblong, apex short acuminate, attenuate, obtuse or obtusely cuspidate, base broadly attenuate or cuneate, chartaceous, 13.7-38[22.5] cm long, 5-14[8.3] cm broad, lower often much shorter and broader, upper surface glabrous except for pubescent midrib, lower uniformly puberulous with crisped hairs intermixed with minute red papillae, not glandular-punctate or -striate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib sunken; secondaries 13-18 on either side of midrib, ascending, slightly arcuate, parallel; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries obscure, oblique, parallel. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious, inflorescence axillary or in axils of fallen leaves, 320 cm long, a laxly-branched pyramidal thyrse with lower branches widely spreading to 6 cm long, flowers subtended by 1-3 lanceolate bracteoles 4-6 mm long, densely golden pubescent or tomentose; pedicel 1-2 mm long. Calyx deeply cyathiform to short cylindrical, 7-8 mm long, closed in bud and splitting irregularly to form 2-4 acute to rounded lobes to 6 mm long, densely crisped pubescent outside. Petals 4(-5), valvate, 11-14 mm long, 2-5 mm broad, oblong or strapshaped, apex acute, densely golden sericeous outside, glabrous within. Staminal tube 8.5-10 mm long, 3-3.5 mm broad, margin undulate, glabrous; anthers 8-10, 1.1-1.5 mm long; antherodes similar, narrower, not dehiscing, without pollen. Nectary a stipe expanded to form an annulus below ovary, 1-2 mm long, glabrous. Ovary 4-5-locular, loculi with 2 superposed ovules, densely strigose; style glabrous above. Pistillode similar, with well-developed but abortive ovules. Fruit unknown. Field characters. A tree to 20 m high, with soft, brown, rather suberous bark, scaling or slightly fissured. The yellowish flowers, which are without scent, are produced in May and June and again in October and November.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1981. Meliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 28: 1-359, 418-449, 459-470.

description: Leaves pinnate with a terminal bud, to 40 cm long; petiole semiterete with a narrow wing at base, rhachis quadrangular, densely golden tomentose to villose. Leaflets subsessile, to 3 pairs, oblong, apex short attenuate to obtusely cuspidate, base ± truncate, coriaceous and strongly bullate, ca. 30 cm long, ca. 11 cm broad, lower ones much smaller, upper surface with tomentose midrib and short pubescent secondary veins, lower surface with densely golden villose midrib and uniformly golden pubescent lamina, hairs intermixed with numerous minute red papillae, not glandular-punctate or -striate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib sunken; secondaries ca. 18 on either side of midrib, ascending, arcuate above, lowest ones divergent, otherwise parallel; intersecondaries very short; tertiaries oblique, very prominent on the undersurface; quaternary reticulum prominent below. Inflorescence 20-30 cm long, a laxly-branched panicle, lower lateral branches to 8 cm long, spreading at right angles to axis, golden tomentose; pedicel 1.5 mm long. Calyx deeply cyathiform, ca. 7 mm long, irregularly 3-4-lobed, lobes 2-4 mm long, ovate, acute or obtuse, golden tomentose. Petals 5, valvate, 14-15 mm long, ca. 4.5 mm broad, oblong, apex acute, golden sericeous outside, glabrous inside. Staminal tube slightly narrowed at throat, ca. 11 mm long, ca. 4 mm broad, margin undulate, glabrous; anthers 10-11, ca. 1.8 mm long. Nectary a stout stipe expanded at apex to form a ring below ovary, ca. 2.5 mm long, glabrous. Ovary strongly longitudinally ribbed, 6-locular, loculi with 2 superposed ovules, densely strigose; style stout, strigose. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Tree to 33 m, flowering in March.

description: Young branches minutely appressed puberulous at first soon glabrous, becoming rough, pale brown or greyish-white, sometimes with a few large lenticels. Leaves pinnate with a terminal bud showing intermittent growth, to 27 cm long; petiole semiterete, rhachis terete, glabrous, becoming woody; petiolule 1-2 mm long. Leaflets to 6 pairs, broadly oblanceolate, obovate, or cuneiform, apex rounded, base narrowly attenuate, coriaceous, 5-6.5 cm long, 2.8-3 cm broad, glabrous, not glandular-punctate or -striate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat; secondaries 9-11 on either side of midrib, shallowly ascending, straight or arcuate at tip, parallel; intersecondaries long and prominent; tertiary reticulum obscure. Inflorescence axillary, small, ca. 5-flowered; flowers 4-merous. Sepals united at base, triangular, very short pilose. Petals sericeo-pilose. Anthers 8. Capsule globose, densely tuberculate-ribbed, sparsely to densely appressed puberulous, ca. 1.5 cm diam., 3-4-valved, valves with 1-2 superposed seeds. Embryo not seen. (The description of inflorescence and flowers is extracted from Urban (1912).)
