description: Subshrubs 0.5-1 m tall, the stems with some stellate hairs, the nodes very short (5 mm or less). Leaf blades oblanceolate, up to 22 x 8 cm, basally truncate, essentially entire (or with minute serrulations), acuminate, slightly discolorous, 3-nerved from the base but appearing penninerved, glabrate above, nearly so beneath, the margins hispid-ciliate; petioles 2-5 cm long, sparsely stellate-pubescent to glabrate; stipules 10-14 mm long, subulate, erect. Inflorescence a leafless open raceme or panicle, each node with 2-3 stipuliform bractlets; pedicels 2-10 cm long, sparsely stellate-pubescent, articulated 6-10 mm below the flowers; involucellar bracts ca. 9, triangular, 6-9 mm long, basally connate forming a cup, the sinuses broadly rounded, sparsely stellate-pubescent; calyx subequal to involucel, pubescent; corolla 12-20 mm long, pink; staminal column 7-8 mm long, glabrous, pallid, the filaments 1-2 mm long. Fruits 9-13 mm diam.; mericarp body 7-8 mm high (excluding spines), straw-colored, essentially glabrous, 3-spined, the spines erect, 4-7 mm long, retrorsely barbed.

description: Subshrubs ca. 0.5 m tall, the stems with minute stellate pubescence, the hairs 0.1 mm long. Leaf blades up to 7 cm long (usually smaller), ovate-triangular to hastate-oblong, basally cordate or hastate with an open acute sinus, coarsely crenate, acute or subobtuse, discolorous, minutely stellate-pubescent, more densely so beneath; petioles Vs the length of the blade or less; stipules ca. 2 mm long, subulate. Flowers sometimes cleistogamic, the pedicels solitary in the leaf axils, 17-23(-40) mm long; involucellar bracts 5, ovate, 4-6 x 2-3 mm; calyx 6-8 mm long, stellate-pubescent; corolla 15-22 mm long, deep rose with a dark center. Fruits ca. 6 mm diam., oblate, minutely pubescent, the mericarps ca. 4 mm long, dorsally rounded and keeled, reticulate-costate. Chromosome number, 2n = 56 (Krapovickas & Cristóbal, 1962).

description: Subshrubs 0.5-3 m tall, the stems with short glandular hairs and setose (hairs 3-4 mm long). Leaf blades mostly 4-10 x 3-7 cm, ovate (sometimes with a weak tendency to lobing), cordate, coarsely crenate, acute or acuminate, palmately 5-7-nerved, softly pubescent (the veins sometimes also pilose), somewhat discolorous; petioles 1-7 cm long; stipules 2-4 mm long, subulate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 4-8 cm long; involucellar bracts 6-8, lanceolate, 8-11 x 1-1.5 mm, ciliate; calyx 5-9 mm long, pilose; corolla 1.5-3.5 cm long, pink, sparsely ciliate on claw; staminal column 1-1.5 cm long, glabrous, the filaments 1-1.5 mm long, in 3 or 4 whorls; styles emergent from the column, the stigmas villous. Fruits oblate 8-9 mm diam., short-pubescent; seeds 3 mm long, obscurely striate, sparsely and minutely pubescent.

description: Subshrubs 0.5-1 m tall, the stems scabridulous, the hairs stellate, 3-6-armed, 1 mm diam. Leaf blades elliptic to oblanceolate, mostly 9-20 x 4-9 cm, basally truncate to cuneate, serrate, acute or acuminate, penninerved or basally 3(-5)-nerved, somewhat discolorous, with minute (0.5 mm diam.) stellate hairs scattered evenly over both surfaces; petioles 1-6(-9) cm long, stellate-scabridulous; stipules subulate, 8 mm long, deciduous. Inflorescence terminal, with elongated peduncle (sometimes branched) rising above the leaves, racemose to subcapituliform; pedicels 0.5-3 cm long, the lower scattered, the upper crowded to sub-umbelliform; involucellar bracts 7-9, lance-linear, basally connate, 6-8 x 1-2 mm, minutely and sparsely stellate-pubescent, marginally ciliate (cilia 1 mm long); calyx 2-3 mm long, sparsely pubescent; corolla 7-10 mm long, pink, externally pubescent, the petals apparently narrow (2 mm wide?); androecium included, the anthers subsessile at apex. Fruits 5-6 mm diam., glabrous; mericarp body 5-6 mm long, smooth, the 3 distal spines erect and parallel, retrorsely barbed, the central spine 9-10 mm long, with a dorsoventrally broadened base, the lateral spines 6 mm long, 1.5-2 mm apart at base.

description: Perennial herb, the stems (presumably trailing) densely stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades triangular or pentangular, 1-1.5 x 1.5-2 cm, sometimes slightly asymmetrical, deeply cordate, obscurely crenate, acute, palmately 5-nerved, densely and finely yellowish-tomentose on both surfaces; petioles 1 cm long or less; stipules 2-3 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-1.5 cm long; involucellar bracts ca. 15, ca. 5 mm long (flowers and fruits otherwise not observable).

description: Shrubs to almost 3 m tall, the stems densely stellate-pubescent, the hairs more or less appressed. Leaf blades 8-10 x 7-9 cm, progressively reduced upward, broadly ovate, cordate, irregularly crenate-serrate, acute, palmately 7-9-nerved, densely and minutely stellate-pubescent; petioles up to 5.5 cm long (progressively shorter upward); stipules 3-5 mm long, subulate. Inflorescence a terminal leafless raceme; pedicels 4-14 mm long, ca. 3 mm diam., stellate-pubescent; involucellar bracts 11-12, ca. half length of the calyx, ovate-lanceolate, the margins revolute and undulate, prominently ciliate (hairs 1-2 mm long); calyx 1.5 cm long, stellate-puberulent; corolla tubular, 1.5-2.5 cm long, dark red, externally pubescent, internally glabrous (including margins of claw); staminal column ca. 2 cm long, glabrous, pallid, the filaments 2 mm long. Fruits 18 mm .diam., oblate, weakly 10-ribbed, densely stellate-pubescent, the hairs more or less retrorse; mericarps 8-10 mm high, ligneous.

description: Sprawling shrubs 1-2 m tall, the stems viscid-puberulent. Leaf blades mostly 6-15 cm long (smaller upward), ca. 1.5 times as long as wide, ovate to more or less 3-lobed, cordate, remotely crenate-serrate to subentire, acuminate, stellate-pubescent, markedly discolorous; petioles ¼-¾ the length of the blades; stipules 5-7 mm long, subulate, recurved. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-6 cm long, viscid; involucellar bracts 5, 15-25 x 1.5-2.5 mm, densely viscid; calyx 10-14(-17) mm long, densely viscid, deeply divided, whitish with green nerves; corolla 2.5-5 cm long, white (drying yellowish) externally stellate-pubescent; staminal column 2.5-3.5 cm long, pallid, glabrous, the filaments 2-4 mm long; styles exceeding androecium by 6-8 mm, pallid, sometimes pubescent, the stigmas villous. Fruits ca. 1 cm diam., sparsely viscid-puberulent, the mericarps 5 mm long, prominently carinate and with raised reticulations.

description: Herbs or subshrubs 0.5-2 m tall, the stems setose (hairs 2-3 mm long) and with dense understory of minute glandular hairs. Leaf blades ovate to shallowly 3-lobulate, mostly 4-8 x 2-5 cm, cordate, serrate, acute to long-acuminate, palmately 5-7-nerved, both surfaces with appressed setae (especially on veins) and obscure but abundant glandular hairs; petioles 2-5 cm long; stipules filiform, 4-5 mm long, somewhat reflexed. Flowers solitary (occasionally paired) in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-7.5 cm long (subequal to or exceeding subtending petioles, or the upper ones exceeding the leaves), slender; involucellar bracts 8-10, linear, viscid and setose, 6-11 mm long; calyx 5-7 mm long, ciliate; corolla 12-22 mm long, pale pink (drying yellowish), glabrous except white-bearded at juncture of claw and staminal column; staminal column 9-15 mm long, glabrous, pallid, declined and somewhat curved, the filaments secund, 2-3 mm long; styles united below, free for distal 3-4 mm, emergent from the column and nearly equaling the petals. Fruits 7-8 mm diam., glabrous, reticulate-veined; mericarps 5-6 mm high, subapically apiculate, minutely winged basally; seeds obscurely striate.

description: Shrubs ca. 1.5 m tall, the stems densely and roughly stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades mostly 7-10 cm long, broadly ovate and often 3-lobulate, subtruncate to deeply cordate, crenate to subentire, rounded-acute, minutely stellate-pubescent above, densely so beneath, discolorous; petioles ¼-¾ the length of the blades; stipules 4-5(-10) mm long, subulate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or in a terminal raceme of 2-6 flowers; pedicels 2.5-4.5 cm long; involucellar bracts 8-10, narrowly triangular, 6-12 mm long, stellate-pubescent; calyx 1.5-1.8 cm long, stellate-pubescent; corolla tubular, 3-4 cm long, yellowish, externally sparsely pubescent; androecium ca. 2 cm long, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles and stigmas exceeding the androecium, shorter than the petals. Fruits 16-19 mm diam., oblate-depressed, 5- or 10-ribbed, retrorsely scabrid (hairs 0.5 mm long), the mericarps 8-10 mm high, woody, dorsally ridged.

description: Dioecious or monoecious shrubs or trees up to 35 m tall; latex yellowish, turning brown or reddish. Leafy twigs 1-6(-8) mm thick, either with yellow to whitish, short appressed hairs, or with very short, patent hairs intermixed with distinctly longer, appressed to patent hairs, lenticels scattered. Leaves elliptic to oblong to lanceolate, usually broadest near the upper end, more or less inequilateral 7-48 cm long, 3-20 cm broad, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, acuminate, acute to obtuse to emarginate at the base, entire to repand to denticulate, glabrescent above, sparsely to rather densely subsericeous to substrigose, or hirsute on the veins, otherwise puberulous to subglabrous beneath; veins nearly plane above, prominent beneath, 13-26 pairs of secondary veins, most tertiary veins parallel; petioles 2-15(-30) mm long; stipules 5-15(-25) mm long, yellow to greyish sericeous to hirsute. Staminate inflorescences 3-6(-10) mm in diameter; peduncle 1-3(-6) mm long; involucre with ca 25-ca 60 deltoid to ovate to triangular, acute (to obtuse), subsericeous bracts in 4-8 series; flowers 10 or more; perianth 0.8-1.1 mm high, tepals free, more or less cucullate, obtuse, yellowish puberulous; filaments free, 0.6-1.1 mm long, broadened towards the base or not, anthers 0.3-0.5 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm broad; rarely some hairs present in the centre of the flower. Pistillate inflorescences solitary or accompanied by staminate ones, 4-15 mm in diameter, subsessile to pedunculate; peduncle up to 3 mm long, usually bracteate; involucre with ca 20-90 deltoid to ovate to triangular, acute (to obtuse), subsericeous bracts in 4-10 series; flowers (5-) 10-ca 50; perianth mostly ca 2 mm high, rarely up to 3.5 mm high, entire to shallowly 4-lobed (or 4-dentate), yellow to whitish puberulous to strigose to hispid; ovary laterally partly adnate to the perianth; style 0.5-1.5(-2.0) mm long, usually hairy, stigmas linguiform, 0.7-1.5 mm long, 0.2-0.7 mm broad, acute to mucronate to obtuse. Infructescences 1-2 cm in diameter; fruiting perianth with sparse to dense very short or long yellowish hairs; fruit (8?-) 12-13 × (6?-)8.5-9.5 mm, partly adnate to the perianth; seed 7-8 × 4-5 mm. Flowering. Flowering from August to April.

description: Trees up to 30 m tall; latex creamy. Leafy twigs 1-4 mm thick, bearing few to many very short, patent hairs intermixed with few to many longer, appressed to ascending hairs, sometimes nearly glabrous. Leaves lanceolate to oblong, often broadest near the lower end, slightly to distinctly inequilateral, 6.5-24 cm long, 2-10.5 cm broad, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, acuminate, obtuse to acute at the base, glabrescent above, the lower surface sparsely to densely puberulous to hirtellous to hirsute, the hairs appressed on the costa and the secondary veins, sometimes rugose; costa prominent, the other veins nearly plane above, more or less prominent beneath, (10-) 14-20 pairs of secondary veins, without or with few to many parallel tertiary veins; petioles 4-13 mm long; stipules 4-10 mm long, sparsely whitish to yellow pubescent, subsericeous, or hirsute. Staminate inflorescences 5-10 mm in diameter; involucre with 14-22 deltoid to ovate to subovate, acute to obtuse, whitish to yellow subsericeous bracts in 3-7 series; filaments 0.3-1.5 mm long, anthers (1.2 ?-)2.o-2.5 mm long, 0.3-0.7 mm broad, apiculate; interstaminal bracts 2-4.5 mm long spathulate to oblanceolate, acute to obtuse, hairy outside. Pistillate inflorescences 2-2.5 mm in diameter; involucre with 10-18 reniform to deltoid or ovate, obtuse to acute, whitish to yellow subsericeous bracts in 3-6 series; perianth 2-2.5 mm high, light yellow velutinous; style 0.8-1.0 mm long, stigmas 5-7 mm long. Fruiting perianth subglobose to ellipsoid, 20-23 × 17-19 mm, light yellow velutinous to sericeous (sometimes glabrescent?). Flowering from February to May; fruiting from March to June.

description: Trees up to 25 m tall. Leafy twigs 2-7 mm thick, covered with yellow to brownish appressed to patent, firm hairs often intermixed with much shorter patent hairs, scars of the stipules mostly prominent. Leaves oblong to lanceolate, sometimes broadest near the lower or near the upper end, slightly inequilateral, 11-33 cm long, 4.5-13.0 cm broad, coriaceous to subcoriaceous, acuminate, acute to obtuse (to emarginate) at the base, almost glabrous to puberulous or hirtellous, glabrescent above, appressed-pubescent to hirtellous, often rugose beneath; costa prominent, the other veins nearly plane to somewhat impressed above, prominent beneath, 16-21 (-25) pairs of secondary veins, most tertiary veins parallel; petioles 4-13 mm long; stipules 6-15 mm long, yellow subsericeous. Staminate inflorescences ca 15 mm in diameter; receptacle concave; involucre with 25-35 reniform to deltoid to suborbiculate to ovate to lanceolate, obtuse(to mucronate), yellow sericeous bracts in 6-8 series; filaments o.2-0.4 mm long, anthers ca 2 mm long, 0.4-0.5 mm broad, apiculate, with hairs at the tip; interstaminal bracts 3-8 mm long, lanceolate to linear, hairy outside. Pistillate inflorescences 2.5-3.0 mm in diameter; involucre with 15-28 reniform to deltoid to ovate, obtuse to acute, yellow sericeous bracts in 3-4 series; perianth ca 3 mm high, brownish velutinous, stigmas 7-8 mm long. Fruiting perianth subglobose, at least 15 mm high, brown velutinous. Flowering from May to November.

description: Revised description: Tree, to 35 m tall. Leafy twigs (1-)2-9 mm thick, with yellow to brownish appressed to patent firm hairs, often intermixed with much shorter patent hairs; scars of the stipules mostly prominent. Lamina oblong to subobovate or to subovate, (8-) 10-33 × 3.5-13 cm, slightly inequilateral, (sub)coriaceous; apex acuminate; base acute to obtuse (to subcordate); upper surface almost glabrous to puberulous or hirtellous on the veins; lower surface appressed-pubescent to -puberulous to hirtellous, sometimes slightly rugose; lateral veins 1421 (-25) pairs; tertiary venation largely scalariform; petiole 0.3-2 cm long; stipules (0.4-)l-1.5 cm long, yellow-sericeous, caducous. Staminate inflorescences ca. 0.8-1.5 cm diam., concave; involucral bracts in 68 series, reniform to suborbiculate to ovate to lanceolate, obtuse (to mucronate), yellow-sericeous; filaments (0.05-)0.1-0.4 mm long; anthers ca. 1.5-2 mm × 0.4-0.6 mm, with apical hairs; interstaminal scales (= tepals) 3-8 mm long, lanceolate to linear, hairy. Pistillate inflorescences 0.2-0.3 cm diam.; involucral bracts in 3-6 series, reniform to ovate, obtuse to acute, yellow-sericeous or yellowish to whitish appressed-puberulous; perianth ca. 2-3 mm long, brownish-velutinous to subsericeous; stigmas 7-9 mm long. Fruiting perianth subglobose to ellipsoid, 1-2.2 cm long, brown-velutinous to sparsely appressed-puberulous, sometimes only at the apex.

description: Trees up to 35 m tall; latex white, turning orange to reddish. Leafy twigs 1-3 mm thick, with white or sometimes yellowish, short, more or less appressed hairs. Leaves (elliptic to) oblong to lanceolate, broadest at the middle, or near the lower or upper end, more or less inequilateral, (2.5-)4-13(18) cm long, 1.5-4.5(5.5) cm broad, characeous to coriaceous, acuminate to acute, acute to obtuse (to emarginate) at the base, except for the costa glabrous above, sparsely puberulous to glabrous beneath; the costa prominent, the secondary veins little prominent to impressed, the other veins plane or nearly so, (9-) 15-2o(-23) pairs of secondary veins, without or with few parallel tertiary veins; petioles 3-10 mm long; stipules 2-8(-12) mm long, sparsely to densely appressed-puberulous to -pubescent. Staminate inflorescences 4-8 mm in diameter, juvenile ones globose to subglobose; involucre with 15-35 reniform, deltoid, suborbiculate, ovate, lanceolate or oblanceolate, obtuse, sparsely appressed-puberulous bracts in 4-8 series; filaments 0.4-1.2 mm long, anthers 1.0-1.6 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm broad, apiculate or not, glabrous or with apical hairs, connectives rather broad; interstaminal bracts many, few, or occasionally none, 1-3 mm long, hairy or glabrous outside. Pistillate inflorescences 2-2.5 mm in diameter; involucre with 10-18 reniform to ovate, obtuse to acute, sparsely appressed-puberulous bracts in 3-6 series; perianth 1.5-2.5 mm high, sparsely to rather densely whitish to sometimes yellowish puberulous; style 0.5-1.0 mm long, stigmas (2.5?-) 4-5(-7) mm long. Fruiting perianth ellipsoid 8-9 × 6-7 mm, puberulous on the whole surface or only near the tip; seed 6-7 × 4-5 mm. Flowering probably throughout the year, mainly from September to November.

description: Shrubs 1-2 m tall, the stems densely covered with short (0.3-0.5 mm) glandular hairs and sometimes also with long (2-3 mm) simple hairs. Leaf blades ovate, mostly 4-8(-12) x 2-5 cm (smaller upward), basally cordate, serrate, acuminate, palmately 7-nerved, somewhat discolorous, the upper leaf surface with mostly simple hairs (0.3-0.4 mm long, arched) interspersed with stellate and glandular hairs, the lower surface with soft stellate pubescence; petioles 3- 7 cm long, stipules 4-9 mm long, linear. Flower solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 4-8 cm long; involucellar bracts 7-10, linear or narrowly ligulate, 9-13 x 0.5-1 mm, viscid and ciliate; calyx 6-10 mm long, ciliate, whitish basally with green veins distally; corolla 1.5-2.5 cm long, ciliate on margins of claws, otherwise glabrous, pink or lavender with darker center; staminal column 15-17 mm long, pallid, glabrous, the filaments ca. 1 mm long or subsessile, with inconspicuous staminodes (sterile filaments) at base of column; styles emergent from the column, pink. Fruits 8-9 mm diam., densely pubescent; mericarps 4-5.5 mm high, dorsally rounded.

description: Shrubs 0.5-1 (-3) m tall, the stems stellate-pubescent or often coarsely hirsute with spreading simple and bifurcate (occasionally stellate) hairs 1-2 mm long. Leaf blades mostly 8-18(-21) x 3.5-10(-15) cm, broadly elliptic or oblanceolate (i.e. widest at or above the middle, often lobulate), penninerved, truncate to cuneate, serrate-crenate, more or less acuminate, the upper surface with appressed simple hairs 0.5-2 mm long, the lower surface with scattered simple and stellate hairs often >1 mm long; petioles 1-5 cm long (shorter upward), the uppermost leaves sometimes subsessile; stipules 8-12 mm long, narrowly falcate, ciliate. Inflorescences capituliform or racemose (but the lowermost flowers often solitary), rising above the leaves, the heads terminal, crowded or open, the pedicels 1-9 cm long, subtended by several ciliate, lance-linear bracts 4-7 mm long; the 8-9 involucellar bracts 5-9 x 1-1.5 mm, basally connate, obscurely pubescent or prominently hirsute; calyx 2.5-6 mm long; corolla 6-9 mm long, white to pink. Fruits 6-9 mm diam., subglabrous, longitudinally costate, the mericarps each 3-spined, the spines erect, retrorsely barbed, the central spine 7 mm long, the lateral spines 4-5 mm long, 3-3.5 mm apart at base.

description: Subshrubs or shrubs to 3 m tall, the stems stellate-pubescent with denser lines of pubescence longitudinally, and with glandular hairs especially in the inflorescence, sometimes pilose with simple hairs 2-3 mm long. Leaf blades mostly 6-12 cm long, as wide as long, ovate, oblong, or shallowly 3-lobed, cordate, serrate, acute or acuminate, discolorous, minutely pubescent; petioles 1/3-2/3(-1) times the length of the blades; stipules 5-10 mm long, falcate, recurved. Inflorescence a widely branched viscid panicle, at least the upper parts leafless; pedicels 1-2.5 cm long; involucellar bracts usually 7-9, linear, 5-10 mm long, viscid and ciliate, sometimes dark-pigmented; calyx ca. 6 mm long; corolla 1-2 cm long, pale yellow to yellow-orange; staminal column 4-5 mm long, pallid, glabrous, the filaments 4-5 mm long; styles pallid, glabrous, the stigmas reddish. Fruits 6-7 mm diam., subglabrous, the mericarps smooth or reticulate-veined. Chromosome number, 2n = 112 (Krapovickas & Cristóbal, 1965; Bates, 1967).

description: Subshrubs or shrubs to 2 m tall (to 4 m in Wedel 149), the stems minutely stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades mostly 6-21 x 2-10 cm, elliptic, oblong, or obovate, truncate, crenate-dentate (the margins often ciliate), acute, slightly discolorous, minutely stellate-pubescent; petioles Va the length of the blades or less; stipules 5-9 mm long, subulate. Peduncles axillary, sometimes exceeding the subtending leaves, bearing a dense headlike inflorescence that is actually a condensed raceme; pedicels up to 12 mm long but usually much shorter; involucellar bracts ca. 8, linear, 4-6 mm long, basally gamophyllous; calyx 4-5 mm long; corolla 6-9 mm long, pink; androecium subequal to petals. Fruits 6-8 mm diam.; mericarp body 5 mm high, smooth, each mericarp with 3 retrorsely barbed spines 2.5-5 mm long.

description: Widely branching shrubs or subshrubs 1.5 m tall, the stems sometimes trailing, stellate-pubescent and with some glandular hairs especially on older stems, sometimes also (e.g., Af. Nee 38211, Pedersen 9410) with setae to 3 mm long. Leaf blades mostly 4-8 cm long, 1.1-1.6(-2) times as long as wide, ovate (in well-grown plants sometimes weakly lobulate), cordate, serrate, acute or acuminate, discolorous, soft-pubescent above and beneath; petioles lA-2A the length of the blades in vegetative branches but shorter in flowering branches, the leaves sometimes subsessile; stipules 2-4 mm long, filiform, recurved. Flowers solitary or paired in the leaf axils, sometimes forming a terminal panicle, the pedicels 2-6.5(-9.5) cm long; involucellar bracts 6-7(-9 in Hatschbach 237211), exceeding the calyx, broadly lanceolate or subrhombic (2.5-4 mm wide, rarely narrower); calyx 6-7 mm long, hirsute; corolla (1-)2-2.5 cm long, bright yellow with purple center; staminal column 5-7 mm long, maroon, the filaments 1-2 mm long; styles emergent from the column, glabrous, the stigmas pallid, villous. Fruits 6-8 mm diam., oblate, with appressed barbs along medial costa and lateral margins of mericarps; mericarps 2.5 mm high, smooth or verruculate, essentially glabrous. Chromosome number, 2n = 56 (Bates, 1976, as P. chiapensis).

description: Shrubs 1-2 m tall, the stems slender, glabrescent or with narrow rows of more or less recurved hairs. Leaf blades mostly 5-10(-15) x 2-5 cm, ovate to lanceolate (or subelliptic), widest below the middle, truncate or subcordate, serrate, acuminate, palmately 3-5-nerved, sparsely pubescent (especially on nerves), with tufts of fine hairs (domatia?) in the axils of the principal nerves beneath and often in the axils of the secondary nerves as well; petioles 4-15 mm long, pubescent distally and on adaxial side; stipules 5-11 mm long, linear-lanceolate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or on lateral axillary branchlets, the pedicels slender, 1.5-6 cm long, evenly and minutely pubescent; involucellar bracts usually 6, lanceolate or oblanceolate, 5-8 mm long, sparsely pubescent; calyx 5-6 mm long, sparsely ciliate, sometimes basally pallid; corolla 8-15(-20) mm long, yellow; staminal column 3-6 mm long, glabrous, pallid, the filaments ca. 1 mm long; styles emergent from the column, pallid. Fruits 6-8 mm diam., the mericarp body 5-6 mm high, glabrous, reticulate-veined, the mericarps each with 3 apical spines, the spines 3-6 mm long, divergent, retrorsely barbed, the barbs usually confined to the spines. Chromosome number, 2n = 56 (Krapovickas & Cristóbal, 1965, as P. malvacea); 2n = 112 (Skovsted, 1941, possibly a misidentification of P. communis?).

description: Shrubs 1-2 m tall, the stems glabrescent or with narrow rows of more or less recurved hairs, sometimes with scattered large stellate hairs. Leaf blades mostly 5-10(-15) x 2-5(-6.5) cm, ovate to lanceolate (or subelliptic), usually widest below the middle, truncate or subcordate, serrate, acuminate, palmately 3-5-nerved, sparsely pubescent to glabrate, the lower surface with sparse uniform stellate hairs, lacking tufts of hairs in the nerve axils; petioles 4-15(-40) mm long, with small rigid stellate hairs; stipules 5-11 mm long, linear-lanceolate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1.5-6 cm long, evenly pubescent with minute recurved hairs; involucellar bracts usually 6, lanceolate or oblanceolate, 7-11 mm long, sparsely pubescent; calyx 5-9 mm long, sparsely ciliate, sometimes basally pallid; corolla 12-22 mm long, yellow; staminal column 3-7 mm long, glabrous, pallid, the filaments 1-2 mm long; styles emergent from the column, pallid. Fruits 7-9 mm diam., the mericarp body 6 mm high, glabrous, reticulate-veined, the mericarps each with 3 apical spines, the spines 3-7 mm long, divergent, retrorsely barbed, the barbs sometimes extending onto the central costa of the fruit body.

description: Subarbusto glutinoso 20-90 cm de alto, con xilopodio, porción basal leñosa, corteza parda con grietas longitudinales que dejan ver el súber blanquecino ca. 1 mm espesor; tallos 1 a varios; ramas jóvenes viscosas, con abundantes pelos glandulares 0.2-0.8 mm long., pelos simples tenues y pelos porrecto-estrellados, radio central 0.7-1.5 mm long., a veces escasos; entrenudos bien desarrollados, 9-20 mm long. Yemas axilares 2, la basal florífera; ramas seriales desarrolladas. Hojas herbáceas, viscosas, un poco discoloras, las apicales a veces marcadamente decrecientes. Estípulas reducidas a 4-7 pares de prominencias subuladas, glandulares, 0.4-0.5 mm long., acompañadas de pelos porrecto-estrellados. Pecíolo (1-)3-17 mm long, cilindrico, con más pelos estrellados que el tallo. Lámina ovada, angustiovada o elíptica, 15-65 x 6-32 mm, relación largo: ancho = 1.6-3.1:1, base brevemente atenuada, redondeada o cuneada; ápice obtuso o agudo; borde ligeramente revoluto, ondulado u ondulado-crenado, dientes con lados aproximadamente iguales; haz con pelos porrecto-estrellados multirradiados, radio central robusto (Fig. 5D), frecuentemente también pelos glandulares; envés verde-grisáceo en vivo, con pelos estrellados densos y pelos glandulares entremezclados; 7-11 pares de venas laterales curvado-ascendentes, ángulo de divergencia 30-50°, hundidas en la haz, prominentes en el envés, con pelos porrecto-estrellados y pelos glandulares, perdiéndose cerca del margen y con ramas que se anastomosan en arcos; venas terciarias a veces visibles en el envés, recurvadas con respecto a la vena media; venación menor inconspicua. Hojas floríferas de tamaño decreciente. Flores axilares, solitarias, heterostilas. Alabastro lacrimiforme. Pedúnculo floral (5-) 11-25 (-35) mm long., indumento como el del pecíolo. Profilos nulos. Pedicelo 2-6(-8) mm long., ligeramente más grueso que el pedúnculo. Cáliz (6,5-)8-14 mm long.; tubo calicino 1.5-3 mm long., piloso por dentro, cara externa tomentosa, pelos porrecto-estrellados y frecuentemente pelos glandulares; lóbulos externos ovados, 7-9 nervados, lóbulos internos angustiovados, con bandas de pelos ordenadamente dispuestos antes de los bordes membranáceos, a veces pilosos hasta el borde mismo, mucrón 0-0,3 mm long. Corola rosado-amarillenta (10-)15-21 mm long.; pétalos obovados con la uña pilosa. Corona brevemente fimbriada, lóbulos unidos a los pétalos obovados, 1.5-2 mm long., lóbulos unidos a los sépalos más cortos. Filamentos estaminales amarillos, subulados, 4-7.5 mm long, en flores longistilas, 6-8 mm long, en flores brevistilas; anteras angustio-vadas, a veces sagitadas, 1.5-2.5 x 0.7-1 mm, base emarginada, ápice obtuso, recurvado a la dehiscencia, filamento inserto en una cavidad basidorsal 0,5-0.7 mm long. Ovario ovoide, hirsuto, 1.5-3 mm long., placentas 12-25 ovuladas; estilos cilindricos, glabros o con algunos pelos en la base, 4.5-7.5 mm long, en flores longistilas, 2.5 mm long., excurvos, en flores brevistilas; estigmas 0.3-1 mm long., multirramosos. Frutos ovoides o esféricos, 5-11 mm long.; valvas ovadas, cara externa castaña en seco, tuberculada, con pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares, cara interna amarillenta, glabra, lisa, vena placentaria no prominente. Semillas obovoides, 2.1-2.5 x 0.8-1 mm, lado rafeal recto; exóstoma cónico ancho y breve; rafe linear apenas marcada; cálaza redondeada no prominente; episperma pilosiúsculo, reticulado, aréolas transrectangulares y cuadrangulares pequeñas; arilo 1-1.5 mm long., unilateral, ancho en la base, luego angosto, borde lobulado.

description: Subarbusto 30-80 cm de alto [seg. Urban]; ramas viejas pardas, con grietas longitudinales que dejan ver el súber blanquecino; ramas jóvenes cilindricas, ligeramente estriadas, sin pelos glandulares, con pelos porrecto-estrellados de brazo central robusto, 1-3 mm long., pelos estrellados paucirradiados; ramas 0.4-0.5 mm long, y pelos simples tenues muy cortos. Yemas seriales no observadas. Hojas coriáceas, disminuyen de tamaño hacia el ápice. Estípulas reducidas a prominencias glandulares subuladas, 0.3-0.5 mm long., escondidas en un mechón de pelos porrecto-estrellados. Pecíolo 0-2 mm long., indumento como el del tallo. Lámina foliar angustiovada o elíptica, 10-40 x 5-25 mm, relación largo:ancho ca. 2:1, base redondeada, a veces cuneada o brevemente atenuada; ápice agudo u obtuso; borde plano, a veces apenas revoluto, aserrado-crenado en hojas inferiores, entero en hojas apicales; haz y envés un poco lustrosos, con pelos estrellados densos paucirramosos, 0.4 mm long., los de la haz y venas principales del envés porrecto-estrellados, brazo largo 0.5-0.6 mm long. (Fig. 6A); venas laterales 4-6, impresas en la haz pero formando una delgada cresta en la depresión, prominentes en el envés, ángulo de divergencia 20-40°, perdiéndose cerca del margen, con ramas hacia los dientes en las hojas inferiores. Flores axilares, solitarias, heterostilas. Pedúnculo 5-20 mm long., indumento como el del tallo. Profilos reducidos a prominencias glandulares, subuladas, 0.3-0.5 mm long., escondidas en un mechón de pelos porrecto-estrellados, situados en el ápice del pedúnculo. Pedicelo articulado, 3-10 mm long. Cáliz 8-15 mm long.; tubo calicino 2-2.3 mm long., cara externa densamente cubierta de pelos porrecto-estrellados dorados, cara interna glabra; lóbulos angustiovados, 3-5 nervados, cara externa con indumento como el del tubo, cara interna con pelos simples y largos sobre las venas, bordes internos membranáceos, con pelos densos casi hasta el borde (en los alabastros los pelos se ven de color más claro, y los radios mayores son antrorsos, más o menos adpresos), ápice a veces con mucrón de 1 mm long. Corola color carne; pétalos con la uña glabra; lámina 15-17 mm long. [seg. Urban]. Filamentos estaminales glabros, base soldada 0,5 mm al tubo calicino, 4-5 mm long, en flores longistilas, 8 mm long, en flores brevistilas [seg. Urban]; anteras angustiovadas, base emarginada, ápice obtuso, recurvado a la dehiscencia, 1.5-1.7 mm long. Ovario ovoide, 2-3 mm long., hirsuto, multi-ovulado; estilos cilindricos, glabros, 4.5-6 mm long, en flores longistilas, 2 mm long, en flores brevistilas [seg. Urban]; estigma penicilado, ca. 1 mm long. Frutos y semilla no observados, descripción según Urban: frutos globosos, 6-7 mm diám.; valvas ovadas, obtusas, cara externa granuloso-tuberculada, con pelos breves hirsutos, cara interna blancoamarillenta. Semillas oblongo-cilindráceas, ligeramente curvadas, 2.3 x 0.7 mm; exóstoma apenas prominente; cálaza no prominente; episperma reticulado; arilo unilateral, blanquecino en seco, más corto que la semilla.

description: Funiculus semimetralis; rami homotini pilis tenuis sim-plicibus obsitis, ceterum pilis stellaris intermixtis. Folia patentia, chartacea, ovata vel elliptica, crenata. Flores solitaria axillares. Fructus tuberculatus. Semina reticulata, minute pilosiuscula; arillo angusto.

description: Subarbusto erecto, ca. 50 cm de alto, tallos 2.5 mm diám.; ramas jóvenes densamente vestidas con pelos simples tenues, pelos estrellados y porrecto-estrellados, radio central 0.5-0.7 mm long.; entrenudos bien desarrollados, 15-20 mm long. Yemas axilares 2, la basal florífera; ramas seriales desarrolladas. Hojas patentes, cartáceas. Estípulas reducidas a 2-3 pares de prominencias glandulares acompañadas de pelos porrecto-estrellados. Pecíolo semicilíndrico 4-15 mm long., canaliculado en la cara superior, indumento como el del tallo, con mayor cantidad de pelos estrellados. Lámina ovada, angustiovada o elíptica, 21-60 x 9-24 mm, relación largo:ancho = 2.2-2.8:1, base cuneada, brevemente atenuada o redondeada; ápice obtuso; borde plano crenado; haz con pelos porrecto-estrellados multi-rradiados de base esférica (Fig. 5C); envés con pelos estrellados densos; 8-11 pares de venas laterales alternas o subopuestas, las básales rectas, luego curvado-ascendentes, ángulo de divergencia 25-35°, dando 1-2 ramas hacia los bordes, con pelos porrecto-estrellados cortos; venas terciarias a veces notables en el envés; venación menor inconspicua. Flores axilares, solitarias. Pedúnculo 17-28 mm long., indumento como el del tallo. Profilos nulos. Pedicelo 9-15 mm long., ligeramente más grueso que el pedúnculo, articulación conspicua. Cáliz 10-12 mm long., tomentoso, con pelos porrecto-estrellados cortos; tubo calicino ca. 2 mm long., glabro por dentro; lóbulos angustio vados, acuminados, los internos con bandas de pelos ordenadamente dispuestos antes de los bordes membranáceos, mucrón 1 mm long. Corola 12-13 mm long., color salmón, venas purpúreas en seco. Corona con borde superior laciniado, lóbulos unidos a los pétalos angustiovados, 1-2 mm long. Filamentos estaminales subulados, soldados 0,5 en la base al tubo calicino, glabros, 4-6,5 mm long.; anteras ovadas, 1.2-1.4 x 0.6-1 mm, base anchamente emarginada, ápice obtuso no recurvado a la dehiscencia, filamento inserto en una cavidad basidorsal 0.5-0.6 mm long. Ovario ovoide, 2-2.7 mm long., hirsuto, placentas 10-26 ovuladas; estilos cilindricos, glabros, 3.5-6 mm long.; estigma ca. 30 ramas, 0.4-1 mm long. Frutos ovoides, 5-10 mm long.; valvas ovadas, cara externa tuberculada, pelos porrecto-estrellados 1 mm long., cara interna amarillenta, glabra, lisa, vena placentaria no prominente. Semillas obovoides, 2-2.3 x 0.8-1 mm; exóstoma hemisférico, romo; rafe linear apenas visible; cálaza obtusa, no prominente; episperma pilosiúsculo, reticulado, aréolas más o menos cuadranglares; arilo 1-1.5 mm long., unilateral, angosto.

description: Plant flowering over 1.5 m high. Leaves rosulate, 5 dm long, sparsely and minutely brown-lepidote; sheaths elliptic, large; blades ligulate, broadly rounded and apiculate, 7 cm wide, green, concolorous. Scape erect, stout; scape-bracts erect, densely imbricate, the lowest foliaceous, the highest broadly elliptic, castaneous when dry, the acute apex apparently green. Inflorescence lax, amply tripinnate, nearly 6 dm long, wholly red except for the petals, castaneous when dry; primary bracts broadly ovate, acute, to 6 cm long, slightly exceeding the naked flattened bases of the branches, obscurely punctulate-lepidote; branches spreading, to 17 cm long, subdense; spikes and flowers more or less deflexed-secund, spikes few-flowered; rhachis slender, slightly geniculate. Floral bracts broadly elliptic, obtuse, cucullate, ecarinate, about equaling the sepals, subchartaceous when dry, nerved, wholly exposing the rhachis; flowers suberect; pedicels stout, 4 mm long. Sepals elliptic, obtuse, 21 mm long, connate for 5 mm, like the bracts; petals pale olivaceous, high-conglutinate, bearing 2 dentate scales, the blades elliptic, 2 cm long, exceeding the stamens.

description: Plant flowering nearly 5 dm high. Leaves to 45 cm long, obscurely lepidote; sheaths ovate, castaneous beneath; blades ligulate, acute, 25 mm wide. Scape erect, slender; scape-bracts erect, very densely imbricate, foliaceous but the highest bright red. Inflorescence laxly bipinnate, 12 cm long; axis glabrous, sulcate; primary bracts very broadly ovate, bright red, very obscurely lepidote, the lower ones long-acuminate, exceeding the spikes, the upper apiculate, shorter than the spikes; spikes short-stipitate, ellipsoid, compactly 3-5-flowered, rhachis short but distinct. Floral bracts oblong-lanceolate, broadly acute, 16 mm long, exceeded by the sepals, carinate toward apex, glabrous, chartaceous, strongly nerved; flowers subsessile. Sepals equally subfree, oblong-lanceolate, broadly acute, 18 mm long, carinate, glabrous, nerved; petals ligulate, obtuse, 20 mm long, yellow, bearing 2 triangular scales well above the base; stamens included, about equaling the style.

description: Small tree covered with spreading hairs 0.2-0.4 mm long on young branchlets, petiol(ul)es, and raches, and to 1 mm long on the perules of the terminal buds. Leaflets (sub)coriaceous, beset with hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long at base above, densely pubescent below with hairs 0.2-0.5 mm long. Lower part of flowering rachis pubescent like young branchlets, upper part glabrous, like the pedicels.

description: Usually a shrub or small tree (1-)2-12 m tall with the trunk to 10 cm in diam, (two records; to 20 cm according to Hassler 416); branchlets 4-7(-9) mm thick, green- or brown-reddish-grayish, shining when young, perules of terminal buds densely pubescent with tawny hairs. Leaves alternate, imparipinnate, occasionally the terminal leaflet lacking, 3-jugate, occasionally some 1-, 2-, or 4-jugate, sometimes 1-foliolate just below inflorescence, with stalked sometimes shifted leaflets, often (broadly) elliptic or subcircular, 11-34(-39) × 10-25 cm; petiole (semi-)terete, slightly canaliculate, strongly ribbed and sometimes subwinged, (2-) 3-10(-13) cm long and 0.1-0.3 cm thick; rachis 1.5-14 cm long, the interspaces 1.5-6 cm, strongly ribbed like the petiole, continuing beyond the upper pair of leaflets without joint, but occasionally the uppermost interspace doubly articulate; terminal petiolule (0-) 1-7 mm long, sometimes to 20 mm long in upper leaves; lateral petiolules inserted at 45-90°, 2-10 mm long; leaflet blades often (narrowly) elliptic or oblong, sometimes slightly (ob)ovate, 4-18 × 2-5.4(-6.5) cm, occasionally some smaller, attenuate and unequal at base, obtuse or rounded at apex, the very tip emarginate, margin revolute and often slightly undulate-crenulate, the blade dull green, much paler beneath, venation slightly brochidodromous to subcamptodromous, principal veins prominulent above, prominent beneath, midvein (occasionally slightly) impressed above. Racemes nearly always solitary, terminal, erect, flexuose, 30-50 × 2-4 cm, with numerous flowers developing in basipetal fashion soon flowering all together; peduncle mostly absent, or obsolete; rachis 2-4 mm thick at base; bracts depressedly triangular, ca. 0.2-0.9 mm long (basal bracts rarely to 1.5 mm) and ca. 1 mm broad, subglabrous; pedicels at anthesis inserted at 90°, (5-)6-17 (in fruit to 18) mm long and 0.7-1.1 mm thick, (sub)glabrous; bractlets 2, transversely or occasionally obliquely inserted 1/3 to mostly 1/2 from base of the pedicel, occasionally higher, alternate or rarely subopposite, rarely beset with glandular hairs at the margin. Flowers 8.5-11 mm in diam.; calyx 5-toothed with apert or valvate to subquincuncial aestivation, 0.5-1(-1.7) mm long; teeth at anthesis occasionally not overlapping, depressedly triangular, 0.2-0.5(-1.4) × 1.1-1.5 mm, obtuse, very thickly coriaceous, beset with few hairs 0.05 mm especially at margin, otherwise glabrous; petals subvalvate, adnate to the gynophore, 3.8-5 × 1.9-2.7 mm, inflexed at tip through 0.3-0.5 mm, thickly coriaceous, bordeaux, the upper side carinate towards tip and slightly or obsoletely impressed, glabrous, venation parallel to slightly actinodromous, the nerves branched towards tip, the median nerve thicker; filaments subulate, slightly flattened towards base, 3-4.8 mm long and 0.5-0.8 mm thick, thick, purplish, glabrous; anthers ovoid, 1.5-2.8 × 0.7-1.5 mm, frequently 1.5 × 1.2 mm, dark ochrous or yellow, with internal gland usually not observable externally; disc 0.5-1.1 mm high and 1.8-3.5 mm in diam., irregularly plicate, glabrous; carpels inserted on a gynophore (0.4-0.5 mm in diam.), 1.1-1.6 mm high, projecting 0.5-0.8 mm beyond the disc, brown-violet, with discharging internal glands, glabrous; ovules 2, superposed; style inserted below tips of carpels, clavate or terete, 0.4-0.8 mm long and 0.5-0.8 mm thick, the free part 0.3-0.7 mm, glabrous; stigma clavate, 0.2-0.4 mm long, green. Mericarps 8-13 x 6-8 mm, dorso-apically blunt usually with an angle of ca. 90°, truncate or slightly convex at apex, shortly mucronate at the very tip, punctate with glands, glabrous, externally wrinkled longitudinally at 90° to the nerves, loculicidally dehiscent up to the dorso-apical angle; mericarps receding from the axis when ripe; axial part of endocarp persistently connected with the immature seed; seeds 1 or rarely 2 per mericarp, kidney-shaped, 7-10 x 4-6 x 3-5 mm, with flattened base and with curved apex ca. 0.2-0.5 mm, dorsally slightly keeled or doubly keeled, testa thinly coriaceous, very dark brown, shining, externally finely colliculate, with flat, irregular roundish collides ca. 0.03 mm long, hilum just below apex, 2.5-3.5 × 1-1.5 mm; embryo ochrous, cotyledons usually ± unequal, ears 0.8-1.2 mm long, radicle conical, 0.8-1.3 × 0.5-0.8 mm and often totally enclosed, plumule obsolete, to 0.2 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Kaastra, Roelof C. 1982. A monograph of the Pilocarpinae (Rutaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 33: 1-198.

description: Subshrubs 0.5-1 m tall, the stems minutely stellate-pubescent, the hairs often appressed. Leaf blades mostly 9-18(-28) x 2.5-7.5(-10) cm, elliptic to oblanceolate or obovate, sometimes subrhombic, penninerved, basally cuneate or narrowly truncate, serrate, acuminate, minutely stellate-pubescent, sometimes subglabrous on upper surface; petioles 0.5-7 cm long (shorter upward); stipules 6-16 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, erect. Inflorescences on long leafless peduncles, open racemes or condensed heads, the pedicels (or groups thereof) subtended by stipuliform bracts, each pedicel 0.5-1 (-5) cm long; involucellar bracts 8-10, basally gamophyllous, 8-10(-14) x ca. l(-3) mm, minutely pubescent, hirsute (hairs 1-2 mm long) or rarely glabrous; calyx 3-6 mm long, largely concealed by involucel, sparsely pubescent; corolla up to 12 mm long, white or pink. Fruits 6-9 mm diam., essentially glabrous, longitudinally costate, the mericarp body 6-9 x 3-4 mm, 3-spined, the spines 4-7 mm long, retrorsely barbed, the lateral spines 3-4 mm apart at base.

description: Shrub or small tree to 7.5 m tall; branchlets 3-7 mm in diam., dull grayish- or reddish-brown; perules of terminal buds often ampulliform and rather abruptly ending in a long, blunt-pointed tip. Leaves alternate, usually crowded at tip of branchlets, 3-foliolate, occasionally some 1-foliolate, or imparipinnate 1-jugate, with stalked leaflets, subcircular or obovate when 3-foliolate, 6-18(-27) × 5-17 (-25) cm; petiole semiterete, strongly ribbed, slightly winged or not, 1.5-7 cm long and 0.1-0.2 cm thick, wings to 0.1 mm broad; rachis, if any, 1-4(-5.5) cm long; petiolules 0-5 mm long, of terminal leaflets to 27 mm; leaflet blades elliptic, subovate, or occasionally oblong, 3.5- 10(- 17) x 1.5-5.5(-8) cm, lateral leaflets unequal at base, rounded or obtuse at apex, the very tip emarginate, margin thick and re volute; leaflet blades shining above, dull and pale below, (densely) pilose on both sides, venation brochidodromous-camptodromous, prominent, midvein plane above. Racemes solitary, subterminal, erect, 10-30 cm long and 3-6 cm wide, with numerous flowers developing in basipetal fashion and soon all flowering together; peduncle absent or obsolete; rachis 2(-4) mm in diam, at base, (densely) pubescent with thin, spreading hairs 0.1-0.4 mm long; bracts broadly triangular, 0.7-1.1 × ca. 1 mm; pedicels inserted at 60-90°, indument like that of the rachis; bractlets 2, alternate, subobliquely inserted just below the calyx. Flowers ca. 9-11 mm in diam.; calyx 5-toothed or 5-lobed, ca. 0.8-1.2 mm high; lobes or teeth subvalvate, some of them overlapping or not, depressedly ovate or roundish, (thickly) coriaceous; petals subvalvate, 3.5-4.5 × 2.2-3 mm, apex inflexed through 0.4-0.6 mm, coriaceous, keeled and impressed above, venation parallel to acrodromous, nerves branched towards margin, median nerve thicker; filaments adnate at base to the disc, subulate, 2.5-3.5 mm long and 0.4-0.7 mm thick, glabrous; anthers ovoid, ca. 1.4-1.7 × 0.9-1.5 mm, pale yellowish, with an oblong, subapical dorsal gland; disc as high as the ovary, ca. 0.7-1.2 mm high and ca. 2.4(-4) mm in diam., (occasionally strongly) plicate, surrounding the base of the filaments, (sub)glabrous, tuberculate in fruit; carpels adnate to the disc, 0.7-1 mm high, punctate with very small outlets of internal glands; ovules 2, superposed; style inserted among the tips of the carpels, clavate or terete, 0.3-1 mm long and 0.5 mm thick, free for 0.2-0.6 mm; stigma capitate, 0.2-0.3 × 0.50.6 mm. Mericarps obovate or subelliptic in outline, 9-13 × 17-10 mm, the ventral axis rather straight, dorso-apically rounded, slightly mucronate or rounded at very apex, with glands 0.2 mm in diam., glabrous or rarely shortly hairy towards tip, sterile mericarps usually hairy at tip, dehiscent up to 1/2-2/3 below tip; seed 1 per mericarp, kidney-shaped, 7-8.2 × 5-6.5 × 4.5-5 mm, flattened at base, rounded and slightly keeled on the back, obtuse at apex, testa black brown, shining, finely colliculate with collides 0.05 mm in diam., wrinkled when immature; hilum tear-shaped; cotyledons ± unequal with ears 1 mm long, radicle 11.2 mm long, plumule 0.1 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Kaastra, Roelof C. 1982. A monograph of the Pilocarpinae (Rutaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 33: 1-198.

description: Perennial herb with many dichasial branches 8-25 cm long forming short vegetative stems during period of dormancy. Leaves and stems slightly scabrid. Leaves sessile, linear, 5-25 x 0.5-3 mm, with acuminate apex. Flowers terminal on pseudodichotomous branches, subtended by bracts similar to leaves. Calyx 2-3 mm long, divided almost to base, lobes with strong midrib and scarious margins. Corolla 2 mm long, white, the lobes rounded, one-third the length of the tube, villous in throat. Stamens dorsi-fixed, inserted above the middle of the corolla tube. Base of ovary adnate to perianth. Capsule obovoid with 20-30 seeds per locule. Seeds translucent, 0.3-0.4 mm long, n = 10, 11.
bibliographicCitation: Norman, E. M. 2000. Buddlejaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 81: 1-225.

description: Shrub 2-3 m tall, glabrous except for young petioles; branchlets 2-5 mm in diam., grayish-brown, especially fast-grown branchlets armed with straight, slender spines 0.7-2.5 cm long, which bear flowers and leaves near the base. Petiole semiterete, 2-3 mm long and ca. 0.7 mm thick, not sharply separated from base of blade, minutely pubescent when young with hairs 0.05 mm long; blade narrowly obovate, 2.2-6.5 × 0.6-1.7 cm, attenuate-cuneate at base, rounded at apex, the very tip emarginate or entire, margin subrevolute, the blade subcoriaceous, shining, grayish-green, venation prominulous, costa plane above and prominent below. Inflorescences erect or spreading, to 8 mm long and wide, 1-5-flowered; peduncle to 1 mm long, side-branchlets (sub)opposite; bracts and bractlets ovate to triangular, ca. 0.5-1 mm long; pedicels to 2.5 mm long. Flowers 8-9.5 mm in diam., glabrous; sepals imbricate, overlapping at anthesis, nearly free or connate at base, very broadly ovate, 1-1.7 × 1.2-1.7 mm, the innermost two smaller than the others, rounded to obtuse at apex, coriaceous with papery margins, venation parallel, the nerves branching distally, with a dorsal false midrib; petals imbricate, reflexed, (broadly) elliptic, 3.5-4.7 × 2.5-3 mm, the innermost ones smaller than the others, obtuse to rounded at apex, subcoriaceous with papery margin, dark red, papillose above, venation parallel to actinodromous, the nerves somewhat branching distally; filaments persistent, seemingly inserted on the disc but actually completely surrounded at base by the disc, reflexed, 1 mm long and 0.20.3 mm thick, fleshy; anthers dorsifixed just below middle, versatile, very broadly heart-shaped, 0.7 × 0.7 mm including a mucro 0.05 mm; disc annular to cupshaped, equalling the carpels or lower, becoming 0.8 mm high and 2 mm in diam., fleshy towards tip, rose to dark purplish, smooth or with few protuberances ca. 0.3 mm long; carpels immersed in the receptacle with their lower half, 0.8 mm high including a trigonous apophysis 0.4 mm, the apophyses beset with ca. 3-4 protuberances 0.05-0.3 mm; ovules 2 per loculus; style persistent, inserted on the connate part of the carpels among the apophyses, ca. 0.9 mm long and 0.3 mm thick, projecting 0.3-0.6 mm beyond the apophyses at anthesis; stigma 4-lobed, 0.2-0.3 × 0.4 mm. Fruits 1 per infructescence, (3-)4-locular capsules, stellately-lobed, 0.8-1 × 1-1.2 cm, with glands, glabrous, the exocarp transversely nerved on both sides, the loculi ± obovate in outline, rounded at apex, with a dorsal apophysis 0.5-2 mm long, projecting downward just above the middle, dehiscent septicidally from base up to tip and loculicidally from apex up to the tips of the apophyses; seed 1 per loculus, ovoid, ca. 6 × 3.5 × 3.5 mm, flattened at base, curved at apex, irregularly wrinkled, finely reticulate-colliculate; hilum ca. 0.7 mm broad; embryo 1, cotyledons unequal with ears 0.2-0.3 mm, radicle conical, projecting beyond the ears.

description: Colonial shrub 20-30 cm high, bark dark, branchlets from puberulent to villous with hairs decreasing in density from apex. Bud-scales absent. Stipules dark, persistent: petioles 3.0-4.0(-5.0) mm long, moderately hairy; leaf-blades thin, 1.2-5.5 cm long, 0.7-2.1 cm wide, oblong or narrowly elliptic-oblong; base acute or obtuse; apex acute, obtuse, or rounded; margin plane or slightly revolute, remotely or conspicuously crenate or crenate-serrulate, 2-6 teeth per cm, mucronate; above sparsely and minutely puberulent or glabrous, green; beneath glabrous and yellowish; major veins above and beneath puberulent or with rather long hairs. Flowering material not seen. Fruits solitary; pedicels 3.0-7.0 mm long and puberulent; drupes 10.0-11.0 mm in diam, glabrous, 3-seeded.

description: Shrub usually ca 1.0 m tall, occasionally treelike, up to 9.0 m tall, evidently evergreen. Young stems usually light-colored and always pubescent, other bark usually dark with less or no pubescence, leaf-scars prominent. Bud-scales absent. Stipules 3.0-4.0 mm long, pubescent, persistent or caducous. Petioles (2-)4-9(-13) mm long with moderate to moderately heavy amounts of longish hairs. Leaf-blades coriaceous with rare exceptions, 1.9-8.5(-13.0) cm long, (0.7-)0.9-3.2(-4.0) cm wide; generally elliptic but may tend toward or actually be oblong, lanceolate, or obovate; ca 2.5-3.0 (or slightly more) times longer than wide; apex acute to acuminate; base cuneate or less commonly rounded; margin plane or revolute, crenate or serrate, usually remotely so, with 3-6(-8) teeth per cm, usually mucronate; above and beneath glabrous (most frequently) or with a moderate amount of mostly erect hairs which are often longer and coarser beneath than above; midrib beset with hairs usually greater in amount than the epidermis and secondary veins less hairy or glabrous, secondary veins 6-10(-13) pairs. Inflorescence a sessile umbel with l-5(-10) flowers; pedicels at anthesis 3.0-8.0(-11.0) mm long; flowers 5-merous; floral cup (1.0-) 1.5-2.0 mm long and 2.0-(-3.0) mm broad, sepals (1.3-)1.5(-2.0) mm long, (0.7-)l.0(-l .7) mm wide; external floral parts with sparse to moderate amounts of usually erect and rather long and coarse hair; petals 1.0 mm long and wide (occasionally up to 1/3 mm longer and broader), marginally somewhat scalloped with margin tapering at about a 45° angle into a short (ca ¼ mm long) but definite claw which tapers into a rather blunt base (neither definitely acute nor definitely obtuse), notch ca 1/3 the length of the petal and usually broad at the apex and tapering at ca a 45° angle to an acute or almost acute base; filaments and anthers (0.5-)0.7-1.0 mm long, filament with broad base, anther enclosed by petals and having an apicule; ovary glabrous and 3-carpellate, style ca 1.0-1.25 mm long with a 3-lobed apex reaching anywhere from base to apex of sepals. description: Apparently shrubs or small trees. Branchlets alternate; pubescent with antrorse appressed gray or tawny hairs; leaves alternate, not crowded. Bud-scales absent. Stipules subulate, 3.0-4.0 mm long, pubescent, caducous. Petioles 4.0:41.0 mm long, pubescent. Leaf-blades lanceolate or broadly lanceolate, (3.0-)4.0-6.0(-8.0) cm long, (9.0-)12.0-20.0(-27.0) mm wide; base rounded or broadly cuneate; apex slightly acuminate (the acumen ca 1.0 cm long, sharp); margin glandular-serrulate; above green and glabrous; beneath slightly paler and nearly glabrous or sparsely antrorse-appressed pubescent on the larger veins; secondary veins 8-10 pairs. Fruiting pedicels 10.0-13.0 mm long or longer; drupes apparently globose, only very young ones seen.

description: Shrub or small tree up to 10 m but usually smaller, evidently evergreen. Stems with light-colored or yellowish antrorse-appressed hairs usually dense terminally becoming moderately abundant or even sparse with age. Bud-scales absent. Stipules 2.0-4.0(-5.0) mm long, pubescent, caducous or persistent but usually a few persist. Petioles 7.0-18.0(-25.0) mm long, pubescent. Leaf-blades (2.0-)3.3-9.0(-14.0) cm long, l.l-3.5(-4.5) cm wide, elliptic to oblong or lanceolate; base cuneate to rounded; apex mostly acuminate with an acumen up to 10 mm long or sometimes acute; margin from plane to revolute but most often the latter, crenate usually or serrate and mostly remotely so, 3-6(-7) teeth per cm, mucro rather long and tapering to a blunt tip; above and beneath usually glabrous but in some cases a few scattered longish hairs or even a moderate amount beneath, above from light to dark olive green, beneath somewhat paler; midrib above and beneath beset with more or less moderate amounts of longish hairs, secondary veins usually with somewhat less, hairs erect above and antrorse-appressed beneath, veins yellowish or sometimes reddish brown and prominent beneath, secondary veins 6-11 pairs. description: Shrub 1.0-2.0 m tall. Bark dark or reddish. Branchlets densely pubescent. Bud-scales lacking. Petioles stout, 2.0-5.0 mm long; leaf-blades 3.2-8.0(-9.2) cm long (averaging ca 6.0 cm), (1.9-)2.1-5.0(-6.3) cm wide (averaging ca 3.8 cm), usually oval or broadly elliptic, less frequently elliptic or obovate, 1.3-1.7(-1.8)times longer than wide (averaging ca 1.5); base rounded; apex rounded, retuse, acute, and rarely mucronate; margin plane, irregularly serrate with 4-6(-8) teeth per cm usually somewhat obscured by pubescence; above densely covered with long, coarse, villous hairs; beneath lighter-colored and with greater amount of hairs than above; veins conspicuous, 5-10 pairs of secondary veins on each side of midrib. Inflorescence an umbel with 5-10 flowers; peduncles up to 12.0 mm long or rarely absent; pedicels 2.0-10.0 mm long with 10.0 mm being rare and 4.0 mm frequent; flowers 5-merous; floral cup campanulate, 1.0-2.0 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm broad; sepals 1.5-2.0 mm long, 1 mm wide; petals enclosing anthers, ca 1.0 mm long, slightly wider, apical notch broad, base abruptly narrowed; filaments ca 0.3-1.0 mm long, anthers nearly 1.0 mm long; ovary glabrous, 3-celled, style 1.0 mm long and extending to about the upper margin of the floral cup, stigma 3-lobed. description: Shrub 1.0-2.0(-7.0) m tall; leaves crowded, young herbage densely pubescent with brownish hairs. Bud-scales absent. Leaf-blades (3.0-)4.0-6.0(-11.0) cm long, (1.2-)1.7-2.5)-4.2) cm wide, narrowly abovate to oblance-oblong, rarely lance-ovate, base rounded-to broadly cuneate, apex obtuse to slightly acutish and occasionally very shortly denticulate (acumen only 3.0-5.0 mm long); margin strongly revolute, remotely crenate, teeth mucronate; above glabrous, dark green and shiny, midrib pubescent or rarely glabrous and tertiary veins deeply indented; beneath glabrous or minutely pubescent or occasionally even tomentose, paler than above, midrib and secondary veins pubescent and prominent, secondary veins (6-)8-11 pairs. description: Shrub (0.5-)2.5-6.0 tall, stem pubescence decreasing from apex to end of leaf-bearing portion, older bark glabrous. Bud-scales absent. Stipules subulate (2.0-)3.0-4.0 mm long, rather persistent. Petioles ca 2.0 mm long (4.0-11.0 in the type collection, however), pubescent, purplish-brown above and greenish and buffy beneath. Leaf-blades usually thick or firmly membranaceous, 4.513.2 cm long, (1.3-)1.5-4.0(-4.6) cm wide; elliptic or lance-elliptic (rarely oblong-elliptic), (1.9-)2.15-3.8(-4.7) times longer than broad; base mostly cuneate but sometimes somewhat rounded; apex with slender acumen up to 1.5 cm long; margin usually plane but sometimes revolute, mostly crenate but also serrate, 3-7 teeth per cm, mucro present or absent on individual teeth; above and beneath glabrous and shiny, above dark or gray-green, beneath almost always paler than above and usually somewhat yellowish, brownish, or reddish; veins above impressed and usually glabrous, beneath raised and prominent, pubescence more abundant on veins of young than old leaves and more on midrib than on secondaries, usually pale-colored but also reddish or brownish; secondary veins ca 8 pairs. description: Young branches sparsely to densely appressed puberulous or pubescent at first, soon becoming glabrous, mid- to dark brown, sometimes with a few pale lenticels, less frequently greyish. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate or rarely a few trifoliolate, (1.5-)3-15(-25) cm long; petiole and rhachis narrowly winged or at least broadened laterally below insertion of leaflets, usually glabrous, less frequently sparsely to moderately puberulous or short pubescent; petiolule 1-2(-3) mm long or leaflets sessile. Leaflets (3-)5-11(-15) pairs, usually oblanceolate, less frequently obovate, cuneiform, spathulate, elliptic, oblong or lanceolate, apex acute, obtuse, rounded or truncate less frequently attenuate, base usually acute, cuneate, or attenuate, rarely asymmetric and then acute to truncate, usually rather coriaceous, (2.4-)5-10(-14.2)[7.6] cm long, (1.1-)2-4(-6)[2.9] cm broad, basal leaflets usually smaller, terminal leaflet often much larger, usually glabrous, less frequently scattered to uniformly pubescent on lower surface and midrib above, often obscurely glandular-punctate and -striate; venation usually brochidodromous, midrib flat or slightly prominent; secondaries 5-10(-13) on either side of midrib, ± straight for most of their length or arcuate, parallel or convergent; intersecondaries short to long and prominent. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious; inflorescence axillary often in axils of fallen leaves, 0.5-2.5(-7) cm long, few- to many-flowered often umbellate or fasciculate, less frequently reduced to a little-branched and few-flowered thyrse, puberulent, pubescent or glabrous; pedicel (1-)2-5(-8) mm long. Calyx usually rotate, less frequently patelliform, (0.5-) 1-1.5 mm long, calyx lobes (3-)4-5, free or united to !4 length, ovate to suborbicular, apex acute, obtuse or rarely attenuate, pubescent to glabrous, ciliate. Petals (3-)4-5, imbricate, (2.5-)3-5(-5.5) mm long, (1-)1.5-3 mm broad, ovate, lanceolate, elliptic or oblong, apex acute to obtuse or rounded, usually glabrous but occasionally sparsely pubescent on one or both surfaces rarely ciliate. Staminal tube broadly cyathiform, 1.5-3 mm long, (1.5-)2-3.5(-4) mm broad; filaments usually completely fused or for 3/4 their length, less frequently fused 1/2 way rarely completely free, terminated by 2 lanceolate, acute appendages, outside glabrous or sparsely pubescent, inside glabrous in lower half, densely to sparsely barbate or rarely quite glabrous in upper half; anthers (7-)8-10(-11), (0.7-)0.8-1.2(-1.7) mm long, glabrous or rarely with few hairs on back; antherodes much narrower, not dehiscing, without pollen. Nectary a small annulus fused to base of ovary, 0.1-0.2 mm high, glabrous. Ovary (2-)3(-4)-locular, loculi with 1-2 collateral or oblique ovules, glabrous (Molina 16071 from Guatemala has a few pubescent ovaries); style glabrous; style-head capitate, pileate or discoid, often deeply 3(-4)-lobed. Pistil equalling or exceeding stamens; pistillode much shorter than stamens, containing smaller or vestigial non-functional ovules. Capsule ovoid to globose, sometimes ± trigonous, with or without a stipe 1-2 mm long, smooth, glabrous, 0.7-1.7 cm long (including stipe), (2-)3-valved, valves wrinkling horizontally on drying sometimes strongly reflexed; pericarp 0.5-1 mm thick, leathery; endocarp thin, cartilaginous. Seeds 1-2, collateral or oblique in each valve, 0.5-1 cm long, 0.4-0.7 cm broad, usually flattened dorsoventrally; arillode small, fleshy, extending from micropyle along adaxial surface of seed to the prominent chalaza, fused to seed throughout its length and leaving a broad scar sometimes partially free from the seed at apex; seed coat hard. Embryo with thin, flat, collateral cotyledons; radicle apical, strongly exserted; copious endosperm present.

description: Treelet 3-4 m tall. Stems terete, glabrous or puberulent, lenticellate, striate. Leaves paripinnate; distal process acicular, ca. 2 mm long; leaflets 4 or 6, opposite, obovate, oblanceolate or elliptic, chartaceous, 5.5-22 × 2.5-8.5 (15.2) cm, glabrous, the adaxial with prominent midvein and slightly impressed secondaries, the abaxial surface with prominent brochidodromus venation, the secondary veins straight, forming a strong submarginal loop, tertiary veins reticulate, the apex obtuse to abruptly acuminate, the base asymmetrical, attenuate or obtuse, the margins entire, slightly revolute; petiolules 5-12 mm long, pulvinate at base, glabrous, adaxially canaliculate; rachis 6-8 cm long, terete or nearly so, glabrous; petioles 5-12.5 cm long, terete, glabrous, less often lenticellate, bulbous at base. Thyrses panicle-shaped, 8-20 cm long, terminal or axillary on distal portion of branches; cataphylls acicular, 2-4 mm long, appressed-pubescent, supra-axillary; axes slightly angled, striate or sulcate, puberulent; bracts and bracteoles subulate, pubescent, ca. 1 mm long; dichasia compound or simple toward distal portion of axis; peduncle less than 1 mm long; pedicels 1-1.5 mm long, articulate above the middle. Flower buds angular-ovoid. Calyx 1.5-2.5 mm long, light green, pubescent to pilose, the sepals 1-1.5 mm long, deltate or ovate-deltate, concave, adaxially glabrous; petals white, 4.5-5 mm long, oblong-lanceolate or lanceolate, glabrous except for the ciliate lower margin, obtuse at apex, cuneate at base; appendage as long as the petal, long deltate, abaxially glabrous or sparsely papillate, adaxially hirsute on upper half; disc 5-lobed, glabrous, 0.5-0.7 mm tall; stamens 5, the filaments of equal length, glabrous, 1.2-2.2 mm long, slightly flattened, the anthers oblong, 1.2-2 mm long, apiculate at apex; ovary glabrous or puberulent, conical, the stigma elongate-trigonous, ferruginous-papillate. Fruit ovoid or ellipsoid, ca. 2 cm long, yellow, the pericarp coriaceous, granulose, ca. 0.5 mm thick, the endocarp glabrous. Embryo with cotyledons lying transversely over each other, both of similar size.

description: Scandent shrub, the branches terete, glabrous, lenticellate. Stipules deltoid or subulate, 0.8-2.0 mm long, 0.7-1.0 mm wide, pilose, caducous; petioles (5.0-)6.0-12.0 (-13.0) mm long, 0.9-2.1 mm thick, sparsely strigose, lamina elliptic to ovate-elliptic, sometimes ovate, 5.0-14.0 cm long, 2.0-5.0 cm wide, subcoriaceous, the margins entire, the apex acute or acuminate, the base oblique; venation brochidodromous or seemingly so, sparsely strigose; the midrib prominulous above, prominent beneath, the secondary veins 9-13 pairs; intercostal pubescence absent above, frequently caducous beneath, sometimes becoming entirely glabrous. Flowers in groups (cincinni) of 1-4 (usually 1-2), solitary on the axes of the ultimate inflorescences, the axes 0.0-4.0 mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm thick, decreasing in length towards the apices of the primary inflorescences; peduncles 0.2-2.5 mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm thick, strigose, often resembling an articulated peduncle with the axes of the ultimate inflorescences, the bracts 2.0-3.0 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, subulate to linear, strigose, caducous; pedicels 1.5-2.5 mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm thick, strigose, the bracteoles 0.7-1.4 mm long, 0.2-0.6 mm wide, deltoid or subulate, strigose; sepals ovate or oblong, (4.0-)4.5-5.1(-5.8) mm long, 1.8-3.0 mm wide, tomentellous or lanate; standard 6.0-7.5 mm long, 2.0-3.5 mm wide, the pouch globose, extending to 2/3 of the length, revolute at the apical portion, barbate at the throat; the wings spathulate, 5.8-6.2 mm long, 3.4-4.0 mm wide, barbate at the base, keel petals 5.0-6.0 mm long, 3.0-4.0 mm wide, the pouch excentric, barbate at the base; stamens 6-7, all fertile, the filaments connate for ½-1/3 of their length, 3.0-3.5 mm long, the anthers subglobose, 0.8-1.0 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm wide; glands 2, 2-3 lobed, ca 0.3 mm long, 0.4 mm wide, glabrous; style 2.8-3.0 mm long, the stigma ca 1.0 mm in diameter; ovary subglobose, 1.0-2.0 mm in diameter, villous, the ovules numerous. Fruit 7.0-9.0 cm long, 1.4-2.0 cm per side; exocarp fleshy, thin (ca 0.5 mm), with a whitish golden-brown velutinous-tomentose pubescence; endocarp cartilaginous, glabrous. Seeds ca 20 per locule, ovoid to globose, 5.0-6.0 mm long, ca 4.0 mm wide, equinate pubescent, the trichomes ca 2.0 mm long.

description: Shrub, the branches terete, slightly lenticellate, densely golden-brown strigose when young, becoming glabrous with age. Stipules subulate, 3.0-6.0 mm long, 1.5-2.0 mm wide, coriaceous, caducous; petioles 3.0-10.0 mm long, ca 1.0 mm thick, very densely golden-brown strigose; lamina broadly elliptic to obovate, sometimes oblong, inequilateral, 5.0-14.0 cm long, 2.0-8-5 cm wide, subcoriaceous, the margins entire, the apex acute to acuminate, the base cuneate to obtuse; venation eucamptodromous, densely golden-strigose pubescent, the midrib plane above, prominulous to prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 6-9 pairs, inserted at angles of ca 70° to midrib; intercostal pubescence very sparsely strigose above, yellowish or greenish-white lanate beneath. Inflorescences terminal and subterminal axillary panicles to 25.0 cm long. Flowers in groups of 1-3, commonly 1-2; peduncles 0.5-3.0 mm long, 0.7-0.9 mm thick, strigose, the bracts subulate to linear, sometimes ovate, 2.0-3.0 mm long, 0.5-1.5 mm wide, strigose, the pedicels 1.8-2.8 mm long, 0.5-1.5 mm thick, strigose, the bracteoles subulate to linear, 1.0-2.0 mm long, 0.4-0.7 mm wide, strigose; sepals ovate or oblong, 4.0-5.5 mm long, 2.0-3.5 mm wide, acute or rounded at apex, lanate along protected portions, strigose along exposed areas; standard 5.0-7.0 mm long, the pouch extending to lA of the length, with the upper half revolute, irregular at apex, barbate at the throat, the wings spathulate, 6.0-6.5 mm long, 2.0-3.0 mm wide, barbate at the base, the keel petals 4.0-5.0 mm long, 3.04.0 mm wide, the pouch extending along 2/3 of the length, barbate at the base; stamens 10-11(-12), 6-7 fertile, staminodes 3-4, the filaments 2.5-3.0 mm long, free for 1/3 of the length, the anthers obovate or oblong, 0.5-0.7 mm long, ca 0.4 mm wide; glands 2, 2-3 lobed, the lobes deltoid, 0.2-0.3 mm per side, glabrous; style 2.5-2.8 mm long, glabrous or slightly villous, the stigma trilobate, ca 0.2 mm in diameter; ovary subglobose, ca 1.0 mm in diameter, barbate pubescent, the ovules numerous. description: Scandent or Subscandent shrub, the branches terete, lenticellate, the young ones densely tomentose, becoming glabrous with age. Stipules caducous (nv); petioles 5.0-25.0 mm long, 0.8-1.2 mm thick, subcanaliculate, tomentose or glabrous; lamina oblong-elliptic to obovate, (3.5-)5.0-15.0 cm long, (2.5-)4.0-8.0 cm wide, chartaceous or subcoriaceous, the margins entire, the apex rounded or acute, the base obtuse to acute; venation eucamptodromous, tomentose to strigose on both surfaces, the midrib prominulous above, prominent beneath, the secondary veins 6-9 pairs; intercostal pubescence absent above, lanate-adpressed to arachnoid when young, frequently becoming glabrous with age. Inflorescences terminal and subterminal thyrses, 7.0-25.0 cm long. Flowers in dichasia of 1-3, arranged ultimately in secondary inflorescences varying from dichotomous dichasia to individual cymules; axes of secondary inflorescences 4.0-7.0 mm long, ca 0.8 mm thick, tomentose, the bracts ovate, 2.0-3.5 mm long, tomentose; peduncles 0.7-2.0 mm long, ca 0.4 mm thick, tomentose; pedicels 1.0-2.0 mm long, ca 0.4 mm thick, tomentose, the peduncular bracts and bracteoles of equal size, 0.8-1.5 mm long, tomentose; sepals ovate or oblong, 2.2-3.5 mm long, 1.2-1.8 mm wide, lanate; standard 3.2-4.0 mm long, 1.2-2.2 mm wide, the pouch globose, extending to ½ of the length, the apex revolute, barbate at the throat, the wings broadly spathulate, 2.8-3.2 mm long, 1.0-1.5 mm wide, barbate at the base, the keel petals 2.7-2.9 mm long, 0.6-1.5 mm wide, sometimes lacking a pouch, glabrous; stamens 8-10, with 6 fertile, staminodes 24, sometimes with knob-like appendages, the filaments 1.0-1.2 mm long, connate to the middle, the anthers oblong, 0.4-0.5 mm long, ca 0.2 mm wide; glands 2, 2-3 lobed, irregular, ca 0.5 mm per side, villous or glabrous; style I.	2-1.3 mm long, slightly villous or glabrous, the stigma trilobate, ca 0.2 mm in diameter; ovary subglobose, ca 0.6 mm in diameter, short-villous, the ovules numerous. Fruit oblong to elliptic, 2.0-3.2 cm long, 1.0-2.0 cm wide; exocarp yellow velutinous-tomentose when young, glabrous when mature. Seeds 6-9 per locule, ovate, ca 4.0 mm long, villous-barbate, the trichomes ca 10.0 mm long.

description: Scandent shrub, the branches terete, lenticellate, lanate when young, becoming glabrous with age. Stipules triangular, 6.0-10.0 mm long, strigulose, caducous; petioles 2.0-8.0 mm long, 0.5-1.0 mm wide, strigose or lanate, sometimes becoming glabrous; lamina elliptic to oblong-elliptic, sometimes ovate or obovate, 5.0-13.0 cm long, 1.0-4.5 cm wide, subcoriaceous, the margins entire or revolute, the apex acute to acuminate, sometimes mucronate, the base obtuse; venation eucamptodromous, slightly strigulose or glabrous above, lanate or strigose beneath, the midrib plane above, prominent beneath, the secondary nerves 10-16 pairs; intercostal pubescence absent above, lanate to adpressed lanate (almost sericeous) beneath. Inflorescences terminal and axillary racemes, or panicles 5.0-10.0 cm long, varying from highly congested to very open (sometimes on the same plant). Flowers in groups (cincinni) of 1-4; peduncles 0.0-5.0 mm long, ca 0.5 mm thick, strigose, the bracts 2.0-6.0 mm long, subulate or triangular, strigose; pedicels 1.0-5.0 mm long, ca 0.5 mm thick, strigose, the bracteoles 1.04.0 mm long, subulate, strigose; sepals ovate or oblong, 3.0-5.0 mm long, 1.5-3.0 mm wide, lanate on protected portions, strigose on exposed areas; 4.5-6.5 mm long, ca 3.0 mm wide, the pouch extending along ½ of the length, barbate at the throat, the keel petals 3.5-5.0 mm long, ca 3.0 mm wide, the pouch extending along 2/3 of the length; stamens 10-11, fertile ones 6-7, staminodes 3-4, the filaments 1.0-2.0 mm long, free for ½ the length, the anthers oblong, 0.4-0.7 mm long, ca 0.3 mm wide; glands 2-3-lobed, trapezoid or rounded, ca 0.4 mm per side, in some cases with short laciniae on the lobes, glabrous; style 1.0-2.0 mm long, glabrous, the stigma trilobate, 0.2-0.3 mm in diameter; ovary subglobose, 1.0-1.5 mm in diameter, densely villous, the ovules numerous. Fruits 3.0-7.0 cm long, 1.0-1.5 cm per side; exocarp thin, velutinous-tomentose or slightly strigose; the endocarp separable from the mesocarp, velutinous-tomentose or partially so, sometimes glabrous. Seeds ovate, barbate pubescent, the trichomes ca 10.0 mm long.

description: Shrub or treelet to 3 m tall; stem densely to sparsely puberulous, with coarse spines to 16 mm long. Leaf blades oblanceolate, 28-61 x 5-11 cm; base short-attenuate or truncate, apex obtuse, margins with 45-65(-75) teeth per side, each to 12 mm long, surfaces between veinlets striate; subepidermal fiber bundles 50-120 cells thick; petioles 6-10 mm long, 5-9 mm thick. Racemes 6.5-16 cm long with 13-20 flowers, erect at first, later becoming deflexed and protruding between leaves; pedicels 15-32 mm long; bracts with free part 4-8 mm long. Calyx lobes narrowly ovate or sometimes ovate, 6.5-9.5 x 3-4.5 mm. Corolla tube 14-20 mm long, lobes very broadly ovate, 6-10 x 6-8 mm, smooth or almost smooth above; staminodes papillose, obtuse-apiculate in center. Filaments 2-3 mm long, anthers 2-3 mm long, apical appendages 1-1.5 mm long. Ovary with 60-80 ovules in 5 or 6 rows, style ca. 2 mm long. Fruit not seen.

description: Shrub or treelet to 2 m, sometimes taller; stem to ca. 5 cm diam., densely to sparsely puberulous, with coarse spines to 11 mm long. Leaf blades oblanceolate to narrowly oblanceolate, 13-55 x 3.5-10 cm, base usually short-attenuate or truncate, apex obtuse or rarely acute, margins with (15-)25-60(-70) teeth per side, each to 6(-11) mm long, surfaces between vein-lets striate; subepidermal fiber bundles 50-120 cells thick; petioles 3-7 mm long, 3-9 mm thick. Racemes 3-7 cm long with 15-35 flowers, erect and crowded, pedicels 2-8.5 mm long; bracts with free part 2-4 mm long. Calyx lobes broadly ovate to ovate, 2.5-4 x 3-5.5 mm. Corolla tube 4.5-7 mm long, lobes very broadly ovate, 3.5-7 x 3.5-6 mm, irregularly bullate above; staminodes smooth or faintly papillose, surface eventually more irregular. Filaments 2-3 mm long, anthers 2-3 mm long, apical appendages 1 mm long. Ovary with 50-90 ovules in 5-7 rows, style ca. 2 mm long. Fruits 20-45 mm diam., sometimes with slightly tapering ends, pericarp thin and brittle, smooth or often faintly pitted. Seeds 5-40(-65), 6-11 (-14) mm long.

description: Shrubs or trees up to 15 m tall; latex yellowish or colorless. Leafy twigs 1-5 mm thick, yellowish to brown appressed-puberulous to hirtellous to (sub)velutinous, usually with uncinate hairs. Leaves (elliptic to) oblong to lanceolate, often broadest above the middle, not or slightly inequilateral, 7-2 2 (-36) cm long, 3-8(-11) cm broad, chartaceous (to subcoriaceous), (acute to) acuminate to caudate, at the base acute to obtuse; margin entire; above glabrous except the costa, sometimes bullate; beneath puberulous to hirtellous on the veins; veins nearly plane to slightly impressed above, prominent beneath, 5-13 pairs of secondary veins, tertiary veins partly parallel; petioles 6-18(-25) mm long, usually with uncinate hairs; stipules 3-8 mm long, appressed-pubescent. Inflorescences turbinate to about fungiform, 4-8 mm high, 4-8 mm in diameter; peduncle 3-7(-13) mm long, shortly brown (sub)-velutinous, often with uncinate hairs; receptacle brown short-velutinous, with or without uncinate hairs; staminate flowers several to many; perianth 1-1.5 mm high, 3-lobed to 3-parted, puberulous, sometimes with uncinate hairs; stamens 3(-2), filaments 0.5-1.5 mm long, narrow or broad, anthers 0.2-0.6 mm long and 0.2-0.8 mm broad, connectives rather narrow, sometimes apiculate; pistillode small, subulate, o.2-0.5 mm long; style 3-3-5 mm long, stigmas 3-4 mm long; bracts ovate to suborbiculate, basally attached or subpeltate, puberulous. Infructescences globose, 2-3 cm in diameter, coronate with the staminate flowers, with sparse or dense uncinate hairs; cotyledons slightly to very unequal. Flowering probably throughout the year.

description: Revised description: Tree, to 15 m tall, or shrub. Leafy twigs 1-5 mm thick, yellowish to dark brown, appressed-puberulous to hirtellous to (sub) velutinous, usually some of the hairs uncinate. Lamina (elliptic to) oblong to subobovate, (2-)7-22(-36) × (1.5-)3-8(-11) cm, not or slightly inequilateral, chartaceous to coriaceous; apex (acute to) acuminate to caudate; base acute to rounded (to subcordate); margin entire, plane to revolute; upper surface glabrous except for the midrib, sometimes ± bullate; lower surface sparsely to densely appressed-puberulous to hirtellous on the veins; lateral veins 5-13 pairs; tertiary venation partly scalariform, the smaller veins plane to prominent beneath; petiole (0.3-)0.6-2(-2.5) cm long, usually with uncinate hairs; stipules 0.3-0.8 cm long, appressed-pubescent, caducous. Inflorescences: peduncle 0.3-0.7(-l .5) cm long, brown-puberulous to (sub)velutinous, often with uncinate hairs; receptacle turbinate to almost fungiform, and 0.4-1 cm diam., brown short-velutinous, with or without uncinate hairs; staminate flowers several to many; perianth 1-1.5 mm long, 3-lobed to -parted, puberulous, sometimes with uncinate hairs; stamens 3 (-2); filaments 0.5-1.5 mm long; anthers 0.2-0.6 × 0.2-0.8 mm; style 3-5 mm long; stigmas 3-7 mm long; bracts ovate to suborbiculate, basally attached or subpeltate, puberulous. Infructescences (sub)globose, 1.5-3.5 cm diam., crowned with the (remnants of the) staminate flowers and usually covered with sparse or short hairs and sparse to dense longer uncinate hairs, greenish or brownish.
