description: Plant flowering to 1 m high. Leaves few in a cylindric rosette, over 6 dm long, covered with minute pale appressed scales on both sides; sheaths very ample; blades ligulate, broadly acute or rounded, apiculate, 10 cm wide, rather densely serrulate, purple toward apex, the apex a stout pungent brown mucro. Scape erect, slender, white-flocculose at anthesis; scape-bracts erect, the lower half as long as the internodes, lanceolate, acuminate, covered with pale appressed scales. Inflorescence contracted, few-branched, or rarely simple, white-flocculose; primary bracts like the scape-bracts, shorter than the spikes or equaling the lowest; spikes stout-ellipsoid, 35-45 mm long. Floral bracts spreading, broadly ovate, acuminate, mucronate, strongly nerved, the lowest to 15 mm long, about equaling the sepals. Sepals ovate, asymmetric, 9-11 mm long including the stout mucro; epigynous tube short.

description: Flowering shoot decurved, 1 m long. Leaves 7 dm long, densely punctulate-lepidote throughout; sheaths elliptic-oblong, 25 cm long, pale brown; blades ligulate, 12 cm wide, laxly serrate with dark spreading teeth 2 mm long. Scape stout; scape-bracts erect, densely imbricate, lanceolate, acuminate to a dark indurate apex, membranaceous. Inflorescence bipinnate, slenderly pyramidal, 4 dm long, finely white-lepidote; primary bracts like the scape-bracts, exceeding the lower spikes; peduncles spreading, slender, complanate, to 5 cm long; spikes subcylindric to ellipsoid, 35 mm long, 10 mm in diameter. Floral bracts broadly ovate with a mucro 2 mm long, nerved at least near the margin, yellow with a dark castaneous median spot, slightly exceeded by the sepals after anthesis, the lower broadly acute, the upper rounded; sepals 5 mm long exclusive of the 1 mm mucro; petals appendaged; ovary subglobose; placentae subapical; ovules obtuse.

description: Plant flowering over 12 dm high. Leaves incompletely known, minutely and inconspicuously appressed-lepidote throughout; sheaths broadly elliptic but only a little wider than the blades; blades ligulate, broadly rounded and apiculate, 7-12 cm wide, entire or sparsely and obscurely serrulate toward base. Scape stout, glabrous. Inflorescence laxly bipinnate or the lowest branches with 2 sessile spikes, glabrous; primary bracts lanceolate, thin, about equaling the lower branches; stipes to 35 mm long; spikes cylindric, 5-8 cm long. Floral bracts broadly ovate, much exceeded by the sepals, bearing a mucro to 4 mm long, even or nearly so, dark castaneous when dry. Posterior sepals elliptic, strongly asymmetric with a lateral wing equaling the terminal mucro, 5 mm long.

description: Plant flowering over 1 m long. Leaves about 9 dm long; sheaths scarcely wider than the blades; blades ligulate, 5-8 cm wide, rounded with a pungent mucro, entire except for a few minute teeth near base, stiffly coriaceous, pale-appressed-lepidote, concolorous. Scape decurved, stout, much shorter than the leaves, white-furfuraceous at first, especially at the bases of the bracts; scape-bracts erect, slightly exceeding the internodes, lanceolate, furfuraceous. Inflorescence hanging down outside the leaf-rosette, many-flowered, laxly bipinnate or the lowest branches occasionally bearing a small second spike at the base of the first, dense only at the apex, 4 dm long, 22 cm in diameter; primary bracts narrowly lanceolate, acuminate, the lower about equaling the spikes; uppermost spikes sessile, the lower on stout angled spreading stalks as long as they, slenderly cylindric, acute, 20-flowered, 4-6 cm long and 23 mm in diameter, subglabrous. Floral bracts erect, ovate, broadly acute with a very short mucro, 15 mm long, about equaling the sepals, coriaceous, strongly nerved, yellow, strongly convex; flowers subsessile, much compressed and bialate, 20 mm long, white. Sepals asymmetric, lance-oblong, 8 mm long with a minute micro; petals acute, 14 mm long, 3 mm wide, lance-oblong, each bearing 2 infundibuliform scales with flaring mouths produced upward along the petal, the scales situated just below the middle of the petal; ovules obtuse.

description: Plant flowering less than 6 dm high. Leaves 12 or more in a broadly funnelform rosette, to 4 dm long; sheaths broadly ovate, 10 cm long, green and densely serrate near apex, elsewhere dark castaneous, brown-lepidote, and entire; blades ligulate, acute, 1-2 cm wide, pale-lepidote, laxly serrate with dark spines to 3 mm long. Scape erect, slender, red, white-lanate, scape-bracts elliptic, spine-tipped, shorter than the internodes. Inflorescence cylindric, very lax except at apex, tripinnate with most of the spikes in sessile fascicles of 3 each, 18 cm long, white-lanate; primary bracts ovate, spine-tipped, exceeding the lowest spikes; spikes sessile, ellipsoid, 2 cm long, 1 cm thick. Floral bracts suborbicular, mucronulate, ca 10 mm long, nerved. Sepals largely exserted above the floral bracts, strongly asymmetric with the large wing exceeding the midnerve, 5 mm long, short-connate, slightly auricled, the lateral ones obtusely carinate with the ovary.

description: Leaves unknown. Scape stout, strongly angled, glabrous; scape-bracts erect, remote, broadly ovate, acute, subglabrous. Inflorescence laxly bipinnate; primary bracts subspreading, broadly triangular, about 3 cm long, equaling or exceeding the axillary spikes, glabrous; spikes remote, sessile, suberect, slenderly ovoid, acute, to 25 mm long. Floral bracts suborbicular, obtuse, minutely apiculate, about 10 mm long, equaling the sepals, strongly convex, rigid, glabrous; flowers strongly compressed. Sepals triangular-ovate, acute, minutely mucronate, asymmetric, wing-carinate, 6 mm long, free; ovary 4 mm long; ovules borne near the top of the cell.

description: Leaves 1 m or longer; sheaths very large, brown, very densely and minutely brown-punctulate-lepidote; blades broadly rounded and emarginate with a subpungent apiculus, to 1 dm wide, rigidly coriaceous, soon glabrous above, densely and minutely pale-lepidote below, serrulate with teeth 1 mm long. Scape shorter than the leaves, green, glabrous; scape-bracts entire, coriaceous, pungent, floccose. Inflorescence bipinnate, of 15-40 spikes; axis floccose; primary bracts like the scape-bracts, equaling or slightly shorter than the spikes; spikes spreading, narrowly ellipsoid to cylindric, 3-5 cm long, three times as long as their stipes, glabrous. Floral bracts very broadly ovate, obtuse with a minute mucro, strongly convex, rigid, even, dark-brown, shiny, shorter than the sepals; flowers 10-12 mm long without the petals. Sepals strongly asymmetric, emarginate, minutely mucronate, of the same texture and surface as the bracts; ovules obtuse.

description: Plant flowering at least 75 cm high. Leaves about 1 m long; sheaths elliptic-ovate, large, densely lepidote with very minute immersed brown scales, brown; blades rounded with a broad apiculate summit, 7-10 cm wide, densely pale-appressed-lepidote throughout but especially below, armed with dark spines 3 mm long but decreasing in size toward the leaf-apex. Scape erect, elongate but much shorter than the leaves, 4-5 mm in diameter, sulcate, soon glabrous; scape-bracts ovate, acute, chartaceous, the upper imbricate or shorter than the internodes. Inflorescence bipinnate with 20-30 spikes; primary bracts very narrowly triangular, shorter or longer than the stipes, entire; spikes all distinctly stipitate, broadly ellipsoid, 2 cm long, the lower about the length of their stipes, the upper distinctly longer, densely tomentose with smoky-ferruginous scales. Floral bracts erect, broadly ovate, obtuse, short-mucronate, 11 mm long, exceeded by the sepals, 12 mm wide, broadly convex, striate toward the apex; flowers strongly compressed. Sepals strongly asymmetric, emarginate, mucronate, 5 mm long, even, rigid, free; petals lance-linear, acute, 8 mm long, each bearing 2 thick scales extending for most of their length and with a very narrow free margin; ovules obtuse.

description: Plant flowering 1.5 m high. Leaves tubular-rosulate (?), to 45 cm long, covered with pale, appressed, dark-centered scales; sheaths elliptic, ample, 20 cm long, entire or slightly serrate near apex, the lower half dark castaneous; blades ligulate, rounded and pungent-apiculate, 4 cm wide, laxly serrate with dark, spreading, 3 mm long spines. Scape erect, slender, soon glabrous; scape-bracts erect, shorter than the internodes, lanceolate, apiculate. Inflorescence laxly subcylindric with short basal branches, 5-7 dm long; axes slender, soon glabrous; primary bracts like the upper scape-bracts, shorter than the axillary branches; branches including spikes 5-10 cm long; spikes subglobose to ellipsoid, few-flowered, 2-3 cm long, white-lanate, exceeding their subtending bracts. Floral bracts broadly ovate, broadly acute or rounded and mucronulate, to 10 mm long. Sepals exserted, strongly asymmetric with a broad wing extending above the midnerve, 6 mm long; petals bearing 2 highly adnate, fimbriate scales; ovary 4 mm high; epigynous tube almost none; placentae apical.

description: Plant flowering over 8 dm high, propagating by stout erect rhizomes. Leaves densely tubular- or funnelform-rosulate, 4-6 dm long, densely punctulate-lepidote on both sides; sheaths large, very broadly elliptic, dark castaneous; blades ligulate, broadly acute, 8 cm wide, subdensely serrate with dark spines 4 mm long. Scape erect, 47 cm or higher, 6 mm in diameter, densely punctulate-lepidote; scape-bracts remote, oblong, acute, 7 cm long (only one seen). Inflorescence elongate, much interrupted; primary bracts spreading or reflexed, like the scape-bract, laxly serrulate, longer than the abortive axillary branches; spikes 2-5 in a corymbose fascicle in each axil, stout ellipsoid, 3 cm long, without any tomentum. Floral bracts suborbicular, pungent-apiculate, slightly shorter than the sepals, obtusely carinate, coriaceous, punctulate-lepidote. Sepals broadly ovate, rounded and mucronulate, 11 mm long; petals appendaged, the blade oblong, obtuse, 7 mm long, yellow; ovary 6 mm long, the epigynous tube minute; ovules caudate.

description: Tree about 20 m tall. Terminal branchlets grayish, glabrous, nitidous, striate-sulcate, markedly quadrangular, compressed, almost ancipital at the ends, puberulent only in very young stage, soon glabrous, sparsely lenticellate, when older strongly tuberculate. Stipules bigeminate, lanceolate-subulate, the proxals 4-5 mm long, the distals 1 mm long, glabrous or puberulent. Leaves simple, opposite, coriaceous. Petiole 6-12 mm long, glabrous or very sparsely puberulous, sulcate above, rounded below, enlarged and embracing at the base. Blades 10-22 cm long, 3-6 cm wide, oblong, narrowed and acute at the apex, attenuate towards the base simulating a long petiole with a decurrent, narrow, marginal limb, minutely and acutely biserrate, the acute, ascending teeth 2-3 mm apart; very pale green, slightly rugose and glabrous above, with impressed, filiform, conspicuous medial and secondary nerves; pale-ochroleucous beneath with yellowish, glabrous and lustrous main nervation, the costa very prominent, striolate, the prominent, secondary nerves 24-28 each side, 3-6 mm apart, parallelly ascending with a divergence angle of 40°-52°, near the margin curving or forking and anastomosing, the tertiary nerves prominent, transversally subparallel, mostly glabrous and very conspicuous, the lesser veins prominulous, minutely reticulate, the alveolae with an appressed arachnoid-lanate, subhyaline-white tomentum. Panicles single and axillary at the end of branchlets, shorter than the leaves, usually 4-8 cm long, the peduncle 1.0-2.5 cm long, like the branching strongly compressed to ancipital, puberulous with sparse, minute, flexuose, pale hairs, the branchlets short, flexuous, supporting one to three flowers, the bracts membranaceous, lanceolate, 1.5-3.0 mm long. Female flowers sessile; calyx pentamerous, expanded 7.58.0 mm in diam, 3.5-4.0 mm long, the lobes triangular-ovate, acute, 2.8-3.0 mm long, about 2 mm wide, almost glabrous inside, sparsely cinereous puberulent outside; staminodia ten, lanceolate, broadening toward the base, glabrous, 1 mm long; anthers about 0.5 mm long, sterile; carpels 3-4, the ovary ovoid-oblong, acute, cinereous-tomentose 1.5-2.0 mm long, the style to 4 mm long, whitish, flexible, moderately curved, glabrous, the medial suture papillose. One to three (to four) follicles developed, about 12 mm long, oblong, acute or subacute, apiculate, densely, minutely crisp-pulverulent lanuginose, cinereous or ochroleucous, the immature seeds reddish, ellipsoid, about 3 mm long, usually two developing; the disc minutely densely cinereous-tomentose.

description: Plant flowering 1-1.5 m high. Leaves many in a dense rosette, 5-8 dm long; sheaths oblong, to 20 cm long, 12 cm wide, dark castaneous, covered with small appressed brown scales, serrulate toward apex; blades linear, 3-4 cm wide, contracted into a stout involute spine 2 cm long, densely pale-lepidote beneath, soon subglabrous above, laxly serrate with dark antrorse spines to 6 mm long. Scape erect, about 1 cm in diameter, flocculose; scape-bracts erect, tightly clasping, ovate, acuminate, pungent. Inflorescence amply tripinnate; primary bracts like the scape-bracts, equaling or shorter than the branches; spikes sessile, ovoid, ellipsoid, or cylindric, subaggregated at the apices of the branches and some lateral, 3-6 cm long, sparsely flocculose. Floral bracts broadly ovate, long-attenuate to a pungent spine, 12-18 mm long, 11 mm wide, strongly convex, carinate, strongly nerved; sepals very asymmetric, 8 mm long, 5 mm wide, short-mucronulate; petals ligulate, acute, 13-16 mm long, purple or yellow, bearing 2 fimbriate scales; stamens included; ovary obconic; placentae apical; ovules caudate.

description: Plant flowering over 1.1m high. Leaf 9 dm long, laxly and inconspicuously lepidote throughout; sheath elliptic, ample, 6 dm long, dark castaneous and entire toward base, green and laxly serrate toward apex with dark retrorse spines 2 mm long; blade ligulate, broadly rounded and spinose-apiculate, 8 cm wide. Scape erect, 9 mm wide, white-lanate; scape-bracts erect, ovate, pungent-apiculate, red, densely white-lepidote becoming more or less glabrous, the lower shorter than the internodes, the upper imbricate. Inflorescence sublaxly cylindric, 2-pinnate with sessile spikes, 3 dm long, soon glabrous; axis slender, straight; primary bracts broadly ovate, acuminate to a slender spine, much shorter than the axillary spikes; spikes few-flowered, suborbicular, 25 mm long. Floral bracts ovate, subtruncate, mucronulate, to 13 mm long, much exceeded by the sepals, nerved when dry; flowers suberect. Sepals slightly asymmetric, narrowly subelliptic, mucronulate, 10 mm long, the lateral ones and the ovary broadly alate; petals bearing 2 highly adnate fimbriate appendages.

description: Leaves to 5 dm long, densely and minutely lepidote throughout; blades ligulate, 78 cm wide at the base, minutely spinulose-serrate, broadly rounded and apiculate. Inflorescence laxly bipinnate, glabrous, 3 dm long or more; primary bracts narrowly lanceolate, about equaling the stipes; spikes all slenderly stipitate, to 8 cm long, 12 mm in diameter, 40-50-flowered. Floral bracts broadly ovate, broadly acute or obtuse, mucronate, much shorter than the sepals, stramineous, strongly nerved; flowers much compressed, 9 mm long without the petals. Sepals asymmetric, nerved, 5 mm long, mucro 1 mm long.

description: Plant flowering to 1.6 m high. Leaves to 8 dm long; sheaths elliptic, ample, ca 3 dm long, dark castaneous; blades ligulate, broadly acute, obscurely pale-lepidote on both sides, laxly and minutely to densely and coarsely serrate with dark flat spines. Scape erect, stout; scape-bracts imbricate, large, lance-elliptic, entire, chartaceous when dry, densely pale-lepidote. Inflorescence amply and very laxly pyramidal, 3-4-pinnate; primary bracts like the upper scape-bracts, much shorter than the sterile bases of the branches; branches spreading, to 45 cm long, secondary bracts narrowly triangular, membranaceous, entire, sparsely pale-furfuraceous at base, the lowest shorter than the secondary branches; heads terminal, composed of 2-3 spikes, to 2 cm long, 3 cm in diameter; spikes few-flowered, sessile. Floral bracts broadly ovate, apiculate, to 16 mm long, much exceeding the immature sepals, serrulate, coriaceous, faintly nerved, minutely and obscurely pale-lepidote, carinate. Sepals free, 8 mm long, strongly asymmetric, mucronulate, serrulate, minutely lepidote; petals green with yellow apices (! Read).

description: Tree 6-14 m tall; terminal branchlets rather slender, glabrous, glaucous, obtusely striate, compressed, the internodes 2.5-3.0 cm long. Young shoots sparsely appressed-pubescent or puberulous; initial minute leaves subappressed-pubescent. Stipules geminate, subulate, 1-2 mm long. Leaves opposite, 5-6-jugate; axis slender, 15-22 cm long, striolate, very narrowly canaliculate above, glabrous or with very sparse, minute, subpatulous hairs, the interjuga 1.5-2.8 cm long, the petiole 6.0-8.5 cm long, the stipels up to 1 mm long. Leaflets subcoriaceous, light yellowish-greenish when dry, opposite; petiolules 2-3 mm long, the terminal ones 10-15 mm long; blades 7.0-11.5 cm long, 2.2-2.8 cm wide, elliptic-lanceolate or lanceolate, attenuate and acuminate, acute at the apex, very asymmetric with one side obtuse, the other side acutely cuneate at the base, crenate-serrulate, the teeth 3-5 mm long, minutely callose-mucronulate; shining and glabrous above with impressed midrib, visible secondary nerves, and barely visible reticulum; rather pale-ochraceous with puberulous main nervation beneath, the costa very prominent and the secondary nerves with short, straight, subappressed or ascending hairs, the prominent nerves in 17-23 pairs, parallel and slightly ascending, 2.5-4.0 mm apart, with angle of divergence 54°-65°, curving at the margin and ending with the callous teeth; tertiary nerves very slender, very sparsely and obsoletely puberulous, the minor veins united into a flat but conspicuous and minute, discolored reticulum, the intra-reticular areoles densely papillose. Inflorescences rather small, axillary, 5-6-13 cm long, to 8 cm broad, the peduncle compressed, sparsely hirsutulous, about 2-8 cm long; branches dichotomous, striate, densely hirtous or hirtellous, the ultimate very short, usually supporting three pedicellate (not pedunculate) flowers. Pedicels sessile, 2-3 mm long, densely hirtellous or tomentellous. Bracts about 1 mm long, lanceolate, deciduous. Flowers tetramerous, the buds globose, subtetragonal, 1.5-1.8 mm in diam; calyx about 2 mm high, when expanded 4.5-5.0 mm in diam, the lobes ovate, 1.8-2.0 mm long, 1.5-1.6 mm wide, sericeous inside, subappressed-pubescent outside; filaments eight, about 2.2 mm long, glabrous except at the base; anthers ellipsoid, 1 mm long, polliniferous; carpels four, the ovaries ovoid, about 0.7 mm long, pubescent with ascending hairs, the style 1.5 mm long, pubescent on the lower part; disc minutely hirsute-tomentose. Follicles suborbicular-ellipsoid, compressed, about 3 mm long, 2.3 mm broad, minutely and densely subappressed-pubescent and with additional longer, subascendent, bristly hairs. Endocarp ellipsoid-ovoid, compressed, 2.5 × 2.0 mm, the insertion angle subacute and the opposite obtuse. Seeds ovoid, compressed, reddish, nitid, about 2.2 × 1.8 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1970. Brunelliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 2: 1-189.

description: Leaves 6 dm long, obscurely pale-lepidote; sheaths elliptic, ca 17 cm long, the apex green and sparsely serrate, elsewhere dark castaneous and entire; blades ligulate, acute, cuspidate, 3 cm wide, laxly serrate with dark antrorse spines to 3 mm long. Scape straight (?), 6 mm wide near apex, white-lanate; scape-bracts (upper) densely imbricate, lanceolate, pungent, red, obscurely pale-lepidote. Inflorescence densely ovoid, 3-pinnate with spikes fascicled in the axils of the primary bracts, 8 cm long, obscurely pale-lepidote; primary bracts ovate, acute, pungent, exceeding the lower spikes, thin, nerved; spikes subglobose, few-flowered, 25 mm long. Floral bracts ovate, acute, pungent, 15 mm long, exceeding the sepals; flowers erect. Sepals (young) 8 mm long, mucronulate, the lateral ones alate-carinate with the ovary; petals blue (! Belem); epigynous tube very short.

description: Plant flowering over 6 dm high. Leaves ligulate, to 6 dm long, 3-6 cm wide, subcoriaceous, minutely lepidote beneath, serrate with fine brown teeth, 1-1.5 mm long and averaging about 6 mm apart, attenuate, terminating in an elongate dark-brown horny mucro. Scape erect, much shorter than the leaves, 5-6 mm in diameter, glabrous at least in age; scape-bracts erect, densely imbricate, narrowly lanceolate, acuminate, chartaceous, pungent, spinulose. Inflorescence bipinnate, thyrsoid, 1-3 dm long, 6-7 cm in diameter, dense at apex, interrupted toward base; primary bracts like the scape-bracts, much indurated toward apex, the lower serrulate and much exceeding the spikes, the upper entire and shorter than the spikes; spikes broadly ellipsoid, 2-3 cm long, short-stalked or sessile. Floral bracts ovate-lanceolate, evenly acuminate into a broad flat dark-brown spine, 10-14 mm long. Sepals strongly asymmetric, 5 mm long including the short mucro, sparsely lepidote with pale appressed scales; ovary much enlarged in fruit, sparsely lepidote; seeds fusiform, 2 mm long.

description: Lianas, glabras; ramos novos achatados, não lenticelados, logo miudamente lenticelados, secos marrons, velhos cilíndricos, fissurados, lenticelados, marrons. Folhas opostas; estípulas triangulares, denticuladas; pecíolos (4-)6(-8) mm, secos marrons; lâminas 6.5-9.1 (-12.2) × 2.1-4.8 cm, elípticas, base cuneada, margem inteira, amarelada quando seca, ápice acuminado, raro emarginado, cartáceas, secas marrons em ambas as faces ou marrom-escuras na adaxial, às vezes mais claras em volta das nervuras na adaxial, nervuras secas amareladas ou acinzentadas em ambas as faces, secundárias promínulas em ambas as faces, terciárias obscuras na face adaxial, promínulas na abaxial. Inflorescências 1.3-2.8(-9.7) × (0.8-)1.5-2(-4.4) cm, tirsóide-paniculadas, ca 18 flores, axilares em nós sem folhas; pedúnculos (5-)7-16 mm, ramos cilíndricos, opostos, brácteas erosas; pedicelos (1.9-)2.9 mm, bractéolas 2. Botões florais esféricos. Flores ca 4.7 mm diâm na antese, rotáceas; cálice gamossépalo, lobos 0.5 × 1 mm, triangulares ou elípticos, inteiros, carnosos; pétalas 2.2 × 1-1.2 mm, elípticas, deflexas, margem sinuada, carnosas, amarelas ou verdes; disco anelar-pulviniforme, 0.5-0.6 × 0.4 mm, margem externa delgada, ca 0.05 mm; estames 1-1.3 mm, filetes 0.8-1.2 mm, anteras 0.2 × 0.2-0.4 mm, oblongas, 2-loculares, lóculos confluentes, deiscência por fendas apicais em ângulo de ca 120°, conectivo inconspícuo; ovário ca 0.65 mm diâm, levemente 3-lobado, estilete ca 0.5 mm, estigma pontual, óvulos por lóculo 2. Bagas imaturas 3.2-5.1 × 2.5-3.3 cm, piriformes, secas marrom pruinosas, rugosas, ás vezes sulcadas na base, maduras não vistas, epicarpo maduro crustáceo. Sementes imaturas 2.8 × 2.3 cm.

description: Plant flowering 12-13 dm high. Leaves to 7 dm long, covered throughout with small pale appressed inconspicuous scales; sheaths broadly elliptic, distinctly wider than the blades, brown-tinged; blades ligulate, broadly rounded and apiculate, 7-11 cm wide, laxly but regularly serrulate. Scape slender, white-flocculose, becoming glabrous with age; scape-bracts erect, lanceolate, barely exceeding the internodes. Inflorescence laxly bipinnate with the upper spikes short-stipitate, 43-47 cm long, glabrous; primary bracts linear, acuminate, shorter than the lowest branches but about equaling their sterile bases; stipes slender, flattened, to 7 cm long; spikes ellipsoid to subglobose, 1525 mm long. Floral bracts broadly ovate, acuminate to a small slender mucro, 5 mm long, much exceeded by the sepals, thin, nerved, stramineous when dry. Sepals strongly asymmetric with a produced lateral wing equaling or exceeding the terminal mucro, 5 mm long, short-connate; petals white, bearing 2 highly adnate infundibuliform appendages.

description: Tree to 20 m, the trunk 30 cm in diameter with almost smooth, light gray, easily detachable bark, and white or roseate, rather soft wood. Crown dense, the terminal branchlets subtetragonal, compressed, sulcate-costate, ferruginous-tomentose, glabrate, lenticellate, the ultimate internodes 2-4 cm long. Young shoots and leaves densely subappressed pilose. Stipules rather thick, very acute, subulate, about 2 mm long, single on each side of the petiole but frequently bifid by a lateral incision, subappressed pilose, caducous. Leaves opposite, 6-8-jugate; axis 17-28 cm long, the petiole moderately thick, sulcate above, slightly thickened towards the base, shortly pubescent or puberulous, 6-10 cm long. Interjuga 2.5-4.0 cm long, more or less spreading-pubescent, rounded or obtusely carinate beneath, sulcate above; stipels minute, lanceolate-subulate, pilose about 1.5 mm long. Leaflets opposite; petiolules thick, striolulate, spreading-pubescent, the lateral one 4-7 mm long, the terminal one 13-15 mm long; blades thin, coriaceous, rigid, 6-12 cm long, 3.0-4.8 cm wide, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, usually rounded at both ends, the base asymmetrical, the apex, often short-attenuate and obtusely acuminate, slightly crenate, the apex of crenulations initially minutely mucronulate, often becoming obtuse; light green or yellowish-green, shining and smooth above, glabrous except for the puberulous, impressed midrib, the secondary nerves slightly depressed, pale, conspicuous, the pale, minute reticulum immersed, almost obsolete; pale ochraceous- or cinereous-green, densely pubescent beneath, the main nervation with subappressed, acute trichomes, the costa brownish and very prominent, the secondary nerves 18-24 on each side, 3-5 mm apart with an angle of divergence 60°-75°, prominent, patulous, curving and anastomosing near the margin, the tertiary and minor veins joined into a minute, very close and prominent puberulous reticulum with patulous, short trichomes, the narrow interreticular areas densely papillose. Inflorescences axillary, shorter than the leaves, 12-28 cm long, the peduncle 4-10 cm long, robust, more or less compressed, striolate, pubescent, with copious subpatulous or subappressed acute hairs; branching trichotomous or dichotomous, the branches very dense, compressed, angular, densely tomentulose with subpatulous, ascendent hairs. Bracteoles small, about 1 mm long, soon deciduous. Pedicels sessile, short, 1-3 mm long, pubescent with short, patulous, acute hairs. Flowers pentamerous rarely hexamerous, crowded at the end of short branchlet; calyx about 6 mm in diam, the five lobes oblong-ovate, acute, 2.0-2.5 mm long, 1.5-1.8 mm broad, rather thick, appressed-pubescent outside, minutely crisp-pilose at the margin and on the upper part inside; staminodia ten, the filaments glabrous 0.7-1.0 mm long, the sterile anthers elliptic, 0.4 mm long. Follicles one-seeded, from three to five developed from one flower, ovoid, slightly compressed, 3.0-3.5 mm long, about 3 mm broad, minutely and densely tomentose with small acute hairs, and hispid with long, rigid, prickling bristles. Endocarp 3.0-2.8 mm, subellipsoid, abruptly acute at the attaching angle and at the opposite side, when dry in a rather closed, not very deep U-shaped with lacerate margin. Seeds red, shining, ovoid, compressed, 2.0-2.4 mm long, about 2 mm broad. Male flowers unknown.

description: Tree to 25 m, copiously branched and densely leafy. Terminal branchlets glabrous, brownish-green, smooth or with few lenticels, the internodes 1-4 cm long, more or less laterally compressed. Stipules single at each side of the petiole, small, thick-subulate, about 1-2 mm long, soon deciduous. Leaves opposite, (3-) 5-8 (-11)-jugate, the axis 15-45(-60) cm long, the petiole subterete, slightly striolate, glabrous, (4-)6-l6(-18) cm long, the inter juga 2-6 cm long, sulcate above, more or less rounded below, glabrous or sparingly puberulous, the stipels geminate, subulate, or rather corniculate, 1-2 mm long. Leaflets opposite, petiolulate; lateral petiolules 2-6 mm long, rarely shorter, the terminal ones 8-20 mm long, glabrous or puberulous; blades subcoriaceous, flexible, 9-17 cm long and (2.0-)3.0-4.5(-5.5) cm wide, oblong or elliptic-oblong, lance-attenuate towards the apex and acute or cuspidate at the apex, obtusely and asymmetrically attenuate at the base with the proximal half rounded and much shorter than the distal half, serrulate-crenate, the teeth 5-10 mm apart with acute, appressed or incurved, short (1 mm) mucros; green and glabrous or somewhat puberulous above when young with impressed midrib and conspicuous secondary nerves; cinereous or pale cinereous-ochraceous beneath, the costa prominent, striolate, the secondary prominent nerves 15-22 on each side, parallel, patulous with angle of divergence 50°-60°, curving near the margin and ending in a tooth, the costa reddish or brownish, conspicuous, the tertiary, transverse nerves slightly prominulous, the minor veins minutely reticulate, the reticulum conspicuous but rather immersed, flat, the main nervation usually somewhat pubescent with thin, patulous or subpatulous hairs, for the rest usually glabrous or with very sparse hairs, sometimes more copiously pubescent, but also and more frequently glabrous, the epidermal surface densely and strongly papillose, the papillas giving a gray or cinereous color. Inflorescences axillary, cymose-paniculate, usually densely branched, crowded with flowers or fruits, 8-18 cm long, 10-26 cm broad; peduncle robust, 3-10 cm long, compressed, almost ancipital, slightly striolate, glabrous or seldom more or less pubescent; first division trichotomous with the main branches patulous, compressed, angulate and slightly striate, sparsely or more or less densely and minutely tomentose; subtending bracts lanceolate, acutely dentate or 2-3-incised, 10-5 mm long, very soon caducous; further divisions dichotomous, the branches extremely divaricate, thin, angulate, densely hirtulose-tomentose. Bracteoles subulate, 2-3 mm long, soon deciduous. Pedicels terete, thin, rigid, minutely tomentose-pubescent, 1-5 m long. Buds 5-angulate-globose, 3.0-3.2 mm in diam, minutely and densely pubescent. Flowers pentamerous, female or hermaphroditic; calyx 3.5-4.0 mm high, when expanded 7.0-8.5 mm in diam, the lobes 2.8-3.0 mm long, 1.7-2.0 mm broad, ovate or oblong-ovate, acute, rather thick, densely and minutely pubescent with subappressed, longer hairs outside and densely sericeous inside, the margin rather minutely tomentose; filamente of fertile stamens in bisexual flowers 3-4 mm long, subulate, the lower one-third thickened, hyaline-hirsute; fertile anthers ellipsoid, shortly attenuate and mucronulate at the apex, scrobiculate, 1.5-1.8 mm long, 1-1.2 mm broad; sterile staminodia in functional female flowers short, the filaments 0.7-1.0 (-1.5) mm long, sparsely pilose at the base; sterile anthers oblong, 0.7-0.8 mm long; ovaries about 0.7 mm long when very young, ovoid, hispid-hirsute; styles 1.5-2.0 mm long, strigose on the lower half, the upper part papillose along the ventral suture; disc shortly and densely tomentose-hispid. Follicles one to five, well developed, trapezoid-ovoid, somewhat laterally compressed, almost carinate on the ventral and upper dorsal margin, elongate in the typical form or more commonly subrotund at the inner upper margin, densely and minutely tomentose and long-hispid, 4.0 × 4.0-4.5 × 5.5 mm; style up to 3 mm, sub-basal, deflexed, the lower thickened part persistently strigose; endocarp cartilaginous, oblong-ellipsoid, 3.5-4.0 × 2.5-3.0 mm in the typical form or more shortly ellipsoid, 3.0-3.5 × 2.0-3.3 mm, the adaxial side straight, when dry and open thickly, shortly U-shaped with an acute incision angle above. Seeds solitary, rarely two, reddish-brown, lustrous, ellipsoid, with obtuse ends, 2.4-3.0 mm long, 1.6-2.0 mm broad.

description: Tree about 15 m tall with gray bark. Branchlets when young ochraceous hirtulous-tomentose with dense, short, curled hairs and longer, erect, spreading ones; when older more or less glabrate, rugose, grayish. Stipules linear-lanceolate, 3-5 mm long, geminate, caducous. Leaves simple, opposite, rigid-coriaceous. Petiole rather robust, tomentulose, striolate, above sulcate, 1.5-2.0 cm long. Blade 17-25 cm long, 7.0-9.5 cm wide, oblong-ovate attenuate to the apex, subacute, narrowed cuneate to the base, slightly and obtusely crenate with double indentation, light-yellowish green and glabrous above, the costa depressed, the secondary nerves thin, impressed, slightly conspicuous, the minor veins almost obsolete; below ochraceous and moderately crisp-tomentose with short, fine, curled, intricate hairs and sparse ones somewhat longer and patulous, the venation very distinct, the costa very robust, striate, brownish, the secondary nerves 20-24 on each side, prominent, subascendent, 6-20 mm apart, the divergence angle 55°-70°, curved and anastomosing near the margin, the tertiary transverse nerves 3-5 mm apart, irregularly parallel, prominent, anastomosing with the minor veins into a thick, minute prominent reticulum, with alveoles narrower than the veins. Inflorescence axillary, ascending, acute angular, about 14 cm long, the peduncle about 3.5 cm long, striate, complanate; first branching trichotomous, then dichotomous, the branchlets as well as the peduncle hirsute-tomentulose with short, crisped, 'entangled hairs and longer (1 mm) fine, flexible and spreading hairs. Ultimate branchlets very short, 1-4 mm long, bearing several (three to seven) sessile or subsessile flowers; the pedicels 0.0-0.3 mm, sessile or subsessile. Bracts and bracteoles strictly linear, 1.5-2.5 mm long, hirtulous. Only male flowers known, pentamerous, sometimes hexamerous, usually with four carpels, sometimes three carpels; calyx expanded 6.5-7.0 mm in diam the lobes triangular, acute 2.0-2.3 mm long 1.6-2.0 mm broad, crispulous-tomentose outside, subglabrous with scarce hairs inside, the margin minutely tomentose; staminal filaments 3 mm long, flexuose-pilose at the base; anthers ellipsoid, 0.8-1.0 mm long; carpels usually four, sterile, the ovary 0.5 mm long, the style 0.8-1.0 mm long, hamate; rarely three carpels. Disc, densely crisped-pilose, white lanuginose.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1970. Brunelliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 2: 1-189.

description: Saprophytic herbs, 5.5-21 cm high. Rhizome ca. 1 cm long, scales 1-2.5 mm long. Stems purple, mostly unbranched. Leaves narrowly to transversely ovate, (to cordate), 0.6-5.3 mm long, (0.5-)0.8-2 mm wide, apex acuminate, auriculate. Inflorescence a bifurcate cincinnus, cincinni 2-4-flowered and 5-20 mm long, flowers 1.4-5 mm apart or the plant having a solitary terminal flower only. Bracts (triangular-)ovate, 2.2-4.8 mm long, 0.8-2.2 mm wide, apex acuminate, often auriculate. Pedicels (0-)0.4-1.0(-2.2) mm long. Flowers white to purple, outer tepals with darker tip, throat and inner tepals more or less yellowish brown, 7.5-14 mm long, sometimes sweet-scented (Maas et al. 2596, Guyana). Outer tepals obovate, 3.5-5.9 mm long, 2.1-4.5 mm wide, margins crenulate and often involute, inner side papillate. Inner tepals narrowly ovate-triangular, 1.5-3.5 mm long, (0.2-)0.4-1 mm wide, sometimes 3-dentate. Floral tube (1.3-)2.8-5 mm long, 0.5-2.9 mm diam. Ribs or wings narrowly semielliptic, 2-4 mm long, 0.2-0.4 mm wide. Stamens purple-brown, filaments 0.6-1.2 mm long, thecae whitish. Style purple, 3.8-6.5 mm long, branches 0.5-0.8(-1.1) mm long. Ovary obovoid to very broadly obovoid, (1.3-) 1.8-3.8 x (1.1-)1.8-3.3 mm. Capsule brownish, broadly to transversely obovoid, rarely rhomboid, 2.5-3.8 x 2.3-4 mm, style exceeding the floral tube by 1.5-4 mm. Seeds 0.2-0.5 x 0.1-0.3 mm.

description: Tree about 12 m high, the trunk about 20 cm diam with gray, smooth bark. Branchlets medium sized, lenticellate-tuberculate, completely glabrous, nodose, the internodes 2-4 cm long, obtusely striate, compressed. Stipules geminate, oblong triangular, acute, about 1.5 mm long, single. Leaves opposite, 3-7-jugate, completely glabrous; axis 10-25 cm long, rather slender, reddish, striolate, narrowly sulcate above, subcarinate below, the inter juga 2-3 cm long, the petiole thickened at the base, 3-5 cm long. Leaflets subcoriaceous or flexible-coriaceous; petiolules reddish sulcate above, 5-8 mm long, the terminal one 12-15 mm long; stipels geminate, acute, 0.7-1.0 mm long; blades 5.5-13.0	cm long, 2-4 cm wide, elliptic oblong, attenuate-cuneate, slightly asymmetric at the base, rounded, obtuse or subacute at the apex, moderately subserrate-crenate, the mucronate teeth very minute, slightly revolute at the margin; green, rather lustrous above, the midrib strongly impressed, the secondary nerves barely visible, the minute, more or less prominulous reticulum conspicuous; pale green with reddish, very prominent, carinate costa beneath, the secondary nerves very slender, rather flexuous, only slightly prominulous, 12-14 each side, 7-10 mm apart, subpatulous, with an angle of divergence 40°-50°, forking and anastomosing near the margin, the minor veins joined into a small, narrow reticulum, flat but conspicuous, the areoles glaucous, minutely papillose. Paniculae axillary, short, 3-7 cm long, sessile, the branches glabrous or with very rare strigae, dividing from the base, shortly divided, angulate, compressed, bearing at the ends glomerate flowers and later very crowded fruits. Pedicels 1-2 mm long, glabrous. Bracts and bracteoles subulate, 1-2 mm long. Flowers pentamerous with five or four carpels; buds globose, about 2 mm in diam; expanded calyx 8-9 mm in diam, the lobes ovate-triangular, acute, about 2.5 mm long, 2 mm wide, glabrous outside, or with very few strigae near the apex, densely sericeous with ascending hairs inside, minutely tomentulose near the margin and apex; usually a gland at the sinuses outside; staminodia with glabrous filaments 0.8-1.0 mm long, the anthers oblong, 0.6 mm long, sterile; disc velvety tomentose. Three to four follicles maturing from a single flower, rarely less or five, about 7 × 5 mm, oblong-ovate, horizontal-divergent, obliquely rounded or obtuse at the base, attenuate-apiculate at the apex, the apiculum 1.0-1.5 mm long, exocarp somewhat subcoriaceous, densely minute-tomentose substrigose (the hairs acute, ascending) and hispid, the bristles rather slender, rigid, acute, patulous, 1.0-1.5 mm long; endocarp 6.5 × 3.5-4.0 mm, corneous, medium hard, ellipsoid-oblong, rounded at one end, arquate apiculate, very acute at apex, when dry and open turtle shell-shaped. Seeds one or two maturing in each fruit, reddish brown, lustrous, ellipsoid, obtuse at both ends, 3.0-3.8 × 2.0-2.3 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1970. Brunelliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 2: 1-189.

description: The following characters show its strong differences with B. foreroi: Terminal young branchlets densely tomentose-hirsute, ferruginous. Leaves thickly coriaceous, deep green, with 11-15 pairs of secondary nerves, deeply and acutely 4-5-dentate; venular reticulum beneath strong, the alveoles deep, the indument dense, hirsute-tomentose, ferruginous; petioles robust, with one pair of stipels. Panicles much smaller than the subtending leaf, the branching robust and rather dense. Calyx usually 5-merous, 8-9 mm diam. Follicles 5 × 4 mm, densely tomentose-hispid.

description: Tree 10-15 m tall. Terminal branches thick, quadrangular, densely hirsute-tomentose, greenish ferrugineous, the youngest parts as well as buds, stipules, and growing leaves velutinous, the older branchlets becoming griseous brownish, lenticellate, cicatricose, the internodes 3-5 cm long, the trichomes patulous, straight or more or less flexuose, 0.4-1.4 mm long. Stipules bigeminate, sometimes three each side of the petioles, verticilate, oblong-triangular or lanceolate-subulate, rather thick, hirsutule-tomentose, the proxals about 10 mm long, the distals 3-6 mm long, soon caducous, leaving marked scars. Leaves simple, opposite, thick coriaceous, rigid. Petiole 3-10 cm long, robust, angulate, densely tomentose, slightly sulcate above, slightly thickened at the base and near the top above, ca 2-4 mm below the blade, a pair of conspicuous, rather thick, triangular-subulate, tomentose stipels 4-5 mm long. Blades 18-40 cm long, 10-24 cm wide, elliptic or obovate-elliptic or ovate-elliptic, rounded or slightly narrowed and shortly acuminate at the apex, obtuse or rounded at the base, strongly biserrate and revolute at the margin, the teeth stout, triangular, to about 5 mm long; velutinous when very young, sparsely pilose, rather dark green, with tomentose main nerves, impressed reticulate and rugose above; densely ochraceous or greenish ferrugineous-tomentose beneath, the costa very thick and prominent, striolate, sometimes slightly tuberculate near the base, the secondary nerves 11-15 on each side, 1.0-2.5 cm apart, very prominent, patulous and curved-ascending, the divergence angle 50°-70°, furcate and anastomosing near the margin, the transverse tertiary nerves with others forming a prominent, lax reticulum more elevated than the other reticulum, also prominent but lower, minute, venose. Male inflorescences cymose paniculate relatively large, axillary at the end of branches, 10-20 cm long, 6-10 cm broad, the peduncle very thick, sulcate-angulate, more or less compressed, as well as the branching, greenish ochraceous or greenish ferrugineous, densely hirsute-tomentose, the hairs, patulous, about 1.0-1.5 mm long. Branches thick, opposite or alternate, subtended by small petiolate leaves, 2-5 cm long, 1.0-1.5 cm wide, on the upper part the subtending bracts lanceolate, deeply incised (about 6 × 2 mm), upwards becoming progressively smaller with fewer narrow lobes; three fertile bracteoles 4.0-1.5 mm long at the end of the peduncles which bear pedicels; pedicels hirsute 0.6-4.0 mm long. Male flowers usually pentamerous, rarely tetramerous, the buds ovoid, 5-angulate, slightly apiculate, 3 × 3 mm; calyx ochraceous-green, 3.0-3.2 mm long, expanded 8.0-8.5 mm in diam, hirsute outside, with scattered white, sericeous, appressed hairs inside, the five lobes ovate-triangular, acute, 2.5-3.0 mm long 1.8-2.5 mm wide; ten stamens, the filaments about 2 mm long with white, sericeous, spreading hairs on the lower half, the anthers ellipsoid, about 1 mm long; rudimentary carpels, the minute, sterile ovary 0.5 mm long, hispid (the bristles 1.0-1.5 mm long), the style 1 mm long; disc densely hispid, the straight, pointed hairs 1.0-1.5 mm long. Female inflorescences similar, broadening when fruiting, ultimate branchlets 1-4 mm long, the pedicels 1-4 mm long, thick, hirsute; fruiting calyx 3.5-4.0 mm long, expanded 8-9 mm in diam, the 5 sepals ovate-triangular, acute, 3.0-3.4 mm long, hirsute outside, sparsely sericeous inside; ten staminodia, the filaments 1.5 mm long, hirsute at the base, the anthers 0.5-0.6 mm long, sterile; carpels 5, the ovary subglobose, biovulate, densely hispid, the style 2 mm long, hirsute at the base, the apex hooked. Usually three to five follicles developed, densely tomentose and hispid, ovate-rotundate, slightly compressed, 5 × 4 mm; endocarp corneous, rounded, laterally compressed, narrowly carinate, 3.2-3.5 mm in diam, 3 mm thick, monosperm, when dry and open urceolar with medial incision or in open U-shape; seed solitary, subglobose, laterally compressed, dark reddish, lustrous, about 2.5 mm in diam, 2 mm thick.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1970. Brunelliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 2: 1-189.

description: Tree 10-15 (-20) m tall with large, spreading crown; branchlets subtetragonal, apparently hexagonal through six longitudinal furrows, more or less compressed laterally towards the end, the internodes 1-5 cm long, lenticellate-tuberculate, densely ferruginous or ochraceous-lanuginose, the hairs rather short, crisped or more or less flexuous, intricate. Buds and young shoots densely ferruginous-lanuginose-tomentose with curled, shorter hairs and longer subflexuous, ascending hairs. Stipules narrowly lanceolate, 1.5-3.0 mm long, geminate or bigeminate, the smaller 0.5-1.0 mm long. Leaves opposite, 4-7-jugate; axis robust, (10-) 20-35 (-50) cm long, subterete, sparsely striate, the upper part narrowly sulcate above, densely and shortly crisped-tomentose, the stipels ungulate, 1.0-1.5 mm long, the interjuga 1.5-4.0(-5.5) cm long, the petiole robust, 7-20 cm long. Leaflets subcoriaceous or coriaceous; petiolules rather thick, sulcate above, 1-6 mm long, rarely none, the terminal leaflet always smaller with a petiolule 15-32 mm long; blades 8.5-18.0 cm long, 3.6-6.7 cm broad, except the lower pair (6.0-9.5 × 2.5-4.5 cm), oblong-elliptic, obtuse or more or less attenuate and acutate at the apex, very asymmetric, obtusely attenuate or subrounded at the base, rarely more attenuate at both ends and somewhat lanceolate, entire or rather often very obtusely undulate-crenate with very minute, callous, inconspicuous mucros, the indentation double; deep green or yellowish-green, green-brownish when dry above, minutely pulverulent, ferruginous or ochraceous-lanuginose when young, later glabrate and lustrous except on the main nerves, the secondary nerves conspicuous, the minute slightly salient reticulum yellowish, very conspicuous under magnification; cinereous or ochraceous, minutely lanuginose beneath with rather thick, somewhat crisped, white, entangled hairs, the costa very prominent, more or less striolate and carinate, 12-15 prominent secondary nerves usually on each side, subascending the angle of divergence 50°-70°, parallel, 6-13 mm apart, curving near the margin, forking and anastomosing, the tertiary nerves regularly or irregularly transverse, prominent, joining the minor veins into a minute, prominent reticulum often concealed by the indumentum. Panicles axillary, shortly pedunculate or sessile, 4-14 cm long and broad, the peduncle 0-3 cm long, the branches mostly dichotomous, ascending at an acute angle, more or less compressed, angular and striolate, densely ochraceous or ferruginous-lanuginose-tomentose, with dense, short, rather thick, crisped, entangled hairs (longer hairs about 1 mm long), subflexuous or flexible patulous. Bracts narrowly linear, long-pilose, 1-3 mm long, soon deciduous. Pedicels mostly obsolete, 0-1 mm long, in fruit to 2 mm long. Flowers mostly pentamerous and also hexamerous, very rarely tetramerous, glomerate at the ends of short branchlets; buds tomentose, subangular-globose, 2.5-3-0 mm in diam; calyx 3-4 mm long, when expanded 6.0-7.5 (-8) mm in diameter, the lobes ovate-triangular, acute, 2.0-2.5 mm long, 1.2-2.2 mm wide, more or less sericeous especially on the medial nerve within, minutely tomentose at the margin, lanuginose outside with dense, short, crisped hairs and flexible, patulous longer hairs; fertile stamens in male flowers with filaments 2.5-3.5 mm long, rather thick and hirsutulous in the lower half, the anthers cordate-ovate, shortly apiculate, acute, 1.0-1.3 mm long, 0.8-0.9 mm broad; staminodia in female flowers with filaments 1.0-1.4 mm long, glabrous or subglabrous, the anthers oblong, sterile, apiculate, 0.5-0.8 mm long; 5-6 carpels in female flowers, the ovary oblique-ovoid, 1.0-1.2 mm long, hirsute-hispidulous, biovulate, fertile, the style 2-3 mm long, the lower half thickened and substrigose, the end glabrous and curved; in male flowers the carpels rudimentary, the ovary 0.5 mm, hirsute, sterile, the style 0.8-1.0 mm long, pilose towards the base. Two to six follicles developed from each flower, 6-7 mm long, about 5 mm broad, ovoid-elliptic, obtuse, reflexed, apiculate, slightly compressed and carinate, densely and minutely tomentose and copiously or densely hispid with additional pungent straight, patulous bristles 1 mm long, the apiculum being the thickened lower strigose remnant of the 3 mm-long, hamate style. Endocarp corneous, obliquely oblong-ellipsoid, retrorsely acute on the outer end, subacute or subobtuse at the inner insertion angle, 5-6 mm long, 3-4 mm broad, when dry rather hard and cyathiform with a very short frontal incision. Seeds in each follicle single or rarely two, oblong-ellipsoid, obtuse at one end, subacute at the other, reddish-brown, 3 x 2 mm, very lustrous. Disc hirsutulous-tomentose.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1970. Brunelliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 2: 1-189.

description: The recent observations-comparing old and new collections-indicate that B. inermis has rather large leaves, up to 60 cm long, 1-4-jugate, with very robust rachis, the blades ovate-elliptic or broad-oblong-elliptic, rounded and sessile at base, 15-25 × 6-10 cm, with 20-29 pairs of secondary nerves (in smaller lower leaflets sometimes less, down to 17 pairs); abaxially the lax reticulum is prominent and more or less visible through the thick lanate indument which conceals a prominulous minor venular reticulum; the areoles are ashy-papillose, and adaxially the reticular venation is usually obsolete. Stipules and stipels are simply geminate. The axis and inflorescence branches are remarkably robust, distally dilated and complanate, even ancipital, bearing at the ends compact glomerules of fruits or flowers, mostly presumably bisexual. Usually 6-merous, 5-merous and 7-merous flowers are also frequent, the calyx 4-4.5 mm long, when expanded 89.5 mm diam., and there are twice as many stamens as sepals, but sometimes 13 additional are present; staminal filaments are 3-4 mm long, copiously villous proximally. Follicles are about 7-8 × 4-4.5 mm, with an additional 2.5-3 mm long apiculum, densely hispid; the endocarp is corneous, 6-7 × 3.5-3 mm, elliptic apiculate, when dry and open deeply pot-shaped, often somewhat laterally compressed and with a short indentation and an apiculum at the sutural line on the margin.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1985. Brunelliaceae (supplement). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 2: 28-103.

description: Tree 10-15 m high, the trunk 20-25 cm in diameter, with light brown bark and soft, white wood. Branchlets subterete, smooth, glabrous, brownish-green, the internodes long, only the terminal one compressed. Buds and very young opening leaves minutely ochraceous-strigose. Stipules geminate, very small, triangular-oblong, acute, 1.0-1.5 m long, soon deciduous. Leaves opposite, 1-4(-5)-jugate, very large, long-petiolate; axis 30-75 cm long, subterete, slightly striolate, narrowly sulcate above, more or less minutely, almost inconspicuously puberulous with very minute (0.05-0.10 mm long) acute, patulous or subpatulous yellowish trichomes more abundant toward the end and in the furrows, sparse toward the petiole, the interjuga 6-11 cm long, the petiole robust, glabrate, 20-40 cm long; stipels geminate, broadly corniculate, 1.0-1.5 mm long. Leaflets thinly coriaceous, large; petiolules rather robust, sulcate above, 8-15 mm long, the terminal one 28-55 cm long; blades 17-28 cm long, 8.0-13.5 cm wide, oblong-elliptic or oblong-ovate, rounded and asymmetric at the base, the terminal cuneate and symmetric, attenuate and acuminate at the apex, coarsely double-dentate-serrate, the small, callose, ascendant teeth 8-15 mm apart; green or dark green, when dry brownish-green; the midrib flat above, very conspicuous, sparsely and minutely strigulose, in part glabrous, the secondary nerves impressed, very conspicuous with an angle of divergence 45°-60°, the tertiary transversal nerves also conspicuous; whitish-green or almost white in vivo beneath, the costa thick and protuberant, the prominent secondary nerves 14-19 on each side, 8-18 mm apart, ascendent, parallel, curving near the margin, the tertiary nerves parallel, transversal, also prominent, the minor veins united into a conspicuous, more or less prominulous reticulum, the flat areoles densely whitish-papillose and with sparse, minute, acute, patulous hairs, the nervation minutely pilose with copious minute, acute, rather patulous or ascending hairs (0.05-0.10 mm long). Panicles axillary, large, long-pedunculate, 30-60 cm long and broad; peduncle robust, subterete, reddish-greenish, 12-22 cm long, glabrous or with very sparse, minute strigae; primary branching (usually subglabrate) trichotomous, the following usually dichotomous, repeatedly dividing, both spreading and ascending into a large floriferous but rather lax inflorescence, the terminal branchlets or peduncles one-flowered; branchlets thin, angular, striate, copiously and minutely strigulose or substrigulose, the hairs subappressed, acute, minute. Bracteoles above the short peduncles subulate, pilose, 0.6 mm long. Pedicels 0.5-1.0 mm long, sparsely strigulose. Flowers hermaphrodite, perfectly pentamerous, the buds angulate-globose, depressed, 1.8-2.2 mm in diameter, strigulose; calyx 2 mm long or shorter, when expanded 4.5-5.0 mm in diameter, the lobes ovate-triangular, acute, sparsely minute-strigulose outside, villous on the upper half inside, minutely tomentulose at the margin, 1.5-1.8 mm long, 1.0-1.4 mm wide; stamens ten, apparently fertile, the filament 1.5-1.8 mm long, at the lower part crisped-pilose, the anthers elliptic, cordate at the base, acute at the apex, 0.8-1.0 mm long, polliniferous; carpels five, the ovary about 0.8 mm long, ovate, hispidulo-hirsutous, biovulate, fertile, the style about 1 mm long, curved, glabrous; disc tomentose-hirsutulous. Follicles (4-) 5 maturing from a flower, round-ovoid, about 2 mm in diameter (specimens seen immature), minutely tomentulose and hispid above, the bristles 0.9 mm long; exocarp mediocre or thin; endocarp cartilagineous, oblong-ellipsoid, 1.8 mm long (immature). Seeds single, ellipsoid-globose, appressed, reddish, about 1.5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1970. Brunelliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 2: 1-189.

description: Young branchlets glabrous or subglabrous, with lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, pale lenticels; buds subsericeous-hirtous. Stipules subulate, about 3 mm long, subhirtous. Leaves opposite, paripinnate or imparipinnate, 4-7-jugate, 9-30 cm long 9-15 cm broad; stipels 2-4 on each node, subulate ca 1 mm long; petiole subterete, glabrous or subglabrous 4-9 cm long. Petiolules 1-4 mm long; blades 4-10 cm long 1.0-3.2 cm broad narrow-elliptic or ovate-elliptic, rounded at the base, acute or acuminate at the apex, crenate-serrate, densely griseous or yellowish sericeous when young, more or less glabrescent at maturity; midrib impressed above, prominent beneath, 18-25 secondary nerves on each side, the divergence angle 75°-80°, slightly arcuate near the apex, beneath prominent; reticulum above obsolete, beneath in adult leaves prominulous. Panicles g axillary, 7-11 cm long, 2.5-5.0 cm broad, peduncle 3.5-5.5 cm long, 3-5 mm thick, glabrous or sparsely pilose; inferior bracts similar to leaves, up to 3 cm long, the superior gradually smaller; fructiferous panicle 20 cm long, 11 cm broad, the peduncle compressed, 7 mm broad; both very much branched, the pedicels short or null, the flowers very glomerate. Prophylles similar to and of the same size as the ultimate bracts, subulate-deltoid or subulate, the margin villous, 1 mm long. Flowers hexamerous, viridulous; calyx valvate, the lobes thick, carnose, lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, sparsely villous outside, densely inside, the apex acute slightly thickened, 3.5-4.0 mm long, 2 mm wide; stamens 12 or 10-12, half the length of the sepals, the filaments subulate, short, the anthers cordiform, connective apiculate; ovary rudimentary, ovoid-subulate, long-pilose hispidulous; follicles spreading, oblong, beaked, expanded to 13 mm long, slightly incurved, hirtous, monospermous; seeds 3.5 mm long, brown, lustrous.

description: Tree to 25 m tall, with robust, terete, leafy branches, grayish or brownish, strongly lenticellate-tuberculate, glabrous, the very young branchlets triquetrous and minutely ochraceous, lanuginose. Stipules geminate, small, lanceolate or oblong-triangular, 1.01.5 mm long. Leaves simple, ternate, very rigid, coriaceous, usually more or less undulate, recurved and fragile. Petiole robust, minutely crisp-tomentose, subtriangular, striolate, sulcate above, the sharp margins usually apically bidentate in the lower, larger leaves; 1.2-2.5 cm long. Blades oblong-elliptic or oblong ovate-elliptic, rounded or obtuse at the base, attenuate and acute or shortly acuminate at the apex, biserrate with callous, acute teeth 2-3 mm apart, up to 0.5 mm high, becoming obuse in age; 7 to 22 cm long, 3-10 cm broad; when very young tomentellous pulverulent, ochraceous greenish above, soon glabrate and completely glabrous when adult, nitidous, yellow-greenish, subrugose-wavy between the nerves, the costa narrow and impressed, the secondary nerves impressed, filiform, ascending half way, the smaller veins loosely reticulate, impressed, marking off the rugosities of the surface; below minutely tomentose, ochraceous or greenish ochraceous with robust, prominent, angulate and striolate costa, secondary nerves prominent in 16-23 pairs, mostly 4-8 mm apart, patulous-ascending, with a divergence angle of 60°-70°, curved and anastomosing near the margin, the tertiary nerves prominent, obliquely and irregularly transversal, anastomosing with the fourth, fifth and sixth smaller degree veins into a minute but thick, very prominent reticulum more or less covered by a close tomentum of short, flexuous, intricate trichomes. The main nerves may become glabrous in age as in the petioles of larger leaves. Inflorescences axillary in young terminal branchlets, erect, shorter than subtending leaves (6-15 cm long), with long, more or less compressed, striate, naked peduncle, only cymose in the upper part, and like the loosely branching cymes and flowers, densely ochraceous or ferrugineous-lanuginose. Bracts linear 1-2 mm long, tomentose, soon deciduous; bracteoles three, usually subtending the thick terete, tomentose pedicels, 1-4 mm long. Buds globose-depressed, more or less angular, 3.0-3.5 mm long, 4 mm in diam. Male flowers pentamerous (rarely hexamerous or tetramerous), calyx 4-5 mm long, expanded about 10 mm in diam, the five lobes 3.0-3.3 mm long, triangular, acute, rather thick, outside and marginally minutely crisp-tomentose, inside crisp-pubescent, especially on the mid-rib; filaments ten, subulate, hirsute on the lower third, the rest glabrous, the apex capillary, incurved; anthers cordate-ellipsoid, apiculate, about 1.3 mm long; carpels only three, the sterile ovary about 1 mm long, densely hispid with two rudimentary ovules, the style 1 mm long, hirsute at the base, curved at the apex; receptacle densely hispid. Female flowers pentamerous (rarely hexamerous), the calyx 4.0-4.5 mm high, expanded 10-11 mm in diam, the lobes rather thick, 3.0-3.2 mm long, acute, tomentose outside, pubescent inside; staminodia usually ten, those facing the sepals longer, filaments 1.5 or 2 mm long, hairy at the base; anthers apiculate, 0.8-0.9 mm long, sterile; carpels 3, with ovary ovoid-oblong, about 2.5 mm long, biovulate, tomentose-hispid, the style about 2.5 mm long, hirsute below the apex, glabrous, acute, hooked; receptacle densely hispid. Follicles solitary or two or three, oblong, basally constricted, 12-15 mm long, abruptly apiculate, minutely tomentose with dense, tiny crisped hairs and sparse longer, straight, patulous hairs; endocarp corneous, ovoid-oblong, rather acute, when dry and open coracle shaped. Seeds single, oblong, subacute, red-brownish, ca 4 mm long, 2 mm broad.

description: Tree with terminal branchlets triquetrous, glabrous, slightly striate, lenticellate, brownish, the internodes 2-3 cm long. Stipules geminate, sometimes an extra one in the middle, lanceolate, about 1 mm long. Leaves simple, ternate, coriaceous, glabrous throughout. Petiole 1-2 cm long, robust, sulcate above, more or less carinate below, slightly broadened and clasping the base. Blades 11-18 cm long, 3-6 cm wide, oblong-lanceolate, narrowing and acute at the apex, cuneate-attenuate at the base, narrowly decurrent to the petiole, bicrenate-serrate, the teeth 4-6 mm apart, 1.0-1.5 mm long, acute but soon obturate; green and shining above, the costa impressed, the secondary nerves thin and depressed, the smaller veins obsolete; dull yellowish green beneath, the costa reddish, nitidous, thickly prominent, the secondary nerves very prominent, 11-12 pairs, 6-8 mm apart, parallelly ascending, with a divergence angle of 30°-40°, usually furcating near the margin, the transversal tertiary veins joining the lesser into a minute prominulous, reddish, very conspicuous reticulum. Cymose panicles axillary, subterminal, glabrous, the peduncle very long, robust, striate, the primary branches also robust, patulous, the ultimate branchlets very short, bearing short pedicellate, glomerate flowers; bracts ovate or oblong, 3-2 mm long, 1.5-1.0 mm broad, the uppermost bracteoles linear, 2.0-1.5 mm long, ciliate toward the apex, Male flowers mostly pentamerous; pedicels thick, glabrous, 1-2 mm long; buds globose, 5-angulate, about 3 mm in diam; calyx carnose, about 8 mm in diam, 3.5 mm high, the lobes ovate, acute 3.0-3.5 mm long, green and sparsely puberulous outside, densely tomentose, yellowish, velutinous inside; stamens usually ten, the filaments 3.5 mm long, subulate, thickened at the hirsutous base, the apex capillary and curving, the anthers elliptic, shortly apiculate, about 1.5 mm long, 1 mm thick; carpels five, rudimentary, the ovary densely hispid, 0.5 mm long, the style glabrous, 0.6-1.0mm long, hooked. Disc densely hispid.

description: Tree 5-10 m tall with a dense crown. Branchlets rather robust, brown-reddish, lenticellate-tuberculate, glabrous or puberulous when young, with short, ascendent or appressed, acute hairs, the internodes 1.5-5.0 cm long, obtusely subtetragonal, and sulcate, the terminal ones compressed. Stipules geminate, triangular, sulcate 2.5-3.0 mm long! Leaves opposite, 2-5-jugate; axis 8-13 cm long, mediocre, reddish, glabrous or sometimes minutely puberulous, striolate, sulcate above, carinate beneath, the inter juga 1.5-3.0 cm long, the petiole 2-4 cm long. Leaflets coriaceous, rigid; petiolules sulcate above, 5-9 mm long, the terminal one 12-20 mm long; stipels geminate, acute, 1-2 mm long; blades 5-12 cm long, 2.3-5.0 cm wide, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, obtusely cuneate or subrotundate, asymmetric at the base, shortly attenuate, subacute or obtuse at the apex, revolute and slightly distally serrulate at the margin, the teeth 6-10 mm apart, minutely mucronulate; yellowish dark green, rather smooth, glabrous and lustrous above, the costa and secondary nerves impressed, the minute venular reticulum inconspicuous; pale with reddish nervation beneath, the costa strongly prominent, carinate, the 10-13 secondary nerves on each side very prominent, ascending parallel with an angle of divergence 45°-50°, curved at the margin, 5-8 mm apart, the tertiary nerves subtransversal, anastomosing into a very lax, irregularly and slightly prominulcus reticulum, the smaller, minor reticulum flat; completely glabrous beneath or with very scattered minute strigae on the main nervation. Paniculae axillary sessile or shortly pedunculate, 3-7 cm long, the peduncle 0-1 cm long, compressed, striate, puberulous, the branching pseudoracemose with a main axis and short dichotomous or trichotomous lateral branchlets, all angular, compressed and minutely puberulous. Bracts and bracteoles linear-subulate, 1-2 mm long, puberulous, the ultimate short branchlets ending with several flowers, frequently three. Pedicels rather thick, 1-3 mm long, minutely strigose. Flowers basically pentamerous with four to five carpels, rarely tetramerous, or irregular (i e 6 sepals or 3 carpels); calyx when expanded 7.4-8.0 mm, the lobes ovate triangular, acute, 2.2-3.0 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, scarcely puberulous with few minute strigose hairs outside, densely sericeous (subappressed) inside, also near the margin and apex, minute tomentulose inside; staminodial filaments about 1 mm long, glabrous or with few hairs at the base, anthers oblong, rather acute at the apex, basally emarginate, 0.7 mm long, sterile; ovaries ovoid-oblong, 1.5 mm long, biovulate, densely hispidulous-hirsute; styles about 1.8 mm long, curved at the apex, pilose near the base. Usually two to three, rarely four to five, carpels developed into fruit; fruits immature, ovoid, compressed, curved at the base, attenuate, acute at the apex, densely, minutely velvety-tomentose with ascendent hairs and abundantly hispid (trichomes pungent, 1.0-1.5 mm long). One or two seeds developed in each follicle, ellipsoid, slightly compressed, obtuse at both ends, brownish purple.

description: Tree about 10 m tall (probably taller) with a large, horizontal crown. Terminal branchlets angular-sulcate-compressed, ochraceous-lanate-tomentose with curled hairs. Stipules bigeminate, subulate, 6-3 mm long. Leaves opposite, 3-7-jugate; axis 16-54 cm long, lanuginose-tomentose, ochraceous or ferruginous, the interjuga 3-6 cm long, subterete or very narrowly sulcate above, the stipels geminate, corniculate, 3-5 mm long; petiole robust, subterete, obtusely angular, 10-20 cm long. Leaflets opposite, subcoriaceous, sessile or very shortly petiolulate (the lateral petiolules up to 1.5 mm long, the terminal 5-30 mm long); blades 8-20 cm long, 2.0-5.6 cm wide, elliptic-lanceolate, oblong, asymmetrically attenuate at the base, narrowing to an acute apex, biserrulate-crenate with short, small, acute teeth; dark yellowish-green and rather shining, slightly rugose above, glabrous or with very sparse hairs, the costa impressed, the secondary nerves also impressed, the minute venulose reticulum more or less conspicuous; greenish-gray or ochraceous when dry and tomentose beneath, with a rather dense indumentum of curled, lanate hairs, the costa very prominent, 20-26 pairs of secondary nerves 4-8 mm apart, prominent, subascendent with angle of divergence 50°-65°, furcate and anastomosing near the margin, the tertiary nerves usually transverse and united with the minor veins into a conspicuous prominulous reticulum, the intrareticular surface green, not conspicuously papillose. Inflorescences axillary, shorter than the subtending leaves, 10-14 cm long and up to 8 cm wide, the peduncle stout, obtusely angular, compressed, minutely and densely lanuginose, 3-12 cm long, the first branching robust, trichotomous or dichotomous, the rest dichotomous; branchlets compressed, densely long-lanuginose-hirsute, the ultimate very short, thick, bearing many conglomerate sessile or subsessile flowers. Bracts subulate, 1-4 mm long. Flowers pentamerous; male buds subglobose-pentagonal, about 3.5 mm in diam; calyx 3.5-4.0 mm tall, when expanded about 9 mm in diam, the lobes ovate, acute, 2.5 mm long, 2.2-2.5 mm broad, rather carnose, subglabrous and only pilose near the acute apex inside, densely lanate-tomentose with flexuous and crisped hairs outside; stamens ten, the filaments about 4.5 mm long, pilose and thicker on the lower half, capillary and glabrous toward the apex; anthers elliptic, shortly mucronulate, 1.2 mm long; carpels five, rudimentary, 1.5 mm long, the ovary very short, 0.5 mm long, hirsute, the minute style hamate and glabrous; disc lanate-hirsute.

description: From the new collections, a description of the fruits of the species is possible as follows: Female flowers pentamerous with three carpels, of which only one or two develop to maturity. Fruiting calyx 7-7.5 mm diam., thick, the lobes 2.5 × 1.82 mm, ovate, acute, outside pulverulent, the hairs minute, flexuous and crisped, inside sparsely puberulous. Follicles 8-10 × 5-6 mm, ellipsoid, shortly apiculate, outside cinereous or ochraceous-cinereous, shortly and densely tomentulose-lanate, the short hairs thin, flexuous or crisped, patent and intricate; endocarp 8-9.2 x 4.3-4.5 mm, ellipsoid, one end obtuse, the other obtusely apiculate, when dry and open, 5-7 x 5-7 mm, thickly corneous, very hard, turtle-shaped, minutely apiculate at one end. Seeds single, irregularly ellipsoid, 3 × 2 mm, reddish brown, shining.

description: Trees at about 15 m tall. Branchlets strongly sulcate-quadrangular, the terminal part compressed to ancipital, densely and extremely appressed, lanate-tomentose or arachnoid-lanate, the ochraceous indumentum deciduous with age, lower parts lenticellate, the internodes 3-5 cm long. Stipules bigeminate, subulate, almost the same length, the proxals 7-8 mm, the distals 6-7 mm long. Leaves simple, opposite, rigid coriaceous. Petiole 5-15 mm long, apparently longer due to the narrowing of the base of the lamina, with densely appressed lanate, more or less caducous indumentum. Blades 10-20 cm long, 4.0-6.5 cm wide, elliptic-oblong, narrowing to a short acumen at the apex, long atenuate to the base like a winged continuation of petiole, acutely biserrate, with callous, mucronate teeth, 3-5 mm apart, 1 mm high, the acute, ascending mucros fragile; when young puberulent or minutely crisp-tomentose above, at maturity glabrous, subnitid, slightly rugose, yellowish green with marked impressed costa and secondary nerves, the minor veins less noticeable between the rugosities; ochraceous beneath, densely and persistently appressed-lanate with a compact arachnoid, flat surface, the costa strong, striate, carinate or subcarinate, the secondary nerves in 20-22 pairs, parallel, 5-8 mm apart, prominent and ascending with a divergence angle of 50°-60°, tapering and anastomosing near the margin, the lax, conspicuous reticulum with an arachnoid layer concealing a minute, lanate base. Cymose, thyrsoid panicles axillary, near the end of branchlets, up to 15 cm long. Branching near the base usually trichotomous, also dichotomous, the peduncle only 1.0-2.5 cm long, angulate, as the rhachis and branches striate-sulcate, densely ferrugineous, crisp-tomentose, the deciduous bracts lanceolate, acute, 4-2 mm long. Bracteoles linear or subulate 1.5-2.5 mm long. Male flowers pentamerous, rarely tetramerous, sessile, usually three at the end of each of the very short peduncles, often congested and glomerulate; buds 2.5-3.0 mm in diam; calyx expanded about 7 mm in diam and 3 mm long, the sepals ovate, acute, 2.6-2.8 mm long, 1.4-1.8 mm wide, minutely tomentose outside and at the margins, sparsely pilose inside; stamens ten (to eight), the filaments thickened and hirsutous on the lower half, glabrous, capillary and curving at the upper  half, anthers ovoid-elliptic, minutely apiculate, 0.8-0.9 mm long; carpels three, rudimentary, sterile, the ovary 0.7 mm long, densely hirsute-tomentose with two rudimentary ovules, the style about 0.8 mm long hirsute at the base, glabrous above with a hooked apex. Female flowers and fruits unknown. Most flowers examined were pentamerous with three carpels. Only exceptionally are there four sepals and eight stamens but still with three carpels.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1970. Brunelliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 2: 1-189.

description: Tree 15 m tall. Terminal leafy flowering branchlets rather thin, subterete, slightly striolate, the youngest internode more or less compressed, usually densely or copiously sericeous-strigose, the hairs rather long, straight, appressed. Young shoots, leaves and buds densely ochraceo-villous-sericeous. Stipules geminate, narrow-triangular, acute, appressed-villous, 2-3.5 mm long. Leaves opposite, imparipinnate, 1-2(-3)-jugate, in branches supporting inflorescences usually reduced to trifoliolate and distally to unifoliolate leaves; petiole 4-12 cm, rigid, strigose, terete except for the narrowly sulcate adaxial side; stipels geminate, linear, acute, sericeous, 2-3 mm long; lateral petiolules 7-11 mm long, sulcate adaxially, sericeous; terminal petiolules 15-36 mm long, slender but rigid, sulcate, striolate and sericeous; blades rigidly chartaceous, 8-16 cm long, 4-7.8 cm wide, ovate oblong or ovate-elliptic, obtuse or rounded or shortly cuneate at base, asymmetrical in the lateral ones, symmetrical in the terminal, attenuate to an acuminate, acute apex, the acumen up to 1.5 cm long, margin sinuate, the long shallow, sinuses with a minute, acute, 0.5-0.7 mm long tooth at the end of each secondary nerve, terminal leaflets conspicuously larger than the lateral ones; abaxially rather dark green, main nerves more or less conspicuous, thinly prominulous and ochraceous-strigose, surface minutely reticulate but flat and sparsely appressed pilose; abaxially pale tawny and somewhat shiny-sericeous, densely strigose, hairs straight 0.4-0.8(-1) mm long, antrorse, prostrate, costa very prominent, obtusely carinate and ± striolate, strigose, secondary nerves prominent, 12-17 each side, 5-8(-12) mm apart, ascending, (deviation angle 60-70°), curving in the upper half and terminating at the margin with a minute, acute tooth, tertiary nerves prominulous, irregularly transverse and anastomosing with minor less prominulous veins into a loose reticulum, the wide areoles flat and covered by the general indument. Panicles axillary 8-15 cm long, the branching short and lax, usually the longer first divisions trichotomous the others short, alternate; the main peduncle 1.5-4 cm long, striate, densely sericeous, the axis upwards and the rather short spreading branches with erecto-patent or patent hairs (hirsutulous); bracts triangular-linear, acute, hirsutulous decreasing in length upwards 5-2 mm long; pedicels 0.5-2 mm, hirtellous, flowers isolated or usually 2-4 crowded in small glomerules; bracteoles linear, 1.5-2 mm long. Flowers hermaphrodite, 5-merous or 4-merous, rarely 6-merous. Calyx 6-7 mm diam, when expanded, lobes triangular-ovoid, acute, 2.63 x 1.5-2 mm, sparsely sericeous outside, glabrous except distally sparsely pilose inside, the margins densely papillose; stamens 10(-8), the filaments ca. 3 mm long, densely pilose below, hairs flexuous and up to 1 mm long, distally glabrous, anthers elliptic, 0.6 mm. Carpels 4-5, the ovaries 1-1.2 mm long, ovate, villous-sericeous and distally antrorse-barbate, the hairs about 0.4 mm. Disk obtusely lobate, tomentose, the trichomes 0.2-0.4 mm. Follicles usually 4-1, rarely five maturing, villose-sericeous proximally, antrorsely hirsutulous or villous distally, 2.2-2.3 × 1.6-1.8 mm; endocarp 2 × 1.5-1.9 mm, U-shaped when open and dry, the seeds single, elliptic-ovoid, 1.6 × 1.2 × 1.5-1 mm, the surface shiny and colliculose.

description: Tree with terminal pubescent branchlets soon glabrate. Stipules unknown. Leaves opposite, 4-6-jugate; axis 12-45 cm long, fulvous-hirsutulo-tomentose, bicostulate and canaliculate above, the interjuga 2.0-3.5 cm long, the petiole 6-9 cm long, the stipels about 1 mm long. Leaflets rigidulous, chartaceous; petiolules 0-1 mm long, the terminal ones 6-8 mm long, tomentose; blades elliptic-oblong, sublanceolate, asymmetrically and acutely cuneate at the base, attenuate and acute or sometimes acuminate at the apex, obscurely crenate and subserrate with minute ascending mucros, 7.5-15.0 cm long, 2.5-3.8 cm broad; brown and very lustrous above, subglabrous, the costa impressed, tomentose, the secondary nerves filiform, conspicuous, the minor veins barely noticeable; fulvous-pubescent beneath, the hairs long, more or less flexuous and patulous on the nervation, the secondary nerves 20-22 on each side, prominent, somewhat ascending with angle of divergence 60°-65°, strictly parallel, the tertiary nerves transverse, prominulous, the minor veins very loosely reticulate, prominulous, minute, the venular reticulum flat, the epidermal ground surface densely papillose. Inflorescences axillary, longer than the petioles, trifurcate and dichotomous, 10 cm long, 8 cm broad, the branches fulvous-tomentose, the peduncle about 2 cm long, the ultimate branchlets very short. Bracteoles linear, 1-2 mm long. Pedicels rather thin, 0.6-2.0 mm long, subtomentose, the hairs rather long, flexible, patulous. Flowers tetramerous, unisexual; calyx 2.0-2.3 mm long, when expanded 5.0-5.5 mm in diameter, the lobes about 2.0 × 1.5 mm, finely tomentulose outside, sericeous inside; filaments about 2.5 mm long, glabrous or with a few, short hairs near the base; carpels in male flowers rudimentary, the ovary very minutely hirsute, the styles suberect, glabrous upwards; disc tomentose-hirsute.
bibliographicCitation: Cuatrecasas, José. 1970. Brunelliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 2: 1-189.

description: Stipules usually two, geminate, 2-3 mm long, thickened toward the base, sometimes, mainly at the distal branchlets, three stipules at opposite sides of the node, the medial one being shorter, rarely two pairs of stipules at each side, the two medial being smaller. Stipels l-2(-2.5) mm, always singly geminate. Leaves 2-6-jugate, the petiole 3.5-4 cm long. Leaflet blades usually 6-12 × 2.5-5.7 cm, the proximal ones always smaller. Lateral petiolules 4-20 mm long, the terminal ones 10-30 mm long. Inflorescences rich in flowers or fruits, usually 8-15 cm and longer than the subtending petiole, often larger, up to 20(-25) cm long and broad. Calyx lobes 2.8-3.5 × 1.7-2.2 mm, sericeous inside. Follicles sericeous or subsericeous, densely covered by short, straight trichomes 0.1-0.2 mm long, appressed or subappressed on the main surface; however at the marginal suture, mainly distally, the hairs may be longer (up to 0.5 mm), antrorsely semierect, but never prickly. Seeds up to 3 × 2 mm, in color from reddish brown to red.
