description: Tree 3-60 m (? deciduous or evergreen), sometimes with large plank-buttresses. Leaves 9-22 × 4-10 cm, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, obovate or obovate-oblong to oblanceolate, acuminate at apex, narrowly cuneate at base, pubescent when young then glabrous or nearly so when mature adaxially, densely pubescent when young then subglabrous to sparsely pubescent when mature abaxially; domatia absent. Venation eucamptodromous or eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 5-8(-10) pairs, distant, originating at moderately to widely acute angles, curved, prominent; intersecondary veins present; tertiary veins percurrent; higher order veins usually distinct; areolation large, well-developed to imperfect, slightly prominent. Petiole 1.5-4.5 cm, pubescent when young, becoming glabrous or more or less so, usually biglandular. Inflorescences 7-14 cm, simple, with all flowers bisexual; peduncle 1.5-3 cm, glabrous to sparsely pubescent; rhachis 5.5-11 cm, glabrous to sparsely pubescent. Flowers pentamerous, 4-6 × 4-5.5 mm; lower hypanthium 2-3 mm, very sparsely appressed-pubescent to tomentose with rufous hairs; upper hypanthium 1.5-2 mm, campanulate, glabrous to sparsely pubescent; calyx lobes 1.5-2 mm, revolute, glabrous to sparsely pubescent; disk villous; stamens 4-6 mm; style 5-6 mm, villous in proximal half. Fruits usually few, disposed along whole length or mostly near apex of rhachis, 2.5-4.5 × 2-4.5 cm, strongly flattened, suborbicular to very broadly elliptic or obtriangular in side view, rounded, emarginate or apiculate at apex, rounded to cuneate (not pseudostipitate) at base, glabrous; wings 2, stiff, equal, 7-15 mm wide, Markedly thickened with spongy material adjacent to body and for most way to margin (thin part of wing only ca. 4-6 mm wide), rounded to strongly angled laterally (the angle nearer the fruit apex); body 0.6-1.2 cm wide but appearing much wider due to thickened base of wings, often 1-2-ridged on 1 face and slightly grooved on other. Reproductive biology. Flowers described as white, cream-colored, yellow, greenish yellow, whitish green, green; no evidence of dichogamy. Flowers sweetly scented, said by Sagot and Aublet to smell like those of Prunus mahaleb L. Flowering June to October; fruiting September to December, April. The corky fruits are presumably suited to water dispersal.

description: Deciduous shrub or tree 2.5-30 m. Leaves 3.5-16 × 1.5-7 cm, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, usually obovate, less often obovate-oblong or -elliptic or narrowly so, rounded to acute or abruptly and shortly acuminate at apex, cuneate to attenuate-cuneate at base, tomentose when young, later glabrous to sparsely pubescent except sparsely to densely pubescent on main veins adaxially, pubescent to densely so abaxially (more densely on main veins) sometimes becoming subglabrous by fruiting, sometimes remaining densely pubescent until next crop of flowers and leaves appear; pocket-shaped or bow -shaped domatia present in secondary veinaxils. Venation eucamptodromous or sometimes eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 5-8 pairs, moderately spaced to distant, originating at moderately acute angles, curved, prominent; intersecondary veins usually absent; tertiary veins closely and very regularly and conspicuously percurrent; higher order veins usually distinct; areolation imperfect, usua11y not prominent. Petiole 0.5-1.5 cm, biglandular at junction with leaf. Inflorescences 5-18 cm, simple with all flowers bisexual; peduncle 1-2.5 cm, pubes cent to tomentose; rhachis 4-18 cm, pubescent to tomentose. Flowers pentamerous, 4-5 × 3-4.5 mm; lower hypanthium 1.8-3 mm, tomentose; upper hypanthium 0.5-1 mm, shallowly campanulate to shallowly infundibuliform, appressed- to patent-pubescent or densely so; calyx lobes 0.3-1 mm, pubescent as upper hypanthium, suberect to patent; disk densely pilose; stamens 2.5-4.5 mm; style 3-4 mm, glabrous. Fruits numerous, disposed along whole length of rhachis, 0.4-0.6 × 1-2.2 cm, usually yellowish brown to pale brown, otherwise as in T. amazonia.

description: Shrub or small tree to ca. 5(-8) m tall, with often contorted trunks and thick, corky, furrowed bark; twigs glabrous to sparsely pubescent, with ± nonchambered pith; buds to ca. 1.5 mm long, leaves re volute. Leaves alternate or subopposite or whorled, often variable in arrangement, even within single twig; coriaceous, ovate to oblong, 2.5-8(-9.3) × 0.8-2.6 cm, base rounded to truncate and often slightly asymmetric, apex acute to acuminate or shortly so, to nearly rounded-mucronate, margin entire and sometimes undulate, plane to very slightly revolute, especially near base, adaxial surface glabrous (sparsely pubescent on midvein), abaxial surface glabrous (very sparsely pubescent on midvein near base), with usually at least few inconspicuous (to conspicuous) glandular dots along midvein; petiole 6-41 mm long, slender, frequently flexuous. Inflorescences axillary racemes to 1-6 cm long; rachis moderately to densely ferruginous/crisped-pubescent; pedicels 2-6 mm long, sparsely to densely ferruginous-pubescent; bracteoles 2, opposite to alternate, from nearly basal to near midpoint of pedicel, narrowly triangular, to ca. 1.1 mm long; floral bracts to ca. 1.7 mm long. Flowers with triangular calyx lobes, with acuminate (to acute) apices, 1-1.8 x 0.5-1.2 mm, abaxial surface essentially glabrous; corolla cylindrical, white (to reddish), 6-10.5 x 2.5-5 mm, glabrous; filaments 3-4.5 mm long; anthers 0.8-1.1 mm long; ovary glabrous to sparsely pubescent. Capsules ovoid to short-ovoid, 3-5 x 4-5 mm, placentae subapical; seeds 1.8-2.5 mm long.

description: Trees to ca. 20 m tall, with thick ridged bark. Inflorescence terminal, racemose or narrowly paniculate. Flowers white or greenish cream, the calyx cupular, lepidote, early caducous, the corolla tubular-salverform or infundibuliform, the lobes poorly defined and deeply laciniate-margined, lacking a differentiated basal portion of tube below stamen insertion; stamens four or five, the anthers exserted or subexserted, pendulous, slightly twisted; ovary linear, the ovules in 2 series; disk thick, fleshy. Fruit a linear capsule, slightly curved, subterete, tapering to base and apex, prominently longitudinally costate, lepidote, the septum thin and flat; seeds thin, bialate, the wings hyaline-membranaceous.

description: Small to medium-sized trees. Leaves palmately 5-9-foliolate, the leaflets cuneate and with poorly developed petiolules. Inflorescence a corymbose terminal panicle. Flowers yellow and brown to yellowish outside and magenta inside, the calyx broadly campanulate, less than 2 mm long, 5-lobed; corolla broadly campanulate from base, the lobes triangular, valvate, the tube puberulous or glandular lepidote outside; stamens didynamous with pubescent anthers; ovary linear-oblong or linear-conical, lepidote and more or less puberulous, the ovules multiseriate in each locule; disk annular-pulvinate. Fruit a linear capsule, longitudinally striate-costate, twisted, more or less terete; seeds bialate, the hyaline-membranaceous wings long, irregular, conspicuously demarcated from the seed body.

description: Tree, usually tall, height to 30-35 m, dbh to 100120 cm. Trunk monopodial, erect, straight, terete and slender, often clear of branches 2/3 to 3/5 its length. Bark thick, rough, scaly, breaking into large plates divided by broad, shallow or deep fissures, reddish brown to dark brown, outer bark grey; on young trees and branches thin, rough and scaly, reddish brown. Branches of first order heavy, long, spreading horizontally or curved down; of second and higher orders ascending or spreading, the lower branches subpendulous, slender. Crown in young trees pyramidal, open, in old trees rounded or flat-topped, open or dense. Shoots at first orange brown or glaucous, rough with persistent, decurrent pulvini. Cataphylls up to 15 X 3-4 mm, subulate, scarious, soon reflexed, with erose-ciliate margins and caudate apex, dark brown. Vegetative buds ovoid to ovoid-acute, the terminal buds 15-30 X 10-15 mm, the laterals smaller, not resinous, brown; the scales spreading or recurved at apex, with long-ciliate, white or brown margins. Fascicle sheaths initially long, 15-30 mm, with ca. 10 imbricate, orange-brown to red-brown scales with ciliate margins, persistent but reduced to ca. 10 mm, with a thickened base, weathering grey-black. Leaves in fascicles of 3-5, spreading at a wide angle from the shoot, persisting 2-3 years, rigid to slightly lax, straight or slightly curved and twisted, (8-)10-20(-25) cm X 0.9-1.8 mm, margins serrulate, apex acute to pungent, light yellowish green or glaucous-green. Stomata on all faces of leaves, in (3-)4-8(-12) lines on the convex abaxial face and in (3-)4(-5) lines on each adaxial face (the abaxial number of lines correlated with width of leaf). Leaf anatomy: Cross section (transverse-)triangular; hypodermis multi-layered, with intrusions into the mesophyll; resin ducts (3-)5-10, medial, usually 3 larger (external) ducts present; stele elliptic in cross section; outer cell walls of endodermis thickened; vascular bundles 2, more or less connate or distinctly separate. Pollen cones densely clustered near the proximal end of a new shoot, subtended by subulate bracts with ciliate margins, ovoid-oblong to cylindrical, 15-20 X 5 mm, yellowish to yellowish brown. Seed cones subterminal, solitary, in pairs or whorls of 3-5, on short, curved, persistent peduncles retaining a few scales on the branches. Immature cones ovoid-globose, ca. 15 X 10-12 mm, with sharp, curved or spreading spines, purple to purplish brown, maturing time two seasons. Mature cones seemingly sessile, ovoid or broadly ovoid with parted scales, asymmetrical at obliquely flattened base, often slightly curved, (4.5-)5-10(-14) X 3.5-6(-8) cm when open. Seed scales ca. 90-140, most numerous at the base of the cone, parting to release the seeds except at the base, thick, rigid, broadly oblong, nearly straight or recurved especially near the base, dark purplish to blackish brown on the abaxial side, light brown with faint marks of seed wings on the adaxial side. Apophysis raised in the central part, rhombic to pentagonal in outline, mostly symmetrical around the cone, transversely keeled, ochraceous to light reddish brown. Umbo dorsal, raised and slightly recurved or nearly flat, rhombic, transversely keeled, 4-8 mm wide, grey, with a minute, deciduous prickle. Seeds obliquely ovoid, slightly flattened, 4-7 x 35 mm, light brown with black spots. Seed wings articulate but effective, held to the seed by two flimsy claws, obliquely ovate, 12-20 X 4-8 mm, semi-transparent, greyish brown with black tinge. Number of cotyledons 10-12.

description: Shrub to 2.5 m tall (subrepent); mature stems terete, striate, short-ferruginous-tomentose becoming cinerous then glabrate; twigs flexuous, terete to subterete, densely short-ferruginous-tomentose. Leaves coriaceous, basically flat, elliptic to elliptic-ovate, (3-)4-7.5 × (1.5-)2-4 cm, base rounded or cuneate and short-decurrent, apex rounded to acute, margin entire, subrevolute, bearing 3-4 pairs of round, sessile to slightly raised, pustular glands near and onto the petiole, young blades ferruginous-tomentose but glabrate and then nitid above, densely and persistently dark brown tomentose beneath; pinnately nerved with midrib impressed above and raised beneath, lateral nerves (3-5 per side) plane to slightly raised above and raised beneath but usually obscure; petiole stout, subterete, (5-)7-13 mm long, tomentose as stems. Inflorescence rarely branched near base, 5-11-flowered; rachis flexuous, subterete, 2-7.5 cm long, densely and shortly ferruginous-tomentose so as to obscure actual surface; floral bract ovate to elliptic, keeled or flat, 3-10 mm long, obtuse, tomentose as rachis; pedicel subterete, 3-7(-10) mm long; bracteoles broadly ovate, 2-4 mm long, acute. Flowers with calyx tomentose as rachis, (5-)6-9 mm long, lobes oblong-ovate to ovate, (3.5-)5-6.5 mm long, acute, tomentose within in distal half; corolla 8-10 mm long, ferruginous-tomentose on exposed surfaces opposite the lobes and glabrous between, dull rose (to blood-red within) when fresh, lobes ovate to deltoid, 4-5 mm long, acute, ferruginous at tips within; stamens 4-7 mm long; filaments 2-5 mm long, densely tufted with reddish to tan hairs; anthers 2-3.5 mm long; thecae ca. 1-2 mm long, base rounded; tubules 1-1.2 mm long, dehiscing by slightly oblique, terminal pores; ovary densely short-ferruginous-tomentose; style glabrous, 2.5-4.5 mm long. Berry spherical, glabrate, ca. 1 cm diam., dark ferruginous-colored.

description: Shrub to 3(-5) m tall with arching branches; mature stems terete, weakly striate, bearing a few hispid hairs or their bases; twigs often distally flexuous, terete to subterete, striate, densely ferruginous-to cinereous-tomentose at tips but glabrate, also moderately to densely hispid with minutely gland-tipped hairs to 2.5 mm long. description: Plant flowering ca 2 m high. description: Tree, to 25 m tall or shrub. Branch bark gray or beige, peeling to dark red-brown beneath, glabrous. Lenticels inconspicuous, minute (< 0.2 mm diam.) to conspicuous, 0.3-1.2 mm diam, granular, plane or raised, pale orange to orange-brown. Leaves simple, thin-coriaceous, drying pale green to pinkish-brown, matte to semi-shiny above, rarely shiny, glabrous. Petiole 0.5-2 cm long × 0.75-2 mm wide at midlength, 1/4-1/6 the length of the lamina, subterete at base, flattening out gradually above, even somewhat sulcate, with lamina sides descending, remaining semiterete beneath, the indumentum adaxially on petioles near the shoot apex, the hairs pale yellow to gray, short, appressed, glabrescent. Lamina 3.5-9 × l-3.5(-5) cm, length:breadth (1.7-)2-3:1, elliptic to narrowly obovate, less frequently widely obovate or oblong; base acute-cuneate, long-cuneate to cuneate-decurrent, flat, symmetrical; apex acute, rounded at the terminus, more rarely obtuse, frequently retuse, always with apical point of midrib protruding; margin generally crenate to bluntly serrate with l-3(-4) pairs of well-spread teeth in upper half, the teeth frequently terminating in apical point of lateral veins, less commonly entire or undulate, revolute in lower half; venation not usually conspicuous above, plane to slightly raised, the midrib frequently narrowly grooved, more conspicuous and prominent beneath, eucamptodromous to semicraspedodromous, the midvein reaching the apex; lateral veins 4-5 pairs. Inflorescence axillary or terminal, unbranched, 2-10.5 × 1.5-2 cm, the indumentum red-brown to ferruginous, short-tomentose to sparsely short-pilose or glabrous; peduncle 0.2-4 cm × 0.8-1.2 mm, the sterile bracts few towards base. Common bracts 0.4-0.5 × 0.4-0.6 mm, short red-brown tomentose to glabrous except for fimbriate margin of wavy, soft, ferruginous hairs. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels 1.5-3 × 0.3-0.5 mm, the indumentum sparse, he hairs appressed, or glabrous. Buds 0.8-1.5 mm broad at the apex, 0.4-1 mm broad at midlength, glabrous. Rowers 5-8 mm long; filaments 0-0.5 mm long, adnate 4-5 mm from base of tepals; anthers 1.5-2.5 × 0.3-0.6 mm; nectary lobes 0.3-0.5 mm long, separate; style not curved at apex; ovary hairs extending 1-1.5 mm from base of ovary, frequently unevenly spread in tufts with glabrous areas in-between, the hairs orange-brown, short-strigose; ovules 0.6-0.7 × 0.2-0.4 mm. Infructescence 5-13 cm long, glabrous. Fruit pedicels 2-3 × 1.5-2.5 mm, glabrous. Fruit 2.5-3.5 × 1.2-1.6 mm, oval-oblong to narrowly obovate, the apex coming to a very brief point or constricted for 1-2 mm, the base constricted for 2-3 mm, upper and lower edges ± equal in outline, sometimes sutured side more flattened, sutured and unsutured sides curved gently or flattened, glabrous, smooth, dark brown becoming gray, style not persistent. Seeds 2-2.4 × 0.9-1.6 mm. Diagnostic characters. Very typical of this species are the generally crenate to serrulate leaf margins with 1-3 pairs of serrations or crenations on the upper half of the leaf. The lower portion of the margin is entire. The ovary is also quite conspicuous in most specimens, with the indumentum usually unevenly distributed in patches or tufts, commonly forming longitudinal bold streaks on the ovary. It could be confused with Roupala pallida, which has a similar leaflet margin, but R. pallida has coriaceous leaves and a glabrous ovary, and it is found on the coastal strip of Santa Catarina, Brazil.

description: Shrub 1.5-3 m tall. Mature stems and older branches terete, fissured, indumentum of closely appressed, gray, linear, flattened, multicellular-multiseriate hairs with a reddish-brown vesiculate base; twigs terete, with loosely appressed, gray, linear flattened, multicellular-multiseriate hairs with reddish-brown vesiculate bases, and sometimes additionally with short, reddish-orange, spreading, multi-cellular-multiseriate, glandular hairs or pustules. Leaves arising from the same terminal bud as the flowers, evergreen, coriaceous, flat, elliptic to slightly oblanceolate, 2.6-6.5 × 0.7-2.1 cm, apex acute with a broad, blunt mucro, base cuneate, margin with long, linear, flattened cilia, sometimes with brown, vesiculate bases; adaxial surface with long, slightly flattened, multicellular-multiseriate hairs and sometimes with scattered, multicellular hairs with vesiculate bases, adaxial surface rugulose, with long, orange, flattened, linear, multicellular-multiseriate hairs, sometimes with very short multi-cellular-multiseriate, glandular hairs; petiole channeled, 3-10 mm long, 0.5-1.0 mm diam., densely covered with long, flattened, multicellular-multiseriate hairs and multicellular-multiseriate, glandular hairs. Inflorescence terminal, an umbelliform raceme, 1-4-flowered; perulae ovate, acute to acuminate, base rounded, margin with long, flattened, multicellular-multiseriate hairs and capitate cilia, adaxial surface as on the underside of the leaf; pedicels ascending, 7-13 mm long, 0.7-0.8 mm diam., densely covered with appressed to slightly spreading, orange, linear, lacerate, multicellular hairs with gland-like, reddish-brown, vesicular bases, the hairs usually small but with larger hairs on the same type intermingled. Flowers 5-merous; calyx 7-15 × 413 mm, campanulate, calyx tube cup-shaped, 1-4 × 4-6 mm, tan to greenish, with fringed-vesicular hairs or multicellular-multiseriate, glandular hairs and flattened, multicellular-multiseriate hairs, lobes lanceolate to ovate, 4.3-10 x 2.1-4 mm, apex acuminate to obtuse or rounded, sometimes erose, margin with elongate cilia, occasionally glandular or with long and short cilia interspersed, adaxial surface with multicellular-multiseriate, glandular hairs or with fringed-vesicular hairs; corolla funnelform to funnel-campanulate, 4-5 × 5.5 cm, reddish-violet to red, tube 15-16 mm long, lobes 22-33 × 13-20 mm, broadly rounded, slightly spreading; stamens 8-10, 23-30 mm long; filaments ca. 0.3 mm diam., with short, translucent scales on the lower portion; anthers 1.7-2 × 0.7-1 mm, with a small nipple at the base; ovary very densely covered with long, fringed-vesicular hairs; style sinuate, glabrous, 3845 mm long, 0.5 mm diam.; stigma truncate. Capsule and seeds not seen on Neotropical material.

description: Shrub, or treelet, 0.5-8 m tall, to 20 cm dbh. Branch bark dark red-brown to dark gray, with short longitudinal fissures, mostly glabrous. Lenticels absent, rarely few, minute, granular, plane, orange-brown. Leaves simple, rigid-coriaceous, drying pale green above, green-brown beneath, matte or shiny, the young leaves with dense indumentum on both sides of lamina, indumentum furfuraceous, dark brown to dark red-brown beneath, sometimes persistent above, pale yellow (seen only with dissecting microscope), the hairs very short, swollen at the base, close-appressed, glabrescent with age, the indumentum sometimes remaining as gray or black patches. Petiole well defined, (0.3-) 1.5-3.5(-6) cm long × 3.5-4 mm broad at midlength, 1/3-1/8 the length of the lamina, rugose, grooved where lamina joins, the indumentum glabrescent, gray hairs sometimes persisting at base. Lamina (3.5-)6-12(-14.5) × (1.5-)4-10 cm, length:breadth ratio 1-2:1, wide-elliptic or wide-ovate, rarely ovate, very wide-ovate, or wide-oblong; base obtuse to rounded to truncate, rarely acute, usually symmetrical, often folded over; apex acute, obtuse, or rounded, the apical point of midrib not protruding; margin entire, very rarely with 2-3 pairs of large crenations, not revolute, the rim markedly thickened; venation conspicuous above, often more so than below, the midrib narrowly and shallowly grooved, the lateral veins slightly impressed to slightly raised above, ± conspicuous to inconspicuous, raised beneath (tertiary venation obscure beneath), semicraspedodromous, the branching very irregular, often angular, with a large distance between lowermost and next lowest pairs of lateral veins (except in leaves with rounded to truncate bases, where the lower pairs tend to be closely juxtaposed), the midvein losing strength towards the apex but generally reaching it; lateral veins 3-6 pairs. Inflorescence 10-25 × 1.8-2.5 cm, axillary, unbranched, overtopping leaves, becoming thickened and woody, the indumentum furfuraceous, the hairs short, close-appressed, dark red-brown, swollen at the base; peduncle 0.8-2 cm × 1.5-2.8 mm, with a few sterile bracts towards the base. Common bracts 0.6-1 × 0.40.8 mm, glabrous within and without except for a fimbriate margin of dark red hairs. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels 2-4.5 × 0.5-1 mm, the indumentum as for inflorescence. Buds 1.2-1.8 mm broad at the apex, 0.8-1.3 mm broad at midlength, robust, square in cross section, dark brown or purple-gray, the hairs swollen at the base, short, sparse especially towards apex, dark red. Flowers 6-12 cm long; filaments 0.5-1 mm long, adnate 4.5-9 mm from base of tepals; anthers 2-3 × 0.4-0.7 mm; nectary lobes 0.4-0.6 mm long, in contact at base, separating farther up; ovary hairs extending 2.5-4 mm from base of ovary, covering entire ovary and base of style, short-strigose, dark red to red-brown; ovules 0.6-0.7 × 0.2-0.3 mm. Infructescences (5)12.5-14.5 cm long, glabrous or glabrescent; fruit pedicels 3-4.5 × (1.2-) 1.5-2.5 mm, the indumentum as for infructescence. Fruit (1.8-)3-3.8 × (1.1-)1.3-1.9 cm, oval, sutured and unsutured sides curved ± to same degree, strong marginal vein running around periphery of fruit, raised, particularly on sutured side, the base constricted for 3-5 mm, the apex a small point, constricted ca. 1.5 mm or less, the style sometimes persistent, smooth or minutely rugulose, glabrous, dark brown. Seeds 1.72.7 × 0.7-1 cm.

description: Tree, 3-10(-20) m tall, or shrub, 1.5-2.5 m tall. Branch bark dark gray to red-gray or brown, the indumentum yellow-brown to red-brown, velutinous to long-tomentose in young stems, becoming short-tomentose and fading to gray, persistent. Lenticels developing eventually after the indumentum lost or sparse, few, inconspicuous, usually < 0.5 mm diam, (seen to 1 mm longest axis), granular, plane becoming raised as rim forms, orange to brown. Leaves simple, lobed and compound, coriaceous, short- to long-petiolate, drying brown, matte or shiny, densely yellow-brown or rufous-velutinous above and beneath when young, gradually glabrescent, the hairs persisting on base of midrib above, and more generally beneath, fading to gray. Compound leaves with 1 -4 pairs of leaflets, sometimes the pairs misaligned so the leaflets are alternate, 13-26 cm long (inclusive of petiole), 7-19 cm broad; petiole 2.5-6(-8.5) cm long. Lateral leaflets 4-11.5 × 1.5-4.2 cm, length: breadth 2-3(4.5):l, the base strongly asymmetrical, the broader side of the lamina facing the terminal leaflet, acute to obtuse, at times the shortest side of the lamina acute, the longer side obtuse, the apex attenuate, 5-8 lateral vein pairs, the margins entire; petiolules 0-0.8 mm long. Terminal leaflets 7.5-14 × 3.2-6(-8) cm, length:breadth 1.5-2.5(-3.5): 1; base obtuse to acute; apex attenuate; lateral veins 6-8(-10) pairs; margins entire; petiolules 0-3 cm long. Compound leaves of juvenile plants with considerably longer and narrower leaves, long-attenuate at apex and long-cuneate at base, length to breadth ratio of lateral leaflets 4-6.5:1, and of terminal leaflets ca. 4.5:1. Simple leaf petiole commonly well defined, 1-6 cm long × 1.5-4 mm broad at midlength, (1/1.8-) 1/2.31/19.5 the length of the lamina, terete proximally, somewhat canaliculate towards blade as lamina sides descending petiole form a channel between them, the indumentum yellow-brown, velutinous to tomentose, fading to gray, rarely becoming completely glabrous. Lamina 6-21 x(3-)4-10(-12) cm, length:breadth 1.1-2.5:1, predominantly ovate, also wide- to narrow-ovate, or narrow-oblong to oblong; base obtuse- or rounded-decurrent, cordate or truncate, symmetrical, one side of lamina folded over the other; apex predominantly attenuate, sometimes acute, obtuse or acuminate, the apical point of midrib not protruding; margin entire, or serrate with 1-3(6) pairs of serrations at transitional stage between simple and compound leaves, not revolute but with prominence of marginal vein giving the appearance of being so; venation raised and ± conspicuous above, the finer reticulation more evident than in other species, and raised and conspicuous beneath, eucamptodromous to semicraspedodromous, the midvein reaching the apex; lateral veins (5-)6-8(-12) pairs. Inflorescences 7-24(-28) × 1.8-2.8 cm, axillary, unbranched, rarely two arising in same leaf axil, densely pale brown, yellow-brown to rufous, velutinous or tomentose; peduncle 1-3.5(-6) cm × 1.2-2 mm, a few sterile bracts persistent. Common bracts l-1.5(-2) × 0.6-1 mm, densely velutinous to tomentose to the outside, glabrous within. Flower-pair axis absent to 1 mm long. Pedicels (1.5-)2-4(-5) mm long, the indumentum as for inflorescence. Buds 1.4-2 mm broad at apex, 0.7-1.2 mm broad at midlength, indumentum as for inflorescence. Flowers 7-11 mm long; filaments 0.3-1 mm long, adnate 5.5-9 mm from base of tepals; anthers 1.7-2.6 × 0.3-0.4 mm; nectary lobes 0.3-0.6 mm long, in contact with each other at the base, then separating as lobes narrowing upward; ovary hairs extending (1-) 1.5-2(-2.5) mm from the base of the ovary, covering entire ovary, long, weak, straight, ferruginous to rufous, also with sericeous hairs, dense, bushing outward; ovules 0.4-0.5 × 0.2-0.3 mm. Infructescence 9-21(-34) cm long, densely tomentose; fruit pedicels (3-)4-6x 1-1.5 mm, tomentose. Fruit 1.8-3.2 × 0.9-1.5 cm, both sutured and unsutured side curved to similar degrees, or sutured side slightly more curved, the base constricted for (l-)3-7 mm, the apex not constricted to constricting for 2.5-3.5 mm, sharp with persistence of style, straight or curved so apex perpendicular to unsutured side, yellow-brown velutinous, sometimes slowly glabrescent, if so, light brown-gray beneath, the marginal vein protruding around periphery of mature fruit; young fruit rounded when immature. Seeds 1.3-1.4 × 0.6-0.9 cm.

description: Tree, 10-21 m tall. Young branch indumentum dense, long, dark brown tomentose, glabrescent; older branch bark gray-brown, becoming fissured. Lenticels absent. Leaves compound, or lobed and simple on fertile adults, thin-coriaceous to coriaceous, drying bicolorous, glaucous above, pale green to pale brown beneath, glabrous above, long-tomentose along midrib and towards base of lamina beneath, glabrescent, the indumentum persistent along midrib on both sides. Compound leaves 9.5-30 × 4-11 cm, one lateral leaflet to seven pairs; petiole 1.5-5 cm long. Lateral leaflets 1.5-10 × 0.6-2.3 cm, length:breadth 2.5-4.7:1, the base cuneate on narrow side, acute to obtuse on broad side, asymmetrical, the apex attenuate; lateral veins 1-6 pairs; margins strongly serrate; petiolules 0-0.4 cm long. Terminal leaflets 4-12 × 1.5-4.5 cm, length:breadth 2.3-3:1, the base acute to cuneate, symmetrical to strongly asymmetrical, the apex attenuate to acute; lateral veins 4-5 pairs; margins as for lateral leaflets; petiolules 0-1.5 cm long. Simple leaf petiole not well defined, 1.5-4 cm long × 1-1.5 mm broad at midlength, 1/1.81/3.5 the length of the lamina, canaliculate at lamina end, subterete at the base, long-tomentose, the indumentum persistent. Lamina 5-13 × 2-5 cm, length:breadth 2.3-3.5:1, narrowly ovate to lanceolate; base narrow to broad cuneate, pressing flat, symmetrical; apex acute to long-attenuate, apical point of midrib not protruding; margin strongly serrate, 11-19 pairs of serrations, the teeth not curving inward, less commonly ± entire, revolute at the base; venation impressed to slightly raised, inconspicuous above, slightly raised, conspicuous beneath, semicraspedodromous; midvein reaching the apex; lateral veins 4-6 pairs. Inflorescences 11-20.5 × 2 cm, axillary, unbranched, the indumentum sparsely long-tomentose, dark brown; peduncle 0.2-1.5(-4) cm × 1.2-1.8 mm, sterile bracts few to abundant at the base. Common bracts 1.6-2.3 × 1-1.2 mm, glabrous both sides, the margin fimbriate, with a tuft of red-brown hairs at the apex, scars conspicuous after bracts have dropped. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels 0.5-2 × 0.3-0.5 mm, glabrous. Buds 0.8-1 mm broad at apex, 0.4-0.5 mm broad at midlength, glabrous. Flowers 7.5-9.5 mm long; filaments 0-0.2 mm long, adnate 6.5-7.5 mm from base of tepals; anthers 2.5-3 × 0.3-0.5 mm; nectary lobes 0.4 mm long, well separated; ovary hairs covering entire ovary evenly, extending 1.5-1.7 mm from base of ovary, short, straight, erect, or slightly spreading-crispate, orange; ovules 0.6-0.7 × 0.2-0.3 mm. Fruit unknown.

description: Small tree, or shrub. Young branch indumentum densely orange- to red-brown tomentose, fading to gray and soon glabrescent. Older stems pale gray to beige, peeling to dark gray beneath, glabrous. Lenticels few, inconspicuous, <0.5 mm diam., raised at the periphery, granular within, orange to reddish-brown. Leaves simple, thin-coriaceous, petiolate, drying reddish-brown, shiny above, glabrous. Petiole 1-2 cm long × 1.75-2 mm wide at midlength, 1/7.8-1/10 the length of the lamina, grooved at lamina end, subterete towards base, residue of short, gray tomentum persisting towards the base, otherwise glabrous. Lamina 9.5-15 × 5-7.5 cm, length:breadth 1.8-2:1, wide-elliptic to elliptic, base acute to obtuse and decurrent; apex obtuse, sometimes abruptly acuminate, apical point of midrib not protuberant; margin entire, revolute at the base; venation slightly raised, ± conspicuous above, raised and conspicuous beneath, semicraspedodromous; lateral veins 6-8 pairs. Inflorescence lateral or axillary, unbranched, 6.5-15 × 2.3-2.5 cm, the indumentum short, sparse, rufous-brown strigose mixed with erect puberulous hairs; peduncle 0.4-2 cm long, 1-1.2 mm broad, sterile bracts few towards the base. Common bracts 0.8 × 0.6 mm, with a few strigose hairs at base and around margin, rufous. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels 2.5-4 × 0.5-0.7 mm, the indumentum as for rhachis. Buds 1.2 mm broad at apex, 0.6 mm at midlength, the indumentum sparse, appressed, rufous puberulous or strigose. Flowers 7.5-10 mm long; anthers ca. 2.2 × 0.3 mm, sessile, attached 7 mm from the base of the tepals; nectary lobes 0.5 mm long, touching each other at the base, well separated above; ovary hairs extending 1-1.2 mm from the base of the ovary, hairs brown, very short, appressed strigose, sometimes indumentum lower on one side than on the other, ovary keeled; ovules 0.6 × 0.3 mm. Fruit not known.

description: Tree, 1.5-15(-25) m, or shrub, 1.5-5 m tall. Young branch indumentum orange-brown, red-brown or dark brown, short to long velutinous, fading to gray and becoming tomentose, slowly glabrescent, the hairs persisting on previous years’ seasonal growth unit; older stem bark often obscured with persistence of indumentum, otherwise brown or sandy yellow, Assuring to dark brown, or dark gray, or red-brown beneath. Lenticel presence frequently obscured by indumentum, minute between fissures when evident, expanding to 0.5 mm long, plane or slightly raised, pores horizontally elongated. Leaves usually simple (juvenile leaves compound), rigid-coriaceous, often splitting on drying, yellow- to olive-green, ochraceous to mid brown above when dried, ferruginous, rufous, or brown beneath with indumentum, ± concolorous after lower indumentum shed. Petiole well defined, 0-3.5 cm long × 2.1-3.3 mm broad at midlength, 1/2.6-1/20 times the length of the lamina, terete or subterete, somewhat flatter adaxially towards lamina, lanate initially, becoming tomentose and fading to gray, slowly glabrescent. Lamina of persistent, mature leaves 2-13 × 2-10 cm (frequently longer and subtended by longer petioles on weak shoots emerging from the trunk and the shoots of new seasonal growth units), length:breadth 1.2-2:1, elliptic to wide-elliptic to suborbiculate, widely obovate or narrowly to widely ovate; base acute, obtuse, rounded, or subcordate, often rapidly decurrent, mostly symmetrical; apex acute through obtuse to rounded, at times retuse, the apical point of midrib not protruding or protruding as minute point; margin often revolute towards base, entire, more rarely serrate with 5-10 pairs of serrations, serrate leaves usually mixed with entire leaflets; venation slightly prominent above, obscure to conspicuous, very prominent below; lateral veins 5-10 pairs, diverging from midrib at an angle of 40-80° at base, 20-60° at mid lamina and (30-)40-60° at the apex, the veins branching, usually between half and three-quarters of the distance from midrib to margin, the basal vein often eucamptodromous, the remaining venation semicraspedodromous, often with double bifurcations of lateral veins forming a double fractiflexed marginal vein; indumentum ferruginous, rufous or brown, short, appressed-tomentose to velutinous above and beneath when new (a sparser covering forming on the leaves produced by thin, weak shoots), rapidly glabrescent above, the hairs sometimes fading to gray beneath, persisting to varying degrees (strongly persistent in var. jahnii and frequently leaving a dirty brown appearance once hairs have been lost, gradually glabrescent beneath in var. pseudocordata), often with a dense covering of short, swollen-based trichomes (glandular ?) predominantly on the lamina, with long, narrow-based trichomes sparse over the lamina, dense along midrib and venation; mid vein reaching the apex. Inflorescences unbranched, axillary, new flush of leaves terminal to inflorescence-bearing region, 5-23 × 1.5-3.5 cm, the indumentum dense, short-tomentose; peduncle 0.3-4.3cm × 2-3 mm, with few or no sterile bracts towards the base. Common bracts 0.5-2 × 0.5-2 mm, ferruginous to rufous, rarely pale yellow-brown, very velutinous, less often tomentose to the outside, glabrous within. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels 0.5-6 × 0.5-1.5 mm, velutinous to tomentose, the indumentum ferruginous to rufous. Flowers 4.5-12 mm long, the perianth indumentum as for pedicel, sometimes shorter and more appressed; filaments 0-1.2 mm long, attached 3.5-5.5 mm from the base of the tepals; anthers 1.2-3 mm long; nectary 0.3-0.5 mm long, the lobes well separated; ovary hairs short-velutinous to long-sericeous, bushing outwards or erect, covering entire ovary, extending 1-3(-5.5) mm from base of ovary, yellow-brown, yellow-orange, or rufous; ovules 0.5-0.8 mm. Infructescence 4.2-22 cm long, glabrescent, patchy tomentose or velutinous, the indumentum gray, black, or ferruginous; fruit pedicels frequently merged with fruit when mature, subsessile, 2.5(-3.5)× 1.5-2 mm. Fruit 2-3.5(-4) × 0.7-1.8 cm, oval to more commonly elongate, both sides curved +/- to same degree, or sutured side frequently flattened or curved inwards with unsutured side gently curved, the base constricted for 1.5-2 mm, the apex constricted for 2.5-4 mm, not curved or only slightly so, densely velutinous when immature, glabrous when mature, the style not persistent. Seed 1.9-2.5 × 0.9-1.1 cm. Diagnostic characters. The leaves of Roupala pseudocordata commonly have persistent indumentum beneath, which is lost very slowly as the leaf ages, so it still remains at the base of the lamina and venation. The inflorescence is densely short-tomentose. Flowers pedicellate; ovary indumentum extending upward (erect), less commonly bushing outward. This species may be confused with Roupala cordifolia and R. barnettiae. Field characters. Spreading tree or shrub with dense to sparse crown; stoloniferous in disturbed, open vegetation. Bark fissured in mature trees, smooth and slightly fissured in trees of narrower girth, dark brown or gray. Wood moderately hard; slash, bark, and crushed leaves emitting strong smell described as similar to tuna or skunk; young branches, petioles, underside of leaves (and upper side of young leaves), and inflorescences with rufous-ferruginous to red-brown to dark brown indumentum. Petiole robust. Leaves spiral, coriaceous, thick, and rigid, breaking easily, often markedly revolute (older leaves crowded near branch terminals and rosulate in var. pseudocordata), shiny or dull, ochraceous or pale green-gray to dark green above when mature, conspicuously discolorous due to indumentum beneath, gray-green when hairs lost; margin entire, undulate, or serrate. Inflorescences erect, green beneath indumentum; flowers lightly fragrant, unpleasant when discoloring; buds and tepals with ferruginous to brown indumentum without, white to yellow to flesh colored and glabrous within, the glands fleshy; ovary pink with brown or white indumentum; style and stigma pale green or yellow-green; anthers white. Young fruit with ferruginous or rufous velvety indumentum.

description: Young branches usually slender, minutely appressed puberulous when young soon glabrous, pale greyish-brown, usually with a few lenticels. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate or paripinnate, with or without some limited apical growth, 8-55 cm long; petiole semiterete, rhachis often canaliculate above, sometimes narrowly winged, puberulous or glabrous; petiolule of lateral leaflets 1-7 mm long, petiolule of terminal leaflet 10-12 mm long. Leaflets opposite or alternate, (5-)8-15(-17), elliptic, oblong or oblanceolate, apex usually short, narrowly attenuate, less frequently acute to obtuse rarely rounded, base acute, cuneate or attenuate, margin rarely revolute, usually chartaceous, 8-20(-32)[14.6] cm long, 3-9(-16)[5.9] cm broad, upper midrib sometimes puberulous, lower surface glabrous or with sparse to dense soft short pubescence on midrib and veins and scattered hairs on lamina, sometimes mixed with a few red papillae; venation eucamptodromous or rarely brochidodromous; secondaries (8-) 10-14(-18) on either side of midrib, broadly spreading, arcuate at tip, parallel or slightly convergent; intersecondaries often rather long; tertiaries usually obscure. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious; inflorescence axillary, 5-30(-60) cm long, usually a slender panicle with short basal branches less frequently with widely spreading branches to 10 cm long, flowers in small clusters or racemose, minutely puberulous or subglabrous; pedicel 0-1 mm long. Calyx patelliform, sepals 0.75-2 mm long, ovate to orbicular, sparsely puberulous or glabrous, ciliate. Petals 5-7(-8) mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm broad, elliptic, oblong or spathulate, apex rounded, glabrous. Staminal tube cyathiform or short cylindrical, 2-6 mm long, 1.5-3 mm broad, margin crenulate or with 10 emarginate lobes, glabrous or sparsely barbate inside; anthers (8-)10(-ll), 0.75-1(-1.1) mm long, sometimes with a short basal appendage, glabrous; antherodes narrower, without pollen, not dehiscing. Nectary a short stout stipe, sometimes swollen below the ovary, 0.25-1(-2) mm long, glabrous. Ovary (2-)3(-4)-locular, loculi with (1-)2 superposed ovules, glabrous or sparsely pubescent near the base; style stout, glabrous; style-head discoid; pistillode similar with well-developed non-functional ovules. Capsule globose or short pyriform, smooth, dark brown (when dry) with large pale lenticels, glabrous, 2-3 cm diam., 3-valved, valves 1-seeded; pericarp 0.5-2 mm thick. Seed ca. 1.5 cm long, 0.7 cm broad, ± ellipsoid, with a thick, fleshy, basal sarcotesta; seed coat thin, membraneous. Embryo with plano-convex, collateral cotyledons; radicle apical, extending to surface.

description: Young branches stout, densely pubescent to tomentose, indumentum persistent. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate, without apical growth, 12.5-24 cm long; petiole semiterete, rhachis terete, tomentose; petiolule of lateral leaflets 2-5 mm long, petiolule of terminal leaflet to 23 mm long. Leaflets opposite, 7-11(-13), elliptic, oblong, oblanceolate or obovate, apex rounded, obtuse or truncate, base slightly oblique, cuneate, acute or obtuse, margin usually strongly revolute, terminal leaflet with a regular (not oblique), attenuate or cuneate base, coriaceous, 10.5-17(-21)[ 15.5] cm long, 5-8.5(10.5)[7.9] cm broad, upper surface with densely pubescent midrib and secondary veins, lamina sometimes with minute crateriform excrescences, lower surface with densely short pubescent to tomentose midrib and secondary veins, lower lamina usually pubescent, hairs intermixed with minute red papillae or less frequently glabrous; venation eucamptodromous to brochidodromous; secondaries 10-15 on either side of midrib, shallowly ascending, prominently raised on lower surface, arcuate, parallel; intersecondaries short to moderate; tertiaries widely spaced, reticulate. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious; inflorescence axillary 25-30 cm long, a slender or broad panicle with lateral, widely-spreading branches to 12 cm long, densely pubescent to tomentose; pedicel 1-2 mm long. Calyx patelliform in open flower, sepals 1-1.5 mm long, ovate-acute to orbicular, ciliate, pubescent to subglabrous outside. Petals 9-9.5 mm long, 2.5-3 mm broad, oblong, apex rounded, glabrous. Staminal tube short cylindrical, 5-7 mm long, 3-3.5 mm broad, margin crenulate, glabrous; anthers 10, 1.5-1.7 mm long, with a short basal appendage, glabrous; antherodes narrower, without pollen, not dehiscing. Nectary a short broad stipe, 0.5-1.5 mm long, glabrous. Ovary 3(-4)-locular, loculi with 2 superposed ovules, glabrous; style stout, glabrous, gradually tapering to discoid style-head; pistillode similar with well-developed abortive ovules. Capsule ± globose, sometimes with a short stipe, smooth, dark brown with large prominent pale lenticels, glabrous, 2-3 cm diam., 3-valved, valves usually 1-seeded; pericarp 2-3 mm thick. Seed 1-1.5 cm long, when solitary in valve then with a thick basal sarcotesta, when 2 superposed in valve then partially surrounded by a fleshy arillode; seed coat membraneous; hilum large. Embryo with plano-convex, collateral cotyledons; radicle apical, extending to the surface.

description: Shrub, 0.5-3 m tall. Branch bark dark red-gray, peeling, glabrous. Lenticels few, inconspicuous, minute, to 0.5 mm longest axis, granular, plane, red-brown becoming gray, growth units clearly marked by dramatic changes in leaf size, large at the start of the season gradually diminishing to minute proportions towards the end of the season, coupled with long-term persistence of old leaves. Leaves simple, extremely rigid, crowded together, erect and imbricate, obscuring branches, drying pale green to brown, matte, rarely shiny above, glabrous, with waxy cuticle above and beneath. Petiole 0.1-0.2 (-0.3) cm long, ca. 1 mm wide at midlength, 1/6 to 1/12 the length of the lamina, rugose, glabrous. Lamina 0.5-3.4x(0.3-)0.5-2.6cm, length:breadth (<1-)1-1.5(-2): 1, orbiculate to suborbiculate, less frequently wide-elliptic or oblate, the surface rugose beneath; base obtuse to rounded, usually decurrent, symmetrical; apex rounded to subtruncate, more rarely slightly emarginate, the apical point of midrib protrudent; margin entire, the rim thickened, slightly revolute at sides; venation obscure above, slightly raised above, the midvein conspicuous, slightly raised beneath, the secondary venation very faint, the tertiary venation invisible beneath, eucamptodromous, semicraspedodromous where veins are more conspicuous, the midvein reaching the apex; lateral veins 3-5 pairs. Inflorescence 4.5-8.5 × 1.2 cm, axillary, unbranched, deeply ridged, glabrous; peduncle 2 cm × 0.8 mm, sterile bracts few towards base. Common bracts 0.6-0.8 × 0.5-1 mm, thickened and rugose towards base, glabrous except for long-fimbriate margin of wavy, ferruginous hairs. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels 1.6-2 × 0.5 mm, rugose, glabrous. Buds ca. 1 mm broad at the apex, ca. 0.6 mm broad at midlength, glabrous. Flowers 3.5-5 mm long; filaments 1 mm long, adnate 1.7-2 mm from base of tepals; anthers 1.1 × 0.4 mm; nectary lobes 0.3 mm long, touching each other at the base, separating upwards; ovary glabrous; ovules 0.5 × 0.2 mm. Infructescence 4-12 cm long, glabrous; fruit pedicels 2-4 × 0.5-1 mm, glabrous. Fruit 1.7-2.6 × 0.6-1 mm, oval to oval-oblong, the curvature of sutured and unsutured sides similar, constricted for 2-5 mm at the base, ending in a small point at the apex, the style sometimes persistent, glabrous, smooth, pale brown or gray. Seeds 1.2 × 0.7 cm.

description: Leaves drying glaucous, to mid brown, soon glabrous beneath; indumentum, if present, of short hairs only, appressed-pilose, pale to mid brown. Inflorescence 5-20(-26) cm long, the indumentum dense to sparse, pale to mid brown, becoming sparser or glabrous towards perianth apices, the hairs straight. Flowers densely clustered at anthesis, drying yellow-brown, orange-brown or mid brown. Common bracts 0.4-1.2(-1.5) × (0.5-)l-2.5 mm, the indumentum of short sericeous hairs not bushing outward, but extending all over. Field characters. Tree 1.5-25(-30) m, shrub 15 m, 5-60(-80) cm dbh, twisted/gnarled trees or dwarf shrubs to forest trees, with strong odor (mephitic/tuna/canned meat) to crushed leaves, broken twigs, and slash; trunk well-branched and spreading with dense crown. Bark rough, flaking, at times corky, dark gray or black, to smooth or slightly fissured, lenticellate, and gray or pale brown. Wood open-grained, hard; white, straw yellow, pale pink, or dark red. Petiole, leaf rachises, and petiolules canaliculate; petiole and base of midrib yellow-green. Leaves compound, lobed, or simple, at times all of these on the same branch; subcoriaceous to coriaceous (rarely chartaceous), sometimes rigid, glabrous to pubescent, highly variable in shape, dull green to dark green above, shiny or matte, paler dull green beneath, at times waxy, serrate, half folded. Petiole, leaf rachises, and petiolules canaliculate; petiole and base of midrib yellow-green. Inflorescence green, whitish green, yellow, pale brown, cinnamon colored or dark brown. Buds whitish-green, green, or scurfy-brown. Flowers white, cream, pale yellow, yellow, ochraceous, greenish-yellow, pale buff, scent likened to honeysuckle; ovary green or pinkish; nectary white; style and stigma pale green, anthers cream. Fruit green to gray-green, maturing pale brown to brown or gray, pubescent when young; few developing per inflorescence.

description: Tree, 12-15 m tall. Twigs thin, spindly; bark beige or gray superficially, dark red-gray beneath, the indumentum cinnamomous-tomentose, fading to gray, quickly glabrescent; lenticels usually < 0.5 mm diam., granular, becoming raised, orange. Leaves simple, chartaceous, drying concolorous, pale green to pink-green, matte above, the indumentum cinnamomous-tomentose beneath and along midrib above on young leaves, glabrescent except towards base of midrib on both sides. Petiole 1.5-4 cm long, canaliculate at lamina end, becoming terete towards the base, gray-tomentose. Lamina 5.5-9 × 2-4.3 cm, length:breadth 2-3:1, narrowly ovate; base narrow-cuneate or acute, decurrent onto petiole, pressing flat, symmetrical; apex attenuate; margin revolute towards the base, coarsely serrate, the serrations incurved; midrib and lowermost lateral veins slightly impressed, inconspicuous above, raised and conspicuous beneath, eucamptodromous as seen above, semicraspedodromous beneath; lateral veins 3-5 pairs. Peduncle 2 × 1 mm; sterile bracts few at the base. Inflorescence 5.2-6.5 × l.3 cm, dense, cinnamomous-tomentose on all parts. Common bracts l × l mm. Pedicels 1.8-2 × 0.6 mm, free to base. Buds 1.5 mm broad at the apex, 1 mm broad at midlength. Flowers 4-4.5 mm long; filaments 0.2-0.3 mm long, adnate 2.5 mm from base of tepals; anthers 1-1.2 × 04 mm; nectary lobes minute, ca. 0.1 mm long, well separated; ovary hairs extending 1-1.2 mm from base of ovary, dense, short, directed outward; ovules 0.6 × 0.2-0.3mm. Infructescence 5-8.5 cm long. Fruit pedicels 1-2 × 1.5-1.8 mm. Fruit 2.6-3 × l.8-1.9 cm, constricted for 1-2 mm at base, not constricted apically, rounded, the sutured and nonsutured sides strongly curved, discoid, the persistent tomentum appressed, cinnamomous, eventually glabrescent. Seeds 2.2 × 1.4 cm.

description: Tree, 30-35 m tall. Bark on branches not visible due to persistent indumentum, chestnut-brown to ferruginous-velutinous, fading gradually to gray, remaining dense on previous seasonal growth unit. Lenticels absent or not visible. Young leaves simple (no mature leaves seen), chartaceous, long-petiolate, chestnut-brown to sparsely ferruginous velutinous above, densely velutinous below. Petiole well defined, 5.5-6.5(-7) cm long × 2.5-2.6 mm broad at midlength, 1/1.7-1/2.2 the length of the lamina, ± terete, chestnut-brown to ferruginousvelutinous. Lamina (9-)11-13(-15) × (7.5-)9-10(-13.5) cm, length:breadth 1-1.5:1, orbiculate or suborbiculate; base slightly cordate to truncate and decurrent; apex strongly retuse to rounded, the apical point of midrib not protruding; margin entire, somewhat irregular, not revolute; venation ± conspicuous above, the veins marked by persistent indumentum, conspicuous below due to prominence of veins, the midvein reaching the apex; lateral veins 8-9 pairs, semicraspedodromous except lowermost vein, which fades towards leaf margin. Inflorescences axillary, unbranched, 24-28(-33)× 4 cm, all parts dense, chestnut-brown to ferruginous velutinous; peduncle 1-2 cm × 2.5-3 mm, with a very few sterile bracts towards base. Common bracts ca. 1 × 1 mm. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels 3-5(-7) × 1-1.5 mm. Buds ca. 2.5 mm broad at the apex, ca. 1.5 mm broad at midlength. Flowers 13-14(-17) mm long; filaments adnate 9-10 mm from base of tepals; anthers sessile, 2.5(-3) × l(-1.5) mm; nectary lobes 0.5 × 0.5 mm, well separated, inconspicuous when gynoecium attached to pedicel; the ovary hairs extending 2.5-3 mm from base of ovary, covering entire ovary, the hairs long, straight, dense, erect or spreading, light ferruginous; ovules 0.7 × 0.2 mm. Fruit unknown.

description: Shrub, or small tree, 4-5 m tall. Branch bark orange-brown to green-brown peeling to gray beneath, with vertical fissures developing, glabrous. Lenticels absent or few, inconspicuous, <0.5 mm, granular, plane to weakly raised; orange-brown, red-brown, or faded to gray. Leaves compound or (more rarely) simple to lobed in adults, thick-coriaceous, petiolate, drying concolorous, pale green, olive, or pale green-brown, or bicolorous, pale green above with pale brown beneath, matte, glabrous. Compound leaves with 1-6 pairs of leaflets, 8.5-38 cm long (incl. petiole), 8-16 cm broad; petiole 2-10 cm long. Lateral leaflets 3-11 × 0.9-3.8 cm, length:breadth ratio 1.9-3.3:1, the base acute to cuneate on narrower side of lamina, acute to obtuse on broader side, the apex attenuate (to retuse), the margins entire; lateral vein (1-)3-5 pairs; petiolules 0-1.5 cm long. Terminal leaflets 4-10.5 × 0.7-5.2 cm, length:breadth ratio of 2-5.7:1, the base long cuneate to acute, symmetrical to strongly asymmetrical, the apex attenuate or acute almost to apex and suddenly rounded, or retuse; lateral veins 1-5 pairs, the margins as for lateral leaflets; petiolules 0-2.5 cm long. Simple leaf petiole not well defined, 2-3 cm long, 1-1.5 mm broad at midlength, 1/4-1/4.1 the length of the lamina, subterete at base, flattening out adaxially upward as lamina sides descend, flat or canaliculate, glabrous. Lamina 8.5-11 × 3.2-4.2 cm, length:breadth 2.5-2.8:l, elliptic; base acute; apex attenuate, the apical point of midrib often protruding; margin entire, revolute; venation ± plane, inconspicuous above, very slightly raised, inconspicuous beneath, the secondaries sometimes almost completely obscure; tertiary venation completely obscure, semicraspedodromous, the midvein reaching the apex; lateral veins 3-5 pairs. Inflorescences 8.5-14 × 2.5-3.2 cm, axillary, unbranched, glabrous or sparsely pilose; peduncle l-2cm × l-1.3 mm broad, the sterile bracts few to many towards the base. Common bracts 0.5-0.8 × 0.4-0.6 mm, usually dropping when buds are in an immature state, orange-brown appressed-pilose or glabrous with fimbriate margin to the outside, glabrous within, the lower half of the bract thickened, rugose, the upper half thin, fragile, smooth, narrowly triangular. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels 3.2-4.5 × 0.4-0.6 mm, the indumentum ferruginous, short, appressed-pilose. Buds 1.3-1.6 mm broad at the apex, 0.6-0.7 mm broad at midlength, the indumentum as for pedicels, sparser towards the apices. Rowers 8-13.5 cm long; filaments 0-0.5 mm long, adnate 7.2-11.5 mm from the base of tepals; anthers 1.5-2 × 0.50.8 mm; nectary lobes 0.3-0.5 mm long, separate; ovary hairs extending 1.5-2.5 mm from the base, covering entire surface, short, straight, appressed, orange-brown; ovules 0.5-0.7 × 0.2-0.3 mm. Infructescence 12.5 cm long, glabrous. Fruit pedicels 4 × 1 mm, glabrous. Fruit 3.2 × 1.2 cm, the base constricted for 5-6 mm, the apex sharp with persistent style, constricted for 5-6 mm, glabrescent, smooth, pale brown. Seeds 3-3.2 × 1.5 cm.

description: Tree, to 30 m tall. Branch bark pale brown, peeling to pale brown, dark red-gray or dark red-brown beneath, the indumentum sparsely pilose to densely tomentose, golden yellow to ferruginous, glabrescent. Lenticels numerous, inconspicuous, plane becoming raised peripherally, at times tuberculate, 0.5-1 mm diam, granular, red- to orange-brown. Leaves simple and compound, thin-coriaceous, drying pale green to pinkish-brown to dark purple-brown, matte, indumentum aureus to ferruginous, short appressed-pilose to long-tomentose at base of lamina, along the petiole, and on the petiolule and rachis of juvenile leaves above and below when young; rapidly glabrescent, or glabrous throughout development. Simple leaves: petiole (l-)2-4(-6.5) cm × l-2mm, (1/1.1-)1/1.6-1/4.6 times the length of the lamina, subterete at base, flattening out towards lamina, canaliculate, the groove formed by lamina sides descending, the indumentum dense, sparsely appressed-pilose to tomentose, golden yellow to ferruginous, fading to gray, quickly glabrescent, persisting longest at petiole base; lamina (2.5-)6-10(-14.5) × (1.5-)3-6(-8) cm, length:breadth 2-2.5(-4):1, elliptic, less frequently widely or narrowly elliptic, narrowly ovate or ovate; base acute to obtuse and decurrent, the lamina tapering gradually down petiole, symmetrical, flat; apex short- to long-attenuate tapering to a point or rounded at the terminus, at times retuse, often folded, the apical point of the midrib not protruding; margin entire, less commonly undulate, crenate or serrate with 3-7 serrations, revolute; venation inconspicuous above, the midrib and lateral veins slightly prominent lower down the lamina, becoming obscure and plane towards the margin, conspicuous and prominent below, semicraspedodromous, the midrib at times slightly grooved, reaching the apex; lateral veins 3-4(-6) pairs, steeply ascending at base (diverging from midrib at very narrow angle of 20-30° at base, 20-40(-50)° towards apex), 0.5-1.5 cm apart at base, 2-4 cm apart at apex; indumentum as for petiole, gradually weaker on ascending the lamina, glabrescent. Compound juvenile leaves: 10-15-jugate, the leaflets opposite at base, remaining so or becoming subopposite to alternate apically, 38-39 × 16-18 cm, the axis 29-38 cm long; petiole 10-11 cm long, terete, densely ferruginous long-tomentose; rachis 2-ridged adaxially (ridges originating from descending lamina margins of leaflets), the indumentum as for petiole; lateral petiolule sessile on apical-facing margin of lamina, 2-3 mm long on basal-facing margin; lateral leaflets 5-10 × 2.5-3.5 cm, small at the base, larger at mid axis, smaller towards apex, shape asymmetrical, length:breadth 2:1, the base strongly asymmetrical, cuneate on both sides, diverging from the midrib at an angle of <45° on shortest side of lamina, >45° on longest side; apex acute to attenuate; margin serrate, with 3-4 and 9-13 serrations on basal-facing and apical-facing margins, respectively; lateral veins 4-5 and 6-9 pairs on basal-facing and apical-facing margins of the lamina, respectively, densely to sparsely ferruginous-pilose at base, glabrous apically; terminal petiolule 1.5-2 cm long, terete, the terminal leaflets 8.5-9.5 × 4.3-5.6 cm, rhombic, the base cuneate, sides of lamina descending to base of petiolule, symmetrical or asymmetrical, the apex acute to attenuate, the margin serrate, with 5-6 serrations to either side, ca. 6 lateral vein pairs, the indumentum as for lateral leaflets. Compound leaves of mature individuals: bilobed or 2-9-jugate, the leaflets opposite at base, remaining so or becoming subopposite to alternate apically 10-20(-30) × 6-14cm, axis 5-12(-18) cm long; petiole (2-)3-6(-10) cm long, terete proximally becoming sulcate distally, densely short-tomentose adaxially to glabrous, glabrous abaxially; rachis sulcate, sparsely pilose to glabrous; lateral petiolule 2-5 mm long on apical-facing margin, to 10 mm long on basal-facing margin, plane or slightly sulcate; lateral leaflets 3-8 × 1.5-4 cm, larger towards apex, symmetrical or asymmetrical, length:breadth 1.5-2:1, ovate or elliptic, the base acute on shortest side of lamina, acute through obtuse to truncate on longest side, the margin entire, undulate, crenate, or serrate, the venation as for simple leaves, glabrous; terminal petiolule 0-2.5(-4) cm long, sulcate towards base; terminal leaflets 6-10(-14) × 3-7 cm, length:breadth 1:1.5-2, ovate or elliptic, symmetrical if distant from ultimate leaflet, asymmetrical if close to it, the base mostly obtuse-decurrent, sometimes with one side broad-cuneate; apex long-attenuate to rounded and short-attenuate at the very terminus, often somewhat folded; margin entire to serrate, venation as for simple leaves, glabrous. Inflorescences lateral or axillary, unbranched, with a new flush of leaves terminal to inflorescence-producing region, (3-)9-19(-30) × 2.5-4 cm, the flower-pairs well spread, sparsely ferruginous-pilose at growing tip, sometimes extending down rachis, densely long-pilose around insertion of flower-pairs, rufous-strigose at base; peduncle 0.5-4.5 cm × 0.6-2.5 mm, with a few sterile bracts towards base, nonpersistent; scars conspicuous. Common bracts 0.6-1(-1.3) mm long × 0.61 mm broad, the margin (or rarely only apex) fimbriate. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels (2-)3-7 × 0.5-l mm, glabrous. Buds 1.2-2 mm broad at the apex, 0.8-1 mm at midlength, glabrous. Flowers 8.5-17 mm long; filaments 0-0.3(-0.8) mm long, attached 6.5-13 mm from base of tepals; anthers 2-4.5 × 0.5-0.8 mm; nectary lobes 0.2-0.5 mm long, free, separated or touching at the base; ovary 1-2 × 0.5-1 mm, not much broader than style, longitudinally compressed, glabrous or with small patches of appressed, rufous puberulent indumentum at the base, drying black, deep grooves from the top of the ovary towards the style; ovules 0.5-0.8 mm long. Infructescence 4.7-20 cm long, glabrous; fruit pedicel 3-5(-8) × 1.5-3 mm, glabrous. Fruit (3-)3.5-5.5 × 2-2.2 cm, frequently pendulous, the sutured side curved more strongly than the unsutured side, the base constricted for 3-12 mm, the apex constricted 2-4 mm, strongly curved curving back towards the pedicel to weakly curved and beaked, the style persisting at times, the sides of the follicle rolling outward and lying in the same plane when dehisced, glabrous, rugulose, drying black when immature, light to mid brown or purple-gray when mature, a strong marginal vein running around periphery of mature fruits. Seed 2.8-3 × 1.3-1.4 cm.

description: Tree, or shrub, 1.5-6 m tall. Bark dark brown to ferruginous-brown, densely velutinous, the indumentum persistent for 2-3 repeating growth units, lost with age. Older stems dark gray to brown. Lenticels (visible only on previous seasonal growth units where indumentum has been lost) numerous to apparently absent, inconspicuous, minute, gray. Leaves compound, lobed, and simple, rigid-coriaceous, often shiny above, drying pale green to yellowish-brown, appressed, ferruginous-sericeous above when young, glabrescent, ferruginous-velutinous beneath when young, fading to yellow or gray and gradually lost except on lower lamina, midrib, and along lower lateral veins. Compound leaves 2-4 jugate, the leaflets usually paired, sometimes staggered, 20.5-31.5 (inclusive of petiole) × 13.5-23.5 cm; petiole 612 cm long. Lateral leaflets 4.5-12.5 × 2.5-8 cm, length:breadth 1.8-3.0:1, lamina base acute, obtuse, or rounded and strongly asymmetrical, the half of the lamina on side facing leaf apex broader than half facing petiole, apex acute, lateral veins 5-6 pairs, margins entire, undulate, or serrate; petiolules 0-0.8 cm long on side facing leaf apex, sessile to 1.5 cm long on side facing petiole. Terminal leaflets 12-14 × 8-14 cm, at times lobed, length:breadth 0.81.6:1, apex and base acute to rounded, the base at times asymmetrical, lateral veins 6-8 pairs, the margins entire, undulate or serrate; petiolules 2-5 cm long. Simple leaf petiole well defined, 1.5-7.5 cm long × 1.5-4.25 mm broad at midlength, 1/1.7-1/9 the length of the lamina, subterete to terete at base, becoming flat towards lamina, the indumentum ferruginous-velutinous, fading to gray, gradually lost from distal end, persistent for longer at proximal end. Lamina of mature leaves 4.5-12 × 3-10.5 cm, orbiculate to wide-elliptic or very wide-ovate to wide-ovate, length:breadth 1-1.5:1; base obtuse, rounded, cordate, or truncate; apex rarely acute, mostly obtuse or rounded, sometimes weakly retuse, the tip of the midrib sometimes protruding minutely beyond the lamina; margin sometimes revolute towards base, entire or undulate, rarely crenate (Peruvian specimen), (leaves transitional between compound and simple may be larger, with length:breadth < 1:1, and margins strongly serrate with teeth 29-37 pairs); venation conspicuous and raised above and beneath, the midvein reaching apex; lateral veins 5-9 pairs, the lowermost vein(s) merging into leaf margin, venation above semi-craspedodromous. Inflorescences lateral, 9.5-20 × 2-2.5 cm, densely ferruginous-velutinous, the indumentum long to very short; peduncle 0.5-1.5 cm × 2-3 mm, with sterile bracts numerous or few at base. Common bracts 1-3 mm long, 2-3 mm broad, densely ferruginous-velutinous to the outside, glabrous within. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels 0.25-1.5(-2.) × 0.8-1.4(-l.7) mm, the indumentum as for inflorescence. Buds 1-3.5 mm broad at the apex, 0.75-2 mm broad at midlength, the indumentum as for inflorescence, rarely sparsely appressed puberulent (Peruvian specimen). Flowers (6-) 8.5-10.5 mm long; filaments 0.2-1.2 mm long, adnate to tepals throughout; anthers sessile, 2-3 × 0.6-1 mm; nectary lobes 0.4-0.7 mm long, well separated; ovary hairs extending 2-3 mm from base of ovary, yellow- to orange-brown, straight to wavy, bushing outward giving the ovary a pom-pom appearance; ovules 0.5-0.8 × 0.2-04 mm. Infructescence 11-19 cm long, the indumentum ferruginous-velutinous, becoming patchy and black with age; fruit pedicels 1-2 mm long, 3-3.5 mm broad. Fruit 2.2-2.8 × l.3-1.6 cm, obovate, the base constricted 1-2 mm, apex constricted for 1-2 mm, curved, densely ferruginous-velutinous, glabrescent, frequently persisting as black patches especially towards the base, old fruit gray or pale brown, smooth; style rarely persistent. Seeds 1.5 × 0.7 cm.

description: Tree, (2-)3-10(-20) m tall, 10-50 cm diam., or rarely a scandent shrub. Branch bark light brown or gray superficially, dark red-gray or gray beneath, glabrous except rufous axillary buds of short, appressed hairs. Lenticels numerous, minute, <0.5 mm diam., raised peripherally, granular, red-brown. Leaves simple, or rarely with bisected midrib or extralaminal tissue as evidence of lobing, thinly coriaceous, drying pale green, green-brown, or brown and usually shiny above, glabrous even when new. Petiole not well defined, (0.5-)1-2.5(-3) cm long, 1-2.5 mm broad at midlength, 1/4-1/8.4 the length of the lamina, smooth to slightly rugose, flat adaxially due to lamina sides descending (curving from the petiole sides to the adaxial petiole surface), terete lower down, a scar often developing between branch and petiole (not stipular), glabrous. Lamina (4.5-)7-15(-21) × 2-6(-7) cm, length to breadth ratio (1.5-)2-4(-5):l, predominantly narrowly oblong, lanceolate or elliptic, also oblong, oblanceolate, narrowly obovate, or widely elliptic; base cuneate, more rarely acute- or obtuse-decurrent, symmetrical; apex obtuse to rounded, attenuate or acute, the apical point of midrib not protruding; margin always entire, revolute towards the base of the leaf; venation raised on both surfaces of lamina, ± conspicuous above, conspicuous below, the tertiary venation faint to obscure beneath, appearing eucamptodromous above, semicraspedodromous below where detail is seen more clearly, sometimes forming a double marginal vein, with a strong inner vein and weaker outer vein, the midvein reaching the apex; lateral veins (4-)6-8(-10) pairs. Inflorescence 5-12(-17)× (1.5-)2-3(-3.5) cm, axillary, rarely lateral, unbranched, glabrous, often shiny, the flowers clustered together or well spaced; peduncle 1-2(-3) cm × 1-1.5 mm, a few sterile bracts persistent. Common bracts 0.3-0.5(-0.7) × 0.3-0.6 mm, glabrous except for fimbriate margin and apex of orange- to red-brown hairs. Flower-pair axis absent, rarely 0.5-1.5 mm long. Pedicels l-2.5(-4.5) × 0.5-0.8(-l) mm, glabrous. Buds 1-1.5 mm broad at the apex, 0.5-1 mm broad at midlength, glabrous or occasionally with short, weak hairs. Flowers 6-12(-14) mm long; filaments 00.5 mm long, adnate 4-9 mm from base of tepals; anthers 2-4.5 × 0.3-0.5 mm; nectary lobes 0.3-0.5mm long, closely appressed giving the appearance of a ring; ovary somewhat compressed longitudinally, the ovary hairs extending (0.7-)l-1.5(-2.5) mm from base of ovary, extending slightly lower on one side, very short, yellowish to light ferruginous, closely appressed, the ovary sometimes glabrous; ovules 0.5-l × 0.2-0.3 mm. Infructescence (5-)9-15 cm long, glabrous; fruit pedicels 2.5-6 × 1-1.5 mm, glabrous. Fruit 2.8-3.8 × 1.2-1.6 cm, both sides curved more or less equally, less commonly with sutured side curved more strongly than unsutured side, the base markedly constricted for (3-)5-7mm length, apex straight to curved to an angle perpendicular to unsutured side, constricted only 1-1.5 mm, the style persistent forming sharp apex, the surface conspicuously ridged due to underlying vascular tissue, the marginal vein generally protruding throughout periphery, beige to black, glabrous even when immature. Seeds 2.1-2.4 × 1.2 cm.

description: Arbusto, ramas jóvenes tomentosas, diminutamente lenticeladas. Hojas im-paripinadas, foliólos 9-11; raquis 9.5-13.5 cm de largo, delgado, tomentoso o glabrescente. Foliolos 4.5-8.5 cm de largo, 1.8-3.5 cm de ancho, oblongo-elípticos, cartáceos, haz oscura, glabra, envés velloso, base redondeada, ápice gradualmente largo-acuminado; venación finamente reticulada; nervaduras laterales 4-5 pares. Flores desconocidas. Inflorescencia axilar; raquila hasta 7 cm de largo, delgada, glabra (o glabrescente). Fruto 1.2 cm de largo, glabro; cáliz en fruto 0.7 cm de largo, sépalos lanceolado-lineales, glabros. Semilla 1 cm de largo.

description: Liana, ramas jóvenes cilindricas, vellosas. Hojas trifolioladas; pecíolo 1-6 cm de largo, densamente tomentoso o velloso; raquis 0.1-4 cm de largo, velloso. Foliolos 4.5-23 cm de largo, 2-10 cm de ancho, ovados u ovado-oblongos, sub-cartáceos, haz oscura, vellosa, envés densamente piloso, nervadura central densamente vellosa en ambas caras, base redondeada, ápice cuspidado, margen revoluto; peciólulo 0.5 cm de largo; venación reticulada, impresa en la haz, prominente en el envés; nervaduras laterales 6-7 pares, ascendentes, formando ángulos de 40-60° con la nervadura central, difusamente anastomosadas cerca al margen. Inflorescencia paniculada, terminal, raquila 2.5-6 cm de largo, densamente vellosa, con pelos glandulosos; brácteas 0.1-0.25 cm de largo, lineares, densamente vellosas, con pelos glandulosos. Flores sésiles o pedicelo 0.1 cm de largo, articulado; sépalos 4 mm de largo, 3 mm de ancho, ovados, densamente vellosos, con pelos glandulosos; pétalos 7 mm de largo, 5 mm de ancho, obovados, glabros, libres; filamentos unidos por 0.3-0.5 mm de su longitud, 5 más largos 3.5 mm de longitud, 5 más cortos 2-2.5 mm de longitud; anteras globosas, 0.5 mm de diámetro; ovario piloso. Fruto desconocido.

description: Tree, to 40 m tall and to 80 cm in diam. Leafy twigs and petioles densely (to sparsely) covered with whitish to brownish, (mostly) appressed, simple hairs generally less than 0.5 mm long. Petioles 7-16 mm long, l-2(-4) mm in diam. Lamina (narrowly) elliptic-ovate, -obovate or -oblong, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, light (olive-)green to light brown (dark, shiny green in vivo) above, greenish-brown to brown (greyish-green in vivo) and often papillate below, (7-)9-17(-35) cm long, 3-7(-14) cm wide, sparsely (to rather densely) covered with whitish to brownish, crisped, appressed to erect, simple hairs above, densely to sparsely covered with whitish, shiny, (mainly) appressed, simple hairs mostly less than 0.5 mm long below, lower epidermal surface mostly greyish farinose in appearance, base variable from cuneate (acute) to rounded (or truncate), apex acuminate, acute, to obtuse, the tip itself acute to obtuse; secondary veins slightly curved to straight, 10-20 on either side of primary vein, occasionally with some intersecondaries, angles with primary vein 40-70°, smallest distance between loops and margin 0.51.5	mm, tertiary veins (1-3 per intercosta, weakly percurrent to) reticulate. Domatia occasionally present. Inflorescences supra-axillary to leaf-opposed, often at the base of new growth, rarely terminal on short axillary shoot, 1-5-flowered, peduncles, pedicels, outer side of bracts, outer side of sepals and corolla densely (peduncles and pedicels to rather densely) covered with (whitish to) brownish, appressed (to erect) hairs mostly less than 0.5 mm long. Peduncles 1-3 mm long, 1-1.5 mm in diam., fruiting peduncles to 5 mm long, to 5 mm in diam. Pedicels (12-) 15-35(-40) mm long, 0.7-1.5 mm in diam., fruiting pedicels to 70 mm long, 2-5 {-7} mm in diam. Bracts triangular to ovate-triangular, 1-1.5(-2) mm long, upper bract almost basal to inserted in the lower 2/5 (rarely more) of the pedicel. Flowers green suffused with red-brown or yellow-orange in vivo. Sepals free, well-spaced to contiguous, appressed, triangular (to broadly triangular), (l-)2-2.5 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, acute to acuminate, gibbous. Corolla tube 2-3 mm high, 5-7 mm in diam., wings obovate (to narrowly obovate), horizontal, 20-30 mm long, 10-18 mm high, 0.5-1 mm thick, index = 1.5-2. Fruit globose to broadly ovoid, 1.5-3.5{-4} cm long, 1.5-3{-4} cm in diam., green, yellowish-green, or greenish-brown in vivo, orange-brown to grey-brown when dry, composed of ca. 30-50(-100) carpels, densely covered with brownish, crisped hairs, areoles hexagonal, mostly not protruding or with tiny apicule, (4-)5-10 × (2-)3-6 mm, apicule acute to obtuse, to 1 mm high, surface smooth to verruculose; wall (1.5-)2-3 mm thick. Seeds 6-9 × 4-5 mm. Chromosome number: 2n = 14.

description: Tree (also with small buttresses), to 25 m tall and 35-60 cm in diam. Leafy twigs and petioles rather densely covered with mostly appressed, whitish to brownish, simple hairs to 0.5 mm long. Petioles 8-16(-21) mm long, 1-2 mm in diam. Lamina elliptic to ovate, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, brown to olive-green above, light (greyish )brown to greyish-green below, 8-20(-27) cm long, 4-8(-10) cm wide, sparsely covered with appressed, whitish, simple hairs to glabrous above, rather densely covered below with erect (to appressed along primary vein below), whitish, simple hairs to 0.5 mm long below, base obtuse to rounded (to truncate), apex acute to acuminate, the tip itself acute to obtuse; secondary veins curved (to straight), 15-22 on either side of primary vein, occasionally with few to many short intersecondaries, angles with primary vein 50-70°, loops indistinct to distinct, smallest distance between loops and margin 0.5-1 mm, tertiary veins 4-6 per intercosta, weakly percurrent to forming composite intersecondaries. Domatia occasionally present, indistinct. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or supra-axillary, often at the base of new growth, 1-4-flowered, peduncles rather densely to sparsely, pedicels, outer side of sepals, and corolla densely covered with whitish (peduncles) to brownish, appressed to erect, straight to (corolla:) crisped hairs. Peduncles 1-4 mm long, 1-1.5 mm in diam. Pedicels 15-30 mm long, 0.7-1.5 mm in diam., fruiting pedicels 3-4 mm in diam. Bracts 1-2 mm long, caducous, upper bract almost basal to inserted in the lower 1/4 of the pedicel. Flowers green to creamish-green in vivo. Sepals free, appressed, triangular, 2-3 mm long, 3 mm wide, acuminate, gibbous. Corolla tube 2-3 mm high, 5-7 mm in diam., wings ovate to oblong, horizontal, 10-22(-25) mm long, 4-10(-13) mm high, 1-1.5 mm thick, index = 2-2.5. Fruit broadly ovoid to globose, 1.5-2.5 cm long and wide, green(ish) or greenish-grey in vivo, brownish when dry, composed of 50-70 carpels, densely covered with brownish, crisped hairs less than 0.5 mm long, areoles (hexagonal-)pulvinate with mostly straight, obtuse to acute apicule in the extreme part of the upper half, 4-5 × 2-4 mm at the base, apicule obtuse to acute, often with an abaxial furrow, ca. 1 mm high, surface smooth to somewhat tuberculate; wall 23 mm thick. Seeds 5-7 × 3-4 mm.

description: Tree, to 20 m tall. Leafy twigs and petioles densely covered with erect and appressed, crisped, pale brown, simple hairs, becoming glabrous. Petioles 8-13 mm long, 1-1.5 mm in diam. Lamina elliptic, chartaceous, 8-19 cm long, 4-7 cm wide, sparsely covered above with crisped, white, simple hairs particularly along primary and secondary veins, densely covered below especially on large veins with erect, crisped, white, very brittle simple hairs to 1 mm long, base broadly cuneate to obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, the extreme tip acute to obtuse; secondary veins straight to slightly curved, 15-22 on either side of primary vein, intersecondaries varying from absent to fairly numerous, slightly impressed to flat above, angles with primary vein 40-70°, occasionally loop-forming down to 1/2 of the length, smallest distance between loops and margin 0.5-1 mm, tertiary veins 11-18 per intercosta, percurrent (to reticulate), tertiary and higher-order venation flat to slightly impressed above. Domatia absent. Inflorescences supra-axillary, leaf-opposed, to sub-axillary, occasionally terminal, 1-4-flowered, peduncles, pedicels, outer side of bracts and sepals, and corolla densely covered with erect and appressed, pale brown, simple hairs, inner side of bracts and sepals densely whitish sericeous. Peduncles 3-4 mm long, 2 mm in diam., fruiting peduncles to 3 mm in diam. Pedicels 10-15 mm long, 1-2 mm in diam., fruiting pedicels to 20(-22) mm long, to 3(-4) mm in diam. Bracts deltate to (broadly) triangular, 1-3(-4) mm long, upper bract inserted in the lower 1/4 to halfway the pedicel. Flowers broken white in vivo. Sepals free, appressed, triangular-elliptic to triangular, 1-2 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, with acuminate apex, gibbous. Corolla tube 3-4 mm high, 5-7 mm in diam., wings obovate, ascending, 9-13 mm long, 4-6 mm high, 1-2 mm thick, index = 2. Fruit only seen in young stage, globose, 1.4-1.6 cm in diam., gray-green in vivo, pale brown when dry, composed of ca. 50 carpels, pale brown sericeous, areoles very shallowly pyramidal to hexagonal-pulvinate with straight apicule in upper half (or about the middle), 3-4 mm at the base, apex or apicule acute, ca. 1 mm high, surface smooth; wall ca. 1 mm thick. Seeds not seen.

description: Tree, up to 30 m tall and up to 50 cm in diam. Leafy twigs with two narrow, low ribs, leafy twigs and petioles densely covered with minute brown hairs variably interspersed with more or less appressed, whitish, simple hairs to 0.5 mm long. Petioles 10-15 mm long, 1.5-2 mm in diam. Lamina elliptic to ovate, chartaceous, brown to dark brown above, light brown and papillate below, 11-19 cm long, 4-7 cm wide, rather densely covered with hairs on large veins, otherwise sparsely covered with more or less erect, often crisped, whitish, simple hairs less than 0.5 mm long, to subglabrous above, rather densely to sparsely covered with appressed, shiny white, simple hairs of same length below, base obtuse to rounded, apex acute to acuminate, the tip itself obtuse; secondary veins straight to slightly curved, 25-35 on either side of primary vein, with short intersecondaries, angles with primary vein 50-70°, smallest distance between loops and margin 0.5-1 mm, tertiary veins 11-16 per intercosta, percurrent and straight to weakly reticulate. Domatia often present, occasionally indistinct. Inflorescences supra-axillary, often at the base of new growth, to infra-axillary, 1-5-flowered, peduncles, pedicels, outer side of bracts, outer side of sepals, and corolla densely covered with brown, appressed hairs less than 0.5 mm long. Peduncles to 3 mm long, to 2 mm in diam. Pedicels 20-30 mm long, 1-2 mm in diam., under the flower conically widened to ca. 4 mm. Bracts triangular, 1-2 mm long, upper bract inserted up to about halfway the pedicel length. Flowers greenish in vivo. Sepals free, appressed, broadly triangular, 1-1.5 mm long, ca. 3 mm wide, acuminate, gibbous. Corolla tube 2-3 mm high, 5-7 mm in diam., wings oblong, horizontal, 12-18 mm long, 5-6 mm high, 1 mm thick, index = 2.5-3. Fruit not seen.

description: Plant flowering 12-15 dm high. Leaves 3-4 dm long; sheaths suborbicular, 4 cm long, brown, glabrous; blades narrowly triangular, attenuate, 2-3 cm wide, covered with minute scales beneath, laxly serrate with straight slender spines 2 mm long. Scape stout, soon glabrous; scape-bracts erect, the upper remote, broadly ovate, acute, entire. Inflorescence simple or few-branched, elongate, subdensely many-flowered, ferruginous-furfuraceous. Floral bracts ovate with triangular apices, ca. 9 mm long, reflexed; pedicels stout, 3 mm long; flowers suberect to spreading, 11 mm long. Sepals elliptic, obtuse, 6 mm long; petals exceeding the stamens, the blades erect or suberect, obovate, broadly rounded, more or less carinate; filaments high-connate above the common tube with the petals, the anthers linear, acute, strongly recurved; style half as long as the ovary.
