description: Trees (type specimen from a 15 m tree). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 610 mm in diam., at first distinctly longitudinally furrowed and with ridges decurrent from the bases of the petioles, with a dense, yellowish-brown cover of short, ± appressed hairs and slightly longer (up to 0.4 mm), ascending hairs, older twigs becoming roundish, their indument persistent as a grey, felted cover; terminal buds elongate-ovate, 7-8 mm long and 3-4 mm thick, densely covered with moderately short (0.20.3 mm), tightly appressed hairs. Petioles 920 mm long, 2.2-3.8 mm thick, roundish below, broadly canaliculate above, in young leaves often ± flat, indument below as on twigs, shorter and denser above, subpersistent Leaves alternate, elliptic, widest at the middle or slightly below, (8-) 12.5-22 cm long, (4-)6-9 cm wide, 1.8-2.7 times longer than wide, the tip obtuse with a minute acumen, the base broadly cuneate to obtuse, margin bent down to narrowly recurved, midrib and secondary veins deeply impressed above, the midrib distinctly, the larger veins sometimes slightly convex, very prominent below, secondary veins (5-)7-9 pairs, diverging at 35-60°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-40° to the midrib, tertiary venation predominantly ± scalariform, occasionally with distinct intersecondaries, level or slightly impressed above, raised below. Indument consisting of ± short, appressed hairs, the longest reaching ca. 0.3 mm, in young leaves (moderately) sparse above but dense on midrib and largest veins, intermediate to moderately dense below, later glabrescent above (sometimes except for the base of the midrib), becoming rather sparse and inconspicuous below. Gland dots seen only in still membraneous leaf. Inflorescences in the axils of just expanding leaves (possibly also some in the axils of cataphylls at the base of the young growth?), 2.3-3.3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 4-9 mm diam., 8-16 cm long, reaching ca. 1/2-2/3 the length of mature leaves, i.e., sometimes more than twice the length of their subtending leaf; peduncle 1-5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/8-1/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 12-18 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched 1-2(-3) times, the lower ones not entirely cymose, indument on peduncle like that on twigs but slightly less dense, closer to the flowers becoming finer and longer. Pedicels ca. 2-4 mm long, 0.6-1.2 mm thick. Flowers 5.57 mm in diam., tepals elliptic to ovate-elliptic, ca. 2.4-3 mm long and ca. 1.6-2.5 mm wide, papillosity moderately dense to dense on the inside surface, often reduced at the margin of the outer tepals. Stamens ca. 1.2 mm long including the short filament of ca. 0.2 mm, anthers distinctly papillose at the tip, ± broadly pentagonal in the two outer whorls, with a short, obtuse tip, in the third whorl roundish-obtrapeziform with an almost truncate tip. Staminodes somewhat clavate, ca. half as long as the stamens, papillose and hairy on abaxial side, glandular at the tip on adaxial side, free. Pistil ca. 1.6 mm long, glabrous, ovary subglobose to ellipsoid, style rather thick, reaching ca. 1/3 the length of the ovary. Receptacle shallowly bowl-shaped, with a few appressed hairs inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Trees. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 2.2-2.8(-3.5) mm in diam., initially slightly angular, soon becoming roundish, with moderately short (up to 0.3 mm), curled, appressed to ascending, cupreous hairs, moderately dense to dense immediately below terminal bud, quickly becoming moderately sparse, finally glabrescent; terminal buds elongate, 5.5-6.5 mm long, 1.5-1.8 mm thick, densely covered with moderately short (up to 0.3 mm), straight to ± curled, ± ascending, cupreous hairs. Petioles 7-13 mm long, 1.2-1.8 mm thick, ± roundish below, (indistinctly) canaliculate above, indument below ± as on twigs, denser above. Leaves alternate, oblong-lanceolate, widest ± at the middle (1/3-3/5 from the base), 9.5-14.5 cm long, 2.7-3.7 cm wide, 3.4-3.9 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base attenuate, margin recurved to very narrowly revolute, but the revolute part usually ending before it reaches the petiole, midrib flat to slightly raised in a slight impression above, usually impressed at the base, prominent below, secondary veins level to slightly raised above, prominent below, 7-9 pairs, diverging at 40-60°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-40° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed, with a small, indistinct percurrent part, ± reticulate, ± level above, scarcely visible, distinctly raised below. Indument consisting mainly of short, appressed hairs, plus a few slightly longer (to ca. 0.3 mm), straight or curled, ascending hairs on veins, apparently very sparse from the beginning above, glabrescent, initially moderately sparse below, becoming sparser, axils of the secondary veins not bearded. Gland dots not visible. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, 0.6-1.3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.1-2.8 mm diam., (3-)8-13.5 cm long, reaching ca. 1/3 of the length to almost the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle (1.6-)4-8 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/2-3/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-4 below the terminal cyme, branched 2-3 times, indument on peduncle ± as on twigs, becoming denser and slightly longer closer to the flowers. Pedicels 2.5-5 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm thick. Flowers 6-7.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elongate-elliptic, 2.7-3.2 mm long and 1.5-1.8 mm wide, densely papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 1 mm long including a short but distinct filament of 0.1-0.3 mm (in the outer whorls adnate to the tepals), anthers relatively weakly papillose, in the outer whorls ± pentagonal to ± trullate, with an obtuse to acute sterile tip, in the third whorl ± obtrapeziform to elongate pentagonal, usually broadly obtuse at the tip. Staminodes slightly clavate, reaching ca. 2/5 the length of the stamens, usually glandular on adaxial side, for ca. half their length united with the inner stamens. Pistil ca. 2 mm long, glabrous, ovary ellipsoid, style ± as long as the ovary. Receptacle relatively shallow tot hemispherical, glabrous inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Trees to 10 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.8-4 mm in diam., initially ± irregularly angular, with a dense, rusty-reddish cover of very short hairs and erect, ± curled, longer hairs (0.30.8 mm), older twigs usually becoming roundish, the indument ± persistent as a matted grey cover, slowly glabrescent (in the type all twigs strongly angular and with a dense, reddish indument); terminal buds ± lanceolate, 4-12 mm long and 1.5-4 mm thick, densely covered with ascending to erect, ± curled, red-brown hairs. Petioles (6-)11-16 mm long, 1-3 mm thick, roundish to distinctly longitudinally ridged below, broadly and shallowly canaliculate above with ridges along the central furrrow, indument ± as on twigs but mostly shorter. Leaves alternate, elliptic to lanceolate-elliptic, widest at the middle or slightly below, 8.5-20(-26) cm long, 2.7-8(-10) cm wide, (1.9-)2.3-3.3 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base acute or rarely obtuse, the very base usually attenuate or at least extended into a short projection along the petiole, margin flat to narrowly bent down, midrib and secondary veins (often distinctly) impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins 5-7(-9) pairs, diverging at 35-50(-55)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 15-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, ± level to clearly impressed above, (usually distinctly) raised below. Indument consisting of short, appressed, pale hairs and ± erect, curled, reddish hairs, even in youngest leaves almost exclusively on midrib and secondary veins above (sometimes only one of the two kinds of hairs present), only a few hairs in the intercostal areas, initially the appressed, pale hairs sparse to quite regular but rather inconspicuous below, the curled, reddish hairs ± sparse in intercostal areas, ± dense on veins, older leaves glabrescent above, but often hairs on basal part of midrib ± persistenL both hairtypes ± slowly becoming rather sparse below. Gland dots in mature leaves not visible, in young leaves sometimes moderately distinct above. Inflorescences in the axils of distal foliage leaves, 1-1.8 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.3-3 mm diam., 2-7 cm long, reaching ca. 1/5-3/5 the length of its subtending leaf; peduncle l-2.5(-3.5) cm long, reaching ca. 1/3-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (0-)2-4 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched 1-2(-3) times, indument similar to that on twigs but becoming shorter and more greyish-brown closer to the flowers, ± dense. Pedicels 1-3 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm thick. Flowers (5-)5.5-6.8(-7.5) mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, (1.9-)2.2-2.8(-3.5) mm long and (1.2-) 1.5-1.9 mm wide, distinctly papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.7-0.9 mm long including a filament of 0.2-0.3 mm, anthers distinctly papillose, in the two outer whorls transversely obtrullate, broadly pentagonal, or almost transverse elliptic with a ± obtuse tip, in the third whorl ± obtrapeziform to axe-shaped with a ± truncate to broadly rounded tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3-1/2 the length of the stamens, capitate, glandular on adaxial side (two lateral glands or confluent), papillose on abaxial side, united with the inner stamens at the very base. Pistil ca. 1.4-1.8 mm long, ovary (often broadly) ellipsoid, glabrous, style reaching ca. 1/2 to 2/3 the length of the ovary, glabrous or papillose. Receptacle urceolate, glabrous or with a few, tightly appressed hairs inside. Berry (immature) ovoid to ellipsoid, ca. 9 mm long and 7-8 mm in diam., cupule slightly more than hemispherical, ca. 6-8 mm high and ca. 10-11 mm in diam., pedicel scarcely thickened.

description: Trees to 30 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. (2.5-)3.8-5.8 mm in diam., initially ± angular and distinctly ridged, with short, ± appressed, whitish hairs, moderately dense to dense below the terminal bud, soon becoming sparse or glabrous, older twigs glabrous, greyish or blackish, often conspicuously lenticellate; terminal buds ovoid to elongate, 4-14 mm long, ca. 24 mm thick, densely covered with short, appressed, white hairs. Petioles 11-27 mm long but sometimes appearing still longer due to the revolute leaf base, 2-4.5 mm thick but often rather flat, ± roundish below, ± flat to broadly guttershaped above due to the ± erect margin, usually somewhat ridged on both sides, indument consisting of short, appressed hairs, initially moderately dense to dense above, moderately sparse to moderately dense below, glabrescent Leaves alternate, elliptic to oblong or lanceolate-elliptic, widest at the middle or slightly below, 13-25 cm long, 5-9.5 cm wide, 2.4-3.3 times longer than wide, tip with a short, indistinct, blunt acumen, acute to almost rounded towards the base, the base itself attenuate due to the revolute margin (in younger leaves at least recurved), midrib convex above, flat, or often with the center impressed and the sides slighdy raised, broadly convex to prominent below, secondary veins raised above, distinctly raised to prominent below, 7-10 pairs, diverging at 40-50° in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed (mainly percurrent) to almost scalariform, widely spaced, finer reticulation almost equally distinct, ± slightly raised above, distinctly raised below. Indument consisting of ± short (rarely reaching ca. 0.3 mm), straight, white, appressed hairs, in young leaves sparse to absent above, ± sparse below, quickly glabrescent above (occasionally except for base of midrib), becoming very sparse below, axils of secondary veins usually bearded with rather long (up to 1 mm), ± erect hairs. Gland dots relatively indistinct if at all visible. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, sometimes also in the axils of cataphylls below the terminal bud, ca. 1-3.5 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2-5 mm diam., 5.5-14 cm long, reaching ca. 1/3-2/3 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 2-6.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/3-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, rarely branched from the base, lateral branches 4-6(-8) below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched 2-4 times, indument consisting of short, appressed to ascending, mostly whitish hairs, moderately sparse to moderately dense on peduncle, dense on flowers. Pedicels 2-5.5 mm long, 0.51 mm thick. Flowers 8-11 mm in diam., tepals broadly elliptic, ca. 3.3-4 mm long and ca. 2.3-3.6 mm wide (the inner ones narrower), densely papillose on the inside surface but also hairy at the base. Stamens ca. 1-1.2 mm long including a hairy filament of 0.2-0.4 mm, anthers apically and on abaxial side with long papillae (and short hairs), in the two outer whorls transverse-elliptic to roundish-squarish, rounded to very slightly emarginate at the tip, in the third whorl ± roundish-rectangular, truncate to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 2/5-3/5 the length of the stamens, almost terete or with a small glandular head. Pistil ca. 1.6-2 mm long, glabrous, ovary subglobose to broadly pyriform, style usually very short, rarely reaching ca. 2/5 the length of the ovary. Berry ellipsoid or rarely subglobose, ca. 20-29 mm long and 18-23 mm in diam., cupule disk-like or slightly undulate, ca. 10-13 mm in diam.

description: Trees, to 20 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud (2.3-)3-6 mm in diam., ± angular but without very sharp angles, initially densely covered with long hairs (ca. 0.3-0.8 mm), ± erect, straight to slightly curled, ± brown, becoming matted on older twigs, then ± slowly glabrescent; terminal buds ± ovoid (usually sprouting at anthesis), 4.5-8.5 mm long, 2.3-4.5 mm thick, densely covered with ascending to erect, brownish hairs (like the twigs). Petioles 7-15 mm long, 2-4 mm thick, roundish-triangular below, shallowly canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs, denser above than below. Leaves alternate, elliptic to obovate, widest at the middle or 3/5 from the base, (12.5-) 17-28 cm long, (4-)7-13.5 cm wide, 1.7-2.6(-3.1) times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base cuneate to obtuse but usually attenuate at the very base, due to the broadly and conspicuously inrolled margin, midrib and secondary veins ± impressed above, very prominent below, secondary veins (5-)6-9 pairs, diverging at 35-50°, in midlamina running at an angle of 25-35° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, slightly impressed above, distinctly raised to almost prominent below. Indument on both surfaces consisting of long (ca. 0.3-0.8 mm), erect hairs, initially very dense on midrib and secondaries above, intermediate in intercostal area, there quickly subglabrescent, persistent on veins for a long time, initially moderately dense below, ± slowly becoming sparser. Gland dots not seen. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, 1.3-3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2.8-8 mm diam., 2.5-16 cm long, reaching ca. 1/8 to 3/4 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 0.6-7 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/5-1/2 the inflorescence length, with an intermediate to dense indument similar to that on twigs, lateral branches 4-8 below terminal cluster of cymes, branched 2-5 times, with a ± dense, brownish indument Pedicels extremely short or up to 1.5 mm long, ca. 0.7-0.9 mm thick. Flowers only ca. 3-4.5 mm in diam. because tepals never spreading, all flower parts drying blackish, tepals ± ovate-elliptic, ca. 2-2.5 mm long and ca. 1-1.5 mm wide, with fine papillae on the inside surface, (moderately) dense on the inner tepals, much sparser on the outer ones. Stamens ca. 0.8-1.4 mm long including the long filament (0.3-0.7 mm), anthers with minute papillae (even on the valves), the outer ones ± ovate, their apex in the first whorl usually minutely apiculate or almost acute, in the second whorl ± rounded, anthers of the third whorl ± roundish-rectangular but usually ± obtuse at the tip. Staminodes reaching slightly less than half the length of the stamens, united with the inner stamens at the base only, thickish and papillose, slightly thickened towards the tip, with a minute glandular patch. Pistil ca. 1.6-1.9 mm long, ovary ± ellipsoid or (inversely) pear-shaped, glabrous, style ca. as long as the ovary, glabrous or with some minute papillae near the tip. Receptacle relatively shallow, cup- or bowl-shaped, with short, appressed to ascending hairs inside, these very sparse or covering the surface completely. Berry spheroidal to rather elongate, 12-28 mm long and 912 mm in diam., cupule variable (often in the same specimen), obconical, funnel-shaped or almost flat, 10-13 mm in diam., 2-7 mm deep, pedicel ± distinctly thickened.

description: Small trees to 6 m (always?). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.5-2.5 mm in diam., initially ± slightly angular/flattened, quickly becoming round, at first with short, appressed hairs, immediately below the terminal bud (moderately) sparse but very soon glabrescent; terminal buds mostly sprouting at anthesis, ca. 2.5-4.5 mm long and 0.8-1.2 mm thick, densely covered with short, appressed, pale brownish hairs. Petioles (7-)9-20 mm long, (0.8-)1.1-1.8 mm thick, ± roundish below, flat or slightly canaliculate above, usually irregularly ridged on both sides, indument consisting of short, ± appressed hairs, very sparse below, slightly denser above, glabrescent. Leaves alternate, elliptic to lanceolate-elliptic or ovate-elliptic, widest 2/5 from the base to almost at the middle, (7-)10-16.5(-20) cm long, (3-)3.5-7.5 cm wide, 1.9-3.2 times longer than wide, tip narrowed to a mostly short acumen, base attenuate to obtuse, margin flat to very narrowly bent down, midrib above slightly impressed but often also slightly convex, prominent below, secondary veins slightly convex above, often in a slight impression, slightly prominent below, secondary veins 5-7(-8) pairs, diverging at 35-60°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-45° to the midrib, tertiary venation ± scalariform, ± level to slightly raised above, often rather inconspicuous, ± raised below. Indument consisting of short, ± appressed hairs, initially sparse on both sides, often slightly denser on veins, quickly glabrescent, sometimes some hairs on base of midrib persistent above, axils of at least some of the secondary veins nearly always bearded with relatively thick, ± straight, longer hairs (up to ca. 0.4 mm) below, spreading mainly from the veins but also from the intercostal area. Gland dots in young leves sometimes moderately distinct above, rarely even below, in mature leaves not visible. Inflorescences in the axils of foliage leaves, occasionally frondulose or (pseudo?)ter-minal, 0.8-1.5 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.2-2.5(-4.5) mm diam., 2.5-9 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4 to slightly more than the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 1.4-5 cm long, reaching ca. 2/5-3/4 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-4 below the terminal cyme, branched 0-2 times, indument consisting of ± short, appressed to ascending hairs, extremely sparse to absent on peduncle, sparse to intermediate on receptacle. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3 the length of the stamens, rather thick, pyramidal to slightly clavate, papillose on abaxial side, usually with a glandular patch in apical part on adaxial side, almost free or p.p. united with the adjacent glands. Receptacle ± hemispherical, glabrous or with a few tightly appressed hairs inside. Berry elongate, ca. 18 mm long, ca. 9 mm in diam., cupule bowl-shaped, ca. 4-5 mm high and ca. 11-14 mm in diam., pedicel slightly but noticeably thickened.

description: Trees, to 30 m (but usually collected from much smaller individuals). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud (1.3-)1.8-3.3 mm in diam., initially slightly angular/furrowed, and/or flattened towards the nodes, usually quickly becoming terete, with a moderately dense to dense cover of ± short, appressed to ascending hairs below the terminal bud (mostly very short hairs, «0.1 mm, and fewer longer hairs, ca. 0.2 mm, very rarely the longer hairs to 0.6 mm long, see discussion), mostly subpersistent, less often quickly becoming moderately sparse, rarely quickly subglabrescent; terminal buds ± elongate, 3-11 mm long, 0.9-3 mm thick, densely covered with short to moderately long (up to 0.4 mm), appressed to ascending hairs, often sprouting at anthesis. Petioles 8-20(-26) mm long, 0.9-2 mm thick, ± roundish or irregularly ridged below, canaliculate above, in young leaves often flattened, indument ± as on twigs, denser above than below, (sub)glabrescent. Leaves alternate to opposite, mostly ± lanceolate, varying towards (narrowly) oblong or (ovate-)elliptic, widest 1/3 from the base to ± at the middle, (5-)8-21(-26) cm long, (1.9-)2.4-5.5(-8.5) cm wide, (2.1-)2.6-5(-6.1) times longer than wide, tip ± tapering towards an indistinct to long and sharply pointed acumen, base mostly acute, less often obtuse or attenuate, margin flat to bent down, rarely very narrowly recurved, midrib flat and ± level to clearly convex above, often in a slight impression, prominent below, secondary veins 5-9(-10) pairs, diverging at (25-)30-60°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of (10-)15-35° to the midrib, slightly raised to slightly impressed above, raised to prominent below, tertiary venation finely scalariform, rarely with a few, weak, laterally oriented intersecondaries, ± level to slightly raised on both sides (more likely raised below than above). Indument consisting of short, ± appressed hairs, and often a few longer, more ascending hairs (up to 0.3 mm, but see discussion), in young leaves dense to subglabrous above, dense to intermediate below (but sometimes very inconspicuous, check at 25x), often distinctly sparser on veins, rarely with tufts of often slightly reddish, ± erect hairs (up to 0.3 mm) in the axils of the secondary veins, older leaves glabrescent above, indument ± persistent below or becoming very sparse. Gland dots in young leaves often ± distinct above (if not concealed by the indument), in mature leaves scarcely to not at all visible. Inflorescences in the axils of foliage leaves, 0.7-2 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of (l-)1.5-3.6(-4.8) mm diam., (1.5-)3-10 cm long, reaching ca. 1/5-3/5 (usually clearly less than half, but see discussion) the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle (0.7-)1.5-4.5(-6) cm long, i.e., ca. 1/3-2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-4 below the terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, branched (l-)2-4 times, indument on peduncle ± as on twigs, or often slightly longer, denser, and less appressed, closer to the flowers becoming still denser and often longer. Pedicels 1-3.5(-5.5) mm long (rarely almost absent), 0.4-0.7 mm thick. Flowers (6-)6.5-10(-11.5) mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, ca. 2.5-4.4(-5.7) mm long and ca. 1.8-3.6 mm wide, heavily papillose on the inside surface. Stamens (Fig. 6N, O) ca. (1.1-)1.3-1.9 (-2.3) mm long including a filament of 0.1-0.3 (-0.5) mm, anthers papillose, in the two outer whorls trullate to ovate, with a distinct acute to parabolic sterile tip, in the third whorl elongate pentagonal to obovate, with a ± obtuse (acute to rounded) sterile tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3-1/2 the length of the stamens, terete to slightly clavate, papillose, usually united with the inner stamens for ca. half their length (rarely less), not rarely completely united with the adjacent glands. Pistil ca. 1.8-2.5 mm long, ovary ellipsoid to spheroidal, glabrous, style reaching ca. 3/5 to ± the length of the ovary, usually papillose, rarely glabrous. Receptacle urceolate to almost spherical, glabrous inside. Berry rather elongate, ca. 19-33 mm long, 10-12(-16) mm in diam., cupule hemispherical, deeply cup-shaped, or usually slightly campanulate (i.e., margin slightly widened), ca. 9-13(-17) mm in diam. and ca. 5-10 mm high, on outside slightly irregularly ridged, pedicel slightly but increasingly thickened.

description: Trees to 20 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 2.2-4.5 mm in diam., at first ± irregularly angular but often quickly becoming roundish, the younger parts covered with a very dense, ± reddish-brown indument of very short to moderately long (up to ca. 0.5 mm), almost straight to curled, erect hairs, becoming felted and grey-ish on older twigs, slowly wearing off; terminal buds ± elongate, 7-14 mm long, 1.8-3 mm thick, densely covered with reddish-brown hairs. Petioles 9-25 mm long, 1.1-3.5 mm thick, flattened in young leaves, later broadly roundish and somewhat ridged below, slightly convex to shallowly canaliculate with ridges along the central furrow above, indument as on twigs. Leaves alternate, ± lanceolate or very rarely elliptic, widest ca. 2/5-1/2 from the base, (7-) 11-28 cm long, (2.2-)4.5-10.5 cm wide, (2.2-)2.8-4.2 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base usually acute, rarely obtuse to broadly rounded, margin flat to slightly bent down, midrib convex above, sometimes in a slight impression, very prominent below, secondary veins slightly impressed to slightly raised (convex) above, (very) prominent below, secondary veins (6-)8-l 1 pairs, diverging at 50-70°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-40(-50)° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, level to slightly impressed above, distinctly raised to prominent below, usually also finer veinlets clearly raised below. Indument consisting of short to long (up to ca. 0.5 mm), ± erect, strongly curled, ± reddish hairs, initially moderately dense to moderately sparse above, quickly glabrescent but often with remnants on midrib and largest veins, initially (very) dense below, with the shorter and paler hairs mainly in the intercostal area, usually covering the epidermis completely, the longer and more reddish hairs mainly on veins, at least the shorter hairs subpersistent. Gland dots usually visible on upper surface of young leaves where the indument is worn off. Inflorescences in the axils of leaves on young growth, 1-2.2 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2-4 mm diam., 4.5-15.5 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4 to 4/5 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 1.8-6 cm long, i.e., 1/3 to 3/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-4(-6) below terminal cyme, branched (0-)l-4 times, indument similar to that on twigs, very dense. Pedicels ca. 1-3.5 mm long, 0.8-1.1 mm thick. Flowers 6.5-11(-13) mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, 3-5.5(-6) mm long and 1.7-4.5 mm wide, papillosity ± dense and (moderately) thick on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 1.2-2(-2.8) mm long including the very short but usually distinct filament, anthers heavily papillose, in the first whorl pentagonal to rhombic, with an acute to obtuse tip, in the second whorl ± trullate with an acute tip, in the third whorl ± elongate-pentagonal to ovate with a long parabolic to acute tip. Staminodes thick, reaching ca. 1/4 to 2/5 the length of the stamens, densely papillose and often with a few hairs, occasionally with a small glandular patch on adaxial side, distinctly united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 2(-3) mm long, ovary spheroidal, glabrous, style ± as long as the ovary, slightly to moderately papillose. Receptacle urceolate, glabrous inside. Berry ovoid to ellipsoid, ca. 12-15 mm long, ca. 8.5-11 mm in diam., cupule deeply cup-shaped, 810 mm high, 12-13 mm in diam., pedicel slightly thickened.

description: Trees to 15 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.8-3.5 mm in diam., initially ± angular and/or longitudinally furrowed, with a dense cover of very short, yellowish hairs and long (0.5-1.5 mm), curled, reddish hairs, older twigs becoming roundish, the shorter hairs ± persistent as a grey cover, slowly wearing off; terminal buds conical to lanceolate, 5-10 mm long and 2-3 mm thick, densely covered with long, curled or almost straight, appressed to ascending, reddish hairs. Petioles 8-18 mm long, 1.2-2 mm thick, roundish below, ± shallowly canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs, more persistent above than below. Leaves alternate, lanceolate or rarely lanceolate-elliptic, widest 1/3 from the base to slightly below the middle, (7-)9-17(-19) cm long, 2.8-5(-6) cm wide, (2.5-)3-4 times longer than wide, the tip tapering towards a narrow acumen, base acute, margin flat or nearly so, midrib ± slightly impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins ± level above, raised to slightly prominent below, 5-7(-9) pairs, diverging at 35-50°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 15-30° to the midrib, tertiary venation ± scalariform, occasionally with a few weak, laterally oriented intersecondaries, usually very inconspicuous, level above, very slightly raised below. Indument consisting of short, yellowish hairs, mainly on the lamina, and slightly longer (up to ca. 0.4 mm), more reddish hairs, mainly on the veins, usually ± ascending above (occasionally appressed), in young leaves (moderately) dense but often inconspicuous, later glabrescent, hairs more appressed below, ± pointing towards the leaf tip, in young leaves very dense and usually golden shining, the longer, reddish hairs more erect, rarely forming indistinct tufts in the axils of the secondary veins, indument almost persistent or very slowly subglabrescent in older leaves. Gland dots not visible to distinct in young leaves above. Inflorescences in the axils of distal foliage leaves, rarely some of them in the axils of cataphylls below the terminal bud, 0.8-2 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-3 mm diam., 2-5(-9) cm long, reaching ca. 1/5-1/2 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 1-2(-3) cm long, reaching ca. (1/4-)1/2(-3/5) the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-4 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched 1-3(-4) times, indument ± as on twigs. Pedicels 0.5-2.5 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm thick. Flowers 5-8 (-9.5) mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, 2-3(-4) mm long and 1.5-2 mm wide, distinctly papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.7-0.9 mm long including a filament of up to 0.2 mm, anthers distinctly papillose, in the two outer whorls broadly pentagonal to broadly rhombic, with an obtuse to almost rounded tip (in the first whorl usually slightly wider than in the second whorl), in the third whorl pentagonal to obtrapeziform, with an obtuse to almost truncate tip. Staminodes ca. half as long as the stamens, occasionally with a small glandular patch at the tip, united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous, ovary ellipsoid, style relatively thick, ca. as long as the ovary. Receptacle deeply urceolate, covered with tightly appressed hairs inside (sometimes only in patches). Berry (immature) ovate-ellipsoid, ca. 12 mm long and 7 mm in diam., cupule deeply campanulate, ca. 9 mm deep and 11 mm in diam., pedicel scarcely thickened.

description: Shrubs or trees to 25 m (but flowering when only 2 m tall). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. (l.l-)1.8-3(-4.5) mm in diam., initially ± angular and longitudinally ridged, the ridges often completely obscured by a dense, usually reddish-brown indument consisting of (short to) long (up to 0.7 mm), straight to slightly curled, usually ascending to erect hairs (but see discussion), becoming greyish and felted, then slowly wearing off; terminal buds ovoid to elongate (mostly sprouting at anthesis), ca. 3.5-13 mm long, ca. 0.8-5.5 mm thick, densely covered with ± long, appressed to ascending, usually cupreous hairs. Petioles 2.5-10(-12) mm long, 1.12.8 mm thick, ± roundish below, ± flat to broadly canaliculate above, indument initially dense, consisting of short to long, appressed to ascending hairs, usually shorter above, paler, and often denser than below, ± slowly becoming sparser. Leaves alternate, lanceolate to oblong or elliptic, widest ± at the middle (2/5-3/5 from base), (7-) 10-22(-24) cm long, (2.5-)3.3-7(-8.5) cm wide, 2.2-4.4 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base ± cuneate to obtuse, not rarely ± cuneate towards the base and the base itself abruptly obtuse, margin flat to narrowly bent down, midrib above ± impressed, flat or its basal part often with a central furrow, distally sometimes ± convex, very prominent below, secondary veins above usually ± convex (rarely flat), level or mostly in a slight impression, (very) prominent below, (4-)5-8 pairs, diverging at (30-)35-55 (-60)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 15-35(-40)° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed, proportion of percurrent to scalariform part variable, widely spaced, often inconspicuous, ± level above (slightly raised to slightly impressed), ± raised or rarely almost prominent below. Indument consisting of fine hairs, usually very short and long (up to 0.6 mm) mixed, appressed to ascending (the shortest hairs, <0.1 mm, occasionally ± erect, Fig. 2E, F), initially intermediate to sparse above, much denser on midrib, glabrescent (often except for base of midrib), initially moderately dense to intermediate below but often very inconspicuous (the short hairs usually less than 0.1 mm apart but apparent only in intense light incident at a very shallow angle), slowly becoming sparser, axils of secondary veins (usually) with ± long (up to ca. 0.6 mm), ± erect hairs, often surrounding a glabrous spot, rarely such hairs also elsewhere along midrib or in higher-order axils. Gland dots in mature leaves not visible to distinct above. Inflorescences in the axils of young foliage leaves and in the axils of cataphylls, below the terminal bud or at the base of the new growth, ca. (0.4-)0.7-1.8(-2.7) mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1-3.5(-5) mm diam., (0.7-)4-15(-22) cm long, reaching ca. 1/4 the length of the closest foliage leaf to almost twice its length; peduncle ca. (0.4-) 1.5—5.5 (-7.5) cm long, i.e., (1/20-)l/4-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (0-)4-12 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched (0-)l-4(-5) times (branches sometimes not entirely cymose), indument consisting of usually mixed short to long (to 0.7 mm) hairs, straight to ± curled, ± ascending, dense to intermediate on peduncle, becoming shorter, denser, paler, and often more appressed closer to the flowers, but often sparser again on the tepals. Pedicels (0.8-)1.5-4.5(-6) mm long, 0.2-0.4 mm thick. Flowers 3.5-6.2(-7.3) mm in diam., tepals! elongate, ca. 1.4-2.8(-3.5) mm long and ca. (0.5-)0.7-1.2(-1.6) mm wide, with a moderately sparse to dense cover of fine papillae on the inside surface, increasingly mixed with hairs towards the base. Stamens ca. 0.4-0.7 mm long including a ± hairy filament of 0.1-0.3 mm, anthers glabrous or slightly papillose at the tip, usually with hairs on back side, in the outer whorls ± transverse-elliptic to roundish-rectangular, broadly rounded to very slightly emarginate at the tip, in the third whorl ± roundish-squarish, ± truncate to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 3/5-5/6 the length of the stamens, with a ± hairy (rarely glabrous) filament and a distinct glandular head. Pistil ca. 0.9-1.2 mm long, glabrous or mostly ± hairy, ovary ± ellipsoid to spheroid, style mostly short, usually less than half as long as the ovary, rarely reaching ca. 3/5 of its length. Receptacle very small, bowl-shaped, glabrous or with some hairs inside. Berry subglobose or occasionally slightly ellipsoid, ca. 6-11 mm long and 6-9.5 mm in diam., cupule bowl-shaped, occasionally slightly dentate, 1.5-4 mm high and ca. 4-7 mm in diam., pedicel scarcely to distinctly thickened.

description: Trees to 20 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.5-2.8 mm in diam., initially somewhat irregularly angular/flattened, with a dense, ± grey-brown cover of very short, ± erect hairs and fewer slightly longer (up to ca. 0.3 mm), ± appressed to ascending hairs, older twigs becoming roundish, the shortest hairs ± persistent as a grey cover, slowly wearing off; terminal buds narrowly lanceolate to ovoid, 3-7 mm long and 0.7-2.5 mm thick, densely covered with short to moderately long (up to 0.4 mm), appressed to ascending, light brown hairs. Petioles 3.5-14 mm long, 1-2.2 mm thick, ± roundish below, slightly ridged, ± flattened above or often shallowly canaliculate at the lamina and with a central ridge at the base, indument ± as on twigs, often denser above than below. Leaves alternate, ± elliptic to lanceolate-elliptic, widest ± at the middle or slightly above, (3.5-)5-13(-18) cm long, (1.5-)2.5-5(-6) cm wide, (1.7-)2.2-3.4(-4) times longer than wide, tip ± acuminate but sometimes acumen very short, base attenuate, acute, or cuneate, rarely obtuse, margin flat to very narrowly recurved, midrib ± convex above, sometimes in a slight impression, prominent below, secondary veins slightly convex and/or slightly impressed above, slightly prominent below, (3-)4-6 pairs, diverging at 40-55°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-40° to the midrib, tertiary venation ± scalariform, rarely with a few, indistinct intersecondaries, often rather inconspicuous, level to slightly impressed above, level to slightly raised below. Indument consisting mainly of short, ± appressed hairs, sometimes with some additional slightly longer (up to 0.3 mm), more ascending hairs above, especially on midrib, initially moderately sparse to subglabrous above, denser on veins, (subglabrescent, initially moderately sparse to moderately dense below, becoming sparser and rather inconspicuous, the axils of the lower secondary veins usually with at least a few ± straight, ± erect, longer hairs, rarely such hairs scattered along the midrib. Gland dots in young leaves occasionally moderately distinct above, later not visible. Inflorescences in the axils of leaves on young growth, (0.3-)0.8-1.5 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1-3(-4) mm diam., (3.5-)5.5-11(-15) cm long, usually ± as long as their subtending leaves or up to twice as long, rarely reaching only ca. 2/5 of their length; peduncle (2-)3.5-7.5(-8.5) cm long, reaching ca. 1/2-4/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-2(-4) below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched 0-2 times, indument consisting of fine, short to moderately long (up to 0.4 mm), ± ascending, often slightly curled, yellow-brown hairs, on peduncle ± short and moderately sparse to moderately dense, closer to the flowers becoming longer and denser, on tepals sometimes again sparse. Pedicels (3-)5-9(-11) mm long, 0.40.6 mm thick. Flowers (6-)7-9.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic to oblong, (2.3-)2.7-3.8 mm long and 1.7-2.8 mm wide, heavily papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 1-1.5 mm long including a filament of 0.1-0.3 mm, anthers heavily papillose, broadly pentagonal to elliptic in the first whorl, with an obtuse to rounded tip, pentagonal to trullate in the second whorl, with an acute to obtuse tip, obtrapeziform to pentagonal in the third whorl, with an obtuse to truncate tip. Staminodes reaching 2/5-2/3 the length of the stamens, thickish, papillose, often with a distinct glandular patch on adaxial side, united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 1.2-1.7 mm long, ovary depressed spheroidal to ovate, glabrous or with a few hairs, style ca. half as long as the ovary (but not exceeding the staminodes), glabrous or with some papillae. Receptacle bowlshaped to almost urceolate, at least at the base ± covered with tightly appressed hairs inside. Berry ellipsoid, ca. 12 mm long, ca. 7 mm in diam., cupule shallow when young, becoming deeply cup-shaped when mature, ca. 5-6 mm high and ca. 7-9 mm in diam., pedicel scarcely thickened.

description: Trees, to 30 m (40 m?) tall. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 3.5-9 mm in diam., with distinct longitudinal ridges and furrows, densely covered with mixed short to long (the longer ones ca. 0.3-0.7 mm), ascending to erect hairs, on older twigs becoming felt-like; terminal buds elongate to ovoid, 7-15 mm long and 2.5-8 mm thick, densely covered with ± ascending hairs similar to the longer ones on the twigs. Petioles 10-23(-32) mm long, 2-5 mm thick, usually ± flattened, broadly roundish below, mostly longitudinally ridged, usually broadly canaliculate above, indument at first ± as on twigs, more persistent above than below. Leaves alternate, obovate to elliptic or oblanceolate, widest 1/2-2/3 from the base (usually slightly above the middle), (11.5-)17-33 cm long, (3.3-)-4.5-15 cm wide, 1.7-3.2(-3.6) times longer than wide, tip with a mostly short acumen, base obtuse to attenuate, usually ± cuneate, margin flat to slightly recurved, midrib convex in a ± distinct impression above, very prominent below, secondary veins impressed and occasionally slightly convex above, very prominent below, 8-12 pairs, diverging at 40-65°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of (15-)20-45° to the midrib, tertiary venation usually scalariform to percurrent, occasionally with some short intersecondaries, ± impressed above, rarely almost level, (almost) prominent below. Indument (Fig. 3 E, F) consisting of short to long (up to 0.6 mm), straight to ± curled hairs, ± ascending above, initially intermediate to sparse, much denser on veins, (subglabrescent, (predominantly) ± erect below, initially moderately sparse to intermediate, denser on veins, slowly becoming ± sparse. Intercostal area often distinctly glaucous below. Gland dots visible only in young leaves. Inflorescences in the axils of foliage leaves and/or in the axils of cataphylls, at the base of the new growth or below the terminal bud, 1.3-3(-5) mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 3-7(-9) mm diam., 9.5-23 cm long, reaching ca. half the length to twice the length of the closest foliage leaf (usually slightly longer); peduncle 4-10 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/4-1/2 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (4-)8-14 below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched (1-)2-3(-4) times, at least the lower inflorescence branches usually themselves thyr-soids, indument ascending to erect, moderately dense to dense on peduncle, often sparser and more appressed on the flowers. Pedicels ca. 0.7-3.3(-7) mm long, 0.2-0.4 mm thick. Flowers 2.8-4.2(-5.6) mm in diam., tepals elliptic to narrowly parabolic, 1.1-1.9(-2.3) mm long and 0.7-1(-1.6) mm wide, usually ± densely covered with rather long, fine, hair-like papillae on the inside surface (sometimes shorter or absent at the lateral margin of outer tepals, rarely shorter and sparser on the entire tepal). Stamens ca. 0.5-0.7 mm long including the very short filament, anthers apically and on abaxial side covered with usually long papillae, in the two outer whorls ± transverse elliptic to roundish-obtrapeziform, broadly rounded to slightly emarginate at the tip, in the third whorl ± obtrapeziform, very broadly obtuse to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/2-3/4 the length of the stamens, slightly clavate, with long papillae on abaxial side, possibly slightly glandular on adaxial side, free. Pistil ca. 1-1.2 mm long, ovary ± pearshaped, glabrous or with a few scattered hairs, style very short Receptacle rather shallow, glabrous inside. Berry subglobose, ca. 13 mm long and ca. 11 mm in diam., cupule (after TRIN 5504) very shallow, ca. 1-2 mm high and ca. 7 mm in diam., often slightly undulate, pedicel distinctly thickened.

description: Trees to 25 m (but mostly collected from much smaller individuals). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.8-6 mm in diam., ± distinctly irregularly angular, the younger parts covered with a dense, ± reddish-brown indument of very short and (fewer) longer (ca. 0.2-0.7 mm), almost straight to curled, ± erect hairs, becoming felted and greyish on older twigs, very slowly wearing off; terminal buds ± ovate to elongate, 6-12 mm long, 2-5.5 mm thick, densely covered with reddish-brown hairs. Petioles 7.5-20 mm long, 1.3-3.2 mm thick, often flattened in young leaves, with prominent midrib and decurrent margin below, later irregularly roundish or irregularly triangular below, ± ridged, flat to shallowly canaliculate with ridges along the central furrow above, indument as on twigs. Leaves alternate (rarely partly opposite), elliptic to ovate, occasionally lanceolate-elliptic or oblong-elliptic, widest ca. 2/5 from the base to slightly above the middle, usually slightly below the middle, 5-20(-27) cm long, 2-9(-12) cm wide, (1.4-)1.8-2.7(-3.6) times longer than wide, tip acuminate (acumen often short), base usually obtuse to broadly rounded, less frequently acute, mainly in smaller leaves, midrib and secondary veins slightly to deeply impressed above, sometimes slightly convex, very prominent below, secondary veins 5-8(-10) pairs, diverging at 35-65°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of (15-)20-45° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform (to percurrent), rarely with a few distinct intersecondaries, level to distinctly impressed above, distinctly raised to prominent below, usually also finer veinlets clearly raised below. Indument usually consisting of short, ± pale, irregularly ± appressed to erect and strongly curled hairs, and longer (up to 0.8 mm), ± erect, curled, reddish hairs, in variable proportion and mostly intergrading, in young leaves the shorter hairs dense to absent above, the longer hairs dense to only on veins, the shorter hairs usually initially dense below, mostly covering the epidermis completely, the longer hairs moderately dense to sparse, denser on veins, older leaves glabrescent above, indument often subpersistent below, sometimes becoming sparse. Gland dots mostly not visible. Inflorescences in the axils of leaves on young growth, 1-3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.8-5.5 mm diam., (2-)3-11(-15) cm long, reaching ca. 1/3 to slightly more than the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle (1-)1.5-6(-8.5) cm long, i.e., 1/3 to 3/4 the length of the inflorescence (usually ca. 1/2), lateral branches (0-)2-4(-6) below terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, branched 1-2(-3) times, occasionally not entirely cymose, indument usually ± as on twigs, very dense. Pedicels extremely short or up to 5 mm long, 0.8-1.5 mm thick. Flowers (6.5-)9-14 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, (2.8-)3.3-6 mm long and (2-)2.3-4.5 mm wide, papillosity ± dense and (moderately) thick on the inside surface but sometimes only fully developed in basal triangle on outer tepals. Stamens ca. (1-)1.3-2.5 mm long including the short but usually distinct filament, anthers heavily papillose, in the first whorl pentagonal, ± ovate or trullate, with an acute to obtuse tip, in the second whorl ± trullate with an acute to parabolic tip, in the third whorl ± elongate-pentagonal to obtrapeziform with an acute to truncate tip. Staminodes thick, usually ± clavate, reaching ca. 1/3 to 1/2 the length of the stamens, papillose and often hairy on abaxial side, mostly with a small glandular patch on adaxial side, united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. (1.3-)1.8-2.9 mm long, ovary ± ellipsoid, glabrous, style ± as long as the ovary, usually papillose, rarely glabrous or with hairs along the comers. Receptacle ± cup-shaped, largely closed by the bases of stamens and staminodes above, glabrous to densely hairy inside (only the receptacular tube, not the bases of stamens and staminodes). Berry ellipsoid, ca. 10-18 mm long, ca. 7-11 mm in diam., cupule deeply cup-shaped, 6-10 mm high, 10-13 mm in diam., pedicel slightly to distinctly thickened.

description: Description of type: Branch 5 cm below most distal leaf ca. 3 mm in diam., slightly angular/ flattened, soon becoming roundish, indument consisting of short (up to 0.2 mm), ± appressed hairs, extremely sparse from the beginning, glabrescent; terminal bud not seen. Petioles 9-15 mm long, 2.5-3 mm thick, ± roundish below, flat above or with a distinct ridge, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves alternate, elliptic, widest ± at the middle, ca. 23 cm long, 11-13 cm wide, tip in all four leaves broken, base broadly rounded, margin flat, midrib above convex in a slight impression, apparently prominent below, not seen, secondary veins slightly impressed above, 9-11 pairs, diverging at 60-70°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 45-60° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed, widely spaced, level to very slightly impressed above. Indument absent above, apparently similar to that of N. japurensis below (seen on fragment only). Gland dots not visible. Inflorescences in the axils of younger foliage leaves, in the axils of cataphylls at the base of the new growth, and (pseudo?) terminal, ca. 1 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of ca. 3 mm diam., 7-15 cm long, reaching ca. 1/3-2/3 the length of the closest foliage leaves; peduncle 4.5-7 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/2-2/3 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 2-6 below the terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, branched 2-3 times, the lower branchlets often not entirely cymose, indument consisting of short (to 0.2 mm), ± appressed to ± erect, curled hairs, very sparse on peduncle, becoming denser (up to moderately dense) closer to the flowers. Pedicels 1.2-3 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm thick. Flowers ca. 3.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, 1.8-2 mm long and 0.9-1.2 mm wide, covered with fine, short papillae on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 1 mm long including a distinct filament of ca. 0.2-0.4 mm, anthers minutely papillose, in the first whorl ± suborbicular, broadly rounded to minutely apiculate at the tip, in the second whorl roundish-trapeziform, broadly rounded to almost truncate at the tip, in the third whorl roundish-rectangular, broadly obtuse to truncate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. half the length of the stamens, ± triangular, minutely papillose, united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 2 mm long, ovary spheroidal, glabrous, style ± as long as the ovary, with fine papillae and a few short hairs. Receptacle urceolate, glabrous inside. Fruit unknown.

description: Trees to 20 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 1.8-3.3(-4.5) mm in diam., initially ± distinctly angular, ± quickly becoming roundish but often with persistent narrow ridges, with a dense to intermediate cover of mostly short or sometimes also up to 0.5 mm long, appressed to slightly ascending, white hairs immediately below terminal bud, ± quickly becoming (moderately) sparse, finally glabrescent; terminal buds elongate, ca. 2.5-11 mm long, ca. 1-2.2 mm thick, densely covered with ± tightly appressed, straight, white hairs. Petioles (4.5-)6-15 mm long, 1-2(-2.7) mm thick, ± irregular to roundish below, ± flat to canaliculate above, indument below as on twigs or sparser, initially denser above, glabrescent. Leaves alternate, ± lanceolate to oblong, occasionally varying towards elliptic, widest ca. 1/3 from the base to slightly above the middle, (7-) 12-21 (-27) cm long, (3-)3.5-6(-9.2) cm wide, 2.3-4.2 times longer than wide, tip ± acuminate, often tapering towards a relatively indistinct acumen, base broadly attenuate to obtuse, margin flat to very narrowly recurved, midrib above flat to convex, often in a slight impression, at the base sometimes concave or with a central furrow, (very) prominent below, secondary veins raised to prominent above, occasionally in a very slight impression, prominent below, (6-)7-11(-12) pairs, diverging at (35-) 40-60(-65)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of (15-)20-45° to the midrib, tertiary venation usually mixed, the larger part scalariform to percurrent, finer reticulation almost equally distinct, on both sides ± raised to almost prominent, rarely almost level above. Indument consisting of fine, straight, mixed short to long (up to 0.6 mm), ± appressed hairs, initially (moderately) sparse above, sparse to intermediate below, mature leaves glabrescent above (sometimes except for base of midrib), indument becoming very sparse below, axils of at least some secondary veins usually with ± long (up to ca. 1 mm), ± erect hairs. Gland dots in mature leaves inconspicuous to moderately distinct above, in young leaves often very distinct. Inflorescences usually in the axils of distal foliage leaves, rarely also in the axils of cataphylls at the base of the new growth, ca. 0.7-2(-2.4) mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of (1-)1.5-4.2 mm diam., (3.5-)6.5-20 cm long, reaching ca. 2/5 the length of the subtending leaf to almost its length; peduncle ca. (1.5-)3-8 (-9) cm long, i.e., 1/5-3/4 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (0-)2-6(-20) below the terminal cluster of cymes, branched (l-)2-3(-4) times (branches sometimes not entirely cymose), indument consisting of ± short (plus occasionally a few longer), ± appressed to erect hairs, moderately dense to very sparse on peduncle, dense and (at least in bud) conspicuously white on flowers. Pedicels 1-5(-6.5) mm long, 0.2-0.5 mm thick. Flowers 4-6.5(-7.3) mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, ca. (1.6-)2-2.8(-3.4) mm long and ca. (1-)1.2-1.7(-2.3) mm wide, on the inside surface ± densely covered with fine papillae, also with some hairs closer to the base. Stamens ca. 0.7-0.9 mm long including a hairy filament of 0.2-0.4 mm, anthers glabrous or slightly papillose at the tip, usually with hairs on back side, in the outer whorls ± transverse-elliptic to roundish-rectangular, broadly rounded to very slightly emarginate at the tip, in the third whorl ± roundish-rectangular, ± truncate to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 3/5-3/4 the length of the stamens, with a ± hairy filament and a distinct glandular head. Pistil ca. 1.1-1.5 mm long, glabrous or rarely with a few hairs (see discussion), ovary ± ellipsoid, style reaching ca. 1/3 the length of the ovary to almost its length. Receptacle bowl-shaped to hemispherical, glabrous or with some hairs inside. Berry ± ellipsoid, ca. 12-15 mm long and 8.5-12 mm in diam., cupule variable, bowlshaped to funnel-shaped or almost obconical, occasionally slightly undulate, 2-3.5 mm high and ca. 5.5-7 mm in diam., pedicel scarcely to distinctly incrassate towards the cupule.

description: Trees to 30 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 3-5.5 mm in diam., initially ± angular/ridged, ± densely covered with mixed very short to long hairs (to ca. 0.6 mm), ± appressed to ascending, white or pale yellowish (the shortest hairs p.p. erect), older twigs becoming roundish and slightly ridged, indument subpersistent or quickly (sub)glabrescent; terminal buds almost conical to elongate, 4-11 mm long, ca. 2-3.5 mm thick, densely covered with short to long hairs (to 0.5 mm), straight, appressed, white (or pale yellowish). Petioles 15-28 mm long, 2-4 mm thick, roundish below, ± flat or at the lamina canaliculate above, usually slighdy ridged, often with an erect margin, indument ± as on twigs, denser above than below, ± quickly becoming sparser. Leaves alternate, ± elliptic to oblong or lanceolate-elliptic, widest at the middle or slightly below, (13.5-)16-28(-45) cm long, (5-)7-14(-19) cm wide, 1.9-3.1 times longer than wide, tip with a distinct (but for the size of the leaf often relatively short) acumen, base acute to obtuse, rarely broadly attenuate or rounded, margin flat to narrowly recurved, midrib above usually deeply impressed near the base, its margins becoming more and more raised towards the tip, distally convex, often with a central furrow, very prominent below, secondary veins distinctly raised to prominent above, prominent below, (5-) 7-13(-15) pairs, diverging at 35-55(-65)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-45(-50)° to the midrib, tertiary venation usually predominantly percurrent (rarely distinctly mixed or almost scalariform), widely spaced, finer reticulation almost equally distinct, distinctly raised to almost prominent on both sides. Indument consisting of mixed very short to long (up to 0.5 mm) fine hairs, ± appressed (the shortest sometimes! erect), only on base of midrib above, initially moderately sparse to moderately dense below (distance between the hairs usually smaller than their length, but hairs often very inconspicuous), becoming sparse and scarcely visible, axils of secondary veins either glabrous or bearded with long (up to 1.2 mm), ± erect hairs, rarely such hairs also elsewhere along midrib or in higher-order axils. Gland dots in mature leaves not visible to moderately distinct above, usually very conspicuous in young leaves. Inflorescences in the axils of cataphylls, below the terminal bud or at the base of the new growth, and/or in the axils of young leaves, ca. 0.8-3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 2.2-6 mm diam., (5-)8.5-20(-25) cm long, reaching ca. 1/3 the length of the closest foliage leaf to slightly more than its length; peduncle (1.7-)3.5-10.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/3-3/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 4-6(-8) below the terminal cluster of cymes, like the rhachis often with a cluster of branchlets at their end, branched (1-)2-3(-4) times, indument consisting of ± short (plus sometimes a few longer), appressed to ascending, whitish hairs, moderately sparse to moderately dense on peduncle, ± dense on flowers. Pedicels l-3.5(-6) mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm thick. Flowers 5.5-8.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic to elongate-obovate, ca. 2.1-3.5(-4) mm long and ca. 1.3-2(-3) mm wide, with a moderate to dense cover of thick, often long papillae on the inside surface, mixed with hairs towards the base. Stamens ca. 0.7-0.9 mm long including a hairy filament of 0.2-0.3 mm, anthers with long papillae (and short hairs) apically and on abaxial side, in the two outer whorls transverse-elliptic to roundish-squarish, rounded to very slightly emarginate at the tip, in the third whorl ± roundish-squarish, truncate to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 3/5-4/5 the length of the stamens, with a hairy filament and a distinct glandular head. Pistil ca. 1.2-1.5 mm long, ovary subglobose to broadly pyriform, ± hairy (at least a few hairs at the base), style very short. Receptacle very shallowly bowl-shaped, ± hairy inside. Berry ellipsoid, ca. 18-24 mm long and 1117 mm in diam., cupule bowl-shaped to almost obconical, ca. 8-11 mm in diam., ca. 4-5.5 mm high, pedicel slightly thickened.

description: Inflorescence always with solitary flowers, white to reddish, 5-30 cm high (from root connection), 2-5 mm diam., glabrous; floral bracts elliptic to ovate 7-20 × 2-10 mm, margins entire or nearly so; pedicels short at anthesis, often somewhat elongated in fruit; floral bracts elliptic to ovate 7-20 × 2-10 mm, margins entire or nearly so. Flowers cylindric; calyx of 4-5 sepals often similar to petals, to 10 mm long; corolla of 3-6 imbricate petals, each 10-20 × 5-15 mm, pubescent within, oblong to oblanceolate, broadly saccate at base, rounded to truncate at apices, only slightly, if at all, reflexed at tip; stamens 8-14, of two series of alternating lengths, 7-15 mm long, bases clasped by elongate, slender, paired, nectariferous lobes; anthers short, appearing peltate, nearly horizontal at anthesis, to 2 mm diam., dehiscent at first by the ends of a terminal slit, often eventually gaping along the entire length; ovary 6-12 mm long, 5-9 mm diam., usually glabrous, locules 5-6; stigma broadly funnelform, 2-6 mm diam., lacking ring of subtending hairs; style stout, tapering to ovary, 2-7 × 2-5 mm. Capsule 7-11 × 5-12 mm, perianth may persist in fruit, capsular segments stout, persistent. Chromosomes: 2n = 48, n = 24 (Maloney & Finocchio, 1981); 2n = 32 (Love & Love, 1982).

description: Inflorescence racemose, rarely reduced to a solitary flower, light yellow to reddish, 5-30 cm high (from root connection), 1-10 mm diam, below lowermost flower, glabrous or variously pubescent; floral bracts elliptic to ovate, 8-15 × 3-15 mm, margins erose, irregularly toothed; pedicels slender, 2-20 mm long, elongating to 30 mm in fruit, 1-2 mm diam., finely pubescent to nearly glabrous, sometimes glandular; bracteoles sometimes present, not consistently so even within populations, to 10 × 5 mm. Flowers cylindric, often constricted distally; calyx distinct from corolla, sepals 4-5 or occasionally absent, 7-12 mm × 1-5 mm, usually pubescent within; corolla of 4-5 petals divergent at apices, 817 × 4-8 mm, oblong to oblanceolate, narrowly saccate at constricted base, rounded to acute at apices, usually reflexed at tip; stamens 8-10 in two series of alternating lengths, 5-14 mm long; anthers hippocrepiform, 0.8-1.5 mm long, each dehiscent by a single terminal slit over the connate sacs; ovary 4-8 × 3-6 mm, usually pubescent, locules 4-5, nectary lobes short, stout, flanking filaments; stigma umbilicate, 1.5-3 mm diam., often subtended by ring of stiff hairs; style uniformly slender, joining abruptly with ovary, 2-10 × 1-2 mm. Capsule 610 × 4-8 mm, perianth segments tending to be early deciduous in fruit, capsular segments often irregularly deciduous. Chromosomes: Reports under the following names M. hypophegea 2n = 16 (Love & Love, 1944), M. hirsuta 2n = 48 (Hagerup, 1944), M. lanuginosa 2n = 32 (Love, 1954), M. hypopithys n = 24 (Baker & Parfitt, 1982); 2n = ca. 48 (Uotila & Pellinen, 1985).

description: Herbs, 6-18 cm high. Rhizome small, scales 0.8-1 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, apex acute to acuminate. Stems white to yellowish white, branched or not. Leaves ovate to broadly ovate, 0.7-1.5 mm long, 0.7-1 mm wide, apex acute. Inflorescence a bifurcate cincinnus, each cincinnus 0.7-2.2 mm long and 1-3-flowered. Bracts ovate to broadly ovate, 0.6-1.6 mm long, 0.6-1 mm wide, apex acute to acuminate. Pedicels absent or up to 0.5 mm long. Flowers white, 6.5 mm long. Floral tube 5 mm long. The base of the floral tube with six prominent, transversely ellipsoid pouches to 0.8 mm diam. Outer tepals 3-lobed, 1.5 mm long and wide; central lobe broadly ovate-triangular, 1.2 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, margins involute; lateral lobes narrowly ovate-triangular, 1.5 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide. Inner tepals ovate to obovate, 0.4-0.5 mm long, 0.3 mm wide. Stamens yellow, inserted ca. 1 mm below the insertion of the inner tepals, connective 0.2 mm long, 0.4 mm wide. Style, including branches and stigmas, ca. 6 mm long, 3-branched, stigmas horseshoe-shaped, 0.4-0.5 mm diam., appendages ca. 0.5 mm long. Ovary ellipsoid, ca. 1.5 mm long, glands ellipsoid, ca. 0.3 mm long. Capsule ellipsoid to globose, 2-4.5 x 2.4-3.5 mm, including the persistent part of the floral tube 4-6 mm long, style exceeding the floral tube by 0.3-0.8 mm. Seeds 0.3-0.4 x 0.2 mm; funicles 0.2-0.5 mm long.

description: Herbs, 5-20 cm high. Rhizome-scales 0.8-2 mm long, 0.3-0.4 mm wide, apex acuminate to long-acuminate. Stems white to yellowish-white, branched or not. Leaves ovate, (0.7-)1.1 -1.8(-2.2) mm long, 0.8-1.2 mm wide, apex acute. Inflorescence a bifurcate cincinnus, each cincinnus 0.3-2 mm long and 1-4-flowered, or the plant having a solitary, terminal flower only. Bracts ovate, 1.3-2 mm long, 0.7-1 mm wide, apex acute, often partly broken off. Pedicels 0.3-0.9 mm long. Flowers white to pale yellow, 7.5-10.2 mm long. Floral tube 5-7.7 mm long, sometimes swollen above the capsule. Outer tepals 3-lobed, 1.8-2.5 mm long, ca. 1.2 mm wide; central lobe broadly ovate-triangular, ca. 1 mm long, ca. 0.9 mm wide, margins involute; lateral lobes narrowly ovate-triangular to ovate-triangular, 0.6-0.8 mm long, 0.1-0.3 mm wide. Inner tepals ovate to obovate, 0.4-0.5 mm long, ca. 0.2 mm wide. Stamens inserted ca. 0.7 mm below the insertion of the inner tepals, connective ca. 0.2 mm long and wide, apex truncate. Style, including branches and stigmas, 2.2-5.3 mm long, each branch ca. 0.2 mm long, stigma horseshoe-shaped, 0.3-0.6 mm diam., sinus 0.2 mm deep, appendages up to 0.7 mm long. Ovary obconical to angular-obovoid, 1.7-3 x 0.9-1.5 mm, glands globose, 0.2-0.4 mm diam. Capsule ellipsoid, 2.5-4.5 x 2-3.5 mm, including the persistent part of the floral tube (3.8-)4.3-8 mm long, style exceeding the floral tube by 0.4-0.8 mm. Seeds 0.3-0.5 x 0.1-0.2 mm; Amides white, 0.2-0.4 mm long.

description: Plant caulescent, scarcely more than 1 dm high. Leaves about 15, all alike, 6-30 cm long, slightly narrowed between sheath and blade; blades to 3 cm wide (usually 8 mm), coriaceous, undulate along the margins, serrulate, sparsely lepidote above, densely beneath. Inflorescence few-flowered. Floral bracts lanceolate, acute, much exceeding the ovary, ecarinate, serrulate; flowers 23-32 mm long. Sepals to 18 mm long, connate from 1/3 to 1/2, the free lobes lanceolate, acute, carinate, laxly and finely serrulate, sparsely lepidote toward apex; petals short-connate, white, the lobes spreading at anthesis and disclosing the stamens, narrowly elliptic, acute; ovary ellipsoid, stout.

description: Plant stemless, propagating by rhizomes. Leaves 15-20 in a dense rosette, 7-20 cm long, not narrowed between sheath and blade, glabrous and wholly green above, strongly nerved beneath and covered with a pale membrane of fused scales; sheaths small, very broadly ovate, entire or serrulate toward apex; blades more or less curved, narrowly triangular, attenuate, pungent, 8-10 mm wide, laxly serrate with slender curved spines 4 mm long. Inflorescence few-flowered. Floral bracts ovate, acute or acuminate, entire or serrulate, exceeding the ovary, lepidote; flowers to 26 mm long. Sepals ovate, rounded or emarginate, mucronulate, 6-7 mm long, connate for 3 mm, minutely serrulate, lepidote; petals high-connate, exceeding the stamens, white to yellow; ovary glabrous or lepidote, 3.5-4.5 mm long.

description: Stolons arising from the inflorescence, elongate, naked, at first erect and scapelike. Leaves about 15 in each rosette, all alike, to 18 cm long, completely covered beneath with brown appressed scales, soon glabrous above; sheaths small and inconspicuous; blades linear-lanceolate, filiform-acuminate, 22 mm wide, subdensely serrulate, the center channeled, the sides undulate; fascicles few-flowered, axillary. Floral bracts broadly ovate, slightly exceeded by the sepals, membranaceous, lepidote. Sepals 10 mm long, connate for 4 mm, the free lobes subsymmetrical, lance-ovate, with a thickened pungent apex, densely pale-lepidote; petals obtuse, 14 mm long, white.

description: Plant short-caulescent. Leaves densely brown-lepidote, becoming glabrous above; sheaths elliptic, subdensely serrulate; blades caudate-acuminate, laxly and minutely serrulate, marked above with a broad pale median stripe, dimorphic, those of the outer leaves linear-lanceolate, distinctly contracted toward the base, to 35 cm long, 25 mm wide, blades of the inner leaves narrowly triangular, not at all contracted toward the base, not over 15 cm long, 13 mm wide. Inflorescence compound with the flowers fasciculate in the axils of foliaceous bracts. Floral bracts elliptic, exceeding the ovary, membranaceous except for the thick pungent apex, serrulate, brown-lepidote. Sepals 16 mm long, carinate, lepidote, connate for 9 mm, the free lobes ovate, acute, entire; petals about 2 cm longer than the sepals, exceeding the stamens, white.

description: Caudex stout. Leaves all alike, to 39 cm long; sheaths oblong, barely differentiated; blades ligulate, acuminate, tapered gradually toward the base, 35 mm wide, covered beneath with brown appressed scales, glabrous above and marked with a broad pale median stripe (?), subdensely serrulate with pale antrorse teeth 1 mm long. Inflorescence 3 cm in diameter. Floral bracts oblanceolate, acuminate, about equaling the midpoint of the sepals, serrulate and lepidote toward apex; sepals 15 mm long, connate for 8 mm, alate-carinate with the wings decurrent on the ovary, the free lobes broadly elliptic, apiculate, serrulate, lepidote near apex; petals 4 cm long; stamens and pistil included; ovary subcylindric, 11 mm long.

description: Plant stemless; leaves all alike, few, over 50 cm long, not narrowed between sheath and blade; sheaths short, broadly ovate; blades straight, suberect, very narrowly triangular, long-acuminate, to 15 mm wide, laxly serrate with pale antrorse curved spines 1 mm long, glabrous above, strongly nerved beneath and covered with appressed scales. Inflorescence few-flowered. Floral bracts ovate, acute, much exceeding the ovary, entire, membranaceous, sparsely lepidote; flowers at least 4 cm long. Sepals 12 mm long, over half connate, the free lobes broadly ovate, acute and mucronulate; petals white; ovary to 10 mm long, much enlarged in fruit.

description: Plants closely aggregated, nearly stemless. Leaves about 12 in each flat rosette, to 20 cm long, covered beneath with pale coarse appressed scales; sheaths small and inconspicuous; blades linear-lanceolate, acuminate, 3 cm wide, becoming glabrous above except near the base, very light green with a narrow reddish margin, the broad flat median stripe somewhat darker than the equally broad undulate marginal stripes, densely serrulate with teeth 0.5 mm long. Inflorescence of few-flowered axillary fascicles, the distal perfect, the central staminate. Floral bracts lance-oblong, acute, exceeded by the sepals, thin, lepidote. Sepals 11 mm long, connate for 6 mm, the free lobes subquadrate with broad wings and thick triangular lepidote apiculus, dark; petals obtuse, 25 mm long, white.

description: Plant essentially stemless, scarcely over 5 cm high. Leaves less than 10 in a dense spreading rosette, scarcely over 8 cm long, narrowed between sheath and blade but not petiolate; sheaths evident, ovate; blades subovate, apiculate, nearly 3 cm wide, slightly if at all undulate on the margins, densely serrulate, densely and coarsely lepidote above except for 2 longitudinal green stripes 7 mm wide, wholly white-lepidote beneath. Inflorescence few-flowered. Floral bracts triangular, acuminate, equaling the sepals, serrulate, membranaceous, lepidote. Sepals 12 mm long, to 3/4 connate, narrowly triangular, acuminate, symmetric, sparsely lepidote; petals 15 mm long, white; ovary slenderly cylindric, 5 mm long.

description: Plant nearly stemless. Leaves few, glabrous above, covered beneath with white appressed scales, heteromorphic, the outer reduced to broadly ovate acute sheaths, the inner distinctly laminate; blades dimorphic, some linear-triangular, not at all narrowed at base, others linear-lanceolate, to 30 cm long, 15-20 mm wide, attenuate toward base but not petiolate, much thickened along a median line, laxly serrate with curved spines 1 mm long. Inflorescence rather few-flowered. Floral bracts lanceolate, acute, shorter than the ovary, carinate, membranaceous, white-lepidote toward apex. Sepals 14 mm long, connate for 10 mm, carinate, the lobes broadly ovate, broadly rounded and apiculate, white-lepidote; petals 30 mm long, connate for 12 mm, white; stamens included; ovary subcylindric, 12 mm long, epigynous tube funnelform, 1.5 mm long; ovules few.

description: Plant stemless or with a large erect stem covered with leaf-sheaths. Leaves 20-25 in a dense rosette or distributed along the stem, 15 cm long; sheaths broad, submembranaceous, glabrous above, sparsely white-lepidote beneath, coarsely spinulose (caulescent form) or densely and finely serrulate (stemless form); blades linear-triangular with a minute terminal spine, not at all contracted at base, 12 mm wide, coriaceous, not at all undulate, wholly green and glabrous above, covered beneath with a white membrane of fused scales, alutaceous-tomentellous on both sides when young, laxly serrate with spreading spines upturned at tip and 2.5 mm long. Inflorescence rather few-flowered. Floral bracts long-acuminate from an ovate base, nearly equaling the sepals, entire, very thin-membranaceous, pellucid, sparsely floccose-tomentellous. Sepals not mucronate, 11.5 mm long, connate for 4.5 mm, the lobes slightly asymmetric, sublanceolate, carinate; petals white; ovary subellipsoid, trigonous, 6 mm long, 3-4 mm in diameter, sparsely floccose-tomentellous, constricted at apex, attenuate toward base; ovules about 30 in each locule; seeds subovate, rounded at one end and acute at the other, 1.5 mm long, brown, longitudinally sulcate-rugulose.

description: Plant acaulescent, propagating by short erect axillary shoots. Leaves about 12 in a flat rosette; sheaths orbicular, inflated; blades linear-lanceolate, acuminate, distinctly narrowed at base but not petiolate, 30 cm long, 4 cm wide, thick and fleshy, strongly undulate-along the margin, subdensely serrulate, maroon above with wavy crossbars formed by coarse gray appressed scales, completely covered by such scales beneath. Inflorescence with primary bracts like reduced leaves but with longer apices and cordate bases; the central fascicles mostly 2-flowered, staminate, the outer fascicles of 3-4 perfect flowers. Floral bracts broadly ovate, about equaling the sepals, membranaceous. Sepals connate into a narrow tube 5 mm long, the free lobes 3 mm long, broadly ovate, apiculate, serrulate; petals white.

Inflorescence rather few-flowered but evidently compound. Floral bracts to 17 mm long, elliptic, sharply carinate, exceeding the ovary; flowers to 32 mm long. description: Plant caulescent; stem 15-70 cm long. Leaves all alike, 10-20 cm long, distinctly narrowed between sheath and blade; blades 3-4 cm wide, rigid, thick, undulate along the margins, minutely serrulate, glabrous or subglabrous above, pale-lepidote and obscurely striped beneath. Inflorescence rather many-flowered with 4-6 flowers in each fascicle. Floral bracts lanceolate, acute, much shorter than the flowers, carinate; flowers to 41 mm long. description: Plant caulescent or subacaulescent, propagating by rhizomes. Leaves about 20 in a spreading rosette, 5-15 cm long, distinctly petiolate; sheaths subtriangular, densely serrulate, glabrous above, sparsely pale-lepidote beneath; petioles 3-8 cm long, 5-9 mm wide, channeled, brown; blades broadly lance-ovate, acuminate, rounded or broadly acute at base, 8-13 cm long, 4-5 cm wide, laxly serrulate, whitish, tinged with rose and spotted with green, glabrous above, covered beneath with a pale membrane of fused scales. Inflorescence few-flowered; primary bracts subfoliaceous, serrulate. Floral bracts lanceolate, acuminate, slightly exceeding the ovary, serrulate, carinate, membranaceous; flowers 25-30 mm long. Sepals about 11 mm long, more than half connate, the free lobes subsymmetric, lanceolate, acuminate, carinate, soon glabrous, green; petals whitish or slightly green, spreading at anthesis and disclosing the stamens; ovary cylindric, 8 mm long; ovules few.

description: Plant flowering nearly 40 cm high; stem elongate, branching, 10-15 mm in diameter including the leaf-sheaths. Leaves covering the stem, to 40 cm long, smooth, glabrous, and green above, covered beneath with a white membrane of fused scales and strongly nerved, slightly wider than the blades; blades arched-recurving, narrowly triangular, long-attenuate, not at all narrowed toward base, 12-20 mm wide, channeled, laxly serrate with slender curved spines 1.5 mm long. Inflorescence terminal, sessile, few-flowered. Floral bracts broadly elliptic, acute, exceeding the ovary, ecarinate, membranaceous, sparsely lepidote; flowers sessile, the outer perfect, the inner staminate. Sepals 10 mm long, somewhat connate, membranaceous, densely white-lepidote, the lobes elliptic, broadly acute but not mucronulate; petals linear, obtuse, 3 cm long, highly conglutinate, white; stamens and style included; pollen globose, even; ovary ellipsoid, 5 mm long.

description: Slender, wiry or virgate, to stout, erect shrub 0.2-1 m tall; mature stems terete, glabrous; bark smooth and lustrous, or cracking reticulately; twigs terete to subterete, short-white pilose, glabrate, or very rarely glabrous. Leaves in whorls of 4, imbricate, ± appressed or more commonly spreading, elliptic to linear-elliptic, or ± oblong, 3.5-8 × 1.2-2.2(-2.5) mm, base tapering, broadly cuneate, short-decurrent, apex blunt to acute (keeled), mucronate with a deciduous, translucent, glandular or eglandular seta 0.3-0.8(-1.3) mm long, apparent margin usually minutely ciliate over entire length, also ± pectinate with few to many, deciduous, translucent, (branched) setae 0.8-2.2 mm long, these usually tipped with deciduous, minutely spherical to cylindric, reddish glands, otherwise lamina glabrous and nitid to densely puberulous, or short-pilose all over and then glabrate; petiole subterete, puberulent above, 1-2 mm long, ciliate (Fig. 2A-E). Inflorescence axillary, flowers 4-7 clustered at tips; floral bract leaf-like in all aspects; pedicel terete, striate, (10-)15-22(-50) mm long, densely short-white-pilose (glabrous), also usually densely glandular-hispid with setae often of varying lengths to 1.3 mm long (eglandular), setae also often minutely pilose at base (bifid to thinly-branched at apex); bracteoles leaf-like but 4-5 mm long. Flowers (5-)6(-7)-merous; calyx 4.5-10 mm long, lobes spreading, flat to keeled, ovate to linear-ovate, 4-9 mm long, long-acuminate, long-mucronate, densely puberulent to short-pilose all over including inner surface, also moderately to densely glandular-hispid at margin and dorsally with trichomes to 1.2(-2) mm long (eglandular); petals erect or spreading and then corolla ± campanulate (imbricate, then corolla ± campanulate-urceolate), obovate, rarely oblong-obelliptic, ca. 10-16 × (4-)5-12 mm, rounded or rarely obtuse, margin conspicuously erose (entire), scarlet to brick-red (salmon-red) when fresh, glabrous (puberulent within); stamens 5-7 mm long; filaments 2.5-5.5 mm long; anthers 2.5-3(-4) mm long; ovary glabrous to weakly puberulent; style usually verrucose at base, 2.5-3 mm long, glabrous. Capsule ovoid to globose, 6-7(-9) × 5-6 mm.

description: Rhizomatous, decumbent, spreading to erect subshrub, 0.1-0.3(-0.5) m tall; mature stems subterete to terete, glabrous; bark ± smooth but coarsely cracking reticulately; twigs subterete, striate, glabrous. Leaves opposite to subopposite, imbricate, bases often equitant, appressed and usually restricted to tips of twigs, linear-oblong, 6-11 × 1-1.3 mm, base tapering imperceptibly into petiole, apex acute, mucronate into a long, translucent seta to ca. 0.8 mm long, actual margins usually not converging or overlapping but forming two parallel lines along the length of the leaf beneath (converging and then contiguous close to apex), apparent margins pectinate with sharp, translucent, eglandular (minutely glandular) setae to ca. 0.5 mm long with basal ones sometimes thinner and more ciliate, then branched, otherwise lamina glabrous; petiole barely distinguishable from lamina, but ca. 1-1.5 mm long, ciliate (Fig. 2F-G). Inflorescence axillary, flowers solitary; floral bract leaf-like in all aspects; pedicels subterete, ribbed to striate, (12-) 15-30 mm long, glabrous to weakly puberulent, also moderately to densely glandular-hispid (eglandular) with hairs to 1.8 mm long; bracteoles leaf-like but 2.5-6.0 mm long. Flowers 6-merous; calyx 5.5-8 mm long, lobes wide-spreading, linear-ovate, 5-7.5 mm long, acuminate, glandular-hispid dorsally and at margin and apex (eglandular); petals wide-spreading (corolla rotate), oblong-elliptic to obovate, 8-12 × 4-7 mm, rounded to obtuse, scarlet (or rose-salmon) when fresh, glabrous; stamens 6-8(-10) mm long; filaments 5.2-7(-9) mm long; anthers 1.8-2.5 mm long; ovary glabrous; style 2.3-3 mm long, glabrous. Capsule ovoid-globose, 5-6 mm diam.
