description: Shrub to tree to 12 m tall, to 40 cm dbh, much-branched tree, with straight trunk, with small buttresses; bark grayish. Leafy branchlets glabrous, terete; older branches rugose, grayish to pale brown; lenticels sparse. Stipules narrowly triangular, glabrous outside, glabrous and with few colleters inside, 28-37 × 7-9 mm, reddish green, readily caducous, leaving a linear scar, ca. 0.5 mm wide, of the same color of the stem. Leaves 25-31 × 13-16 cm, LAV 1.6:1 to 1.7:1; broadly elliptic to broadly obovate, acute to rounded (BA = 30-45°) at base, obtuse and short-acuminate at apex; the acumen to 1 cm long; blade pale green above, yellowish green below, semi-coriaceous; drying pale green, semi-leathery; glabrous above and below; pellucid punctate; primary and secondary veins glabrous, prominent below; secondary veins 16-21 each side; tertiary veins starting subparallel and openly reticulate in the center, faintly evident above and below; petioles 2-3 cm long, 3-4.5 mm thick, adaxially narrow-concave to flattened, glabrous, basally thickened but not pulvinated; domatia absent. Inflorescences laxly paniculate, pyramidal, lateral branches decussate; 30-46 cm long, basal branches 22-30 cm long, lateral branches 6-8 pairs, basal portion of axis not branched 7-11 cm long; rachis terete, rachis and branches glabrous to minutely hirtellous; distal bracts 4-5 × 4-5 mm, deltoid; bracteoles subtending flowers 2-3 × 2-3 mm, deltoid, glabrous. Flowers pedicellate, pedicels 4-6 mm long, glabrous to minutely puberulent; hypanthium narrowly obconical, 4-6 × 2-3 mm, glabrous; flower buds cylindrical, pointed at apex. Calyx cupular with small lobes, membranous, glabrous, greenish white, 1.5-3 mm long; lobes 5, 1-2.5 × 1.5-2 mm, ciliolate. Corolla tubular with a basal constriction and reversed lobes, 1.5-1.9 cm long, white, semi-fleshy when fresh; tube subcylindrical with basal constriction, 5-6 × 2 mm, 3.5-4 mm wide at the orifice; glabrous, minutely verrucate outside; microscopically (40×) granulate inside, without a ring of hairs; lobes 5, 2/3 of corolla length, 9-11 × ca. 3 mm, narrowly triangular, reversed, glabrous, minutely verrucose outside, densely ascending short-strigose at base, minutely papillose throughout, microscopically (40×) papillose at margins inside. Stamens 5, fully exserted, subequal, attached 4-5 mm from the base of the tube; filaments ca. 3 mm long, flattened, widened at base, with a tuft of ascending strigose hairs (0.3-0.5 mm long); anthers cylindrical, subsagittate at base, rectilinear to slightly curved (not convex), 6.5-7 × ca. 1.5 mm, dorsifixed near the base, the thecae subequal at base, papillose throughout. Pollen exine densely foveolate (non-echinate). Style exserted, 16-20 mm long, glabrous; style branches ovate, 3-3.5 × 1-1.3 mm, stigmatic surface papillose. Capsules obovoid, apex obtusely hemispherical, 812 × 7-9 mm, without lenticels, glabrous throughout, dark-brown; dehiscing loculicidally, disk septicidal dehiscence absent even in old capsules. Seeds 2.25-2.9 × 0.65-0.75 mm.

description: Trunk mauve-brown to mauve-gray, to 15 m tall, ca. 34 cm diam. Leaves ca. 15, lowest leaves hanging well below the horizontal; crownshaft ca. 2 m long; petiole ca. 80 cm long; rachis 3.2-3.6 m long; middle segments 95-104 cm long and 3.7-4 cm wide. Inflorescence ca. 1.3 m long and 1 m wide; prophyll 40-42 cm long and 12-13 cm wide, peduncular bract ca. 1.2 m long, widest above middle, apex acuminate; rachillae 17-20 cm long and 1.4-2 mm diam. Staminate flowers violet, darker toward the base of the petals and filaments; sepals triangular, ca. 0.9 mm long and 1.2 mm wide; petals ovate, ca. 5.1 mm long and 2.9 mm wide; stamens 6, ca. 5.8 mm long; filaments awl-shaped, ca. 3.7 mm long; anthers ca. 3.7 mm long, purple; pistillode minute. Pistillate flowers violet, 2-2.5 per cm; sepals reniform, ca. 1.2 mm long and 3.3 mm wide; petals ovate, coriaceous, ca. 3 mm long; staminode shallowly 6-lobed, ca. 2.3 mm long, free for ca. 1.2 mm; gynoecium ca. 2.4 mm long and 2.5 mm diam. Fruits spheroid to ellipsoid, 12-13.7 mm long, 8.1-9 mm dorsiventral thickness, and 7.8-8.5 mm wide; epicarp brown to black, stigmatic scar plain; endocarp ellipsoid, fragile, 7.8-8.5 mm long, 5.9-6.6 mm dorsiventral thickness, and 6.2-6.5 mm wide; seed dorsiventrally compressed ellipsoid, 5.8-9.3 mm long, 4.3-5.3 mm dorsiventral thickness, and 5.3-6 mm wide; raphe circular. Eophyll linear-lanceolate, exstipitate, weakly costate.

description: Trunk gray-white, to 15 m tall. Leaves not seen; middle leaf segments 85-90 cm long and 4-4.8 cm wide. Inflorescence ca. 95 cm long; prophyll to 66 cm long; peduncular bract ca. 1.2 m long, apex acuminate; rachillae 23-27 cm long and 1.5 mm diam. Staminate flowers white; sepals triangular, ca. 1 mm long; petals ovate to oblong; stamens as long as petals; filaments awl-shaped, 4 mm long; anthers 2 mm long; pistillode minute. Pistillate flowers white, ca. 3.5 per cm; sepals reniform, 1-1.5 mm long and 2.5 mm wide; petals ovate, 3.5 mm long; staminode deeply 6-lobed, 3 mm long, free for 1.4 mm. Fruits ellipsoid, 9.8-10.5 mm long, 8.1-8.5 mm dorsiventral thickness, and 8.1-8.7 mm wide; epicarp black, stigmatic scar stellate and 6-pointed; endocarp spheroid to ellipsoid, 8.4-9 mm long, 6.6-6.8 mm dorsiventral thickness, and 6.2-6.8 mm wide; seed dorsiventrally compressed spheroid, 6.1-6.5 mm long, 3.9-4.6 mm dorsiventral thickness, and 5.2-5.8 mm wide; raphe circular. Eophyll not seen.

description: Trunk gray-white, to 20 m tall, 35-47 cm diam. and often ventricose. Leaves ca. 15, lowest leaves hanging well below the horizontal; crownshaft ca. 2 m long; petiole 0.2-0.7 m long; rachis 4-5.8 m long; middle segments 87-132 cm long and 2.5-4.5 cm wide. Inflorescence ca. 1 m long and 1 m wide; prophyll not seen; peduncular bract ca. 1.8 m long, widest at the middle, apex acuminate; rachillae puberulent, 14-31 cm long and 1-2.8 mm diam. Staminate flowers white; sepals reniform with acute apices, 0.7-1.5 mm long and 1.5-2.1 mm wide; petals ovate, 4.7-Ó.4 mm long and 2.9-4.2 mm wide; stamens 6(-10), 4.1-12 mm long, filaments awlshaped, 4-5.4 mm long, anthers 2.7-4.5 mm long, pistillode minute. Fruits ellipsoid, 11.3-14 mm long, 9.2-11.2 mm dorsiventral thickness, and 8.8-11.1 mm wide; epicarp black, stigmatic scar plain; endocarp spheroid to ellipsoid, hard and durable, 9.1-12.2 mm long, 7-9.2 mm dorsiventral thickness, and 7.4-8.6 mm wide; seed dorsiventrally compressed spheroid, 7.9-9.9 mm long, 5.6-6.7 mm dorsiventral thickness, and 6.6-1.1 mm wide; raphe circular. Eophyll linear-lanceolate, weakly stipitate or exstipitate, costate.

description: Trunk gray-white, to 20 m tall, ca. 38 cm diam. Inflorescence ca. 1 m long and 1 m wide; prophyll not seen; peduncular bract ca. 2 m long, narrowly acuminate, as long as the crownshaft, widest in the middle; rachillae ca. 37 cm long and 1-1.3 mm diam., stiff. description: Trunk gray-brown to cinnamon-brown, to 15 m tall, 26.2-47. cm diam. description: Stems cespitose with 3-6 stems, rarely solitary, sometimes procumbent and partly subterranean, 1.4-3.5 m tall, 2-5 cm diam., brown or green, with nodulated roots visible at base. Leaves 4-10, arching; sheath open and not forming a crownshaft, 17-27 (-774) cm long, persistent, with brown scales, fibrous on margins, the ligule short or absent; petiole 0.3-1 m long, densely covered with closely appressed, brown hairs, glabrescent; rachis 0.5-1.8 m long, with hairs like those of petiole, glabrescent; pinnae 8-20 per side, regularly arranged and spreading in one plane, subopposite, elliptic or subsigmoid, contracted proximally and distally, distally abruptly and asymmetrically long apiculate, the filiform apex to 10 cm long, the apical pinna irregularly bifid, ± glabrous abaxially, with prominent midvein and several, obscure lateral veins, with thin and inconspicuous ramenta on midvein abaxially; basal pinna 18-32 x 1.8-4 cm; middle pinnae 19-54 x 2.5-8 cm; apical pinna 19-24 x 1.8-4 cm. Inflorescences corymbose, interfoliar, arching, spicate or branched; peduncle 6-50 cm long, 2-7 mm diam., terete, with scattered brown scales or pubescent with soft pale hairs, glabrescent; prophyll (1.2-)4.5-22 cm long, 1.1-2.5 cm diam., glabrous or with scales or hairs; peduncular bract (9-)29-90 cm long, including a 1 cm long umbo, 1-2 cm diam. at middle, covered with appressed, light-brown scales, persistent; rachis 2.5-15 cm long (absent if inflorescence spicate), with stellate, white hairs; rachillae 1-11, 8-32 (-47) cm long, all ± equal in length, ca. 2 mm diam. at anthesis, thickening to ca. 3 mm diam. in fruit, glabrous or with simple to furcate, substellate or stellate, 0.1 mm long, white hairs; flowers in triads almost to apex of rachillae, white at anthesis, the triads very close together, ± sunken in the rachillae; triad bracteole rounded; first flower bracteole obscure, second and third flower bracteoles ± equal, apiculate, 0.3 mm long; staminate flowers 2-4 mm long, sessile or on short flattened pedicels; sepals deltate, 1-1.5 mm long, gibbous, ciliate; petals triangular, 2-4 mm long, glabrous or with tuft of white hairs at apex; stamens arranged on a short receptacle; filaments 1-3 mm long, flattened, adnate proximally to petals; anthers 0.8-2 mm long, oblong; pistillode 1-2 mm long, deeply trifid at apex; pistillate flowers 2.5-3 mm long; sepals very widely ovate, 2 mm long, fleshy, minutely ciliate, glabrous or with white hairs abaxially; petals very widely ovate, 2 mm long, not fleshy; staminodes digitate; fruits globose, 0.8-1 cm diam., stigmatic remains lateral; epicarp black, glabrous or minutely tuberculate; seeds globose, 6-7 mm diam.; endosperm lightly (then almost homogeneous) to deeply ruminate; eophyll not seen.

description: Stems 0.5-3 m tall, 2-5 cm diam. Leaves pinnate; apical pinna 12-40 x 2.5-6 cm, usually wider than the other pinnae. description: Stems cespitose with 1 or 2 well-developed stems, or occasionally appearing solitary and then with basal shoots, 0.5-4 m tall, 3-4(-10) cm diam., brown, occasionally procumbent. Leaves 3-6(-10), spreading, regularly pinnate or occasionally simple; sheath open and not forming a crownshaft, somewhat persistent, 30-60 cm long including a ligule to 5 cm long, reddish, fibrous distally at margins; petiole (0.3-)0.9-2.5 m long, ± terete, densely covered with appressed, peltate-lacerate scales, glabrescent, or glabrous; rachis 1-2.4 m (22-48 cm in simple leaves) long, with scales like those of petiole; pinnae (on pinnate leaves) 13-36(-54) on each side, regularly arranged and horizontally spreading in the same plane, subopposite or alternate, linear-lanceolate, aristate, with prominent midvein and lateral veins, midvein lacking scales abaxially, with punctations abaxially, basal pinna 32-60 x (0.2-)1-1.5 cm; middle pinnae 35-70(-90) x 2-4.5(-6) cm; apical pinna 17-35 x 1-4 cm; simple leaves obovate, 38-87 cm long, 20-28 cm wide, bifid apically, with 16-20 main veins per side. Inflorescences racemose, interfoliar, erect in bud and at anthesis, arching in fruit; peduncle (0.4-)0.8-1.4 m long, 4-10(-20) mm diam., terete; prophyll 18-55 cm long, 1.5-5 cm wide; peduncular bract (0.6-)1-2.2 m long including a 5-6 cm long umbo, persistent; rachis 18-66 cm long, densely to moderately covered with reddish brown, branched hairs; rachillae (7-)21-59 (-101), 8.5-27 cm long proximally, 4-10 cm long distally, ca. 1 mm diam. at anthesis, 1.5-1.7 mm diam. in fruit, slightly zig-zag, angular and almost rectangular in cross section, tending to be distichously arranged, especially distally, densely to moderately covered with clusters of reddish brown, branched hairs (occasionally glabrous); flowers in triads on proximal ca. 1/2 rachillae, paired or solitary staminate distally, the triads tending to distichously arranged on the rachillae; triad bracteole low, rounded to prominent, deltate, to 1 mm long; first flower bracteole obscure,  second and third bracteoles ± equal, rounded, 0.5 mm long; staminate flowers 3.5-5.5 mm long; sepals triangular, 1-1.5 mm long, keeled; petals ovate, 2.5-5 mm long; stamens arranged on a short receptacle; filaments 1.5 mm long, linear, flattened; anthers 1-2 mm long; pistillode 0.5-1 mm long, trifid at apex; pistillate flowers 2-3.5 mm long; sepals widely ovate, 1.5-2 mm long, fleshy; petals triangular, 1-3.5 mm long; staminodes digitate; fruits globose, 0.7-1 cm diam., the stigmatic remains lateral; epicarp purple-black, minutely tuberculate; seeds globose; endosperm ruminate; eophyll bifid.

description: Tree; young shoots subglabrous or finely appressed puberulous, becoming greyish or greyish-buff, smooth, usually lenticellate. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged to subopposite, 5.8-17.5 × 3.68 cm, broadly oblong, elliptic or obovate, apex rounded or truncate, base shortly attenuate, margin often revolute, coriaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower surface often slightly glaucous, glabrous or with minute scattered appressed hairs; venation eucamptodromous to brochidodromous, usually with a marginal vein, midrib usually slightly raised, but recessed on upper surface, secondary veins 7-13 pairs, widely spreading, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate, slightly impressed in the upper surface; intersecondaries moderate to long; tertiaries obscured. Petiole 1-3 cm long, not or only slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 2-7-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 4-6 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals 5-6, 5-6 mm long, broadly ovate or elliptic, apex acute or obtuse, appressed puberulous outside, sparsely appressed puberulous inside. Corolla cyathiform to shortly tubular, 5.5-6.5	mm long, tube 3.5-5 mm long, lobes 5-6, 1.5-2.5 mm long, triangular, apex acute, finely appressed puberulous outside on tube and lower part of lobes, glabrous inside. Stamens 5-6, fixed in the lower half of the corolla tube; filaments 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous; stamens absent in female. Staminodes absent. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid or conical, 2-4-locular, appressed puberulous; style 1.5-2.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous above; style-head simple. Fruit 3-3.2 cm long, globose (sometimes oblate when immature), smooth, finely appressed puberulous to glabrous. Seeds 1-2, ca. 2.1 cm long, ellipsoid, rounded at both ends, slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, almost full-length, oblong-elliptic, ca. 9 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent.  Field characters. Tree to 32 m high and 60 cm diam, with steep buttresses and pale grey to grey-brown vertically cracked bark which peels in irregular plates, slash streaked with orange, exuding a small amount of white latex; flowers greenish- or yellowish-tan, fruit maturing yellow. Flowering Sep-Oct, fruit maturing Feb-May. Local name. Chuponcillo (Venezuela). Relationships. Pouteria ambelaniifolia is characterized by the broad leaves with rounded or truncate apex, few widely spreading secondary veins, large flowers (corolla larger than any other species of this section), the globose or oblate fruit, and seed with relatively broad scar. Although the number of ovary locules varies from two to four (other species of this section are almost uniformly bilocular), it is placed confidently in this section due to the similar vegetative facies and floral structure, including lack of staminodes. It also belongs in this section on wood anatomical grounds (Kukachka, 1979e).

description: Tree; young shoots minutely appressed puberulous, soon glabrous, greyish, smooth or finely cracked, lenticellate. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 7-12.5 × 2.4-4.8(-6) cm, elliptic or oblanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate or acuminate, base narrowly attenuate, thinly coriaceous, glabrous or sometimes with some minute appressed hairs persisting on the lower surface; venation eucamptodromous, marginal vein usually present, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 10-12 pairs, slightly convergent, arcuate; intersecondaries moderately long or absent; tertiaries finely reticulate, rather conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 0.7-1.5 cm long, flat, not channelled, broadened by the decurrent leaf base, subglabrous. Fascicles axillary and clustered on short leafless axillary shoots 1-2 cm long, 3-7-flowered. Pedicel 2-4 mm long, with some minute appressed hairs. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) or apparently bisexual. Sepals 4-5, 1.25-1.5 mm long, ovate, apex acute to rounded, appressed puberulous on both surfaces. Corolla 1.75-2 mm long, tube equalling the lobes; lobes 4-5, ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, usually with sparse appressed hairs on the outside of the tube. Stamens 4-5, fixed at or near the top of the corolla tube; filaments 0.3-0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.3-0.6 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous, absent in female flowers. Staminodes 4-5, 0.5-0.75 mm long, lanceolate-subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary conical (flattened in male (?) flowers), bilocular, puberulous; style 0.5-0.6 mm long after anthesis, included, puberulous or glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit solitary or paired on stout stalks 1-2 cm long, ca. 4 × 2.3-2.5 cm, ellipsoid, apex rounded, base acute, hard-skinned, rough, finely and sometimes prominently lenticellate, glabrous. Seed solitary, 2.5-2.8 cm long, ellipsoid, rounded both ends, slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, sometimes extending round the base, 4-6 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 45 m high and 120 cm diam. with small buttresses and fluted bole. Bark brown, scaling, latex white, abundant to scarce. The leaf undersurface is slightly glaucous. Flowers greenish-cream, fruit rather woody, ripening yellowish-brown. Flowering mostly Nov to Mar, with a few records in Jui, fruiting Mar to May.

description: Tree; young shoots appressed puberulous with golden-brown indumentum, soon glabrous, pale greyish, slightly scaling, lenticellate. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 6-12 × 1.9-3.4 cm, oblong, elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, apex acute to shortly narrowly attenuate, base narrowly attenuate to rounded, thinly coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, marginal vein present, midrib flat or slightly convex on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-15 pairs, slightly convergent and arcuate; intersecondaries moderately long; tertiaries few, reticulate, not much stronger than the conspicuous areolate-reticulate quaternaries. Petiole 0.7-1.9 cm long, flat or slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 2-6-flowered, axillary and loosely clustered on leafless axillary shoots 1-2.5 cm long. Pedicel ca. 1 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals 4-5, 2-2.5 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse, sparsely appressed puberulous outside, sericeous inside, sometimes ciliate. Corolla shortly tubular, 2-3 mm long, tube ? about equalling the lobes, lobes 4-5, ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens 4-5, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments 0.3-0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.6 mm long, broadly lanceolate, glabrous; absent in female. Staminodes 4-5, ca. 0.5 mm long, subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary broadly ovoid, 4-5-locular, densely long-pubescent; style ca. 2 mm long, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 3-3.5 cm long, narrowly or broadly ellipsoid, apex and base acute to obtuse, smooth, thin-walled (shrinking on drying), glabrous. Seed solitary, ca. 2 cm long, oblong-ellipsoid, rounded at base and apex, testa smooth, shining, 0.3-0.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length, 1-1.2 cm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Tree to 35 m high and 65 cm diam. with rough bark; slash reddish, with scant white sap. Flowers cream-coloured, fruit green. Flowering and fruiting Apr to Jun and Sep.

description: Tree; young shoots minutely sericeous-puberulous at first, soon glabrous, dark grey or black, smooth, with dense small lenticels. Leaves loosely clustered,spirally arranged, 6.5-15 × 1.8-5 cm, narrowly elliptic or oblong, apex and base narrowly attenuate, chartaceous, glabrous, drying dark brown or black; venation brochidodromous, thin marginal vein present, secondary veins joining to form a submarginal vein, midrib slightly raised on upper surface, secondary veins 15-20 pairs, parallel or slightly convergent, slightly arcuate, slightly raised on upper surface; intersecondaries long, often extending to near margin; tertiaries reticulate and some horizontal. Petiole 5-8 mm long, slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 2-7-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 3-6 mm long, with sparse minute appressed indumentum or glabrous. Sepals five, 2-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate, apex rounded, glabrous outside, sericeous inside, inner ones ciliate. Corolla broadly tubular, 2-3.5 mm long, tube equalling the lobes, lobes five, ovate, apex truncate or rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed in the lower half of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 1.75 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, broadly lanceolate, apiculate, glabrous. Staminodes absent. Disk absent. Ovary tapering gradually to style, 3-5-locular, appressed puberulous; style ca. 2 mm long after anthesis, slightly exserted, appressed puberulous in lower half; style-head minutely 3-5-lobed. Fruit 2-3 cm long, globose or ellipsoid, rounded at base and apex, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, 1.8-2 cm long, broadly ellipsoid, rounded or obtuse at base and apex, testa smooth, shining, 0.15-0.3 mm thick; scar adaxial, full length, 5-9 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons; radicle slightly exserted; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 35 m high and 55 cm diam with white latex. Flowers greenish-yellow, fruit maturing red. Flowering recorded Apr, Jun, Oct-Jan, mature fruit Feb-Apr and Aug.

description: Tree; young shoots glabrous, dark brown to greyish, becoming finely cracked and scaling, sometimes lenticellate. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 5.5-15(-l 9) × 2.5-6 cm, elliptic to oblanceolate, apex acute to narrowly attenuate, base narrowly attenuate, coriaceous, glabrous, lower surface usually minutely punctate; venation eucamptodromous, marginal vein present, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 7-11 pairs, convergent, arcuate; intersecondaries moderate to long; tertiaries conspicuous, parallel to the secondaries and reticulate. Petiole 0.5-1.8 cm long, slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 2-20 flowered, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves. Pedicel 2-6 mm long, with sparse minute appressed hairs or glabrous. Flowers unisexual and bisexual (functionally male?; plant apparently monoecious or dioecious. Sepals 4-5, 1-1.5 mm long, broadly ovate or suborbicular, apex rounded, sparsely appressed puberulous on both surfaces, or glabrous. Corolla 1.75-2.25 mm long, tube equalling or slightly longer than the lobes; lobes 4-5, ovate to suborbicular, apex obtuse, rounded or truncate, glabrous. Stamens 4-5, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 0.1 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.3-0.5 mm long, inflexed, ovate to lanceolate, glabrous; stamens absent in female flowers. Staminodes 4-5,0.3-0.4 mm long, ovate to subulate, glabrous, reduced to a vestige in female flowers. Disk absent. Ovary flattened (ovoid in female flowers), bilocular, puberulous, style 0.4-0.5 mm long after anthesis, included, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 2.5-6 cm long, ellipsoid or obovoid, apex rounded, base acute to obtuse or rounded, hard-skinned, smooth, glabrous. Seed 2-3.5 cm long, ellipsoid, laterally compressed, rounded at both ends, testa shining, nearly always wrinkled or verrucose, rarely smooth, 0.3-1 mm thick; scar full-length, adaxial, 2-4 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 35 m high and 40 cm diam., buttressed to 2 m high, slash exuding copious milky latex. Flowers greenish-yellow, fruit ripening orange-yellow. The cotyledons are reported to be purple (FDBG 4106). Flowering and fruiting throughout the year. The fruits are eaten by the monkey Cebus apella (Foster & Janson 8279, Peru).

description: Tree; young shoots sparsely and finely appressed puberulous or subglabrous, becoming pale brown, thinly scaling, with a few lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 8-15 × 3.5-6 cm, oblanceolate, apex obtusely cuspidate to shortly narrowly attenuate, base narrowly attenuate, chartaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-11 pairs, parallel or slightly convergent, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries fine, oblique; higher order reticulum visible with lens. Petiole 0.8-1.2 cm long, channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 2-6-flowered, axillary. Pedicel 3-6 mm long, finely appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals four, 3-4 mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, closely appressed puberulous on both surfaces, inner pair with a broad, glabrous margin and ciliate. Corolla tubular, 5.5-6 mm long, tube 3.5-4 mm long; lobes six, 1.5-2 mm long, oblong to lanceolate, apex obtuse to rounded, papillose. Stamens six, fixed near the apex of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 0.5 mm long, geniculate, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, broadly lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes six, ca. 1 mm long, linear-subulate, papillose. Disk absent. Ovary globose, (four-)six-locular, densely stiff-pubescent; style 3.5-4.5 mm long after anthesis, exserted or equalling the corolla, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 50 cm diam. with white latex. Flowers greenish white. Flowering Aug-Oct and Feb.

description: Tree; young shoots appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, greyish, cracked and fissured, sometimes lenticellate. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 9-20 × 3.8-7.2 cm, broadly oblanceolate, obovate or elliptic, apex obtuse or rounded, base acute or narrowly attenuate, often decurrent, coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 8-11 pairs, parallel or slightly convergent, arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries numerous, oblique to horizontal; quaternaries to right angles to the tertiaries. Petiole 0.5-1.5 cm long, slightly channeled, glabrous. Fascicles 1-3-flowered, mostly below the leaves. Pedicel 3-4 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals six, in a closely overlapping whorl, outer 2-3 mm long, inner ca. 6 mm long, broadly ovate or suborbicular or broader than long, apex rounded, emarginate or deeply divided, appressed puberulous on both surfaces, except for sometimes glabrous margin, sometimes ciliate. Corolla broadly tubular, expanded at the apex, 1.1-1.3 cm long, tube 7-9 mm long, lobes five, ca. 4 mm long, broadly oblong to suborbicular, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments 1.5-2.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 1 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, 2.5-3 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary broadly ovoid, (four-)five-locular, densely pubescent; style 0.8-1 cm long after anthesis, slightly exserted, glabrous; style-head simple or minutely lobed. Fruit 3.5-4.7(-6) cm long, globose, apex and base rounded, rough-skinned with dense scaly lenticels, glabrous. Seed solitary, 2.5-2.8 cm long, globose, rounded at base and apex, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.5 mm thick; scar covering one-third to two-thirds of the seed surface; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 70 cm diam., trunk sometimes fluted near the base; bark granular, reddish-brown, with copious sticky white latex. Flowers scented, greenish-yellowish-white, fruit pale brown. Flowering Dec-Apr and Jul, apparently bearing fruit throughout the year.

description: Tree, young shoots ferruginous-tomentose, indumentum persistent, becoming longitudinally cracked and scaling, without lenticels. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 18-30 × 5.5-11 cm, oblanceolate to broadly oblanceolate, apex rounded, sometimes shortly and obtusely cuspidate, base acute to narrowly cuneate, bullate, chartaceous, upper surface glabrous or midrib tomentose, lower surface tomentose on midrib and secondary veins, uniformly pubescent on lamina with erect stalked two-branched hairs; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly raised but recessed on the upper surface, secondary veins 18-20 pairs, slightly convergent or parallel, arcuate; intersecondaries short; tertiaries oblique; quaternaries mostly at right angles to the tertiaries; venation strongly raised on the lower surface. Petiole 1.8-2.2 cm long, not channelled, densely tomentose. Fascicles 3-5-flowered, below the leaves. Pedicel 3-4 mm long, tomentose. Flowers bisexual. Sepals four, ca. 5 mm long, broadly elliptic or ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, outer two densely tomentose outside, inner two appressed puberulous outside, all glabrous inside. Corolla broadly tubular, ca. 7 mm long, tube ca. 4.5 mm long, lobes four, ca. 2.5	mm long, broadly oblong, apex rounded, glabrous, fringed-ciliate. Stamens four, fixed about two-thirds up the corolla tube; filaments ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 2 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes four, ca. 1.5 mm long, narrowly oblong, fringed ciliate. Disk absent. Ovary conical, four-locular, densely long-strigose; style ca. 4 mm long after anthesis, included, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit ca. 5 cm long, ellipsoid, apex and base obtuse, smooth to slightly verrucose, densely tomentose. Seed solitary, ca. 3 cm long, ellipsoid, rounded at both ends, slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.4-0.6 mm thick; scar adaxial and extending around the base, ca. 1 cm wide near the apex, gradually tapering to the base; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 15 m high and 20 cm diam. with white latex. Flowers greenish-white, fruit maturing yellow. Flowers and fruit in Nov.

description: Tree; young shoots shortly pubescent at first, soon glabrous, becoming greyish-brown, cracked and fissured, roughened with numerous leaf and inflorescence scars, without lenticels. Leaves spirally arranged, 10-28 × 3-10 cm, oblanceolate, apex acute to rounded, base tapering, finally acute or rounded, coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat or slightly raised on upper surface, secondary veins 11-14 pairs, ascending, parallel or slightly convergent, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries few, short or long; tertiaries obscure; fine areolate reticulum present. Petiole 1.5-3 cm long, channelled at the apex, shortly appressed pubescent. Fascicles few-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Flowers sessile. Sepals five, 4-5 mm long, strongly imbricate, ovate to lanceolate, apex acute or obtuse, appressed pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Corolla (not seen, description from Kuhlmann) cylindrical, 6-7 mm long, lobes five, ovate-oblong, glabrous. Stamens five, ? fixed in middle of corolla tube (see note below); anthers ovate-cordate. Staminodes five, equalling the stamens, lanceolate-subulate. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, densely pubescent; style ca. 4 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 4-5 × 3.5-4 cm, ellipsoid or ovoid, apex and base rounded, minutely verruculose, glabrous. Seeds 1-3, 3-3.5 cm long, narrowly obovoid, sometimes plano-convex or shaped like the segment of an orange, apex obtuse to rounded, base acute to obtuse, testa smooth, shining, 0.75-2 mm thick; scar adaxial, full length, 0.5-1 cm wide, often tapering from above halfway to the base; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle exserted ca 2 mm; endosperm absent. Field characters. Large tree with reddish bark; slash smelling strongly of almonds. Flowering May, mature fruit Oct.

description: Tree; young shoots glabrous to coarsely pubescent, soon glabrous, pale greyish-white to dark brown, scaling, usually without lenticels. Leaves loosely clustered or spaced, spirally arranged, (3-)5-18(-25) × 1.7-5(-8) cm, oblanceolate or elliptic, apex narrowly attenuate, rarely acute or rounded, base narrowly attenuate or acute, sometimes decurrent, usually chartaceous, usually glabrous, rarely shortly pubescent; venation usually eucamptodromous, less frequently brochidodromous, marginal vein present, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 8-13(-16) pairs, nearly always convergent and arcuate; intersecondaries short or well-developed, or absent; tertiaries few, oblique to reticulate; fine quaternary reticulum conspicuous on lower surface (lens). Petiole (0.2-)0.5-1.5(-2.3) cm long, usually not channelled, usually glabrous, less frequently shortly pubescent. Fascicles l-3(-5)-flowered, axillary and below the leaves, sometimes densely clustered. Pedicel 0-2 mm long, appressed puberulous to glabrous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals four, 3-5.5 mm long, broadly ovate or elliptic, apex acute to obtuse, sparsely strigose outside, or outer pair glabrous, all glabrous inside. Corolla tubular, usually swollen at the middle, 4-7.5 mm long, tube 3-5 mm long, lobes four, 1.5-2.5 mm long, broadly oblong to suborbicular, apex rounded or truncate, usually ciliate. Stamens four, fused about halfway up the corolla tube or slightly lower; filaments 2-3 mm long, traces often visible to base of corolla tube, glabrous; anthers 0.5-1.3 mm long, broadly lanceolate to ovate, sometimes apiculate, glabrous. Staminodes four, 1-1.5 mm long, narrowly lanceolate or subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary shortly ovoid, four-locular, densely long-strigose; style 3.5-8.5 mm long after anthesis, usually slightly exserted, glabrous; style-head simple or minutely lobed. Fruit 2.7-7.5 cm long, narrowly ellipsoid, ovoid or globose, apex acute to rounded, base rounded to truncate, smooth, pubescent, velutinous or glabrous. Seeds 1-4, 1.5-5 cm long, oblong to ellipsoid, often slightly laterally compressed, base and apex usually rounded or obtuse, testa smooth, usually glossy, 0.3-1 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length, 1-6 mm wide (often broader in cultivated strains with large seeds); embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent.  Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 50 cm diam., but usually fertile when much smaller. Trunk of larger specimens fluted, bark dark reddish-brown to greyish-brown, scaling and shallowly fissured; slash cream with scanty white latex. Flowers pale green, with slight scent, fruit maturing yellow with whitish translucent flesh. Flowering throughout most of its range, (except in coastal Brazil) Aug-Nov, with the great majority in Sep; in coastal Brazil flowering occurs Dec to Jan. It is not clear whether there is a well defined season for mature fruit, as fruit at all stages of development can be found throughout the year.

description: Tree, young shoots finely appressed puberulous with golden hairs, indumentum persistent, twigs striate, pale brown, usually with some lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 18-35 × 7-11 cm, usually broadly oblanceolate, less frequently elliptic, apex narrowly attenuate or obtuse and finally long acuminate, base long-tapering, finally narrowly attenuate or cuneate, margin slightly revolute, coriaceous, upper surface glabrous, except for residual indumentum on the midrib, lower surface pale or golden appressed-puberulous, indumentum persisting; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 12-22 pairs, parallel or slightly convergent, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries few, oblique; fine quaternary areolate network visible on the upper surface. Petiole 2-3 cm long, not channelled, appressed puberulous. Fascicles 15-20-flowered, axillary. Pedicel 6-9 mm long, appressed-puberulous. Flowers ? bisexual. Sepals five, ca. 1.5 mm long, broadly ovate or suborbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, spreading widely, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside, ciliate. Corolla (immature bud) ca. 1.5 mm long, tube ca. 0.5 mm long, lobes five, ca. 1.5 mm long, broadly ovate, apex rounded, glabrous, ciliate. Stamens five, fixed near the top of the corolla tube, filaments ca. 0.3 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 0.6 mm long, lanceolate-subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, longitudinally ribbed, unilocular; style ca. 0.5 mm long, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 3-3.5 cm long, ellipsoid, apex obtuse or rounded, base obtuse, leathery-fleshy, smooth, sparsely and finely appressed puberulous. Seed solitary, ca. 2.5 cm long, ellipsoid, apex acute, base rounded, not laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.5-1 mm thick; scar adaxial, full length, 1-1.1 cm broad, embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons; radicle extending to the surface. Field characters. Tree to 20 m high and 40 cm diam. with short buttresses and slightly fluted bole. Bark greyish-brown, shallowly fissured or cracked; slash pink, with some white latex. The lower surface of the leaves is pale or greyish-green. Flowers creamy yellow, fruit maturing pale green, with copious latex in the pericarp. Flowering Aug to Oct, fruit maturing Feb to Apr.

description: Tree; young shoots finely sericeous, soon glabrous, greyish-brown, finely cracked, lenticellate. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 7.9-25(-33) × 2.7-7(-15) cm, narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate, acute or rounded, base narrowly attenuate or cuneate, chartaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib raised on the upper surface, thin marginal vein usually visible, secondary veins 9-18 pairs, parallel or slightly convergent, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries usually absent; tertiaries oblique, and finer lower order reticulum present. Petiole 1-2.5(-4.5) cm long, not channelled, finely appressed puberulous. Fascicles 2-3-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 0.81.1 cm long, finely appressed puberulous. Flowers ? unisexual (see note below). Sepals 5-6, 0.45-1.1 cm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, finely sericeous outside, glabrous inside, usually ciliate. Corolla cylindrical 0.75-1.35 cm long, tube exceeding the lobes, 57, oblong, apex rounded or truncate, usually with scattered appressed hairs outside, glabrous inside, papillose. Stamens 5-7, fixed at the top or in the upper half of the corolla tube; filaments 1.5-2.5 mm long, geniculate at apex, glabrous; anthers 1.25-2 mm long, oblong-lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes 5-7, 2-4 mm long, subulate, papillose. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid to conical, 5-7-locular, pubescent; style 0.35-1 cm long after anthesis, exserted in bud and open flower, glabrous; style-head simple or capitate. Fruit 2.5-7 cm long, ellipsoid to subglobose, apex obtuse to shortly rostrate, base tapering or obtuse, smooth, glabrous, or with residual pubescence near base. Seed 1-6, 2-3.8 cm long, ellipsoid or shaped like the segment of an orange, apex and base acute or obtuse, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length, width dependent on the number of seeds in the fruit, but usually broad and often equalling the width of the seed; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 25 m high and 50 cm diam., but often flowering at less than 10 m high. Larger specimens are buttressed, and sometimes with a slightly fluted bole. Bark greyish to dark brown, finely fissured and scaling in small thin longitudinal strips; slash pinkish-cream, exuding copious white sticky latex. Branches in younger specimens often in whorls of 3-4; sympodial branching conspicuous. Flowers pale green, scented; fruit maturing orange, yellow or dark green, with yellow pulp and plentiful white latex. Flowering mostly Dec to Jun throughout the range, with fruit maturing Mar to Oct.

description: Tree; young shoots shortly tomentose at first with crisped ferruginous hairs, becoming greyish-brown, soon glabrous, smooth or finely cracked, lenticellate or not. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 8.8-17 × 3.6-7 cm, oblanceolate or oblanceolate-elliptic, apex obtuse, obtusely cuspidate, rounded, or slightly emarginate, base narrowly attenuate, margin often revolute, coriaceous, densely tomentose at first with ferruginous, scurfy, crisped hairs, soon glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, thick marginal vein, secondary veins 7-11 pairs, parallel, straight or arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique to horizontal, obscure. Petiole 1.3-2.5 cm long, not channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 2-8-flowered, axillary and clustered below the leaves. Pedicel 0.5-1 cm long, densely ferruginous crisped-pubescent. Flowers unisexual (?) (see note below). Sepals five, ca. 5 mm long, broadly ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, densely ferruginous crisped-pubescent outside, pubescent or glabrous inside. Corolla shortly and broadly tubular, ca. 6.5 mm long, tube 2.5-3 mm long, lobes five, ca. 3.5 mm long, broadly ovate, apex obtuse, auriculate, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed in the upper half of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 2 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 2 mm long, lanceolate, apiculate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 3 mm long, lanceolate, carnose, glabrous. Disk a densely pubescent annulus surrounding the ovary. Ovary sunken in disk, five-locular, densely long-pubescent; style ca. 3 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit ca. 3.5 × 2 cm, ellipsoid, apex rounded or truncate, base tapered, smooth or slightly warty, glabrous or with some residual indumentum around the base. Seed solitary, 2.3-2.5 cm long, ellipsoid, laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, adherent to pericarp, 0.75-1 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length or nearly so, 2-4 mm wide; embryo with thin foliaceous free cotyledons, radicle exserted ca. 2.5 mm; endosperm present, about equalling the cotyledons in thickness. Field characters. Tree to 46 m high and 1 m diam., with steep, rounded, branched buttresses to 2 m high. Trunk fluted or cylindrical. Bark brown to dark grey, slightly vertically cracked and scaling, and becoming dappled, slash pinkish or straw coloured, exuding abundant sticky white latex. Flowers cream-coloured, fruit yellow, with a tough pinkish outer pericarp; the inner 3-4 mm of pericarp is transparent, gelatinous and adheres to the smooth seed. Flowering recorded sporadically throughout the year, fruit in Oct and Nov.

description: Tree; young shoots glabrous, pale greyish-buff, becoming slightly thin-scaly, lenticellate. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 8.1-15 × 4.1-6 cm, oblong-elliptic or elliptic, apex obtusely cuspidate to shortly narrowly attenuate, base rounded or obtuse to shortly narrowly attenuate, coriaceous, glabrous, venation eucamptodromous, marginal vein present, midrib flat or slightly raised in the upper surface, secondary veins 8-11 pairs, slightly convergent and arcuate; intersecondaries moderately long; tertiaries open reticulate tending to horizontal. Petiole 0.8-1.5 cm long, not or only slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 2-10-flowered, axillary. Pedicel ca. 2 mm long, bearing 1-2 small bracts, sparsely appressed, puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, ca. 2.5 mm long, ovate to suborbicular, apex rounded, appressed puberulous on both surfaces. Corolla (young), shortly tubular, ca. 2.5 mm long, tube equalling or slightly longer than the lobes, lobes six, ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens six, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 0.4 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.5 mm long, ovate-lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes six, ca. 0.75 mm long, subulate, sometimes bearing vestigial anthers, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary broadly ovoid, five-locular, long-pubescent; style ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 3.2-3.6 cm long, obovoid, apex obtuse or rounded, base tapered, smooth, thin-walled (shrinking on drying), glabrous or with some residual appressed indumentum near the base. Seed solitary, 2-2.5 cm long, broadly ellipsoid, rounded at base and apex, testa adherent to the pericarp, smooth to the naked eye, but minutely pitted and honeycombed under a lens, ca. 0.5 mm thick, scar adaxial and extending around the base, 7-8 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 75 cm diam. with high buttresses; slash with sticky which latex. Fruit maturing greenish-yellow. Flowering and fruiting in Feb.

description: Tree, young shoots not seen, larger twigs rough, scaling, greyish-brown, with prominent leaf and inflorescence scars. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 34-41 × 12-15.5 cm, broadly oblanceolate, apex obtuse, base long narrowly attenuate, thinly coriaceous, glabrous above, scattered appressed pubescence along midrib below; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, marginal vein present, secondary veins 17-20 pairs, parallel, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique, numerous; quaternaries mostly at right angles to the tertiaries (lens). Petiole 1-1.8 cm long, not channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 1-2-flowered, on old wood. Pedicel ca. 5 mm long, puberulous. Flowers ? bisexual. Sepals five, 0.7-1.1	cm long, inner generally larger than outer, broadly ovate, apex rounded or obtuse, puberulous outside, puberulous inside in the upper half. Corolla broadly cylindrical, 1.1-1.2 cm long, tube 7-8 mm long, lobes five, 4-5 mm long, broadly oblong, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed near the top of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 1.5 mm long, geniculate at apex, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.5 mm long, oblong-lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, 2-3 mm long, oblong, glabrous. Disk irregularly cyathiform, pubescent. Ovary irregularly ovoid, five-locular, densely stiff-pubescent; style ca. 9 mm long after anthesis, slightly exserted, pubescent in lower half; style-head simple. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 45 cm diam. with rough brown, fissured bark ca. 2 cm thick; slash pinkish-brown with white latex; corolla greenish-white; flowering May.

description: Tree; young shoots minutely appressed puberulous with golden-ferruginous hair, becoming glabrous, greyish-brown, smooth or scaling, lenticels few or none. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 12.5-24 × 5.7-10.1 cm, broadly elliptic, oblong-elliptic or broadly oblanceolate, apex shortly narrowly attenuate, obtuse or rounded, base narrowly attenuate, chartaceous or thinly coriaceous, glabrous above, lower surface glaucous, finely and sparsely appressed puberulous with golden-brown hairs; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 13-18 pairs, parallel, slightly arcuate or straight; intersecondaries long, often extending to the margin; tertiaries reticulate. Petiole 1-2 cm long, not channelled, appressed puberulous. Fascicles borne below the leaves, 5-10 flowered. Pedicel 5-7 mm long with sparse minute appressed hairs. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals (young flower bud) five, ca. 1.5 mm long, broadly ovate, apex obtuse, sparse minute appressed hairs on both surfaces. Corolla ca. 2 mm long, ? tube about equalling the lobes, lobes five, glabrous. Stamens five, ? fixed in the upper half of the corolla tube, glabrous. Staminodes five, lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary flat-topped, bilocular, puberulous; style glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 4-6 cm long, ellipsoid, apex acute to rounded, base rounded, hard-skinned, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, 3.5-4.5 cm long, ellipsoid, rounded at base and apex, not laterally compressed; testa smooth, adherent to the pericarp, 0.7-0.8 mm thick; scar full-length, adaxial and extending around the base, 8-9 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 45 cm diam. with low narrow buttresses. Bark greyish to brown, smooth or finely fissured, with prominent lenticels; slash pink or reddish, exuding white latex. Mature fruit yellow or orange. Young flowers collected Sep, mature fruit May (Colombia) and Sep (Ecuador).

description: Tree; young shoots minutely appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, pale greyish-white to mid-brown, thinly scaling, lenticellate or not. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, (4.7-)6-21 × (1.3-)2.5-8.5 cm, elliptic, oblong or oblanceolate, apex acute, narrowly attenuate, obtusely cuspidate, obtuse, rounded or retuse, base narrowly attenuate, rarely revolute, usually coriaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower surface glaucous or not, appressed puberulous with minute closely appressed pale hairs, or glabrous; venation brochidodromous, marginal vein usually present, secondary veins sometimes joining to form a submarginal vein, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondaries 10-20 pairs, parallel, mostly straight, usually impressed on the upper surface, and sometimes impressed on both surfaces; intersecondaries usually extending to near the margin; tertiaries parallel to secondaries, often obscure. Petiole 0.4-2 cm long, not or only slightly channelled, subglabrous. Fascicles 2-2 5-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 0.4-1 cm long, sparsely and minutely appressed puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals (4-)5(-6), 2-3 mm long, ovate, apex acute or obtuse, sparsely and minutely appressed puberulous outside, glabrous or with some minute appressed indumentum inside. Corolla cyathiform or shortly tubular, 1.75-3.5(-4) mm long, tube 0.75-2 mm long, equalling or slightly shorter than the lobes, lobes (4-)5(-8), 1-2.5 mm long, lanceolate to ovate, apex acute to rounded, glabrous or occasionally with sparse minute appressed indumentum at base of tube outside. Stamens (4-)5(-8), fixed in the upper half of the corolla tube, usually near or at the apex; filaments 0-0.75 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.7-1 (-1.25) mm long, lanceolate or ovate, glabrous; stamens absent in female. Staminodes 0-3(-5), usually vestigial, but occasionally up to 1 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous, or bearing vestigial anthers. Disk absent. Ovary truncate, ovoid or conical, 2(-4)-locular, shortly pubescent; style 0.5-1 mm long after anthesis, appressed puberulous to glabrous; style-head simple or minutely lobed. Fruit 2.3-5.5 cm long, oblong to ovoid, apex rounded or obtuse, base acute to tapered, sometimes forming a short stipe, smooth, with residual indumentum of minute appressed hairs at least near base. Seed one(two), 1.4-2.7 cm long, ellipsoid to broadly oblong, rounded or obtuse at apex and base, laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.3-1.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length and sometimes extending around the base, 1-3(-5) mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent.

description: Young shoots finely appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, medium brown, smooth, with a few lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 8-17 × 2-4 cm, narrowly elliptic or elliptic oblanceolate, apex acute, base tapering, acute, chartaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, marginal vein present, midrib flat or slightly raised on upper surface, secondary veins 13-15 pairs, ascending, slightly convergent and arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries horizontal to oblique. Petiole 1-1.5 cm long, not channelled, glabrous. Fascicles axillary, 3-5-flowered. Pedicel 3-4 mm long, appressed puberulous. Sepals (young flowers only) four, ca. 4 mm long, oblong-lanceolate, apex obtuse, outer pair appressed puberulous outside, inner pair glabrous. Corolla cylindrical, 3.5-3.9 mm long, tube exceeding the lobes, lobes four, fringed-ciliate. Stamens four, fixed in the lower half of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 2 mm long, anthers 0.65-0.75 mm long, ovate, apiculate, glabrous. Staminodes four, oblong-spathulate, slightly shorter than corolla lobes. Disk absent. Ovary four-locular. Fruit unknown.

description: Tree; young shoots densely appressed golden-ferruginous puberulous, becoming glabrous, greyish, smooth, often lenticellate. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 9.5-15 × 3.6-5.7 cm, oblong, elliptic or oblanceolate, apex shortly narrowly attenuate to obtuse, base narrowly attenuate, coriaceous, soon glabrous above, lower surface persistently shortly golden-ferruginous sericeous; venation brochidrodromous, marginal vein present, midrib generally sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 20-25 pairs, parallel, almost straight, sometimes slightly impressed on the upper surface; intersecondaries obscure, often long; tertiaries obscure. Petiole 1.2-2 cm long, not channelled, golden-sericeous at first. Fascicles 5-20-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 3-6 mm long, shortly sericeous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, ca. 2 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse to rounded, united at base, appressed puberulous outside with a glabrous hyaline margin, glabrous inside. Corolla cyathiform, 2.5-3 mm long, tube equalling the lobes, lobes 4-5, obovate, apex acute to rounded, outside glabrous or with scattered appressed hairs near base of tube, glabrous inside. Stamens 4-5, fixed in the upper half of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 1 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous; stamens absent in female. Staminodes 1, vestigial, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary broadly oblate, 2-3-locular, pubescent; style 0.75-1.25 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit ca. 3 × 1 cm, narrowly oblong, apex acute or obtuse, base slightly tapered, smooth, thin-walled (shrinking on drying), finely appressed puberulous with ferruginous hairs. Seed solitary, ca. 2.3 cm long, narrowly oblong-ellipsoid, apex and base rounded or obtuse, laterally compressed, testa smooth, pale, shining, ca. 0.4 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length, 2-2.5 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 12m high with white latex, leaves conspicuously rufous below, flowers greenish-white. Flowering Sep-Oct, fruit maturing Dec-Apr.

description: Tree; young shoots sparsely pubescent with pale greyish-white to golden indumentum, soon glabrous, buff to greyish-brown, cracked and scaling, usually without lenticels. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered, 7.5-26 × 1.6-4.5(-7.5) cm, narrowly oblong, elliptic or oblanceolate, apex acute to rounded, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, chartaceous, glabrous; venation usually eucamptodromous, rarely brochidodromous, marginal vein often present, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 12-22 pairs, usually slightly convergent, arcuate or straight; intersecondaries well-developed; tertiaries forming an open reticulum. Petiole 0.2-1 cm long, not channelled, usually glabrous. Fascicles 5-15-flowered, axillary and below. Pedicel 3-7 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals four, 2.5-4 mm long, outer ovate or lanceolate, obtuse, inner elliptic, rounded, appressed puberulous outside, inner pair with broad glabrous margin, glabrous inside. Corolla broadly tubular, 3.5-5 mm long, tube 2.25-3.5 mm long, lobes four, 1.25-2 mm long, broadly oblong, rounded or truncate, ciliate. Stamens four, fixed halfway to two-thirds up the corolla tube; filaments 1-2 mm long, glabrous; anthers 1-1.5 mm long, ovate or lanceolate, flattened, glabrous, absent in female. Staminodes four, 0.75-1.5 mm long, oblong or lanceolate, apex rounded, ciliate. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid to globose, 2-3-locular, densely long strigose; style 2.5-3.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous above; style-head simple. Fruit 2.5-3.5 cm long, obovoid, apex rounded, base tapering, sometimes to a short stipe ca. 5 mm long, smooth, subglabrous. Seeds 1-2, 1.9-2.4 cm long, broadly ellipsoid (plano-convex when two in a fruit), testa smooth, adherent to the pericarp, ca. 1 mm thick; scar adaxial, oblong, ca. 7 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle included; endosperm absent. Field characters. Stout-trunked tree to 15 m high and 150 cm diam.; slash with small amount of white latex. Flowers greenish, fragrant, fruit ripening yellowish to red and delicately perfumed. Flowering Sep to Feb, fruit Dec-Apr.

description: Tree, young shoots appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, pale grey-brown, cracked and scaling, lenticellate. Leaves loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 35-5 5 (-6 5) × 16-25 cm, broadly oblong to subelliptic, apex rounded, base obtuse to truncate, thickly coriaceous, glabrous above, sparsely appressed puberulous below with brown hairs; venation eucamptodromous-brochidodromous, midrib slightly sunken, marginal vein present, secondary veins 17-19 pairs, widely spreading (lower at right angles to midrib), slightly raised on upper surface, parallel, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique; quaternaries reticulate. Petiole 2.5-3.5 cm long, up to 1 cm wide, strongly channelled, appressed puberulous. Fascicles 2-6-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel ca. 1 mm long, Flowers (not seen, description from Diels & Pilz). Sepals five, ca. 5 mm, ovate, finely rufous pubescent. Corolla 2.5-3 mm long (immature), tube less than 1 mm long, rufous pubescent, lobes five, rounded, rather thick, glabrous. Stamens five; filaments ca. 0.5 mm long, stout, fixed at the top of the corolla tube. Staminodes five, 1-2 mm long, stout, apex sometimes bilobed. Ovary five (?)-locular, densely rufous pubescent; style ca. 1 mm long. Fruit 5-12 cm long, subglobose, rounded at base and apex, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, ca. 3 cm long, narrowly obovoid, apex obtuse, base acute, testa finely wrinkled, shining, ca. 0.6 mm thick; scar adaxial, full length, ca. 9 mm wide near apex, tapering to base; embryo not seen. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 1 m diam., buttressed to 1 m high. Bole slightly fluted below. Bark pale buff-brown, slash pale brown with white latex. Branches widely spreading, forming a broad round crown; plant deciduous for a short period. Old fruit collected Jun.

description: Tree; young shoots appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, pale greyish or buff, scaling in large irregular thin plates, without lenticels. Leaves clustered at the apex, spirally arranged, 6-20(-24) × 2.7-6(-8.5) cm, usually oblanceolate, rarely elliptic, apex narrowly attenuate, obtuse or rounded, base narrowly attenuate, cuneate, acute, obtuse or rounded, chartaceous, glabrous above, lower surface sericeous with yellowish-buff-coloured hairs, or minutely puberulous with loosely appressed whitish hairs usually forming a pellicle, often becoming sub-glabrous with age; venation eucamptodromous, sometimes with a thin marginal vein, midrib not raised on the upper surface, sometimes slightly sunken, secondary veins 10-17(-19) pairs, convergent or parallel, usually slightly arcuate; intersecondaries usually absent; tertiaries oblique to horizontal, often numerous; finer higher order reticulum usually visible. Petiole 0.3-1 (-1.6) cm long, not channelled, appressed puberulous. Fascicles 2-10-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 0.5-1 (-1.5) mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious or dioecious). Sepals four, 2-3(-4) mm long, ovate to oblong-lanceolate, apex acute to rounded, often hooded, outer two appressed puberulous outside, inner two glabrous or appressed puberulous along the centre, all sepals glabrous inside. Corolla broadly cylindrical, 2-3.5 mm long, tube 1.5-2.5 mm long, lobes four, 0.5-1.5 mm long, broadly oblong, apex rounded or truncate, glabrous or occasionally slightly ciliate. Stamens four, fixed in the lower half of the corolla tube; filaments 0.6-2 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.5-1(-1.25) mm long, lanceolate to ovate, often apiculate, glabrous; stamens absent or reduced to vestigial filaments in female flowers. Staminodes four, 0.3-1 mm long, lanceolate or oblong, apex rounded, glabrous or rarely slightly ciliate. Disk absent. Ovary depressed-globose to ovoid, four-locular, densely long-strigose; style 1-2.5 mm long after anthesis, included, glabrous; style-head simple or minutely four-lobed. Fruit 2.5-9 cm long, often broader than long, globose or depressed globose, or very irregular and knobbly, apex and base truncate, surface rough or smooth, glabrous or with some residual scurfy indumentum near the base. Seeds one-several, 2-4.5 cm long, broadly ellipsoid (when solitary) or planoconvex, smooth shining area of testa reduced to a small abaxial segment, testa 1-3 mm thick, woody; scar area covering most of seed surface, often verrucose; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent.

description: Leaf base and apex narrowly attenuate, undersurface persistently sericeous with yellowish-buff indumentum. Field characters. Tree to 25 m high and 50 cm diam. with fluted bole; bark greyish-white to greyish-brown, finely fissured; slash straw-coloured, with scanty white latex; the silvery brown lower leaf surface is conspicuous; flowers sweetly scented, pale cream to greenish-white, fruit maturing yellowish to pale brown; flowering throughout the year, most mature fruit recorded Jan to Jun.

description: Tree; young shoots glabrous, usually covered in transparent resin, becoming pale buff or grey, smooth at first, finally scaling in thin papery pieces, without lenticels. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 5.7-20 ×s 1.8-6 cm, oblanceolate, apex obtuse or rounded, base narrowly attenuate, usually decurrent, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, glabrous; venation brochidodromous, with a submarginal vein, midrib slightly raised (rounded) on the upper surface, secondary veins 20-35 pairs, parallel, straight; intersecondaries numerous, long (usually extending to the margin); tertiaries reticulate. Petiole 0.5-2 cm long, not channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 3-10-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 3-4 mm long, glabrous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals four, 2.5-3.5 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, glabrous. Corolla broadly tubular, 4.25-5 mm long, tube ca. 2-3 mm long, lobes four, ca. 2-2.5 mm long, equalling or shorter than the tube, oblong, apex rounded or truncate, ciliate. Stamens four, fixed about one-third up the corolla tube; filaments 2-2.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.25 mm long, lanceolate, laterally flattened, glabrous, absent in female. Staminodes four, 1.5-2 mm long, subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, four-locular, pubescent; style ca. 4 mm long after anthesis, equalling or exceeding the corolla, glabrous in upper half; style-head simple. Fruit 4.5-5.5 cm long, obovoid or ellipsoid, apex obtuse to rounded, base tapering (forming a stipe when dried), smooth, glabrous. Seeds 1-2, 3-3.2 cm long, ellipsoid, laterally compressed, apex rounded, base acute, testa smooth, shining, 0.5-0.6 mm thick; scar adaxial, 4-5 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex free cotyledons, radicle exserted ca. 2 mm; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 80 cm diam., larger specimens buttressed to 1 m; bark scaling, slash brown with copious white latex. Flowers green, fruit ripening yellow to orange. Flowering Jun-Oct, mature fruit collected Mar-May, 2nd Aug.

description: Tree; young shoots finely appressed puberulous to shortly pubescent, soon glabrous, pale grey to dark brown, finely cracked and usually lenticellate. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 9-18.3 × 3.2-7.3 cm, oblanceolate to oblong, apex shortly attenuate, obtuse or rounded, base narrowly attenuate, margin usually revolute, coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-16 pairs, parallel, arcuate or straight; intersecondaries usually absent; tertiaries oblique to reticulate. Petiole 0.6-3 cm long, not channelled, usually glabrous. Fascicles 2-10-flowered, mostly axillary. Pedicel 0.41.7 cm long, appressed puberulous to glabrous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals four, 0.7-1.1 cm long, outer shorter than inner, broadly ovate or elliptic, apex acute to rounded, appressed puberulous outside, often with a broad glabrous margin, appressed puberulous near the margin inside, or glabrous. Corolla broadly cylindrical, 1-1.6 cm long, tube 0.65-1.1 cm long, lobes 6-8, 3.5-4 mm long, oblong to narrowly elliptic, apex acute to obtuse, usually scattered appressed hairy on the outside of lobes, rarely glabrous, papillose. Stamens 6-8, fixed near the top of the corolla tube; filaments 1-1.75 mm long, not geniculate, glabrous; anthers 1.75-2 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes 6-8, 2-3.5 mm long, narrowly lanceolate to subulate, papillose. Disk absent. Ovary broadly cylindrical with a truncate apex, or globose, 6-15-locular, shortly pubescent; style 0.7-1.1 cm long after anthesis, pubescent in the lower half; style-head capitate or minutely lobed. Fruit 3.5-6 cm long, globose to depressed globose, sometimes considerably broader than long, and constricted between the seeds, apex and base rounded to truncate, smooth, pubescent to velutinous, indumentum sometimes falling before maturity. Seeds one-several, 3-3.5 cm long, shape variable dependent on number of seeds in fruit, testa smooth, shining, 0.75-1 mm thick; scar adaxial, broadly elliptic or extending over the seed to cover up to three quarters of the surface; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 15 m high and 30 cm diam. with thick bark, and viscid white latex. Flowers pale green, fruit with reddish-brown indumentum. Flowering recorded Jan-Sep, fruit Sep-Oct.

description: Tree; young shoots subglabrous, pale buff, smooth or slightly scaly, lenticellate. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 7.3-19 × 2.4-5.5 cm, oblanceolate, oblong or elliptic, apex narrowly attenuate or acuminate, base narrowly attenuate, coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, with a strong marginal vein, midrib not raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-11 pairs, slightly convergent and arcuate; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries mostly horizontal to open reticulate, quaternary reticulum obscure. Petiole 0.4-1.5 cm long, flat or slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 1-5-flowered, axillary and arranged along short leafless axillary shoots 1-3.5 cm long. Pedicel ca. 1 mm long, subglabrous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 4-7, outer ca. 1 mm long, inner ca. 2 mm long, ovate, apex rounded, subglabrous outside, sericeous inside, ciliate. Corolla broadly tubular, 2.5-3 mm long, tube 1.5-2 mm long, lobes five, 0.75-1 mm long, broadly ovate, apex rounded, sometimes auriculate at base, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments 0.1-0.3 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.4-0.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, 0.6-0.7 mm long, lanceolate or subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary globose to ovoid, five locular, densely pubescent; style ca. 1.5 mm long after anthesis, included, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 2-3 cm long, subglobose, rounded at apex and base, smooth, thin walled (wrinkling on drying), glabrous. Seed solitary, 1.3-2.5 cm long, broadly ellipsoid or subglobose, rounded at base and apex, testa smooth, shining, 0.3-0.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, covering about half the seed surface; embryo with piano convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 40 cm diam., buttressed to 1 m high; bole cylindrical; bark reddish-brown to greyish, scaling, slash with white latex. Flowers pale green or cream-coloured, fruit rusty-brown. Flowering Mar-May, fruit Aug-Nov.

description: Tree; young shoots densely short-tomentose with crisped, yellowish-brown indumentum, soon glabrous, dark brown, cracked and scaling; without lenticels. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 11-18.5 × 4.2-5.5 cm, oblanceolate, apex long narrowly attenuate or acuminate, base acute to rounded, coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, marginal vein present, midrib raised on upper surface, secondary veins 13-15 pairs, ascending, strongly arcuate and convergent; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries few, oblique; fine evident quaternary reticulum. Petiole 1-1.5 cm long, not channelled, densely crisped-tomentose, becoming glabrous. Fascicles 1-2-flowered, axillary. Pedicel 1-1.5 mm long, densely crisped-tomentose. Sepals six, in a closely imbricate spiral, outer ca. 3 mm long, innermost ca. 6 mm long, ovate to broadly elliptic, apex acute to rounded, outermost crisped-tomentose outside, inner glabrous outside, all sericeous inside, sometimes ciliate. Corolla ca. 6.5 mm long, tubular, slightly expanded at the apex, tube ca. 5 mm long, lobes five, ca. 2 mm long, ovate, apex subtruncate, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the apex of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 1 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.8-1 mm long, ovate, glabrous. Staminodes five, 1.5-1.75 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, apex truncate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, densely pubescent; style 5-6 mm long after anthesis, exserted, glabrous; style-head minutely five-lobed. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Tree to 20 m high and 15 cm diam. with white latex. Flowering Aug.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Tree; young shoots with sparse short appressed indumentum or glabrous, pale greyish-brown, becoming fissured and scaling, usually without lenticels. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 6-17.5 × 3.3-6.5 cm, oblanceolate, apex obtuse or rounded, base acute to narrowly attenuate, thinly coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly prominent on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-13 pairs, slightly convergent, arcuate; intersecondaries short to moderately long; tertiaries forming an open reticulum. Petiole 1-2.2 cm long, not channelled, glabrous. Fascicles axillary, but mostly in the axils of fallen leaves, 2-15-flowered. Pedicel 2-3 mm long, glabrous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals subvalvate, (three-)five, 2-3 mm long, ovate or triangular, apex acute, glabrous except for a small tuft of hairs at the apex. Corolla 2.5-3.5 mm long, tube 0.5-1.5 mm long, lobes five, ca. 2 mm long, broadly ovate, acute, glabrous. Stamens five, free; fiaments 1-1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.61 mm long, oblong-lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, 0.75-1.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary expanded horizontally, five-locular, pubescent; style 0.75-1 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 6-9 cm long, globose or obovoid, apex and base rounded, smooth and lenticellate or roughskinned, glabrous. Seeds several, 3.3-4.2 cm long, ellipsoid to slightly plano-convex, laterally compressed, testa not shining, rough, adherent to the pericarp, ca. 1 mm thick; scar adaxial, extending moist of the length of the seed, 3-4 mm wide. Embryo with thin foliaceous cotyledons and long exserted radicle, surrounded by copious endosperm. Tree to 50 m high and 65 cm diam., unbuttressed, bole cylindrical, bark ca. 2 cm thick, pale brown, finely vertically cracked, slash cream to pale brown, exuding scarce or copious sticky white latex. Flowers cream or white, fruit maturing bright yellow, with few or many brown or black lenticels, flesh rather tough, cream or pinkish-cream; seed surrounded by, and adherent to a layer of greenish gelatinous pulp. Flowering Feb-Jun, fruit at various stages of development all year, falling in French Guiana in May.

description: (Description of fruit and seed from Radlkofer.) Fruit 3.5-5 cm diam., globose, rugose, with latex; seed ovoid-ellipsoid, plano-convex, ca. 3.2 × 2.2 × 2 cm; scar elliptic, full-length; embryo with thick cotyledons.

description: Shrub or small tree; young growth finely appressed puberulous at first, becoming glabrous, pale greyish-buff, scaling and fissured, lenticellate. Stipules 1.5-2.5 mm long, broadly lanceolate, subglabrous. Leaves 4-17 × 3.1-6.4 cm, elliptic to oblanceolate, apex acute to rounded and sometimes emarginate, base acute to obtuse, glabrous or lower surface often with closely appressed whitish indumentum forming a pellicle; coriaceous; midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 15-18 pairs, higher order venation reticulate or areolate. Petiole 0.6-2.7 cm long, slightly channelled, subglabrous. Flowers solitary or paired. Pedicel 1.5-3 cm long (to 4.5 cm long in fruit) strongly reflexed in bud, appressed scurfy-puberulous. Sepals 0.8-1 cm long, oblong-lanceolate, acute to obtuse, slightly swollen at base and abruptly contracted into the pedicel, scurfy-puberulous outside, sparsely appressed puberulous inside. Corolla not carnose, glabrous, 0.9-1 cm long, tube 2-3 mm long; lobes six, divided to base into three segments; median segment broadly elliptic, apex acute or obtuse, lateral segments slightly shorter than the median segment, narrowly elliptic (much narrower than median segment). Stamens six, glabrous; filaments 2-2.5 mm long, anthers ca. 3.5 mm long, connective slightly produced, lanceolate. Staminodes (6-8) ca. 2 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, entire. Ovary ovoid, 6-12-locular, finely appressed puberulous; style 0.9-1.4 cm long after anthesis, glabrous. Fruit 3.5-7 cm long, globose or depressed globose, rough-skinned and scaly. Seed not seen. Field characters. A shrub or small tree to 10 m high with whitish flowers. Flowering in Sep and Dec to Mar, mature fruit Dec to Feb.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Tree, young shoots short crisped puberulous to tomentose with brown or reddish-brown hairs, becoming glabrous, grey, sometimes lenticellate, fissured. Stipules absent. Leaves 4-10 × 2-5.9 cm, broadly oblanceolate or obovate, apex rounded, truncate or emarginate, base acute to narrowly attenuate; glabrous above, short brown or reddish-brown tomentose below, indumentum persisting or falling to leave an underlying layer of closely appressed silvery or greyish hairs; midrib sunken on the upper surface; secondaries 12-15 pairs, often obscure, higher order venation areolate-reticulate, sometimes obscured; venation usually slightly impressed on the upper surface. Petiole 0.3-1.9 cm long, slightly channelled, tomentose to glabrous. Flowers 5-7 in a fascicle. Pedicel 1-1.5 cm long, shortly tomentose to sparsely puberulous, strongly reflexed in bud. Sepals 5-6 mm long, lanceolate, acute, shortly tomentose to sparsely appressed puberulous outside, appressed puberulous around the margin inside. Corolla glabrous, ca. 5 mm long, tube ca. 1 mm long; lobes six, divided to base into three segments, median segment narrowly boat-shaped, apex obtuse; lateral segments equalling the median segment, narrowly lanceolate, sometimes irregularly toothed. Stamens six, glabrous; filaments ca. 2.5 mm long, free; anthers ca. 1.5 mm long, lanceolate. Staminodes six, glabrous, 1.52 mm long, oblong, apex bilobed. Ovary ovoid, 8-11-locular, glabrous; style ca. 5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous. Fruit ca. 2 × 1.5 cm, ovoid, ellipsoid or globose apex and base rounded, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, ca. 1.3 × 0.9 × 0.5 cm, laterally compressed, with a hard smooth shining testa 0.75-1.5 mm thick; scar basi-ventral, ca. 7 × 2 mm. Field characters. A tree to 20 m high with yellowish latex. Mature fruits orange to red (Ducke, 1957: 656). Flowering Sep to Feb, with mature fruit recorded from Aug to Oct, and in Feb.

description: Small to large tree; young branches pale greyish, finely appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, becoming rough and scaly, often lenticellate. Stipules minute or absent. Leaves 4-13 × 2-5.7 cm, usually oblanceolate or cuneiform, less frequently elliptic, apex usually rounded, often emarginate, less frequently obtuse, base narrowly attenuate or acute, glabrous or with scattered minute appressed hairs on the lower surface; coriaceous; midrib sunken or raised but recessed on the upper surface; secondary veins 10-16 pairs, venation usually impressed on the upper surface, quaternary venation finely areolate, numerous fine striations parallel to the secondary vein usually present on the upper surface. Petiole 0.5-2.1 cm long, channelled, glabrous. Flowers (2-)3-10 in a fascicle. Pedicel 0.7-1.5(-3.3) cm long, sparsely appressed puberulous. Sepals 4-5 mm long, lanceolate, apex acute, appressed puberulous outside, subglabrous inside. Corolla glabrous, 3.5-4.5 mm long, tube 0.75-1.25 mm long; lobes six, divided to base into three segments, median segment narrowly boat-shaped with rounded apex and clawed base, lateral segments equalling the median lobe, narrowly lanceolate or oblong, apex acute to rounded. Stamens six, glabrous; filaments 1.5-2 mm long, free or slightly fused with the staminodes; anthers 1-1.5 mm long, lanceolate. Staminodes six, glabrous, 1.6-2.5	mm long, deeply 2-lobed. Ovary ovoid, (7-)8-10-locular, glabrous; style 3.5-4.5 mm long after anthesis. Fruit 2-2.5 × 1.7-2.5 cm, ellipsoid or globose, apex and base obtuse or rounded, smooth, glabrous. Seeds 1-2, 1.3-1.5 × 0.8-0.9 × 0.5-0.6 cm, laterally compressed; testa hard, smooth, shining, brown, 0.75-1.5 mm thick; scar basi-ventral, rather broad, ca. 8 × 4 mm, lanceolate. Field characters. Coastal and cerrado plants are usually small trees less than 10 m high, but inland (in Bahía and Maranhão) in lowland rain forest they attain heights up to 30 m or more. The bark is fissured and the slash contains plentiful white viscous latex. The flowers are sometimes scented, and whitish or cream in color. The fruit matures through reddish-orange to purple or black. Most flowering occurs from Jul to Oct, and mature fruits have been collected in Apr, Oct and Dec.
