description: Tree; young shoots glabrous, apex often covered with a varnish-like layer, dark to pale brown, becoming rough, scaly and fissured, with a few lenticels. Stipules absent. Leaves 10-19 × 3.7-6 cm, oblong to oblong-elliptic or oblanceolate, apex acute or obtuse, base acute to narrowly attenuate, glabrous above, lower surface glabrous or with a thin pellicle; chartaceous or subcoriaceous; midrib sunken on the upper surface; secondaries 16-22 pairs, sometimes forming an indistinct submarginal vein, higher order venation obscure. Petiole 2.2-3.7 cm long, not or only slightly channelled at the apex, glabrous. Flowers 5-6 in a fascicle. Pedicel 1.1-1.3 cm long, appressed puberulous. Sepals 6-6.5 mm long, lanceolate, apex acute or obtuse, outside densely scurfy-puberulous, inside puberulous near the margins. Corolla glabrous, 6.5-8 mm long, tube ca. 2 mm long; lobes six, divided to the base into three segments, median segment elliptic, clawed, apex obtuse; lateral segments shorter than the median segments, lanceolate. Stamens six, glabrous, anthers ca. 3 mm long. Staminodes six, glabrous, ca. 4 mm long, lanceolate, subentire. Ovary ovoid, 6-locular, appressed puberulous; style ca. 5.5 mm after anthesis, appressed puberulous below, glabrous above. Fruit ca. 2 cm long, globose, rough skinned and scaly. Seed not seen. Field characters. A tree to 25 m high, with white milky latex. It flowers in Mar, and Jun-Oct, with mature fruit from Jun to Jan (Adams, 1972: 572).

description: Tree; young shoots glabrous, brown, becoming very rough, cracked, lenticellate. Stipules absent. Leaves 11-15 × 5-5.7 cm, oblong elliptic, apex rounded, base shortly narrowly attenuate, glabrous above, densely puberulous below, forming a pellicle; chartaceous; midrib sunken on the upper surface; secondaries 20-25 pairs, higher order venation obscure. Petiole 2.4-3.4 cm long, slightly channelled at the apex, glabrous. Flowers 3-5 in a fascicle. Pedicel ca. 1 cm long, scurfy-puberulous. Sepals 6-6.5 mm long, broadly lanceolate, apex acute to obtuse, scurfy puberulous outside, glabrous inside except for some indumentum near the margin. Corolla glabrous, ca. 6.5 mm long, tube ca. 2 mm long; lobes six, divided to base into three segments, median segment elliptic, clawed, apex obtuse; lateral segments shorter than the median segment (ca. 3.5 mm long), lanceolate, acute. Stamens six, glabrous; filaments ca. 3 mm long, shortly connate to the staminodes; anthers 2-2.2 mm long, lanceolate. Staminodes six, glabrous, ca. 3 mm long, broadly oblong or irregular and expanded above, with a deeply cut and fimbriate margin. Ovary ovoid, 9-locular, appressed puberulous; style ca. 5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous. Fruit unknown. Field characters. A tree 30-40 m high, with fissured bark. Flowering Sep.

description: Shrub or small tree to 10 m high; young branches dark brown, glabrous or appressed puberulous at first, becoming pale grey, prominently lenticellate, rough and fissured. Stipules minute or absent. Leaves 4.6-12 × 2.2-5.5 cm, oblanceolate or cuneiform, apex obtusely cuspidate, obtuse, rounded or emarginate, base acute, narrowly cuneate or attenuate, glabrous above, lower surface with a thin layer of closely appressed whitish or greyish hairs at first, often becoming glabrous; usually coriaceous; midrib sunken on the upper surface or slightly raised but recessed; secondaries 12-16 pairs, venation usually slightly impressed on the upper surface, quaternary venation finely areolate; fine striations parallel to the secondary veins often present on the upper surface. Petiole 0.7-2.4 cm long, channelled, sparsely puberulous or glabrous. Flowers 3-10 in a fascicle. Pedicel 0.7-1.6 cm long, sparsely appressed puberulous or glabrous. Sepals 4-7 mm long, lanceolate, apex acute, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside, sometimes ciliate. Corolla glabrous, 4.5-6.5 mm long, tube 1-1.5 mm long; lobes six, divided to base into three segments, median segment slender, boat-shaped with obtuse apex and clawed base, lateral segments equalling the median segment, narrowly lanceolate, acute. Stamens six, glabrous; filaments 2-3.5 mm long, shortly connate with the staminodes; anthers 1.5-2.5 mm long, narrowly oblong or lanceolate. Staminodes six, glabrous, 2.5-5 mm long, variously divided, lobed or toothed. Ovary ovoid, 7-11 -locular, glabrous; style 4.5-6 mm long after anthesis. Fruit  1.5-2.5 × 1-1.5 cm, ellipsoid or globose, apex and base rounded, smooth, glabrous. Seed 1-2, 1.2-1.5 cm long, laterally compressed, testa hard, smooth, shining, brown, 0.3-0.5 mm thick; scar basi-ventral, ca. 7 × 3 mm. A shrub or small tree to 10 m high in restinga, but reaching 20 m high in the rain forests of Parana and Santa Catarina. The bark is rough, grey and with white latex. The scented flowers are greenish-white to yellow and the fruit ripens orange to red.

description: Shrub or small tree; young branches greyish-brown, glabrous, often lenticellate, rather rough. Stipules absent. Leaves 2.5-5.5 × 1-2.5 cm, oblanceolate, apex emarginate, base acute or attenuate, glabrous; coriaceous; midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface; secondary veins 12-17 pairs, higher order venation finely areolate and slightly impressed on the upper surface. Petiole 3-5 mm long, channelled, glabrous. Flowers 1-3 in a fascicle. Pedicel 1-1.6 cm long, reflexed in bud, subglabrous. Sepals ca. 3.5 mm long, broadly lanceolate, apex obtuse, outer whorl densely scurfy puberulous, inner whorl appressed puberulous. Corolla glabrous, ca. 3.5 mm long, tube ca. 1 mm long; lobes six, divided to base into three segments, median segment boatshaped, clawed, apex rounded; lateral segments equalling the median segment, lanceolate. Stamens six, glabrous; filaments ca. 1.5 mm long, free; anthers ca. 1.5 mm long, lanceolate-sagittate. Staminodes six, glabrous, ca. 0.5 mm long, apex truncate or irregularly short-lobed. Ovary ovoid, 6-locular, glabrous; style ca. 2.5 mm long after anthesis. Fruit 1-1.1 × 0.8 cm, ellipsoid, apex and base rounded, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, ca. 8 × 4 × 2.5 mm, laterally compressed and keeled at the apex; testa hard, smooth, shining brown, 0.2-0.3 mm thick; scar narrow, basi-ventral, ca. 2 × 0.75 mm. Field characters. An evergreen, intricately branched shrub or small tree to ca. 3 m high (sometimes reaching 8 m high on the sandy "tabuleiros" of Ceará (Ducke 1957: 653)). Latex present in the trunk. Flowers greenish-white to yellow and the fruit orange or red changing to black when fully mature. Flowering May, and Jul to Nov, mature fruit Feb, Aug and Oct.

description: Tree; young growth finely appressed puberulous, soon glabrous, pale greyish-brown, becoming cracked and rough, lenticellate. Stipules present, ca. 1.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Leaves 8-14.2 × 3.2-5.6 cm, oblong or oblong-elliptic, rounded, often emarginate, or obtuse, base rounded or truncate, rarely acute, glabrous above, finely and closely appressed puberulous below, forming a pellicle, drying pale greyish or brown, coriaceous; midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondaries 14-20 pairs, higher order venation finely areolate. Petiole 0.9-2 cm long, slightly channelled, glabrous. Flowers 2-10 in a fascicle. Pedicel 1-2 cm long, appressed puberulous. Sepals 4.5-5 mm long, broadly elliptic or ovate, apex acute to rounded, appressed puberulous outside, appressed puberulous near the margin inside. Corolla glabrous, 4.5-6 mm long, tube 1-2mm long, carnose; lobes six, divided to base into three segments, median segment erect, oblanceolate, apex acute or obtuse, clawed, not carnose, lateral segments widely spreading, equalling the median lobe, broadly ovate, carnose in the lower part. Stamens 11-12, glabrous; filaments 0.75-1.5 mm long, carnose; anthers 1.2-2 mm long, lanceolate. Staminodes absent (rarely 1, petaloid ca. 2.5 mm long). Ovary narrowly ovoid, 6-9-locular, finely appressed puberulous; style ca. 4 mm long after anthesis, glabrous. Fruit (not seen, description from Pierre, 1904: 176) 1.2-1.6 cm diam., pericarp crustaceous. Seed (immature) 10-12 × 7 × 4-5 mm; scar narrow, basi-ventral. Field characters. Described as a large tree, but the only accurate information to hand indicates a tree ca. 10 m high. The fresh leaves are whitish below, a colour which is usually retained in dried specimens. The flowers are yellowish-white.

description: Tree; young growth shortly tomentose with loose rich brown hairs, soon becoming glabrous, pale, rough, cracked or fissured, lenticellate. Stipules absent. Leaves 6.6-14.4 × 2.1-5.2 cm, usually elliptic or oblong-elliptic, less frequently oblanceolate, apex acute or narrowly attenuate, less frequently obtuse or rounded, base narrowly attenuate or acute, glabrous above, lower surface with residual brown tomentum along the midrib, or glabrous, chartaceous; midrib slightly prominent on the upper surface, or flat or slightly sunken; secondaries 15-23 pairs, higher order venation finely areolate. Petiole 1-3 cm long, slightly channelled in the upper part, shortly tomentose to glabrous. Flowers solitary. Pedicel 0.8-2 cm long, shortly tomentose. Sepals (6.5-)7-9.5 mm long, ovate to lanceolate, apex acute to obtuse, apex of inner whorl obtuse to rounded, outer surface of outer whorl shortly tomentose, inner whorl puberulous, inner surface of both whorls appressed puberulous near the margin. Corolla (7-)8-11 mm long, tube 4-6(-7) mm long, nearly always equalling or exceeding the lobes; lobes six(-seven), entire or irregularly 2-3-toothed or divided, or regularly divided into a narrow slightly boat-shaped and sometimes clawed median segment and two broader lateral segments, usually glabrous, occasionally pubescent at the apex of the lobes or on the outside of the tube below the insertion of the staminodes. Stamens six, glabrous; filaments 0.75-1.5 mm long, sometimes strongly incurved; anthers 1.5-2 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes six, (2-) 2.5-5 mm long, oblong, elliptic or lanceolate, rarely clawed, often thickened and with a rounded adaxial keel, apex entire, toothed or rarely two-lobed or truncate, usually glabrous, occasionally pubescent on the abaxial surface. Ovary broadly ovoid to conical, often sunken in a fleshy annulus, 8-12-locular, densely pubescent; style 5-9 mm long after anthesis, glabrous. Fruit 3.58 × 3-6 cm, broadly ovoid or ellipsoid, apex obtuse to rounded, base rounded to truncate, rough-skinned and scaly. Seeds 2-10,1.5-2.5 cm long, strongly laterally compressed, with a hard smooth shining testa 1-2 mm thick; scar adaxial or basi-ventral, narrow, 1-1.5 × 0.1-0.2 cm. Field characters. A tree to 45 m high and 125 cm diam., without buttresses but often slightly fluted near the base. The bark is light grey to dark brown, dependent on situation, deeply and regularly fissured and grid-cracked. The inner bark is pinkish and contains sticky white latex. Mature trees throughout the range are recognised by the diagonal scars on the trunk indicating the incisions made by chicle collectors. The crown is dense, dark green with conspicuous sympodial branching in which the leaves are clustered at the shoot apices. Young specimens often have whorled branches. The sweetly scented flowers are greenish-white or cream, and the fruits pale brown, rough-skinned and scaly, containing abundant latex when immature.

description: Tree; young shoots closely appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, greyish or brown, thinly scaling, usually without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 10-17 × 3-7 cm, oblanceolate or oblong, apex shortly narrowly attenuate or acuminate, base usually acute or narrowly attenuate, less frequently obtuse or rounded, usually chartaceous, glabrous, or with some residual appressed hairs along the undersurface midrib, venation brochidodromous, marginal vein weak or absent, submarginal vein present, very close to the margin and sometimes fusing with the marginal vein, midrib flat or slightly but sharply raised on the upper surface, secondary and tertiary venation finely striate, about equally prominent. Petiole 0.9-1.2 cm long, channelled, with appressed hairs or glabrous. Fascicles 1-12-flowered, axillary. Pedicel 4-8 mm long, sparsely appressed-puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious(?)). Sepals four, 1.53 mm long, ovate, apex acute to rounded, sparsely appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Corolla 2-4 mm long, campanulate; tube 1.5-2.5 mm long; lobes four, 0.5-1.5 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens four, included; filaments 0.3-0.4 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 1 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous, absent in female flowers. Staminodes four, ca. 1.25 mm long (male), ca. 0.5 mm long (female), lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid or pyramidal, 3-4-locular, densely pubescent; style 1-1.5 mm long, after anthesis, included, glabrous; style-head simple or minutely lobed. Fruit 4-4.7 cm long, ellipsoid, strongly 4-winged or ribbed (ribs 3-4 mm deep), apex narrowly attenuate, base acute or obtuse, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, ca. 1.2 cm long, laterally compressed, tapering to the base, testa transversely wrinkled, shining, 0.40.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, 3-4 mm wide. Field characters. Tree to 25 m high, but often flowering when much smaller. Bark grey, with scarce white latex. The cut trunk produces sucker shoots. The tetramerous flowers are greenish-yellow and the fruit matures yellowish-orange. According to Ducke (1925: 159), the fruit resembles that of Averrhoa carambola in color and shape, but with a rather dry, spongy mesocarp. Flowering mostly Jun to Oct, fruit maturing Sep to Mar.

description: Tree; young shoots finely appressed puberulous at first, becoming glabrous, greyish-brown to black, rough, cracked, usually without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous or spirally arranged, 5.3-19 × 1.9-9.2 cm, elliptic, oblong-elliptic or oblanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate, acute, obtusely cuspidate or rounded, base acute, narrowly cuneate or attenuate, usually coriaceous, glabrous above, lower surface usually silvery or less frequently ferruginous with closely appressed minute sericeous indumentum, venation brochidodromous to eucamptodromous, often with a submarginal vein, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 1225 pairs, parallel, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries strong, but tending to disappear below the margin; higher order venation finely areolate, often obscured. Petiole 1-2.8 cm long, channelled, appressed puberulous to glabrous, margins usually decurrent on the stem as two raised lines. Fascicles axillary, 3-20-flowered, usually developing into stout, recurved, densely bracteate brachyblasts to ca. 0.5 cm long, these persisting on the old wood. Pedicel 2-5 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, 2-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, appressed puberulous outside, appressed puberulous or glabrous inside. Corolla 2.5-3 mm long, shortly and broadly tubular or campanulate, tube 1.5-2 mm long, lobes five, 1-1.5 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, included, filaments ca. 0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, broadly lanceolate, glabrous; stamens absent in female flowers. Staminodes five, 0.5-1.25 mm long, ovate to narrowly triangular, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary broadly ovoid or truncate, five-locular, densely pubescent; style 0.9-1 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 1.6-3.5 cm long, ellipsoid to obovoid, apex rounded or obtuse, sometimes apiculate, base usually tapered, smooth, appressed puberulous to glabrous. Seed solitary, 1.4-2.3 cm long, laterally compressed, testa hard, smooth, shiny, 0.3-1 mm thick; scar adaxial, 1.5-2 mm wide. Field characters. Tree to 40 m high and 80 cm diam. with large narrow plank buttresses; bark grey to pale brown, smooth, with pinkish-brown slash and copious sticky white latex. The decurrent petiole margins continue down the stem as two prominent raised lines, a feature often mentioned by collectors. Flowers yellowish-green and fruit maturing purple to black. Flowering Feb, Apr-Jul, fruit maturing Dec-Jun.

description: Tree; young shoots shortly appressed pubescent, soon glabrous, pale greyish, thinly scaling, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 5.5-11 × 2-3.2 cm, elliptic or oblanceolate, apex tapering, usually long caudate, base acute or narrowly cuneate, thinly coriaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower surface finely appressed sericeous with silvery hairs, becoming glabrous, venation craspedodromous or brochidodromous with a strong marginal vein, submarginal vein, if present, very close to the margin, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins shallowly ascending, finely striate, indistinguishable from the intersecondaries and tertiaries. Petiole 5-7 mm long, channelled, appressed pubescent. Fascicles 1-2-flowered, axillary or in the axils of fallen leaves. Pedicels 0.5-2 mm long, shortly appressed pubescent. Flowers unisexual (?). Sepals five, ca. 2.5 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse, shortly appressed pubescent outside, scattered appressed hairs inside. Corolla ca. 3.5 mm long, shortly cylindric, tube ca. 2.5 mm long, lobes five, ca. 1 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, included; filaments ca. 0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 1 mm long, subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, four-locular, long stiff-hairy; style ca. 1.25 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit ca. 2.5× 1.2 cm, ellipsoid, apex acute, apiculate, base rounded, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, ca. 2.1 cm long, laterally compressed, testa minutely transversely wrinkled, shining 0.2-0.4 mm thick; scar adaxial, ca. 2 mm wide. Field characters. Tree to 15 m high and 25 cm diam. with white latex. Fruit maturing purple. Flowering Jul to Sep, fruit maturing Jun to Aug.

description: Shrub or weak-stemmed tree; young shoots shortly pubescent with golden-brown ferruginous hairs, soon glabrous, pale greyish-brown, rough and scaling, usually without lenticels. Leaves spaced, usually spirally arranged, or rarely alternate and distichous, 3.5-9.5 × 1-4.2 cm, oblong, oblong-lanceolate, elliptic or oblanceolate, apex obtuse, acute, narrowly attenuate or obtusely cuspidate, coriaceous, glabrous or with sparse residual pubescence on the undersurface midrib, venation craspedodromous or brochidodromous, marginal vein strong, submarginal vein present, very close to or fusing with the marginal vein, midrib sunken on the upper surface, venation finely striate with the intersecondaries and tertiaries indistinguishable from the secondaries. Petiole 0.3-1.0 cm long, channelled, shortly pubescent to glabrous. Fascicles 2-6-flowered, axillary or in the axils of fallen leaves. Pedicel 2-4 mm long, shortly pubescent. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious (?)). Sepals (four-) five, 1.75-2.5 mm long, ovate, obtuse to rounded, appressed puberulous to shortly pubescent outside, scattered appressed hairs inside or glabrous. Corolla 2-4.5 mm long, tube 1.25-3.25 mm long, lobes (four-)five, 0.75-1.5 mm long, ovate or triangular, apex obtuse to rounded, glabrous. Stamens (four-)five, included; filaments 0.5-0.75 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.5-0.7 mm long, ovate or lanceolate, glabrous; stamens reduced to minute vestiges in female flowers. Staminodes (four-)five, 0.5-1 mm long, lanceolate to subulate, glabrous. Small annular hairy disk often present below the ovary in male flowers. Ovary ovoid, (four-)five-locular, densely stiff-hairy; style 0.75-1.5 mm long after anthesis, included, glabrous; style-head simple or minutely lobed. Fruit ca. 1 × 0.7 cm, broadly ellipsoid, apex and base rounded, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, ca. 0.9 cm long, laterally compressed, with a smooth, shining testa, ca. 0.25 mm thick; scar adaxial, ca. 1.5 mm wide. Field characters. Shrub or weak-stemmed tree to 15 m high and 40 cm diam.; larger specimens with fissured bark. Exudate present, white or yellowish. Flower slightly scented, pale yellowish-cream to light green, fruit maturing reddish.

description: Shrub or small tree; young shoots tomentose with crisped, golden brown or ferruginous hairs, becoming glabrous, greyish, with numerous brown elongate lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous or spirally arranged, 3.5-6 × 1-2.1 cm, elliptic or lanceolate, apex acute, base rounded, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, upper surface usually glabrous, lower surface with residual crisped pubescence along the midrib and at the base of the lamina, venation craspedodromous or brochidodromous, marginal vein strong, submarginal vein present, very close to or fusing with the marginal vein, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary and tertiary veins appearing finely striate to the naked eye, but with a lens the parallel intersecondaries and tertiaries can be distinguished from the slightly stronger secondaries. Petiole 1.5-2.5 mm long, channelled, shortly tomentose. Fascicles axillary, 5-10-flowered. Pedicel 1.5-3 mm long, shortly tomentose. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals (four-)five, ca. 2 mm long, ovate apex acute to obtuse, pubescent outside, glabrous within. Corolla ca. 3 mm long, shortly tubular, tube ca. 1.75 mm long, lobes (four-)five, ca. 1.25 mm long, ovate, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens (four)five, fixed near the apex of the tube, but with long traces, filaments ca. 0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.5 mm long, suborbicular, glabrous. Staminodes (four)five, ca. 0.75 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, densely pubescent; style ca. 1 mm long after anthesis, included, glabrous. Fruit 1.2-1.5 cm long, ellipsoid, apex and base rounded, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, 0.9-1.4 cm long, laterally compressed, testa finely transversely wrinkled, shining, 0.5-1 mm thick; scar adaxial, sometimes extending round the base of the seed, 1.5-2 mm wide. Field characters. Shrub or small tree to 6 m high, with white latex. Flowers pale green or cream-coloured. Flowering Sep to Feb and Jun, fruit Oct to Apr.

description: Tree; young shoots finely appressed puberulous or less frequently erect and spreading puberulous, hairs ferruginous to greyish, becoming glabrous, greyish to black, cracked and scaling, usually without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous or spirally arranged, 3.5-20(-30) × 1.7-7(-11.4) cm, elliptic, oblong-elliptic or oblanceolate, apex obtusely cuspidate or narrowly attenuate, obtuse or rounded, base narrowly attenuate, cuneate, acute, obtuse or rarely rounded, usually coriaceous, glabrous above, finely golden or reddish-brown sericeous below, or sparsely appressed puberulous, less frequently glabrous, indumentum turning paler with age, venation brochidodromous, sometimes with a marginal vein, secondaries joining below the margin to form a submarginal vein, midrib usually sunken on the upper surface, or less frequently flat or slightly raised, secondary veins 15-30 pairs, parallel, usually slightly arcuate; intersecondaries long; often extending to the margin and often almost as strong as the secondaries; higher order venation finely reticulate-areolate, but sometimes with additional stronger veins lying parallel to the secondaries. Petiole 0.4-3 cm long, channelled, appressed puberulous to glabrous, margins often decurrent on the stem as two raised lines. Fascicles axillary, 2-20-flowered, usually developing into stout, recurved densely scaly shoots up to ca. 1 cm long, these persisting on the old wood. Pedicel (1.5-)2-7 mm long, appressed or spreading puberulous, hairs golden to ferruginous. Flower unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, (1.75-)2-3.5(-4) mm long, ovate to suborbicular, apex acute to rounded, golden to ferruginous appressed puberulous on both surfaces, margin sometimes ciliate. Corolla 2.25-4 mm long, shortly and broadly tubular to campanulate, tube 1.25-3.5 mm long, lobes (four-)five, 0.75-1.5 mm long, usually broadly oblong with truncate or rounded margin, glabrous. Stamens (four-)five, included; filaments 0.25-0.6(-l) mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.4-0.75 mm long, lanceolate or ovate, glabrous, absent in female flowers. Staminodes (four-)five, 0.5-1(-1.25) mm long, lanceolate, subulate or oblong, glabrous. Annular pubescent disk usually present around the base of the ovary in male flowers, obscure or absent in female. Ovary broad, usually flattened in male flowers, ovoid or conical in female, five-locular, long-pubescent; style slightly exserted in bud, 0.75-2 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple or minutely lobed. Fruit 1-2.8 cm long, ellipsoid or obovoid, apex rounded, often apiculate, base rounded or tapered, smooth, finely appressed puberulous to glabrous. Seed solitary, 0.75-2.1 cm long, laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.3-0.75 mm thick; scar adaxial, 1-3.5 mm wide.

description: Leaves usually more than 15 cm long, broadly elliptic or broadly oblong-elliptic, often about twice as long as broad, base obtuse or rounded; petiole usually more than 2 cm long. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 30 cm diam. with abundant white or yellowish sticky latex. The leaves are conspicuously tan, rufous or golden on the lower surface. Flowers yellowish-green or cream-coloured, fruity juicy, olive-green, with an easily removed ferruginous pubescence. Flowering Mar to Sep, fruiting Sep to Feb.

description: Tree; young shoots shortly appressed pubescent with ferruginous hairs, soon glabrous, greyish, thinly scaling, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 4.3-9 × 1.9-4.7 cm, lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, apex long narrowly acuminate or caudate, base obtuse, rounded or truncate, coriaeous, glabrous above, densely and finely appressed sericeous below with ferruginous or paler silvery hairs, becoming sparser with age, venation craspedodromous with a strong marginal vein, leaf margin slightly revolute, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins widely spreading or shallowly ascending, finely striate, indistinguishable from the intersecondaries and tertiaries. Petiole 5-8 mm long, channelled, appressed pubescent with ferruginous hairs decurrent on the stem as a raised line. Fascicles 1-3-flowered, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves. Pedicel 2-4 mm long, shortly appressed ferruginous pubescent. Flowers unisexual (?). Sepals five, 2.5-4 mm long, narrowly ovate or elliptic, apex obtuse, appressed pubescent outside, glabrous inside, margin ciliate. Corolla 3.5-5 mm long, shortly cylindric, tube 2.53.75 mm long, lobes 1-1.25 mm long, lanceolate, obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, included, fixed near the top of the corolla tube but with traces visible to near the base; filaments 0.5-0.75 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 1 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary narrowly ovoid, five-locular, shortly pubescent; style ca. 1 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head minutely lobed. Immature fruit ca. 1 cm long, ellipsoid, shortly rostrate, subglabrous. Seed not seen.  Field characters. Tree to 15 m high and 12 cm diam., unbuttressed. Slash reddish, with a trace of latex. Ferruginous indumentum conspicuous on the lower leaf surface. Flowers greenish-white, fruit ripening dark wine-red. Flowering Jun to Nov, fruit reported in Aug (Huber & Krai 7970).

description: Tree; young shoots appressed puberulous, becoming glabrous, dark brown, cracked and fissured, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 21-23 × 7.9-8.8 cm, broadly oblong, apex rounded, base obtuse to acute, margin revolute, coriaceous, glabrous above, sparse residual appressed hairs near base below, venation brochidodromous, midrib slightly prominent on the upper surface, submarginal vein present, secondary veins, 35-40 pairs, widely spreading, parallel, slightly arcuate, not striate and clearly separable from the parallel higher order venation. Petiole 1-2 cm long, slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 5-10-flowered, in the axils of fallen leaves. Pedicel 1-1.4 cm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals five, ca. 6 mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex rounded, appressed ferruginous-puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Corolla ca. 1.3 cm long, cylindrical, slightly broader at the apex, tube ca. 9.5 mm long, lobes five, ca. 3.5 mm long, broadly lanceolate to triangular, reflexing, glabrous. Stamens five, exserted; filaments 7-8 mm long, geniculate at apex when young, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 2.5 mm long, lanceolate-subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary broadly triangular, five-locular, pubescent; style ca. 3 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Tree 6 m high with yellow leaves. Flowers collected Jan.

description: Small tree; young shoots sparsely appressed puberulous, soon glabrous, pale greyish, smooth or slightly scaling, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 7-15.3 × 2.3-6.9 cm, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, apex narrowly acuminate to caudate, base obtuse, acute or narrowly attenuate, usually chartaceous, often drying pale green, glabrous, venation brochidodromous, marginal vein weak or absent, submarginal vein present, very close to the leaf margin, midrib not raised or sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins numerous, widely spreading, slightly stronger than the parallel intersecondaries and tertiaries, the leaf appearing striate. Petiole 0.7-1.1 cm long, channelled, subglabrous. Fascicles axillary or in the axils of fallen leaves, 1-4-flowered. Pedicel 5-7 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals five, 3-5 mm long, lanceolate to ovate, often slightly hooded, apex acute to rounded, sericeous outside, the inner ones with a broad glabrous margin, glabrous inside. Corolla 5-6.5 mm long, tubular, tube 4-5 mm long, lobes five, ca. 1.5 mm long, lanceolate or ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, included; filaments 0.6-1 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.75-1 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 1.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid to globose, five-locular, densely long stiff hairy; style 2.5-3 mm long after anthesis, included, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit ca. 5 cm long, 2-2.5 cm broad, ellipsoid, with a long attenuate rostrate apex, base acute, smooth, glabrous. Seeds 1-2, ca. 2.5 cm long, laterally compressed, base and apex acute, testa rough, minutely transversely wrinkled, matt, not shiny, ca. 0.4 mm thick; scar adaxial, ca. 3 mm wide. Field characters. Small understorey tree to 12 m high and 20 cm diam, with greyish-brown bark and scarce white latex. Flowers white in Jul and Aug, fruit maturing Mar.

description: Tree; young shoots appressed puberulous with brown hairs, soon glabrous, pale greyish, becoming fissured and cracked, usually without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 3.813 × 1.8-5.2 cm, elliptic or lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate or acuminate, base narrowly attenuate to rounded, margin often revolute, coriaceous, glabrous or with residual indumentum along the undersurface midrib, venation craspedodromous with a marginal vein or brochidodromous and then with a submarginal vein very close to or merging with the marginal one, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 15-25 pairs, widely spreading, parallel, straight; intersecondaries variable, long or absent; tertiary reticulum usually visible. Petiole 4-7 mm long, channelled, appressed puberulous to glabrous. Fascicles axillary, 1-2-flowered. Pedicel 2-3 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers unisexual (?). Sepals five, 2.5-3 mm long, ovate, apex acute, appressed ferruginous puberulous outside, with a few appressed hairs near apex inside. Corolla 3-3.5 mm long, tube 2-2.5 mm long, lobes five, 1-1.5 mm long, ovate, rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, included; filaments ca. 0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.4 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 0.6 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, pubescent; style ca. 2 mm long after anthesis. Fruit 4-5 cm long, broadly ovoid or subglobose, apex obtuse, acute or shortly rostrate, base rounded or truncate, smooth, glabrous. Seeds several, 2.5-2.7 cm long, laterally compressed, or shaped like the wedges of an orange, testa hard, smooth, shining, 0.5-0.75 mm thick; scar adaxial, 2-4 mm wide. Field characters. Tree to 20 m high. Leaves with prominently sulcate midrib. Flowers white, fruit ripening reddish. A single flowering record from Jan, fruit collected Feb, Apr, Nov, Dec.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Tree; young shoots finely appressed puberulous, becoming glabrous, greyish-white, shallowly fissured, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 12.9-15 × 7-7.5 cm (up to 35 × 15 cm on sterile shoots), broadly oblanceolate or elliptic, apex obtuse, base obtuse or rounded, coriacious, glabrous above, lower surface finely appressed puberulous with brown hairs, venation brochidodromous, secondaries joining below the margin to form a submarginal vein, midrib slightly prominent on the upper surface, secondary veins 20-24 pairs, parallel, arcuate; intersecondaries moderately developed; tertiaries forming an open reticulum; higher order venation minutely areolate (visible on the upper surface). Petiole 3.2-3.5 cm long, channelled, appressed puberulous, margins decurrent on the stem as two raised lines. Fascicles 5-10-flowered, axillary, developing into persistent, densely scaly brachyblasts, 1-2 cm long. Pedicel 6-8 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals five, 4-4.5 mm long, ovate, acute or obtuse, appressed puberulous on both surfaces, margin sometimes ciliate. Corolla ca. 5 mm long, broadly tubular, tube ca. 3.5 mm long, lobes five, ca. 1.5 mm long, broadly oblong, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, included; filaments ca. 1 mm long, strongly recurved, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.8 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 1.25 mm long, lanceolate-subulate, glabrous. Disk present, annular, densely long-hairy. Ovary conical, five-locular, pubescent; style ca. 2.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous, not exserted; style-head simple. Fruit (according to Ducke) similar to that of Af. cyrtobotrya (=M. guyanensis subsp. guyanensis). Field characters. Tree to 50 m high with cracked bark (Ducke, 1930: 851). Flowers pale green, present in Nov.

description: Tree; young shoots appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, pale grey, thinly scaling, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 15-19.5 × 8.3-11.5 cm, obovate, apex truncate or retuse, base narrowly attenuate, margin revolute, coriaceous, glabrous, venation brochidodromous, midrib flat, secondary veins 15-25 pairs, joining close to the margin to form a submarginal vein, shallowly ascending, parallel, arcuate; intersecondaries long, usually extending to the margin; tertiaries forming an open reticulum. Petiole 1.5-2.5 cm long, not channelled, appressed puberulous. Fascicles in the axils of fallen leaves and ramiflorous, 10-15-flowered. Pedicel 1-1.3 cm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals five, ca. 2.5 mm long, broadly ovate, apex obtuse, appressed puberulous on both surfaces. Corolla ca. 4.5 mm long, tubular, tube about equalling the lobes, lobes five, oblong, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, included; filaments ca. 1 mm long, geniculate at apex, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.2 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 1.5 mm long, lanceolate-subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary conical, five-locular, pubescent; style ca. 1.5 mm long after anthesis, not exserted, pubescent; style-head simple. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Tree about 15 m high with latex.

description: Tree; young shoots finely appressed puberulous, soon glabrous, greyish-brown, becoming cracked and scaling, lenticels present or absent. Leaves spaced, alternate & distichous, 9-17.2 × 4-7.4 cm, broadly elliptic, apex shortly narrowly attenuate to acuminate, base acute, narrowly cuneate or attenuate, margin often revolute, thinly to moderately coriaceous, glabrous, venation brochidodromous, marginal vein present, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, submarginal vein present, very close to the margin, secondary and tertiary venation spreading widely, appearing finely striate to the naked eye, but with a lens the parallel intersecondaries and tertiaries can be distinguished from the slightly stronger secondaries. Petiole 0.8-1.8 cm long, slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 3-10-flowered, axillary. Pedicel 4-7 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious (?)). Sepals five, 2-2.5 mm long, ovate, apex acute or rounded, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside, margin ciliate. Corolla 2-3 mm long, shortly tubular to campanulate, tube 1.25-2 mm long, lobes 4-5, 0.75-1 mm long, ovate, apex obuse, sparsely appressed hairy outside, glabrous inside. Stamens 4-5, included; filaments ca. 0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.4 mm long, ovoid, glabrous; stamens vestigial in female flowers. Staminodes 4-5, ca. 0.75 mm long, subulate to ovate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, densely pubescent, style ca. 1 mm long after anthesis, included, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 3.5-6 cm long, broadly ovoid, ellipsoid or subglobose, apex obtuse or shortly beaked, base rounded or obtuse, smooth, glabrous. Seeds several, 2-2.8 cm long, laterally compressed, testa hard, smooth, shining, 1-1.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, 2-3 mm wide. Field characters. Tree to 17 m high with pale green flowers. Fruit maturing yellow or orange. Flowering Mar to May, and Sep, fruiting Mar to Jul.

description: Tree; young growth persistently short-pubescent with pale brown hairs, eventually glabrous, greyish, fissured, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous. (7-) 16.5-20 × (3.2-)5.7-6.2 cm, oblong or oblong elliptic, apex obtusely cuspidate, base obtuse to shortly attenuate, thinly coriaceous, glabrous, above, appressed pubescent below with pale brown indumentum, venation brochidodromous, marginal vein present, submarginal vein present, very close to the margin, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins (25-)40-50 pairs, widely spreading, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries strong, extending to the margin; tertiaries reticulate-areolate. Petiole 1-1.4 cm long, not or slightly channelled, densely pubescent. Fascicles axillary, several-flowered, some developing into short scaly brachyblasts 2-3 mm long. Pedicel 0.5-1 mm long, pubescent. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, 3-3.5 mm long, elliptic or ovate, obtuse, appressed pubescent outside, subglabrous within. Corolla 3-4 mm long, shortly tubular, tube 2-3 mm long, lobes five, ca. 1 mm long, ovate, margin truncate, glabrous. Stamens five, included, filaments ca. 0.75 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous; stamens reduced to a vestigial filament ca. 0.5 mm long in male. Staminodes five, 0.75-1 mm long, ovate or irregular, glabrous. Disk annular, pubescent, absent in female flowers, ovary globose, five-locular, pubescent; style ca. 1.5 mm long after anthesis, included, glabrous; style-head minutely lobed or simple. Immature fruit oblong, densely velutinous-villose, ca. 1 cm long. Seed not seen. Field characters. Tree to 20 m high and 20 cm diam., with pale green or cream-coloured flowers. Flowering Jun to Sep (Peruvian and Brazilian populations), immature fruit collected Jan, Mar and Jun (Brazil).

description: Tree; young shoots minutely appressed ferruginous-puberulous, becoming glabrous, greyish, smooth or slightly scaling, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 8.5-12 × 2.4-3.6 cm, narrowly elliptic or oblong-elliptic, apex narrowly acuminate, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, coriaceous, subglabrous, venation craspedodromous, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, marginal vein obscure, secondary and higher order venation obscure, finely striate, widely spreading. Petiole 0.9-1 cm long, slightly channelled, minutely appressed puberulous to glabrous. Ramiflorous fascicles 5-10-flowered. Pedicel 2.8-3 cm long, thickened below the flower, finely appressed ferruginous-puberulous. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals five, 0.9-1 cm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex rounded, minutely appressed ferruginous-puberulous outside, glabrous inside, margin ciliate. Corolla 1.9-2 cm long, cylindrical, tube ca. 1.75 cm long, lobes five, ca. 2.5 mm long, broadly oblong or suborbicular, apex rounded, erect; corolla tube appressed pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Stamens five, exserted; filaments ca. 8 mm long, geniculate in bud, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.5 mm long, oblong-lanceolate, glabrous. Disk a thick, densely pubescent annulus below the ovary. Ovary broad, five-lobed, densely pubescent, tapering gradually to the style; style ca. 7 mm long after anthesis, longitudinally five-ribbed, glabrous above; style-head simple. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Tree 25 m high, lower leaf surface yellowish-green. Flower greenish-yellow, in Apr.

description: Tree; young shoots minutely appressed puberulous with golden-brown hairs, soon glabrous, greyish-white, rough and slightly scaling, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 8-12 × 2.8-4.5 cm, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, apex narrowly attenuate or acuminate, base acute, margin strongly revolute, deeply sulcate along the midrib, coriaceous, glabrous, venation craspedodromous, secondary and higher order venation finely striate, obscure, shallowly ascending, slightly arcuate. Petiole 5-8 mm long, slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves, 2-15-flowered. Pedicel 2-4 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals five, ca. 2.5 mm long, suborbicular, apex rounded, glabrous. Corolla (immature) 1.5-2 mm long, lobes five, slightly exceeding the tube, shortly oblong, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, included; filaments ca. 0.4 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.6 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 0.75 mm long, lanceolate-subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, strigose, surmounted by a short, pubescent style and minutely lobed style-head. Fruit unknown.  Field characters. Tree to 30 m high with milky sap. The deeply sulcate midrib and strongly revolute leaf margin are characteristic. Flowers (immature) green, in Dec.

description: Frutex ca. 1 m altus. Ramuli juveniles pilis rigidis, flexis muniti. Folia decussata, 6-13 x 2.5-8.0 cm; lamina elliptica vel obovata, apice rotundata vel acuta, basi rotundata vel cuneata, supra hispidula, infra albo-tomentosa et pilis longis irregulariter flexis munita, costa et nervis lateralibus prominentibus; petiolus 2-12 mm longus, hispidulus, glandula munitus. Inflorescentia 10-15 x 4-7 cm, axibus pallido-tomentosis vel hispidulis et strato pilorum hirsuto munitis. Calycis lobi elliptici vel oblongi, 6-8 x 2.0-3.5 mm, extus tomentosi et strato pilorum villoso vel hirsuto muniti. Corolla 10-12 mm longa, infundibuliformis; lobi 5, plerumque oblongi, apice rotundati. Antherae ca. 2.5 mm longae. Fructus 1.6-2.2 x 2.2-3.0 cm.

description: Shrubs or small trees ca. 1 m tall. Young stem bearing crowded, tawny to ferrugineous, stiff, antrorse hairs to 1.5(-2) mm long, often distinctly stratified. Stipular lobes abaxially hirsute. Leaves decussate, 6-13 x 2.5-8.0 cm; lamina broadly elliptic to narrowly obovate, usually rounded, sometimes obtuse or acute at apex, rounded to cuneate at base, adaxially hispidulous, abaxially (between major veins) the pubescence highly variable, tending to be stratified, the shorter layer white-tomentose (when present), the longer layer consisting of irregularly bent, white hairs to 0.75(-1.5) mm long, the costa and lateral nerves bearing appressed or inclined pale hairs to 1.5 mm long, the higher order veins conspicuous, sometimes darkly colored and enclosing white-tomentose areoles; petiole 2-12 mm long. Inflorescence 10-15 x 4-7 cm; axes with pubescence usually in 2 layers, the shorter layer pale-tomentose to hispidulous, the longer layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs 0.5-1.5 mm long. Calyx lobes 6-8 x 2.03.5 mm, elliptic or oblong, externally with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer white-tomentose, the longer layer pale- to ferrugineous-villous or hirsute, the hairs to 1 (-1.5) mm long, internally white-sericeous with hairs to 0.75 mm long. Capsule 1.6-2.2 x 2.2-3.0 cm, ca. 0.5 cm thick, puberulent, with reddish cast (dry). Seed 1.0-1.3 (along diam. through hilum) x 1.5-2.0 cm, the wing ca. 2 mm wide.

description: Trees 5-20 m tall, the trunks to 60 cm diam.; bark gray, forming rectangular segments. Young stems striate or angled, with pubescence usually in 2 layers, the shorter layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-hispidulous, the longer layer brown-hirsute with hairs 1.0-2.5(-3.5) mm long. Stipular lobes 1.5-6.6 x 0.7-1.4 cm, narrowly deltoid or oblong, acuminate at apex, adaxially densely covered with tawny, antrorse hairs 0.5-2.0 mm long, abaxially with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer cinereous-hispidulous or strigillose, the longer layer ferrugineous-hirsute with hairs (0.6-)1.5-3.0(-4) mm long. Leaves 3-4-whorled, (8-)12-20(-23) x (3.5-)5-8(-9) cm; lamina elliptic to oblanceolate, rounded to obtuse (sometimes acute) at apex, rounded to (usually) cuneate at base, with (8-)l 1-16(-18) pairs of lateral nerves, adaxially bearing sparse, soft, white to straw-colored hairs (0.7-) 1.3-2.2(-2.7) mm long between major veins (this pubescence most concentrated along margins), sometimes lacking such hairs, then scabrous to hispidulous, the costa flush, densely cinereous- to ferrugineous- antrorse-hirsute with hairs to ca. 3 mm long, the lateral nerves sunken, abaxially usually tawny- to ferrugineous-pilose with hairs 0.7-2.2(-3) mm long, sometimes with shorter, cinereous to variously brown tomentose understory, the costa and lateral nerves prominent, with pubescence usually in 2 layers, the shorter layer consisting of minute, cinereous, appressed or erect hairs (this layer sometimes lacking), the longer layer tawny- (sometimes ferrugineous-) antrorse-hirsute with hairs 1-3 mm long, the tertiary veins prominulous and conspicuous; petiole 3-13 mm long, pubescent like corresponding side of costa, bearing abaxially near base strongly developed but highly variable glands, these single and U-shaped (with distance between apogee and tips often nearly as long as petiole), or 3-5 arranged in U-shaped pattern, sometimes borne on stalks to 5 mm long. Inflorescence ca. 7 cm tall, with 2-3 orders of branching; axes with pubescence usually in 2 layers, the shorter layer cinereous-tomentose, the longer layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-hirsute to pilose with hairs (0.6-)1.0-2.2(-3) mm long; distal bracts and bracteoles 3-14 x 0.5-2.5 mm, subulate, adaxially white villous or with appressed hairs (sometimes as described for abaxial surface), abaxially with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer white-villous, the longer layer ferrugineous-hirsute. Hypanthium broadly obconic, pubescent like inflorescence axes; calyx lobes (4-)5(-6), unequal, 4-7 (-9) x (1.5-)2-5-6) mm, oblong to lanceolate, rounded to acuminate at apex, sometimes apiculate, externally with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-tomentose, the longer layer ferrugineous- or (less frequently) cinereous-villous to hirsute with hairs to 2(-3) mm long, internally white-to ferrugineous-sericeous with hairs to 0.7(-1.3) mm long; corolla 1.0-1.5 cm long, funnelform, abruptly flared below middle of tube, conspicuously zygomorphic, externally pink, white- to variously brown-sericeous, the hairs to 2(-2.5) mm long, internally pink with red markings, yellow-bearded, otherwise glabrous, corolla lobes 3.5-8.0(-10) x 2-5 mm, oblong to broadly ovate, acute to rounded and often apiculate at apex; filaments inserted below the middle of tube, 2-4 mm long; anthers 2.5-3.0 mm long, narrowly elliptic, usually apiculate; style 3-9 mm long, glabrous; stigmatic lobes 0.5-1.0 mm long, papillose. Capsule (3.2-)3.8-5.0 x (3.5-)4.0-6.5 cm, 1.5-2.0 cm thick, dark brown and rugose on surface, variously puberulent to hirsute or glabrous. Seed 2.3-2.5 (along diam. through hilum) x 3.6-4.7 cm, light tan (dry), the wing 3-10 mm wide. Seedling with reniform cotyledons, these 2.7-4.0 x 5.0-6.7 cm, with palmate veins, glabrous; petiole 4-8 mm long, tawny-hirsute. Hypocotyl and epicotyl tawny-hirsute. Early foliage leaves short-petiolate, the lamina narrowly elliptic, adaxially white-hispidulous, the hairs longest (to 0.8 mm) on costa and along margin, abaxially white- to tawny-hispidulous, the hairs on costa antrorse.

description: Shrubs or small trees, 3-9 m tall, the trunks (rarely) to 50 cm diam. (smallest diam. for a fertile tree ca. 5 cm), with strongly ascending branches; bark dark gray in rectangular segments. Young stem striate to angled, glaucous, the epidermis dark-colored (often purple), glabrous or minutely puberulent. Stipular lobes 1.2-2.0 x ca. 0.5 cm, narrowly deltoid (sometimes slightly constricted at base), rounded to pointed at apex, adaxially densely covered with stiff, white, antrorse hairs 1-3 mm long, abaxially glaucous and glabrous. Leaves clustered at ends of branches, usually 3-whorled (sometimes decussate or 4-whorled), 7-21 x 3-11 cm, ovate to broadly elliptic, rounded to obtuse at apex, rounded to cuneate at base, with 11-18 pairs of lateral nerves, adaxially sometimes glaucous, minutely puberulent on costa and along margins, otherwise glabrous, the costa prominulous to slightly sunken, the lateral nerves usually slightly sunken, abaxially glaucous, glabrous except for minute puberulence sometimes on costa, this prominent and striate, the lateral nerves prominent, the higher order veins more or less flush; petiole (5-)8-12(-17) mm long, often glaucous, glabrous or minutely puberulent, bearing abaxially near base an oblong-elliptic to lunate, black gland 1.3-2.5(-4) x (3-)6-12 mm. Inflorescence strongly pedunculate, the peduncle glabrous or nearly so, tending to be glaucous, the distal axes densely white- to brown- (often rose-tinged) tomentose to hispid, the hairs to 0.5(-1.7) mm long. Flowers in crowded clusters; hypanthium broadly obconic to crateriform, pubescent like distal inflorescence axes, the pedicel inserted off-center; calyx lobes 4, not parted to top of ovary, 48 x 1.5-5.0 mm, oblong to narrowly deltoid (sometimes ovate), acute to acuminate at apex, externally red, white- or cinereous-tomentose along margins, otherwise white- to ferrugineous- (often rose-tinged) hirsute to tomentose, the hairs to 1(-1.5) mm long, internally densely covered with pale, antrorse hairs 0.2-0.5(-0.7) mm long; corolla narrowly tubular, only slightly narrower at base than at sinuses between lobes, slightly curved, slightly zygomorphic, 1.0-1.5(-2) cm long, externally pink, densely white- to tawny-hirsute, the hairs 0.5-2.0 mm long, internally pink with red spots, yellow-bearded, the tube minutely puberulent; corolla lobes 2-5(-6) x (1-)1.5-2.0 mm, spreading, oblong or deltoid, pointed at apex, filaments inserted slightly below middle of tube, 4-6 mm long; anthers 3-5 mm long, elliptic to oblong; style 8-11 mm long, glabrous or sparsely hispidulous; stigmatic lobes 1-2 mm long, broad, flattened, densely papillose. Capsule broader than long, (2-)2.2-3.7 cm x 2.5-4.7 cm, 0.5-1.5 cm thick, emarginate at both ends, pink when young, dark brown (dry), rugose, glabrous or bearing white to brown irregularly bent hairs. Seeds 1.3-2.0 (along diam. through hilum) x 2-3 cm, less than 1 mm thick, elliptic, conspicuously wrinkled on surface (dry), the narrow marginal wing 1-7 mm wide.

description: Young stem with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-hispidulous, the hairs of longer layer light tan to fulvous (occasionally ferrugineous), to 2(-3) mm long. Lamina adaxially strigose, the hairs to 0.6(-2.3) mm long, abaxially usually bearing white to tawny, variably bent hairs to 1.5 (-2.5) mm long; petiole usually with U-shaped gland abaxially near base, this (2-)3-6(-9) mm in longest dimension. Inflorescence axes with pubescence usually in 2 layers, the shorter layer densely white- to ferrugineous-tomentose to hispidulous, the longer layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-hirsute to pilose, the hairs to 1.8(-3) mm long. Calyx lobes (5-)6-8(-12) x l .5-2.5(-5) mm, acuminate to acute at apex; corolla (1.2-)1.5-2.0(-2.2) cm long; corolla lobes (4-)5-9(-ll) x 4-8 mm, rounded to acute at apex; filaments 4-8 mm long, inserted 2-6 mm from base of tube. Capsule 2.5-3.5(-4) x 2.8-3.5(-4) cm. Embryo 0.8-1.5 x 1.8-3.0 cm. n = 20(-21).

description: Young branches dark brown to near-black. Stipules unknown. Leaves 8-17 x 3-7 cm; lamina elliptic or oblanceolate, acute to rounded at apex, rounded to cuneate at base, adaxially glabrous (sometimes with variably bent, cinereous hairs to 1 mm long along margins), abaxially glabrous; petiole 0.5-2.0 cm long. Inflorescence 12-16 x 6-9 cm, with 2 orders of branching, glabrous (or bearing minute, appressed, cinereous to ferrugineous pubescence) at base; distal axes usually cinereous- to ferrugineous-tomentose to hispidulous beneath longer (to 1.5 mm), cinereous- to ferrugineous-hispid layer; distal bracts and bracteoles 1-3 mm long, linear to subulate, abaxially bearing appressed, variably colored hairs to 0.3 mm long, sometimes with ferrugineous-hirsute layer to 0.8 mm long. Hypanthium broadly obconic, pubescent like distal axes of inflorescence; calyx lobes 5, 6-9 x 2-4 mm, oblong-elliptic to lanceolate (rarely obovate), acute to acuminate at apex, externally cinereous- to ferrugineous-tomentose and usually bearing longer (to ca. 1 mm), scattered, tawny hairs, internally with white to tawny, antrorse hairs to 1.5(-2) mm long; corolla funnelform (8-) 10-16 mm long, externally white or pink, white- to tawny-hirsute, the hairs to 1.5(-2) mm long, internally spotted, yellow-bearded, otherwise glabrous; corolla lobes variably shaped, (4-)6-9 x 3-4 mm; anthers ca. 3 mm long, narrowly elliptic, apiculate. Fruit unknown. Seed ca. 2.8 cm in longest dimension.

description: Trees to 25 m tall, with trunks to 18 dm in diam. Young stem striate, glaucous, sometimes minutely puberulent. Stipules unknown. Leaves decussate, (10-)13-18(-25) x (2-)3-6(-8) cm; lamina narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate, acute to acuminate at apex, cuneate to caudate at base, with 13-16(-20) pairs of lateral nerves, adaxially scabrous between major veins, with white to tawny, parallel, bent hairs to 1(-1.5) mm long along margins, the costa flush to sometimes prominulous, this glabrous or bearing sparse, light-colored hairs to 1.5(-2.5) mm long, the lateral nerves and tertiary veins flush or nearly so, abaxially with white, waxy papillae, usually bearing white or tawny, appressed, minute (rarely to 0.5 mm long) hairs between major veins (sometimes on tertiary veins only but not between them), the lateral nerves similarly pubescent but the hairs generally to 0.3(-2.0) mm, the costa prominent, tawny  to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs to 1.5(-2.5) mm long; petiole 1.2-2.0(-2.5) cm long, glaucous, glabrous or abaxially pubescent like abaxial side of costa, bearing abaxially near base a U-shaped gland, this 1.3-4.0 mm long (between apogee and tips), 1-2 mm wide (across glandular strip). Inflorescence 10-15 x 4-10 cm, with 2-3 orders of branching; axes near base glaucous, glabrous or nearly so, distally densely rufous-hirsute, the hairs 0.5-1.5(-2) mm long, often with shorter, light-colored, tomentose or hispidulous layer; distal bracts and bracteoles 3-13 x ca. 1 mm, linear to subulate, adaxially white-hispidulous, abaxially pubescent like distal inflorescence axes. Hypanthium broadly obconic, pubescent like distal inflorescence axes; calyx lobes 5, 7-11 x 2-4 mm, narrowly deltoid, oblong, or lanceolate, obtuse to acuminate at apex, externally the pubescence in 2 layers, variably colored, the shorter layer tomentose, the longer layer consisting of parallel, bent hairs to 1(-1.6) mm long, internally white-hispid, the hairs to 1(-1.2) mm long; corolla (1.5-)2.0-2.6 cm long, zygomorphic, broadly funnelform, abruptly flared 4-5 mm from base, externally white- to tawny-hirsute, the hairs 1-3 mm long, often with shorter tomentum, internally red-streaked, yellow-bearded, sparsely tomentose at apex of some lobes, bearing pilose ring at base of tube, otherwise glabrous; corolla lobes 7-10(-12) x 4-8 mm, oblong to ovate, rounded to acute at apex, usually cuspidate; filaments inserted 4-8 mm from base of tube, 4-8 mm long; anthers 3-4 mm long, narowly elliptic or fusiform, apiculate; style 8-10 mm long, glabrous on basal half, white-hispidulous on distal half; stigmatic lobes 1.0-1.5 mm long, oblong, papillose.

description: Small trees to 4 m tall, the trunk to 8 cm diam. Young stem striate, tawny- to ferrugineous-hispid, becoming glabrous, the epidermis black (dry). Stipular lobes 6-9 mm long, abaxially densely ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs 0.4-1.4 mm long. Leaves 3-whorled, in tight clusters at ends of branches, 4-9 x 1.5-4.0 cm; lamina elliptic to oblong or obovate, retuse to rounded at apex, cuneate or caudate at base, the margin conspicuously revolute, with 10-12 pairs of lateral nerves, adaxially strigose to scabrous (sometimes hispidulous), the hairs cinereous to tawny, to 1 mm long, the costa sunken, bearing stiff, brown, parallel, bent hairs 0.5-1.5 mm long, the higher order veins prominulous, abaxially tawny-villous, the hairs to 0.6(-1) mm long, the costa prominent, with dense, ferrugineous, antrorse pubescence, the hairs 0.5-1.5 mm long, the lateral nerves and higher order veins prominent, forming conspicuous, dark brown reticulum; petiole 2-6 mm long, densely covered with tawny to ferrugineous, parallel, bent hairs, bearing abaxially near base a black, subquadrate to elliptic, horizontal gland ca. 1.0-1.5 x 1.5-3.0 mm. Inflorescence 6-8 x 2.5-5.0 cm, usually with 2 orders of branching, the pubescence dense, usually in 2 layers, the shorter layer a variably colored tomentum, the longer layer tawny- to ferrugineous-hispid, the hairs to 1(-1.3) mm long; bracts and bracteoles linear or subulate, 1.0-3.2 x 0.5-4.0 mm, adaxially bearing tawny to ferrugineous irregularly bent hairs, abaxially pubescent like inflorescence axes. Hypanthium obconic or broadly obconic, pubescent like inflorescence axes, calyx lobes (in bud) 5, 2-4 x 1-2(-3) mm, deltoid, externally pubescent like inflorescence axes, internally white-sericeous, the hairs ca. 0.5 mm long. Flower red with sweet aroma (fide Fróes).

description: Small trees, 3-8 m tall. Young stems purple-tinged, cinereous-strigillose to hispidulous. Stipules interpetiolar, caducous, ca. 3 x 0.5-1.0 cm, abaxially fer-rugineous-hispidulous, adaxially densely white-sericeous, the hairs 1.0-2.7 mm long. Leaves decussate or ternate; lamina 7.5-9.5 x 4-5 cm, elliptic or obovate, rounded or obtuse at apex, rounded to cuneate at base, with 13 or 14 pairs of lateral nerves; adaxial surface hispidulous, the hairs mostly with swollen bases and minute, costa and lateral nerves flush to slightly sunken, the revolute margin usually bearing stiff, parallel, bent, cinereous to tawny hairs, abaxially the major veins prominent and purple (dry), with stiff, bent or appressed, cinereous to tawny hairs to 0.6(-l .0) mm long, tertiary and higher order veins forming conspicuous brown (dry) reticulum enclosing white-tomentose areoles; petiole 4.5-6.0 mm long, purple to black, glaucous, with minute, cinereous hairs, bearing abaxially near insertion a dark-colored, subcircular, elliptic, or lunate gland 1.5-2.0 x 2.54.0 mm, the long axis perpendicular to long axis of petiole. Inflorescence terminal, pedunculate, dark red (alive), consisting of elongate central axis and dichasial branches; peduncle glabrous or nearly so, brownish-red (dry), other axes white-to ferrugineous-hispidulous, the most distal axes having darkest and longest hairs; bracts intergrading with foliage leaves near base of inflorescence, distal bracts and bracteoles sessile, subulate, 1.5-2.5 x 0.2-0.6 mm wide, cinereous- to tawny-tomentose (sometimes hispidulous). Hypanthium broadly obconic, bent at pedicel, pubescent like distal axes of inflorescence; calyx lobes 5, unequal, 6-7 x 1.5-2.8 mm, mostly lanceolate, some oblong or narrowly deltoid, mostly acute or acuminate at apex, externally cinereous- to tawny-tomentose and usually with longer, sparse, bent, stiff, brown hairs, internally sericeous to tomentose, the hairs white to light tan, to 0.8 mm long; corolla broadly funnelform, zygomorphic, white and spotted within, 10-12 mm long, externally densely hirsute with hairs to 2 mm long, those near base creamy to tawny, more distally ferrugineous, usually also with distinct, shorter, tomentose layer, this the only layer on margins of lobes, internally with light-colored, irregularly bent hairs on and below lobes; corolla lobes 5, 4-6 mm x 3-5 mm, mostly broadly ovate, some oblong or broadly deltoid, rounded to acute at apex; style glabrous except for sparse pubescence near apex, purple-tinged; stigma ca. 1 mm long, oblong. Capsule 2.0-2.5 x 2-3 cm, ca. 0.5 cm thick, emarginate at both ends, dark brown, rugose, bearing minute, white to brown, appressed or irregularly bent hairs. Seed 12-14 (along diam. through hilum) x 17-20 mm, ca. 1 mm thick, dark brown to black (dry), papillose near the hilum.

description: Small trees, 15-20 m tall, with flaking bark. Young stem striate, the epidermis tan to gray (dry), with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer cinereous-hispid-ulous, the longer layer sparsely cinereous- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs 1.02.7 mm long. Leaves 3-whorled, 13-27 x 3.5-9.5 cm; lamina elliptic to elliptic-oblanceolate, acute, obtuse, or rounded at apex, cuneate at base, with 16-21 pairs of lateral nerves, adaxially pilose (sometimes nearly glabrous), the hairs usually cinereous, sometimes brown, concentrated on costa, (0.5-)0.8-2.0(-3) mm long, the major veins mostly sunken, abaxially with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer white- to cinereous-tomentose, the longer layer white- to ferrugineous-villous, the hairs 0.5-1.8(-2.2) mm long, the costa prominent, this with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer cinereous-hispidulous or tomentulose, the longer layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs antrorse, (0.4-) 1.0-2.5(-3) mm long; petiole 3-10(-12) mm long, pubescent like corresponding side of costa, sometimes bearing abaxially near base an elliptic gland ca. 1.5 x 1 mm. Inflorescence ca. 16 x 22 cm; axes with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-tomentose, the longer layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-hispid or pilose, the hairs 0.7-1.8(-2.2) mm long. Calyx lobes tending to persist on fruit, 5-6 x 1.5-2.0(-4) mm, deltoid, obtuse to acuminate at apex, externally with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer white to ferrugineous-tomentose, the longer layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs (0.5-)1.0-1.5(-2) mm long, internally white- (to infrequently ferrugineous-) sericeous, the hairs to 0.2 (-0.3) mm long. Capsule 3.5-4.8 x 4.2-5.8 cm, ca. 1.5 cm thick, the surface red-brown, with irregular bumps and ridges, tawny-puberulent or tomentose. Seed ca. 2.5 (along diam. through hilum) x 4.2-4.7 cm, ca. 2 mm thick, light tan (dry), wrinkled.

description: Large trees. Young stems dark-colored (surface of epidermis), tawny- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs to 3(-4) mm long. Stipular lobes caducous, 0.5-5.0 x 0.5-1.2(-l.5) cm, ovate to lanceolate, acuminate at apex, adaxially with dense, creamy to tawny antrorse hairs to 2.2 mm long, abaxially sometimes glaucous, tawny- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs 1-3(-3.5) mm long. Leaves decussate, (7-) 11-20 x 2.8-7.0(-8) cm; lamina elliptic or infrequently obovate to oblanceolate, usually acuminate at apex, sometimes acute or rounded, cuneate or caudate at base, with (11-) 14-20(-23) pairs of lateral nerves, adaxially with pubescence usually in 2 layers, the shorter layer hispidulous or strigillose, the longer layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-strigose, the hairs 0.4-1.8(-2) mm long, usually villous along margins with hairs to 2.5 mm long, the costa flush or sunken and villous with hairs to 3.5 mm long, the lateral nerves slightly sunken, abaxially with conspicuous white excrescences and tawny to ferrugineous, soft, bent hairs 0.5-3.5 mm long, these most crowded, most spreading, and longest on major veins, the costa and lateral nerves prominent, the higher order veins inconspicuous; petiole (0.8-)1-2(-2.5) cm long, glaucous, densely tawny- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs 1.0-3.5 mm long, bearing abaxially near base a rectangular or lunate gland, this 1 x 2-5 mm. Inflorescence (8-)10-18 x 7-13 cm, with 2-3 orders of branching; axes ferrugineous-hirsute to pilose, the hairs to 2.5(-3) mm long, often with inconspicuous, shorter, white tomentum, the peduncle frequently near-glabrous and glaucous; distal bracts or bracteoles linear to subulate, 3-9 x 0.2-1.0 mm, adaxially with minute, variously bent, white hairs, sometimes with longer, brown-hispid layer, abaxially the pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer a tomentum, the longer layer tawny- to ferrugineous-hispid, the hairs 0.7-1.5 (-2) mm long. Hypanthium broadly obconic, pubescent like inflorescence axes; calyx lobes 5, (4-)6-9 x 0.8-4.5 mm, oblong to lanceolate, rounded to acuminate at apex, externally cinereous- to ferrugineous-tomentose and with scattered, longer (to 1.8 mm), ferrugineous hairs, internally white- to ferrugineous-tomentose or sericeous, bearing longer (0.5-2.0 mm) layer of light-colored, antrorse hairs; corolla 1.2-2.0 cm long, externally white, densely creamy- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs inclined, (1-)1.5-2.5(-3) mm long, white-tomentose at margins of lobes, internally with red markings, with yellow beard and pilose ring at base of tube, otherwise glabrous; corolla lobes 3-10 x 3-8 mm, broadly deltoid to ovate, acute to infrequently obtuse or rounded at apex; filaments inserted ca. 2 mm from base of tube, ca. 4 mm long; anthers 4.2-4.5 mm long, linear-elliptic, apiculate; style 5-8 mm long; stigmatic lobes ca. 1.5 mm long, elliptic, densely papillose; capsule 4.5-5.0 x 3.5-4.0 cm, ca. 0.8 cm thick, emarginate at both ends, dark brown or red-brown, bearing stiff-hairs to 0.3 mm long and sparse layer of longer (0.8-2.5 mm) hairs. Seeds D-shaped, 2.0-2.3 (along diam. through hilum) x 4.8-5.0 cm, papillose near hilum, the wing 1-8 mm across. Embryo ca. 1.7 (parallel to radicle) x ca. 3.3 cm.

description: Large trees with well differentiated trunks and crowns, 25-60 m tall, trunks to 1 m in diam.; bark scaly, dark brown. Young stem striate, often square, frequently purple-tinged, glaucous, usually glabrous. Stipular lobes caducous, (1-) 1.5-2.5(-6) x 0.3-1.0 cm, narrowly deltoid to lanceolate, adaxially densely white-hirsute, the hairs 1-3(-4) mm long, abaxially with white to fulvous antrorse hairs to 1,5(-2.5) mm long, frequently nearly glabrous, often glaucous. Leaves decussate, (7.5-) 10-17 x (2-)3-7 cm; lamina narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate, acute or acuminate at apex (rarely rounded), the base cuneate to caudate, sometimes obtuse, with (10-)13-16(-18) pairs of lateral nerves, revolute at margins, adaxially seabrous, strigillose, or nearly glabrous (often provided at margins with sparse, light-colored, bent hairs to 2 mm long, the costa sometimes with appressed, white hairs to 1 mm long), abaxially with white, waxy papillae and appressed white hairs ca. 0.2(-0.5) mm long, the costa prominent, sparsely white- or tawny-hirsute, the hairs to 1.5(-2.5) mm long, the lateral nerves prominulous; petiole (1-)1.2-2.0 (-3) cm long, glabrous or with sparse, white to tawny, bent hairs to 1.5 mm long, sometimes glaucous, provided abaxially near base with curved or rectangular gland, the glandular surface 1-2 mm wide. Inflorescence (8-) 11-17 x (5-)8-16 cm, with 2-4 orders of branching, usually branched near base, there glaucous and glabrous, distally with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer ashen-tomentose, the longer layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs 0.5-1.0(-1.5) mm long; distal bracts and bracteoles linear or subulate, 1.5-4.5 mm long, pubescent like distal axes of inflorescence or darker. Hypanthium broadly obconic, pubescent like distal axes of inflorescence; calyx lobes 5, 6-12 x 2-4 mm, oblong to lanceolate (sometimes narrowly deltoid), externally with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer a white tomentum, the longer hairs antrorse, to 0.8(-1.2) mm long, internally densely white-sericeous, the hairs to 1(-1.2) mm long; corolla broadly funnelform with lobes tending to be reflexed, scented, (1.3-)1.5-2.5 cm long, externally white or pink, white- or tawny-hirsute, the hairs 0.7-2.0 mm long, internally white with red streaks on lobes, red in throat, yellow-bearded, with pilose ring at base of tube, otherwise glabrous; corolla lobes (5-)8-14(-17) x (3-)4-8 mm, usually oblong to obovate, usually rounded to acute at apex, sometimes acuminate, usually with irregularly notched margins; filaments pink, 5-7 mm long, flattened, inserted near base of tube; anthers 3-4 mm long, narrowly elliptic, cordate at base, acuminate or apiculate at apex; style 8-10 mm long, glabrous; stigmatic lobes ca. 1.5 mm long, tapered, curled, papillose. Capsule 46 x 3.5-5.5 cm, ca. one cm thick, dark brown, warty and rugose, brown-puberulent. Seed 1.8-2.7 (along diam. through hilum) x 4-6 cm, the wing 0.2-1.4 cm wide. Embryo 1.0-1.5 (parallel to radicle) x 2.5-4.2 cm, the radicle completely invested by cotyledons. Seedlings with elliptic-oblong cotyledons, these 4.5-5.5 x 5-7 cm, coriaceous, puberulent abaxially on major veins, otherwise glabrous; petiole puberulent. Hypocotyl bearing tawny, antrorse hairs to l(-2) mm long, these concentrated and longest near cotyledons. Epicotyl densely ferrugineous-hispid, the hairs to 0.8(-1.2) mm long. Early foliage leaves sessile, elliptic, acuminate at apex, cuneate at base, adaxially the costa bearing sparse, bent, tawny hairs to 1.5 mm long, the lateral nerves sunken, abaxially with minute, light-colored, appressed hairs, the major veins prominent, bearing longest hairs (to 0.8 mm).

description: Arbor ca. 30 m alta. Ramuli juveniles fulvo- vel ferrugineo-hirsuti et tomentosi strato pilorum brevium muniti. Stipulae anguste laneolatae, ca. 6 cm longae, fulvovel ferrugineo-hirsutae et tomentosae strato pilorum brevium munitae. Folia ternata, 14-21 x 4.5-6.0 cm; lamina plerumque oblanceolata, apice rotundata, basi cuneata vel caudata, supra cinereo- vel fulvo-hispidula vel strigosula, costa hirsuta, infra ferrugineo- vel fulvo-pilosa, nervis principalibus prominentibus et antrorsus hirsutis. Petiolus ca. 1 cm longus, hirsutus et tomentosus strato pilorum brevium munitus. Axes inflorescentiae pallide- vel ferrugineo-hirsuti vel hispiduli et tomentosi strato pilorum brevium muniti. Fructus immaturus rugosus, ferrugineo-tomentosus et sparsim fulvo-hispidus.

description: Trees, ca. 30 m tall, the trunks 50 cm diam. Young stem striate and angled, with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer densely tomentose-hispidulous, the longer layer tawny- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs 0.5-2.0(-3) mm long. Stipular lobes to 6 x 1 cm, narrowly lanceolate, abaxially with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-tomentose, the longer layer tawny-to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs (0.5-) 1 -3(-3.5) mm long. Leaves 3-whorled, (14-)17-21 x 4.5-6.0 cm; lamina narrowly oblanceolate, chiefly rounded, apically, cuneate to caudate at base, with 17-22 pairs of lateral nerves, adaxially cinereous- to tawny-strigillose to hispidulous, most hairs with swollen bases, the costa sunken, bearing crowded, cinereous to ferrugineous, parallel or irregularly bent hairs to 2(-2.5) mm long (these highly variable), the lateral nerves slightly sunken, abaxially sparsely tawny- to ferrugineous-pilose, the hairs to 1.5(-2) mm long, the costa and lateral nerves prominent, bearing crowded, tawny to ferrugineous, parallel, bent hairs to 2.2(-3) mm long; petiole ca. 1 cm long, with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer tomentose-hispidulous, the longer layer tawny-hirsute, bearing abaxially near the base a small black (dry) gland 2-3 mm wide. Axes of inflorescence with pubescence mostly in 2 layers, the shorter layer cinereous- to ferrugineous-tomentose to hispidulous, the longer layer predominant on distal axes, tawny- to ferrugineous-hirsute, the hairs to 3 mm long. Immature fruit taller than broad, the surface irregularly rugose and warted, with pubescence in 2 layers, the shorter layer densely ferrugineous-tomentose, the longer layer sparsely tawny-hispid, the hairs 0.5-2.5(-3) mm long.

description: Trees to 20 m tall, to 40-50 cm dbh, without buttresses; bark smooth, pale brown; wood brownish yellow, hard. Leafy branchlets 2.5-5 mm thick, terete to compressed, glabrous to puberulent, cinnamoneous; older branches glabrate, terete, brown; lenticels sparse, whitish, linear. Stipules free at base, contorted in bud, narrowly triangular, acuminate, appressed puberulent to gray-sericeous outside, glabrous with basal colleters inside, 15-27 × 2-4 mm, readily caducous, deep-green, leaving a white scar encircling the stem above petiole attachments, 0.5-1 mm wide. Leaves (10-)13-30 × 4-10 cm, LAV = 2.5:1 to 3:1, elliptic to oblong-obovate, acute-decurrent at base, acute and acuminate at apex, the narrowly triangular acumen 1.5-2.5 cm long; dark green above, pale green below, foliaceous to thinly coriaceous; drying olive-green to pale-brown, stiff-chartaceous to coriaceous; glabrous above and below; primary, secondary and tertiary veins glabrous to very sparsely puberulent below; secondary veins 10-18 each side; tertiary veins subparallel; petioles 10-26 mm long, 1-2 mm thick, adaxially concave, glabrous; domatia absent or a few puberulent hair. Inflorescences corymbiform panicles, with opposite decussate branches, short-pedunculate, 5.5-11 cm long; basal branches 2-8 cm long, lateral branches 2-5 pairs; rachis basally terete to subterete, decussately compressed distally, without lenticels, rachis and branches densely puberulent; flowers in terminal few-flowered cymules. Flowers sessile to short-pedicellate; pedicels to 1.5 mm long, puberulent; hypanthium obovoid, faintly bilobed, 0.50.9 × 0.6-0.7 mm, puberulent. Calyx minutely cupular, short-lobed, 1-1.5 × 1.5-2 mm, glabrous; lobes narrowly triangular, 0.6-1.7 × 0.3-0.6 mm; several flowers of the same inflorescences with one calyx lobe expanded into small calycophyll. Calycophylls 7-13 × 3-5 mm, blades elliptic to ovate, with the adaxial side covered with a thick mat of glandular hairs (0.2-0.4 mm long). Corolla tubular-campanulate, shortly lobed, the lobes reflexed at anthesis, 3-4 mm long, glabrous throughout, white to cream-white; tube short cylindrical, 2-3 × 0.5-0.6 mm; lobes 5, 0.5-0.7 × 0.4-0.6 mm, oblong-linear, round at apex. Stamens 5, exserted well above the corolla, equal in length, attached 1-1.5 mm from the base of the tube; filaments 4-5 mm long, slender-terete, basally flattened and short-pubescent; anthers narrowly elliptic, 1-1.5 × 0.3-0.4 mm, dorsifixed near the middle. Pollen exine irregularly reticulate. Style exserted, elongating only after anthers dehiscence, 3-5 mm long, terete, glabrous; style branches clavate, reflexed, 0.5-1 mm long, stigmatic surface minutely papillose. Capsules sessile to short-pedicellate, strongly bilobed the two sides globose, rounded at base and at apex, 3-4.5 × 4.5-6 mm, without lenticels, rust-brown, glabrous throughout; disk not exceeding the calyx; disk septicidal dehiscence absent. Seeds hemi-elliptic in outline, 2.2-4.5 × 1.5-2.5 mm, with lateral wing with entire margin; seed embryo about one half the size of the seed outline.

description: Stems solitary, very shortly aerial, 10-15(-100) cm long, with prominent roots visible at base. Leaves 4-9, spreading; sheath closed, not forming a crownshaft, 20-30 cm long including a ligule 1-2 cm long; petiole 0.24-1 m long; rachis 1-1.2 m long; pinnae 11-15 per side, regularly spaced, alternate, linear-lanceolate, aristate, horizontally spreading in the same plane, with prominent midvein, lacking scales and punctations abaxially; basal pinna 22-37 x 0.5-2.5 cm; middle pinnae 32-49 x 2.5-5.5 cm; apical pinna 17-27 x 1-1.5 cm. Inflorescences interfoliar, erect in bud and at anthesis; peduncle 67-98 cm long, 0.5 cm diam., terete, with a few, brown, appressed scales; prophyll 18-45 cm long, 1.5-2 cm diam., flattened; peduncular bract 0.7-1 m long including a 2-3 cm long umbo, 1-1.5 cm diam., ± terete; rachis absent; rachilla 27-51 cm long, 3 mm diam. at anthesis, 4 mm diam. in fruit, with dense to loose clusters of intertwined, whitish, flexuous, hairs to 0.3 mm long; triads slightly sunken in rachilla, very closely spaced; flowers in triads for ca. 2/3 the length of rachilla, paired or solitary staminate distally; triad bracteole raised, rounded; first flower bracteole apiculate, second and third flower bracteoles prominent, apiculate, 0.7 mm high; staminate flowers 4-5 mm long; sepals connate into a prominently 3-lobed cupule, 2-3 mm long; petals lanceolate, 4-5 mm long; filaments slightly connate proximally, free distally, 3 longer (3.5 mm long) and 3 shorter (2.5 mm long); anthers 3 mm long; pistillode trifid, 1-2 mm long; pistillate flowers 4.5 mm long; sepals deltate, 3 mm long; petals deltate, 4 mm long; fruits ellipsoid-oblong, 0.9-1 cm long, 0.5-0.6 cm diam., the stigmatic remains apical; epicarp black; seeds ± globose, ca. 5 mm diam.; endosperm deeply ruminate; eophyll pinnate with short rachis.
