description: Trees, to 10 m tall, dioecious. Stems: green, smooth but covered with conspicuous lenticels, trunk 30-40 cm in diam. (dbh), bark peeling in yellow, papery sheets; latex copious, cloudy in younger shoots but red in older branches. Leaves: deciduous, stipules obsolete, petioles 1-4 cm long and 0.5-0.8 mm in diam., blades ovate-oblong, unlobed, 7-8 x 1.2-3.4 cm, membranous, base cuneate, margins entire (not glandular), apex rounded, venation pinnate, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral, staminate many-flowered cymes, peduncles 3.5-5.5 cm long; pistillate solitary, bracts linear, 0.5 mm long; pedicels 2-3 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate, 1.2-1.5 x 0.6-0.8 mm, distinct, margins entire, apex acute to rounded, glabrous on adaxial surface and pubescent on abaxial; corollas subglobose, dark red, petals 5.8-7 x 0.8-1.5 mm, connate along nearly entire length, apex round, pubescent at apex on adaxial side and glabrous on abaxial; stamens (9-)10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 1.5-2 mm long and distinct, those of inner series 4-4.5 mm and connate to ca. ½ of length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 1.6-2.3 x 0.7-1 mm; petals 5.9-7.5 x 0.7-1.8 mm; carpels 2(-3), styles 4.8-5.2 mm, connate along entire length. Capsules: laterally ellipsoid, bilocular and distinctly bilobed, 2.5-2.8 cm x 1.6-1.9 mm, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: brown with yellow spots, spherical, ca. 1 cm in diam., caruncle vestigial.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, to 3 m tall, monoecious. Stems; terete, grayish or reddish brown, glabrous or hispidulous; short shoots present; latex clear in younger stems but cloudy in older. Leaves: deciduous, borne on nodes but sometimes clustered on short shoots; stipules obsolete, petioles 0.5-2.5 cm long and 0.3-0.5 mm in diam.; blades ovate, undivided, 2-4 x 1-3 cm, chartaceous, base cordate, margins ciliate, apex acuminate, venation palmate with 5 noticeably raised veins from base, sparingly tomentose to glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal, many-flowered cymes, often with a coflorescence, peduncles 1-1.2 cm, paracladia hispidulous; bracts oblong-lanceolate to oblanceolate, 4-5 x 1.2-1.3 mm, glabrous or tomentulose; pedicels 0.5-11 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals lanceolate, 2.5-4.8 x 1.2-2 mm, distinct, margins entire, apex obtuse or subacute, variously glabrous or sparsely pubescent on both surfaces; corollas tubular-campanulate, pale green; petals 5.5-6 x 1.5-2 mm, coherent ca. 1/3 of length, oblong, glabrous abaxially but pubescent adaxially in lower half; disk glands nearly square in outline, 0.5-0.6 mm high; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), outer filaments 1 mm long, mostly distinct, inner filaments 3-4 mm long, connate ca. ½ of length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals elliptic to lanceolate, 5.5-6.5 x 2.5-3.8 mm; petals 6.5-7 x 1.8-2.5 mm, coherent ca. 1/3 of length, hirsute adaxially; disk somewhat rounded; carpels 3, smooth, glabrous, sharply carinate; styles 3 mm long, connate ca. ½ of length. Capsules: ± spherical, 1.2-1.4 cm in diam, smooth, 3-lobed with a distinct ridge on each lobe, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: brownish, ellipsoidal, small 1-1.2 x 2.5-4 mm; caruncle prominent and deeply lobed.

description: Trees, to 8 m tall, dioecious. Stems: green, branches numerous, lenticels conspicuous, few short shoots, trunk diam. 40 cm (dbh), bark peeling in large, yellow, papery sheets revealing the shiny green trunk beneath; latex copious during active growth and cloudy but yellow and viscous in older branches. Leaves: deciduous, stipules caducous; petioles subsessile, 5-10 mm long and 1-1.4 mm diam.; blades mostly on nodes but some on short shoots, widely ovate to obovate, 7-11 x 7.2-12.5 cm, ± coriaceous, base cuneate, margins entire but mostly with 2 pairs of stipitate glands near base, apex round, venation pinnate, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral with continued growth, staminate many-flowered cymes with peduncles 4.8-7.5 cm, pistillate solitary, bracts 0.8-1 mm; pedicels 2-5 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate, 1.4-1.5 x 1.1-1.3 mm, distinct, margins entire, apex acute, glabrous on adaxial surface and pubescent on abaxial; corollas urceolate, white, petals 8.5-11 x 1.5-3 mm, connate for nearly entire length, apex round, glabrous on abaxial side but sometimes with a few short hairs on adaxial; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 2.5-3 mm long and distinct but those of inner series 4.5-6.0 mm and connate for nearly entire length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 4.2-5.1 x 1.5-1.9 mm; corollas subglobose, petals 7.5-10 x 1.8-3 mm; carpels 2(-3 or rarely 4); styles 2(-3)4-5 mm long, connate to ca. ¾ of length. Capsule: mostly bi- but rarely tri- or quartilocular, ovoid and distinctly angular, 2.8-3.5 x 1.6-2 cm, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: yellow-brown, spherical, 1.2 cm in diam., caruncle vestigial.

description: Shrubs, 2-3 m tall. Stems: brown, intricately spreading branches, glabrous, short shoots common; latex cloudy in younger stems but blood-red in older and lower parts. Leaves: deciduous, exstipulate; sessile; borne primarily at terminus of short shoots; blades linear, 9-10 x 2-2.5 mm, chartaceous, base cuneate, apex rounded, venation pinnate, margins entire, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces. Inflorescences: on short shoots, staminate few in a group, pistillate mostly solitary but may be 2 or 3 in a group; bracts minute; pedicels 1-2 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate, 2 x 1.2 mm, free, margins entire, oblong, apex acute, glabrous on adaxial surface and sparsely pubescent on abaxial; corollas tubular, white, petals linear-spathulate, 4 x 1.3 mm, distinct, imbricate, apex round and reflexed, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 10, diadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series ca. 2.5 mm long and mostly free, those of inner series 3.5 mm and connate to ca. ¾ of length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but campanulate-tubular, sepals 4 x 1.3 mm and petals 5 x 1.5 mm long; carpel 1, glabrous; style 1 (-2), ca. 3 mm long. Capsules: unilocular or rarely bilocular, spherical, 0.9 cm long and wide, shortly apiculate, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: brownish black, spherical, 0.8 cm in diam., caruncle vestigial.

description: Trees, 2-10 m tall, dioecious. Stems: gray-brown, branches succulent, numerous suckers arising from the roots, trunk diameter ca. 20 cm; latex yellow and copious in younger shoots and branches but reddish in lower part of trunk. Leaves: deciduous, stipules lanceolate, caducous, 3 mm when present; petioles 4-8 cm long and 1.2-3 mm in diam.; blades orbicular to ovate-cordate, often shallowly 3- to 5-lobed, 10.5-22 x 9-16.5 cm, ± coriaceous, base cordate, apex broadly acute to acuminate, venation palmate with 5-7(-9) primary veins, margins entire, bright green on adaxial side, densely brownish pubescent on abaxial. Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral, staminate many-flowered cymes, main florescences 7-7.5 cm long and coflorescences 2-6.5 cm long; pistillate solitary; bracts linear-lanceolate, 2-7 mm long; pedicels 1-4 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.8-4 x 1.6-1.8 mm, margins entire, apex broadly acute, glabrous on adaxial surface but pubescent on abaxial, corollas urceolate, white, petals ovate-lanceolate, 7-8 x l.5-2.8 mm, connate to ca. ¾ of length, apex round, tomentose on adaxial surface and glabrous on adaxial, stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), aments of outer series 3-4 mm, connate ca. ½ of length and those of inner series 4.5-5 mm and connate or entire length; anthers 1.1-1.7 mm long. Pistillate flowers; like staminate but sepals foliaceous, 9-12 x 3.5-4 mm, distinct petals 12.5-14 x 4.5-5.5 mm, distinct, carpels 3, styles 3, 1.8-2.3 mm long, connate to ca. ¾ of length. Capsules: ovoid, 1.9-2.5 x 1.5-1.8 cm, ribbed, ±  pubescent, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: spherical, 9-10 mm in diam., caruncle vestigial.

description: Shrubs or small trees, 4-7 m tall, dioecious. Stems: branches reddish brown, bark smooth white, exfoliating, latex watery and somewhat cloudy in younger shoots but reddish in older branches; arrested short shoots present and with few leaves. Leaves: deciduous; stipules caducous; petioles 1.5-5.5 cm long and 0.5-0.8 mm in diam.; blades widely cordiform to orbicular, 1.5-4 x 1.5-3.5 cm, membranous, base reniform to rotund, margins entire, apex acute, venation palmate with 3-5 primary veins, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal, staminate few-flowered, paniculate cymes; peduncles 3-4 cm long; bracts linear, 2-3 mm long, margins entire, sparsely pubescent; bracteoles 1-1.5 mm long; pedicels 2 mm long; pistillate flowers few. Staminate flowers: sepals lanceolate, 1.3-3 x 1.1-1.7 mm, distinct, apex round, margins entire, pubescent on both surfaces; corollas urceolate, rose-colored, petals connate nearly to top, 6.5-8 x 1.6-1.9 mm, glabrous on both surfaces, apex round; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5+5), filaments of outer series 2 mm long and connate to ½-¾ of length, those of inner series 3.5 mm and connate to ca. ¾ of length; anthers 0.8 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 2.4-4.5 mm x 1.3-2.1 mm, corollas 10-11 x 4-5 mm; carpels 2, glabrous; styles ca. 1.5 mm; connate to ¾ or more of length. Capsules: 2(-3)-lobed, pyriform, 2.5 x 1.5 cm, tardily dehiscent, glabrous. Seeds: black with yellow markings, ellipsoidal, 1.4 x 0.9 cm, caruncle vestigial.

description: Shrubs, to 1.5 m tall. Stems: reddish when young but pale to dark brown when older, glabrous, bark thin and papery, ± sparsely branched, ± succulent; trunk reddish brown, somewhat fissured; latex reddish, viscid. Leaves: persistent; stipules branched, stipitate glands, 3-4 mm long; petioles 2-5 cm long and 0.4-0.5 mm in diam.; blades rhomboid, 3(-5)-lobed, 2.6-5.5 x 3-4.7 cm, lobes 1-2.8 cm wide, base cordate to cordate-truncate, membranous, margins dentate, gland-tipped, apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; venation palmate with 3-5 primary veins. Inflorescences: terminal, few-flowered cymes; coflorescences present and nearly equal to main florescences, peduncles 1-6 cm long; bracts linear-lanceolate, 3-7 mm long, margins with stipitate glands; pedicels 2-7 mm. Stammate flowers: sepals ovate, 4-5 x 1.6-2.5 mm, margins beset with uncommonly long, stipitate glands, apex acute or infrequently rounded, glabrous on both surfaces, corollas cupulate, pinkish red, petals oblong-obovate, 5 5-6.5 x 2.5-3.5 mm, distinct, apex obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 10, mostly uniseriate but sometimes biseriate early, filaments 3.5-4.5 mm long, connate to ca. ¾ of length, disc glands distinct, ± spherical. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals linear-lanceolate, 6.5-9 x 3.5-4.2 mm, petals 7.5-10 x 3.5-4.5 mm; carpels 3, ovary glabrous, style 2.4-3 mm, connate ½ to ¾ of length. Capsules, spherical, 1-1.3 cm in diam., glabrous, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: cream with brown mottling, oval, 8-10 x 5-6.5 mm, caruncle prominent and lobed.

description: Shrubs, 1-4.5 m tall, dioecious. Stems: whitish gray, smooth, erect, younger branches with velvety, tawny reddish tomentum, ± succulent, leaf scars crescentshaped; latex copious, clear and watery in younger shoots but cloudy yellowish in older branches. Leaves: deciduous, reddish brown when young becoming dull green when mature, clustered mostly at stem apices; stipules diminutive, persistent, lanceolate and densely pubescent when present on actively growing shoots; petioles green, pubescent, 9-22 cm long and 1-1.6 mm in diam. blades orbicular-ovate, entire to shallowly 3(-5)-lobed, 10-19 x 11-22 cm, chartaceous, base roadly cordate, apex acute-acuminate, venation palmate with 5(-7) primary veins, margins entire, densely villous-pubescent on both surfaces. Inflorescences: lateral in leaf axes, staminate few-flowered, loosely branched, compound cymes, peduncles 7-11 cm long; pistillate solitary or few-flowered, bracts lanceolate-ovate, 6-14 x 3-4 mm, densely covered with tawny tomentum on both surfaces; pedicels ca. 1-2 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate, 2-2.4 x 1.4-1.6 mm, connate at base, margins hirsute, villous on both surfaces, corollas campanulate, yellowish green, petals ovate, 4-4.3 x 2.2-2.5 mm, distinct, imbricate, apex markedly reflexed, villous on abaxial surface, glabrous on adaxial; stamens 10, monadelphous biseriate, outer filaments ca. 2 mm long, mostly free, inner filaments ca. 2.2 mm long and connate ¾ of length; anthers ca. 1 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals oblong-ovate, ± foliaceous, 5.5-6.5 x 1.6-2 mm, apex acute-rostrate, margins beset with hirsute indumentum, villous on both surfaces; petals ovate, 5-5.5 x 2.4-2.7 mm, connate to ca. ½ of length; ovary glabrous, styles slender, ca. 1.5 mm long, connate 2/3 of length. Capsules: green with reddish carinate ribs, ± drupaceous, ellipsoid, 2.5 x 1.2 cm, apiculate, glabrous, and tardily dehiscent. Seeds: dark brown, oblong-ellipsoid, 1.8- 1.5 x 0.8-1 cm, caruncle vestigial.

description: Shrubs, 1-2 m tall. Stems: gray, erect, sparsely branched, caudiciform and succulent, bark peeling in papery sheets, covered with persistent, hardened, outwardly spinose stipules; latex clear in younger shoots but cloudy to reddish in older branches. Leaves: persistent or semievergreen (leaves abscise in response to drought or low temperatures), stipules persistent, branched glands that become indurate with age, 3-4 mm; petioles stout, 16-28 cm long and 2.5-4.5 mm in diam.; blades orbicular, peltate, shallowly 3- to 5-lobed, 14-22.5(-32) x 8.5-19(-23.5) cm, lobes 6-10 cm wide, membranous to ± coriaceous, margins entire, base orbicular, apex acute-acuminate, venation palmate with 7-9 primary veins from center, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal, compact, capitate cymes, peduncles stout, (6-)12.5-36 cm, paracladia orange-red, bracts 1-3 mm long, margins entire, glabrous; pedicels orange-red, 1.5-3 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate, 1.5-2.5 x 1-1.2 mm, connate to ca. ½, margins entire, apex round, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas rotate-cupulate, orange-red, petals 6-8(-12) x 2.5-3 mm, distinct, obovate, apex round, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens (6-)8(-9 tol4), monodelphous-uniseriate, 3-4 mm long, distinct. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 1.5-2.7 x 1.3-1-7 mm, distinct; petals 7.0-11.0 x 2.5-3.2 mm; carpels 3, styles 1-1.1 mm long, distinct. Capsules: spherical, 1.3-1.5 cm diam., glabrous, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: dark to golden brown, oval, 9-11 x 5.5-6 mm, caruncle prominent.

description: Trees or large shrubs to 10 m tall, dioecious. Stems: yellowish brown, sparsely branched, young branches densely tomentose, soft and succulent, with chambered pits, spreading, densely tomentose early, not peeling, latex copious, cloudy in younger shoots but reddish in older parts of plant; trunk to ca. 30 cm diam. (dbh.). Leaves: deciduous; stipules linear to lanceolate, 1.5-2(-6) mm long; petioles 8-14.5(-26) cm long and 2.5-4.5(-7) mm in diam., glabrous; blades peltate, orbicular, 13-36 x 9-27 cm, reddish when young, with 3-5 shallow lobes, 6-20 cm wide, membranous or ± chartaceous, base shallowly cordate, margins entire (not glandular, except on eophylls), apices broadly acute to acuminate, venation palmate, with 7-9 primary, pinkish red veins radiating from the center and noticeably thickened and raised on abaxial side; sparsely pubescent on veins on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral with continued growth; staminate large and with numerous paracladia but pistillate much smaller and with few paracladia; peduncles (5-)l 1-19 cm long in staminate and 2-9 cm long in pistillate; bracts ovate-lanceolate, 1-7 mm long; pedicels 2-3 mm long in staminate flowers and 4.5-10 mm long in pistillate. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate, sparingly pubescent on both surfaces but sometimes glabrous on adaxial surface, apex round, margins entire, free, 2.5-3.5 x 15-2.2 mm wide; corollas tubular-campanulate, white; petals 7-8 x 2.5-3 mm, connate to ¾ of length, apex round, strongly reflexed, tomentose on adaxial surface and glabrous on abaxial; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 2.5-4 mm long and connate ca. ½ of length, those of inner series 4-5 mm and connate ca. ¾ of length, anthers 1.1-1.5 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals foliaceous, 9-13 x 3-7 mm; petals 8-10 x 4-5 mm; carpels 3 or exceptionally 4 in the uppermost, central flower; styles 3, 1.5-2 mm long, connate ¼-½ of length. Capsules: 3-locular (or rarely 4-locular), oval, 27-3.8 x 2.5-3 cm, narrower on top than on bottom. Seeds: light brown with darker mottling, nearly spherical, 1.8-2.2 cm diam., caruncle vestigial.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Trees, 3-10 m tall, dioecious. Stems: gray-green, covered with whitish waxy bloom, much-branched, bark exfoliating in yellow, papery sheets showing smooth, green trunk and numerous lenticels beneath; latex copious, yellow, dries powdery. Leaves: deciduous, lateral on nodes but sometimes clustered on branch tips, stipules rotund, ca. 0.5 mm; petioles 1.5-2 cm long and 1-1.3 mm in diam.; blades lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 9.8-13 x 2-3.2 cm, base cuneate, membranous, margins entire, apex acute and typically slightly reflexed, venation pinnate, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral, bracts 2-2.3 mm, staminate many-flowered cymes 3-6 cm, pistillate solitary; pedicels 1.9-2.5(-3.1) mm. Staminate flowers; sepals ovate-lanceolate, 2-2.3 mm, margins entire; corollas subglobose, rose-colored, petals 9.5-11 x 1.6- 2.2 mm; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 4.1-4.4 mm long and connate to ca. ½-2/3 of length, inner series 6.8-7.1 mm and connate ca. ¾ of length. Pistillate flowers: sepals somewhat unequal, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 4.4-8.3 x 2.2-2.6(-3.5) mm; corollas urceolate, petals gamopetalous, 11.6-14 mm; carpels (2-)3, connate ca. ¾ of length. Capsules: yellow when mature, spherical, 2.5 cm in diam., glabrous, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: spotted brown, oval, 1.8-2.1 x 1.6-1.8 cm, caruncle vestigial.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Subshrubs to 50 cm tall. Stems: green, herbaceous, from a subterranean caudex; latex clear and somewhat viscid. Leaves: deciduous with cauline stems, stipules branched, stipitate glands, 4-6 mm long; petioles 0.8- 1.5 long and 1.5-2 mm in diam., covered with stipitate glands; blades elliptic, only exceptionally lobed, 11-15 x 5.5-7.5 cm, membranous to ± chartaceous, base acutely rounded to cordate, margins glandular-ciliate, apex acute, venation pinnate, pubescent on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal, few-flowered cymes, main florescences 5-8 cm and coflorescences 2.5-5.5 cm; peduncles 2.3-6.8 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 6-12 mm, entire or with few glands; pedicels ca. 2-5 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals lanceolate, 3.5-6 x 1.2-1.6 mm, distinct or connate only at base, margins glandular-ciliate, apex acuminate, glabrous on adaxial surface but pubescent on abaxial; corollas campanulate, greenish yellow to yellow, petals obovate, 7-10 x 1.7-2.9 mm, distinct, imbricate, apex round and somewhat reflexed; stamens 8 (-9), diadelphous-biseriate (5 + 3), outer series 4-5.5 mm long and connate ½-¾ of length, inner series 4.5-6 mm long and connate ¾ of length, anthers ca. 2 mm long; basal glands fusiform. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 4.5-6.5 x 1.4-1.7 mm, tomentose abaxially but glabrous abax-ially; petals 7-9 mm x 1.8-2.8 mm; carpels 3, styles ca 4 mm long, connate only at base or distinct. Capsule: oblong-ellipsoid, distinctly 3-lobed, 1.1 x 0.9 cm, glabrous, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: yellowish, mottled light brown, oval, 6.0-7.5 x 4-5 mm, caruncle prominent, lobed.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, to 2 m tall. Stems: sparsely branched, young shoots pilose, bark reddish brown becoming grey with age; latex clear to cloudy. Leaves, semi-deciduous; stipules caducous, minutely setaceous when present early; petioles 3-5.5 cm long and ca. 2 mm in diam; blades deeply divided nearly to base, 1-9 but usually 3-5 linear-lanceolate segments, sometimes lower segments appearing shortly hastate, 2-14.5 x 1-2.5 cm; membranous-subcoriaceous, base cuneate to cordate depending on lobing, margins mostly entire but sometimes distantly glandular-denticulate near base, apex obtuse or nearly pungent, veins palmate with 1 vein in each segment; sparsely pilose on abaxial side but nearly glabrous on adaxial. Inflorescences: terminal, compact cymes, bracts lanceolate, glandular-denticulate, ca. 3 mm long and 1 mm wide; peduncles 7-11 cm long; pedicels 4-6.5 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals green, ovate-lanceolate, 3.5-4.5 mm long, connate to ca. ½ of length, margins entire, apex obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas red-scarlet, rotate, petals spathulate, 0.8-1.2 x 0.5-0.7 cm; distinct but imbricate on lower ½, apex obtuse, adaxial surface villous at base; stamens 10, diadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series ca. 3 mm long and those of inner series ca. 5 mm, both series connate 2/3 or more of length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but petals 1-1.6 x 0.6-0.9 cm wide; carpels 3, ovary glabrous, styles distinct, ca. 7 mm long. Capsules, spherical, 1.2-1.4 cm long and wide, distinctly lobed and carinate. Seeds: ellipsoidal, somewhat flat, 1-1.2 x 0.7-0.9 cm, yellow-brown mottled black; caruncle distinct but flattened.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, 1.5-3 m tall. Stems: gray, caudiciform-succulent, sparsely branched, smooth and glabrous, bark peeling in yellow sheets; latex clear. Leaves: deciduous, borne mostly near tops of stems, stipules branched, stipitate glands, 3-5 mm long; petioles 8.5-11 cm long and 1.5-2 mm in diam.; blades 5-lobed, divided nearly to base, 13-14 x 8-10.5 cm, lobes 4-4.5 cm and all nearly equal in size, but central one sometimes larger than laterals, segments bright red to nearly purple at point of attachment to petiole and extending to veins; membranous to slightly coriaceous, base cordate, margins entire, apex acuminate, venation palmate with a single vein in each segment, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal, many-flowered, elongated cymes, peduncles 9.5-18 cm long and 3-5 mm diam., paracladia distantly spaced and spirally arranged; bracts ovate-elliptic, 5-6 mm, margins entire; pedicels 3-5 mm. Staminate flowers; sepals ovate-lanceolate, 3.5-4 x 1.1-1.7 mm, margins entire, apex acuminate to apiculate, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas campanulate, pinkish in bud, otherwise yellow and infrequently with a red stripe on abaxial side, petals obovate, 7-10 x 3.8-5 mm, distinct, apex orbicular and reflexed, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 8, biseriate and connate at anthesis but soon uniseriate and distinct; basal glands oval. Pistillate flowers; like staminate but sepals 3.5-5 x 1.2-2 mm; petals 8-12 x 4-5.5 mm, carpels 3, styles ca. 3 mm, connate ¾ of length, rarely with a few staminodes at base; basal glands ± square. Capsules: oval, 1.6-2 x 1.2-1.4 cm, glabrous, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: light tan with darker mottling, somewhat flattened, oval, 8-10 x 5.5-8 mm, caruncle prominent.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs or trees, 2-10 m tall, dioecious. Stems: green, glabrous, short shoots present, bark peeling in yellow sheets; latex yellowish. Leaves: deciduous, on short shoots and nodes, stipules caducous but with a few cilia early; petioles slender, 5-17 cm long and 0.5-1.5 mm in diam., sparsely puberulent; blades oblong-ovate to elliptic, 2.2-6 x 3.5-5.7 cm, membranous, base cordate to nearly cuneate, margins mostly entire but occasionally with a few glands near base, apex acute to rounded, venation pinnate, glabrous on abaxial surface but densely puberulent on adaxial. Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral, staminate few-flowered cymes, peduncles 4.5-6 cm long; pistillate sessile, solitary or few, bracts lanceolate, 0.4-0.6 mm. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate-lanceolate, 2.5-3.5 x 1.5-1.7 mm, distinct, margins mostly entire but sometimes with a few glands, apex rounded, glabrous on adaxial surface and puberulent on abaxial; corollas narrowly urceolate, red or red with white adaxial surface, petals 7-10 x 2-2.5 mm, connate nearly to top, apex acuminate, not reflexed, glabrous on adaxial surface but pubescent on abaxial; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 2.5-4 mm and distinct, those of inner series 4.5-6 mm and connate to ca. ½ of length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals ovate-elliptic, larger, 4.5-6 x 2-3 mm, margins beset with stipitate glands; corollas widely urceolate, petals 8-12 x 2-3.5 mm, apex rounded, reflexed; carpels 3, styles 7-9 mm, distinct. Capsules: oval, 13 x 8 mm, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: n.v.

description: Shrubs, 0.5-2 m tall. Stems: reddish brown, smooth, cinereous, ligneus (not rubbery), short shoots common; latex clear. Leaves: stipules deltoid, 6-7 mm, caducous; petioles 2.5-6 mm long, glabrous; blades obovate to oblanceolate, 2.6-3.4 x 0.8-1.6 cm, predominantly fascicled on short shoots, base cuneate, margins entire, apex obtuse and sometimes emarginate, venation pinnate, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: staminate many-flowered cymes; pistillate solitary; bracts reddish, deltate, 0.9-1.1 mm long; pedicels sessile. Staminate flowers: sepals deltate-ovate, 2.2-2.5 x 1.1-1.4 mm, puberulent on adaxial surface; corollas tubular, ivory-white with yellow tinge, petals spathulate, united, 5-5.6 x 1.2-1.9 mm; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate, filaments of outer series 4-5 mm long, connate 2/3 of length, those of inner series 5.5-6 mm, connate ¾ of length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals oblong-lanceolate, 5-6 x 1-1.3 mm, puberulent on abaxial surface but glabrous on adaxial; petals 4.5-5 x 0.8-1 mm, carpels 2 (sometimes 1 by abortion), styles usually 2, connate ca. 2/3 of length. Capsules: bilocular, 1.3-1.5 x 1.5-2.6 cm, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: brown, spherical ca. 1.2 cm in diam., caruncle vestigial.

description: Shrubs, 1-2.5 m. Stems: gray, smooth, sparsely branched, succulent and quite fleshy, leaf scars round and somewhat protruding; latex copious, clear in actively growing shoots but cloudy in older branches Leaves: deciduous; stipules unbranched, stipitate glands, 2-5 mm long; petioles 4-6.8(-13.0) long and 1.3-1.5(-2) mm in diam.; blades peltate, orbicular in outline, shallowly and evenly 5- to7-lobed, 7.5-15.5 x 4-9.5 cm, lobes acute, 2.6-5 cm, membranous or + coriaceous, base cordate, margins entire or with few to many, short, stipitate glands, apex acuminate, venation palmate with 5-7 primary veins; glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal, many-flowered cymes peduncles 5-14 cm long and 0.3-1 mm in diam.; bracts oblong-ovate, 3-7 mm, margins with a few glandular teeth near the acuminate apex, glabrous; pedicels 3-6 mm. Staminate flowers: sepals pinkish, ovate to elliptic-triangular, 2-4.5 x 1-2 mm, distinct to connate ca. ½ of length, margins glandular-denticulate, apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas rotate, orange-red, petals obovate, 9-12(-14) x 3.5-5.5 mm, distinct but imbricate on lower Vá, apex round, not reflexed, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 8, biseriate (3 + 5) and filaments connate to ca. ½ of length at anthesis but soon uniseriate, 4-6 mm. Pistillate flowers: like staminate, but sepals 2-4.8 x 1.2-2.3 mm; petals 10-14 x 3.2-5.8 mm; carpels 3, styles green, 3-4 mm long, distinct. Capsules: spherical, 1.3-1.6 cm diam., glabrous, ecarinate, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: yellow to orange-brown with dark brown mottling, oval, 8-10 x 6-7 mm, caruncle large and distinctly lobed.

description: Shrubs, 1-3 m tall. Stems: orange to tan, branches few and mostly from base, stout, rubbery succulent with a thick base, glabrous, peeling bark, short shoots common; latex copious, orange in younger shoots but dark red in older branches. Leaves: deciduous, clustered on short shoots; stipules orange-brown, filiform-setose, 5-8 mm, covering the short shoots; petioles sessile; blades obovate, undivided, 0.9-2 x 1.1-2.4 (-4.5) cm, membranous-chartaceous, base cuneate, margins entire, apex round or sometimes retuse, venation pinnate, pubescent on both surfaces. Inflorescences: lateral on short shoots, usually solitary or in pairs, peduncles of staminate subsessile, 1-2 mm long, bracts indistinguishable if present, pedicels 1-2 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals grayish green to reddish, ovate to obovate, 3-5 x 0.8-1 mm, connate at base, margins entire, apex acute-acuminate, tomentose on both surfaces; corollas subglobose-tubular, pink to red with white lobes, petals 6-8 x 1.2-2 mm, connate ¾ or more of length, apex rounded, sharply reflexed, sparingly pubescent on both surfaces; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments mostly distinct, outer series 3.5-4 long and inner series 4-5 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals ovate-lanceolate, incised, 3.2-5.5 x 1-1.3 mm, petals 7.5-10.2 x 1.2-2.2 mm; carpels 2, distinctly lobed, styles 3 mm. Capsules: paired, nearly rounded, 2-lobed locules, 2-2.5 x 1.3-1.7 cm, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: light to dark brown with large, dark spots, spherical, 1.3 cm in diam., caruncle vestigial.

description: Shrubs or small trees, to 7 m. Stems: yellow-brown to gray, erect, sparsely branched, covered with lenticels and round leaf scars; latex cloudy and viscous. Leaves: semievergreen, mostly borne on upper parts of branches; stipules branched, filiform, 6-15(-25) mm; petioles 11-29 cm long and 2.5-3.5 mm in diam.; blades variable, ovate-cordate to nearly orbicular in outline, 16-30 x 10-22 cm, pinnatifid, deeply dissected into 9-11 lobes nearly to base, segments 1.2-4 cm, distinctly narrow early but wider later, membranous, base rounded, margins incised, apices acuminate, venation palmate with a single vein in each lobe, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal becoming subterminal with continued growth, many-flowered, capitate cymes; peduncles 12-30 cm, paracladia orange-red; bracts lanceolate, 2-4.5 mm, margins entire, glabrous; pedicels 3.5-6 mm. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate, 1.5-3 x 1-1.2 mm, connate to ½ of length, margins entire, apex round, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas cupulate, orange-red, petals 5-7 x 2.5-3 mm, distinct, apex rounded, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 8, monodelphous-uniseriate, filaments distinct, 2.2-2.5 mm. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but significantly fewer in number and somewhat larger; sepals 2-3.5 x 1.1-1.3; petals 6-8.2 mm x 2-3.2 mm; carpels mostly 3 (-2 tol by abortion), styles distinct, 1-1.2 mm. Capsules: ellipsoidal, 3-3.4 x 2.7-2.9 cm, bright yellow when mature, distinctly triangular and carinate, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: yellow to light brown, mottled with dark brown spots or stripes, spherical, 1.4-1.8 cm in diam., caruncle vestigial.

description: Shrubs, to 1 m tall, monoeicous. Stems: brown with white epidermal markings, succulent and with a small, but distinct woody caudex; bark fissured but not peeling; short shoots not evident; latex clear and watery. Leaves: stipules absent; petioles glabrous, 4.5-7 cm long and 2 mm in diam.; blades cordate in outline, shallowly 5-lobed, 2.5-5.5 x 1.5-3 cm, ± coriaceous; base cordate, margins ciliate with stipitate glands 2-4 mm long, apex cuspidate, venation palmate with 5 prominent veins, dark green on adaxial side but lighter green on abaxial, papillose on both surfaces but hirsute adaxially near the margins. Inflorescences: subterminal (occasionally appearing terminal or lateral), compound, few-flowered cymes, paracladia of 1 or 2 dichasia each terminating in a pistillate flower; coflorescences present and often distinct; downy, ca. 2-4.5 cm long, bracts lanceolate, ca. 3-7 mm, entire or rarely with 1 or 2 glands, hirsute; pedicels 4-6 mm long, downy. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate-elliptic, 2.5-3 x 2-2.5 mm, connate 1/3 of length, apex acute, margins entire (not glandular), downy; corollas tubular-campanulate, white, petals 4-5 x 3-3.5 mm, connate to about ½ of length, apex rounded, reflexed, glabrous on both surfaces; disc segments 5, spherical, ca. 1-1.5 mm; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 3.5-4 mm long, connate ca. 1/3 of length, those of inner series 5-6.5 mm, connate to top. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals foliaceous and unequal, widely ovate-cordiform, 7-14 x 12-18 mm wide, apex acute, papillose on both surfaces; corollas campanulate, petals 5-6.5 x 4-4.5 mm, reflexed, glabrous on both surfaces; disc segments broader than tall, ca. 1.5-2.5 x 0.8-1 mm; carpels 3, styles 5-6 mm, connate ca. 2/3 of length. Capsules: widely oval and distinctly trilobed, 1.2-1.4 x 1.5-2 cm, somewhat dry and ± tardily dehiscent. Seeds: grayish brown, ellipsoid, 1-1.5 x 1.2-1.7 mm, caruncle prominent, lacerate.

description: Leaves: stipules glandular and branched, 2-7 mm long; petioles 5-21.5 cm long and 1.2-3.5 mm in diam.; blades 5-lobed, 11-13 x 7-8.5 cm, lobes equal in size, 7-18.5 cm wide, darker above, paler below, margins mostly serrate, rugose-pubescent on abaxial surface, light green below. Inflorescences: bracts 4-14 mm, peduncles 11-19 long and 2-3 mm in diam. Staminate flowers: sepals 3-4.5 x 1.8-2.5 mm, glabrous on adaxial surface but pubescent on abaxial, margins glandular; corollas predomiantly red, 6-11 x 3.0-4 5 mm. Pistillate flowers: sepals 4-10 x 2-3.5 mm, glabrous on both surfaces; petals 10-11 x 4-7 mm.

description: Shrubs or small trees, 1.5-3.5 m tall, dioecious. Stems: gray, erect, smooth, leaf scars crescent-shaped, younger branches pubescent, trunk fissured or cracked but not peeling; latex clear to cloudy in older stems. Leaves: deciduous; stipules caducous but narrowly lanceolate when present; petioles 8-12 cm long and 1.5-2.5 mm in diam.; blades ovate-cordate in outline, mostly 15-29.5 cm long and nearly as wide, with 5-7 (-9) lobes, 62-6.1 cm wide, the 3-4 upper lobes deeper than lower, membranous, base broadly cordate, margins entire and devoid of glands, apex cuspidate, venation palmate, with 7(-9) primary veins; pubescent on both surfaces particularly on the veins. Inflorescences: terminal, compound cymes in both sexes but pistillate few-flowered; peduncles 7-2 cm long in staminate and 5.5-6.5 cm in pistillate, tomentose in both, paracladia terminating in a single flower, bracts entire, lanceolate, pubescent, 3-6.5 mm in staminate; pedicels of staminate flowers 1-1.5 cm, somewhat longer in the pistillate, tomentose. Staminate flowers: sepals lanceolate to ovate-elliptic, 4-7 x 2-3 mm, partially imbricate, acuminate, margins entire (not glandular); corollas tubular-campanulate, bright green, petals obovate, 5.5-8 x 2-3.5 mm, connate to about ½ or more of length, villous abaxially, hirsute adaxially; disc segments 5, massive, ellipsoid, ca. 2-3.5 x 1-1.5 mm; stamens 10, monadelphous-uniseriate at anthesis, filaments ca. 3-5 mm long, connate to ca. ½ of length; anthers oblong elliptic, somewhat flattened at apex, about 1.5-2 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 7-10 x 3.5-5 mm, imbricate; petals 1-1.3 x 2.5-4 mm; carpels 3, glabrous; styles thickened, connate to ca. ½-¾ of length, stigmas massive, dark green. Capsules: 3-locular, ellipsoid, ca. 20 x 15 mm, ± fleshy, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: light brown, ellipsoid, 10-12 x 8-10 mm, caruncle appressed to the beak and nearly vestigial, ca. 1 x 1.5-2 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, to 2.5 m tall. Stems: green when young becoming gray-brown with age, upright, sparsely branched, smooth, leaf scars circular; latex clear and watery. Leaves: persistent to semievergreen, stipules branched, stipitate glands, 6-8 mm long; petioles 14-16 cm long and 1.8-2 mm in diam.; blades suborbicular in outline, peltiform with 5(-7) deeply lobed segments, 17-28 x 10-11.5 cm, lobes 5.5-8 cm long, membranous to somewhat coriaceous, base cordate, margins entire, apex acuminate, venation palmate, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal becoming subterminal, long-pedunculate, compact cymes; bracts lanceolate, 1.7-3 x 0.3-0.4 cm long, margins beset with long-stipitate glands; peduncles 22-36 cm long, coflorescences absent; pedicels 2-3 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate-lanceolate, 8 x 1.7 mm, distinct, margins glandular, apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas tubular-salverform, red-purple in bud but yellow-green and sometimes with reddish purple lines at anthesis, petals 12.5-14 x 3 mm, connate ¾ of length, apex rounded, strongly reflexed, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 6, monadelphous-uniseriate, connate ½ or more at anthesis but become distinct. Pistillate flowers: like staminate, carpels 3, styles 2(-3), 5 mm long, distinct. Capsules: spherical, 2.5 cm diam., glabrous, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: yellow-brown with black markings, oval, 1.5 x 0.8 cm, caruncle prominent.

description: Shrubs or small trees, to 7 m, dioecious. Stems: whitish gray or sometimes purplish, erect, young branches somewhat succulent, densely tomentose, branches many and often from base, bark smooth, leaf scars crescent-shaped; latex watery and clear in younger shoots but reddish bloodlike in older branches. Leaves: deciduous, sometimes a few remain near branch tips, stipules caducous; petioles 5-8 cm long and 1-1.5 mm in diam., densely pubescent when young; blades broadly ovate in outline, usually 3- to 5-lobed, 6.5-9(-16.5) x 6.5-12(-14.5) cm, lobes 2-7.5 cm, membranous, base cordate, margins entire, apex broadly acuminate, venation palmate with 5-7(-9) primary veins, whitish pubescent on both surfaces particularly when young. Inflorescences: lateral, few-flowered cymes, staminate with peduncles of main florescences 2-3.4 cm long and those of coflorescences 1-1.5 cm; pistillate sessile, bracts 2-4 mm long, lanceolate, margins entire, pubescent on both surfaces; pedicels 2.5-3 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals oblong to ovate-elliptic, 2.5-4.5 x 1.2-2 mm, margins entire, apex obtuse to rounded, glabrous on adaxial surface but mostly pubescent on abaxial; corollas tubular, white, petals obovate, 6-7 x 1.8-2.5 mm, distinct to variously connate to ½ of length, apex round, reflexed, tomentose on adaxial surface but glabrous on abaxial; stamens 10, biseriate-diadelphous (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 2.5-3.5 mm long and sometimes ± distinct after anthesis, those of inner series 3-4.5 mm long and connate ½-2/3 of length. Pistillate flowers: mostly like staminate but sepals oblong-elliptic and longer than the corolla but not foliaceous, 5.5-6.5 x 2.2-3 mm, apex acute; petals 6.5-8.2 x 1.8-2.4 mm; carpels 3, styles 2-3.5 mm long, connate ½ or more of length; rarely with a few staminodes. Capsules: ellipsoid, 1.6-2 x 1.2-1.8 cm, drupaceous, apiculate, distinctly ribbed, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: dark brown with black mottling, oval, 1.2-1.4 x 0.9-1.1 cm, caruncle present.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Perennial herbs, to 0.5 m tall. Stems: subterranean caudex, fleshy, to 12 cm in diam., stems and root scars round; cauline stems green, erect, herbaceous, and somewhat succulent, glabrous, often sparsely branched; latex clear; short shoots absent. Leaves: deciduous together with cauline shoots, lateral on stems; stipules persistent, filiform-divided, 4-10 mm; petioles 4.8-10-5 (-13.5) cm long and 1.5-1.8 (-2.8) mm in diam.; blades heteromorphic, cordate in outline, (3-)5-7(-9) lobes extending to middle, 11-16 x 9.3-11.2 cm, membranous, base cordate, margins coarsely dentate, apices acuminate, venation palmate with 5-7(-9) primary veins, glabrous on both surfaces except pubescent on veins of abaxial side. Inflorescences: terminal and subterminal, many-flowered cymes; peduncles 1.5-4.5 cm; bracts (6-)8-16 mm, margins serrate, glabrous; pedicels 2.5-4 mm. Staminate flowers: sepals lanceolate, 5-7 x 1-2 mm, distinct or connate to ½ of length, margins divided, apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas rotate-campanulate, light pink and often with white striations, petals 8-11.5 x 2.5-4.5 mm, distinct or connate ¼ of length, apex rounded, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 8(-9), biseriate-diadelphous (5 + 3), filaments of outer series 3.5-6 mm, distinct, inner series 4.5-9 mm, connate to ½ of length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but slightly larger; carpels 3; styles 3.5-4 mm, distinct or connate only at base. Capsules: spherical but distinctly 3-lobed, 1.2-1.3 cm in diam. Seeds: pale gray, ellipsoidal, 8-9 x 6-6.5 mm; caruncle prominent.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, to 3 m tall. Stems: grayish white, erect, succulent with soft wood and chambered pith, leaf scars large, protruding and pointed; latex clear in younger shoots but cloudy in older branches; bark peeling near base. Leaves: deciduous, exstipulate; petioles 6-13.5 (-38) cm long and 2-3.5(-4) mm in diam.; blades deeply divided or parted into 3 large and 2 smaller, elliptic segments, 11-19(-31) x 5.7-13.5(-19.5) cm, lobes 3.3-8 cm wide, ± coriaceous, base cordate, margins entire and narrowly hyaline-yellow, apex acuminate, venation palmate with each lobe having a single primary vein, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral with continued growth, elongated, paniculate cymes, paracladia spiral, peduncles (5.7-)10-19.5(-32) cm long; bracts lanceolate, 4.5-15 mm long, margins entire, glabrous; pedicels 1.5-2 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 3.5-5 x 1-1.5 mm, distinct, margins entire but sometimes serrulate (not glandular), apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas campanulate, red in bud, yellowish pink and often bicolor (adaxial side yellow and abaxial side reddish or red-tinged), petals oblong-obovate, 10-13 x 3.5-4.5 mm, distinct, apex acute, not reflexed, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 8 (-9 or 10), biseriate (5 + 3 or 4 + 4), filaments connate ca. ½ of length at anthesis but apostemonous at maturity, outer series 1-2.5 mm long and inner series 2-4 mm; anthers saggitate, 1.5-1.7 mm long; disc glands large, distinct. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 4-6 x 1.7-2.5 mm; petalsl 1-14 x 4-5 mm; carpels 3, styles 3(-4), short, ca. 1 mm long, distinct, stigmas capitate, fleshy. Capsules: spherical, 2-2.1 cm long and wide, initially yellow turning green when mature, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: yellow to golden-brown with light brown mottling, oval, ± flat, 1.2-1.3 x 1-1.1 cm, caruncle large and prominent.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, to 2 m tall. Stems: light gray with prominent, round leaf scars, thick, ± upright but mostly decumbent, succulent with a few leafless branches and chambered pith, smooth and shiny epidermis beneath peeling whitish bark; latex cloudy and sticky. Leaves: deciduous or semievergreen; stipules obsolete, petioles 3-15.5 cm long and 1-1.5 mm in diam.; blades 7-11 x 6-9.5 cm long, deeply 3- to 5-lobed, lobes widely ovate to rotund, 3.5-5 cm wide, central lobe often overlapping 2 laterals, membranous, base cordate, margins entire, apex acute-acuminate and sometimes mucronate, glabrous on both surfaces and covered with pellucid spots on adaxial surface. Inflorescences: terminal becoming subterminal with continued growth, compact cymes, peduncles 5-12.5 cm or more long; bracts 3-6.5 mm long, pedicels to 1.0-4.0 mm long but longer in fruit. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 3-5 x 1.5-2.5 mm, distinct, margins entire, apex acute to rounded, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas rotate, bright red to scarlet, petals oblong, 1.6-2 x 0.7-1.3 cm, distinct but imbricate in lower 1/3, apex round, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 8(-9 or 10), uniseriate or rarely biseriate (5 + 3), filaments of outer series 1-2 mm long and those ot inner series 3-4 mm, distinct, anthers ca.1.5 mm long and as wide; basal glands free, nearly inconspicuous. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but somewhat larger, sepals 4-5 x 2-3 mm wide; petals 1.8-2.5 x 0.15-1.1 cm, sometimes with a few short, fertile stamens and a few staminodia; carpels 3, styles 3, ca. 2 mm long, distinct, massive and deeply lobed. Capsules: initially yellow turning green at maturity, nearly spherical, 2.0 x 1.8 cm, 3-lobed. Seeds: brown, ± striated, ellipsoid,1.5 x 1 cm, caruncle prominent, fissured.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs 2.5-5 m tall. Stems: dark brown and somewhat striated, erect, much branched; latex clear in younger shoots but cloudy in older branches. Leaves: stipules obsolete, petioles 1-5.5 cm long; blades heteromorphic, elliptic-ovate, obovate, lyrate, or panduriform, often shallowly 3-lobed-hastate, 7.5-15.3 x 2.9-12.5 cm, membranous to ± coriaceous, base rounded, cordate or cuneate, apex acuminate, margins entire but sometimes with 2-4 basal glands or filiform, eglandular hairs, venation pinnate but sometimes with 2 weak laterals from base, or palmate when lobed, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal and subterminal, many-flowered cymes, peduncles 5.2-21 cm long, coflorescences absent; bracts lanceolate, 10-12 mm long, pedicels 2-8 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals reddish brown, ovate, 2.5-3(-4) x 1-1.7 mm, distinct, margins entire, apex obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas rotate, dark red to scarlet, or pink, petals 8.4-12.1 x 2.5-43 mm, distinct or coherent, obovate, apex obtuse, covered with tufts of hairs on basal portion of adaxial sides but glabrous on abaxial; stamens 10, ± bisenate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 7-9 mm long and those of inner series 9-12 mm, filaments of both series connate ½-¾ of length; anthers 2.0-3.5 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 3 1-3 8 X 1.2-2.2 cm; petals 9-17 x 5-10 mm; carpels 3, ovary glabrous; styles 3-4 mm, connate of length Capsules: oval, 1-1.3 x 0.7-1.1 cm, glabrous, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: cream-colored and mottled with red and black spots, ellipsoidal, 7-10 x 4-6.5 mm, caruncle small but conspicuous, lobed.

description: Shrubs, to 4 m tall. Stems: pale gray to gray-brown sparsely branched, branches succulent with oval leaf scars, smooth in younger shoots but striated or shallowly wrinkled in older branches, with short, reddish pubescence when growing actively; latex cloudy in young shoots but darker in older branches. Leaves: deciduous, stipules branched, fimbriate with glandular tips, 6-15 mm long, petioles 8-15 cm long and 1.5-2 mm in diam.; blades orbicular in outline, peltate, with 3-5(-6) shallow, obtuse lobes, 5-16 cm long and wide, ± coriaceous, base round, margins stipitate glandular-ciliate, apex obtuse, venation palmate with 5-7 primary veins, glabrous on both surfaces, darker above, lighter below. Inflorescences: terminal, becoming subterminal with continued growth, compact, capitate cymes, peduncles 7-14.5 cm long; bracts linear-lanceolate, 2-8 mm long; pedicels 2-8 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate-lanceolate to ovate, 2-4 x 1-1.5 (-2) mm, distinct or only slightly connate at base, margins erose, apex mostly erose, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas rotate, red to scarlet, petals obovate, 8.5-12 x 4-6 mm, distinct, apex round, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 8, uniseriate-monadelphous, filaments 2-4.5 mm long, connate at anthesis, becoming distinct at maturity, red with yellow pollen. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but slightly larger, sepals 3-4 x 1.5-1.8 mm, petals 9-14.5 x 4-5 mm, carpels 3, styles distinct, 1.5-2 mm long, red. Capsules: spherical, 3-locular but distinctly 6-lobed, 1.2-1.5 cm long and wide, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: dark brown with few darker spots, oblong, 7.5-12 x 5.5-6.5 mm, caruncle large and prominent, grooved.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, 1.5-2 m tall. Stems: green to yellowish gray, suffrutescent, leaf scars round; latex clear in actively growing shoots but cloudy in older branches. Leaves: persistent; stipules 6- to 14-branched, stipitate glands; petioles green, 6.5-14 cm long and 1.4-2.8 mm in diam., glandular-ciliate; blades orbicular in outline, 3- to 5-lobed and sometimes to near base, 10.5-20 x 7_14 cm, lobes 4.4-8 cm wide, membranous, base cordate, apex acute to acuminate, margins glandular-ciliate, sometimes minutely serrate, venation palmate with 5(-7) primary veins, glabrous on adaxial side but sparsely pubescent on abaxial. Inflorescences: terminal, lax but many-flowered, elongated cymes; peduncles 11-37 cm long; bracts lanceolate, 6-18 mm long, apex acuminate, margins glandular-ciliate; pedicels 1.5-2.3 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.5-3.5 x 1-1.8 mm, distinct, margins entire to ± glandular-ciliate, apex acuminate, glabrous to slightly pubescent on both surfaces; corollas dull red to reddish brown, campanulate, petals oblanceolate to obovate, 4-7.5 x 2-2.8 mm, free or basally connate to ca. ¼ of length, imbricate, glabrous on abaxial side but glabrous to sparsely pubescent on adaxial; stamens 8(-9 or 10), biseriate (5 + 3), filaments of outer series 1-2.5 mm long, those of inner series 2-3 mm long, anthers 0.5-1 mm long; basal glands spherical. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 3-5.5 x 1.5-2 mm wide; petals 5-6 x 2.5-3.2 mm; carpels 3, ovary glabrous; styles 0.2-0.6 mm long, distinct; stigmas horseshoe-shaped, fleshy; basal glands turbinate. Capsules: ellipsoid, 11—13 x 5-9 mm, glabrous, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: dark brown with black mottling, oblong, 5.5-8 x 4-4.5 mm, caruncle prominent.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrub, to 4 m tall. Stems: green when young, becoming gray-brown; ± succulent, leaf scars round, forming a sharp spine-like protrusion, bark peeling in thin, brown sheets on lower portions near base, latex watery in younger shoots but cloudy in older. Leaves: evergreen in moister climates but deciduous to semievergreen with a few leaves at shoot apices in drier regions; stipules branched, stipitate glands, 2-5 mm long, petioles 7-14 cm long and 2-2.5 mm in diam.; blades cordate in outline, 9-17 x 7-12.5 cm, 5-lobed, lobes 3.7-6.7 cm wide, membranous or ± coriaceous, base cordate, margins coarsely serrate-dentate with bristle tips (not glandular), apex acuminate, venation palmate with 7(-9) primary veins; glabrous on both surfaces or rarely sparsely pubescent on veins on abaxial side and sometimes glaucous (plants from Argentina). Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral with continued growth; many-flowered cymes, bracts setaceous-glandular to ± lacerate, 5-12 mm long; peduncles 11.5-18 cm long, sparsely pubescent; pedicels 1.5-3 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals reddish brown on abaxial side and green on adaxial; ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 3-4.5 x 1-2.5 mm, connate ca. ¼ at base, margins dentate and sometimes with short, glandular cilia, apex acute-acuminate and sometimes apiculate, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas rotate-campanulate, yellow and often with a red tinge in bud and on abaxial side at petal apex, petals obovate, 9-11 x 3.5-4.5 mm, distinct but imbricate, apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 8, monadelphous-uniseriate, filaments 2-4 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but slightly larger, sepals 3.5-5(-8.5) x 1-2.5 mm; petals 10.5-12 x 4-7.5 mm; carpels 3, styles nearly sessile, connate, stigmas massive. Capsules: 3-locular, distinctly lobed and carinate, spherical, 2-2.3 cm long and wide. Seeds: yellow mottled with light brown spots, oval, 1.1-1.4 x 1-1.1 cm, caruncle large and prominent.

description: Shrubs or small trees 6-7 m tall. Stems: slender, green turning grayish green. Leaves: persistent; petioles green, 4.5-10 cm long and ca. 0.7-1.4 mm diam., blades green, subpeltate, somewhat smaller than those of var. portoricensis, 4-10.5 x 6-13 cm, unlobed or 3-lobed; glabrous on both surfaces, veins mostly palmate but sometimes pinnate in smaller leaves, light green.

description: Shrubs, to 1.5 m tall. Stems: brown, erect, young shoots somewhat succulent, pubescent early, becoming glabrous, leaf scars crescent-shaped; latex clear in actively growing shoots but cloudy in older branches. Leaves: semievergreen to deciduous; stipules dark brown, branched, stipitate glands, 3.5-7 mm long; petioles 3.5-4.7 cm long and 1-1.5 cm in diam. covered with branched, glandular hairs; blades orbicular in outline, unlobed to shallowly 3(-5)-lobed, 6.2-8.2 x 4.8-7 cm, lobes 3.1-5.1 cm wide, ± coriaceous, base cordate, margins ciliate-glandular, apex acute to apiculate, venation palmate, glabrous or scarcely pubescent on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal, few-flowered cymes, peduncles of main florescences 3.5-7 cm long and of coflorescences 1-3 cm; bracts linear, 4-6 mm long, margins glandular; pedicels 1-2 mm. Staminate flowers: sepals lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 2.5-3 x 0.7-1 mm, distinct, margins glandular-ciliate but infrequently entire, apex acute, glabrous on one or both surfaces; corollas rotate, red to dark red, petals 4.6-5 x 1.6-2. mm, distinct, imbricate, apex acute-acuminate, mostly glabrous on both surfaces, stamens 8, diadelphous-biseriate (5 + 3), filaments of outer series 2.8-3.5 mm long and those of inner series 3.5-4 mm, connate ¼-½ of length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 3-3.5 x 1.2-2; petals 5.8-6 x 1.5-3 mm; carpels 3, styles 2-2.5 mm long, distinct. Capsules: ± spherical, 0.8-1.1 cm in diam., pubescent, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: light yellow mottled yellowish brown, ellipsoid, ca, 1.2 x 8 mm, caruncle prominent.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, 0.5-1 m tall. Stems: rhizomatous, gray, glabrous, upright to procumbent, branches few to many, ± fleshy, latex clear in younger shoots but cloudy (not milky) in older branches. Leaves: persistent to semi-deciduous, stipules minute, 1-2 mm long, setaceous, eglandular, petioles 6.5-12 cm long and 1-1.5 mm in diam.; blades 3- to 5-lobed, 8.2-15.2 x 5.5-13 cm, lobes obovate-elliptic, 2.4-5.2 cm wide, basal lobes smaller and auriculate, membranous, base cordate, margins irregularly dentate but not glandular, apices acute-acuminate, venation palmate with 3-5(-7) primary veins, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral with continued growth, many-branched, capitate cymes, peduncles 9-14 cm long; bracts lanceolate, glabrous, 5-10 mm long; pedicels 3-5 mm long. Stanimate flowers: sepals mostly ovate-lanceolate, 2-2.5 x 1 mm, connate to ca. ¼ of length, apex acute but sometimes apiculate, margins minutely serrate, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas rotate, red-scarlet, petals oblanceolate-obovate, 6-12.5 x 2.5-5 mm, apex round, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 8, monadelphous-uniseriate, filaments connate to ca. ½ at anthesis but soon distinct, 3.5-4 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but somewhat larger, sepals 2.5-3.5 x 1-1.5 mm; petals 7.2-14 x 3.5-6.5 mm; carpels 3, glabrous, styles 3, free from base, 2-3 mm long, stigmas fleshy, dolabriform; basal glands ellipsoid and conspicuous. Capsules: nearly spherical, distinctly 3-lobed, 1.8-2.2 cm long and wide, glabrous. Seeds: gray-brown with darker brown mottling, ellipsoid to nearly oval, 1-1.1 x 0.8-1 cm, caruncle large and prominent.

description: Shrubs, 2-3 m tall. Leaves: predominantly 5-lobed, cordate at base, lobes widely elliptic to nearly ovate, 9-13.5 x 6-14 cm; margins denticulate or sparsely glandular; glabrous on both surfaces or with a few hairs on abaxial-surface veins; developing and mature leaves red to maroon. Corollas: pinkish to light red with yellowish green center.

description: Shrubs, to 3 m tall. Stems: brown turning gray with age, erect, hirsute, glandular when young, soft and pliable; latex clear and viscous. Leaves: mostly persistent but sometimes semideciduous in drier areas, stipules few- to many-branched and unbranched, stipitate glands, 2.5-2 mm long; petioles 3-14.5 cm long and 1-1.4 mm in diam., covered with sticky, stipitate glands; blades cordate to ovate in outline, dark red, brownish, to green, 3- to 5-lobed, 4-8.2 x 4.2-3.4 cm, membranous, base cordate, margins sometimes doubly serrate, serrulate-denticulate or glandular-ciliate or rarely entire, apices acuminate, venation palmate with 5-7 primary veins, surfaces glabrous or sparsely pubescent especially on veins. Inflorescences: terminal and subterminal, few-flowered cymes, peduncles of main florescences 2.5-0.5 cm long and those of coflorescences 2-7 cm; bracts ovate, 6-16 mm long, margins glandular; pedicels 1-2 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.2-2.5 x 2.5-4 mm, sometimes connate to ¼ of length, margins beset with stipitate glands, apex round, glabrous or sparsely pubescent on both surfaces; corollas campanulate, red to purple and sometimes with yellowish green center, petals 3.5-5.5 x 1.8-3 mm, obovate, connate ¼-½ of length, apex round and somewhat reflexed, glabrous or sparely pubescent on one or both surfaces; stamens 8, diadelphous-biseriate (5 + 3), filaments in each series ¼-½ or more connate, outer series 1.4-3 mm and inner series 1.8-4 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but infrequently with staminodes sometimes with a few pollen grains, sepals 2.5-4 x 1-1.7 mm; petals 4-6.5 x 2-3.5 cm; carpels 3, styles 1-2 mm long, connate to Va of length. Capsules: ellipsoidal to nearly spherical, 1-1.2 x 0.8-1 cm, pubescent, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: gray-brown, mottled with dark brown spots, oval, 6.5-7 x 3.8-4.5 mm, caruncle prominent.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, 2-3.5 m tall. Stems: light brown, glabrous, lenticels common, few branches, mostly from base with leaves mostly near shoot apices; latex clear to cloudy. Leaves: stipules small, 1-1.5 mm long, subulate; petioles often reddish in young leaves, 4-8.5 cm long and 1-1.5 mm in diam.; blades spotted to mostly reddish brown on adaxial side, heteromorphic, mostly widely ovate and shallowly 3-lobed with middle lobe noticeably wider than laterals or less commonly ovate-elliptic and unlobed or sometimes panduriform, 5.5-9.5 x 2.4-5.8 cm, membranous, base cordate or somewhat truncate, eglandular, margins entire, apex acuminate, venation palmate in lobed and pinnate in unlobed leaves but sometimes with 2 or 4 distinct laterals from near the base; glabrous and darker on adaxial side and glaucous and reddish purple or sometimes yellow on abaxial. Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral with continued growth, corymbiform many-flowered cymes; peduncles 7-10 cm long; bracts linear, 1.5-3 mm long, margins entire or infrequently glandular-denticulate, glabrous; pedicels 3-5 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals green, ovate, 2.5-3.3 x 2-2.5 mm, connate ca. Vs of length, margins entire, apex obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas rotate, imbricate at base, crimson-red, obovate-spathulate, 1.4 x 1.1 cm, apex obtuse, villous near base on adaxial side and glabrous on abaxial, disc glands free; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate, filaments distinct, outer series 2-3 mm long and inner series 8-11 mm long; anthers linear-oblong, ca. 2 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 3-4 x 2.2-2.7 mm; petals 1.6 x 1.2 cm; carpels 3, glabrous; stigmas 2-3 mm long connate to ca. ½ of length. Capsules: nearly spherical 1-1.2 mm long and as wide, glabrous. Seeds: cream-colored mottled with red and black spots, ellipsoidal 7-1 x 4-6.5 mm, caruncle small but conspicuous.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, to 1.5 m tall, gynodioecious. Stems: whitish gray, caudex thickened, stem and branches succulent, sparingly pubescent, spreading and decumbent; short shoots numerous and distinct on older branches, 2-5 cm long, bark fissured and peeling on older branches. Leaves: deciduous, on nodes, and small leaves crowded at apex of short shoots; stipules obsolete; petioles green, 3.5-8.5 cm long and 3-7 mm in diam.; blades broadly ovate-suborbicular, 4.5-6.2 x 3-5.5 cm, unlobed, membranous to ± succulent, base cordate, margins entire (completely devoid of glands), apex acute, venation palmate with 5 prominent veins and 2 weaker laterals; pubescent on veins adaxially, otherwise glabrous. Inflorescences: terminal on branches or more often on short shoots; staminate many-flowered, paniculate cymes but with a solitary, central, terminal, pistillate flower; peduncles 5-2 cm long; pistillate inflorescences few-flowered cymes of 2-5 flowers, peduncles 1.5-2.5 cm; axis villous; bracts ca. 1-2 mm long in staminate and 3-7 mm long in pistillate, margins entire (not glandular), narrowly lanceolate, villous on both surfaces; pedicels 3-4 mm long, densely villous. Staminate flowers: sepals elliptic, 2-3 x 1-1.5 mm, distinct, margins entire (not glandular), apex acute; corollas tubular-subglobose, dark red, petals 7.5-10 x 5-7.2 mm, connate 2/3 or more of length, pubescent adaxially; disk segments spherical, massive, ca. 1 mm tall and wide; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 3.5-4 mm long and connate 2/3 of length, those of inner series ca. 5-6.5 mm long, connate ca. ¾ of length; anthers elliptic, ca. 1-3-1.5 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals larger and ± foliaceous, 1.5-2 x 1-1.33 cm, distinct; corollas ± campanulate, petals 10-12 x 4.5-5 mm (slightly larger in [female] of the staminate inflorescences), densely villous on abaxial side; disc glands dissected, (8-)10 glands, taller than broad, ca. 0.7-1 mm wide and 0.8-1.1 mm high; ovary glabrous, (3-)2 carpels (always 3 in the terminal, pistillate flower of the staminate inflorescences); styles 2(-3), 2.5-3.2 mm long, connate to above middle, dilated to 2(-3) multifid stigmas. Capsules: spherical, 2-2.5 cm long and wide, 2(-3)-lobed, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: grayish brown, ± spherical, 1-1.5 cm in diam., caruncle vestigial.

description: Trees, 5-10 m tall. Stems: gray-green, profusely ranched, soft and pliable, leaf scars crescent-shaped, glabrous, trunk diam. 15-20 cm (dbh), bark smooth, not exfoliating; latex copious, pale cloudy throughout. Leaves, semievergreen, stipules caducous, small tufts of hair on actively growing shoots; petioles 2.5-12.5 cm and 1-2.5 mm diam., blades cordate, infrequently shallowly 3-lobed, 6-12.3(-16.7) x 6-14.2(-17) cm, ± coriaceous, base cordate and sometimes with 1 or 2 stipitate glands when lobed, otherwise margins entire and without glands, apex apiculate, venation palmate with 5-7 primary veins, glabrous on both surfaces. inflorescences: terminal, hysteranthius (before new leaf development), many-flowered, paniculate cymes, much branched from base, peduncles l.3-3 cm, bracts triangular, 2-3 mm long; pedicels 0.5-1.5 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate, pink to light red, 1-2 x 1-1.5 mm, connate to ca. ¾ of length, margins entire, apex round, glabrous on both surfaces, corollas tubular-urceolate, white to creamy white, petals 5-6 x 1.1-2 mm, apex rounded, pilose on adaxial surface but glabrous on abaxial; stamens 8, diadelphous-biseriate (5 + 3), filaments of outer series 0.51 mm long and those of inner series 1.5-3 mm, both connate to ca. ¼-½ of length, anthers 2.0-2.8 mm long; basal glands spherical. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 1.7-2.2 x 1.3-1.7 mm; petals 5.5-7 x 1.5-2.4 mm, carpels 3, styles ca. 1.5 mm; basal glands discoid-lenticular. Capsules: spherical, 1.8-2 cm, minutely apiculate, carinate, distinctly 6-ribbed, surface ± verrucate, explosively dehiscent. Seeds: brown with darker brown mottling, oval, 1.3-1.5 x 0.8-1 cm, caruncle small but prominent.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Trees, to 8 m tall, dioecious. Stems: gray-green, many branched, covered with lenticels, short shoots common, bark yellow, exfoliating, trunk yellow-green, actively growing shoots puberulent; latex cloudy in younger but red in older branches. Leaves: semievergreen, borne on short shoots and stems, stipules stipitate glands, caducous, 0.2-0.3 mm; petioles 2-3.5(-6.6) long and 0.5 cm in diam.; blades ovate-deltoid, rarely shallowly 3- to 5-lobed, 1.8-3.3 x 2.1-4.5 cm, membranous, base cordate to obtuse-cordate, margins entire or sometimes with a few gland-tipped dentations, apex obtuse-acuminate, venation palmate with 1 central primary vein and 4 weaker laterals from base, glabrous on both surfaces but verrucate on adaxial. Inflorescences: terminal and lateral, staminate few-flowered cymes, peduncles and rachis 7.5-10 cm, pistillate solitary or few, bracts caducous, deltoid, ca. 0.5 mm when present early; pedicels 2.5-5 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals oblong to elliptic-obovate, 2.5-3 x 1-1.8 mm, distinct, margins entire to sparsely glandular, apex round, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas campanulate, cream-colored sometimes with reddish veins, petals 5.8-6.2 x 3-4 mm, distinct or connate only at base, imbricate, obovate, apex round, glabrous on adaxial surface but scarcely pubescent on adaxial; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 2-4 mm long and distinct or connate only at base, those of inner series 4.5-6 mm and connate ¼-½ of length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 5-6 x 2.2-3 mm, with glandular margins, petals 7-8 x 3.3-3.5 mm; carpels 2, styles ca. 2 mm, connate ca. ½ of length. Capsules: transversely ellipsoid, distinctly bilobed, 2.4-2.8 x 1.6-1.9 cm. Seeds: spherical, 2.2 cm in diam, reddish when mature, caruncle vestigial.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, to 1 m tall, monoecious. Stems: reddish when young, compact, multibranched and with short shoots; latex cloudy in young shoots but yellow in older branches. Leaves: deciduous, mostly on nodes but sometimes on short shoots, stipules caducous, petioles 2-5(-9) cm long and 2-3 mm in diam.; blades widely ovate, unlobed or shallowly 3-lobed, 2-2.5 x 2-3 cm, membranous, base cordate, margins ciliate and infrequently with 1 to few stipitate glands, apex obtuse, venation palmate with 3(-5) primary veins, canescent on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal, compact cymes, peduncles 1-1.8 cm; bracts 5 mm, Margins entire, pilose; pedicels subsessile or sessile. Staminate flowers: sepals oblong-elliptic, 3 x 2.5 mm, margins entire, glabrous on adaxial side but pubescent on abaxial, apex round; corollas rotate, yellowish green, petals 5 x 2 mm, distinct, obovate, tomentose on adaxial side but glabrous on abaxial, apex round; stamens 10(-9), monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 2-2.2 mm long and connate to ca. 2/3 of length, those of inner series 2.3-3 mm and connate to ca. ¾ of length. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but sepals 5 x 3 mm, petals 5.2 x 2.2 mm, carpels 3, styles 3 mm long and connate to ca. ¾ of length. Capsules: trilocular, ± ellipsoid, 1.5 x 1.2 cm, beaked, marked by distinct red ribs from the apical portion. Seeds: yellowish brown, ellipsoid, 1.3 x 0.6 mm, caruncle prominent.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs or small trees, 3-8 m tall, dioecious. Stems: brownish gray, short shoots common. Leaves; predominantly on short shoots; stipules caducous, minute when present early; petioles mostly sessile but some subsessile and 1-4 mm long; blades spathulate, 3-6 x 1-3 cm, unlobed or occasionally trilobed, margins entire, venation pinnate, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences; staminate compound cymes, 1.5-1.9 cm long, peduncles 0.9-1 cm long, bracts triangular, 0.3-0.5 mm long; pistillate solitary; pedicels 2-3 mm long, longer in fruit. Staminate flowers; sepals oblong, 3.2-3.5 x 1.3-1.5 mm, connate at base, margins entire, apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas tubular-campanulate, white; petals obovate, 6-8 x 1.5-2 mm, apex acute, reflexed, glabrous on both surfaces, stamens 10, diadelphous-biseriate, filaments of outer series 2-2.1 mm long and mostly distinct, those of inner series 3.2-3.5 mm and connate to ca. ½-¾ of length; anthers ovoid, 1.6-1.8 mm long; basal glands ovoid. Pistillate flowers; like staminate but sepals 5.5-6.5 x 1.5-1.7 mm; petals 9-10 x 1.5-2 mm; basal glands nearly spherical; carpels l(-2 ?), ovary glabrous, styles 1, 3-4 mm long. Capsules; unilocular, ellipsoid, ca. 2x8 mm, shortly apiculate, tardily dehiscent. Seeds, brown, speckled black, ellipsoid, 9 x 7 mm, caruncle vestigial.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Subshrubs, to 0.5 m. Leaves: oblong-spathulate, sessile to subsessile, undivided, 1.5-2.5 x 0.2-0.4 cm, with a single primary vein. Flowers: sepals connate at base; corollas white; stamens connate less than ½ of length.

description: Shrubs, to 1.5 m tall, dioecious. Stems: green, erect, bark exfoliating in papery, golden-yellow sheets. Leaves: lateral at nodes except crowded at apex of suckering shoots; stipules short, stipitate glands, caducous; petioles 1.4-3.1 cm long and 0.5 mm in diam., glabrous, with a swelling at point of attachment to stem resembling a pulvinus; blades oblong-elliptic to ovate, 2-3.4 x 2.2-2.35 cm, membranous, base rounded or truncate, margins entire (without glands), apex acute to rounded, venation palmate (strong central vein and 2 or 4 weaker laterals from base), glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: terminal becoming lateral, staminate cymose, 2.4-5.3 cm; pistillate simple mon or dichasial cymes with a pair of flowers or rarely flowers solitary, peduncles 0.8-2.6 cm long; bracts triangular-ovate, 0.4-0.7 mm, pubescent. Staminal flowers: sepals elliptic to widely oblong, 0.9-1.4 margins entire, glabrous; corollas tubular-urceo a rose-colored; petals 6-6.8 x 1.5-1.7 mm, united; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 2.1 mm and connate ¼-½ of length, those of inner series 3.6 mm and connate to ca. ½ of length. Pistillate flowers: pedicels 2.5-3.2 mm, sepals unequal, oblong to ovate-lanceolate (1.6-)3-5.1(-7) mm, margins glandular (?), pubescent on abaxial surface; corollas subglobose, red, petals 6.4-8.2 x 2 mm; carpels 2, styles ca. 4 mm long, connate to ca. ½ of length. Capsules: bilocular, tardily dehiscent (n.v.). Seeds: n.v.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Trees, 8-15 m tall, monoecious. Stems: green in younger branches but grey-green in older, erect, somewhat succulent, leaf scars crescent-shaped; latex copious, clear in younger branches but cloudy in older. Leaves. deciduous in drier, cooler climates but semievergreen to evergreen in warmer, moist regions; stipules caducous but narrowly lanceolate when present on actively growing shoots; petioles 9-19 cm long and 1.4-3 mm in diam.; blades cordate to orbicular in outline, shallowly 3- to 5-lobed or sometimes unlobed, 9-15 cm wide and long, membranous, base cordate, apex acuminate, margins entire or eophylls and young leaves with few glands, venation palmate with 3-5(-7) primary veins, both surfaces glabrous or occasionally sparsely pubescent on abaxial veins. Inflorescences: bisexual, terminal becoming subterminal to lateral with continued growth, many-flowered, compound, capitate cymes, flowers predominantly staminate, peduncles of main florescences 5-10 cm long and those of coflorescences 1.5-5 cm; bracts 3-10 mm long; bracteoles 1.5-2 mm long; pedicels 1-3 mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate-elliptic, 4-6 x 2-3 mm, connate at base, margins entire; apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas campanulate, greenish white to greenish yellow, petals 4-5 x 2-2.5(-3) mm, distinct or connate ca. ¼ of length, ovate-oblong, apex round and strongly reflexed, tomentose on adaxial side but glabrous on ab-axial; stamens 10, ± biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 3-4.5 mm long and those of inner series 3-5 mm, anthers 1.4-2 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate but slightly larger and much fewer in number, infrequently with fertile staminodes; sepals 5-7.5 x 2-2.5 mm, connate to ca. ½ of length; petals 6-8 x 2-3.5 mm, glabrous on both surfaces; carpels 3, styles connate, 0.5-1.5 mm long, stigmas 3-lobed, lobes bifurcate; ovary usually unlobed but sometimes slightly 3-lobed. Capsules: ellipsoid, 2.6-3 x 2.2-2.8 cm, trilocular, drupaceous, black at maturity, tardily dehiscent. Seeds, black or black mottled with some white spots, oblong-ellipsoidal, 1.8-2 x 1.1-1.3 cm wide, seed coat smooth, caruncle small to nearly vestigial.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, to 2 m tall. Stems: yellow to yellowish brown or gray, spreading, much-branched, rhizomatous but sometimes upright, woody-succulent with a deep, central root, glabrous; short shoots common; latex yellow in young branches but red in older shoots. Leaves: deciduous, usually fascicled on short shoots; stipules obsolete; petioles absent (usually sessile); blades obovate-spathulate, unlobed or shallowly 3-lobed on active shoots, 0.3-0.9 x 0.7-1.9 cm, chartaceous, base attenuate, margins entire, apex rounded or sometimes emarginate, venation pinnate (palmate with 3 primary veins when 3-lobed), glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences: on short shoots, staminate few-flowered, pedunculate cymes but pistillate flowers few or solitary; bracts 0.4-1 mm, entire, glabrous; pedicels 1-4 (-6.5) mm long. Staminate flowers: sepals ovate-lanceolate, 1.5-3 x 0.5-1 mm, connate at base, margins entire, apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces; corollas tubular-urceolate, white, petals 4-6 x 1.3-2 mm, connate ¾ of length, apex rounded, glabrous on both surfaces; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments connate almost to the top in both series, outer series 1-2.5 mm long, inner series 2.5-4 mm long. Pistillate flowers: like staminate, but sepals 2.5-4 x 0.6-1 mm, distinct; petals 4-4.5 x 1-1.5 mm; carpel 1, style 0.5-1 mm. Capsules: spherical, 0.9-1.1 cm, tardily dehiscent. Seeds: solid dark to golden brown, spherical, 1 cm in diam.; caruncle absent.

description: Shrubs or small trees, 2-5 m tall, dioecious. Stems: grayish brown, ferruginous-hirsutulous at growing tips, becoming glabrate, terete, and channeled, trunk to 20 cm in diam., bark not peeling; latex reddish. Leaves: deciduous; stipules shortly stipitate glandular, ca. 0.5 mm; petioles slender, hirsutulous, (2-)4-9 cm long and 1.5-2 mm in diam.; blades mostly ovate, shallowly and obtusely 3- to 5-lobed, (4-)9-18(-21) x (-4)7-18(-21) cm, membranous, base shallowly but distinctly cordate, apex minutely apiculate, venation palmate with 5-7 primary veins, felty-tomentose on both surfaces when young, becoming sparsely hirtel-lous on adaxial surface, lightly villous on abaxial. Inflorescences: staminate cymes terminal becoming subterminal, peduncles of main florescences 6.2-8.5 cm, coflorescences 1.5-4.5 cm; pistillate terminal, solitary or rarely in pairs; bracts lanceolate, entire, ca. 0.5-1 mm long; pedicels ca. 0.8-1 mm long. Staminate flowers; sepals narrowly lanceolate, 2.8-4.5 x 0.9-1.5 mm; distinct, margins entire, apex obtuse or subacute, glabrous on adaxial surface but hirsute on abaxial; corollas campanulate-tubular, creamy white, petals linear-oblong, 4.5-6 x 0.5-2.5 mm, apex rounded, glabrous on abaxial surface and sparsely hirsutulous on adaxial; stamens 10, monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments distinct, outer series 2-3 mm long and inner series 4.5-5 mm. Pistillate flowers; like staminate but pedicels densely tomentose, ca. 1 mm long at anthesis, becoming 2-6 mm in fruit; sepals 5-7 x 1.8-2 mm; petals 7.5-8.5 x 1.8-4 mm, pubescent near tip; carpels 3, glabrous; styles ca. 3 mm, connate at anthesis but becoming distinct, 1-1.2 mm. Capsules: oblate, somewhat drupaceous, distinctly 3-lobed and carinate, 3.0-3.5 cm in diam., tardily dehiscent. Seeds: grayish black with brownish spots, ellipsoidal-cylindrical, 1.7-2 x 1.3-1.4 cm; caruncle present but diminutive.
bibliographicCitation: Dehgan, Bijan. 2012. Jatropha. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 110: 1--274.

description: Shrubs, 2.0-4.0 m tall, monoecious. Stems: grey or grey-reddish but smooth and green beneath the exfoliating, golden-yellow bark, short shoots present. Leaves: on short shoots, stipules solitary, stipitate glands; petioles 1.5-2.4 cm long and ca. 1 mm in diam., glabrous; blades peltate, orbicular in outline, widely ovate, 2-3 x 2-2.8 cm, base rounded to widely cordate, margins unlobed, densely ciliate-glandular, glands 0.2-0.3 mm, apex rounded or rarely emarginate, venation palmate with 5 primary and 2 minor veins from base, light green and glabrous or sometimes verrucose on adaxial surface and woolly on abaxial. Inflorescences: lateral on branches and short shoots; few-flowered cymes, peduncles 1-1.2 cm (or inconspicuous), 2 or 3 flowers with pedicels 3-3.1 mm; pistillate flowers solitary with pedicels 2 mm. Staminate flowers: sepals angular-ovate, 1.3 x 1.2 mm, strigose; corollas urceolate, red, petals ca. 6 mm, apex reflexed; stamens 10 monadelphous-biseriate (5 + 5), filaments of outer series 3-3.5 mm long, connate ½ of length, those of inner series 5-5.5 mm and connate 1/3 of length. Pistillate flowers: sepals strigose, oblong-lanceolate, 9-12 mm, margins beset with cilia and stipitate glands; corollas and pistils unknown. Capsules: bilocular (or rarely unilocular), 1-1.1 x 1.5-1.6 cm, sepals persistent. Seeds: globose.
