description: Tree or shrub up to 5 m high. Leaves alternate, up to 20 cm long. Petiole bearing a single gland on upper side between base and first pair of pinnae. Pinnae 3-8 pairs, opposite. Leaflets to 25-35 pairs per pinna, opposite, oblong or somewhat sigmoid, 13-26 x 3-6 mm, apex obtuse, rounded, or retuse; main nerve somewhat sigmoid, curving towards distal margin at apex; secondary nerve at proximal margin prominent. Compound inflorescence axis ± erect, projecting shortly beyond foliage, unbranched, to 20 cm long. Peduncles 1-6 per inflorescence, alternate, ± erect, 1-7(-11) cm long. Capitula clavate with basal staminodial fringe absent or only weakly developed, 5-6 x ca. 4 cm, apical part ± spherical. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 7.5-9 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 0.5-1 mm), the lobes ca. 1.5 mm long; corolla 9-11 mm long, the lobes 2-3 mm long; filaments exserted ca. 3-6 mm beyond calyx, free ± to base. Nectar-secreting flowers: calyx 6-8 mm long. Staminodial flowers few, usually weakly developed: calyx 4-6.5 mm long; corolla 6-9 mm long, the lobes ca. 1.5 mm long; filaments 9-13 per flower, exserted to 17 mm beyond calyx. Pods oblong in outline, (4.5-)8-14 (including stipe of 0.5-2 cm) x 2.5-5 cm, the somewhat coriaceous, velutinous valves dehiscent along adaxial suture and sometimes tardily so along the abaxial one, scarcely corrugated; cavity lacking gum. Seeds 6-15 per pod, 12-15 x 6.5-8.5 x 4-4.5 mm; testa black. Field characters. Distinguished from most other Parkia species by its size. Near the Força Aérea Brasileira airbase on the Serra do Cachimbo, it is small tree or shrub occurring infrequently in undisturbed vegetation and commonly in areas which have been cut, burned or grazed, where it is often multistemmed. Leaves somewhat shiny above. Buds dark brown and velutinous, or green and more or less glabrous, with the basal constricted region variable in length. Capitula at anthesis yellow, and staminodial fringe, if present, cream colored and thin. Pods brown to red-brown, comparatively thin-walled. After dehiscence, the seeds either remain in the pod if the gap between the valves is narrow, hang at the edge of the pod suspended by their funicles, or drop to the ground.

description: Tree 8-15 m high. Leaves to 30 cm long, opposite or alternate. Petiole bearing a single gland on upper side between base and first pair of pinnae. Pinnae 6-10 pairs, opposite. Leaflets 21-31 pairs, opposite, oblong, 9-18 x 3-5 mm, apex truncated, rounded, or retuse, base weakly auriculate; main nerve ± central and straight at apex; secondary venation reticulate, prominent. Compound inflorescence axis ascending, unbranched, ca. 0.25(-1) m long. Peduncles 3-9 per inflorescence, alternate, probably pendent, (0.5-)5-11 cm long. Capitula 4-4.5 cm long, biglobose, the basal staminodial fringe ca. 3-3.5 cm diameter and the apical part ± spherical, ca. 2.5 cm diam. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 5-6 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 0.5-1 mm), the lobes ca. 1 mm long; corolla 6-7.5 mm long, the lobes 1-1.5 mm long; filaments exserted 1-2.5 mm beyond calyx. Nectar-secreting flowers: calyx 5-6 mm long. Staminodial flowers: calyx 5-6 mm long; corolla 7-8 mm long, the lobes ca. 4 mm long; filaments exserted to 15 mm beyond calyx. Pods strap-shaped, ca. 15-26 (including stipe of 4-6 cm) x 3-3.5 cm, sutures thickened, symmetrically attenuate into stipe, and the coriaceous, probably indehiscent, glabrous valves shallowly corrugated; presence of gum unknown. Seeds ca. 15 per pod; testa unknown. Field characters. Buds golden brown. Capitula at anthesis yellow.

description: Tree to 18 m high. Leaves either opposite or alternate, spaced to 3 cm apart, or in whorls arising from thin brown twigs bearing prominent lenticels, to 22 cm long. Petiole bearing a small circular or elliptical gland on upper side half way between base and first pair of pinnae. Pinnae 9-18 pairs, opposite or subopposite. Leaflets 60-100 pairs, opposite, linear, 4.5-8 x 1 mm. Compound inflorescence axis distal to leaves, horizontal, or ± pendent, at edge of crown not projecting beyond foliage, often branched towards base or several arising together, to 50 cm long, the branches ca. 10 cm long. Peduncles alternate or sometimes opposite, ± pendent, stiff, 15-35(-50) cm long. Capitula 3.8-5.2 cm diameter x 2.7-3.5 cm long. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 8-10 mm long (including pseudopedicel of ca. 1 mm), the lobes 1.5-2 mm long; corolla 9.5-13 mm long, the lobes 7-8 mm long; filaments exserted 7.5-10 mm beyond calyx, united for ca. 8 mm from the base. Nectar-secreting flowers: calyx 8.5-9 mm long; corolla 9-10 mm long, the lobes 4.5-6.5 mm long. Pods oblong in outline, often curled, or sometimes folded longitudinally down mid-line, 9.5-22 (including stipe of 1-8 cm) x 1.9-3.6 cm, the sutures not thickened and the tough-fleshy, pitted, glabrous, sticky valves somewhat corrugated and indehiscent; endocarp forming cell around each seed; without gum. Seeds to 34 per pod, in two series, ca. 6.5-9 x 5-6.5 x 3-3.5 mm; testa light brown. Field characters. Medium sized tree with a short, stout bole to 45 cm dbh, branching low, without buttresses. Bark thick, dark gray-brown, reddish when fresh, in rectangular flakes. Crown often large, rounded and widespreading, to 20 m across, sometimes reaching to within 1 m of the ground. Foliage dark green. Buds brown, or pinkish when full sized. Capitula at anthesis bright red, turning purplish the next day. Pods are green tinged with red when young, at maturity brownish-yellow or purplish-black, and readily detached from the receptacle; the seeds rattle.

description: Tree to 40 m or more high. Leaves opposite or subopposite, to 28 cm long. Petiole with single elliptical gland on upper side between base and first pair of pinnae. Pinnae 3-9(-12) pairs, opposite or subopposite. Leaflets 21-35(-47) pairs, opposite, usually perpendicular to secondary rachis, oblong, (8.5-)10-25 x 2.5-6.5 mm, often with white coating on underside and less frequently also on upper side, apex rounded or retuse, base strongly or weakly auriculate; main nerve straight at apex. Compound inflorescence axis horizontal or ± ascending, projecting beyond foliage, to 1 m or more long, often branched at base, branches to 70 cm long. Peduncles 1-3 pairs inserted in axils of opposite or subopposite caducous bracts at each of 3-6 nodes of the inflorescence axis, when more than one pair then serially inserted, all pendent, 2.5-16 cm long. Capitula 4.5-8 cm long, biglobose with basal staminodial fringe 4-7.5 cm diam. and apical part ellipsoid to obovoid, 2.2-3.3 cm diam. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 6-10 mm long (including pseudopedicel of ca. 1 mm), the lobes 0.5-1.5 mm long; corolla 6.5-11 mm long, the lobes 0.5-2 mm long; filaments exserted ca. 1-3 mm beyond calyx, ± free at base. Nectar-secretingyZmmx calyx 5.5-11 mm long. Staminodial flowers: calyx 6.5-15 mm long; corolla 8-16 mm long, the lobes either 1-3.5 mm long or in some flowers towards base of capitulum free almost to base; filaments exserted up to 20-35 mm beyond calyx, united for part of length. Pods strapshaped, often falcate, ca. 20-40 cm long [including stipe of 1-7(-12) cm] and (3.3-) 4-5.5(-6) cm broad, the sutures somewhat thickened and the coriaceous, indehiscent, glabrous or glabrescent valves shallowly corrugated; the cavity when fresh containing amber-colored sticky or crystalline gum. Seeds to ca. 20(-23) per pod, ca. 17-22 x 8-11 x 5.5-8.5 mm; testa black. Field characters. Medium sized or large trees, often with a large rounded or rarely somewhat flattened crown; briefly deciduous. Bark grayish, sometimes smelling of methyl salicylate or garlic. Buttresses in large specimens to 2 m high. The white waxy coating which is sometimes present on the leaves is always absent in newly flushed leaves, seedlings, and small saplings. When present the wax develops with age and then flakes off as the leaves become old. The upper side of old leaves is sometimes dark gray-green and ± shiny, giving the crown a silvery appearance. Buds brown. Capitula at anthesis have a creamy-white to yellow-orange staminodial fringe, sometimes tinged with red, and bright yellow fertile flowers, but turn dirty yellow the day after flowering. The pods are dark brown or black, but the abaxial suture often remains green. A considerable range in dimensions can sometimes be found within a population (pers. obs., near Manaus). The pod wall is very tough compared with P. panurensis and P. igneiflora the pod morphology of which is otherwise similar.

description: Tree to 40 m high. Leaves alternate or in whorls at end of twigs, to 70 cm long. Petiole bearing a single or rarely double orbicular gland on upper side at base. Pinnae 12-35 pairs, opposite or subopposite. Leaflets ca. 30-65 pairs, opposite, oblong, 5-12.5 x 1.5-3 mm, apex rounded or obtuse; main nerve straight at apex. Compound inflorescence axis either distal to a whorl of leaves, sparsely branched, the main axis erect and projecting beyond foliage and to 45(-75) cm long, or proximal to a whorl of leaves, usually unbranched, ± horizontal, not projecting beyond foliage, 15-30 cm long. Peduncles to 30 per inflorescence axis or branch, alternate, 1.5-7.5 cm long. Capitula 2-5(-6) cm diam. Hermaphrodite flowers of largest capitula: calyx ca. 12-15 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 0.5-2 mm), the lobes 2-2.5 mm long; corolla ca. 18-26 mm long, the lobes ca. 3-5 mm long and sometimes recurved, splitting readily into longer lobes, united in middle and sometimes free at base; filaments exserted to 18 mm beyond corolla, united at base for 8-11 mm. Hermaphrodite flowers of smallest capitula: calyx 6-9 mm long, the lobes 1-1.5 mm long; corolla 9-14 mm long, the lobes 1-3 mm, at least sometimes recurved. Pods broadly crescent-shaped, (8-) 15-32 x (4-)7-9(-11) x 1.5-2 cm, borne on 0-5(-6.5) cm stipe, the sutures rounded and the ligneous, indehiscent, glabrous valves not corrugated; epicarp when old breaking by means of mosaic-like cracks into tiny fragments. Seeds to 21 per pod, ca. 35-60 x 10-17 x 11-16.5 mm; testa black. Field characters. A large to very large tree with a characteristic bole, 0.4-1 m dbh, straight, cylindrical, narrowing slowly, with gray or rarely reddish, smoothish bark. Plank buttresses sometimes present to 3 m high and extending outwards for 2 m, forking towards ends; when these are absent, base of bole has dumpy thickenings. Crown large, often over-topping neighboring trees, with distinctive appearance because of the whorled leaves, similar to Parkia velutina but twigs thinner. Buds golden-brown. Capitula at anthesis cream-colored, smelling of garlic (Ducke, 1949), but odor perhaps varies between populations. Pods black. Pods and seeds unique in genus.

description: Tree to 40 m high. Many parts including leaf-bearing twigs, leaf rachides, inflorescence axes, peduncles, buds, and pod valves covered with dense red-brown velutinous pubescence. Leaves in whorls at ends of thickened twigs ca. 3 cm diam., to 70(-95) cm long. Petiole bearing an orbicular or broadly elliptical gland on upper side at or just above base. Rachis deeply grooved. Pinnae (17-)30-45(-55) pairs, opposite or subopposite. Leaflets 40-110 pairs, opposite, linear to narrowly sigmoid, 5-11.5 x 1-2 mm, apex acute or rarely rounded; main nerve curved towards distal margin at apex. Compound inflorescence axis proximal to whorl of leaves, ± horizontal, not projecting beyond foliage, unbranched, deeply grooved, to 20 cm long. Peduncles to ca. 15 per inflorescence, alternate, 1.5-4 cm long. Capitula 2.5-3.5 cm diam. Hermaphrodite calyx 7-8 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 1 mm), the lobes 1-1.5 mm long; corolla 11.5-13 mm long, the lobes 1.5-2.5 mm long; filaments shortly exserted, united for ca. 6 mm above base. Pods strap-shaped, sometimes curved, 18-50 (including a stipe of 3-13 cm) x 4.7-6(-8) cm, the sutures not thickened and the subligneous or ligneous, velutinous valves dehiscent along adaxial suture and at least sometimes tardily so along the abaxial one, not corrugated. Seeds to 36 per pod, ca. 18-20 x 9-10 x 5-6 mm; testa black. Field characters. Large tree with buttresses to 2 m high and extending outwards to 2 m. Crown distinctive because of whorled leaves. The previous year’s growth, immediately below the leaves, is not velutinous and bears leaf scars and the inflorescences. Several inflorescence axes may arise on one twig from more or less adjacent axillary buds. Buds dark brown. Capitula at anthesis deep red and sweetsmelling.

description: Large tree, the bole to 1.5 m dbh, sometimes with plank buttresses to 2 m high and extending outwards for ca. 1.5 m. Crown large and rounded, briefly deciduous. Leaves darkish green and somewhat shiny above. Buds covered with greenish-hoary pubescence. Capitula at anthesis like tiny powder puffs, creamy white with white filaments and yellow anthers, and a strong sweet smell, turning yellow the next day. Pods densely velutinous, and green or fawn when young, brown or reddish-brown when mature, and glabrescent when old.

description: Tree 25-30 m high. Leaves alternate, to 22 cm long. Petiole bearing a single ovoid gland on upper side between base and first pair of pinnae. Pinnae 10-16 pairs, opposite or subopposite. Leaflets 40-44 pairs, opposite, linear-oblong to sigmoid, 5-9 x 1-1.5 mm, apex pointed, base strongly auriculate; main nerve weakly sigmoid. Compound inflorescence axis unbranched, ca. 40 cm long. Peduncles to ca. 8 per inflorescence, alternate, pendent, 8-22 cm long. Capitula ca. 5.5 cm long, biglobose. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 5-5.5 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 0.5-1 mm), the lobes 0.5-1 mm long; corolla ca. 6.5 mm long, the lobes 1 mm long; filaments exserted ca. 1.5 mm beyond calyx, free ± to base. Nectar-secreting flowers: calyx to ca. 5 mm long. Staminodial flowers: calyx 7-7.5 mm long; corolla 7.5-9 mm long, the lobes 1-1.5 mm long; filaments exserted to 15 mm beyond calyx, ± united within corolla. Pods strap-shaped, 28-35 (including stipe of 7-10 cm) x 3-3.8 cm, the coriaceous, indehiscent, usually glabrous valves having distinct reticulate venation and depressed around widely spaced seeds; presence of gum unknown. Seeds ca. 11-15 per pod; testa unknown. Field characters. Buds brown. Capitula at anthesis sulfur yellow. Pods brown.

description: Tree. Leaves opposite, to 50 cm long. Petiole bearing a circular or elliptical gland on upper side, half way between base and first pair of pinnae. Pinnae 5-15 pairs, opposite or subopposite. Leaflets 50-80 pairs, opposite, linear, sometimes curved, 7-15 x 1-2 mm. Compound inflorescence axis usually proximal to leaves, pendent, unbranched, to ca. 40 cm long. Peduncles in up to 3(-5) pairs per axis, opposite, pendent, very flexible, ca. 30-80 cm long. Receptacle apex spherical. Capitula ca. 4 cm diameter x 3 cm long. Hermaphrodite calyx 9.5-11.5 mm long (including pseudopedicel of ca. 1 mm), the lobes 1.5-2.5 mm long; corolla 11-13.5 mm long, the lobes 5-7 mm long; filaments exserted 4-8 mm beyond calyx, united for ca. 8 mm above base. Nectar-secreting flowers: calyx 9-11.5 mm long; corolla 9.5-12 mm long, the lobes 2.5-4 mm long. Pods strap-shaped, sometimes curved, ca. 25 (including stipe of ca. 6-8 cm) x 3.5-4.2 cm, the adaxial suture much thickened and secreting large quantities of sticky amber-colored gum into which the seeds are released, and the subligneous, glabrous, uncorrugated valves dehiscent only down the adaxial suture; the cavity without gum. Seeds to ca. 28 per pod, in two series, similar in size to those of P. pendula. Field characters. A large tree (fide Ducke), although there are fertile collections from trees only 10-15 m. Ducke (1925b) says that it is similar in appearance to Parkia pendula, thus implying a flattened crown. Petioles and leaf-bearing twigs have prominent lenticels. Buds golden-brown. Capitula at anthesis purplish. Immature pods green, mature ones black.

description: Tree to 18 m high. Leaves usually alternate, to 40 cm long. Petiole bearing a single or sometimes double, ovate to orbicular gland on upper side. Pinnae 3-7 (-10) pairs, opposite. Leaflets 17-26 pairs, opposite, ± perpendicular to secondary rachis or sometimes at an obtuse angle to rachis beyond point of insertion, oblong, 27-39 x 5.5-10 mm, apex rounded or retuse; main nerve straight at apex. Compound inflorescence axis ± erect, projecting far beyond foliage, sparsely branched or unbranched, to 5 m long. Peduncles to ca. 12 per inflorescence branch, alternate or distichous, pendent, 5-40 cm long. Capitula 6.5-8.5 cm long, biglobose with basal staminodial fringe 5.5-8 cm diam. and apical part ellipsoid, 3-3.5 cm diameter. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 8-11.5 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 1-1.5 mm long), the lobes to 1-1.5 mm long; corolla 10-13 mm long, the lobes 1.5 mm long; filaments exserted ca. 2-3 mm beyond calyx, free to within 2 mm of base. Nectar-secreting flowers: calyx ca. 10 mm long. Staminodial flowers: calyx 8-12 mm long; corolla 10-21 mm long, the lobes either 1.5-2 mm long or often in flowers towards base of capitulum free ± to base; filaments exserted to 15-35 mm beyond calyx, either free ± to base or irregularly united to neck of corolla. Pods strap-shaped, sometimes slightly curved or twisted, ca. 20-35 (including stipe of 2.5-6.5 cm) x 3-4.4 cm, the sutures somewhat thickened and the coriaceous, indehiscent glabrescent or subglabrous valves shallowly corrugated; endocarp septate, the cavity when fresh containing amber-colored sticky or crystalline gum. Seeds to 25 per pod, ca. 15.5-18 x 9-11 x 6-8 mm, testa black. Field characters. Small to medium sized tree with straight narrow bole to 35 cm dbh and small buttresses in largest individuals. Bark dark reddish-brown. Crown small and rounded, briefly deciduous. The far-exserted compound inflorescence makes the trees distinctive from a distance but the axis is perhaps shorter in some populations (see below). Buds brown. Capitula at anthesis are either reddish, with bright red, orange or purplish staminodia, or yellow, with intensely yellow staminodia (see below). Fertile flowers of capitula with red staminodia have been described as brownish-red, brownish-pink, or yellow; on trees I have studied, the fertile flowers had pink-red corollas and pink anthers dusted with yellow pollen. Mature pods dark brown.

description: Tree to 45 m. Leaves opposite, to 22 cm long. Petiole bearing a single elliptical gland just above base. Pinnae 3-5(-6) pairs, opposite. Leaflets 15-20 pairs, opposite, oblong, broadening towards base, 29-43 x 6.5-9.5(-l2) mm, usually with white waxy coating on underside, apex acute, base weakly auriculate; main nerve straight or very slightly curved towards distal margin at apex. Inflorescence axis pendent, within crown, unbranched, ca. 25-65 cm long. Peduncles 1-4(-6) per inflorescence, opposite, 11-45 cm long. Capitula biglobose, 15-21.5 x 5-8 cm, the basal staminodial fringe and ellipsoid apical part ± equal in diameter. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 15-20 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 1.5-2 mm long), the lobes to 4 mm long; corolla 20-26 mm long, the lobes 1.5-2.5 mm long; filaments exserted 8-14 mm beyond calyx, free ± to base. Nectar-secreting flowers: calyx ca. 14 mm long. Staminodial flowers: calyx ca. 13-15 mm long; corolla 21-24 mm long, the lobes 2-3 mm long; filaments exserted ca. 40-45 mm beyond calyx. Pods strap-shaped, sometimes twisted, ca. 52-62 (including stipe of 9-10 cm) x 5.3-5.9 cm, the sutures somewhat thickened and the coriaceous, indehiscent, glabrous valves shallowly corrugated; the cavity containing gum (fide Duarte, 1978). Seeds to ca. 30 per pod, 18-19.5 x 9-13 x 4-6 mm; testa black. Field characters. Described by Ducke and Black (1953) as one of the largest trees of the hylea. Bole to ca. 1 m diameter with narrow forking buttresses extending outwards ca. 2 m and ca. 1 m high, merging abruptly with the bole. Bark lacks smell (fide Ducke). Crown briefly deciduous, rather open, sometimes flattish, silvery-gray because of waxy coating on underside of leaves, which is lacking in new leaves and seedlings. Upper surface of leaves somewhat shiny. Buds red-brown. Capitula at anthesis have a white fringe, the fertile flowers are lemon yellow from the corolla and filaments, and the anthers are yellow with red sutures. Capitula turn dirty yellow the day after anthesis. Pods brown.

description: Tree to 40 m high. Leaves decussate, to 20(24) cm long. Petiole bearing a single gland on upper side between base and first pair of pinnae. Pinnae 4-6(-9) pairs, opposite. Leaflets 21-35 pairs, opposite, oblong, (15-)20-28 x (3-)4-6 mm, apex rounded or retuse; main nerve straight at apex. Compound inflorescence axis erect, projecting above foliage, unbranched, to ca. 1 m long. Peduncles to 8 per inflorescence, decussate, erect, 8-45 x 0.6-1 cm. Capitula clavate, 5.5-7.5 cm long, basal part 2-3 cm diam., apical part broadly ellipsoid, to 5 cm diam. Hermaphrodite flowers: calyx 10-14 mm long (including pseudopedicel of 1-2 mm), the lobes to 2 mm long; corolla 11.5-15 mm long, the lobes 1.5-3 mm long; filaments exserted ca. 3-5 mm beyond calyx, free ± to base. Nectar-secreting and staminodial flowers: calyx 6.5-9 mm long; corolla ca. 1 mm longer than calyx, the lobes free or readily splitting; filaments scarcely exceeding corolla. Pods strap-shaped, (15-)30-55 (including stipe of 5-9 cm) x 3.5-6 cm, the sutures somewhat thickened and the coriaceous to subligneous, indehiscent, velutinous valves having many cross-wise cracks, scarcely corrugated; the cavity containing amber-colored sticky or crystalline gum. Seeds to 25 per pod, ca. 19-22 x 9-11 x 7-9 mm; testa black. Field characters. Bole 30-60 cm dbh, branching high. Bark reddish-brown. Buttresses ca. 50(-100) cm high and extending outwards to 50 cm. Crown briefly deciduous, sometimes small and poorly formed. Leaves darkish glossy green above, 1-3 pairs produced on each year’s growth. Pinnae often not flat in plane of rachis but held at an angle of less than 180° between upper sides. Buds red-brown. Capitula at anthesis bright lemon-yellow at apex, red at base. As buds begin to open, the whole capitulum is yellow because all the flowers have a yellow corolla. By late afternoon the capitula are bicolored because although the fertile and upper nectar-secreting flowers have yellow anthers, the basal flowers have short red filaments. There is no staminodial fringe. In contrast to other species in section Parkia the flowers at the very base of the capitulum secrete small droplets of nectar. Pods brown. This species may be under-collected because the capitula and fruits project directly above the crown and are therefore not visible from below. The seedling is distinctive. The leaves are red when grown in shade. The pinnae are held in a flat plane with the rachis, and with an angle of 20°-50° between secondary rachides. In a leaf with more than one pair of pinnae the terminal pair has more leaflets.

description: Árvore grande, 25-30(-40) m de altura. Ramos, pecíolos e inflorescência ferrugíneo-puberulentos. Folhas 2-pinadas, pecioladas, 20-35 cm de comprimento, com 7-9 pares de pinas primárias altemas, subopostas ou opostas, pecioladas; pecíolo comum espesso, cilíndrico, densamente avermelhado-pubescente, 6-8 cm de comprimento; pecíolo primário 6-2 mm de comprimento; pinas primárias de 5-15 cm de comprimento, com 6-12 pares de pínulas altemas, curto-pecioladas; pecíolo secundário de 2-1 mm de comprimento; pínulas oblongas, 2.5-5 cm de comprimento por 1-1.5 cm de largura, a face superior lisa, glabra, a inferior, principalmente sobre as nervuras, finamente pubescente; base obtusa ou arredondada; ápice agudo ou obtuso; margem lisa. Nervura primária impressa na face superior, proeminente na face inferior; nervuras secundárias finamente impressas em ambas as faces. Inflorescência paniculado-corimbosa, densamente ferrugíneo-pubescente, formada de várias espigas densifloras, longo-pedunculadas, de 2-5 cm de comprimento. Flores cremes, sésseis, 2.5-3 mm de comprimento; cálice urceolado, 1-1.5 mm de comprimento, 5-laciniado no ápice, na face externa esparsamente pubescente; lacínias curtas, arredondadas no ápice; corola com cinco pétalas livres, glabras, obovado-espatuladas, cuculadas, 2,5 mm de comprimento, com unha curta. Estames cinco, epipétalos glabros, com anteras oblongas, introrsas; estaminódios cinco, decíduos, livres, de ápice estreito, ovoide-claviforme. Ovário fusiforme, ligeiramente pubescente ou subglabra, subséssil; estilete curto e estigma apical. Fruto legume plano, reto, oblongo, curto-estipitado, espesso, indeiscente, glabra, 20-24 cm de comprimento por 3.5-4 mm de largura.

description: Árvore de 10 m de altura e de rara ocorrência (Ducke, 1959). Ramos, pecíolos e inflorescêntia finamente ferrugíneo-pubescentes. Folhas 2-pinadas, pecioladas, 25-30 cm de comprimento com 4-5 pares de pinas opostas; pecíolo comum 6-8(-11) cm de comprimento, raque glabrescente; pecíolo primário 1-1,5(-2) cm de comprimento, glabrescente, espesso e enrugado transversalmente na região do pulvino, delgado e anguloso na raque; pinas 5-8 cm de comprimento com 5-7(-8) pares de folíolos opostos, curto-peciolados; pecíolo secundário 2-3 mm de comprimento, rugoso, glabro; folíolos secundários oblongo-lanceolados, alternos, 4-6.5 cm de comprimento por 1.5-2.5 cm de largura, coriáceos, glabros e lustrosos na face superior, na inferior opacos e ligeiramente ferrugíneo-puberulentos; base obtusa ou cuneada, ligeiramente desigual; ápice agudo e margem inteira. Nervuras primárias e secundárias imersas na face superior, na inferior apenas a nervura primária proeminente, as secundárias ligeiramente promínulas ou inconspícuus. Inflorescência paniculado-corimbosa, 11-18 cm de comprimento, composta de numerosas espigas longo-pedunculadas. Flores pequenas, sésseis, 4-5 mm de comprimento; cálice com hipanto, ferrugíneo-tomentoso extemamente, 1.5-3 mm de comprimento, 5-laciniado no ápice; tubo alargando-se para o ápice, de 1.5-2 mm de comprimento com pequeno hipanto na base; lacínias profundamente partidas, triangulares e arredondadas, extemamente subglabras ou apenas escabrosas; corola com cinco pétalas livres (na prefloração imbricadas), espatuladas, 2.5-3 mm de comprimento, glabras em ambas as faces. Estames cinco, epipétalos, 2 mm de comprimento; glabros; anteras oblongas, dorsifixas, introrsas de deiscência rimosa, estaminódios cinco, longos, 2.5-3 mm de comprimento, filiformes, ápice dilatado, claviforme. Ovário fusiforme, piloso; pelos longos, ferrugíneo; estilete curto, glabro, recurvado e estigma apical cônico. Fruto desconhecido.

description: A subespécie congestiflora é perfeitamente distinta das subespécies glabrifolia e macrostachya principalmente pela pilosidade amarelo-seríceo-dourada que recobre o dorso dos folíolos, maior intensidade de pelos na raque das folhas e inflorescência mais robusta; as folhas e os folíolos em geral são maiores e estes em maior número, com textura submembranácea, sedosa; a casca da árvore é lisa e exuda secreção aqüosa marrom-translúcida (ex A. G. Alston 348).

description: Árvore de 12-15 m de altura por 30-60 cm de diâmetro; córtex subíntegra, apenas fissurada, acinzentado-escura. Folhas grandes, 2-pinadas, pecioladas, com 10 pares de pinas opostas ou subopostas, pecioladas; pecíolos comum de 14 cm de comprimento, canaliculado, com 13-14 pares de folíolos altemos peciolados; pecíolo primário subglabra, 7 mm a 1,4 cm de comprimento; pecíolos secundários 2-3 mm de comprimento; folíolos secundários altemos, elíticos, 2.5-4(-5) cm de comprimento por 1.5-2 cm de largura, quando jovens densamente pilosos em ambas as faces; subcoriáceos ou apenas cartáceos; base arredondada; ápice obtuso ou atenuado, em geral levemente emarginado; margem subrevoluta. Nervura primária na face superior imersa, na inferior proeminente e densamente pilosa; nervuras secundárias apenas promínulas na página inferior. Inflorescêntia corimboso-paniculada, compacta, 20-30 cm de comprimento, composta de espigas densas, de 6-12 cm de comprimento. Flores amarelas, pequenas; cálice urceolado, 2-2.5 mm de comprimento, 5-lobado no ápice; lobos arredondados, ciliados nas margens, pilosos em ambos os lados; pelos híspidos; corola com cinco pétalas, espatuladas, conchiformes, 3-3.5 mm de comprimento margem escariosa, delgada e seca, extemamente híspida. Estames cinco, epipétalos, glabros, 5.3-3.5 mm de comprimento; anteras rimosas, introrsas, quase do tamanho dos filetes; estaminódios cinco, lineares, ápice dilatado, face interna clavada. Ovário fusiforme, anguloso, glabro, 2-2.5 mm de comprimento, multiovulado (20-30 óvulos); estilete espesso, em geral recurvado, 0.5 mm de comprimento; estígma punctiforme. Fruto, legume piano, curto, estipitado, liso, um pouco recurvado, espesso e rígido, castanho-escuro, 15-22 cm de comprimento por 3.5-4.5 cm de largura, truncado no ápice, estreitado na base, internamente com polpa alva, aromática; sementes vermelhas, brilhantes, elipsoides, 16-21 mm de comprimento por 6-7 mm de largura.
bibliographicCitation: Freitas da Silva, Marlene. 1986. Dimorphandra (Caesalpiniaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 44: 1-128.

description: Árvore grande, de 10-30 m de altura por 35-40 cm de diâmetro. Ramos com córtex esbranquiçado, lenticeloso, ou quando jovem ferrugíneo-pubescente. Folhas 2-pinadas, longo-pecioladas, até 25 cm de comprimento com 4 pares de pinas primárias opostas, pecioladas; pecíolo comum subcilíndrico, 8 cm de comprimento; pecíolo primário, 1-1.5 cm de comprimento; pecíolo secundário cilíndrico espesso, pubescente 2-4 mm de comprimento; pinas primárias com 7-9 pares de pínulas alternas, oblongas a ovado-oblongas, 3.5-5 cm de comprimento por 1.5-2 cm de largura, ligeiramente oblíquas ou arredondadas na base, agudas até cuspidadas no ápice, margem inteira, um pouco ondulada, membranáceus, glabrus e lustrosas na face superior, na inferior pubérulas. Inflorescência corimboso-paniculada, 10-12 cm de comprimento, constituída de pequenas espigas densiflorus, de 4 cm de comprimento. Flores esverdeadas, 3-4 mm de comprimento; cálice glabrescente, 2,5 mm de comprimento, 5-laciniado no ápice; lacínias subtriangulares, arredondadas no ápice; corola com cinco pétalas, 4-4.5 mm de comprimento, glabras, cuculadas. Estames 5.4-5 mm de comprimento, anteras dorsifixas, introrsas; estaminódios cinco, livres, glabros, filiformes, apenas o ápice dilatado, 5 mm de comprimento. Ovário fusiforme, glabro, estígma séssil. Fruto legume achatado, reto, lenhoso, indeiscente, 14 cm de comprimento, incluindo o estípete.
bibliographicCitation: Freitas da Silva, Marlene. 1986. Dimorphandra (Caesalpiniaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 44: 1-128.

description: Árvore pequena 8-12(-15) m de altura por 25-30 cm de diâimetro, com todas as suas partes glabras ou glabrescentes. Folhas 2-pinadas, pecioladas, com 2 pares de pinas opostas, pecioladas; pecíolo comum longo, 5-7(-9) cm de comprimento, subcilíndrico, estriado longitudinalmente; pinas com 3-4(-5) pares de folíolos altemos em geral o terminal abortado, pecioladas; pecíolo primário subcilíndrico, 2.5-3 cm de comprimento; pecíolo secundário cilíndrico 4,5 mm de comprimento; folíolos secundários ovado-lanceolados, 7.5-8(-12,5) cm de comprimento por 3-3.8(-5) cm de largura, base arredondada ou atenuada, subigual, ápice caudado-acuminado, margem inteira, cartáceos, nitidamente venulosos, na face inferior opacos, pálidos; nervura primária impressa na face superior, as secundárias e superiores a estas promínulas, na face inferior proeminentes. Inflorescência corimboso-paniculada, constituída de várias espigas curtas, longo-pedunculadas, eretas, 3.5-4.5(-5) cm de comprimento, as intemas menores, glabras ou esparsamente pilosas; pelos amarelados, pequeníssimos, visíveis somente sob lente. Flores amarelas, fétidas, glabras, sésseis, 3-3,5 mm de comprimento; cálice curto, 1-1.2 mm de comprimento, glabro, tubuloso, 5-laciniado no ápice; lacínias iguais, obtusas no ápice, de margem irregularmente recortada, ou íntegra; corola exserta do cálice, 2-3 vezes o seu comprimento; pétalas cinco, iguais, obovadas, de prefloração imbricada, 3 mm de comprimento. Estames cinco, epipétalos 3.5 mm de comprimento, menores do que os estaminódios; filetes lineares, glabros, espessos, eretos; anteras oblongas, dorsifixas, introrsas, de deiscência rimosa; estaminódios cinco, alternando com os estames férteis, lineares, de ápice claviforme-espatulado, 4 mm de comprimento. Ovário sessil, oblongo ou elipsoide, 2.5 mm de comprimento; estilete espesso, e estigma cônico, diminutamente perfurado no ápice, inserto na flor. Fruto, legume aplanado, 9-10 cm de comprimento por 3.5-4 cm de largura, ereto, ligeiramente recurvado; base cuneada e ápice agudo, de superfície glabra, reticulado-venosa, indeiscente e de margem espessa; sementes elíticas, testa glabra, dura, 1.5-2 cm de comprimento por 0.5 cm de largura.
bibliographicCitation: Freitas da Silva, Marlene. 1986. Dimorphandra (Caesalpiniaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 44: 1-128.

description: Árvore mediana até grande com 18-24 m de altura. Ramos jovens, pecíolos e inflorescências finamente ferrugíneos-tomentosos. Folhas 2-pinadas, pecioladas com 13-15 pares de pinas alternas; pecíolo comum cilíndrico, robusto, tomento-ferruginoso, 26-28 cm de comprimento, base espessada, subcilíndrica, na parte superior quase tetraédrico; pinas opostas, 9-12 cm de comprimento as inferiores menores, 35-40 pares de folíolos, raque espessada na base, sulcada na face superior, na inferior cilíndrica ferrugíneo-tomentosa; folíolos lineares, coriáceos, a face superior brilhante, a inferior opaca, tomentela, base obliquamente truncada, ápice obtuso, margem inteira subrevoluta. Nervura primária impressa na face superior, na inferior ferrugínea com pelos esparsos, amarelos e brilhantes; nervuras secundárias e superiores inconspícuas. Inflorescência racemoso-paniculada com poucos rácemos por inflorescêntia; rácemos longos, 35-43 cm de comprimento por 2-2.5 cm de espessura na antese. Flores: calice ciatiforme, curtamente 5-laciniado no ápice, ferrugíneo-tomentoso em ambas as faces, na maturação subglabra; lacínias subtriangulares com o ápice obtuso; corolo com cinco pétalas de prefloração valvar; pétalas obovadas, côncavas, 6 mm de comprimento, ápice obtuso, arredondado, unguiculatus na base; unha estreita e curta. Estames cinco, epipétalos, menores do que os estaminódios, filetes espessos, pianos, anteras subbasifixas, introrsas, oblongas; estaminódios cinco, glabros, petaloides, conatos no ápice; filete espesso, cilíndrico na base. Ovário fusiforme, longo-estipitado, híspido-tomentoso; pelos avermelhados, 1-locular, 10-ovulado, em média; estilete curto, glabro; estigma terminal punctiforme; óvulos elítico-arredondados, parietas, presos na sutura marginal superior do ovário. Fruto: legume falciforme até 15 cm de comprimento por 6-7 cm de largura, glabro, escuro e finamente reticulado na superficie; sementes poucas ou até 10, oval-oblongas, achatadas, com testa lisa, escura e muito dura.
bibliographicCitation: Freitas da Silva, Marlene. 1986. Dimorphandra (Caesalpiniaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 44: 1-128.

description: Árvore pequena a mediana, 3-5(-8) m de altura por 12 cm de diâmetro, muito raramente atingindo maior porte, 10-20 m (Rizzini, 1976), e geralmente de crescimento tortuoso; copa ampla, folhosa e elegante; casca castanho-acinzentado, rugosa; ramos jovens, pecíolos e raque das folhas acinzentado-pubescentes, depois a subglabros, glabrescentes ou perfeitamente glabros, lenticelosos. Folhas 2-pinadas, pecioladas, até 30-40 cm de comprimento, com 5-8(-9) pares de pinas primárias alternas, subopostas ou opostas; pecíolo comum até 13 cm de comprimento, subcílindrico, profunda e estreitamente canaliculado; pecíolo primário 5-10(-15) mm de comprimento; pecíolo secundário 1-2 mm de comprimento; pinas primárias com 10-20 pares de panículas secondárias altemas; panículas ovais ou oblongas, 22.5 cm de comprimento por 1-1.6 mm de largura, finamente seríceas na face inferior, na superior glabrescentes; base cordada, retusa ou obtusa; ápice emaiginado ou ligeiramente subagudo; margem inteira, plana ou apenas ligeiramente revoluta; nervuras primárias e secundárius imersas na face superior, na inferior apenas a nervura central proeminente, as demais promínulas ou inconspícuus. Inflorescência paniculado-corimbosa, 1.5-20 cm de comprimento, constituída de espigas curtas, densifloras, reunidas em pequenos corimbos longo-pedunculados, de 5-6 cm de comprimento; as espigas internas menores. Flores pequenas, amarelas ou cremes, fétidas, sésseis, 3.5 mm de comprimento, cálice glabro, 1 mm de comprimento, tubuloso, 5-laciniado no ápice; lacínias obtusas ou arredondadas, intemamente com alguns pelos; corola com cinco pétalas oblongas, espatuladas, 2 mm de comprimento, glabras em ambas as faces, reflexas na antese; estames cinco, epipétalos, 5 mm de comprimento, glabros; filetes delgados; anteras oblongas, de base sagitada, introrsas; estaminódios cinco, filiformes, longos, ápice dilatado, carnoso; ovário oblongo, fusiforme, glabro com estilete muito curto e estigma cartilaginoso, estreito. Fruto indeiscente, estipitado, 8-15 cm de comprimento, ereto na árvore, reto ou ligeiramente recurvado, fortemente pedunculado, comprimido lateralmente, superfície glabra, marrom e pouco rugosa quando maduro.

description: Árvore mediana a grande, 15-18(-30) m de altura por 90 cm de diâmetro, tronco e copa semelhantes ao Guapuruvú [Schizolobium parahyba (Vell.) Blake]. Ramos jovens, raques, pecíolos e inflorescêntia finamente puberulentos. Folhas 2-pinadas, longo-pecioladas, até 30 cm de ccmprimento, com 4-6 pares de pinas opostas, pecioladas; pecíolo comum subcilíndrico, 6-10 cm de comprimento; pecíolo primário, 5-10 mm de comprimento; pecíolo secundário cilíndrico, 1-2(-3) mm de comprimento, densamente piloso; pinas 8-10(-20) cm de comprimento, com 12 pares de folíolos altemos, oblongos a oblongo-lanceolados, 3-4 cm de comprimento por 1-1.5 cm de largura, base arredondada ou obtusa, ápice acuminado, mucronado, margem inteira, membranáceos, subcartáceos, aparentemente glabros porém escabrosos na face superior, na inferior apenas puberulentos. Inflorescência corimboso-paniculada, 12-15 cm de comprimento, constituída de pequenas espigas multifloras, de 3-4 cm de comprimento. Flores amareladas ou cremes, 3-4 mm de comprimento; cálice glabro, 2 mm de comprimento, profundamente laciniado no ápice; lacínas cinco, regulares, arredondadas, com as margens ou apenas o ápice ciliado, do mesmo tamanho do tubo; corola com cinco pétalas oblongas, espatuladas ou obtusas no ápice, 2.5-3(-4) mm de comprimento, glabras em ambas as faces, levemente cuculadas, com unha curta, geralmente o dobro do comprimento do cálice; estames cinco, epipétalos, 2-3 mm de comprimento, glabros, filete linear, anteras dorsifixas, introrsas, ovado-oblongas, 1.5 mm de comprimento; estaminódios cinco, livres, glabros, 3 mm de comprimento, filetes filiformes, ápice dilatado-petaloide, lanceolado, 1 mm de comprimento; ovário fusiforme, glabro, 2-2.5 mm de comprimento, estreito, estigma dilatado, séssil. Fruto, legume achatado, quase reto, lenhoso, escuro, indeiscente, espesso, de superfície lisa, brilhante, 10-15 cm de comprimento por 3-4 cm de largura; sementes subcilíndricas, 10-12 por fruto, com testa dura, lisa, brilhante.
bibliographicCitation: Freitas da Silva, Marlene. 1986. Dimorphandra (Caesalpiniaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 44: 1-128.

description: Árvore de porte em geral mediano ou bastante grande, 10-25(-40) m de altura, fuste robusto, cilíndrico, copa ampla, umbeliforme. Ramos jovens, pecíolos, raque e pedúnculo da inflorescência densamente avermelhado-tomentosos. Folhas alternas, 2-pinadas, longo-pecioladas, 17.5 cm de comprimento com 8.10.14(-16) pares de pinas opostas; pecíolo comum espesso, 3.5-6 cm de comprimento; pecíolo primário, 4 mm de comprimento; pinas de 9 cm de comprimento, as basais menores; folíolos pequeninos, 22-38 pares opostos, sésseis, 8-10 mm de comprimento por 1 mm de largura, coriáceos, na face superior lisos, brilhantes, convexos, glabros, na inferior ferrugíneos, opacos, estrigosos, lineares, ligeiramente falcados, algumas vezes côncavos, auriculados unilateralmente na base, ápice obtuso, margem inteira, revoluta, ciliada. Nervura primária impressa na face superior, na inferior proeminente, pilosa. Inflorescência paniculado-racemosa, longo-pedunculada; rácemos longo-pedimculados, espessos, em número de 2-5, com 20-40 cm de comprimento por 1.2-1.5 cm de largura na antese. Flores pequeninas, alaranjadas, numerosas, pediceladas; pedicelos de 0.5-1 mm de comprimento; cálice alaranjado, cupuliforme, 1 mm de comprimento, 5-lobado; lobos curtos, glabrescentes; corola com cinco pétalas glabras, 3 mm de comprimento, oblongas; estames cinco, livres, glabros, mais curtos do que os estaminódios; estaminódios cinco, livres, glabros, 4 mm de comprimento, lineares, recurvados na região mediana, clavado-espatulados no ápice, com antera rudimentar, caduca na antese. Ovário fusiforme, subséssil de densamente amarelo-pubescente. Fruto, legume piano, falcado, 17 cm de comprimento por 7.5 cm de largura, lenhoso, longo-estipitado, de superfície finamente estriada, com poucas sementes.
bibliographicCitation: Freitas da Silva, Marlene. 1986. Dimorphandra (Caesalpiniaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 44: 1-128.

description: Árvore alta, 50 m ou mais, com altas sapopemas na base do tronco. Ramos jovens, pecíolos, pedúnculos e raques das folhas e inflorescêntia densamente pilosos; pelos avermelhados ou vermelho-ferrugíneo. Folhas 2-pinadas, longo-pecioladas, alternas, com 18-27 pares de pinas altemas, de 23 cm de comprimento médio; pecíolo comum subcilíndrico, ligeiramente achatado na face ventral, densamente ferrugíneo-pubescente, 4 cm de comprimento; pecíolo primário espesso porém muito curto, cônico, 1 mm de comprimento; pinas com 32-50 pares de folíolos; folíolos secundários com 4-7 mm de comprimento, os apicais menores, os maiores com 1 mm de largura, sésseis, oblongos, ligeiramente falcado, subcoriáceos, a face superior glabra, pouco lustrosa, a inferior pálida, opaca e subglabra; base truncada, um pouco obliqua, subauriculada unilateralmente; ápice agudo, mucronado; margem inteira revoluta. Nervura mediana apenas marcada na face superior, proeminente e pouco pilosa na face inferior. Inflorescência amplamente paniculado-racemosa, constituída de 7-14 rácemos delgados, longos, até 15-18 cm de comprimento, com o pedúnculo e raque moderadamente espesso e densamente ferrugineo-puberulentos. Flores subsésseis, numerosas, com uma bractéola lateral longa, delgada e pubescente; os botões jovens completamente sésseis; cálice densamente ferrugíneo-pubescente, 5-laciniado no ápice; corola com cinco pétalas não reflexas (ainda muito jovens). Estames cinco, glabros; estaminódios cinco, livres, glabros, de ápice laminar com antera rudimentar. Ovário cilíndrico, amarelo-viloso. Fruto (colhido sob a árvore) plano, falcado, estipitado, com poucas sementes, segundo Ducke (1935), muito parecido com o de D. velutina.

description: Árvore grande alcançando até 30-40 m de altura, com volumoso fuste de 1 m de diâimetro, freqüentemente dominante na área onde ocorre; casca rajada, acinzentada, com estrias longitudinais; copa densa, aberta, e a extremidade dos ramos glabrescentes, lenticelosa. Folhas 2-pinadas, pecioladas, 33 cm de comprimento, com 2 pares de pinas opostas; pecíolo comum esparsamente pubescente, 5.5-6.5 cm de comprimento; pecíolo primário de 2-4 cm de comprimento; pinas com 2-4(-5) pares de folíolos peciolados (os superiores as vezes abortados); folíolos secundários alternos ou subopostos, elíticos ou oblongos, variando de 8-12 pares por pina, 5.8-15 cm de comprimento por 2.5-5.5 cm de largura, peciolados, cartáceos ou subcartáceos, discolores, brilhantes, glabros ou glabrescentes ou ainda com fina camada de substância cerífera branca na face superior, na inferior cinéreo-puberulento; base arredondada ou atenuada, ligeiramente cordada ou obtusa, retusa ou ainda agudo-cuneada; ápice curtamente agudo-acuminado, e margem inteira, pecíolo secundário de 2-4 cm de comprimento. Nervuras secundárias cerca de 12 pares, promínulas na face superior, na inferior proeminentes. Inflorescêntia paniculado-racemosa, rácemos em geral solitários, 10.5-17 cm de comprimento por 2,5 cm de diâmetro na antese (pode ocorrer aos pares, porém, muito raramente em maior número); rácemos longo-pedunculados, especialmente os superiores, ferrugíneo-tomentosos; pedúnculo fortemente espesso, pubescente, 3.5-10 cm de comprimento. Flores brancas ou amarelo-pálido; pedicelos tomentosos, 3-5 mm de comprimento; cálice 5-lobulado, turbinado-campanulado, 4-5 mm de comprimento, extemamente seríceo-pubescente, 5-lobulado no ápice; lóbulos deltoide-triangulares, obtusos, 1 mm de comprimento por 1,7 mm de largura; corola com cinco pétalas obovado-oblongas, espatuladas, 7-7.5 mm de comprimento por 1.8 mm de largura, glabra na face externa, na interna, na parte inferior restante, densamente seríceo-pilosa. Estames cinco, glabros, filetes de 6.5-7.5 mm de comprimento; antera oblonga, 2 mm de comprimento por 1 mm de largura, introrsa; estaminódios cinco, concrescidos no ápice com antera rudimentar, livres na base, decíduos, glabros, em forma de cúpula, 1-1.5 cm de comprimento; ápice espesso, laminar, freqüentemente elítico-lanceolado. Ovário estipitado ou ainda subséssil, 2.5 mm de comprimento; estilete estreitamente fusiforme, ligeiramente falcado, 7-7.5 mm de comprimento por 1 mm de largura, densamente amarelo-ceríceo, piloso, estígma punctiforme; óvulos 5 ou mais. Fruto legume reto ou ligeiramente recurvado, ereto na árvore, vermelho-escuro, oblongo, 15-20 cm de comprimento por 3.5-4 cm de largura, comprimido, lenhoso e elasticamente deiscente, base estreita, estipitada; estípite de 2-4.5 cm de comprimento; ápice acuminado; acume de 1 mm de comprimento.

description: Árvore pequena ou muito alta, 5-6(-9) m podendo alcançar até 22 m de altura. Ramificação aberta, copa ampla; ramos no ápice costado-sulcados, 5 mm de diâmetro densamente cúpreo-tomentosos, depois subglabros; botões florais e inflorescência densamente cúpreo-tomentosos, mesmo quando dessecados. Folhas 2-pinadas, 14-20(-32) cm de comprimento, pecioladas, com 7-16(-22) pares de pinas opostas ou subopostas, pecioladas; pecíolo comum de 3,5-7 cm de comprimento, cúpreo-tomentoso como os ramos; pecíolo primário cônico, 3-4(-5) mm de comprimento, raque densamente cúpreo-tomentoso; pinas 5-11(-14) cm de comprimento, as menores na parte inferior da folha; folíolos bicolores, sésseis, multijugos, em geral 20-40 pares (ou mais) opostos, estreitos, linear-oblongos, 1-1.8 cm de comprimento, 2-4.5 mm de largura, coriáceos, face superior glabra e brilhante, a inferior densamente ferrugíneo ou cúpreo-pubescente; base truncado-auriculada; ápice arredondado e margem plana ou revoluta. Nervura primária canaliculado-impressa na face superior ou obscura, glabra, na inferior proeminente e densamente pilosa; nervuras secundárias e superiores inconspícuas. Inflorescência racemosa, em geral os rácemos solitários, nas axilas das folhas, 3-4(-5) agrupadas no ápice dos ramos, cúpreo-tomentosas; rácemos longo-pedunculados; pedúnculo de 4.5-5.5(-7) cm de comprimento, a parte florífera de 18-26(-35-40) cm de comprimento por 1.5-2 cm de diâmetro; botões florais cremes, as flores avermelhadas, aromáticas; pedicelos de 1-2(-3-4) mm de comprimento; bractéolas subuladas, 2 mm de comprimento, densamente pilosas; cálice campanulado, 5-lobulado no ápice, 3-4 mm de comprimento por 4 mm de largura, cúpreo-tomentoso em ambas as faces; lobos largamente ovado-triangulares ou obtusos, arredondados no ápice; corola com cinco pétalas obovado-oblongas, obovadas, 4.5-5(-7) mm de comprimento, com ou sem unha. Estames cinco, glabros, filetes de 3-4 mm de comprimento, anteras elítico-oblongas de 2-2.5 mm de comprimento, introrsas com ou sem pelos na região mediana; estaminódios cinco, glabros, filiformes, 1-7 mm de comprimento com o ápice laminar-espatulado, livres, ou concrescentes em forma de cúpula, com ou sem anteras rudimentares. Ovário subséssil ou curto-estipitado, densamente pubescente (pelos longos, híspido, amarelo-dourados ou cúpreos), ovoide ou elipsoide; estilete glabro de 1-4(-5) mm de comprimento; estigma glabro com abertura punctiforme. Fruto, vagem falciforme, plana, longo-estipitada, densamente ferrugínea ou cúpreo-to-mentosa, velutina quando jovem, mais tarde glabrescente, 12-25(-30) cm de comprimento por 7-10 cm de largura na região mediana; sementes poucas por fruto.

description: Árvore mediana até grande, ramos jovens, folíolos, pecíolos e raques das inflorescências tomentoso-acinzentados. Folhas 2-pinadas, longo-pecioladas com 12-16 (raramente 11 ou 17) pares de pinas opostas ou ligeiramente subopostas, pecioladas; pecíolo comum espesso, curto, 5 cm de comprimento; pecíolo primário curto, 2-3 m de comprimento; folíolos secundários sésseis (22-23 pares opostos), 7-11 mm de comprimento, 2-4 mm de largura, gradativamente menores da base para o ápice, linear-oblongos, base obliqua e auriculada unilateralmente, ápice retuso, maigem revoluta, coriáceo, pubescente, quando adulto subglabro; face superior brilhante, freqüentemente rugosa com a nervura mediana imersa, as demais inconspícuas; a face inferior pálida com a nervura mediana proeminente. Inflorescêntia paniculado-racemosa, constituída em geral de 2-7 rácemos, raramente 1, geralmente de 28-38 cm de comprimento, com 1.5-1.8(-2) cm de espessura na antese, longo-pedunculada, raque espessa. Flores vermelho-brilhantes, numerosas, subsésseis ou curto-pediceladas; pedicelo de 0.5 mm de comprimento; cálice cupuliforme, 5-lobulado no ápice, 1.5-2 mm de comprimento, às vezes um pouco maior; lobos curtos, largos, de ápice agudo, finamente pubescente externamente; corola com cinco pétalas oblongo-espatuladas, 3-4 mm de comprimento, externamente cinza-pubescentes, mais tarde glabrescentes. Estames cinco, glabros, 4-5 mm de comprimento, antera setácea, introrsa, glabra; estaminódios cinco, livres, glabros, até 6.5 mm de comprimento, lâmina clavado-espatulada, com antera rudimentar no ápice, filete linear, recurvado no botão. Ovário subséssil, densamente piloso; pelos amarelos, eretos. Fruto, legume piano suborbicular (ou ainda jovem), lenhoso, curto-estipitado de superfície finamente reticulado-venosa.

description: Ávore grande e belíssima pelo tom vermelho-ferrugíneo de sua copa vista á distâneia e de debaixo de árvore; atinge de 30-35(-40) m de altura, por 30-35(-80) cm de diâmetro; fuste cilíndrico, em geral com pequena sapopema na base; casca fina com manchas linquênicas brancas. Folhas 2-pinadas, pecioladas, nos ramos estéreis até 90 cm de comprimento com 6-7 pares de pinas opostas; pecíolo comum espesso, cilíndrico, escuro, 20 cm de comprimento por 1 cm de diâmetro na base, fortemente estriado longitudinalmente e densamente ferrugíneo-puberulento; pecíolo primário delgado, finamente caniculado, quase cilíndrico, 1,5-2(-2,5) cm de comprimento; pinas primárias de comprimento variável, as basais maiores, pecíoladas, com 7-19 pares de folíolos altemos; pecíolo secundário espesso, achatado, rugoso, 3-4 mm de comprimento; pínulas oblongo-lanceoladas, raramente ovais, 4-9 cm de comprimento por 1,5-2,5 cm de laigura, glabras, verdes e brilhantes na face superior, na inferior avermelhado-ferrugíneo-pubescentes; base cuneada ou arredondada, ápice longamente caudado-acuminado, margem inteira; nervuras primárias e secundárias imersas na face superior, na inferior proeminentes e densamente pilosas. Inflorescência paniculado-corimbosa, fortemente pedunculada, ereta, curta 12-15(-30) cm de comprimento, constituída de espigas curtas, 6-7(-10) cm de comprimento, densifloras. Flores cremes, pequenas, sésseis, 4 mm de comprimento; cálice subglabra, 1,5-2 mm de comprimento, tubuloso, 5-laciniado no ápice; lacínias curtas, 1,5 mm, obtusas ou subagudas no ápice; pétalas 5, livres na prefloração imbricadas, espatuladas, 3 mm de comprimento, glabras em ambas as faces. Estames 5, epipétalos, 2 mm de comprimento, glabras, filetes delgados, anteras oblongas, dorsifixas, introrsas; estaminódios 5, livres, filiformes, glabras, 3 mm de comprimento, recurvados na região mediana, ápice dilatado-espatulado. Ovário fusiforme, subcílindrico, densamente piloso, 3 mm de comprimento; pelos híspidos, longos; estilete curto, glabra, com estigma apical. Fruto legume indeiscente, fortemente estipitado, vermelho quando jovem, escuro quase preto quando maduro, ereto na árvore, acima da copa, fortemente coriáceo, espesso, comprimido, poucos por infrutescência, 20-25(-30) cm comprimento por 5(-6) cm de largura, piano, glabérrimo, lustroso ou opaco, com muitas sementes; sementes vermelho-escuras, oblongas, 22-24 mm de comprimento por 4-6 mm de espessura, testa dura, lustrosa. Distribuição. Aparentemente restrita aos Estados do Amazonas e Pará (Fig. 31). Habita a mata alta de terra firme, em solo aigiloso. A floração foi registrada em junho, julho e setembro e a frutificação em março, agosto e novembro.

description: Árvore pequena, 3-4 m de altura. Folhas 2-pinadas, pecioladas, 6-18 cm de comprimento com 5-7 pares de pinas opostas ou subopostas, pecioladas; pecíolo comum cilíndrico, espesso, 3-5 cm de comprimento; pecíolo primário com rugas longitudinals, 6 mm de comprimento; pinas com 28-34 pares de folíolos secundários, sésseis, os maiores de 17 mm de comprimento por 3 mm de largura, linear-oblongos, retos, quando jovens avermelhados, face superior glabra, lustrosa, no dorso opacos, puberulentos; base truncada, ligeiramente auriculada em um dos lados; ápice obtuso; margem inteira ligeiramente revoluta. Nervura primária imersa na face superior, na inferior proeminente, as demais inconspícuas nas duas faces. Inflorescência paniculado-racemosa; rácemos curtos, 25 cm de comprimento, na antese 1.5 cm de espessura. Flores curto-pediceladas alaranjado-pálidas; pedicelos 0.5 mm de comprimento; cálice subglabra, enegrecido, 5-lobado, lóbulos suborbiculares; corola com 5 pétalas; pétalas de 2 mm de comprimento. Estames cinco, epipétalos; estaminódios cinco, livres, ápice petaloide, dilatado, obovado, com antera rudimentar no ápice. Ovário fusiforme, piloso, ferrugíneo, glabro com estígma curto. Fruto, legume menor do que em D. urubuensis (17 x 7.5 cm) menos da metade do comprimento, lenhoso, curto-estipitado, de superfície fina e estriada obliqüamente, com poucas sementes.

description: Arbores R. formosae similes sed ab ea corollis majoribus 18-22 mm longis, 4-6 mm latis (nec 15-18 mm longis, 22.5 mm latis), corollae lobis secus medium glabris, intus juxta margines pilis glandulosis biseriatis provisi (nec basi albo-strigosis intus juxta margines dense papillosis) antheris ±5 mm latis (nec 1-1.5 mm) basi extensioribus sphaeroidesis papillosis auctis (nec nudis) diversa.

description: Trees; bark grayish. Leafy branchlets glabrous, terete; older branches rugose, grayish; lenticels many, punctiform to linear, 0.5-3 mm long. Stipules not seen (readily caducous), leaving a white linear scar. Leaves 34-38 × 10-11 cm, LAV 3:1; oblanceolate, cuneate (BA = 20-25°) at base, obtuse at apex, sometimes with a deltoid acumen ca. 1 cm long; dark green above, yellowish green below, semi-coriaceous; drying olive-green, subcoriaceous; glabrous above, glabrous below; pellucid punctate; primary and secondary veins glabrous, prominent below, secondary veins 15-17 each side, subparallel; tertiary veins starting subparallel and reticulate in the center; petioles 41-45 mm long, 2.5-3 mm thick, terete or adaxially narrowly concave, thickened at base, but not pulvinate; domatia absent. Inflorescences openly paniculate, pyramidal, with opposite or alternate, decussate branches; ca. 36 cm long, basal branches to 20 cm long, in ca. 5 pairs, basal portion of axis not branched ca. 8 cm long; rachis decussately compressed, narrowly rhombic or narrowly elliptic in cross section, rachis and branches glabrous; flowers on tertiary branches alternate or in terminal lax cymules; distal bracts 6-10 × 3-5 mm, narrowly triangular to deltoid; bracteoles subtending flowers 3-5 × 2-4 mm, narrowly deltoid. Flowers pedicellate, pedicels 9-12 mm long, glabrous; hypanthium obovate to obconical, 4.5-7 × 4-6 mm, glabrous; flower buds cylindrical, pointed at apex. Calyx cupular, semi-membranous, with barely distinguishable lobes, 2-3.5 × 6-8 mm; lobes 5, ca. 1 × ca. 3 mm, shallowly deltoid. Corolla short-tubular with spreading-reflexed lobes, 1.8-2.2 cm long, white to cream-white inside and outside, thick and fleshy when fresh; tube faintly funnelform, 8-10 mm long, ca. 4 mm wide at base and ca. 6 mm wide at the orifice, glabrous outside, with a white glabrous basal zone inside, with a ring of ascendent-pilose hairs 6-7 mm from the base, at the same point of the filament attachments at base of lobes; lobes 5,14-2/3 of corolla length, 12-14 x 4-5 mm, narrowly triangular, glabrous outside, glabrous in central zone with two rows of minute (40 ×) glandular hairs inside, near the margins. Stamens 5, exserted because of spreading lobes, subequal, attached ca. 6 mm from the base of the tube; filaments ca. 7 mm long, with a compact tuft of white ascending hirsute hairs at base; anthers cylindrical, narrowly oblong, ca. 9 × ca. 5 mm, dorsifixed near the base, base rounded, with papillose spheroid extension at base, smooth throughout. Pollen exine densely foveolate, minutely echinate. Style exserted, 20-23 mm long, glabrous; style branches narrowly ovate, ca. 2 mm long, stigmatic surface microscopically (40 ×) papillose. Capsule not seen. Seeds not seen.

description: Plants dioicous, dull brown, leafy shoot 1.0-2.5 mm wide, profusely branched. Stems in cross section 100-190 µm in diameter, medullary cells 11-22, thick walled, ca. 4 µm thick, ventral cells 20-65 × 20-65(-90) µm, dorsal cells, quadrate or irregularly shaped, 40-65 × 35-65 µm. Flagelliferous branches not seen. Leaves imbricate, leaf lobe strongly concave, ovate, 400-1125 × 520-1300 µm, apex rounded to acute, margins entire, irregularly crenulate or with 1-4 teeth at the apex, teeth mostly singlecelled, to ca. 20 µm long; median leaf lobe cells isodiametrical, 10-35 × 10-50 × 12.5-30 µm, smooth or conspicuously mammillose, intermediate thickenings frequent; oil bodies apparently lacking in normal cells; ocelli rounded, 25-45 × 25-55 µm, 1-21 per leaf, scattered in leaf lobe, or rarely moniliate at leaf lobe base, row 80-95 µm, ocellar oil bodies botryoidal, rounded, gray, filling the lumen; lobule inflated toward the keel, elongate, never reduced, 0.4-0.6 the leaf lobe length, free margin plane, lobule tooth sometimes scarcely projecting. Utriculi absent, single or in pairs at the base of lateral branches. Underleaves 240870 × 300-750 µm, 1.5-4 × stem width, margins entire and plane, apex entire or emarginate, lobes rounded, occasionally with scattered ocelli in the lobe. Androecia lateral on main branches or terminal on secondary branches, in spikes of 4-8 bract pairs, 100-1500 Jim long; bracteoles, 125-150 × 150-180 µm, 2 per spike, apex entire. Gynoecia on short lateral branches or on main branches with one sterile or repeatedly fertile innovation; bract lobe obovate, ca. 600 × 1000 µm, margins entire or crenulate, bract lobule ligulate, ca. 230 × 670; bracteole obovate, ca. 550 × 700 µm, apex entire. Perianth obconic, 450625 × 750-1000 µm, surface strongly mammillose, with four bulbous horns, 200-450 µm long. Elaters, 15 × 450-550 µm. Spores irregularly shaped, mostly rectangular, 20-40 × 45-70 µm, greenish-brown, papillose-tuberculate; rosettes complex, aperture ca. 7 Jim in diameter with ca. 15 teeth.

description: Small to medium sized tree, the young branches sparsely puberulous-glabrescent. Leaves oblong to oblong-elliptic, coriaceous, 5.5-11.5 cm long, 1.8-4.2 cm broad, acuminate at apex, the acumen 5.0-10.0 mm long, cuneate to subcuneate and equal or slightly unequal at base, glabrous beneath; midrib impressed above, prominent and glabrous beneath; primary veins 6-8 pairs, arcuate, anastomosing; petioles 5.0-10.0 mm long, sparsely puberulous becoming glabrous with age, shallowly canaliculate. Stipules triangular, 1.5-2.0 mm long, tomentose, caducous. Flowers androdioecious, borne in dense-flowered sessile glomerules inserted on upper portion of petioles; pedicels 1.5-2.0 mm long, tomentellous; bracteoles ca 0.5 mm long, persistent, pubescent. Calyx 3.0-4.0 mm long, gray-tomentellous on exterior, the lobes slightly unequal. Corolla exserted well beyond calyx lobes, of 3 equal lobes two of which are markedly bicucullate, and the third only slightly bifid, united at base into a long tube, the tube puberulous-glabrescent on exterior, tomentose within. Fertile stamens 3, alternating with corolla lobes, the filaments short and broad, staminodes absent. Ovary reduced to a residual swelling in 6 flowers examined. Fruit not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1972. Dichapetalaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 10: 1-84.

description: Small tree, the young branches puberulous, soon becoming glabrous. Leaves oblong, membraneous, 9.0-13.0 cm long, 2.8-5.0 cm broad, cuspidate-acuminate at apex, the acumen 10.0-18.0 mm long, rounded to subcuneate and unequal at base, glabrous beneath except for a few stiff appressed hairs; midrib impressed above, prominent and with a stiff appressed pubescence beneath; primary veins 7-16 pairs, arcuate, inconspicuous, anastomosing near margin; petioles 1.0-4.0 mm long, appressed pubescent, shallowly canaliculate to terete. Stipules ca 2.0 mm long, oblong, caducous. Flowers hermaphrodite, borne in few-flowered sessile glomerules on lower portion of lamina midrib; pedicels ca 1.0 mm long; bracts ca 0.5 mm long, broadly ovate, pubescent, persistent. Calyx 5.5-7.0 mm long, shortly pubescent on exterior, the lobes unequal. Corolla far exceeding calyx lobes, with 2 large bicucullate lobes and three small narrow lobes, the large lobes free to near base, the other lobes joined in a long strap, the lobes slightly fused at base only, densely pubescent at base of lobes and filaments within, with a few sparse hairs only on exterior. Fertile stamens 3, alternating with corolla lobes, inserted on base of corolla, 2 staminodes present. Ovary 3-locular with 2 ovules in each loculus, tomentose on exterior. Style with trifid apex, pubescent throughout. Fruit ellipsoid, unilocular or bilocular; epicarp sparsely tomentellous; mesocarp thin; endocarp hard, bony, thin, glabrous within. This species is divided into two varieties.

description: Evergreen, rhizomatous shrub to 3(-5) m tall, usually from underground woody burl or swelling, spreading vegetatively by horizontal underground rhizomes, with longitudinally furrowed bark; twigs slightly to moderately angled, slender, ± sparsely lepidote, otherwise very sparsely to densely pubescent; buds ovoid, 1-2 × ca. 1 mm. Leaf blades elliptic to ovate or obovate, 1-6.7 × 0.5-3.5 cm, sometimes quite strongly reduced in size toward branch tips, ± flat to very slightly recurved to concave, coriaceous, ca. 0.17-0.26 mm thick; base attenuate, narrowly to broadly cuneate (rounded); apex acuminate, acute to rounded; margin usually plane or very slightly revolute, apical portion entire (very obscurely and irregularly toothed), basal portion entire; venation brochidodromous, 3° veins ± reticulate; adaxial surface lepidote but scales quickly deciduous; slightly to densely pubescent on midvein, especially basal portion, the midvein usually not depressed, the 2° veins visible to obscure, usually not depressed, the 3° and higher-order veins slightly visible to obscure; abaxial surface moderately to densely lepidote, otherwise usually glabrous (with a few hairs on mid vein, or very sparsely to densely pubescent throughout), the 3° and higher-order veins flat or nearly so, very slightly and laxly reticulate to obscure, the 2° veins visible to obscure; scales rust colored to dark orange or brownish, sometimes becoming whitish with age, ± persistent, ca. 0.08-0.25 mm in diam., erose to entire; petiole 2-9 mm long, lepidote, otherwise pubescent adaxially to occasionally all around; flower buds ± intermixed with vegetative buds. Inflorescences fasciculate, 2-10-flowered; pedicels clearly articulated with calyx, slender, 4-14 mm long, lepidote, otherwise glabrous to sparsely pubescent; bracteoles subopposite, basal or nearly so, narrowly triangular, 0.7-1.5 mm long; floral bracts to ca. 2 mm long. Flowers (4-)5 (-6)-merous; calyx lobes triangular, with acuminate apices, 1-2 × 0.5-1.8 mm, adaxial side sparsely to moderately pubescent, especially near apex or margins, abaxial side lepidote, otherwise glabrous or very sparsely pubescent near base; corolla urceolate, white, 2.5-5 × 2.5-4.5 mm, abaxially sparsely lepidote; filaments roughened, 1.3-2.5 mm long, unappendaged or with pair of minute spurs near anther-filament junction; anthers 0.7-1.3 mm long; ovary lepidote, otherwise pubescent, placentae ± subapical. Capsules usually subglobose to short-ovoid, 2.5-4(-5) × 2.5-4.5 mm, sparsely lepidote, otherwise usually sparsely pubescent, especially near base, the pale, very thick sutures separating as unit from adjacent valves (with additional pale lines alternating with and resembling sutures); seeds 1-2 mm long.

description: An evergreen erect to decumbent-spreading, sparsely branched shrub to 1(-1.4) m tall with a thickened burl-like stem just below soil surface, frequently sprouting from base after fire or disturbance; mature stems terete, with longitudinally furrowed, dark brown bark; twigs terete, light gray to reddish, slender to stout, densely covered with unicellular hairs to lacking such hairs, sparsely to densely covered with multicellular, multiseriate, short- to long-stalked, glandular-headed hairs, and lacking to densely covered with multicellular, multiseriate, long-celled hairs; buds minute, to 0.3 mm long, densely covered with glandular-headed and long-celled hairs. Leaves alternate and sparsely to densely distributed along stem [ca. 4-25(-30) leaves per cm], linear to ovate, (3-)3.5-14 × 0.5-3(-4) mm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acute, margin entire, strongly revolute, adaxial surface densely covered with unicellular hairs to lacking such hairs, very sparsely to densely covered with short- to long-stalked glandular-headed hairs, and lacking to sparsely covered with long-celled hairs, abaxial surface sparsely to densely covered with unicellular hairs, occasionally such hairs completely lacking, with scattered short- to long-stalked glandular-headed hairs and sometimes also long-celled hairs; venation obscurely brochidodromous; petiole essentially lacking to 1.5 mm long. Inflorescence a solitary flower, or occasionally a 2-4-flowered fascicle or short raceme, these borne in the axils of leaves or bract-like leaves at ends of branches, thus forming a pseudoterminal cluster; pedicels 4-14 mm long, densely covered with unicellular hairs to lacking such hairs, with scattered glandular-headed hairs and sometimes also long-celled hairs; bracteoles 2, opposite and basal, ovate-triangular to narrowly triangular, 1-3 mm long, with unicellular hairs and glandular-headed hairs. Flowers with calyx lobes narrowly triangular to ovate-triangular with acuminate to acute apices, 3-6 mm long, 0.8-2.3 mm wide, green, adaxial surface densely covered with unicellular hairs to lacking such hairs, with or without scattered glandular-headed and/or long-celled hairs, abaxial surface with a few unicellular hairs near apex to densely covered with such hairs, with scattered glandular-headed hairs, sometimes also long-celled hairs; corolla white to pink, 6-12 × 8-17 mm, adaxial surface sparsely covered with unicellular hairs toward base, abaxial surface with glandular-headed and sometimes also long-celled hairs, occasionally with a few unicellular hairs; filaments 3-5 mm long, sparsely to moderately covered with unicellular hairs near base and glabrous above; anthers 0.7-1.2 mm long; pollen released in tetrads with viscin strands; ovary ± globose, moderately to densely covered with glandular-headed hairs, sometimes also with a few unicellular hairs, with axile placentation and centrally located placentae; style 3.5-7 mm long. Capsule 1.7-3 × 2-4 mm, sparsely to densely covered with glandularheaded hairs, sometimes also with a few unicellular hairs; seeds ovoid, 0.4-0.7 mm long, with testa of slightly elongated and minutely pitted cells, not extending past the ends of the seed.

description: Tree with the petioles terete, tomentose; rachis 13.5-15 cm long, slightly canaliculate on the upper surface, tomentulose; leaflets 4-jugate, the petiolules ca 3 mm long, tomentulose, the blades 8.5-14 cm long, 5.5-6 cm wide, oblong, oblong-oblanceolate or oblong-elliptic, rounded-obtuse basally, the apex rounded and shortly acute, the tip blunt, glabrous on the upper surface, tomentose sparingly beneath, the costa and the primary veins impressed on the upper surface, salient beneath; inflorescence cauligerous, racemose, 12-20 cm long, the axis velutinous, the bracts ca 1 mm long triangular, persistent, the bracteoles lacking; pedicels 6-9 mm long, minutely strigulose; buds ca 7 mm diameter, globose; calyx segments glabrous within, densely strigulose externally, persistent with the young fruits; petal yellow, oblanceolate, ca 18 mm long and 10 mm wide, sparsely sericeous on the costa externally; larger stamens 6, the filaments ca 7 mm long, sparingly villose, the anthers lanceolate, the connective prolonged-apiculate, 5-5.5 mm long, 1 mm wide, the smaller stamens glabrous, the filaments 4-7 mm long, the anthers 3 mm long, 1 mm wide; stigma truncate; style 1 mm long, sericeous; ovary 4 mm long, 2 mm wide, oblong, falcate, sericeous-velutinous, the gynophore 4 mm long, densely sericeous; fruits not seen.

description: Tree 3-10 m tall, the branchlets densely strigulose minutely; stipules persistent, 1.5-2 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, strigulose densely; leaves unifoliolate, the petioles 5-9 mm long, shortly stipellate apically, densely strigulose minutely, the petiolules 3-4 mm long, densely strigulose minutely, the blades glabrous, 9.5-17 cm long, 3.5-7 cm wide, oblong to elliptic, the base rounded, obtuse to acute, acuminate apically, the venation prominulus, the costa and primary veins salient on both surfaces of the leaflets or the costa impressed above; inflorescences axillary, the axes densely strigulose minutely, 3-6 cm long, the bracts persistent, ca 1.5 mm long, linear, densely strigulose, the bracteoles 1-2 mm long, lanceolate to narrowly linear-lanceolate, densely strigulose; pedicels (10-) 15-24 mm long, densely strigulose; buds oval in outline, ca 9 mm long and 7 mm diameter; calyx segments 4, persistent with the mature fruits, densely strigulose externally, pilose within but glabrescent; petal (in bud) white, the blade broadly ovate, 2.5-3.5 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, sericeous externally, glabrous within; larger stamens 5, glabrous, the anthers linear-lanceolate; gynoecium glabrous except for the densely strigose margins and apex of the gynophore, the stigma punctiform, the style glabrous, ca 1 mm long, the ovary oblong; fruit 2.5-3 cm long, ca 1.8 cm diameter, oval in outline, glabrous, orange-colored, the stipe 12-15 mm long, glabrous; seed 1 per fruit, ca 22 mm long and 12 mm diameter, elliptic in outline, black, nitid, the aril white, fimbriate, covering most of one side of the seed.

description: Tree 15-20 m tall, the trunk 1 m diameter, the bark smooth, gray, the branchlets densely micro-strigulose, glabrescent; stipules persistent, 0.4 mm long and wide, triangular, micro-strigulose; petioles 3-4.5 cm long, micro-strigulose; rachis 5-7.5 cm long, micro-strigulose, terete but slightly sulcate on the upper surface, not stipellate; leaflets 2- or 3-jugate, the petiolules 3-5 mm long, micro-strigulose, the blades of the lowermost pair 6-8 cm long, 4-4.5 cm wide, the other pairs 10.5-15 cm long, 5.5-8.5 cm wide, acute at the base, the apex rounded, glabrous on the upper surface, micro-strigulose beneath, the venation plane above, salient beneath; inflorescence 8-10 cm long, ramuligerous, the axis micro-strigulose, the bracts persistent, 0.5 mm long, semicircular-triangular, minutely strigulose externally; bracteoles lacking; pedicels 1-1.5 mm long, minutely strigulose; buds almost globose, apiculate, 3 mm diameter, minutely strigulose; calyx segments persistent, minutely strigulose externally, glabrous within; petal lacking; stamens not seen; stigma truncate; style ca 2.5 mm long, glabrous, uncinate; ovary sparsely strigulose, narrowly elliptic, the gynophore ca 2.5 mm long, sparingly to sparsely strigulose; fruits elliptic in outline, ca 5 cm long and 2 cm wide, 2-seeded, bright orange-colored; seeds 1-1.5 cm diameter, the aril bright red and very sweet-tasting.

description: Tree with the branchlets minutely strigulose but soon glabrescent; stipules caducous, 2-2.5 mm long, linear-subulate, glabrous; petioles 7-10 mm long, minutely strigulose sparingly, stipellate apically; rachis 4.5-5.5 cm long, slender, stipellate at each pair of leaflets, minutely strigulose; leaflets 3-jugate, glabrous, strongly discolorous, the petiolules 2-2.5 mm long, the blades 5.5-7.5 cm long, 2-2.5 cm wide, lanceolate-elliptic, the base acute, the apex acuminate, often mucronulate, the venation inconspicuous, finely reticulate, plane on both surfaces, except the costa impressed on the upper surface; inflorescences of fasciculate racemes, 6-10 cm long, the axis minutely strigulose, the bracts persistent, 0.5-0.6 mm long, triangular, minutely strigulose externally, glabrous within, the bracteoles lacking; pedicels 3-4.5 mm long, minutely strigulose; buds subglobose to elliptic in outline, 3-3.5 mm long, 3 mm diameter, sparsely strigulose minutely; calyx segments 4, glabrous; petal not developed; larger stamens 2, glabrous, the filaments ca 2 mm long, the anthers ca 1.5 mm long and 0.8 mm wide, oval-oblong, the smaller stamens ca 25-30, glabrous, the filaments 4-5 mm long, the anthers oval to oblate; gynoecium glabrous or with a few minute hairs basally, the stigma truncate, the style 0.4 mm long, strongly reflexed, parallel to the long axis of the ovary, the latter ca 3 mm long, 1 mm wide, oblong, arcuate apically, the gynophore ca 1 mm long; fruit unknown.

description: Arbor vel arbuscula, ramulis novellis puberulis; stipulae caducae falcato-ovatae acutae; petioli 34-40 mm longi, apice stipellati ad apicem, rhaches 12.5-16.5 cm longae, leviter marginatae ad basim foliolorum stipellatae; foliola 4- vel 5-jugata, petiolulis 1.5-2 mm longis, puberulis, laminis ovalibus ad oblongis, 5-10 cm longis, 3-4.5 cm latis, basi rotundatis apicaliter abrupte breviter acutis, supra glabris infra leviter pilosis; inflorescentiae ramuligerae, 8.5-10.5 cm longae, axe subappresso-pilosulo, bracteis persistentibus, ca 1 mm longis et 3 mm latis, late ovatis, bracteolis pedicellorum ad apicem nascentibus, ca 3 mm longis, lanceolatis, dense strigulosis externe; pedicelli 6-7 mm longi, pilosuli; alabastra ca 8 mm diametro, globosa dense pilosulosa; calycis segmenta pilosulosa externe et intus strigoso-sericea, pilis aureis; petalum extus leviter villosum, unguiculo ca 4 mm longo, lamina ca ovali et 10 mm longa; stamina maiora 4, filamentis 8-9 mm longis, villosis, antheris oblongis, ca 3 mm longis, stamina minora glabra; gynoecium sericeum, ovario ca 4 mm longo et 1.5 mm lato, gynophoro 5 mm longo; fructus non visus.

description: Arbor magna, ramulis sparse strigulosis minute, glabrescentibus; stipulae persistentes 3.5-5 mm longae anguste lanceolatae glabrae, rigidae acuminatae; petioli 2.5-4 cm longi sparse strigulosi minute apice minute stipellati; rhaches 4.5-7 cm longae minute strigulosae sparse stipellatae minute; foliola (1- vel) 2-jugata, petiolulis (3-)4-5 mm longis glabris laminis coriaceis ellipticis, 7.5-12 cm longis, 3-5 cm latis basi cuneato-decurrentibus apice acuminatis supra nitidis et glabris subtus leviter strigulosis et opacis, supra venulis reticulo prominente minute anastomosantibus supra costa impressa subtus saliente; inflorescentiae racemosae ramuligerae fasciculatae 7.5-16 cm longae, axe minute striguloso, bracteis persistentibus, 1-1.5 mm longis triangularibus, bracteolis saepe nullis sed aliquando inflorescentiarum versus basim evidentibus; pedicelli ca 3 mm longi minute strigulosi; alabastra subglobosa ca 4-4.5 mm diametro minute strigulosa leviter; calycis segmenta 3 vel 4, persistentia; petala nulla; stamina maiora 2 glabra, filamentis ca 5 mm longis eis staminorum minorum glabris 4.5 mm longis; gynoecium glabrum, stigmate punctiformi, stylo ca 1 mm longo, ovario ca 2.5 mm longo et 1.5 mm lato oblongo-ovali, gynophoro ca 2 mm longo; fructus aurantiacus ovalis, ca 2.5 cm longus et 2 cm diametro 1-seminatus; semen 22-24 mm longum ovale nitido-nigrum, arillo albo.

description: Lianas, glabras; ramos novos subcilíndricos, sulcados, lisos, secos cinzentos, velhos cilíndricos, sulcados, lenticelados, cinzentos. Folhas opostas ou subopostas; estípulas triangulares, inteiras ou erosas; pecíolos (3-) 8-10(-12) mm, secos marrons; lâminas (2,7-)6.2-11.3(-20.7) × (1.2-)3.1-5.5(-10) cm, elípticas ou raro suborbiculares, base cuneada ou arredondada, margem inteira ou obscuramente crenulada, ápice agudo ou acuminado, raro obtuso, extremidade aparentemente glandular, coriáceas, secas cinza-esverdeadas na face adaxial, marrom-acinzentadas na abaxial, rugosas, nervuras secas de cor inconspícua em ambas as faces, na face adaxial secundárias impressas, na abaxial planas ou promínulas, terciárias obscuras em ambas as faces. Inflorescências (0.8-)2.1-5.8 × (0.8-)2-3.7(-11) cm, tirsóide-paniculadas, 30-200 flores, axilares, comumente em nós sem folhas; pedúnculos 0-2(-7) mm, ramos cilíndricos, alternos a subopostos, verdes, brácteas denticuladas na base, erosas; pedicelos 1.9-3.2 m; bractéolas 0-2. Flores 3.5-4 mm diâm na antese, rotáceas, aromáticas; sépalas (0.6-)0.8-1(-1.4) × 0.7-0.9 (-1.2) mm, elípticas, cuculadas, escariosas, esparso denticuladas, papilosas, mais ou menos carnosas, esverdeadas; pétalas (1.7-)1.8 -2.2 × 1-1.8 mm, elípticas ou ovais, deflexas, margem papilosa, plicada, mais ou menos carnosas, amareladas, brancas ou verdes; disco ca 0.2 mm alt., sinuado ou não, verde; estames 0.9-1.2 mm, filetes 0.75-1 mm, anteras 0.1-0.25 × 0.35-0.4 mm, oblongas, deiscência por fendas oblíquas em ângulo de ca 120°, amarelas, conectivo inconspícuo, não proeminente acima das tecas; ovário 0.6-0.7 mm diâm, hemisférico, mais ou menos 3-lobado, estilete 0.15-0.3 mm, estigma pontual, óvulo por lóculo 1. Bagas 1-2.9 × (0.7-)1.6(-2,2) cm, esferóides ou elipsóides, secas marrom-escuras a pruinosas, lisas, maduras alaranjadas a amarelas. Sementes 2.3-3.4 × 1.1 × 0.9-1 cm.
