description: Lianas, glabras; ramos novos achatados, esparso miúdo lenticelados, secos enegrecidos, enegrecidos esverdeados ou cinzentos, velhos cilíndricos, lenticelados, cinzentos. Folhas opostas; estípulas triangulares, hialinas, inteiras; pecíolos (10-)15-16(-19) mm, secos cinzentos, às vezes pontuados de cor clara, minutamente frisados; lâminas (5.5-)11.1-13.5(-15.5) × 3.1-4.9(-6.9) cm, elípticas, base arredondada a cuneada, raro truncada, margem inteira, ápice agudo a acuminado, cartáceas, levemente buladas, minutamente pontuadas na face abaxial, secas cinza-esverdeadas ou marrom-escuras na face adaxial marrom ou marrom-claras na abaxial, nervuras secas amareladas na face adaxial, principal marrom ou marrom-amarelada, restantes amareladas na abaxial, secundárias e terciárias promínulas em ambas as faces. Inflorescências fasciculadas, 1-6 flores, axilares ou às vezes em braquiblastos afilos laterais; brácteas inteiras; pedicelos 6-9.3 mm, secos enegrecido pruinosos. Botões florais ovóides. Flores 4.3-6.6 mm diâm na antese, campanuliformes; sépalas 1.3-1.6 × (1.8-)2.1-2.5 mm, transverso-elípticas, erosas ou inteiras, escariosas, carnosas, verdes; pétalas 2.7-3.3 × 2.3-3.1 mm, rômbicas a elípticas, deflexas, parte distal reflexa, escariosas, inteiras, mais ou menos carnosas, amarelo esverdeadas a verde-amareladas; disco anelar-pulviniforme, 1.2-1.35 × 1-1.4 mm, fundido aos lobos do ovário, margem externa obtusa, arredondada; estames 1.6-1.7 mm, filetes 1.25 -1.45 mm, anteras 0.25-0.3 × 0.5 mm, oblongas, 2-loculares, lóculos confluentes por fenda em ângulo de ca 150°, conectivo inconspícuo; ovário e disco 2,6 mm diâm, ápice 3-lobado, estilete ca 0.5 mm, estigma pontual, óvulos por lóculo 8. Bagas inteiras não vistas, ca 13.2 cm diâm, elipsóides, epicarpo ca 1.2 cm espessura. Sementes não vistas, ca 4.2 cm diâm.

description: Lianas, glabras; ramos novos achatados, não lenticelados, sulcados, secos acinzentados, velhos cilíndricos, sulcados, esparso lenticelados, cinzentos. Folhas opostas ou ás vezes alternas; estípulas triangulares, denticuladas; pecíolos 4-6(-9) mm, secos marrons; lâminas 3,8-8.8(-11.6) × (1.6-)1.8-4.1 cm, elípticas, base cuneada, raro arredondada, margem inteira, ápice agudo, raro acuminado ou obtuso, cartáceas, minutamente pontuadas na face abaxial, secas marrom-escuras em ambas as faces ou marrom-acinzentadas na adaxial, nervuras secas de cor inconspícua em ambas as faces, ou principais cinzentas em ambas as faces, secundárias às vezes cinzentas na abaxial, secundárias e terciárias obscuras na face adaxial, promínulas ou obscuras na face abaxial. Inflorescências 1.5-4.7 × 0.6-4 cm, tirsóide-paniculadas, ca 60-96 flores, axilares; pedúnculos 1-7 mm, ramos cilíndricos, opostos, brácteas escariosas, esparso denticuladas; pedicelos 0.6-1.1 mm; bractéolas 2. Botões florais esféricos. Flores (2.4-)3.5(-4.3) mm diâm na antese, rotáceas; sépalas 0.5-0.7 × 1-1.2 mm, triangulares, inteiras, carnosas; pétalas 1.7-1.9 × 1.2-1.4 mm, elípticas, deflexas, inteiras, margem revoluta, carnosas, amarelas ou verdes; disco anelar-pulviniforme, 0.4- 0.45 × 0.3-0.6 mm, margem externa com dobra elevada de 0.1-0.35 mm larg.; estames 0.6-0.75 mm, filetes 0.4-0.45 mm, anteras 0.2-0.4 × 0.3 mm, oblongas, 2-loculares, lóculos confluentes por fenda em ângulo de ca 120°, conectivo inconspícuo; ovário 3-lobado, estilete 0,15-0,3 mm, estigma pontual, óvulos por lóculo 2. Bagas imaturas 4.9-6 × 4-4.8 cm, esferóide a elipsóide, secas marrons, lisas. Sementes 2.5-4 × 1.5-3 cm.

description: Árvores, 5-14 m, ou arbustos, 5-6 m, glabros; ramos novos achatados a cilíndricos, não lenticelados ou esparso lenticelados, secos avermelhados a enegrecidos, minutamente frisados, velhos cilíndricos, lenticelados com lenticelas circulares e longas longitudinais, marrons, levemente frisados; córtex interno avermelhado. Folhas opostas ou subopostas; estípulas não vistas; pecíolos (8-)10-12(-18) mm, secos enegrecidos, minutamente frisados; lâminas (12.5-)16.9-30 (-33.5) × (4-)5-11.2(-12.4) cm, elípticas, base cuneada ou arredondada, margem inteira, ápice agudo ou menos comumente acuminado, coriáceas, levemente buladas, secas lustrosas na face adaxial, marrons, marrom-escuras ou avermelhadas na face adaxial, marrons na abaxial, nervuras secas de cor inconspícua na face adaxial, marrom-escuras na abaxial, na face adaxial secundárias planas a promínulas, terciárias obscuras, na abaxial secundárias planas a promínulas, terciárias impressas. Inflorescências fasciculadas, 1-7 flores, ramifloras em nós sem folhas ou truncifloras, produzindo floradas em sucessivas estações; brácteas fimbriadas; pedicelos (2.5-)4.1-5.4 mm. Botões florais esféricos. Flores (2.8-)4.1-5.1 mm diâm na antese, rotáceas; sépalas 0.7-1 × 1(-1.4) mm, triangulares, inteiras ou fimbriadas, cartáceas, verdes; pétalas 1.5-2.4 × (1-)1.8-2 mm, elípticas a rômbicas, deflexas, inteiras, escariosas, margem ondulada ou não, às vezes revoluta, mais ou menos carnosas, amarelas, amarelo esverdeadas, brancas, amareladas ou esverdeadas; disco anelar-pulviniforme, levemente 5-gono, 0.4-0.5 × 0.55-0.6 mm, margem externa obtusa, arredondada; estames (0.7-)1-1.2 mm, filetes (0.5-)0.7-0.9 mm, anteras 0.2-0.3 × 0.25-0,4 mm, oblongas, 2-loculares, lóculos confluentes por fenda em ângulo de ca 150°, conectivo inconspícuo; ovário ca 0.7 mm diâm, 3-lobado, estilete ca 0.3 mm ou indistinto, estigma pontual, óvulos por lóculo (1-)2. Bagas 1.2-1.6 × 1.4-1.8 cm, esferóides, secas marrons com faixas negras longitudinais, lisas, levemente 3-lobadas na base, imaturas pruinosas, rajadas de verde-e branco, maduras amarelas, alaranjadas ou esverdeadas, epicarpo maduro crustáceo. Sementes ca 1 × 0.7 cm.

description: Lianas, ou árvores, 3-10(-20) m, glabras exceto pelas flores; ramos novos subcilíndricos, lisos ou minutamente verrucosos, secos marrons a marrom-avermelhados, velhos cilíndricos, minutamente verrucosos, depois lenticelados, marrom-escuros a enegrecidos, às vezes mais ou menos pruinosos; córtex avermelhado. Folhas opostas; estípulas não vistas, deixando cicatrizes interpeciolares; pecíolos 7-13(-21) mm, secos marrons a enegrecidos; lâminas (7.1-)10.3-16.4(-21.9) × (2.5-)5.1-6.7(-9.2) cm, elípticas ou obovais, base cuneada a arredondada, margem inteira, ápice acuminado a agudo, cartáceas ou mais ou menos carnosas, secas às vezes lustrosas em ambas as faces, verde-escuras, marrons ou marrom-avermelhadas na face adaxial, verde-claras, marrons ou marrom-avermelhadas na abaxial, esparso pontuadas de negro ou alvo na face abaxial, nervuras secas de cor inconspícua em ambas as faces, em ambas as faces secundárias e terciárias promínulas ou terciárias obscuras. Inflorescências (0.9-)2.2-5(-8.6) × (1.2-)2.5-5.1(-8.9) cm, 150-640 flores, axilares; pedúnculos 0-4(-6) mm, ramos achatados, sulcados, opostos, verdes, secos pruinosos; brácteas erosas, afastadas ou não das ramificações; estipetes florais 3.5-5.3 mm, articulados na região mediana; bractéolas reduzidas a anel protuberante na articulação. Flores 3.2-5.2 mm diâm na antese, campanuliformes ou mais ou menos rotáceas; sépalas 0.7-1.7 × 0.9-1.2 mm, triangulares, margem papilosa, carnosas, verdes; pétalas 2-2.5(-3.3) × 1.2-1.4(-2.1) mm, elípticas a obovais, mais ou menos oblíquas, erosas, carnosas, densamente pubérulas em ambas as faces, às vezes papilosa na face abaxial, exceto pelas margens, raro glabras em ambas as faces, amarelas, amarelo alaranjadas, laranja ou verde-amareladas; disco 0.3-0.6 mm alt.; estames 0.8-1.15(-1.3) mm, opostos aos lobos do estigma, brancos, filetes 0.4-0.85(-1) mm, anteras 0.25-0.4 × 0.4-0.55 mm, reniformes, deiscência transversa; ovário e disco ca 1 mm diâm, ovário 3-lobado, estilete 0.35-0.5 mm, seção triangular, estigma 3-lobado, 0.4-0.5 mm diâm, lobos emarginados, patentes, óvulos por lóculo (1-)2. Bagas imaturas 3.7 × 2 cm diâm, elipsóides, levemente triangulares, secas enegrecidas, minutamente reticuladas ou rugosas, maduras laranja (n.v.), epicarpo crustáceo. Sementes não vistas.

description: Árvores (3-)4-13 m, de ramos flexuosos, ou às vezes lianas, glabras; ramos novos achatados, lisos, secos marrons, velhos cilíndricos, lisos ou fissurados, cinzentos; córtex interno laranja, alburno avermelhado. Folhas opostas a subopostas; estípulas lanceoladas a triangulares, inteiras, deixando cicatrizes oblíquas; pecíolos (6-)8-10(-15) mm, secos marrom-acinzentados; lâminas (2.5-)5.9-16.3(-19.7) × (1-)2.3-5.8(-6.3) cm, elípticas, base cuneada, raro arredondada, margem crenada, serreada, crenulada ou obscuramente crenulada, ápice agudo, cartáceas, secas marrom-esverdeadas na face adaxial, marrom-avermelhadas ou marrom-esverdeadas na abaxial, nervuras secas de cor inconspícua em ambas as faces ou marrons na face abaxial, em ambas as faces secundárias promínulas e terciárias levemente promínulas a obscuras. Inflorescências (1.1-)1.8-2.7(-4) × (1-) 1.6-4(-4.9) cm, 50-100 flores, axilares; pedúnculos (0-)2-3(-11) mm, ramos subcilíndricos, sulcados, opostos ou alternos; brácteas (0.6-)1.1(-1.6) mm, triangulares, escariosas, fimbriadas, afastadas das ramificações; pedicelos 0.5-0.6 mm; bractéolas 0-2. Flores 2.3-3.1 mm diâm na antese, campanuliformes; sépalas 0.8-1.1 (-1.4) × 0.8-1.3 mm, triangulares, escariosas, fimbriadas, ± carnosas; pétalas (1.6-)1.9-2.1 × (1-)1.1-1.4 mm, obovais, mais ou menos oblíquas, inteiras, mais ou menos carnosas, amarelas, amareladas, amarelo esverdeadas, esverdeadas ou verdes; disco 0.3 -0.45 mm alt.; estames 1-1.1 mm, alternos aos lobos do estigma, filetes 0.6-0.7 mm, anteras 0.3-0.4 × 0.4-0.6 mm, reniformes, deiscência transversa; ovário e disco ca 1.05 mm diâm, ovário 3-lobado, estilete 0.2-0.4 mm, seção triangular, estigma 3-lobado, 0.3 -0.5 mm diâm, lobos inteiros, agudos ou obtusos, deflexos ou patentes, óvulos por lóculo 4. Bagas 7.4-7.9(-12.7) × 3.2-7.6 cm diâm, elipsóides, secas marrons, pruinosas, rugosas, maduras marrons, epicarpo maduro lenhoso. Sementes 3 × 1.3 cm.

description: Árvores ca 12 m; ramos novos subcilíndricos, verrucosos ou esparso pilosos, secos marrons, velhos cilíndricos, glabrescentes, lenticelados ou verrucosos. Folhas opostas ou subopostas; estípulas aciculares a triangulares, inteiras; pecíolos 6-19 mm, secos marrons; lâminas (7.9-)11-11.2(-21) × 3.2-5.5(-9) cm, elípticas, base cuneada, margem obscuramente crenulada, ápice agudo, cartáceas, secas cinza-esverdeadas na face adaxial, marrom-claras na abaxial, nervuras secas de cor inconspícua na face adaxial, exceto principal amarelada, marrom-amareladas na abaxial, na face adaxial secundárias planas, terciárias obscuras, na abaxial secundárias e terciárias promínulas. Inflorescências 1.2-3.9 × 0.6-3.5 cm, dicásio composto, número indeterminado de flores, axilares; pedúnculos 5-18 mm, ramos subcilíndricos, opostos, papilosos, brácteas denticuladas, escariosas, estipetes florais articulados, papilosos, glabros; bractéolas 2, glabras. Flores 1.8-1.9 mm diâm na antese, campanuliformes; sépalas 0.7-1 × 0.6-0.8 mm, triangulares, erosas, escariosas, papilosas, papiráceas; pétalas 1.2-1.3 × 0.8 -1 mm, elípticas, erosas, escariosas, glabras, papiráceas, verde-amareladas; disco ca 0.4 mm alt., eroso; estames ca 1.2 mm, filetes ca 0.7 mm, anteras ca 0.45 × 0.35 mm, triangulares, rimosas, conectivo triangular, proeminente acima das tecas; ovário ca 0.55 mm diâm, ± piramidal, estilete não visto, estigma não visto, óvulos por lóculo 2. Bagas não vistas. Sementes não vistas.

description: Lianas, ou arbustos, 2-3 m, glabras exceto pelas flores; ramos novos conspicuamente tetrangulares, breve alados, minutamente verrucosos, secos verdes, logo marrom-claros, velhos subtetrangulares passando a cilíndricos, com remanescentes longitudinais das alas ou ângulos, lenticelados, cinzentos. Folhas opostas a subopostas; estípulas triangulares, inteiras; pecíolos (4-)5-7(-9) mm, secos esverdeados; lâminas (4.5-)7-11.1(-15.1) × (1.7-)2-3.7(-6.4) cm, elípticas, base cuneada, raro arredondada, margem inteira, ápice longo-acuminado, às vezes uncinado, ou menos comumente acuminado, papiráceas, levemente buladas, secas esverdeadas em ambas as faces, às vezes pontuadas de negro ou marrom na face abaxial, nervuras secundárias fortemente ascendentes, nervuras secas de cor inconspícua ou às vezes amareladas em ambas as faces, em ambas as faces secundárias proeminentes, terciárias promínulas. Inflorescências (2.7-) 3.3(-4.3) × 1.2-2.2 cm, 14-56 flores, axilares; pedúnculos 0-2(-10)mm, ramos achatados, sulcados, alternos, secos levemente pruinosos, ou não; brácteas erosas, afastadas das ramificações; estipetes florais (0.5-)1.3-1.6 mm, articulados na região mediana, raro não articulados; bractéolas reduzidas a protuberâncias na articulação. Flores (2.3-)2.5 -3.2(-4.2) mm diâm na antese, campanuliformes; sépalas 0.9 -1.2 × 0.9-1.2 mm, triangulares, erosas, carnosas, verdes; pétalas (1.9-)2.1-2.6 × (0-9-)1.3-1.5 mm, elípticas a espatuladas, mais ou menos oblíquas, parte distal deflexa, inteiras, carnosas, densamente papilosas na face abaxial, amarelas, verde-amareladas; disco 0.45(-0.7) mm alt.; estames 1.2-1.35 mm, alternos aos lobos do estigma, filetes 0.85-1.1 mm, anteras 0.25-0.35 × 0.35-0.5 mm, reniformes, deiscência transversa; ovário e disco ca 1.05 mm diâm, ovário 3-lobado, estilete 0.5.-0.7 mm, seção triangular, estigma 3-lobado, 0.4-0.6 mm diâm, lobos emarginados, patentes, óvulos por lóculo 2. Bagas 3.4-3.7(-4.5) × 1.6-2 cm diâm, elipsóides, secas marrons, minutamente tuberculadas, maduras amarelas, epicarpo maduro crustáceo. Sementes não vistas.

description: Lianas, ou árvores (1-)4-7.6 m, glabras; ramos novos achatados, não lenticelados, secos verdes passando a marrom-avermelhados e fissurados, velhos cilíndricos, fissurados, comumente escamantes, marrons ou marrom-avermelhados. Folhas opostas a subopostas, raro alternas; estípulas triangulares, inteiras; pecíolos (4-)7-11(-18) mm, secos verdes, minutamente frisados; lâminas (6.9-)12.5-22.3(-34.6) × (2.4-)3.6-4.9(-10.5) cm, elípticas, base cuneada, raro arredondada, margem inteira, ápice acuminado a agudo, cartáceas, às vezes levemente buladas, secas às vezes imperceptivelmente pontuadas em ambas as faces, às vezes lustrosas na face adaxial, verdes em ambas as faces, nervuras secas verde-claras na face adaxial, verde-amareladas na abaxial, secundárias e terciárias promínulas em ambas as faces, terciárias mais ou menos paralelas entre si. Inflorescências (4.7-)7.9-13.1(-22.4) × (1.4-)3.5-8.9 (-17.5) cm, tirsóide-paniculadas, ca 23 flores, axilares; pedúnculos 0–7(–28) mm, ramos subcilíndricos, alternos, verdes, brácteas escariosas, inteiras; estipetes florais (5.3-)6.1-6.4(-10) mm, articulados na base ou na região mediana; bractéola 0-1, quando presente entre a articulação mediana e base do pedicelo, ca 0.3 mm. Botões florais esféricos. Flores (4.1-)5.4-5.7(-10.3) mm diâm na antese, rotáceas; sépalas 0.6-1(-1.4) × (1-)1.7 mm, transverso oblongas, largo triangulares ou subcirculares, esparso denticuladas ou inteiras, escariosas, papiráceas, esverdeadas, secas ferrugíneas; pétalas 2.6-4 × 1.9-3.9 mm, elípticas, deflexas, inteiras, margem revoluta quando secas, papilosas na face adaxial, principalmente na margem, papiráceas, amarelas, brancas, branco esverdeadas, amareladas, laranja, esverdeadas ou verdes, secas ferrugíneas; disco anelar, 0.6 × 0.4-0.6 mm, margem externa delgada, inteira ou erosa e mais ou menos sinuada; estames 0.8-1 mm, filetes 0.5-0.7 mm, anteras 0.2-0.25 × 0.15-0.25 mm, subtriangulares, 2-loculares, lóculos confluentes por fenda em ângulo de ca 150°, conectivo inconspícuo; ovário 0.8-1 mm diâm, 3-lobado, estilete ca 0.3 mm, estigma pontual, óvulos por lóculo 2. Bagas 2.5-4.4 × 2-4 cm, esferóides, secas verdes a laranja, minutamente verrucosos, imaturas pruinosas, esbranquiçadas a azul esverdeadas, maduras amarelas, laranja, marrom-alaranjadas ou marrons, epicarpo maduro crustáceo. Sementes 1.5-3.5 × 0.9-2.9 cm.

description: Lianas, glabras; ramos novos achatados a cilíndricos, não lenticelados ou muitos esparso lenticelados, secos esverdeados ou amarelados, às vezes minutamente frisados, velhos cilíndricos, fissurados, lenticelados, minutamente frisados, cinzentos. Folhas opostas a subopostas; estípulas triangulares, inteiras; pecíolos (4-)8(-11) mm, secos cinzentos, às vezes pontuados de cor clara, minutamente frisados; lâminas (6.3-)8.1-14(-22) × 1.9-3.9(-6.5) cm, elípticas, base cuneada a arredondada, margem inteira, ápice agudo, raro acuminado, cartáceas, secas esverdeado enegrecidas em ambas as faces, nervuras secas de cor inconspícua em ambas as faces a cinzentas na face abaxial, secundárias e terciárias obscuras na face adaxial, na abaxial secundárias levemente promínulas a planas, terciárias obscuras. Inflorescências fasciculadas, número indeterminado mas elevado de flores, truncifloras em protuberâncias densas que produzem flores por várias estações; brácteas denticuladas; pedicelos 10-17 mm, secos enegrecido a pruinosos. Botões florais esféricos. Flores 8.5-13.5 mm diâm na antese, campanuliformes, secas enegrecidas; receptáculo ca 1.7 mm diâm; sépalas (1.4-)2.2-3.5 × 1.9-3.5 mm, altamente desiguais, 2 menores e 3 maiores, triangulares, inteiras ou denticuladas, escariosas, carnosas, verdes; pétalas 3.3-6.2 × 3.9-6.1 mm, largo-elípticas, mais ou menos oblíquas, cuculadas, inteiras, papiráceas, venação enegrecida visível por transparência, marrons a marrom rosadas; disco anelar-pulviniforme, 0.75-1.45 × 1.1-1.5 mm, margem externa extrema delgada, secando amarelada; estames 1.4-3 mm, filetes 0.75-2.3 mm, anteras 0.4-0.6 × 0.6-0.7 mm, oblongas, 2-loculares, lóculos confluentes por fenda em ângulo de ca 150°, conectivo inconspícuo; ovário ca 1.15 mm diâm, 3-lobado, estilete 0.4-1 mm, estigma pontual, óvulos por lóculo 5-6. Bagas 3.1-7.3 × 2.6-7.4 cm, esferóides, secas enegrecidas, mais ou menos pruinosas, tuberculadas, maduras amarelas a laranja, epicarpo maduro coriáceo. Sementes não vistas.

description: Tree, ca. 30 m tall. Leafy twigs and petioles densely to rather densely covered with light brown, appressed, simple hairs (mostly) less than 0.5 mm long. Petioles 10-13 mm long, to 1 mm in diam. Lamina elliptic (to narrowly elliptic), subcoriaceous, dark brown above, (orange-) brown and papillate below, 5-8 cm long, 2-3.5 cm wide, rather densely to sparsely covered with appressed to erect, straight to crisped, whitish to light brown, simple hairs to 0.5 mm long on large veins, otherwise almost glabrous above, rather densely covered with appressed, light brown (to whitish), simple hairs to 0.5 mm long below; lower epidermal surface somewhat farinose in appearance, base acute to narrowly cuneate, to somewhat attenuate at the extreme base, apex obtuse (?); secondary veins slightly curved to straight, 10-12 on either side of primary vein, often with some short intersecondaries, angles with primary vein 40-60°, smallest distance between loops and margin 1-1.5 mm, tertiary veins (3-4 per intercosta and weakly percurrent to) reticulate. Domatia absent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, often near the base of fresh axillary shoots from older branchlets, or sprouting from leaf axils on older branchlets, single to few-fasciculate, 1-3-flowered, peduncles, pedicels, outer side of bracts, outer side of sepals, and corolla densely covered with light brown, appressed, simple hairs mostly well under 0.5 mm long. Peduncles to 1 mm long. Pedicels 20-30 mm long, 1-1.5 mm (to 2 mm below the flower) in diam. Bracts triangular, 1-2 mm long, upper bract inserted in the lower to upper Vi of the pedicel. Flowers only seen in juvenile stage. Sepals free to connate just at the base, appressed to patent, transversely elliptic to depressed ovate, 1.5-2 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, abruptly acuminate, strongly gibbous with hump to ca. 2 mm long and often somewhat flattened laterally. Corolla tube to 3 mm high, to 5 mm in diam., wings elliptic, horizontal, to 6 mm long, to 4 mm high, less than 1 mm thick, index =1.5. Fruit not seen.

description: Tree, to 8 m tall. Leafy twigs and petioles rather densely covered with mostly appressed, brown, simple hairs up to 0.3 mm long, intermixed with sparse hairs up to 1 mm long. Petioles 5-10 mm long, 0.7-1.5 mm in diam. Lamina elliptic (to narrowly elliptic-ovate), membranaceous to chartaceous, dull brownish- to greyish-green on both sides, 7-22 cm long, 3.5-12 cm wide, rather densely covered on primary vein, sparsely so on secondary veins, otherwise sparsely covered with appressed to (particularly on large veins:) erect, whitish, simple hairs, to glabrous, above, same below, but with mostly appressed, brownish, simple hairs, the hairs to 0.5 mm long (with few to 1 mm long), base acute to obtuse, the base itself sometimes more or less decurrent, apex acuminate to long-acuminate, the tip itself sharply acute to obtuse; secondary veins curved, 8-12 on either side of primary vein, with occasionally very weak intersecondaries, angles with primary vein 45-60°, smallest distance between loops and margin 1.5-5 mm, tertiary veins 6-8 per intercosta, percurrent and perpendicular to primary vein to reticulate. Domatia absent. Inflorescences supra-axillary (to nearly leaf-opposed), 1-2-flowered, pedicels, outer side of bracts, outer side of sepals, and corolla densely to rather densely covered with appressed, brown(ish) hairs to 0.2 mm long intermixed with some hairs to 0.5(-1) mm long. Peduncles inconspicuous. Pedicels 8-15 mm long, 0.5-1 mm in diam, (to 1.5 mm in diam, below the flower). Bracts triangular to triangular-ovate, ca. 1 mm long, upper bract inserted in the lower 2/5 to the upper 3/5 of the pedicel, or missing. Flowers only seen in probably immature condition. Sepals free, appressed, triangular(-ovate), 2.5-3 mm long, 2.5-3.5 mm wide, acute to acuminate, not gibbous. Corolla tube 2.5-3 mm high, ca. 4 mm in diam., wings oblong-obovate to narrowly oblong, horizontal to slightly reflexed, 3.5-5 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm high, to 0.5 mm thick, index = 2. Fruit not seen.

description: Shrub or tree, up to about 20 m tall. Leafy twigs and petioles densely to rather densely covered with more or less erect, often somewhat crisped, (light) brown, (mostly) simple hairs to 0.5 mm long. Petioles 3-6 mm long, (0.5-)1(-1.5) mm in diam. Lamina narrowly elliptic, chartaceous, dull (brownish-)green above, light greyish-green below, (2-)3-10 cm long, 1-3.5 cm wide, sparsely to rather densely hairy on large veins, otherwise glabrous above, rather densely hairy below, with erect, whitish to brownish, simple and also furcate hairs to 0.5 mm long, base acute, apex acute to acuminate, the tip itself acute to obtuse; secondary veins curved to almost straight, 7-15 on either side of primary vein, rarely with some short intersecondaries, angles with primary vein 40-50°, smallest distance between loops and margin 0.5-1.5 mm, tertiary veins 4-6 per intercosta, weakly percurrent to reticulate. Domatia scarce, indistinct. Inflorescences supra-axillary, 1-3-flowered, peduncles, pedicels, outer side of bracts, and outer side of sepals rather densely to densely covered with appressed to erect, brownish, simple hairs to 1 mm long, corolla densely covered with whitish but otherwise the same hairs. Peduncles 1-2 mm long, to 1 mm in diam., fruiting peduncles to 2 mm long, to 2.5 mm in diam. Pedicels 8-12 mm long, 0.5-1 mm in diam., fruiting pedicels to 2.5(-3) mm in diam. Bracts (broadly) triangular-ovate, 0.5-1.5 mm long, upper bract inserted in the lower 1/4 to the upper 3/4 of the pedicel, or missing. Flowers green, yellow-green, or cream-colored in vivo. Sepals free, appressed, (very) broadly triangular-ovate, ca. 2 mm long, 2.5-3 mm wide, acute, not gibbous. Corolla tube 2-3 mm high, 4-5 mm in diam., wings broadly elliptic to broadly elliptic-oblong, horizontal to slightly recurved, 5-7 mm long, 4-5 mm high, 1(-1.5) mm thick, index = 1-1.5. Fruit globose to very broadly ovoid, 1.5-2.5 cm long, 1.8-3.0 cm in diam., yellow in vivo, blackish-grey when dry,composed of 10-40 carpels, rather densely covered with erect, light brown simple hairs to 0.5 mm long, areoles semiglobose to depressed ovoid, 2-3 mm high, 56 × 4-5 mm in diam, at the base, with mostly indistinct apicule in upper half, surface verruculose; wall to 1 mm thick. Seeds to 8 × 4 mm.

description: Tree or shrub, 2-9 m tall. Leafy twigs densely covered with weak, white to pale brown, crisped, erect, simple hairs to 0.5 mm long, becoming glabrous. Petioles 3-5(-10) mm long, 0.5-1 mm in diam. Lamina ovate to elliptic, 4-7(-10) cm long, 1.5-3(-5) cm wide, chartaceous, dark greenish-brown above, green to brown below, rather densely to densely covered with weak, white, crisped, simple hairs to 0.2 mm long above, rather densely covered with weak, white, erect to semiappressed, crisped, simple hairs to 0.3 mm long below, base obtuse to slightly cordate, apex obtuse to slightly emarginate; secondary veins curved to straight, (5-)6-8 on either side of primary vein, rarely with short intersecondaries, angles with primary vein 40-60°, occasionally loop-forming down to more than 1/2 of the length, smallest distance between loops and margin mostly 1-3 mm, tertiary veins 2-3 per intercosta, weakly percurrent to reticulate. Domatia scarce, indistinct. Inflorescences leaf-opposed (to supra-axillary), 1 (-rarely 3)-flowered, (peduncles), pedicels, outer side of bracts and sepals, and (most of) corolla densely to rather densely covered with appressed to erect, brownish (to whitish), crisped to straight, simple hairs to 0.3(-0.5) mm long. Peduncles 0-0.5 mm long, 0.7-1 mm in diam., fruiting peduncles to 1 mm long, to 1.5(-2) mm in diam. Pedicels 10-20 mm long, 0.5-1 mm in diam., fruiting pedicels 1-2 mm in diam. Bracts broadly (ovate-)triangular, 1-2 mm long, upper bract inserted in up to 1/3 (or halfway) of the pedicel. Flowers red, fragrant in vivo. Sepals slightly connate at the base, patent, broadly ovate, 1-3 mm long, 3-5 mm wide, shortly acuminate, not gibbous. Corolla tube 3-4	mm high, 3-4 mm in diam., wings suborbicular to obovate, ascending, 7-12 mm long, 6-9 mm high, less than 0.5 mm thick, index = 1-1.3. Fruit subglobose in outline, 2-4 cm in overall diam., apocarpous, green, maturing yellow, orange, or red in vivo, black to dark brown when dry, carpels 15-20, obovoid, 8-13(-l 4) mm long, 4-6(-8) mm in diam., gradually narrowed into a stipe 12 mm long, sparsely covered with white, crisped, simple hairs (to ca. 1 mm long), with obtuse apex, surface slightly to distinctly verrucose; wall ca. 0.2 mm thick. Seeds 8-9 × 4-6 mm, pale brown, pitted.

description: Shrub or small tree, 1-6 m tall. Leafy twigs and petioles densely covered with ferruginous, erect to appressed, simple hairs to 0.5 mm long. Petioles 2-5 mm long, ca. 1 mm in diam. Lamina ovate to elliptic or narrowly so, 4-8(-10) cm long, 1-4 cm wide, chartaceous, dark green, grey, green, or dark brown above, pale green to brownish-green below, densely covered (hirsute) on primary vein, otherwise rather densely covered (secondary veins) with erect hairs to 0.5 mm long, to (almost) glabrous above, densely covered with white to pale brown, erect, simple hairs to 0.5 mm long below, base acute (rarely obtuse), apex acute to very shortly acuminate; secondary veins slightly curved, 6-10 on either side of primary vein, rarely with some short intersecondaries, angles with primary vein 40-70°, loop-forming usually over most of the length at acute to right (to obtuse) angles, secondary arches sometimes conspicuous, smallest distance between loops and margin (0.5-)1-2 mm, tertiary veins 2-3 per intercosta, weakly percurrent to reticulate. Domatia scarce, indistinct. Inflorescences supra-axillary to (pseudo-)axillary, 1 (-rarely 2)-flowered, pedicels, outer side of bracts and sepals, and wings of corolla densely covered with ferruginous, erect to appressed, simple hairs to 0.5 mm long, inner side of sepals glabrous. Peduncles scarsely visible. Pedicels 10-17 mm long, 0.5-1 mm in diam. Bracts ovate, 0.5-1 mm long, rather frequently wanting (upper bract or both bracts), upper bract (if present) inserted near the base at up to ca. 1/3 of the pedicel. Flowers white to yellow, inner center purple in vivo. Sepals free, patent, ovate-deltate, 3-4 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, acute, not gibbous. Corolla tube 3-4 mm high, 4-5 mm in diam., wings semicircular, horizontal to ascending, 2-3 mm long, 2-4 mm high, 1 -5-2.5 {-4} mm thick, index = 1. Fruit subglobose in outline, 2-2.5 cm in diam., apocarpous, rarely carpels connate over xh of the length, yellow-orange to orange when mature in vivo, carpels 1-6, ellipsoid to obovoid, 7-12 mm long, 4-6 mm in diam., shortly stipitate (stipe 1-2 mm long), glabrous, with obtuse to shortly apiculate apex, surface often strongly verrucose; wall less than 0.2 mm thick. Seeds 9 × 5 mm, pale, shiny brown, pitted.

description: Tree (or shrub), 4-25 m tall and to 40 cm in diam. Leafy twigs and petioles densely covered with ferruginous, crisped, erect and appressed, simple hairs, at last glabrescent with only appressed hairs left. Petioles 6-20 mm long, 1.5-2 mm in diam. Lamina elliptic (to obovate), coriaceous, greyish-green, shiny, above, pale brown and papillate below, (11-) 13-30 cm long, (5-)6-11(-15) cm wide, primary and secondary veins covered with white, crisped, simple hairs, otherwise glabrous above, densely to rather densely covered with ferruginous to white, erect, crisped, simple hairs to 1 mm long below, base obtuse to rounded (or broadly cuneate), apex acute to obtuse, to very shortly acuminate, the tip itself acute to obtuse; secondary veins curved to straight, 18-30 on either side of primary vein, intersecondaries varying from short and weak to more than 1/2 of the length of the secondary veins, angles with primary vein 60-80°, loops indistinct to distinct, smallest distance between loops and margin (0-)0.5-1.5 mm, tertiary veins 6-8 per in-tercosta, weakly percurrent. Domatia occasionally present. Inflorescences leaf-opposed to supra-axillary, 2-4(-5)-flowered, peduncles, pedicels, outer side of bracts, outer side of sepals, and corolla densely covered with erect and appressed, ferruginous (to greyish), crisped hairs to 0.5(-l) mm long, inner side of bracts and inner side of sepals subglabrous. Peduncles 2-4 mm long, 2-3 mm in diam., fruiting peduncles to 6 mm long. Pedicels 15-20 mm long, 1-2 mm in diam., fruiting pedicels to 35 mm long, 2-3 mm in diam. Bracts deltate to triangular, 2-7 mm long, upper bract to at 1/3 of the pedicel length. Flowers green, brownish-green, to creamy, fragrant (Maas et al 6949) in vivo, greyish-brown to brown when dry. Sepals free, appressed, triangular-elliptic to shallowly triangular, 3-4 mm long, 4-6 mm wide, acute, strongly gibbous. Corolla tube 3-5 mm high, 5-9 mm in diam., wings narrowly obovate, ascending when young, subhorizontal when mature, 6-15 mm long, 5-6 mm high, 1-1.5 mm thick, index = 1-2.5. Fruit subglobose to broadly ovoid, 1.8-2.6 cm long, 2-2.6 cm in diam., green, maturing yellow in vivo, brown when dry, composed of 50-75 carpels, densely covered with brownish, appressed hairs, areoles pyramidal and straight, to pulvinate with straight apicule in (the extreme part of) the upper half, 3-7 × 3-4 mm at the base, apex or apicule acute to obtuse, sometimes with abaxial furrow below the apicule, 1-3 mm high, surface smooth to sub verrucose; wall ca. 1 mm thick. Seeds 7-8 × 5-6 × 2-4 mm. Chromosome number: 2n= 14.

description: Shrub or small tree, up to 6 m tall. Leafy twigs and petioles densely covered with erect, straight or more or less crisped, light (orange-)brown to whitish, simple to stellate hairs to 0.5(-l) mm long. Petioles 4-10 mm long, 1-2 mm in diam. Lamina elliptic (to narrowly elliptic), chartaceous, dull green to brown above, green to brownish-green below, 4-12(-14) cm long, 2-5 cm wide, rather densely to sparsely covered above and densely covered below with whitish, erect, predominantly 2-5(-10)-armed stellate hairs to 0.5(-l) mm long, base acute (to rounded), apex shortly acuminate to acute (or obtuse), the tip itself acute to obtuse; secondary veins (slightly) curved, 7-9 on either side of primary vein, angles with primary vein 30-50°, smallest distance between loops and margin 0.5-1.5 mm, tertiary veins 6-7 per intercosta, percurrent. Domatia present, sometimes indistinct. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or supra-axillary, 1-2-flowered, (pedun cles and) pedicels, bracts, sepals (both sides) densely to rather densely covered with appressed to erect, brownish hairs as on the branchlets to 0.5(-l) mm long, corolla densely covered with more or less erect to crisped, whitish hairs mostly under 0.5 mm long. Peduncles 0(-l) mm long. Pedicels 12-25 mm long, 1 mm in diam., fruiting pedicels 35 mm long, 1-2 mm in diam. Bracts broadly triangular (to semicircular), to 0.5(-l) mm long, upper bract inserted near the base to in the lower 1/3 of the pedicel, or missing. Flowers with sepals basally connate, appressed to patent, very broadly ovate-triangular, 2-3 mm long, 3 mm wide, not gibbous, acute to acuminate. Corolla tube 3-4 mm high, 5-6 mm in diam., wings oblong to (? when mature:) almost circular, ascending to horizontal, to 8 mm long, 3.5-5 mm high, 1-2 mm thick, index = (1-)1.5-2. Fruit globose to ellipsoid, 1.5-2 cm long, 1-2 cm in diam., greyish-white when dry, composed of ca. 15-20 carpels, rather densely covered with appressed to semierect, greyish, mostly simple hairs to 0.5 mm long, areoles flat or nearly so, of irregular shape, often bordered by a tiny elevated rim, with a minute apicule, 7-8 × 3-5 mm, apicule acute, up to 1 × 1 mm high, smooth to somewhat tuberculate; wall ca. 0.5 mm thick. Seeds 7-9 × 5-6 mm.

description: Tree, ca. 15 m tall. Leafy twigs and petioles rather densely to sparsely covered with brownish, mostly appressed, simple hairs to 0.5 mm long. Petioles 5-8 mm long, 1-1.5 mm in diam. Lamina narrowly elliptic, chartaceous, dark brown to dull dark green above, brown to brownish-green, more or less shiny below, 9-15 cm long, 3-5.5 cm wide, rather densely covered with whitish, more or less erect, simple hairs to 0.5 mm long on primary vein, otherwise (subglabrous above, sparsely covered with whitish (to brownish), appressed, simple hairs less than 0.5 mm long below, base obtuse to acute, apex acuminate, the tip itself acute to obtuse; secondary veins curved, 6-10 on either side of primary vein, angles with primary vein 40-60°, loops indistinct to distinct, smallest distance between loops and margin 0.5-1.5 mm, tertiary veins 5-8 per intercosta, weakly percurrent. Domatia absent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, 1-3-flowered, peduncles, pedicels, outer side of bracts, and outer side of sepals rather densely (to sparsely) covered with brown, (mostly) appressed, simple hairs less than 0.5 mm long, corolla same, but densely covered and hairs appressed to erect. Peduncles 1-1.5 mm long, to 1.5 mm in diam. Pedicels 10-13 mm long, 1-2 mm in diam. Bracts (broadly) triangular to subulate, 1-2 mm long, upper bract inserted (almost) at the base to in the upper 2/3 of the pedicel. Flowers bright green to pale yellow in vivo, fragrant. Sepals free, appressed to somewhat reflexed, triangular, to 3 mm long, to 2 mm wide, acute, not gibbous. Corolla tube ca. 3 mm high, 5-6 mm in diam., wings obovate to elliptic, horizontal, 5-6 mm long, 3-5 mm high, 1.5-2 mm thick, index = 1-1.5. Fruit not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Maas, Paulus J. M., et al. 1992. Rollinia. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 57: 1-188.

description: Tree, 5-20 m tall. Leafy twigs and petioles rather densely to sparsely covered with appressed, whitish to light brown, simple hairs less than 0.5 mm long, occasionally intermixed with hairs to 1 mm long. Petioles 10-20 mm long, 1-2(-3) mm in diam. Lamina (narrowly) elliptic, obovate, or (narrowly) oblong, chartaceous, brown to dark (olive-)brown above, light greyish-brown to greyish-green and papillate below, 10-25(-30) cm long, 3-11 (-14) cm wide, sparsely covered above with appressed to erect, more or less crisped, whitish, simple hairs less than 0.5 mm long, to glabrous, rather densely to sparsely covered below with appressed, whitish to light brown, simple hairs less than 0.5 mm long (to ca. 0.7 mm long on large veins), lower epidermal surface often microscopically whitish-rugulose, base acute, (broadly) cuneate, or obtuse, apex (shortly) acuminate, the tip itself acute to obtuse; secondary veins straight to curved, 17-26 on either side of primary vein, rarely with few, mostly short intersecondaries, angles with primary vein 40-60°, smallest distance between loops and margin 1-2 mm, tertiary veins 10-13 per intercosta, (weakly) percurrent. Domatia scarce. Inflorescences supra-axillary, rarely leaf-opposed or terminal on axillary shoot, l-2(-3)-flowered, peduncles and pedicels densely to rather densely covered with appressed, brownish, simple hairs to 1 mm long, outer side of bracts and sepals densely covered with appressed, whitish to brownish, simple hairs less than 0.5 mm long, intermixed or not with a variable quantity of straight, appressed to suberect hairs to 0.5 mm long. Peduncles 1-3 mm long, 1-1.5 mm in diam., fruiting peduncles to 5-7 mm in diam. Pedicels 10-23 mm long, (l-)1.5-2 mm in diam., fruiting pedicels to 30 mm long, to 5-7 mm in diam. Bracts (broadly) triangular to semicircular, 1-2.5 mm long, upper bract inserted in the lower 1/4 (or less) to the lower 1/3 of the pedicel. Flowers yellow, (light) yellowish-green, creamy, or green in vivo. Sepals free, well spaced to contiguous, appressed, triangular to triangular-ovate, 2-4 mm long, 2.5-4.5 mm wide, acute to acuminate, gibbous to weakly gibbous. Corolla tube 3-4 mm high, 7-8 mm in diam., wings narrowly oblong to narrowly obovate-oblong, (sub)erect to horizontal (or slightly reflexed), straight to slightly incurved, 20-25 mm long, 6-8 mm high, 1-1.5 mm thick, index = 3-3.5. Fruit globose to broadly ovoid, to ca. 5 cm in diam., green-yellow in vivo, brownish when dry, composed of 150-250 carpels, densely covered with tiny, granulose, brown hairs, intermixed with (eventually shed) whitish, appressed hairs to 0.5 mm long, areoles pyramidal, broadly pyramidal, to conical, straight to slightly incurved, 4-7 × 2-4 mm at the base, with (mostly) acute apex, 2-3 mm high, surface rugulose to smooth; wall 2-4 mm thick. Seeds 8-10 × 5-6 × 2.5 mm.

description: Tree, ca. 8 m tall. Leafy twigs and petioles rather densely covered with brownish, erect or ascending, mostly (?) simple hairs to 0.5 mm long. Petioles 8-10 mm long, (1.5-)2-3 mm in diam. Lamina (narrowly) elliptic to (narrowly obovate-elliptic, chartaceous to membranaceous, dark brownish-green above, brownish-green below, 10-18 cm long, 3.5-6.5 cm wide, rather densely covered above on large veins, otherwise (very) sparsely covered with brownish, erect, mainly stellate, up to ca. 6-armed hairs to 0.5 mm long, rather densely covered below with brownish, erect, simple or mostly stellate, to ca. 6-armed hairs of 0.5-1 mm long, base acute (or cuneate) to obtuse, somewhat attenuate at the very base, apex acuminate, the tip itself acute to obtuse; secondary veins straight to curved, 8-11 on either side of primary vein, rarely with short intersecondaries, angles with primary vein 4050°, smallest distance between secondary veins and margin 0-0.5 mm, tertiary veins 10-14 per intercosta, weakly percurrent (to more or less forked to reticulate). Domatia numerous. Inflorescences supra-axillary to leaf-opposed, 1-3(-6: fide R. E. Fries)-flowered, peduncles, pedicels, outer side of bracts, outer side of sepals, and corolla densely covered with appressed to erect, brown hairs to 0.5 mm (or slightly more) long. Peduncles 0.5-1.5 mm long, up to 1.5 mm in diam. Pedicels 8-11 mm long, l-(below flower:)2 mm in diam. Bracts triangular-ovate, 1-2 mm long, upper bract near the base. Flowers with sepals connate over 1-2 mm, appressed (to more or less patent), ovate-triangular to triangular, 46 mm long and wide, acute to acuminate, not (or weakly) gibbous. Corolla tube to 3 mm high, 56 mm in diam., wings (becoming) obovate-elliptic, ascending, to 11 mm long, to 7 mm high, 1-1.5 mm thick, index =1.5. Fruit not seen.

description: Small tree or shrub generally up to 6.0 m, rarely higher. Branchlets slender, elongate, young parts more or less densely short-hairy, older ones glabrescent. Leaves oblong-elliptic, apex narrowly acuminate, base cuneate, membranaceous to chartaceous, dull, glabrous above, set with appressed longer and shorter hairs on midrib and lateral nerves, less densely so on the intervenium beneath, entire, 8.0-14.0 cm long, 3.0-4.0 cm broad, lateral nerves 5 or 6 pairs, very slightly impressed above, raised beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather obscure on both faces; petiole short-pubescent, 4.0-6.0 mm long; stipules subulate, silky, ca 9.0 mm long, caducous. Spikes slender, ca 10.0 mm long, 1.0 mm diam; flower-subtending bracts acutish, slightly shorter than the sepals, the latter 4, obovate, obscurely denticulate, ca 0.5 mm long. Disk fleshy, entire, low. Ovary patently pubescent at least in the upper part; styles 3, very short. Fruit subglobose, sessile, more or less densely covered with short hairs, 5.0-6.0 mm long.

description: Shrubs or small trees, to 10 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.7-3 mm in diam., slightly angular, the youngest part covered with a dense, light brownish indument of relatively long hairs (up to ca. 0.4 mm), ascending to erect, first becoming greyish and less dense on older twigs, then wearing off; terminal buds ovate to elongate, 4-7.5 mm long, 1.2-2 mm thick, densely covered with ascending to erect, light brownish hairs. Petioles 3.5-10 mm long, 1.2-2.5 mm thick, roundish below, slightly longitudinally ridged, canaliculate above, but the furrow often concealed by the dense indument, which has a structure ± like that on twigs, and is clearly denser above than below. Leaves alternate, ± lanceolate, rarely with a tendency towards elliptic or oblanceolate, widest ± at the middle (more frequently below than above the middle), 9-21 cm long, 3-6.5 cm wide, ca. (2.5-)3-4 times longer than wide, tip acuminate, base narrowly cuneate to obtuse but attenuate at the very base, margin flat to narrowly bent down, distinctly recurved to revolute at the base, midrib and secondary veins ± impressed above, prominent below, secondary veins 5-9 pairs, diverging at 30-50(-65)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 15-30(-50)° to the midrib, tertiary venation scalariform, level to slightly impressed above, mostly inconspicuous, ± distinctly raised below, finer venation level on both sides or slightly raised below. Indument consisting of relatively long hairs (ca. 0.30.5 mm), straight to ± slightly wavy, ± erect, pale to reddish, in youngest leaves dense on midrib and largest veins above, intermediate to sparse in intercostal area, the latter quickly glabrescent, indument for a long time persistent on veins, initially intermediate to dense below, in older leaves intermediate to sparse, or finally persistent only on veins. Gland dots sometimes moderately distinct on upper surface of young leaves, otherwise not visible. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, 0.6-1.3 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-2.8 mm diam., 3.5-13 cm long, reaching ca. 2/5-5/6 the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 1.4-3.5 cm long, i.e., ca. 1/4 to 2/5 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 6-12 below terminal cyme, branched 2-4 times, indument ± as on twigs, ± moderately dense, denser on the receptacle. Pedicels 0.5-1.8 mm long, ca. 0.4 mm thick. Flowers 4-4.5 mm in diam., tepals ± ovate to oblong, 1.5-2 mm long and ca. 1 mm wide, with fine, long papillae on the inside surface, their density gradually increasing from (sub)glabrous at the base of the tepal to (moderately) dense at the tip. Stamens ca. 0.8-1 mm long including a distinct filament of 0.3-0.4 mm, anthers papillose, in the two outer whorls ± transverse-elliptic, broadly rounded to almost truncate or minutely apiculate at the tip, not prolonged beyond the pollen sacs, in the third whorl anthers roundish-obtrapeziform, ± truncate at the tip. Staminodes ca. half as long as the stamens, ± clavate, papillose-hairy on abaxial side. Pistil ca. 1.3-1.7 mm long, ovary ellipsoid, glabrous, style ca. as long as the ovary, glabrous or with some papillae. Receptacle urceolate to almost tubular, covered with relatively long, appressed to ascending hairs inside. Berry spheroidal, ca. 8 mm in diam., cupule ± trumpet-shaped, the cup itself shallow, only ca. 2-3 mm deep and ca. 8 mm in diam., gradually merging into the distinctly thickened lenticellate pedicel.
bibliographicCitation: Rohwer, Jens G. 1993. Lauraceae: Nectandra. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 60: 1-332.

description: Decumbent subshrubs, the stems purplish, with scattered stellate hairs ca. 1 mm long. Leaf blades sagittate, mostly 3-7 x 1.5-3 cm, deeply cordate-sagittate basally (the lobes sometimes equaling the petiole), clearly serrate to obscurely undulate-serrate or subentire, acute, palmately 7-nerved, notably discolorous, evenly stellate-pubescent on upper surface (hairs 0.5 mm long), densely matted-canescent beneath; petioles 8-15 mm long; stipules filiform, 3-4 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels ca. 1 cm long, slender; involucellar bracts 5, lance-ovate, 8-9 x 3-4 mm, softly tomentose; calyx subequal to involucel, softly tomentose; corolla ca. 1 cm long, rose with darker veins. Fruits 6-7 mm diam., minutely pubescent; mericarps rugulose, 4 mm high, apiculate at apex. Chromosome number, In = 56 (Fernández, 1981).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1999. Pavonia Cavanilles (Malvaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 76: 1-284.

description: Shrubs to 1.5 m tall, the stems pilose (hairs 2-3 mm long) and with a sparse understory of minute glandular hairs and narrow lines of dense, recurved hairs. Leaf blades ovate (reduced upward to narrowly triangular), sometimes hastately lobed, cordate, serrate, acute, up to 12 x 9 cm (narrower and smaller upward), both surfaces with appressed simple hairs 0.5-1.5 mm long (and also stellate hairs beneath); petioles 0.5-8 cm long; stipules 7-15 x 2-5 mm, asymmetrically ovate or falcate, reflexed. Flowers usually in a terminal raceme or panicle more or less above the leaves; pedicels 2-3 cm long; involucellar bracts 5-6(-8), lanceolate, 7-9 x 0.5-2 mm, ciliate; calyx 5-7 mm long, ciliate; corolla 8-10 mm long, yellow; androecium shorter than to subequal to corolla; styles glabrous, exserted from staminal column and from corolla, proximally united, distally free for 2 mm. Fruits 7 mm diam., minutely scabridulous, obscurely rugose. Chromosome number, 2n = 56 (Fernández, 1981).

description: Erect shrubs 1-1.5 m tall, the stems coarsely ferruginous-hirsute, the hairs stellate, 1-2.5 mm long. Leaf blades sagittate-oblong to sagittate-elliptic, mostly 3-8(-10) (excluding lobes) x 1-5.5 cm, basally cordate-sagittate (the lobes 5-15 mm long), shallowly dentate, acute to obtuse, palmately 5-7-nerved, discolorous, the upper surface with erect (i.e., tufted) stellate hairs ca. 1 mm long, the lower surface whitish, with denser and finer stellate pubescence; petioles 1-2 cm long; stipules 1-3 mm long, subulate, often hidden by density of pubescence. Flowers solitary (or paired) in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-4 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, broadly ovate or suborbicular, 5-8 x 3-7 mm, distally revolute, densely hirsute, discolorous; calyx 8-10 mm long, densely ferruginous-hirsute; corolla pink with red center and red venation, 1.5-3.5 cm long. Fruits 7 mm diam., minutely pubescent; mericarps 4-5 mm high, carinate, smooth. Chromosome number, 2n = 56 (Krapovickas & Cristóbal, 1962; Fernández, 1981).

description: Shrubs 1-2 m tall, the stems minutely puberulent or glabrescent, with prominent leaf scars. Leaves congested apically, the blades lanceolate-acuminate, entire or obscurely denticulate, 8-15 x 1.5-3 cm, glabrate above, scabrid beneath; petioles 1-3 cm long, deflected, scabridulous; stipules linear-lanceolate, 8 mm long. Flowers congested apically, forming a terminal capitulum, the pedicels 8-13 mm long, minutely puberulent; involucellar bracts ca. 15, linear-acute, tomentose, slightly shorter than calyx, in two series, the bracts of the outer series fewer and shorter; calyx tomentose, 5-lobed, the lobes more or less lanceolate; petals erect, narrow, twice length of calyx (i.e., exserted), dark purple; staminal column exserted, the filaments emerging in upper portion of column; styles exserted from staminal column, glabrous, with capitellate stigmas. Fruits unknown.

description: Subshrubs, procumbent to ascending, to 0.5 m tall, the stems covered with minute appressed stellate (sublepidote) hairs. Leaf blades hastate-triangular, mostly 10-20 x 8-15 mm, basally hastate-cordate, crenate, acute to obtuse, palmately 3-5-nerved, discolorous, minutely stellate-pubescent above, densely canescent beneath; petioles 3-14 mm long; stipules subulate, 2(-4) mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-2 cm long; involucellar bracts 5-6, lance-ovate, 4-7 x 2.5-3 mm; calyx 6-7 mm long, densely puberulent; corolla 1-1.5 cm long, lavender with a purplish center; staminal column 5 mm long, glabrous, purplish, the filaments 1.5-2 mm long; styles purplish, the stigmas pallid and villous. Fruits ca. 7 mm diam., minutely pubescent; mericarps 4 mm high, carinate, reticulate-veined. Chromsome number, 2n = 56 (Krapovickas & Cristóbal, 1962).

description: Subshrubs 0.5-1 m tall, the stems densely stellate-pubescent, the hairs 0.5 mm long. Leaf blades oblong-lanceolate, mostly 4-6(-9) x l-2(-4) cm, basally truncate to sagittate (with an acute sinus), serrate, acute, palmately 3-5-nerved, discolorous, the upper surface with simple, bifurcate, and stellate hairs, the lower surface densely stellate-tomentulose; petioles 1-2 cm long; stipules subulate, 2-4 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 0.5-3 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, lanceolate, 7-9(-18) x 2-4(-5) mm, hirsute; calyx 7-10 mm long, hirsute; corolla 2.5-3 cm long, white or pale lavender with reddish veins and a purplish center, densely pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column 6-10 mm long, glabrous, purplish, the filaments 1.5-3 mm long; styles purplish, the stigmas pallid, villous. Fruits 7 mm diam., minutely puberulent; mericarps 5 mm high, prominently rugulose. Chromosome number, 2n = 56 (Krapovickas & Cristóbal, 1962).

description: Procumbent perennial herb, the stems loosely stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades subovate to subrotund (sometimes triangular to pentagular), mostly 1-2.5 cm long, about as wide, basally cordate, coarsely crenate-dentate, acute to obtuse, palmately 5-veined, with scattered stellate hairs beneath, with simple, bifurcate, and stellate hairs above, the hairs ca. 1 mm long; petioles 1-1.5 cm long; stipules subulate, 2-3 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-4 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, ligulate to spatulate, 7-11 x 1-2 mm, ciliate; calyx 7-10 mm long, sparsely ciliate; corolla 1.5-2.5 cm long, rose with purplish center and veins, pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column 7-8 mm long, glabrous, the filaments 1-2 mm long; styles emergent from the column. Fruits ca. 7 mm diam., minutely pubescent; mericarps 4 mm high, carinate, reticulately veined but relatively smooth.

description: Shrubs 1-2 m tall, the stems stellate-pubescent, the hairs of variable size. Leaf blades ovate-triangular to lance-oblong, mostly 2-8(-10) x 1-2.5 cm, basally cordate to subsagittate, coarsely crenate-dentate, acute, palmately 5-nerved, discolorous (whitish beneath), stellate-pubescent on both surfaces; petioles 1-2.5 cm long; stipules subulate, 2 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-4 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, ovate, 5-8 x 2-4 mm, stellate-pubescent; calyx 6-9 mm long, ciliate; corolla (sometimes cleistogamous) 2-3 cm long, rose-pink with dark red center, minutely pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column 5-9 mm long, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles emergent from the column, purplish, free for distal 3-4 mm. Fruits 7-9 mm diam., minutely pubescent; mericarps 5 mm high, carinate (the ridge apically prolonged and acute), rugose, usually with acute excrescences on each side.

description: Prostrate to ascending perennial subshrubs (rarely shrubs to 2.5 m: Arbo et al. 5443), the stems variably pubescent (with minute glandular hairs in Pernambuco; stellate-pubescent or glandular in Bahia; setose in Minas Gerais and Bolivia). Leaf blades hastately 3-lobed to palmately 5-7-lobed, slightly asymmetrical, deeply cordate, crenate-serrate, acute to obtuse, densely tomentose on both surfaces (sometimes also with scattered 3-4-armed spicules), mostly 2-6 x 3-9 cm; petioles 1.5-4 cm long; stipules subulate or filiform, 3-6 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-4 cm long; involucellar bracts 14-16 (-22 in Pernambuco), 1-2 cm long, arcuate, copiously hirsute; calyx 7-10 mm long, hirsute, usually concealed by involucel; corolla 3 cm long, yellow fading orange. Fruits 6-7 mm diam., subglabrous, the mericarps strongly rugose, with 3 erect subapical points 1-2 mm long.

description: Subshrubs ca. 1 m tall, the stems loosely stellate-pubescent, the hairs 0.5-1 mm long. Leaf blades lance-elliptic, mostly 4-13 x 2-4.5 cm, distichous, basally subtruncate to cuneate and more or less asymmetrically so, serrate, acute, penninerved or palmately 3-nerved, somewhat discolorous, the upper surface densely covered with appressed simple hairs ca. 1 mm long, the lower surface with simple and bifurcate (occasionally stellate) hairs 0.5-1 mm long (especially on veins); petioles 4-10 mm long; stipules 3-6 mm long, subulate. Flowers solitary or paired in the leaf axils or aggregated terminally or on lateral branches in subcapitate clusters, the pedicels 1-3 cm long, with pubescence similar to that of stem except more or less antrorsely oriented; involucellar bracts 7-8, narrowly linear with acute to narrowly rounded sinuses, 6-7 mm long, connate below, hirsute; calyx ca. 4 mm long, ciliate; corolla white, 8-12 mm long, minutely pubescent externally. Fruits 6 mm diam., glabrous, subglobose, the mericarp body 5-6 mm high, smooth, 3-spined, the spines 4-7 mm long, more or less erect, retrorsely barbed, the central spine dorsoventrally buttressed at base, the lateral spines 3 mm apart at base.

description: Shrubs 1.5-2 m tall, the stems scurfy, rarely stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades elliptic to slightly oblanceolate, to 15-30 x 5-8 cm, basally cuneate, subentire or with a few denticulations near the apex, acuminate, penninerved (the midrib raised beneath), essentially glabrous (or with a few scabrid hairs beneath); petioles 3-5 cm long, scabrous, canaliculate; stipules linear-lanceolate, 15-20 x 1-2 mm, with scabrous stellate hairs, erect and rigid. Flowers solitary in the upper axils, the pedicels 1.5-3 cm long, pubescent with both stellate and simple hairs; involucel of ca. 16 bractlets in two series, the inner 8 erect, ca. 20 mm long, subspatulate, reddish, the outer bractlets half as long, apparently spreading; calyx 13 mm long, deeply divided, the lobes lanceolate, 3-nerved; petals subequal to or slightly longer than the involucel, externally greenish and stellate-pubescent. Fruits unknown (the ovary glabrous).

description: Shrubs or small trees up to 6 m tall, the stems finely puberulent. Leaf blades narrowly to broadly ovate, shallowly cordate, serrate to subentire, acute or acuminate, mostly 3-8 x 2.5-8 cm, markedly discolorous, palmately 9-nerved, with minute glandular hairs on upper surface (appearing glabrous), finely and densely canescent on lower surface; petioles 2-6 cm long; stipules 2-3 mm long, subulate. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels slender, 3-6 cm long; involucellar bracts 8-10, linear, 1.5-2 x 0.5-1.5 mm, puberulent; calyx 18-30 mm long, finely puberulent, sometimes setose, the lobes 6-10 mm long; corolla 30-38 mm long, red; androecium slightly exserted, the filaments 4-5 mm long; (gynoecium not observed). Fruits 6-7 mm diam., ovoid, the mericarps pubescent, 7 mm high (twice height of column), rugose; seeds pubescent.

description: Shrubs 1-2.5 m tall, the stems densely and minutely glandular-pubescent. Leaf blades broadly ovate, sometimes 3-lobulate, mostly 4-8 x 3.5-7 cm, cordate to subtruncate, crenate-dentate, acuminate, palmately 7-nerved, sometimes discolorous, with minute simple and bifurcate hairs above and beneath, the hairs 0.2-0.3 mm long, and with a few large 2-3armed spicules scattered on lower surface, at least on younger leaves; petioles 2-6 cm long; stipules subulate, 3 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 3-8 cm long, slender; involucellar bracts 5, lance-linear, 8-11 x 2-4 mm, minutely glandular-pubescent; calyx 8-10 mm long, ciliate (hairs 1.5-3 mm long); corolla 2.5-3 cm long, white; staminal column subequal to petals, glabrous, the filaments 3-4 mm long; styles exserted, often exceeding the corolla. Fruits subglabrous, ca. 1 cm diam.; mericarps 4.5-5 mm high, reticulate-rugose, the crest prolonged and acute apically. Chromosome number, 2n = 28 (Krapovickas & Cristóbal, 1962).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1999. Pavonia Cavanilles (Malvaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 76: 1-284.

description: Shrubs 1.5-3.5 m tall, the stems scabridulous with minute stellate hairs and narrow rows of fine recurved hairs. Leaf blades ovate to narrowly triangular to more or less 3-5-lobed, basally truncate to cordate, acute or acuminate, 5-8 x 6-8 cm, smaller and narrower upward, the upper surface with minute appressed hairs (0.3 mm long, frequently bifurcate), the lower surface densely villous on main veins and with widely scattered 3-armed stellate hairs; petioles 2-10 mm long; stipules ca. 10 x 2-4 mm, falcate or triangular, reflexed. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or forming terminal panicles by apical congestion, the pedicels 1-2 cm long; involucellar bracts 10-13, linear, 10-13 mm long, ciliate (hairs 1-2 mm); calyx 6-9 mm long, hirsute; corolla yellow, 2.5 cm long. Fruits 7-8 mm diam., glabrous, the mericarps 5-7 mm long, strongly rugulose, often carinate, the base elongated.

description: Shrubs to 1.5 m tall, the stems sparsely pubescent with minute glandular and stellate hairs intermingled. Leaf blades triangular to lance-oblong, mostly 2.5-7 x 1-3 cm, basally cordate-sagittate, coarsely dentate, acute, palmately 5-nerved, with widely scattered simple and stellate hairs above and beneath, becoming subglabrous, except prominently hirsute at base of blade beneath; petioles 1-3 cm long, prominently hirsute distally (hairs 1 mm long) especially on abaxial side; stipules filiform, 8-11 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1.5-4 cm long, articulated ca. 5 mm below the flower, often hirsute above articulation especially at juncture with involucel; involucellar bracts 5, ovate (subtrullate, basally constricted), acuminate, 8-11 x 3-5 mm, sparsely stellate-pubescent; calyx 8-12 mm long, deeply divided, the lobes cordate, acuminate, sparsely pubescent to nearly glabrous, the veins with purplish pigmentation, the intercostal areas whitish; corolla 2-2.5 cm long, pale rose with purplish center; staminal column 6-7 mm long, purplish, the filaments 1-3 mm long; styles emergent from the column, purplish. Fruits ca. 8 mm diam., minutely pubescent; mericarps 4-5 mm high, carinate, rugulose with 3 excrescences on each side.

description: Procumbent perennial subshrubs, the stems trailing from a woody rootstock, hirsute with hairs 1-2 mm long and with an understory of fine stellate hairs, or sometimes with the long hairs absent, rarely glabrate. Leaf blades orbicular, deeply cordate, crenate-dentate, obtuse or subacute, 1.5-5 x 2-6.5 cm, palmately 7-nerved, softly stellate-puberulent, somewhat discolorous; petioles 1-6 cm long; stipules subulate, 4-8 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-9 cm long; involucellar bracts 9-11, linear-lanceolate, 6-10 x 1 mm (shorter than to longer than the calyx), puberulent or ciliate, sometimes viscid; calyx 7-10 mm long, pubescent; corolla 1.5-2.5 cm long, yellow (drying reddish) with a sharply defined red center, pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column 7-9 mm long, reddish (at least basally), the filaments 1-2 mm long, the anthers purplish; styles emergent from the column, united except for distal 1 mm, nearly equaling the petals. Fruits oblate, 9-10 mm diam., glabrous, the mericarps 5-6 mm high, more or less ridged and reticulate, sometimes the ridge projected subapically into a triangular protruberance; seeds 5 mm long, striate.

description: Shrubs 1-3 m tall, the stems sparsely and minutely lepidote (the hairs 0.1 mm diam.) to glabrate. Leaf blades elliptic, mostly 10-20 x 3-7 cm, basally cuneate, shallowly serrate (at least distally), acute or acuminate, penninerved, the midrib raised above and beneath, minutely and very sparsely stellate-pubescent to subglabrous; petioles 0.5-4.5 cm long, adaxially bearded, sometimes obscurely so; stipules subulate, curved, 12-13 mm long, ciliate toward base. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-2 cm long, densely pilose, the hairs 2 mm long; involucellar bracts ca. 14, red, dimorphic, the smaller ones reflexed, 10-15 x 8-10 mm, the longer ones erect, 35 x 10-16 mm, both forms abaxially stellate-pubescent (the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm diam.), adaxially hirsute with simple hairs 1-2 mm long, both ovate-acuminate; calyx and rest of flower concealed by involucel in available specimens. Fruits unknown.

description: Shrubs or small trees 1-4 m tall, the stems minutely glandular- and stellate-puberulent (the proportions of the two hair-types varying), rarely also with scattered setae in addition (Irwin et al. 20693). Leaf blades ovate (rarely lobulate), mostly 4-10 x 2.5-9 cm, subtruncate to deeply cordate, obscurely serrulate to subentire, acute to acuminate, palmately 7-9-nerved, discolorous, the upper surface very minutely glandular-pubescent (usually seemingly glabrous) and sometimes with longer simple hairs on veins, the lower surface minutely velutinous and with glandular hairs; petioles 2-7 cm long; stipules 4-11 mm long, filiform. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-7 cm long; involucellar bracts 12-14 (8 in Mello-Silva et al 483), lance-linear, 16-21 x 1-3(-4) mm, glandular-pubescent, sometimes also setose; calyx ca. 17 mm long; corolla 2.5-3.5 cm long, tubular or funnelform, red or orange with dark venation; androecium subequal to corolla or slightly exserted, dark red; styles exserted. Fruits 8-10 mm diam., glabrous, prominently reticulately veined, the raised veins dark-pigmented; mericarps 7 mm high, crested; seeds 4.5 mm long, sparsely pubescent.

description: Shrubs 0.5-1 (-2) m tall, the stems hispid (hairs ferruginous, 1-2 mm long) and with underlying finer pubescence. Leaf blades mostly 6-15 x 2-5 cm, narrowly elliptic (sometimes slightly asymmetrical), basally cuneate, serrulate, acuminate, penninerved, the upper surface with appressed simple hairs 1-2 mm long, those of the lower surface simple or bifurcate (rarely stellate); petioles 2-5(-12) mm long, the leaves often subsessile; stipules 3-4 mm long, subulate, hispid. Flowers solitary in the uppermost leaf axils, the pedicels 1-7 cm long, densely hispid, the hairs somewhat retrorse; involucellar bracts 13-16, filiform, 16-20 mm long, arcuate, copiously ciliate, the hairs 2-5 mm long, ferruginous; calyx ca. 5 mm long, stellate-pubescent and hispid; corolla subequal to involucel, white; staminal column ca. 4 mm long, glabrous, the anthers subsessile at apex. Fruits 10-12 mm diam., the mericarp body 6 mm high, glabrous, reticulate-veined, the mericarps each with 3 apical spines, the spines 6-10 mm long, divergent, retrorsely barbed.

description: Shrubs 1-2 m tall, sometimes scandent to 3 m, the stems stellate-pubescent, the hairs of variable size (i.e., heterotrichous). Leaf blades ovate, mostly 5-14 x 2-8 cm, truncate to subcordate, serrate, acute or acuminate, palmately 5-nerved, discolorous, sparsely to densely stellate-pubescent, more densely so beneath; petioles 0.3-2(-3) cm long; stipules filiform, 5-12 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 0.5-5.5 cm long; involucellar bracts 5-7, linear-lanceolate, 7-12 x 1-2 mm, ciliate; calyx 6-11 mm long, ciliate; corolla 2-3.5 cm long, yellow, obscurely pubescent externally, bearded on margins of claw; staminal column 1 cm long, glabrous, the filaments 1-2 mm long; styles exserted from column for 5-6 mm, free for distal 2-3 mm. Fruits 8-10 mm diam., the mericarp body 7 mm long; mericarps strongly keeled, the keel retrorsely scabrid, rugose, 3-spined, the spines divergent, 3-6(-8) mm long, retrorsely barbed. Chromosome number, 2n = 112 (Krapovickas & Cristóbal, 1965, as P. spinifex).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1999. Pavonia Cavanilles (Malvaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 76: 1-284.

description: Subshrubs 0.5 m tall, the stems minutely and sparsely squamose to glabrate. Leaf blades narrowly spatulate, 20-40 x 5-12 mm (widest near apex), basally attenuate-cuneate, the margins entire (more or less undulate), obtuse, the midrib prominent (lateral nerves suppressed), minutely and sparsely squamose (hairs 0.1-0.2 mm diam.) to glabrate; petioles up to 2 mm long (the leaves subsessile); stipules vestigial. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels recurved, 4-8 mm long (to 12 mm in fruit); involucellar bracts 5-6, linear-lanceolate, 1-5 mm long, squamose; calyx 5-6 mm long, squamose or glabrate; corolla 8-11 mm long, white; gentitalia included, the anthers subsessile. Fruits 7 mm diam. (excluding spines), the mericarps 7 mm high, glabrous, 2-spined, the spines divergent, stout, 16-19 mm long, obscurely and minutely barbed toward apex, the spines of adjacent mericarps connivent.

description: Shrubs to 3 m tall, the young stems densely stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades broadly ovate, mostly 4-8 x 3-5.5 cm, subtruncate to shallowly cordate, crenate-dentate, acute, palmately 5-7-nerved, densely and softly stellate-tomentose; petioles 7-30(-40) mm long, evenly tomentose; stipules 4-7 mm long, subulate. Flowers solitary, the pedicels 2-10 mm long at anthesis, to 25 mm in fruit; involucellar bracts 8, lanceolate to spatulate, 7-9 (accrescent to 15) x 2-3 mm, tomentose, basally connate; calyx 5-7 mm long; corolla 21-23 mm long, narrowly tubular, red, externally pubescent and marginally ciliate; staminal column exserted, glabrous, the filaments 0.5-1 mm long, the anthers purplish; styles purplish, barely exserted from column. Fruits oblate, 11-12 mm diam., glabrous, smooth, the mericarps 7-9 mm high, ligneous. Chromosome number, 2n = 56 (Fryxell & Stelly, 1993).

description: Shrubs 1.5-2.5 m tall, the stems sometimes prominently hirsute, usually with narrow longitudinal lines of fine curved hairs and otherwise glabrate. Leaf blades narrowly elliptic, mostly 12-26 x 2-8 cm, basally truncate to cuneate, obscurely to prominently serrate, acuminate, with appressed simple hairs to glabrous or subglabrous, penninerved (6-8 secondary nerves on each side), the midrib raised on both surfaces; petiqles 2.5-12 cm long, sometimes prominently hirsute, usually minutely pubescent on adaxial surface and otherwise glabrous; stipules subulate, erect, 9-13 x 0.5-1 mm. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils or often in axillary fascicles of 2 or 3, the flowers often crowded apically because of shortened internodes and deciduous leaves, the leaf scars prominent, the pedicels up to 7 cm long, minutely pubescent; involucellar bracts 20-24, seemingly in two series, the outer spreading to reflexed, shorter than the arcuate to erect inner bracts, all narrowly ligulate, stellate-pubescent and ciliate, sometimes reddish, the longer bracts 12-20(-30) mm long; calyx 1-2 cm long, deeply divided, with stellate and glandular hairs, sometimes basally setose; corolla tubular, 2-2.5 cm long, barely exceeding calyx to twice length of calyx, externally stellate-pubescent, yellow (reddish in bud) or dark purple in cultivated (selected?) forms; androecium exserted, ca. twice length of corolla, pallid or purplish, the filaments 3-5 mm long; styles exserted, slender, the stigmas villous. Fruits 7-9 mm diam., short-beaked, glabrous, yellowish; mericarps 7-9 mm high, smooth. Chromosome number, 2n = 56 (Bates, 1967).
bibliographicCitation: Fryxell, Paul A. 1999. Pavonia Cavanilles (Malvaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 76: 1-284.

description: Shrubs 2 m tall, the stems densely stellate-tomentose, the hairs 0.5 mm long or less, yellowish. Leaf blades broadly ovate, 5-7(-13) cm long, about as wide, deeply cordate, remotely serrate to subentire, acute, strongly discolorous, obscurely pubescent above, the hairs 0.2-0.3 mm long, often bifurcate, densely and softly yellowish-tomentose beneath, palmately 7-9-nerved; petioles 3-5 cm long, with pubescence like stem; stipules subulate, 2-3 mm long, caducous. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 3-5 cm long, densely stellate-tomentose; in-volucellar bracts 4(-6), broadly cordate-ovate, 2 x 2.5 cm, deeply cordate, densely tomentose; calyx almost as long as involucel, tomentose, short-lobed, largely concealed by involucel; corolla tubular, the petals ligulate, 3-4.5 x 1 cm, exserted from the involucel by 1-2 cm, yellow with red veins (Mello-Silva et al. 518) or red with white veins (Mello-Silva et al. 500) (perhaps varying with time of day), the androecium reddish, subequal to corolla, the styles slightly exserted. Fruits (ex descr.) 2.5-3 mm tall, reticulate-veined (otherwise unornamented), apparently glabrous, ca. twice the height of the column.

description: Shrub up to 1.5 m; stems pubescent, the trichomes glandular, up to 4 mm long. Leaves slightly aniso-phyllous, 18-25 X 10-13 cm, 5-nervate, membranaceous, elliptic to ovate, base round to obtuse, apex shortly accuminate to caudate; petioles 2-4 cm long, with pubescence as on the stems; domatia present, fusiform, 1.2-1.7 X 0.7-1.1 cm, the apical 1/3-1/5 immersed in the blade. Inflorescence terminal, highly reduced, resembling a capitulum, with 20-35 flowers. Flowers sessile; bracts absent; hypanthium 5 mm long, puberulent; outer calyx teeth reduced over the inner teeth, inner calyx teeth ovate up to 4 mm long, pubescent; petals 5, white; anthers 10, all the same size, a blunt, reduced, dorsal, connective tooth present; ovary partly inferior; style glabrous; stigma capitate.  Tococa undabunda is known only from the type collection. Macbride suggested that this species could be related to T. racemifera, based on the domatia, which are fusiform and partially immersed in the blade. The compressed and capitate inflorescence resembles that of T. capitata, although T. undabunda lacks the characteristic bracts of T. capitata. However, leaf shape and pubescence as well as the overall morphology of the hypanthium and calyx resemble those of T. guianensis and closely related species. In fact, the similarities in floral characters suggest that it may be only a form of T. guianensis with compressed inflorescences. Without more material, it is difficult to assess the real status of this taxon, given that some specimens of T. guianensis have inflorescences with different levels of compression and reduction of the different axes.

description: Shrub, to 0.5-2.0 (-3.0) m tall; stems densely glandular-setose, the trichomes 1.5-2.5 mm long, persistent, the nodes glabrous. Leaves isophyllous, ovate to oblong, 8-16 X 4-8 cm, apex acute, base cordate, the sinus up to 1 cm wide, adaxial surface adpressed-setose, abaxial surface sparsely glandular-setose, hirsute on the primary and secondary nerves, light green, 5-nervate, membranaceous, ciliolate; petioles 0.5-1.0(-l.5) cm long, glandular-setose; domada 1/4-1/3 immersed in the leaf blade, globose to ovoid, 0.8-1.2 X 0.7-1.1 cm. Inflorescence a pseudoaxillary panicle, rarely terminal, of 3-9 flowers, 512 cm long, the axis dark red to magenta, flattened, sparsely glandular-setose, branched above a peduncle 2-3 cm long, subtended by a caducous, sheathing bract, 2.5 cm long. Flowers on pedicels 6-10 mm long, not flared at the apex, articulated at the base of the hypanthium; bracts unknown; hypanthium conical, 3.5-5.0 mm long, glabrous; outer calyx teeth reduced and inconspicuous, sometimes with a short apical glandular seta or a sessile gland, 0.2 mm long, inner calyx teeth deltoid to ovate, fused at the base 1/2 of the length, 2.5 mm long, the inner surface covered by minute sessile glands; the ring inside the torus glabrous; petals 5, oblong, 10.5-12.0(-13.5) X 4.0-5.5 mm, base oblong to slightly attenuate, apex round and slightly emarginate, smooth, glabrous, white; stamens all the same size; filaments 5.0-5.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers yellow; the connective with a dorsal-basal blunt tooth; thecae 2.7-3.2 mm long, opening by a ventrally inclined pore; ovary 3-locular, 1/3 inferior, the superior portion broadly conical, the apex truncate; style glabrous, 12-14 mm long; stigma funnelform to capitate, papillate. Fruits globose, with the calyx persistent and slightly reflexed, 4.5-6 mm long, black, glabrous; seeds not evident through the pericarp, truncate-obovate, 0.7-1.3 mm long, without capitate trichomes in the raphal area, without sculpturing, anticlinal walls straight, periclinal walls straight, boundaries between periclinal walls raised.

description: Young branches strigulose with dibrachiate hairs soon glabrous, mid- or grey-brown. Bud scales absent. Leaves unifoliolate, petiole ca. 2 cm long, semiterete, minutely strigulose or glabrous. Leaflets oblong to broadly elliptic, apex shortly narrowly attenuate, base narrowly attenuate to obtuse or rounded, chartaceous, 11-14[12.5] cm long, 4-6[5] cm broad, glabrous, glandular-punctate and -striate or not; venation eucamptodromous or brochidodromous, midrib prominent; secondaries 11-12 on either side of midrib, ascending, arcuate above, ± parallel; intersecondaries long; tertiaries faint. Inflorescence axillary, 1-2 cm long, a small few-flowered, thyrsoid panicle, sparsely strigulose to subglabrous; pedicel 0.5-1 mm long. Calyx patelliform or shallowly cyathiform, 0.5-1 mm long, with 4-5 very shallow lobes or margin subtruncate, subglabrous. Petals 4-5, free, valvate or slightly imbricate, spreading, 2.5-3 mm long, 0.75-1 mm broad, lanceolate, apex acute, glabrous. Staminal tube cyathiform to shortly cylindrical; filaments completely fused, ca. 1.25 mm long, ca. 1 mm broad, margin with 7-8 short acute lobes alternating with anthers and ca. 1/3 their length, glabrous or with a few scattered hairs in throat; anthers 7-8, 0.5-0.8 mm long, glabrous. Nectary absent or represented by an indistinct swelling around base of ovary. Ovary ovoid, 3-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, sparsely appressed puberulous; style glabrous; style-head capitate equalling base of anthers. Fruit unknown.

description: Young branches appressed puberulous or pubescent (trichomes basifixed), soon glabrous, brown with pale lenticels. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate or trifoliolate, 1.8-7.5 cm long; petiole and rhachis semiterete, usually broadened below insertion of leaflets, glabrous; petiolule 2-7 mm long (terminal to 12 mm). Leaflets opposite, 3-5(-11), elliptic, oblanceolate or sometimes lanceolate, apex acuminate or attenuate (often rounded in trifoliolate leaves), base usually asymmetric, narrowly attenuate, sometimes decurrent, chartaceous, (2.7-)4.7-10(-14)[7.6] cm long, (1.0-)1.4-4(-4.6)[2.8] cm broad, glabrous above, lower surface glabrous except for tufts of bearded hair in axils of secondary veins and midrib and sometimes scattered on lamina, finely glandular-punctate; venation eucamptodromous or brochidodromous, midrib flat or slightly prominent; secondaries 612 on either side of midrib, ascending, straight, or arcuate, parallel or slightly convergent; intersecondaries and tertiaries obscure. Inflorescence axillary, 3-7 cm long, a slender thyrse, lateral branches sometimes densely-flowered, glabrous; pedicel 1-1.5 mm long. Calyx patelliform to shallowly cyathiform, 0.5-1 mm long, with 5 broadly ovate or triangular, acute or obtuse lobes, 1/4-1/2 length of calyx, subglabrous or rarely sparsely ciliate, persistent in fruit. Petals 5(-6), free, imbricate, 2.5-4.5 mm long, 0.75-1.5 mm broad, lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, apex acute, subglabrous. Staminal tube urceolate, cyathiform, or shortly cylindrical; filaments completely fused or occasionally free at apex, 1.5-3.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, margin with 9-10 acute appendages alternating with anthers and 1/3-2/3 their length (when filaments are free at apex then terminated by 2 short acute appendages), nearly always glabrous rarely with few hairs in throat; anthers 910, 0.7-0.8 mm long, glabrous. Nectary a small annulus fused to base of ovary, or absent. Ovary ovoid, 3-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, glabrous; style usually short, stout and glabrous; style-head capitate-conical with 3 small pointed lobes. Capsule ellipsoid, apex truncate or emarginate, tapering to an acute or obtuse base, often drying with a short stipe, weakly verruculose and ± glabrous, 1.4-2.3 cm long, 1-1.3 cm broad, 3-valved; pericarp ca. 1 mm thick; endocarp thick-cartilaginous. Seed solitary in each valve or only 1 in each fruit, ca. 1.3 cm long, ca. 0.5 cm broad, tapering from near apex to base, partially surrounded by a thick fleshy arillode which envelops at least upper half of seed and sometimes extends further leaving only a small uncovered area on back of seed; arillode free except for attachment around apex of seed and along raphe; seed coat thin, soft. Embryo with plano-convex, collateral cotyledons, one cotyledon subdivided into small angular segments; radicle apical, extending to surface. Residual endosperm present.
