description: Shrub or scandent shrub, the branches terete, lenticellate, when young, lanate to strigose, becoming glabrous with age. Stipules narrowly triangular, membranaceous, 15.0-25.0 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, slightly strigose, persistent; petioles 6.0-8.0 mm long, ca 1.5 mm thick, densely strigose; lamina elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 6.0-13.0 cm long, 3.0-7.5 cm wide, subcoriaceous, smooth, the margins entire, the apex acute to acuminate, the base obtuse; venation eucamptodromous, the midrib plane above, prominulous beneath, strigose on both surfaces, the secondary nerves 14-16 pairs, usually opposite to subopposite, usually less than 10.0 mm from one another;intercostal pubescence very slightly villous above, lanate beneath. Inflorescences terminal and subterminal axillary panicles, sometimes reduced to racemes, to l0.0 cmlong. Flowers in groups (cincinni) of 1-3 (usually 1); peduncles, when present, 0.1-0.5 mm long, strigose, the bracts ovate, 4.04.5 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm wide, the pedicels 0.5-1.0 mm long, ca 0.5 mm thick, strigose; sepals oblong to deltoid, 4.0-6.0 mm long, 2.0-4.0 mm wide, strigose on the exposed portions, lanate on the protected areas, acute to rounded at the apex; standard 6.0-6.5 mm long, 4.5-5.0 mm wide, the pouch extending 1/3 of the length, the upper portion erect to revolute, barbate at the throat, the wings spathulate, 5.5-6.0 mm long, 2.5-3.0 mm wide, the apex rounded, densely barbate at the base, the keel petals 4.5-5.0 mm long, 2.5-2.8 mm wide, the pouch extending along most of the length, the apex revolute; stamens 8, 6-7 fertile, 1-2 staminodes, the filaments 2.5-3.0 mm long, free along ½ of the length, the anthers oblong to obovate, 0.6-1.1 mm long, ca 0.6 mm wide, one of them smaller; glands 2, 2-lobed, more or less rectangular to trapezoid, ca 0.6 mm high, 1.0 mm long, glabrous to slightly pilose; style 2.5-3.0 mm long, barbate, the stigma trilobate, approximately triangular, 0.5-0.6 mm per side; ovary subglobose, 1.0-1.5 mm in diameter, barbate-pubescent, the ovules numerous. Fruit 10.5-11.0 cm long, the valves 9.0-10.0 mm wide; exocarp thin, fleshy, velutinous-tomentose; endocarp cartilaginous. Seeds not seen.

description: Plants robust, pink-tinged below, branched, more or less pendent; rhizoids violet-purple; stems to 5 cm tall. Leaves acuminate above broad shoulders, 5-6 mm long, flexuous-spreading and tubulose when dry; margins narrowly bordered all around with hyaline cells, conspicuously ciliate-spinose toward leaf tip, entire below; cancellinae distinct, ventrally bulging distally; median cells 5-7 x 12-16 pm, smooth dorsally, bulging ventrally; gemmae in tight clusters at leaf tips. Sporophyte unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Reese, William D. 1993. Calymperaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 58: 1-102.

description: Plants pale green. Stems monomorphic, unbranched, at least 2 mm long x 1.5 mm wide; rhizoids not seen; axillary hyaline nodules not observed; transverse section of stem not examined. Leaves crispate when dry, loosely imbricate, lanceolate, acute, 1.4-1.6 mm long x 0.3 mm wide; margin serrulate, distally denticulate, weakly limbate on proximal parts of vaginant laminae of cauline leaves, limbidiuim intralaminal, limbidial cells unistratose; costa anomalous [not examined in transverse section, but according to protologue and surface examination there are internally 2 files of enlarged cells], ending 5-6 cells below apex to percurrent; dorsal lamina narrowed to insertion, not decurrent or slightly so; vaginant laminae of cauline leaves ± 1/2 leaf length, acute, unequal, minor lamina ending ± midway between costa and margin; laminal cells distinct, gut-tulate, firm-walled, smooth, irregularly quadrate to hexagonal, 9-10 pm long, marginal cells often smaller, 6 µm long, proximal juxtacostal cells of vaginant laminae ± pellucid, eguttulate, quadrate to oblong, to 45 µm long x 22 µm wide. Gametangia, sporophyte, spores, and calyptra unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Pursell, Ronald A. 2007. Fissidentaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 101

description: Plants small, glossy; rhizoids purple; stems to 1 cm tall. Leaves lanceolate above scarcely broader base, mostly 2-3 mm long, involute and incurved when dry; margins of upper lamina entire, bordered all around with elongate hyaline cells; margins of lower lamina entire to ciliate at shoulders; median leaf cells isodiametric, mostly ca. 10-12 m, smooth to bulging-papillose dorsally and ventrally; gemmae infrequent, on ventral surface at leaf tips. Sporophytes nearly immersed; seta 2-2.5 mm long; capsule 1 mm long; peristome lacking; operculum 0.75 mm long. Spores 33-38 µm, finely and bluntly papillose. Calyptra mitrate-campanulate, 1.1 mm long, papillose above.

description: Plants moderately robust; rhizoids very scanty, dark red; stems 2-8 cm tall, little branched. Leaves linear-acuminate, ending in a short, slender, coarsely toothed tip composed mostly of costa, 6-7 mm long, involute and flexuous-spreading when dry; margins of upper lamina bearing a double row of coarse multicellular teeth above, thickened, with the thickenings extending down into lower lamina as conspicuous teniola-like features, margins of lower lamina entire; cancellinae small, fragile, eroded in older leaves, not more than 1/3 length of lower lamina, longer next to margins than along costa; median leaf cells incrassate, mostly rectangular, mostly ca. 7 x 13 µm, smooth dorsally, bulging ventrally. Gemmae and sporophytes unknown.

description: Plants yellowish-green or darker, sometimes tinged below with pink or purple, mostly to 10 mm tall, in thin to dense tufts or turfs, often glossy when dry due to exposed refractive cancellinae. Leaves somewhat dimorphic, mostly 3-4.5 mm long, involute and curved when dry, ligulate to lanceolate from broader base; margins thickened, serrate; teniolae conspicuous; cancellinae distinct, often glossy when dry, their ventral distal cells notably mammillose with the mammillae pointing distally, (but mammillose cells sometimes restricted to distal edges of cancellinae); cells at midleaf mostly 5-7 x 7-10 µm, papillose dorsally, mammillose-papillose ventrally; costa mostly smooth dorsally, mammillose-papillose ventrally ; gemmiferous leaves scarcely differentiated or often very narrowly acuminate and reduced to naked costa distally, bearing often spherical clusters of gemmae all around on tip of costa. Seta 3-4.5 mm; capsule 2.5-3 mm long; operculum 0.6-0.8 mm long. Spores finely and densely papillose, 20-26 pm diam. Calyptra 3.5-4.5	mm long.

description: Plants olive-green, rhizoids reddish-brown; stems simple, to 1 cm tall. Leaves mostly ca. 3.5 mm long, curved when dry, dimorphic, vegetative leaves oblong-elliptic from broader base, gemmiferous leaves reduced to narrow wings along costa, margins of upper lamina slightly thickened, rarely unistratose, narrowly winged and coarsely serrate-spinose above, sometimes showing stereids in section, margins of lower lamina mostly entire or somewhat serrate at shoulders; teniolae lacking but shoulders bordered by up to six (mostly fewer) rows of elongate thick-walled cells; cancellinae broad above; median leaf cells in vertical rows, rounded to oblong, mostly 8-11 x 8 µm, bulging dorsally and ventrally; gemmae borne in distinct gemma receptacle on ventral surface of costa. Sporophytes unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Reese, William D. 1993. Calymperaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 58: 1-102.

description: Plants small, mostly 2-3 mm tall, pale-green, in loose or dense tufts and turfs. Leaves involute and slightly contorted when dry, oblong-lanceolate, 2-2.5 mm long, lacking evident shoulders; margins entire, uni- or bistratose above, composed of broad areas of square green cells exterior to cancellinae in leaf base; teniolae lacking or rarely vestigial; cancellinae distinct, small, more or less truncate distally; cells at midleaf 6-8 pm diameter, finely papillose dorsally, mammillose ventrally; costa papillose-roughened, especially distally; gemmiferous leaves with costa excurrent and bearing gemmae all around at apex in conspicuous pale spheres. Sporophytes unknown in the Americas.

description: Plants sordid green. Stems monomorphic, unbranched and branched, to 9 mm long x 3 mm wide; rhizoids basal, smooth, reddish; axillary hyaline nodules absent; epidermis and outer 1-2 tiers of cortical cells small, incrassate, pigmented; inner cortical cells larger, thin-walled, hyaline; central strand present. Leaves crispate when dry, loosely imbricate, as many as 15 pairs, oblong-lanceolate, acute, to 2.5 mm long x 0.4 mm wide; margin entire to irregularly serrulate, limbate on all laminae, limbidium confluent at leaf apex, frequently not reaching base of dorsal lamina, frequently spurred, limbidial cells tri- to quadris-tratose; costa percurrent to short-excurrent, bryoides type; dorsal lamina rounded proximally, not decurrent; vaginant laminae of cauline leaves ± 1/2 leaf length, acute, equal; laminal cells obscure, eguttulate, irregularly bistratose in ventral and dorsal laminae, firm-walled, mostly pluripapillose, irregularly quadrate to irregularly hexagonal, 4-5 pm long. Monoicous (gonioautoicous, rhizautoicous, infrequently cladautoicous); perigonia gemmiform, axillary or terminal on longer stems; perichaetia terminal on stems and branches. Sporophytes 1-6 per perichaetium, yellow, darkening with age; seta smooth, 2-3 mm long; theca exserted, ± erect, ± bilaterally symmetric, 0.4-0.5 mm long, stomatose, exothecial cells quadrate to oblong, vertical walls thicker than horizontal walls; peristome scariosus type; operculum conic, long-rostrate, 0.5 mm long. Spores finely papillose, 9-13 µm diam. Calyptra cucullate, smooth, 0.8 mm long.

description: Plants dark green to blackish. Stems monomorphic, unbranched to profusely branched, to 80 mm [8 cm] or more long x to 5 mm wide; rhizoids basal and axillary, smooth, reddish; axillary hyaline nodules absent; epidermis and outer 1-3 tiers of cortical cells small, incrassate, pigmented; inner cortical cells larger, thin-walled, hyaline; central strand present. Leaves ± crispate when dry, imbricate, as many as 80 pairs, lanceolate, acute, to 4.6 mm long x 0.4 1.0 mm wide; margin ± entire, limbate on all laminae, limbidium ending below leaf apex or confluent at apex, usually ending above insertion of dorsal lamina, limbidial cells 1-3-stratose; costa percurrent or nearly so, bryoides type; dorsal lamina narrowed, short-decurrent; vaginant laminae of cauline leaves 1/2-2/3 leaf length, acute, equal; laminal cells ± obscure, eguttulate, irregularly bi- or tristratose, firm-walled, plane, smooth, quadrate to irregularly hexagonal, 5-10 µm long. Monoicous (rhizautoicous); perigonia and perichaetia terminal on main stems and branches. Sporophytes 1 per perichaetium, reddish; seta smooth, to 10 mm long; theca exserted, erect, radially symmetric or inclined, bilaterally symmetric, 0.7-0.9 mm long, stomatose, exothecial cells quadrate to oblong, vertical walls thicker than horizontal walls; peristome bryoides type; operculum conic, short-rostrate, 1 mm long. Spores finely papillose, 18-22 µm diam. Calyptra not seen.

description: Plants to 8 cm high, in whitish-green, rarely blackish loose to dense tufts, variable in size and appearance. Stems erect, sometimes branched, densely foliate with imbricate leaves ("leucobryoid"). Leaves 6-8 mm long, from oblong base narrowed to an acumen of variable length, entire at margins, or with a few teeth at the extreme apex. Costa very broad, filling 4/5 of the leaf width, excurrent, narrowed at leaf base, in transverse section with lax ventral hyalocysts, a median band of chlorocysts and a band of chlorocysts alternating with leucocysts at the dorsal side, ridged at back in the upper part of the leaf. Alar cells lacking. Basal laminal cells hyaline, rectangular, 16-32 × 38-96 µm, at margins in 5-15 rows narrower, elongate, forming a distinct border. Upper laminal cells oval, 5-10 × 10-19 µm incrassate. Lamina vanishing below midleaf. Seta 6-8(-15) mm long, brownish, sinuose. Capsule 1.5 mm long, erect, symmetric, ovoid, brownish, furrowed when empty. Operculum long-rostrate, 1 mm long. Calyptra ciliate at base.

description: Plants pale green. Stems dimorphic, delicate, unbranched or branched from older parts; infertile ones to 5 mm long x to 2 mm wide, fertile ones shorter; rhizoids basal, smooth, reddish; axillary hyaline nodules present; epidermis and outer tier of cortical cells small, incrassate, pigmented; inner cortical cells larger, thin-walled, hyaline; central strand absent. Leaves ± críspate when dry, distant to imbricate, as many as 18 pairs, often more numerous on infertile stems, lanceolate, acute to ± obtuse, to 1.6 mm long x 0.1-0.3 mm wide, perichaetial leaves longest; margin ± entire to somewhat serrulate, particularly distally, elimbate or irregularly limbate, limbidium ending below leaf apex, sometimes weak on dorsal and ventral laminae, often present only on vaginant laminae, limbidial cells uni-or bistratose; costa ending 2-5 cells below apex to percurrent, bryoides type; dorsal lamina narrowing proximally, ending slightly above or at insertion; vaginant laminae of cauline leaves 1/2-2/3 leaf length, acute, ± equal, minor lamina ending on or near margin; laminal cells distinct, eguttulate, unistratose, smooth, plane or slightly bulging, most irregularly hexagonal, somewhat longer than wide, 9-18 µm 6-11 µm. Monoicous (rhizautoicous); perigonial stems gemmiform at base of fertile and infertile stems; perichaetia terminal. Sporophytes 1-2 per perichaetium, yellow, darkening with age; seta smooth, 2.5-12 mm long; theca exserted, ± erect, radially symmetric to inclined, bilaterally symmetric, 0.2-0.8 mm long, stomatose, exothecial cells quadrate to oblong, vertical walls thicker than horizontal walls, collenchymatous; peristome bryoides type; operculum conic, short-rostrate, 0.2 mm long. Spores finely papillose, 14-27 µm diam. Calyptra not seen.

description: Plants light to sordid dark green. Stems monomorphic, 5-17 mm long x to 3 mm wide; unbranched and branched; rhizoids basal and axillary, smooth, reddish; axillary hyaline nodules present; epidermis and outer tier of cortical cells small, incrassate, pigmented; inner cortical cells larger, thin-walled, hyaline; central strand present. Leaves crispate when dry, imbricate, as many as 27 pairs, lanceolate, acute to short-acuminate, to 3.1 mm long x 0.2-0.5 mm wide; margin sharply dentate, especially on vaginant laminae and at leaf apex, but sometimes dentations nearly obsolete, limbate on all laminae, limbidium confluent at apex or ending 2-3 cells below apex, limbidial cells bi- to tristratose; costa percurrent, bryoides type; dorsal lamina narrowed, ending at or slightly above insertion; vaginant laminae of cauline leaves ± 1/2 leaf length, acute, ± equal; laminal cells ± obscure, eguttulate, unis-tratose, firm-walled, smooth, bulging, irregularly quadrate to irregularly hexagonal, 5-11 µm long, ± twice as deep as wide. Monoicous (rhizautoicous); perigonia and perichaetia terminal on stems of ± equal length. Sporophytes 1 per perichaetium, deep orange to reddish; seta smooth, 4-6 mm long; theca exserted, 0.5-1.2 mm long, erect or slightly inclined, ± bilaterally symmetric, stomatose, exothecial cells quadrate to oblong, vertical walls thicker than horizontal walls; peristome bryoides type; operculum conic, short-rostrate, to 0.5 mm long. Spores and calyptra not seen.

description: Plants pale-green; rhizoids reddish-brown; stems to ca. 9 mm tall. Leaves involute-subulate, mostly 4.5-5 mm long, strongly inrolled and contorted when dry; margins of upper lamina entire, mostly strongly infolded from apex to just above shoulders, unistratose above, thickened below, sometimes showing stereids in section, margins of lower lamina sharply serrate-serrulate; teniolae usually distinct, of elongate cells with often thickened, pitted and irregular walls; cancellinae irregularly rounded or truncate distally; median leaf cells very thick-walled, rounded to elliptiç mostly 10-12 µm, smooth dorsally, bulging to mammillose ventrally; gemmae infrequent, on ventral tips of leaves. Seta 3 mm long; capsule 1.5 mm long; operculum 1 mm long. Spores smooth, 22 pm. Calyptra 4 mm long.

description: Plants dull green. Stems monomorphic, unbranched and branched, to 8.5 mm long x 2 mm wide; rhizoids basal, smooth, reddish; axillary hyaline nodules absent; epidermis and outer 1-2 tiers of cortical cells small, incrassate, pigmented; inner cortical cells hyaline, thin-walled, hyaline; central strand present. Leaves crispate when dry, loosely imbricate, as many as 18 pairs, lanceolate, gradually narrowed to rounded apices, to 1.6 mm long x 0.2-0.3 mm wide; margin serrulate, limbate in lower 1/2-2/3 of vaginant laminae of perichaetial and most distal leaves and sometimes in all leaves of a stem, often spurred, intralaminal, bordered by 1-3 rows of papillose, chlorophyllose cells, limbidial cells unistratose; costa ending 2-6 cells below leaf apex, bryoides type; dorsal lamina truncate or rounded at insertion, not decurrent; vaginant laminae of cauline leaves ± 1/2-2/3 leaf length, acute, ± equal; laminal cells obscure, eguttulate, unistratose, firm-walled, pluripapillose, rounded-hexagonal, 4-7 µm long, in transverse section ± twice as deep as wide. Monoicous (gonioautoicous and rhizautoicous); perigonia gemmiform, axillary or terminal on short stems; perichaetia terminal on stems and branches. Sporophytes 1-2 per perichaetium, yellow, darkening with age; seta smooth, to 4 mm long; theca exserted, erect, radially symmetric or inclined, ± bilaterally symmetric, to 0.8 mm long, stomatose, exothecial cells quadrate to oblong, vertical walls thicker than horizontal walls, collenchymatous; peristome scariosus type; operculum conic, long-rostrate, 0.5 mm long. Spores finely papillose, 9-13 µm diam. Calyptra cucullate, smooth, 0.7 mm long.

description: Plants yellowish green to bright-green, in loose, somewhat rigid, dull mats. Stems complanate-foliate, to 3.5 cm long, 1.0-2.5 mm wide, simple or irregularly and sparingly branched; axillary hairs with a single short brown basal cell and 3 short-rectangular hyaline apical cells. Leaves lax, close, loosely erect, ± contorted when dry, 1.9-2.5 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm wide, lanceolate, gradually long-acuminate; margins often recurved at base, entire; costa extending 1/2 length of leaf; cells smooth, median cells 89-118 µm long, 9-12 µm wide; alar cells subquadrate to oblong, 25-50 µm long, 14-28 µm wide. Autoicous. Setae ca. 1 mm long, orange; capsules ca. 1.5 mm long, broadly cylindric; opercula conic, short-rostrate, ca. 0.8 mm long. Spores 11-14 µm, finely roughened.

description: Plants gregarious, very small; rhizoids red-purple; stems to 5 mm tall. Leaves linear or slightly tapering above somewhat broader shoulders, rounded to nearly spatulate at tips, 2-2.3 mm long, folded or channeled and variously contorted when dry, margins of upper lamina entire, bordered all around with hyaline cells, margins of lower lamina entire or serrate; cancellinae often eroded in older leaves, broadly rounded to acute distally; median leaf cells rounded-quadrate to vertically elongate, ca. 10-14 x 12-17 µm, bulging-pluripapillose dorsally and ventrally; gemmae clavate, slender, small, ventral on leaf tips. Seta 2.3 mm long; capsule 1 mm long; peristome of low, imperfect, segmented teeth, ca. 96 µm tall; operculum ca. 1 mm long. Spores granular, 12-14 µm. Calyptra 1 mm long, papillose on rostrum.

description: Plants yellowish, in thin, loose, glossy mats. Stems complanate-foliate, to 2 cm long, 2-3 mm wide, simple or irregularly and sparingly branched. Leaves lax, 1.5-1.8 mm long, 0.3-0.4 mm wide, lanceolate, flat, gradually acuminate; margins plane, entire, indistinctly bordered by elongate cells; costa extending ca. 1/2 the leaf length; median cells 94-141 µm long, 5-9 µm wide; alar cells quadrate, subquadrate or oblate, 14-24 µm long, 9-14 µm wide. Autoicous. Setae reddish brown, 1.3 cm long; capsules erect, light-to yellow-brown, ca. 2 mm long, cylindric, not contracted below mouth when dry; opercula conic-rostrate, ca. 0.5 mm long. Spores 11-15 µm in diam.

description: Plants tiny, gregarious; rhizoidspurple-brown, inconspicuous; stems 3-4(-5) mm tall. Leaves crowded, rarely dimorphiç short broad gemmif- erous leaves sometimes present in comae, vegetative leaves oblong-lingulate to broadly lanceolate, tubulose and secund when dry, 2-3.5 mm long; margins entire where bordered, serrulate by papillae and cell angles where unbordered, narrowly bordered in lower 1/2-3/4 with hyaline cells, or border irregular and restricted to shoulder region or more or less lacking (the hyaline cells sometimes intramarginal and teniola-like); cancellinae ending distally in acute angles; median leaf cells thick-walled, isodiametric to short-rectangular, mostly 6-8 x 9-10 µm, sharply unipapillose dorsally, strongly mammillose to mammillose-papillose ventrally, lumina often triangular as seen in section; gemmae unknown. Monoicous; sporophytes minute, equalled or slightly exceeded by perichaetial leaves; setae 1-3 per perichaetium, 1.5-2.2 mm long; capsule 1-1.3 mm long; peristome teeth brown, delicate, transversely barred, ca. 85 pm tall; operculum ca. 0.75 mm long. Spores smooth, 16.8-21.6 pm. Calyptra cucullate, deeply lobed at base, sharply papillose above, ca. 1.8 mm long. Illustration. Reese (1981, figs. 1-7).
bibliographicCitation: Reese, William D. 1993. Calymperaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 58: 1-102.

description: Plants small to medium, pale-green, tinged with pink below; rhizoids dark-purple; stems to 7 cm tall but mostly much less, mostly simple. Leaves ligulate to lanceolate, 3-6 mm long, variously curved and contorted when diy; margins ciliate below, cilia sometimes extending nearly to leaf tip or reduced or lacking in some leaves; cancellinae distinct; median cells mostly 6-7 x 9-12 µm, dorsally smooth, ventrally bulging; gemmae ventral on leaf tips. Seta red, 5 mm long; capsule 1 mm long; peristome of low, blunt, imperfect teeth; operculum rostrate. Spores not seen. Calyptra 2 mm long.

description: Plants dull-green, solitary, gregarious, or tufted; rhizoids scanty, reddish-brown; stems to 1 cm tall but mostly shorter. Leaves dimorphic? vegetative acuminate to linear or broadly linear above scarcely broader base, acute, 2-3.5 mm long, crispate-contorted when dry, erect-spreading to squarrose when moist, often folded-falcate on microscope slide; margins of upper lamina undulate, bordered all around, toothed in upper portion, margins of lower lamina entire; can-cellinae acute to broadly acute distally; median leaf cells obscure, isodiametric? mostly 6-10 x 7-10 µm, pluripapillose dorsally and ventrally; gemmiferous leaves oblong-acute to nearly deltoid, gemmae filamentous, borne along costa at midleaf. (Description of sporophyte based on Buck 18344, 18653, NY.) Seta reddish-brown, 2-2.5 mm long; capsule ovoid-cylindric, brown, 1-1.5 mm long, set somewhat obliquely on the seta, stomata not seen; peristome teeth imperfect, with yellow-orange tips, smooth, segmented, 52-65 µm tall, bases fused into a pale membrane; operculum 1 mm long. Spores extremely variable in size and shape, 21-47 µm diam., spherical to ellipsoidal, dark-green, finely granular, some small, colorless, empty, and collapsed. Calyptra 2.5 mm long, divided into several narrow segments from base to rostrum.

description: Plants yellowish-green, slender, to 8 cm tall, freely forked; rhizoidsinconspicuous, yellowish-brown. Leai’es fragile, loosely flexuous-spreading, to 15-20 mm long, long linear-acuminate from scarcely broader base, reduced to mere wings along costa distally, apex often merely the excurrent, spinose-toothed costa; margins sharply serrate at shoulders, irregularly toothed above, mostly unistratose but slightly thickened here and there, especially distally; cancellinae broad, persistent, extending to or beyond leaf shoulders; median leaf cells thick-walled, square to rectangular, 8.5-13 x 7-8.5 µm, smooth, bulging or bluntly papillose dorsally, strongly bulging ventrally. Gemmae and sporophytes unknown.

description: Thallus 3-4 mm wide, light or yellowish green with narrow, purplish margin; apical adventitious branches frequent, often short. Epidermis finely granulose; epidermal cells 28-35 × 21-24 µm, with medium-sized or large, often nodulose trigones. Epidermal pores 15-20 per mm2, raised above epidermis, usually 28-35 Jim diam., bounded by (2-) 3(-4) concentric rings of (7-)8(-9) cells with strongly thickened radial walls. Ventral scales purplish or dark red, with border of 1-2 rows of light-red or hyaline, sinuose cells; appendages usually 2-3, narrowly triangular, apex acuminate, with row of 3-4 cells apically, hyaline, contrasting with the dark scale body, widest basally, 10-14 cells wide, not constricted or plicate, length/width ratio 4-5:1, margins not differentiated, sometimes with some teeth and papillae. Male receptacle dorsal or at base of apical adventitious branch, usually reniform, with 20-30 antheridia. Scales of male and female receptacles hyaline or purplish, or partly tinged with purple, acuminate, with row of 3-5 cells apically, margins with scattered papillae. Archegoniophores dorsal or at base of apical adventitious branch, stalk 2.3-4 mm long, with thickened, dark-red epidermal cells. Involucres 2-3, light brown or purplish. Spores 94-118 µm diam., light or dark brown, both faces areolate, areoles and ridges tuberculate. Elaters with 2-3 helical bands. Gametophytic chromosome number n = 9.

description: Thalli in gregarious patches; lobes 1-3 times forked, 5-8 mm long, 1-2.5 mm wide, obtuse apically; dorsal side light green or brownish green, margins thin, membranaceous; ventral face brown, sometimes black. Median groove narrow apically, vanishing below. Epidermal cells convex. Idioblasts in epidermis and dorsal and ventral tissue, with glossy, dense, orange-red body, filling nearly the cell. Ventral scales imbricate, entire, lunate, extending beyond lobe margins, orange-red, purplish or violet, cells 60-95 × 32-48 µm, marginal cells partly hyaline, partly orange-red. Cross section of lobes 2-A (-5) times as wide as high; dorsal edge convex laterally, acute, with short, thin wings ending in single cell; flanks ascending vertically or obliquely, abruptly narrowed into the wings; ventral edge convex. Monoecious. Antheridial necks protruding, colorless. Archegonial necks protruding, red or nearly black. Sporangia large, numerous, bulging. Spores tetrahedral, 75-120 µm diam., yellow-brown or orange-brown; wing 4-5 µm wide, 6-7 µm at level of pores, light yellow, translucent, papillose; distal face vermiculate rather than areolate, with 8-15 ill-defined areoles across diam., with inconspicuous ridges and numerous, rounded, contracted or branched tubercles or, sometimes, some slender tubercles only near equator; proximal face with similar ornamentation, but with smaller tubercles, triradiate scar narrow, conspicuous. Gametophytic chromosome number n = 8.

description: Thalli forming rosettes or gregarious patches; lobes 2-4 times forked, 2-5.5 mm long, 0.7-1.5 mm wide; dorsal side light green, sometimes glaucous; margins, flanks, ventral side and scales dark violet to nearly black; flanks inflexed when dry. Median groove deep apically, wider and shallower below, vanishing toward base. Epidermal cells disintegrating except in groove, spherical. Cilia on flanks and margins, from top to bottom of lobes, numerous especially apically, intercrossing along midline, white, stiff, erect or slightly arched, acute, smooth, 400-1000 |Lim long, 30-40 µm wide basally, walls with helical thickenings, or flexuose, smooth, thin-walled setae, 500-900 µm long, 40-60 µm wide basally. Ventral scales small. Cross section of lobes as high as wide apically, to 1.5-2.5 times as wide as high below; dorsal edge rounded laterally; flanks arched; ventral edge convex. Monoecious. Antheridial necks protruding (50-100 µm), white or violet. Archegonial necks hardly protruding, usually violet. Sporangia often indicated by a red or dark violaceous spot on dorsal side of lobes, with 1-12 cilia shorter than those of flanks, and 1-2 setae similar to those of flanks. Spores 60-120 µm diam., dark brown; wing narrow (2 µm), irregular, vanishing partly, granulose distal face with 8-14 areoles across diam., with thick, granulose ridges and conspicuous tubercles; proximal face with similar ornamentation, but with lower ridges, triradiate scar distinct. Gametophytic chromosome number n = 8 or 16.

description: Thalli in gregarious patches; lobes 1.5-5 mm long, 0.7-1 mm wide, 1-3 times forked, obtuse or slightly emarginate apically, margins obtuse; dorsal side blue-green, with dark violet margins when moist; flanks inflexed when dry, dark red-violet, with wide, purplish strip inside; ventral edge colorless. Median groove shallow apically, wider and flattened below. Epidermis disintegrating except in groove, cells rounded, mamilliform. Ventral scales short, irregular in shape, 2-3 cell layers in height, bordered by hyaline or violet projecting cells, or by hyaline, papilliform cells. Papillae numerous, on lobe margins and on upper part of flanks, hyaline, sometimes violaceous, smooth or granulose, rounded or obtuse apically, 25-130 µm long, 25-45 µm wide basally, erect or slightly arched, together with nearly acute, hyaline, strongly granulose papillae. Cross section of lobes 12 times as wide as high, without wings; dorsal side rounded laterally; flanks ascending, rounded apically; ventral edge convex or nearly flat. Dioecious. Antheridial necks protruding, violet. Spores subspherical, 85-115 µm diam., black or dark brown, wingless, crenulate on margin; distal face with 12-17 areoles across diam., with thick, black ridges and large tubercles; proximal face with similar ornamentation but usually without tubercles, triradiate scar weak.

description: Plants pale to olive green, often tinged brown. Steins monomorphic, unbranched and branched near distal ends, to 6 mm long x 2 mm wide; rhizoids basal and axillary, smooth, reddish; axillary hyaline nodules absent; epidermis and outer tier of cortical cells small, incrassate, pigmented; inner cortical cells larger, thin-walled, hyaline; central strand present. Leaves ± inrolled parallel to costa when dry, distant to loosely imbricate, as many as 11 pairs, lanceolate to ± elliptic, acute to cuspidate, to 2 mm long x 0.30.5 mm wide; margin crenulate-serrulate, often weakly and inconspicuously limbate and ± entire in proximal parts of vaginant laminae, limbidial cells unistratose; costa ending 2-3 cells below apex, bryoides type; dorsal lamina narrowed, usually rounded at insertion, not decurrent; vaginant laminae of cauline leaves 2/5-1/2 leaf length, acute, unequal, minor lamina usually ending 1/2 the distance between costa and margin, infrequently rounded and attached along costa; laminal cells distinct, guttulate, unistratose, firm-walled, smooth, irregularly quadrate to elongate-hexagonal, 14-20 µm long, marginal cells somewhat smaller, 11-15 µm long, often somewhat wider. Monoicous (gonioautoicous and cladautoicous); perigonial branches often somewhat elongate and emergent to extending well above enveloping vaginant laminae; perichaetia terminal on stems and branches. Sporophytes 1 per perichaetium, yellow, darkening with age; seta smooth, 0.9-1.9 mm long; theca exserted, cylindric, inclined to pendent, radially symmetric, 0.5-0.7 mm long, stomatose, exothecial cells mostly oblong, collenchymatous; peristome anomalous, teeth erect whether wet or dry, divided nearly their entire length into 2 slightly unequal prongs, ± horizontally thickened proximally, spirally thickened distally, ventral trabeculae wider than lamellar thickenings, lacking fimbriae; operculum conic, long-rostrate, 0.30 mm long. Spores smooth, 11-18 µm diam. Calyptra cu-cullate, smooth, 0.35 mm long.

description: Thallus flat when moist, xeromorphic, becoming strongly inrolled when dry, 1.5-5(-6) mm broad, green above, dark purple beneath and on margins; branching mostly by ventral intercalary branches. Epidermal cells with somewhat thickened walls. Epidermal pores of 3-4 concentric rings of 7-9 rows of cells. Air chambers irregular, spongy, in several layers. Ventral scales wine-red or purple, with scattered oil cells and marginal papillae, with 1-2 narrowly lanceolate appendages, not constricted at base, margin entire, apex subulate. Antheridia in a small cluster without scales on short stipitate-based ventral branches. Archegoniophore borne in apical notch on small obcordate stipitate-based ventral branch, stalk slender, 10-25 mm long, with a few whitish hanging scales at apex; carpocephalum hemispherical, with 2-4 descending lobes, covered with low tubercles to almost smooth. Involucre an entire flap. Pseudoperianth lobes (8-) 10-12, hyaline, remaining united at apex. Spores brown or red-brown (light brown according to Whittemore, in lit.), 105-135 µm diam., sculpturing similar on distal and proximal faces, distally with 4-5 large areoles across face, areoles ± smooth within, muri flat in section, alveolate, wing strongly differentiated, almost smooth. Elaters with 2 helical bands. Gametophytic chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Bischler, Hélène, et al. 2005. Marchantiidae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 97: 1--262.

description: Thallus thin and broad, flat, hygromorphic, not inrolling when dry, 8-15 mm broad, green above, purple beneath and on undulate margins; branching fanlike, by repeated apical adventitious branches and terminal branches. Epidermal cells with thin walls and small trigones. Epidermal pores of 3-4 concentric rings of 5-7 rows of cells. Air chambers irregular, spongy, in several layers. Ventral scales purple, with scattered oil cells and marginal papillae, with l(-2) linear appendages, not constricted at base, margin often with 1-2 teeth, apex acuminate. Dioecious. Antheridia in distinct elongate-elliptic clusters without scales along middle of main thallus and main branches, often several clusters in a line. Archegoniophore borne at apex of main thallus but lobes at each side of stalk continuing fanlike growth, stalk short, stout, curved, 5-10 mm long, naked but with a few whitish scales at apex, in type specimen deeply ribbed and with vestigial air chambers in wings; carpocephalum hemispherical, unlobed, with low tubercles, bearing up to 4 pseudoperianths. Involucre not seen. Pseudoperianth lobes 12-14, hyaline or brownish, remaining united at apex. Spores (only 4 seen) black-brown, 100-120 µm diam., sculpturing dissimilar on distal and proximal faces, distally with smooth narrow ridges forming incomplete areoles ca. 10 µm diam., areoles and muri smooth, proximal facets with scattered large pores, wing weakly differentiated, sculptured. Elaters with 2 helical bands. Gametophytic chromosome number unknown.

description: Thallus flat when moist, 1.5-5 (-6) mm broad, xeromorphic, becoming inrolled when dry, green but purplish beneath and on margins; branching mostly by ventral intercalary branches, sometimes by apical adventitious branches. Epidermal cells with somewhat thickened walls. Epidermal pores of 2-3 concentric rings of 5-7 rows of cells. Air chambers irregular, spongy, in several layers. Ventral scales purplish, with scattered oil cells and marginal papillae, with l(-2) narrowly lanceolate appendages, narrow but not constricted at base, margin entire, apex subulate. Antheridia in an irregular cluster without scales on short ventral branch. Archegoniophore borne in apical notch on small ventral branch, stalk slender, 15-20 mm long, with scattered scales and beard of longer scales at apex; carpocephalum hemispherical, with 4 descending lobes with low tubercles. Involucre an entire flap. Pseudoperianth lobes 10-12, hyaline or purplish, remaining united at apex. Spores brown or purplish brown, 100-115 µm diam., sculpturing similar on distal and proximal faces, areoles absent, distally with 25-30 minute alveolae across face, wing moderately differentiated, sculptured. Elaters with 2 helical bands. Gametophytic chromosome number unknown.

description: Thallus 4.4-5 mm wide, yellowish green, often partly tinged with purple, with narrow, purplish margins; apical adventitious branches frequent, often long. Epidermis smooth; epidermal cells 33-35 × (21-)24-28 µm, with medium-sized or large, sometimes nodulose trigones. Epidermal pores 8-20 per mm2, raised above epidermis, 14-24 µm diam., bounded by 2-3(-4) concentric rings of 6-8(-10) cells, radial walls strongly thickened. Scales purplish or orange, with border of 1-2 rows of light-red, sinuose cells; appendages (1-)2-3, narrowly triangular, apex acuminate and acute, with row of 1-2 cells apically, light red or purplish, rarely hyaline, widest basally, 12-15 cells wide, not constricted or plicate, length/width ratio 3-4:1; margins often with some teeth, without papillae. Male receptacle usually at base of apical adventitious branches, rounded or reniform, with 20-30 antheridia. Scales of male and female receptacles hyaline, or partly tinged with purple, acute, with row of 2-3 cells apically, margins often toothed and with scattered papillae. Archegoniophores dorsal, stalk 0.2-0.4 mm long, with thickened, dark-purplish epidermal cells. Involucres 2-3, light brown or purplish. Spores 82-100 µm diam., light or dark brown, with complete or incomplete areoles on both faces, ridges ± densely tuberculate. Elaters with 2-4, sometimes interrupted helical bands. Gametophytic chromosome number unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Bischler, Hélène, et al. 2005. Marchantiidae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 97: 1--262.

description: Thalli in gregarious patches, not forming rosettes; lobes 2-3 times forked, 3-5 mm long, 0.5-1.4 mm wide, rounded or obtuse apically, margins acute; dorsal side bluish green; flanks black-violet, inflexed; ventral side light grayish green. Median groove shallow or absent. Epidermal cells rounded or pyriform, disintegrating except in groove. Papillae sometimes present on margins and near lobe apex. Ventral scales small, black-violet, of few cells, crenulate by violet projecting marginal cells, and with papilliform cells 60-65 µm long, violet or violaceous basally, becoming hyaline toward apex. Cross section of lobes 0.40.7 mm high, as wide as high in apical part of lobe to twice as wide as high beyond; dorsal edge rounded laterally; flanks ascending vertically; ventral edge convex. Monoecious. Spores tetrahedral, 70-107 µm diam., dark brown or nearly black, wingless, crenulate on margin; distal face with (16-)20-25 areoles across diam., each of 3-6 µm diam., with thick ridges; proximal face with similar ornamentation, triradiate scar weak.

description: Gametófito mediano, verde-amarelado, apresentando ou não coloração azulada na quando seco (principalmente na região apical), 0,5-1,1mm larg. Ramos adventícios ventrais raros. Talo piano a subplano, dicotomicamente ramificado, dicotomias irregulares, de dois tipos: ligeiramente atenuado e ascendente (ramo gemíparo), e não atenuado com ápice truncado, com papilas mucilaginíferas. Em seção transversal lâmina uniestratificada, (8—) 11—18(—22) células larg. da costa a margem, células pequenas a medianas, planas, hialinas, paredes ligeiramente espessadas, trigônios pequenos, cutícula lisa, 22-42(-50) × 20-30 µm; costa plana a fracamente arqueada para ambos os lados, 2 fileiras de células epidérmicas em ambas as superfícies, dorsal e ventral; células medulares distintas das epidérmicas, medula com 6—12(—15) células, em 2-3(-4) camadas, células de parede ligeiramente espessada. Talo esparsamente hirsuto, rizóides pequenos a longos, eretos, ramificados ou não, na margem, superficie ventral da costa, esparsos na superfície ventral da lamina, na margem esparsos (500µm=5-12 rizóides), 1 rizóide por célula, 34-190 µm. Gemas marginais numerosas, concentradas nos ápices dos talos atenuados, discóides a elípticas, côncavas, apresentando ou não coloração azulada, rizóides rudimentares ou ausentes (5-7 células larg.). Dióico. Ramo masculino pequeno, globoso a subgloboso, rizóides ausentes ou ocasionais, ca. 4 anterídios, 200-330 µm. Invólucro feminino cordado, com entalhe apical, hirsuto, rizóides eretos, na margem e ocasionalmente na superfície externa, 150-250 µm. Caliptra membranosa, obpiriforme, hirsuta, rizóides eretos, dispostos por toda a superfície externa, 0,8-1,0mm compr., seção transversal 3-4 camadas de células. Seta em seção transversal ca. 19 células, 14 corticais, 5 medulares, 4 diâm., células de paredes delgadas, sem trigônios, regularmente arranjadas. (Segundo Kuwahara, 1986): Cápsula globosa, valvas com espessamentos nodulosos pequenos na parede externa (Tipo-3 e 4), ocasionalmente com expansão tangencial, e espessamentos semianulares esparsos na parede interna (Tipo-3 e 4), sem expansão tangencial, 420-620 µm. Elatérios medianos, 190-400 µm. Esporos pequenos, castanhos, granulosos, 19-24 µm.

description: Thallus 1.5-3.5 mm wide, light green, margins crisped, purplish. Epidermal cells thin-walled, with distinct trigones. Epidermal pores 40-80 µm diam., with ring of 4-6 cells, without hyaline inner ring, radial walls thin. Air chambers in 1-2 layers, high and narrow. Ventral scales purplish, lanceolate, acute apically, ending usually in row of 2 cells, without papillae and oil cells, reaching or projecting beyond thallus margins. Dioecious? Antheridia in irregular, large groups, scales absent. Archegonia in cushions, bounded by a few, minute purplish or partly hyaline scales. Receptacle of archegoniophore 2-lobed, with purplish hyaline scales. Spores 42-54 µm diam., with 5-6 rounded protuberances across diam. Elaters with 2-3 helical bands.
bibliographicCitation: Bischler, Hélène, et al. 2005. Marchantiidae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 97: 1--262.

description: Gametófito mediano, verde-amarelado quando seco, 1,0-1,5 mm larg., pendente. Ramos adventícios ventrais raros. Talo fortemente convexo, canaliculado, dicotomicamente ramificado, dicotomias irregulares, ápice obtuso, cuculado. Em seção transversal lâmina uniestratificada, 10-23 células larg. da costa a margem, células medianas, planas, hialinas, paredes ligeiramente espessadas, trigônios pequenos, cutícula lisa, 32-57 × 21-33 µm, na margem maiores; costa com 2 fileiras de células epidérmicas em ambas as superfícies, dorsal e ventral, ocasionalmente 3 fileiras na superfície ventral; células epidérmicas ligeiramente distintas das medulares; medula 10-19 células, em 3-4 camadas, células de parede delgada a ligeiramente espessada. Talo esparsamente hirsuto, rizóides curtos a medianos, eretos a flexuosos, dispostos na margem, ausentes na superfície ventral da costa e da lâmina, na margem esparsos a uniformes (500 µm= 12-20 rizóides), 1 rizóide por célula, raramente 2, 30-90(-180) µm. Gemas desconhecidas. Dióico. Ramo masculino subgloboso, sem rizóides, 600-550 µm. Invólucro feminino robusto, largo, conchiforme, alado, com pequeno entalhe apical, hirsuto, rizóides eretos, dispostos na margem, 500-1000 µm. Caliptra membranosa, obpiriforme, hirsuta, paredes com grandes apêndices laminares, apêndices hirsutos na margem (ca. 80 células), até 2,5 mm compr., seção transversal (2-)3-4 camadas de células. Seta pequena, 0,2-0,5(-l,0) mm compr., seção transversal 15-18 células, 11-13 corticais, 4-5 medulares, 4-5 diam., paredes delgadas, sem trigônios, regularmente arranjadas. Cápsula subglobosa, valvas com espessamentos radiais na forma de cogumelos na parede externa do Tipo-3 (únicos para o gênero), e espessamentos nodulosos inconspícuos na parede interna (Tipo-1), 510-700 µm. Elatóforo bem desenvolvido nos ápices das valvas. Elatérios castanho-avermelhados. Esporos pequenos a medianos, granulosos, 21-50 µm diam.

description: Thalli in gregarious patches; lobes 3-4 times forked, 5-10 mm long, 0.9-1 mm wide apically and rounded, progressively narrowed and 0.7 mm wide basally; dorsal side pale green, grayish or whitish when dry, bright green when moist, with narrow, hyaline or light brown margins; flanks violaceous or violet; ventral side brown or violaceous. Median groove deep, vanishing toward base of lobes. Epidermal cells disintegrating. Scales hyaline or violaceous-brown, not extending beyond lobe margins. Cross section of lobes 1-3 times as wide as high; dorsal edge laterally acute, with short wings; flanks obliquely ascending or erect; ventral edge convex; dorsal tissue in 2-4 layers. Monoecious. Spores subtetrahedral, 96-120(-132) µm diam., red-brown to violet-brown, wingless but sometimes with an incomplete, light brown, narrow, granulose strip at equator; distal face with 6-8(-9-10) complete areoles across diam., with thick ridges and conspicuous tubercles; proximal face with similar areoles and ridges, triradiate scar weak. Gametophytic chromosome number n = 8.

description: Plant flowering over 7 dm high; stem unknown. Leaves to 42 cm long; sheaths suborbicular or reniform, 3 cm long, stramineous; blades narrowly triangular, coriaceous but scarcely pungent, 35 mm wide, very obscurely punctulate-lepidote throughout, very narrowly cartilaginous-margined, laxly serrulate toward base. Scape erect, 1 cm in diameter at base, the scales small, white, linear or dendritic-lacerate; scape-bracts erect, subfoliaceous but entire, much exceeding the internodes but the upper ones not covering the scape. Inflorescence pyramidal, very laxly bipinnate, 4 dm long, minutely tomentose-lepidote especially on the bracts, verruculose; primary bracts very narrowly triangular, to 6 cm long, exceeding the sterile bases of the branches; branches spreading, 13 cm long, laxly many-flowered. Floral bracts linear, 4 mm long; pedicels spreading, slender, 7 mm long; only immature flowers known. Sepals suborbicular, 3.5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Lyman B. & Downs, Robert J. 1974. Pitcairnioideae (Bromeliaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 14 (1): 1-658.

description: Plant stemless, flowering 4 dm high. Leaves densely rosulate, 35-45 cm long; sheaths distinct, ovate, 15 cm long, violet on the inside toward the apex, brown-punctulate-lepidote; blades ligulate, attenuate, 4-5 cm wide, often recurving near the apex, green or tinged with purple, inconspicuously punctulate-lepidote. Scape erect, stout, much shorter than the leaves; scape-bracts densely imbricate, foliaceous with elongate blades, the upper ones often red, making a gradual transition into the primary bracts. Inflorescence equaling or shorter than the leaves, compound with simple branches, substrobilate, 15-20 cm long, 4-7 cm in diameter; primary bracts erect, broadly ovate with elongate, narrowly triangular, red blades, much exceeding all the axillary spikes, subglabrous; spikes subsessile, elliptic, 3-4-flowered, 6 cm long, strongly complanate. Floral bracts elliptic, acute, 35-40 mm long, exceeding the sepals, carinate, subchartaceous, slightly nerved, glabrous; flowers erect, short-pedicellate. Sepals sublanceolate, obtuse, submembranaceous, slightly nerved, glabrous, equally subfree; petals linear, 6 cm long, tubular-erect, violet; stamens and pistil exserted. Capsule stout, subellipsoid, abruptly acute, 4 cm long.

description: Plants epipetric or terrestrial; fronds erect to arcuate, determinate; rhizome long-creeping, dorsiventral, with ventral root insertion, scaly, the scales 3-4 cm x 0.4-0.6 mm, lanceolate, the apex long-attenuate, clathrate, castaneous, ciliate, the cilia simple, present on scale margins and apex (apical cilia sometimes furcate); petiole 1-2 cm x 0.2-0.3 mm, dark brown, terete, sparsely pubescent, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, spreading, simple or 1-furcate, 2- to 3-celled, whitish to reddish; lamina 7-10 cm long, linear-lanceolate, chartaceous, deeply pinnatisect, 15-25 pairs of segments, abruptly reduced at the base with 4-6 basal segments shorter than the median ones, the lowermost auriculiform not decurrent onto petiole base, broadest in the middle, not showing periodic constrictions, apex abruptly reduced, pinnatifid, not ending in a subconform segment; rachis straight, with dark sclerenchyma visible on both sides, sparsely pubescent to glabrous abaxially, the hairs 0.1 mm long, appressed, simple or 1-furcate, 2- to 3-celled, whitish to dark brown, sparsely pubescent adaxially, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, spreading, simple, 1- to 2-celled, castaneous to reddish; segments 0.5-0.7 x 0.2-0.3 cm, plane, set 80-90° to rachis, widened and symmetric at the base, short-decurrent on both sides, sometimes slightly cuneate acroscopically, the base attached parallel on the rachis (i.e., both sides inserted along the same radius), not lobulate or, if slightly lobulate, not overlapping the base of the next segment, the apex obtuse, the margin entire, recurved, abaxial lamina surface sparsely pubescent, the hairs simple, reddish, adaxial lamina surface glabrous; sinuses narrower or about twice as broad as the segments; venation pinnate, with 5-7 pairs of veins per segment; costae with blackish sclerenchyma obscured by laminar tissue on both sides, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, the hairs similar to those of the rachis abaxially; veins simple, with blackish sclerenchyma restricted to base and obscured by laminar tissue, ending in hydathodes that lack calcareous deposits; sori medial, rounded, protruding beyond the margin, up to 6 pairs per segment, superficial; sporangial capsules glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Labiak Evangelista, Paulo H. 2013. Grammitid ferns (Polypodiaceae). I. Lellingeria. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 111: 1--130.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, the branches sometimes sarmentose and hanging over other plants, 2-6(-12) m tall and reaching a dbh of 14 cm; young and older branchlets subangular, densely stellate-pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles (2-)2.5-4(-7) cm long; lamina drying dark green to dark brown, smooth, elliptic to broadly elliptic, 18-35 X 10-21 cm, the base truncate to cordate, occasionally rounded or auriculate, the apex acute to acuminate, both surfaces more or less densely pubescent with tufted hairs, glabrescent on the upper surface, with (8-) 12-13 (-15) pairs of secondary veins, these distinctly visible on the upper surface, slightly raised and yellowish brown pubescent on the lower surface, the tertiary venation dense and distinctly visible, the margin denticulate. Cymes 2-5 cm long, pubescent with spreading hairs to tomentose, with 10-15 flowers. Fresh flowers yellow to creamy white; male floral cup broadly ob-conical, 3-4 mm in diam., 4-5 mm high, densely covered with yellowish spreading hairs, the floral roof distinctly raised, glabrous, the 4-5 tepals triangular, l.5-2.5 mm long, glabrous or occasionally with a few hairs on the adaxial tepal tips; stamens 6, often with 4 outer and 2 central ones, fleshy and containing whitish oil cells, the outer stamens distinctly exserted at anthesis; female floral cup of the same size and shape, except the tepals 2.3-3.5 mm long and the floral roof centrally more bulging; styles 20-30. Fruiting receptacle globose, about 1.5 cm in diam. (when fresh to 3 cm in diam.), glabrescent, immature green with pink spots, mature light red and with a strong lemon smell when crushed, the 20-26 drupelets distinctly protruding in dried material, each drupelet with a stylar aril.
bibliographicCitation: Renner, Susanne S. & Hausner, Gerlinde. 2005. Siparunaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 95: 1--247 pp.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, often with the branches hanging over other trees, 3-8(-15) m tall, reaching a dbh of 6.5 cm; young branchlets terete or rarely subquadrangular, with scarce stellate hairs, glabrescent, or glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles (2.5-)3-5(-9) cm long; lamina drying khaki to brown, thin, smooth, brittle, elliptic or obovate, 20-30 X 12-14.5(-17) cm, the base truncate, cordate, or rarely almost rounded, the apex acuminate, the tip 0.5-1(-1.5) cm long, above with few stellate hairs on the veins, otherwise subglabrous or glabrous, below moderately stellate-pubescent, with 9-13(-15) pairs of secondary veins, the veins smooth above, hardly raised below, the margin finely dentate or crenate. Cymes axillary in extant leaves or on leafless nodes, 2-7 cm long in the males, 1-3 cm long in the females, densely covered with conspicuous golden-brown or grayish stellate hairs, rarely glabrescent, with 15-25 flowers. Fresh flowers greenish yellow, yellow, or orange-red; male floral cup narrowly obconical, 2.5-3(-6) mm in diam., 3.57 mm high, pubescent like the cymes, the tepals 4-6, triangular, 2.5-3 mm long, with a few stellate hairs on the adaxial tepal tips, otherwise glabrous, the floral roof glabrous and centrally raised to a thin-walled tube surrounding the pore; stamens 6-7, the four outer ones exserted at anthesis and with their tips (pollen sacs) bent backwards (Fig. 12A); female floral cup similar to the male cups except sometimes more densely pubescent, the acutely triangular tepals 4-5 mm long, the floral roof conspicuously acute-conical; carpels 9-14, the styles often fused to a long, thin column. Fruiting receptacle globose, 1.5-2 cm in diam., stellate-pubescent and crowned by the persistent tepals, when fresh and mature dull red with white spots and with an astringent odor; drupelets 8-14, each with a stylar aril.
bibliographicCitation: Renner, Susanne S. & Hausner, Gerlinde. 2005. Siparunaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 95: 1--247 pp.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 2-12 m tall and reaching a dbh of 10 cm; young branchlets terete and with minute appressed stellate hairs. Leaves opposite; petioles 2.5-7 cm long; lamina drying brown, olive-brown, or grayish brown above and olive-brown below, papery and brittle, obovate to oblanceolate, 15-29 X (7-) 10-14 cm, the base acute to obtuse, sometimes with small domatia to 0.5 cm long, the apex cuspidate, the tip 0.5-1.5 cm long, both surfaces with minute appressed stellate hairs sometimes mixed with a few stellate-lepidote hairs on the midrib, with 9-13 pairs of secondary veins, veins flat above, slightly raised below, the margin finely dentate. Cymes ample, 4-8 cm long, with 40-60 flowers. Fresh flowers pale yellow or cream; male floral cup subglobose or urceolate, 1.3-1.7 mm in diam., 1.1-1.2 mm high, with few minute appressed stellate hairs or glabrescent, the tepals forming a narrow rim, the floral roof slightly raised, glabrous; stamens 8-10; female floral cup subglobose, 1.5-1.8 mm in diam., 1.3-1.5 mm high, the floral roof usually raised and with a short central tube sheathing the styles; styles 5-8. Fruiting receptacle globose and smooth, 0.8-1 cm in diam., the narrow tepal rim persistent in fruit, immature green with white spots, mature yellow and purple and with a strong lemon smell, drying black and with the ca. 8 drupelets distinctly protruding; fresh drupelets blue-gray with a red stylar aril.
bibliographicCitation: Renner, Susanne S. & Hausner, Gerlinde. 2005. Siparunaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 95: 1--247 pp.

description: Tree, to 20 m tall. Leafy twigs 2-5 mm thick, minutely puberulous, the older parts conspicuously lenticellate. Lamina elliptic, (5-)10-35 × (3-)7-17 cm, ± inequilateral, (subcoriaceous; apex ± abruptly acuminate; base rounded to obtuse at the broad side, acute to obtuse at the narrow side; margin entire; upper surface minutely puberulous, ± on the main veins; lower surface minutely puberulous on the (main) veins; venation plane above, ± prominent beneath; lateral veins 810 pairs, the basal pair often running parallel to the margin; tertiary venation reticulate or partly scalariform; petiole (1.5-)2.5-3.5(-5) cm long, 1.5-2.5 mm thick, minutely puberulous; stipules 0.3-0.8 cm long, puberulous, caducous. Staminate inflorescences in the leaf axils, pendulous, ca. 16-33 cm long, including 0.51.8 cm long, sparsely puberulous peduncle; rachis sparsely puberulous; flowers ± spaced, broadly sessile; perianth 2.5-3 mm long, 4-parted, sparsely ciliolate; stamens 4, isomorphic or anisomorphic, straight or slightly incurved at anthesis; filaments 0.2-0.6 mm long; anthers 0.8-1.2 × 0.7-12 mm, the connective broad, not apiculate. Pistillate inflorescences in the leaf axils or below the leaves, pendulous, ca. 6-17 cm long, to 40 cm long in fruit; peduncle 0.5-3 cm long, minutely puberulous; rachis minutely and yellowish-puberulous; flowers ca. (10-)20-60; pedicel 0.1-0.2 cm long, to 1.5 cm long in fruit, yellowish-puberulous; perianth 2-2.5 mm long, minutely puberulous, the upper part ± ruminate; stigmas ovate, ca. 0.5 mm long. Fruiting perianth ellipsoid to globose, 2-2.5 mm long, black.

description: Decumbent-ascending herb or subshrub, the stems stellate-pubescent, the hairs 0.5-1 mm long. Leaf blades triangular to oblong, mostly 1-3.5 x 0.6-1.5 cm, basally hastate or sagittate, crenate-dentate, acute, coarsely stellate-pubescent on both surfaces, the hairs ca. 1 mm long; petioles 0.5-1.5 cm long; stipules subulate, 2-4 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-2.5 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, broadly lanceolate, 6-8 x 1.5-2.5 mm, hirsute; calyx 6-7 mm long, more or less hirsute (hairs 0.5-1 mm long), the nerves with reddish pigmentation; corolla 12-15 mm long, rose with dark red center; staminal column 3-4 mm long, reddish, the filaments ca. 1 mm long; styles emergent from the column, purplish. Fruits oblate, ca. 6 mm diam., minutely pubescent; mericarps carinate, rugulose, 4-5 mm high.

description: Small tree, the young branches glabrous. Leaves elliptic, coriaceous, 10.0-16.0 cm long, 3.5-6.0 cm broad, acute to bluntly acuminate at apex, cuneate and equal at base, glabrous beneath; midrib plane to weakly impressed above, prominent and glabrous beneath; primary veins 9-10 pairs, arcuate, anastomosing; petioles 6.0-10.0 mm long, glabrescent, terete, rugose. Stipules lanceolate, glabrescent, to 4.0 mm long, caducous. Flowers hermaphrodite, borne in dense-flowered sessile glomerules on petiole, with long pedicels to 5.0 mm long; bracteoles 0.5-1.0 mm long, persistent, sparsely tomentellous. Calyx 5.0-6.0 mm long, sparsely puberulous on exterior, the lobes unequal, puberulous near apex on exterior. Corolla exserted well beyond calyx lobes, of a long exserted tube and 5 small entire equal lobes, the tube glabrous on both surfaces. Fertile stamens 5, alternating with corolla lobes, the anthers sessile, inserted at mouth of corolla tube. Ovary trilocular with 2 ovules in each loculus, shortly tomentellous on exterior. Style single but deeply divided into three for upper portion, shortly tomentellous. Fruit not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T. 1972. Dichapetalaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 10: 1-84.

description: Subarbusto 50 cm de alto, corteza color castaño claro con grietas longitudinales que dejan ver el súber blanquecino; ramas nuevas con pelos glandulares 0.3-0.4 mm long., estrellados, porrecto-estrellados con radio central 1-1.2 mm long, y pelos simples, tenues, cortos. Yemas axilares 1-2, la basal florífera; ramas seriales a veces desarrolladas. Hojas herbáceas, viscosas. Estípulas nulas. Pecíolo 1-5 mm long., indumento como el del tallo. Lámina elíptica, a veces angustiovada o angustiobovada, 18-40 x 7-16 mm, relación largo:ancho = 2.5-3.1:1; base cuneada o atenuada; ápice obtuso o subagudo; borde plano, aserrado, con pelos glandulares, dientes agudos u obtusos; haz opaca o ligeramente lustrosa, con pelos estrellados laxos y porrecto-estrellados con radio central 0,5-1 mm long., orientado diagonalmente y 6-10 radios cortos; envés opaco, con pelos estrellados; venas laterales 5-7 pares, ángulo de divergencia 2535°, rectas, ligeramente salientes en la haz, poco prominentes en el envés, con pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares; venas terciarias y venación menor inconspicuas. Flores axilares, solitarias, homostilas. Pedúnculo floral delgado, 15-25 mm long., con pelos simples, glandulares y algunos porrecto-estrellados. Profilos nulos, a veces alguno desarrollado, diminuto. Pedicelo ligeramente más grueso, 2-4.5 mm long, con mayor cantidad de pelos glandulares. Cáliz 5-10 mm long.; tubo calicino 2 mm long., brevemente piloso por dentro, por fuera con pelos glandulares y estrellados especialmente sobre las venas; lóbulos angostos, 7-nervados, angustiovados o triangulares, los internos glabrescentes a ambos lados de la vena media, bordes membranáceos, ápice brevemente mucronado. Corola color durazno, con venas oscuras; pétalos con uña brevemente pilosa; lámina 14-15 x 9-10 mm. Corona fímbriada, lóbulos de pétalos y sépalos 0,6 mm long. Filamentos estaminales 5-7.5 mm long., soldados 0.5 mm en la base al tubo calicino; anteras 1-1.9 x 0.6-0.9 mm, base emarginada, filamento inserto a 0.4-0.7 mm de la base, ápice recurvado después de la dehiscencia. Ovario ovoide 1.7-2 mm long., placentas 8-10 ovuladas; estilos glabros, cilindricos, 7.5-9.5 mm long.; estigma penicilado amarillo ca. 1 mm long. Frutos 4-8 mm long.; valvas ovadas, verrucosas por fuera, con pelos glandulares y simples; por dentro lisas, lustrosas, blanquecinas, vena placentaria poco saliente. Semillas obovoides, rectas, 1.8-2.3 x 1-1.2 mm (Fig. 12A); exóstoma cónico pequeño; rafe apenas marcada; cálaza redondeada; episperma glabro, reticulado, aréolas transrectangulares con una depresión punctiforme en cada una (Fig. 15A); arilo angosto, pequeño, unilateral, más corto que la semilla.
bibliographicCitation: Arbo, María M. 1995. Turneraceae --- Parte I. Piriqueta. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 67: 1-156.

description: Dioecious treelet, 4-10 m tall; young branchlets quadrangular and sometimes sulcate, yellowish pubescent, glabrescent. Leaves in whorls of 3; petioles 2-9 cm long; lamina drying brownish, papery and brittle, lanceolate, 28-44 X 9-15 cm, the base obtuse to acute, the apex acute, both surfaces more or less densely pubescent with tufted hairs, with 16-22 pairs of secondary veins, the veins flat above, distinctly raised below, the margin crenate-dentate. Cymes umbel-like, 3-5 cm long including the 1-2 cm long peduncle, densely pubescent like the young branch-lets, with 15-20 flowers. Fresh flowers yellow or creamy white; male floral cup obconical, 2.5-4 mm in diam., 2-3.5 mm high, sparsely pubescent with short, few-branched and more or less spreading hairs interspersed with short tubercles, about 0.2 mm long, the 4-6 tepals broadly triangular, 2-3 mm long, with few minute hairs on the adaxial tepal tips, the floral roof distinctly raised, glabrous; stamens 20(-30); female floral cup of the same size but with longer tubercles, up to 2 mm long, the floral roof a cylindrical bulge separated by a groove from a central acutely conical tube sheathing the styles; styles 7-12. Fruiting receptacle pear-shaped, 1.5-2 cm long, with thick conspicuous tubercles and crowned by the persistent tepals, when fresh and mature reddish and with a strong pungent scent; drupelets 5-10, each with a stylar aril.
bibliographicCitation: Renner, Susanne S. & Hausner, Gerlinde. 2005. Siparunaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 95: 1--247 pp.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 3-10 m tall and reaching a dbh of 11 cm; young branchlets usually quadrangular and strongly sulcate, densely pubescent with yellowish brown hairs. Leaves opposite; petioles 1.5-5.5 cm long; lamina drying greenish brown, chartaceous and sometimes slightly bullate, oblanceolate, 30-65 X 13-25 cm, the base more or less decurrent, the apex acuminate, the tip 1.5-3 cm long, upper surface with simple or few-branched tufted hairs, lower surface tomentose, especially on the veins, with 1832 pairs of secondary veins, the veins more or less inconspicuous above, slightly raised below, the margin irregularly dentate. Cymes 5-8 cm long (Fig. 5B), pubescent like the young branchlets, with 40-60 flowers. Fresh flowers pale yellow, turning reddish; male floral cup subglobose, 2-3 mm in diam., 2-2.5 mm high, with tubercles bearing long spreading hairs, the tepals 4-5, triangular, 2.5-4.5 mm long, the floral roof slightly raised, glabrous; stamens 5-6, scarcely exserted at anthesis; female floral cup subglobose, 33.5 mm in diam., 2.8-3.3 mm high, at anthesis with conspicuous tubercles, ca. 2 mm long and densely covered with long tufted hairs (Fig. 51C, right), the tepals 3.5-4.5 mm long, the floral roof raised to a cylindrical bulge with a central narrow tube sheathing the styles; styles 5-6. Fruiting receptacle globose and with spinelike tubercles, 1.5-2 cm in diam., when fresh and mature pink or green suffused with red, strongly lemon-scented; drupelets 5-7, each with a red stylar aril.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 3-7 m tall, with arching branches; young branchlets terete and densely covered with reddish brown or golden brown tufted hairs. Leaves opposite; petioles 1-3.5 cm long; lamina drying greenish brown, chartaceous, elliptic or lanceolate, 8-26 X 3.5-13.5 cm, the base acute to obtuse, the apex acuminate, the tip 1-2 cm long, both surfaces pubescent with tufted hairs, these denser on the lower surface, with 8-12 pairs of secondary veins, the veins almost flat above, slightly raised below, the margin finely dentate. Cymes 3-4 cm long, pendent and more or less densely covered with short spreading hairs, with 5-12 flowers. Fresh flowers creamy yellow to reddish; male floral cup subglobose, 3.5-4 mm in diam., 2.5-3 mm high, more or less densely covered with spreading hairs on minute pedestals, ca. 0.1 mm long (Fig. 3G, 7D), the 4-6 tepals broadly triangular and 2-4 mm long, adaxially densely persistently tomentose, the floral roof conical, pubescent to gla-brescent, in fresh flowers tinged red; stamens 10-20, when fresh red; female floral cup subglobose, 4-5 mm in diam., 3.2-3.7 mm high, the tepals typically fused at their base for 2-3 mm, apically broadly triangular to lobed, the free parts of the tepals 0.8-2 mm long, the indumentum as in the male flowers, the floral roof differentiated into a cylindrical bulge separated by a distinct groove from a central tube sheathing the stylar column (the styles fused where they emerge from the floral roof, Fig. 8A); styles 7-12, barely exserted from the pore. Fruiting receptacle ovoid to globose, 1-1.5 cm in diam., with minute wartlike outgrowth often tipped by spreading hairs, crowned by the persistent tepals, when fresh and mature purple with white spots and a strong pungent smell, drupelets 3-8, each with a bright red stylar aril.
bibliographicCitation: Renner, Susanne S. & Hausner, Gerlinde. 2005. Siparunaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 95: 1--247 pp.

description: Tree, to 15 m tall. Leafy twigs 1.5-2.5 mm thick, puberulous to hirtellous; periderm flaking off. Lamina elliptic to oblong to subobovate, 6-15 × 1.8-5 cm, subcoriaceous; apex (subcaudate; base (sub)acute; margin plane; both surfaces glabrous; lateral veins 8-13 pairs; tertiary venation reticulate; petiole 0.3-0.8 cm long, puberulous, the epidermis ± flaking off; stipules 0.5-1 cm long, sparsely puberulous, subpersistent or caducous. Staminate inflorescences unknown. Pistillate inflorescences in the leaf axils or just below the leaves, 1.2-2 cm diam., subsessile; involucre with broadly ovate to oblong bracts in ca. 5 rows, the inner ones ± scarious and subglabrous (and straw-colored when dry); flowers ca. 5-10; free parts of the tepals subulate, sparsely and minutely puberulous, ca. 0.3-0.6 cm long (and straw-colored when dry); stigmas ca. 2 mm long. Infructescences subglobose, 2.5-4 cm diam.; free parts of the tepals to 1 cm long, subulate (to aculeate).

description: Tree, to 25 m tall. Leafy twigs 3-4 mm thick, brown-(sub)velutinous. Lamina oblong, 22-40 × 8-14 cm, coriaceous; apex acuminate; base obtuse to rounded; upper surface sparsely puberulous on the midrib; lower surface brownish-(sub)velutinous on the veins; lateral veins 18-26 pairs; tertiary venation largely scalariform; petiole 0.5-1 cm long, brown-velutinous; stipules 0.5-1 cm long, densely brownish to whitish-hirtellous to subvelutinous. Staminate inflorescences 2-5 together in the leaf axils and below the leaves, 0.8-1.3 cm diam.; peduncle 0.3-0.5 cm long, bracteate; involucral bracts in ca. 7 series, broadly ovate to semicircular, densely yellowish to brownish-puberulous to subvelutinous; perianth ca. 2.5-3 mm long, tepals 4-6, basally connate (or free), ± densely yellow-hairy. Infructescences 6-8 cm diam., (sub)sessile; involucral bracts in 6-8 series, ovate to lanceolate, yellow-strigose to subsericeous, the inner ones to 2 cm long; flowers/fruits numerous; free parts of the tepals dispersed, aculeate, yellow-strigose to subsericeous; style ca. 4 mm long; stigmas 2-3 mm long, tongue-shaped.

description: Shrub or tree, to 12(-20) m tall. Leafy twigs 1-2.5 mm thick, sparsely and minutely puberulous. Lamina oblong to elliptic (to lanceolate), 3.5-17 × 1.5-6.5 cm, broadest at or above the middle, ± inequilateral, coriaceous; apex acuminate; base acute to rounded; margin entire; upper surface minutely puberulous on midrib; lower surface sparsely and minutely puberulous on the (base of the) midrib; venation (almost) plane above, prominent beneath; lateral veins 8-12 pairs; tertiary venation reticulate (or tending to scalariform); petiole 0.3-0.8 cm long, 1-2 mm thick, (minutely) puberulous; stipules 0.3-0.5 mm long, (minutely) puberulous, caducous. Staminate inflorescences patent (?), 0.8-4.5 cm long, including the 0.1-0.2 cm long puberulous peduncle; flowers rather crowded to ± dispersed, narrowly (or broadly) sessile; perianth 1-1.5 mm long, 4-parted, ciliolate, sparsely and minutely puberulous outside; stamens (3 or) 4, straight, isomorphic; filaments 0.51.2 mm long; anthers ca. 0.5-0.7 × 0.4-0.7 mm, the connective broad, apiculate. Pistillate inflorescences patent (?), 0.5-3 cm long, to 5 cm long in fruit, including the 0.1-0.8 cm long, puberulous peduncle; rachis sparsely and minutely puberulous; flowers 3-12, (sub)sessile, pedicellate in fruit; pedicel to 1 cm long, (very) sparsely hispidulous to minutely puberulous; perianth ca. 2 mm long, glabrous, the upper part hemispherical to broadly ovoid; stigmas tongue-shaped, ca. 1 mm long, coarsely papillate. Fruiting perianth subglobose, ca. 0.7-0.9 × 0.7-0.9 cm, with the apical part ± discoid and the lower part with a ruminate, almost glabrous surface.

description: Shrub, or small tree, 2.4-4 m tall. Bark beige to gray superficially, dark red-gray beneath, the indumentum short, pale ferruginous, shortly appressed-tomentose towards apices, fading to gray and glabrescent with age. Lenticels numerous, inconspicuous, minute (<0.5 mm diam.), granular, raised, pale orange-brown or gray, contrasting somewhat with the dark bark. Leaves simple or slightly lobed basally, thin-coriaceous, drying pale green to yellow-brown or pinkish-brown, with minute red specks on lower surface, shiny, glabrous. Petiole well defined, 1-4 cm long × 1.25-3.5 mm broad at midlength, ca. 1/10-1/5 the length of the lamina, canaliculate, with tomentose indumentum persistent on adaxial surface, gradually glabrescent. Lamina (8-)12-19 × (3.5-)4.5-10.5 cm, length:breadth 1.5-2.5:1, oblong or narrow-obovate (more rarely to wide-obovate); base sometimes obscured by doubling over of lamina on pressing, symmetrical, or strongly asymmetrical (specimen with lobed leaf), the sides of the lamina joining the petiole and descending it adaxially, forming a channel; apex obtuse to rounded and at times retuse, the apical point of midrib rarely protruding; margin entire to serrate with 13-29 pairs of serrations, revolute towards base or not; venation plane to commonly sunken, moderately conspicuous above, prominent and conspicuous beneath, craspedodromous to semicraspedodromous, the midvein reaching the apex; lateral veins 6-8 pairs. Inflorescence axillary, unbranched, 14.5-21.5 × ca. 3 cm, short, orange-brown tomentose-pilose; peduncle 1-1.5 cm × 2-3 mm broad, with a few sterile bracts at base. Common bracts 0.4 × 0.6 mm, broader than long, shortly ferruginous-tomentose. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels very short, 0.2-0.5 × 1 mm, indumentum as for inflorescence. Buds 1.2 mm broad at apex, 0.5 mm broad at midlength, short yellow-orange tomentose. Flowers 15-17 mm long, the perianth indumentum as for inflorescence; filaments 0.6-1.3 mm long, attached 8-8.5 mm from base of tepals; anthers 1.8 × 0.5 mm; nectary lobes 0.5 mm long, well separated; ovary laterally compressed, the hairs extending 2.5-3.5mm from base, covering entire surface evenly, ferruginous or rufous, appressed, densely puberulent; ovules 0.6 × 0.3 mm. Infructescence 24-30 cm long, glabrous. Fruit pedicel not seen. Fruit (mature ?) 2.8 × 0.8-1.3 cm, the sutured side curved but flattened at the top, the unsutured side curved, the base and apex not constricted or briefly so, the apex weakly curved, the style not persistent, gray-brown, glabrous, smooth.

description: Subshrubs 0.5-1.5 m tall, the stems minutely stellate- or glandular-pubescent and with scattered setae 1.5-2 mm long. Leaf blades ovate, 3-5(-8) x 2-4(-6) cm, basally cordate, serrate, acute, palmately 5-nerved, discolorous, the upper surface minutely pubescent with stellate and bifurcate hairs, the lower surface softly tomentose, also with scattered 2-3-armed stellate spicules or these sometimes absent; petioles 0.5-2 cm long; stipules filiform, 2-3 mm long. Flowers solitary or paired in the leaf axils, the pedicels 3-6 cm long; involucellar bracts 6-7, lanceolate, 11-13 x 1-3 mm, minutely stellate-pubescent and also ciliate, especially toward the base, the hairs 1-2 mm long; calyx 6-8 mm long, minutely stellate-pubescent and maiginally ciliate, the hairs 1-2 mm long; corolla 1.5-2.5 cm long, pubescent on margins of claw, yellow, with small red center. Fruits 6-7 mm diam., minutely and retrorsely scabridulous; mericarp body ca. 5 mm tall, with 2 lateral wings and a subapical apiculum 1-2 mm long; seeds 3-4 mm long, glabrous, striate.

description: Shrub or small tree to 7.5 m high with a trunk to 6.5 cm in diam, glabrous except for the inflorescence; young twigs terete; wood dark, strong, and hard. Petioles 0.8-3.0 mm long; blades purplish when very young, the purple area becoming restricted to the outer lateral 2/3 of each half of the blade as it unfolds, the blade then becoming light green, then dark green at maturity; blades 2.6-10.0 cm long, 1.5-5.0 cm wide, elliptic to elliptic-ovate or elliptic-oblong or broadly so, rarely narrowly so, the latter apparently only on saplings or sucker shoots, blades abruptly acute or apiculate at the apex or on narrow leaves sometimes acuminate, cordate at base, rounded to a small notch 0.5-1.2 mm deep or on narrow leaves rarely truncate; midrib plane or slightly rounded above, prominent and with 2 narrow horizontal wings below; blade surface smooth when fresh, the lateral nerves not prominent, becoming obscurely to moderately visible above and below when dry. Midrib xylem tubular; stomatal crypts Type III, averaging in a leaf ca 35-65 µ in diam, 22-28 µ high, 75-90 per sq mm (extremes 20-100 µ diam, 20-30 µ high, 50-95 per sq mm); upper epidermis varying irregularly from one to two and sometimes three cells thick in the same leaf, often some of the inner cells greatly enlarged, mucilaginous walls common in cells contacting the palisade and sometimes in other cells; hypodermis none, but enlarged inner cells of the upper epidermis sometimes simulate one; free stone cells present along the length of the midrib but tending to be few and scattered toward the tip; terminal sclereids essentially stellate but sometimes armless, the central body roundish or squarish to elliptic or rectangular, 1-3 times as long as wide, the arms none to many, short and sharp. Inflorescences axillary and at leafless nodes of twigs to 3.5 mm thick, 1-8 per side, each 1-5-flowered, 1.0-5.4 mm long to base of farthest pedicel measured along the axes and with 1-3 internodes in that length; bracts 1.1-2.3 mm long, triangular, persistent till just before anthesis. Axes of inflorescence, bracts, pedicels, and upper parts of calyx lobes minutely puberulent. True pedicels 0.6-3.0 mm long; calyx including inferior ovary 3.8-4.7 mm long, campanulate, the locules bulging slightly externally; free hypanthium ca 1.5-1.7 mm long; calyx lobes before anthesis 0.8-1.4 mm long, 1.1-2.1 mm wide, 1.4-2.0 mm long from the stamen attachment, triangular, acute or slightly obtuse, splitting apart at anthesis a further length of 0.5-0.8 mm. Petals white or (Wright 2468) apparently sometimes light purple, 3.2-5.1 mm long, 2.4-3.9 mm wide, broadly ovate, acute at apex, short-clawed at base. Antesepalous filaments ca 3.0-mm long, antepetalous ones ca 4.5 mm long; anthers 2.1-2.5 mm long; sporangia 1.7-2.0 mm long, dehiscing by elongate apical pores; gland 0.5-0.6 mm long, 1.5-2.0 mm from apex of anther when measured from center of gland; cauda 0.7-0.9 mm long. Ovary (3-)-5-locular; placentae axile or nearly axile-basal, the ovules borne on all sides of a short column, 3-7 per placenta, 17-20 in all; style ca 10 mm long. Fruits 1-4-seeded, subglobose when 1-seeded and then with the hypanthium located near or adjacent to the pedicel through differential development, deeply and very prominently lobed according to the number of seeds when 2-4-seeded, the pedicel then basal and opposite the pit of the hypanthium; a few calyx lobes often persistent; individual lobes of fruit ca 6.0-7.5 mm wide and high when dry, estimated 7.0-9.0 mm when fresh, the overall width of the fruit when more than 1-seeded ca 12-14 mm when dry, estimated ca 14.5-17.0 mm when fresh. Seeds dark brown, polished, subglobose, 6.0-7.5 mm in diam. with a broad rather flat roundish to slightly heart-shaped hilum 4.0-5.0 mm in diam, the hilum lateral in the several seeds examined.

description: Small tree. Leafy twigs 3-6 mm thick, brown tomentose. Leaves lanceolate, 18-42 cm long, 5.5-12 cm broad, coriaceous, acuminate, obtuse to cordate at the base, glabrous above, except for short, brown, appressed hairs on the costa, otherwise minutely puberulous, glabrescent beneath; the costa prominent, the other veins slightly prominent to impressed above, prominent beneath, 24-27 pairs of secondary veins, tertiary veins partly parallel; petioles 4-10 mm long; stipules ca 15 mm long, yellowish sericeous, brownish tomentose at the lower end. Pistillate inflorescences subsessile to pedunculate; peduncle 2-4 mm long; involucre with ca 20-40, reniform to deltoid, obtuse, appressed-puberulous to shortly sericeous bracts in 5-8 series; flowers 12-25; perianth 4 or more? mm high, 4-8-lobed to 4-8-parted, brown velutinous, perianth segments scale-like, glabrous inside; style 10-12 mm long; stigmas vittiform, 9-13 mm long; pseudobracts peripherally in 1-3 series, spine-like, 4-5 mm long, brown tomentellous to velutinous. Infructescences at least 2-3.5 cm in diameter; perianth 7-8 mm high; pseudobracts spine-like, 6-7 mm long, often curved. Mature infructescences in December.
