description: Tree, 10 m tall. Leafy twigs 1-3 mm thick, yellowish-tomentose to hirtellous, the hairs distinctly different in length and partly crinkled. Lamina coriaceous, oblong to subobovate, 2.5-11 × 1-4.5 cm, slightly inequilateral; apex acuminate; base subacute to obtuse; margin entire, ± revolute; upper surface puberulous to tomentose, mainly on the veins; lower surface tomentose to hirtellous; lateral veins 12-18 pairs; tertiary venation reticulate to subscalariform; petiole 0.2-0.4 cm long, tomentose to hirtellous; stipules 0.8-1.2 cm long, yellowish-(sub)sericeous, caducous. Staminate inflorescences solitary or in pairs in the leaf axils, subsessile, (immature) 0.5-0.7 cm diam.; involucre with ca. 7 rows of semiorbicular to ovate, yellowish-subsericeous to appressed-puberulous bracts; stamens (immature) with filaments ca. 0.2-0.3 mm long, anthers ca. 0.7-0.9 mm long, apiculate, glabrous; interstaminal scales (= tepals) 1-1.3 mm long, filiform to narrowly subspathulate, the upper part with dense and relatively long hairs.

description: Tree, to 25 m tall. Leafy twigs 3-6 mm thick, drying purplish brown to blackish, yellowish to whitish appressed-puberulous to strigillose, with hairs of ± different to almost equal length. Lamina coriaceous, oblong to elliptic, (7-)10-24(-38)  × 4.5-11(-17) cm, slighty to distinctly inequilateral (at the base); apex acuminate; base subacute to rounded to subtruncate; margin entire (or when juvenile dentate to crenate); upper surface sparsely appressed-puberulous on the midrib or also the lateral veins, and initially with dense brown globose-capitate pluricellular hairs; lower surface yellowish to whitish appressed-puberulous to strigillose on the veins, often also with some longer hairs, (initially) with dense, brownish, ovoid- to ellipsoid-capitate, pluricellular hairs; lateral veins (13-) 18-24 pairs; tertiary venation scalariform; petiole 0.7-1.2(-2) cm long, yellowish to whitish appressed-puberulous to strigillose; stipules 1.2-2.5 cm long, rather sparsely, yellowish to whitish appressed-puberulous to strigillose mainly on the midrib and towards the base outside, puberulous inside, caducous. Staminate inflorescences 2-4 in the leaf axils, (sub)sessile, (immature) ca. 0.4 cm diam.; involucre with ca. 6-7 rows of semiorbicular to (broadly) ovate, sparsely, yellowish to whitish, appressed-puberulous bracts; (immature) stamens with filaments ca. 0.2-0.3 mm long, anthers ca. 6-7 mm long, apiculate, glabrous; interstaminal scales (= tepals) oblanceolate to narrowly subspathulate, on the upper part with relatively short hairs.

description: Tree. Leafy twigs 4-8 mm thick, greyish, whitish appressed-pubescent; periderm more or less wrinkled. Leaves lanceolate, 17-32 cm long, 5-9 cm broad, coriaceous to subcoriaceous, acuminate, acute at the base, glabrous above, sparsely pubescent on the costa and secondary veins beneath; the costa and the proximal parts of the secondary veins prominent, otherwise the venation nearly plane above, veins prominent beneath, secondary veins 18-19 pairs, straight, joined by a rather distinct submarginal vein; petioles 6-10 mm long; stipules 10-15? mm long, appressed-pubescent. Infructescence ca 6 cm in diameter, sessile; involucre with ca 25 deltoid to suborbiculate to ovate to subovate, up to 2 cm long, obtuse, appressed-puberulous bracts in 5-6 series; flowers 22; perianth 5-7 mm high, 8-io-lobed to 8-10-fid, puberulous, perianth segments rather plane and obtuse; style ca 4 mm long, stigmas filiform, to vittiform 12-13 mm long; pseudobracts also numerous among the flowers, lanceolate, thick, 3-7 mm long, involute, obtuse, puberulous; seed 10 × 12 mm. Mature infructescences in February.

description: Completion of the description: Staminate inflorescences up to 5 together in the leaf axils; peduncle 0.5-0.8 cm long; involucral bracts in 4-5 series, ovate, obtuse, the outer ones pale yellow appressed-puberulous, the inner ones only ciliolate; perianth ca. 1 mm long; tepals 4-5, cucullate, thickened at the apex, ciliolate; stamens 3-5; filaments ca. 0.5 mm long; anthers elliptic, 0.8-1 × 0.7-0.8 mm. description: Monoecious shrub or treelet, 1-6 m tall, reaching a dbh of 10 cm; young branchlets terete, minutely stellate-pilose. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.5-0.8 cm long; lamina often drying light green or yellowish green, thin and papery, elliptic to lanceolate, 9-18 X 3-6.5 cm, the base acute to obtuse, the apex acuminate, the tip 1-2 cm long, glabrous above except for stellate hairs on the midrib, sparsely softly pilose below, with 7-8 pairs of secondary veins, these slightly raised above and below, the margin entire. Cymes few-branched, 2-3.5 cm long, more or less densely covered with stellate hairs, with 10-15 flowers; pedicels 2-4 mm long. Fresh flowers yellow; male flowers cup-shaped, 1.2-1.9 mm in diam., 1.2-1.5 mm high, the indumentum as on the cymes; tepals and floral roof barely developed; stamens 5-7, flat and almost transparent, with a broad filament, at anthesis distinctly protruding from the floral pore; female flowers globose to subglobose, 1.7-2.2 mm in diam., 1.5-2.1 mm high, the tepals forming a narrow rim, the floral roof conical and glabrous, carpels 5-7, the styles fused and protruding (up to 0.9 mm) from the narrow floral pore. Fruiting receptacle globose, 0.8-1 cm in diam., mature reddish purple and with a strong astringent smell; drupelets commonly 5, lacking a stylar aril.

description: Monoecious tree, 5-20 m tall and reaching a dbh of at least 34 cm; branchlets terete but flattened at the nodes, densely grayish-brown puberulous or glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles 1-1.8(-3) cm long; lamina drying dark reddish brown, stiff-chartaceous to coriaceous, elliptic, lanceolate, or oblong, 20-35(-40) X (8-)10-15 cm, the base acute to obtuse, the apex cuspidate, the tip to 1 cm long, the lamina above and below glabrous except for the midrib which may be minutely puberulous near the petiole, with 8-13 pairs of secondary veins, flat above, slightly raised below, the margin entire. Cymes 2-3 cm long, short-branched and mostly borne in pairs in the leaf axils (Fig. 28a), with 15-20 flowers, the pedicels 2-4 mm long and densely puberulous. Fresh flowers cream; male flowers subglobose, 1.5-2.2 mm in diam., puberulous as the cymes, the 5 tepals fused to a thick rim, the floral roof a barely visible membranous rim within the tepal rim; stamens (5-)9-20(-30); female flowers closely resembling the male flowers except the floral roof forming a short cylinder tightly sheathing the styles (Fig. 28d); styles usually 5. Fruiting receptacle 1.5(-2) cm in diam., conspicuously tuberculate, the tubercles fleshy and up to 4 mm long; mature fruits purple or red when fresh, drying brown or black; drupelets 1-4, lacking a stylar aril.

description: Arbusto, ramas jóvenes tomentosas, maduras pilosas, inconspicuamente len-ticeladas o lenticelas ausentes. Hojas imparipinadas; folíolos (11-) 15-27; pecíolo 0.05-1 cm de largo, tomentoso; raquis 6-10 cm de largo, piloso. Foliolos 0.8-3.7 cm de largo, 0.6-1 cm de ancho, oblongos u oblongo-lanceolados, cartáceos, haz oscura, brillante, esparcidamente pubescente, envés claro, opaco, densamente marrón-tomentoso, nervadura central densamente pilosa, base cordada, cuneada en el folíolo terminal, ápice redondeado, margen revoluto; foliolos sésiles o pe-ciólulo 0.1 cm de largo; venación difusa en ambas caras; nervaduras laterales 56 pares, formando ángulos de 60-90° con la nervadura central. Inflorescencia en panícula reducida, axilar o pseudo-terminal; raquila 2-3 cm de largo, tomentosa; brácteas 0.3-0.5 cm de largo. Flores desconocidas. Pedúnculo articulado, 0.5 cm de largo. Fruto 1.3-1.5 cm de largo, glabrescente, densamente velloso cerca al ápice; estilo persistente, conspicuo; cáliz tomentoso. Semilla 1 cm de largo; ariloide 0.4 cm de largo.

description: Cataphylla nulla; stipulae fuscae persistentes; petioli 2-5(-7) mm longi; laminae foliorum (1.2-)1.4-3.2(-3.7) cm longae, 0.6-1.3(-1.6) cm latae, remote crenulatae vel serrulatae basi cuneatae rotundataeve, supra glabrae vel margine modice pubescentes pilis ad 0.25 mm longis, subtus pallidiores glabrae vel saepe sparsim pubescentes pilis ad 0.3 mm longis; flores non visi; drupa 4-6 mm diametro; putamina saepe 2.

description: Small shrub. Bark mostly brown (reddish when young, grayish when older), hair in moderate amounts on leaf-bearing portions and decreasing to none on older portions. Branchlets 1.5-10.0 cm long with uncrowded leaves (internodes 1-12 mm long). Stipules up to 2.5 mm long, dark-colored with external hairs and revolute margins, persistent; petioles 2-5(-7) mm long with shallow canal above and moderate amount of antrorse or erect hairs; leaf-blades moderately thick, flexible when dry about 45° before breaking, (1.2-) 1.4-3.2(-3.7) cm long, 0.6-1.3(-l.6) cm wide, elliptic; base cuneate to rounded; apex obtuse, acute, very short acuminate, or mucronate; margin revolute or plane, remotely crenulate or serrulate with (3-)5-6(-8) teeth per cm, each having or lacking a dark-colored mucro; above either entirely glabrous or with moderate amount of short (up to ¼ mm) erect hairs on margin, beneath somewhat paler than above (rarely with yellowish or brownish tinge) and sparsely hairy with hairs up to 1/3 mm long and erect or appressed or less commonly glabrous; midrib above and beneath beset with hairs, secondaries with fewer hairs or glabrous, venation dark- or pale-colored and usually conspicuous, secondary veins 5-7(-8) pairs on either side of midrib. No flowering collections seen. Fruit usually one (rarely two) per axil; pedicels 2.0-5.0 mm long; floral cup ca 2.0 mm in diam, very shallow, undulant, and with entire margin; pedicel and floral cup with short erect hairs; drupes 4.0-6.0 mm in diam, glabrous, mostly 2-seeded (less commonly 3-seeded) with an additional abortive carpel sometimes visible.

description: Shrub or small tree to 6 or 8 m tall, trunk 10.5-30 cm in diam.; branchlets 2-5(-10) mm in diam., brown, shining, lenticels spindle-shaped or fissured, up to more than 5 mm long, (sub)glabrous. Leaves 1-3-foliolate with leaflets subsessile; sheath to 7 mm long, ciliate with hairs to 0.5 mm, densely pubescent, becoming glabrous in age; petiole subterete, 10-60 mm long and 1-3 mm thick, rarely shorter, usually glabrous, or pubescent with spreading hairs to 0.05 mm long; wings obsolete or up to 0.1-0.2 mm broad; leaflet blades (narrowly) elliptic or obovate, (3-)5-20(-28) × (1.2-)2-7.5(-13) cm, mostly up to 13 × 5 cm, (long-) attenuate to narrowly cuneate at base, acuminate to, occasionally, obtuse or emarginate at apex, the very tip obtuse or occasionally emarginate, margin revolute toward base, the blades chartaceous or somewhat subcoriaceous, somewhat shining, mostly glabrous on both sides, or pubescent below with spreading hairs to 0.3 mm long and soft to the touch, venation ± prominent, particularly beneath, midvein plane or prominulent above. Inflorescences terminal near tips of branchlets, widely paniculate, in general longer than the leaves, (10-)20-35 × 2-30 cm, with numerous flowers, pubescent with spreading hairs 0.05-0.2 mm long, lower bracts sometimes leaf-like and up to 10 × 2 mm, upper ones usually narrowly triangular, 0.8-2(-5) × 0.5-1.2 mm, usually ± densely pubescent on both sides with hairs to 0.1 mm long, or subglabrous below; pedicels 1.5-7 mm long and 0.4-0.7 mm thick, pubescent with spreading hairs 0.05 mm; bractlets 2, subopposite. Flowers (6-)6.5-10(-12) mm in diam., especially the buds becoming very dark purplish when dried; calyx lobes separate to subvalvate, depressedly ovate or -triangular, 0.5-1 × 0.7-1.3 mm, obtuse, upper side glabrous or sometimes near margin pubescent, lower side subglabrous or pubescent with spreading hairs to 0.1 mm long; petals deciduous, valvate, very widely spreading, ovate or elliptic, 3-5 (-5.5) × 1.5-2.5(-3) mm, unguiculate with claw 0.2-0.5 mm, acute at apex, thickly coriaceous becoming thinly so, claret or dark purplish when living, brownish-or red-purplish when boiled, the upper side densely pubescent with spreading hairs to 0.1 mm long, the lower side glabrous, or towards the tip pubescent like the sepals; filaments deciduous or persistent, 0.8-1.5 mm long and 0.1-0.2 mm thick, the tip acuminate but later on subobtuse due to shrinking, purplish in the upper half, glabrous; anthers very broadly heart-shaped, 0.5-0.8 × 0.5-0.8 mm, finely purplish-pigmented and papillose; disc in upper half 5-partite, each part slightly or obsoletely lobed, no longer than the ovary, ca. 1-1.2 mm high and 1.7-2.1 (-2.5) mm in diam., purplish, charged with tubercles up to 0.1 mm; carpels 0.6-0.8 mm, usually on a raised receptacle, provided with orbicular or ovoid, glandular tubercles 0.1-0.2 mm, which are usually glabrous, or pilose with hairs 0.05-0.1 mm long; style inserted half-way on the carpels, not or only slightly projecting beyond them before the shedding of the pollen, but after that slightly elongating to become 0.5-0.8 mm long, 0.2 mm thick, and projecting up to 0.5 mm, becoming purplish, with glands, glabrous; stigma capitate, slightly lobed or not, 0.20.3 × 0.3-0.4 mm. Fruits somewhat depressed, stellately-lobed, 14-20 × 22-30 mm, up to 35 mm wide when dehisced, loculi provided with a dorsal, blunt apophysis 3-5(-7) mm long 1/2 or 2/5 below the tip, transversely wrinkled with prominent parallel nerves on both sides of the wall, ± muricate-tuberculate, the tubercles to 2 mm long, septicidally dehiscent from some mm above base to 2 mm below top, and loculicidally up to half-way the apophysis; seeds 1 or 2 per loculus, (depressedly) ovoid, or roundish, 5-8.2 × 4-6 × 4-6 mm with a mucro 0.2 mm, flat at or near base; testa coriaceous, dull dark brown, often provided with slight longitudinal pustulate ridges; chalazal area roundish, ca. 3-4 mm broad, dark brown-black, shining; hilum ca. 0.6 mm broad; cotyledons strongly unequal, not punctate, with ears 0.5 mm, radicle thick, 0.4-0.7 mm long, obtuse, projecting but not exceeding the cotyledons, plumule 0.2-0.3 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree 1-6 m tall with trunk reported as 7 cm in diam, (once reported from São Paulo as a tall tree); dead bark very thin, gray-purplish-brown with minute elongate-reticulate cracks, falling off in minute chips, with green boundary layer and a living bark 2.5 mm thick (according to Lindeman); branchlets 2-4 mm thick, grayish-green-brown, shining when young, pubescent with hairs 0.05-0.1 mm long, becoming glabrous in age; perules of terminal buds triangular, strigillose with yellow-tawny hairs ca. 0.3 mm long. Leaves alternate or subopposite, crowded or not at the apex of branchlets, simple or indistinctly 1-foliolate; petiole semiterete, canaliculate towards base by erect wings, distally sometimes turgid-geniculate, 4-25(-40) mm long and 1 mm thick, glabrous or pubescent with hairs 0.05-0.1 mm; the wings formed by the decurrent base of the blade, up to 0.2-0.3 mm broad; blade (narrowly) elliptic to (narrowly) obovate, 5.5-16 cm long (-30 cm near ends of branchlets) and 1.8-5.5 cm broad (-9 cm near ends of branchlets), long-attenuate or narrowly cuneate towards base, decurrent along petiole, obtuse or acuminate at apex, the very tip retuse, emarginate, or entire, margin revolute; the blade chartaceous or subcoriaceous, grayish-green, shining, glabrous or pubescent with spreading hairs 0.05-0. l(-0.2) mm at base and midvein below, venation brochidodromous, midvein usually plane and longitudinally wrinkled above, principal veins prominulous. Racemes 1 or 2 per branch, subterminal, erect, 5-40 × 1.5-2.5(-3) cm, in fruit to 45 cm long, many-flowered, developing acri- and basipetally; rachis 1-1.5 mm thick, glabrous or puberulous with hairs 0.1 mm long; bracts and bractlets depressedly triangular, to 0.7 mm long, subglabrous; pedicels inserted at 70-90°, 2.5-9(-11) × 0.5-1 mm, indument like that of rachis; bractlets (2-)3-4, alternate or subopposite at variable height. Flowers 7-9 mm in diam.; calyx 5-lobed; lobes separate, depressedly ovate or suborbicular, 0.4-0.7 × 0.9-1 mm, rounded, thinly coriaceous, glabrous; petals cochlear to subvalvate, 3-3.9 × 1.7-2.4 mm, at tip inflexed through 0.7 mm, slightly carinate above, coriaceous, yellowish-green, shining underneath, glabrous but beneath in bud often beset with hairs 0.05 mm long, venation actinodromous, median nerve thicker; filaments truncate, flattened, 2-3 × 0.3-0.5 mm, yellowish-green; anthers ovoid, heart-shaped or suborbicular, recurved, (1-) 1.2-1.5 × (0.8-) 1-1.5 mm, with a dorsal gland 0.2-0.5 mm; disc 0.5-1 mm high and 2-3 mm in diam., irregularly 10-plicate, glabrous to mostly strigose with yellowish-tawny, hyaline hairs 0.1-0.4 mm; carpels 0.7-0.9 mm high, protruding 0.3-0.6 mm beyond the disc, indument like that of the disc, with internal glands; ovule 1 per carpel; style at anthesis obsolete to 0.1 mm long and 0.7 mm thick, after anthesis to 0.2 mm long; stigma subsessile, capitate, 0.2-0.5 × 0.5-0.7 mm. Mericarps ellipsoidal or obovoid, (6-)7-15 × (5-)7-14 mm, dorso-apically rounded, blunt or rounded at very apex, with glands to 0.5 mm, glabrous but young and sterile ones usually sparsely strigillose, dehiscent to 1/3-1/2 below tip; seed 1 per mericarp, ellipsoidal, 7.7-12 × 4.3-8.5 × 3.8-4 mm, at apex curved or not, ventral axis straight, slightly keeled on the back, testa externally flatly colliculate with angular interspaces 0.05-0.1 mm; hilum in the upper part of the ventral axis, ca. 2.5-3 × 1.2-1.3 mm; embryo 1 or 2, if 1: provided with 2 or 3 cotyledons (or the third cotyledon belonging to a second, incomplete embryo?), if 2: provided with 4 or 2 cotyledons, dirty greenish, (one of them) large, with or without an internal, small, thin cotyledon and an external, large cotyledon ca. 8 × 4.6 × 3 mm with ears 0.4-1 mm long, radicle 1.1-1.2 mm long, projecting or enclosed, plumule 0.3-0.7 mm long; radicle and especially the plumule (rather densely) strigose with tawny, hyaline hairs 0.05-0.4 mm, or subglabrous; the second embryo, if any, smaller, with an external cotyledon ca. 6.5 × 3.5 × 1.5 mm, glabrous.

description: Rami novelli tomentosi usque ± subvillosi, indumento persistente, vulgo nonnullis lenticellis conspersi. Perulae nullae. Folia imparipinnata vel pinnata uno foliolo paris ultimi ad instar folioli terminalis ordinato, 23-42 cm longa; petiolus cum rhachide semiteres, tomentosus vel villosus; petiolulus 1-2 mm longus. Foliola alterna vel subopposita, 6-9, oblanceolata, apice abrupte attenuata usque breviter acuminata, basi anguste cuneata, interdum abrupte in petiolulum abeun-tia, chartacea, margine interdum revoluta, 18-35[25.6] cm longa, 5-12[8.2] cm lata, supra secus costam nervosque secundarios dense pubescentia, subtus ubique tomentosa vel villosa, margine dense pubescentia, nonnumquam obscure glanduloso-punctata et -striata; venatio eucamptodroma, costa prominente; nervi se-cundarii 22-28 utroque costae latere, adscendentes, recti vel subarcuati, paralleli, intersecundarii breves, tertiarii obscuri, obliqui. Flores unisexuales (planta dioica); inflorescentia axillaris, vulgo plures in brevi surculo fasciculatae, plantae [male] 9-19	cm longa, in paniculam graciliusculam multifloram disposita, plantae [female] ca. 3 cm longa, pauciflore paniculata, dense pubescens usque villosa; pedicellus ca. 0.5 mm crassus. Calyx cyathiformis, 1-1.5 mm longus, vadosissime et obtuse 5-lobatus vel margine ± truncatus, grosse puberulus. Petala 5, libera vel fere ad dimidium coalita, valvata, dein reflexa, 4.5-6 mm longa, 1-1.5 mm lata, oblonga usque lanceolata, apice acuta, nonnumquam cucullata, extus dense adpresso-pu-bescentia usque sericea. Tubus stamineus urceolatus, cyathiformis vel breviter cylindricus, filamentis toto coalitis, 2-5 mm longus, 1.25-2 mm latus, margine 8-10-lobatus	(lobis brevibus, acutis, alternantibus cum antheris et longitudinem suam 1/3 attingentibus), glaber; antherodia gracilia, polline expertia, non dehis-centia. Nectarium nullum. Ovarium ovoideum, (2-)3(-4)-loculare, dense pubescens; loculi (l-)2 ovulis collateralibus; stylus glaber; styli capitulum capitatum, ima antherodia aequans; pistillodium gracile, ovulis minoribus abortivis instructum, styli capitulo antheris breviore. Fructus ignotus.

description: Young branches puberulous or short pubescent, soon becoming glabrous, greyish-white, usually without lenticels. Bud scales absent. Leaves digitately 2-4-foliolate; petiole 1.5-2.2 cm long, semiterete, sparsely puberulous or glabrous; petiolule 1-2 mm long or leaflets subsessile. Leaflets 2-4, oblanceolate or cuneiform, apex truncate, rounded or obtuse, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, coriaceous, 5-7.5[6] cm long, 2-3[2.5] cm broad, glabrous, not glandular-punctate or -striate; venation craspedodromous with a prominent marginal vein, midrib ± flat; secondaries 12-20 on either side of midrib, ascending, straight and parallel; intersecondaries long; tertiary reticulum prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence axillary, 2-4 cm long, a small slender thyrse with lateral branches 2-3 mm long, puberulous or short pubescent; pedicel 0.5-1 mm long. Calyx shallowly cyathform, 1-1.25 mm long, with 4-5 shallow triangular, obtuse or acute lobes 1/4-1/3 length of calyx, short pubescent. Petals 4-5, free or fused just above base, valvate, 2.5-3 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, oblong or narrowly elliptic, apex acute, hooded, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Staminal tube cyathiform, 1.5-1.75 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad; filaments completely fused, margin with 8 short acute lobes alternating with anthers and ca. 1/4 their length, glabrous; anthers 8, ca. 0.8 mm long, glabrous. Nectary absent. Ovary ovoid or conical, 2-3-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, densely hirsute or strigose; style stout, glabrous at apex; style-head small, capitate, below anthers. Capsule oblong, base and apex rounded, smooth, densely coarse pubescent, ca. 1.9 cm long, 1.2 cm broad, 3-valved, valves slightly reflexed; pericarp ca. 0.5 mm thick; endocarp thin-cartilaginous. Seeds 2 in each fruit, ca. 1 cm long, oblong, partially surrounded by a free arillode; seed coat thin and soft. Embryo with plano-convex, collateral cotyledons, radicle apical, included. Endosperm absent.

description: Cataphylla nulla; stipulae persistentes; Petioli 2.0-7.0 mm longi; laminae foliorum ellipticae 1.6-5.5(-7.5) cm longae, 0.8-1.9(-2.6) cm latae (1.8-)1.9-3.3-plo longiores quam latiores basi cuneatae rotundataeve obliquaeve utrinque glabrae praeter nervos nervis utrinque atrocastaneis; pedicelli fructiferi demum, 9.0-15.0 mm longi vel rarissime breviores; cupula floralis sub fructudemum integra; drupa 5.0-6.0 mm diametro; putamina 3.

description: Shrub 1.0-1.5(-3.0) m tall. Bark dark-colored. Branchlets rarely longer than 15.0 cm, straight, with leaves not crowded and with hairs of 0.5-0.7 mm long dense terminally and decreasing. Bud-scales absent. Stipules with pubescence similar to stem, dark-colored and persistent. Petioles 2.0-7.0 mm long with pubescence similar to or somewhat denser than portion of stem giving rise thereto. Leaf-blades firm-textured, flexible to no more than a 45° angle; 1.6-5.5(-7.5) cm long, 0.8-1.9(-2.6) cm wide; elliptic with a width of 0.3-0.5(-0.56) that of length; base rounded or cuneate or oblique; apex obtuse (usually small leaves) or acute (usually medium-sized leaves) or acuminate (mostly large leaves); margin plane to slightly revolute, crenate to serrate with teeth (4-)5-8(-9) per cm and rather inconspicuous, mucro present or lacking; above glabrous except for midrib with sparse to moderate amounts of hairs up to 0.7 mm long, usually dull olive green with dark reddish-brown veins imparting a somewhat bronzed overall appearance; beneath glabrous except for midrib and sometimes secondary veins with hairs similar to that above, paler colored; secondary veins 6-12 pairs. No flowers observed. Fruits 1 per axil, pedicels rarely shorter than 9.0 mm and up to 15.0 mm in length and sparsely beset with hairs; floral cup circular at upper margin with hairs like those of pedicel; other floral parts not seen; fruits 5-6 mm in diam, black or dark brown in prepared specimens, glabrous, 3-seeded.

description: Subshrubs 1.5-2 m tall, the stems scabridulous with sparse stellate hairs and with minute glandular hairs on younger growth. Leaf blades broadly ovate (with reduced upper leaves sometimes hastately or palmately lobed), truncate or cordate, serrate, acute or acuminate, palmately 7-9-nerved, minutely pubescent (the hairs of the upper surface 0.2-0.3 mm long, simple, bifurcate, or stellate), those of the lower surface somewhat larger and with scattered 3-4-armed spicules, mostly 4-13 x 3-10 cm; petioles 1-4(-7) cm long, stellate-scabridulous and adaxially bearded; stipules triangular or falcate, 3-7 x 2 mm, often reflexed. Flowers generally in a terminal panicle; pedicels 0.5-3 cm long, slender; involucellar bracts 5(-6), linear, 5-7 x 1 mm, sparsely pubescent; calyx 4-6 mm long, short-ciliate; corolla 8-11 mm long, yellow, pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column 4-5 mm long (ca. half the length of the petals), glabrous, pallid, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles exserted from column, subequal to petals, connate nearly to apex, the stigmas scarcely separated. Fruits 4 mm diam., glabrous, unornamented.

description: Annual subshrubs to 1.5 m tall, the stems with dense longitudinal lines of minute recurved hairs, densely to sparsely setose with simple hairs 0.5-1 mm long and with underlying minute glandular hairs especially on younger stems. Leaf blades ovate to more or less hastate, 3-9 x 2.5-8 cm, narrower upward, basally cordate to truncate, crenate-dentate, acute, palmately 5-7-nerved, the upper surface with appressed or suberect simple hairs 0.5-1 mm long especially on the nerves, the lower surface similar and with scattered 3-armed stellate spicules; petioles 1-4 cm long (shorter upward), densely bearded on adaxial side, otherwise sparsely setose; stipules 3-7 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, more or less reflexed, ciliate. Pedicels solitary in the leaf axils, 1-3 cm long, setose and with underlying minute recurved hairs; involucellar bracts 12-14, arcuate, 10-20 x ca. 0.5 mm, prominently ciliate (hairs 2-3 mm long) and with minute glandular hairs; calyx 5-7 mm long, shallowly 5-lobed, ciliate and with minute glandular hairs; petals yellow, 1.5-2 cm long(?), the genitalia included. Fruits 8-9 mm diam., subglabrous; mericarps 3.5-4 mm tall, obovoid, blackish, weakly reticulate-veined.

description: Decumbent subshrubs to 0.5 m tall, the stems often reddish, minutely glandular-pubescent and sometimes also with scattered setae. Leaf blades ovate-triangular, mostly 1.5-3.5 x 10-22 mm, basally cordate, irregularly serrate, acute or acuminate, essentially concolorous, palmately 5-nerved, the upper surface with minute glandular hairs to glabrate, the margin minutely glandular-ciliate, the lower surface with minute glandular hairs and widely scattered 3-armed spicules 1.5 mm diam. (the spicules sometimes lost in age); petioles 1-2.5 cm long; stipules subulate, 3 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2.5-6 cm long; involucellar bracts 6-8, linear, 8-14 x 0.5-1 mm, viscid and also setose; calyx 5-8 mm long, setose, with white intercostal areas; corolla 1-1.5 cm long, yellow, glabrous on margins of claw; staminal column 6 mm long, pallid, the filaments 1 mm long; styles yellowish, exceeding the staminal column by 2-3 mm. Fruits oblate, 6-7 mm diam., minutely punctulate and scabridulous along suture, otherwise glabrous, more or less reticulate-veined; seeds striate, glabrous, 3 mm long.

description: Delicate subshrubs or perennial herbs from a woody rootstock, probably ascending or scandent, the stems slender, minutely and obscurely stellate-pubescent and with narrow longitudinal lines of dense curled hairs. Leaf blades narrowly lance-elliptic or lance-oblong, mostly 25-50 x 3-7 mm, mostly 6-10 times as long as wide (except juvenile leaves shorter and wider, broadly elliptic or sometimes suborbicular), basally truncate or subcordate, shallowly serrulate to subentire, acute, palmately 3-nerved or penninerved, somewhat discolorous, minutely stellate-pubescent on both surfaces; petioles 2-4 cm long (longer on juvenile leaves); stipules subulate, 2-3 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 3-8 mm long; involucellar bracts ca. 10, narrowly oblanceolate, 2-5 x 0.5 mm or less, ciliate; calyx 2.5-4(-6) mm long, stellate-pubescent and ciliate; corolla 8-11 mm long, yellow, glabrous (including margins of claw); staminal column slightly shorter than corolla, glabrous, apparently asymmetrically declined, the anthers subsessile; styles and stigmas subequal to corolla or slightly exserted. Fruits oblate, 4.5-6 mm diam., 3.5-4 mm high, with appressed simple and bifurcate hairs (rarely glabrous), the apex rounded, the two lateral spines usually suppressed (e.g., Shafer 10483) or up to 1.5 mm long with a few retrorse hairs; seeds glabrous, not striate.

description: Shrubs 1-1.5 m tall, the stems densely tomentose, the hairs stellate, 0.5-1.5 mm long. Leaf blades ovate, mostly 4-9 x 3-8 cm, basally cordate, crenate-dentate (or subentire in juvenile leaves), acute to subobtuse, palmately 7-9-nerved, discolorous, the upper surface stellate-tomentose, the lower surface more densely so and with larger 3-4-armed spicules scattered among the softer hairs; petioles 2.5-5 cm long; stipules subulate, 4 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-5.5 cm long, slender; involucellar bracts 6 (rarely 7), broadly spatulate to subrotund, 6-10 x 4-6.5 mm, obtuse or acute, softly tomentose, more densely so toward base; calyx 5-7 mm long, wooly-pubescent; corolla 1.5-2(-3) cm long, externally stellate-pubescent, yellow (without red center, or with weakly developed red center in Hassler 11070); androecium subequal to corolla or shorter. Fruits 7-8 mm diam., oblate, 10-ribbed, subglabrous but obscurely scabridulous along ridges; mericarps 3.5 mm high, dehiscent.

description: Shrubs or trees up to 6 m tall, the stems with narrow longitudinal lines of curled hairs 0.5-1 mm long, otherwise subglabrous. Leaf blades elliptic, mostly 4-11 x 2-5 cm, basally rounded or subtruncate, manifestly or obscurely serrate to entire, acute or acuminate, penninerved (the midrib raised above and beneath), glabrous above, very sparsely stellate-pubescent beneath especially on veins, sometimes vernicose beneath; petioles 7-11 mm long, densely bearded on adaxial surface, otherwise subglabrous; stipules 3-13 mm long, subulate, erect, deciduous. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels (7-) 12-15 cm long, slender, sparsely pubescent, the hairs mostly simple, ca. 1 mm long, more abundant on adaxial surface and at distal end; involucellar bracts 8-10, linear-lanceolate to spatulate, more or less incurved, 17-23 x 1-2 mm, sometimes ciliate (densely so at juncture with pedicel), connate basally for 1-1.5 mm; calyx 9-12 mm long, sparsely ciliate, the lobes prominently 3-nerved; corolla 1.5 cm long, yellowish, ca. 7 mm wide distally, with long narrow claw; androecium subequal to corolla, the filaments 1-2 mm long. Fruits 8-9 mm diam., subglabrous; mericarps 5-6 mm high, smooth and rounded, obscurely crested apically.

description: Shrubs 1.5-3 m tall, the stems with whitish hairs 0.5-1 mm long and with an understory of minute stellate hairs. Leaf blades elliptic or oblong-elliptic, mostly 10-19 x 3-6 cm, basally cuneate, obscurely serrate to subentire, acuminate, penninerved, the midrib raised above and beneath, with minute stellate (sublepidote) pubescence to glabrate; petioles 0.5-3.5 cm long, adaxially pubescent; stipules single or often divided into 2-3 unequal elements, ligulate to falcate, 15-19 x 2-5 mm, erect, with minute stellate (sublepidote) hairs, sometimes also ciliate, the cilia 1-1.5 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, often at terminal nodes above the leaves, the pedicels 2-3.5 cm long; involucellar bracts 4, broadly ovate, deeply cordate at base, 2.5-3.5 x 13-19 mm (enclosing and concealing the calyx), sparsely pubescent or sometimes ciliate, reddish; calyx 1.5-2.5 cm long, puberulent, deeply divided, the lobes with prominent midribs; corolla tubular, 2.5-3 cm long (subequal to involucel), red, externally pubescent; androecium exserted, reddish (at least distally), the filaments 3-7 mm long; styles emergent from the column. Fruits unknown.

description: Shrubs 1 m tall, the stems densely hispid, the hairs 2-3 mm long, spreading, tan. Leaf blades oblong to oblanceolate, 12-16 x 4-5 cm, basally narrowly truncate, entire or irregularly undulate, acuminate, penninerved, the midrib raised beneath and somewhat hispid near base, the blade otherwise glabrous; petioles 4-7 mm long, densely hispid like stem; stipules narrowly ligulate, sometimes double, 10-15 x 1.5-2 mm, attenuate, ciliate, persistent or tardily deciduous. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 4-6 cm long, hispid like stem and with minute underlying glandular hairs; involucellar bracts 5-7, ovate to lanceolate, 12-15 x 5-7 mm, glandular-pubescent; calyx 7-8 mm long (concealed by the involucel), glandular pubescent; petals shorter than the calyx, 4-5 mm wide; staminal column subequal to petals, the filaments 2 mm long, distally inserted, purplish; styles emergent from the column by 5 mm, purplish, the stigmas capitate. Fruits unknown.

description: Glabrous shrub. Branchlets very slender, striate lengthwise. Leaves elliptic to elliptic-oblong, rarely narrowly so, apex gradually attenuate or subacuminate, tip subacute, base acutely attenuate, the very base decurrent to the petiole, firmly chartaceous, grayish-olivaceous and somewhat shining above when dry, sparsely tuberculate on both surfaces, edge a little revolute, (2-)4-6 x (1-) 1.5-2 cm, in sterile shoots to 10 x 5 cm, midrib a little raised above, more distinctly so beneath, lateral nerves 5-6 pairs rather straight from the midrib, curved-ascending and looping before the margin, slightly prominent on both surfaces, reticulation of veins visibly raised above only; petiole 2-3 mm long. Flower(s) 1 or usually 2 on top of solitary axillary very slender peduncles (8-15 mm long), sessile; bracteoles of the epicalyx more or less completely connate into a shallowly lobed ciliolate cup 1 mm long. Corolla whitish-green except its purple base, ovate-cylindric and 5(-5.5) mm long in the dolichostylous flowers, 5-lobed in the upper 1/3, lobes ovate-triangular, reflexed. Corolla in the brachystylous flowers more cylindrical, 4.5-5 mm long, and lobed to ¼ only. Disk and top of ovary glabrous. Drupe ellipsoid, red, turning black, (10-) 12 x 8-9 mm.

description: Frutices; cataphylla nulla; laminae foliorum (5.8-)8.0-l 1.6(-12.8) cm longae, (2.1-)3.0-4.6 cm latae, margine planae conspicue serratae vel dentatae, dentibus amplitudine formaque irregularibus nonnunquam mucronatis, supra sparse vel modice pubescentes subtus modice pubescentes, costa et nervi secundarii pubescentiis densioribus; petioli 4.0-20.0 mm longi; stipulae 1.5-2.5 mm longae; inflorescentia axillaris sessilis saepe 3-floris; pedicelli per anthesin 4.0-5.0 mm longi, demum 6.0-11.0 mm longi; flores 5-meri hermaphroditi, cupula floralis 1.5-2.0 mm longa 2.5 mm lata; sepala 1.5-2.0 mm longa, 1.01.25 mm lata, petala ca 1.0 mm longa; fructi 1-3 in quoque axilla, 6-8 diametro, trispermi.

description: Shrub or tree up to 4.5 m tall. Branchlets with dark gray or dark, pubescence tawny, tomentulose terminally to glabrate to few cm below leafbearing portion; leaf-scars prominent; lenticels somewhat conspicuous. Bud-scales absent. Stipules 1.5-2.5 mm long, pubescent, persistent at leaf-bearing nodes or not; petioles 4.0-20.0 mm long with moderate to moderately heavy pubescence; leaf-blades (5.8-)8.0-11.6(-12.8) cm long, (2.1-)3.0-4.6 cm wide, elliptic, less commonly obovate-elliptic or oblong; base cuneate to rounded; apex acuminate (acumen ca 1.0 cm long) or less commonly acute; margin plane, conspicuously serrate or dentate with teeth irregular in size and shape, 5-10 per cm, sometimes mucronate; above with very sparse to moderate amounts of pubescence between veins, somewhat denser on the major veins; beneath with moderate amounts of pubescence with hairs generally more numerous, longer, and coarser than above, midrib and secondary veins with somewhat more hairs than between veins especially on lateral margin, yellowish and conspicuous; secondary veins 8-11 pairs. Inflorescences sessile axillary umbels of usually 3 flowers, pedicels 4.0-5.0 mm long, floral cup 1.52.0mm deep, 2.5 mm broad; sepals 5,1.5-2.0 mm long, 1.0-1.2mm broad; petals 5, ca 1.0 mm long; ovary usually glabrous (pubescent only on King and Soderstrom 5103 and 5041 and Hinton 6552). Fr 1 -3 per axil; pedicels 6.0-11.0 mm long elongating after anthesis; cup with margin circular and undulant; fruits 6-8 mm in diam, glabrous or pubescent, 3-stoned.

description: Slender glabrous shrub, 2.5-4 m tall. Branchlets compressed, distinctly longitudinally ridged, often flexuous, divaricate, early corticate. Leaves elliptic, oblong-or ovate-elliptic, apex rounded, very tip shortly subglandular-apiculate, base broadly attenuate to rounded, occasionally subcordate, coriaceous, stiff, dark brown or olivaceous when dry, lustrous mainly above, sparsely or not tuberculate on both surfaces, edge markedly revolute, (1.5-)2-3.5(-4.2) x (0.5-)1.5-2.5(-3) cm, midrib plane or slightly immersed above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves (4-)5-6 pairs rather straight from the midrib, irregularly divergent, obscurely looping before the margin, usually faintly raised on both surfaces in fully mature leaves (slightly impressed in very young ones!), sometimes evanescent, as is the coarse reticulation of veins; petiole transversely rugulose, (1-)2-3 mm long. Peduncles solitary from foliate axils, slender, glabrous, nodding, (6-)8-12 mm long, bearing on top 2(rarely 3) sessile flowers. Epicalyx cup-shaped, shortly sinuately 3-lobed, 1.5 mm long. Flower-axis 1.5 mm high. Corolla only known in the brachystylous form (Ekman 4050), subovate-cylindrical, 4.5 mm long, 5-lobed in the upper 1/3, the lobes erect. Disk and top of ovary glabrous. Drupe ellipsoid, glabrous, 8-10 x 6-7 mm.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 1-8 (rarely to 16) m tall; young branchlets subangular or terete, subglabrous or sparsely stellate-pubescent. Leaves in whorls of 3 or opposite; petioles 0.7-5 cm long; lamina drying reddish brown, oblanceolate to obovate, rarely broadly elliptic, coriaceous, 8-14(-26.5) X 2.7-5 (-11) cm, the base and apex acute to obtuse, the tip 0.5-0.8 cm long, leaves above and below with few minute appressed stellate to sublepidote hairs, occasionally glabrescent, young leaves above sometimes with conspicuous appressed silvery stellate-lepidote hairs, with 9-12 pairs of secondary veins, these flat above, distinctly raised below, the margin serrulate or serrate. Cymes 2.5-4 cm long and often pendent, pubescent like the young branchlets, with 10-15 flowers. Fresh flowers greenish yellow or whitish; male floral cup broadly obconical to semiglobose, 2-2.9 mm in diam., 1.5-2.5 mm high, glabrous except for a few appressed bifid or few-branched hairs, the tepals 4-5(-6), narrowly oblong to almost spatulate, 2-4 mm long (Fig. 46b), the floral roof distinctly raised, and glabrous; stamens 9-12; female floral cup subglobose, 3.5-4 mm in diam., 3-3.5 mm high, the pubescence as in the male flowers, the tepals triangular or broadly triangular, ca. 1.4 mm long, the floral roof raised to a cylindrical bulge separated by a groove from an acute central tube sheathing the styles (Fig. 46f), drying dark brown; styles 2-5. Fruiting receptacle 1-1.5 cm in diam., globose and usually with minute (less than 1 mm long) blunt protuberances basally, when fresh and mature red with small cream spots (lenticels) and a strong lemon smell; drupelets 1-3, each with a sty lar aril.

description: Dioecious tree let, 4-5 m tall; branchlets distinctly quadrangular, with four raised longitudinal ridges, flattened at the nodes, with short, simple or few-branched hairs. Leaves opposite; petioles 2.5-9.5 cm long; lamina drying greenish brown, papery and brittle, broadly obovate, 26-37 X 17-19 cm, the base obtuse, rounded, or truncate, the apex short-acuminate, both surfaces with scarce short simple (cf. Fig. 4A), bi or trifid hairs, with 16-18 pairs of secondary veins, these flat above, distinctly raised below, the margin denticulate, the teeth most pronounced near the lamina base. Cymes up to 7.5 cm long in the male, 3- or 4-branched, often on leafless nodes, with 10-12 flowers, pubescent like the branchlets. Fresh flowers yellowish; male floral cup subglobose, 1.3-2.1 mm in diam., 1.1-1.6 mm high, with short (0.05-0.2 mm long) simple to three-branched whitish hairs, some of these also on the tepal surfaces and margins, the 4 tepals spatulate to oblong, 3-10 X 1.5-3.5 mm, the floral roof moderately raised, glabrous; stamens 2224; female floral cup 3.3-3.7 mm in diam., 3-3.5 mm high, the floral roof tightly surrounding the styles; styles 15-20. Fruiting receptacle immature globose and smooth, mature fruits unknown.

description: Shrub, to 2.5 m tall; stems with a mix of glandular and nonglandular setae, the trichomes 1.0-2.0 mm long, caducous, the nodes glabrous. Leaves isophyllous, oblong to oblong-ovate, 10-25 X 5-13 cm, apex acuminate to abruptly acuminate, base cordate, the sinus up to 10 mm long, adaxial surface sparsely glandular- setose, abaxial surface sparsely glandular-pubescent, densely hirsute to glandular-setose on the primary and secondary veins, light green, (5-)7-plinervate, chartaceous, slightly ciliolate-serrulate; petioles 2-11 cm long, glandular; domatia immersed in the leaf blade, with base of blade attached to adaxial surface, ovoid, 1.5-2.0(-3.0) X 1.0-1.7 cm, 4-lobulate on the abaxial side. Inflorescence a terminal panicle, of 6-15(-20) flowers, 8-12 cm long, the axis green, flattened, sparsely glandular-setose, each dichasium subtended by early caducous, suborbicular bracts, up to 3 cm long. Flowers on pedicels 2-6 mm long, flared at the apex, subtended by caducous bracts, elliptic to obovate, 20-30 X 15-30 mm, the margins ciliate; hypanthium broadly conical to globose, 6 mm long, sparsely or densely glandular-setose; outer calyx teeth highly reduced, 0.2-0.5 mm long, not projecting above the inner teeth, inner calyx teeth deltoid to ovate, 1.5-3.0 mm long, fused at the base 1.5-2.1 mm, glandular-setose; the ring inside the torus glabrous; petals 5, obovate, 13-14 X 8-9 mm, base attenuate, apex emarginate, pruinose, with an apical, caduceus, glandular seta, pink; stamens all the same size; filaments 7.5-8.0 mm long, glabrous; anthers blue; the connective with a dorsal-basal blunt tooth; thecae 7 mm long, opening by a dorsally inclined pore; ovary 3-locular, ½ inferior, the superior portion conical, the apex with a glandular-pubescent collar; style glabrous, 15-17 mm long; stigma capitate, 1.5 mm wide. Fruits urceolate, 18-23 mm long, blue, densely glandular-pubescent; seeds not evident through the pericarp, narrowly ovate, 2.2-2.8 mm long, with capitate trichomes in the raphal area, without sculpturing, anticlinal walls straight, periclinal walls flat, boundaries between periclinal walls flat.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 3-6 m tall; branchlets somewhat angular and with distinct large lenticels, the nodes bearing an 0.5-2 mm wide collar or interpetiolar ridge. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.5-2 cm long; lamina drying dark brown, brittle, narrowly elliptic or obovate, 15-21 X 5-8.5 cm, the base cuneate, the apex acute or blunt, both surfaces with scarce short simple or few-branched hairs, 0.05-0.2 mm long, with 11-14 pairs of secondary veins, these flat above, slightly raised below, the margin subentire or finely denticulate. Cymes 2.5-3 cm long, few-branched (Fig. 75B) and with the same indumentum as the leaves, with 5-15 flowers. Fresh flowers greenish yellowish; male floral cup broadly obconical, about 2 mm in diam., 1.5 mm high, the tepals broadly triangular or lobed, adaxially glabrous, the floral roof distinctly raised and glabrous; stamens 9-10, containing large yellow or whitish oil inclusions; female floral cup of the same size and shape, the floral roof flat and tightly sheathing the styles; styles 5-7. Fruiting receptacle globose, 1.5-2 cm in diam., sometimes with minute warts and crowned by the persistent tepals, when fresh and mature apparently cream (Madison et al. 3456).

description: Shrub, or tree, to 20 m tall. Young branches sparsely appressed villous, glabrescent, with rounded to elliptic lenticels 0.2-0.8 mm, not conspicuous, the older branches with bark grayish on the surface and with small vertical fissures, inside greenish; wood cream colored. Leaves alternate, subopposite, or decussate; lamina thickly coriaceous, elliptic to narrowly ovate or obovate, 2.5-5.7 × 1.3-2.5 cm; base cuneate to obtuse, rarely attenuate, slightly decurrent; apex rounded obtuse, the margin revolute and thickened; midrib slightly tortuous towards tip; lateral veins 6-8 pairs, the upper surface glabrous, the lower surface usually glabrous or shortly appressed-tomentose; midrib sometimes more pubescent toward base; venation conspicuously reticulate beneath; petioles 3-5(-7) × 0.5-1 mm glabrescent. Inflorescences terminal, compound racemes, the principal axis 2.2-5 cm, secondary axes 3-8, 1.1-5.5 cm long; raceme-subtending bracts 2-6 mm, leaflike or filiform. Pedicels 3-6(-7.7) mm, tomentulose. Flowers with a strong fragrance of myrtle; tepals 3.5-5 mm, white, outside appressed-puberulous or appressed-tomentulose; filaments 3-3.5 mm, free; anthers 0.9-1 mm; disk cupular, 0.8 mm, the sinuses broadly rounded to slightly subcordate; ovary ca 0.9-1.2 mm, tomentose to sericeous, hairs pale, 0.5 mm; style 3-3.5 mm. Mature fruit unknown. Diagnostic characters. The tortuous midrib and the small leaves with revolute margins distinguish this species from Panopsis polystachya and P. pearcei, to which it is most similar. It is also very close to P. omatinervia, from which it differs in the tortuous midrib and more reticulate venation.

description: Tree, (6-)18-30m tall. Branch bark gray to beige peeling to dark red-gray or dark brown, the indumentum rufous-velutinous, persistent on new growth unit, patchy at region separating previous growth unit and current one, slowly glabrescent. Lenticels few to numerous, minute to 0.5 mm diam., granular, plane, rufous to brown. Leaves simple, sometimes bilobed, thin-coriaceous, glaucous above, pale green-brown beneath, matte, the indumentum appressed, ferruginous-pilose above, glabrescent, dense rufous-velutinous below, the hairs persistent, especially towards base of lamina and along midrib and lateral veins. Petiole not well defined, (1.5-)2.5-7(-8) cm long × 1.1-1.5 mm broad at midlength, 1/1.6-1/4.5, terete at base, semi-terete towards lamina, flattening out above or at times sulcate, rufous velutinous over entire petiole in leaves of current growth unit, hairs persistent near the base adaxially, fading to gray in mature leaves. Lamina 4.5-12(-14) × 3-7.5(-9) cm, length:breadth 1.2-2(-2.5):1, suborbiculate or wide-elliptic, rarely elliptic; base 90° to obtuse (more rarely, acute or rounded), strongly decurrent onto petiole, usually symmetrical; apex mostly obtuse-acuminate, less frequently rounded, attenuate, or emarginate, often folded, the mid vein not protruding; margin entire to slightly undulate, revolute at the base, less pronounced towards the apex; venation obscure above, the midrib and lateral veins plane to slightly impressed, conspicuous and prominent below, eucamptodromous to craspedodromous, the secondary veins joining to form faint marginal vein, lateral veins (3-)4-5(-7) pairs, diverging from midrib at 30-40° at base to 20-30° apically, at times branching halfway between the midrib and margin, and again near the margin, the midvein reaching the apex. Inflorescences (3.6-)8.5-13.5 × 1.5-2.5 cm, axillary, unbranched, rufous-velutinous, the flower-pairs densely clustered; peduncle 0.4-1.5 cm × 1.5-2 mm, few to many sterile bracts at the base. Common bracts 1-1.3 × 0.7-1.5 mm, dense, rufous, tomentose-strigose to the outside, glabrous within. Flower-pair axis absent. Pedicels 1-2.3 × 0.6-1 mm, the indumentum sparse, straggly, rufous to ferruginous-tomentose to dense velutinous. Buds 1-1.5 mm broad at the apex, ca. 0.5 mm broad at midlength, the indumentum as for pedicels. Flowers 7-10 mm long; filaments 0-1.5 mm long, adnate 4.5-7 mm from base of tepals; anthers 2-2.8 × 0.50.8 mm; nectary lobes 0.4 mm long, separated; ovary 1-2 × 0.7-1.3 mm, the indumentum long, sericeous-villous, the hairs rufous to pale ferruginous, extending 1.3-1.5 mm from base of ovary, covering entire ovary, erect to appressed; ovules 0.4-0.6 × 0.2-0.3 mm. Infructescence 11-14 cm long, short rufous-tomentose; fruit pedicel 4 × 2 mm, sparser than rhachis. Fruit 5-6 × 2 cm, elongate, both sutured and unsutured sides curved equally, base constricted for 0.5-1.2 cm, the apex not constricted or constricted ca. 1 mm, curved strongly, sutured margin commonly thinner, set in, purple to rufous velutinous, glabrescent, persistent at the base, rugulose, mid brown beneath, style not persistent. Seed 4 × 1.7 cm, apical end thicker for 1.2 cm.

description: Tree, to 31(> 45) m tall. Stems thin, spindly; bark gray superficially, dark red-brown to black beneath, the indumentum dense to pilose at the apices of new twigs, the hairs orange-brown, rapidly glabrescent. Lenticels numerous, minute (< 0.5 mm diam.), inconspicuous, granular, becoming raised, orange-brown to brown. Leaves simple, chartaceous, short-petiolate, drying brown, matte or shiny above, minutely bullate (white gland dots on new leaves); the young leaf indumentum pilose, with short hairs above, yellow to orange-brown, long hairs beneath, rufous, more abundant along lower midrib, with orange to red specks on lower lamina when trichomes have broken off. Petiole not well defined, 0.5-1 (-1.5) cm long × ca. 1 mm broad at midlength, 1/51/7 the length of the lamina, subterete, the lamina sides descending to base, glabrous. Lamina 4.5-15 × 2-4.5 cm, length:breadth 2-3.5(-4):1, oblong to narrow-oblong, sometimes elliptic; base cuneate (acute), usually somewhat decurrent onto petiole, pressing flat, symmetrical; apex attenuate, less frequently acute or obtuse, the apical point of midvein not protruding; margin entire, slightly undulate, revolute almost to apex; venation plane above, inconspicuous except midrib, which is paler than the rest of the lamina; midrib sometimes narrowly grooved, slightly raised beneath except prominent midrib; semicraspedodromous, with a fractiflexed marginal vein, the midvein reaching the apex; lateral veins 6-9 pairs. Inflorescence unknown. Infructescence axillary, unbranched, 8.5-9 cm long, gray to black velutinous, patchy towards the apex; fruit pedicels 2 × 1.8-2 mm, the indumentum as for infructescence. Fruit 4.7-4.8 × 1.4-1.5 cm, oblong, flat-sided, the unsutured edge flat, the sutured edge gently curved, the base constricted for 0.7-0.9 mm, the apex curved, not constricted, ending in a small point, gray, glabrous, smooth (minutely blistered), style not persistent. Seed not seen.

description: Leaves: stipules glandular and often unbranched, 3.9-4 mm long; petioles 6.5-7.5 cm long and 1.3-1.5 mm in diam.; blades 5-lobed, 11-13 x 7-8.5 cm, lobes equal in size, 3.5-3.9 cm wide, darker above, paler below, margins entire or with few serrations, villous-pubescent on both surfaces, light brown below. Inflorescences: bracts 5-7 mm, peduncles 10-13 x 8-10 cm. Staminate flowers: sepals 6.2-7.5 x 2.8-3 mm, densely pubescent on both surfaces, margins sparsely glandular; corollas whitish yellow with red apex or stripes, red in bud, 9.4-11 x 3.7-5.5 mm. Pistillate flowers: sepals 6.5-8 x 3-3.3 mm, glabrous on both surfaces; petals 11-12.3 x 5-6.3 mm.

description: Plants epiphytic; fronds pendent, indeterminate; rhizome erect, radial, with ventral root insertion, scaly the scales 1-2 x 0.1-0.3 mm, ovate-lanceolate, the apex short-attenuate, clathrate, dark golden brown, glabrous or with only a single apical cilium; petiole 0.5-2 x 0.5 mm, dark brown, narrowly winged, glabrescent or sparsely pubescent, the hairs ca. 0.1 mm long, appressed, simple, 2-celled, yellowish; lamina 10-15 cm long, linear-lanceolate, membranaceous, pinnate, 10-20 pairs of segments, abruptly reduced at the base with 2-3 basal segments shorter than the median ones, the lowermost auriculiform and long-decurrent onto petiole base, broadest above the base, but showing periodic constrictions, the apex gradually reduced, pinnatifid, not ending in a conform or sub-conform segment; rachis straight to slightly flexuous, with dark sclerenchyma visible on both sides, glabrescent abaxially, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, appressed, simple, 2-celled, yellowish, glabrescent adaxially, hairs ca. 0.1-0.2 mm long, appressed, simple, 2-celled, yellowish; segments 0.4-0.5 x 0.3-0.5 cm, sinuate, set 80-90° to rachis, widened and asymmetric at the base, long-decurrent basiscopically, strongly cuneate and slightly lobulate acroscopically, the base attached parallel on the rachis (both sides inserted along the same radius), the lobule not overlapping the base of the next segment, the apex obtuse, the margin slightly crenulate, sinuate, glabrous, abaxial lamina surface glabrescent, the hairs similar to those of the rachis abaxially, adaxial lamina surface glabrous; sinuses narrower than the segments; venation pinnate, with 2-3 (-4) pairs of veins per segment; costae with blackish sclerenchyma obscured by laminar tissue on both sides, sparsely pubescent abaxially, the hairs similar to those of the rachis abaxially, glabrous adaxially; veins simple, without blackish sclerenchyma, ending in hy-dathodes that lack calcareous deposits; sori medial, rounded, not protruding beyond the costa and margin, up to 2(-3) pairs per segment, slightly sunken; sporan-gial capsules glabrous.

description: Plants epiphytic; fronds pendent, determinate, rhizome short-creeping, dorsiventral, with ventral root insertion, scaly, the scales 3-4.5 x 0.2-0.3 mm, late, the apex long-attenuate, clathrate, golden brown ciliate, the cilia simple, present on scale margins apex (apical cilia sometimes furcate); petiole 3-8 x 0.7-1 mm, dark brown, marginate, slightly pubescent, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, spreading, 1-furcate, 2- to 3-celled, whitish; lamina 30-40(-60) cm long, lanceolate, chartaceous, pinnatisect, 20-40(-50) pairs of segments, abruptly reduced at the base, with 5-7 segments shorter than the medial ones, auriculiform, decurrent onto petiole base, broadest above the base, not showing periodic constrictions, the apex abruptly reduced, pinnatifid, not ending in a conform or subconform segment; rachis straight, with dark sclerenchyma visible only abaxially, covered by laminar tissue adaxially (not visible), glabrescent abaxially, the hairs ca. 0.1 mm long, simple, appressed, 1- to 2-celled, whitish to yellowish, glabrous to glabrescent adaxially, the hairs similar to those from the abaxial side; segments ca. 4—8(—10) x 0.2-0.3 cm, flagelliform, plane, set 35-45° to rachis, slightly asymmetric at the base, long-decurrent basiscopically, short surcurrent acroscopically, the base attached parallel on the rachis (i.e., both sides inserted along the same radius), not lobulate or overlapping the base of the next segment, the apex acute, the margin plane to sinuate, glabrous, abaxial lamina surface glabrescent, the hairs similar to those of the rachis abaxially, adaxial lamina surface glabrous; description: Evergreen, low, spreading shrub to ca. 0.5 m tall, with gray, longitudinally furrowed bark; twigs slightly angled, slender to stout, moderately lepidote, otherwise glabrous or very sparsely pubescent; buds ovoid, 1-2 x 1-1.8 mm. Leaf blades ovate to broadly elliptic to orbicular, 1.1-3.1 × 0.9-2.6 cm, ± flat, coriaceous, ca. 0.5-0.6 mm thick; base rounded to widely cuneate; apex truncate or rounded to nearly acute; margin plane to sometimes slightly revolute, apical portion obscurely and irregularly toothed, basal portion toothed to entire; venation brochidodromous, 3° veins ± reticulate; adaxial surface lepidote but scales usually quickly deciduous, sparsely pubescent on basal portion of midvein, veins obscure to sometimes faintly visible; abaxial surface moderately to densely lepidote, otherwise densely pubescent, with 2° and higher-order veins usually obscure or nearly so (only very rarely raised and forming dense, fine reticulum); scales rust colored, persistent to deciduous, ca. 0.08-0.2 mm in diam., usually ± erose; petiole 3-5 mm long, lepidote, otherwise adaxially pubescent; flower buds ± intermixed with vegetative buds. Inflorescences fasciculate, ca. 5-8-flowered; pedicels clearly articulated with calyx, slender, 2-6 mm long, lepidote, otherwise glabrous or very sparsely pubescent; bracteoles ± opposite, basal, narrowly triangular, 1.5-2 mm long; floral bracts to ca. 2.5 mm long. Flowers 4-5-merous; calyx lobes triangular, with acuminate apices, 1.5-2 × 0.7-1.4 mm, adaxial side pubescent, especially near apex, abaxial side lepidote, otherwise glabrous; corolla cylindrical, white, 5-6.5 × 3-4 mm, abaxially sparsely lepidote; filaments roughened, ca. 3.5 mm long, essentially unappendaged; anthers ca. 1.3 mm long; ovary lepidote, otherwise pubescent, placentae ± subapical. Capsules ± globose to short-ovoid, 3-4 × 3-4 mm, slightly lepidote, otherwise sparsely pubescent, especially near base, the pale, very thick sutures separating as unit from adjacent valves; seeds 1.4-2 mm long.

description: Evergreen, low spreading shrub to moderate-sized tree to ca. 12 m tall with gray, longitudinally furrowed bark; twigs slightly angled, slender, usually densely lepidote, otherwise glabrous; buds ovoid, 1-2 × 0.7-1.4 mm. Leaf blades widely ovate or elliptic to nearly orbicular, 1-2.5(-3.5) × 0.8-2.5(-3) cm, ± flat, coriaceous, ca. 0.29-0.4 mm thick; base cuneate to rounded or slightly cordate; apex acute to truncate (slightly acuminate); margin plane to slightly revolute, apical portion strongly to obscurely and irregularly toothed (nearly entire), basal portion obscurely toothed to entire; venation brochidodromous, 3° veins reticulate; adaxial surface often roughened due to thickened scale bases, lepidote (but scales usually quickly deciduous), sparsely pubescent on basal portion of mid vein, with 2° and 3° veins obscure, not depressed (2° veins slightly depressed); abaxial surface moderately to densely lepidote, otherwise densely pubescent, with all veins raised, forming dense and fine reticulum, often not visible without magnification; scales orange to orange-brown, persistent to less commonly deciduous, 0.12-0.34 mm in diam., usually erose; petiole 1-5 mm long, lepidote, otherwise adaxially pubescent; flower buds ± intermixed with vegetative buds. Inflorescences fasciculate, ca. 4-9-flowered; pedicels clearly articulated with calyx, slender, 2-7 mm long, lepidote, otherwise glabrous to very sparsely pubescent; bracteoles ± opposite, basal, narrowly triangular, 1-1.8 mm long; floral bracts to ca. 2 mm long. Flowers 4-5-merous; calyx lobes triangular, with acuminate apices, 0.8-1.3 × 0.4-0.8 mm, adaxial side sparsely pubescent at margins and near apex, abaxial side lepidote, otherwise glabrous; corolla cylindrical to long-urceolate, white, 3-4.5 × 1.8-2.5 mm, abaxially sparsely lepidote; filaments roughened, 1-2.7 mm long, essentially unappendaged; anthers 0.6-1 mm long; ovary lepidote, otherwise pubescent, placentae ± subapical. Capsules narrowly ovoid, (2.5-)3-4.5 × 1.5-2.5 mm, slightly lepidote, otherwise sparsely pubescent, the pale, very thick sutures separating as unit from adjacent valves; seeds 1.7-2.8 mm long.

description: Arbusto(?), ramas jóvenes levemente estriadas cerca al ápice, pubérulas o tomentosas y con pelos glandulosos, conspicuamente lenticeladas. Hojas impari-pinadas; foliolos 11-13; pecíolo 2-3.5 cm de largo, tomentoso, con pelos glandulosos; raquis 8 cm de largo, tomentoso, con pelos glandulosos. Folíolos (1-)2.2-4.3 cm de largo, (0.7-) 1.2-1.4 cm de ancho, oblongos u oblongo-elípticos, folíolos jóvenes membranosos, maduros cartáceos, haz oscura, brillante, glabres-cente, envés claro, tomentoso, base cordada, a veces levemente desigual, atenuada en el folíolo terminal, ápice agudo, apiculado o mucronado, margen revoluto; peciólulo 0.1 cm de largo; venación reticulada, más o menos difusa; nervaduras laterales 7-9 pares, formando ángulos de 60-70° (cerca a la base) y 85° (cerca al ápice) con la nervadura central. Inflorescencia paniculada, axilar a pseudoter-minal; raquila (3-)5-7 cm de largo, tomentosa, con pelos glandulosos; brácteas ca. 0.2 cm de largo, lineales, con pelos glandulosos. Pedicelo conspicua o inconspicuamente articulado, 0.5 cm de largo; sépalos 5 mm de largo, 3 mm de ancho, ovados u oblongo-ovados, densamente tomentosos y con pelos glandulosos exteriormente, tomentosos interiormente; pétalos 8 mm de largo, 2.5 mm de ancho, connados por encima de la base, glabros; filamentos unidos por ca. 1.5 mm de su longitud, 5 más largos ca. 2.5 mm de longitud, 5 más cortos ca. 1.5 mm de longitud; anteras globosas; ovario piloso; estilo tomentoso, con pelos glandulosos esparcidos; estigma capitado, bilobulado. Fruto 1.3 cm de largo, 0.5 cm de ancho, glabrescente, velloso cerca al ápice; estilo persistente, conspicuo; cáliz en fruto ascendente, 0.7 cm de largo, tomentoso, con pelos glandulosos. Semilla 0.8-1 cm de largo, ca. 0.4 cm de ancho; ariloide 0.2 cm de largo.
bibliographicCitation: Forero, Enrique. 1983. Connaraceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 36: 1-208.

description: Liana, ramas jóvenes levemente estriadas, pubérulas, lenticeladas. Hojas im-paripinadas; foliólos 5(-7); pecíolo 1-5 cm de largo, pubérulo; raquis 2-4 cm de largo, pubérulo. Foliolos 2-7 cm de largo, 1-2.5 cm de ancho, elípticos o angosto-elípticos, cartáceos, haz oscura, brillante, glabra, envés claro, opaco o algo brillante, glabro, nervadura central glabra en la haz, pubérula en el envés, base redondeada o atenuada, ápice acuminado; peciólulo 0.2-0.4 cm de largo, delgado; venación reticulada, difusa, plana o promínula en la haz, promínula en el envés; nervaduras laterales 5-8 pares, formando ángulos de 70-90° con la nervadura central, anastomosadas claramente cerca al margen. Inflorescencia paniculada, axilar o pseudoterminal; raquila 4-6 cm de largo, delgada, esparcidamente pubérula; brácteas ca. 0.1 cm de largo, lineales. Pedicelo articulado, 0.3-0.6 cm de largo; sépalos 3 mm de largo, 2 mm de ancho, ovados, esparcidamente pubérulos, margen ciliado; pétalos 5 mm de largo, 2 mm de ancho, obovado-oblongos, glabros, libres; filamentos unidos por 0.8-1 mm de su longitud, 5 más largos ca. 4.5 mm de longitud, 5 más cortos ca. 3.5 mm de longitud; anteras globosas; ovario piloso; estilo pubescente. Fruto 1.3 cm de largo, 0.6 cm de ancho, glabro, ápice velloso; cáliz en fruto 0.4 cm de largo, glabrescente, margen ciliado. Semilla 1 cm de largo, 0.6-0.7 cm de ancho; ariloide 0.3 cm de largo.

description: Bejuco, ramas jóvenes esparcidamente tomentosas. Hojas imparipinadas; foliolos 3-7; pecíolo 4-6(-10) cm de largo, tomentoso; raquis 5.5-10.5 cm de largo, tomentoso. Foliolos 6-11.5 cm de largo, 4-7 cm de ancho, anchamente elípticos, ovados u orbiculares, cartáceos (raramente subcoriáceos), haz oscura, glabra, envés claro, tomentoso, nervadura central densamente tomentosa en ambas caras, base obtusa, ápice acuminado; peciólulo 0.2-0.4 cm de largo; venación reticulada, promínula en ambas caras; nervaduras laterales 5-7 pares, formando ángulos de 50-60° con la nervadura central, anastomosadas más o menos claramente cerca al margen. Inflorescencia paniculada, pseudoterminal o axilar; raquila 8-16 cm de largo, densamente gris-tomentosa; brácteas 0.1-0.2 cm de largo, lineales, tomentosas. Pedicelo articulado, densamente tomentoso, 0.4 cm de largo; sépalos 3-4 mm de largo, 2 mm de ancho, gris-tomentosos, oscuramente glanduloso-pubescentes exteriormente, tomentosos interiormente; pétalos 5 mm de largo, 2 mm de ancho, glabros, libres; filamentos cortamente unidos, 5 más largos ca. 4 mm de longitud, 5 más cortos ca. 3 mm de longitud; anteras globosas; ovario velloso-lanado. Fruto 1.5 cm de largo, 0.5 cm de ancho, glabro, ápice esparcidamente piloso; cáliz en fruto 0.5 cm de largo, tomentoso. Semilla 1 cm de largo, 0.4 cm de ancho; ariloide 0.3 cm de largo.

description: Bejuco, arbusto escandente o pequeño árbol, ramas jóvenes pubérulas o tomentosas, conspicuamente lenticeladas. Hojas imparipinadas; foliolos 5-7; pecíolo 1-3.5 cm de largo, pubérulo; raquis 2-5 cm de largo, pubérulo a tomentoso. Foliolos 2-8.5 cm de largo, 1-4.5 cm de ancho, elípticos, rígido-cartáceos, haz oscura, glabra, envés claro, glabro, con las nervaduras laterales pubérulas o esparcidamente tomentosas, nervadura central pubérula a tomentosa en ambas caras, base cuneada, ápice acuminado; peciólulo 0.1-0.2 cm de largo, tomentoso a densamente tomentoso; venación reticulada, promínula en ambas caras; nervadura central impresa en la haz; nervaduras laterales 6-7 pares, formando ángulos de 50-80° con la nervadura central, claramente anastomosadas cerca al margen. Inflorescencia paniculada, delicada, axilar o pseudoterminal; raquila 6-10 cm de largo, glanduloso-pubérula; brácteas 0.1 cm de largo, con pelos glandulosos. Pedicelo articulado, con pelos glandulosos, 0.2-0.3 cm de largo; sépalos 3 mm de largo, 1-2 mm de ancho, esparcidamente glanduloso-pubérulos exteriormente, pubérulos interiormente; pétalos 3-4 mm de largo, 1.5-2 mm de ancho, glabros, libres; filamentos cortamente unidos, 5 más largos ca. 2 mm de longitud, 5 más cortos ca. 1 mm de longitud; anteras globosas; ovario piloso. Fruto 1-1.5 cm de largo, 0.6 cm de ancho, glabro; cáliz en fruto 0.4-0.6 cm de largo, pubérulo. Semilla 0.8-1 cm de largo, 0.4 cm de ancho; ariloide 0.3-0.4 cm de largo.

description: Pequeño árbol o bejuco leñoso, ramas jóvenes esparcidamente pubérulas, len-ticeladas. Hojas imparipinadas; foliolos (1-)3-5; pecíolo 6-9 cm de largo, a veces longitudinalmente estriado, esparcidamente pubérulo; raquis 1-9 cm de largo, raramente obsoleto, esparcidamente pubérulo, a veces longitudinalmente estriado. Foliolos 9.5-20 cm de largo, 3-9 cm de ancho, elíptico- u obovado-oblongos, subcartáceos, haz oscura, glabra, envés claro, glabro, las nervaduras esparcidamente pubérulas o tomentosas, base atenuada (raramente redondeada), ápice cuspidado; peciólulo 0.3-0.5 cm de largo; venación impresa en la haz, promínula en el envés; nervaduras laterales 5-7 pares, formando ángulos de 30-60° con la nervadura central, ascendentes; nervaduras terciarias transversales. Inflorescencia paniculada, axilar a pseudoterminal; raquila 5-8 cm de largo, pubérula; brácteas 0.15 cm de largo. Pedicelo articulado, 0.1-0.2 cm de largo, glabro; sépalos 3 mm de largo, 2 mm de ancho, anchamente ovados o suborbiculares, acuminados, glabros o glabrescentes, margen ciliado, ápice barbado; pétalos 5 mm de largo, 2 mm de ancho, glabros, libres; filamentos cortamente unidos, 5 más largos ca. 4 mm de longitud, 5 más cortos ca. 3 mm de longitud; anteras globosas; ovario lanado; estigma bilobulado. Fruto hasta 1.5 cm de largo, glabro, curvo; cáliz en fruto 0.4 cm de largo, glabrescente. Semilla 1.3 cm de largo, 0.5 cm de ancho; ariloide 0.4 cm de largo.

description: Arbusto 2.5 m de alto, ramas jóvenes estriadas, marrón pilosas, sedosas. Hojas trifolioladas; pecíolo 7-16 cm de largo, esparcida a densamente piloso; raquis 310 cm de largo, esparcida a densamente piloso. Foliolos 8-20 cm de largo, 3.5-11.5 cm de ancho, anchamente elípticos, anchamente ovados u oblongo-ovados, subcartáceos o membranosos, haz oscura, levemente brillante, glabra, envés claro, opaco, tomentoso a piloso, nervadura central esparcidamente pubérula en la haz, densamente tomentosa en el envés, base truncada (atenuada en los foliolos distales), ápice corta y abruptamente acuminado; peciólulo 0.5-0.7 cm de largo, densamente piloso; venación plana en la haz, promínula en el envés; nervaduras laterales 4-6 pares, formando ángulos de 20-50° con la nervadura central, ascendentes; nervaduras terciarias transversales. Inflorescencia paniculada, axilar a pseudoterminal; raquila 5-10 cm de largo, densamente tomentosa; brácteas grandes, hasta de 0.6 cm de largo, pilosas, triangular-lanceoladas. Flores sésiles o pedicelo 0.1 cm de largo; sépalos 2-4 mm de largo, ovados o elípticos, ápice agudo o redondeado, glabrescentes exteriormente, glabros interiormente; pétalos 4 mm de largo, 4-5 mm de ancho, anchamente obovado-oblongos, glabros, libres; filamentos libres o tubo muy corto, 5 más largos ca. 4 mm de longitud, 5 más cortos ca. 3 mm de longitud; anteras globosas; ovario piloso; estilo glabro; estigma bilobulado. Fruto desconocido.

description: Herbs, propagating by rhizomes. Leaves fasciculate, not contracted between sheath and blade; scape well developed; scape-bracts foliaceous. Inflorescence simple, densely polystichous-flowered. Floral bracts well developed; flowers perfect, sessile. Sepals free, nearly symmetric; petals free, bearing 2 scales; stamens of the second series highly adnate to the petals; pollen ellipsoid, biporate; ovary in slight part superior; ovules caudate.

description: Shrubs or trees up to ca. 4 m high, usually at least partially covered with dense indumentum; hairs unicellular, simple, often curled. Leaf venation brochidodromous. Inflorescence uniflorous or a 3-flowered dichasium, these simple inflorescences sometimes aggregated in bracteate shoots: flowers tetramerous, the Calyx-lobes suborbicular to oblong; bracteoles persistent or caducous before anthesis; stamens ca. 20-90, short and erect in the young bud, the filaments at first shorter than the anthers, then lengthening rapidly at anthesis to exceed the petals, stiff, dark red, the anthers ca. 1 mm long; petals dark red to light purple or pink, somewhat fleshy or waxy, strongly glandular; ovary 2-4-locular, the locules usually not completely fused at anthesis, the placenta peltate, sometimes appearing parietal because of lack of fusion in the locule walls; ovules 6-60 per locule. Fruit a globose or ellipsoidal berry. Seeds several to many, flattened horizontally, sometimes packed in vertical rows, C-shaped or about round, the outer seed coat subcrustose to rather hard, the inner seed coat membranous; embryo C-shaped or spiral, cylindric, the cotyledons about as long as the hypocotyl.
bibliographicCitation: Landrum, Leslie R. 1986. Campomanesia, Pimenta, Blepharocalyx, Legrandia, Acca, Myrrhinium, and Luma (Myrtaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 45: 1-178.

description: Perennial, almost always acaulescent herbs or medium stature, frequently propagating by basal rhizomes. Leaves densely rosulate or fasciculate with the sheaths usually forming a tank, usually spinose-serrate. Scape usually well developed. Inflorescence compound or simple. Flowers distichous or polystichous, sessile or stipitate, not showy, perfect. Sepals free or connate, usually strongly asymmetric; petals regular, free, bearing 2 basal more or less adnate appendages or these rarely more or less aborted (Subgenus Chevaliera). Stamens shorter than the petals, free or the second series more or less adnate to the petals, unappendaged; anthers dorsifixed; pollen with 2, 3, 4, or numerous pores or sulcate in the doubtfully included Ae. muricata (Arruda da Camara) L. B. Smith; ovary wholly inferior; ovules mostly caudate. Fruit usually but slightly enlarged from the ovary; seeds small.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Lyman B. & Downs, Robert J. 1979. Bromelioideae (Bromeliaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 14 (3): 1493-2142.

description: Dioecious trees or shrubs, rarely vinelike. Leaves usually glabrous, base of lamina decurrent onto petiole. Inflorescence a raceme with 1-3 (-4) flowers per bract; bracts ± peltate, caducous; bracteoles (if present) minute; rachis glabrous, papillate or puberulous. Flowers green to yellow-green or white, pedicellate, 4-5-merous, unisexual; tepals free, glabrous, papillate or puberulous; stamens with filaments filiform, exceeding the perianth; disk lobed or annular to urceolate (lobes fused); in [male] flowers the pistil rudimentary, in [female] flowers stamens wanting; disk usually annular and much smaller; pistil with sessile stigma. Drupe ellipsoid, sometimes more or less globular, to 3 cm long; pedicel cylindrical or thicker toward apex.
bibliographicCitation: Hiepko, Paul H. 2000. Opiliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 82: i-iv + 1-53.

description: Trees, rarely shrubs or climbers, sometimes with xylopodium. Leaves alternate, evenly distributed along branchlets, evergreen, rarely deciduous, penninerved or sometimes triplinerved, glabrous above, glabrous beneath, rarely pubescent. Domatia sometimes present. Inflorescences paniculate, evenly distributed along branchlets, rarely congested, in axils of foliage leaves. Flowers hermaphrodite, 1-3.5 mm long, pedicellate, their bracts caducous; floral tube longer than or rarely as long as perianth, obconical, cylindrical or campanulate; tepals 6, erect, equal, tube and tepal base pilose within; stamens usually 12, two-celled, mostly included, the innermost whorl rarely irregularly developed, whorl I with cells, whorl II and III with or without cells, cells introrse, latrorse or extrorse; filaments narrower than anthers; valves of anther cells opening upwards, elliptic; connective ± protruding beyond cells; stamens of whorl III provided with two large sessile glands; staminodes IV stipitiform, triangular or clavate; ovary ovoid or globose, glabrous included in floral tube; style cylindrical or enlarged towards stigma; stigma discoid, as big or bigger than cross-section of style. Berry 1-2 cm long, ellipsoid, base sometimes included for a few mm in woody cupule; fruiting pedicel enlarged, merging into cupule, woody.
bibliographicCitation: Kubitzki, K. & Renner, Susanne S. 1982. Lauraceae I (Aniba and Aiouea). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 31: 1-125.

description: Monoecious, pleonanthic, acaulescent, unarmed, understory palms. Stems subterranean, solitary or sometimes clustered; creeping. Leaves pinnate, reduplicate with woolly hairs or ramenta on rachis and blades; sheaths fibrous with persistent short woolly indumentum; petiole slightly curved, 14-100 cm long; rachis 0.5 to 1 m long, triangular in crosssection; pinnae short to elongate, lanceolate, 20-70 per side, subopposite, irregularly arranged, inserted on rachis at acute angles (<45°) or spreading at various angles (near to perpendicular), the apex lobate or acute, split asymmetrically, with or without ramenta on midrib. Inflorescence spicate, protandrous, erect in bud, interfoliar, bisexual or occasionally unisexual; prophyll flattened, bicarinate 2-keeled; peduncular bract woody; flowers in spirally arranged triads, trimerous, sessile, the perianth parts cymbiform, gibbous, membranous to coriaceous; staminate flowers with 6-18 stamens; anthers slightly sagittate, medifixed near the base, the connective truncate; pollen monocolpate, spherical to ellipsoid, the exine tectate; pistillate flowers tricarpellate, triovulate with a minute apical trifid stigma. Fruit ellipsoid to turbinate, glabrous to variably covered by floccose or woolly hairs, subtended by a short to enlarged persistent perianth; seeds 1 (rarely 2) per fruit, developed from 1 carpel, with homogeneous endosperm; pores near the base of the endocarp; germination remote-ligular; eophyll entire, lanceolate or bifid.
bibliographicCitation: Moraes R., Mónica. 1996. Allagoptera (Palmae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 73: 1-35.

description: Low herbs with woody subterranean rootstock, annual leafy shoots up to 50 cm tall; young parts sparsely pubescent, becoming completely glabrous. Leaves palmatinerved, orbicular to reniform in outline, base cordate, either subentire or deeply parted into 5-9 lobes to at least 4/5 of their length. Cymes terminal, few-flowered; peduncle 2.5-5.0 cm long. Flowers zygomorphic, 5.0-7.5 cm in diam. Sepals linear to oblong-ovate, acute, imbricate, the upper one slightly shorter. Petals yellow, obovate, base cuneate to attenuate; lower petal without marks, lateral petals with one conspicuous mark at the base, slightly asymmetric, upper petals with two conspicuous marks at the base. Stamens unequal, in two sets, filaments and anthers of the lower set slightly longer and tinged dark red; anthers with two apical and occasionally two basal pores. Ovary 3-merous, imperfectly 3-celled with axile placentation, pubescent, becoming glabrous. Style incurved, slightly longer than the lower set of stamens. Capsule globose to ovate, acute, truncate, pointing downward with incurved stalk; pericarp strong, woody, glabrous, striate; placentae united in the lower part, forming a solid and persisting column, free in the upper part, dissepimenta thin and fragile; endocarp pergamentaceous, fragile; exocarp dehiscing only partially, the endocarp remaining united marginally with the pericarp, the seeds shed through fissures of the endocarp. Seeds reniform to subglobose, glabrous, pilose or minutely echinate, seed coat adhering or crustaceous and fragile.

description: Small to medium-sized trees. Leaves simple, alternate, borne singly on the twigs. Inflorescence a solitary flower or a few-flowered fascicle terminal or cauliflorous on bracteate short shoots from older twigs and branches. Flowers with the calyx large, rupturing irregularly, usually bilabiate, sometimes subtruncate, rarely spathaceous; corolla greenish-white, variously tubular-campanulate, usually with an inconspicuous transverse fold in the throat, thickish; stamens subexserted, the anthers glabrous, the thecae thick, somewhat divergent; pollen grains single, inaperturate to multiporate, the exine microreticulate; ovary ovoid-elliptic, more or less lepidote, incompletely 2-locular. Fruit a pepo or calabash, spherical to ellipsoidal, indehiscent, with a relatively fragile woody shell and soft pulp; seeds thick, large, more than 1.3 cm long and 1.4 cm wide, not winged, embedded in the pulp.

description: Plant not producing stolons. Leaves densely rosulate, scarcely enlarged at base. Scape evident, erect. Inflorescence densely strobiliform, usually crowned with a tuft of sterile foliaceous bracts, often producing slips at the base; flowers sessile. Sepals free, obtuse, slightly asymmetric; petals free, erect, violet or red, each typically bearing 2 slenderly funnelform scales; stamens included, pollen ellipsoid with 2 pores; ovaries coalescing with each other and with the bracts and axis to form a fleshy compound fruit; epigynous tube short; placentae apical; ovules caudate.

description: Large showy epiphytic herbs. Leaves rosulate, spinose-serrate. Scape central, erect. Inflorescence compound with simple, reduced, or divided branches. Spikes polystichous-flowered. Flowers functionally unisexual on different plants, sessile. Sepals free, asymmetric, mucronate; petals short-connate, naked; stamens included; filaments short, adnate; anthers each bearing 2 foliaceous appendages at the apex; ovary wholly inferior; epigynous tube short; ovules numerous, borne along the upper part of the cell, acute.
bibliographicCitation: Smith, Lyman B. & Downs, Robert J. 1979. Bromelioideae (Bromeliaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 14 (3): 1493-2142.
