description: Small tree of unknown height. Young twigs and petioles totally covered with pale yellow, stellate hairs 0.2-0.6 mm in diam. Petioles 1-4 mm long, 1-2 mm in diam. Lamina narrowly elliptic, 6-16 cm long, 2.5-6.5 cm wide, leaf index 2.6-2.9(-3.4), chartaceous, greyish green to pale green above, pale brown below, glabrous above, but primary vein totally covered with pale green to yellow, simple and stellate hairs 0.2-0.6 mm in diam., sparsely covered with pale yellow, stellate hairs 0.2-0.6 mm in diam. below, primary vein and base of secondary veins totally so, base acute, slightly oblique, apex acuminate (acumen (5-) 10-20 mm long), primary vein impressed above, secondary veins curved, 8-12 on either side of primary vein, raised above, angles with primary vein 60-85°, loopforming at right angles, loops distinct, smallest distance between loops and margin 2-9 mm, tertiary veins flat above. Inflorescences among leaves, sub-axillary, 1-2-flowered, to 4 flowers in succession. Indument: peduncles, pedicels, and both sides of bracts, sepals, and petals totally to densely covered with yellowish, stellate hairs 0.1-0.6 mm in diam., inner basal 1/3 of petals glabrous. Peduncle 1-14 mm long, 1-2 mm in diam. Sympodial rachis to 4 mm long, with distinctly-spaced flowers. Pedicels 2-12 mm long, 1-2 mm in diam., grooved. Upper bract halfway the pedicel, more or less foliaceous, ovate, 10-20 mm long, caducous. Flower buds broadly ovoid, acute. Flowers cream in vivo. Sepals free, ovate, 11-18 mm long, 6-8 mm wide, acute. Outer petals ovate, 12-13 mm long, 4-7 mm wide, acute, inner petals not seen. Stamens 0.6-1.2 mm long, apex of connective discoid, 0.1-0.4 x 0.3-0.6 mm, papillate. Carpels of unknown number, 3-5 mm long, densely covered with simple hairs 0.1-0.3 mm long. Fruit not seen.

description: Tree or shrub, 2-10 m tall, to 25 cm in diam. Young twigs and petioles rather densely covered with stellate scales 0.1-0.3 mm in diam. Petioles 4-6 mm long, 14 mm in diam. Lamina narrowly elliptic, 18-36 cm long, 4-14 cm wide, leaf index 2.5-4.5, chartaceous, dark, dull green above, pale green to greenish brown below, glabrous above, sparsely covered with stellate scales 0.2-0.4 mm in diam. below, base obtuse to subcordate, slightly oblique, apex acuminate (acumen 5-20 mm long), primary vein impressed above, secondary veins curved, 10-16 on either side of primary vein, impressed to raised above, angles with primary vein 60-85°, loop-forming at right to obtuse angles, loops distinct, smallest distance between loops and margin 2-5 mm, tertiary veins flat to raised above. Inflorescences among leaves, leaf-opposed, supra-axillary or rarely sub-axillary, 1-2-flowered; rarely at/near base of lateral shoot and then becoming (densely) ramified and glomerulate. Indument: peduncles, pedicels, and outer side of bracts, sepals, and petals densely covered with stellate and fimbriate scales 0.1-0.3 mm in diam., inner side of sepals glabrous or sparsely covered with stellate hairs 0.10.5 mm in diam., inner side of petals totally covered with stellate hairs 0.1-0.5 mm in diam. Peduncle 1-2 mm long, 2-3 mm in diam. Pedicels 5-15 mm long, 23 mm in diam. Upper bract at 1/5 of base of pedicel, depressed ovate, 3-6 mm long, amplectent. Flower buds depressed globose. Flowers with cream to creamy yellow petals and green sepals in vivo. Sepals connate for 15-25%, triangular to ovate-triangular, 25-45 mm long, 20-25 mm wide, acute. Petals subequal, triangular-ovate, 40-60 mm long, 20-30 mm wide, acute, primary vein prominent, inner base of inner petals callose, papillate. Stamens 2.5-4 mm long, yellow, apex of connective discoid, 0.5-0.7 x 1.2-1.5 mm, densely covered with hairs. Carpels 5-6 mm long, glabrous, except for a few, scattered simple hairs <0.1 mm long at the apex of the stigma. Fruit white in vivo when young, black in sicco, globose, 3-4 cm in diam., basal collar absent, fertile carpels 40-70, obtrulloid, 10-17 mm long, 5-12 mm in diam., free, areoles pyramidal, 1-5 mm high, obtuse, apiculate (apicule to 2.5 mm long), polygonal, 6-ribbed, verrucose, glabrous. Seeds obovoid, 9-15 mm long, 7 mm in diam., rounded, orange-yellow, not shiny.

description: Tree, 3-22 m tall, 5-25 cm in diam. Young twigs and petioles totally covered with greyish white, stellate hairs 0.1-0.5 mm in diam. Petioles 2-5 mm long, 2.54 mm in diam. Lamina elliptic (to narrowly obovate), 12-36 cm long, 4-10 cm wide, leaf index 3.1-3.5, chartaceous, pale green to brown above, white to greyish white below, glabrous above, totally covered with stellate hairs 0.1-0.4 mm in diam. below, base rounded to cordate, oblique, apex acuminate (acumen 5-15 mm long) to acute, primary vein impressed above, secondary veins curved, 18-23 on either side of primary vein, flat above, angles with primary vein 60-85°, loop-forming at obtuse angles, loops distinct to indistinct, smallest distance between loops and margin 2-4 mm, tertiary veins flat above. Inflorescences among leaves, leaf-opposed, supra-axillary, or terminal, 1-2-flowered. Indument: pedicels and outer side of bracts, sepals, and petals and inner side of sepals and petals densely to totally covered with stellate hairs 0.1-0.4 mm in diam., inner base of petals glabrous. Peduncle 2-10 mm long. Pedicels 10-30 mm long, 2-3.5 mm in diam., fruiting pedicels to 6 mm in diam. Bracts generally foliaceous at least with the first flower. Upper bract at 1/3 to 2/3 of base of pedicel, broadly ovate, 6-22 mm long, distinctly veined. Flower buds very broadly ovoid, distinctly 3-ridged by recurved edges of the sepals. Flowers cream or yellowish in vivo, inner base of petals purplish to clear pink. Sepals free, broadly ovate, 15-25 mm long, 13-20{-28} mm wide, obtuse, slightly apiculate. Petals subequal, broadly ovate, 15-30 mm long, 16-23 {27} mm wide, obtuse, inner base of inner petals callóse, pitted. Stamens 2.4-3 mm long, pinkish red, apex of connective discoid, 0.5-0.7 x 0.9-1.1 mm, densely to sparsely covered with simple hairs 0.1 mm long. Carpels 5-7 mm long, ovary densely covered with tufts of small hairs, stigma glabrous or sparsely covered with simple hairs. Fruit green in vivo, globose to subglobose, 3-5.5 cm in diam., basal collar composed of 18-22 connate, sterile carpels, 10-12 mm in diam., not protruding below the fruit, fertile carpels 150-300, obovoid to obtrulloid, 15-25 mm long, 3-8 mm in diam., free, laterally flattened, areoles very shallowly pyramidal, flattened, 4-5 mm high, acute to obtuse, prominently 4-6-ribbed, longitudinally wrinkled in between, totally covered with a velutinous, greyish indument of stellate hairs 0.1-0.2 mm in diam. Seeds obovoid, 13-16 mm long, 5-7 mm in diam., rounded, orange-brown to dark brown, shiny.

description: Shrub 1-4 m tall, usually with erect, rarely virgate branches and Subscandent, or usually treelet or tree 4-10(-20) m; trunk to 45 cm diam.; bark gray. Branchlets slender, flexuous, striate lengthwise, hardly transversely wrinkled, tips patently puberulous or very shortly pubescent as are the young leaves, petioles, and whole inflorescence, older parts gray-corticate. Leaves lanceolate to oblong, not rarely elliptic-oblong or ovate, apex short- to long-acuminate, tip subacute, base cuneate or rounded, membranaceous to chartaceous, rather firmly so at full age, brownish-or yellowish-olivaceous and shiny above, paler and dull often more greenish-olivaceous beneath in dry specimens, shortly softly pubescent beneath initially but glabrescent there with age, glabrous except the midrib and often tuberculate above, finally glabrescent to practically glabrous on both surfaces, usually markedly wax-coated beneath when young, less distinctly or not so at maturity, 8-10 (-12, -15) x (2.5-)3-5(-8) cm, edge subrevolute, lateral nerves (5-)6(-7) pairs arcuate-ascending and looping before the margin, sometimes slightly impressed in mature leaves above, slightly raised beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets inconspicuous, a little prominent finally on both surfaces; petiole slender, hardly or not wrinkled, (2.5-)3-4 x 1 mm. Inflorescence racemose or subcorymbose-panicled from usually defoliate axils of lateral branchlets, sparsely 4-8(-12)-flow-ered, patently puberulous all over or short-pubescent, often more densely so on calyx and pedicels, sometimes glabrescent; rhachis slender, straight or slightly geniculate, (1.5-)2-3.5 cm long; pedicels ca. 2 mm long; bracts ovate-lanceolate, minute, caducous. Calyx turbinate, edge truncate, 2 mm long. Petals linear-lanceolate, puberulent or rarely subglabrous, white, cream, or bright yellow, 6-7 x 1-1.3 mm. Stamens ca. 5 mm long; filaments densely hairy. Staminodes hairy. Free top of ovary broadly conical to hemispherical, more or less distinctly abrupt with the style, densely white-hairy; style slender, glabrous or hairy below only, slightly exceeding the stamens in the dolichostylous, hardly reaching the base of the anthers in length in the brachystylous form. Drupe oblongoid, sometimes broadly or obovoidly so, broadly attenuate at base, usually orange, rarely more reddish, when fresh to 3 x 1—1.5 cm, when dry ca. 2 x 1-1,3(-1.5) cm, the dry pericarp often forming two vertical opposite obtuse wings, on peduncle 6-8 x 1.5 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Small tree to 10 m tall. Branchlets robust (3-4 mm diam.), obtusely angled, transversely rugulose, glabrous. Leaves oblong to ovate-oblong, apex short-attenuate to rounded, sometimes a little emarginate, base obtuse to rounded, rusty-greenish when fresh, shiny and olive-brownish when dry, stiffly coriaceous, not wax-coated, entire, edge somewhat revolute, (7-)10-13 x (4.5-)5-6.5 cm, midrib raised on upper surface, rugulose, lateral nerves 6-10 pairs and straight, spreading-ascending, looping before the edge, plane, veins obscure; petiole transversely rugulose, 5 x 3 mm. Inflorescences axillary, racemose-paniculate, ca. 10-flowered, glabrous, ca. 2 cm long; rhachis slightly geniculate; pedicels 4-5 mm long. Calyx shortly cup-shaped, edge shallow. Petals 6, connate in lower 1/3, ligulate, fleshy, white, ca. 10 x 1.3 mm. Stamens attaining only half the length of the petals; anthers broadly oval, sparsely hairy on back, 2 mm; filaments free for 1 mm, hairy. Ovary depressedly hemispherical at free apex and puberulent-tomentulose there, abruptly narrowed into the style, the latter glabrous, ca. 2.7 mm long, i.e. equaling the base of the anthers in length; stigma 3-lobed. Fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Shrub 2-4 m, or slender tree to 8 m tall; trunk to 10 cm diam.; bark with shallow vertical fissures. Branchlets slender, yellowish in dry specimens, sulcate-striate and patently puberulous at tips, older parts transversely rugulose. Leaves oblong to oblong-elliptic, sometimes narrowly or ovately so, apex short-attenuate or -subacuminate, tip subacute or obtuse, base cuneate to rounded, slightly inequilateral, membranaceous to thin-chartaceous, olivaceous-greenish or -yellowish, somewhat shiny and more or less wrinkled-tuberculate above, dull and covered with a thin layer of wax (which disappears and becomes shiny where the lamina is heated) on the undersurface, glabrous above except the hairy midrib, short-hairy all over the undersurface, edge somewhat revolute, 5-8(-10) x 2-3.5 cm, midrib rather plane above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves ca. 6 pairs curved-ascending, inconspicuously looping, slightly raised beneath only, reticulation obscure; petiole somewhat rugulose, short-hairy, 2-4 x l mm. Inflorescences from foliate axils, racemose-corymbose, 5-8-flowered, densely short-hairy all over; rhachis straight, 0.5-1.5(-2) cm long; bracteoles oblong, 1.5 mm long, caducous. Calyx shortly funnelform, edge undulate, irregularly 5-lobed, 1-1.5 mm high; pedicel ca. 2 mm long. Petals linear-oblong, white or greenish-cream, 78 x 1.5 mm. Stamens ca. 6 mm long; filaments hairy. Staminodes hairy below. Free distal part of ovary narrowly conical, hairy, tapering gradually to the slender style which is hairy almost to the top and attains the base of the anthers in the brachystylous, hairy at the base only and exceeding the stamens somewhat in length in the dolichostylous form. Drupe unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Tree 4-10 m high. Branchlets virgate, slender, yellowish when dry, strongly longitudinally striate-sulcate, but faintly or not transversely rugulose, tips with a few spreading very short hairs or papillae otherwise glabrous, shiny. Leaves ovate-lanceolate or -oblong, rarely ovate, apex gradually attenuate, tip subacute, base very broadly attenuate to rounded, thin-chartaceous, olive-green, usually markedly wax-covered, rarely less distinctly so beneath, glabrous and shiny above, rather dull and glabrous except a few very short hairs on the lowest part of the midrib (and on the petiole) beneath, (3.5-)5-7(-8.5) x (2-)2.5-3(-4.5) cm, midrib yellowish, prominent beneath only, lateral nerves 4-5 pairs irregularly rather straight-ascending, slightly or hardly raised beneath; petiole slender, 2-3(-4) mm long. Racemes 4-8(-12)-flowered, sparsely short-hairy or puberulent on the geniculate rhachis (1-2 cm long) and pedicels (2 mm long). Calyx-tube obconical, 2 mm long, subglabrous, membranaceous, edge inconspicuously 5-lobed. Petals linear-oblong, glabrous, sulphur-yellow or cream, scented, glabrous, 6-7 mm long. Staminodes hairy below. Stamens 3-4 mm long; filaments hairy. Free top of ovary broadly conical, more or less distinctly abrupt with the style, densely short-hairy; style averaging or slightly exceeding the anthers in the dolichostylous form, hairy at base, in the brachystylous form unknown. Drupe in immature state oblongoid-obovoid, ca. 12 x 7 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Shrub, or usually tree, (6~) 14—30 m tall; trunk 15-40 cm diam., sometimes slightly buttressed; bark rough, with strong unpleasant scent. Branchlets longitudinally sulcate, dark when dry, with a fine patent pubescence. Leaves lanceolate to oblong or elliptic-oblong, sometimes narrowly oblong, apex subacuminate-attenuate, tip subacute, base cuneate, slightly inequilateral, thin-chartaceous, flexible, green when fresh, shiny olivaceous to brownish and rather smooth above when dry, grayish-glaucous-papillose and dull beneath by a waxy coating (which disappears when the leaf is heated), edge undulate and more or less revolute, 6-10(-12) x (2-)2.5-4(-5) cm, midrib papillose, transversely rugose in its lower part as is the petiole, slightly raised above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves (5-)6(-7) pairs (the lowest pair from above the base of the lamina) rather irregularly arcuate-ascending, somewhat prominent beneath only, reticulation of veins and veinlets usually obscure; petiole 3-4(-5, -7) x 1 mm. Inflorescences axillary, simple or mostly 1-2-forked racemes or panicles, 5-10(-16)-flowered, sweet-scented; rhachis flexuous, (0.5-)1-1.5(-2) cm long, gray-papillose or papillose-puberulous all over as are calyx and petals; pedicels 1-2(-3) mm long; bracts minute. Calyx depressedly cup-shaped, edge 5-undulate, 1 mm high, tapering down to the pedicel. Petals oblong-lanceolate, tip inflexed, fleshy pale green or yellowish, 5-6(-7) x ca. 1.3 mm. Stamens 4-5 mm long; filaments hairy; anthers orange, 1 mm long. Staminodes white, hairy below, as long as petals. Upper free part of ovary conical-pyramidal, or narrowly conical, more or less attenuate to the style, densely hairy as is the lower lh of the style which is slightly 3-lobed and attains the base of the anthers in the brachystylous or is as long as or slightly longer than the stamens in the dolichostylous form. Drupe ellipsoid or broadly or subovoidly so, truncate at both ends, 2.7 x 2.4 cm in the fresh, 2-2.3 x 1.5 (-2) cm in the dry state, the umbonate top tomentulose; 1 or sometimes 2 drupes at end of the stoutish rhachis, on a short peduncle; pericarp soft, yellow or orange, ca. 3 mm thick in fresh, 1.5-2 mm thick in dry drupes; endocarp bony, 0.3 mm thick.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Treelet or tree, (3-)10-15(-18) m tall; trunk (5-)10-35(-60) cm diam.; bark gray, fissured. Branchlets virgate, tomentulose by dilutely ferrugineous spreading short hairs as are petiole and midrib (much less the lateral nerves) on the upper surface of the leaves. Leaves oblong, narrowly elliptic, or ovate, apex obtusely acuminate, tip mucronulate, base cuneate, subcoriaceous, dark brown and shiny above, paler beneath when dry, not wax-covered, glabrous except the rusty-hir-sutulous or -tomentellous midrib above, 6-8 x (2-)2.5-3(-4, -5) cm, midrib prominent beneath, yellowish and transversely wrinkled as the petiole, lateral nerves 6-7 pairs, curved and distinctly looping in 2-4 mm distance from the slightly revolute edge, often somewhat impressed above, hardly raised beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets usually rather obscure; petiole 2-3(-4) mm long. Racemes solitary or rarely two per leaf axil, sometimes shortly pedunculate, 2-4(-5)-flowered; rhachis rather straight, 0.5-1 (-1.5) cm, puberulous as the pedicels (1-2 mm long); bracts small. Calyx obconical, edge undulate, membranaceous, glabrous, 2 mm long. Petals linear, subacute, glabrous, white or pale green, 34 x l mm. Stamens ca. 3 mm long; filaments hairy, 2 mm long; anthers 1 mm long. Staminodes hairy below, as long as petals. Ovary glabrous in its free part; style glabrous, more or less equaling the stamens in the dolichostylous form, the brachystylous one unknown. Drupe oblongoid-obovoid, 1.7-2 x ca. 1.3 cm, the apex, i.e. the umbonate free part quite glabrous, orange or yellow, on stoutish peduncles 2-5 mm long; endocarp thin-woody.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Weak Subscandent shrub or slender tree to 4 m tall. Branchlets slender, longitudinally striate-sulcate, often also transversely wrinkled, glabrous, usually yellowish, sometimes dilutely brown in dry specimens. Leaves lanceolate- or ovate-oblong, apex subobliquely and rather gradually acuminate, tip subacute, base broadly cuneate, slightly inequilateral, membranaceous to firmly chartaceous or subcoriaceous, slightly shiny and yellowish-olivaceous, rarely brownish in dry state, glabrous or practically so except for the very short hairs on the midrib above, part of the lamina tuberculate mainly on the upper surface, edge slightly revolute, (8-)11-16 x (3-)3.5-4.5(-6, -8) cm, midrib prominent within a low depression above, strongly raised and wrinkled at base beneath, paler than the lamina, lateral nerves 5-6(-8) pairs irregularly arcuate-ascending, looping, hardly raised or sometimes a little immersed above, slightly prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets fine and dense, very slightly prominent on both surfaces; petiole yellowish, transversely wrinkled, 3-4(-5) x 1-1.5(-2) mm. Racemes axillary, glabrous in all outer parts, 5-7(-10)-flowered; rhachis slender, somewhat geniculate, 0.8-1.5 cm long; bracteoles ovate, subpersistent, 0.5 mm long; pedicels 0.7-1 (-1.5) mm long. Calyx narrowly funnelform, edge undulate, 1.5 mm long. Petals linear-oblong, glabrous or practically so, white, ca. 5 x 1 mm. Stamens 3 mm long; filaments glabrous. Staminodes 3-4 mm long, glabrous. Free part of ovary hemispherical, glabrous; style abrupt with the ovary, glabrous, attaining the base of the anthers in the brachystylous and much exceeding them in the dolichostylous form. Drupe oblongoid, or slightly obovoidly so, apex rounded, the umbonate top glabrous, base broadly attenuate, ca. 2.5 x 2 cm when fresh, 1.8-2 x 0.8-1 cm when dry, on slender peduncle 1.5-2.5 cm long; pericarp yellow-orange, ca. 2 mm thick, sometimes forming two wings in much pressed dry fruits.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Shrub or slender tree to 7 m tall; trunk to 12 cm diam.; bark gray. Branchlets slender, finely striate lengthwise, papillose-puberulous. Leaves oblong or ovate, usually oblong-ovate, apex shortly attenuate to subacuminate, tip subacute, base broadly cuneate to almost rounded, initially membranaceous and becoming dark brown when dry, at maturity subcoriaceous and olivaceous, neither tuberculate nor wax-coated, rather dull on both surfaces, glabrous, (4-)5-8 x 3-4.5 cm, midrib yellowish, slightly raised above, strongly so beneath, lateral nerves 7-8(-9) pairs more or less straight towards the edge, looping, rather obscure, a little raised mainly beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets faintly though distinctly raised on both surfaces at maturity; petiole transversely rugulose, 2-4 x ca. 1 mm. Racemes from foliate and defoliate axils, slender, 6-12-flowered; rhachis slender, straight, papillose-puberulous as are calyx and pedicels, 1.5-2 cm long; bracteoles ovate, minute, caducous. Calyx cup-shaped, much attenuate toward the pedicel (2 mm long), edge undulate. Petals linear-oblong, (sub)glabrous, white to greenish, 5-6 x ca. 1 mm. Stamens ca. 4 mm long; filaments hairy. Staminodes sparsely hairy below. Free part of ovary depressedly conical or hemispherical, tomentulose, abrupt with the style, the latter glabrous, slightly exceeding the stamens in length in the dolichostylous, reaching the base of the anthers in the brachystylous form. Drupe (Plowman et al. 10094) obovoid-oblongoid, olive-green, 2-2.2 x 1.2 cm, the umbonate apex short-hairy, on stoutish subglabrous peduncle ca. 4 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Shrub or small tree. Branchlets yellowish and strongly longitudinally striate-sulcate in dry specimens, patently short-pubescent, older parts covered with cork and distinctly transversely rugulose. Leaves ovate to ovate-oblong or oblong, apex broadly attenuate with obtuse tip or rounded, base usually rounded, sometimes very broadly attenuate, thin-chartaceous, olivaceous-brownish and dull when dry, initially sparingly very shortly pubescent, finally glabrescent above, permanently softly short-pubescent beneath and rather indistinctly or not wax-coated there, (2.5-)3-6(-7) x 2-3.5 cm, midrib plane above, somewhat raised beneath, lateral nerves 4-5 irregular pairs (the lowest pair from the base of the lamina), faintly raised beneath as is the rather inconspicuous reticulation of veins; petiole slender, hairy, 2-4 x ca. 1 mm. Flowers 2-3(-5, -8) per subcorymbose raceme from usually defoliate axils, covered with grayish short and soft hairs all over; rhachis rarely to 1.5 cm long; bracts caducous, not observed; pedicels stoutish, 2-3 mm long. Calyx obconical, edge subentire, 1.5-2 mm long. Petals linear-oblong, ca. 6 x 1 mm. Stamens 4-5 mm long. Staminodes and filaments hairy. Free top of ovary depressedly conical or subhemispherical, abruptly narrowed into the style, tomentulose; style hairy below, surpassing somewhat the anthers in the dolichostylous form, the brachystylous one unknown. Drupe unknown.

description: Tree 3-6 m tall. Branchlets dark red-brown, obtusely angled, striate lengthwise and transversely rugulose, glabrous, 1.5-2 mm diam. Leaves ovate-oblong, apex shortly attenuate to obtuse, base broadly attenuate to obtuse, dull and dark olive-green when fresh, darker and more brownish when dry, more or less stiffly coriaceous, glabrous, not wax-coated, edge hardly revolute, 5-9 x 3-5 cm, midrib raised and rugulose on both surfaces, lateral nerves 4-5 pairs, rather straight from midrib, forked before the edge, slightly to deeply impressed above, rather obscure beneath, as is the coarse reticulation of veins; petiole transversely rugulose, 24 x 1.5-2 mm. Inflorescence subterminal and axillary, racemose, few-flowered, 3-5 cm long. Flowers unknown. Drupe dark olive-green when fresh, broadly ellipsoid or ovoid-oblongoid, apex subtruncate, base rounded, 2-2.5 cm long, 1.72 cm broad, the free apex somewhat short-hairy; endocarp stony, 1 mm thick.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Shrubs 4-6 m tall, exceptionally trees to 12 m tall, to 30 cm dbh, much-branched, sometimes with small buttresses; bark yellowish grayish. Leafy branchlets grayish-tomentulous, tetragonous-terete; older branches glabrate, rugose, terete, grayish; lenticels punctiform, 0.5 mm wide. Stipules narrowly triangular, acuminate, tomentulous outside, glabrous with basal colleters inside, (15-)25-35 × 13-16 mm, pale green, readily caducous, leaving a white-grayish linear scar. Leaves (22-)25-38(-54) × (7-)9-17(-23) cm, L/W 1.6:1 to 2:1; elliptic to oblanceolate to obovate, acute to obtuse (BA = 30-50°) at base, rounded at apex; dark green above, pale green-grayish below, semi-coriaceous; drying grayish olive-green, chartaceous; glabrous above, glabrous to golden-pilose below; pellucid punctate; primary and secondary veins glabrous to golden-pilose, prominent below, secondary veins 12-16 each side, subparallel; tertiary veins openly reticulate, faintly evident; petioles (10-) 13-18(-25) mm long, 2.5-3 mm thick, adaxially concave to flattened, glabrous to golden-pilose, pulvinus absent; domatia absent or a tuft of sparse hairs 1-1.5 mm wide, hairs white 0.2-0.4 mm long. Inflorescences openly paniculate, pyramidal, with opposite or subopposite decussate branches; 24-30(-36) cm long, (8-) 14-20 cm wide at base, lateral branches 4-8 pairs, basal portion of axis not branched (4-)6-14 cm long; rachis decussately compressed or quadrangular (rarely terete) in cross section, rachis and branches glabrous (rarely minute- puberulent); flowers alternate on distal branches; distal bracts decreasing distally from 12 to 3 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, linear, narrowly triangular to deltoid, bracteoles subtending flowers 1-1.5 × 1-1.5 mm, deltoid, glabrous to minutely puberulent, often ciliolate. Flowers pedicellate, pedicels 3-5 mm long, glabrous (rarely minute puberulent), fragrant; hypanthium narrowly obconical, 3-5 × 1.5-2.5 mm, glabrous; flower buds cylindrical. Calyx small-cupular, truncate or with barely distinguishable lobes, 3-4 mm wide; lobes 5, 0.2-0.4 × 0.9-1.2 mm, shallowly deltoid, ciliolate. Corolla tubular with spreading-reversed lobes, 1.5-1.8 cm long, white to cream-white, rarely pink-reddish at base outside, white inside, semi-fleshy when fresh; tube narrowly funnelform, 9-12 mm long, 2-2.2 mm at base and ca. 2.5 mm wide at the orifice, glabrous to minutely puberulent outside, glabrous inside, with a ring of white-sericeous hairs (0.5-1 mm long), 4-5 mm from the base, at the same point of the filament attachments at base of lobes; lobes 5, 1/3-1/2 of corolla length, 5-7 × 0.9-1.2 mm, narrowly triangular, glabrous to minutely puberulent outside, white-strigose at base (hairs 0.5-1 mm long), margins densely papillose inside. Stamens 5, exserted because of spreading lobes, subequal, attached 4-5 mm from the base of the tube; filaments 4-5 mm long, very thin, pendulous, glabrous, barbate at base, with a tuft of white sericeous hairs (0.8-1 mm long); anthers cylindrical, narrowly oblong, 6-8 × 1-1.5 mm, dorsifixed near the base, base rounded, microscopically (40x) papillose-echinate throughout. Pollen exine densely foveolate (non-echinate). Style exserted, 20-25 mm long, glabrous; style branches oblong, 0.9-1.1 mm long, stigmatic surface glabrous to microscopically (40×) papillose. Capsules obovoid to subglobose, acute at base, apex subtruncate, 5-7 (-8) × ca. 5 mm, dark brown with small lenticels, glabrous throughout. Seeds 1.4-1.6 × 0.48 mm.

description: Subshrub to 1 m tall, the stems densely pubescent with appressed stellate hairs, the hairs usually 4armed, with the arms aligned longitudinally, parallel with the stem axis. Leaf blades broadly oblanceolate, to 21 x 8.5 cm, basally cuneate, apically acuminate, the margin subentire proximally to shallowly dentate distally, penninerved, the upper surface subglabrous but with widely scattered simple or bifurcate hairs (rarely stellate) 0.5 mm long, especially toward the base, the lower surface stellate-pubescent, the hairs <1 mm diam., the pubescence of the nerves similar to that of the stem; petioles up to 4 cm long, with pubescence like stem; stipules lanceolate, 11 x 2 mm, erect, ascending-pubescent. Inflorescence capituliform, the peduncle with scattered appressed 3-4-armed stellate hairs similar to those of the stem but sparser; pedicels 2-4 mm long. Flowers and fruits crowded; involucel 8 mm long, with appressed bifurcate and stellate hairs, the bractlets 10-12, connate in basal half, ovate and somewhat overlapping, 2-4 mm wide, acuminate; calyx ca. 5 mm long, wholly concealed by involucel; corolla light rose. Fruits glabrous, the mericarp body ca. 11 x 3 mm, carinate and with 2 subparallel lateral ribs, with 3 apical retrorsely barbed spines, the central spine erect, 7 mm long, the lateral spines erect, 3 mm apart at base, 4-5 mm long, the retrorse spines extending down the lateral ribs of the mericarp body.

description: Shrubs 1.5 m tall, the stems densely stellate-tomentose. Leaf blades sagittate-oblong, mostly 2-6 (excluding the lobes) x 1.5-3 cm, basally deeply cordate-sagittate (the lobes 6-15 mm long), obscurely crenate, acute to subobtuse, palmately 5-7-nerved, discolorous, evenly stellate-pubescent beneath, the upper surface with simple and bifurcate (and some stellate) hairs; petioles 1-4 cm long; stipules subulate, 3-4 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-3 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, lance-ovate, 8-10 x 3-4 mm, puberulent and ciliate; calyx 9-11 mm long, ciliate, the lobes with red veins; corolla (not seen) 7 mm long. Fruits 9 mm diam., sparsely and minutely puberulent; mericarps 4 mm high, carinate and reticulately rugose. Chromosome number, 2n = 56 (Krapovickas & Cristóbal, 1962).

description: Trees to 15 m or shrubs. Branchlets slender, midway along flush 2-3 mm diam., distally weakly angular, soon terete, densely pubescent, the surface concealed by the indument cover to barely visible, the hairs short, to 0.5 mm, straight, appressed, ascending, or erect, silvery-grey to rust-brown; terminal buds slender, 3 × 1 mm, densely pubescent, the hairs as on branchlets. Leaves alternate, widely and evenly spaced along current flush; petioles slender, to 1 × 0.2 cm, semi-terete, the indument as on branchlets; laminae chartaceous, plane, ovate, 8-17 × 2-4 cm, the base obtuse to rounded, briefly decurrent, the apex acute, acuminate for up to 2 cm, the margins minutely recurved throughout; upper surface dull greyish green to dark olive-brown, waxy, the midrib sunken, secondary and higher-order venation raised, their prominence decreasing with rank; lower surface densely sericeous or tomentose, the hairs appressed, ascending, or erect, uniformly distributed, all vein orders raised, their prominence decreasing with rank; secondary veins 4-6 per side, ± evenly spaced, slightly more distant around midlamina, ascending at 50-60° (more obtuse around midlamina), arcuate, distal pairs loop-connected; tertiaries roughly horizontal to oblique to midrib, between secondaries straight to forked. Staminate inflorescences evenly spaced along current flush in the axils of foliage leaves, to 10 cm long with 8 lateral branches, branch orders 3-4, the highest order dichasial, lax, the flowers distant, the axes sparsely rusty to grey-strigillose; bracts and bracteoles caducous by anthesis, lanceolate, the indument as on axes, denser; pedicels terete, to 3 mm long, those supporting secondary flowers slightly shorter. Flowers rotate, 5 mm diam., sparsely rusty strigillose outside; receptacle patelliform, 0.5 × 1 mm, densely rusty tomentose inside. Tepals chartaceous, obovate, 2 × 1 mm, spreading, the androecium exserted at anthesis, the outer surface sparsely rusty to grey-strigillose, the inner surface sparsely rusty to grey-strigillose near base, otherwise minutely papillose throughout, the margins papillose. Stamens of whorls I and II stipitate, 0.7 mm tall, the anthers transversely oblong to obovate, 0.3 × 0.4 mm, glabrous, the apex truncate, the connectives level with or broad above the 2 locelli, these suborbicular, the filaments laminar, narrower than anthers, slender, glabrous; whorl III stamens stipitate, ca. 1 mm tall, the anthers oblong, 0.5 × 0.3 mm, bowed towards the outer whorls, locelli 4, upper pair introrse-latrorse, lower pair extrorse-latrorse, the filaments narrower than anthers, laminar, glabrous, the basal glands sessile, globose; whorl IV wanting; pistillode fusiform. Pistillate inflorescence with indument and color as in staminate plants, but shorter and with fewer lateral branches, the flowers similar in size and shape; stamens sterile, smaller; ovary glabrous; style slender, distinct from ovary; stigma trilobed, 0.4 mm diam. Fruits borne on claviform pedicels of up to 1 × 0.5 cm; cupules scarcely broader, patelliform, to 0.6 cm diam., strigose inside, the margins lobed, tepal bases persisting; drupes ellipsoid, to 1.2 × 0.6 cm.

description: Trees to 10 m. Branchlets slender to stout, midway along flush 3-6 mm diam., terete, densely pubescent, the surface barely visible to concealed by the indument cover, the hairs relatively long, to 0.6 mm, straight to crooked, erect, reddish or a few grey; terminal buds plump, 5 × 3 mm, densely rusty pubescent, the hairs as on branchlets, straight, appressed to ascending. Leaves closely spiraled at tips of current flush; petioles robust, to 2 × 0.3 cm, semi-terete, the indument as on branchlets; laminae coriaceous, sub-bullate, lanceolate to oblong, or elliptic, 10-25 × 2-8 cm, the base obtuse to rounded, the apex obtuse to acute, acuminate for up to 1.5 cm, the margins minutely recurved throughout; upper surface green to olive-brown, minutely punctulate, the midrib prominent, the secondaries impressed, the higher-order venation immersed, inconspicuous against the lamina; lower surface sparsely pubescent, the hairs 0.6 mm long, sprawling to weakly ascending, rusty, denser on main veins, soon lost, all vein orders raised, their prominence decreasing with rank; secondary veins 14-20 per side, ± evenly spaced, slightly more distant around midlamina, patent, diverging at 70-85° (more obtusely around midlamina), abruptly ascending after midcourse, brochidodromous, or strongly loop-connected by midlamina; tertiaries oblique to midrib, between secondaries straight to forked. Staminate inflorescences distally clustered in the axils of cataphylls, to 20 cm long with 15 lateral branches, branch orders 3-4, the highest order botryoid, or irregular, lax, the flowers loosely crowded, the axes sparsely rusty tomentose, the hairs restricted to first-and second-order branches, soon lost; bracts and bracteoles persistent at anthesis, lanceolate, sparsely rusty tomentose, glabrescent; pedicels terete, to 2 mm long, those supporting secondary flowers slightly shorter. Flowers campanulate, 2 mm diam., glabrous outside; receptacle cyathiform, 0.6 × 0.6 mm, glabrous inside. Tepals chartaceous, ligulate, 1.3 × 0.6 mm, spreading to recurved at anthesis, the inner surface papillose near tips, otherwise glabrous. Stamens of whorls I and II stipitate, 0.6 mm tall, the anthers transversely oblong, 0.3 × 0.4 mm, glabrous, the apex truncate or emarginate, the connectives level with or reduced between the 2 locelli, these suborbicular, introrse, the filaments laminar, much narrower than anthers, sparsely grey-villose; whorl III stamens stipitate, 0.6 mm tall, the anthers equal to outer whorls, erect, locelli 2, extrorse-latrorse, the filaments narrower than anthers, laminar, sparsely grey-villose, the basal glands sessile, globose; whorl IV wanting; pistillode filiform. description: Trees to 15 m. description: Shrub or tree, 0.15-11 m tall with trunk to 10 cm in diam.; branchlets 2-5 mm in diam., often reddish-brown when young, grayish-brown when older, minutely pubescent with spreading hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, becoming glabrous. Leaves (sub)opposite, 3-foliolate, with stalked leaflets; petiole semiterete, strongly canaliculate, winged or not, 2-6 cm long, the wings 0.2-0.4 mm broad and terminating in a small ear 0.2 mm long, minutely puberulous with hairs 0.2 mm long, a trigonous tubercle 0.2-1 mm long usually present; petiolules to 20 mm long, not sharply separated from base of leaflets; leaflet blades elliptic or slightly obovate, rarely ovate, (4.5-)5.5-16 × (2.0-)2.5-5.5 cm, lateral leaflets somewhat smaller than terminal one and unequal at base, long-attenuate, acuminate at apex, the very tip obtuse or occasionally emarginate, rarely subcaudate, the margin revolute, the blade chartaceous or rarely (sub)coriaceous, dull, rarely sublustrous, much paler beneath, nearly glabrous above but the midvein sparsely minutely puberulous with hairs 0.05-0.3 mm long, sericeous-pubescent below near the proximal part of the midvein with mostly straight hairs to 0.8 mm long, occasionally subglabrous below with the midvein minutely pubescent with appressed hairs 0.05-0.3 mm long, venation camptodromous, in subcoriaceous leaflets prominent beneath, midvein impressed, rarely plane. Inflorescences terminal, erect, (occasionally widely) paniculate, nearly always longer than the leaves, (5-) 13-25 × (4-)8-25 cm, usually loosely but many-flowered, the side-branchlets of first order opposite and subtended by a bract, or the lower ones by a 3-foliolate, rarely simple leaf, the side-branchlets of higher order alternate distally, pilose with spreading hairs 0.05-0.2 mm, distally more dense, glabrescent; bracts except the lower ones persistent, ovate, ca. 0.8-2 × 0.5-1 mm, minutely puberulous with hairs 0.05-0.1 mm long; pedicels to 2 mm long; bractlets subopposite. Flowers usually 4.5-5.5 mm in diam., protandrous; calyx lobes quincuncial, very broadly to depressedly ovate with rounded tip, 0.7-1.5 × 1-2 mm, coriaceous with transparent margin, glabrous above, glabrous or minutely pubescent below with hairs 0.05-0.1 mm long, venation parallellodromous, false midrib present; petals persistent, imbricate, spreading, subovate, elliptic or oblong, 2-2.5 × 1.2-1.6 mm, rounded at tip, semitransparent-papery, whitish when fresh, brown when dried with 0.1-0.3 mm broad, the ochreous margins becoming creamish-white when boiled, glabrous or minutely puberulous below with appressed hairs 0.1 mm, venation camptodromous to somewhat suprabasally actinodromous, occasionally some showing a false midrib; filaments persistent, adnate at base to the disc, subulate, slightly convex abaxially, convex adaxially, 1.4-1.5 mm long and 0.3-0.4 mm thick, glabrous; anthers dorsifixed 1/3 to 2/5 from base, heart-shaped, 0.6-0.7 × 0.5 mm, including a tip 0.05 mm; disc cup-shaped, with 5-10 slight incurvations and a thickened upper margin, 0.5 mm high (as high as the ovary with its protuberances), 0.2-0.3 mm thick at the margin, 1.4-1.6 mm in diam., glabrous; carpels adnate to the disc and connate in their lower half, 0.5 mm high, provided with numerous finger-like, glandular protuberances to 0.2-0.4 mm long and glabrous or rarely beset with some hairs 0.1 mm long; style inserted near base of the carpels, 0.8-0.9 mm long and 0.2-0.3 mm thick at maturity, free for 0.6-0.7 mm, before the shedding of the pollen 0.4-0.6 mm long and free for 0.3 mm, glabrous; stigma capitate, 0.1-0.2(-0.5) × 0.3 mm. Fruits ca. 4-10 per infructescence, subglobose, 10-15 × 10-14 mm (-20 mm when dehisced), glabrous; loculi rounded on the back, muricate with numerous ± hooked prickles ca. 2(-4) mm long which are sharp with a broad base or occasionally 2 with a common base, and beset with glands, dehiscent septicidally to ca. 2 mm above the base and loculicidally to 1/5 or 1/2 from the base; seeds (l-)2 per loculus, superposed, (narrowly) ovoid, 6.5-7.5 × 2.7-2.8 × 2.8-2.9 mm, when 2 truncate at base or ventrally near the base, flattened on the back, beaked at apex, testa dark brown, colliculate with interspaces 0.05 mm in diam.; chalazal area irregular in shape, 1-1.2 mm in diam., often much swollen, dark brown; hilum 0.5 mm broad; granular endosperm 0.1-0.2 mm thick; embryo 1, the cotyledons provided with ears 0.3 mm long, finely punctate, radicle long-projecting, thick-conical, 0.8-1.1 × 0.7-0.8 mm, the plumule 0.1 mm long.

description: Leaflets usually ca. 3-9 × 1.2-3.2 cm or smaller. Inflorescences to 7(-20) cm long with side-branchlets to 3(-10) cm; bracts and bractlets somewhat swollen, to 1-1.5 mm long; flowers more numerous than in var. grandiflora. Calyx lobes 1-1.3 × 1.4-1.8 mm; petals 3.4-4.8 × 2.2-2.8 mm, thinly coriaceous; carpels to 0.5 mm high with protuberances to 0.4 mm and some to 0.8 mm long.

description: Shrub to 6 m tall with trunk 5-8 cm in diam. Leaves varying from 3- to 1-foliolate, the 1-foliolate ones frequently 2-parted or 2-cleft, or the leaflets of a 2-foliolate leaf ± connate; petiole provided with wings ca. 0.6-1.3 mm broad ending in blunt ears 3-4 x 1-1.5 mm or shorter; apex of leaflets acuminate, mostly rostrate-caudate with a usually blunt, laterally curved acumen (2-)7-25 mm long; lateral leaflets sometimes greatly reduced in size with a slightly unequal base, curved and with an admedial midvein.

description: Tree. Young stems dark reddish-brown, the indumentum short, dark rufous-tomentose, glabrescent, weakly striate; older branches dark reddish-brown to black, glabrescent or glabrous, minutely striate, un-fissured. Lenticels few, minute, ca. 0.5 mm or less, orbicular to linear, slightly prominent, beige to ferruginous, not producing fissures. Petiole (1.9-)3.5-4.9 cm long, terete, (1-)2-2.75 mm diam, at the base, indumentum ferruginous to rufous, commonly glabrous to puberulent or very sparsely villose, rarely velutinous. Leaf rhachis (3.9-)5.5-12 cm long, the terminal appendix 5.5-8 mm long, 0.5-0.75 mm broad, frequently with lighter colored or denser indumentum than rhachis; leaflets short-petiolate, petiolules 5-10 mm long, (l-)2-3mm diam, at the base. Leaflets 4-5 pairs, less commonly three, opposite to strongly subopposite, frequently overlapping, weakly bicolorous to concolorous, drying light green to brown, less frequently black, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, matte, rarely shiny, glabrous above with sparsely ferruginous or rufous short-villous or puberulous indumentum around and on venation and near the base, puberulent to sparsely ferruginous- or rufous-villous beneath, commonly asymmetrical, oblong, oblong-lanceolate to elliptic to narrowly ovate, less commonly narrowly obovate; basal pair generally broader and more elliptic than other leaflets, (2.7-)6.2-8.1 × 1:7-4.3 cm; other leaflets (4.3-)6.7-12.6 ×(1.65-)3.6-4.3 cm; base equal or not, decurrent to narrowing or acute; apex acute, acuminate to obtuse, rarely rounded, commonly minutely mucronulate due to extension of midvein; margin broadly serrate to denticulate, frequently appearing almost entire with the exception of a few minute blunt teeth, revolute, rarely pressing flat; venation cladodromous to brochidodromous, with 4-5 lateral veins, the midvein prominent throughout, reaching the apex, the secondaries fine, narrow, prominent, the higher order venation narrowly reticulate to obscure above. Inflorescence moderately congested, axillary, less frequently lateral, 2-2.2 cm diam., commonly longer than the leaf rhachis; peduncle 1.9-3.1 cm long, 1.25-2 mm diam, immediately below inflorescence; floral rhachis 7-12 cm long, ferruginous-rufous, puberulent to velutinous; bracteoles more or less uniform, the basal ones 1.5-2 mm long, narrowly triangular, the superior ones slightly shorter, frequently slightly reflexed; flower-pair peduncle 1-3 mm mm long, ferruginous-puberulent to sparsely velutinous; pedicels 1-3 mm long. Buds 1.75-2 mm broad at apex, 0.6-75 mm broad at midlength, essentially erect, puberulent to sparsely short-villous. Flowers 3.5-7 mm long, all tepals recurving at anthesis; tepals 0.6-0.7 mm across at midlength, not keeled. Anthers sessile, ca. 1.25 mm long. Hypogynous nectaries fused into a quadrangle 0.25-0.8 mm high and 1-1.5 mm across, an abaxial gap narrow or absent. Ovary 1.5-2 mm long, ovoid, short rufous-hirsute, the indumentum covering entire ovary. Fruit unknown.

description: Tree, or shrub, to 12 m. Young stems orangish to dull brown, ferruginous- to rufous-velutinous to short-pubescent, weakly striate; older branches dark brown to gray-black, glabrous to patchy short yellow-gray velutinous, or with patches of a white cuticle, striations faint to very prominent, short fissured. Lenticels numerous, generally minute and inconspicuous, <0.5 mm long, sometimes measuring 3.6-6 mm, beige to reddish, slightly to strongly prominent, frequently producing a network of shallow fissures. Petiole 3.2-10 cm long, terete, 2-3.5 mm diam, at the base, glabrescent to densely whitish- or ferruginous-puberulent, the indumentum closely appressed, rarely spreading. Leaf rhachis (3.5-)7-12.2cm long, the terminal appendix 2-7 mm long, 0.5-1 mm broad, rarely reaching 6 mm long and producing an undeveloped pair of leaflets; leaflets sessile or subsessile, the petiolules 3-10 mm long, 2-4 mm diam, at the base. Leaflets 2-4 pairs, opposite or subopposite, overlapping or not, drying black, rarely pale green above, brown beneath, chartaceous to coriaceous, glabrous to sparsely puberulent above, ferruginous-puberulent in young leaves, shiny or matte above, glabrous to sparsely white or ferruginous-puberulent beneath, especially on and near the midvein at the base of the leaflet, the hairs generally closely appressed, rarely spreading, commonly asymmetrical, narrowly obovate to oval, less frequently elliptic, often curving; basal pair similar to lateral ones but sometimes suborbicular, 3.2-10 × 3.5-5.6 cm; other leaflets 8.4-14.4 × 3.9-5.8 cm; base equal to weakly oblique, decurrent; apex acute to rounded, sometimes truncate in basal leaflets, commonly retuse to emarginate; margin entire, frequently revolute, especially at apex or base of lamina; venation reticulodromous to cladodromous, with 3-5 lateral veins, the midvein prominent throughout or only on lower half of lamina, reaching the apex or frequently losing strength or forking towards the apex, the secondaries faintly prominent, the higher-order venation conspicuous on both sides of lamina, venation same color as lamina. Inflorescence lax to moderately congested, unbranched, axillary or nearly terminal, 2-3.3 cm diam.; peduncle (2.3-)3.3-5.7cm long, 1.5-3 mm diam, immediately below inflorescence; floral rhachis (5.6-)7.8-24.5 cm long, densely rufous-puberulent to velutinous-tomentose; bracteoles heteromorphic basal, to 2 mm long, linear, ferruginous-hirsute, the superior bracteoles smaller, <1 mm long, not recurved; flower-pair peduncle 0.5-3 mm long, rufous-ferruginous-velutinous to short-pilose; pedicels 1.5-5 mm long. Buds 2.25-3 mm broad at apex, ca. 0.75-1 mm broad at midlength, descending to ascending, the indumentum ferruginous-velutinous to short-pilose. Flowers 7-11 mm long, all tepals recurving at anthesis; tepals 0.5-0.75 mm across at midlength, not or weakly keeled. Anthers subsessile, 1.5-2 mm long. Hypogynous nectaries fused into a quadrangle 0.5-1.25 mm high and 1.25-2 mm across, the abaxial gap narrow or absent, the nectaries closely juxtaposed. Ovary 2-2.5 mm long, ovoid to pyriform to semi ovoid, rufous-hirsute, the indumentum covering entire ovary. Fruiting peduncle ca. 5.8 cm long; infructescence ca. 25 cm long; fruit pedicel ca. 2 mm thick. Young fruit ovoid, smooth, 14 mm long and 8.5 mm diam.

description: Tree, to 20 m, very rarely a shrub. Young stems reddish-brown, glabrescent to ferruginous-tomentose, the indumentum commonly lost with maturity, the striations narrow, multiple, not visible in very young stems; older branches dark brown to black, glabrous to tomentose, striations conspicuous, unfissured or with numerous shallow fissures. Lenticels few, minute and inconspicuous to large and conspicuous, <0.5-3 mm long, suborbicular to narrowly elliptic, prominent or not, light brown, rarely producing fissures or only very small ones. Petiole 3.8-18.8 cm long, terete, 2-3.5 mm diam, at the base, sparsely appressed-puberulous (seen only under magnification). Leaf rhachis 2.4-21.5 cm long, the terminal appendix commonly 2-5 mm long and 0.5-1.5 mm broad, rarely producing a small terminal leaflet; leaflets subsessile to short-petiolate, the petiolules to 8 mm long, 2.5-3 mm at the base. Leaflets 2-4(-5) pairs, opposite to subopposite, overlapping or not, drying light green to brown to black, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, matte to shiny, glabrous to glabrescent with venation ferruginous-tomentose above, glabrous to ferruginous-pilose beneath when the latter, the midvein and secondary veins densely ferruginous-tomentose, symmetrical to asymmetrical, the shape very variable, narrowly to broadly obovate, elliptic-ovate to oblong-ovate; basal pair elliptic to oval to suborbicular, 4.5-13.2 × 3-10.4 cm; other leaflets 7.9-25.9 × 3.6-11.2 cm; base generally strongly oblique, acute to attenuate; apex acute to rounded, sometimes broadly mucronate to attenuate, rarely retuse or emarginate, minutely mucronulate in some leaves due to extension of midrib; margin various, entire to remotely serrate, undulate or not, the leaflets frequently complicate and folded over in dry specimens; venation cladodromous to weakly brochidodromous, with 4-7 lateral veins, the midvein prominent throughout, reaching the apex, the secondaries prominent, the higher order venation conspicuous on both surfaces, less frequently obscure above. Inflorescence moderately to very congested, occasionally branched or with two inflorescences per leaf axil, axillary, rarely lateral, 2.7-3.5 cm diam.; peduncle 1.7-3.5 cm long, 1.25-1.5 mm diam, immediately below inflorescence; floral rhachis 5-14.5 cm long, ferruginous appressed-puberulent to sparsely appressed-pubescent; bracteoles strongly heteromorphic, the basal ones 3-5 mm long, frequently absent, usually broken off, linear, velutinous, the superior ones 1-1.5 mm long, triangular, ferruginous-pubescent, frequently contrasting against the sparsely indumented rhachis, the inferior bracteoles frequently reflexed; flower-pair peduncle absent to 4 mm long, appressed , ferruginous-puberulent; pedicels 1.5-4 mm long. Buds 2-2.5 mm broad at apex, 0.5-0.75 mm broad at midlength, essentially erect, sparsely ferruginous-puberulent. Rowers 6-10 mm long, all perianth segments recurving at anthesis; tepals 1-1.3 cm long, 0.25-0.75 mm across at midlength, keeled. Anthers subsessile, ca. 1.5 mm long. Hypogynous nectaries fused into a quadrangle, usually 1 mm high and 1 mm across, frequently dwarfing the ovary, the abaxial gap not present. Ovary 1-1.5 mm long, generally narrow, slightly wider than the style, sometimes pyriform, glabrous, very rarely with some very sparse pubescence on the lower half. Infructescence 8.4-9.2 cm long; fruit pedicels 56 mm long, 1-1.25 mm thick. Fruit (immature) subglobose to broadly obovoid, occasionally slightly compressed, 1.2-1.6 × 0.8-1.2 cm, drying dark brown, minutely pustulate, rough to the touch. Exterior mesocarp 0.5 mm thick, black; interior mesocarp 1-1.25 mm thick, porous, light in color.

description: Tree, to 10 m. Young stems dull rufous brown to light ferruginous, densely tomentose, the indumentum ferruginous; trichomes occasionally present; older branches dark brown to black, glabrous or sparsely pubescent (glabrescent), sometimes with patches of tomentum, striate. Lenticels absent or visible only on mature stems, sometimes conspicuous against the dark bark, numerous, minute to 0.75 mm long, orbicular, elliptic to linear, slightly prominent, beige to orangeish-red, often producing very fine fissures making the lenticels appear linear. Petiole 3.2-9 cm long, terete, 2-3.25 mm diam, at the base, glabrescent to ferruginous-tomentose. Leaf rhachis 9.7-15.5 cm long, the terminal appendix 3.5-7 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, commonly yellowish pubescent, contrasting with the sparser rhachis; leaflets subsessile to short-petiolate; petiolules 3-15 mm long, 2-3 mm diam, at the base. Leaflets 4-5 pairs, opposite to rarely strongly subopposite, frequently complicate, drying folded in herbarium material, commonly overlapping, drying medium green to brown or black, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, matte, rarely shiny, glabrescent to sparsely yellow-pilose, rarely glabrous above, essentially glabrous to pubescent beneath, the pubescence concentrated on venation, the young leaves densely yellowish-pilose on both surfaces of lamina, symmetrical to strongly asymmetrical, commonly curved, lanceolate to broadly ovate or oblong-ovate to narrowly elliptic; basal pair similar to terminal leaflets but frequently broader, 5.4-11 × 2.2-5.5 cm; lateral leaflets 7.1-13.5 × 3.4-4.2 cm; base equal to strongly oblique, narrowing, decurrent or if clearly petiolate acute; apex acute to narrowly acuminate, less frequently obtuse in terminal leaflets, the basal leaflets like terminal leaflets but usually broader at the apex, often obtuse to rounded; margin remotely serrate to frequently remotely serrulate, in some instances the teeth minute, frequently undulate; venation cladodromous to brochidodromous, less frequently eucamptodromous, with 4-5 well-defined lateral veins, the midvein narrow, prominent, reaching the apex, the secondaries narrow moderately prominent to very prominent, higher-order venation commonly faint to obscure above, conspicuous beneath. Inflorescence congested, rarely branched, axillary, frequently with more than one inflorescence per leaf axil, 1.4-2.1 cm diam.; peduncle 1.2-5 cm long, 1.5-2mm diam, immediately below inflorescence; floral rhachis 713.7 cm long, ferruginous-tomentose to sparsely pubescent; bracteoles weakly heteromorphic, minute, 1-2 mm, ferruginous-pubescent, triangular to triangular-oval, not reflexed; flower-pair peduncle absent to 4 mm long, ferruginous-tomentose; pedicels 0.5-4 mm long. Buds 2-2.3 mm broad at apex, 0.7-1 mm broad at midlength, erect to ascending, appressed ferruginous-pubescent to densely tomentose, sometimes lighter towards the apex. Flowers 4-10 mm long, all tepals generally recurving at anthesis; tepals 0.6-0.75 mm across at midlength, not keeled. Anthers subsessile, ca. 1 mm long. Hypogynous nectaries fused into a quadrangle or closely juxtaposed, an abaxial gap present. Ovary 0.5-2.5 mm long, globose, less frequently conical, long rufous-hirsute with spreading hairs, indumentum covering entire ovary, rarely covering only lower half. Fruit unknown.

description: Tree. Young stems reddish-brown to grayish, the indumentum rufous- to ferruginous-tomentose, fading to gray or lost with maturity, striations occasionally visible; older branches dark grayish to brownish-black, glabrous or with sparse pubescence (glabrescent), unfissured or small fissured. Lenticels few to numerous, generally minute and inconspicuous, 0.25-0.5 mm long, suborbicular to linear, slightly prominent, ferruginous, fissures rarely produced or very small, frequently interspaced with very large suborbicular to elliptic lenticels to 3 mm long, dull brown. Petiole 3-8 cm long, terete, 3-4 mm diam, at the base, ferruginous-tomentose. Leaf rhachis 9-15 cm long, the terminal appendix 2-5 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm broad, frequently absent; leaflets short-petiolate, the petiolules 4-8 mm long, 2-4 mm diam, at the base. Leaflets 3-4 pairs, opposite to strongly subopposite, overlapping; drying weakly bicolorous, green to black above, reddish beneath, subcoriaceous, matte, glabrous to sparsely ferruginous-pubescent above, denser on midvein and near the base, sparsely ferruginous-pubescent beneath, the venation densely tomentose, symmetrical to asymmetrical, elliptic or oval-oblong to broadly obovate or oval-elliptic, less frequently oblong-ovate; basal pair ovate, ovate-oblong to suborbicular, 3.2-7 × 1-3.7 cm; lateral leaflets 4.5-14 × 1.2-5.1 cm (the smaller diameter due to folding over of leaflets); base equal to weakly oblique, rounded to briefly acuminate; apex acute to rounded, sometimes retuse or emarginate, the midvein frequently extending to form a minute mucro; margin entire to remotely serrulate, the teeth usually concentrated towards the apex, undulate or not, sometimes strongly revolute; venation cladodromous to brochidodromous, with 3-7 lateral veins, the midvein prominent below, reaching the apex, the secondaries thin, prominent, higher order venation conspicuous on both sides of lamina. Inflorescence congested to lax, unbranched, axillary to terminal, 1.3-3.2 cm diam., frequently longer than the leaves; peduncle 1.8-3 cm long, 1.5-2.75 mm diam, immediately below inflorescence; floral rhachis (5.8-) 16.3-22 cm long, ferruginous-tomentose to rufous tomentose-pubescent; bracteoles uniform, minute, 1-2 mm long, broadly to narrowly triangular, ferruginous-pilose to ferruginous-tomentose, not reflexed; flower-pair peduncle 1.75-4.5 mm long, ca.1 mm diam., ferruginous-tomentose to long rufous-tomentose; pedicels 1-5 mm long. Buds ca. 2.5 mm broad at the apex, ca. 1 mm broad at midlength, essentially erect, ferruginous-tomentose. Flowers 5-8 mm long, all perianth segments recurving at anthesis; tepals ca. 0.75 mm across at midlength, weakly keeled. Anthers sessile, 1-1.5 mm long. Hypogynous nectaries fused into a quadrangle, 0.5-0.75 mm high and 1-1.5 mm across, or distinct, trigonous, with a large abaxial gap. Ovary 0.5-2.5 mm long, pyriform to ovoid, glabrous to ferruginous-pubescent, the indumentum covering only lower half. Fruit unknown. Diagnostic characters. This species may be identified by its combination of medium sized leaflets which are sparsely pubescent beneath, glabrous ovary, with occasional pubescence at the base, and densely tomentose perianth indumentum.

description: Tree, to 7 m. Young stems grayish to yellowish-brown or orangish, glabrescent to grayish-yellow or light ferruginous-velutinous to densely pubescent, with ribbon-like trichomes absent to numerous, the striations obscure to broadly prominent; older branches light to dark brown, glabrescent with grayish cuticle, striate or not; fissures numerous, broad and shallow to long and deep. Lenticels few to numerous, especially conspicuous in older branches, minute to 2 mm long, orbicular to narrowly elliptic, prominent, beige to dark red or orangish, often with a clear split in the center, producing fissures when mature. Petiole 3-6.5 cm long, terete, 1.75-3 mm diam, at the base, yellowish to ferruginous, glabrescent to densely pubescent or tomentose, frequently with numerous trichomes. Leaf rhachis 5.8-14.5 cm long, the terminal appendix 2-5 mm long, 0.5-1 mm broad; leaflets subsessile to short-petiolate, the petiolules 2-9 mm long, 1.5-2 mm diam, at the base. Leaflets (2-)3-5 pairs, opposite to almost alternate, commonly overlapping, drying light green to brown, chartaceous, matte, glabrous to sparsely pubescent above, glabrescent to sparsely pubescent beneath, indumentum appressed or spreading, the venation sparsely to densely pubescent with numerous trichomes, weakly asymmetrical, oblong, to oblong-ovate to broadly elliptic, less frequently strongly obovate, occasionally folded in specimens; basal pair similar to lateral leaflets, but generally broader and frequently suborbicular, (3.2-)4.2-11 × 1-4.5 cm; other leaflets (5-)6-13.2 × (2.5-)3.3-5.7 cm; base equal or oblique, decurrent; apex subacute, acuminate to obtuse, less frequently cuspidate, retuse, truncate or rounded, the basal leaflets frequently truncate; margin remotely serrulate, to crenate to almost entire, frequently lobed and undulate; venation eucamptodromous to cladodromous, with 3-7 lateral veins, the midvein very prominent throughout or becoming obscure towards the apex, reaching the apex, the secondaries very fine, generally prominent, the higher order venation conspicuous on both sides of lamina, rarely obscure above. Inflorescence congested to moderately congested, unbranched, axillary, rarely terminal, sometimes with more than one inflorescence per leaf axil, 2-3 cm diam.; peduncle 1-5.7 cm long, 1.5-2.5 mm diam, immediately below inflorescence; floral rhachis 7.7-16.9 cm long, ferruginous-yellowish appressed-puberulent to appressed-pubescent, without trichomes; bracteoles uniform, 0.5-1 mm long, triangular, yellowish hirsute to ferruginous-pubescent, not recurved; flower-pair peduncle 1-3.5 mm long, light ferruginous-velutinous to ferruginous-pubescent; pedicels absent. Buds 2-2.5 mm broad at apex, sometimes with a small beak, 0.8-1 mm broad at midlength, erect to ascending, yellowish to ferruginous appressed-pubescent. Flowers 7-12 mm long, one tepal remaining erect at anthesis; tepals ca. 0.5 mm across at midlength, keeled or not. Anthers subsessile, ca. 1-1.5 mm long. Hypogynous nectaries distinct, the abaxial ones positioned higher up, the nectaries well separated from each other, the abaxial gap very broad, but lateral gaps and adaxial gaps also present. Ovary 1-3 mm long, pyriform to ovoid, sparsely pubescent to pilose, the indumentum yellowish to ferruginous, covering entire ovary. Fruit unknown. Diagnostic characters. This species is characterized by the oblong or elliptic-oblong leaflets with broadly serrulate margins, predominantely yellowish-gray indumentum, sessile flowers, yellowish to ferruginous ovary indumentum covering the entire ovary, and the distinct hypogynous glands. It is also one of two species with ribbon-like trichomes (see also Euplassa incana).

description: Tree, to 30 m. Young stems orangish-brown, ferruginous-velutinous to glabrous, the striations narrow, multiple; older branches light brown to black, glabrescent, patchy, sometimes with a thin white coating, striate or small fissured. Lenticels numerous to few, minute and inconspicuous, 0.50.75 mm long, suborbicular to narrowly elliptic, prominent, ferruginous to rufous, rarely producing fissures and if so, very small ones. Petiole 4.8-12(-20) cm long, terete to laterally compressed, 2-3.5(-5.5) mm diam, at the base, velutinous or rarely glabrescent with rows of pilose (villous) hairs. Leaf rhachis 6-21.7(45) cm long, the terminal appendix 1.5-5 mm long, ca. 1 mm in broad, usually absent; leaflets subsessile to short-petiolate, the petiolules to 1.3 cm long, 2.25-2.5 mm diam, at the base. Leaflets 34(-5) pairs, opposite to almost alternate, commonly overlapping, drying olive green to black; coriaceous to subcoriaceous, occasionally chartaceous, if the latter then shiny; glabrous above, glabrous to very sparsely white-puberulent beneath, the indumentum if present short and closely adpressed and concentrated on venation, frequently asymmetrical, elliptic to broadly elliptic, less commonly obovate or ovate, usually curving; basal pair similar to terminal ones, 6.5-14.5(-22.7) × 3.2-5.5(-7.5) cm; lateral leaflets 10.8-13(-24.5) × 4.3-7.6 cm; base equal to rarely weakly oblique, decurrent; apex acute to obtuse, less frequently rounded, truncate or retuse, especially in the basal leaflets, sometimes broadly mucronate; margin entire to denticulate, commonly undulate; venation cladodromous to brochidodromous, with 4-7 lateral veins, midvein prominent throughout, reaching apex, the secondaries faintly prominent, the higher order venation always conspicuous beneath, in coriaceous leaves obscure above. Inflorescence moderately lax, occasionally branched, axillary, 2.1-3 cm diam.; peduncle 2.9-9.4 cm long, 1.5-2 mm diam, immediately below inflorescence; floral rhachis 12.4-16.5 cm long, ferruginous to gray, densely appressed-puberulent; bracteoles heteromorphic, the basal ones unusually long, to 4 mm long, linear, light ferruginous-hirsute, the superior ones smaller, 0.5-1.25 mm long, broadly triangular, not recurved; flower-pair peduncle 1-4 mm long, ferruginous-velutinous; pedicels 1.5-5 mm long. Buds 2.5-3 mm broad at apex, (rostrate) possessing a pronounced beak to 1 mm long, ca. 0.8-1 mm broad at midlength, essentially erect, the indumentum ferruginous-villous, but often sparser and lighter in color. Flowers 7-11 mm long, all tepals recurving at anthesis, rarely one remaining erect; tepals 0.5-0.75 mm across at midlength, keeled or not. Anthers subsessile, 1-1.2 mm long. Hypogynous nectaries fused into a quadrangle or ring 0.5-0.75 mm high and 1-1.25 mm across, the abaxial gap large. Ovary 1.5-2 mm long, narrow, cylindrical-pyriform, square in cross section, rufous-hirsute to short-pilose, the indumentum covering entire ovary, more or less appressed. Infructescence 13.1-14 cm long; fruit pedicel 8-9 mm long, ca. 2 mm thick. Young fruit ovoid, 15-16 mm long and 10-11 mm diam.

description: Tree. Young stems dark reddish-brown, the indumentum short, densely ferruginous- or rufous-crispate, lost with maturity, strongly striate; older branches grayish to black, glabrescent, intermittently striated, generally small fissured. Lenticels absent to moderately numerous, especially on young branches, minute, < 0.5 mm long, circular to narrowly elliptic, slightly prominent, beige to reddish, producing minute fissures. Petiole 3.2-7.2 cm long, terete, 2.25-3 mm diam, at the base, ferruginous to rufous-crispate. Leaf rhachis 4.2-7.3 cm long, the terminal appendix 2-4 mm long, ca. 1.5 mm broad, frequently absent; leaflets subsessile to short-petiolate, the peti-olules 1-5 mm long, sometimes absent, 2.5-3 mm diam, at the base. Leaflets 2-3 pairs, opposite to weakly subopposite, commonly overlapping, drying olive green to dark brown above, bright ferruginous beneath; subcoriaceous, matte, glabrous to glabrescent above with crispate pubescence at base of lamina, very densely ferruginous-crispate beneath, the indumentum obscuring lamina and tertiary venation, symmetrical to asymmetrical, suborbicular, obovate, oblong to broadly elliptic; basal pair similar to other leaflets but generally more suborbicular, 4.4-9.2 cm × 3.9-5.8 cm; other leaflets 7-9.6 cm × 4.75.7 cm; base equal to weakly oblique, briefly narrowing; apex rounded or obtuse, rarely truncate (although common in basal leaflets), frequently retuse, sometimes minutely mucronulate due to slight extension of the midvein; margin essentially entire, but frequently unevenly and remotely crenate, sometimes undulate; venation cladodromous to less frequently brochidodromous, with 4-6 lateral veins, the midvein prominent, generally reaching the apex, sometimes forking, secondaries not prominent but well marked, higher order venation obscure on both sides of lamina. Inflorescence moderately congested, unbranched, 1.5-2.lcm diam., axillary; peduncle 2.3-3.2 cm long, 1.5-2 mm diam, immediately below inflorescence; floral rhachis 5.2-10.2 cm long, ferruginous- to rufous-crispate; bracteoles strongly heteromorphic, the basal ones 3-8 mm long and 2-6 mm broad, leaf-like, frequently absent, the superior ones linear but with some expansion of distal end, ca. 3 mm, all ferruginous-crispate, curved strongly upwards; flower-pair peduncle 1-3 mm long, 0.8 mm diam., ferruginous- to rufous-crispate; pedicels absent. Buds 2-2.3 mm broad at apex, 1-1.25 mm broad at midlength, essentially erect, ferruginous- to rufous-crispate. Flowers 6-9 mm long, one perianth segment remaining erect at anthesis; tepals ca. 0.5 mm across at midlength, not keeled. Anthers subsessile, ca. 1.5 mm long. Hypogynous nectaries distinct, the two abaxial nectaries closely juxtaposed, trigonous, positioned farther up than the adaxial nectaries, the latter rounded, a large abaxial gap present. Ovary 1-2.5 mm long, pyriform, glabrous. Fruit unknown. Diagnostic characters. Euplassa rufa is easily identified by its characteristic leaflets with entire margins and a bright ferruginous-crispate indumentum beneath that obscures the lamina. The flowers are sessile and subtended by a common peduncle. The ovary is glabrous. Field characters. Unknown.

description: Tree, to 9 m. Young stems ferruginous-brown, the indumentum short, dense, ferruginous-tomentose, the striations faint or absent; older branches grayish-brown to black, glabrescent, frequently with a few remains of gray-white tomentum; fissures numerous, shallow, forming a network. Lenticels apparently absent but probably obscured by fissures. Petiole 3.2-5.5 cm long, terete, 2.75-3.5 mm diam, at the base, dense ferruginous-tomentose. Leaf rhachis 6.5-11.7 cm long, the terminal appendix 3.5-13 mm long, 1.25-1.5 mm broad, occasionally absent; leaflets subsessile or short-petiolate, the petiolules to 8 mm long, 2.54 mm diam, at the base. Leaflets (2-)34(-5) pairs, opposite to weakly subopposite, overlapping, subcoriaceous, shiny or matte, glabrous to pubescent, venation densely pubescent to tomentose especially towards the base, occasionally spreading to base of lamina, ferruginous-pubescent beneath, the indumentum appressed or erect, the venation ferruginous-tomentose, symmetrical to weakly asymmetrical, ovate-oblong to oval to narrowly obovate; basal pair similar to terminal leaflets to suborbicular, 5.4-8.3 × 3.2-6.3 cm; other leaflets 7.5-12.6 × 4.3-7.8 cm; base equal to oblique, decurrent; apex obtuse to rounded, frequently retuse or emarginate; margin entire, sometimes minutely revolute towards the base; venation cladodromous, with 4-5 lateral veins, the midvein prominent, especially towards the base, reaching the apex, rarely forking, the secondaries very narrow, prominent, higher order venation minutely reticulate, faint on both surfaces of lamina. Inflorescence very congested, axillary, 2-3 cm diam.; peduncle 1.4-2.6 cm long, 2-2.5 mm diam, immediately below inflorescence; floral rhachis 10.2-12 cm long, short ferruginous-tomentose; bracteoles heteromorphic, the basal ones ca. 1.5 mm long, linear, the superior ones ca. 0.5 mm, broadly triangular, all ferruginous-tomentose, not reflexed; flower-pair peduncle 2.54 mm long, ferruginous-tomentose; pedicels 0.75-1 mm long. Buds 2.5-3 mm broad at apex, 1-1.5 mm broad at midlength, erect to nodding, ferruginous-tomentose. Rowers 5-8 mm long, all perianth segments recurving at anthesis, occasionally one tepal remaining erect; tepals 0.5-0.75 mm across at midlength, not keeled. Anthers subsessile, 1-1.5 mm long. Hypogynous nectaries fused into a quadrangle or ring 5 mm high and 1-1.25 mm across, a small abaxial gap present. Ovary ca. 2.5 long, narrowly ovoid to pyriform, the indumentum long, light ferruginous-villous. Infructescence ca. 13 cm long (from single specimen); fruit pedicel ca. 1.5 mm thick. Fruit ovoid to narrowly ovoid, 3-3.4 cm long and 1.8-2.2 cm diam., drying brown, rugulose to corrugated.

description: Erect shrub (0.15-)l-3(-5) m tall; mature stems terete, striate, glabrate; bark reddish-brown, cracking longitudinally; twigs subterete, densely strigose with golden to ferruginous, straight to distally crisped, eglandular hairs 2-3 mm long; buds terete, ovate, scales ovate, obtuse, apiculate, ciliolate and short-pilose distally, reddish-brown. Leaves coriaceous, ovate to elliptic-ovate, (3-)5.5-8.5(-11) × (1.5-) 2-3(-5) cm, base broadly cuneate, obtuse, or rounded, apex acuminate, slightly apiculate, margin obviously crenate with each tooth terminating in a deciduous, basally swollen hair to 2 mm long, newly unfolding leaves densely golden to ferruginous strigose with eglandular hairs which do not obscure surfaces, when mature upper surface appressed sub-setose, glabrate, lower surface usually persistently strigose or glabrate and then swollen hair bases remaining as tiny papillae; midrib, lateral nerves (3-4 per side), and reticulate veinlets all impressed above and raised beneath; petiole subterete, rugose, canaliculate above, (3.5-)4.5-9 mm long, pubescent as stems. Inflorescence axillary, racemose, 10-15 (-20)-flowered; rachis subterete, bluntly angled, 3-5.5(-7.5) cm long, densely strigose to hirsute with straight, golden to ferruginous, eglandular or minutely gland-tipped hairs 1.5-2 mm long, at base circumscribed by a series of ovate to oblong-elliptic, obtuse, striate, ciliolate bracts to 8 mm long; pedicels terete, 6-10(-12) mm long at anthesis, pubescent with appressed to hirsute, crisped, golden to ferruginous, eglandular or minutely gland-tipped hairs ca. 1-1.5 mm long (also weakly short-pilose with white hairs); bracteoles basal or nearly so, chartaceous, often wide-spreading, linear-ovate, 3-4(-4.5) × 0.5-0.8(-1.2) mm, acuminate, ciliolate, often distally short-pilose (marginally subsetose with minutely gland-tipped hairs); floral bract coriaceous, elongate, concave to cochleariform, spreading or often reflexed, oblong, elliptic to oblanceolate, conspicuously striate, 8-12 × 2.5-6 mm, acute, ciliolate, basally subsetose along margin with minutely gland-tipped hairs. Flowers with calyx 3.5-5 mm long, moderately to densely appressed-hirsute with straight or somewhat crisped, golden to ferruginous, eglandular or very rarely minutely gland-tipped hairs (also weakly short-pilose with white hairs at very base, or only pilose), lobes broadly ovate, 2.5-3 × 2-2.2 mm, acuminate, ciliolate and often short-pilose distally within; corolla cylindric-urceolate, subterete to bluntly 5-angled, 6-7(-8) × 4-5 mm, densely appressed subsetose with straight, golden to ferruginous, eglandular hairs, glabrous or short-pilose within, (white?) pink to red when fresh, lobes triangular, obtuse, ca. 1 mm long; stamens 4.3-5 mm long; filaments 3.4-4 mm long, moderately to densely white-villous; anthers 1.6-2 mm long, awns short (inconspicuous); ovary globose, densely short-pilose with white or cinereous hairs (glabrate after anthesis); style 3.5-5 mm long, moderately to densely short-pilose or glabrous. Fruiting calyx globose, 8-10 mm diam., blue-black, persistently pubescent. Chromosome number: n = 11, 2n = 22 (Luteyn & Cotton 11307).

description: Erect to clambering shrub. Petioles and midrib of leaf lamina adaxially glandular with black, minute (0.2 mm long), clavate setae. Floral bract and bracteoles 3, with surface glabrous, but ciliate; pedicels glabrous or only weakly puberulent and often with gland-tipped setae. Calyx lobes ciliate and often also marginally glandular-fimbriate; corolla rotate-campanulate, ± gibbous at base, glabrous, pale yellowish-green; stamens ca. 2.6 mm long; filaments ca. 1.6 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.3 mm long; ovary glabrous or nearly so; style 2-2.6 mm long, glabrous.

description: Young branches densely to sparsely puberulous or pubescent, soon becoming glabrous, typically smooth, dark brown with conspicuous pale lenticels, less frequently pale greyish-brown. Leaves pinnate with a terminal bud showing intermittent growth, to 35(-45) cm long; petiole semiterete, rhachis semiterete and canaliculate above or terete, puberulous or pubescent at first, soon glabrous; petiolule 1-6(-8) mm long. Leaflets opposite or rarely subopposite, to 9(-14) pairs, usually elliptic, oblong, or oblanceolate rarely lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate or acuminate less frequently acute, base usually acute, cuneate, or attenuate rarely obtuse or rounded, chartaceous or rarely subcoriaceous, (10-) 12.5-25(-35)[16.2] cm long, (2.5-)4-7(-10)[5.1] cm broad, glabrous or rarely with a few hairs on midrib below, usually obscurely glandular-punctate and -striate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly sunken; secondaries (6-)9-12(-17) on either side of midrib, steeply arcuate ascending, parallel to slightly or rarely strongly convergent; intersecondaries short; tertiaries oblique, ± parallel. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious; inflorescence usually axillary or rarely borne in axils of fallen leaves or on short lateral shoots, (4-)10-25(-45) cm long, thyrsoid, usually slender pyramidal with lower branches only 0.5-3 cm long, less frequently broadly pyramidal with lower branches to 25 cm, sparsely appressed, spreading puberulent, or pubescent; pedicel l(-2) mm long or flowers sessile. Calyx rotate, patelliform or cyathiform, (0.5-) 1-2.5(-3) mm long, with (2-)3-4(-5) acute to rounded or irregular lobes 0.25-2(-2.5) mm long or rarely margin truncate, sparsely or less frequently densely appressed puberulous or pubescent outside. Petals (3-)4-5), valvate or slightly imbricate, (5-)5.5-7.5(-9.5) mm long, (0.5-) 1-2(-2.5) mm broad, usually oblong less frequently lanceolate, apex acute, sparsely to densely appressed, spreading puberulous, or pubescent outside, papillose or glabrous inside. Staminal tube cylindrical, 3.5-7 mm long, (1-) 1.5-2.5(-3) mm broad, margin truncate, undulate, or rarely shallowly lobed, glabrous or occasionally slightly papillose; anthers (7-)8(-11), (0.6-)0.75-1.25 mm long; antherodes narrower, not dehiscing, without pollen. Nectary a stipe expanded above to form an annulus below ovary, (0.5-)1-2 mm long, glabrous. Ovary (3-)4(-5)-locular, loculi uniovulate, sparsely to densely appressed puberulent or pubescent rarely strigose or subglabrous; style appressed puberulent, pubescent, or glabrous; pistillode similar, with well-developed abortive ovules. Capsule globose to fig-shaped, apex truncate, usually abruptly contracted at base into a short stout stipe, smooth not wrinkling on drying, shining, nearly always with conspicuous sometimes pustular, pale lenticels, glabrous, 1.5-2.5 cm diam., 4-valved, valves 1-seeded; pericarp 12 mm thick, leathery. Seed ovoid, 1-1.3 cm long, 0.6-0.8 cm broad, surrounded by a thin orange sarcotesta which is slightly thickened at base, apex, and along adaxial surface; seed coat thin, cartilaginous; hilum 0.8-1 cm long. Embryo with thick, plano-convex, superposed or rarely oblique cotyledons; radicle abaxial towards the apex, extending to surface.
