description: Tree to 35 m high with a trunk to 65 cm in diam, glabrous except for the inflorescence; young twigs 4-channelled, 4-angled, or very narrowly 4-winged; bark of older trunk grayish to brown to dark reddish, shallowly fissured, often scaling off in irregular lengthwise pieces; inner living bark pale orange, very thin and brittle; wood brown to red-brown, hard and heavy. Petioles 4.0-8.0 mm long; blades rather coriaceous, usually an intense green and shining above, lighter below, 6.0-12.0 cm long, 1.7-4.7 cm wide, ovate to ovate-elliptic to oblong-elliptic, often narrowly so, acuminate or abruptly so at the apex, rounded to acute at base; midrib slightly grooved above at least when dry, prominent below, rounded at base, usually becoming 2-angled 1/6-1/2 of the way to the apex, seldom rounded most of the way; lateral nerves visible below and usually above when dry. Midrib xylem tubular; stomatal crypts Type II, averaging in a leaf ca 37-67 p in diam, 16-20 p high, 45-87 per sq mm (extremes 22-90 p diam, 15-27 p high, 36-105 per sq mm); upper epidermis one cell thick, without mucilaginous walls; hypodermis present, with frequent mucilaginous walls; free stone cells present only in petiole base; terminal sclereids basically stellate, the central body narrow, l-3(-6) times as long as wide, with downward arms and usually with a short stout vertical branch above with arms radiating upward, giving the hourglass form found in Af. grandiflora, sometimes the sclereid approaching the columnar condition. Inflorescences in the lower leaf axils and at upper leafless nodes on twigs up to 5.0 mm thick, 1-7 per side, often densely clustered, each 1-11-flowered, 1.0-5.5 mm long to base of farthest pedicel measured along the axes and with 1-3 internodes in that length; bracts 1.0-1.8 mm long, triangular to ovate-triangular, mostly deciduous by anthesis. Axes of inflorescence, bracts, and pedicels often minutely puberulent, the flower glabrous. True pedicels 2.0-4.5 mm long; calyx light green to yellowish-green, the calyx including the inferior ovary 4.2-5.0 mm long, campanulate; free hypanthium 1.4-1.7 mm long; calyx lobes before anthesis 0.9-1.2 mm long, 2.0-2.5 mm wide, 1.0-1.4 mm long from stamen attachment, broadly rounded-triangular and often apiculate, separating at anthesis a further length of 0-0.2 mm. Petals rose or light rose, 5.0-5.3 mm long, 4.2-4.6 mm wide, trullate to ovate, acute or abruptly so at apex, the base sessile or with a claw to 0.8 mm long, the margin minutely erose. Antesepalous filaments ca 4.0 mm long, antepetalous ones ca 4.5 mm long; anthers 2.0-3.0 mm long; sporangia 1.4-2.2 mm long, dehiscing by apical pores; gland 0.4-0.9 mm long, 1.3-1.9 mm from apex of anther when measured from center of gland; cauda ca 0.7-0.8 mm long. Ovary 4-5-locular; ovules axile-basal, produced only outwardly from each placenta, 14 or 15 in all; style 9.0-11.5 mm long. Fruit edible, orange to yellowish, globose to depressed-globose, not lobed, ca 20-28 mm long and 22-30 mm in diam when dry, ca 25-35 mm high and 28-38 mm in diam when fresh (said to be up to 50 mm high), with a terminal flat round calyx scar 4.0-9.0 mm in diam and a short obconic stipe at base 1.0-3.0 mm long, the flesh ca 1 cm thick; the fruits when ca ¼-¾ full size tend to be broadest above the middle, but this form is not seen in fully ripe fruits. Seeds 2-4, medium to dark brown, 14.0-16.3 mm long, 8.3-11.6 mm wide, 6.89.2 mm thick, irregularly ellipsoid, flattened on the contact faces, with a rough roundish to half-round to elliptic hilum 1.0-2.5 mm high and 2.5-4.5 mm wide at the base facing one side.

description: Young branches sparsely short pubescent (trichomes basifixed) becoming glabrous, pale greyish-brown, usually lenticellate. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate or pinnate with one leaflet of ultimate pair orientated to simulate a terminal leaflet, 10-20 cm long; petiole and rhachis semiterete, short pubescent to subglabrous; petiolule 2-6 mm long. Leaflets alternate or opposite, dimorphic, 5-9 with 1-3 pairs of greatly reduced often caducous leaflets ("pseudostipules") near base of petiole, elliptic to oblong or oblanceolate, apex short acuminate or attenuate, base often oblique, acute or cuneate to rounded or truncate, chartaceous, 9-12[10.4] cm long, 3.5-4.2[3.9] cm broad, upper surface glabrous, lower midrib sometimes puberulous or short pubescent, usually glandular-punctate and -striate; basal reduced leaflets linear, spathulate, ovate or reniform, 0.7-2 cm long; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat or slightly sunken; secondaries 13-16 on either side of midrib, ascending, straight or slightly arcuate, parallel or slightly convergent; intersecondaries short; tertiaries moderately prominent. Flowers unisexual, plant dioecious; inflorescence axillary, 11-15 cm long, often branched only in upper half, a rather densely-flowered, slender or pyramidal thyrse, sparsely pubescent; pedicel stout 0.75-1.5 mm long. Calyx patelliform or cyathiform, 0.75-1.5 mm long, with 4-5 shallow obtuse to rounded lobes or margin undulate, short pubescent. Petals 4-5, fused 1/3-2/3 their length, valvate, spreading, 4.5-6 mm long, 1-2 mm broad, lanceolate, apex acute, outside sparsely to moderately appressed pubescent, inside glabrous. Staminal tube cylindrical sometimes slightly narrower at throat; filaments completely fused, 4-4.5 mm long, 1.5-3 mm broad, [male] with alternate filaments slightly shorter, margin truncate or terminated by 2 short acute lobes, [female] with filaments ± same length, glabrous or with a few sparse hairs in throat, anthers (7-)8-10, 0.8-1 mm long, glabrous; antherodes slender, not dehiscent, without pollen. Nectary absent or sometimes represented by a small swelling at base of ovary. Ovary ovoid, 3-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, densely tomentose; style stout, glabrous above; style-head capitate, equalling anthers; pistillode very small, conical, containing small non-functional ovules and bearing a long slender style. Fruit unknown.

description: Young branches slender, pubescent, densely pubescent or rarely villose, usually soon becoming glabrous, greyish-brown to dark brown with prominent pale lenticels. Bud scales absent. Leaves trifoliolate or rarely unifoliolate; petiole 24.5 cm long, semiterete, sometimes expanded laterally below insertion of leaflets, usually glabrous, less frequently sparsely to densely pubescent (straight erect hairs); petiolule 1-3 mm long. Leaflets opposite, (l-)3, narrowly elliptic or oblanceolate, apex usually attenuate, acute or acuminate, rarely rounded, base attenuate, cuneate or acute, sometimes slightly oblique, chartaceous, 5.5-13(-17)[10.1] cm long, 1.3-3.2[2.3] cm broad, terminal leaflet sometimes larger than laterals, upper surface usually glabrous, rarely with puberulous or pubescent midrib and scattered pubescent lamina, lower surface usually glabrous, less frequently sparsely to densely pubescent especially on midrib and veins, granular red papillae sometimes present, prominently glandular-punctate and -striate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib sharply prominent; secondaries (10-) 13-18(-25) on either side of midrib, shallowly to steeply ascending, arcuate, parallel or slightly convergent; intersecondaries short to moderately long. Flowers unisexual, plants monoecious or dioecious; inflorescences clustered on new growth in axils of caducous scale-leaves, 1.5-12 cm long, usually a slender thyrse with lateral branches to 1 cm long, less frequently racemose, sparsely to densely pubescent or glabrous, rarely villose; pedicel 1-3 mm long. Calyx cyathiform or patelliform, (0.75-) 1-2 mm long, sepals (4-)5, free or fused 1/3 their length, aestivation open or slightly overlapping at base, ovate to triangular, apex acute or attenuate, pubescent to glabrous, often ciliate. Petals (4-)5, free, imbricate, 2.5-3(-4) mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate, apex acute to rounded, sometimes ciliate, usually glabrous outside or less frequently papillose or sparsely pubescent, inside usually papillose. Staminal tube cyathiform, 1-1.75(-2) mm long, (1-) 1.5-2 mm broad; filaments free or fused 2/3 their length, terminated by 2 short acute or triangular appendages or apex truncate, outside crisped puberulous to subglabrous, inside crisped puberulous to barbate especially in upper half; anthers 10, 0.7-1.2 mm long, glabrous; antherodes shrunken, not dehisced, without pollen. Nectary in [male] flowers usually conspicuous, annular or less frequently patelliform, fused to reduced pistillode, glabrous; in 2 flowers reduced to a small swelling around base of swollen ovary. Ovary broad ovoid, 3-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, glabrous (sometimes developing puberulous indumentum after fertilization); style short, stout, glabrous surmounted by a large 3-lobed, broad style-head; pistillode much reduced, sunken in annular nectary, containing small nonfunctional ovules, style longer than in 2 flowers. Capsule ovoid, oblong or ellipsoid, apex acute or rounded, base truncate or rounded, weakly tuberculate at least in upper half, usually glabrous, less frequently pubescent, 0.8-2 cm long, 0.5-1.3 cm broad, 3-valved; pericarp 0.75-1 mm thick; endocarp thick, cartilaginous. Seed 1 per fruit, 0.8-1.5 cm long, 0.50.9 cm broad, ellipsoid, completely covered by thin fleshy 3-partite arillode which is closely appressed to but not fused with the seed coat; seed coat thin, soft. Embryo with plano-convex, collateral cotyledons (1 of these rarely reduced to a vestige); radicle apical, extending to surface. Endosperm absent.

description: Young branches strigulose (some trichomes dibrachiate) soon glabrous, rough, greyish-brown, lenticellate. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate or pinnate with one leaflet of ultimate pair orientated to simulate a terminal leaflet, 4.9-10.5 cm long; petiole and rhachis narrowly winged, wing slightly broadened below each leaflet, glabrous; petiolule 0-1 mm long. Leaflets alternate to opposite, 5-9, usually elliptic, less frequently oblanceolate, oblong or lanceolate gradually narrowed to a slender emarginate apex, base narrowly attenuate, subcoriaceous, 8-11.5[9.2] cm long, 2.2-3.2[2.6] cm broad, upper midrib sometimes puberulous, otherwise glabrous, glandular-punctate and -striate or not; venation eucamptodromous or brochidodromous, midrib prominent; secondaries 13-19 on either side of midrib, ascending, arcuate, usually ± parallel; intersecondaries often long; tertiaries obscure. Flowers unisexual, plant probably monoecious; inflorescence axillary or several clustered on a short axillary shoot, 3-7 cm long, a small panicle or thyrse, often branched from base, sparsely strigulose; pedicel 0.5-1.5 mm long. Calyx patelliform, 0.5-1 mm long, with (3-)4-5 shallow triangular to rounded lobes to 1/2 length of calyx or margin subtruncate, sparse minute appressed hairs on outer surface or glabrous. Petals (3-)4(-5), free, valvate or slightly imbricate, reflexed, 2.5-3.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, lanceolate, apex acute, sometimes hooded. Staminal tube cyathiform; filaments completely fused, ca. 1.5 mm long, 1.5-2 mm broad, margin with 7-10 short acute lobes alternating with anthers and to Vi their length, outer surface with a few crisped hairs near apex and sparse coarse indumentum in throat; anthers 7-10, 0.8-1 mm, glabrous; antherodes slender, not dehiscent, without pollen. Nectary absent. Ovary ovoid, 3-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, short appressed puberulous; style stout, glabrous; style-head capitate or discoid, equalling anthers; pistillode conical, with small nonfunctional ovules. Fruit unknown.

description: Young branches sparsely strigulose, appressed, crisped or erect puberulous, or moderately to densely erect stiff pubescent (hairs mostly simple basifixed, sometimes with a few dibrachiate), becoming glabrous, greyish-white or -brown, usually lenticellate. Bud scales absent. Leaves usually imparipinnate, less frequently trifoliolate rarely unifoliolate, 0.5-12(-18.5) cm long; petiole and rhachis semiterete, minutely puberulous to densely stiff pubescent or glabrous; petiolule 0-4 mm long. Leaflets opposite or subopposite, strongly dimorphic, (1-)3-7(-9) with 1 pair of greatly reduced basal leaflets ("pseudostipules") clasping base of petiole, oblanceolate, elliptic, oblong or lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate or acuminate, less frequently obtusely cuspidate to obtuse rarely minutely emarginate, base nearly always asymmetric, cuneate, acute, rounded, truncate, or minutely cordate to auriculate, base of terminal leaflets usually symmetric and narrowly attenuate, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, (4.5-)5.5-12(-28)[10.6] cm long, 2-5.5(-10)[3.9] cm broad, terminal usually larger, basal pair often much smaller, upper surface nearly always glabrous rarely with midrib sparsely puberulous, lower surface usually glabrous less frequently midrib and veins sparsely to densely puberulous or stiffly pubescent rarely with lamina pubescent, glandular-punctate and -striate or not; basal reduced leaflets usually orbicular or ovate with a cordate or reniform base less frequently obovate to spathulate, with a short petiolule, 0.1-2.5(-3.9) cm long, persistent; venation eucamptodromous to brochidodromous, midrib flat or slightly prominent or slightly sunken; secondaries 8-12(-16) on either side of midrib, ascending, straight or arcuate, parallel or convergent; intersecondaries often moderate to long; tertiary reticulum usually obscure. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious; inflorescence axillary, to 2 cm long, a small few- to many-flowered fascicle with thyrsoid branching, $ inflorescence often reduced to 1-2 flowers, puberulous to glabrous; pedicel 0.25-0.5(-l) mm long. Calyx patelliform or cyathiform, 0.5-1(-1.5) mm long, with (3-)4-5(-6) broadly triangular or ovate lobes, ca. 1/2 length of calyx, puberulous on outer surface or glabrous. Petals 3-5, fused their length, valvate, reflexing, 2.5-4(-4.5) mm long, 0.75-1.25(-1.5) mm broad, lanceolate or narrowly triangular, apex acute, usually hooded, glabrous or sparsely strigulose or appressed puberulous on outer surface. Staminal tube urceolate or shortly cylindrical; filaments completely fused, 1.5-3.5 mm long, 0.75-2(-2.5) mm broad, margin with (4-)5-8(-9) short acute lobes alternating with anthers and 1/4-2/3 their length, outside crisped puberulous in upper half or glabrous, sparsely coarse pubescent to barbate in throat; anthers (4-)5-8(-9), 0.7-1.2 mm long, glabrous; antherodes slender, not dehiscent, without pollen. Nectary absent. Ovary ovoid, 3-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, puberulous to dense stiff pubescent; style glabrous; style-head capitate equalling or slightly below antherodes; pistillode conical containing small non-functional ovules and bearing a style-head set well below anthers. Capsule oblong or ellipsoid, apex acute to rounded, apiculate, smooth to verrucose, usually appressed puberulous less frequently densely papillose intermixed with a few stiff appressed hairs, 1-2.5 cm long, 0.5-1.3 cm broad, 3-valved; pericarp 1-1.5 mm thick; endocarp thin, cartilaginous. Seeds 2, collateral in each fruit, to 1.8 cm long; arillode thick, fleshy, strongly developed only at apex of seed and along adaxial surface, free except for line of attachment from micropyle and along raphe; seed coat thin and soft. Embryo with plano-convex, collateral cotyledons; radicle apical, included. Endosperm absent.

description: Young branches densely stellate-tomentose finally becoming glabrous, pale grey-brown or brown with some small lenticels. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate, 8-15 cm long; petiole semi terete, rhachis ± terete, stellate-tomentose; petiolule 1-1.5(-3) mm long. Leaflets opposite, 9-11, usually oblanceolate, rarely elliptic, apex obtuse or obtusely cuspidate or rounded, base usually truncate or minutely cordate, less frequently rounded or broadly cuneate, chartaceous, 4.8-10[6.9] cm long, 2-4.2[3.1] cm broad, upper surface sparsely stellate-pubescent to subglabrous, denser along midrib, lower surface stellate-tomentose, not glandular-punctate or -striate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib usually sunken; secondaries 10-13 on either side of midrib, shallowly ascending, straight, parallel; intersecondary and tertiary venation obscure. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious; inflorescence axillary, 2-4 cm long, a rather dense flowered thyrse, stellate-tomentose; pedicel 0.25-0.5 mm long. Calyx shallowly cyathiform, 1.5-2  mm long, with 4-5 broadly triangular acute lobes 1/3-1/2 length of calyx, densely stellate-tomentose. Petals 5, free, slightly imbricate to subvalvate, 4-5 mm long, 1-2 mm broad, oblong, elliptic or narrowly lanceolate, apex acute, appressed lepidote-stellate outside, glabrous inside. Staminal tube cyathiform or short cylindrical, ca. 3 mm long, 1.5-2 mm broad; filaments fused 1/3-1/2 their length, apex rounded or emarginate, usually glabrous but rarely with a few appressed stellate hairs on outside; anthers 10, 0.7-0.8 mm long, glabrous. Nectary an annulus around base of pistillode, stellate-pubescent. Ovary not seen; pistillode conical, 3-locular, locules with 2 small collateral, nonfunctional ovules, stellate-pubescent; style glabrous at apex; style-head clavate or capitate, below or equalling anthers. Capsule globose or flattened-globose, densely dendroid-stellate, ca. 1 cm diam., 3-valved, valves opening widely; pericarp 0.75-1 mm thick, endocarp very hard cartilaginous. Seeds 1-2, collateral in each valve, ca. 0.5 cm long, 0.3-0.4 cm broad, with a thick fleshy ± apical arillode which extends down adaxial surface of seed; arillode free except for attachment from micropyle to raphe; seed coat hard, shining brown. Embryo with thin flat, ± orbicular collateral cotyledons; radicle superior, long exserted; embryo embedded in thin residual endosperm.

description: Young branches stout or massive, puberulous at first soon glabrous, pale greyish-brown, lenticellate, terminated by a small congested cluster of broadly lanceolate bud scales. Leaves pinnate, with limited apical growth(?), 20-50 cm long; petiole semiterete, rhachis terete, puberulous or glabrous; petiolule 1-2 mm long. Leaflets opposite or alternate, 12-24, oblong to lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate, base slightly asymmetric, usually obtuse to truncate less frequently narrowly attenuate or acute, chartaceous, (9-)11-18[13.3] cm long, (2.6-)4-6.5[4.5] cm broad, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat; secondaries 14-18 on either side of midrib, ascending, arcuate at tip, parallel or slightly convergent; intersecondaries and tertiary reticulum prominent. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious; inflorescences clustered in axils of fallen bud scales, 8-15 cm long, a slender panicle with short branches at base to 1 cm long, racemose above, minute puberulous or glabrous; pedicel 0.5-1 mm long. Calyx rotate to patelliform, sepals 0.75-1.5 mm long, ovate to orbicular, puberulous outside, ciliate. Petals 5.5-6.5 mm long, 1.5-2 mm broad, oblong or narrowly spathulate, apex rounded, subglabrous outside, glabrous inside. Staminal tube cyathiform or short cylindrical, 45 mm long, 2-3 mm broad, margin undulate or shortly 10-lobed, glabrous; anthers 10, 0.6-0.75 mm long, without a basal appendage, glabrous; antherodes slender, without pollen, not dehiscing. Nectary annular or a short stipe expanded below ovary, 0.25-1 mm long, glabrous. Ovary 3-locular, loculi with 2 superposed ovules, glabrous; style stout, glabrous; style-head discoid; pistillode similar, with well-developed non-functional ovules. Capsule ± globose, with or without a short stout stipe, rather rough, dark brown (when dry) with numerous large pale lenticels, glabrous, 3.5-4.5 cm diam., 3-valved, valves with 1-2 superposed seeds; pericarp 1-1.5 mm thick. Seed 1.3-2.5 cm long, 1-1.7 cm broad, ellipsoid when solitary, if 2 in a valve then upper truncate at base, lower truncate at apex, when solitary then with a thickened basal sarcotesta, when 2 superposed in valve then partially surrounded by a free fleshy arillode; seed coat membraneous; hilum ca. 1.2 cm long, 0.9 cm broad. Embryo with plano-convex, collateral cotyledons; radicle apical, extending to the surface.

description: Young branches appressed puberulous (some trichomes ± dibrachiate) soon becoming glabrous, dark to grey-brown, usually lenticellate. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate or pinnate with one leaflet of ultimate pair orientated to simulate a terminal leaflet, 6-25(-40) cm long; petiole and rhachis semiterete, usually glabrous or subglabrous, less frequently puberulous or rarely coarse pubescent; petiolule (1.5-)2-4(-5) mm long. Leaflets usually alternate, rarely subopposite or opposite, 5-15, elliptic or oblong, apex attenuate or acuminate, base often slightly asymmetric usually attenuate, less frequently acute or cuneate rarely obtuse, chartaceous to coriaceous, 8.5-17(-25) cm long, (2-)3-5(-6.5) cm broad, lower ones often much smaller, glabrous above, usually glabrous below but occasionally pubescent on midrib and secondary veins, sometimes glandular-punctate and -striate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat or slightly prominent; secondaries 9-20 on either side of midrib, arcuate ascending or ± straight, parallel to slightly convergent; intersecondaries present, short. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious (Skutch 2115 from Suchitepequez, Guatemala is apparently hermaphrodite); inflorescence axillary, (3-)5-20(-30) cm long, a few- to many-flowered thyrse, 9 inflorescence often shorter and with fewer flowers than [male], puberulous or glabrous; pedicel 0.5-1.5(-2) mm long. Calyx patelliform or shallowly cyathiform, 0.5-1.5 mm long, with (4-)5 ovate or triangular, acute, obtuse or rounded lobes 1/4-1/2 length of calyx, aestivation open, puberulous to subglabrous. Petals (4-)5(-6), usually fused 1/3-2/3 their length less frequently fused only at base or free, valvate, becoming reflexed, 3-4 mm long, 1-1.5(-2) mm broad, lanceolate, apex acute, sparsely appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Staminal tube cyathiform, urceolate or short cylindric; filaments completely fused, 1.5-3 mm long, (l-)1.5-2 mm broad, margin with (6-)8-10 acute or subulate lobes alternating with anthers and 1/4-1/2 their length, sparsely long hairy or glabrous outside, densely to sparsely long hairy inside especially at throat or subglabrous; anthers (6-)8-10, (0.6-)0.7-0.9(-l) mm long, glabrous or with a few hairs on back; antherodes slender, without pollen. Nectary absent. Ovary ovoid, (2-)3(-4)-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, densely strigose; style glabrous at least at apex; style-head minute, capitate, usually held well below anthers. Pistillode conical with well-formed non-functional ovules. Capsule broadly ellipsoid, ovoid or obovoid, usually smooth less frequently verrucose with irregular small rounded tubercules, sericeous to golden tomentose, 1.6-2.4 cm long, 1.4-1.6 cm broad, (2-)3(-4)-valved, valves remaining erect; pericarp 1-2 mm thick, rather soft; endocarp thin, cartilaginous. Seeds 1-2, collateral in each fruit, ca. 1.2 cm long, 0.8-0.9 cm broad, broadest above middle, completely surrounded by a thin, soft, fleshy arillode; arillode thickened somewhat at base and apex of seed, free except for a thin line of attachment from micropyle to raphe; seed coat thin, membraneous. Embryo with thick plano-convex, collateral cotyledons; radicle central or apical, included. Endosperm absent.

description: Young branches densely to sparsely oppressed puberulous (some trichomes ± dibrachiate) becoming glabrous, greyish or pale brown, lenticellate. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate or pinnate with one leaflet of the ultimate pair orientated to simulate a terminal leaflet, 10-30 cm long; petiole semiterete, rhachis semiterete below usually terete above or occasionally slightly canaliculate, sparsely puberulous to glabrous; petiolule 1-4 mm long. Leaflets alternate or rarely subopposite, 5-9(-10), narrowly elliptic, oblong or oblanceolate, apex acute to attenuate or long acuminate, base attenuate, usually subcoriaceous, 10-15(-20)[12] cm long, (2.5-)3-4.5[3.72] cm broad, terminal leaflet usually larger and basal ones much smaller, upper surface glabrous except for occasional sparse puberulous indumentum on midrib, lower surface usually glabrous, less frequently sparsely strigulose on midrib (including a few dibrachiate hairs), usually obscurely glandular-punctate and -striate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib prominent above; secondaries 13-16 on either side of midrib, usually arcuate ascending, slightly convergent or rarely ± parallel; intersecondaries usually rather long and prominent. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious; inflorescence axillary, 10-20 cm long, a slender or broad, few- to many-flowered thyrse, puberulous to subglabrous; pedicel 0.5-1 mm long. Calyx rotate to patelliform, 0.5-1 mm long, with 4-5 shallow, broadly triangular to obtuse lobes to 1/2 length of calyx or margin undulate, aestivation open, indumentum of scattered minute appressed hairs. Petals 4-5, free, valvate to rarely slightly imbricate, 2-2.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, ovate to lanceolate, apex acute, sparsely appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Staminal tube cyathiform or rarely urceolate; filaments completely fused, 1-1.5 mm long, 1-2.5 mm broad, margin with (7-)8(-9) subulate lobes alternating with anthers and 1/2-3/4 their length, outside usually glabrous rarely with scattered short hairs in upper half, inside pubescent at throat or glabrous; anthers (7-)8(-9), 0.6-0.8 mm long, glabrous; antherodes slender, not dehiscent, without pollen. Nectary absent, or rarely represented by a small swelling around base of ovary. Ovary ovoid, 3(-4)-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, densely puberulous; style glabrous; style-head capitate or small discoid, held ca. level with anthers. Pistillode smaller, conical, with small non-functional ovules. Capsule oblong to ellipsoid, densely verrucose with prominent narrow verrucae which are often united to form irregular ridges, usually intermixed with sparse appressed hairs, drying dark brown or black, 1.4-2 cm long, 0.8-1.2 cm broad, 3(-4)-valved, valves spreading; pericarp 1-3 mm thick, rather fleshy; endocarp thin, cartilaginous. Seed 1 or 2, collateral in each fruit, 0.8-2.2 cm long, 0.6-1 cm broad, completely surrounded by a thin fleshy arillode, thickened somewhat at apex, also developing around abortive ovules, arillode free except for thin line of attachment from micropyle to raphe; seed coat membraneous. Embryo with plano-convex, collateral cotyledons; radicle apical, included. Endosperm absent.

description: Young branches usually stout, densely villose or tomentose, indumentum persistent. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate, without terminal growth, 9.528 cm long; petiole and rhachis semiterete, terete, or with a ridge along upper surface, densely villose to tomentose; petiolule of lateral leaflets 0-2 mm long; petiolule of terminal leaflet 2-4 mm long. Leaflets opposite, 17-41, closely set and overlapping, sometimes conduplicate, elliptic to oblong, sometimes falcate, apex acute, obtuse or rounded, base usually asymmetric, acute to truncate, coriaceous, 3.5-8.5(-l 1)[6.4] cm long, 2-2.9(-4.3)[2.4] cm broad, upper surface with pubescent midrib and glabrous or sparsely appressed puberulous lamina, lower with villose to tomentose midrib and veins and sparsely pubescent or puberulous lamina, minute red papillae present on lower surface; venation eucamptodromous to brochidodromous, midrib flat; secondaries 12-15 on either side of midrib, shallowly ascending, straight or arcuate above, ± parallel; intersecondaries prominent; tertiary reticulum sometimes prominent below. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious; inflorescence axillary, 3.5-11 cm long, a slender panicle with flowers in small rather dense clusters sometimes with a few short lateral branches near base; pedicel 0.5-1.5 mm. Calyx patelliform, sepals 1-2 mm long, ovate to orbicular, sparsely puberulous or pubescent, ciliate. Petals 5.5-7.5 mm long, 2-2.5 mm broad, oblong, oblanceolate or spathulate, apex rounded, glabrous, sometimes ciliate. Staminal tube short cylindrical, 4.5-5 mm long, ca. 2 mm broad, margin undulate or crenulate, glabrous; anthers 10, 1.3-1.5 mm long, without a basal appendage, barbate at base; antherodes narrower, ca. 1 mm long, without pollen, not dehiscing. Nectary a stout stipe expanded at apex, 0.5-1 mm long, glabrous. Ovary 3-locular, loculi with 2 superposed ovules, glabrous; style stout, glabrous; style-head discoid; pistillode similar with well-developed abortive ovules. Capsule globose, smooth, dark brown with pale lenticels, glabrous, 1.52 cm diam., 3-valved, valves 1-seeded; pericarp ca. 1 mm thick. Seed ca. 1.2 cm long, 1 cm broad, with a thick basal sarcotesta; seed coat membraneous. Embryo with thick, plano-convex, collateral cotyledons; radicle apical, extending to the surface.

description: Young branches tomentose, indumentum persistent. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate without terminal growth, 7-25 cm long; petiole semiterete, rhachis terete, tomentose; petiolule of lateral leaflets ca. 1 mm long, petiolule of terminal leaflets 4-5 mm long. Leaflets opposite, 9-15, broadly lanceolate, elliptic or oblong, apex rounded to short attenuate, base slightly asymmetric and acute to obtuse, terminal leaflet oblanceolate with an attenuate base, coriaceous, 8-10.5 cm long, 4-5 cm broad, upper midrib pubescent, lower surface with tomentose midrib and veins, and lamina densely pubescent with crisped hairs intermixed with numerous red papillae; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly sunken; secondaries 8-10 on either side of midrib, shallowly ascending, arcuate, ± parallel; intersecondaries long and prominent; tertiaries obscure. Inflorescence axillary, 10-25 cm long, a densely-flowered, slender or broadly pyramidal panicle, lateral branches to 5 cm long, densely short pubescent; pedicel 0.5-1 mm long. Calyx patelliform, sepals 0.5-0.75 mm long, ovate, acute, pubescent, ciliate. Petals ca. 3 mm long, ca. 1 mm broad, oblong or oblanceolate, apex rounded, glabrous. Staminal tube urceolate, ca. 2 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, margin with 7-9 short emarginate lobes alternating with anthers, outside with a few long hairs, inside glabrous; anthers 7-9, ca. 0.5 mm long, with a small basal appendage, glabrous. Nectary absent or represented by a very short stipe. Ovary 3(-4)-locular, loculi with 2 superposed ovules, glabrous; style glabrous, surmounted by a discoid style-head. Fruit unknown.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 1.5-7 m tall and reaching a dbh of at least 7 cm; young branchlets terete and covered with small reddish brown or yellowish spreading hairs. Leaves opposite or rarely in whorls of 3, the petioles 1-6.5 cm long, the lamina drying greenish to greenish brown, chartaceous, obovate or elliptic, (6-)8-23 X (3-)4-9(-12) cm, the base cordate, rounded, obtuse, or acute, the apex obtuse to acuminate, the tip about 1 cm long, both surfaces more or less densely pubescent, the lower surface usually velvety to the touch, with 8-9(-10) pairs of secondary veins, the veins flat above, slightly raised below, the margin denticulate to serrulate, drying flat. Cymes 1-2(-3) cm long, pendent and more or less densely covered with tufted hairs, with (5-) 15-35 (-50) flowers. Fresh flowers creamy yellow; male floral cup subglobose, 1-2.4 mm in diam., 1-2 mm high, pubescent as the cymes, the 4-7 tepals triangular and 0.8-1.2 mm long, adaxially loosely pubescent, the floral roof broadly conical and moderately to distinctly raised and often forming an upright rim around the floral pore, glabrous; stamens 1-12; female floral cup subglobose, 2-3.5 mm in diam., 1.9-3.3 mm high, the roof raised, consisting of an outer bulge separated by a groove from a central tube tightly surrounding the styles, the indumentum as in the male flowers; styles 4-12. Fruiting receptacle subglobose, about 1.8 cm in diam., crowned by the persistent tepals, when fresh and mature purple with white spots and a strong pungent smell, when dried the 4-8 drupelets somewhat protruding, drupelets fresh gray-blue and bearing a red stylar aril.

description: Dioecious or rarely monoecious shrub or treelet, 1.5-8 m tall and reaching a dbh of 10 cm, often drooping over other vegetation, the bark gray and smooth, branchlets terete and with a few simple or few-branched hairs. Leaves in whorls of 3 or rarely 4, sometimes opposite, often drying shiny; petioles 1-2.5 cm long, occasionally with conspicuous stiff hairs; lamina drying light or medium brown, brittle, elliptic to lanceolate, 7-15 (-21) X 3-7(-10) cm, the base obtuse, rarely rounded or acute, occasionally with small mite domatia, the apex acuminate, the drip tip about 1 cm long, the lower surface glabrous except for a few simple or bifid hairs on the veins and midrib, with 7-9(-12) pairs of secondary veins, these slightly raised above, distinctly raised below, the margin often crenulate and revolute. Cymes typically 2-3.5 cm long, 3- to 5-branched, deciduously pubescent or glabrous, with (6-) 15-20 flowers. Fresh flowers yellow to pale orange; male floral cup obconical to subglobose, 2-3.5(-5) mm in height and diam., the tepals 4-6, obtusely triangular to rounded and to 0.9 mm long or sometimes reduced to a narrow rim 0.3-0.5 mm broad, the floral roof broadly conical and distinctly raised, glabrous; stamens 5-6(-8), containing conspicuous yellowish oil cells, sometimes large and distinctly exserted from the floral pore; female floral cup of the same size and shape, the floral roof with an acutely conical tube sheathing the styles; carpels 8-14(-30), usually only a few styles exserted from the floral pore. Fruiting receptacle globose and smooth, to 2 cm in diam., when fresh and mature red with whitish or yellow-green spots and very fragrant, the pedicels elongating during maturation and becoming up to 6.5 cm long and pendent, the 12-30 drupelets distinctly protruding in dried receptacles, the fresh drupelets gray-blue with a red stylar aril.

description: Dioecious or very rarely monoecious scrambling shrub or treelet, 3-7 (-10) m tall and reaching a dbh of 10 cm; young branchlets angular or terete, more or less densely covered with golden-yellow or silvery-transparent peltate scales and/or stellate-lepidote hairs (Figs. 4C-E). Leaves opposite, rarely in whorls of 3; petioles 0.8-2(-3.5) cm long; lamina drying olive-brown or olive-yellow, chartaceous, brittle and sometimes subbullate, elliptic, ovate to obovate or lanceolate, 8-17(-43) X 4-8(-23) cm, the base acute to obtuse, occasionally with domatia, the apex acuminate, the tip 1-1.5 cm long, the tomentum on both surfaces as on the young branchlets, with 8-11 pairs of secondary veins, flat on both sides, the margin dentate to serrate. Cymes 5-8 cm long, densely lepidote, with 10-20 flowers. Fresh flowers yellow; male floral cup broadly obconical to subglobose, 2-3.5 mm in diam., 1.2-2.5 mm high, densely lepidote with silvery or almost transparent scales up to 0,25 mm in diam., the floral roof raised and with a relatively wide pore, glabrous, the 4-6 tepals triangular to rounded; stamens 5-8(-10), containing conspicuous whitish oil cells; female floral cup subglobose to urceolate, the tepals up to 0.8 mm long, the roof broadly conical or slightly raised and either with a conical central tube, up to 1 mm long; styles 3-11, typically thin and elongate. Fruiting receptacle globose and smooth, 1-1.5 cm in diam., when fresh and mature reddish purple and smelling strongly of lemon; pedicels elongating during fruit maturation and becoming up to 3 cm long; drupelets 5-9, each with a reddish stylar aril.

description: Dioecious or very rarely monoecious shrub or tree, 2-15(-20) m tall and reaching a dbh of 25 cm; young branchlets quadrangular or terete, yellowish tomentose with spreading hairs, glabrescent, older branchlets often with conspicuous petiole scars and large lenticels (Figs. 2A, 5A). Leaves in whorls of 3-4 or opposite; petioles 1-3(-5) cm long; lamina drying dark green or olive-brown, thin and brittle, lanceolate or oblanceolate, (4-) 10-25(-34) X 2.5-7.5(-13) cm, the base acute to obtuse, the apex acute to shortly acuminate, the tip to 0.5 cm long, the upper surface loosely covered with simple or few-branched hairs, glabrescent, the lower surface more densely pubescent with brownish yellow few-branched to tufted hairs, glabrescent, with 10-17 pairs of secondary veins, these slightly raised on both surfaces, the margin dentate, crenate, or serrate (Fig. 2D). Cymes umbel-like (Fig. 5A), 3-4(-12) cm long including the 1-3 cm long peduncle, generally sparsely pubescent, rarely densely tomentose, glabrescent, with 15-40 flowers. Fresh flowers yellowish green; male floral cup (2.5-)6-8(-10) mm in diam., 2-3(-4) mm high, pubescent or glabrous, sometimes with minute tubercles, the tepals 4-7, triangular or oblong-triangular, 0.5-5 (-10) mm long, the floral roof a thin, narrow membrane, glabrous; stamens (20-)50-72, membranaceous; female floral cup urceolate, 2.5-3 mm in diam., 2-3 mm high, the receptacle with short tubercles, ca. 0.3 mm long, the floral roof moderately raised, with a central cylinder sheathing the styles, glabrous; styles (2-)3-5(-7), relatively long and with prominent stigma papillae. Fruiting receptacle globose, 1-2 cm in diam., conspicuously spiny-tuberculate and crowned by the persistent tepals, mature receptacles purplish red and strongly orange or lemon-scented; drupelets commonly 3.

description: Dioecious scrambling shrub, 2-4 m tall and reaching a dbh of 5 cm, with thin elongate stems and branches; branchlets terete, loosely or densely pubescent with yellow simple or few-branched hairs. Leaves in whorls of 4 or 3, rarely opposite; petioles 0.5-1 (-2) cm long, conspicuously yellowish pilose; lamina drying brownish, lanceolate, oblanceolate, or elliptic, 4-15(-21) X 2-5(-10) cm, the base obtuse or rounded, rarely acute, the apex acuminate, the tip to 0.5 cm long, both surfaces sparsely pubescent with yellow few-branched or simple hairs, the midrib and leaf margin more densely and persistently pubescent; lamina with 7-9 pairs of secondary veins, sometimes drying subbullate, the margin crenate or serrulate, often revolute and outlined by conspicuous yellow hairs. Cymes typically 2-5 cm long, pendent, with 612 flowers, yellow-pubescent with stellate or few-branched hairs. Fresh flowers yellowish; male floral cup obconical to subglobose, 2.5-3 mm in diam., 2-2.5 mm high, the tepals 5-6, broadly triangular and up to 1 mm long, often fused to a shallowly lobed wavy rim, the floral roof raised and membranaceous, glabrous; stamens 3-8; female floral cup of the same shape as the male cups but slightly larger, the tepals broadly rounded, to 1.4 mm long, sometimes forming an undulate rim, the floral roof raised and consisting of an outer bulge separated by a groove from a conical central tube sheathing the styles; styles 3-8. Fruiting receptacle globose, glabrescent, about 1 cm in diam., pendent on elongated infructescence axes, when fresh and mature pale red with white spots; drupelets 2-5, distinctly protruding in dried fruits, fresh gray and with a red stylar aril.

description: Dioecious or rarely monoecious shrub, 2.5-8 m tall; branchlets somewhat angular and with long simple or few-branched hairs. Leaves in whorls of 3 or 4, rarely opposite, ascending; petioles 0.2-0.5 cm long; lamina drying light brown, brittle, ovate-elliptic to elliptic-oblong, 5-6(-8) X 2.5-3(-4) cm, the base cordate or rounded, the apex shortly acuminate or blunt, both surfaces with few or many stiff, simple or few-branched hairs especially on the veins, the hairs on the veins slightly longer than on the lamina, with 7-8 pairs of secondary veins, these flat above, raised below, the margin serrulate or denticulate. Cymes 1.53 cm long, few-branched and densely strigose, with 3-9 flowers. Fresh flowers greenish yellow; male floral cup broadly obconical, about 3 mm in diam., the 4-6 tepals 1.5-2 mm long and narrowly triangular or oblong, adaxially glabrous, the floral roof distinctly raised and glabrous; stamens 7-12, with many yellow or whitish oil inclusions; female floral cup of the same size and shape, the floral roof flat and tightly sheathing the styles; styles 10-15, often fused to a column. Fruiting receptacles hanging on elongated infructescence axes up to 5 cm long, globose, about 1.2 cm in diam., sometimes with minute tubercles and crowned by the persistent tepals, when fresh and mature maroon and very fragrant, when dried the 5-10 drupelets distinctly protruding, each drupelet bearing a stylar aril.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 4-10 m tall and reaching a dbh of at least 20 cm, sometimes somewhat scandent; branchlets quadrangular to distinctly 4-ridged, finely brown pubescent, older branchlets glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles 1.5-6 cm long; lamina drying rusty brown, chartaceous, obovate to broadly elliptic, 15-40 X 7-17 cm, the base cuneate or acute, the apex generally acute to short-acuminate, above strigilose with simple or few-branched spreading hairs, below more densely pubescent, with 10-17 pairs of secondary veins, the margin denticulate. Cymes axillary or on older leafless nodes, 1-3 cm long, densely pubescent, with 5-15 flowers. Fresh flowers yellow to pale orange; male floral cup semiglobose to broadly obconical, 2-3 mm in diam., 1.52.5 mm high, densely pubescent, the tepals forming an 0.8-1.4 mm broad spreading rim, the rim margin cicular or wavy, the floral roof barely raised and densely stellate-pubescent with short grayish hairs; stamens 12-30; female floral cup of about the same size and shape as the male, the tepal rim persistent in fruit and then completely circular, the floral roof almost flat to slightly bulging with a short central cylindrical tube sheathing the numerous (20-30) styles. Fruiting receptacle globose with a crateriform depression at the apex surrounded by the tepal rim, 1.52.5 cm in diam., mature light yellowish green to dull white and bursting irregularly to display usually fewer than 10 gray drupelets each with a fleshy, rose colored sty lar aril.

description: Monoecious treelet or tree, 3-12(-25) m tall, reaching a dbh of 20 cm; young branchlets distinctly flattened below the nodes (Fig. 2B), with few appressed stellate hairs. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.8-1.5 cm long; lamina drying grayish brown, brown, or greenish brown, chartaceous, oblong to elliptic, 11-18 X 3.3-7 cm, the base obtuse to acute, the apex acuminate, the tip 1-2 cm long, with few stellate hairs, especially on the midrib, glabrescent, with 912 pairs of secondary veins, these flat on both surfaces, the margin entire. Cymes 1-1.5 cm long (to 3 cm long in fruit), covered with stellate hairs, with 515 flowers. Fresh flowers greenish yellow; male floral cup obconical, 2.6-2.8 mm in diam., 2.4-3.5 mm high, the indumentum as on the cymes; tepals 4(-5), broadly triangular, 2-3.5 mm long, adaxially densely tomentose like the floral roof; stamens 8-14; female floral cup of the same size and shape as the male except the floral roof acutely conical; styles 5-10, fused and forming a column that emerges from the floral roof. Fruiting receptacle globose and crowned by the persistent tepals, 1-1.5 cm in diam. (fresh to 2 cm diam.), when fresh and mature yellow or green tinged red to completely red, smelling strongly of lemon, bursting open irregularly to expose the drupelets; drupelets 8-10, lacking a stylar aril.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 2-5 (-10) m tall and reaching a dbh of 26 cm; branchlets terete or subangular, with few short simple or stellate hairs, glabres-cent, often completely glabrous and pale brown, gray, or whitish. Leaves in whorls of 3 or 4, rarely opposite; petioles 0.5-4(-6) cm long; lamina drying brown or greenish, papery and brittle, obovate to oblanceolate, 12-40 X (4-)8-10(-21) cm, the base truncate, subcordate, or auriculate, the apex acuminate, the tip about 1 cm long, above with few simple or stellate hairs, below more densely pubescent, both surfaces usually glabrescent, with 9-12(-17) pairs of secondary veins, these and the midrib often drying yellowish, flat above and slightly raised below, the margin serrulate, denticulate, or rarely doubly serrate. Cymes 2.5-3.5(-6) cm long, loosely covered with stellate hairs, glabrescent, with 10-20 flowers. Fresh flowers yellow; male floral cup subglobose, 2-3.5 mm in diam., 2-3 mm high, the tepals 4-6, narrowly triangular or rarely rounded, 2-6 mm long, often of unequal lengths, the floral roof moderately raised, glabrous; stamens 6-8(-10), hardly or distinctly exserted from the pore depending on flower age; female floral cup obconical or slightly urceolate, 3-4.5 mm in diam., 3-5 mm high, the floral roof with a central conical tube sheathing the styles; styles 10-28. Fruiting receptacle globose, when fresh red and with a distinct lemon odor, 1-2.5 cm in diam. (fresh to 3.5 cm), drupelets 10-25, each with a stylar aril.

description: Dioecious or rarely monoecious shrub or treelet, 1-12 m tall; young branchlets terete and densely covered with reddish brown or golden yellow tufted hairs, sometimes sarmentose and straggling. Leaves in whorls of 3 or 4 or opposite; petioles 1-3.5 cm long; lamina often drying reddish brown, more rarely greenish or golden-brown, relatively thick-chartaceous, oblong-ovate, lanceolate, or elliptic, 8-23(-50) X 4-10(-20) cm, the base rounded or cordate, sometimes acute or obtuse, rarely eared, the apex acute or obtuse, the tip 0.5-1 cm long, both surfaces typically densely velvety pubescent, with 8-12(-15) pairs of secondary veins, the veins almost flat above and below, the margin denticulate or serrulate (Fig. 2E), drying flat. Cymes 2.5-8(-12) cm long, pendent, densely covered with tufted hairs, with a moderate number of flowers (ca. 5-20). Fresh flowers yellowish orange or creamy yellow; male floral cup subglobose, 2-3.5 mm in diam., 1.5-2.3 mm high, pubescent like the cymes, the 4-8 tepals broadly triangular, up to 1.4 mm long, sometimes fused to a narrow or shallowly lobed rim, rarely obsolete (Fig. 11C), the floral roof broadly raised and more or less densely pubescent with short spreading hairs, glabrescent, or glabrous; stamens 5-15, very rarely to 35, flat and often distinctly exserted from the floral pore and bent backwards (Fig. 11 C); female floral cup subglobose, 2.5-3.6 mm in diam., 2.2-3.5 mm high, the tepals broadly triangular or rounded, up to 1.5 mm long, the floral roof more or less raised and with a central tube sheathing the styles; styles 3-13(-26). Fruiting receptacle globose, about 2 X 1.5 cm, crowned by the persistent tepals, when fresh and mature red with greenish white spots and a strong pungent smell, when dried sometimes with minute pustules (to 1 mm long), the drupelets fresh tan and bearing a red stylar aril.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 3-12 m tall and reaching a dbh of 23 cm; young branchlets terete or subangular, densely covered with appressed stellate-lepidote brownish hairs. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3 or 4; petioles 1-3 (-6) cm long, often slightly unequal in length on the same node; lamina drying búllate, dark green to dark brown, often brittle, oblong, lanceolate, or broadly elliptic, (6-)12-20(-37) X 3.5-6.5(-20) cm, the base acute to rounded, sometimes with domatia (Fig. 68C), the apex acuminate, the tip 0.5-2 cm long, upper surface with appressed stellate-lepidote hairs, lower surface with spreading stellate and stellate-lepidote hairs, the latter especially on the veins, with 13-22 pairs of secondary veins, these impressed above, raised below, the margin dentate to crenate. Cymes 2-4(-8) cm long, densely covered with stellate-lepidote hairs, with 20-30 flowers. Fresh flowers yellowish green with a purple center; male floral cup semiglobose, 3-4.5 mm in diam., 2-3.5 mm high, stellate-lepidote pubescent, the tepals 4-5(-6), triangular, 0.7-1.5 mm long, adaxially glabrous, the floral roof distinctly raised, glabrous; stamens (5-)8-11, little exserted at anthesis; female floral cup of the same size and shape, the floral roof almost flat and with a short central tube tightly surrounding the styles; styles 5-8, reddish. Fruiting receptacle globose, 1-1.5 cm in diam., crowned by the persistent tepals and covered with stellate-lepidote hairs, sometimes with minute pustules, when fresh and mature red with green spots, strongly lemon-scented; drupelets 5-8, gray with a bright red stylar aril.

description: Trees up to 20 m tall; latex white to yellow. Leafy twigs 1-3 mm thick, brownish, sparsely whitish to yellow or brownish puberulous to more or less densely pubescent or subtomentose. Leaves lanceolate to oblong, not or rather strongly inequilateral, 5-17 cm long, 1.5-5.5 cm broad, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, (abruptly) acuminate, obtuse to acute at the base, glabrous; the costa and the proximal parts of the secondary veins prominent, otherwise the venation nearly plane; veins prominent beneath, 10-19 pairs of secondary veins, mostly straight and arched 2-4 mm from the margin; petioles 3-10 mm long, 1-1.5(-2) mm broad, narrowly canaliculate; stipules 7-17 (-25) mm long, yellow to greyish subsericeous to appressed-puberulous. Staminate inflorescences 6-8 mm in diameter; peduncle 5-12 mm long, puberulous; involucre with 7-10 suborbiculate to deltoid to oblong to ovate, obtuse, minutely and sparsely puberulous bracts in 3-4 series; perianth 1.5-1.8 mm high, with 3-7 free tepals; stamens 2-4, filaments 0.8-1.2 mm long, anthers 0.6-0.9 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mm broad. Pistillate inflorescences 7-15 mm in diameter, sessile or subsessile; involucre with 10-25 deltoid to suborbiculate to subovate, obtuse to acute, minutely puberulous bracts in 3-5 series; flowers 5-20, stigmas, tepals, and pseudobracts visible at anthesis; perianth 1-3 mm high, with 3-6 tepals, tepals cushion-shaped and apiculate to pyramidate or subulate, puberulous; style 1-1.5 mm long, stigmas vittiform, either 2.5-3.3 mm or 6-9 mm long; pseudobracts mainly peripheral, if long and narrow also numerous among the flowers, similar to the tepals. Infructescences convexly discoid to hemispherical, 2-4 cm in diameter; tepals and pseudobracts cushionshaped, apiculate, angulate, and up to 3 mm long, or pyramidate to spine-like, acute to apiculate, angulate, and 5-6 mm long; fruit 8-9 × 5-6 mm. Flowering from April to November.

description: Monoecious shrubs or trees up to 30 m tall, with or without buttresses; latex white to yellow. Leafy twigs 1-3 mm thick, sparsely to densely white to brown puberulous. Leaves elliptic to lanceolate, more or less inequilateral, often broadest above or below the middle, (2-)4-13 cm long, (1-)2-6cm broad, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, acuminate (to caudate), acute, obtuse, or sometimes emarginate, at the base acute to obtuse (to subcordate); margin entire, or occasionally dent(icul)ate towards the apex, often more or less revolute; above glabrous and shining; beneath nearly glabrous, appressed-puberulous, (sub) velutinous, or scabridulous; veins more or less prominent, 6-14 pairs of secondary veins, without parallel tertiary veins; petioles 2-6 mm long; stipules 2-5 mm long, puberulous to nearly glabrous, caducous or sometimes persistent. Inflorescences usually bisexual, discoid to broadly turbinate or hemispherical, often more or less lobed, 3-12 mm in diameter, subsessile to pedunculate; peduncle up to 20 mm long, often bracteate; staminate flowers few to many; perianth o.2-0.4 mm high, 3-4-lobed, puberulous; stamen 1, filaments 0.3-0.8 mm long, anthers 0. 1-0.3 mm long and 0.1-0.25 mm broad, connectives broad and swollen; pistillate flowers one to several; style o.4-1.0mm long, stigmas 0.1-0.3 mm long; bracts many to numerous, puberulous, 0.4-1.o mm in diameter. Infructescences (sub)globose or subturbinate and ca 12 mm in diameter, or if containing two or more fruits more or less lobed and up to 16 mm in diameter, reddish at maturity; seed ca 8 × 5 mm. Flowering throughout the year, mainly from September to January.

description: Dioecious or sometimes monoecious trees up to 30 m tall; latex yellowish. Leafy twigs 1-7 mm thick, yellow to brownish puberulous, tomentellous, tomentose, velutinous or hirtellous. Leaves (elliptic to) oblong to lanceolate, sometimes broadest near the upper end, ca inequilateral, 5-32 cm long, 2-15 cm broad, chartaceous to coriaceous, acuminate to mucronate (to acute), acute to obtuse (to truncate or emarginate) at the base, entire to faintly repand, or rarely denticulate near the apex, except for the costa glabrescent, sometimes scabridulous above, sparsely to densely puberulous to tomentellous to tomentose to hirtellous beneath; veins nearly plane above, prominent beneath, 8-17 pairs of secondary veins, often many parallel tertiary veins; petioles 4-17 mm long; stipules 3-10 mm long, subsericeous. Staminate inflorescences up to 15 together, 3-9 mm in diameter; peduncle 3-18 mm long, puberulous to tomentellous; involucre with deltoid to ovate, acute, velutinous bracts in ca 4 series; perianth 1-2 mm high, (3-)4(~5)-lobed to (3-) 4(-5)-parted, densely puberulous towards the tip; stamens 4, rarely 2 staminodial or wanting, filaments 1.3-4.5 mm long, those of the outer stamens often shorter than those of the inner ones, anthers 0.2-0.9 mm long, o.2-0.5 mm broad, apiculate or not, connectives narrow or broad, anthers of the outer whorl as a rule longer and narrower than those of the inner whorl and distinctly apiculate. Pistillate inflorescences solitary or sometimes accompanied by 1 or 2 staminate ones, hemispherical to subglobose (to globose), 5-8 mm in diameter, sessile to pedunculate; peduncle up to 10 mm long, puberulous to tomentellous; involucre with reniform to ovate to subulate, acute, brownish velutinous bracts in 4-8 series; flowers (3-) 5-15; perianth 2-2.5 mm high, 4-par ted, brownish velutinous; style 0.7-1.7 mm long, lateral, hairy at the upper end, stigmas vittiform, 2.5-5 mm long, often strongly twisted. Infructescences subglobose to globose, 2.5-5 cm in diameter; fruiting perianth yellowish to brownish velutinous; fruit 6-7 × ca 5 mm; seed ca 5 × ca 4 mm. Flowering mostly from August to February.

description: Leafy twigs densely yellow to brownish hirtellous to velutinous to subsericeous. Leaves oblong to lanceolate, mostly broadest near the lower end, 24-46 cm long, 10-17 cm broad, coriaceous, deeply cordate to subcordate at the base, entire to repand, rarely dentate towards the apex, densely hirtellous on the veins and usually rugose beneath; 18-24 pairs of secondary veins; stipules 4-6 cm long, yellow sericeous often subpersistent. Staminate inflorescences 9-20 mm in diameter; peduncle 10-30 mm long; involucre with ca 90-100 deltoid to subovate bracts in 6-8 series; perianth 1-1.5 mm high; filaments 0.8-1.5 mm long, strongly broadened towards the base, anthers o.2-0.4 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm broad, mostly apiculate. Pistillate inflorescences 20-30 mm in diameter; peduncle 5-15 mm long; involucre with ca 150-400 ovate to subulate, acute bracts in 10-12 series; flowers ca 40-100; perianth 6-6.5 mm high, 4-dentate to 4-fid, free segments 2-3 mm long, narrow, style 4-5 mm long, stigmas (1.0-) 1.2-2.2 mm long, 1.2-3.0 mm broad, acute to mucronate. Infructescences 3.5-4.5 cm in diameter; fruiting perianth 14-20 mm high; style 7-8 mm long (longer if ovary has not developed); fruit 12-13 × 7-8 mm.

description: Leafy twigs yellow secrieous. Leaves oblong to lanceolate, mostly broadest near the lower end, 40-52 cm long, 16-22 cm broad, coriaceous, deeply cordate with overlapping lobes at the base, repand (to dentate), subsericeous on the costa and secondary veins, for the rest puberulous to sparsely hirtellous and mostly rugose beneath; 20-25 pairs of secondary veins; stipules ca 6 cm long, yellow sericeous, subpersistent. Staminate inflorescences 15-30 mm in diameter; peduncle 25-60 mm long; involucre with ca 40-90 deltoid to subovate bracts in 4-5 series; perianth 1.2-2.5 mm high; filaments 1.2-2.7 mm long, broadened towards the base or not, anthers 0.35-0.60 mm long, 0.25-0.60 mm broad, apiculate or not.

description: Revised description: Tree, to 30 m tall, mostly dioecious. Leafy twigs 1.5-4.5(-7) mm thick, with very short patent hairs intermixed with dense, distinctly longer, appressed to patent, brownish to yellow to whitish hairs. Lamina elliptic to oblong to (sub)ovate, 6-36 × 2.5-14 cm, slightly inequilateral, chartaceous to coriaceous; apex acute to acuminate to mucronate; base obtuse to subcordate; margin entire to repand to dent(icul)ate; upper surface strig(ill)ose to hirsute, except for the midrib glabrescent, ± bullate and ± scabrous to almost plane and smooth above; lower surface densely yellowish-hirsute to hirtellous to puberulous with patent or partly ± appressed hairs; lateral veins (12-) 15-22 pairs, loop-connected 1-1.5 mm from the margin; tertiary venation largely scalariform; petiole 0.1-1 cm long; stipules (0.5-)1-2.5(-3) cm long, yellow-hirsute to subsericeous, sometimes subpersistent. Staminate inflorescences up to 8 together in the leaf axils, 0.8-1.6 cm diam.; peduncle 1-3 cm long; involucral bracts in 6-9 rows, broadly to narrowly ovate to lanceolate to linear, acute to caudate, appressed-pubescent to hirtellous, the inner ones to 0.8 cm long and incurved before anthesis; flowers numerous; perianth 1.7-2.5 mm long, 2-3-lobed to -fid, puberulous at the upper end; stamens 2-3; filaments 2-3 mm long; anthers 0.8-1.3 × 0.2-0.3 mm. Pistillate inflorescences solitary or sometimes accompanied by 1-2 staminate ones, 0.8-1.2 cm diam.; subsessile or peduncle to 0.5 cm long; involucral bracts in 4-7 rows, broadly to narrowly ovate to lanceolate, acute to caudate, appressed-pubescent to hirtellous, the inner ones incurved before anthesis; flowers 6-30, free or basally connate; perianth 2-3 mm long, entire to 4-dentate, hirtellous, setose near the base or not; style ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous; stigmas 2-3(-5) mm long. Infructescences 1.5-2.5 cm diam.; fruiting perianth hirtellous to hirsute or puberulous; fruit almost entirely adnate to the perianth. Two subspecies can be recognized.

description: Small trees; latex white. Leafy twigs 1-3 mm thick, greyish to yellowish appressed-puberulous to tomentose. Leaves lanceolate to oblong, often broadest near the upper end, 8-i8(-23) cm long, 2.5-4.5(-6.5) cm broad, subcoriaceous, more or less abruptly acuminate, acute at the base, glabrous or nearly so; the costa prominent, the secondary veins impressed, the other veins nearly plane above, veins more or less prominent beneath, 15-23 pairs of secondary veins; petioles 3-10 mm long, 1-1.5(-2) mm broad; stipules 5-12 mm long, greyish to yellow appressed-puberulous to subsericeous, sometimes subpersistent. Staminate inflorescences 4-7 mm in diameter; peduncle 1-2 mm long, puberulous; involucre with 9-11 deltoid to reniform to suborbiculate to ovate, obtuse, appressed-puberulous bracts in 3-4 series; perianth 1.2 mm high, with 3-5 free tepals; stamens 2-4, filaments 0.8-1.6 mm long, anthers 0.5-0.8 mm long, o.3-0.5 mm broad, usually difform. Pistillate inflorescences 4-7 mm in diameter, sessile; involucre with ca 10 reniform to deltoid to subovate, obtuse to acute, appressed-puberulous bracts in 3-4 series; flowers 2-4; perianth 2-3 mm high, with 4-6 basally connate tepals; style ca 2 mm long, stigmas filiform, ca 7 mm long; pseudobracts mainly peripheral, subulate, 1-3 mm long, puberulous. Infructescences ovoid to subglobose, 12-18 mm in diameter; pseudobracts and tepals spine-like, 1.5-3 mm long, broadened at the base; fruit ellipsoid 10 × 7-8 mm. Flowering from April to December.
bibliographicCitation: Berg, Cornelius C. 1972. Olmedieae, Brosimeae (Moraceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 7: 1-229.

description: Trees up to 30 m tall. Leafy twigs 0.5-2.5 mm, often dark brown to blackish, glabrous or sparsely puberulous. Leaves oblong to lanceolate, not or distinctly inequilateral, 4-14(-19) cm long, 1.5-4.5(5-5) cm broad, subcoriaceous, acuminate (to acute), attenuate to acute to subobtuse at the base, glabrous; the costa prominent, otherwise the venation slightly prominent to plane above, beneath the costa mostly plane, otherwise the venation more or less prominent, secondary veins 14-21 pairs, straight or slightly curved, arched 1-2 mm from the margin; petioles 5-13 mm long; stipules 4-14 mm long, glabrous or sparsely puberulous. Staminate inflorescences 4-8 mm in diameter; peduncle 1-4 mm long, sparsely puberulous; involucre with 9-12 reniform to deltoid to suborbiculate to ovate to subovate, obtuse (to acute), sparsely puberulous bracts in 3-5 series; flowers 10 or more; perianth 1.0-1.8 mm high, with (o-)1-5 free tepals; stamens 1-4, filaments 1.0-1.8 mm long, anthers o.4-0.6 mm long and broad. Pistillate inflorescences 4-8 mm in diameter, sessile to pedunculate; peduncle up to 1.5 mm long; involucre with 9-12 reniform to deltoid, obtuse (to acute), sparsely puberulous bracts in ca 5 series; flowers 1-4; perianth 0.5-1 mm high, with 4-6 free, cushion-shaped, puberulous tepals; style 1-1.5mm long, stigmas filiform to vittiform, 2-3.5 mm long; pseudobracts mainly peripheral, similar to the tepals. Infructescences subglobose, 1-1.5 cm in diameter; tepals and pseudobracts cushion-shaped to more or less pyramidate, up to 2 mm high. Flowering from September to February.

description: Trees up to 30 m tall. Leafy twigs 2-4 mm thick, brown velutinous. Leaves oblong to lanceolate, sometimes broadest near the upper end, 8-26 cm long, 3-7.5 cm broad, coriaceous, acuminate, acute at the base, glabrous or nearly so; the costa prominent, the other veins plane above, beneath the veins prominent, the costa sometimes nearly plane, 17-23 pairs of secondary veins; petioles 6-20 mm long, 2-4 mm broad; stipules 5-14 mm long, brownish subsericeous. Staminate inflorescences 4-6 mm in diameter; peduncle 1-2 mm long, pubescent; involucre with 9-20 deltoid to suborbiculate to ovate, obtuse, appressed-pubescent bracts in 3-6 series; perianth 2-2.5 mm high, with 1-4, mostly 3, free tepals; stamens 1-3, mostly 2, filaments 1-2 mm long, anthers o.5-0.6 mm long, 0.4-0.6 mm broad. Pistillate inflorescences 1-2? cm in diameter, sessile to pedunculate; peduncle up to 3 mm long; involucre with ca 40-50 reniform to deltoid, obtuse, brown velutinous bracts in 5-8 series; flowers ca 25-40; perianth cushion-shaped to crateriform, brown velutinous, tepals entirely connate; style 0.6-0.7 mm long, stigmas vittiform, 2-4 mm long; pseudobracts wanting. Infructescences subglobose, 2.5-4 cm in diameter; perianth cushion- to dome-shaped; inner involucral bracts thickened. Flowering in October and November.

description: Tree. Leafy twigs 3-3.5 mm thick, sparsely yellow strigose. Leaves oblong to lanceolate, broadest near the lower end, slightly inequilateral, 9-16 cm long, 3-7 cm broad, chartaceous, acuminate, obtuse to subcordate at the base, entire, glabrescent; veins nearly plane above, prominent beneath, 12-13 pairs of secondary veins, most tertiary veins parallel; petioles 3-5 mm long; stipules 7-10 mm long, yellow sericeous. Pistillate inflorescences ca 15 mm in diameter; peduncle 10-15 mm long; involucre with deltoid to ovate, acute to acuminate to caudate, subsericeous bracts in 3-4 series; flowers 6-9, free; perianth 2.5-3 mm high, hirtellous in the upper part, setose in the lower part; stigmas ca 3.5 mm long. Infructescences ca 2.5 cm in diameter; fruiting perianth yellow hirsute.

description: Shrub or tree, to 20 m tall. Leafy twigs 1-4 mm thick, hispid to hispidulous, or strigose to strigillose, ± scabrous. Lamina oblong to lanceolate, (3-) 10-25(-40)  × (1-)3-7(-15) cm, mostly broadest above the middle, inequilateral, chartaceous to subcoriaceous; apex acuminate to caudate; base acute; margin dentate to denticulate or subentire; upper surface scabrous to scabridulous to almost smooth; lower surface hispid to hispidulous to strigillose, ± scabrous; venation above plane, beneath prominent; lateral veins (6-)8-20(-24) pairs; tertiary venation partly scalariform; petiole 0.3-1.2 cm long, strigillose, caducous; stipules 0.5-1.2 cm long, strigillose to hispidulous, caducous. Staminate inflorescences solitary or in pairs (or as many as 6 together on short-shoots) in the leaf axils, discoid-capitate, 0.4-1 cm diam., subsessile or with to 0.6 cm long peduncle, involucrate; involucral bracts in 3-4 rows, ovate to lanceolate, hispidulous to strigillose; flowers 10-30, sessile; perianth 4-parted, 2-3 mm long, strigillose; filaments ca. 3.5 mm long; anthers 1.3-1.8 × 0.5-0.9 mm, the connective narrow, sometimes appendiculate; pistillode sometimes present, filiform. Pistillate inflorescences solitary or in pairs (or as many as 5 together on short-shoots) in the leaf axils, discoid-capitate, 0.3-0.4 cm diam., subsessile or with to 0.6 cm long peduncule, involucrate; involucral bracts in 5-7 rows, narrowly to broadly ovate, 1-3 mm long, strigillose; flowers 1 (or 2); perianth 3-3.5 mm long, dentate, strigillose; ovary free, partly strigillose; style 1-4 mm long; stigmas 7-11 mm long, minutely puberulous. Fruiting perianth fleshy, orange to red; fruit free, subglobose, ca. 4.5-5 mm; inner involucral bracts, enlarged, to 10 mm long, those of the innermost row ± fleshy, orange inside, spreading at fruit maturity.

description: Trees up to 25 m tall; latex watery and bitter. Leafy twigs 1.5-4.5 mm thick, greyish to brownish, densely brownish puberulous to sparsely whitish puberulous, periderm irregularly wrinkled, peeling off in very small flakes. Leaves (oblong to) lanceolate (to linear), often broadest near the lower or upper end, 4-22(-33) cm long, 0.5-7.5(-11) cm broad, subcoriaceous to chartaceous, acuminate, acute or obtuse at the base, glabrous or nearly so, grey to greenish when dry; the costa and the secondary veins prominent, otherwise the venation nearly plane above, veins prominent beneath, 15-23 pairs of secondary veins; petioles 3-11 mm long; stipules 3-11 mm long, sparsely puberulous to subsericeous, often curved. Staminate inflorescences 3-5 mm in diameter, subsessile or pedunculate; peduncle up to 3 mm long, puberulous; receptacle cup-shaped; involucre with 18-24 ovate to deltoid to suborbiculate to subovate, acute to obtuse, sparsely puberulous to subsericeous bracts in ca 7 series; some tens of flowers, basally connate; perianth 2.5-3.5 mm high, 3-4-parted, puberulous; stamens 1-3, usually 2, filaments 3.5-4.0 mm long, anthers o.7-1.0 mm long, o. 1-0.3 mm broad, connectives narrow. Pistillate inflorescences solitary or occasionally accompanied by staminate ones, 10-15 mm in diameter, sessile; involucre with ca 25-35 deltoid to reniform to ovate to lanceolate, obtuse, acuminate, or acute, puberulous bracts in ca 6 series; flowers ca 20-50; tepals free, subulate to spine-like to subclavate, 1-2 mm long, acute, puberulous; style 1-3 mm long, hairy, stigmas vittiform to linguiform, 1-2 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm broad, sometimes unequal; pseudobracts similar to the tepals. Infructescences hemispherical to subglobose, 4-4.5 cm in diameter; tepals and pseudobracts more or less spine-like, 3-7 mm long, broadened at the base, straight or curved. Flowering from September to May.

description: Stems cespitose and forming large clumps, 2.5-5 m tall, 2.5-5 cm diam., spiny on internodes. Leaves number unknown; leaf spines somewhat clustered, black, terete, to 4 cm long, on lateral surfaces of sheath and petiole, fewer on abaxial surface of rachis; sheath to 40 cm long; ocrea not seen; petiole to 16 cm long; rachis to 1.6 m long; pinnae numerous, irregularly arranged, spreading in more or less the same plane, linear, spinulose along the margins, whitish tomentose and setose abaxially; middle pinnae to 50 x 2 cm. Inflorescences interfoliar; peduncle to 20 cm long, recurved, sparsely spiny; prophyll 15-17 cm long; peduncular bract 25-30 cm long, densely covered with appressed, black spines to 1 cm long; rachis 2 cm long; rachillae ca. 14, to 8 cm long; triads irregularly arranged among paired or solitary staminate flowers; staminate flowers not seen; pistillate flowers to 6 mm long; calyx cupular, 3 mm long; corolla tubular, 6 mm long, spinulose; staminodes 6, linear, or absent; fruits ca. 2 cm diam., depressed-globose, purple-black, densely covered with 1.5 mm long, curved, bulbous-based spines, these whitish at the base and black at the tip; mesocarp not seen; endocarp depressed-globose, the sterile pores slightly displaced longitudinally; fruiting perianth with minute calyx and spinulose, lobed corolla, without staminodial ring.

description: Trees. Leafy twigs 1-3 mm thick, brown, glabrous or sparsely appressed-puberulous; terminal buds not pungent. Leaves lanceolate to oblong, sometimes distinctly inequilateral, 9-21 cm long, 2.5-5.5 cm broad, subcoriaceous to chartaceous, acuminate, acute at the base; the costa and the proximal parts of the secondary veins prominent, the venation otherwise nearly plane above, veins prominent beneath, 15-19 pairs of secondary veins; petioles 5-9 mm long, narrowly canaliculate; stipules 4-11 mm long, sparsely appressed-puberulous. Staminate inflorescences 7-10 mm in diameter; peduncle 3-12 mm long, sparsely puberulous; involucre with ca 10 deltoid to suborbiculate to obovate, obtuse, sparsely and minutely puberulous to nearly glabrous bracts in 3-4 series; perianth 1-2 mm high, with 0-6 tepals; stamens 1-4, filaments 0.8-1.8 mm long, anthers 0.8-1.2 mm long, 0.4-0.7 mm broad. Pistillate inflorescences 2-2.5 cm in diameter, sessile; involucre with ca 25 deltoid to ovate to lanceolate, up to 1.5 cm long, acute, minutely puberulous bracts in 6-7 series; flowers ca 60; tepals free, more or less clavate to oblong and flattened, 2-3.5 mm long, acute, puberulous; style ca 3 mm long, stigmas filiform, 8-10 mm long, unequal; pseudobracts similar to the tepals. Flowering in August.

description: Twigs with appressed to more or less patent hairs. Leaves coriaceous to subcoriaceous, slightly or not bullate and hardly or not scabrous, the lower surface (rather) sparsely hirtellous to puberulous and mostly rugose, on the costa longer, more or less appressed hairs. Pistillate flowers basally connate; perianth with short, dense equal hairs; fruiting perianth connate, hirtellous.

description: Trees up to 15 m tall; latex white to yellow. Leafy twigs 2-6(-10) mm thick, brownish, sometimes greyish, whitish or yellow appressed-puberulous to pubescent to brown velutinous; lenticels often conspicuous; periderm sometimes more or less wrinkled. Leaves lanceolate (to oblong), 13-35(-53) cm long, 3.5-11 (-14.5) cm broad, coriaceous to subcoriaceous, acuminate, acute or subobtuse at the base, glabrous or sparsely to somewhat rough beneath; margin mostly revolute; costa and the proximal part of the secondary veins prominent, otherwise plane to impressed above, veins more or less prominent beneath, secondary veins, 15-24 pairs, straight and joined by a rather well-defined, slightly arched, submarginal vein; petioles 8-20 mm long, 2-4 mm broad; stipules 8-20 mm long, yellow subsericeous. Staminate inflorescences 8-15 mm in diameter; peduncle 4-10 mm long, puberulous; involucre with 9-13 reniform to deltoid to ovate to subovate, obtuse, sparsely pubescent to puberulous bracts in 4-5 series; perianth 2-2.7 mm high, tepals 3-7, free; stamens 2-4, filaments 0.5-2 mm long, anthers 0.5-1.1 mm long, 0.4 -0.7 mm broad, sometimes apiculate. Pistillate inflorescences 5-10 mm in diameter, sessile to pedunculate; peduncle up to 6 mm long; involucre with 15-20 reniform to deltoid to ovate to subovate, obtuse to acute, appressed-pubescent to puberulous bracts in 4-6 series; flowers 4-13; perianth 1.3-3.5 mm high, 5-8-fid to 5-8-parted, puberulous; style 2-2.5 mm  long, stigmas vittiform to filiform, 6-12 mm long; pseudobracts mainly peripheral, 1-3.5 mm long, subulate to spine-like, acute, puberulous. Infructescences convexly discoid to subglobose, 1.5-5 cm in diameter; fruiting perianth 1.5- ca 10 mm high, broadened at the base, free parts 1-4 mm long, if long straight or, if short, incurved; pseudobracts 1-7 mm long, more or less spinelike to subulate, broadened at the base; fruit subglobose, 7-30 mm long. Flowering from September to February.

description: Trees up to 20 m tall; latex cream, turning red. Leafy twigs 0.5-2 mm thick, appressed-puberulous, often with uncinate hairs. Leaves elliptic to lanceolate, 2-12 cm long, 1-4 cm broad, subcoriaceous, acuminate to caudate, at the base acute (to obtuse); margin entire; above at first with uncinate hairs; beneath sparsely appressed-puberulous, glabrescent; veins more or less prominent, 5-10 pairs of secondary veins, tertiary veins not parallel; petioles 4-8 mm long, often with uncinate hairs; stipules ca 2 mm long, appressed-puberulous. Inflorescences cylindrical to narrowly turbinate, 5-7 mm high, ca 3 mm in diameter, peduncle 1-6 mm long, peduncle and receptacle densely puberulous to short-velutinous, often with uncinate hairs; staminate flowers 2-5; perianth ca 1 mm high, 3-lobed, short-velutinous to puberulous; stamens 3, 1 mm long, filaments broad; pistillode subulate, very short; style ca 1 mm long, stigmas ca 1.5 mm long, hardly extending beyond the perianth; bracts reniform to ovate to suborbiculate, basally attached or (sub)peltate. Infructescences globose, ca 1.5 cm in diameter, yellow at maturity; seeds ca 8 mm in diameter, cotyledons slightly to very unequal. Flowering probably throughout the year.

description: Shrub or small tree 1-8 m high, glabrous to pubescent on young growth; hairs whitish, yellowish-brown, or reddish-brown, up to ca. 0.5 mm long; young twigs glabrous to densely pubescent, dark or light reddish-brown or yellowish-brown, often strongly glandular, the older bark somewhat flaky. Leaves probably deciduous, normally mature at anthesis, ovate, lanceolate, obovate, or elliptic, 1.5-7 cm long, 1-4 cm wide, 1.2-2.9 times as long as wide, glabrous to densely pubescent beneath sparsely pubescent to glabrous above; sharply acute, acuminate, rounded, or obtuse; base acute, rounded, obtuse to cordate; petiole channeled or not, pubescent to puberulent or glabrous, 1-13 mm long, 0.5-1 mm thick; midvein flat or slightly impressed above, prominent below, straight or sinuate; lateral veins moderately prominent to weak, ca. 4-7 pairs, each leaving the midvein at an angle of ca. 45 degrees, the venation brochidodromous, the secondary veins forming an extensive network between the laterals; blade subcoriaceous, probably not stiff when fresh, drying olive-green, yellow-green, or reddish-brown, more or less lustrous above, strongly glandular, the margin entire, repand or crenulate. Peduncle solitary, uniflorous, glabrous to densely pubescent, 3-40 mm long, 0.3-1 mm wide, arising from the axils of leaves or bracts, the bracts sometimes deciduous; bracteoles linear to linear-lanceolate, ca. 1-2 mm long, mainly deciduous before anthesis; Calyx-lobes triangular, ovate, oblong, or hemiorbicular, 1-3 mm long and wide, 0.3-1.5 times as long as wide, strongly glandular, glabrous to sparsely pubescent without, sparsely puberulent or pubescent within, sometimes glabrescent with age; petals obovate to oblanceolate, 3-8 mm long; hypanthium obconic or campanulate, 2-5 mm long, puberulent to glabrous, strongly glandular, often prolonged beyond the summit of the ovary; disk 2-5 mm across, pubescent to glabrous; stamens 60-200, ca. 5-10 mm long; anthers ca. 0.5-0.8 mm long; style glabrous or sparsely pubescent at base, 3-8 mm long; ovary 4-10-locular; ovules ca. 4-11 per locule. Fruit yellow, glandular, subglobose, ca. 6-13 mm in diam. Seeds 1-2 in fruits seen, ca. 4-5 mm long including locular wall, the wall submembranous, one gland thick.

description: Small tree up to ca. 6 m high; hairs whitish or reddish-brown, dibrachiate, usually about symmetrical, ca. 0.1-0.8 mm long; young twigs densely strigose-pubescent, the young bark light brown, becoming light grey. Leaves obovate, oblanceolate, or elliptic, 3-5 cm long, 1-3 cm wide, 1.6-3 times as long as wide, densely covered with appressed hairs beneath, essentially glabrous, or often with appressed hairs along the midvein above, losing some hairs with age, the margin generally revolute, the upper surface sometimes papillose with many convex glands; apex broadly rounded, obtuse, or emarginate; base cuneate to rounded; petiole scarcely channeled, 2-5 mm long, 1-2 mm thick, densely strigose, less so to completely glabrescent with age; midvein impressed slightly proximally above, prominent below; lateral veins indistinct, or poorly differentiated from the secondary veins, or ca. 5-7 pairs leaving the midvein at an angle of ca. 45°, the secondary veins sometimes forming a visible reticulate pattern; marginal veins equalling laterals in prominence; blades subcoriaceous to coriaceous, drying dark reddish-brown, light or dark grey-green, light tan above, usually whitish because of the covering of hairs beneath. Inflorescence a compact panicle, sometimes reduced to a few flowers, densely strigose-pubescent, the peduncle ca. 1-2 cm long, ca. 0.7 mm wide; bracteoles and bracts linear, ca. 1-2 mm long, mostly caducous before anthesis, densely pubescent; Calyx-lobes four, ovate-triangular, concave, ca. 1-1.5 mm long and wide, densely pubescent; petals suborbicular, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., sparsely pubescent; hypanthium obconic, ca. 1.5 mm long, densely pubescent; stamens ca. 25, ca. 3 mm long; anthers ca. 0.3 mm long; styles glabrous, ca. 3.5 mm long; ovary 1 -locular, 1-ovulate, the ovule pendulous. Fruit subglobose, ca. 7-8 mm in diam. Seed one, the testa subcartilaginous.

description: Shrub or tree, 1.8-5(-10) m tall. Branchlets spreading, slender, flexuous, subangular, youngest parts glabrous or patently puberulous, early covered with dark cork and elongate lenticels. Leaves ovate-lanceolate, sometimes in part in the same specimen ovate or ovate-oblong, apex gradually attenuate or subacuminate, tip subacute, base broadly attenuate to the petiole or rounded, subcoriaceous, dark brown to olivaceous or even nigrescent above, usually paler beneath, dull and brittle in the dry state, not properly tuberculate, 3.5-6(-9) x 1.8-3(-4) cm, midrib hardly raised above, more distinctly so beneath, lateral nerves 4-5 pairs, the lowest 1 or 2 pair(s) curved and high-ascending, the upper ones more straight, not properly looping, slightly raised or rather inconspicuous on both surfaces, reticulation of veins and veinlets obscure; petiole 2-3 x 1 mm. Spike-like racemes solitary or geminate from the nodes; rhachis (including peduncle 5-8 mm long) distinct, bearing several spaced groups of 2, or rarely 3 flowers, glabrous or puberulous except corollas and flower-axes, (1-) 1.5-2(-3) cm long. Bracts and bracteoles of the epicalyx free to almost the base, ciliate, 1 mm long. Flower-axis cup-shaped, low, ca. 1 mm long. Flowers subsessile or sometimes on pedicels to 1 mm long, 4- or 5-merous, pale yellow, suffused with red, or reddish. Corolla in the doli-chostylous flowers urceolate, 6-7 mm long including lobes, the latter ca. 1.5 mm long, finally recurved; style attaining the orifice of the corolla tube. Corolla in the brachystylous flowers similar, slightly narrower, 7(-8) mm long. Top of ovary glabrous. Drupe subobovoid-ellipsoid, finally blackish, 10-11 x (6-)7-8 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.
