description: Treelet. Branchlets purplish when dried, sparsely golden-brownish strigose when young, glabrescent when older. Leaves apparently opposite; petioles 5-12 mm long, sparsely golden-brownish strigose when young, glabrescent when older; stipules deciduous, (narrowly) deltoid, 0.5- 12.5 x 0.25 mm, herbaceous, golden-(brownish) strig(ill)ose to glabrescent, ciliolate, mucronulate; lamina (narrowly) (ob)ovate to elliptic, acuminate to cuspidate, 7-17.5 x 3-6.5 cm, herbaceous, glabrous on both sides; costa glabrous above, sparsely golden-brownish pilosulous beneath when young, glabrescent when older; domatia wanting; lateral veins 9-11 (acumen excluded); tertiary venation reticulate; base rounded to cuneate, sometimes slightly decurrent into the petiole; margin subentire, not cili(ol)ate; acumen 1-2 cm long, sometimes falcate, apex subobtuse to subacute. Inflorescences axillary, lateral and subterminal, solitary or 2-fasciculate, racemose (0.5-) 1.25-17.5 x ca. 0.25 cm; central axis golden-brownish pilosulous; ‘pedicels’ ca. 1 mm long, articulate at 1/5 from the base, golden-brownish pilosulous; bracts and bractlets deltoid to ovate, herbaceous, carnose, golden-brownish pilosulous along the costa, ciliolate, apex subobtuse to subacute, mucronulate; bracts 1-1.25 x 1 mm; bractlets subopposite, 0.3 x 0.25 mm. Flower buds ovoid to conical, slanting erected to the apex of the inflorescence, becoming strongly deflexed when flowering. Sepals subequal to unequal, ovate to deltoid, 0.5-1 x 0.3-0.6 mm, herbaceous, costate, golden-brownish pilosulous along the costa, ciliolate along the margin, apex obtuse, mucronulate. Petals ovate, 2.25-2.5 x 1-1.5 mm, herbaceous, carnose near the costa and scarious near the margin, glabrous, slightly purplish striate along the costa and near the base, margin sparsely ciliolate, apex obtuse to rounded. Stamens ca. 2 mm long; anterior filaments embodied in fused dorsal glands, usually only one posterior filament and dorsal gland free; free filaments ca. 0.25 x ca. 0.2 mm; free dorsal glands ca. 0.3 x ca. 0.25 mm; glandular tissue carnose, glabrous; anthers ovoid, ca. 0.75 x ca. 0.5 mm, glabrous, apex obtuse, unappendaged; connective outside, linear, subobtuse, ca. 0.6 x 0.1 mm, glabrous; connective scales lateral as well as apical, ovate, ca. 1.75 x ca. 0.25 mm, scarious, orange-brown, pectinate near the base, erose near the apex, apex obtuse. Ovary subglobose, ca. 1 mm in diam., golden-brownish pilose; ovules two per placenta. Style filiform, erect to slightly curved, ca. 1.5 x 0.2 mm, exceeding the stamens by 0-0.5 mm, completely glabrous; stigma truncate. Fruits unknown.

description: Plant flowering 5-6 dm high. Leaves 2-3 dm long, wholly covered with small appressed scales; sheaths broadly elliptic, distinctly broader than the blades and nearly as long castaneous-lepidote; blades subligulate, broadly acute and apiculate, 35-50 mm wide, cinereous-lepidote, densely and finely brown-maculate beneath, the apex strongly recurved. Scape erect, stout, glabrous; scape-bracts erect and clasping the scape but with recurved apices, elliptic or ovate, apiculate, lepidote toward apex, the upper ones equaling or slightly exceeding the internodes. Inflorescence densely bipinnate, to 14 cm long, 45 mm in diameter; primary bracts suborbicular, apiculate, much shorter than the racemes; racemes erect, laxly few-flowered, without sterile bracts; rhachis slightly flexuous. Floral bracts distichous, suborbicular, minutely apiculate, 18-20 mm long, 15 mm wide, obtusely carinate toward apex but not incurved, exceeded by the sepals, pale green or yellowish like the sepals; flowers suberect, not secund, yellow; pedicels short, stout. Sepals narrowly elliptic, obtuse, 21 mm long, ecarinate; petals ligulate, ca 35 mm long, bearing 2 lanceolate acute scales; stamens exserted.

description: Young twigs and under side of midrib puberulent; petioles 0.4-2.4 mm long; blades 16-50(-59) times as long as the petiole, 1.4-2.8 times as long as wide; true pedicels (1.2-)2.0-4.4 mm long (-5.0 mm in fruit); free part of calyx lobes 1.0-2.5 mm long; calyx length from stamen attachment 1.6-3.5 mm; petals 3.6-5.6 mm long, 2.0-3.6 mm wide, 1.2-2.1 times as long as wide; anther sporangia 1.2-1.8 mm long.

description: Small tree, or shrub. Young branches with closely appressed indumentum, tomentose or villous, yellow-orange to orange-brown, especially around nodes, glabrescent; bark dark gray-brown; lenticels numerous, small, to 0.8 × 0.5 mm, plane becoming raised and more conspicuous, granular, light brown to orange-brown. Axillary buds solitary in leaf axils, or elaborately lobed with flower buds developing in situ prior to raceme elongation, ferruginous-villous. Leaves subcoriaceous to coriaceous, usually drying shiny above, spirally arranged, decussate, or rarely verticillate towards shoot apex, the indumentum closely appressed-sericeous, shorter beneath than above, glabrescent, persisting longer at base of lamina, pale yellow to orange-brown. Petiole (3-)5-10 mm long, 1(-1.5) mm wide, flat, thick, base of lamina often descending petiole, faintly bulbate above, wrinkled and longitudinally ridged beneath, indumentum above dense, appressed, tomentose or villous, orange-brown fading to gray, beneath, sparsely long pilose, glabrescent. Lamina 4-15 × (l-)1.3-3.5(-4.2) cm, narrowly oblong, elliptic to narrowly elliptic or oblanceolate; base symmetrical, acute or cuneate; apex rarely rounded, more often obtuse to acute; margin revolute, more so at base; venation not usually conspicuous, raised above, brochidodromous from base of lamina, forming a double marginal vein at times, less often eucamptodromous at base; midrib ± plane above, rarely slightly raised or sunken; lateral veins 5-8(-10) pairs, leaving midrib at (20-)30-50(-70)°, the lowermost vein usually more acute to the midrib than the others, ascending very steeply. Primary axis of inflorescence branched, 3-11 cm × 1-1.5 mm (at times two axes emerge together due to nondevelopment of the apical meristem), the entire structure often broader than long, forming a pseudocorymb; (2-)3-8(-10) lateral inflorescences at (l-)2-6(-9) nodes, (0.7-)2-9 cm × 0.5-1 mm, spirally arranged, lowermost lateral inflorescences axillary to full-sized leaves which gradually reduce in size on ascending the primary axis, at times lateral inflorescences further branched, and accessory branching common; indumentum short-tomentose or short-villous to pilose, orange-brown, at times hairs short and closely appressed mixed with long, erect, fine, wavy hairs. Common bracts 0.7-3 mm long, orange-brown to yellow-brown long-tomentose to villous on exterior. Pedicels 4.5-9.5 × 0.2-0.3 mm, usually continuing to elongate after perianth parts shed, to 11.5 mm, the indumentum pale yellow to yellow-brown short-villous to pilose. Flowers 4-5.5 mm long; perianth indumentum pale yellow to yellow-brown, closely appressed, short sericeous-pilose; free part of filaments 1.5-3 mm long, adnate 2-3 mm from base of perianth; anthers l × 0.2-0.5 mm long, oblong; hypogynous nectary 0.4-1 mm long, acutely lobed; ovary hairs extending 1.5-2(-2.5) mm from base, straggly; style 0.2-0.3 mm wide at midlength, very slightly clavate. Fruit pedicel 5-7 × 2-3 mm. Fruit 3 cm diam., (elliptic to) globose, the apex slightly mucronate, smooth dark brown-black, sometimes speckled pale brown, the surface pale orange-brown pubescent when young, glabrescent; pericarp 1 mm thick; outer mesocarp very thin; mid mesocarp 0.8 mm thick; inner mesocarp thin. Seed coat fused to pericarp. Seed 2 cm diam., fleshy, pale brown. Field characters. Shrub or tree 2-8 m tall. Flowers white to cream or greenish yellow, fragrant.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 3-10 m tall, to 18 cm in dbh, with spreading branches; wood soft and with a clear resin smelling of turpentine, the young branch-lets terete or slightly angular, sparsely pubescent with tufted, few-branched or long simple hairs, or glabrous. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3; petioles 0.53 cm long, the lamina drying greenish brown, thin-chartaceous, obovate, oblanceolate to lanceolate, 12-22 X 5-9 cm, the base acute to obtuse and often flared, the apex acuminate, the tip 1-2 cm long, both surfaces more or less densely pubescent with whitish or yellowish simple, few-branched, or tufted hairs, glabrate with age, with 7-10 pairs of secondary veins, these flat above and raised below, the margin more or less profoundly serrate, dentate, or denticulate, the teeth usually conspicuously pubescent. Cymes 1-3 cm long, often pendent, pubescent like the young branch-lets, with 15-25 flowers. Fresh flowers white or yellow; male floral cup obconical, 2.5-3 mm in diam., ca. 2.2 mm high, pubescent like the young branchlets, the tepals 5-7, narrowly triangular, 2.2-2.6 mm long, the floral roof moderately raised and glabrate; stamens 8-14; female floral cup subglobose, 2.5-3.5 mm in diam., 2.4-3.2 mm high, the tepals up to 3 mm long; styles 10-15. Fruiting receptacle globose and crowned by the persistent tepals, l(-2) cm in diam., the 8-12 drupelets distinctly visible in dried receptacles, when fresh green with whitish spots or warts and a strong lemon odor, the drupelets with a reddish stylar aril.

description: Tree, to 20 m tall, mostly dioecious. Leafy twigs 3-4 mm thick, with (sparse) very short patent hairs intermixed with (rather) sparse distinctly and longer mostly ± appressed yellow to brownish hairs; periderm flaking off or persistent. Lamina elliptic to oblong to (sub)ovate, 8-20(-30) × 4-9(-14.5) cm, slightly inequilateral, chartaceous to coriaceous; apex acuminate; base obtuse to subcordate; margin (sub)entire; upper surface sparsely strig(ill)ose to hirtellous to subglabrous, sparsely hirtellous on the main veins or only the midrib, glabrescent, smooth or faintly bullate; lower surface (rather) puberulous and with longer yellow to brownish, mostly ± appressed hairs; lateral veins 12-16 pairs, loop-connected 2-4 mm from the margin; tertiary venation largely scalariform; petiole 0.3-0.6 cm long; stipules 0.5-1 (-1.5) cm long, yellow-subhirsute to subsericeous. Staminate inflorescences up to 7 together on minute spurs in the leaf axils or just below the leaves; peduncle 0.7-1 cm long, slender, minutely puberulous; receptacle 0.4-0.7 cm diam., discoid; involucre with bracts in ca. 5 rows, the bracts minutely puberulous, the outer ones ovate and ca. 1.5-3 mm long, the inner ones lanceolate and 3-8 mm long, with the upper part incurved; tepals 3-4, (almost) free, 1-1.5 mm long, minutely puberulous; stamens 2-4; filaments ca. 1.5 mm long; anthers ca. 0.8-1 × 0.4-0.5 mm. Pistillate inflorescences solitary or sometimes accompanied by as many as 3 staminate ones, ca. 1-1.5 cm diam.; subsessile or peduncle to 1.5 cm long; involucral bracts in 6-9 rows, broadly to narrowly ovate, acute to caudate, appressed-puberulous to subsericeous; flowers ca. 5-10, free or connate; perianth 2.5-3 mm long, entire to 4-dentate, puberulous to hirtellous to hirsute, if the perianth free, then setose near the base; style 1-1.5 mm long, glabrous, stigmas 2-3.5 mm long. Infructescences 2.5-4 cm diam.; fruiting perianth brown to yellowish hirtellous to hirsute or puberulous.

description: Shrubs to scandent shrubs: with long, slender and sparsely branched shoots; branches basitonic, in axils of cataphylls or foliage leaves; twigs terete, 3-4 mm diam.; epidermis brownish, barely visible due to in-dument cover; terminal bud plump, ca. 6 X 3 mm; cataphylls persisting on current flush (and for at least three flushes), to 6 mm long; indument pubescent, persisting for at least two flushes, the hairs dense, to 0.8 mm long, straight, erect, brownish. Leaves: petioles robust, 0.5-1.5 cm X 0.3-0.5 mm, terete; blades coriaceous to chartaceous, flat to búllate, elliptic, 15-32 X 7-13 cm; base obtuse to rounded (almost cordate), (80-)120-140(-180)°; apex obtuse to rounded, (70-)100-140°, acuminate for up to 3 cm; margin plane to recurved; primary vein above raised, below prominent; secondary veins (7-)9-11(-14) pairs, equidistant to closer together towards the apex, brochidodromous, above impressed, below raised, diverging at 55-65°, evenly arching, chordal angle ca. 30°, lowest pair more obtuse than rest; tertiary veins above flat, below slightly raised, random-reticulate; higher-order veins above inconspicuous, below slightly raised; surface above shiny brown, below olive-green to brown, the veins lighter; indument above absent, the primary vein basally tomentose, below tomentose to pubescent, the hairs sparse, to 1 mm long, straight, erect, yellowish brown, denser on the veins, persisting for at least two flushes. Staminate inflorescences: basitonic, erect?, peduncles 5-19 cm long, the hypopodia 1-8 cm x ca. 1 mm, branch orders 4, the second-order branches to 14, dispersed, lowest branch to 0.5-3.5 cm long, color and indument of all axes as on twigs; bracts persistent, to 4 mm long, adaxially glabrous; bracteoles persistent, to 2 mm long, adaxially glabrous. Staminate flowers: pedicels ca. 2.5 x 0.7 mm, the diameter even throughout; receptacle obconical, ca. 0.8 X 1.8 mm; tepals membranaceous, elliptic, ca. 1.6 X 1.3 mm, at anthesis spreading, reddish, adaxially glabrous; stamens of whorls I and II spathulate, laminar, the anthers oblong, ca. 0.8 X 0.8 mm, glabrous, the locelli 4, in two almost superposed pairs, introrse, the glands absent; whorl III columnar, ca. 1.4 X 0.5 mm, with a few few hairs at base, the anthers oblong, the locelli 4, the upper pair latrorse, the lower pair extrorse, the glands globose, ca. 0.8 mm diam.; whorl IV absent; all stamens reddish; pistillode absent. Pistillate flowers: pistil ca. 1.6 X 0.6 mm; ovary ovoid, ca. 0.8 mm long, glabrous. Fruits: pedicels to 10 X 3 mm, often thickening well below the bracteoles, gradually enlarging to form the cupule; cupule trumpet-shaped, to 1 x 1 mm, smooth, the margin undulate to straight, tepals persisting or caducous; berry elliptic, to 3 X 2 mm.

description: Small trees. Leafy twigs 1-3.5 mm thick, yellow to brownish subtomentose to velutinous. Leaves oblong to lanceolate, often broadest near the lower end, mostly strongly inequilateral, 6-18 cm long, 1.5-8 cm broad, coriaceous to subcoriaceous, acuminate, the broader half mostly obtuse at the base, glabrous above, sparsely puberulous, glabrescent beneath; the costa and the proximal parts of the secondary veins prominent, otherwise the venation nearly plane to slightly impressed above, veins more or less prominent beneath, 13-20 pairs of secondary veins; petioles 3-10 mm long; stipules 7-17 mm long yellow to brownish subsericeous, often subpersistent. Staminate inflorescences 7-8 mm in diameter; peduncle 2-6 mm long, puberulous; involucre with 9-14 reniform to suborbiculate to ovate to subovate, obtuse to acute, sparsely puberulous to nearly glabrous bracts in 3-5 series; perianth 1.5-2.5 mm high, with 1-3 free tepals; stamens 2-4; filaments 1.0-1.5 mm long, anthers 0.4-0.8 mm long, o.2-0.5 mm broad, occasionally apiculate. Pistillate inflorescences 6-9 mm in diameter, sessile; involucre with 17-20 reniform to suborbiculate to deltoid to ovate to lanceolate, obtuse to acute, appressed-pubescent bracts in 5-6 series; flowers 5-8, only stigmas visible at anthesis; tepals free?, 0.5-1.5 mm long, about subulate, puberulous; style 1-1.5 mm long, stigmas vittiform, 9-12 mm long; pseudobracts similar to the tepals. Flowering from November to February.

description: Tree, tall, height to 40-45(-50?) m, dbh to 150— 200 cm. Trunk monopodial, erect, columnar, straight, terete. Bark rough, scaly, divided into small, rectangular scales, exfoliating with small flakes, grey brown, weathering grey; on young trees and branches smooth, greenish grey. Branches of first order long, slender, spreading horizontally, the lower branches somewhat drooping; of second and higher orders slender, spreading and/or assurging. Crown pyramidal to broad conical, with branches down to 2/3 or ¾ of tree height. Shoots mostly glabrous or current year’s shoots brownish puberulent, grooved; pulvini prominent, short decurrent. Cataphylls small, 5-10 mm long, subulate, with erose margins, dark brown, soon deciduous. Vegetative buds small, hidden in leaf tufts, the terminal buds 8-15 X 5-8 mm, ovoid-oblong, the laterals smaller, ovoid, not or only slightly resinous; the scales subulate-linear, acute, free, dark purplish brown. Fascicle sheaths 15-20 (-25) mm long, with ca. 5-7 loose, oblong, orange-brown or red-brown scales, deciduous. Leaves in fascicles of 5, very rarely 6, in dense, lax tufts toward the upturned ends of ultimate branches, persisting 23 years, straight or slightly curved or twisted, spreading at 40-60° from the shoot but not drooping, (8-)10-15(-18) cm X 0.7-1 mm (-1.5 mm on vigorous coning shoots), margins (weakly) serrulate, apex acute, green or grey-green with two whitish stomatal bands. Stomata on the two adaxial faces only, in two dense bands of 3-6 intermittent lines. Leaf anatomy: Cross section triangular, with roughly equal sides, the abaxial side slightly convex; hypodermis uniform, mostly with a single layer of cells; resin ducts 2-4 (-7), external, the largest number usually on the abaxial side; stele terete; outer cell walls of endodermis not thickened; vascular bundle 1. Pollen cones crowded at the proximal end of a new shoot, spreading, subtended by reddish brown, scarious bracts, ovoid to short cylindrical, 7-10 mm long, yellow, turning orange-brown. Seed cones toward the end of main branches, subterminal, axillary to the terminal bud, solitary or more often in pairs or whorls of 34 on short (to 25 mm) peduncles which usually fall with the cone. Immature cones elliptic to cylindrical, straight or curved, more or less erect, purple, turning green, maturing in two seasons. Mature cones short pedunculate, pendulous, cylindrical, curved, tapering toward apex, usually >3 times longer than wide when open, (10-)15-40(-50) X 7-15 cm when open. Seed scales ca. 100-150, readily parting to release the seeds, spreading at 40-80° from the axis, thin, flexible or more rigid, straight, the proximal scales recurved, transversely nearly flat or concavo-convex, long (5-7 cm), with parallel to diverging sides, the distal scales narrowing, (abaxially) rugose or grooved, dull brown or dark reddish brown abaxially, with light brown marks of seed wings on the adaxial side. Apophysis thin or thick, irregularly trullate, recurved or reflexed toward the apex, or the apex curved up below the umbo, longitudinally grooved, dull light brown, very resinous. Umbo terminal, broadly triangular, obtuse, 5-10 mm wide, grey, usually covered with resin. Seeds in two cup-like depressions at the base of the scale, (broadly) obovoid, laterally flattened, 8-15 X 6-9 mm, dull brown with black spots, usually equally developed but sometimes of slightly different size on one scale. Seed wings adnate, (2-3.5 X) longer than the seed, oblique, with a curved side or broad truncate, 20-35 X 8-12 mm, light brown with dark striations or dark brown. Number of cotyledons not observed.

description: Treelet 1-3 m tall. Stems terete, cano-velutinous, smooth. Leaves paripinnate; distal process acicular, 4-6 mm long; leaflets 12-22, opposite to alternate, oblanceolate to nearly oblong, 9-18 × 3.2-6 cm, chartaceous to coriaceous, the adaxial surface glabrous except for the sometimes canescent midvein, the abaxial surface canescent, the venation brochidodromus, plane on adaxial surface, prominent on abaxial surface, tertiary veins reticulate, the margins entire, revolute, ciliate, the apex obtusely and abruptly acuminate or less often acuminate, the base cuneate-obtuse, conspicuously asymmetrical; petiolules nearly cylindrical, velutinous, thickened for their entire length, slightly flattened adaxially, 3-4 mm long, velutinous; rachis terete, bicanaliculate toward distal portion, cano-pubescent, 16.5-20 cm long; petioles 9-13 cm long, terete, cano-pubescent, thickened at base. Thyrses panicle-shaped, pyramidal, terminal, to 50 cm long, lateral basal branches to 20 cm long; cataphylls pinnate, 6.5-10 cm long, cano-velutinous to -pilose, congested at distal portion of stem; axes nearly terete, striate to sulcate, tomentulose to tomentose; bracts oblong, tomentulose to tomentose, persistent, 3-4 mm long; dichasia compound; peduncles, 6-15 mm long, flattened; pedicels < 1 mm long, tomentose, articulate at base. Calyx 4.5-6 mm long, tomentose, the sepals ovate, the 3 outer ones ca. 3 mm long, the 2 inner ones ca. 2 mm long; petals white, nearly spatulate, 6-9 mm long, reflexed at anthesis, abaxially tomentose on lower half, adaxially glabrous, the apex rounded, the base clawed; appendages oblong, as long or little shorter than the petals, bifid, erect, tightly convergent, villous on both surfaces; disc cup-shaped, 5-lobed, hirsute, ca. 1 mm tall; stamens 8, the filaments sparingly woolly-pubescent, of equal length, ca. 2.5 mm long, the anthers oblong, ca. 2.2 mm long, glabrous, apiculate at apex; ovary conical, tomentose, the stigma cylindrical, papillate. Fruits nearly ovoid, appressed ferruginous-pubescent, ca. 3 cm long, minutely granulose, apiculate, the pericarp woody, ca. 1.5 mm thick, the endocarp puberulent. Seed solitary or less often two per fruit, ovoid, the sarcotesta very thin, not noticeable when dry. Embryo of 2 equal, erect cotyledons, or these obliquely superimposed.

description: Field characters. Small tree to 15 m with pale or dark grey-brown bark which is scaling in thin strips in older specimens. description: Young branches pubescent becoming glabrous, brown, with numerous lenticels. Bud scales absent. Leaves pinnate with one leaflet of the ultimate pair orientated to simulate a terminal leaflet, ca. 35 cm long; petiole and rhachis semiterete, pubescent when young soon glabrous; petiolule ca. 1 mm long. Leaflets opposite to alternate, 5-6, broadly oblong to oblanceolate, apex broadly short cuspidate to narrowly attenuate, base narrowly attenuate (lower ones broadly short attenuate to subtruncate), subcoriaceous, ca. 23 cm long, ca. 12 cm broadly glabrous, glandular-punctate and -striate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib prominent; secondaries 13-16 on either side of midrib, shallowly ascending, slightly arcuate, ± parallel; intersecondaries short; tertiaries widely spaced, indistinct. Inflorescences clustered in axils of developing leaves, to 7 cm long, a much-branched, densely-flowered pyramidal panicle, subglabrous; pedicel ca. 2.5 mm long. Calyx cyathiform, 1.5-2 mm long, with 4 irregular, shallow lobes, sparsely pubescent on outer surface. Petals 3-4 (when 3, often one split 1/2way), free, slightly imbricate, 6.5-7 mm long, 2-4 mm broad, oblong to lanceolate, apex acute, sericeous on outer surface. Staminal tube cylindrical; filaments completely fused, ca. 5.5 mm long, ca. 2.5 mm broad, margin with 7-8 short acute appendages alternating with anthers and ca. 1/3 their length, sparsely and coarsely hairy in upper half on both surfaces; anthers 7-8, ca. 1.2 mm long, glabrous. Nectary annular, torulose, ± glabrous. Ovary slender, 2-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, densely pubescent; style tapering from base to apex, pubescent; style-head conical, equalling base of anthers. Fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1981. Meliaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 28: 1-359, 418-449, 459-470.

description: Young branches appressed puberulous to pubescent becoming glabrous, rough, greyish or brown, usually lenticellate. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate or very rarely with a few trifoliolate, (2.5-)3.5-7.5 cm long; petiole and rhachis semiterete, sparsely short pubescent to glabrous; petiolule 0.5-3 mm long. Leaflets opposite or alternate, (3-)5-9, oblanceolate, obovate or broadly elliptic, apex varying from rounded or obtuse to short narrowly attenuate sometimes minutely emarginate, base broadly rounded to cuneate, acute, or narrowly attenuate sometimes slightly oblique, coriaceous, 2.8-7.5[5] cm long, 1.7-3.5[2.2] cm broad, upper surface glabrous or with a puberulous midrib, lower surface glabrous or with scattered appressed indumentum of dibrachiate or medifixed hairs, not glandular-punctate or -striate; venation brochidodromous, midrib flat; secondaries 813 on either side of midrib, shallowly ascending, straight, parallel; intersecondaries prominent, long; tertiary reticulum prominent. Flowers unisexual, plants dioecious; inflorescence axillary, 2.5-12 cm long, a slender raceme or thyrse, puberulous; pedicel 0.5-1 mm long. Calyx cyathiform, 0.75-1 mm long, with 4-5 triangular, acute lobes 1/3-1/2 length of calyx, appressed puberulose. Petals (3-)4, fused 1/3-1/2 their length, valvate, (2-)3-3.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, oblong, elliptic or lanceolate, apex acute to obtuse, hooded, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Staminal tube short cylindrical, 1.25-2 mm long, 0.75-1 mm broad; filaments completely fused, margin with 4-5 attenuate to subulate lobes alternating with anthers and 1/3-3/4 their length, outside glabrous, inside with sparse coarse pubescence or glabrous; anthers 4-5, 0.6-0.8 mm long, glabrous; antherodes slender, not dehisced, without pollen. Nectary absent. Ovary ovoid, 2-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, strigose; style short, stout; style-head small discoid bearing a conical stigmatic area, below level of anthers. Capsule ellipsoid, apex and base rounded, smooth, sparsely papillose, ca. 1.7 cm long, 1 cm broad, 2-valved, valves reflexing; pericarp ca. 0.5 mm thick; endocarp thin-cartilaginous. Seeds 1-2 in each valve, ca. 1 cm long, 0.6 cm broad, shaped like the segment of an orange, completely surrounded by a thin, free, fleshy arillode which is attached to seed by a thin line from micropyle along raphe; seed coat thin, soft. Embryo with plano-convex collateral cotyledons; radicle apical, included. Endosperm absent.

description: Young branches appressed puberulous soon glabrous, greyish-white, rough, lenticellate. Bud scales absent. Leaves imparipinnate or trifoliolate, 3-5 cm long; petiole and rhachis semiterete, minutely puberulous; petiolule ca. 0.5 mm long. Leaflets opposite or alternate, 3-7, broadly cuneiform (obtriangular), apex acute and with the 2 lateral lobes produced into a sharp spine 2-3 mm long, base narrowly cuneate, coriaceous, 3.5-5[4.1] cm long, 3.5-4[3.6] cm broad, glabrous, not glandular-punctate or -striate; venation craspedodromous with a prominent marginal vein, midrib flat or slightly sunken; secondaries 10-12 on either side of midrib, spreading at right angles or very shallowly ascending, straight or slightly arcuate, parallel; intersecondaries moderately prominent; tertiary reticulum prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence axillary, 2.5-4 cm long, a slender few-flowered thyrse, appressed puberulous; pedicel 0.5-1.25 mm long. Calyx patelliform or shallowly cyathiform, 0.5-1 mm long, with 5 shallow, obtuse to short attenuate lobes ca. 1/2 length of calyx, appressed puberulous. Petals 5, free or fused ca. 1/4 their length, valvate, 3-3.5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm broad, narrowly lanceolate, apex acute, hooded, appressed puberulous with dibrachiate or medifixed hairs outside, glabrous inside. Staminal tube short cylindrical, 2-2.5 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm broad; filaments completely fused, margin with 10 short acute lobes alternating with anthers and 1/3-1/2 their length, glabrous; anthers 10, ca. 1 mm long, glabrous. Nectary absent. Ovary ovoid 3(-4)-locular, loculi with 2 collateral ovules, short appressed pubescent or strigose; style short, stout, glabrous at apex; style-head capitate, equalling base of anthers. Capsule oblong, apex and base rounded, verrucose, sparsely puberulous, ca. 1.6 cm long, 1 cm broad, 3-valved; pericarp 1-1.5 mm thick; endocarp cartilaginous. Seed solitary, ca. 0.7 cm long, 0.4 cm broad (excluding arillode), completely surrounded by a thick fleshy 3-partite arillode which is free except for a thin line of attachment from micropyle to chalaza; seed coat thin, soft. Embryo with plano-convex, collateral cotyledons; radicle apical, included. Endosperm absent.

description: Erect subshrubs, the young stems yellowish-tomentose. Leaf blades broadly ovate or suborbicular (rarely indistinctly 3-lobed), 4-6 x 3.5-5 cm, 7-8-nerved, softly canescent-tomentose beneath, darker and subtomentose above; petioles straight, 2.5-3 cm long (ca. half-length of blade); stipules subulate, 5-7 mm long, cinereous, caducous. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils; pedicels 3-7 mm long; involucel campanulate, subequal to calyx, striate, gamophyllous and indistinctly bilabiate, the 3-4 lobes ovate-acuminate, 6-8 mm long; calyx campanulate, 12-14 mm long, yellowish-tomentose, indistinctly striate, more or less bilabiate, with 3 free lobes ca. 3 mm long, 2 connate lobes 1-1.5 mm long; corolla 2.5-3 cm long, narrowly cylindric, the petals red, narrowly linear; staminal column ca. 3.5 cm long, glabrous, very slender, apically 5-dentate and with slender filaments; ovary glabrous, the filiform styles glabrous, ca. 4 cm long (free for distal 5-6 mm), the stigmas 9 (10?), capitate, pilose. Fruits more or less included in the calyx; mericarps 5, indehiscent, apically 3-horned, dorsally not or scarcely carinate, yellowish, thin-walled, 8-10 mm long, ca. 5 mm wide; seeds solitary, 6 mm long, dark brown, sparsely pubescent.

description: Shrubs 2 m tall, the stems densely and very minutely puberulent (including glandular hairs), the younger branches with overlying large stellate spicules. Leaf blades ovate to 3-lobed, mostly 2-3 x 1.5-2.5 cm, basally cordate, serrate, acute, palmately 5-7-nerved, discolorous, densely puberulent above, whitish puberulent beneath and with overlying large stellate spicules; petioles 1-1.5 cm long, usually more prominently covered with spicules than stem; stipules subulate, 2-3 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 10-12 mm long, slender, minutely puberulent (glandular?); involucellar bracts 5, ligulate, 5 x 1 mm, minutely pubescent; calyx 7-8 mm long, minutely pubescent, ecostate; corolla ca. 1 cm long, red, externally pubescent (with large stellate spicules), the petals acuminate; staminal column subequal to corolla to clearly exserted, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles exserted by 1 cm or more, connate nearly to apex. Fruits ca. 7 mm diam., rugose, glabrous, straw-colored; mericarps prominently crested, apically acute, 6 mm tall; seeds glabrous, obscurely striate.

description: Shrubs with stems densely and minutely stellate-pubescent, the hairs 0.2-0.3 mm long, yellowish. Leaf blades ovate-pentagonal to weakly 5-lobed, becoming narrowly triangular upward, mostly 3-8 x 3-4(-6) cm, basally cordate, serrate-crenate, acute, palmately 7-nerved, somewhat discolorous, minutely pubescent above and beneath, especially on veins, the hairs simple, bifurcate, and stellate, 0.5 mm long or less, and with scattered 3-4-armed stellate spicules beneath; petioles 2-4 cm long; stipules 1-2 mm long, nearly obsolete. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-3 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, linear, 6 x 1 mm, hispid-ciliate; calyx 10-11 mm long, costate, densely hispid-ciliate; corolla ca. 3 cm long, reddish, the petals somewhat reflexed distally; staminal column ca. 2.5 cm long, the filaments mostly apical, 3-4 mm long; styles exserted, free for distal 4-5 mm. Fruits 8-9 mm diam., minutely scabridulous; mericarps 5.5 mm tall, reticulate-veined and strongly carinate (the ridge apically prolonged and subacute), with weakly developed lateral excrescences.

description: Trees or shrubs 3-7 m tall, the young stems minutely stellate-pubescent, glabrate in age. Leaf blades broadly ovate, mostly 6-15 x 4-10 cm, deeply cordate, obscurely crenate to entire, acuminate, palmately 7-nerved, more or less discolorous, the upper surface essentially glabrous and more or less vernicose, the lower surface hirsute in the axils of the principal nerves, slightly pubescent on principal nerves, otherwise glabrous; petioles up to 6 cm long, progressively shorter upward; stipules subulate, 4-5 mm long, deciduous, becoming connate in the inflorescence to form persistent bifid bracts subtending the pedicels. Inflorescence a terminal leafless raceme; pedicels 1-1.5(-2.5) cm long; involucellar bracts 6-7, ligulate to ovate, basally connate, 6-9 x 2-5 mm, sparsely stellate-pubescent; calyx 9-10 mm long, sparsely stellate-pubescent externally, densely whitish-puberulent internally; corolla 13-16 mm long, greenish yellow, externally pubescent, tubular; androecium subequal to corolla or slightly exserted. Fruits 10-12 mm diam., crowned with 5 broad alate ridges (the ridges sometimes scabridulous or retrorsely barbed), otherwise glabrous; mericarps ligneous, reticulate-veined, 7-10 mm high (including wings).

description: Shrubs 0.5 m tall, the stems with widely scattered 3-6-armed stellate hairs ca. 0.5 mm diam., and with longitudinal lines of dense smaller (somewhat recurved) hairs. Leaf blades elliptic or oblong-elliptic, mostly 7-14 x 2-5 cm, basally asymmetrical (distichous), serrate, acuminate, penninerved, slightly discolorous, with minute stellate hairs (mostly 4-5-armed) evenly scattered over upper surface, the lower surface with fewer hairs; petioles 4-12 mm long, densely stellate-pubescent, especially on adaxial side; stipules subulate, 5-7 mm long, erect. Flowers sometimes solitary in the leaf axils, more commonly in terminal corymbose inflorescences, the pedicels 2-5 mm long, stellate-pubescent; involucellar bracts 7-10, linear, 5-6 x 0.5-1 mm, ciliate; calyx ca. 2 mm long, glabrous; petals pink, 10-12 mm long; androecium ca. Vi length of petals, the anthers few, subsessile. Fruits 4-5 mm diam., glabrous; mericarps ca. 5 mm long, dorsally rounded, smooth, with single apical spine 8-10 mm long (retrorsely barbed) that is basally buttressed dorsoventrally, the 2 lateral spines suppressed.

description: Shrubs 0.5-2(-3) m tall, the stems densely stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades ovate-elliptic, up to 10(-12) x 5 cm, basally truncate or rounded, serrate, acute, palmately 5-nerved, somewhat discolorous, minutely stellate-pubescent above and beneath (the hairs beneath slightly larger but <0.5 mm diam.); petioles 3-12 mm long, densely stellate-pubescent; stipules 5-8 mm long, subulate-filiform. Flowers axillary but usually aggregated apically in a relatively congested inflorescence; pedicels 0.5-3 cm long with subarachnoid pubescence (finer than that of stem); involucellar bracts 5-6, lanceolate, 7 mm long, <1 mm wide, hirsute; calyx 5 mm long, ciliate (the hairs 1 mm long); petals yellow, 11-20 mm long, pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column 11 mm long, glabrous, the filaments 2-3 mm long; styles and stigmas emergent from column by 4-5 mm, almost equaling the petals. Fruits 6-7 mm diam.; mericarps 3-spined, the central spine erect, the lateral spines divergent, all 5 mm long, the spines retrorsely barbed, the mericarp body carinate and reticulate-nerved with retrorse barbs on all of the nerves.

description: Shrubs to 2 m tall, the younger stems minutely and obscurely sublepidote (the hairs 0.1 mm diam.) to glabrate. Leaf blades oblong-elliptic, mostly 9-19 x 3-7 cm, basally rounded or subcuneate (and minutely auriculate), entire, acuminate, penninerved, glabrous or subglabrous; petioles 0.5-2.5 cm long; stipules foliaceous, 1.5-2.5 x 0.8-1.5 cm, ovate-elliptic, sessile, basally cuneate to cordate-clasping, acute or obtuse, glabrous. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 18-24 cm long, filiform (0.5 mm diam.), distally dilated forming 4 flanges or buttresses; involucellar bracts 4-5, foliaceous, red, 2.5-4 x 1-2.5 cm, ovate, entire, acute, glabrous; calyx 10-12 mm long, externally sparsely and minutely puberulent to subglabrous, internally densely puberulent; corolla subequal to calyx or somewhat shorter; staminal column 1-1.5 cm long, the filaments 6-9 mm long, erect, exserted from calyx/corolla. Fruits unknown.

description: Large shrubs of unknown stature, with glabrate stems. Leaf blades to 23 x 10 cm, lance-ovate, essentially truncate basally, very coarsely dentate (the teeth 4-6 per 10 cm), especially distally, to subentire, apically acute or acuminate (the tip itself rounded), penninerved, the midrib slightly raised above, prominently raised beneath, with 5-7 secondary veins on each side, glabrous or glabrate above and beneath, nearly concolorous; petioles 1.5-3(-5) cm long, very minutely puberulent to glabrate; stipules not seen but leaving prominent scars. Flowers axillary, borne on short lateral spurs with crowded internodes, thus appearing fasciculate; pedicels ca. 1 cm long, slender; involucellar bracts 3-4, broadly ovate, 1.5-2 x 1-1.5 cm, subglabrous (brightly colored?); calyx 10-13 mm long (concealed by involucel), minutely and sparsely stellate pubescent (especially on lobes), ca. halfdivided, the lobes ovate; petals subequal to or slightly exceeding the calyx (color?); staminal column glabrous, exserted, exceeding the involucel, the filaments 4-5 mm long; styles slender, exserted from androecium. Fruits unknown.

description: Dwarf shrub to ca. 0.3(-0.5) m tall, subprostrate or erect, unbranched or with 1 or 2 branches, stems brown, unarmed, young shoots densely puberulous. Leaves in 1-3 pseudowhorls towards summit of stems, blade narrowly obovate, sometimes obovate or oblanceolate, 6.5-22 x 3-6.5 cm, sometimes puberulous on lower side, midvein prominent beneath, somewhat impressed above, base truncate or shortly attenuate, apex obtuse, margins undulate, serrate, usually strongly so, teeth 15-30 per side, pungent, 2-6 mm long, both surfaces striate; subepidermal fiber bundles 5-25 cells thick; petiole 2-5(-10) mm long, 1.2-2.3 mm thick, densely puberulous, at least towards base, pedicels 4-6 mm long; bracts 0.5-1.5 mm long, puberulous. Calyx glandular-punctate, lobes ovate, 2.5-2.7 x 2-2.5 mm. Corolla tube ca. 2 mm long, lobes broadly ovate, ca. 4.5 x 5.5 mm. Filaments ca. 1.5 mm long, anthers ca. 2 mm long, apical appendages ca. 0.5 mm long, projection descending as a keel on adaxial side of anther. Ovary with 7-10 ovules in 2 or 3 rows, style 1.5-2 mm long. Fruits 0.8-3.5 cm diam. Seeds 0.8-1.2 cm broad.
bibliographicCitation: Ståhl, Bertil. 2010. Theophrastaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 105: 1-160.

description: Shrub ca 2 m or less high. Bark reddish or grayish, ridged, and with some short hairs. Branchlets and leaves not crowded. Stipules often up to 6 per node and at the base of the pedicels, up to 2 mm long, pubescent and persistent; petioles (3.0-)4.0-10.0(-13.0) mm long, yellowish, usually densely beset with hairs somewhat longer than those on the leaves; leaf-blades 2.4-8.3(-l 1.5) cm long and 0.8-2.5(-3.2) cm wide, mostly lanceolate but less often oblong and elliptic, 2.4-3.5(-4.6) times longer than wide; base obtuse to cuneate; apex acute to acuminate; margin usually plane or somewhat revolute, serrate (most frequently) or crenate with teeth often remote (3-10 per cm), either antrorse or spreading, mucronate; above green or gray-green and usually densely beset with short fine often bundled hairs; beneath paler than above (rarely the same) and densely beset with short hairs which may or may not obscure the epidermis and often arise in groups of two or more; midrib and secondary veins conspicuous above and beneath but moreso beneath and less hairy than epidermis; 8-13 pairs of secondary veins on either side of midrib. Flowers in sessile axillary umbels of 1-10(-20) but more often the smaller number; pedicels (1.0-)3.0-7.0(-8.0) mm long, sometimes arcuate, with scattered sometimes bundled hairs; floral cup 1.0-1.5 mm deep and 2 mm broad with scattered external hairs, sepals 5, 1.5 mm long and 1 mm wide at base with scattered external hairs; petals 5, ca 1 mm long and wide, notch broad and obtuse, base truncate forming a distinct claw ca 0.25 mm long and broad narrowing somewhat toward the insertion end; filament ca 0.6-1 mm long, anthers 5, 0.6-0.75 mm long, enclosed by petals; style reaching slightly above base or to midpoint of sepals. Fruits l-2(-3) per axil; pedicel (4.0-)6.0-8.0(-10.0) mm long, elongating after anthesis, with scattered often bundled short hairs; drupes obovoid, 5.0 10.0 mm in diam, glabrous, 3-seeded.

description: Tree to 12 m tall, the branchlets subtetragonal, very minutely and glabrescently puberulous, with whitish lenticels. Leaves bipinnate, to 40 cm long, with 8 to 26 pinnae, each pinna with glabrous or adaxially sparsely puberulous rachis and 9-29(-35 fide Correll & Correll, 1982) sessile, asymmetrically oblong-elliptic leaflets, these (0.5-)1-2 cm long and (0.3-)0.5-1 cm wide, apex rounded to subacute, the base cuneate, more or less lepidote below, otherwise glabrous except for minute trichomes along margin and sometimes midvein, often with a beard of longer trichomes along base of midvein below. Inflorescence an open panicle, minutely puberulous, with caducous bracts. Flowers with the calyx campanulate, shallowly acutely 5-dentate (2-3-)5-6 mm long, ca. 3 mm wide, puberulous with subappressed trichomes; corolla purplish blue, tubular-campanulate above a narrow neck which is curved and enlarged toward the base, 3.5-4 cm long, 1-1.4 cm wide at the mouth, the lobes ca. 0.8 cm long, the tube 2.5-3 cm long, puberulous outside, with sessile lepidote glands and minute simple trichomes, villous on lower lobe, glabrous inside, even at stamen insertion; stamens didynamous, the anthers monothecate, the second theca reduced to a minute appendage, each theca 2-2.5 mm long, the long staminode ca. 2 cm long, subexserted, the middle third and apex glandular pubescent; ovary flattened-ovate, 2 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, glabrous; disk cylindric, 1 mm long, 1.5 mm wide. Fruit elliptic, woody-valved, rounded to truncate at base and apex, 3.5-5 cm long, 2.5-3.5 cm wide, the margin not undulate but rolling up at dehiscence, glabrous, drying tannish brown; seeds small-bodied with a surrounding suborbicular wing 0.9-1.4 cm long, 1.8-2 cm wide, the wing hyaline-membranaceous with radial brownish striations, clearly demarcated from the seed body.
bibliographicCitation: Gentry, Alwyn H. 1992. Bignoniaceae--part II (Tribe Tecomeae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 25: 1-370.

description: Leaves oblong to oblong-elliptic, sometimes elliptic, densely lanate beneath, the margins entire; petioles 1.5-3.0 mm long. Flower buds ca 5.0 mm long, the bracts 3.0-6.0 mm long. Glands laciniate. Fruit ca 4.0 cm long; endocarp with very short velutinous-tomentose pubescence.

description: Glabrous tree; trunk cylindrical. Branchlets smooth, reddish-brown when dry. Leaves oblong to lanceolate-oblong, apex subabruptly acuminate for 1-2 cm, base broadly attenuate, subcoriaceous, shiny above, less so beneath, smooth, i.e. neither wrinkled nor tuberculate, brown when dry, edge a little revolute, (5.5-)8-14 x (2.5-)3-6 cm, midrib stout, impressed above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves 5-7(-8) pairs curved-ascendent, flat above, slightly raised beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets obsolete; petiole robust, smooth and paler in lower half, rugulose, dark and somewhat thickened above, 7-14 x 2 mm. Flowers pale green, 1-2 per axil; pedicels 2-3 mm long. Calyx minute, 5-lobed. Petals ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, 3 mm long. Stamens 10, alternately unequal. Calyx much accrescent towards fructification, finally elongately um-shaped, coriaceous, brittle, green, 3-4 cm long, 2-3 cm diam., its upper 1/3 (which exceeds the drupe) shortly irregularly (3-) 5-lobed and -plicate, thinner in texture than the basal part. Drupe barrel-shaped, apex truncate with a shallow circular apical depression, dark, 1.82 cm long, 1.2-1.5 cm diam.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Glabrous shrub or usually tree, (1.5-)4-12 m tall; trunk to 25 cm diam. Branchlets slender, youngest parts angular, older ones covered with gray transversely fissured cork. Leaves variable in shape and size, oblong to elliptic- or obovate-oblong, sometimes narrowly so, or even lanceolate, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, apex short-acuminate, sometimes subfalcate, tip subacute or obtuse, base broadly cuneate to obtuse or rounded, laticifers flat or hardly raised, usually faintly visible in dry specimens, somewhat shiny on both surfaces, olive- to dark brown in the dry state, more or less densely tuberculate on both surfaces, not properly wrinkled, edge slightly revolute, (6-) 10-15(-20, -25) x (2-)3-5(-8, -10) cm, midrib impressed above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves (6-)7-9(-11) pairs rather straight from midrib, curved-ascending and looping only before the edge, usually faintly impressed (as is the reticulation) above, though not rarely practically plane or even obscurely raised there, always raised beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets finely though distinctly prominent beneath; petiole rugulose lengthwise, not swollen distally, 1-1.5 cm x ca. 1.5 mm. Flowers few to rather numerous in dense axillary clusters on small multibracteolate cushions, subsessile, i.e. pedicels rarely to 1 mm long in anthesis. Calyx 5-lobed halfway or more, lobes triangular with a minute apical gland, 1-1.5 mm long. Petals lanceolate, subacute, white to greenish, hairy at the middle inside, 2.5(-3) x 1.5(-2) mm. Stamens 10; filaments filiform. Ovary thickened at base. Drupe ellipsoid, sometimes subobovoid, smooth, whitish or pale, ca. 10 x 7 mm. Fruit-calyx thick-membranaceous, fleshy when fresh, scarlet red, 5-lobed to almost the base, expanded (2-)2.5(-3) cm diam., lobes ovate, subacute, or obtuse, plicate, remaining erect, including the drupe; peduncle slender, 2-3(-5) mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Very thorny shrub 1-4 m tall; thorns 1.2-2.3 cm long. Leaves elliptic to ovate, apex obtuse or retuse, with mucro to 0.5 mm, base obtuse, membranaceous to coriaceous, glabrous, 3.2-5.5 x 1.9-2.6(-3.6) cm; petiole puberulous to glabrous, 3-4.5 mm long. Flowers functionally bisexual, 2-4 per axillary (sub)umbel; peduncles puberulent, 1.5-4.5 mm long; pedicels glabrous to puberulent, 2-3 mm long. Sepals 4(-5), glabrous to puberulent, apex ciliate, 0.3-0.6 mm long. Petals 4(-5), white to yellow-green, ciliate, white-bearded at inner surface to within 0.52 mm of apex. Stamens 8 (or 10); filaments 2-4.2 mm long; anthers 1.7-2.5 mm long. Ovary lanceoloid, 1.8-3 mm long; style 1.4-1.5(-2) mm long. Drupe ellipsoid, 1.5 cm long, 1.3 cm diam.; seed 1.2-1.3 x 0.9-1 cm.

description: Glabrous tree, 5-15 m high; bole cylindric, straight, to 30 cm diam.; bark fissured, reddish. Branchlets terete, striate lengthwise, brownish-blackish, younger parts prominently lenticellate. Leaves elliptic to elliptic-oblong, sometimes subovate-elliptic or even ovate in the same specimen, apex acuminate for 1-1.5 cm, base usually cuneate, rarely broadly so or rounded, subcoriaceous, dull green-olivaceous, rarely brownish, wrinkled and sparsely to densely tuberculate on both surfaces or above only when dry, edge slightly revolute, (5-)8-15 x (2.5-)3-5 (-7) cm, lateral nerves 4-6(-7) pairs, curved-ascending, excurrent before the edge, flat or slightly impressed above, prominent beneath as is the midrib, reticulation of veins and veinlets inconspicuous on both surfaces; petiole thickened-rugose distally, 1-1.8 cm x 1-1.5 mm. Flowers (2-)3-5(-8) per axillary or slightly supra-axillary fascicle which sometimes comes from an axis or peduncle 2-5(-8) mm long; pedicels rather stoutish, (2-)3-6 mm long. Calyx cup-shaped, flattish, limb 4-denticulate for 1-1.5 mm at anthesis. Petals 4, oblong, fleshy, whitish-greenish or pale orange, glabrous outside, densely set with a sordid-white brush-like tomentum of ± retrorse hairs all over or at least partly inside, (4-)5-6(-7) x 2-2.5 mm. Drupe ellipsoid or ovoid-subglobose, (1.8-)2-2.5 x 1.5-2.1 cm, enclosed by the accrescent calyx except for its conical umbonate apex (2 mm long); endocarp woody, 1.5 mm thick; seed globose, 1.2-1.5 cm diam.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1984. Olacaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 38: 1-159.

description: Dioecious shrub or treelet, 3-10 m tall and reaching a dbh of at least 7 cm; young branchlets distinctly angular, densely brown-puberulous. Leaves in whorls of 3; petioles 2-9 cm long; lamina drying dark brown, papery to chartaceous, obovate, 16.5-27 X 7.5-15.5 cm, the base acute, obtuse, or almost rounded, the apex acute or acuminate, the tip to 1.3 cm long, both surfaces loosely covered with small appressed stellate or short upright hairs, especially along the midrib, with 12-18 pairs of secondary veins, these flat above, distinctly raised below, the margin doubly serrate or dentate. Cymes 2-4 cm long, sparsely pubescent with spreading few-branched hairs, with 10-15 flowers. Fresh flowers yellowish green to yellow; male floral cup broadly obconical, 2.5-3.5 mm in diam., 2-2.5 mm high, the receptacle pubescent with few-branched hairs, the tepals mostly 5, broadly triangular, the floral roof moderately raised, glabrous and membranous; stamens 20-22, the filaments broad and membranaceous; female floral cup similar to the male cups except for minute outgrowths (at anthesis shorter than 0.5 mm), the receptacle and tubercles with short fewbranched hairs, the floral roof slightly raised and glabrous; styles 5-8. Fruiting receptacle globose, 1-1.5 cm in diam., with few minute stellate hairs and conspicfious tubercles or spines, 1-7 mm long, these either simple or few-branched, when fresh and mature whitish, cream or yellow, strongly lemon-scentedzor with a pungent odor; drupelets 2-5, each with a stylar aril.

description: Shrub to tree: branches basitonic, in axils of cataphylls; twigs terete, 1-2 mm diam.; epidermis brownish; terminal bud unknown; cataphylls persisting on current flush, to 4 mm long; indument puberulous, caducous after one flush, the hairs sparse, to 1 mm long, straight to curved, appressed ascending, brownish. Leaves: petioles slender, 1-1.5 cm x 1 mm, terete; blades chartaceous, flat, narrowly elliptic, 9-15 X 2.5-4.5 cm; base acute, 70-100°; apex acute, 50-70°, ultimately acuminate for up to 1.5 cm; margin plane; primary vein above and below raised; secondary veins 5-8 pairs, equidistant, brochidodromous, above slightly raised, below raised, diverging at ca. 60°, evenly arching, chordal angle ca. 30°, the angle uniform along blade length; tertiary veins above and below slightly raised, random-reticulate to scalariform; higher-order veins above and below slightly raised; surface above and below brown, the veins similar; indument above absent, the primary vein puberulous at base, below puberulous, the hairs sparse, to 0.3 mm long, straight to curved, appressed, brownish, somewhat denser on the veins, persisting for at least two flushes. Staminate plant unknown. Pistillate inflorescence: basitonic, erect?, peduncle 4 cm long, hypopodium ca. 4 cm X 2 mm, branching unknown, color and indument as on twigs; bracts not seen. Pistillate flowers unknown. Fruits: pedicels 25 X 5 mm, abruptly enlarging to form the cupule; cupule hemispherical, 18 x 13 mm, smooth, the margin undulate, tepals persisting; berry elliptic, 28 X 18 mm.

description: Trees: branches basitonic, in axils of cataphylls or basal foliage leaves; twigs angular and remaining so for at least two flushes, 2.5-3 mm diam.; epidermis black; terminal buds slender, ca. 5 X 2 mm; cataphylls caducous; indument puberulous, caducous after one flush, the hairs dense, to 0.1 mm long, straight, appressed, reddish. Leaves: petioles slender, 1-2 cm X 1-1.5 mm, terete; blades chartaceous, flat, elliptic, (6-)9-18 X 3-6 cm; base acute, 50-80°; apex acute, 50-80°, acuminate for up to 2.5(-3) cm; margin plane; primary vein above slightly impressed, below prominent; secondary veins 3-4(-5) pairs, equidistant, brochidodromous, those towards apex occasionally forked, above flat, below slightly raised, diverging at 40-60°, arching near base, chordal angle 2030°, the angle uniform along blade length; tertiary veins above and below slightly raised, random-reticulate to scalariform; higher-order veins above and below slightly raised; surface above dark shiny brown, below light dull brown; indument above absent, below puberulous, the hairs sparse, to 0.3 mm long, straight, erect, yellowish, persisting for at least two flushes. Staminate plant unknown. Pistillate inflorescence: acrotonic, erect (curved upwards), peduncles 4-8 cm long, the hypopodia 2-4 cm X 1-1.5 mm, branch orders 3, the second-order branches 5-6, dispersed, lowest branch to 2 cm long, all axes blackish, sparsely puberulous, the hairs reddish; bracts and bracteoles caducous (not seen). Pistillate flowers: pedicels ca. 2 x 0.1 mm, the diameter gradually increasing apically; receptacle obconical, ca. 2 X 2 mm; tepals coriaceous, ovate, ca. 1 x 1 mm, at anthesis erect to spreading, black, adaxially patchy puberulous; staminodes of whorls I and II spathulate, the anthers reniform, ca. 0.3 X 0.3 mm, glabrous, the locelli 4, apical, in a shallow arch, introrse (outer two often latrorse), the glands absent; whorl III capitate, ca. 0.3 X 0.4 mm, glabrous, the locelli 4, the upper pair latrorse, the lower pair extrorse, the glands forming a continuous segmented ring; whorl IV absent; all stamens blackish; pistil ca. 1.5 X 0.5 mm; ovary globose, ca. 0.8 mm long, glabrous. Fruits: pedicels to 20 X 3 mm, abruptly enlarging to form the cupule; cupule spreading to 15 mm diam., smooth, the margin undulate; berry elliptic, to 30 X 20 mm.

description: Slender tree or treelet, (3)9-20 m tall (ca. 50 m fide Bentham), unbranched or with few ascending, sympodial branches on distal portion. Trunk to 20 cm in diam; bark brown, with numerous black, protruding lenticels; inner bark orangish. Distal portion of stem sulcate, glabrous, lenticellate. Leaves paripinnate, spirally arranged on distal portion of stem(s); distal process minute, truncate at apex; leaflets 8-16 (20), opposite or alternate, elliptic, oblong or less often oblanceolate, coriaceous, (6.5)11.5-30 (54) × (2.3) 3-8.5 (14) cm, glabrous, the adaxial surface with prominent midvein, the abaxial surface with scurfy-like punctations, with prominent midvein and secondary veins, tertiary veins reticulate, the apex acute to acuminate or less often rounded, the base inequilateral, one side obtuse the other acute or attenuate; petiolules 0.5-1 × 0.2-0.7 cm long, conical, pulvinate; rachis (19) 25-45(60) cm long, glabrous, triangular at base, trullate and sharply angled towards apex; petioles 30-45 cm long, sharply trigonous, striate, gradually swollen toward base. Thyrses panicle-shaped, terminal or axillary on distal part of branches, 19-50 cm long, lateral branches to 17 cm long; cataphylls acicular to subulate, persistent, 1-2 cm long; axes puberulent, obtusely angled, sulcate; bracts deltate, ca. 1 mm long; dichasia compound, sessile; pedicels 1-2 mm long, tomentose, articulate on distal portion. Calyx yellowish green, 1.2-2.5 mm long, pubescent to tomentulose, the sepals 0.5-1 mm long, oblong or ovate, concave; petals white, 2.5-4.5 mm long, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, appressed-puberulent or pubescent on the lower half of the abaxial surface, sometimes completely pubescent, glabrous adaxially, ciliate at margins, rounded at apex, clawed at base; appendage as long as the petals, long-triangular, hirsute on the distal half of the adaxial surface, glabrous abaxially, the base cuneate to clawed; disc annular, tomentose; stamens 5, the anthers lanceolate, apiculate, glabrous, 1.2 mm long, the filaments pilose or glabrous, white, of equal length; ovary densely appressed- and grayish tomentose, the style elongate with an elongated, trilobate, papillate, pinkish stigma. Fruit usually 1-3-locular, orange-yellow at maturity, trigonous-ellipsoid, 2-2.5 cm long, puberulent, the pericarp coriaceous, ca. 2 mm thick, granulose, the endocarp usually scattered pilose. Seeds ellipsoid, 1 or 2 per fruit; cotyledons superimposed, the upper cotyledon larger than the lower one.
bibliographicCitation: Acevedo-Rodríguez, Pedro. 2003. Meliococceae (Sapindaceae): Melicoccus: and Talisia. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 87: 1-178.

description: Tree 12-14 m tall, with stout lateral branches on upper one-third of trunk; trunk reaching 25 cm in diam.; buttressed at base; bark brown or reddish brown, rough, thin, peeling off in irregular plates; inner bark reddish brown. Branches terete, puberulent, becoming lenticellate. Leaves paripinnate; distal process acicular, ca. 3 mm long, tardily deciduous leaving a truncate base ca. 0.6 mm long; leaflets 4 or 6, opposite or alternate, ovate, widely oblong, elliptic, or widely elliptic, chartaceous, 4-14.5 × 1.8-6.6 cm, adaxially glabrous or sometimes the midvein ferruginous, appressed-pubescent, abaxially glabrous to densely puberulent, very often with midvein and secondaries ferruginous-hirsutulous, the venation brochidodromus, tertiary veins reticulate, the apex long-acuminate to caudate, the base obtuse, acute, to nearly rounded, sometimes slightly inequilateral; petiolules cylindrical, 2-5 mm long, glabrous, puberulent or pubescent, less often with scattered ferruginous erect hairs; rachis 1.2-5.4 cm long, terete or nearly so, with same indumentum as the petiolules; petioles 2-11 cm long, adaxially slightly flattened, with same indumentum as the rachis, slightly enlarged at base. Thyrses racemiform, solitary and supra-axillary or terminal and congested, 4-8 cm long; cataphylls clustered, acicular, 1.5-2 mm long; axes sulcate, puberulent, sometimes with glandular papillae; bracts and bracteoles deltate or subulate, < 0.6 mm long; dichasia simple or the flowers solitary (due to aborted lateral flowers), especially toward distal portion of inflorescence; peduncle slightly flattened, 1-2 mm long, with same indumentum as the axes; pedicels 0.5-1 mm long, articulate at base. Calyx pale green, 2-2.5 mm long, puberulent, margins ciliate, the sepals unequal, free to the base or nearly so, oblong to ovate; petals white, rhombate, 2-2.5 mm long, glabrous, the margins ciliate, extended, inrolled (appendage-like) at base, the apex obtuse, the base cuneate; appendages wanting; disc annular, unlobed or slightly lobed, glabrous, ca. 0.5 mm tall; stamens 8, spreading, the filaments of unequal length, 2-3 mm long, sparsely woolly-pubescent to nearly glabrous, the anthers wide-elliptic, ca. 0.5 mm long, shortly apiculate or nearly retuse; ovary conical, glabrous, the stigma trilobed, sometimes sparsely pubescent. Fruit ellipsoid, apiculate, 1.8-2 cm long, glabrous, the pericarp coriaceous, granulose, ca. 0.7 mm thick; endocarp glabrous. Seed 1(2) per fruit, ellipsoid, with a thin fleshy testa. Embryo with cotyledons of similar size, lying transversely over each other. Melicoccus pedicellaris is easily distinguished by its cylindrical, elongated petiolules. The specific epithet seems to refer to the conspicuous pedicels.

description: Slender tree or treelet, 1.5-7 m tall, unbranched or with few ascending, sympodial branches on distal portion. Trunk 2.5-8 cm in diam. Distal portions of stem nearly terete, smooth, puberulent. Leaves imparipinnate, spirally arranged on distal portions of stem(s); distal process early deciduous leaving a truncate patch at apex; leaflets 3-15 alternate or opposite, elliptic or oblong, chartaceous, 12-35.5 × 6-13 cm, glabrous, the adaxial surface with prominulous midvein and sunken secondary veins to produce a weakly bullate lamina, the abaxial surface with prominent midvein, secondary and tertiary veins, tertiary veins reticulate, the apex acuminate, the base inequilateral, one side rounded the other obtuse; petiolules to 8 mm long, pulvinate (conical), drying dark brown; rachis 20-75 cm long, glabrous, triangular at base, trullate and sharply angled towards apex; petioles 17-35 cm long, sharply triangular, striate, gradually swollen toward base. Thyrses panicle-shaped, terminal or axillary on distal part of branches, or less often cauliflorous, 11-30 cm long; cataphylls acicular, minute; axes puberulent to nearly glabrous, obtusely to sharply angled, sulcate; bracts and bracteoles deltate, 0.5-1 mm long, tomentulose; dichasia compound, sessile; pedicels 1.5-2 mm long, tomentulose, articulate above the middle. Calyx cream-colored, 1.5-2.7 mm long, pubescent, the sepals 1-1.5 mm long, ovate, concave; petals white, 3.5-5 mm long, lanceolate, abaxially appressed-pubescent, adaxially papillate, obtuse at apex, cuneate at base; appendage slightly shorter than the petals, triangular, adaxially sericeous, abaxially glabrous or papillate; disc annular, tomentose; stamens 8, the anthers lanceolate, apiculate at apex, glabrous, 1-1.3 mm long, the filaments glabrous, of equal or slightly unequal lengths, 1.2-1.4 mm long; ovary ferruginous-sericeous, the stigma elongated, capitate, papillate. Fruit 1-locular, orange-yellow at maturity, ellipsoid, glabrescent, granulate, 2-2.5 cm long, the pericarp coriaceous, ca. 1 mm thick, the endocarp usually glabrous. Seeds ellipsoid, 1 or 2 per fruit. Embryo with cotyledons superimposed, the upper cotyledon larger than the lower one.

description: Lianas, glabras; ramos novos subcilíndricos, lisos ou esparso lenticelados, secos avermelhados, velhos cilíndricos, esparso lenticelados, marrons. Folhas opostas ou subopostas, raro algumas alternas; estípulas triangulares, esparso denticuladas; pecíolos (3-)4-7 (-10) mm, secos marrons ou amarelo acinzentados; lâminas (3.4-)6.7-11.6(-16.5) × (1.3-)2.6-4.8(-7) cm, elípticas, base cuneada, margem inteira, ápice acuminado, agudo, ou longo-acuminado, cartáceas, secas marrom-escuras em ambas as faces ou marrom ferrugíneo na adaxial, minutamente pontuado-glandulares na face abaxial, nervuras secas de cor inconspícua em ambas as faces ou amarelo acinzentadas, secundárias e terciárias promínulas a planas em ambas as faces. Inflorescências 1.1-2.4(-4.8) × 1.5-2.5(-4.1) cm, tirsóide-paniculadas, 48-56 flores, axilares, às vezes em ramos laterais curtos sem folhas; pedúnculos 0(-5) mm, ramos cilíndricos, opostos, secos levemente pruinosos, esverdeados, brácteas erosas; pedicelos (1.2-) 3.6 mm; bractéolas 2. Flores 4-4.1 mm diâm na antese, rotáceas; sépalas (0.5-)0.7-1.1(-1.6) × (0.5-)0.7 (-0.9) mm, triangulares, escariosas, inteiras, mais ou menos carnosas, secas com pontuações marrons translúcidas; pétalas (1-)1.4-1.7 × (0.5-)0.6-0.8(-0.9) mm, elípticas, deflexas, escariosas, inteiras, carnosas, brancas a esverdeadas, secas com pontuações marrons translúcidas; disco 0.25-0.45 mm alt., inteiro, sinuado ou não, ápice reflexo; estames 0.7-1.1 mm, filetes 0.55-1 mm, anteras 0.1-0.2 × 0.2 -0.3 mm, oblongas, deiscência por fendas oblíquas em ângulo de ca 120°, conectivo inconspícuo, não proeminente acima das tecas; ovário 0.6-0.7 mm diâm, hemisférico, mais ou menos 3-lobado, com 1 óvulo por lóculo, estilete 0.25-0.4 mm, estigma pontual. Bagas (1.5-)1.6-2.3(-3.3) × 1.1-1.7(-1.8) cm, elipsóides ou subpiriforme, secas marrons pontuadas de amarelo, lisas, maduras amarelas, laranja a vermelhas, às vezes pontuadas de branco. Sementes 1.7 × 1.1 cm.

description: Trees: branching unknown; twigs terete, ca. 6 mm diam.; epidermis brownish, barely visible due to indument cover; terminal bud plump, ca. 6 X 4 mm; cataphylls caducous; indument velutinous, persisting for at least two flushes, the hairs dense, to 1 mm long, straight to curved, erect, yellowish. Leaves: petioles robust, 1-1.5 cm X 3-4.5 mm, adaxially flattened; blades coriaceous, flat, elliptic, 10-21 X 5-8 cm; base obtuse to rounded, 80-110°; apex obtuse, 70100°; margin recurved at base; primary vein above slightly raised, below prominent; secondary veins 7-10 pairs, equidistant, weakly brochidodromous, above flat, below raised, diverging at 65-70°, evenly arching (forked), chordal angle 45°, the angle uniform along blade length; tertiary veins above flat to slightly impressed, below slightly raised, random-reticulate; higher-order veins above inconspicuous, below slightly raised; surface above greenish to reddish brown, below reddish brown; indument above puberulous, the veins tomentose, caducous by next flush, below velutinous, the hairs dense, to 1 mm long, straight to curved, erect, golden to reddish brown, denser on the veins, persisting for at least two flushes. Staminate inflorescences: basitonic, pendulous, peduncles 5-11 cm long, the hypopodia 3.5-6 cm X ca. 2.5 mm, branch orders 3(-4), the second-order branches 4, dispersed, lowest branch to 2 cm long, color and indument of all axes as on twigs, epidermis drying black; bracts and bracteoles caducous (not seen). Staminate flowers: pedicels ca. 6 X 1 mm, the diameter gradually increasing apically; receptacle ob-conical, ca. 1.5 X 4.5 mm; tepals coriaceous, obovate, ca. 2.8 X 3 mm, at anthesis erect to spreading?, black, adaxially puberulous to tomentose; stamens of whorls I and II, the anthers sessile, chubby trapezoid to ovate, ca. 1.2 X 1 mm, glabrous, the locelli 4, apical, in a shallow arch, introrse, the glands absent; whorl III columnar, ca. 1.2 X 0.8 mm, glabrous, the anthers trapezoid, the locelli 4, the upper pair latrorse, the lower pair extrorse, the glands absent (? or fused in a ring); whorl IV absent; all stamens reddish black; pistillode absent. Pistillate flowers and fruits unknown.

description: Shrub or small tree 2-5(-10) m tall. Branches moderately glandular-puberulent when young, glabrescent when older. Leaf blades simple, unlobed, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, acute to acuminate at apex, glabrate to sparsely puberulent or pubescent adaxially, moderately to densely puberulent or pubescent abaxially; petioles glabrous to moderately puberulent, often with stalked glands. Trunk leaves not represented. Crown leaves 3-4 per sympodial unit, simple, unlobed, the blade elliptic or oblong to ovate, 5-23 cm long, 3-11.5 cm wide, length: width ratio (1-) 1.5-2.5(-3): 1, the base cuneate, truncate, or rounded to subcordate with basal lobes less than 1 cm long; petioles 1-4 cm long. Inflorescence unbranched, 15-40(-100)-flowered, 3.5-15(-47) cm long; peduncle 1.5-3.5(-6) cm long; rachis 1.5-10.5(-44) cm long; pedicels 15-25 mm long, 20-35 mm long in fruit, 1-3(-10) mm apart, articulated at or near the base, leaving pedicellar remnants up to 1 mm long; peduncle, rachis, and pedicels glabrate to moderately glandular-puberulent. Flower buds ovoid to ellipsoidal, acute or obtuse at apex. Calyx fleshy or subcoriaceous, moderately glandular-puberulent, the radius 2-3 mm, the lobes 0.5-1.5 mm long, 1.5-2 mm wide, deltate, apiculate. Corolla green, white, pink, or purplish, chartaceous to membranaceous, stellate, the radius 9-16 mm, the tube 1-2 mm long, the lobes narrowly triangular, 8-15 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, glabrate to sparsely puberulent(-pubes-cent) abaxially, moderately tomentose to ciliate adaxially, the margin tomentose to ciliate, the apex acute. Anther thecae purplish, lanceolate, 5-6 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, the pores directed distally; connective purple, lanceolate, 5-6 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide at base, abaxially nearly equal to thecae at apex, slightly exceeding them at base by 0.5-1 mm, adaxially present as a linear swelling near base of thecae. Ovary glabrous or glandular-puberulent; style cylindrical, glabrous, not to very slightly dilated distally, 5-8 mm long, 0.5-1 mm in diam., exserted 1-2 mm beyond stamens; stigma truncate, 0.5-1 mm in diam. Fruits ellipsoidal to fusiform, acute at apex, 3-7 cm long, 1.5-3 cm in diam., sparsely to moderately puberulent when young, glabrescent when older, light green with darker green stripes when immature, yellow when ripe; mesocarp with stone cell aggregates; seeds 3.5-5 mm long, 3-4 mm wide, rugose.

description: Monoecious tree, 8-30 m tall, to at least 28 cm in dbh; young branchlets terete, glabrescent. Leaves opposite, rarely temate; petioles 1.5-3 cm long; lamina drying stiff-chartaceous and dark brown, elliptic, 1020 X 6-10 cm, the base acute to obtuse, the apex acuminate, glabrous, with 6-9 pairs of secondary veins, smooth or very slightly raised above and below, the margin entire. Cymes to 1.5 cm long, sparsely covered with minute appressed stellate hairs, with 9-12 flowers in the axils of early caducous 6-12 mm long bracts, the pedicels ca. 1 mm long. Fresh flowers greenish; male flowers obconical or urceolate (Fig. 7B), 1.5-2.5 mm in diam., 2.5-4 mm high, the indumentum as on the cymes, tepals and roof reduced to a thin rim; stamens 2-6, thick-fleshy (Figs. 7B right, 7C), with four outer ones and two central ones; female flowers ovoid, 3-3.5 mm in diam., 3.5-4.5 mm high, the tepals minute, triangular with apical hydathodes, the floral roof conical, thick; styles hardly protruding from the floral roof (Fig. 7B), usually 2-3 visible (the carpels more numerous). Fruiting receptacles globose, when fresh yellow and with a sweet pulp, drying black and shiny (Fig. 13B), not splitting open at maturity, dry 3.5-4 cm in diam. (fresh to 6 cm in diam. [Lima & Saraiva 272]), the drupelets 1.4-1.6 X 1-1.1 cm large, exo- and mesocarp fleshy and becoming slimy, the endocarp stony (ca. 1 mm thick) and with a thick layer of stiff brownish bristles (Fig. 13-I.D).

description: Plants predominantly epiphytic, growing in moss layers, rarely terrestrial. Rhizomes horizontal, moderately to short-creeping, 0.8-1.0 mm diam., rarely branched, branches short (less than 10 mm long). Fronds to 26 cm long, usually pendent, in terrestrial plants ascending, inserted onto the rhizomes at right angles, moderately spaced to closely arranged (internodes 2-5 mm), not caespitose. Rhizome scales 3.0 x 0.6 mm, (12—>14—16(—18) cells wide across bases, clathrate, dark brown to brown, strongly iridescent, broadly cordate to pseudopeltate at bases, acute to attenuate at tips, apical cells 2-5, bifurcate or furcately arranged. Petioles 25-50(-70) mm long, 0.6-0.8 mm thick, marginate near the laminar bases, otherwise terete, glabrous to glabrescent, without setiform/ciliform hairs, with a few to many, simple and branched, clavate hairs 0.3 mm long on crosiers and young fronds, usually persistent on older fronds. Laminae 50-205 x 6-45 mm, linear to narrowly elliptic (broadest in the middle), cuneate to long-decurrent at bases, long-acute to caudate at tips, abaxially white. Rachises dark brown to black, planar and slightly sunken between segments adaxially, hemispherically protruding abaxially, with many, ephemeral, branched, clavate hairs abaxially. Largest segments 5.0-13.0(-20.0) x 1.2—1.5(—2.0) mm (ca. 4-7 times longer than broad), segments weakly to rarely strongly ascending (30-60°), linear-oblong to long-deltate, bases equilateral or weakly basiscopically decurrent, fully adnate, tips obtuse to acute; midveins hidden or protruding in dried specimens; proximal 3—5 segment pairs markedly smaller than the subsequent segments, lowermost segments usually auriculiform. Sori (2)3-10 pairs per segment, without hairs.

description: Semi or briefly deciduous shrub or tree 3.5-40 m, with (especially when juvenile) or without spines on branches. Leaves subcoriaceous, 2-11 × 1-6 7 cm broadly to narrowly obovate, sometimes elliptic or oblanceolate, subacute or obtuse to rounded to retuse at apex, cuneate or broadly so at base, sometimes slightly revolute at margin, glabrous adaxially, sparsely pubescent except more pubescent on midvein but be coming subglabrous abaxially; domatia absent. Venation brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent or scarcely so; secondary veins (3-)4-8(-11) pairs moderately spaced, originating at moderately or sometimes narrowly acute angles, sometimes decurrent on to midvein, curved or slightly curved, usually scarcely prominent; intersecondary veins common-tertiary veins randomly reticulate; higher order veins usually not distinct; areolation incomplete, not or scarcely prominent. Petiole 0.2-1.2 cm, pubescent, becoming subglabrous, biglandular. Inflorescences (2.5-)4-19 cm, simple, usually elongate but rarely subcapitate, with many crowded flowers all bisexual; peduncle 1.5-9 cm, pubescent; rhachis (l-)2.5-10 cm, pubescent; bracts ca. 1 mm, ovate-triangular, densely pubescent abaxially. Flowers pentamerous, 3-5 × 3-4 mm; lower hypanthium 1-2 mm, tomentose to appressed-pubescent; upper hypanthium 1-2 mm, widely cupuliform, subglabrous to tomentose; calyx lobes 0.2-0.7 mm, suberect, subglabrous to tomentose; disk pilose; stamens 3-5 mm; style 2.5-5 mm, pilose proximally, sometimes nearly to apex. Fruits many along whole length of rhachis, 0.4-0.7 × 0.2-0.45 cm (excl. upper hypanthium), terete, ovate or narrowly ovate (often asymmetrically curved) in side view, woody and achene-like. abruptly or gradually narrowed to beak 0.02-0.2 cm at apex, rounded at base, densely to sparsely pubescent, the upper hypanthium persistent on the beak. Reproductive biology. Flowers white, cream-colored, or yellow, strongly protogynous, strongly fragrant. The outer whorl of stamens ripens (and often anthers fall) before the inner whorl extends and dehisces. Flowering and fruiting throughout most of year.

description: Arbusto o bejuco hasta de 3 m, lenticelas presentes, verrucosas, elípticas. Hojas trifolioladas; pulvínulo cilindrico, rugoso o raramente Asurado, glabro, 0.2-0.7 cm de largo; pecíolo cilindrico, levemente estriado, glabro, 2-13.5(-21) cm de largo; raquis cilindrico, liso o levemente estriado, glabro, 0.5-3(-4) cm de largo. Folíolos (4.5-)5-20(-27) cm de largo, 2-8(-10) cm de ancho, elípticos, ovado elípticos o angosto-elípticos, cartáceos, algo brillantes u opacos, glabros o algo pubérulos sobre la nervadura central en la haz, envés opaco, oscuro, glabro o pubérulo a lo largo de la nervadura central, base redondeada, levemente cordada o subpeltada, ápice acuminado (acumen 1-1,5(-2) cm de largo), margen entero o levemente revoluto; peciólulo cilindrico, 0.3-0.7 cm de largo; venación más o menos transversal en la mitad inferior del folíolo, el resto reticulada, nervadura central prominente en el envés, plana o impresa en la haz; nervaduras laterales 5-7(-9) pares, formando ángulos de 70° con la nervadura central, más o menos claramente anastomosados cerca al margen, promínulas en el envés, planas en la haz; nervaduras terciarias levemente promínulas en el envés, planas o impresas en la haz. Inflorescencias paniculadas, axilares o pseudoterminales; raquila hasta 25 cm de largo, pubérula o vellosa, pubescencia ferrugínea. Pedicelo pubérulo o velloso, pubescencia marrón, 0.2-0.5 cm de largo; sépalos 2.2-3.5 mm de largo, ca. 1.2 mm de ancho, angosto elípticos, con puntuaciones más o menos conspicuas, numerosas, pubérulos o vellosos exteriormente, glabros o pubérulos en el margen y en la mitad superior interiormente, ápice agudo; pétalos (3.7-)4-5 mm de largo, 1.1-1.4 mm de ancho, angosto-elípticos, connados en su parte media, con numerosas puntuaciones inconspicuas, glabros; filamentos unidos por 0.4-0.5 mm de su longitud, 5 más largos 2.5-4 mm de longitud, 5 más cortos 2.1-3.5 mm de longitud, con pelos glandulosos o raramente glabros; anteras globosas, 0.3-0.4 mm de diámetro; ovario y estilo tomentosos o vellosos. Fruto estipitado, estípite 0.2 cm de largo, el fruto 2 cm de largo, 1.2 cm de ancho, glabro, cáliz presente en el fruto. Semilla 1.4 cm de largo, 0.7 cm de ancho, ariloide 0.4 cm de largo.

description: Liana, lenticelas presentes, inconspicuas, ramas jóvenes glabras. Hojas trifolioladas, pulvínulo glabro, pecíolo cilindrico, estriado, glabro, 3-7.5 cm de largo; raquis cilindrico, rugoso, glabro, 0.8-1.5 cm de largo. Foliolos (3-)8-15 cm de largo, (2-)3.5-7 cm de ancho, elípticos, cartáceos, haz oscura, algo brillante, glabra, envés claro, opaco, papiloso, glabro, base angostada o cuneada, ápice suavemente acuminado, acumen hasta 1.5 cm de largo, margen entero; peciólulo cilindrico, glabro, hasta 0.8 cm de largo; venación transversal, más pálida que la superficie de la haz, con 3 venas principales naciendo desde la base pero separándose a 0.5 cm de ésta, nervadura central prominente en el envés, plana en la haz; nervaduras laterales 2-3 pares, formando ángulos de 45° con la nervadura central, no anastomosadas pero con ramificaciones que terminan en el margen, promínulas en el envés, planas en la haz; nervaduras terciarias levemente promínulas en el envés, planas en la haz. Inflorescencias paniculadas agrupadas en las axilas, densifloras; raquila hasta 4 cm de largo, pubérula; brácteas pequeñas. Pedicelo delgado, glabrescente, 4-5 mm de largo; sépalos 2.5 mm de largo, 0.7 mm de ancho, oblongos(subrectangulares), esparcidamente pubérulos o glabrescentes exterior-mente, glabros interiormente, ápice barbado, obtuso, margen ciliado; pétalos 4 mm de largo, 1.2 mm de ancho, oblongos(subrectangulares), glabros; filamentos 10, 5 más largos ca. 3 mm de longitud, 5 más cortos 2 mm de longitud, glabros; anteras globosas, 0.3 mm de diámetro; ovario con 5 carpelos pubérulos, sésiles, estilo glabro, estigma capitado. Fruto desconocido.

description: Liana, lenticelas presentes, ramas jóvenes densamente rufo-tomentosas. Hojas trifolioladas, pulvínulo cilindrico, rugoso, tomentoso, hasta 0.8 cm de largo; pecíolo cilindrico, grueso, estriado, tomentoso, 4.5-16 cm de largo; raquis cilindrico, tomentoso, 0.2-1(-1.5) cm de largo. Folíolos (5-)8-17 cm de largo, (2.5-)4.5-12 cm de ancho, suborbiculares a subromboideos, cartáceos, haz oscura, brillante, pubérula en las venas, envés opaco, claro, marrón tomentoso, densamente papiloso, base redondeada, levemente cordada o algo cuneada en el foliolo terminal, algo irregular en los laterales, ápice cortamente acuminado, margen entero o levemente revoluto; peciólulo cilindrico, rugoso, tomentoso, hasta 0.7 cm de largo; venación transversal, nervadura central prominente en el envés, impresa en la haz; nervaduras laterales 2 que nacen en la base y 5 pares más, formando ángulos de 45° con la nervadura central, no anastomosadas en el margen, prominentes en el envés, impresas o planas en la haz; nervaduras terciarias promínulas en el envés, planas en la haz. Inflorescencia en panícula, axilar o pseudoterminal; raquila hasta de 22 cm de largo, densamente tomentosa, marrón; brácteas conspicuas. Pedicelo pubérulo, 0.3-0.5 mm de largo; sépalos ca. 2-2.3 mm de largo, ca. 1-1.2 mm de ancho, ovados, pubérulos exteriormente, glabros interiormente, ápice agudo, barbado, margen ciliado; pétalos ca. 2.5-3 mm de largo, ca. 1 mm de ancho, oblongo-elípticos, glabros; filamentos libres, 5 más largos 1.5—2.5 mm de longitud, 5 más cortos 1.2-2 mm de longitud, glabros; anteras globosas, 0.3 mm de diámetro; ovario con 5 carpelos vellosos, sésiles, estilo parcialmente velloso, estigma capitado. Fruto maduro desconocido, inmaduros varios carpelos en cada flor, glabros, hasta de 0.9 cm de longitud.
