description: Shrubs or mostly small trees, rarely up to 20 m tall. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 2.25 mm in diam., longitudinally furrowed and often distinctly irregularly angular, the younger parts with a yellowish to reddish-brown indument of mostly both very short hairs and longer (0.20.7 mm), erect hairs, in flowering collections the short hairs ± dense and subpersistent, the longer hairs becoming sparser with age, in postfloral and fruiting collections the short hairs (almost) absent; terminal buds ± elongate-ovate, 4.3-9 mm long, 1.5-3.3 mm thick, densely covered with appressed to ascending, yellowish to reddish hairs. Petioles 5-16 mm long, (1.6-)2-3 mm thick, in young leaves often flattened, irregularly roundish below, often longitudinally furrowed, usually canaliculate with ridges along the central furrow above, indument as on twigs. Leaves alternate, mostly ± oblanceolate but varying towards obovate, elliptic, oblong or lanceolate, widest at or mostly slightly above the middle (up to 2/3 from the base), 9-27 cm long, 4-11.5 cm wide, (2.1-)2.4-3.6(-4) times longer than wide, tip acuminate (acumen often short but always distinct), basal part of the leaf broadly acute to narrowly cuneate, the base itself abruptly obtuse to truncate, margin flat to narrowly bent down, midrib above convex in a slight impression, very prominent below, secondary veins slightly impressed above, prominent below, the distal ones often loop-connected, 9-14 pairs, diverging at 40-60(-75)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 30-55° to the midrib, tertiary venation usually scalariform, rarely percurrent or with some laterally oriented intersecondaries, usually ± level above, often scarcely visible, raised below. Indument (in leaves developed at anthesis, see below) consisting of pale yellowish, strongly curled, short hairs on the entire surface and more erect, reddish hairs on midrib and largest veins above, the former initially very dense but often quickly wearing off, consisting of short, appressed hairs and longer, ascending to erect, straight to curled, reddish hairs below, mainly on veins, not uncommonly crowded in the axils of secondary veins, in young leaves sparse to moderately dense, but always less dense than above, in mature leaves the short hairs becoming very sparse, the longer ones often lost completely. Gland dots present but often rather inconspicuous. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves, 1.1-1.8(-2.5) mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.8-5 mm diam., (3-)5-13 cm long, reaching ca. 1/4 to 2/3 the length of the subtending leaf (mostly ca. 1/2); peduncle (1.8-)2.5-6.5 cm long, i.e., 3/5 to 2/3 the length of the inflorescence (usually slightly more than 1/2), lateral branches (0-)2-4 below terminal cluster of cymes, branched (l-)2-4 times, indument dense, consisting of both short and longer, ± erect, yellowish to slightly reddish hairs. Pedicels very short or up to 3.5 mm long, 0.4-1 mm thick. Flowers 7.5-11 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic to elongate-obovate, 3.2-4 mm long and 2-2.8 mm wide, papillosity dense and (moderately) thick on the inside surface, often relatively long. Stamens ca. 1.3-1.7 mm long, subsessile or filament reaching up to 1/4 the length of the anther, anthers heavily papillose, in the two outer whorls long ovate to trullate, longer than wide, the sterile tip acute to parabolic, in the third whorl anthers roundish-rectangular or ob-trapeziform, the tip obtuse to truncate. Staminodes thick, distinctly united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 2.2-2.5 mm long, ovary relatively small, ± ellipsoid, glabrous, style as long as the ovary or slightly longer, papillose or glabrous. Receptacle spheroidal (upper part formed by united bases of stamens and staminodes), glabrous inside. Only immature fruit known, berry elongate-ellipsoid, ca. 15 mm long, and ca. 7 mm in diam., cupule cup-shaped, at this stage ca. 5 mm high and 8 mm in diam., pedicel very slightly thickened.
bibliographicCitation: Rohwer, Jens G. 1993. Lauraceae: Nectandra. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 60: 1-332.

description: Shrubs or trees to 15 m (very tall fide Martius). Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud ca. 1.7-3 mm in diam., initially somewhat irregularly angular but quickly becoming roundish, indument consisting of extremely short, papillae-like hairs, and slightly longer (ca. 0.2 mm), ± ascending hairs, usually moderately dense to dense below terminal bud, usually slowly becoming sparser, rarely quickly subglabrescent; terminal buds depressed ovoid to elongate, ca. 1.5-3.5 mm long and 1.3-2.5 mm thick, densely covered with ± short, ± appressed, brownish hairs. Petioles 7-15 mm long, 0.8-2 mm thick, ± roundish below, broadly canaliculate to almost flat or irregularly ridged above, indument ± as on twigs, glabrescent. Leaves alternate, elliptic to lanceolate, widest ± at the middle (more frequently above than below), 9.5-20 cm long, 3.58 cm wide, 2.1-4.4 times longer than wide, tip with a usually short but distinct acumen, base attenuate to obtuse, margin flat or nearly so (only in Schunke 1661 narrowly revolute), midrib flat to convex above, level or in a slight impression, prominent below, secondary veins level to slightly impressed above, prominent below, 7-11 pairs, diverging at 30-55°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-45° to the midrib, tertiary venation predominantly scalariform (to percurrent), often inconspicuous, level to very slightly impressed above, slightly raised below. Indument consisting of short (up to 0.2 mm), ± appressed hairs, even in young leaves very sparse to absent above, sometimes slightly denser on midrib and largest veins, scarcely visible below on a surface which at 25x appears like plastic foam due to a papillose epidermis (Fig. 4C, D), axils of the lower secondary veins as a rule with small tufts of ± short, erect, brownish hairs. Gland dots indistinct to invisible above. Inflorescences in the axils of younger foliage leaves, sometimes also in the axils of cataphylls on new growth below the terminal bud, rarely (pseudo?)terminal, 0.82 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-3.2 mm diam., 3.5-13 cm long, reaching ca. 1/3 to ca. the length of the closest foliage leaves; peduncle 1-5 cm long, i.e., less than 1/10 to almost half the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches (4-)6-14 below the terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, branched 1-3 times, the lower branchlets often not entirely cymose, indument on peduncle ± like that on twigs but often more erect, sparse to moderately dense, becoming still denser closer to the flowers. Pedicels 1.2-4 mm long, 0.3-0.4 mm thick. Flowers 3.5-4.5 mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, 1.3-2.1 mm long and 0.8-1.4 mm wide, covered with fine, short papillae on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 0.7-1 mm long including a distinct filament of ca. 0.20.4 mm, anthers minutely papillose, in the two outer whorls ± suborbicular to rounded-squarish, broadly rounded to almost truncate at the tip, rarely obtuse, in the third whorl roundish-rectangular, broadly obtuse to truncate at the tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3-3/5 the length of the stamens, triangular to slightly clavate, minutely papillose, united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 1.7-2 mm long, ovary ellipsoid to subglobose, glabrous, style almost as long as the ovary, mostly with very fine papillae or with a few very short hairs, rarely glabrous. Receptacle cup-shaped to narrowly parabolic but almost closed above by the bases of stamens and staminodes, glabrous or with some tightly appressed hairs inside. Berry ellipsoid, ca. 15 mm long, ca. 10 mm in diam., cupule minutely bowl-shaped, not more than 1 mm high, ca. 4-5 mm in diam. (up to 11 mm in Ruiz & Pavon s.n.), pedicel slightly thickened towards the cupule.

description: Shrubs or trees to 12 m. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.3-2.6 mm in diam., at first ± slightly angular with small longitudinal ridges, quickly becoming roundish, with ± straight, ± short (occasionally up to 0.4 mm long), ± appressed hairs, dense to intermediate below terminal bud, quickly becoming sparser; terminal buds ovoid to elongate, minute or up to ca. 7.5 mm long and 1.7 mm thick, densely covered with ± straight, ± appressed hairs. Petioles 3.5-11 mm long, 0.8-1.8 mm thick, roundish below, canaliculate above, indument ± as on twigs below, initially denser above, glabrescent. Leaves alternate or occasionally some of them opposite, elliptic to lanceolate or oblong, widest ± at the middle, (4.3-)5.5-12(-14) cm long, 1.7-4.5 cm wide, (1.8-)2.3-3.5(-4.3) times longer than wide, tip (mostly short) acuminate, base usually ± acute, rarely attenuate or obtuse, margin flat to very slightly bent down, midrib ± level to slightly impressed above, sometimes slighty convex, prominent below, secondary veins ± level above, slightly raised to almost prominent below, 5-10 pairs, sometimes rather inconspicuous above, diverging at 45-70°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-60° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed, percurrency very indistinct, scarcely more developed than the network of finer veinlets, ± level and often inconspicuous above, raised to almost level below. Indument inconspicuous, consisting of ± short, ± appressed hairs, in young leaves sparse above to absent except for the more pubescent midrib, moderately sparse to subglabrous below, axils of some secondary veins at least in some leaves with ± erect hairs, mature leaves glabrous above or with a few hairs on base of midrib, indument ± persistent or glabrescent below. Gland dots rarely visible, on upper surface of young leaves. Inflorescences most frequently in the axils of cataphylls below terminal and axillary vegetative buds, often also in the axils of foliage leaves (less often exclusively in this position), 0.4-0.8 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of ca. 0.8-2 mm diam., 0.7-8(-l 1) cm long, reaching up to 2/3 the length of the closest foliage leaf, (usually much shorter), branched immediately at the base or with a peduncle of up to 4.5 cm length, i.e., in small inflorescences up to 3/5 their length, lateral branches 0-4(-6) below the terminal cyme or cluster of cymes, unbranched or branched once, occasionally the whole inflorescence reduced to a three-flowered cymule, indument consisting of short, ± appressed hairs, sparse to moderately dense but still leaving most of the epidermis visible. Pedicels 1-3.5(-6.5) mm long, 0.20.5 mm thick. Flowers 3.5-5(-6.5) mm in diam., tepals ± elliptic, 1.3-2(-2.8) mm long and 0.8-1.3(-2) mm wide, papillosity ± fine on the inside surface, distinct but at least on outer tepals not covering the entire surface. Stamens ca. 0.50.7 mm long including the very short filament (but see below), anthers distinctly papillose, in the first whorl ± transverse-elliptic, broadly rounded to almost truncate at the tip, rarely indistinctly obtuse, in the second whorl narrower, usually ± suborbicular, rounded to indistinctly obtuse at the tip, in the third whorl ± obtrapeziform, very broadly obtuse to slightly emarginate at the tip. Staminodes slightly clavate, reaching half to almost the length of the stamens, often slightly glandular at the tip, free. Pistil ca. 0.9-1.3 mm long, glabrous, ovary ellipsoid to broadly pear-shaped, style thick, reaching up to 1/3 the length of the ovary. Receptacle shallow, ± bowlshaped, glabrous or with some tightly appressed hairs inside. Only immature fruit known, berry ellipsoid, ca. 10 mm long and ca. 6.5 mm in diam., cupule ± trumpet-shaped, ca. 2.5 mm high and 5 mm in diam., pedicel increasingly thickened, merging into the cupule.

description: Trees. Branchlets 5 cm below terminal bud 1.9-3.5 mm in diam., ± flattened towards the nodes, with longitudinal ridges and furrows, the youngest part covered with a dense, reddish brown indument of both very short and fewer longer (ca. 0.5 mm), ± erect hairs, first becoming matted and grey on older twigs, then lost; terminal buds ± ovate, 2.5-3.5 mm long, 1.2-2 mm thick, densely covered with relatively long, ascending, reddish-brown hairs. Petioles 3-9 mm long, 1.2-2 mm thick, roundish below, slightly ridged, canaliculate above, usually with two ridges along the central furrow, indument as on twigs. Leaves (sub)opposite, ± orbicular, or some leaves with a tendency towards elliptic or obovate, widest ± at the middle, 2.2-9 cm long, 1.5-6 cm wide, as long as wide or a few leaves up to 1.8 times longer than wide, tip broadly rounded but sometimes with a minute and indistinct acumen, rarely slightly retuse, base rounded or sometimes obtuse, margin thickened, narrowly bent down, at the base narrowly recurved, venation (midrib, secondaries and reticulation) distinctly impressed above and prominent below (i.e., leaves slightly bullate), secondary veins (2-) 3-5 pairs, diverging at 35-50°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 25-40° to the midrib, tertiary venation mixed, predominantly percurrent, finer venation almost equally distinct. Indument consisting of ± curled, reddish hairs above, moderately sparse to moderately dense in youngest leaves, denser on veins, quickly becoming sparse, persistent for some time on veins, finally glabrescent, consisting of short, irregularly appressed, pale hairs in the intercostal area below and long, erect reddish hairs mainly from the veins, the former dense in young leaves and becoming only slightly sparser with age, the latter at first moderately dense to moderately sparse, becoming much sparser, sometimes much denser in the axils of the secondary veins. Gland dots mostly visible on upper surface of younger leaves, but usually not very conspicuous. Inflorescences in the axils of distal leaves on new growth, or occasionally pseudoterminal (the proximal branches sometimes subtended by a pair of frondose bracts which resemble foliage leaves but are smaller and more elongate), 0.8-1.4 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.5-4 mm diam., 0.9-3 cm long, reaching up to ca. half the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle 0.3-1.8 cm long (up to 2.4 cm in frondose inflorescences), i.e., 1/3 to 3/4 the length of the inflorescence, lateral branches 0-2 below terminal cyme, branched once (3-flowered cymes), indument dense, similar to that on twigs but becoming shorter closer to the flowers. Pedicels 1.5-4 mm long, 0.6-1 mm thick. Flowers 5.5-6 mm in diam., tepals elliptic to oblong, 1.7-2.2 mm long and ca. 1.3 mm wide, papillosity short and moderately fine on the inside surface, especially on outer tepals not very dense. Stamens ca. 1 mm long, anthers pentagonal, approximately as wide as long, almost without papillae, the sterile tip broadly obtuse, filament short but distinct Staminodes very small, subulate. Pistil ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous, ovary broadly ellipsoid, style short (ca. 0.5 mm). Receptacle deeply paraboloidal, glabrous inside. Berry elongate, 20-22 mm long, 10-12 mm in diam., cupule funnel-shaped, shallow, 3-4 mm high, 8-9 mm in diam., somewhat irregular, pedicel very slightly thickened.

description: Trees, to 30 m (already flowering when only 5 m tall). Branchlets S cm below terminal bud 1.5-3.7 mm in diam., initially slightly angular or flattened, quickly becoming terete, with at least a few relatively long (ca. 0.3-0.7 mm), straight to slightly curled, ± ascending, copper-colored hairs at the tip, sometimes additionally with short, appressed hairs, immediately below the terminal bud moderately dense or sparser, very quickly (sub)glabrescent; terminal buds elongate, 5-14 mm long, 0.9-2.5 mm thick, at least their apical part densely covered with short, often ± curled, and longer (up to 0.7 mm), ± straight, ± ascending copper-colored hairs. Petioles 818 mm long (often appearing longer due to the revolute leaf base), 0.9-2 mm thick, irregularly roundish below, canaliculate to ± flat above, indument below ± as on twigs, much denser above, consisting mainly of ± short, ± ascending hairs, (subglabrescent Leaves alternate, ± lanceolate, widest ± at the middle or slightly below, (6-) 1221 cm long, (2-)3.5-5.5(-7) cm wide, 2.7-4 (-4.5) times longer than wide, tip tapering towards a long and fine acumen, ± acute to cuneate towards the base, the base itself attenuate due to the revolute margin that runs parallel to the petiole for ca. 5-13 mm (in mature leaves), midrib distinctly convex in an impression above, very prominent below, secondary veins usually both slightly impressed and slightly convex above, prominent below, (4-)6-10 pairs, diverging at 40-60(-70)°, in mid-lamina running at an angle of 20-35(-45)° to the midrib, the distal ones often loop-connected, tertiary venation densely scalariform, ± raised on both sides, rarely ± level above. Indument of two types (see discussion): in the Brazilian material (except Ducke s.n. and Krukoff 8586) consisting of fine and mostly short (rarely up to 0.3 mm), ± curled, pale yellowish hairs above, which initially cover the epidermis completely, plus sometimes some longer hairs on veins, consisting of ± short, appressed to erect hairs below, initially ± moderately sparse on the lamina, and longer (up to 0.5 mm), ± erect, curled hairs mainly on midrib and secondary veins, crowded in their axils; in the Peruvian material (and the collections mentioned above) consisting of short to long (up to 1 mm), ± straight, ± ascending hairs only on midrib and largest veins above, consisting of ± short, ± appressed and/or ± curled hairs below, almost exclusively on and along midrib and secondary veins, sometimes axils of secondary veins bearded with longer (up to ca. 0.5 mm), ± straight hairs, older leaves in both groups glabrescent above (sometimes except for the base of the midrib), intercostal area (subglabrescent below, indument on veins partly persistent Gland dots initially ± distinct on both sides (if not concealed by the indument), in mature leaves less distinct but usually still visible above. Inflorescences in the axils of distal foliage leaves, 0.9-1.7 mm in diam. at the base, on a twig of 1.4-3 mm diam., (4.5-)8-16 cm long, reaching ca. 1/2 to almost the length of the subtending leaf; peduncle (2-)4.5-8 cm long, i.e., 2/5-3/5 the length of the inflorescence, glabrous or mostly with some straight to curled, ± ascending hairs of up to 0.5 mm length, lateral branches (0-)2-6 (-8) below the terminal cyme (rarely with a terminal cluster of cymes), branched 1-4 times, closer to the flowers with an increasingly dense cover of ± short (up to 0.3 mm), ± spreading, greyish to whitish hairs. Pedicels 3-7(-10) mm long, 0.3-0.6 mm thick. Flowers (6.5-)7.5-10 mm in diam., tepals oblong elliptic to elongate obovate, (2.5-)3.5-5 mm long and 1.8-2.5(-3) mm wide, distinctly papillose on the inside surface. Stamens ca. 1.5-2.1 mm long including a filament of 0.1-0.4 mm, anthers papillose, in the two outer whorls elongate-ovate to trullate with a rather long parabolic to acute tip, in the third whorl elongate-elliptic to elongate-pentagonal with a long obtuse to parabolic tip. Staminodes reaching ca. 1/3-1/2 the length of the stamens, terete or slightly club-shaped, papillose, united with the inner stamens at the base. Pistil ca. 2.1-2.5 mm long, ovary ± ellipsoid, glabrous, style ± as long as the ovary, glabrous or with a few scattered papillae. Receptacle cup-shaped to urceolate, closed by the bases of stamens and staminodes above, glabrous or with some appressed hairs inside. Only immature fruit known, cupule bowl-shaped to hemispherical but with six very thick ribs, these at the margin continued into thick obtuse lobes, in the immature fruit curved inwards, overarching the still very small berry.

description: Trees: branches basitonic, in axils of cataphylls; twigs angular, soon becoming terete, ca. 4 mm diam.; epidermis black, barely visible due to indument cover; terminal bud plump, ca. 1 x 2 mm; cataphylls caducous; indument pubescent, caducous after one flush, the hairs dense, to 1 mm long, straight to curved, erect, reddish. Leaves: petioles slender, 1-1.7 cm X 1.4-2.2 mm, terete; blades chartaceous, flat, narrowly ovate to elliptic, 4-12 X 2-4 cm; base acute to obtuse, 60-110°; apex attenuate to acute, 35-90°, ultimately acuminate for up to 1.5 cm; margin plane; primary vein above raised, below prominent; secondary veins 3-6 pairs, equidistant, eucamptodromous, above flat, below prominent, diverging at 50-60°, abruptly arching near margin, chordal angle 15-20°, the angle uniform along blade length; tertiary veins above inconspicuous, below raised, random-reticulate to scalariform; higher-order veins above inconspicuous, below slightly raised; surface above brown in young leaves, shiny olive-green in older leaves, below brown; indument above puberulous, the primary and secondary veins puberulous, caducous by next flush, below tomentose, the hairs dense, to 1 mm long, curved to crisped, erect, reddish brown, denser on the veins, persisting for at least two flushes. Staminate inflorescences: along whole length of flush, erect, peduncles 4-9 cm long, the hypopodia 1-3 cm X 1-2 mm, branch orders 3-4, the second-order branches 47, dispersed, lowest branch to 1.5 cm long, color and indument of all axes as on twigs; bracts and bracteoles caducous (not seen). Staminate flowers: pedicels ca. 6 x 1.6 mm, the diameter even throughout; receptacle flat, ca. 3.5 x 7.2 mm; tepals coriaceous, ovate to obovate, ca. 4 x 3.5 mm, at anthesis erect to spreading, reddish black, adaxially patchy puberulous; stamens of whorls I and II, the anthers sessile, chubby, trapezoid, ca. 1.6 X 1.6 mm, glabrous, the locelli 4, apical, in a shallow arch, introrse, the glands absent; whorl 111 columnar, ca. 2.4 X 1.2 mm, glabrous, the locelli 4, the upper pair latrorse, the lower pair extrorse, the glands globular, ca. 1 mm diam.; whorl IV absent; all stamens reddish; pistillode absent. Pistillate flowers and fruits unknown.

description: Treelet ca. 2 m tall. Branchlets orange-brown to purplish when dried, provided with small whitish callose lenticels, ferruginous hispid and hispidulous. Leaves apparently opposite or ternate at the apex of the branchlets, alternate near the base; petioles 1.5-10 mm long, ferruginous hispid(ulous) above, ferruginous strigose beneath; stipules deciduous, narrowly ovate, gradually acuminate, 2.25-5 x 0.75-1.5 mm, herbaceous, sometimes ferruginous hispid along the costa, margin scarious and ferruginous ciliolate; lamina obovate, acuminate, 5.5-17 x 2.5-7 cm, papery to herbaceous, slightly whitish to brownish hispidulous to glabrescent on both sides; costa above whitish to brownish hispidulous, ferruginous to brownish hispid(ulous) beneath; domatia wanting; lateral veins 11-18 pairs (acumen excluded), whitish to ferruginous hispidulous) to glabrescent on both sides; tertiary venation ± scalariform, glabrescent or sparsely whitish to brownish hispidulous; base rounded to cuneate, asymmetric, oblique, rounded, subcordate or subauriculate at the petiole; margin serrate to crenate, mucronulate; acumen (0-) 1.5- 2.5 cm long, apex (sub)obtuse, mucronulate. Inflorescences axillary, lateral and subterminal, solitary, thyrsoid, more or less laxiflorous, 4.5-7 x 1-1.75 cm; central axis ferruginous hirsute, golden to yellowish hirtellous, cymules 1-7 flowered; common peduncle 1.25-2 mm long, golden to brownish hirtellous; pedicels 2.5-3 mm long, articulate near the middle or near the base, golden to brownish hirtellous; bracts and bractlets narrowly ovate, gradually acuminate, herbaceous, scarious near the margin, sometimes golden to whitish hispidulous, costate, veined, ciliolate; bracts 3.5-4.25 x 1-2 mm, 9-veined; bractlets 1-1.25 x 0.3-0.4 mm. Flower buds ovoid to conical, obtusish. Flowers drooping, white. Sepals (sub)equal, narrowly ovate to deltoid, acuminate, 2.25-3 x ca. 0.75 mm, scarious, golden pilose near the apex of the costa, obscurely 2-4 veined, margin whitish to golden ciliate, apex subacute. Petals ovate, 4.25-6 x 1.75-2.5 mm, herbaceous, glabrous or rarely sparsely pilose along the costa, margin not ciliolate, apex obtuse. Stamens 3.5-3.75 mm long; filaments free, 0.40.5 x ca. 0.25 mm, glabrous; dorsal glands free, adnate to the filaments, narrowly elliptic, ca. 0.75 x ca. 0.25 mm, slightly longer than the filaments, carnose, glabrous; anthers ovoid, 1.5-1.75 x ca. 0.75 mm, glabrous, apex of thecae obtuse to rounded, usually appendaged by l(-2) cusps, 0.4-0.8 x 0.1 mm; connective outside narrowly deltoid, acute, 1.25 x 0.25 mm, glabrous; connective scales lateral as well as apical, narrowly elliptic, 2.75-3.25 x 0.75-1 mm, scarious, yellowish when fresh, brownish when dried, margin erose to fringed especially near the base, apex rounded, suberose to subentire. Ovary subglobose, 1-1.25 x 0.75-1.25 mm, slanting to erect brownish pilose; ovules one per placenta. Style filiform, erect or slightly curved, 3-3.75 mm long, exceeding the stamens by 0.5-1 mm, predominantly glabrous. Fruits unknown.

description: Shrubs 2-4 m tall, the stems stellate-pubescent, the hairs 1 mm long and with dense rows of shorter (sometimes glandular) pubescence. Leaf blades usually hastately or palmately 3-lobed (smaller and narrower upward, ovate to subhastate), truncate or subcordate, serrate, acute or acuminate, 4-9 cm long (the central lobe seldom >2 cm wide), the upper surface with erect (but curved) simple hairs ca. 0.5 mm long, the lower surface villous on main veins and with scattered 3-4armed stellate spicules; petioles 2-22 mm long; stipules 2-8 mm long, subulate or falcate, spreading or reflexed. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1.5-3 cm long; involucellar bracts 10-12, linear, 11-19 x ca. 1 mm, ciliate; calyx 8-9 mm long, ciliate; corolla yellow, 2-3.5 cm long, minutely pubescent externally, otherwise glabrous; staminal column glabrous, 15-21 mm long, the filaments 3-5 mm long; styles exserted and distinct for distal 4 mm, sometimes exceeding the petals. Fruits 6 mm diam., glabrous, the mericarps 5-5.5 mm long, carinate, weakly reticulate (sub)apically acute but scarcely beaked.

description: Subshrubs 0.5-1 m tall, the stems with coarse stellate hairs ca. 1 mm long. Leaf blades lance-oblong, mostly 2-4.5 x 1-1.5 cm, basally truncate or subhastate, serrate, acute, palmately 3(-5)-nerved or seemingly penninerved, with scattered stellate hairs 0.5-1 mm diam. above and beneath, very sparse above; petioles 8-18 mm long; stipules filiform, 3-4 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 0.5-2.5 cm long; involucellar bracts 5, lanceolate, 5-6 x 2-2.5 mm, stellate-pubescent; calyx 8-9 mm long, stellate-hirsute, plicate-pentangular in bud, the lobes cordate, 5-6 mm wide; corolla lavender with a dark center, 1.5-2 cm long, glabrous throughout; staminal column 6-7 mm long, glabrous, reddish, the filaments 2 mm long. Fruits ca. 7 mm diam., minutely pubescent; mericarps 4 mm high, dorsally carinate, with raised reticulations, enclosed by calyx.

description: Shrubs 1-2 m tall, the stems densely and minutely stellate-pubescent. Leaf blades ovate or ovate-elliptic, mostly 2-10 x 1-5 cm, basally truncate to cordate, obscurely or prominently crenate-serrate, acute or acuminate, markedly discolorous, sparsely and minutely stellate-pubescent above, densely and finely tomentulose beneath, palmately 5-7-nerved, the nerves sunken above, raised beneath; petioles 0.5-4 cm long; stipules subulate to filiform, 3-7 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 5-25 mm long; involucel cupuliform (basally gamophyllous), 6-10 mm long, the lobes 5(-6), narrowly triangular, sparsely pubescent (densely so at base); calyx 6-11 mm long, stellate-pubescent, especially on nerves; corolla 1.8-3 cm long, rose or red, tubular, glabrous; androecium exserted, purplish, the filaments 4-8 mm long; styles exceeding the column, free for distal 5 mm. Fruits ca. 5 mm diam., minutely puberulent; mericarps 5 mm high, with a dorsal crest or wing (ca. 1 mm wide apically) and with 2 or 3 acute excrescences on each side.

description: Subshrubs or shrubs 0.5-3 m tall, the stems stellate-hispidulous, the hairs more or less appressed. Leaf blades mostly 9-16 cm by up to 9 cm (usually <5 cm wide), oblong-lanceolate to oblanceolate, basally slightly asymmetrical, truncate to cuneate, serrulate, acuminate, penninerved or weakly 3-nerved, stellate-pubescent (sparsely so on upper surface); petioles 2-7 mm long; stipules ca. 2 mm long. Flowers sometimes solitary but usually on 3-6-flowered axillary or terminal peduncles, the individual pedicels 4-25 mm long; involucellar bracts 8-9, gamophyllous, ca. 4 mm long, stellate-pubescent; calyx 5-6 mm long (exceeding involucel), stellate-pubescent; corolla ca. 1 cm long, white. Fruits 5-6 mm diam., the mericarp body 6.5 mm high, glabrous, the mericarps 3-spined, the spines retrorsely barbed, erect, 4-5 mm long, the lateral spines ca. 2 mm apart at base.

description: Shrubs 1.5-2 m tall, the stems minutely glandular-pubescent and also setose, hairs 1-2 mm long. Leaf blades ovate, deeply cordate, serrate-crenate, acute or acuminate, discolorous, mostly 4-11 x 3-8 cm, minutely glandular-pubescent and also appressed-villous, the hairs 0.5-1 mm long; petioles 1.5-6 cm long; stipules filiform, 4-10 mm long. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 2-4 cm long; involucellar bracts 12-14, filiform, ca. 10 x 0.5 mm or less, viscid and also setose; calyx 18-21 mm long, hirsute; corolla 3.5 cm long, tubular, orange or red with dark venation, subglabrous; androecium subequal to petals; styles slightly exserted. Fruits obovoid, ca. 8 mm diam., glabrous, the mericarps 8-9 mm high, reticulate-veined.

description: Shrubs 1-3 m tall, the stems strigillose with minute appressed stellate hairs and narrow lines of dense recurved hairs. Leaf blades sometimes ovate, sometimes palmately lobulate, usually hastately 3-lobed, basally truncate to cordate, serrate, acute or acuminate, palmately 5-9-nerved, sparsely pubescent to subglabrous, sometimes with short simple hairs above and stellate hairs beneath, mostly 4-15 cm long; petioles 1.5-12 cm long; stipules 8-12 mm long, falcate, reflexed. Flowers solitary or paired in the leaf axils, the pedicels 0.5-2.5 cm long, slender; involucellar bracts (7-) 10-12, linear, 9-14 mm long, ciliate; calyx 5-8 mm long, ciliate; corolla 2 cm long, yellow, pubescent on margins of claw; staminal column more or less declined, ca. 1 cm long, pallid, glabrous, the filaments 3-5 mm long; styles exserted from the column, the stigmas subequal to the petals. Fruits 8 mm diam., glabrous, the mericarps 4-6 mm high, rugulose, with a small (sub)apical beak.

description: Tree to 5.5 m high, glabrous except for the inflorescence; young twigs very narrowly 4-winged. Petioles 1.0-2.0 mm long; blades coriaceous, shining, 5.0-12.0 cm long, 1.5-3.1 cm wide, narrowly ovate-elliptic, acuminate at the apex, cordate at the base with a notch 0.8-2.0 mm deep; midrib low-rounded above with a shallow groove along each side, prominent below and sharply 2-angled; lateral nerves moderately raised and visible above, obscurely to moderately so below, when dry. Midrib xylem tubular; stomatal crypts Type II, averaging in a leaf ca 25-35 µ in diam, 29 m high, 87-115 per sq mm (extremes 15-50 µ diam, 23-32 µ high, 165-250 per sq mm); upper epidermis one cell thick, all cells with mucilaginous walls; hypodermis none; free stone cells present along the length of the midrib; terminal sclereids mostly stellate with a rectangular to rounded central body 1-2 times as long as wide and with short irregular arms, seldom the arms none. Inflorescences axillary or at leafless nodes of twigs up to 3.0 mm thick, 1-5 per side, densely clustered, more or less united at base, each 1-3-flowered, the flowers 3-5 per side altogether, each inflorescence 0-1.5 mm long to base of farthest pedicel and with 0-2 internodes in that length or the internodes not plain; bracts (0.3-)0.8-1.2 mm long, ovate-triangular, acute, the shortest ones at the base. Internodes of inflorescence, bracts, and pedicels more or less minutely puberulent. True pedicels 2.5-3.5 mm long; calyx including inferior ovary 3.4-3.8 mm long, campanulate, nearly truncate at base, the 5 locules within bulging externally; apparent free hypanthium as measured to style base ca 2.2 mm long; calyx lobes before anthesis ovate-triangular or triangular, blunt, 0.8-1.3 mm long, 1.6-2.3 mm wide, 1.2-1.9 mm long from the stamen attachment, separating at anthesis a further length of 0-0.2 mm. Petals white or pinkish, 3.7 mm long, 2.4 mm wide, obovate, acute. Length of filaments at anthesis unknown; anthers 2.5-2.7 mm long; sporangia 2.5-2.6 mm long, dehiscing by elongate apical pores; gland 0.6-0.7 mm long, 1.9 mm from apex of anther when measured from center of gland; cauda 0-0.6 mm long. Ovary 5-locular, the locules widely separated and appearing as if in the base of the hypanthium; placentae basal or parietal-basal in each locule, the ovules borne on all sides of a short basal or parietal-basal column, 3 per locule, 15 in all; style ca 12.5 mm long. Fruit unknown, probably similar to that of M. nervosa.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1976. Melastomataceae tribe Memecyleae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 15: 1-295.

description: Tree to 12.2 mm high with a trunk to 15.2 cm in diam, sometimes shrubby in aspect, glabrous except for the inflorescence; young twigs terete or very narrowly 4-ridged. Petioles 0.5-1.0 mm long; blades subcoriaceous, dark green above, pale green beneath, 10.6-17.0 cm long, 5.2-8.0 cm wide, ovate to ovate-elliptic or seldom ovate-elliptic-oblong, acute, sometimes rather abruptly so, to short acuminate at the apex, cordate at base with a notch 1.5-3.0 mm deep; midrib flat or slightly elevated above, low-rounded beneath; lateral nerves obscure or invisible above and below when dry. Midrib xylem tubular; stomatal crypts none; upper epidermis one cell thick; mucilaginous walls none; true hypodermis none but one is simulated by the upper layer of the palisade parenchyma whose cells either contain fewer chloroplasts than those of the lower layers or contain only crystals; free stone cells present only near base of midrib; terminal sclereids stellate to columnar, the arms few, short to long, rather sharp, most sclereids with a central body 2-8 times as long as wide, often branched, often with 1 or more columnar arms. Flowers mostly on old wood, apparently often on the main trunk but sometimes also in the terminal axils and presumably sometimes on the branches, inflorescences 1 to many per side of stem, each l-3(-5)-flowered, 4.5-9.1 mm long to base of farthest pedicel measured along the axes and with 1-3 internodes in that length; bracts 1.2-2.6 mm long, triangular or somewhat ovate-triangular, acute at apex, the upper ones overlapping so as to appear perfoliate but not actually so, bracts mostly deciduous by fruiting. True pedicels rose-red, 1.05.4 mm long; buds greenish-white in lower half, dull rose in upper; calyx including inferior ovary 7.08.0 mm long, campanulate; surfaces of inflorescence, calyx, and inferior ovary minutely puberulent; free hypanthium 3.7-4.0 mm long; calyx lobes before anthesis broadly rounded to truncate, 0.7-1.3 mm long, 2.03.2 mm wide, 2.4-2.9 mm long when measured from stamen attachment, the calyx splitting between the lobes at anthesis a distance of 1.4-2.0 mm; narrow rim on inside of calyx just above stamen attachments sparsely to abundantly fringed with short thick hairs 0.2-0.3 mm long. Petals whitish at least within, apparently sometimes lilac without, 8.010.5 mm long, 5.06.0 mm wide, ovate, acute at apex, with a suggestion of a short broad claw at base. Filaments ca. 14 mm long; anthers 3.5-4.0 mm long, sporangia 3.5-4.0 mm long, dehiscing by apical pores; gland ca. 0.5 mm long, 2.2-2.6 mm from apex of anther when measured from center of gland; cauda none. Ovary 5-locular; ovules axile-basal, produced only outwardly from each placenta, 15 in all; style ca 12-16 mm long, puberulent except at tip and base. Fruit orange-pink, depressed-globose, crowned with the remains of the calyx, ca 8.5-12.0 mm high excluding calyx and 9.013.0 mm in diam when 1-seeded, to ca 15.0 mm wide when 2- or 3-seeded, dry, estimated ca 11-16 mm high and 12-17 mm in diam when 1-seeded or up to 20 mm wide with 2 or 3 seeds when fresh, the calyx directly opposite the pedicel when seeds are 2 or 3, the fruit asymmetric and the calyx as little as 90° from the pedicel when the seed is single. Seeds 1-3, smooth, shiny, medium brown with a dark brown area on the micropyle side, roundish when single, flattened somewhat on the contact faces when more than one, ca. 6.7 mm high and 6.7-7.6 mm thick, with a basal hilum ca. 3.6 mm in diam.

description: Glabrous tree, sometimes low and bushy, to 30 m high with a trunk to 50 cm in diam; young twigs terete; bark thin, papery, dark-colored, rather shaggy through flaking off in irregular pieces; inner bark yellowish; sapwood hard and brownish-white; heartwood reddish- or pale pinkish-brown with twisted grain, very hard and heavy. Petioles 1.0-5.0 mm long; blades dark green and shining above, paler green below, rigid, sometimes somewhat fleshy, 5.0-11.0(-13.4) cm long, 3.0-7.0(-8.5) cm wide, moderately to broadly elliptic or ovate-elliptic, seldom almost round, apiculate to shortly and abruptly acuminate at the apex, acute with a 60° included angle to broadly rounded at base, abruptly attenuate on the petiole; midrib plane or slightly raised or grooved above, rounded to nearly flat below; lateral nerves obscurely visible to invisible above and below when dry. Midrib xylem tubular; stomatal crypts none; upper epidermis mostly two cells thick, rarely one cell thick in the same leaf, mucilaginous walls frequent in the inner of the doubled cells and in the single cells; hypodermis none; free stone cells present only near base of petiole; terminal sclereids columnar, vertical or slanting and moderately weaving, branching at both ends, more above than below. Inflorescences axillary or at leafless nodes of twigs up to 5.0 mm thick, 1 or 2 per side, each 1-3-flowered, 2.6-17.0 mm long to base of farthest pedicel measured along the axes and with 1 or 2 internodes in that length; bracts 2.0-2.4 mm long, narrowly triangular, mostly deciduous by anthesis. True pedicels 5.0-15.0 mm long; calyx including inferior ovary obovoid with fully fused calyx enclosing the petals in bud, 10.0-15.0 mm long, 6.0-8.0 mm wide, drawn up into an abruptly acuminate point at the apex, the calyx bursting irregularly at anthesis; free hypanthium ca 2.4 mm long; calyx limb ca 5.0-8.5 mm long measured from the stamen attachments. Flowers fragrant or the odor unpleasant. Petals white, 8.5-15.0 mm long, 9.0-11.0 mm wide, broadly elliptic to obovate or subrotund, the margin crisped, the apex abruptly acute, the base with a claw 1.8-2.0 mm long, ca 1.3 mm wide. Filaments declined, ca 9.0-13.0 mm long; anthers yellow, 3.8-5.2 mm long; sporangia 3.6-4.8 mm long, dehiscing by elongate apical pores; gland 0.4-1.3 mm long, 2.7-3.5 mm from apex of anther when measured from center of gland; cauda 0-1.0 mm long. Ovary 5-6 locular; ovules axile-basal, produced only outwardly from each placenta, 25-30 in all; style white, declined with the stamens, 14.0-22.0 mm long. Fruit edible, orange or yellow-orange, globose or subglobose, crowned with the circular base of the hypanthium or sometimes other remains of the calyx, ca 17-22 mm high excluding calyx and 17-23 mm thick when dry, estimated 20-27 mm high and 20-29 mm thick when fresh. Seeds (2-)5, dark brown, smooth, hard, not very shiny, 9.5-12.5 mm long, 6.1-8.0 mm thick, rounded on the periphery, flattened on the contact faces so as to be wedge-shaped when several; hilum basal, roundish, flattish, ca 3.5 mm wide.

description: Rami novelli, indumento persistente, dense hispidi (pilis subrectis, erectis, rigidis), interdum serius lenticellosi. Perulae nullae. Folia imparipinnata, 7.5-15 cm longa; petiolus anguste alatus; rhachis semiteres, utraque dense hispida; petiolulus 1-2 mm. Foliola opposita vel subopposita, 7-9, oblanceolata, apice acuminata vel obtuse usque acute cuspidata, basi cuneata vel attenuata, chartacea, 9-18[15] cm longa, 3-5.5[4.9] cm lata, costa superiore dense pubescente, pagina inferiore passim sparse, ad costam nervosque densius hispida, nec glanduloso-punctata nec -striata; venatio brochidodroma, costa et nervi secundarii tertiar-iique omnes supra impressi; nervi secundarii 14-16 utroque costae latere, arcuati, adscendentes, subconvergentes, intersecundarii breves sed prominentes, tertiarii obliqui. Flores unisexuales (planta dioica); inflorescentia axillaris vel plures in brevi surculo axillari fasciculatae, 2-4 cm longae, ± fasciculatae ramis patulis paene a basi, densiusculis fasciculis ± sessilibus florum onustae, hispidae; pedicellus 0.5-1 mm longus. Calyx sparse et grosse pubescens, patelliformis, 0.5-1.5 mm longus, lobis 5 late triangularibus, acutis usque attenuatis, 1/2-2/3 calycem aequantibus, margine sparse ciliatis. Petala 5, libera, subimbricata, 3-3.5 mm longa, 0.75-1 mm lata, anguste elliptica, oblonga vel lanceolata, apice acuta, glabra. Tubus stamineus cyathiformis, 1-2 mm longus, 1.5-2 mm latus, apice rotundatus vel breviter bilobatus (lobis rotundatis vel acutis), filamentis per 1/4-1/3 longitudinem coalitis, totus extus glaber, intus basi glaber, in libera parte filamentorum rigide hirtus; antherae 10-11, 0.4-0.5 mm longae, hirtae; antherodia gracilia, polline carentia, non dehiscentia. Nectarium nullum. Ovarium ovoideum, 3-loculare, dense strigosum, loculis uniovulatis; stylus brevis, crassus, rigide pubescens; styli capitulum parvum, discoideum; pistillodium parvum, complana-tum, parvis ovulis abortivis instructum, longo stylo pubescente coronatum, capitulum inexpansum discoideum antheris aequilongum gerente. Capsula anguste ellipsoidea, ad basin attenuata, laevis, dense hispida, 2-2.5 cm longa, ca. 1 cm lata, 3-valvata; pericarpium ca. 0.75 mm crassum, endocarpio tenui, cartilagineo. Semen solitarium, ca. 1.4 cm longum, ca. 1 cm latum, obovoideum, de ultra medium basin versus attenuatum, tenui arillodio carnoso, tripartito, apice incrassata undique circumdatum; arillodium praeter juncturam circa micropylen et secus raphen liberum; testa tenuis, membranacea. Embryo cotyledonibus crassis, plano-convexis, collateralibus; radicula superior, inclusa. Endospermum nullum.

description: Glabrous shrub or tree 3-6, rarely to 10 m high. Branches often spreading and drooping. Branchlets slender, subterete. Leaves obovate to oblong-obovate, apex rounded, rarely a little emarginate, base cuneate and almost decurrent to the petiole, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, dark olivaceous to brown, dull and usually not tuberculate on both surfaces in dry specimens, edge somewhat revolute, (2-)2.5-4 x (1-) 1.5-2.5 cm, sometimes microphyllous, lateral nerves 2-3 pairs from and a little above the base of the lamina, steeply ascendent and more or less looping, slightly raised as is the midrib on both surfaces, reticulation of veins less obvious; petiole flattened, 1.5-3(-5) mm long. Inflorescences 1-5 from foliate or defoliate axils, glabrous; peduncles 2-4(-8) mm long, usually 2-, rarely 1- or 3-flowered. Flowers sessile, yellowish-pink to pale carmine or dark red. Epicalyx cup-shaped, entire, i.e. the bracts and bracteoles completely adnate, 1.5 mm long. Flower-axis 1.5 mm long. Brachystylous flowers; corolla cylindrical to ovoid-cylindrical, 4(-5.5) mm long in all, 4- or 5-lobed in the upper 1/3 lobes ovate-triangular, reflexed; anthers shortly ovate; style 1.2-1.5 mm long. Dolichostylous flowers: corolla cylindric-campanulate, ca. 4 mm long, 4- or 5-lobed in the upper 2/5 part, lobes reflexed; anthers subquadrate; style 3 mm long. Top of ovary glabrous. Drupe obovoid-ellipsoid, reddish or yellow with orange top, 7-8 x ca. 5 mm.

description: Shrub, or tree. Young branches with indumentum appressed-tomentose, short and long hairs interspersed, buff to pale gray, glabrescent; bark dark brown to black; lenticels few to numerous, small (to 0.5 mm diam.), plane to slightly raised, granular, light brown to orange-brown. Axillary buds usually becoming lobed laterally or sometimes two buds closely juxtaposed one above the other, rounded, solid with very densely compacted, light orange-brown to red-brown hairs. Leaves coriaceous, decussate, at times subopposite-decussate, the indumentum above dense, appressed villous-tomentose, yellow-brown fading to gray, glabrescent, often persisting somewhat along midrib, short, close-appressed tomentose beneath, buff, slowly glabrescent, floccose in places, leaving thin, scurfy layer beneath. Petioles 1-3 cm long × 1.5-3 mm wide (to 5 mm at base), flat and thick to subterete, with base of lamina descending the petiole forming a minute ridge; rugose-ruminate, the indumentum short-tomentose, buff to gray (rarely light orange-brown) with a few rufous hairs occasionally interspersed, eventually glabrous. Lamina 6.5-25 × 3-9.5 cm, widely elliptic when young; becoming widely obovate to narrowly obovate; base symmetrical or asymmetrical, obtuse to rounded, rarely acute, rapidly decurrent; apex rounded, occasionally obtuse; margin slightly revolute; venation inconspicuous (at times drying conspicuous), brochidodromous, lowermost vein(s) usually eucamptodromous, the marginal vein rarely conspicuous as veins become obscure towards margins, slightly raised above where lateral veins first emerging from midrib, then becoming plane; midrib prominent above only to ca. half its length then becoming plane; lateral veins 8-16 pairs, leaving midrib at (50-)60-70(-90)°, the basal vein(s) arcing immediately, the other veins running straight and parallel before arcing near to the leaf margin. Primary axis of inflorescence branched, 7-19 cm × 1.5-3 mm; 4-7 (difficult to determine as scars near the base of the primary axis could be those of leaves or lateral inflorescences), lateral inflorescences at 2-6 nodes, 4-17 cm × 1-1.5 mm, spirally arranged, well spaced; indumentum short-villous to tomentose, buff to pale yellow-brown, pedicel scars prominent. Common bracts 1-1.5 mm long, frequently paler in color than buds, orange-brown fading to buff villous. Pedicels 2-4.5 mm long, 0.3-0.6 mm wide, short-villous to tomentose, orange-brown, pilose with maturity. Flowers 4-4.5 mm long, the perianth indumentum short-villous to pilose, orange-brown, calvescent; filaments 3-4 mm long, free to base of perianth parts; anthers 0.6-1 × 0.3-0.5 mm; hypogynous nectary 0.40.5 mm long, lobed to less than halfway from apex; ovary hairs extending to 1.5-2 mm from base, frequently with few hairs up style to 3 mm; style 0.2-0.3(-0.4) mm wide at midlength, only slightly clavate. Fruit pedicel 2-3 × 3-4mm. Fruit 5.5-6 × 4.5-5.5 cm, globose, very slightly mucronate to 2 mm, markedly offset from fruit axis, smooth, glabrous, dull, dark brown suffused red; pericarp 4 mm thick; outer mesocarp 0.5 mm thick; mid mesocarp 3 mm thick; inner mesocarp thin. Seed coat fused to pericarp. Seeds not seen. Field characters. Shrub or tree, to 15 m, the branching starting low to ground. Leaves rigid, rufous. Flowers white or yellow; fruit green.

description: Plants epiphytic; fronds erect to arcuate, determinate; rhizome short-creeping, dorsiventral, with dorsiventral root insertion, scaly, the scales 0.3-0.5 x 0.1-0.2 mm, lanceolate, the apex short-attenuate, clathrate, castaneous, ciliate, the cilia simple, present on scale margin and apex; petiole 0.5-1.5 cm x 0.6 mm, dark brown, terete, densely pubescent, the hairs 0.1 mm long, spreading, simple, 1-celled, whitish; lamina to 15 cm long, elliptic, chartaceous, deeply pinnatisect, 15-25(-30) pairs of segments, gradually reduced at the base with 3-6 basal segments shorter than the medial ones, the lowermost auriculiform, not long-decurrent onto petiole base, broadest near the middle, not showing periodic constrictions, the apex abruptly reduced, pinnatifid or rarely ending in a subconform segment; rachis straight, with dark sclerenchyma visible on both sides, sparsely pubescent abaxially, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, entire or 1-furcate, 1- to 3-celled, whitish to castaneous, glabrous adaxially; segments 0.5—1(—1.2) x 0.2-0.25 cm, plane, set 60-70° to rachis, more or less symmetrical, widened at the base, short-decurrent basiscopically, slightly surcurrent acroscopically, the base attached parallel on the rachis (i.e., both sides inserted along the same radius of the rachis), not lobulate, the apex acute to obtuse, the margin entire, glabrous, abaxial lamina surface glabrous, adaxial lamina surface glabrous; sinuses narrower or about the same size of the width of the segments; venation pinnate, with 5-8 pairs of veins per segment; costae with the black sclerenchyma obscured by laminar tissue, glabrous; veins simple, without blackish sclerenchyma, ending in hydathodes that lack calcareous deposits; sori medial, rounded, not protruding beyond the costa and margin, 5-8 pairs per segment, deeply sunken; sporangial capsules glabrous.

description: Plants epipetric; fronds erect to arcuate, determinate; rhizome short to long-creeping, dorsiventral, with ventral root insertion, scaly, the scales 2-3 x 0.6-0.8 mm, lanceolate, the apex short-attenuate, clathrate, castaneous, ciliate, the cilia simple, present on scale margins and apex (apical cilia sometimes furcate); petiole 1—3(—4) cm x 0.4-0.6 mm, dark brown, terete, conspicuously pubescent, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, spreading, simple or 1-furcate, 2- to 3-celled, whitish to reddish; lamina 6—12(—15) cm long, linear-lanceolate, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, deeply pinnatisect, 25-35 pairs of segments, gradually reduced at the base with 3-6 basal segments Vi shorter than the median ones, the lowermost auriculiform, broadest in the middle, not showing periodic constrictions, the apex abruptly reduced, pinnatifid, not ending in a subconform segment; rachis straight, with dark sclerenchyma visible on both sides, sparsely pubescent to glabrous abaxially, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, appressed, simple or 1-furcate, 2- to 3-celled, whitish to dark brown, densely pubescent adaxially, the hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long, spreading, sirnple, 1- to 2-celled, castaneous to reddish; segments 0.3-0.6 x 0.2-0.3 cm, plane, set 60-70° to rachis, widened and symmetric at the base, short-decurrent on both sides, sometimes slightly cuneate acroscopically, the base attached parallel on the rachis (i.e., both sides inserted along the same radius), not lobulate or, if slightly lobulate, not overlapping the base of the next segment, the apex obtuse, the margin entire, recurved, abaxial lamina surface sparsely pubescent, the hairs similar to those of the rachis abaxially, adaxial lamina surface glabrous; sinuses narrower or about twice as broad as the segments; venation pinnate, with 3-6 pairs of veins per segment; costae with blackish sclerenchyma obscured by laminar tissue on both sides, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, the hairs similar to those of the rachis abaxially; description: Shrubs 0.3-3.0(-5) m tall, deciduous or evergreen. Bark variable in color with usually a moderate amount of mostly straight and erect short to long hairs. Branchlets (0.6-)0.9-9.5(-16.0) cm long with leaves not very crowded. Bud scales 1-2 mm long, coriaceous, dark-colored, with marginal or dorsal hairs, and with apex broadly obtuse and occasionally notched. Stipules 2.0-5.0(-6.0) mm long and ca 0.5 mm wide, thin or moderately thick, pale-colored, and with sparse to moderate amounts of hairs which are scattered or exclusively on the margin or midvein, quickly deciduous or persistent; petioles 1.0-4.0(-5.0) mm long with moderate to dense amounts of short to moderately long hairs which may be confined to or concentrated on a ventral furrow; leaf blades (0.3-)0.5-4.2(-8.4) cm long and (0.1-)0.4-1.5(-2.0) cm wide, from broadly elliptical and ovate to oblong and lanceolate, from thin and flexible to firm and moderately thick; apex acute or obtuse or occasionally acuminate or retuse; margin revolute or plane, serrate or crenate, teeth with mucros pale to dark in color and from large to small or absent; above either actually or apparently glabrous, the short erect hairs usually visible only if leaf-surface is at an angle to the lens, beneath yellowish to brownish or the same color as above or occasionally simply paler green than above and either glabrous or with short erect hairs; venation above inconspicuous or conspicuously pallid and either glabrous or with midvein usually hairy and secondaries with the same amount of hair or less or sometimes glabrous, hairs erect and of variable lengths. Flowers associated with mature leaves, 1-3 (rarely 4 or 5) per axil; peduncles absent; pedicels usually 3 mm long or shorter (rarely up to 6 mm); flowers monoecious or polygamodioecious or protandrous, 4-merous; floral cups varying in shape from funnelform through urceolate and campanulate to hemispheric (the latter uncommon), (0.6-)1.0-1.5(-2.0) mm deep (usually shallower in 9 than in cr flowers), 1.0-2.0 mm broad, usually broader than deep glabrous or with sparse to moderately sparse short, erect pubescence; sepals 1.0-2.0 mm long, 0.6-1.5 mm wide (usually smaller in 9 than in cr flowers), glabrous or with sparse to moderate pubescence; petals 0.5-1.1 mm long (shorter in 9 flower), enclosed by petal partially in cr flower and completely in 9 flower. Fruits 1-2 per axil; pedicels (1.5-)2-4(-6) mm long; floral cup with petal, uniformly colored or with the distal portion darker; anther 0.5-0.75 mm long (shorter in flower), enclosed by petal partially in cr flower and completely in 9 flower. Fruits 1-2 per axil; pedicels (1.5-)2-4(-6) mm long; floral cup with margin entire or notched on two sides and glabrous or with short hairs; drupe (3.0)4.0-6.0(-8.0) mm broad, either globose or somewhat prolate, glabrous, 2-seeded (rarely 3-seeded); style retained or not, stigma bifurcate or trifurcate.

description: Shrub or treelet 3-7.5 m tall, trunk 3-7.5 cm in diam., bark bitter; branchlets 2-4 mm in diam., grayish-green-brown, shining when young, puberulous with hairs 0.05-0.1 mm long, glabrous in age, young branchlets often crowded. Leaves alternate to opposite, imparipinnate, 1-5-jugate but mostly 3-4-jugate with sessile leaflets, elliptic, 5-15 × 4-6 cm; petiole semiterete, canaliculate by incurved wings, 0.5-3.5 cm long and 0.2 cm thick, (sub)glabrous, the wings 0.5-1.0 mm broad with revolute margin and ending in a small, round ear; rachis like the petiole, 2-6 cm long, interspaces 1-3 cm, the wings broader distally; leaflet blades ovate to elliptic, the terminal one often obovate, 2-5.5 × 1-3.5 cm, or those of the upper leaves smaller, shortly attenuate-cuneate and strongly unequal at base, the terminal leaflet also long-attenuate and usually equal at base, obtuse or rounded at apex, the very tip always emarginate, margin revolute towards base; leaflet blades chartaceous, green and shining on both sides, glabrous, venation brochidodromous-camptodromous, somewhat prominent on both sides, midvein prominent above, plane to prominent below. Racemes solitary, terminal to axillary, to 30 cm long, ca. 0.5 cm wide, with numerous flowers, (sub)glabrous; peduncle absent or obsolete; rachis 0.5-l(-2) mm thick; bracts broadly triangular to ovate, 0.2-0.3 mm long; pedicels 0.1-1.5 mm long and 0.3 mm thick, in fruit 1.5-2.5 mm long and 1 mm thick; bractlets 2, alternate, obliquely inserted in upper part of pedicel. Flowers 4-5 mm in diam., quite glabrous; calyx 5-toothed; teeth separate, very broadly to depressedly triangular, or subcircular, ca. 0.2-0.4 × 0.4-0.6 mm, obtuse or rounded at apex, coriaceous; petals subvalvate, 1.8-2.3 × 1.1-1.2 mm, apex inflexed through 0.3 mm, thinly coriaceous, semitransparent, brown when dried, the upper side carinate distally and impressed, venation imperfectly acrodromous; filaments subulate, flattened towards base, ca. 1-2 mm long and 0.20.4 mm thick; anthers ca. 0.5-0.7 × 0.4-0.6 mm, with an oblong dorsal gland; disc ca. 0.5 mm high and 1.2-1.5 mm in diam., slightly 10-plicate, light-colored, foveolate; carpels ca. 0.5 mm high, projecting 0.2 mm beyond the disc; style inserted below tips of carpels, not projecting beyond the ovary, 0.2-0.3 mm long and 0.1 mm thick; stigma capitate, 0.2 × 0.4 mm. Mericarps subovoid, 7-10 × 58 mm, dorso-apically rounded, obtuse or rounded, minutely notched at the very apex, punctate with glands 0.2-0.3 mm, glabrous, wrinkled towards base, dehiscent up to 3/4 below tip; seed 1 per mericarp, ca. 5.2-7 × 4.2-5 × 3.8-5.1 mm, flattened at base, rounded at apex, slightly carinate dorsally; testa very dark black-brown, externally flatly reticulate with interspaces 0.05-0.1 mm long; hilum ca. 1.4-2.5 × 0.5-1 mm; cotyledons subequal with ears ca. 0.4-1 mm long, radicle conical, 0.5 mm long, plumule 0.05 mm long.

description: Treelet 2-4 m tall. Branchlets appressed brownish to golden pilosulous. Leaves apparently opposite; petioles 2.5-6 mm long, brownish to golden puberulous or pilosulous, especially beneath, glabrescent when older; stipules deciduous, narrowly deltoid, subacute, 2.5-4 x 1-2 mm, herbaceous, brownish to golden strigulose, costate, margin scarious and ciliolate; lamina (narrowly) elliptic to obovate, acuminate, (5-)6.5-18.5 x (1.5-)3-6.5 cm, papery to coricaeous, glabrous above, appressed golden to whitish pilosulous beneath; costa and lateral veins glabrous above, sometimes appressed pilosulous near the base; domatia wanting; lateral veins 11-16 pairs (acumen excluded); tertiary venation scalariform; base rounded to cuneate, slightly decurrent into the petiole; margin (sub)entire; acumen 0.42 cm long, apex (sub)acute to (sub)obtuse, mucronulate. Inflorescences axillary, lateral and subterminal, solitary, narrowly thyrsoid, (3.5-)8-18.5 x 1-2 cm; central axis golden puberulous to strigillose; cymules 1-7 flowered; common peduncle 0.2-0.3 mm long, golden puberulous to strigulose; ‘pedicels’ 1-3.5 mm long, articulate below the middle, golden puberulous to strigulose; bracts and bractlets ovate to deltoid, herbaceous, golden strigulose, ciliolate apex subacute; bracts ca. 0.75 mm long and wide; bractlets 0.25-0.75 mm long and wide. Flower buds tolpoid to ovoid. Flowers drooping, whitish. Sepals (sub)equal, narrowly ovate, 2-2.5 x, 1-1.25 mm, herbaceous, golden strigulose on both sides, margin scarious and ciliate, apex obtuse to emarginate, mucronulate. Petals narrowly ovate, (2.5-)3-4 x 1-1.25 mm, herbaceous, golden strigulose on both sides, especially near the middle inside, margin scarious, ciliate in juvenile flowers, apex obtuse. Stamens 1.75-2.25 mm long, filaments nearly completely fused to a tube; apical part free, 0.1-0.2 x 0.05-0.1 mm, glabrous; filamental tube 0.2-0.3 mm high, sinuate, ciliate; dorsal glands completely fused with the filamental tube; anthers ellipsoid to ovoid, 0.8-1 x 0.5-0.8 mm, glabrous, apex of thecae obtuse, sometimes appendaged by two cusps or setae, up to 1 mm long; connective outside ovate to deltoid, obtuse, 0.3-0.5 x ca. 0.25 mm, glabrous; connective scales lateral as well as apical, (narrowly) ovate, 1.5-2 x 0.5-1 mm, scarious, brownish, glabrous, margin erose, apex obtuse, suberose to subentire. Ovary (sub)globose to trapezoid, ca. 1 x 0.5-0.75 mm, golden villosulous along the ribs; ovules one per placenta. Style filiform to subclavate, erect, deflexed or slightly sigmoid curved towards the anterior petal, 1.25-1.75(-2) mm long, exceeding the stamens by 0.25-0.5(-0.75) mm, completely glabrous; stigma apiculate to obtuse. Capsule often asymmetric, (sub)orbicular, sometimes subtended by subpersistent floral parts, coriaceous, densely minutely golden to whitish pilosulous; valves three, unequal to subequal, the larger one 0.9-1.2 x 0.2-0.5 cm; the two smaller ones ca. 0.6 x 0.2-0.5 cm. Seeds one per valve, (sub)globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., glabrous, shining.

description: Slender tree or treelet, 4-10(13) m tall, unbranched or with few ascending, sympodial branches on distal portion; trunk to 8 cm in diam.; bark grayish to dark brown, smooth or lenticellate. Stems terete, minutely hirsute, sometimes hollow in the center and inhabited by ants. Leaves paripinnate, spirally arranged on distal portion of stem(s); distal process acicular, early deciduous, usually curved; leaflets chartaceous, 10-16 (32), opposite to alternate, oblong, elliptic or lanceolate, (5.5) 9-27(53) × (2)3.5-8.5(12) cm, the venation brochidodromus, tertiary veins reticulate, the adaxial surface with impressed venation, glabrous or the midvein minutely tomentose, the abaxial surface minutely hirsute, with prominent venation, the apex acuminate to caudate, the base inequilateral, one side obtuse or rounded the other attenuate or cuneate, the margins entire slightly revolute; petiolules pulvinate, 4-6 mm long, minutely hirsute to glabrescent; rachis 22-60 cm long, terete, or slightly angled on distal portion, minutely hirsute; petioles 1227 (40) cm long, terete, minutely hirsute, greatly enlarged at base. Thyrses panicle-shaped, 30-60 cm long, terminal or axillary on distal part of branches; cataphylls acicular, 5-10 mm long, hirsute, axes terete or slightly angled, hirsute; bracts and bracteoles lanceolate or subulate, hirsute, 1.3-3.5 mm long; dichasia simple, sessile; pedicels < 1 mm long, articulate at the apex. Calyx light green, urceolate, 23-A mm long, minutely hirsute, sometimes intermingled with glandular hairs, the sepals 1.63 mm long, ovate-deltate; petals white, 5.5 mm long, oblong, abaxially glabrous, adaxially papillate, rounded at apex, cuneate or cuneate-attenuate at base; appendage as long as the petal, long-deltate, abaxially papillate, adaxially hirsute on upper half; disc 5-lobed, minutely hirsute at apex, ca. 0.8 mm tall; stamens 8, the filaments of equal or nearly equal length, glabrous, 2-4 mm long, nearly filiform, the anthers oblong or linear-lanceolate, 1.5-1.8 mm long, apiculate at apex; ovary conical, sericeous-hirsute, the stigma elongate-trigonous, ferruginous-papillate. Fruit yellow to orange-yellow at maturity, ovoid to globose, 2-2.5 cm long, densely to sparsely hirsutulous, the pericarp woody, smooth, to 2.5 mm thick. Seed ellipsoid, the testa woody, with a thin, fleshy, yellowish to orange-yellow upper layer, rugulate when dried. Embryo with cotyledons lying dorsiventrally to obliquely dorsiventrally over each other, the lower one almost twice as large as the upper one.

description: Description based on wet and dry specimens. Dioecious (inflorescence unisexual), red-orange to pink or dark red root parasites. Total length from point of contact with host root (4-)9-l 1 (-23) cm. Tuber subspherical, 1-5 cm diam., giving out short, cylindrical, horizontal rhizome-like structures about 1 cm diam. Stem appearing at intervals from rhizome-like organs or sometimes apparently directly from the tuber, cylindrical, (2-)5-8(-18) cm long and 0.7-1.5 cm wide. Leaves scaly, numerous in 6 vertical ranks, first densely imbricate, almost triangular, acute (6-)7-9(-l 1) mm long and (5-)7-10 mm wide at base, erect. Inflorescence ellipsoid to cylindrical-ellipsoid, 2-7 x 1-2.5 cm, densely covered by imbricate, 6-ranked bracts when young. Bracts transversely triangular, acute, 6-12 x 7-16 mm at base, inserted by a broad-canaliculate 3 mm long petiole, which is transversally extended and attached along the entire lower margin of the limb, twice bent at obtuse angles about 130°-150°, early deciduous and thus leaving a twice bent scar in the dense layer of filiform hairs covering the inflorescence. The hexagonal, transversally extended, area delimitated by the scars of four neighboring bracts represents one extremely depressed branch subtended by the lowermost bract. Hairs thinly clavate, 2.4 mm long. Male flowers 20-30 on each branch, at first embedded in layer of hairs, later growing to about 5 mm with a lower, tubular part about 2.5 mm and tepals ovate, concave, 2.5 x 1.2 mm. filaments fused into a column 6-7 mm long, tubular, inserted at base of perianth-tube, below synandrium split into 3 free filaments. Synandrium ovoid-ellipsoid, composed of 3 anthers each with 2 cells, dehiscing above insertion of filaments, 1.1 x 1.0 mm. Rudimentary ovary (?) protruding as a short, conical structure into lower part of perianth-tube. Pollen grains spheroid, 6-pantopororate, 40-44 µm diam., exine 2 µm, nuclei 2. Female flowers with perianth adnate to ovary, 2 short and broad, lip-like segments protruding above ovary. Ovary 1.3-1.4 mm long, compressed, 0.4 mm wide, with flat side generally facing insertion of bracts; styles 2, 1.7 mm long, appearing above layer of hairs; stigmas capitellate, 0.2 mm across. Fruit a small, 1-seeded achene.

description: Treelet. Branchlets whitish pilosulous. Leaves apparently opposite; petioles 2-7 mm long, whitish pilosulous; stipules deciduous, ovate to deltoid, 2-2.5 x ca. 1.5 mm, coriaceous, strigose along the costa, ciliolate, apex (sub)obtuse; lamina (narrowly) elliptic, acuminate to cuspidate, 4-11.5 x 1.5-4.5 mm, coriaceous, glabrous above, whitish to yellowish hirtellous beneath; costa above slanting whitish pilosulous to glabrescent; lateral veins 6-12 pairs (acumen excluded); tertiary venation densely reticulate, more prominent beneath than above; base rounded, slightly decurrent into the petiole; margin entire, thick walled especially beneath, yellowish or whitish colored, rudimentarily mucronulate; acumen 0.3-1 cm long, apex subobtuse to subacute, mucronulate. Inflorescences axillary, lateral and subterminal, solitary, racemose, (1-)2-3.5 cm long, central axis golden hispidulous; pedicels 1.75-3 mm long, articulate at 1/3-2/3 from the base, golden to brownish hispidulous; bracts and bractlets ovate to deltoid, herbaceous, strigose along the costa, margin ciliolate, apex subacute, sometimes mucronulate; bracts 0.75-1 x ca. 0.75 mm; bractlets 0.6-0.8 x ca. 0.6 mm. Flower buds ovoid to conical, obtuse. Flowers pendulous, color unknown. Sepals subequal to unequal, outer sepals ovate to deltoid, inner ones ovate to orbicular, 1.25-2 x 1.25-1.75 mm, herbaceous, golden to whitish strigulose along the costa especially near the apex, 7-9 veined, 7-9 ribbed when dried, margin golden to whitish ciliolate, apex subobtuse to subacute, sometimes mucronulate. Petals ovate, 3.75-4.75 x 1.25-1.5 mm, herbaceous, predominantly glabrous, margin whitish ciliolate near the base, apex obtuse and slightly pilosulous. Stamens 3.25-3.75 mm long; filaments free, ca. 0.5 x ca. 0.25 mm, glabrous; dorsal glands free, adnate to the filaments, obovate to subclavate, ca. 0.5 x 0.2-0.4 mm, carnose, sparsely pilosulous, apex free, subobtuse; anthers ovoid, 1.4-1.8 x ca. 0.75 mm, apex of thecae obtuse, usually appendaged by (1-)2 cusps, ca. 0.2 x 0.05-0.1 mm; connective outside narrowly deltoid, obtuse, 1-1.25 x ca. 0.25 mm, sparsely pilosulous to glabrescent; connective scales lateral as well as apical, ovate, 2.75-3.25 x ca. 1 mm, scarious, orange-brown, margin suberose near the base, apex obtuse. Ovary pyriform to subconical, 1-1.25 x 0.3-0.4 mm, golden-brownish strigose; ovules three to four per placenta. Style filiform, erect, 2.25-2.5 mm long, equaling the stamens, slanting pilosulous at the base; stigma truncate, subobtuse or subacute. Capsule more or less symmetric, ovoid, acuminate, coriaceous to subligneous, slightly pilosulous to glabrescent, veined; valves three, (sub)equal 3.25-3.5 x 0.75-1 cm. Seeds two to three per valve, 7.5-10 x 7.5 mm, golden-brownish pilosulous.

description: Treelet 1-4 m tall. Branchlets purplish with whitish callose lenticels (when dried), sparsely strigulose, indument golden to ferruginous. Leaves apparently opposite; petioles 5-17.5 mm long, golden to ferruginous strigulose on both sides; stipules deciduous, narrowly ovate to deltoid, ca. 6 x ca. 1.25 mm, herbaceous, veined and golden-brownish strigose, margin ciliolate, apex subacute, mucronulate; lamina narrowly ovate, widest at 1/3 from the base, long tapering to the apex, acuminate to cuspidate, 11.5-17 x 4-5.5 cm, coriaceous, glabrous on both sides; costa sparsely strigulose above near the base, sparsely ferruginous strigose beneath; domatia wanting; lateral veins 11-14 pairs (acumen excluded); tertiary venation reticulate; base rounded to cuneate, symmetric, obtuse to rounded at the petiole; margin serrate, mucronulate; acumen 2-2.5 cm long, apex (sub)obtuse, mucronulate. Inflorescences axillary, lateral or subterminal, solitary, racemose, 4-4.5 cm long; central axis sparsely strigulose or hispidulous, indument golden to ferruginous; ‘pedicels’ 2-3 mm long, articulate at ½-¼ from the base, sparsely golden to ferruginous hispidulous to strigulose; bracts and bractlets deciduous, narrowly ovate, herbaceous, pilosulous, ciliolate; bracts 1.5-1.75 x 0.75-1 mm; bractlets 1.25 x 0.5 mm. Flower buds ovoid, obtuse. Flowers dropping, yellow. Sepals (sub)equal ovate to deltoid, acuminate, 2-2.5 x 1.5-2 mm, herbaceous, golden to ferruginous strigulose, especially near the apex, 5-7 veined, margin ciliolate, apex subacute. Petals (narrowly) ovate, acuminate, ca. 5 x 1.75-2.25 mm, herbaceous, pilosulous near the apex, margin ciliolate near the base, apex subacute. Stamens 3.75-4 mm long; filaments free, ca. 0.5 x ca. 0.25 mm, glabrous; dorsal glands free, adnate to the filaments, ovate, 0.2-0.5 x ca. 0.2 mm, 0.5-1 x as long as the filaments, carnose, glabrous, apex obtuse; anthers narrowly deltoid, 1.5-1.75 x 0.4-0.8 mm, apex obtuse, usually appendaged by two cusps, 0.3-0.4 x 0.1 mm; connective outside narrowly deltoid, obtuse, ca. 1.5 x ca. 0.25 mm, glabrous; connective scales lateral as well as apical, ovate, 3.25-3.75 x ca. 1.25 mm, scarious, orange-brown, margin suberose, apex obtuse. Ovary subglobose, ca. 1.25 x 1 mm, ferruginous strigulose; ovules two per placenta. Style filiform, erect, 2.75-3 x 0.2-0.4 mm, exceeding the stamens by 0.25-0.5 mm, strigulose near the base; stigma truncate. Juvenile fruits green when fresh, indument ferruginous strigulose.

description: Tree or treelet 4-15 m tall. Branchlets minutely pilosulous to puberulous; glabrescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 3-7 mm long, minutely pilosulous to glabrescent; stipules soon deciduous, usually wanting; lamina usually narrowly elliptic to obovate, acuminate to cuspidate, 7-20.5 x 2-7.5 cm, papery to coriaceous; lamina, costa and lateral veins glabrous on both sides; lateral veins 8-10 pairs (acumen excluded); tertiary venation scalariform; base rounded to cuneate; margin crenate to serrate, mucronulate; acumen 0-2.5 cm long, apex subobtuse, mucronulate. Inflorescences axillary, lateral and subterminal, 1-5 fasciculate, thyrsoid, 2-7 x 1.52 cm; central axis pilosulous, whitish; cymules 1-5(-7) flowered; common peduncle 1.5-7 mm long, pilosulous, whitish; ‘pedicels’ 2-5 mm long, articulate ½-1/5 from the base, pilosulous, whitish; bracts and bractlets, narrowly ovate to deltoid, herbaceous to scarious, whitish pilosulous, margin ciliolate, apex obtuse, mucronulate; bracts 0.5-1 x 0.25-0.5 mm; bractlets subopposite, 0.25-0.75 x 0.2-0.4. Flower buds ovoid, obtuse. Flowers white. Sepals subequal, elliptic to ovate, 1-1.5 x 0.75-1 mm, herbaceous, obscurely 1-3 veined, margin cili(ol)ate, apex obtuse to rounded. Petals subelliptic, 2.75-3 x 1.25-2 mm, herbaceous, glabrescent, obscurely 1-3 veined, margin scarious and cili(ol)ate, apex rounded. Stamens (2-)2.5-3(-3.5) mm long; apical part of filaments free, 0.4 x 0.2 mm; filamental tube glandular 0.3-0.6 mm high, carnose, 5-lobulate; anthers ovoid, 0.75-1 x 0.4-0.5 mm, barbate at the base, apex obtuse, sometimes appendaged by two cusps ca. 0.3 x ca. 0.1 mm; connective outside linear, ca. 0.5 x ca. 0.2 mm, sometimes barbate at the base; connective scales, exclusively apical, ovate to elliptic, 1-1.75 x 0.75-1 mm, usually longer than the anthers, scarious, orange-brown, margin fringed, apex rounded and fringed. Ovary subglobose to 3-lobed, 1 x 0.75-1 mm, glabrous; ovules one per placenta. Style filiform, slightly curved, (1.5-)2-2.25 mm long, exceeding the stamens by 0-0.5 mm, completely glabrous; stigma truncate or pulvinate. Capsule more or less symmetric, orbicular to ellipsoid, subtended by subpersistent floral parts, coriaceous, glabrous, smooth to obscurely veined; three valves, subequal, 4.25-7 x 2-3 mm, style often subpersistent at the apex of one of the valves. Seeds one per valve, globose, 2.5-3.5 mm in diam., glabrous, shining.

description: Plants glossy, pale green above, blackish in older parts, in grass-like tufts. Leaves rigidly erect to flexuous, wiry, narrowly linear, mostly broken off at midleaf, to 25 mm long, lamina interrupted above cancellinae by interval of naked costa; margins thickened, remotely toothed above, entire to serrate or toothed at shoulders; cancellinae sharply distinct; cells of upper lamina smooth, transversely elongate, often bi-tristratose; costa smooth. Sporophytes unknown.

description: Plants bright green, becoming sordid, sometimes encrusted with diatoms and black detritus, especially costa and limbidium. Stems monomorphic, usually branched, 3.5-16.0mm long x 1.5-3.0 mm wide, usually branched; rhizoids mostly basal, smooth, reddish; axillary hyaline nodules absent; epidermis and outer 1-2 tiers of cortical cells small, incrassate, pigmented; inner cortical cells larger, thin-walled, hyaline; central strand present or absent. Leaves ± crispate when dry, imbricate, as many as 25 pairs, mostly narrowly oblong, infrequently ovate, acute-mucronate or short-acuminate, 0.9-2.7 mm long x 0.3-0.4 mm wide, perichaetial leaves usually longest; costa usually ending in muero or apiculus, bryoides type; margin ± entire, sometimes serrulate distally, rarely distantly serrulate all around, limbate on all laminae, limbidium usually cartilaginous, usually confluent with costa distally and ending above the insertion of dorsal lamina, limbidial cells (1-) 35 (-7)-stratose, outer ones sometimes short and chlorophyllose; dorsal lamina narrowed to insertion, somewhat decurrent; vaginant laminae of cauline leaves mostly 1/2 leaf length, acute, equal; laminal cells distinct, eguttulate, unistratose, infrequently bistratose juxtacostally, firm-walled, smooth, slightly bulging, irregularly quadrate to hexagonal, 6-13 µm long x 6-10 µm wide, in transverse section about as deep as wide, rarely larger in the vaginant laminae. Monoicous (rhizautoicous); perigonia and perichaetia terminal on stems of ± equal length. Sporophytes 1-3 per perichaetium, yellow, darkening with age; seta smooth, 3-6 mm long; theca exserted, erect, radially symmetric or inclined, arcuate, bilaterally symmetric, 0.5-1.0 mm long, stom-atose, exothecial cells quadrate to oblong, vertical walls thicker than horizontal walls; peristome bryoides type; operculum conic, short-rostrate, 0.50.6 mm long. Spores finely papillose, 13-27 p,m diam. Calyptra cucullate, smooth, 0.6-0.7 mm long, covering only rostrum of operculum.

description: Plants olive green. Stems monomorphic, 4-7 mm long x 2-3 mm wide, unbranched; rhizoids basal, smooth, brown; axillary hyaline nodules present; epidermal and outer tier of cortical cells small, incrassate, pigmented; inner cortical cells larger, thin-walled, hyaline; central strand absent. Leaves little changed when dry, imbricate, in 10-20 pairs, linear, acute, 1.8-3.0 mm long x 0.18-0.20 mm wide; margin ± entire, elimbate or infrequently weakly limbate on proximal parts of vaginant laminae of distal-most leaves; costa percurrent or ending 2-3 cells below leaf apex, oblongifolius type, distal part in transverse section showing 2 stereid bands separated by 6 enlarged cells arranged in 2 rows; dorsal lamina narrow, ending well above insertion; vaginant laminae of cauline leaves 1/2 leaf length, acute, ± unequal, minor lamina ending near margin; laminal cells distinct, eguttulate, bistratose in dorsal and ventral laminae, unistratose in vaginant laminae, firm-walled, smooth, slightly bulging, irregularly quadrate to hexagonal, 7-20 µm, marginal cells smaller, juxtacostal cells larger. Gametangia, sporophyte, spores, and calyptra not seen.

description: Plants dark-green, solitary, in clusters of a few or gregarious; rhizoids brown; stems to 2 cm tall but mostly much shorter, not much forked. Leaves to 5 mm or more long, involute and incurved when dry, basically dimorphic, vegetative ones lingulate-lanceolate, gemmiferous ones broadly lanceolate to triangular and clustered in comae at stem tips; margins entire, mostly bordered at least in part with elongate, hyaline cells, sometimes unbordered; cancellinae distinct, distally acute; median cells ca. 7 µm, smooth to unipapillose dorsally and ventrally; gemmae filamentous, borne ventrally along costa from near cancellinae to leaf tip. Seta reddish, 3-4 mm long; capsule 1-2 mm long; peristome teeth irregular, blunt; operculum ca. 1 mm long. Spores 24-36 µm, irregular in shape, granular. Calyptra 3 mm long.

description: Plants pale- to yellow-green, brownish green with age, in loose or dense, glossy mats. Stems complanate-foliate to subjulaceous, to 3 cm long, 1-3 mm wide, simple or irregularly and sparingly branched; axillary hairs with a single short brown basal cell and 3 elongate hyaline apical cells. Leaves lax to stiff, close to distant, erect-spreading, usually imbricate when dry, 1-2 mm long, 0.4-0.8 mm wide, ovate-lanceolate to oblong-ovate, flat or sometimes slightly concave, acuminate, rarely acute; margins plane or incurved below the middle, entire or serrulate near the apex; costa 1/2-3/4 the leaf length; cells smooth or minutely prorulose on dorsal surfaces, median cells 47-165 µm long, 7-9 pm wide; alar cells quadrate to short- rectangular, sometimes oblate, 14-33 pm long, 11-24 µm wide. Autoicous, usually fruiting. Setae yellowish to reddish brown, 0.5-0.8 cm long; capsules orange to reddish brown, inclined to cernuous, 0.8-1.5 mm long, ellipsoidal to ovoid, contracted below mouth when dry; opercula obliquely conic to short-rostrate, 0.2-0.5 mm long. Spores 15-27 pm in diameter.

description: Plants pale- to yellow-green, dark-green to brownish green with age, in loose or dense, glossy mats. Stems usually subjulaceous or sometimes somewhat complanate-foliate, to 4 cm long, 2-4 mm wide, simple or irregularly and sparingly branched; axillary hairs with a single short brown basal cell and 5 rectangular hyaline apical cells. Leaves stiff, close to distant, erect-spreading, mainly imbricate when dry, flat, 1.0-2.5 mm long, 0.5-0.8 mm wide, oblong-lanceolate to oblong-ovate, sometimes lingulate, occasionally cultriform, obtuse or rarely broadly acute; margins plane, serrate to serrulate at the apex, sometimes serrulate below; costa ending at or somewhat above the leaf middle; cells smooth, sometimes weakly prorulose at upper ends on dorsal surfaces near leaf apex; median cells 52-114 µm long, 4-9 |µm wide; alar cells quadrate to short-rectangular, sometimes oblate, 9-24 µm long, 9-14 µm wide. Autoicous. Setae orange to reddish brown, 0.7-1.3 cm long; capsules orange to reddish brown, cernuous, 1.0-1.5 mm long, ellipsoidal to ovoid, contracted below mouth when dry; opercula obliquely short-conic, 0.30.6 mm long. Spores 19-25 µm in diameter.
