description: Dioicous. Plants to 4 cm long × 1.5-3.5 mm wide, glossy green to blackish brown when dry. Branching Lejeunea-type. Stems 0.12-0.25 mm in diam., in cross section composed of 10-13 epidermal cells surrounding 30-70 much smaller ‘medullary cells, the cell walls ± thickened. Leaves imbricate, plane or with upcurved margins when dry, dorsal lobe broadly ovate to suborbicular, 0.7-2 × 0.6-1.8 mm, dorsal margin plane, ventral plane or upcurved, when flattened forming an angle of 90-150× with the keel, margins toothed all around with 10-22 teeth, teeth consisting of 1-10 cells, ventral tooth much larger, of up to 40 cells; median cells ca. 30-45 µm long, frequently somewhat wider than long, orientated in transverse rows, with large cordate trigones and l(-2) intermediate thickenings on longer cell walls; oil bodies small, homogeneous, Massula-type, 15-25 per cell. Lobules triangular-ovate to subrectangular, ca. 0.2-0.8 mm long, l/4-2/5× lobe length, keel concave or almost straight, free margin with (3-)4-6 incurved teeth, teeth 1-3 cells long. Underleaves imbricate, orbicular to transversely ovate, 0.4-0.8 × 0,5-1.5 mm, 4-6× stem width, margins plane or recurved, sharply dentate, teeth often recurved, bases cordate, folded and seemingly auriculate, the "auricles" acute-acuminate, insertion line arched to 0.15-0.3 mm deep. Androecia as in the genus. Gynoecia: bract lobes about as large as leaves, the margins toothed with 12-17 teeth; bracteoles obovate, ca. 0.7-0.9 mm long, margins toothed. Perianths with two dentate-ciliate lateral keeds and one smooth or slightly dentate ventral keel; beak 4-7 cells long, not or slightly recessed. Sporophyte not observed. Vegetative reproduction: cladia occasionally present, basal leaves with rounded apex, margins with numerous small teeth.

description: Gametófito mediano a robusto, verde-claro, verde-amarelado a Castanho, azulado quando seco, prostrado, ramos gemíparos ascendentes, enrolados quando secos, formando emaranhados, 0,5-2,0 mm larg. Ramos adventícios ventrais pouco freqüentes. Talo piano, ligeiramente convexo, a fortemente convexo, dicotomicamente ramificado, dicotomias irregulares, de dois tipos: fortemente atenuado para o ápice formando um flagelo, e não atenuado com ápice obtuso. Em seção transversal lâmina uniestratificada, plana, 15-25(-29) células larg. da costa a margem, células medianas, mamilosas, paredes espessadas, trigônios pequenos, cutícula lisa, (20-)30-50(-60) × 20-36(-42) µm; costa formada por 2 fileiras de células epidérmicas em ambas as superficies, dorsal e ventral; células medulares distintas das epidérmicas; medula 19-24 células, em 4-5 camadas, células de paredes espessadas. Talo esparsamente hirsuto, rizóides medianos, eretos a flexuosos, ramificados ou não, dispostos na margem e superfície ventral da costa, ocasionalmente na superfície ventral da lâmina, na margem esparsos (500 µm = 5-10 rizóides), 1 rizóide por célula, originado na superfície ventral, com extensas regiões sem rizóides, (32-)88-152(-200) µm. Gemas marginais, concentradas no ápice do talo atenuado (ramos ascendentes), discóides, côncavas, células mamilosas, rizóides rudimentares (ca. 4 células larg.). Dióico. Ramo masculino grande, globoso a subgloboso, sem rizóides, 280-380 µm. Invólucro feminino obovado, com entalhe apical, hirsuto, rizóides na margem e superfície externa, 250-300 µm. Apresenta desenvolvimento externo do invólucro feminino em talo vegetativo. Caliptra membranosa, obpiriforme a cilíndrica, hirsuta, rizóides pequenos, abundantes no ápice e ausentes na base, seção transversal 3-4 camadas de células, 1,0-1,3 mm compr. Seta não observada. Cápsula oblonga, valvas com espessamentos nodulosos conspícuos na parede externa (Tipo-3), sem expansão tangencial, e espessamentos semianulares conspícuos na parede interna (Tipo-3), sem expansão tangencial. Elatérios pequenos a medianos, castanho-avermelhados, 112-375 µm compr. Esporos pequenos a medianos, castanhos, finamente granulosos, 20-27 µm diâm.

description: Paroicous. Plants rather long and slender, ca. 4-5 cm long, green to black when alive, becoming dark brown to black in the dried condition. Branching Frullania-type, Lejeunea-type branches not observed. Stems averaging 0.2 mm in diam., in cross section composed of 18-25 epidermal cells surrounding ca. 45-70 smaller medullary cells; ventral merophyte 8 cell rows wide. Leaves loosely imbricate, dorsal lobe ovate, 1-1.2 × 0.6-0.8 mm, apex apiculate, recurved. Lobules ovate-triangular, 0.4-0.5 × 0.3-0.4 mm, with 5-6 teeth, the teeth (2-)3-4 cells long, erect with the upper cell(s) inflexed. Underleaves contiguous to subimbricate, suborbicular, averaging 0.7-0.8 mm wide, with rather small auricles and deeply arched insertion line. Androecia located a few leaf cycles below the gynoecium, bracts in 3-6 series, similar to leaves, lobule tooth not reduced, antheridia one per bract. Gynoecia as in F. densifolia spp. densifolia. Sporophyte not observed.

description: Gametófito mediano a robusto, castanho-amarelado quando seco, 1,2-1,7 mm larg. Ramos adventícios ventrais raros. Talo convexo, dicotomica-mente ramificado, dicotomias irregulares, de dois tipos, gradualmente atenuado e não atenuado, ápice obtuso, sem papilas mucilagiíferas. Em seção transversal lâmina uniestratificada, 18-25 células larg. da costa à margem, células medianas a grandes, planas, paredes ligeiramente espessadas, trigônios pequenos, cutícula lisa, 33-96 × 18-44 µm; costa ligeira a fortemente arqueada para ambas as superfícies, 2-6 fileiras de células epidérmicas em ambas as superfícies, dorsal e ventral, células dorsais protundentes; células medulares ligeiramente distintas das epidermicas; medula com 21-44 celulas, em 4-7(-8) ca-madas, celulas de paredes ligeiramente espessadas. Talo masculino menor que o feminino, 0,5-1,5 mm de larg., costa 2-4 fileiras de células epidérmicas em ambas as superfícies, lâmina 11-22 células. Talo densamente hirsuto, rizóides medianos a longos, fortemente falcados, densamente dispostos na margem e superfície ventral da costa, esparsos na superficie ventral da lâmina, na margem densos (500 µm=20-25 rizóides), 2 rizóides por célula, mesclados com 1 ou 3 rizóides, 160-300 µm. Gemas mucilaginosas nos ápices atenuados, gemas marginais ocasionais, nos ápices dos talos atenuados, planas, discóides a elípticas, rizóides eretos (4-6 células de larg.). Dióico. Ramo masculino subgloboso, sem rizóides, 220-540 µm. Invólucro feminino obovado, com ou sem entalhe apical, hirsuto, rizóides eretos, dispostos na margem e superfície externa, 120-280 µm. Caliptra claviforme, densamente hirsuta, rizóides eretos, concentrados no ápice, 1,0-1,2 mm compr. Esporófito maduro desconhecido.

description: Thalli forming rosettes 6-10 mm in diam., or in gregarious patches; lobes 2-4 times deeply forked, 2.5-3 mm long, 0.5-1 (-1.5) mm wide, flat and thin basally, rounded or slightly emarginate apically; dorsal side light brown or grayish when dry; flanks hyaline, often with pink-violaceous spots. Median groove shallow, wide. Ventral scales hyaline or pink-violaceous, short, not reaching lobe margins. Cilia few, on lateral borders of dorsal side and in upper part of flanks, numerous near apex of lobes, isolated or absent below, 60-215 µm long, 30-35 µm wide basally, acute or obtuse apically, granulose to 1/2-2/3 of length. Cross section of lobes 0.6 mm high, 7-8 cells thick; dorsal edge ascending and rounded laterally; flanks rounded apically; ventral edge convex; dorsal and ventral tissues hardly distinct. Monoecious. Spores (85-) 100-120 µm diam., orange-brown or light red-brown; wing 4-5 µm wide, irregular, sometimes narrow or nearly absent, translucent, margins crenulate-mamillose; distal face with (10-) 12-16 areoles across diam., each of 10-15 µm diam., with dark ridges often thickened near pole and large tubercles; proximal face with numerous areoles of 10 µm diam., with low ridges, the ridges ill-defined, papillose and tuberculate, triradiate scar weak.

description: Dioicous; plants usually long and robust, 3-10 cm long × 2.5-4 mm wide, deep green to blackish, becoming brown or blackish when dry. Stems in cross section composed of ca. 18-25 epidermal cells surrounding numerous medullary cells; ventral merophyte 7-10 cell rows wide. Leaves loosely imbricate, widely spreading when moist, bent downwards when dry, dorsal lobe ovate-oblong to oblong, ca. 1.1-2.8 mm long × 1-1.25 mm wide, apex broadly rounded, sometimes apiculate, margins plane or somewhat recurved, ventral margin almost straight, forming a sharp angle with the keel, margins toothed near apex and along the ventral margin, the teeth regularly spatiated, on stems ca. 4-15 per leaf, fewer on branches, teeth l-3(-4) cells long, the tooth at apex often longer; median cells about 20-35 µm in largest diam.; oil bodies homogeneous, Massula-type, 12-20 per cell, oblong-ovate, 4-7 µm long. Lobules obovate-obtriangular, never reduced, up to l/4× lobe length, keel straight or arched, free margin ± straight, with 3-4 short, evenly spatiated teeth, teeth 1-2 cells long, often inflexed. Underleaves subimbricate, strongly concave and with recurved apex and lateral margins, broadly orbicular, 4-6× stem width, apex rounded, margins sharply toothed to near the base or in the upper half only, bases broadly decurrent, sometimes auriculate. Androecia with 8-12 series of bracts. Gynoecia with two subfloral innovations, bract lobes ca. 2 mm long × 1 mm wide, apex acute-apiculate, margins sharply toothed in the upper half or ± entire, lobules narrow ovate-lanceolate, up to l/2× lobe length, with a few teeth; bracteole ± oblong, 1-1.5 mm long, apex short bifid with sharply pointed lobes, margins sharply and irregularly dentate-ciliate above. Perianths usually long exserted, ca. 3 mm long × 2 mm wide. Sporophyte as in the genus.

description: Plants medium-sized or small; green, or brownish green. Stem somewhat rigid, irregularly branched in one plane; central strand present and slender or absent in weaker stems; hyalodermis absent; pseudoparaphyllia broad, rounded or triangular; paraphyllia absent; rhizoids smooth, slightly branched, inserted at or just below costa insertion; axillary hairs with 1-3-celled upper part, this hyaline when young. Stem leaves slightly to strongly falcate-secund (gradually curved) from ± erect or sub-complanate base, rarely almost straight, slightly twisted when dry, ovate or triangular-ovate or narrow-triangular-ovate, narrowing gradually to acuminate or short-acuminate or often blunt apex, curved, strongly concave, not decurrent; margin near apex denticulate, otherwise entire; costa double, thin, ending to 40% of way up leaf, sometimes forked and ending to 60% of way up leaf, sometimes very short, often variable within the same plant; median laminal cells 23.0-88.0 × 5.0-7.5(-8.5) µm, unistratose, incrassate or slightly incrassate, eporose, toward leaf apex frequently distally and abaxially prorate (especially in leaves with relatively short apices); alar cells undifferentiated or with a few rectangular or isodiametric cells that form a small and poorly delimited isodiametric or triangular group in outermost leaf comer. Branch leaves smaller, usually more ovate and more short-acuminate than stem leaves (thus more often with prorate upper laminal cells); proximal branch leaves ovate or almost orbicular, with rounded apex. Dioicous. Perigonial leaves narrowing abruptly from broad base to long acumen (as long or almost as long as basal leaf); apex acuminate. Inner perichaetial leaves erect-flexuose, narrowing abruptly to long, narrow acumen; apex acuminate; not plicate; vaginula with paraphyses. Calyptra not seen. Seta long (13-20 mm), orange, smooth; capsule cylindrical, straight, curved in transition to seta, constricted below mouth when dry, horizontal to cernuous; operculum conical, with central mammilla; annulus separating; stomata round- or ovate-pored. Exostome well developed, yellow-brown, cross-striolate on outer surface below, sometimes with minute papillae on top of striolations, shallowly furrowed in upper part of cross-striolate portion, papillose above; margin entire or almost so, border not or hardly widened at zone of transition in outside pattern, trabeculae normally developed. Endostome well developed, with high basal membrane; segments not perforate; cilia 1-3, long and nodose. Spores 14.5-17.0 µm, finely papillose.

description: Planta minor, brunnea. Caulis irregulariter multi-ramosus, 3-4 ordines medullosos cellularum habens. Folia imbricata, ovata, apice rotundata. Amphigastria minora, ad 1/2 inciso-biloba, sinu lato, marginibus dentatis. Gynoecia uno latere innovata; folia floralia obovata, integerrima; amphigastrium florale oblongum, ad 1/2 inciso-bilobum. Perianthia pyriformia, apice cuadriplicata, plicis latis, comis nullis.

description: Plants dioicous?, light brown, leafy shoots 0.4-0.6 mm wide; sparsely branched. Stems 30-45 µm in diameter, medullary cells 3-4 in cross section, ventral cells in surface view mostly rectangular, 25-35 × 3555 µm, thin-walled, dorsal cells mostly rectangular, 25-40 × 30-45 µm, thin-walled. Flagelliferous branches not seen. Leaves imbricate, lobes ovate, 160-260 × 250-350 µm, apex rounded, plane, margins entire or slightly crenulate; median leaf cells isodiametrical to elliptical, 10-25 × 20-30 µm, walls thick, irregularly thickened, intermediate thickenings frequent, trigones conspicuous, sometimes confluent, marginal cells quadrate to short rectangular, 10-15 X 10-20 JLim; oil bodies not seen; ocelli 15-30 X 3555 JLim, basal, 2 per leaf, contiguous; lobules ovoid or reduced, 0.3-0.6 the leaf lobe length, free margin involute, apical tooth unicellular, curved, hyaline papilla proximal. Utriculi absent. Underleaves 50-100 X 95-145 |im, bifid to Vz, sinus U-shaped, lobes lanceolate-acuminate, uniseriate tip 1-3 cells long, each margin constantly bearing l(-2) unicellular teeth. Androecia intercalary on main branches, with 1-3 pairs of bracts, 250-560 µm long. Gynoecia on lateral branches with one sterile innovation; bracts obovate, 270 × 500 µm, margins entire or slightly crenulate, apex rounded or broadly acute, bract lobules obovate, 140-170 × 400-450 µm, apex acute; bracteole long rectangular, 175 × 375-400 µm, bifid to ca. 1/2, lobes long acuminate, uniseriate tip 2-3 cells long, with 1-2 teeth on the sinus margin. Perianth obconic, 430-470 × 630-650 µm, with four inflated carinae that do not protrude from the perianth body. Sporophyte with short seta; capsule with four colorless valves, 60 × 115 µm. Elaters 7.5 × 160 µm, single spiraled, 5(?) per valve. Spores not seen.

description: Plants dioicous or monoicous, pale brown, leafy shoot 0.5-1.5 mm wide; sparsely branched. Stems in cross section 70-110 µm in diameter, medullary cells 6-15, ventral cells in surface rectangular to quadrate, 25-45 × 25-85 µm, dorsal cells rectangular to quadrate, 20-40 × 25-55 (im. Flagelliferous branches not seen. Leaves imbricate, lobe ovate to slightly asymmetric-ovate, 320-780 × 400-950 µm, apex rounded or broadly acute, plane or slightly incurved, margins entire or crenulate by projecting cells; median leaf lobe cells isodiametrical to short-elliptical, 15-30 × 25-45 (µm, marginal leaf lobe cells quadrate to rectangular, 10-25 × 15-30 µm, intermediate thickenings rare, middle lamellae with hardly noticeable pale brown color, cuticle smooth or papillose; oil bodies not seen; ocelli scarcely differentiated from normal leaf cells, 25-0 × 40-70 µm, 2(0-5) per leaf, suprabasal or basal, contiguous or isolated, when basal, frequently distant from the lobule free margin; lobules inflated or completely reduced, 0.2-0.4 the leaf lobe length, free margin involute. Utriculi absent. Underleaves distant to imbricate, broadly ovate to reniform, 110-300 × 140-300 µm, bifid to 1/3, sinus broad, lobes acuminate, uniseriate tip 1-2 cells long, margins crenulate by bulging cells or with blunt projections, plane. Vegetative reproduction by gemmae rare, gemmae marginal on old stem leaves, irregularly shaped, papillose. Androecia on lateral branches, rarely intecalary, in spikes of 3-6 pairs of bracts, spikes 600-900 µm long. Gynoecia on lateral branches with one sterile innovation; bracts elliptical to obovate, 400-430 × 700-800 µm, margins entire, bract lobule lanceolate, 230 × 300 µm; bracteole ovate, 340 × 550 (im, bifid to 1/3, lobes acuminate, margins entire, connate at the base with the bracts. Perianth obconic, 300-410 × 450-600 µm, with four flat, short distally collapsed and ramified horns, ca. 130 µm long, margins irregular. Sporophyte not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Dauphin L, G. 2003. Ceratolejeunea. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 90: 1-86.

description: Autoicous. Plants to 4 cm long × 1.5-2.0 mm wide, dull, yellow brown to dark brown (not black) when dry. Branching irregularly pinnate, Lejeunea-type, flageliform branches lacking. Stems in cross section ca. 7-8 cells across, composed of ca. 10-15 epidermal cells surrounding ca. 20 medullary cells, cell walls colorless and thickened, those of the medulla more strongly than those of the epidermis, epidermis symmetric. Leaves contiguous to imbricate, dorsal lobe often convex, asymmetrically ovate-oblong, 0.5-1  × 0.3-0.7 mm, apex rounded to apiculate, plane or narrowly recurved, margins entire, dorsal base straight, ventral margin forming an angle of 120-170° with the keel; leaf cells in mid-leaf 25-50 µm, trigones strong, radiate, intermediate thickenings frequent, well-developed; oil bodies not observed. Lobules ovoid-triangular, sometimes reduced, when well-developed 0.25-0.35 × 0.20.3 mm, l/4-l/2× lobe length, free margin without or with a rudimentary tooth. Underleaves distant to subimbricate, transversely ovate to reniform, ca. 0.3-0.4 mm long × 0.4.5-0.9 mm wide, (4-)5-8× stem width, apex plane, bases straight or rounded, sometimes decurrent, insertion line arched, to 100 µm deep. Androecia on specialized branches, bracts in 6-7 series. Gynoecia on short or long branches, without true subfloral innovations, occasionally with a pseudo-innovation of the Lejeunea-type, bract lobes plane or convex with incurved apex, asymmetrically oblong, acute-apiculate, dorsal margin strongly toothed above, ventral margin with a few teeth or entire, lobule narrow rectangular-ligulate, l/3-l/2× lobe length, not extended beyond the keel, margin entire or with l(-2) teeth near apex; bracteoles ovate, ca. 0.8 mm long × 0.8-1 mm wide, up to l/2× perianth length, apex short bifid, margins dentate above, plane. Perianths exserted to 1/2 of its length, obpyriform, apex truncate, with 4-5 sharp keels: 2 lateral keels, 2 ventral keels and sometimes a low dorsal keel, lateral and ventral keels extending over 1/2-3/4 of perianth length, sparingly dentate above, dorsal keel entire, short or lacking short or lacking; beak low, ca. 3 cells long, not recessed. Sporophyte not observed. Terpenoids: 5-hydroxycalamene is the major component of this species (Gradstein et al., 1985).
bibliographicCitation: Gradstein, S. Robbert. 1994. Lejeuneaceae: Ptychantheae, Brachiolejeuneae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 62: 216.

description: Dioicous. Plants 1-3 cm long × 1-1.5 mm wide, brownish-green when dry. Stems 0.1-0.12 in diam., in cross section composed of 16-20 epidermal cells surrounding 30-35 medullary cells; ventral merophyte 4-6 cell rows wide. Leaves subimbricate, plane, diverging from stem at an angle of 60°-75°(-90°), sometimes falcate, dorsal lobe asymmetrically oblong, 0.5-0.9 × 0.3-0.5 mm, apex broadly rounded, capped by a group of thin-walled, elongated, 20-25 µm long dead cells in 2-4 rows, forming a whitish border, border fragile, breaking off in older leaves, leaving an irregularly crenate leaf tip; ventral leaf margin straight, forming an almost continuous line (angle 160°-190°) with the keel except for a small indention at the sinus; row of ocelli 8-20 cells long, uniseriate throughout, separated from leaf base by 0-2 ordinary cells; oil bodies not observed. Lobules ovoid, ca. 0.15 × 0.1 mm, 1/5-1/3 leaf length, flattened towards free margin and apex, keel slightly curved, smooth, border cells of free margin colorless, apical tooth 3-5 cells long, 2 cells wide at base. Underleaves orbicular to transversely ovate, 0.2-0.3 mm long x 0.25-0.4 mm wide, 3-4x stem width, plane, insertion line straight or slightly curved. Androecia on short-specialized branches or terminal on elongated branches, bracts in 3-5 series, underleaves present throughout the spike but becoming smaller above. Gynoecia with 1-2 sterile or fertile innovations, bract lobules ovate-triangular, 2-Ax longer than the keel, apex of lobules rounded to obtuse, keel with a 1 cell wide wing, row of ocelli short or rudimentary, consisting of a few groups of 1-3 ocelli separated from each other by 1-2 ordinary cells; bracteoles elongated obovate, 0,5 mm long × 0,4 mm wide, apex rounded. Perianths with or without distinct auricles, when with auricles obovate-oblong, distinctly emergent, ca. 1-1.2 mm long × 0.7-0.8 mm wide, apex deeply and narrowly retuse, lateral keels narrowly and interruptedly winged (wing 1-3 cells wide), especially on the auricles, ventral keel well-developed, rounded or with 2 (-3) folds in the upper half, sometimes horn-like expanded distally, dorsal keel low and narrow; when without auricles (e.g. Puerto Rico, Evans 143) obcuneate, 0.6-0.7 × 0.5-0.6 mm, apex truncate or shallowly emarginate, lateral keels unwinged or with rudimentary wings, ventral keel low, with two folds, dorsal keel lacking. Sporophyte not observed.
bibliographicCitation: Gradstein, S. Robbert. 1994. Lejeuneaceae: Ptychantheae, Brachiolejeuneae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 62: 216.

description: Small tree 4-8 m tall. Branches glabrous or sparsely puberulent with glandular and eglandular hairs less than 0.5 mm long. Leaf blades simple, unlobed, subcoriaceous, acuminate at apex, glabrous to sparsely eglandular-pilose and glandular-puberulent adaxially, glabrous to sparsely glandular-puberulent abaxially; petioles glabrous or minutely papillose. Trunk leaves simple, unlobed, the blade ovate-elliptic, 20-37 cm long, 15-28 cm wide, length: width ratio ca. 1.5:1, the base cordate with basal lobes 3-4 cm long; petioles 10-22 cm long. Crown leaves 4 per sympodial unit, simple, unlobed, the blade ovate, 5-18 cm long, 4-13 cm wide, length:width ratio 1-2:1, the base cordate, sometimes oblique, with basal lobes 1-3.5 cm long; petioles 2-7.5 cm long. Inflorescence branched, 40-100+ -flowered, 8-20 cm long; peduncle 3-5 cm long; rachises 3-14 cm long; pedicels 15-25 mm long, 40 mm long in fruit, 1-2(-5) mm apart, articulated at the base, leaving pedicellar remnants 0.5-1 mm long; peduncle, rachises, and pedicels glabrous or sparsely glandular-puberulent. Flower buds ovoid to ellipsoidal, acuminate at apex. Calyx succulent, glabrous, the radius 4-5 mm, the lobes 1-3 mm long, 3 mm wide, obtuse, minutely apiculate. Corolla lavender or greenish-purple mottled with dark violet, coriaceous, stellate, the radius 10-19 mm, the tube 1-2 mm long, the lobes narrowly triangular, 8-17 mm long, 2.5-3 mm wide, glabrous abaxially, sparsely to moderately puberulent adaxially especially toward apex, the margin tomentose, the apex acute. Anther thecae purple, lanceolate, 6-7 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide, the pores introrse and directed distally; connective dark purple, lanceolate, 5-7 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, abaxially slightly shorter than thecae at apex, equal to or slightly exceeding them at base, adaxially present between bases of thecae. Ovary glabrous; style cylindrical, glabrous, not dilated distally, 6-7 mm long, 0.5-1 mm in diam., slightly shorter than to exserted 1-2 mm beyond stamens; stigma truncate, 0.5-1 mm in diam. Fruit ellipsoidal, ovoid, or globose, obtuse at apex, 6-10 cm long, 5.5-7 cm in diam., glabrous, yellow or orange when ripe; mesocarp with stone cell aggregates; seeds 6-9 mm long, 4-7 mm wide, densely pubescent.
bibliographicCitation: Bohs, Lynn A. 1994. Cyphomandra (Solanaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 63: 154.

description: Plants dioicous?, green or brown to almost black, creeping to hanging, leafy shoot 0.75-2.0 mm wide, with profuse, short lateral branches (subsimple). Stems 125-145 µm in diameter, medullary cells 18-29 in cross section, ventral cells in surface view quadrate to rectangular, 25-70 × 25-110 µm, dorsal cells quadrate to rectangular, 45-60 × 55-70 µm. Lateral branches becoming flagelliferous, leaflets 150-460 × 240-700 µm, antical leaflet lobe margins entire in younger branches to roughly toothed in older ones, with 5-10 teeth. Stem leaves imbricate; lobe ovate from a wide base, sometimes asymmetrical, 620-720 × 830-900 µm, antical margins entire or sometimes toothed at the apical region, teeth 0-4, 1-2 cells long, ca. 10 µm long, postical margin entire, apex rounded or broadly acute, incurved or plane; median leaf lobe cells isodiametrical to elliptical, 20-30 × 20-60 µm; marginal cells quadrate to rectangular, 10-20 × 1520 µm; oil bodies granular, elliptical, 2-5 per cell; ocelli long-hexagonal, 30-40 × 50-60 µm, basal, 0-1 per leaf; lobules ovoid, reduced or spherical, 0.2 the leaf lobe length, free margin involute or plane, with apical tooth short or long and curved; hyaline papilla bulging. Utriculi frequent, in pairs or solitary at the base of lateral branches, rounded to reniform. Underleaves imbricate, long ovate to reniform, 370-950 × 310-880 µm, lobes acute, ending in a one-celled tip, margins entire, plane or rarely incurved, base frequently cordate, with rounded asymmetrical lobes. Vegetative regeneration from laminar leaf lobe cells reported by Fulford (1944b). Androecia in lateral spikes of 3-6 pairs of bracts, spikes 500-1125 µm long. Gynoecia with one or two innovations, fertile or sterile, bracts toothed to laciniate; bracteole ovate, 300-500 × 400-550 µm. Perianth obconical, 400-450 × 530-920 µm, horns long, slender. Sporophyte seta 145 µm in diameter, ca. 1200 µm long. Elaters 290 µm long. Spores 32.5 × 77.5 µm, rosettes simple.
bibliographicCitation: Dauphin L, G. 2003. Ceratolejeunea. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 90: 1-86.

description: Plants autoicous, pale green to reddish brown, leafy shoot 0.5-1.5(-l.8) mm wide, profusely and irregularly branched (plumose). Stems in cross section 65-90(-125) µm in diameter, medullary cells 10-21, ventral cells in surface view quadrate to rectangular, 15-40(-65) × 30-50(-85) µm, dorsal cells subquadrate to rectangular, 20-40(-55) × 25-60(-80) µm. Flagelliferous branches common, 0.3 mm wide including leaves; lobes of leaves on flagelliferous branches with rounded apices, 90-120 × 180-230 µm, lobules 0.7 the leaf lobe length. Leaves imbricate, lobe asymmetric-ovate, frequently patent, 250-540 (-650) × 420-680(-920) µm, antical margin entire, crenulate or finely to roughly toothed, with 0-30 teeth, 5-25(-35) µm long, postical margin usually entire or with 2 teeth; median leaf cells with rounded to short-elliptic lumina, 10-25(-35) × 15-50 µm; walls thin, intermediate thickenings rare; ocelli 25-50 × 40-75 µm, basal or geminate, l-4(-7) per leaf; oil bodies smooth (Dauphin 2691 (GOET)); lobules ovoid, spherical or rarely reduced, 0.2-0.5 the leaf lobe length, free margin involute or plane, apical tooth projecting, curved. Utriculi frequent, solitary or in pairs at the base of lateral branches. Underleaves distant to subimbricate, ovate, 120-400 × 110-400 µm, bifid to 2/3, lobes rounded or acute, ending in a one-celled tip, margins entire, crenulate or with a tooth, plane. Androecia lateral or terminal on main stems, in spikes of 2-4(-8) pairs of bracts, 340-650(-800) µm long, bracteole single, ovate, 65-181 X 75-180 µm, bifid to 1/2. Gynoecia on lateral branches, with one sterile innovation; bracts obovate, 300 × 450-550 µm, margins entire, toothed distally; bracteoles ovate to ligulate, 200-620 × 350-780 µm, bifid to 1/4, margins entire or sparsely toothed. Perianth 330-450 × 430-650 µm, with four inflated, erect horns, 110-200(-600) µm long. Elaters 12.5 × 265-330 µm. Spores irregularly shaped, mostly rectangular, 15-25 × 40-70 µm, surface verruculose.
bibliographicCitation: Dauphin L, G. 2003. Ceratolejeunea. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 90: 1-86.

description: Subshrub 0.4-1.5 m, the branchlets terete, puberulous, occasionally with whitish lenticels. Leaves simply pinnate, with puberulous canaliculate rachis and (3-)5-9 sessile or very short petiolulate obovate to oblong-elliptic leaflets, these 1.5-9 cm long and 0.7-5 cm wide, apex rounded or retuse, sometimes slightly apiculate, the base cuneate to rounded, usually scabrous above with small erect trichomes, with longer erect trichomes below, these concentrated along the intricately prominent tertiary and secondary venation, coriaceous, more or less bullate, the margin entire or occasionally with a few coarse teeth, the upper surface intricately prominulous-reticulate. Inflorescence usually a narrow racemiform terminal panicle, sometimes more freely branching, densely puberulous, sometimes with small oblanceolate leaf-like bracts. Flowers with the calyx cupular, 5-dentate, 3-6 mm long, 3-6 mm wide, puberulous, sometimes in part with gland-tipped trichomes; corolla magenta with bluish lobes, tubular-campanulate above a narrow basal tube, 3-5 cm long, 0.7-1.5 cm wide at mouth, the lobes 0.5-1 cm long, the tube 2.5-4 cm long, sparsely puberulous outside with short simple and gland-tipped trichomes, especially near base, inside glabrous except at the stamen insertion; stamens didynamous, the anthers dithecate, each theca 2 mm long, the long staminode 2.5-3.5 cm long, subexserted, the middle third glandular-villous, the apex mostly nonglandular villous, with short gland-tipped trichomes on apical bifurcation, otherwise glabrous; ovary flattened-ovate, 1.5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, glabrous; disk annular-pulvinate, 0.5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide. Fruit orbicular or suborbicular, subwoody, 2.5-3 cm long, 2-3 cm wide, the margin not undulate at dehiscence, somewhat lepidote, otherwise glabrous, drying blackish; seeds not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Gentry, Alwyn H. 1992. Bignoniaceae--part II (Tribe Tecomeae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 25: 1-370.

description: Plant flowering 4-9 dm high. Leaves several in a subfasciculate rosette, to 4 dm long, densely white-cretaceous, especially toward the base, light green; sheaths elliptic, about as long as the blades; blades triangular, acute, 4-5 cm wide. Scape erect, 5-10 mm in diameter, soon glabrous; scape-bracts erect, the lower foliaceous and densely imbricate, the upper very broadly ovate, apiculate, often shorter than the internodes. Inflorescence bipinnate or rarely simple, up to 3 dm long; primary bracts very broadly ovate, apiculate, mostly shorter than the sterile base of the spike; spikes suberect, long-stipitate, rather laxly many-flowered. Floral bracts broadly ovate to suborbicular, obtuse, 6-8 mm long, coriaceous; flowers perfect or rarely dimorphic (Mexico), suberect. Sepals strongly asymmetric, obovate, to 12 mm long and 9 mm wide, equaling or exceeding the petals, coriaceous; petals ovate-elliptic, white; stamens included, unequal, the first series distinctly longer than the second; filaments of the second series short-connate with the petals; anthers obtuse, 2 mm long; style distinct, one third as long as the ovary. Capsule stoutly ellipsoid, barely exceeding the sepals.

description: Plant imperfectly known. Leaves probably all alike and persistent, 7 dm long or more, exceeding the inflorescence; blades narrowed for a long distance above the base but not distinctly petiolate, 35 mm wide, entire, coriaceous when dry, glabrous above, covered below with a dense pulverulent layer of buff scales. Scape distinct, soon glabrous; scape-bracts foliaceous, elongate and exceeding the inflorescence, acuminate, green, densely and coarsely tomentose-lepidote especially below. Inflorescence simple, sub-corymbose, few-flowered. Floral bracts like the scape-bracts, 6-8 cm long, much exceeding the sepals, sparsely villous-lepidote below; pedicels slender, 1 cm long, tomentulose with ferruginous scales. Sepals acuminate, 25 mm long, ecarinate, glabrous; ovary two-thirds superior.

description: Plants epiphytic; fronds pendent, determinate; rhizome erect, radial, with ventral root insertion, scaly, the scales 1-1.5 x 0.2-0.3 mm, lanceolate, the apex short-attenuate, clathrate, dark brown, glabrous or with only a single apical cilium; petiole absent to 1 x 0.3 mm, dark brown, narrowly winged, glabrescent, the hairs ca. 0.1 mm long, appressed, 1-furcate, 3-celled, yellowish; lamina tol2 cm long, narrowly oblong to narrowly elliptic, membranaceous, deeply pinnatisect, 15-30 pairs of segments, abruptly reduced at the base with 2-4 basal segments about 1/2 shorter than the median ones, long-decurrent onto petiole base, broadest in the middle, but showing periodic constrictions, the apex gradually reduced, pinnatifid, not ending in a conform or subconform segment; rachis straight to slightly flexuous, with dark sclerenchyma visible on both sides, sparsely pubescent abaxially, glabrescent adaxially, hairs ca. 0.1 mm long, appressed, simple, 2-celled, yellowish; segments ca. 5 x 2 mm, undulate, set 70-80 to rachis, widened and symmetric at the base, short-decurrent basiscopically, cuneate and lobulate acroscopically, the base attached parallel on the rachis (i.e., both sides inserted along the same radius), the lobule not overlapping the base of the next segment, the apex acute, the margin deeply crenulate to pinnatifid on both sides, plane, glabrous, abaxial lamina surface glabrescent, the hairs similar to those of the rachis abaxially, adaxial lamina surface glabrous; sinuses about the same size as the segments; venation pinnate, with 3-4 pairs of veins per segment; costae with blankish sclerenchyma obscured by laminar tissue on both sides, sparsely pubescent abaxially, the hairs similar to those of the rachis abaxially, glabrous adaxially; veins simple, without blackish sclerenchyma ending in hydathodes that lack calcareous deposits-sori medial, rounded, not protruding beyond the costa and margin, to 2(-3) pairs per segment, slightly sunken; sporangial capsules glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Labiak Evangelista, Paulo H. 2013. Grammitid ferns (Polypodiaceae). I. Lellingeria. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 111: 1--130.

description: Hierba 10-35 cm de alto, base leñosa; ramas una a numerosas, frecuentemente decumbentes, tortuosas, corteza rojiza con grietas longitudinales; ramas jóvenes con pelos glandulares, porrecto-estrellados, radio central 2-3 mm long, y simples cortos tenues. Yemas axilares 1-2, la basal florífera; ramas seriales a veces desarrolladas. Hojas a veces viscosas, discoloras en seco. Estípulas reducidas a prominencias glandulares cónicas 0.3-0.4 mm long. Pecíolo 0.5-4 mm long., indumento como el del tallo. Lámina ovada o latiovada, a veces elíptica, angustiovada o suborbicular, raramente obovada, 14-31 x 9-24 mm, relación largo:ancho = 0.8-2.2:l, base redondeada o cuneada, a veces cordada; ápice obtuso o subagudo; margen plano o ligeramente revoluto, aserrado-crenado o crenulado, dientes subagudos u obtusos, con pelos glandulares; haz lustrosa, oscura, pardo-rojiza, con pelos porrecto-estrellados 4-8-radiados, 0.5-2 mm long.; envés con pelos estrellados y glandulares, 4-5 pares de venas laterales poco prominentes, con pelos porrecto-estrellados, rectas o incurvas, ángulo de divergencia 30-45°, perdiéndose cerca del margen; venas terciarias y venación menor inconspicuas. Flores axilares, solitarias, heterostilas. Alabastro lacrimiforme. Pedúnculo cilindrico, 6-20 mm long. Profilos no desarrollados o reducidos a prominencias glandulares. Pedicelo ligeramente más grueso, 3-11 mm long., indumento como el del tallo. Cáliz 7-14 mm long.; tubo calicino 1.5-2 mm long, indumento laxo por fuera, pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares; lóbulos internos glabrescentes a ambos lados, sin banda de pelos sedosos antes de los bordes membranáceos, cara interna glabra, mucrón 0.3-1 mm long. Corola rosada o color salmón pálido o subido, 12.5-20 mm long.; pétalos 10-18 x 8-10 mm, venas violáceas o purpúreas. Corona fucsia o purpúrea, 1-1.5 mm long., borde superior laciniado. Filamentos estaminales amarillos, soldados 0.6 mm en la base al tubo calicino, glabros, 3.5-4 mm en flores longistilas, 7-8 mm long, en flores brevistilas; anteras 2-2.5 mm long., filamento inserto a 0.6-0.8 mm de la base emarginada, ápice recurvado en la dehiscencia. Ovario hirsuto, 2-2.5 mm long., placentas 8-12 ovuladas; estilos amarillos, 4 mm long, en flores longistilas, 1.5-2.5 mm en flores brevistilas, cilindricos, glabros o con algunos pelos; estigma 0.6-1 mm long., penicilado. Frutos 5.5-7 mm long.; valvas pardo-amarillentas o pardo-rojizas, tuberculadas por fuera, con pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares, por dentro glabras, ligeramente reticuladas, algo lustrosas, amarillentas o jaspeadas. Semillas obovoides, 2-2.4 x 1-1.4 mm, rectas, lado rafeal casi convexo; exóstoma cónico, breve; rafe linear; cálaza entre redondeada y anchamente cónica; episperma glabro, reticulado, aréolas más o menos cuadrangulares o transrectangulares; arilo más corto que la semilla, ancho, envolvente o unilateral, 1.2 mm long.

description: Shrub or small tree to 9 m high, often gnarled and tortuous in appearance, the trunk to 20 cm in diam; plants glabrous except for the inflorescence; young twigs terete or narrowly 4-winged; bark of older trunk thick and somewhat corky ; wood soft. Petioles 1.0-3.0 mm long; blades thick, 3.3-8.0(-10.0) cm long, 1.7-3.2(-3.9) cm wide, oblong-elliptic to ovate-elliptic to elliptic or slightly obovate-elliptic, mostly rounded to emarginate at the apex or seldom acute, with a mucro, acute with an included angle of 60° to rounded or rarely cordate with a shallow notch at base; midrib plane or slightly elevated above, low-rounded to plane below or with 2 low angles or rarely with very narrow wings; lateral nerves invisible or nearly so above and below when dry. Midrib xylem tubular; stomatal crypts a modified Type III, averaging in a leaf ca 22-35 µ in diam, 46-68 µ high, 140-282 per sq mm (extremes 18-55 µ diam, 45-70 µ high, 140-350 per sq mm); upper epidermis varying from one to two cells thick in the same leaf, almost always with mucilaginous walls occasional to frequent in the inner of the doubled cells and sometimes in the single cells; hypodermis none; free stone cells present only in petiole; terminal sclereids columnar, often slanting and curving, branching at both ends, spreading out beneath the epidermises. Inflorescences mostly ramiflorous, at leafless nodes on twigs 1.5-22.0 mm thick or by report on the trunk as well, rarely in the lower leaf axils, 1-several per side, each 1-5-flowered, 1.0-9.0 mm long to base of farthest pedicel measured along the axes and with 1-3 internodes in that length; bracts 0.8-5.0 mm long, narrowly triangular to ovate-triangular, the apex slightly obtuse, the lower ones shortest, the bracts mostly deciduous by anthesis. Axes of the inflorescence, pedicels, upper parts of calyx lobes, and sometimes the lower parts of calyx lobes and ovary minutely puberulent, the lower calyx lobes and ovary sometimes with whitish exfoliating patches. Flowers fragrant. True pedicels 2.0-6.5 mm long; calyx including inferior ovary 5.5-8.0(-9.0) mm long, obconic to campanulate; free hypanthium 2.6-3.6 mm long; calyx lobes before anthesis 1.2-2.6 mm long, 2.2-3.7 mm wide, 2.5-3.8 mm long from the stamen attachment, triangular to rounded-triangular, the apex acute to rounded, the calyx splitting between the lobes 0.6-1.4 mm at anthesis. Petals mostly white, sometimes yellowish-white or rose, sometimes white with red spots or with a median purplish zone at base on the back, 9.0-12.0 mm long, 6.2-9.0 mm wide, broadly obovate to broadly elliptic or oblong-elliptic, acute or apiculate at the apex, sessile or short-clawed at base. Filaments white, the antesepalous ones 15.0-21.0 mm long, the ante-petalous ones 19.0-25.0 mm long; anthers yellow or yellowish-purple, 2.4-3.8 mm long; sporangia 2.4-3.6 mm long, dehiscing by elongate apical pores; gland 0.6-0.8 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm from apex of anther when measured from center of gland; cauda 0.2-0.6 mm long Ovary 2-4-locular; ovules axile-basal, produced only outwardly from each placenta, 9-13 in all; style 22.0-28.0 mm long Fruit edible, red to black, globose, obliquely globose, or depressed-globose, crowned with the hypanthium and perhaps sometimes a few calyx lobes, ca 11-14 mm high and 11-15 mm thick when dry, estimated ca 14-18 mm high and 14-19 mm thick when fresh. Seeds 4 in the fruits examined, ca 8.8-10.5 mm long, 6.4 mm wide, 5.5 mm thick when not quite mature (no fully mature ones available), irregularly and broadly ellipsoid, flattened on the contact faces, with a demarcated slightly fuller part below, and with an oblique lateral-basal irregularly half-round hilum 3.2-3.6 mm long times 2.0-3.4 mm wide.
bibliographicCitation: Morley, Thomas. 1976. Melastomataceae tribe Memecyleae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 15: 1-295.

description: Shrubs or trees to 9 m high, glabrous except for the inflorescence; young twigs gray, terete or with 4 rounded angles. Petioles 2.0-4.0 mm long; blades drying dark, 4.1-6.7 cm long, 1.2-2.1 cm wide, narrowly elliptic, ovate-elliptic, or ovate-elliptic-oblong, abruptly acuminate to long acuminate at the apex, acute at base; midrib grooved above, rounded below at the base, usually becoming 2-angled 1/8-1/2 of the way to the apex; lateral nerves obscurely visible or not visible when dry. Xylem of lateral nerves open above; stomatal crypts Type I or II, averaging in a leaf ca. 15-30 µ in diam, 15-20 µ high, 5-40 per sq mm (extremes 13-38 µ diam, 15-20 µ high, 3-60 per sq mm); hypodermis present or absent, often present but interrupted; mucilage walls none; free stone cells present only in base of petiole; terminal sclereids round to elliptic to rectangular, l-2(-3) times as long as wide, arms none to few or sometimes abundant, short. Inflorescences 1 or 2 in the axils on hardened twigs, not on new growth, each 1-7-flowered, 5.0-19.0 mm long to base of farthest pedicel measured along the axes and with 2 or 3 internodes in that length; bracts 0.9-1.8 mm long, 1.0-1.4 mm wide at base, triangular or ovate triangular, acute at apex, often ridged, slightly perfoliate below or separate, some persistent and some deciduous at anthesis; upper axes of inflorescence and upper bracts minutely puberulent, the lower ones glabrous. True pedicels 0-0.8 mm long; calyx including inferior ovary glabrous, 3.0-3.7 mm long, obconic to slightly campanulate; free hypanthium 0.7-1.2 mm long; calyx lobes low-rounded and apiculate, 0.5-0.8 mm long, 1.3-1.8 mm wide, 0.8-1.0 mm long when measured from stamen attachment, the lobes not separating further at anthesis. Petals yellow or sometimes white, 3.9-4.6 mm long, 1.5-2.3 mm wide, oblong-lanceolate, acute to short-acuminate or abruptly so at the apex. Antesepalous filaments 3.0-3.5 mm long, antepetalous ones 4.0-4.5 mm long; anthers yellowish, 2.8-3.8 mm long; sporangia 1.2-1.7 mm long, dehiscing by apical clefts; gland 0.4-0.6 mm long, 1.7-2.4 mm from apex of anther when measured from center of gland; cauda 1.2-1.6 mm long. Ovary 1-locular; ovules 10 or 11, free-central, all at the same level; style ca 7-8 mm long. Fruits globose to depressed-globose, crowned with the calyx, ca 9-13 mm high excluding calyx and 11-14 mm thick when dry, estimated 11-15 mm high and 13-17 mm thick when fresh, not grooved nor ridged. See 1, roundish, ca. 10-13 mm high and wide, ca 7-12 mm thick, the hardened and polished area representing the outer face of the ovule narrow, ca 7.5-10.0 mm high (measured along the surface), widest above where it is 3.0-4.0 mm wide, abruptly narrowed below; rest of surface of outer seed face slightly rugose.

description: Shrubs or subshrubs 0.5-1 (-1.5) m tall, the stems sparsely to densely stellate-pubescent, the hairs variable in size, often twisted. Leaf blades mostly 4-9 cm long, 2.5-4 times as long as wide, elliptic, serrate, of variable pubescence (see discussion below); petioles to 16 the length of the blades (usually <14, the leaves sometimes subsessile); stipules 3-7 mm long, lanceolate, erect. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1-3.5 cm long in flower to 6 cm in fruit, with minute recurved pubescence, sometimes also with a few larger hairs; involucellar bracts 6-8, linear-lanceolate, 6-9 mm long, hirsute; calyx subequal to involucel, hirsute; corolla 9-15 mm long, yellow, ciliate on margins of claw; staminal column ca. half length of petals, glabrous, pallid, the filaments 1-1.5 mm long; styles pallid, nearly glabrous, the stigmas prominently villous. Fruits 8-10 mm diam., excluding spines, yellowish, pubescent, the mericarp body ca. 5 mm long; mericarps reticulate-veined, 3-spined, the spines (3-)7-10 mm long, retrorsely barbed, divergent.

description: Rami novelli puberuli (trichomatibus basifixis), mox glabri, asperi, brunnei, vulgo lenticellosi. Perulae nullae. Folia trifoliolata, imparipinnata vel pinnata uno foliolo paris ultimi ad instar folioli terminalis ordinato, 1-5 cm longa; petiolus cum rhachide semiteres, puberulus; petiolulus (0.5-)2-4 mm longus. Foliola opposita usque alterna, dimorpha, 3-5 cum (l-)2 paribus foliolorum valde reduc-torum ("pseudostipularum") sub basin petioli; foliola normalia elliptica vel rarius oblanceolata, apice acuminata, basi anguste attenuata, 6-10.6[8.9] cm longa, 2.2-4.2[3.4] cm lata (foliolo terminali vulgo majore, ad 14 cm longo), interdum ad costam superiorem subpuberula, cetera glabra, modo glanduloso-punctata vel -striata, modo non; venatio eucamptodroma, costa prominula; nervi secundarii 8-11 utroque costae latere, arcuato-adscendentes, convergentes, intersecundarii breves, tertiarii ± obliqui. Foliola basalia reducta lanceolata usque ovata basi cordata, vel reniformia, petiolulata, 0.2-1.6 cm longa, vulgo persistentia. Flores unisexuales (planta dioica); inflorescentia axillaris, 4.5-21 cm longa, subtiliter puberula, in thyrsum gracilem, laxe ramosum, sat pauciflorum vel multiflorum disposita, ramis lateralibus ad 8 cm longis, perpendiculariter ad axem parentibus; pedicellus 0.5-1 mm longus. Calyx patelliformis, 0.5-1 mm, 4-5-lobatus lobis late triangularibus vel vadosissimis usque dimidium calycem aequantibus, indumento puberulo conspersus vel subglaber. Petala (3-)4(-5), per 1/2-2/3 coalita, valvata, erecta vel paullum patula in flore aperto remanentia, [male] 1.75-2 mm, [female] 2-2.5 mm, ovata usque lanceolata, apice acuta, extus minutis pilis adpressis conspersa. Tubus stamineus cyathiformis vel urceolatus, filamentis toto coalitis, [male] 0.75-1.25 mm longus atque latus, [female] ca. 1.75 mm, margine 7-8-lobatus (lobis acutis usque subulatis, alternantibus cum antheris et longitudinem suam 1/2-3/4 attingentibus), glaber vel interdum aliquot pilis longis ad fauces vestitus; antherae 7-8, 0.4-0.8 mm longae, glabrae; antherodia similia, non dehiscentia, polline expertia. Nectarium nullum. Ovarium ovoideum, puberulum, sensim attenuatum in brevem stylum glabrum; 3-loculare, loculis 2 ovulis collateralibus; styli capitulum capitatum, antherodia aequans; pistillodium minus, complanate ovoideum, ovulis minoribus abortivis instructum; styli capitulum imas antheras aequans. Fructus ignotus.

description: Frutex gracilis viscidus; laminis foliorum parvis anguste ovatis dense pubescentibus; pedicellis 1.5-2 cm longis axil-laribus; bracteolis involucellorum 6 linearis viscidis; calyce quam involucello breviore; corollis 1.5 cm longis subroseis; columnis staminalis inclusis, antheris subsessilibus; fructibus ignotis.

description: Slender-stemmed shrub (scandent?), the stems densely glandular-puberulent (hairs 0.5 mm long). Leaf blades ovate, mostly 12-18 x 5-8 mm, basally truncate, serrulate, acute, palmately 3-5-nerved, discolorous, the upper surface densely pubescent with stellate and glandular hairs, the lower surface velutinous (the epidermis hidden), the stellate hairs of variable size, including scattered 3-4-armed spicules ca. 1 mm diam.; petioles 2-5 mm long, glandular-puberulent; stipules 3 mm long, subulate, glandular-puberulent. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 1.5-2 cm long, glandular-puberulent; involucellar bracts 6, linear, 5-7 x 0.5-0.7 mm, glandular-puberulent; calyx 5 mm long, minutely pubescent; corolla 1.5 cm long, pink, externally stellate-pubescent, densely bearded on margins of claw; staminal column 8-9 mm long, the anthers subsessile; styles exserted from column by 3 mm, the stigmas pinkish, subequal to corolla. Fruits oblate, 6 mm diam.; mericarps 3.5 mm high, glabrous, verruculose.

description: Shrubs 1-2.5 m tall, the stems with purplish glandular hairs and also dense longitudinal lines of simple twisted hairs and occasional long spreading simple hairs. Leaf blades ovate, basally cordate, 4-7.5 x 2-4.5 cm, crenate-serrate, acute, palmately 7-9-nerved, strongly discolorous, the upper surface with scattered stellate and glandular hairs to glabrescent, the lower surface densely canescent-tomentose with stellate and glandular hairs, the veins with appressed simple hairs; petioles 1-2.5 cm long; stipules filiform, 2.5-4 mm long. Pedicels 2.5-7.5 cm long, articulated 2.5-5 mm below the flower; involucellar bracts 7 (6-8), elliptical, 8-11 x 2-3.5 mm, subequal to calyx, ciliate and with glandular and stellate hairs, basally hirsute; calyx 8-10 mm long, stellate- and glandular-pubescent, the lobes ciliate; petals ca. 3 cm long, rose or whitish; staminal column 1.5-1.7 cm long, the filaments 1-2 mm long. Mericarps 3.5-4 mm long, trigonal, umbonate, glabrous, verrucose, the dorsal surface with reticulate venation, laterally winged; seeds 3-3.5 mm long obovoid, striate.

description: Large shrubs or small trees (evidently), the stems obscurely pubescent to glabrate. Leaf blades lance-ovate, mostly 15-29 x 7-11 cm, basally truncate to subcuneate, entire (or very coarsely serrate), acute or acuminate, penninerved (i.e., basally 3-nerved), the midrib raised above and beneath (with 5-7 pairs of secondary nerves), glabrous above and beneath; petioles 4-6 cm long, obscurely pubescent adaxially (the hairs very small), otherwise glabrous; stipules 17-22 x 1-2 mm, ligulate, glabrous, rarely divided into 2 unequal elements. Flowers solitary or paired in the leaf axils, the pedicels 0.5-2 cm long, slender, usually of reduced lateral branchlets bearing stipuliform elements 4-6 mm long; involucellar bracts 4, ovate, 1.5-2 x 9-14 mm, entire, acute, subglabrous, reddish showing prominent venation and white margin; calyx included in (and largely concealed by) the involucel, 1 cm long, deeply divided, minutely stellate-pubescent; corolla subequal to calyx, pale pink, white distally; androecium exserted from involucel, the column white, the filaments 4-7 mm long, reddish; styles emergent from the staminal column, white. Fruits unknown.

description: Shrubs 4 m tall, the stems densely hispid, the hairs simple, yellowish, 1.5-2 mm long. Leaf blades elliptic, mostly 6-12 x 2-3.5 cm, basally cuneate, distally serrate, acuminate, the upper surface with evenly distributed simple hairs that are erect or more or less appressed, the lower surface similar, except the hairs more variable in size and on average smaller, penninerved, the midrib raised both above and beneath, more prominently so beneath; petioles 5-10 mm long, hispid; stipules 13-21 mm long, erect, linear or falcate, hispid-ciliate, divided to base into 2 or 3 elements of unequal length, deciduous leaving separate scars (i.e., 4-6 stipular scars per node). Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels 12-16 cm long, hispid, the hairs 1.5-2 mm long, yellowish, somewhat antrorse; involucellar bracts 12-14, subulate, of variable length, the longest 20 mm long, hispidciliate; calyx 9-11 mm long, densely hispid; corolla 12-13 mm long, white (drying yellowish), apparently glabrous or with a few stellate hairs externally; androecium slightly exserted, the column glabrous, subequal to corolla, the anthers golden; styles and stigmas exserted, the stigmas capitate. Fruits 9 mm diam., glabrous, yellowish, retuse; mericarps 9 mm tall, carinate, slightly reticulate-veined.

description: Description based on wet and dry specimens. Monoecious or dioecious root parasites (inflorescence bisexual or unisexual). Total length from point of contact with host root 15-20 cm. Tuber subspherical, 2.5-5 cm high and 2.5-7.5 cm across, surface slightly tessellate. Stems up to 10 from one tuber or complex of tubers, cylindrical, 7-11 x 1-1.5 cm. Leaves scaly, numerous, apparently whorled and arranged in 8-12 vertical ranks, densely imbricate, almost triangular, acute, 10-14 x 3.5-6 mm, erect. Inflorescence subspherical to ellipsoid, 2.8-5 x 2.5-3.5 cm, densely covered by imbricate, (10-)14-20 ranked, scaly bracts when young. Bracts transversely triangular, acute, margins crenate to fringed, 13-19 x 9-14 mm, inserted by a broad-canaliculate 3 mm long petiole, which is transversally extended and attached along the entire lower margin of the limb, twice bent at obtuse angles about 120°-140°, early deciduous and thus leaving a twice bent scar in the dense layer of filiform hairs covering the inflorescence. The hexagonal, transversally extended area delimitated by the scars of four neighboring bracts represents one extremely depressed branch subtended by the lowermost bract. Hairs thinly clavate, 1.5 mm long. Most inflorescences in the material studied purely female with only 2-3 rudimentary (?) male flowers in the centre (top) of each branch. One inflorescence with a few female branches basally and purely male branches above. Male flowers as in S. jamaicense with a lower tubular part crowned by 3 tepals, the filaments forming a column splitting below the synandrium into 3 free filaments. Pollen grains spheroid, 6-pantopororate, 44.5 µm diam., exine 1.5 µm. Female flowers with perianth adnate to ovary, 2 short and broad, lip-like segments protruding above ovary. Ovary compressed, 1.2 mm long and 0.3-0.4 mm wide with flat side generally facing insertion of bracts; styles 2, 1.9 mm long, appearing above layer of hairs; stigmas capitellate, 0.2 mm across. Fruit a small, 1-seeded achene.
bibliographicCitation: Hansen, Bertel. 1980. Balanophoraceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 23: 1-80.

description: Leaves 3.5-5.0 cm long, 1.5-2.5 cm wide, strigose. Inflorescences terminal racemes, 1.5-3.5 cm long. Flowers in 1-florate cymules. Fruit (immature) ca 2.5 cm long.

description: Tree, 18-40 m tall, to 80 cm diam. Branch bark initially brown, later dark gray, the indumentum short, appressed, brown-pilose, fading to whitish-gray, glabrescent. Lenticels absent to numerous, inconspicuous, minute to 0.5 mm at the longest axis, granular, plane to slightly raised, orange-brown. Leaves simple, thin-coriaceous, petiolate, drying olive-green to dark brown, shiny or matte above, glabrous. Petiole 2-4.5 cm long × ca. 1.5 mm wide at midlength, 1/2-1/3 the length of the lamina, subterete at the base, flattening out above and at times slightly canaliculate, glabrous except short-tomentose at base adaxially, the hairs orange-brown fading to gray. Lamina 6-9 × 4-7 cm, length:breadth ratio 1.4-1.5:1, wide obovate; base obtuse- to acute-cuneate, decurrent onto petiole, symmetrical, flat; apex rounded, flat, the apical point of midrib not protruding; margin entire to undulate, revolute at the base; venation semicraspedodromous, plane, not conspicuous above, raised, conspicuous below, the midvein not reaching apex, branching 0.5-1.4 cm before the apex; lateral veins 4 pairs. Inflorescence unknown. Infructescence unbranching, ca. 8 cm long, sparsely ferruginous-pilose, more densely so around pedicel insertions. Common bracts 0.7 × 0.6 mm, rufous-strigose to the outside, glabrous within. Fruit pedicels 3 × 2 mm, sparsely ferruginous-pilose. Fruit 5.5-6 × 2.5-2.7 cm, oval, the sutured and unsutured sides more or less curved equally, strongly curved at the base, constricted for 0.8-1.3 cm, strongly curved to a beak at the apex, the apical point commonly facing backward, glabrous, smooth, with small tubercles seen at high magnification, mid brown or beige, peeling to dark brown beneath. Seed not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Prance, Ghillean T., et al. 2007. Proteaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 100: 1-218.

description: Dioecious tree 7-8 m tall; bark light grey, fissured, trunk reaching 25-30 cm in diam. Stems terete, glabrous, striate, brownish. Leaves paripinnate; distal process minute, subulate, persistent, occasionally a terminal leaflet is produced; leaflets 4, opposite, 4-9 × 2-4.5 cm, elliptic to broadly elliptic, chartaceous, glabrous, dull, venation brochidodromus, abaxially prominent, tertiary veins finely reticulate, the margins entire, strongly revolute, the apex obtuse or rounded, the base asymmetrical, one side obtuse the other rounded; petiolules ca. 1 mm long, drying brownish, glabrous; rachis 1-3.5 cm long, subterete, or rarely narrowly winged, striate, glabrous; petioles 2.4 cm long, glabrous, subterete, pulvinate at base. Inflorescence a raceme, 5-6 cm long, on distal portion of branch; cataphylls broadly ovate, 1-2 mm long; axes angled, glabrous; bracts early deciduous; pedicels 6-7 mm long, not articulate. Calyx 4-merous, the sepals green, ovate, concave, 1-1.2 mm long, ciliate along margins; petals 4, oblong to wide-elliptic, whitish, ca. 2.2 mm long, ciliate along margins, lacking appendages, or with a pair of minute, basal appendages; disc annular, 4-lobed, glabrous; stamens 8, spreading, the filaments glabrous, slightly unequal, ca. 2.5 mm long, the anthers oblong-elliptic, ca. 0.4 mm long, retuse at apex; pistillode minute, glabrous; ovary glabrous, ovoid, the stigma nearly sessile, 2-lobed. Fruits yellowish, ellipsoid or ovoid, ca. 2.5 cm long, the pericarp leathery, ca. 0.7 mm thick. Seed solitary, ca. 1.5 cm long, with fleshy, yellowish, edible, sour fleshy testa. Embryo with cotyledons diagonally superimposed, the upper one much larger than the lower one.
bibliographicCitation: Acevedo-Rodríguez, Pedro. 2003. Meliococceae (Sapindaceae): Melicoccus: and Talisia. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 87: 1-178.

description: Leaves drying dark olive-green, narrowly elliptic to elliptic, length:breadth ratio 2-3:1, soon glabrous beneath; indumentum, if present, of short hairs only, if persistent, ferruginous red-brown; base narrowly cuneate. Inflorescence 2-13 cm long, indumentum dense to sparse, red to dark brown, the hairs straight, appressed. Flowers not densely clustered at anthesis, drying dark brown. Ovary indumentum appressed, hairs extending 1-2 from base. Field characters. Shrub or small tree 2-10 m tall, 6-11.5 cm diam. Branches ascending, crown dense. Bark gray to grayish-brown; external bark 3 mm thick, brown; internal bark 8 mm thick, pink, bitter to taste. Wood yellow to cream, or cream to red; hard. Leaves coriaceous, dark green, shiny above, new leaves ferruginous beneath. Inflorescence pale brown to dark brown to ferruginous. Buds green tinged orange-brown to yellowish-brown. Flowers fragrant, white, cream, pale yellow, greenish-white, or yellowish green; stigma pale green; ovary ferruginous to brown; nectary white. Fruit green, lightly ferruginous, maturing brown to grayish-brown with persistent style. Seeds pale brown.

description: Subprostrate to procumbent shrub, to 1.0-1.5 m tall, the branches up to 2.5 m long, with adventitious roots, 1-7 cm long, developing on the portions closer to the ground; stems and nodes glabrous. Leaves isophyllous, elliptic to ovate, 1.5-7 X 1.0-3.2 cm, apex broadly acute to obtuse, base acute to obtuse, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface sparsely hirsute, hirsute on the primary and secondary veins, light green, 3(-5)-nervate, the tertiary veins not evident, coriaceous, entire, addressed ciliate, sometimes revolute; petioles 0.3-1.0 cm long, glabrous; domatia absent. Inflorescence a terminal cyme of 2-4 flowers, 1-3 cm long, the axis dark red to magenta, terete. Flowers on pedicels 1-3 mm long, flared at the apex, subtended by persistent until anthesis bracts, elliptic, glandular-setulose, 0.7-1.3 X 0.3 mm; hypanthium globose, with the base as wide as the pedicel, 4.4-5.0 mm long, glabrous; outer calyx teeth reduced and inconspicuous, sometimes with a short apical glandular seta or a sessile gland, sparsely glandular pubescent, 0.2 mm long, inner calyx teeth deltoid, fused at the base, 1.0-1.5 mm long; the ring inside the torus glabrous; petals 5, obovate, 6.5-11 X 5.0-6.5 mm, base attenuate, apex emarginate, slightly pruinose, glabrous, red to dark pink; stamens all the same size; filaments 5-6 mm long, glabrous; anthers yellow; the connective with a dorsal-basal blunt tooth; thecae 5 mm long, opening by a slightly ventrally inclined pore; ovary 3-locular, 1/3 inferior, the superior portion terete, the apex truncate; style glabrous, 12-14 mm long; stigma truncate. Fruits globose, 4.5-6 mm long, black, glabrous, with the calyx persistent and slightly reflexed; seeds not evident through the pericarp, truncate-obovate, 0.4-0.5 mm long, without capitate trichomes in the raphal area, without sculpturing, anticlinal walls straight, periclinal walls flat, boundaries between periclinal walls flat.

description: Shrub, to 1.5-2.0 m tall; stems hirsute, the trichomes 6-9(-12) mm long, flattened at the base, caducous in the older branches, the nodes glabrous. Leaves anisophyllous, the larger ones elliptic to oblong, 11-20 X 5-8 cm, the smaller ones 4.5-6 X 1.0-2.5 cm, apex acute to acuminate, base acute to narrowly obtuse, adaxial surface sparsely adpressed-setose, abaxial surface with sparse setae on the primary and secondary veins, light green, 5-nervate (small leaves 3-nervate), membranaceous, ciliolate-serrulate; petioles 1.5-2.5 cm long (0.5-1.0 in small leaves), hirsute; domada present in the larger leaves only, free from the leaf blade, globose to ovoid, 1.2-1.7 X 1.2-1.5 cm. Inflorescence a terminal panicle, up to 30 cm long, glabrous to sparsely hirsute. Flowers on pedicels 10-20 mm long, not flared at the apex, subtended by caducous bracts, lanceolate, 1.5 X 0.1 mm; hypan-thium obconical, 4.5-5.0 mm long, glabrous to sparsely glandular-setose near the base; outer calyx teeth filiform, 11-16 mm long, inner calyx teeth broadly deltoid, connate 2/3-4/5 of the length, flaring towards the outside of the central axis of the hypan-thium, 1.1-1.3 mm long; the ring inside the torus glabrous; petals 6, elliptic to oblong, 8-9 X 5 mm, base truncate to obtuse, apex obtuse, surface pruinose to smooth, glabrous, pink; stamens all the same size; filaments 4-5 mm long, glabrous; anthers yellow; the connective with a dorsal-basal blunt tooth; thecae 5.0 mm long, opening by a ventrally inclined pore; ovary 4-locular, 2/3 inferior, the superior portion broadly conical, the apex truncate; style glabrous, 11 mm long; stigma funnelform, papillate. Fruits unknown; seeds unknown.

description: Lax, scandent herb, at least 0.5 m tall. Leaves with blades 4.8-12 x 4-8.5 cm; petioles 3.5-10 cm long, 1-2.2 cm wide at base, otherwise 0.31 cm wide. Inflorescence intercalary, composed of (1-)2-4 pairs of 6-32-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 8.8-21 cm long, the pedicels 1.25 cm; cyme bracts 3-6 x 1.7-4.2 cm, subordinate bracts absent. Sepals ovate to lanceolate, acuminate, 8-11 x 4-6.3 mm at anthesis (later up to 14 x 9 mm). Corolla with upper lip 5-8 x 5-9 mm; lower lip 13-18 x 10-15 mm. Stamens with anthers 3-4.1 mm, the thecae divariate or slightly ascending, elliptic or obovoid, dehiscing in 65-75% of their length.

description: Subshrub, 0.3-1 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems lanate or densely sericeous with whitish to huffish hairs (often purplish tinged in exposure). Leaves with blades ovate, 2.5-6.5 x 1.6-4.2 cm, rounded or broadly cuneate at base, the margins shallowly serrate or crenate, ± revolute, often seemingly entire; upper surface grayish-green or olivaceous, ± densely velutinous. Inflorescence with cyme bracts absent or present in the lowermost cyme pair only. Stamens with filaments 0.6-1.2 mm. 2n = 36 (Løjtnant & Molau 15165).

description: Leaves obtuse, 10-14(-18) x 1-1.5 mm. Sepals acute, pale green to yellowish-green. Corolla lemon-yellow or sulphur-yellow, the upcurved portion of lower lip 13-22 x 5-10 mm. Stamens with anthers 2-2.5 mm, the thecae divaricate; filaments 0.5-1.0 mm. Style 1.8-2.2(-3) mm. In = 36 (Harling et al. 14844).

description: Inflorescence with cyme bracts absent. Corolla with elaiophore absent. Stamens type 5 (thecae deflexed); filaments 1-1.4 mm. Style 3-4.5 mm. 2n = 36 (Molau & Öhman 1206, new record).

description: Erect or ascending herb, 0.3-2 m tall; stems and peduncles hispid or hirsute with white glandular hairs. Leaves with upper surface of blades bright to deep green, pilose; petioles very narrowly winged (merely margined) in the distal half, 0.2-0.5 mm wide at the distal end. Inflorescence composed of 2-5 (-6) pairs of cymes, the bracts 4-7.5 x 2.3-5.6 cm. Corolla light yellow to sulphur yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 5-10 x 612 mm, the lower lip 18-32 x 15-30 mm, saccate in 70-80% of length. Stamens with anthers yellowish-white to buff, 3.6-5 mm; filaments 1.4-2.5 mm. Style straight, 4-5.5 mm. 2n = 36 (Harling & Andersson 11659, Harling et al. 14889, Løjtnant, Molau & Madison 11713).

description: Stems and inflorescence glutinous, glabrous or sparsely glandular-puberulous, ± purplish. Leaves with blades 4.3-8.6(-11) x 1.4-2.7 cm, rounded at base; petioles 3-8(-15) mm. Corolla bright yellow-orange throughout. 2n = 36 (Mo-lau et al. 544, new record).

description: Leaves with blades ovate to lanceolate, 12-24 x 6-16 mm, the margins distinctly lobulate with 4-6 lobes along each side of blade; petioles 5-15 mm. Sepals 4.5-6.2 x 3.2-4 mm at anthesis. Corolla usually with red dots in the throat.

description: Ascending or prostrate herb, 0.3-1 m tall, the stems and inflorescence glandular-hirsute. Leaves with blades ovate to almost circular in inclusive outline, 2.6-1 A x 2.8-6.7 cm, acute, cordate or truncate at base, 7-15-lobate, the lobes serrate or biserrate; lower surface palmate-venose, the major veins pilose, interspaces glabrous or glandular-pilose; petioles 0.7-3.5 cm, hirsute or hispid with white hairs. Sepals with the margins entire. Stamens type 1; anthers pale yellow to yellowish-white, glabrous, 3.6-4.7 mm, dehiscing throughout, the thecae subequal, divaricate, somewhat arcuate; filaments 1-2 mm. Style 1.5-2.4 mm long. Capsule 6-8 mm long, ± acuminate.

description: Subshrub, (0.1-)0.2-1.8 m tall. Leaves with blades acute, (1.7-)2.9-8 x (1.3-)2.2-6.2 cm, the lower surface pilose to lanate. Inflorescence composed of 2-4 pairs of 4-12-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.3-7.7 cm, the pedicels 1.4-2.7 cm; cyme bracts absent or present (then elliptic and with the margins ± entire). Sepals light yellow-green (in shady sites) to bright lemon yellow (in exposure), 5.5-8.8 x 4-7.8 mm at anthesis. Corolla with upper lip light yellow (in semi-shade) to sulphur yellow (in exposure); lower lip bright yellow (semi-shade) to golden yellow (in exposure), the throat internally pure white in the upper half, deep yellow in the lower half, often with red dots in the sides. Stamens with anthers 2-2.9 mm across. 2n = 36 (Molau 790, Hjerting 5302, new record).

description: Leaves with blades slightly cordate at base; lower surface ± reticulate-venose. Inflorescence composed of 8-16-flowered cymes. Sepals light green, 4-5.5 x 3-4.2 mm at anthesis, acute or shortly acuminate, externally shortly glandular-hirsute, internally glandular-puberulous. Stamens with anthers bicolorous, pale brown at base, purple dorsally, 3-3.8 mm long.

description: Low shrub; inflorescence and distal parts of stems red-brown, hirsute with coarse, pale buffish, ascending, glandless hairs. Leaves with blades elliptic or obovate, 6-14(-23) x 3-10(-13) mm; upper surface olive to deep green, flexuose, tomentose or hirsute with glandless hairs; lower surface pale grayish-green, villous or (usually) lanate with whitish hairs, the glandular tissue ± concealed. 2n = 36 (Molau 805, new record).

description: Subshrub or low shrubby plant, the stems ± tufted, erect or ascending, 0.2-0.8(-2) m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems hirsute or hispid with coarse, white, eglandular hairs. Leaves with blades herbaceous or subcoriaceous, ovate or elliptic, obtuse, cuneate or rounded at base, 0.8-2.2(-2.6) x 0.3-1.3(-2.1) cm, the margins deflexed or revolute, crenate; upper surface hirsute or hispid with coarse hairs, some of which are gland-tipped; lower surface glandular-villous or finely glandular-hirsute. Inflorescence composed of 1-3 pairs of 2-16-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 1.1-7.5 cm; pedicels 0.8-2.8 cm. Corolla with lower lip 11-28 x 6-20 mm. Stamens with anthers 2.8-4.5 mm. Style 1.9-3.6 mm. 2n = 36 (Molau 828, new record).

description: Plants 0.2-1.3(-3) m tall. Leaves with blades lanceolate, rarely ovate or narrowly elliptic, 2.8-7.7 x 0.8-2.5 cm; upper surface olive green, dull, ± smooth, glandular, ± densely short-hirsute (sometimes puberulous in Bolivian specimens) with grayish-white hairs; lower surface light grayish-green, reticulate-venose (often predominantly pinnate-venose in Peruvian specimens), the major veins short-tomentose, the interspaces glabrous, sessile-glandular. Inflorescence composed of 1-2(-4) pairs of 2-12-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 1.5-7.6 cm; pedicels 1-3.2 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals yellow-green to light greenish-yellow, ovate, the dorsal sepal 5.4-9.2 x 3.8-6.8 mm at anthesis. Corolla bright yellow, in Peruvian specimens usually with faint red dots in the sides of the throat; upper lip 36 x 5-7 mm; lower lip (upcurved portion) 1526 x 10-17 mm. Stamens with anthers 3.6-5 mm; filaments 1.1-1.9 mm. 2n = 36 (tetraploid, Molau 592, 684, new record) or 72 (octoploid, Molau 579, Straw 2382, cf. Straw in Löve, 1970).

description: Leaves with blades ovate to narrowly elliptic, obtuse or subacute at apex, cuneate or attenuate at base, 4.6-9.5 x 1.8-3.5 cm, the margins denticulate or entire; upper surface strongly glutinous and ± nitidous; lower surface reticulate-venose; petioles 10-20 mm.

description: Scandent subshrub, 0.3-1.5 m tall, the branches divaricate; inflorescence and distal parts of stems villous or loosely lanate with long, white, glandless hairs and ± densely short-hirsute with glandular hairs, glabrescent with age. Leaves decussate; blades herbaceous or subcoriaceous, ovate 1-2.6 x 0.5-2.1 cm, obtuse, cordate at base, the margins crenulate and revolute; upper surface grayish or silvery green, rugose or deeply flexuose, sericeous or velutinous with silver white hairs; lower surface silver white, villous or arachnoid-lanate, the venation concealed; petioles 15 mm, arachnoid-lanate. Inflorescence composed of two or three pairs of 4-24-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 0.8-2.5 cm, the pedicels 0.5-1.5 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals ovate, yellow-green to silvery green, 4.2-6.7 x 2.3-4.4 mm at anthesis, acuminate, pilose or villous externally, glabrous internally (or puberulous just at apex). Corolla type VIII, light yellow or lemon yellow, the throat internally pale yellow and with two or three crossbands of ± confluent red spots (rarely unspotted); upper lip 2-4 mm long and 4-8 mm wide and about as high; lower lip distally conspicuously 3-5-lobate, saccate in 30-40% of length, the upcurved portion 6-13 x 5-9 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers huffish or yellow-brown, glabrous, 1.7-2.6 mm, the thecae ± divaricate; filaments 0.8-1.4 mm. Style almost straight, 1.7-2.6 mm. Capsule conic, 5-7 mm long, acuminate, glandular-pilose.

description: Sepals lanceolate, greenish-yellow, 8-11 x 4.27 mm at anthesis. Corolla with upper lip 5-7 x 5-6 mm, acuminate, tapering into a very narrowly truncate apex ca. 1 mm wide; lower lip 17-27 x 9-16 mm. Stamens with anthers 2.5-3.4 mm, the thecae divaricate, their distal ends usually somewhat upeurved. 2n = 36 (Løjtnant & Molau 12277).

description: Leaves with blades 4-7.5(-11) x 1.4-3.2(-5.8) cm, the upper surface dark green, nitidous, flexuose, the lower surface greenish-white, pinnate-venose; petioles 6-18(-38) mm, dorsally tomentose with grayish or buffish hairs. Inflorescence with cymes 4-12-flowered. In = 36 (Harling et al. 15075, cf. Molau, 1979a: 35; the same chromosome number was reported by Srinath, 1939: 106).

description: Decumbent herb, at least 0.5 m long; stems and inflorescence minutely glandular-puberulous. Leaves with blades triangular to ovate, 4.2-6.3 x 2.8-4.2 cm, acute at apex, cordate at base, the margins ciliate, biserrate or lobulate-serrate; upper surface deep green, white-tomentose on the major veins, otherwise short-pilose; lower surface pale green, sparsely pilose; petioles 1.53 cm long, 1.1-2.2 cm wide at base, 0.4-0.6 cm wide at the distal end, the margins serrate, often almost entire in the distal part. Inflorescence intercalary, composed of one pair of 2-8-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 3.5-5.8 cm, the pedicels 1.5-2.2 cm; cyme bracts 1.8-4.5 x 1.1-1.8 cm, subordinate bracts present in well-developed cymes. Sepals green, ovate, 6.2-8.7 x 3.5-4.8 mm at anthesis, acuminate, minutely glandular-puberulous on both sides, the margins entire, short-ciliate. Corolla type XIV, pale yellow, unspotted; upper lip 4-5 x 5-6 mm; lower lip 13-15 x 8-10 mm, saccate in ca. 40% of its length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 1; anthers medium brown, 2.8-3.3 mm, glabrous, the thecae divaricate or slightly deflexed, subglobose, unequal; filaments 1.1-1.5 mm. Style straight, 4.7-5 mm. Capsule not seen at maturity.

description: Low shrubby plant or subshrub, 0.2-0.5 m tall, the stems erect, tufted; inflorescence and distal parts of stems villous to arachnoid-lanate with white, interwoven hairs. Leaves decussate, subsessile or short-petiolate; blades subcoriaceous, linear to lanceolate, 5-15 x 1-5 mm, obtuse and hamate at apex, cuneate or attenuate at base, the margins entire or crenulate, strongly revolute; upper surface silver-white sericeous; lower surface white arachnoid-lanate; petioles 0-5 mm. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 2-4-flowered cymes, the peduncles 0.5-3 cm, the pedicels 1-2.2 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals pale grayish-green, 2.5-5 x 1.2-3.5 mm at anthesis, acute or subacute, externally glandular and white-villous, internally glabrous, ± purplish, the margins entire. Corolla type XV, light purple (occasionally white), internally with purple spots at the bases of the filaments; upper lip triangular, somewhat acuminate, 2-5 mm long and wide; lower lip obovate, pendent, 5-15 mm long and wide, saccate in 30-50% of length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 10; anthers whitish, 1.6-3.2 mm, the thecae unequal, subglobose, dehiscing distally in 70-90% of their length, somewhat ascending; filaments 1-1.5 mm. Style straight or slightly arcuate, 4.5-7 mm. Capsule conical or ovoid, 5-6 mm long, purplish, glandular-puberulous to glandular-hirsute.

description: Erect or ascending shrub, 0.4-2 m tall, much branched, the stems glabrous. Leaves with blades ovate to obovate, glabrous, 2.3-6 x 1.4-3.5 cm, acute or acuminate, cuneate or attenuate at base, the margins somewhat irregularly sharp-serrate; upper surface deep bluish-green, ± smooth, glutinous; lower surface whitish-green, predominantly pinnate-venose; petioles 4-12 mm, glabrous, papillose. Inflorescence composed of 1 or 2 pairs of 4-8-flowered cymes, the peduncles puberulous, 1.2-5.3 cm, the pedicels puberulous to hirsute, 0.9-2.5 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals light yellow-green, ovate, 6-8 x 3.9-6.4 mm at anthesis, subacute, externally shortly villous or hirsute, internally puberulous or short-hirsute and with a short-villous border along the margins. Corolla type II, bright yellow, the upper lip 3-6 x 5-10 mm, the lower lip 15-21 x 10-16 mm, saccate in 50-60% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers pale buff to yellowish-white, 4-4.9 mm, the thecae subequal; filaments 1.1-1.8 mm. Style 2.5-3.6 mm, curved distally. Capsule ovoid, slightly acuminate, brownish, 6-7 mm long, shortly glandular-hirsute.

description: Erect or ascending subshrub, 0.1-1(-1.5) m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems strigose or ascending-tomentose with whitish hairs. Leaves decussate or (rarely, only about 2% of the specimens examined) ternate, petiolate; blades herbaceous (sometimes almost subcoriaceous at extremely high altitudes), ovate to subcircular, 1.25 x 0.7-3.4 cm, acute or subacute, truncate to cuneate at base, the margins shallowly serrate, flat or somewhat deflexed; upper surface olive-green, ± densely short-hirsute, flexuose, dull; lower surface pale or grayish-green, pinnate-venose, the veins raised, strigose (rarely almost villous), interspaces glabrous or pilose, conspicuously glandular; petioles 2-10(-21) mm, whitish-tomentose. Inflorescence composed of (1-)2-4(-6) pairs (rarely triplets) of (l-)4-12-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 0.8-5 cm; pedicels 0.5-2.4 cm; cyme bracts present, though sometimes rudimentary or absent in the upper cymes. Sepals ovate to elliptic, light green to olivaceous, sometimes tinged purple, 2.6-5 x 2.3-4.3 mm at anthesis, subacute or broadly acute, externally puberulous or short-villous, internally minutely puberulous, the margins white-ciliate. Corolla type VIII, light yellow, bright yellow, or bright lemon yellow, internally with a broad purple crossband or blotch (rarely two or three crossbands) in the throat, in some populations with additional dots on top of the lower lip; upper lip white; upcurved part of lower lip 8-15 x 5-12 mm. Stamens with anthers brownish-yellow to light brown, 1.6-2.4 mm, the thecae divaricate; filaments 0.8-1.5 mm. Style 1.4-2.1 mm. Capsule 4-5 mm long, conic, shortly glandular-hirsute. In = 36 (Molau 582, new record).

description: Erect or ascending subshrub, 0.3-1 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems densely sericeous or arachnoid-lanate with huffish-white hairs. Leaves decussate, petiolate; blades herbaceous, ovate, 1.8-6.2 x 1.3-3.7 cm, acute, rounded at base, the margins subentire (shallowly serrulate); upper surface grayish-green, densely short-tomentose or short-sericeous and with sessile glands, somewhat flexuose; lower surface pale grayish-green, pinnate-venose, the veins raised, velutinous or densely sericeous, interspaces glabrous, conspicuously and densely gland-dotted; petioles 3-12 mm, arachnoid-lanate. Inflorescence composed of 1-4 pairs of 6-12-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 1.4-4 cm; pedicels 1-1.7 cm; cyme bracts present (usually absent in upper cymes). Sepals very pale green, 4.4-6 x 4-5 mm at anthesis, acute or somewhat acuminate, externally glandular and whitish-villous, internally glabrous. Corolla type VIII, pale yellow or pale greenish-yellow, the upper lip white, the lower lip internally with a broad purple crossband in the throat, its upcurved portion 9-14 x 7-11 mm. Stamens with anthers medium to dark brown, 2.4-2.6 mm, the thecae divaricate; filaments (1-)1.7-1.9 mm. Style 1.7-2.3 mm long. Capsule ovoid or conical, 5-7 mm long, glandular-papillose, often suffused with purple.
