description: Lax, scandent or ascending shrub or subshrub (vine), 1-2 m tall, the branches divaricately spreading; inflorescence and distal parts of stems tomentose with ascending buffish-white hairs. Leaves decussate, very short-petiolate; blades herbaceous, ovate, 3.7-8 x 1.8-4.3 cm, acute or slightly acuminate at apex, rounded or cuneate at base, the margins serrate; upper surface dull green, sparsely short-pilose, almost smooth; lower surface light green, ± reticulate-venose, the major veins pilose or short-tomentose, interspaces glabrous; petioles 2-8 mm, tomentose. Inflorescence composed of 2-4 pairs of 4-8-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 1.5-4 cm; pedicels 0.5-1.5 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals light green to yellowish-green, 4-6 x 3-4.2 mm at anthesis, acute, short-tomentose on both sides. Corolla type VIII, pale yellow, internally with a pale red to maroon-red patch in the throat; up-curved portion of lower lip 7-13 x 6-9 mm. Stamens with anthers 1.9-2.3 mm, brown, the thecae divaricate; filaments 0.9-1.5 mm. Style 2-2.3 mm long. Capsule ovoid, 4-6 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Vine, 1-4 m long, the branches divaricate; inflorescence and distal parts of stems purplish-hirsute, the bark of older stems peeling off. Leaves with blades herbaceous, elliptic or ovate, 1.5-3.4 x 0.5-1.3 cm, acute, cuneate to rounded at base, the margins crenate or bluntly serrate; upper surface deep green, shallowly rugose, sparsely pilose; lower surface pale green, pinnate-venose, the veins pilose or hirsute with undulate hairs, interspaces glandular; petioles 2-5 mm, hirsute. Inflorescence distal, composed of 2 or 3 pairs of 1-4-flowered cymes on peduncles 0.5-2.8 cm long; cyme bracts present; pedicels 0.7-2.6 cm. Sepals bright green or yellow-green, ovate, somewhat unequal, 4.2-7 x 2.8-4.5 mm at anthesis, acute or slightly acuminate, externally short-villous, internally glabrous except for the short-tomentose border along the margins, the margins densely ciliate. Corolla type VI, bright yellow and with 2 or 3 cross-bands of bright red spots in the throat, upper lip 4-5 x 6-11 mm, lower lip 10-17 x 9-15 mm, flattened, saccate in 40-50% of length, elaiophore absent (or rudimentary). Stamens type 1; anthers medium to dark brown, glabrous, 2.2-3 mm, the thecae equal; filaments 0.8-1.3 mm. Style yellow, arcuate, (2.5-)3.2-5.2 mm. Capsule widely ovoid, brownish-green, 4-6 mm long, glandular-puberulous. 2n = 36 (Molau 768, new record).

description: Ascending, rosulate or subrosulate herb, 5-30 cm tall. Leaves indistinctly petiolate; blades elliptic to lanceolate, 2.9-7.6 x 1.3-3.8 cm, obtuse, attenuate or cuneate at base, the margins entire or very shallowly serrate; petioles 0.5-2.8 cm, pilose. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 4-8-flowered cymes (sometimes just a single cyme), the primary peduncles villous, 3.513 cm, the pedicels 0.6-2.8 cm, cyme bracts present. Sepals light green, acute or subacute, 2.8-5.2 x 1.5-3.6 mm at anthesis. Corolla type X, bright yellow above, light yellow beneath, the throat sometimes with a purplish area inside; upper lip rounded-triangular, 2-4 x 3-5 mm; lower lip flattened, obovate, markedly truncate at apex, 10-20 x 7-19 mm, saccate in 75-90% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers pale buff, 1.5-2.1 mm; filaments 1-1.5 mm. Style 1.1-1.5 mm. Capsule ovoid, 4-5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Molau, Ulf. 1988. Scrophulariaceae Part I. Calceolarieae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 47: 1-325.

description: Ascending, lax herb, 3-40 cm tall, the stems and inflorescence white-villous, purplish. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate, 2.8-6.2 x 1.5-3.8 cm, acute or subacute, cordate to cuneate at base, the margins densely white-ciliate, shallowly serrate; upper surface bright green, short-pilose; lower surface pale green, the veins white-hispid, interspaces glabrous or pilose; petioles 5-15 mm, villous. Inflorescence with peduncles (when present) 3.2-6.3 cm; pedicels 0.8-3.1 cm, becoming sigmoid in late anthesis. Sepals ovate to lanceolate, green, 3-4.6 x 1.8-3.3 mm at anthesis, obtuse, externally white-hirsute, internally short-hirsute in the distal part, otherwise subglabrous, the margins entire, ciliate. Corolla type VI, apricot yellow; upper lip arched, 3-5 x 5-7 mm; lower lip 7-12 x 5-8 mm, saccate in 40-50% of length, the throat with a faint red crossband inside (sometimes absent); elaiophore absent, even the infolded lobe reduced and vestigial. Stamens with anthers yellow, glabrous, 1.1-1.4 mm long; filaments 1.6-3 mm. Style straight or slightly arcuate, 1.4-2.2 mm, the stigma capitate. Capsule semi-inferior, oblong, 6-10 mm long, sparsely glandular-puberulous. 2n = 18 (Molau 708).

description: Erect or ascending (rarely decumbent) herb, 0.1-1 m tall. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate in inclusive outline, (1.2-) 1.7-10 x (0.8-) 1.5-8.6 cm, dissected to the midrib or less (sometimes lobate or subentire) with 1-2(-3) pairs of lateral pinnae, the margins serrate or biserrate; petioles 1-4.4 cm long, unwinged or very narrowly winged, 1-2 mm wide, proximally somewhat dilated and connate across the nodes with narrow wings or ridges 0.3-1.6 mm wide. Inflorescence of vigorous specimens with primary peduncles 3-15 cm long; pedicels 1.6-5 cm. Sepals ovate, green, acuminate, 4.2-8.2 x 1.6-6.5 mm at anthesis, the margins ± dentate (rarely entire). Corolla type X (almost type III in some large-flowered populations), bright or (less commonly) deep yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 3-5 x 3-6 mm, the lower lip (8-)l 1-24 x 10-22 mm, saccate in 80-90% of length, the throat glabrous or pilose; elaiophore present. Stamens with anthers (3.3-)4-5.4 mm long; posterior theca fertile, whitish, sessile or subsessile, 1.2-2.2 mm long; anterior thecae sterile, vestigial; connective with a dorsal tooth 0.1-0.3 mm high and a sigmoid lower connective arm 1.7-3.5 mm long, orange to brown, terete, distally expanded into a deflexed knob (serving as a lever in pollination); filaments 0.7-1.6 mm. Style arcuate, 2-3.4(-4) mm. Capsule broadly conic to subglobose, 5-8 mm long, pale green to purplish, glandular-hirsute. 2n = 32, Molau et al. 549, Molau 867, new record), 2n = 64 (Løjtnant & Molau 11318, Løjtnant, Molau & Madison 12339, 12401, Molau 792, 832), n = ca. 27 (Straw 2383, Straw in Löve, 1970: 268).

description: Stout herb, usually erect, sometimes ascending, 0.3-2(-3) m tall; stems and foliage glandular-pubescent, very sticky. Leaves with blades deltoid, 4.2-19 x 4.1-20 cm, acute, deeply cordate at base, the margins lobulate and biserrate; upper surface slightly rugose, pilose to hispid; lower surface pale green, the major veins hirsute or hispid with white glandular hairs, the interspaces pilose to villous; petioles 2.9-18 cm long, (1.5-) 3-8.5 cm wide at base, the margins serrate or serrulate, at least proximally. Inflorescence intercalary, composed of 2-6 pairs of 4-36-flow-ered cymes; primary peduncles 6.5-37 cm long; pedicels 1.4-7.5 cm; cyme bracts large, subordinate bracts absent or (rarely) rudimentary. Sepals ovate, pale to bright green, often suffused with purple, 9-21 x 6.6-14 mm at anthesis, acuminate and ± caudate, externally glandular-pilose or finely glandular-villous, internally glan-dular-puberulous, the margins entire, ciliate. Corolla type I, yellow, usually unspotted; elaio-phore present. Stamens type 3; anthers 3.6-6 mm, glabrous, the thecae unequal or subequal, arcuate or slightly sigmoid. Style straight or arcuate, always decurved at apex. Capsule ovoid or subglobose, 7-12 mm long, villous or hirsute with glandular hairs. 2n = 36.

description: Densely tufted subshrub, the stems erect or ascending, 0.2-1 (-2) m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems white-villous. Leaves with blades herbaceous or subcoriaceous, suborbicular (rarely almost ovate), 3-5-lobate (rarely to 9-lobulate), the lobes entire, obtuse, the margins revolute, truncate or slightly cordate at base; upper surface olive to bright green, finely white-sericeous, flexuose; lower surface whitish, densely lanate; petioles 3-8 mm, white-villous. Inflorescence composed of 1-3 pairs of 1-8-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 0.8-3.7 cm, the pedicels 0.6-3.5 cm. Sepals ovate or lanceolate, bright to deep green, sometimes suffused with purple, acute or subacute, 3.3-5(-6.5) x 2.4-3.8 mm at anthesis, externally villous or sericeous with white hairs, internally densely glandular-papillose, the margins entire. Corolla type XII, pale yellow to bright yellow, the throat internally light yellow-green in the upper third and provided with 1-3 deep red to purple crossbands or bands of spots (sometimes absent); upper lip 35 mm long and wide; lower lip 10-20 x 7-15 mm, saccate in 60-75% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers yellowish-white to brownish-yellow, glabrous, 2.3-3.2 mm, dehiscing throughout, the thecae equal or nearly so, divaricate or very slightly deflexed; filaments 1.2-2.0 mm. Style curved, 1.6-3.2 mm. Capsule ovoid, 5-6 mm long, glandular-hirsute, often suffused with purple. 2n = 36 (Molau & Sanchez Vega 852, new record).

description: Lax, ascending herb, at least 0.7 m tall. Leaves short-petiolate; blades herbaceous, ovate to elliptic, 2-3.7 x 1.3-2.6 cm, acute or subacute, cuneate or almost truncate at base, the margins irregularly serrate or biserrate with rounded teeth; upper surface bright green, somewhat flexuose, densely villous; lower surface grayish-green, reticulate-venose, coarsely lanate with most of the hairs glandless; petioles lanate, 3-6 mm. Inflorescence composed of two pairs of 6-16-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 2.2-3.5 cm, the pedicels 0.6-1.5 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals green, ovate, 3.2-4 x 1.9-2.6 mm at anthesis, acute, externally pilose, internally with some short-stalked glands in the distal part, otherwise glabrous, the margins entire, shortly glandular-ciliate. Corolla type VI, yellow, unspotted; upper lip truncate, ca. 3 x 4-5 mm; lower lip 11-13 x 7-10 mm, saccate in 20-39% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 2; anthers shortly hirsute, yellow-brown, 2.3-2.5 mm; thecae equal, divaricate; filaments 1.2-1.4 mm. Style straight, 3-3.6 mm. Capsule conic, brownish, 5-7 mm long, acuminate, glandular-puberulous.

description: Stout herb, erect or ascending, 0.3-1.5(-2) m tall; stems and inflorescence densely arachnoid-lanate with white to pale huffish hairs. Leaves with blades ovate or rounded-triangular, 6.414 x 4.4-10 cm, rather fleshy, acute or subacute at apex, truncate to cordate at base, the margins ± lobulate and bicrenate or biserrate; upper surface bright to olive green, pilose to villous with coarse hairs, somewhat rugose; lower surface densely white-lanate; petioles 3.3-9.2 cm long, 3-7.4 cm wide at base, 0.5-2.1 cm at the distal end, the margins entire or crenate to serrate in the proximal part. Inflorescence distal, composed of 1-5 pairs of (2-)8-16-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 7.2-17 cm long; pedicels 2-5.4 cm; cyme bracts 2.5-7.7 x 1.5-4.8 cm, subordinate bracts absent. Sepals ovate, pale green to yellow-green, often suffused with purple, 8.216 x 6.4-12 mm at anthesis, acuminate, externally villous to arachnoid-lanate, internally puberulous or villous, the margins long-ciliate, entire or (rarely) denticulate. Corolla type I, light lemon yellow to bright yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 5-7 x 7-11 mm, the lower lip 19-25 x 15-20 mm, saccate in 60-70% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 10; anthers buff to yellowish-white, glabrous, 4.8-7 mm, the thecae unequal, somewhat ascending; filaments 1.5-2.5 mm. Style 3-4.5 mm, straight, decurved at apex. Capsule ovoid or subglobose, ± purplish, 5-7 mm long, glandular-hirsute. 2n = 36 (Molau 822, new record). A previous report of 2n = 36 for C. tomentosa (Huynh, 1965: 106) most probably refers to C. trilobata subsp, herzogiana (see below).

description: Herb or (at higher altitudes) low shrubby plant, 0.1-0.6 m tall, the stems erect or ascending; inflorescence and distal parts of stems short-hirsute to villous with white glandless hairs. Leaves decussate, short-petiolate or subsessile; blades herbaceous, narrowly triangular, (0.9-) 1.8-7.5 x (0.3-)0.6-3.5 cm, obtuse, cordate at base, the margins crenate, deflexed or somewhat revolute; upper surface light green to olive green, ± flexuose, puberulous to hispid with white glandless hairs; lower surface pale green, reticulate-venose, the major veins villous with glandless hairs, interspaces puberulous or pilose; petioles 1-3 mm, villous. Inflorescence composed of two or three pairs of 4-20-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 0.8-4 cm; pedicels 0.5-2.7 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals greenish-yellow to bright yellow-green, 2.89-5.5 x 2.4-5.2 mm at anthesis, obtuse or subacute, externally villous to short-hirsute, internally puberulous, the margins entire. Corolla type XII, bright to deep yellow, internally with deep red spots in the sides of the throat; upper lip subglobose, shallowly emarginate, 2-4 x 35 mm; lower lip 9-15 x 5-10 mm, saccate in 50-60% of length; elaiophore present, arched, submarginal. Stamens type 10; anthers light to medium brown, 3-4.3 mm, the thecae unequal, ± ascending, dehiscing distally in 30-70% of length; filaments 0.4-0.8 mm. Style curved near apex, 2.2-2.9 mm. Capsule ovoid, 5-7 mm long, slightly acuminate, olivaceous, shortly glandular-hirsute. 2n = 36 (Hjerting & von Bothmer 6342, Molau 710, new record).

description: Erect or ascending subshrub, 0.5-1 m tall, the branches ± divaricate; inflorescence and distal parts of stems villous or sericeous with coarse buffish hairs. Leaves petiolate, decussate (some Peruvian specimens) or ternate; blades herbaceous, ovate, 3-7.9 x 2.2-5 cm, acute or subacute at apex, truncate or slightly cordate at base, the margins coarsely serrate; upper surface bright green, flexuose, hirsute or strigose; lower surface pale green, pinnate-venose, the veins sericeous to velutinous, interspaces villous; petioles 5-14 mm, villous or sericeous. Inflorescence composed of 3-4 pairs or triplets of 8-20-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 0.7-4.5 cm; pedicels 0.5-1.8 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals light green, 3.8-7 x 3.2-5 mm at anthesis, acute, externally villous, internally glabrous or puberulous. Corolla type VIII, sulphur yellow, internally with a large purplish spot in the throat; upcurved portion of lower lip 8-15 x 6-10 mm. Stamens with anthers brown, 1.7-2.3 mm, the thecae divaricate or slightly deflexed; filaments 0.7-1.2 mm. Style 1.5-1.9 mm long. Capsule not seen at maturity.

description: Erect, ascending, or scandent subshrub, the stems 1-4 m long; inflorescence and distal parts of stems tomentose with ascending, pale purplish hairs. Leaves decussate, sessile; blades herbaceous, ovate or broadly ovate, (2.8-)4-8 x (1.5-)2.7-6 cm, acute at apex, cordate or rounded at base (leaves of main shoots clasping), the margins serrate; upper surface dull green, short-pilose, somewhat flexuose; lower surface pale green, reticulate-venose (but with faint tertiary veins), the major veins raised, villous or tomentose, interspaces pilose or glabrescent. Inflorescence composed of two or three pairs of 8-22-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 0.8-4.5 cm; pedicels 0.6-1.8 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals ovate or elliptic, light green, often turning red in exposure, 4.8-6.5 x 3-5.2 mm at anthesis, subacute, externally villous, internally puberulous. Corolla type VIII, pale yellow, the upper lip ± white, the lower lip internally with a broad purple crossband and/or series of spots in the throat, its up-curved portion 8-15 x 6-10 mm. Stamens with anthers brown, 2.0-2.6 mm, the thecae divaricate; filaments 0.8-1.1 mm. Style 1.7-2.3 mm long. Capsule ovoid, 4-6 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Erect or ascending herb or subshrub, 0.5-1 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems sericeous with thin white hairs. Leaves decussate, petiolate; blades ovate to (rarely) almost elliptic, herbaceous, 2-5 x 1.2-3.2 cm, acute, ± rounded at base, the margins serrate; upper surface dull, olivaceous, ± smooth, densely short-hirsute; lower surface pale green, pinnate-venose, the veins white-tomentose or -sericeous, interspaces glabrous or pilose, conspicuously gland-dotted; petioles 3-12 mm, white arachnoid-lanate. Inflorescence composed of 1-2(-3) pairs of 4-14 (-20)-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 1-8.3 cm; pedicels 0.6-1.9 cm; cyme bracts usually absent, sometimes present in lowermost cymes. Sepals pale green, 4.7-6.5(-8.8) x 3.3-5(-6) mm at anthesis, acute or slightly acuminate, externally sericeous or minutely villous, internally puberulous or glabrous. Corolla type VIII, pale yellow or greenish-yellow, the upper lip often white, the throat internally with a large purple spot; upcurved portion of lower lip 8-13 x 611 mm. Stamens with anthers brown, 2.2-2.7 mm, the thecae divaricate; filaments 1-1.6 mm. Style 1.8-2.2(-2.8) mm long. Capsule narrowly conical, 4-7 mm long, shortly glandular-hirsute. 2n = 36 (Løjtnant & Molau 15899).

description: Vine or ascending shrub, the branches divaricate, the stems 0.3-3 m long; inflorescence and distal parts of stems glabrous and glutinous. Leaves connate, blades lanceolate, 9-13 x 2.5-3.9 cm, slightly acuminate, rounded at base, dark to bright green above, pale green and reticulate-venose or predominantly pinnate-venose below, the margins entire or sparsely denticulate. Inflorescence composed of two pairs of 4-flowered cymes, the peduncles 1-4 cm, the pedicels 1-2.2 cm; cyme bracts mostly absent but sometimes present in the lower cyme pair. Sepals green or yellow-green, 4.8-6 x 3.2-4.2 mm at anthesis, acute or slightly acuminate. Corolla type IV, bright yellow; upper lip flattened, circular, 8-13 mm high and 10-16 mm wide; lower lip up-curved, saccate in about 50% of length, the up-curved portion 12-20 x 11-18 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens with anthers huffish or yellow brown, 2.4-3 mm, the thecae equal; filaments 0.7-1.2 mm. Style slightly curved, 1.5-2.6 mm. Capsule 4-6 mm long. 2n = 36 (Lojtnant & Mo-lau 15017).

description: Erect shrub, 0.3-1 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems shortly glandular-hirsute and strongly glutinous. Leaves short-petiolate, ± fasciculate on lateral short shoots; blades sclerophyllous, ovate to elliptic, glabrous, 7-16 x 47 mm, acute or subacute, rounded at base, the margins entire or sparsely denticulate, revolute; upper surface dull green, nitidous, slightly flexuose; lower surface grayish-green (turning yellowish when dried), pinnate-venose; petioles 13 mm, glandular. Inflorescence composed of 12 pairs of 6-12-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.2-1.8 cm long; cyme bracts present; pedicels 0.6-1.6 cm. Sepals yellow-green, acute or subacute, 2.8-3.6 x 1.7-3 mm at anthesis, glandular-papillose on both sides. Corolla type VIII, bright yellow, unspotted; upper lip 2-3 x 3-4 mm; lower lip ascending from a vertical neck, saccate in 40-50% of its length, the upcurved portion 10-13 x 6-9 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers pale to deep yellow, glabrous, 1.9-2.5 mm, the thecae slightly deflexed; filaments 1.1-1.5 mm. Style arcuate, yellow, 1.22 mm. Capsule conic, slightly acuminate, 4-7 mm long, yellow-brown, glandular-papillose. 2n = 36 (Molau et al 574).

description: Erect or ascending Shrublet, 0.1-0.8 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems puberulous or short-villous with white hairs. Leaves decussate, not fasciculate; blades herbaceous, lanceolate, acute, cuneate or rounded at base, 1.3-4.6 x 0.4-2.4 cm, the margins sharply serrate or biserrate, with 8-18 teeth on each side of leaf; upper surface bright or grayish-green, sparsely puberulous to short-villous, slightly rugose; lower surface pale green, reticulate-venose, the major veins strigose or puberulous, interspaces glabrous or puberulous, yellowish-glandular; petioles 2-6 mm, white-villous. Inflorescence composed of 1-4 pairs of 1-4-flowered cymes, the peduncles 1.1-3.2 cm, the pedicels 0.5-1.3 cm; cyme bracts present, unusually large, lanceolate, 5-20 mm long, the margins entire or sparsely serrate. Sepals pale yellow-green, 4-6.7 x 3-6 mm at anthesis, acute, externally glandular and short-villous, internally puberulous. Corolla type VIII, unspotted, both lips white or whitish-yellow proximally, pale yellow or lemon yellow distally, the throat white inside; upper lip 2-3 mm long, 5-7 mm wide, and 7-9 mm high; lower lip saccate in 40-50% of length, the upcurved portion 10-19 x 6-11 mm. Stamens with anthers chestnut brown, 2.5-3.5 mm, the thecae divaricate; filaments 0.8-1.6 mm. Style 1.2-2.3 mm. Capsule semi-inferior, ovoid, acuminate, 5-8 mm long, glandular-puberulous to subglabrous. 2 n = 72 (Molau 709, new record).

description: Erect, rosulate herb, 3-16 cm tall, solitary or forming loose cushions. Leaves with blades ovate to spathulate, 1.2-4.1 x 1-3 cm, obtuse, cuneate or attenuate at base, the margins entire to crenulate or serrate, always entire in the proximal third; upper surface bright green to grayish-green, short-hirsute to villous with coarse white hairs, smooth or somewhat flexuose; lower surface pale green, pinnate-venose, villous to lanate with coarse white hairs, at least on the major veins; petioles ill-defined, reddish, 5-18 mm. Inflorescence composed of 1-8 erect 1-flowered peduncles (1.5-)6.5-16 cm long, representing ¼-4 pairs of cymes; peduncles reddish, glandular-puberulous or shortly glandular-villous; pedicels and cyme bracts reduced, absent. Sepals somewhat unequal, light green to yellow-green, often ± suffused with purple, obtuse, externally puberulous to villous with glandular hairs, internally glandular-papillose, the dorsal sepal 4.2-8 x 2.8-5.2 mm at anthesis. Corolla close to type XIV, bright yellow; upper lip ovate or subcircular, ascending, the margins infolded, always with dark purple-brown spots inside, 8-16 x 9-13 mm; lower lip pendent, subcircular to obovate, 10-18 x 8-19 mm, saccate in 40-60% of length, the throat often with purple-brown spots; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 4, exposed; anthers red-brown to purple, glandular-papillose to subglabrous, 1.6-2.8 mm across, the thecae strongly ascending, 1.8-3.2 mm long; filaments 2.2-4 mm. Style yellow, straight, (1.9-)2.8-5 mm long. Capsule broadly ovoid, 5-7 mm long, glandular-puberulous. Seeds reticulate-foveate.

description: Low shrubby plant, 10-40 cm tall, the stems ascending; inflorescence and distal parts of stems hirsute or villous with white glandless hairs mixed with minute, short, glandular hairs. Leaves decussate, short-petiolate or subsessile; blades ovate to elliptic, herbaceous, 8-18 x 3-9 mm, obtuse, cuneate at base, the margins deflexed or slightly revolute, crenate; upper surface bright green or grayish-green, shortly white-hirsute, slightly rugose; lower surface pale green or whitish, pinnate-venose, the veins white-hirsute, interspaces glandular-pilose; petioles 1-4 mm, villous or hirsute. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 2-4-flowered cymes, the peduncles 1.3-3.7 cm, the pedicels 1.2-1.9 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals yellow-green, turning purple in exposure, 4.2-7.3 x 3.2-5.9 mm at anthesis, subacute to slightly acuminate, externally tomentose with white glandular hairs, internally glandular-puberulous or glabrescent and with a short-tomentose border along the margins, the margins entire. Corolla type II, bright yellow or bright lemon yellow, internally with numerous wine-red spots in the throat (sometimes lacking in some flowers of a specimen); upper lip rounded triangular, 36 x 4-6 mm; lower lip 14-23 x 9-15 mm, inflated, distally upcurved, saccate in 40-60% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 9; anthers yellowish-white to huffish, 3.9-5.1 mm, the thecae unequal, dehiscing distally in 80-90% of their length; filaments 0.7-1.5 mm. Style arcuate, 2.5-4 mm. Capsule ovoid, 5-7 mm long, shortly glandular-hirsute. 2n = 36 (Molau 808, new record).

description: Low shrubby plant, 10-40 cm tall, the stems erect or ascending; inflorescence and distal parts of stems glandular-puberulous or shortly glandular-villous. Leaves decussate, short-petiolate; blades subcoriaceous, narrowly triangular to linear, 6-14(-33) x 2-6(-11) mm, obtuse and ± hamate at apex, cordate to truncate at base, the margins crenate, usually strongly revolute; upper surface olive green, glandular-puberulous or shortly glandular-hirsute, bullate; lower surface pale green, pinnate-venose, glandular-hirsute or glandular-villous; petioles 1-3 mm, puberulous to hirsute with glandular hairs. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of l-4(-20)-flow-ered cymes; primary peduncles 0.3-1.4 cm; pedicels 0.5-1.5 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals yel low-green, 2.3-3.7 x 1.7-3.4 mm at anthesis, obtuse or subacute, externally glandular-puberulous or shortly glandular-hirsute, internally glandular-puberulous or papillose, the margins entire. Corolla type XII, bright to deep yellow, usually with a deep red blotch in the throat; upper lip 2-3 x 3-4 mm; lower lip 7-14 x 5-9 mm, saccate in 40-50% of length; elaiophore present, small, linear to rectangular, marginal. Stamens type 10; anthers yellowish-white to pale buff, 2.5-3.9 mm, the thecae unequal, ± ascending, dehiscing distally; filaments 0.5-0.8 mm. Style decurved at apex, 1.4-2.5 mm. Capsule ovoid or narrowly ovoid, 4-7 mm long, usually slightly acuminate, shortly glandular-pilose.

description: Erect or ascending shrub, 0.25-1.5 m high, much branched; inflorescence and distal parts of stems puberulous or short-hirsute with glandular hairs. Leaves ± fasciculate on lateral short shoots; blades narrowly elliptic to linear, 10-25 x 2-4 mm, acute and ± mucronulate at apex, attenuate at base; upper surface dark grayish green, smooth (but with the midrib impressed), glabrous, glutinous; lower surface white, incanous, the midrib prominent, other venation obsolete; margins entire, revolute; petioles 1-3 mm, glandular. Inflorescence composed of 2-5 pairs of 1-4-flowered cymes on peduncles 0.4-1.3 cm long; cyme bracts present; pedicels 0.5-1.6 cm. Sepals yellow-green, ovate, acute or subacute, 3.8-6.4 x 1.2-3.6 mm at anthesis, externally glandular-puberulous, internally glabrous. Corolla type II, bright yellow, unspotted; upper lip subglobose, 2-4 x 3-4 mm; lower lip U-shaped when seen in lateral view, 13-20 x 7-10 mm, saccate in 40-60% of its length, the sac ascending; elaiophore present. Stamens type 11; anthers buff, 3-4.8 mm, the thecae divaricate or slightly deflexed; filaments 0.8-1.4 mm. Style arcuate, 1.6-2.8 mm, glabrous or minutely glandular-puberulous proximally. Capsule ovoid, 6-8 mm long, brownish, glandular-puberulous.

description: Erect or ascending subshrub, 0.3-1.2(-2) m tall, often densely tufted; inflorescence and distal parts of stems villous or hirsute with coarse whitish hairs. Leaves petiolate, ternate or less often (ca. 40% of the specimens studied) decussate; blades herbaceous or subcoriaceous, ovate, (1.2-)2.7-7.4 x (0.9-)2-4.8 cm, acute or subacuate, truncate or slightly cordate (rarely broadly cuneate) at base, the margins sharply serrate or (usually) biserrate; upper surface olive green, nitidous, short-pilose, flexuose and slightly bullate; lower surface grayish-green, pinnate-venose, the veins raised, roughly pilose or villous, interspaces glabrous or finely villous, glandular; petioles (2-)6-16(-28) mm, coarsely whitish-villous. Inflorescence composed of (1-)2-4 pairs or triplets of (2-)4-12-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 0.8-7.4 cm; pedicels 0.6-1.8(-2.5) cm; cyme bracts present in lowermost cymes, otherwise absent. Sepals light green or light yellow-green, 3.36 x (2.0-)3-4.6 mm at anthesis, acute or subacute, externally pilose or villous with coarse hairs, internally minutely puberulous. Corolla type VIII, light yellow or light greenish-yellow, internally wih a large purple spot or one or two crossbands in the throat; upcurved portion of lower lip 7-15(-18) x 5-12 mm. Stamens with anthers light brown, 1.8-2.6 mm, the thecae divaricate or slightly deflexed; filaments 0.7-1.5 mm. Style 1.5-2.4 mm long. Capsule conic, 46 mm long, slightly acuminate, shortly glandular-hirsute.

description: Frutex, 0.3-1.5 m altus, ramosissimus, cauli-bus rufo-hirsutis. Folia decussata, breviter petiolata; lamina subcoriacea, ovata, subacuta, ad basin rotundata vel cuneata, 1.3-3.2 x 0.8-1.5 cm, utrimque hirsuta, infra pinnato-venosa, nervis purpureis, margine leviter serrato, deflexo; petiolo dense purpureo-hirsuto, 2-4 mm longi. Inflorescentia terminalis, 1-2 paria cymarum 4-12 florum complectens; pedunculis primariis 1.5-3.5 cm longis; bracteae cymarum adsunt, ovatae, citrinae, ca 1 cm longae. Sepala ovata, citrina, mucronata, 8-11 x 6.3-8.5 mm sub anthesi, utrimque glanduloso-villosa, margine integro. Corolla vivide flava, immaculata, labio superiore 5-7 x 7-10 mm, labio inferiore 22-30 x 16-20 mm; elaeophorus adest. Antherae bubalinae, ad basin glanduloso-puberulae, 4.5-5 mm longae, totae dehiscentes, thecae divaricatae, arcuatae, aequales. Stylus rectus, 4-4.5 mm.

description: Erect shrub, much branched, 0.3-1.5 m tall, stem to 2 cm diam. at base, distal parts of stems densely reddish-hirsute with coarse, glandless hairs. Leaves decussate, short-petiolate; blade subcoriaceous, ovate, 1.3-3.2 x 0.8-1.5 cm, subacute, cuneate or rounded at base, the margins shallowly serrate, deflexed or narrowly revolute; upper surface deep green, flexuose, dull, hirsute with coarse, reddish-septate, glandless hairs; lower surface pale green, pinnate-venose (tertiary veins weakly raised), the major veins purple-hirsute; petioles 2-4 mm, densely reddish-hirsute. Inflorescence distal, composed of 1-2 pairs of 4-12 flowered cymes; primary peduncles 1.5-3.5 cm, densely reddish-hirsute; cyme bracts present, conspicuous, yellow-green, ovate, ca 1 cm long, glandular-hirsute; pedicels 1.2-2.7 cm, lemon-yellow, densely glandular-villous. Sepals herbaceous, ovate, lemon-yellow, 8-11 x 6.3-8.5 mm at anthesis, mucronate at apex, shortly glandular-villous on both sides, the margins entire. Corolla type 1, bright yellow, unspotted, the upper lip glandular-hirsute, 5-7 x 7-10 mm, emarginate at apex, the lower lip projecting, 22-30 x 16-20 mm, saccate in 55-65% of its length, glandular-pilose (most densely so proximally); elaiophore present. Stamens type 7; anthers buff to yellow-brown; 4.5-5 mm long, dehiscing throughout, glandular-puberulous at base, otherwise glabrous, the thecae slightly arcuate and somewhat deflexed, equal; filaments glabrous, 1.2-1.5 mm long. Style straight, glabrous, 4-4.5 mm. Capsule not seen at maturity.

description: Erect or ascending subshrub, 0.5-1.5 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems densely puberulous. Leaves with blades ± circular in inclusive outline (rarely rhombic), 0.9-1.7(-2.7) x 0.9-2.3 cm, acute, cordate or truncate at base, the margins deflexed or revolute, lobate or lobulate with 2-4 lobes on each side, rarely serrate; upper surface dark green, smooth, densely puberulous; lower surface incanous (densely tomentose with short grayish-white glandless hairs), the midrib and secondary veins raised, other venation ± obsolete; petioles 4-10 mm, short-tomentose. Inflorescence composed of two pairs (rarely a single pair) of (4-) 12-40-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 0.6-3.4 cm; pedicels 0.7-1.4 cm; cyme bracts absent. Sepals light green to brownish-green, 2.3-3.5 x 1.8-2.6 mm at anthesis, acute or slightly acuminate. Corolla type VIII, bright golden yellow, unspotted; upper lip 3-4 x 4 mm; lower lip strongly upcurved, saccate in 50-60% of length, the upcurved portion 9-14 x 6-10 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers whitish, 1.5-1.8 mm, the thecae divaricate or slightly deflexed; filaments 0.8-1.2 mm. Style 1.3-2 mm, curved distally. Capsule conical, usually slightly acuminate, 5-7 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Erect or ascending subshrub, 0.5-1.5 m tall; stems and inflorescence glabrous or puberulous, strongly glutinous. Leaves sessile; blades subcoriaceous, lanceolate or narrowly elliptic, (4.5-)6-12(-15) x (0.4-)0.7-1.8 cm, acute, cuneate or attenuate at base; upper surface vivid green, rugose, glabrous, glutinous; lower surface villous or lanate with coarse greenish-white hairs; margins denticulate, revolute. Inflorescence composed of 2-4 pairs of 4-14-flowered cymes on primary peduncles 0.8-7 cm long; cyme bracts absent; pedicels 0.8-2.5 cm. Sepals triangular to ovate, green, 2-3.5(-4.5) x 1.8-3.5(-4.5) mm at anthesis, acute, glabrous, glandular. Corolla type V, bright to deep yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 4-6 x 7-10 mm, the lower lip 12-18 x 914 mm, saccate in 40-60% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers buffish, glabrous, 2-3 mm; filaments 0.8-1 mm. Style slightly curved, 1.5-2.3 mm. Capsule ovoid or conical, 4-6 mm long, brown, glandular-puberulous. 2n = 36 (Harling & Andersson 12668, Harling et al 14969).

description: Erect or ascending herb, 0.3-1 m tall, the stems succulent, light green, purple at the nodes, to 2 cm diam. at base. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate (rarely lanceolate), acute or acuminate, (4-)6-12 x (2.6-)4-8.8 cm, cuneate to truncate at base, deeply lobate with 2-5 pairs of lateral lobes, the margins sharply biserrate; petioles 1.3-6 cm long, hardly winged, connate across the nodes with ridges 2-4 mm wide. Inflorescence with primary peduncles 3.1-13 cm long, pedicels 1.7-4.7 cm. Sepals ovate, light green with purple margins, acute or acuminate, 5.2-9.6 x 3.6-7.8 mm at anthesis, externally sparsely short-pilose, internally glandular-puberulous, the margins dentate. Corolla type III, pale or light yellow, unspotted, the throat with a large deep yellow area inside in the middle part, otherwise light yellow; upper lip 2-4 x 3-6 mm; lower lip (10-) 13-20 x 715 mm, saccate in 70-80% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens 4.2-6.5 mm long, the thecae strongly unequal, light brown, both stipitate, the posterior one 1.3-2.2 mm long, the anterior 0.5-1.3 mm, the connective light to orange-yellow, elongated, dorsally with a blunt to sharp tooth 0.1-0.2 mm high (sometimes absent); filaments 0.5-1.5 mm. Style arcuate, 2.5-4.7 mm. Capsule subglobose, 5-8 mm long, light green, ± suffused with purple, sparsely glandular-puberulous. 2n = 64 (Molau 696, 722, new record).

description: Erect shrub, 0.6-2 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems villous with grayish-white hairs. Leaves with blades ovate, oblong, or obovate, 1.5-2.6 x 0.6-1.2 cm, acute or subacute, cuneate at base, the margins denticulate or entire, deflexed or somewhat revolute; upper surface dark green, almost smooth, glutinous, villous (glabrescent with age) with whitish hairs; lower surface pale or whitish-green, reticulate-venose, the midrib villous, otherwise glabrous; petioles 3-6 mm, villous to lanate. Inflorescence composed of a single pair of 4-12-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.5-2.6 cm, the pedicels 1.2-2.4 cm; cyme bracts rudimentary, linear, 15 x 0.5-1 mm. Sepals ovate, bright yellow, acute, 3.6-6.2 x 3-4.5 mm at anthesis, externally glandular-puberulous or glabrous, internally glabrous, the margins whitish-villous. Corolla type XV, deep yellow; upper lip arched, 3-5 x 4-7 mm; lower lip oblong, flattened, pendent, 8-15 x 5-8 mm, saccate in 25-40% of length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 4; anthers dark brown, 2.1-2.5 mm across, glandular-papillose at base, the thecae ascending, equal, 1.2-1.6 mm long; filaments 1.2-2 mm. Style arcuate, 3.6-7.3 mm. Capsule widely ovoid, ± acuminate, brownish, 3-5 mm long, glandular-puberulous or -hirsute.

description: Ascending herb or subshrub, at least 0.5-1 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems puberulous to villous with glandular hairs. Leaves with blades herbaceous, ovate, 3.2-6.9 x 2.8-5.5 cm, acute, truncate to cordate at base, the margins lobate with 5-13 lobes along each side of blade, the lobes irregularly serrate; upper surface olive to deep green, puberulous or pilose, somewhat rugose; lower surface pale green, reticulate-venose (though predominantly pinnate-venose), the major veins villous or hirsute with white glandular hairs, interspaces glandular-hirsute; petioles 1.2-3.5 cm, dorsally densely white-villous, otherwise puberulous or pilose with glandular hairs. Inflorescence composed of 2-4 pairs of 8-32-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles divaricate, 1.6-6.2 cm, the pedicels 1.3-2.1 cm. Sepals ovate to lanceolate, olivaceous, 5.8-10 x 3.6-7.3 mm at anthesis, acute, externally glandular-puberulous, internally glandular-papillose, the margins entire. Corolla type III, the lower lip distally deep yellow to orange-yellow, otherwise bright yellow, the throat with a large purple blotch inside; upper lip 4-6 x 4-5 mm; lower lip saccate in 25-40% of length, the upcurved portion 1519 x 11-13 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens type 9; anthers yellowish-white, glabrous, 4.7-6 mm, dehiscing distally, the thecae unequal or subequal, divaricate or somewhat ascending; filaments 1.5-1.9 mm. Style 3.4-5 mm, decurved at apex. Capsule ovoid, 6-7 mm long, glandular-hirsute.

description: Ascending or semi-scandent shrub or subshrub, 0.7-3 m tall, the shoots sparsely branched, the lateral branches short; inflorescence and distal parts of stems tomentose or short-villous with whitish hairs. Leaves with blades narrowly elliptic to linear, 2-4.2 x 0.2-0.7 cm, subacute, cuneate or attenuate at base; upper surface deep green, short-strigose with white hairs, the midrib sunken, otherwise smooth; lower surface whitish-green, the midrib villous, otherwise incanous, pinnate-venose (lateral veins often obsolete); petioles 1-5 mm, villous. Inflorescence composed of 2-4 pairs of 12-16-flowered cymes on primary peduncles 1.3-3.5 cm long; pedicels 1.1-2.2 cm. Sepals greenish-yellow, ovate, acute or subacute, 3.3-5.2 x 2.8-3.7 mm at anthesis, short-villous on both sides. Corolla type XV, bright yellow with numerous red dots in the throat; upper lip somewhat hooded, acuminate, 4-6 x 5-6 mm, tapering into a truncate apex; lower lip 9-12 x 5-10 mm, obovate to almost circular, somewhat flattened, projecting or slightly pendent, saccate in 25-40% of length, the saccate portion concave, the orifice wide open, exposing dots and anthers; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 12; anthers dark or medium brown, 2.5-3.8 mm across, the thecae deflexed, each one 1.8-2.7 mm long, the connective acute or acuminate; filaments 1.2-1.9 mm. Style arcuate, slender, 3.8-5.4 mm, yellow-green, the stigma capitate. Capsule ovoid, yellow-brown, 5-6 mm long, short-villous. 2n = 36 (Molau 760, new record).

description: Erect or ascending, low shrubby plant, 0.2-0.6 m tall, rarely semi-scandent and up to 1.5 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems sparsely white arachnoid-lanate. Leaves decussate, indistinctly short-petiolate; blades coriaceous or subcoriaceous, lanceolate to linear, 0.8-2.5 x 0.20.8 cm, obtuse at apex, cuneate or rounded at base, the margins revolute, entire or crenulate in the distal part; upper surface grayish-green, sparsely arachnoid-lanate; lower surface densely white arachnoid-lanate; petioles 1-3 mm, arachnoid-lanate. Inflorescence composed of 1-3(-4) pairs of 1-4-flowered cymes on peduncles 0.6-4.5(-8.5) cm long; pedicels 0.6-3.3 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals yellow-green to light yellow, acute, 3.5-5.7(-8.2) x 2.5-4.4(-6.1) mm at anthesis, externally glandular and sparsely arachnoid-lanate, internally glabrous, the margins entire. Corolla type XI, light yellow or bright lemon yellow, with one or two crossbands of red spots in the throat; upper lip 3-5 x 3-6 mm; lower lip 11-23 x 7-18 mm, saccate in 70-80% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 9; anthers buff or yellowish-white, 3-4.5(-5.5) mm, the thecae subequal, dehiscing in about 75% of their length; filaments 0.6-1.5 mm. Style curved, (1.7-)2-3.5 mm. Capsule conical or ovoid, 5-7 mm long, yellowish-brown, shortly glandular-hirsute.

description: Low shrubby plant, 10-40 cm tall, much branched; inflorescence and distal parts of stems glandular-hirsute. Leaves decussate, short-petiolate; blades subcoriaceous, lanceolate, 11-18 x 4-8 mm, the margins crenate, deflexed or somewhat revolute; upper surface dark olive green, somewhat flexuose, glandular-hirsute; lower surface grayish-green, pinnate-venose, shortly glandular-pilose; petioles 1-4 mm, hirsute. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 2- 6-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 1.6-6 cm; pedicels 1.2-3.2 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals bright green, turning purple in exposure, 4-8 x 3.1-4.4 mm at anthesis, acute or slightly acuminate, externally shortly glandular-hirsute, internally glandular, subglabrous, the margins entire or few-denticulate. Corolla type XV, bright yellow, internally with a blackish-purple crossband in the throat just below filaments; upper lip acuminate, 6-9 x 5-6 mm; lower lip pendent, flattened, obovate to almost circular, 13-17 x 11-14 mm, saccate in 50-60% of length, elaiophore absent or composed of a few minute and remote glands. Stamens type 10; anthers yellowish-white, 3.7-5 mm, the thecae unequal, divaricate or slightly ascending, dehiscing distally in 40-50% of length; filaments 1-1.4 mm. Style arcuate to almost straight, curved at apex, 4.2-7.9 mm. Capsule ovoid, 6-8 mm long, acuminate, shortly glandular-hirsute.

description: Scandent shrub, the stems up to 4 m long, much branched, the branches divaricately spreading; inflorescence and distal parts of stems densely villous with pale purplish or purplish-white hairs. Leaves with blades herbaceous, ovate to elliptic, 3.7-7.9 x 1.4-2.8 cm, acute, attenuate at base, the margins serrate or crenate; upper surface yellowish-green, rugose, pilose or short-villous; lower surface pale green, essentially pinnate-venose, densely white-villous; petioles ill-defined, 4-11 mm, densely villous. Inflorescence diffuse, intercalary, composed of 1-4-flowered axillary cymes, the peduncles 1-2.6 cm long; cyme bracts present; pedicels 1.5-4.8 cm. Sepals subequal, ovate, light yellow-green, acute, 4.5-6.3 x 3.1-4.8 mm at anthesis, externally villous, internally glabrous except for the short-tomentose border along the margins. Corolla type VII, bright to deep yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 5-8 x 9-13 mm, the lower lip 16-28 x 12-20 mm, saccate in 50-60% of its length; elaiophore present but narrow and not very dense, the glands not forming a dense cushion. Stamens type 1; anthers medium to dark brown, glabrous, 2.52.9 mm, the thecae equal; filaments 1-1.8 mm. Style slightly curved, 2.6-3.2 mm. Capsule ovoid, light brownish-green, 5-6 mm long, densely beset with short-stalked glands.

description: Subrosulate ascending herb, only one or two vegetative internodes developed, 25-50 cm tall; stems and inflorescence pilose or villous with huffish to purplish hairs. Leaves sessile or (at lowermost nodes) petiolate; blades herbaceous, ovate, 2-5.9 x 1.2-2.9 cm, subacute, cuneate at base, the margins serrulate or almost entire (on upper leaves); upper surface olive green, flexuose, coarsely hirsute; lower surface light green, pinnate-venose, the veins hirsute, interspaces pilose; petioles, when present, 5-15 mm, hirsute. Inflorescence composed of a single pair (rarely 2) of 8-12-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 4.511 cm, the pedicels 1.2-2.2 cm; cyme bracts absent. Sepals purplish-green, ovate, 2-2.4 x 1.52 mm at ahthesis, acute or subacute, the margins entire, externally shortly glandular-hirsute, internally glabrous at base, distally glandular-puberulous. Corolla type XV, pale yellow, the upper lip arched, 3-4 x 4-6 mm, the lower lip ± pendent, flattened, 10-15 x 7-11 mm, saccate in 40-50% of length, the throat with red dots inside (sometimes absent); elaiophore absent. Stamens type 1; anthers buff, 1.5-2 mm, glabrous, the thecae divaricate, equal; filaments 0.81 mm. Style 3.2-4 mm, arcuate or almost straight. Capsule ovoid, slightly acuminate, purplish, 46 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Caulescent or acaulescent herbs of very variable habit. Leaves rosulate or fasciculate or distributed along a stem, polystichous or distichous, entire; blades ligulate to narrowly triangular or linear; leaf-scales centrally symmetric. Scape usually distinct. Inflorescence various, usually of distichous-flowered spikes or sometimes reduced to a single polystichous-flowered spike by the reduction of the spikes to single flowers or rarely the whole inflorescence reduced to a single flower. Floral bracts conspicuous to minute; flowers perfect, mostly short-pedicellate. Sepals convolute, usually symmetric, free or equally or posteriorly joined. Petals free, naked. Stamens of various lengths relative to the petals and to the pistil. Ovary superior glabrous. Ovules usually many, caudate. Fruit a septicidal capsule. Seeds erect, narrowly cylindric or fusiform, the plumose appendage basal, straight, white.

description: Plants rather dull olive green to brown or black, ascending or pendent, not dendroid. Branching Lejeunea-type, short curved flagelliform branches present. Stems rigid, epidermal cells as large as medulla cells, all cell walls strongly thickened and brown; ventral merophyte four or more cell rows wide. Leaves when dry suberect-convoluted (plane in the Asiatic subgen. Sandeanthus), when moist widely spreading and convex, often somewhat falcate, lobe ovate to oblong, apex rounded or acute-apiculate, margins toothed or entire, dorsal base auriculate; leaf cells elongate, with cordate trigones and intermediate thickenings (cells isodiametrical with almost evenly thickened walls in subgen. Sandeanthus), trigones usually coarse and often coalesced, oil bodies coarsely segmented, Calypogeia-type, ca. 3-10 per cell, ocelli lacking; vitta present or absent. Lobules usually small, l/4× lobe length or less, never reduced, inflated along the keel, with 1-2 teeth; hyaline papilla positioned on the inner side of the lobule near the proximal base of the first tooth. Underleaves ± spathulate to subquadrate, often somewhat squarrose and concave due to upcurved margins, gibbose in the lower half, apex rounded to emarginate, margins toothed or entire, bases cuneate, usually slightly auriculate, insertion line straight; underleaf base at the rhizoid disc bistratose. Androecia on short or long shoots with 3-25 series of bracts, bracts usually smaller than leaves, lobules enlarged, hypostatic or epistatic, underleaves present throughout; antheridia two per bract. Gynoecia with 1-2 lejeuneoid subfloral innovations, bracts in l(-3) series, as large as or slightly larger than leaves, margins toothed (rarely entire), lobules well-developed, keel unwinged or occasionally with a small wing; bracteoles undivided or short bifid, margins toothed, rarely entire. Perianths flattened, with 3 sharp keels, keels toothed, rarely entire. Sporophyte: seta not articulate; elaters 72 per capsule; otherwise as in the tribe. Vegetative reproduction by regeneration from leaf cells.

description: Plants large, to 10 cm high, Dicranum-like, in loose, yellowish green tufts. Stems erect, unbranched, tomentose, equally foliate with tortuose, recurved leaves. Leaves ca. 1 cm long, from ovate base gradually contracted into a long subula, strongly serrate in the upper third. Costa filling 1/3-1/2 of the leaf base, excurrent, in transverse section with ventral and dorsal rows of stereids, ridged at back in the basal part, lamellose at back in the upper part, the lamellae being serrate. Alar cells large, inflated, thin-walled, reddish-brown. Basal laminal cells longly rectangular, incrassate and pitted, at margins shorter (2-3:1), not pitted. Upper laminal cells subquadrate, incrassate. Setae in bundles of 3-4 arising from the tip of the stems, ca. 9 mm long, brownish. Capsules curved, inclined, brownish, 2 mm long. Operculum 1.5 mm long, darker coloured, obliquely rostrate.

description: Plants to 4 cm high, robust, densely foliate with strongly falcate, homomallous leaves. Leaves 4-5 mm long, from ovate base contracted into a long, slender tip. Costa filling 1/3 of leaf base, in transverse section with bands of median deuter cells and dorsal and ventral stereids, excurrent in a long, only slightly serrate subula. Alar cells inconspicuous. Inner basal laminal cells rectangular, thin-walled, pellucid, 15-18 × 30-45 µm. Outer basal laminal cells in 10 rows narrow and elongate, 2-4 × 25-35 µm, chlorophyllose. Upper laminal cells rectangular, incrassate and pitted, 10-13 × 40-70 µm. Lamina vanishing below midleaf. Sporophyte not known.

description: Shrubs or small trees (rarely subscandent in T. capensis). Leaves simple, 3-foliolate or imparipinnately compound, the leaflets serrate. Inflorescence a terminal raceme or racemose panicle. Flowers with the calyx cupular, with five shallow, often apiculate deltoid lobes; corolla yellow or orange-red, tubular-campanulate to narrowly tubular-salverform, glabrous outside, the stamens exserted or included, the anthers divaricate to basally divergent, glabrous or pilose; pollen grains single, oblong, 3-colporate, the exine microreticulate; ovary narrowly cylindric, more or less lepidote, the ovules 2-seriate in each locule; disk cupular-pulvinate to pulvinate-cylindric. Fruit a linear capsule, somewhat compressed parallel to the septum but dehiscing perpendicular to it, the valves smooth, more or less glabrous; seeds thin, bialate, the wings hyaline-membranaceous, sharply demarcated from the seed body.

description: Shrub 3-5 m tall, much branched, with slender branches, outer branches often scandent. Leafy branchlets glabrous, dark green, terete; older branches pale brown to grayish; lenticels sparse, punctiform to linear. Stipules present only in bud, narrowly triangular, glabrous outside, glabrous, with few colleters inside, 30-40 × 5-6 mm, dark green, readily caducous, leaving a linear whitish scar, ca. 0.5 mm wide. Leaves 30-45(-60) × 8.5-12 cm, LAV 3:1 to 3.5:1; narrowly lanceolate, oblanceolate to narrowly elliptic, acute (BA = 20-30°) at base, acute at apex, sometimes tapering to an acumen 2-3 cm long, dark green above, pale green below, subcoriaceous; drying brown, stiff-chartaceous; glabrous above, glabrous to hirsutulous below, pellucid punctate; primary and secondary veins glabrous to hirsutulous, prominent below; secondary veins 15-25 each side; tertiary veins starting subparallel and openly reticulate in the center, evident below; petioles 2-7.5 cm long, 2.5-4.5 mm thick, subterete, glabrous to hirsutulous, basally thickened but not pulvinate; domatia absent. Inflorescences racemoid secundiflorous panicles to thyrsoid-secundiflorous with opposite or subopposite decussate branches, sometimes without lateral branches, 25-60 cm long, to 17 cm wide, basal branches to 20 cm long, lateral branches usually ascending and to 4 pairs, basal portion of axis not branched 2-15 cm long; rachis terete, rachis and branches glabrous (rarely hirsutulous); flowers alternate on distal branches or rarely in cymules, usually hanging downward, secund (pedicel attachments opposite or alternate); distal bracts 1-3 × 2-3 mm, deltoid; bracteoles subtending flowers 0.5-0.8 × 1-2 mm, deltoid, glabrous. Flowers pedicellate, pedicels 4-25 mm long, glabrous to hirtellous; hypanthium narrowly obconical, 4-6 × 2- 2.5 mm, glabrous to hirtellous; flower buds cylindrical. Calyx reduced to a wavy margin with barely distinguishable lobes, ca. 1 mm long. Corolla tubular with small erect lobes (not spreading), 2.5-4 cm long, greenish yellow (rarely pinkish yellow), semi-fleshy when fresh; tube subcylindrical, faintly striate, 1.5-2.5 cm long, 2.5-4 mm wide at base and 3.5-5 mm wide at the orifice, glabrous outside; antrorse-strigose at base inside, without a ring of hairs, the remaining medial and superior zones glabrous; lobes 5, 1/4-1/3 of corolla length, 9-13 × 1.5-3 mm, triangular to ovate, glabrous outside, glabrous, with minute conical-bul-late hairs (hairs 0.1-0.3 mm long) inside. Stamens 5, included (only the very tip exserted), subequal, attached 4.5-5.5 mm from the base of the tube; filaments 6-7 mm long, flattened at base, microscopically (40 x) papillose throughout, minutely barbate at base with white puberulent hairs; anthers cylindrical, rectilinear (never convex), 9-12 x 1.5-2 mm, dorsifixed near the base, base elliptic, smooth throughout. Pollen exine densely foveolate (non-echinate). Style exserted, 30-40 mm long, glabrous, microscopically (40×) papillose; style branches ovate, 1-1.5 mm long, stigmatic surface smooth; immature fruits reddish green, semi-fleshy. Capsules obovoid to oblong, apex shallowly hemispherical, (10-)15-20 × 7-9 mm, without lenticels, dark brown, glabrous throughout; disk black, obviously exceeding the calyx; disk septicidal dehiscence absent even in old capsules. Seeds 1.17-1.67 × 1-1.33 mm.

description: Stem cylindrical, 10-22 m tall, to 20 cm in diam., gray, smooth, with nodes obscure and internodes to 30 cm long; stilt roots diagonal, closely spaced, branched near or below ground level, 12 m x 8-10 cm, with blunt spines. Leaves 4-6, spreading; sheaths forming a compact crown-shaft, 1.2-1.5 m long, glaucous, gray-green, outer surface covered with small apiculate brown scales or densely brown-tomentose; petiole 2-20 cm long (including apical part of sheath), ca. 5 cm in diam., proximally rounded abaxially and shallowly grooved adaxially, terete from middle upwards, glabrescent; rachis 2.4-2.5 m long, ridged and densely-brown-tomentose adaxially, rounded abaxially; pinnae 31-37 per side, subopposite, cuneate with entire margins and blunt praemorse apices, green glabrous adaxially, gray-white waxy abaxially with minute regularly arranged brown scales, these sometimes elongated into hairs, and with lines 3 mm wide of dense white or brown tomentum running parallel to veins, split to the base into 2-9 stiff segments inserted at different angles and radiating in different planes; veins prominent abaxially, yellow, several on proximal segment of each pinna, one on distal segment, with similar scales to pinnae; proximal pinna split into 1-3 segments, proximal segment to 50 cm long and 1 cm wide at mid-point; middle pinna split into nine segments, proximal segment 90-108 cm long, 4 cm wide at mid-point, distal segment to 80 cm long, 2 cm wide at mid-point; apical pinna entire, deeply bifid, to 30 cm long, 8 cm wide at mid-point. Inflorescence pendulous in bud and at anthesis, to 1.5 m long; peduncle terete, curved, 45-50 x 3 cm, densely brown-tomentose, glabrescent; prophyll inserted near base of peduncle, caducous, ancipitous, coriaceous, to 6 cm long, splitting apically; peduncular bracts ten, inserted ca. 3 cm apart, brown-tomentose, glabrescent, proximal ca. 3 to 16 cm long and similar to prophyll, distal remainder to 150 cm long, woody, with non-splitting apex; rachis 40-45 cm long, rachillae to 50, glabrous, spirally arranged, cream-colored at anthesis, with a flattened sterile proximal section to 14 cm long, proximal ones branched into seven rachillae to 75 cm long, distal ones simple to 70 cm long, triads spirally arranged, to 5 mm apart, ebracteolate; flowers proximally in triads, distally sta-minate in pairs or solitary, yellow; staminate flowers 6-8 mm long; sepals depressed-ovate, 1.5 x 1.5 mm, very shortly connate proximally, imbricate, strongly gibbous; petals ovate-lanceolate, 6-7 x 2 mm, valvate; stamens six; filaments linear, 1 mm long; anthers 6 mm long, sub-basifixed; pistillode 0.5 mm, blunt, 3-lobed; pollen with clavate or clavate-rugulate exine; pistillate flowers 2-3 mm long; sepals depressed-ovate, 2 x 2 mm, gibbous, imbricate; petals ovate, 2 x 2 mm, imbricate proximally, valvate distally; staminodes six, dentiform; stigmas sessile, triangular, 0.5 mm long; ovary glabrous, 3-locular; ovules apically attached; fruit more or less globose, 3-3.5 x 2.5-3 cm, stigmatic scar basal; epicarp glabrous, thin, greenish-yellow at maturity and splitting irregularly; mesocarp 3-4 mm thick, white; endocarp papery; seeds more or less globose, 2-2.5 x 1.5-2 cm, basally attached; raphe branches reticulate, spreading from base; hilum rounded; embryo basal; eophyll bifid.

description: Plants in dense tufts, light green to brownish green, to 3.5 cm high. Stems equally foliate with appressed leaves, slender, filiform. Leaves only 2.5 mm long, lanceolate, ending in a canaliculate leaf tip. Margins entire. Costa filling 2/3 of the leaf base, excurrent, in transverse section with ventral hyalocysts, slightly ridged at back. Alar cells lacking. Basal laminal cells hyaline, thin-walled, rectangular, 5-10 × 45-60 µm, towards the margins in 5-7 rows narrower. Upper laminal cells short rectangular, ca. 2:1, 10-16 × 16-32 µm, incrassate. Sporophyte not known.

description: Plants in compact, light to yellowish green tufts, to 5 cm high. Stems equally foliate with ap-pressed leaves. Leaves ca. 6 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, gradually narrowed into a long, smooth subula. Costa filling 3/4 of the leaf-base, excurrent, in transverse section with ventral hyalocysts and a band of dorsal substereids, smooth at back. Alar cells lacking or poorly developed. Basal laminal cells rectangular, thin-walled, 6-12 × 29-58 µm, at margins in 7-9 rows narrower, elongate, forming a hyaline border. Upper laminal cells elongate oval, incrassate, 3-6 × 16-22 µm, ca. 6-8:1. Sporophyte as in C. nivalis.

description: Small tree. Young shoots glabrous, pale to midbrown, with a few lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 7-11.3 × 3.2-4.1 cm, elliptic-oblong to broadly oblanceolate, apex caudate, base acute or slightly attenuate, chartaceous, glabrous; venation brochidodromous, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 15-25 pairs, parallel, slightly arcuate, joining near the margin to form a submarginal vein; intersecondaries long; tertiaries parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin. Petiole 5-8 mm long, channelled, glabrous. Flowers axillary, solitary or paired. Sepals 5-6, ca. 1.5 mm long, rounded, sparsely appressed hairy outside, ciliate. Fruiting pedicel slender, 1.4-1.5 cm long, glabrous. Fruit 1.8-2.2 cm long, narrowly ellipsoid, apex acute, with persistent style, base acute, thin-walled, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, 1.6-1.7 cm long, slender-ellipsoid, apex rounded, base acute, slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.2 mm thick; scar basi-ventral, extending half way up the seed, or slightly more; embryo with thick flat, free cotyledons, radicle exserted; endosperm present, about equalling the thickness of the cotyledons. The flowers of this plant have not yet been collected, and the leaf, fruit and seed structure are scarcely sufficient to place it in Sideroxylon. The leaf venation is a type commonly found in American species of Sideroxylon, but it is also consistent with many species of Chrysophyllum sect. Chrysophyllum. The basi-ventral seed scar reaching to halfway up the seed is also typical of Chrysophyllum sect. Chrysophyllum, but unknown in Sideroxylon. In the latter the seed scar is usually basi-ventral and confined to the lower part of the seed, or rarely completely adaxial, and then almost full length. The characteristics of the embryo also suggest Chrysophyllum. It has thick flat cotyledons, surrounded by a well developed layer of endosperm. The embryo of Sideroxylon has either foliaceous cotyledons with well-developed endosperm, or thick plano-convex cotyledons with no endosperm.

description: Young branches velutinous or tomentose, indumentum persistent. Leaves pinnate with a terminal bud showing intermittent growth, 15-30 cm long; petiole semiterete, rhachis terete, velutinous becoming subglabrous; petiolule 2-4 mm long. Leaflets 2-6 pairs, elliptic, oblong or lanceolate, apex attenuate or short acuminate, base (at least upper ones) usually truncate or obtuse often slightly asymmetric, coriaceous, 10-17.5[12.8] cm long, 4.6-7.3[5.8] cm broad, upper surface glabrous or midrib puberulous, lower uniformly and often densely puberulous with crisped hairs intermixed with minute red papillae, undersurface often drying dark brown, sometimes obscurely glandular-punctate and -striate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat; secondaries 7-12 on either side of midrib, ascending, ± straight, parallel or slightly convergent; intersecondaries sometimes present, to half length of secondaries; tertiaries oblique or obscure. Inflorescence axillary, 4-33 cm long, a pyramidal thyrse, lower branches to 8.5 cm long, densely pubescent; pedicel 0.5-1.5 mm long. Calyx patelliform, ca. 2 mm long, with 3-4 acute, obtuse, or rounded lobes 1-2 mm long, sparsely appressed puberulous outside. Petals 3-5, valvate or slightly imbricate at apex, 7-9 mm long, 1.5-2.5 mm broad, oblong, apex acute, appressed pubescent outside, glabrous within. Staminal tube 6-7.5 mm long, 2-2.5 mm broad, margin undulate or truncate, pubescent or glabrous outside, glabrous inside; anthers 8-9, 1-1.3 mm long. Nectary a stipe expanded to form an annulus below ovary, 1-1.5 mm long, glabrous. Ovary prominently ribbed, 4-5-locular, loculi uniovulate, densely pubescent or strigose; style glabrous. Capsule (immature) globose, apex truncate, base rounded, bearing 12-16 thin convoluted and anastomosing longitudinal wings 5-7 mm deep, puberulous, hairs intermixed with numerous red papillae, 2.5-3 cm diam.; 4-valved, valves 1-seeded; pericarp (excluding wings) 3-5 mm thick. Seed not seen. Field characters. A tree to 30 m high with greenish-white to cream-coloured flowers. Flowering occurs in October and the fruits are semi-mature by March.

description: Sous-arbrisseaux ou plantes herbacées vivaoes ou annuel les. Feuilles généralement succulentes, altemes ou verticillés, sans stipules. Fleurs solitaires ou fasciculées à l'aisselle des feuilles, terminales ou latérales, ou pseudoaxillaires en cymes scorpioides; hétérostylées, actinonorphes mais aussi à une tendance à la zyganorphie, calice gamosépale campanulé, poculiforme ou tubuleux, 5-fide ou 5-lobé ; corolle gamopétale 5-lobée, parfois bilabiée, à préfloraison plicative ou contortée à l'état de bouton et contortée, condupliquée ou indupliquée-valvaire à l'anthèse; largement ou étroitfiment infundibuliforroe, tubuleuse-infundibuliforme ou hypocratériforme. Etamines 5, insérées sur le tube de la corolle vers la base ou plus haut, plus ou moins inégales, filets filiformes ou élargis vers la base, souvent plus ou moins poilus; anthères incluses ou exsertes, introrses, à deux thèques s'ouvrant par deux fentes longitudinales. Disque hypogyne, plus ou moins saillant et chamu, souvent patelliforme à marge sinuée. Un seul style terminal ou basilaire (= gynobasique) ; stigmate capité, 2-5 lobé, ou pelté. Ovaire supère (-3) 5-20 (-27) carpellaire, carpelles en un ou deux verticilles, 1-8 loculaires, chaque locule à 1-7 ovules anacanpylotropes unitégumentés et à placentation axillaire. Fruit accatpagné du calice et formé de 3-27 nucules pyriformes, mamelonnées ou lenticulaires, soudées entre elles latéralement ou séparées, disposées sur 1-2 verticilles superposés ; chaque nucule à 1-7 graines, chacune d1 elles dans un locule et attachées au disque; pericarpe dur, sclérifié. Graines à endosperme abondant, de type cellulaire. Eitibryon très courbé, radicule très longue, cotyledons linéaires, oblongs, subtérétés ou oblancéolés étroits (1/1 = 5/1), hypocotyle très court, fusiforme. Chaméphytes, hémicryptophytes rosettés ou scapeux et thérophytes. Nombre chronosomique : n = 12

description: Shrub or small tree to 8 m tall with trunk 20 cm in diam.; bark usually light gray and smooth, crown spreading with crooked branches; branchlets 4-8 mm in diam., grayish-brown, strongly longitudinally wrinkled, grayish-white-tomentose with hairs 0.5 mm long, becoming glabrous, leaf scars with swollen margin. Leaves alternate, simple; petiole semiterete, 0.8-2.5 cm, tomentose with hairs 0.6 mm long; blade elliptic or oblong, rarely ovate, (2.8-)4-12(-19.3) × (1.7-)1.8-6(-8.8) cm but in the inflorescences smaller, at base (very) shortly attenuate, cuneate, or rounded, slightly unequal, at apex emarginate to retuse, or rarely obtuse, margin slightly revolute or not, the blade chartaceous to subcoriaceous, dull grayish-green on both sides, tomentose or pilose, with spreading ± curved hairs 0.3-0.8 mm long, soft to the touch, becoming less densely hairy above, venation distinctly camptodromous and finally prominent, costa plane above. Inflorescences densely flowered consisting of terminal and axillary, erect, paniculate, partial inflorescences 3-9 × 3-6 cm, indument like that of the young vegetative branches, side-branchlets alternate and subtended by a bract or a small leaf; bracts caducous, narrowly triangular, ± conduplicate, to 4 × 1 mm, glabrous above, densely pilose below with spreading hairs 0.5 mm long; pedicels to 3 mm long; bractlets 2, alternate. Flowers 10.5-15 mm in diam., with "sickish-sweet" odor; calyx lobes quincuncial, broadly or depressedly ovate, 1-2 × 1.7-2.5 mm, rounded at tip, thickly papery, margin membranous, (dispersedly) pilose below with spreading hairs to 0.5 mm long, venation parallel but the nerves distally branched; petals persistent, quincuncial or cochlear, adnate to the disc at base, spreading, broadly elliptic, 5-6.5 x 3.7-5 mm, rounded at the apex, transparent-papery, yellowish when dried, creamish-white when fresh, the indument like that of the calyx but less dense, venation actinodromous, the nerves branched towards the margin; filaments persistent, adnate at base to the disc, subulate, 3-5.5 mm long and 0.7 mm thick, glabrous; anthers ovoid, (1.3-)1.6 × 1.2 mm including a slightly incurved tip 0.1-0.2 mm, papillose; disc annular, rosette-like, irregularly 10-lobed to 1/3 of its thickness, 0.8 mm high and 1.6 mm thick, 3-4.2 mm in diam., thickly fleshy, glabrous; carpels to 1 mm high, provided with numerous fingerlike outgrowths varying to 0.5 mm long, glabrous; style inserted on the proximal half of the carpels, 3.2-3.5 mm long, 0.2-0.4 mm thick, the free part 1.5-2.5 mm, glabrous; stigma capitate, obsoletely 5-lobed, 0.3-0.5 × 0.4-0.7 mm. Fruits 2-3 per infructescence, stellately-globose, depressed, 2-2.5 × 3-4 cm, to 6 cm broad when dehisced; loculi rounded on the back, (mostly strongly) muricate to echinate with rather sharp prickles varying in length to 6 or 10 mm, charged with glands, glabrous, incompletely dehiscing septicidally from 2 mm above base to 2 mm from tip, and loculicidally to ± Vs above base, the fruit walls strongly spreading finally; exocarp with ± reticulately branched nerves; seed usually 1 per loculus, obliquely subglobose, 10-14 × 11-14 × 9-10 mm, with a blunt or shortly beaked apex 0.05 mm, testa dark brown, shining, linear-colliculate with the interspaces (up to 0.20 × 0.05 mm) parallel together in patches alternating with granulate patches; chalazal area not visible; hilum to 3 mm broad, permanently covered with the axial part of the endocarp; embryo 1, cotyledons unequal with ears 0.8 mm long, radicle 1.3 mm long projecting 0-0.5 mm beyond the ears.

description: Tree; young shoots finely appressed puberulous with ferruginous-brown hairs, soon glabrous, dark brown, smooth, finally greyish, finely cracked and scaling, without lenticels. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 12.5-25 × 4.5-9.5 cm, broadly oblanceolate, apex shortly attenuate to rounded, base acute or narrowly attenuate, coriaceous, glabrous or with some residual appressed hairs along the midrib (lower surface); venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 1420 pairs, mostly parallel, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries numerous, fine, horizontal. Petiole 0.5-1.5 cm long, not channelled, appressed puberulous to glabrous. Fascicles 2-3-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 0.5-2 mm long, densely ferruginous-puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, 0.7-1.2 cm long, increasing in size centripetally, ovate, apex acute or obtuse, densely puberulous outside, and in the upper half inside. Corolla cylindrical slightly broader in the middle, 1.5-1.8 cm long, tube about twice as long as the lobes, lobes five, oblong or elliptic, apex rounded or truncate, papillose, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments 2-3 mm long, usually geniculate at apex, glabrous; anthers 1.75-2 mm long, ovate-lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, 3-4.5 mm long, oblong to subulate, apex sometimes slightly bifid, papillose. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, densely pubescent; style 1.15-1.4 cm long after anthesis, exserted in bud and equalling or exceeding the corolla in open flower, pubescent in lower half; style-head simple. Fruit 10-12 × 7-8 cm, ovoid-oblong to globose, velutinous with purplish-brown hairs becoming glabrous. Seed solitary, 6-9 × 5-6 cm, ovoid or ellipsoid, rounded or truncate at apex and base, testa ca. 1 mm thick, bony, scar area strongly rugose, covering the entire seed, except for a narrow, shining abaxial strip; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 45 m high and 90 cm diam., slightly fluted at the base, with thick light yellowish-brown scaling bark; slash dull pink with scarce white latex. Flowers scented, with whitish-cream corolla tube and pale green lobes. The pulp of the fruit is light yellow, granular. Flowering in the dry season and beginning of the rainy season, May to Dec, and fruit maturing in the wet season, Feb to Apr.

description: Shrub or small tree, young shoots finely appressed puberulous or sericeous, indumentum persistent, eventually glabrous, grey, smooth, usually finely lenticellate. Leaves spaced, opposite, in whorls of three, or spirally arranged, 3.5-7.7 × 1.8-4.8 cm, broadly elliptic or obovate, apex obtuse, rounded or emarginate, base obtuse to narrowly cuneate, margin revolute, thickly coriaceous, glabrous above, finely and closely appressed puberulous or sericeous below, indumentum pale yellowish-brown; venation obscure, brochidodromous, midrib deeply sunken on upper surface, secondary veins 12-15 pairs, parallel, straight; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries obscure, upper surface sometimes faintly striate, striations running parallel to secondary veins. Petiole 5-8 mm long, channelled, appressed puberulous, base decurrent on stem as 1-2 raised lines. Fascicles 5-10-flowered, axillary. Pedicel 4-6 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, ca. 3.5 mm long, ovate, apex acute to rounded, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside, ciliate. Corolla cyathiform, 6-6.5 mm long, tube ca. 2 mm long, lobes five, 4-4.5 mm long, ovate to broadly elliptic, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube, exserted; filaments ca. 4 mm long, geniculate at apex, glabrous; anthers 1.7-1.8 mm long, lanceolate-sagittate, glabrous. Staminodes five, 2-3 mm long, lanceolate, sometimes incised in upper half, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, pubescent, style 3.5-5 mm long after anthesis, slightly exserted in bud and open flower, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit ca. 3 cm long, ellipsoid, apex rounded, bearing persistent style, base obtuse, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, 2-2.5 cm long, oblong, apex rounded, base obtuse, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.3 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length, ca. 7 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle exserted ca. 1.5 mm; endosperm absent. Field characters. Shrub or small tree to 6 m high. Fruit maturing red, orange or yellow. Flowering Aug-Jan, fruit mature Oct (only a single date available).

description: Tree, young shoots densely soft-pubescent with pale brown to grey, stalked, two-branched hairs, becoming glabrous, grey, smooth, with small lenticels. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 5.5-22 × 2.1-8 cm, oblanceolate to elliptic, apex narrowly attenuate, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, chartaceous, indumentum on upper surface confined to midrib and secondary veins, lower surface densely soft-pubescent at first, indumentum soon falling to leave a sparse covering of short hairs; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 11-12 pairs, parallel or slightly convergent, arcuate; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries few, widely spaced, oblique; fine areolate reticulum visible on both surfaces. Petiole 0.4-1.2 cm long, not channelled, pubescent. Fascicles 5-10-flowered, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves. Pedicel ca. 0.5 mm long, pubescent. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals five(-six), ca. 1.25 mm long, ovate, apex acute, densely short-pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Corolla cyathiform, ca. 1.5 mm long, tube equalling the lobes, lobes five, suborbicular, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 0.1 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.4 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 0.2 mm long, subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, unilocular, glabrous; style ca. 0.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit ca. 2 cm long, ellipsoid, apex and base acute or obtuse, smooth, pubescent. Seed solitary, ca. 1.7 cm long, oblong-ellipsoid, laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.3 mm thick; scar adaxial and extending slightly around the base, ca. 2 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 40 cm diam. with latex. Flowers whitish, Jun to Aug, fruit Aug.

description: Young shoots appressed or spreading pubescent, crisped or stiffly tomentose, or hispid-tomentose, becoming glabrous, pale greyish to midbrown, cracked and scaling, without lenticels. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 7-45 × 3.1-15(—17) cm, oblanceolate, with or without a long tapering base, apex narrowly attenuate to obtusely cuspidate, rounded or emarginate, base acute or narrowly cuneate to rounded or truncate, chartaceous to coriaceous, glabrous above or with some indumentum along the midrib, pubescent or tomentose below with crisped hairs, or with stiff erect two-branched hairs, or glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, or sometimes brochidodromous in the lower half, marginal vein present, midrib not or slightly raised on the upper surface, sometimes recessed, secondary veins 14-25(-37), pairs, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries reticulate to oblique, often close and numerous; quaternaries coarsely to finely reticulate. Petiole 0.4-6.5 cm long, weakly to strongly channelled, appressed or spreading pubescent, crisped or stiffly tomentose, sometimes becoming glabrous. Fascicles few-flowered, usually clustered below the leaves. Pedicel 0-2 mm long, appressed or spreading pubescent or tomentose. Flowers bisexual. Sepals four 0.3-1.5 (-2) cm long, broadly ovate or elliptic, apex obtuse to rounded, crisped pubescent to sericeous outside, subglabrous inside. Corolla tubular, (0.4-)0.7-1.6 cm long, tube (0.3)0.4-1.3 cm long, lobes four, (1-)2-4 mm long, broadly oblong to suborbicular, apex rounded or truncate, often ciliate. Stamens four, fixed halfway to three-quarters up the corolla tube; filaments 2-4.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 1.25-2 mm long, lanceolate, oblong or ovate, often flattened, sometimes apiculate, glabrous. Staminodes four, 1-3 mm long, lanceolate or subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid to depressed globose, four-locular, densely long-strigose; style 0.5-1.6 cm long after anthesis, exserted, glabrous; style-head simple or minutely four-lobed. Fruit 3-6.5 cm long, ellipsoid, ovoid or globose, apex obtuse to rounded, base rounded to truncate, smooth to verrucose, finely pubescent to densely covered in short hairy processes. Seeds 1-4, 1.7-3.5 cm long, ellipsoid, usually rounded at base and apex, often planoconvex, sometimes slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.5-0.75 mm thick; scar adaxial and often extending around the base, 0.2-1 cm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent.

description: Tree. Leaves usually 16-25 cm long, apex obtuse to shortly narrowly attenuate, secondary veins 14-19 pairs, higher order venation differentiated into oblique tertiaries and finely reticulate quaternaries, lower surface glabrous. Fruit verrucose, 5-6 cm long, densely covered with hairy projections.  Field characters. Buttressed tree to 30 m high and 50 cm diam, with white latex. Rowers greenish-white, fruit orange or yellow. Flowering Mar (Yucatán), fruit maturing Jun-Aug.

description: Tree. Leaves usually 15-45 cm long, with narrowly attenuate to obtusely cuspidate apex, secondary veins 17-37 pairs, higher order venation clearly differentiated into oblique tertiaries and finely reticulate quaternaries, lower surface with indumentum of stiff erect two-branched hairs. Fruit verrucose, 4.5-6.5 cm long, densely covered with hairy projections. Field characters. Tree to 35 m high and 60 cm diam., larger specimens with slender buttresses and fluted bole. Bark dark brown, scaling in thin longitudinal strips and sometimes becoming shallowly fissured; slash cream, with a variable amount of milky white latex. Sympodial branching conspicuous, the branches often whorled, and terminated by dense clusters of leaves. Flowers whitish to pale green, fruit maturing dull orange or yellow. Flowering Apr (Belize), Jul-Aug (Peru), fruit in various stages of development throughout the year. Parrots have been observed eating the fruit in Panama (Bristán 581, 1208, 1225).
