description: Hemicriptófita rizomatosa, 10-40 cm de alto, base leñosa 2-10 mm diám., tallos 1-5, erectos, a veces sinuosos o en zig-zag, cilindricos, longitudinalmente estriados, 1.5-2.5 mm diám., a veces ramificados, con pelos porrecto-estrellados, radio central 0.6-2.5 mm long., pelos glandulares patentes 0.4-1.2 mm long, y pelos simples crespos 0.1-0.3 mm long. Entrenudos bien desarrollados, los básales más largos, con hojas pequeñas en los nudos, los siguientes 10-22 mm long., más cortos que las hojas bien desarrolladas. Yemas axilares 1-2, la basal florífera. Estípulas ausentes o reducidas a prominencias triangulares, 1-2 a cada lado de la base foliar, 0.3-0.4 mm long., acompañadas por pelos glandulares. Hojas cartáceas, sésiles o subsésiles. Pecíolo brevísimo, 0.3-1.5 mm long., en hojas apicales ausente, indumento como el del tallo. Lámina ovada o elíptica, a veces latiovada, latielíptica o suborbicular, 23-40 x 9-29 mm, relación largo:ancho = 1.2-2.7:1; base redondeada o cuneada, a veces brevemente atenuada; ápice agudo u obtuso; borde aserrado hacia el ápice, 27-90% de su longitud, con pelos glandulares y pelos estrellados; haz lustrosa y glabrescente en hojas básales, luego subtomentosa, con pelos porrecto-estrellados, radio central 0.5-1.5 mm long., cuando glabrescente, pelos reducidos al radio central, también algunos pelos glandulares sobre venas y cerca del margen; envés opaco con pelos estrellados, a veces lustroso, glabrescente; venas laterales 4-5 pares, más un par situado muy cerca de la base, ligeramente incurvas, ángulo de divergencia 22-45°, perdiéndose cerca del margen, poco visibles a prominentes en la haz, prominentes en el envés, con pelos porrecto-estrellados; venas terciarias marcadas en hojas glabrescentes; venación menor conspicua, prominente en hojas glabrescentes. Alabastro ovoide, ápice agudo. Flores axilares, solitarias, heterostilas. Pedúnculo cilindrico, 11-40 mm long., 0.4-0.6 mm diám., con pelos estrellados, pelos simples, cortos y pelos glandulares 0.3-0.6 mm long. Profilos ausentes o desarrollados, 0.4-0.7 mm long., opuestos en la articulación o desplazados 1-2 mm hacia abajo. Pedicelo 4.5-12 mm long., 0.6-0.9 mm diám., dilatado hacia el ápice, indumento más denso y con más pelos glandulares. Cáliz 9-14 mm long.; tubo calicino 2-3 mm long., con pelos porrecto-estrellados y pelos glandulares especialmente sobre las venas, glabro por dentro; lóbulos ovados o angus-tiovados, a veces triangulares, 5-9 nervados, los internos con bandas de pelos adpresos, estrellados y simples, ordenadamente dispuestos antes de los bordes membranáceos, mucrón 0-0.3 mm long. Corola blanca, garganta a veces amarilla, 20-32 mm diám., 6-10 mm más larga que el cáliz; pétalos con la uña glabra; lámina 13-20 x 7-12 mm, obovada, obtusa o brevemente apiculada. Corona membranácea, blanquecina, lóbulos unidos a los pétalos 0.7-1.3 mm long., lóbulos unidos a los sépalos 0.4-0.6 mm long., borde superior laciniado. Filamentos estaminales glabros, soldados 0.6-0.9 mm en la base al tubo calicino, 3.5-5 mm long, en flores longistilas, 5.5-8.7 mm long, en flores brevistilas; anteras ovadas, 1.5-2.5 x 0.7-1 mm, base emarginada, ápice obtuso recurvado en la dehiscencia, filamento inserto dorsalmente a 0.5-0.8 mm de la base. Ovario elipsoide u ovoide, 1.8-2.7 x 1.5-2 mm, con pelos glandulares 1,5 mm long, y pelos simples; estilos cilindricos, glabros, a veces con algunos pelos simples adpresos, 3.5-5.5 mm long, en flores longistilas, 1.2-2 mm long, en flores brevistilas; estigmas penicilados, 18-24 ramas 0.6-1 mm long. Frutos suborbiculares, ca. 9 mm diám.; valvas tuberculadas por fuera, erizadas de pelos glandulares y pelos porrecto-estrellados, cara intema lisa, lustrosa. Semillas obovoides, 3-3.5 x 1-1.7 mm; exóstoma cónico; rafe linear; cálaza oscura, ligeramente deprimida; episperma glabro [seg. información de L. Ramella (G)], reticulado, aréolas rectangulares pequeñas, muros verticales más marcados que los transversales; arilo 2-2.5 mm long., unilateral, lobulado cerca de su inserción, luego angosto.

description: Subarbusto viscoso, tomentoso, 25-50 cm de alto, ejes subterráneos rizomatosos gruesos; base leñosa 3-9 mm diám.; tallos erectos o ascendentes, ramificados en la porción superior, cilindricos, 1.5-4 mm diám.; ramas viejas con corteza parda, longitudinalmente estriada; ramas jóvenes con pelos estrellados amarillos, algunos porrecto-estrellados y pelos glandulares, entrenudos básales 10-30 mm long., entrenudos floríferos 2-10 mm long. Yemas axilares 1-2, la basal florífera; ramas seriales a veces desarrolladas. Hojas tomentosas, agrupadas hacia los ápices, hojas básales diminutas, deciduas. Estípulas ausentes o reducidas a 2-3 prominencias cónicas glandulares escondidas entre el indumento. Pecíolo 2-15 mm long., semicilíndrico, indumento como el del tallo. Lámina elíptica o lanceolada, 24-64 x 8-20 mm, relación largo:ancho = 2.1-4.5:1; base cuneada o atenuada; ápice agudo, raramente obtuso; borde simple o doblemente aserrado, 66-82% de su extensión, con pelos glandulares; haz con pelos porrecto-estrellados; envés con pelos estrellados, sobre las venas principales pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares; venas laterales 3-6 pares, rectas o ligeramente incurvas, hundidas en la haz, prominentes en el envés, ángulo de divergencia 17-30°; venas terciarias ligeramente prominentes en el envés; venación menor inconspicua. Alabastros ovoides, apiculados, con los mucrones libres en el ápice. Flores axilares, solitarias, heterostilas. Pedúnculo floral 5-20 mm long., 0.3-0.6 mm diám., indumento como el del tallo. Profilos 2, opuestos en la articulación, subulados, desiguales, 0.6-3 mm long. Pedicelo 4-12 mm long., 0.5-0.7 mm diám., indumento más denso. Cáliz 812 mm long.; tubo calicino 1.8-2.5 mm long., cara interna con pelos simples, adpresos, cara externa con pelos estrellados, venas con pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares; lóbulos ovado-lanceolados, con 5 venas importantes, cara interna glabra, cara externa como la del tubo, los internos con bandas de pelos sedosos, adpresos antes de los bordes membranáceos, mucrón 1-1.5 mm long. Corola de color amarillo pálido, 6.5-10 mm long., más corta que el cáliz; uña pilosa; lámina glabra, obovada, 4-7 x 3-4.5 mm, base cuneada, borde superior eroso, redondeado, venas coloreadas. Corona glabra, borde laciniado, lóbulos unidos a los pétalos 0.6-0.9 mm long., lóbulos unidos a los sépalos 0.3-0.7 mm long. Filamentos estaminales glabros, cilindricos, soldados 0.5-0.6 mm en la base al tubo calicino, 3-3.5 mm long, en flores longistilas, 3.5-4 mm long, en flores brevistilas; anteras ovadas, amarillas, 1.2-1.5 x 0.5-0.7 mm, recurvadas después de la dehiscencia, ápice obtuso, base brevemente emarginada, filamento inserto en una cavidad basidorsal 0.3-0.4 mm long. Ovario elipsoide, 1.5-2.3 x 1.5-2 mm, densamente cubierto de pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares, placentas 15-20 ovuladas; estilos cilindricos, glabros, 3-3.7 mm long, en flores longistilas, 1.3-1.5 mm long, en flores brevistilas; estigmas multífidos, 0.2-0.6 mm long, en flores longistilas, 0.2-0.4 mm long, en flores brevistilas. Frutos latielipsoides u ovoides, 5-9 mm diám.; valvas latielípticas u ovadas, cara externa granulosa, pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares, cara interna lisa, lustrosa, amarillenta, ápice obtuso. Semillas ligeramente curvadas, 3-3.5 x 1 mm, estrechadas por encima del exóstoma hemisférico; rafe linear apenas saliente; cálaza redondeada; episperma pilosiúsculo (Fig. 14C), negruzco, reticulado, aréolas rectangulares pequeñas; arilo unilateral, angosto, lacerado, 2-3 mm long.

description: Tree; young shoots shortly and densely golden-brown tomentose, indumentum rather persistent, eventually glabrous, dark greyish-black, rough, without lenticels. Leaves loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 18-30 × 8-12.5 cm, broadly oblanceolate or elliptic, apex narrowly acuminate to obtusely cuspidate, base acute or narrowly attenuate, bullate, margin slightly revolute, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, glabrous above except for residual tomentum on the midrib, lower surface finely pubescent with stalked two-branched hairs, denser on the midrib and veins; venation eucamptodromous to brochidodromous in the upper half, midrib raised but recessed on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-13(-16) pairs, slightly convergent, arcuate, sunken on upper surface, strongly raised on the lower surface; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries oblique to reticulate; fine areolate network visible on both surfaces; secondary and tertiary venation strongly raised on lower surface. Petiole 1.5-3.5 cm long, not channelled, tomentose. Fascicles borne below the leaves, 2-10-flowered. Pedicel 0.6-2 cm long, tomentose. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, 2-4 mm long, united at base, lanceolate to broadly ovate, obtuse, tomentose outside, sparsely puberulous to glabrous inside. Corolla cyathiform, ca. 4 mm long (female), 5-8 mm long (male), tube equalling the lobes; lobes five, broadly elliptic to suborbicular, apex rounded or obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed in the upper half of the corolla tube, strong filament traces to near the base of tube; filaments ca. 0.2 mm long, glabrous anthers 1.5-2 mm long, broadly lanceolate, glabrous, converted to narrowly lanceolate sterile staminodes in female flower. Staminodes five, 1.5-3 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Stamens and staminodes incurved to cover the ovary. Disk absent. Ovary broad, with truncate apex, sometimes deeply longitudinally ribbed, unilocular, densely long-pubescent; style 1.25-1.5 mm long after anthesis, pubescent; style-head simple or discoid. Fruit ca. 3 cm long, 3-4 cm broad, globose or depressed globose, apex and base rounded to truncate, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, ca. 2 cm long, ellipsoid, acute at apex and base, not laterally compressed, testa smooth, ca. 0.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length, ca. 2 mm wide; embryo not seen. Field characters. Tree to 18 m high and 25 cm diam. with reddish scaly bark and white latex and whitish-green or yellowish flowers. Flowers Sep-Dec, fruit (old) Jun.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: (Description of leaves and fruit from Rusby.) Young shoots glabrous. Leaves to 12 × 4 cm, oblong, apex obtuse, base attenuate, margin revolute, coriaceous, glabrous; secondary veins 1820 pairs; intersecondaries present; higher order venation anastomosing. Fruit subsessile, clustered along the branches. Sepals persistent, 4-5 mm broad, rounded. Fruit ca. 3.5 cm broad, depressed globose, glabrous. Seeds ca. four, ca. 1.2 cm long, ellipsoid, laterally compressed, apex and base obtuse, testa smooth, shining; scar adaxial, full-length, 3-4 mm wide.

description: Shrub or tree; young shoots puberulous (whitish to brown hairs), becoming glabrous, pale brown, cracked and fissured, without lenticels. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 8-16 × 47.1 cm, broadly oblong or elliptic to oblanceolate apex narrowly attenuate to rounded, base narrowly attenuate or acute, thinly coriaceous, glabrous and often shining above, lower surface sparsely appressed puberulous with brown hairs, or glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 7-12 pairs, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries widely spaced, oblique; quaternaries mostly at right angles to the tertiaries. Petiole 2.5-4 cm long, slightly channelled, puberulous to glabrous. Fascicles 3-6-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 1.5-2.5 mm long, puberulous. Flowers probably unisexual (see discussion below). Sepals four, 4-4.5 mm long, outer broadly ovate, hooded, apex obtuse, inner broadly elliptic, apex rounded, sericeous outside, inner pair with broad glabrous margin, glabrous inside. Corolla broadly tubular, 4-5 mm long, tube 3-3.5 mm long, lobes four, ca. 1.5 mm long, broadly oblong, apex rounded, fringed-ciliate. Stamens four, fixed about halfway up the corolla tube; filaments ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 1-1.25 mm long, broadly lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes four, ca. 1 mm long, narrowly oblong, apex rounded, fringed-ciliate. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, four-locular, densely long-strigose; style ca. 2 mm long after anthesis, glabrous in upper half; style-head minutely four-lobed. Fruit ca. 4 cm long, globose, apex and base rounded, or base slightly tapered, smooth, glabrous. Seeds 1-4, 2-2.5 cm long, ellipsoid, rounded at base and apex, slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, adherent to pericarp, woody, 1-1.5 mm thick; scar adaxial and extending around the base, 7-8 mm wide, verruculose; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Shrub or tree to 10 m high and 30 cm diam. with scaly bark; slash contains white latex. Flowers whitish, fruit yellow to orange, speckled with red. Flowering in May and Sep-Nov, fruit maturing Mar to Sep. A recent study of the phenology of this species (J. C. de Andrade & A. G. de Andrade, 1983; A. G. de Andrade & J. C. de Andrade, 1984a), describes flowers with atrophied anthers (probably female) and flowers with fully formed anthers (functionally male?) from the same tree, which also produced fruit. Flowering and fruiting were erratic over a three year period, and the tree produced fully formed fruit only once during this time. The authors suggest that bats are the dispersal agents for this species.

description: Tree; young shoots minutely appressed puberulous, becoming glabrous, dark brown, cracked and scaling, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 8-19 × 4.8-9.5 cm, broadly elliptic, apex obtusely cuspidate to shortly narrowly attenuate, base obtuse to rounded, coriaceous, glabrous above, densely and persistently brown-puberulous below; venation eucamptodromous, marginal vein present, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 10-12 pairs, parallel, slightly to strongly arcuate; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries oblique to reticulate; fine areolate quaternary reticulum visible on both surfaces (with a lens). Petiole 2-2.5 cm long, not channelled, puberulous. Fascicles 10-15-flowered, axillary. Pedicel ca. 2 mm long (young), puberulous. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals (young flower buds) five, ca. 1.5 mm long, ovate, obtuse, appressed puberulous on both surfaces. Corolla tube ? equalling the lobes, lobes 5, glabrous. Stamens five, ? inserted in the upper half of the corolla tube, glabrous. Staminodes five, subulate. Disk absent. Ovary conical, unilocular, pubescent; style-head simple. Fruit 3.5-4 cm long, asymmetrical (one side convex, the other straight), apex and base obtuse or rounded, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, 2.5-2.7 cm long, laterally compressed, adaxial surface strongly convex, abaxial surface straight, testa finely transversely striate, shining; scar adaxial, full length, ca. 2 mm wide. Field characters. Tree to ca. 20 m high and 20 cm diam.

description: Tree; young shoots appressed puberulous or crisped puberulous with short spreading hairs, soon glabrous, pale brown to greyish, usually smooth, often lenticellate. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 5-22 × 1.8-8 cm, usually oblanceolate or elliptic, less frequently lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate or acuminate, base usually narrowly attenuate, occasionally acute to rounded, often decurrent, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, glabrous, usually minutely punctate on the lower surface, venation eucamptodromous or brochidodromous, marginal vein usually visible, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 8-16 pairs, usually slightly convergent and arcuate; intersecondaries usually present, variable in length; tertiaries reticulate; fine areolate higher order network usually visible, sometimes raised on one or both surfaces. Petiole (0.3-)0.5-1.5(-2) cm long, flat or slightly channelled, subglabrous. Fascicles (l-)3-20-flowered, axillary or in the axils of fallen leaves, occasionally clustered on leafless axillary shoots 1-3 cm long. Pedicel 1.5-8(-10)mm long, sparsely to densely puberulous with appressed or crisped spreading hairs. Flowers unisexual or bisexual (? functionally male), (plants ? dioecious). Sepals 4-5(-6), 1-2 mm long, free or partially united, ovate or lanceolate, apex acute to rounded, outside appressed or spreading puberulous, inside usually glabrous, less frequently with sparse appressed indumentum. Corolla 1.5-3 mm long, tube equalling or rarely shorter than the lobes; lobes (4-)5(-6), ovate, oblong or suborbicular, apex rounded, glabrous or scattered hirsute on both surfaces of lobes, nearly always ciliate. Stamens (4-)5(-6), fixed in the upper half or at the top of the corolla tube; filaments 0.20.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.4-0.75(-l) mm long, lanceolate or oblong, sparsely hirsute or glabrous, converted to lanceolate-oblong sterile staminodes in female flower. Staminodes (4-)5(-6), 0.5-l(-1.5) mm long, narrowly triangular to lanceolate, glabrous or occasionally hairy. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid or conical, unilocular, puberulous; style 0.4-1 mm long, after anthesis glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 1.5-4 cm long, ellipsoid or ovoid, apex acute to obtuse or rounded, base truncate, rounded or tapered, soft-skinned and fleshy, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, 1-2.5 cm long, ellipsoid, obtuse at base and apex, usually slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, usually free from the pericarp, occasionally adherent, 0.2-1 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length or nearly so, 0.2-1 cm broad; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle included or slightly exserted; endosperm absent.

description: Young shoots ferruginous-pubescent or tomentose, indumentum becoming grey with age, soon glabrous, greyish, slightly cracked and scaly, usually without lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged or subopposite or subverticillate, 4-9.7 × 2.7-5.8 cm, oblanceolate, obovate or elliptic, apex rounded, truncate or emarginate, base narrowly attenuate to rounded or truncate, margin revolute, strongly coriaceous, upper surface glabrous or with residual tomentum along midrib, lower surface often glaucous, ferruginous-tomentose to glabrous, indumentum turning greyish with age; venation brochidodromous to eucamptodromous, marginal vein often present, midrib flat or sometimes slightly raised in the upper half of the leaf, secondary veins 6-9 pairs, parallel, straight; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries open-reticulate, obscure. Petiole 0.3-1 cm long, not channelled, pubescent to tomentose. Fascicles 1-6-flowered, axillary. Pedicel 1-4 mm long, ferruginous-pubescent. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, 1.5-3.5 mm long, ovate, apex acute, ferruginous-pubescent outside, puberulous inside. Corolla cyathiform to shortly tubular, 2-4 mm long, tube 0.5-1.5 mm long, lobes five, 1.25-2.5 mm long, oblong or ovate, apex obtuse to rounded, glabrous or with sparse appressed pubescence outside. Stamens five, fixed in the upper half of the corolla tube; filaments 0.75-1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.5-0.75 mm long, ovate or lanceolate, glabrous; stamens absent in female. Staminodes 0-1, ca. 0.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, bilocular, densely pubescent; style 0.5-1 mm long, glabrous above; style-head simple or slightly expanded. Fruit 1-1.5 cm long, subglobose, or obovoid, apex rounded, base obtuse, smooth, ferruginous-pubescent. Seed solitary, ca. 8 mm long, ellipsoid, apex and base rounded, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.3 mm thick; scar adaxial, almost full-length, ca. 1.5 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent.

description: Tree; young shoots shortly tomentose with crisped ferruginous hairs, indumentum persisting, eventually glabrous, dark greyish, smooth or somewhat scaly, lenticellate. Leaves loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 20-27 × 8.5-10.7 cm, elliptic, oblong-elliptic or broadly oblanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate to obtusely cuspidate, base shortly narrowly attenuate to acute, thinly coriaceous, glabrous above, uniformly pubescent below with ferruginous two-branched, crisped hairs; venation eucamptodromous, midrib not raised on upper surface, secondary veins 14-15 pairs, parallel, arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique, widely spaced; quaternaries reticulate. Petiole 1.7-4 cm long, not or only slightly channelled, shortly pubescent. Fascicles 2-6-flowered, mostly below the leaves. Pedicel 3-5 mm long, densely ferruginous-pubescent. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, (male) ca. 5 mm long, (female) ca. 2.5 mm long, ovate, apex acute or obtuse, densely ferruginous-pubescent outside, puberulous in upper half inside. Corolla (male) ca. 6 mm long, tube ca. 2 mm long, lobes ca. 4 mm long, (female) ca. 4 mm long, tube ca. 1.5 mm long, lobes ca. 2.5 mm long; lobes five, ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments (ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 2 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous; stamens absent in female flowers. Staminodes five, (male) ca. 2 mm long, (female) 0.2-0.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, bilocular, shortly pubescent; style 1.5-2 mm long after anthesis, glabrous above; style-head simple. Fruit not seen. Field characters. Tree to 15 m high and 30 cm diam. with white flowers. Flowering May to Jun.

description: Shrub; stems terete, densely and shortly pilose, hairs ferruginous or whitish, turning grayish, glabrate. Leaves thick-coriaceous, strongly convex above and concave below, elliptic, 1.5-3 × 0.7-1 cm, base obtuse to broadly cuneate, short-decurrent, apex obtuse or rounded, margin entire, strongly revolute, bearing 1 pair of pustular glands at the lamina base, glabrous above, densely ferruginous-tomentose beneath so as to obscure surface; pinnately nerved with midrib impressed above and raised beneath, lateral nerves (apparently 3-4 per side) obscure; petiole subterete, shallowly canaliculate above, rugose, 2-4 mm long, pubescent as stems. Inflorescence 1-5-flowered, with rachis, pedicels, floral bracts, bracteoles, and exterior surfaces of calyx densely and shortly ferruginous-tomentose, glabrate; rachis subterete, angled, 2-8 mm long; floral bract ovate, ca. 1.5 mm long, obtuse; pedicel subterete, angled, ca. 3 mm long; bracteoles broadly ovate, ca. 1.5-2 mm long, acute. Flowers with calyx ca. 8 mm long, lobes ovate, ca. 6 mm long, acuminate, sparsely short-pilose within at tips; corolla immature but buds densely short-pilose and anther base short-mucronate; ovary densely ferruginous-pilose so as to obscure surface; style ca. 5 mm long, glabrous. Berry not seen.

description: Young shoots subglabrous, smooth, greyish-white to brown, lenticellate or not. Leaves spaced, opposite, 5.4-17 × 3.4-8.2 cm, broadly elliptic or obovate, apex obtuse, rounded, truncate or emarginate, base usually rounded or truncate, less frequently narrowly cuneate or acute, thinly coriaceous, glabrous or finely brown- to greyish-sericeous on lower surface; venation eucamptodromous or brochidodromous, strong marginal vein, submarginal vein sometimes present, midrib flat (not raised or sunken) on upper surface, secondary veins 14-22 pairs, parallel, straight or arcuate, flat or slightly raised on upper surface; intersecondaries long, usually extending to the margin; tertiaries reticulate. Petiole 0.4-1.3(-1.8) cm long, usually slightly channelled at the apex, sparsely appressed puberulous to glabrous, stipels absent. Fascicles 5-25-flowered, clustered below the leaves. Pedicel 1-8 mm long, minutely appressed puberulous to glabrous. Sepals (4-)5(-6), 1-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, sparsely appressed puberulous or glabrous outside, glabrous inside. Corolla 2-4(-4.5) mm long, tube 0.75-2 mm long, lobes (4-)5(-6), 1.25-3 mm long, lanceolate to ovate, apex acute to rounded, subglabrous. Stamens (4-)5(-6), fixed at the base of the corolla lobes; filaments 1.5-3 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.5-1.25 mm long, broadly lanceolate or ovate, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, (4-)5(-6)-locular, appressed pubescent; style 0.6-1.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 1.2-2 cm long, broadly ellipsoid or obovoid, apex rounded, style sometimes persistent, base rounded or tapered, smooth, minutely appressed puberulous to subglabrous. Seed solitary, 0.85-1.5 cm long, subglobose to ellipsoid, usually slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.2-0.3 mm thick; scar adaxial, about two-thirds the length of the seed, 2-5 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle exserted 1-2 mm; endosperm absent.

description: Tree; young shoots finely appressed puberulous, soon glabrous, grey-brown, rough and sometimes scaling, lenticellate. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 5.5-13.2 × 2.2-5.4 cm, elliptic or oblanceolate, apex acute to obtuse, barely rounded, base acute, coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, marginal vein present, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-14 pairs, parallel, slightly arcuate, slightly impressed on the upper surface; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries fine, oblique to reticulate. Petiole 0.8-1.2 cm long, channelled, glabrous. Fascicles few-flowered, below the leaves. Pedicel 0.5-2 mm long, appressed puberulous. Sepals five, ca. 1.5 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, sparse minute appressed hairs outside, glabrous inside. Corolla ca. 2.5 mm long, tube 1-1.25 mm long, lobes five, 1.25-1.5 mm long, oblong-ovate, apex obtuse, appressed puberulous on outside of tube, glabrous inside. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 1 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, appressed puberulous; style ca. 0.75 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple or minutely lobed. Fruit 2-4 cm long, ellipsoid, apex obtuse, base slightly tapered, smooth, finely appressed puberulous, becoming glabrous. Seed solitary, 1.6-2.5 cm long, oblong-elliptic, slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.3-0.4 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length, 4-9 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 32 m high and 80 cm diam., larger specimens buttressed to 1 m, bole fluted, with small dark brown bark, and sparse white latex. Flowers greenish-yellow, fruit yellow. Flowering Jan-Mar (Surinam, Guyana, Brazil: Roraima), Aug (Brazil: Pará), fruit recorded Feb, Apr, Jul, Aug, Nov.

description: Tree; young shoots minutely appressed puberulous, soon glabrous, whitish-grey to mid-brown, smooth, sometimes lenticellate. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged or alternate and distichous, 6.524 × 2.3-9.4 cm, elliptic, elliptic-lanceolate or oblong-elliptic, apex narrowly acuminate or caudate, base narrowly attenuate to obtuse or rounded, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous to brochidodromous, marginal vein present, midrib flat or slightly raised on upper surface, secondary veins 8-12 pairs, convergent, arcuate; intersecondaries short to moderately long; tertiaries forming a lax reticulum. Petiole 0.2-1.3 cm long, slightly channelled, subglabrous. Fascicles 1-8-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 1-3.6 cm long, often recurved or coiled, minutely appressed puberulous or glabrous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, 1.5-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate, apex acute to rounded, appressed puberulous on both surfaces, or sometimes glabrous inside. Corolla globose or broadly cyathiform, 2.5-5 mm long, tube about equalling or slightly exceeding the lobes, lobes five, ovate or triangular, apex acute, sericeous outside, or lobes glabrous, inside of tube finely puberulous. Staminodes five, 0.5-1.25 mm long, triangular or broadly ovate, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid to cylindrical, 2-5-locular, puberulous; style 0.5-1.5 mm long after anthesis, puberulous; style-head simple or minutely lobed. Fruit 1.8-3.2 cm long, subglobose to ellipsoid, apex acute to rounded, base rounded to tapered, smooth, glabrous or sparsely and minutely appressed puberulous. Seeds 1-2, 1.2-1.7 cm long, usually laterally compressed, rounded at base and apex, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.3 mm thick; scar adaxial and usually extending around the base, 2-4 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent.

description: Tree; young shoots appressed puberulous with rich brown indumentum, becoming glabrous, scaling in irregular pieces, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 8.5-11.5 × 3-5.2 cm, broadly elliptic, oblong-elliptic or oblong-lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate, base rounded to narrowly attenuate, thinly coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous-brochidodromous, marginal vein present, midrib slightly raised on upper surface, secondary veins 7-9 pairs, ascending, parallel or slightly convergent, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries moderately long; tertiaries forming a lax reticulum. Petiole 0.8-1 cm long, not or only slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 3-8-flowered, mostly below leaves. Pedicel 2-3 cm long, appressed puberulous. Sepals five, ca. 4 mm long, broadly elliptic, apex obtuse or rounded, sericeous outside, sparsely appressed puberulous inside. Corolla ca. 4 mm long, tube equalling the lobes, lobes five, broadly ovate or triangular, apex obtuse, appressed pubescent or glabrous outside, glabrous inside. Stamens five, fixed near the top of the staminal tube, anthers sessile, ca. 1 mm long, lanceolate, inflexed, glabrous; stamens reduced to small lanceolate hairy vestiges in female. Staminodes five, 1-1.5 mm long, broadlly triangular, strongly inflexed, appressed pubescent on outer surface. Ovary conical, with expanded wing at base (male) or conical and longitudinally ribbed (female), 3-locular, appressed pubescent; style 1-1.5 mm long, appressed pubescent in lower half; style-head simple. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Tree to 12 m high with white latex; flowers yellowish. Flowering Nov-Dec.

description: Tree; young branches tomentose-villose with pale buff hairs, becoming glabrous, grey, fissured, without lenticels. Spines usually present, axillary and sometimes terminating lateral branches. Leaves spirally arranged, spaced or loosely clustered, sometimes becoming fascicled, 2.2-6 × 1.2-2.8 cm, broadly oblong-elliptic, elliptic or lanceolate, apex obtuse to rounded, base usually obtuse to rounded or truncate, chartaceous, upper surface pubescent with crisped hairs, lower surface villose-tomentose; venation eucamptodromous or occasionally slightly brochidodromous, with a narrow marginal vein, midrib not raised; secondary veins 6-10 pairs, ascending, arcuate, slightly convergent; intersecondaries small or absent; tertiaries reticulate. Petiole 310 mm long, not channelled, villose. Flowers bisexual, fascicles axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves, 3-10-flowered. Pedicel ca. 2.5 mm long, villose. Sepals five, ca. 3 mm long, ovate, apex acute or obtuse, villose-tomentose outside, crisped pubescent towards the apex inside. Corolla ca. 4 mm long, tube ca. 1 mm long, glabrous; lobes five; median segment broadly elliptic, rounded; lateral segments narrowly acute, ca. 1 mm long. Stamens five, glabrous; filaments ca. 3 mm long, anthers 0.75-1 mm long, lanceolate. Staminodes five, ca. 2.25 mm long, narrowly lanceolate, margin erose, incurved and infolded, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, 5-locular, pubescent; style ca. 2.5 mm long after anthesis, pubescent to the apex; style-head simple. Fruit 1.2-2 cm long, ellipsoid, apex and base rounded, smooth, glabrous; pericarp 0.5-3 mm thick, fleshy. Seed one(two), 1.3-1.4 cm long, broadly ellipsoid; testa hard, smooth, shining, 0.3-0.5 mm thick; scar basi-ventral, 7-9 × 4-7 mm, ellipsoid; embryo vertical to oblique, with plano-convex cotyledons and slightly exserted radicle, surrounded by a thin skin of endosperm. Field characters. A tree to 10 m high with cream-coloured flowers. Flowering Apr, fruiting Aug.

description: Tree; young shoots finely appressed puberulous at first, becoming glabrous, pale grey, with a few lenticels. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 6.5-11 × 2.8-4.7 cm, elliptic, apex obtuse or rounded, base narrowly attenuate and slightly decurrent, thinly coriaceous, glabrous; midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 8-12 pairs, ascending, parallel, slightly arcuate. Petiole 1-1.5 cm long, not channelled, glabrous. Pedicel 6-7 mm long (in fruit). Sepals five, 1.3-2 mm long (in fruit), outer shorter than inner, apex rounded. description: Tree; young shoots pubescent with spreading pale, whitish hairs, soon glabrous, smooth or finely striate, usually lenticellate. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 5.5-11.5 × 2-3.7 cm, elliptic, apex acute or narrowly attenuate, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, chartaceous, lower surface slightly glaucous, glabrous or with scattered residual loose indumentum on midrib and veins below; venation usually eucamptodromous, rarely slightly brochidodromous, marginal vein present, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 10-14 pairs, parallel, straight; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique and reticulate. Petiole 3-9 mm long, not channelled, pubescent. Fascicles axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves, 1-3-flowered. Pedicel 0.4-1 (-2) cm long, slender, pubescent to glabrous. Flowers unisexual (female) and bisexual (or functionally male ?) on separate plants. Sepals (4-)5(-6), 2-3 mm long, ovate, apex acute to rounded, sparsely pubescent outside, glabrous or with some appressed pubescence inside, sometimes ciliate. Corolla cyathiform, 3.5-4 mm long, tube 1-1.5 mm long, lobes 5 (-6), 2-3mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex rounded, glabrous or occasionally with a few hairs at the base of the tube outside. Stamens 5(-6), fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments 0.5-1 mm long, glabrous; anthers lanceolate, 1.5-1.6 mm long, glabrous, absent in female flowers. Staminodes 5(-6), 1.5-2 mm long, narrowly lanceolate to subulate, often with ventral keel, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary broadly conical, 2(-3)-locular, pubescent; style ca. 1.5 mm long after anthesis, included, pubescent at base; style-head simple. Fruit 1-1.7 cm long, broadly ellipsoid, rounded at base and apex, sometimes apiculate, thin-walled, smooth, with some residual appressed pubescence or glabrous. Seed solitary, 0.9-1.4 cm long, ellipsoid, moderately laterally compressed, rounded at base and apex, testa smooth, or slightly wrinkled, shining, ca. 0.3 mm thick; scar full length, adaxial and extending around the base, ca. 5 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 10 m high and 25 cm diam. with white latex. Flowers greenish, ripe fruit black. Flowering mostly Sep to Nov, fruiting Sep to Dec.

description: Tree; young shoots finely appressed puberulous, eventually glabrous, smooth, grey-brown, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 10.5-22 × 3.2-8 cm, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, apex narrowly acuminate, base narrowly attenuate, chartaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower surface finely pale-golden-sericeous; venation eucamptodromous to brochidodromous, midrib slightly sunken on upper surface, thin marginal vein present, secondary veins 18-20 pairs, shallowly ascending, parallel or slightly convergent, mostly slightly arcuate; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries open-reticulate to oblique. Petiole 1-1.6 cm long, not channelled, finely appressed puberulous. Fascicles axillary, 2-5-flowered. Pedicel 1-1.3 cm long, finely appressed puberulous, broadening gradually into the calyx. Sepals five, ca. 3.5 mm long, ovate to broadly elliptic, apex acute to rounded, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Corolla (young flower) ca. 3.5 mm long, tube ca. 0.75 mm long, lobes five, ca. 2.75 mm long, elliptic, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, free; filaments ca. 2 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.5 mm long, oblong, glabrous. Staminodes ca. 2 mm long, narrowly oblong, apex rounded, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary conical, five-locular, appressed pubescent; style ca. 2 mm long, slightly exserted in young flowers, appressed pubescent in lower half; style-head simple. Young fruit ca. 2 cm long, broadly ovoid or globose, apex rounded, base truncate, with finely appressed golden indumentum. Field characters. Tree to 10 m high with white latex.

description: Tree; young shoots minutely puberulous or glabrous, becoming reddish-brown to greyish, rough, scaling, lenticellate. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 5.5-12.5 × 1.9-4.5 cm, elliptic or lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate or acuminate, base shortly narrowly attenuate, thinly coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, with a strong marginal vein, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-15 pairs, slightly convergent and arcuate; intersecondaries short to moderately long; tertiaries forming a loose reticulum; quaternaries finely areolate. Petiole 0.6-1.2 cm long, usually slightly channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 3-12-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 0.5-2 mm long, sometimes bearing 1-2 small bracts, sparsely appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 5-6, outer 1.5-2 mm long, inner 3-3.5 mm long, broadly ovate or elliptic, apex rounded, sparsely appressed puberulous to glabrous outside, sericeous inside, ciliate. Corolla shortly tubular, 3-5.5 mm long, tube 1.75-3.5 mm long, lobes five(-seven), 1-2 mm long, broadly oblong to suborbicular, apex truncate or rounded, glabrous. Stamens five(-seven), fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments 0.3-0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.5-0.75 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes five(-seven), 0.5-1.5 mm long, lanceolate or subulate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid or globose, five-locular, densely pubescent; style 2.5-4 mm long after anthesis, slightly exserted from flower bud and equalling or slightly exceeding the open corolla, glabrous; style-head simple or minutely five-lobed. Fruit 3.5-4 cm long, broadly obovoid, apex rounded, base attenuate, smooth, thin walled (often shrinking on drying), with residual appressed puberulous indumentum. Seeds 1-2, 23 cm long, broadly ellipsoid, rounded at base and apex, testa smooth to slightly verruculose, 0.4-0.6 mm thick; scar adaxial and usually extending around the base, 0.6-1.2 cm wide, roughened; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle extending to the surface. Field characters. Tree to 45 m high and 1 m diam., larger specimens buttressed to 2 m high; slash with white latex. Flowers yellowish-green, without scent, fruit ripening yellow or orange. Flowering throughout the range mostly Jui to Nov, fruit Jan-Aug.

description: Plants in loose, gray-green tufts, to 3.5 cm high, radiculose below. Leaves appressed below, longer and somewhat curled when dry above, 7-8 mm long, with bases shiny-whitish, slenderly long-pointed from an ovate-lanceolate base, slightly toothed at the extreme apex. Costa about 2/3 of the leaf base, excurrent; in section showing large ventral leucocysts and small dorsal groups of 1-2 substereidal cells. Alar cells red-brown, thin-walled. Inner basal cells lax, hyaline, 40-48 × 7-9.5 µm, the outer cells small, elongate, forming a border of 6-8 rows. Upper laminal cells elongate oval (about 4:1), 17-21 × 5 µm, extending about 2/3 along the costa in 2-3 rows. Sporophytes unknown.

description: Plants to 5 cm high, yellowish green, in loose tufts. Stems appressed foliate, abruptly ending in a comose tip consisting of long, flexuose leaves with numerous small, heteromorphic brood leaves. Leaves about 5 mm long, lanceolate, from ovate base gradually contracted to a serrate tip. Costa filling 1/2 to 2/3 of the leaf width, excurrent, in transverse section with ventral hyalocysts and dorsal groups of (sub)stereids. Brood leaves 2 mm long, narrow lanceolate, with poorly developed lamina, contracted at base, often hooked or curled. Alar cells hardly developed. Basal laminal cells hyaline, thin-walled, rectangular, 16-26 × 45-80 µm, narrower at margins. Upper laminal cells sharply differentiated from the basal ones, incrassate, 8-13 × 13-19 µm, nearly quadrate. Sporophyte not known.

description: Plants to 6 cm, blackish, erect, equally foliate with erect spreading leaves. Leaves to 8 mm long, narrow lanceolate. Costa filling 2/3-3/4 of the leaf width, excurrent in a long, smooth or only in the apex slightly serrate awn, in transverse section with dorsal and ventral bands of stereids, smooth at back or slightly ridged in the upper part of the leaf. Lamina reaching only of the leaf length. Alar cells lacking. Basal laminal cells thin-walled, shortly rectangular (ca. 3:1), ca. 45-55 × 15-20 µm. Upper laminal cells elongate, incrassate, pitted, ca. 70-80 × 8-10 µm (8-10:1). Sporophyte not known.

description: Plants pale yellowish green or whitish green, in dense mats. Stems to 3 cm high, equally foliate, reddish tomentose below. Leaves erect, ca. 4-5 mm long, from an ovate base gradually narrowed to an acumen of varying length. Costa filling of the leaf base, excurrent, denticulate at the extreme apex, in transverse section with ventral hyalocysts, median chlorocysts and dorsal hyalocysts alternating with chlorocysts, grad- ually merging with the lamina, slightly ribbed at back. Alar cells conspicuous, inflated, reddish or hyaline, occupying part of the costa. Basal laminal cells rectangular, hyaline, thin-walled, 16-38 × 58-90 µm, narrower at margins. Upper laminal cells irregularly rectangular, 13-26 × 39 µm, vanishing near midleaf. Setae 15 mm long, pale brown, curved and twisted. Capsules 2 mm long, pale brown, cylindric. Opercula long rostrate. Vegetative propagation by means of small microphyllous branches in the axils of the upper leaves.

description: Tree; young branches densely ferruginous-tomentose, indumentum persistent, eventually becoming glabrous, grey and rough, lenticels absent. Unarmed. Leaves spirally arranged, not clustered, 11-14.5 × 5.5-7.7 cm, broadly elliptic or oblanceolate, apex obtusely cuspidate, base acute or narrowly attenuate or cuneate, coriaceous, upper surface with residual tomentum on the midrib only, lower surface with tomentose midrib and veins and arachnoid-pubescent lamina, hairs ferruginous; venation eucamptodromous, margin slightly revolute, midrib flat on the upper surface; secondary veins 8-10 pairs, ascending, arcuate, parallel or convergent, prominent below; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique, widely spaced. Petiole 1-2 cm long, not channelled, ferruginous tomentose. Flowers bisexual, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves, fascicles very dense, 5-15 flowered, subtended by bracts 2-4 mm long. Pedicel 2-4 mm long, densely ferruginous tomentose. Sepals five, 5-6 mm long, broadly elliptic, obtuse or rounded, outside densely ferruginous tomentose except for the glabrous hyaline margin, inside glabrous. Corolla glabrous, 6.5-7 mm long, tube 2-2.5 mm long, lobes five; median segment suborbicular or obovate, apex rounded; lateral segments lanceolate-falcate, often erose, 2.5-5 mm long. Stamens five, glabrous; filaments 3.5-4.5 mm long, sometimes with two acute appendages near the base, anthers ca. 2.5 mm long, lanceolate-sagittate. Staminodes five, 3-4 mm long, lanceolate to broadly elliptic, infolded, margin erose to deeply cut, glabrous. Ovary slender, tapering gradually into the style, 5-locular, glabrous; style 2.5-3 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit (immature) ca. 2.5 cm long and broad, obovoid, with truncate-apiculate apex and obtuse base, smooth, glabrous; pericarp 2-5 mm thick, fleshy. Seeds two, with a long broad adaxial scar; embryo vertical, with plano-convex cotyledons and no endosperm.  Field characters. A tree to 20 m high, with latex and white flowers. All collections, both flowering and fruiting, are from August.

description: Large tree; young branches minutely appressed ferruginous puberulous, soon glabrous, becoming brown, cracked and ridged, without lenticels. Unarmed. Leaves spirally arranged, spaced or loosely clustered at the stem apex, 6-16 × 2-4.1 cm, oblong-elliptic or elliptic, apex and base narrowly attenuate, leaf base somewhat decurrent, chartaceous, glabrous; venation brochidodromous, leaf margin slightly recurved; secondary veins 10-13 pairs, ascending, parallel, straight, intersecondaries long; tertiaries descending from the margin and parallel to the secondaries, or obscure. Petiole 1-2 cm long, not channelled, glabrous. Inflorescence axillary, in 5-15-flowered fascicles borne at the apex of a peduncle 1-4 cm long, sparsely and minutely appressed puberulous; pedicel ca. 2 mm long, minutely appressed puberulous. (Mature flowers not seen), buds pentamerous; sepals sparsely appressed ferruginous puberulous outside, corolla glabrous, corolla lobes with a median segment and two lanceolate, erose, lateral segments. Stamens glabrous. Staminodes ovate, erose, glabrous. Ovary five-locular, glabrous, with a short style. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Sideroxylon jubilla is described as a large tree. Flowering Nov and Jan.

description: Plants to 5 cm, rarely to 8 cm high, in loose tufts, brownish, blackish, green to yellowish green. Stems mostly conspicuously equally foliate when dry, giving the plants a filiform appearance, erect spreading when moist, sparsely radiculose at base. Leaves straight, 3-7 mm long, from a contracted base, lanceolate, longly subulate. Perichaetial leaves with broad sheathing base, suddenly contracted to long fine subula, enclosing the seta from 1/4 to nearly to the capsule. Costa at base 1/5-1/2 of the leaf width, excurrent in a short awn, smooth, denticulate at the extreme tip, or excurrent in a long serrate hyaline awn, in transverse section with ventral and dorsal stereids, smooth, ribbed or lamellose at back. Alar cells not differentiated, rarely inflated and reddish. Lower laminal cells thin-walled, hyaline, rectangular, narrower at margins, extending upwards along leaf margins, rarely incrassate. Upper laminal cells thick-walled, oblique, rhomboidal, oval, elongate-oval or short rectangular. Seta 1-2 cm long, erect. Capsule 2-4 mm long, light brown, cylindrical, sometimes broader at base, straight, without stomata. Peristome teeth 16, on a basal membrane, undivided or split to the base, densely papillose. Annulus present, dehiscent. Operculum longly rostrate, erect. Calyptra cucullate, fringed at base with long cilia, rarely smooth. Spores ca. 13 in diameter, yellowish to brownish, smooth to minutely papillose.

description: Plants small, only 3-6 mm high, in dense, yellowish to yellowish-green tufts. Stems radiculose at base, frequently with clusters of brood leaves in the comal tufts. Leaves 2-3 mm long, erecto-patent when wet, curled when dry, lanceolate, gradually contracted to a short, canaliculate apex; margins entire. Perichaetial leaves with broader base, abruptly contracted to a narrow leaf tip. Costa filling 2/3 of the leaf base, 155-180 µm wide, not sharply differentiated from the lamina, excurrent, in transverse section with lax dorsal and ventral hyalocysts (ventrally often with two rows of hyalocysts), and a median band of stereids (becoming substereidal towards the margins). Alar cells weakly differentiated, hyaline. Basal laminal cells hyaline, consisting of 8-10 rows, bistratose towards the costa, rectangular, 19-55 × 4-19 µm, narrower at margins. Upper laminal cells rectangular, 24-55 × 3-7 µm. Seta 5-6 mm long, yellowish, sinuose and twisted sinistrorsely in the upper part. Capsule erect, yellowish green, 0.5 x 1.2 mm, smooth, contracted towards the peristome. Exothecial walls incrassate, variable, without stomata. Annulus present. Peristome teeth entire (or rarely perforated ("windowed") in fully developed capsules), yellowish, striate at base and papillose at tips, 210-240 µm long. Spores yellowish green, smooth, 10-13 µm. Calyptra cucullate, fringed at base.

description: Stems solitary or cespitose, erect, 2-8 m tall, 5-7 cm diam., brown. Leaves 4-12, ± erect; sheath open and not forming a crownshaft, persistent, 52-67 cm long, red or light-brown, with yellow to reddish brown scales, fibrous on the margins; petiole 7-10 cm long, with scales like those of sheath; rachis 1.4-1.8 m long, with scales like those of sheath; blade simple, oblong-cuneate, bifid at the apex, 1.9-2.5 m long, 58(-90) cm wide, glabrous or with a few, scattered hairs abaxially, with 36-42 prominent primary veins on either side, with poorly developed ramenta on veins abaxially. Inflorescences corymbose, interfoliar or infrafoliar, recurved at anthesis; peduncle 48-86 cm long, 1.3-1.5 cm diam., subterete, with reddish brown, appressed scales, glabrescent, curved; prophyll 25-34 cm long, ca. 7 cm diam.; peduncular bract 1-1.6 m long including a 2-3 cm long umbo, 7 cm diam.; rachis 60-69 cm long, with appressed, crusty hairs; rachillae 32-48, to 74 cm long proximally, 2.5-6 mm diam. in fruit, zigzag, covered with very small, brown, branched crustose hairs; flowers in triads almost throughout rachillae, paired or solitary staminate flowers only on distal few cm; triad bracteole apiculate; first triad bracteole low, apiculate, second and third flower bracteoles ± equal, apiculate, 1 mm high; staminate flowers 4-6 mm long, sessile; sepals ovate to ovate-triangular, 1-2 mm long, gibbous, minutely ciliate; petals triangular to lanceolate, 4-5.5 mm long; stamens arranged on a short receptacle; filaments 3 mm long, flattened; anthers 2-3 mm long; pistillode 1.5-2 mm long, deeply trifid apically; pistillate flowers 3-4 mm long; sepals very widely ovate, 3 mm long; petals very widely ovate, 4 mm long; staminodes digitate; fruits globose to subglobose, 0.9-14 cm diam., the stigmatic remains lateral; epicarp purple-black at maturity, densely and minutely tuberculate; seeds subglobose, 7-8 mm diam.; endosperm ruminate; eophyll bifid.

description: Tree 5-25 m tall. Stems terete, glabrous, lenticellate. Leaves paripinnate, 1.5-3 m long; distal process acicular, ca. 1 cm long; leaflets 6-12, opposite or alternate, oblanceolate or less often elliptic, 40-55 × 6.5-20.5 cm, sub-coriaceous, glabrous, flattened to slightly bullate, dull on both surfaces, the venation brochidodromus, not forming a sub-marginal loop, the adaxial surface with a prominent midvein and slightly raised secondaries, the abaxial surface with strongly prominent midvein, secondary and tertiary veins prominulous, tertiary veins reticulate, the margins undulate, the apex abruptly acuminate, the base slightly asymmetrical, obtuse; petiolules woody, enlarged, 0.6-1.6 × 0.5-0.9 cm, glabrous, adaxially canaliculate; rachis terete, striate, glabrous; petioles at least 21 cm long, nearly terete, striate, glabrous, bulbous at base. Thyrses panicle-like, terminal; cataphylls minute, scale-like; dichasia simple or compound; pedicels ca. 2.5 mm long, articulate at the middle. Calyx 2.5-3 mm long, puberulent, the sepals 1-1.7 mm long, ovate, concave, obtuse at apex; petals elliptic, 5.5-6 mm long, white, adaxially glabrous, abaxially tomentulose at base, ciliate at margins, the apex rounded-obtuse, the base cuneate; appendages oblong-lanceolate, as long as the petal, villose sericeous-tomentose on both surfaces, adaxially glabrous at base; disc cup-shaped, 5-lobed, puberulent, ca. 1 mm tall; stamens 8 (9), the filaments of unequal length, 3-3.5 mm long, slightly flattened, woolly-pubescent, the anthers 1-1.5 mm long, elliptic, glabrous, apiculate at apex. Pistillate flower unknown. Fruits brown, ovoid to globose, 3-3.2 cm long, glabrous, rugulate, the pericarp woody, ca. 4 mm thick, the endocarp glabrous, smooth. Seeds solitary, nearly globose, the testa apparently not fleshy. Embryo sub-globose, the cotyledons laying obliquely transverse over each other, of similar size.

description: Shrub 3-7 m tall. Stems slightly sulcate, nearly terete, ferruginous-velutinous. Leaves imparipinnate or paripinnate; distal process acicular, to 1.5 cm long, early deciduous, leaving a truncate base; leaflets 8-11, alternate, opposite or subopposite, 19-75 × 7-19 cm, elliptic to oblanceolate, chartaceous, the adaxial surface completely glabrous or velutinous along the sunken primary and secondary veins, the abaxial surface pilose to sparsely velutinous, especially along veins, the venation brochidodromus, with secondary veins alternate or subopposite, tertiary veins clathrate-reticulate, prominent on abaxial surface, the margins wavy, the apex abruptly acuminate, mucronate, the base obtuse to rounded, slightly asymmetrical; petiolules 8-15 mm long, velutinous, nearly cylindrical; rachis 16-32 cm long, velutinous, striate, nearly terete; petioles 27-56 cm long, velutinous, striate, terete, slightly enlarged at base. Thyrses fasciculate, cauliflorous; cataphylls acicular, to 1.2 cm long, velutinous, congested in supra-axillary buds; axes 2-15 cm long, angled, velutinous-tomentose; bracts subulate, persistent, 2-A mm long, sparsely tomentose to glabrous; bracteoles similar to bracts but smaller; dichasia compound, sessile; pedicels ca. 1 mm long, articulate above or below the middle. Flowers congested along inflorescence axes. Calyx (2.5) 4-5.2 mm long, sericeous-tomentose, the sepals ovate-deltate, ca. 1.5-2.3 mm long, obtuse at apex; petals elliptic to nearly spatulate, obtuse at apex, long-attenuate at base, 5-6.7 mm long, abaxially glabrous, adaxially papillate; appendages as long or slightly longer than the petals, oblong or deltate, erect, adnate to attenuate base of petal, adaxially villous, abaxially sparsely villous and papillate; disc poculiform, 5-lobed, hirsute, ca. 1 mm tall; stamens 8, the filaments unequal, 2.5-3.5 mm long, glabrous, the anthers 0.7-1.2 mm long, ellipsoid, glabrous, apiculate at apex. Fruits (young) ellipsoid, ferruginous, sericeous-velutinous, the pericarp thick-woody.

description: Treelet 2-7 m tall, sometimes with a few upright branches on distal portion, theses with determinate growth due to a terminal inflorescence. description: base; corolla blue or blue-purple to magenta, rarely white, tubular-campanulate above a narrow basal tube, pubescent to essentially glabrous outside; anthers glabrous, often 1-thecate, the staminode elongate, exceeding the stamens, variously glandular-pubescent especially at the tip; pollen grains 3-colpate, the exine smooth; ovary flattened-cylindrical, glabrous or pubescent (even in the same species), the ovules ca. 8-seriate in each locule; disk pulvinate. Fruit an oblong capsule strongly flattened perpendicularly to the septum, dehiscing perpendicular to the septum and parallel to the plane of compression, the valves variously glabrous or lepidote, often with undulate margins; seeds thin, winged, the wings membranaceous, hyaline or brownish. A neotropical genus of 49 species, ranging from Guatemala and the Antilles to northern Argentina. The presumably primitive section Dilobos is concentrated in Brazil; section Monolobos is more evenly distributed but has more species in northwestern South America and the West Indies.

description: Shrubs to trees, the bark often rather thick and vertically fissured, lacking pseudostipules or interpetiolar glandular fields, the branchlets stellate pubescent. Fruit a round to broadly obovoid capsule, slightly compressed, densely tannish tomentose, verrucose with spine-like enations; seeds thin, more or less orbicular with the hyaline wing surrounding the rather large body.

description: Plants yellowish to brownish green, slender, in dense mats, to 3(-5) cm high. Stems often partly defoliate, sometimes with homomallous leaves at tips. description: Low shrub; twigs moderately to slightly angled, slender, sparsely lepidote, otherwise sparsely pubescent; buds ovoid, 0.8-1 × 0.6-1 mm. Leaf blades ovate to elliptic, 1-3.5 × 0.7-2.3 cm, ± flat, often strongly coriaceous, ca. 0.45-0.56 mm thick; base rounded to slightly cordate; apex acute to rounded; margin plane to slightly revolute, apical portion entire to sinuous or occasionally very obscurely toothed, basal portion entire; venation brochidodromous, 3° veins reticulate; adaxial surface lepidote but scales usually quickly deciduous, sparsely pubescent on basal portion of midvein, 3° and higher-order veins visible to less commonly obscure, midvein not depressed, 2° veins not depressed; abaxial surface sparsely lepidote, otherwise glabrous (very sparsely pubescent on midvein near petiole), the 3° and higher-order veins very slightly raised, slightly and laxly reticulate, as prominent as 2° (or nearly so), the 2° veins raised and visible; scales rust colored, persistent to deciduous, ca. 0.12-0.17 mm in diam., ± entire; petiole 1-5 mm long, lepidote, otherwise pubescent all around or less commonly only adaxially flower buds ± intermixed with vegetative buds. Inflorescences fasciculate, ca. 1-10-flowered; pedicels usually clearly articulated with calyx, slender, 10-31 mm long, lepidote, otherwise sparsely to moderately pubescent; bracteoles subopposite to alternate, near base of pedicel, narrowly triangular, 0.5-1 mm long; floral bracts to ca. 2 mm long. Flowers (4-)5-merous; calyx lobes triangular, with acuminate to acute apices, 2-3 × 1-1.7 mm, adaxial side often sparsely lepidote near margins, otherwise sparsely pubescent, especially near apex, abaxial side lepidote, sometimes densely so, otherwise glabrous to moderately pubescent near base; corolla urceolate, pink(?), 5-7 × 3.5-5 mm, abaxially ± moderately lepidote, sometimes appearing golden; filaments roughened, ca. 3 mm long(?), usually with very short spurs to ca. 0.1 mm long near anther-filament junction; anthers ca. 1.2 mm long(?); ovary lepidote, otherwise pubescent, placentae ± subapical. description:
Tree; young shoots puberulous or shortly pubescent with golden brown to ferruginous hairs, soon glabrous, grey to whitish-grey, finely cracked, lenticellate or not. Leaves spaced, usually alternate and distichous, less frequently spirally arranged, 3.8-9.3 × 1-3.4 cm, elliptic, lanceolate or rarely oblong, apex caudate or narrowly attenuate, base narrowly attenuate to rounded, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, glabrous, venation craspedodromous or brochidodromous, marginal vein strong, submarginal vein present, very close to or fusing with the marginal vein, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary and tertiary venation appearing uniformly finely striate to the naked eye, but with a lens the parallel intersecondaries and tertiaries can usually be distinguished from the slightly stronger secondaries. Petiole (1.5-)2-5 mm long, channelled, pubescent to glabrous. Fascicles axillary, 3-15-flowered. Pedicel 1.5-5 mm long, shortly pubescent. Flowers unisexual (always?) (plant monoecious). Sepals 4-5, (1-)1.5-2(-3) mm long, ovate, apex obtuse to rounded, shortly pubescent outside, appressed puberulous to glabrous inside. Corolla 1.25-3 mm long, shortly tubular to campanulate, tube 1-2.25 mm long (exuding or sometimes equalling the lobes), lobes 4-5, 0.75-1.5 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, glabrous. Stamens 4-5, included, fixed near the top of the corolla tube, but with long traces visible to near the base of the tube; filaments 0.2-0.75 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.30.6 mm long, lanceolate or ovate, glabrous, stamens vestigial or absent in female flowers. Staminodes 4-5, 0.3-0.75 mm long, ovate or lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, 4-5-locular, densely stiff-pubescent; style 0.5-1.5 mm long after anthesis, included, glabrous; style-head 4-5-lobed or simple. Fruit 1.2-3.2 cm long, subglobose to broadly ellipsoid, apex and base acute to rounded, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, 1-1.5 cm long, laterally compressed, testa finely transversely wrinkled, shining, 0.5-1 mm thick; scar adaxial and sometimes extending around the base of the seed, 1.5-2.5 mm wide.

Field characters. Tree to 40 m high and 100 cm diam.; exceptional specimens may be as much as 70 m high and 150 cm diam, above the buttresses. The tree has long steep buttresses to 3 m high, with a cylindrical or fluted bole. Bark greyish-brown, finely fissured or more commonly scaling with small dapple marks or finely grid-cracked, with reddish-brown slash exuding plentiful milky white latex. Flowers pale green to cream-coloured, fruit maturing yellow or sometimes tinged red. Throughout its range most flowering is recorded between May and Jan, with mature fruit present throughout the year. There are many records of the fruit being dispersed by birds.

description: Tree; young shoots with a few short appressed hairs, soon glabrous, grey to dark brown, smooth, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 5-14 × 1.7-5.4 cm, oblanceolate or rarely narrowly elliptic, apex usually narrowly attenuate, rarely rounded or emarginate, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, glabrous; venation brochidodromous, often with a marginal vein, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 17-25 pairs, usually parallel, straight or slightly arcuate, looping below the margin to form a submarginal vein, raised on both surfaces; intersecondaries long; tertiaries mostly parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin. Petiole 1.2-2.3 cm long, channelled, glabrous. Fascicles (2-)5-15-flowered, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves. Pedicel 7-9 mm long, with sparse appressed hairs or subglabrous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, 2-3 mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex rounded or obtuse, sparsely appressed puberulous outside, usually glabrous inside. Corolla 3-3.5 mm long, lobes about equalling the tube, five, broadly ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed in the lower half of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 2 mm long, often geniculate, glabrous; anthers ca. 1 mm long, ovate or lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes absent. Ovary short, broad, truncate, five-locular, densely long-strigose; style 1-1.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head capitate or minutely lobed. Fruit 1.8-3 cm long, broadly ellipsoid or globose, apex obtuse to rounded, base rounded to truncate, often contracted between the seeds, smooth, glabrous. Seeds 2-5, 1.4-1.9 cm long, laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 1-1.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, extending most of the length of the seed, 1.5-2 mm wide; embryo with thin foliaceous cotyledons and long exserted radicle, surrounded by copious endosperm. Field characters. Tree to 25 m high with smooth bark. Rowers greenish-white, scented, fruit maturing yellow. Flowering Oct to Dec, fruit maturing May to Sep.

description: Tree; young shoots closely appressed puberulous, becoming glabrous, greyish to dark brown, rough and scaling, without lenticels. Stipules 1-2 cm long, lanceolate, often longitudinally striate, appressed puberulous on the abaxial surface, often with a broad glabrous margin. Leaves usually densely clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 16-42 × 6.5-16.5 cm, usually oblanceolate, rarely oblong-elliptic, apex narrowly attenuate to obtusely cuspidate, base usually narrowly attenuate, cuneate, or acute, less frequently obtuse, thinly coriaceous, glabrous or with scattered appressed hairs on the midrib below, venation eucamptodromous, sometimes with a marginal vein, midrib sunken on the upper surface or prominent but recessed, secondary veins 20-33 pairs, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique, parallel; higher order venation usually obscure or absent. Petiole 2-4 cm long, channelled, appressed puberulous. Fascicles axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves, 5-10-flowered. Flowers unisexual (? plant monoecious). Sepals five, 2.5-4 mm long, ovate or lanceolate, apex acute to rounded, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Corolla 3-5.5 mm long, tube 1-2.75 mm long, lobes 5-7, 1.75-2.75 mm long, ovate, apex acute, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed about halfway up the corolla tube or near the top, filaments 1.25-1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ovate to broadly lanceolate, usually apiculate, glabrous; the stamens absent in female flowers. Ovary ovoid to globose, 7-9-locular, densely long-strigose; style 0.5-1.25 mm long after anthesis, glabrous above; style-head simple or slightly lobed; ovules rudimentary in male flowers. Fruit 5-6 cm long, globose, apex rounded or obtuse, base truncate, thick walled, smooth, minutely puberulous to glabrous. Seeds several, 2-3 cm long, broadly ellipsoid or shaped like the segment of an orange, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.5 mm thick; scar adaxial and extending round the base of the seed, 5-9 mm wide. Field characters. Tree to 35 m high and 50 cm diam. without buttresses. Bole cylindrical, bark dark brown or blackish, strongly dappled. Slash cream to orange, with copious sticky white latex. Flowers greenish-white to yellow, fruit orange-yellow with rather spongy mesocarp, the seeds surrounded by white pulp. Flowering mostly Aug to Nov, fruit maturing Jan to Jul.

description: Tree; young shoots closely ferruginous-puberulous with crisped hairs, indumentum becoming greyish with age, eventually glabrous, greyish, rough, fissured and grid-cracked, without lenticels. Stipules 0.5-1 cm long, ovate or lanceolate, finely appressed puberulous along the centre, with a broad glabrous margin. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 12-22 × 5-11.3 cm, broadly elliptic to oblanceolate, apex obtusely cuspidate to rounded, base acute to obtuse or rounded, strongly coriaceous, sulcate above, upper surface glabrous or with residual pubescence on the midrib, lower surface tomentose with very short crisped ferruginous hairs, venation eucamptodromous, with a marginal vein, midrib and secondary veins sunken on the upper surface, or midrib sometimes prominent but recessed, secondaries 17-26 pairs, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries absent, tertiaries oblique, parallel, numerous; higher order venation usually obscure. Petiole 12 cm long, channelled, at least at the apex, puberulous. Fascicles axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves, 5-10-flowered. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious). Sepals five, 2.5-4 mm long, lanceolate or ovate, apex acute, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Corolla 3-4.5 mm long, tube 1-1.5 mm long, lobes five, 2-3 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed near the top of the corolla tube; filaments 1-1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.6-1 mm long, ovate, apex rounded, glabrous; stamens absent in female flowers. Ovary broadly ovoid or pulvinate, five-locular, densely long-strigose; style 1-1.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head minutely lobed; ovules vestigial in male flowers. Fruit (immature) ca. 2 cm long, globose, apex truncate, apiculate, base rounded, shortly ferruginous-tomentose. Seed not seen. Field characters. Tree to 15 m high, with characteristic strongly sulcate leaves. The color of the leaf undersurface gives a dark brown effect to the landscape on Cerro Jaua, Bolívar, Venezuela (Steyermark 97984). Thick white latex present. Flowers olive-green to greenish-yellow, fruit castaneous brown. Flowering recorded Feb-Mar, May, Nov, young fruit Sep.

description: Leaves usually 11-22 × 4.6-8.5 cm, apex obtuse, obtusely cuspidate, rounded or emarginate, lower surface not glaucous, secondary veins not impressed on lower surface. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 45 cm diam. with branched, slender, slightly concave buttresses to ca. 1 m high, bole cylindrical, bark finely vertically cracked, pale greyish-buff, slash pinkish-brown, thin, with some sticky white latex; flowers scented, yellowish-white, fruit yellowish-green to purple. Flowering and fruiting for this subsp, have been recorded throughout the year.

description: Arbor; ramuli novelli initio minute et adpresse puberuli, mox glabri, nigri, laevi, elenticellati, demum asperi persistentibus inforescentiae basibus. Folia congesta, spiraliter disposita, 9.5-15 × 3.9-6.6 cm, plerumque late elliptica, apice breviter et anguste attenuata usque obtuse cuspidata, basi acuta usque rotundata vel subtruncata, tenuiter coriacea, glabra; venatio eucamptodroma; costa supra elevata (rotundata); nervi secundarii 13—15-jugi, paralleli, recti vel leviter arcuati, in superficiebus ambabus elevati; nervi intersecundarii nulli; nervi tertiarii obliquei. Petiolus 2-3.5 cm longus, non canaliculata, glaber. Fasciculi 3-5-flori, axillares et sub foliis dispositi. Pedicellus 1-2 mm longus, subtiliter adpresse puberulus. Sepala quatuor, 4.5-5 mm longa, sepala externa ovata, apice acuta, sepala interna late oblonga, apice rotundata, extus adpresse puberula, sepala interna margine lata glabra, intus glabra. Corolla tubularis, ca. 5.5 mm longa; tubus ca. 3.5 mm longus; lobi quatuor, ca. 2 mm longi, late oblongi, apice rotundati vel truncati, fimbriato ciliati, aliter glabri. Stamina quatuor, medio tubo corollae affixa; filamenta ca. 2.5 mm longa, glabra; antherae 1.25-1.5 mm longae, lanceolatae, ad apicem penicillatae. Staminodia quatuor, inter lobos corollae affixa, ca. 1.5 mm longa, anguste oblonga, apice rotundata, fimbriato-ciliata. Discus nullus. Ovarium latum, sensim in stylum decrescens, quadriloculare, dense et longe strigosum; stylus post anthesin ca. 2.5	mm longus, corollam aequans vel leviter exsertus, supra glaber; styli capitulum simplex vel minute 4-lobatum. Fructus 5.5-8 cm longus, ellipsoideus, apice et basi rotundatus, pericar-pium durum, laeve, minute et adpresse puberulum, demum glabrum. Semina plura, 2.8-4.3 cm longa, ellipsoidea, apice et basi rotundata, interdum leviter lateraliter compressa, testa laevis vel leviter aspera, ad pericarpium adherens, ca. 1.5 mm crassa; cicatrix adaxialis, per totam longitudinem et circa basim extensa, aspera et torulosa, apice ca. 8 mm lata, ad ca. 4 mm basi decrescens; embryo non visus.

description: Tree; young shoots minutely appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, black, smooth, without lenticels, older shoots rough with persistent inflorescence bases. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 9.5-15 × 3.9-6.6 cm, mostly broadly elliptic, apex shortly narrowly attenuate to obtusely cuspidate, base acute to rounded or subtruncate, thinly coriaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib raised (rounded) on the upper surface, secondary veins 13-15 pairs, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate, raised on both surfaces; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique. Petiole 2-3.5 cm long, not channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 3-5-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 1-2 mm long, finely appressed puberulous. Sepals four, 4.5-5 mm long, outer pair ovate, apex acute, inner pair broadly oblong, apex rounded, appressed puberulous outside, inner pair with broad glabrous margin, glabrous inside. Corolla tubular, ca. 5.5 mm long, tube ca. 3.5 mm long, lobes four, ca. 2 mm long, broadly oblong, apex rounded or truncate, fringed-ciliate, otherwise glabrous. Stamens four, fixed about half way up the corolla tube; filaments ca. 2.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 1.25-1.5	mm long, lanceolate, with a small tuft of hairs at apex. Staminodes four, fixed between the corolla lobes, ca. 1.5 mm long, narrowly oblong, apex rounded, fringed-ciliate. Disk absent. Ovary broad, tapering gradually to style, four-locular, densely long-strigose; style ca. 2.5 mm long after anthesis, equalling the corolla or slightly exserted, glabrous above; style-head simple or minutely four-lobed. Fruit 5.5-8 cm long, ellipsoid, apex and base rounded, pericarp hard, smooth, minutely appressed puberulous, becoming glabrous. Seeds several, 2.8-4.3 cm long, ellipsoid, apex and base rounded, sometimes slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth or slightly uneven, adherent to pericarp, ca. 1.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length and extending around the base, rough and torulose, ca. 8 mm wide at apex, tapering to ca. 4 mm wide at base; embryo not seen.  Field characters. Tree to 25 m high with short buttresses ascending to 2-3 m high; bark brown to yellow-brown, scaling in small pieces. Rowers whitish. Flowering (Colombia) Oct-Dec, mature fruit Aug-Sep (Peru), Apr (French Guiana). Local names. Quinilla (Peru).

description: Tree; young shoots subglabrous, pale brown, becoming scaly, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 19-21 × 7.9-9.5 cm, broadly elliptic, apex and base narrowly attenuate, chartaceous, glabrous above, uniformly and closely sericeous below; indumentum pale whitish buff; venation eucamptodromous, thin marginal vein present, midrib not raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-10 pairs, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries numerous, oblique. Petiole 2.5-4 cm long, not channelled, subglabrous. Fascicles 2-5-flowered, axillary. Pedicel 4-5 mm long, sericeous. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals four, ca. 3.5 mm long, broadly ovate or elliptic, apex rounded or obtuse, pale sericeous outside, inner pair with broad, glabrous margin, glabrous inside. Corolla broadly tubular, 4-4.5 mm long, tube slightly longer than lobes, lobes four, broadly oblong, apex truncate, fringed ciliate. Stamens four, fixed almost halfway up the corolla tube; filaments ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 1 mm long, broadly lanceolate, apiculate, glabrous. Staminodes four, ca. 1 mm long, lanceolate, fringed ciliate. Disk absent. Ovary globose, four-locular, densely long strigose; style ca. 2 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit unknown. Field characters (from Standley’s protologue). Tree 15 m and 15 cm diam. with a clear bole of 7.5 m, with narrow buttresses, and thin bark, somewhat stringy below; sap slightly milky; twigs hollow, flowers yellowish-white.

description: Inflorescences unbranched to branched, the axes glabrous to densely puberulent and often also sparsely pilose. Calyx chartaceous, glabrous, the radius 2-8 mm, the lobes 1-6 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide, deltate to narrowly triangular, acute to apiculate at apex. Fruits ellipsoidal or globose, obtuse at apex, (l-)2-3(-5?) cm long, (1-)2-3 cm in diam. Seeds 4-6 mm long, 4-5 mm wide.

description: Plants tall, to more than 10 cm high, in yellowish green, loose tufts. Stems equally foliate, tomentose below. Leaves 10-15 mm long, gradually narrowed into a long, fine, nearly smooth or slightly serrulate point, spreading or attached to the stem. Costa filling more than of the leaf base, excurrent, in transverse section with large ventral hyalocysts covering more than half of the transverse section and dorsal groups of stereids, smooth at back. Alar cells conspicuous, forming large auricles protruding into the costa, reddish inside and hyaline outside. Basal laminal cells incrassate, short rectangular, often slightly pitted, 5-10 × 50-65 µm, narrower and paler at margins. Upper laminal cells small, incrassate, oval to oblique, 3-6 × 19-26 µm. Seta to 15 mm long, arising from short pseudolateral branches, sinuose or curved, yellowish to light brown. Capsule 2.5-3 mm long, curved, strumose, nearly smooth or furrowed when emptied, olive to dark brown. Peristome dark red. Operculum shortly rostrate, half as long as the capsule. Calyptra ciliate at base.

description: Plants dark green to brownish green or blackish, to 1 cm, rarely to 2 cm high, in loose tufts. Stems with appressed or erect patent leaves. Leaves lanceolate, 2.5-4 mm long, the margins entire and convolute in the upper part. Costa 1/3 of the leaf width, excurrent in a hyaline point, in transverse section with dorsal stereids and a small group of ventral stereids in the median part of the leaf. Alar cells lacking. Basal laminal cells rectangular, incrassate, 13-19 × 35-50 µm. Upper laminal cells oblique to oval, incrassate, 56 × 19-25 µm. Capsule globose, ca. 1 mm in diam., scabrous at base, shortly rostrate. Seta 2-4 mm long, curved. Calyptra long-ciliate at base.

description: Slender tree or treelet, 4-10 m tall; trunk to 8 cm in diam. Stems sulcate, glabrous, lenticellate, usually hollow, inhabited by ants. Leaves paripinnate or imparipinnate, spirally arranged on distal portions of stem; distal process acicular, 5-7 mm long; leaflets (7)11-15, opposite or alternate, oblanceolate, oblong-elliptic, sometimes obovate or falcate, chartaceous, (14-) 17-43 x 4.5-10.5 cm, the adaxial surface glabrous, with prominulous midvein and slightly sunken secondary veins (sometimes bullate), the abaxial surface glabrous or sparingly pubescent, primary and secondary veins prominent, tertiary veins reticulate, prominulous, the apex abruptly acuminate to nearly caudate, the base inequilateral, one side obtuse the other acute or cuneate, the margins undulate; petiolules brownish (drying dark brown), pulvinate, adaxially furrowed, 7-14 mm long; rachis 20-54 cm long, terete, striate to bicarinate on distal portion, glabrous, yellowish brown, glossy; petioles 20-29 cm long, terete, striate, glabrous, enlarged at base. Thyrses panicle-shaped, 20-42 cm long, terminal or axillary on distal part of stem, lateral branches to 15 cm long; cataphylls acicular or pinnate, 1.5-5 cm long, clustered at leaves axils; axes angled, sulcate, sericeous-tomentose; bracts deltate, sericeous-tomentose, ca. 1 mm long; bracteoles similar to the bracts but smaller; dichasia simple or compound; peduncle 5-8 mm long on proximal dichasia, ca. 1 mm on distal dichasia; pedicels 1-1.5 mm long, articulate near the middle, sericeous-tomentose. Calyx 4-7 mm long, abaxially ferruginous-sericeous-tomentose, the sepals 2-3.5 mm long, ovate to rounded, concave, imbricate, abaxially glabrous around the woolly-pubescent margins, adaxially glabrous, the outer sepals shorter than the inner ones; petals white to orangish, 8-9 mm long, elliptic, reflexed at anthesis, abaxially ferruginous-sericeous-tomentose except along upper margins, adaxially papillate, the margins woolly to ciliate, clawed at base, the claw ca. 3.5 mm long, slightly fleshy, white, glabrous; appendage as long as or shorter than the petal, white, erect, connivent, strap-shaped or elongated deltate, sericeous-tomentose on both surfaces; disc 5-lobed, completely or only apically tomentose, ca. 1 mm tall; stamens 8, the filaments white, glabrous, of unequal length, 4-5 mm long, the anthers oblong-lanceolate, 1.5-1.7 mm long, apiculate at apex; ovary ferruginous-tomentose, the stigma ellipsoid, papillate. Fruit maturing yellow, orange-yellow or red, oblong-ellipsoid to nearly globose, apiculate, 2-3.2 cm long, velvety pubescent, becoming glabrous at maturity, the pericarp ca. 1.5 mm thick, coriaceous, smooth or less often granulate. Seed solitary, ellipsoid with lilac, sweet fleshy testa. Embryo with cotyledons diagonally overlapping, the lower one larger than the upper one.
