description: Roots shallow, forming an open system along which are often found more dense clumps of branched roots; ultimate branch segments usually free for a short distance. Inflorescences nodding, racemose or reduced to a solitary flower; bracts present, sometimes similar to perianth; bracteoles present in some specimens of M. hypopitys. Flowers nodding at anthesis, becoming erect in fruit, more or less fleshy, (3-)4-5(-6)-merous; calyx similar to corolla, quite distinct or apparently absent, similar or not in color to corolla, glabrous or sparsely glandular pubescent, color ranging from white to yellowish, orange, or pink shades; corolla cylindrical, or slightly flared distally, polypetalous, imbricate in bud, petals saccate at base, often pubescent on inner surface, apices acute to truncate, color ranging from white to yellowish, orange, or pink shades; stamens 8-10, generally twice as many as corolla lobes, in two series of alternating lengths, included, color similar to corolla, no appendages; anthers with connate sacs in a horizontal plane or erect and hippocrepiform, smooth, dehiscence terminal; ovary usually pubescent, 5(4-6) locular, placentation axile; nectary present as 8-10 lobes projecting basipetally from between staminal bases, paired opposite the saccate bases of the petals; style cylindric, slender or stout, elongate or short, included, conspicuously articulated with ovary; stigma umbilicate to deeply funnelform, with 4-6 shallow lobes, glabrous or with a dense ring of subtending hairs. Fruit a loculicidal capsule, pedicels erect at maturity, capsular segments persistent or irregularly deciduous, vascular bundles between separated capsular segments may persist in fruit linked by several lateral smaller vascular bundles; seeds spindleshaped, minute, 0.5-1 mm long, light brownish; embryo two-celled (Olson, 1980); chromosome number: n = 24 (Hagerup, 1944; Maloney & Finocchio, 1981; Baker & Parfitt, 1982) or 2n = 32 (Löve & Löve, 1982); Monotropa hypopitys, 2n = ca. 48 (Uotila & Pellinen, 1985).

description: Low shrubs, the stems hirsute, the hairs stellate, grayish. Leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 11-14 x 5-7 cm, basally rounded or subcordate, crenate-serrate, shortly acuminate, palmately 5-nerved, pubescent above and beneath; petioles 3-5 cm long, angulate, hirsute; stipules linear or subspatulate, erect, subscabrous. Flowers solitary in the leaf axils, the pedicels slightly shorter than the leaves, hirsute; involucellar bracts 5, ovate-acuminate, hirsute; calyx slightly shorter than the involucel, subtomentose, 5-parted; petals reddish, subequal to the involucel; staminal column subequal to the corolla, the anthers yellowish, subglobose; stigmas capitate, purplish. Mericarps obovate, more or less reticulate, apically mucronate.

description: Epiphytic and terrestrial shrub ca. 1.5 m tall; stem base to 2 cm in diam.; mature branches terete or obtusely angled, smooth or minutely striate, glabrate, tan or reddish-brown; twigs terete, obtusely angled or conspicuously flattened, minutely striate, glabrate or densely short-pilose. Leaves linear, linear-lanceolate, or elliptic-lanceolate, averaging 5-6 times longer than wide (4.5-)7.5-12(-14.5) X (0.5-) 1-2(-2.5) cm, basally narrowing, rounded and usually slightly cordate, apically long-attenuate to an ultimately blunt tip, glabrous, marginally strongly revolute (rarely flat); pinnately nerved, lowest primary nerves sometimes arcuate to about middle where they anastomose and form a collective nerve with remaining nerves which runs to leaf apex, midrib deeply impressed above and conspicuously raised beneath, lateral nerves and veinlets raised and conspicuous above, slightly raised but obscure beneath; petioles subterete, rugose and often longitudinally ribbed, 3.5-6.5(-9) mm long and 1-2.5 mm in diam., densely short-pilose adaxially becoming glabrate. Inflorescence solitary or rarely two in terminal axils, 8-28-flowered with lowest 3-8 nodes usually sterile, viscid; rachis conspicuously bluntly angled, minutely striate, glabrous, purple, 5.5-13 cm long and 1-2.5 mm in diam.; floral bracts conspicuously nerved, concave or cucullate, ovate, 3-6.5 X 2.5-4.5 mm, basally rounded and truncate, somewhat auriculate, apically acute to obtuse, glabrous, distal 2/3 of margin glandular-callose, dark purple with greenish tinge; pedicels subterete, striate, swollen apically, glabrous, 11-18(-24) mm long and 0.5-1 (-1.5) mm in diam., dark purple; bracteoles located up pedicel, conspicuously nerved, concave, ovate, 1.5-2.5(-3) x (0.5-)1.5(-3) mm, basally continuous (not articulated) with tissue of pedicel, apically acute, glabrous, distal 2/3 glandular-callose, dark purplish-green. Flowers: calyx glabrous, (5-)6-7(-8) mm long, sometimes slightly stipitate; hypanthium cylindric, rugose and ribbed, surface often muricate, (1.5-)2-3(-4.5) mm long, basally strongly apophysate and deeply lobed, green when immature, dark purple at anthesis but turning greenish after anthesis; limb cylindric or spreading, rarely campanulate, ribbed, (2-)4-4.5 (-5.5) mm long; lobes triangular, 1-1.5(-2) X (1.5-)2-2.5(-3) mm, erect after anthesis, completely glandular-callose or rarely margins slightly thinner than main body, purple; sinus obtuse to broadly rounded; corolla slightly constricted basally and narrowed at throat, densely short, white pubescent without with trichomes 0.2-0.4 mm long (rarely glabrous), sparsely pilose within, (16-)18-21,5(-22) mm long and 4-8 mm in diam., pale purple at constricted base, purple above, lobes triangular, 1-1.5 mm long, glabrous, reflexed at anthesis often exposing tips of anthers; stamens 15.5-19.5 mm long; filaments glabrous or more commonly with long ones medially pilose and short ones distally pilose, alternately 2-3.5 mm and 5-7.5 mm long; anthers alternately 15.5-18 mm and 12.5-14.5 mm long; thecae alternately 5.5-6.5 mm and 4-5.5 mm long; style exserted at anthesis. Berry 12-15 mm in diam.

description: Tree; branchlets minutely tomentellous, ca. 3 mm thick, glabrescent; terminal buds fulvo-sericeous. Leaves evenly distributed along branchlets, chartaceous, elliptic-lanceolate or lanceolate, 2.5-3 times longer than wide, 16-19 x 5-7 cm, base acute or angustate, apex indistinctly and shortly acuminate, glabrous, midrib and nerves flat or slightly impressed above, minutely and laxly appressed-pubescent, glabrescent (?), with prominent midrib and nerves beneath, nerves 6-8 pairs, ascending, looped and fused ca. 2 mm from margin; petioles minutely tomentellous, hardly grooved, 1-1.2 cm long. Panicles subterminal, pauciflorous, laxly tomentellous, 6-8 cm long. Flowers minutely appressed-pilose, 2.5 x 1.5 mm; floral tube inside at base glabrous; pedicels thin, 3-5 mm long; tepals erect, thin, inside subglabrous and laxly pellucid-punctate, 1 mm long, outer ones ovate, ciliate at margin, inner ones obovate, fimbriate at margin; stamens included, 0.8-1 mm long, those of ser. I and II with glabrous, ovate anthers, large cells and filaments narrower than anthers, those of ser. III with glabrous anthers and pilose, biglandulate filaments; staminodes absent; pistil papillose, 2.5 mm long; ovary laxly pilose; style glabrous and longer than ovary; stigma small. Fruit unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Kubitzki, K. & Renner, Susanne S. 1982. Lauraceae I (Aniba and Aiouea). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 31: 1-125.

description:
Tree, indumentum of young parts appressed and spreading. Lower leaf surface densely sericeous-tomentose with golden or ferruginous hairs; leaves oblong, not thinly chartaceous, secondary veins straight or arcuate. Corolla tube 1.5-3 times as long as the lobes, creases at base of corolla lobes short or absent, indumentum on corolla tube and lobes. Fruit 1-2.5 cm long, ellipsoid, one-seeded.

Field characters. A tree to about 15 m high with white latex. Flowers cream, mature fruit purple or black. Flowering Oct to Feb, fruiting Feb to Apr.

description: Tree; indumentum of young parts closely appressed. Lower leaf surface glabrous, leaves elliptic or oblong, thinly chartaceous, secondary veins straight. Corolla tube 3-4 times as long as lobes, creases at base of lobes often long and equalling the lobes, indumentation present on corolla tube and lobes. Fruit unknown. Field characters. A slightly buttressed tree to 25 m high with fluted bole, the bark with white milky latex. The flowers are yellowish-green, and the fruit ripens violet, with copious latex in the pericarp. Flowering Jul to Oct, fruit maturing Feb.

description: Tree; young shoots densely appressed brown-pubescent at first, soon glabrous, greyish-brown, lenticellate, cracked and fissured. Leaves loosely clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 940 × 3.3-12.5 cm, oblanceolate to narrowly cuneiform, apex obtuse, rounded or truncate, base long tapering, finally obtuse, rounded or truncate, margin shallowly spinulose-serrate, thinly coriaceous, glabrous above, some residual matted indumentum below or glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, with a marginal vein, midrib slightly raised on upper surface, secondary veins 11-31 pairs, usually slightly convergent, arcuate, slightly raised on the upper surface, strongly raised below; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries mostly oblique to horizontal. Petiole 1.4-2.5 cm long, shortly pubescent or glabrous. Fascicles axillary or in the axils of fallen leaves, five-many-flowered. Pedicel 5-9 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, 3-4 mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex rounded, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous or scattered appressed puberulous inside. Corolla 4-5 mm long, tube equalling or slightly exceeding the lobes; lobes 5-6, ovate, obtuse, glabrous. Stamens 5-6, fixed at or near the base of the corolla tube; filaments 2.5-3 mm long, geniculate, glabrous; anthers ca. 1 mm long, lanceolate-sagittate, glabrous. Staminodes absent. Ovary broadly ovoid, five-locular, densely strigose; style ca. 2 mm long after anthesis, strigose; style-head simple. Fruit ca. 3 cm long, subglobose, apex obtuse to acute, base truncate or depressed, smooth, glabrous. Seeds several, ca. 2.2 cm long, laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.5-1 mm thick; scar adaxial, extending for most of the length of the seed, ca. 2 mm wide; embryo with thin foliaceous cotyledons and long exserted radicle, surrounded by copious endosperm. Field characters. A large tree, flowering Nov, fruit Jun.

description: Tree; young shoots sparsely appressed pubescent, soon glabrous, greyish brown, rough and cracked, with numerous small lenticels. Leaves spaced, spirally arranged, 5.8-20.2 × 1.3-6.8 cm, usually oblanceolate, less frequently oblong or narrowly elliptic, apex variable, from rounded to narrowly attenuate, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate or acute, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, sparse whitish appressed indumentum on young leaves, soon glabrous; venation usually eucamptodromous, less frequently brochidodromous, often with a marginal vein, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 11-15(-22) pairs, convergent, raised on both surfaces; intersecondaries moderately long, short or absent; tertiaries reticulate, but tending to be parallel with the secondaries. Petiole 0.6-1.7 cm long, slightly channelled, appressed pubescent to glabrous. Fascicles 1-5-flowered, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves. Pedicel 1-2(-3) mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, (1.5-)2-3(-4) mm long, broadly ovate or orbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Corolla 2.5-4 mm long, tube equalling or slightly exceeding the lobes, lobes five, ovate to lanceolate, apex acute or obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed halfway up the corolla tube or in the lower half; filaments 1.25-2 mm long, often geniculate, glabrous; anthers 0.9-1.25 mm long, lanceolate, apex acute or apiculate, glabrous, stamens absent in female flowers. Staminodes absent. Ovary ovoid, conical or short, broad and truncate, 4-5-locular, densely long strigose; style 1-1.75 mm long, glabrous; style-head simple or minutely lobed. Fruit 1.3-2.2 cm, broadly ellipsoid to globose, strongly constricted between the seeds, apex rounded or truncate, apiculate, base rounded, smooth, glabrous. Seeds 1-5, 1.2-1.4 cm long, laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.5-1.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, extending most of the length of the seed, ca. 1 mm wide; embryo with thin foliaceous cotyledons and long exserted radicle, surrounded by copious endosperm. Field characters. Tree to 25 m high and 60 cm diam., but often flowering as a small treelet 1-2 m high. Bark of mature specimen blackish-grey to dark brown, scaly, with white latex. The pale yellowish green leaf colour, so characteristic of dried herbarium material, is also notable in the field. Flowers green or yellowish green, fruit ripening yellow. Flowering throughout the range Sep to Dec, mature fruit May to Dec.

description: Small tree; young growth with dense short stiff spreading and erect pubescence of reddish-golden hairs, becoming glabrous, greyish, rough and fissured, lenticellate. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 4.5-11.5 × 2-4.3 cm, elliptic, oblong-elliptic or oblong, apex obtuse, rounded or acute, base obtuse to narrowly attenuate, margin strongly revolute, upper surface glabrous or with pubescent midrib, lower surface sparsely but uniformly covered with short erect and spreading hairs; venation brochidodromous, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 10-11 pairs, parallel or slightly convergent, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries long; tertiaries parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin, or sometimes slightly reticulate. Petiole 4-7 mm long, not channelled, densely short stiff pubescent. Fascicles 5-10-flowered. Pedicel 0-0.5 mm long, densely stiff pubescent. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five(-seven), ca. 1.5 mm long, lanceolate, apex acute to rounded, densely stiff pubescent outside, appressed puberulous inside. Corolla 4.5-5 mm long, tube 3.25-4 mm long, lobes five, ca. 1 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, sericeous outside, indumentum sometimes confined to base of lobes and tube, glabrous inside. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments 0.2-0.3 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.3-0.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, appressed puberulous; style 0.5-0.6 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head lobed. Fruit 1.1-1.3 cm long, globose or broadly ellipsoid, apex and base rounded, smooth, puberulous. Seed solitary, ca. 1.1 × 0.8 × 0.7 cm, ellipsoid, slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shiny, ca. 0.5 mm thick; scar broad, basi-ventral, about two-thirds the length of the seed; embryo with thinly plano-convex cotyledons and exserted radicle, surrounded by thin endosperm. Field characters. A small tree with yellowish flowers and black fruit. Flowering Oct to Dec, fruit ripening in Feb.

description: Tree; young shoots closely ferruginous-brown tomentose or villose, becoming glabrous, grey-brown, cracked and fissured, with prominent leaf scars, without lenticels. Leaves densely clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 12.5-28 × 7-16, broadly elliptic, apex rounded, base rounded or obtuse, slightly decurrent on the broad petiole, strongly coriaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower surface densely and persistently ferruginous tomentose with short strongly crisped hairs; venation eucamptodromous, with a marginal vein, midrib and secondary veins sunken on the upper surface, very prominent below, secondaries 17-18 pairs, parallel, slightly arcuate or straight; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique, numerous, close, prominent below. Petiole 2-3 cm long, broad, flat and slightly winged, tomentose at first. Ramiflorous, fascicles many-flowered, the flowers subsessile, unisexual (plant dioecious). (Description of flowers and fruit from Aubreville & Pellegrin and Rodrigues (see synonymy above)). Sepals five, 5 mm long, densely villose. Corolla (female) 4 mm long, tube 1.5 mm long, lobes five, 2.5 mm long, ovate; (male) 5 mm long, tube equalling the rounded lobes. Stamens absent in female, (male) five, fixed at the base of corolla tube; filaments ca. 3 mm long; anthers ca. 1 mm long, ovate-lanceolate, apiculate, base cordate, convex, glabrous. Ovary (female) five-locular, hairy; style short; stigma five-lobed. Fruit 3.5-5 cm diam., subglobose, apex depressed, densely rufous-villose, pericarp ca. 7 mm thick, hard-woody, subtended by the accrescent, glabrescent calyx. Seeds five, ca. 1.7-2.2 cm long, 1-1.4 cm broad, 0.7-1.0 cm thick ovoid or ellipsoid, obtuse, testa brown, shining; scar narrowly oblong or linear, ca. 2.0-2.4 cm long, ca. 2-3 mm broad, curved above the base; cotyledons foliaceous, endosperm copious. Field characters. Tree to 25 m high and 40 cm diam. with white latex and discolorous leaves.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Young shoots sparsely appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, pale greyish-white, scaling, without lenticels. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged or subopposite, 10-18 × 3-4.5 cm, oblong-elliptic, apex attenuate, base obtuse, chartaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly raised on upper surface, secondary veins 13-14 pairs, ascending, parallel or slightly convergent, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries oblique. Petiole 1.5-2 cm long, not channelled, glabrous. Flowers unknown. Fruit ca. 3.8 cm long, broadly ellipsoid, apex rounded, apiculate, glabrous, borne on a stalk ca. 1.2 cm long. Seed solitary, ca. 2.5 cm long, ellipsoid, testa smooth, shining; scar adaxial, broad; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons. The fragmentary type specimen is too poor to give any definite leads to the relationships of this species.

description: A genus with three species, one each in the neotropics, tropical Africa and tropical SE-Asia. All species are morphologically closely related and may appear to be geographical vicariants of the same species. A monographic study will likely result in a better understanding of the interrelationships of these taxa. The species of Bryohumbertia were originally described in Campylopus. They differ in their long, relatively straight setae, opercula longer than the urn, the presence of an annulus, smooth cell walls on the inner surface of the peristome teeth and in their laminal cells, that lack a sharp differentiation between basal and upper laminal cells (Frahm, 1982a).

description: Plants to 2.5 cm high, yellowish green, in loose tufts. Stems equally foliate with appressed or erect patent leaves, the fertile plants comose at tips, giving a pencil-like appearance. Leaves 5 mm long, narrow lanceolate, gradually contracted to a long acumen, serrate at tips. Costa filling 1/3 of the leaf base, excurrent, in transverse section with ventral hyalocysts and dorsal groups of stereids, smooth at back. Alar cells reddish, inflated. Basal laminal cells shortly rectangular, ca. 1:1.5-3, incrassate, 6-16 × 13-35 µm, smaller and subquadrate at margins. Upper laminal cells quadrate to short rectangular, 6-13 × 8-20 µm, ca. 2:1.  Seta 5-7 mm long. Capsule upright, symmetric, 1.5 mm long, yellowish to dark brown, furrowed when emptied. Calyptra ciliate at base.

description: Plants to 5 cm high, strongly resembling the common P. gracilis, yellowish or dirty brownish green to blackish. Leaves 4-6 mm long. Costa ending in a long, hyaline hairpoint, short in lower leaves but forming a long, serrate awn in upper, especially in perichaetial leaves, on dorsal side with lamellae 2-4 cells high; end cells of lamellae with thicker outer cell walls. Basal laminal cells thin-walled, hyaline. Upper laminal cells oblique to short oval, incrassate, 6 × 6-9 µm. Seta to 1 cm long. Capsule ca. 2 mm long, cylindric, broader at base. Peristome teeth filiform, split to the base.

description: Leaf blades sparsely to densely puberulent-pubescent adaxially, more so on veins, densely pubescent to pilose abaxially. Crown leaves with blade ovate to elliptic-ovate, 6-22 cm long, 3.5-15 cm wide, length:width ratio 1.5-2:1, the base cordate with basal lobes 1-2.5 cm long. Inflorescence branched, 30-40-flowered, ca. 20 cm long; peduncle 7-13 cm long; pedicels 15-25 mm long, 20-30 mm long in fruit. Calyx radius (4-) 7-10 mm, the lobes (3-)5-8 mm long, 2-6 mm wide, ovate to lanceolate. Corolla radius ca. 1525 mm, the tube (4-)5-7 mm long, the lobes 11-25 mm long, 7-14 mm wide. Fruit ellipsoidal, acute at apex, ca. 2 cm long, 1 cm in diam.; seeds unknown.

description: Plants 3-5 cm high, dirty green to brownish, in dense tufts. Stems equally foliate with loosely patent leaves. Leaves 4-5 mm long, lanceolate, margins entire, slightly canaliculate at tips. Costa filling 1/3 of leaf base, excurrent, the excurrent part slightly serrate, in transverse section with ventral hyalocysts and dorsal groups of stereids. Alar cells large, inflated, hyaline or reddish. Basal laminal cells rectangular, incrassate, slightly pitted, 10-35 × 6-10 µm, at margins shorter and narrower. Upper laminal cells oval, 1:4, 3-6 × 10-26 µm. Sporophyte not known.

description: Dioecious tree 6-20 m tall; bark dark brown, in small plates; trunk reaching to 1 m in diam. Stems glabrous, angled. Leaves paripinnate; distal process early deciduous, rarely developing into a terminal leaflet; leaflets 2, opposite, strongly asymmetrical, one half of blade elliptic, the other oblong, or obovate, 4-11.5 × 2-4.5 cm, chartaceous, glabrous on both surfaces, the abaxial surface sometimes minutely puberulent, the venation brochidodromus, prominent on both surfaces, tertiary venation reticulate, the margins entire, undulate, the apex, obtuse, rounded, less often acute or mucronulate, the base inequilateral, one side obtuse or truncate the other acute or cuneate; petiolules less than 1 mm long, drying dark brown; petioles 1-3 cm long, glabrous, flattened, cuneate, or less often distally winged, narrowing toward the base. Inflorescence a terminal simple or basally branched raceme, 2-4.8 cm long, the axes glabrous, with a few scattered papillae; cataphylls broadly ovate, 1-1.5 mm long; bract triangular or subulate, 0.5-1 mm long, ciliate at margins; pedicels 3-4 mm long, not articulate. Flowers fragrant; calyx 4(-5)-merous, the sepals in 2 unequal pairs, 1.5-2 mm long, greenish, connate at base, ovate, concave, glabrous, ciliate at margins; petals 4(-5), whitish to yellowish, obovate, 2.5-4 mm long, concave, rounded at apex, woolly-pubescent along margins, with a pair of minute (1-1.5 mm long), linear, woolly-pubescent appendages; disc 4-lobed, swollen, glabrous, brownish; stamens 8, spreading, the filaments of unequal lengths, glabrous, 3.5-6 mm long in male flowers, and ca. 1 mm long in female flowers, the anthers elliptic, ca. 0.5 mm long, retuse at apex; ovary glabrous, ovoid, the style 1.5-2 mm long, the stigmas bilobed, papillate. Fruit ellipsoid, light yellow, 2.5-3.3 cm long, the pericarp coriaceous, ca. 1 mm thick, the endocarp woolly-pubescent. Seeds solitary, 1-1.8 cm long, with a yellowish, fleshy, edible fleshy testa. Embryo with erect, or slightly curved, similar-sized cotyledons.

description: Tree 20-25 m tall; trunk reaching 30-40 cm in diam., not buttressed. Branches terete, glabrous. Leaves paripinnate or imparipinnate; distal process acicular, truncate, 2-4 mm long; leaflets (2-) 8-12, opposite to alternate, oblong-elliptic, oblong or oblanceolate, coriaceous, 5.5-11.5 (-16) × 2-4 (-6.5) cm, glabrous, the adaxial surface with prominulous midvein, secondary veins plane or slightly impressed, the abaxial surface glandular-punctate, with prominent midvein and secondary veins, tertiary veins reticulate, the apex rounded, usually retuse and sometimes mucronate, the base attenuate or obtuse, decurrent on to the petiolule; petiolules pulvinate at base, 4-7 mm long; rachis 3-20 cm long, obtusely angled, adaxially bisulcate, abaxially striate, glabrous; petioles 1.7-11 cm long, slightly flattened along adaxial surface, abaxially striate, glabrous, enlarged at base. Thyrses panicle-shaped, 10-40 cm long, terminal or axillary; cataphylls supra-axillary, clustered, acicular, glabrous or puberulent, 2-5 mm long; axes nearly terete, sulcate, puberulent; secondary axes to 20 cm long; bracts and bracteoles subulate, early deciduous; dichasia simple or compound; peduncle 0.5-1 mm long, tomentose; pedicels 0.5-0.7 mm long, tomentulose, articulate at apex. Calyx ca. 2.2 mm long, puberulent on both surfaces, the sepals 1.5-2 mm long, ovate or rounded-ovate, ciliate at margins; petals white, oblong, or elliptic, 4.8-6.2 mm long, abaxially glabrous except for the appressed-pubescent base, adaxially sparsely papillate, the base clawed, the apex rounded, the margins ciliate; appendage as long as the petal, deltate, sometimes bifurcate, abaxially papillate, adaxially sericeous; disc 5-lobed, glabrous, 0.8-1 mm tall; stamens (7) 8, the filaments glabrous, slightly unequal, 1.5-3.3 mm long, the anthers oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 1.2 mm long, apiculate at apex; ovary ovoid to globose, glabrous, the stigma cylindric, papillate. Fruits ellipsoid, to nearly globose, 3.33.7 cm long, orange-yellow or orange when ripe, glabrous, smooth, the pericarp coriaceous, ca. 2 mm thick, endocarp irregularly woolly-pubescent. Seeds solitary, the testa fleshy, brownish. Embryo of 2 nearly equal, erect cotyledons, perpendicular to the radicle, or laying obliquely dorsiventrally over each other.

description: Treelet or tree, with sympodial branching, 2-8 (30) m tall; trunk to 8 (35) cm in diam.; bark grayish to dark brown, smooth or lenticellate. Stems nearly terete, striate, glabrous, becoming lenticellate, sometimes hollow in the center and inhabited by ants. Leaves paripinnate, spirally arranged on distal portion of stem(s); distal process woody, truncate, early deciduous, 2-4 mm long; leaflets (2) 8-16 (32), opposite or alternate, oblong, narrow-oblong, elliptic, narrow-elliptic, obovate, oblanceolate or less often falcate, chartaceous to coriaceous, 14-36(-61) × 3.5-10.4 (-21) cm, flattened or less often bullate, the adaxial surface glabrous, with prominent midvein but impressed secondaries and tertiaries, the abaxial surface glabrous or less often puberulent, with prominent brochidodromus venation, the secondary veins alternate, forming a prominent intramarginal vein, tertiary venation reticulate, the apex long-acuminate or less often obtuse, the base asymmetrical to very strongly asymmetrical, one side obtuse the other cuneate or attenuate, the margins entire or undulate, revolute or slightly so; petiolules enlarged, cylindrical or bulbous (longer than wider), 7-12 mm long, glabrous or puberulous, adaxially canaliculate; rachis glabrous or puberulous, (7.5-) 21-41 cm long, slightly flattened dorsiventrally, sharply angled toward the margins on distal portion, nearly terete on proximal portion; petioles 14-41 (56) cm long, terete, striate, glabrous, less often lenticellate, enlarged at base. Thyrses panicle-shaped, 30-60 cm long, terminal or axillary on distal part of branches; cataphylls acicular, 5-15 mm long, appressed-pubescent; axes slightly angled, striate or sulcate, puberulent to tomentose; bracts and bracteoles deltate, puberulent to tomentose, ca. 0.5 mm long; dichasia compound; peduncle 1-2 mm long; pedicels < 1 mm long, articulate at the middle, with the same indumentum as the axis. Flowers buds angular-ovoid. Calyx 2-3 mm long, light green, puberulent to tomentose, the sepals 1-1.2 mm long, oblong-rounded or ovate, slightly concave; petals white, 4.5-7 mm long, lanceolate or less often oblong, glabrous or adaxially papillate, obtuse or rounded at apex, cuneate at base, the margins usually ciliate on lower portion; appendage as long as the petal or slightly shorter, long deltate, abaxially papillate or less often glabrous, adaxially hirsute above the base; disc 5-lobed, puberulent, tomentose or sparsely hirsute, 0.7-1 mm tall; stamens 5, the filaments of equal length, pilose to glabrous, 2.2-2.5 mm long, slightly flattened, the anthers oblong to lanceolate, 1.3-2.2 mm long, apiculate at apex; ovary tomentose, conical, the stigma elongate-capitate, ferruginous-papillate. Fruits yellow to orange-yellow at maturity, ellipsoid or ovoid-ellipsoid, apiculate, 1.8-3 cm long, glabrescent, minutely rugulate, the pericarp woody, 1-3 mm thick, the endocarp smooth, sparsely tuberculate and sparsely appressed or woolly-pubescent. Seed 1(2) per fruit, ellipsoid, the testa woody, with a thin, fleshy, upper layer. Embryo with cotyledons lying dorsiventrally to obliquely dorsiventrally over each other, both cotyledons of similar size or the lower one larger than the upper one.

description: Tree 7-30(?) m tall; trunk to 140 cm in diam. Stems terete to obtusely angled, puberulent, becoming glabrous and lenticellate with age. Leaves paripinnate or less often imparipinnate; distal process truncate, minute; leaflets (2) 4-6, opposite or alternate, elliptic to lanceolate, or less often oblanceolate, 2.5-10 × 1.2-4.5 cm, coriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces, the venation brochidodromus, the midvein plane or sunken on adaxial surface, prominent on abaxial surface, secondary veins inconspicuous, or less often prominulous on abaxial surface, tertiary veins reticulate, the margins entire or slightly undulate, slightly revolute, the apex acute to long-acuminate, glandular- mucronulate, or less often obtuse, obtusely apiculate, retuse, or nearly rounded, the base rounded, obtuse or acute, sometimes asymmetrical or slightly so; petiolules canaliculate, 2-5 mm long, puberulent or glabrous; rachis 0.7-2.5 cm long, slightly flattened, striate, lenticellate, puberulent; petioles 2-5 cm long, slightly flattened, lenticellate, canaliculate, wider at base. Thyrses paniculate, terminal, to 15 cm long, the branches to 10 cm long; cataphylls lacking; axes angled, sulcate, minutely tomentose; bracts minute, early deciduous, minutely tomentose; dichasia simple, sessile, sometimes reduced to a single flower; pedicels ca. 1.5 mm long, articulate below the middle or at the base. Calyx 2.3-3.2 mm long, tomentose, the sepals free to the base, concave, ovate, obtuse at apex; petals elliptic, 3.2-5.5 mm long, reflexed, woolly-pubescent on lower abaxial surface, adaxially glabrous, ciliate at margins, the apex obtuse, the base tapering; appendages slightly shorter than the petals, elliptic, erect, densely woolly-pubescent adaxially, minutely woolly-pubescent on abaxial surface; disc cup-shaped, 5-lobed, minutely tomentose, ca. 1 mm tall; stamens 8, the filaments of unequal length, 0.8-2 mm long, glabrous, the anthers ca. 1 mm long, elliptic, glabrous, apiculate at apex; ovary nearly conical, tomentose, the stigma obconical, tomentulose, papillate. Fruits ellipsoid, tomentose, 2.2 cm long (immature), green, shortly apiculate at apex, the pericarp 1 mm thick, woody. Seeds ellipsoid, ca. 1.7 cm long, with fleshy testa. Embryo with cotyledons superimposed, of equal size.

description: Perennial, glabrous, cushion-forming herbs. Stems more or less regularly forked and covered with persisting leaves. Leaves regularly, densely, and strictly distichously inserted along the stem, with a wide sheath clasping the leaf above. Blade shorter than the sheath, terete. Inflorescence reduced to a single, lateral, subapical flower. Plants dioecious. Pedicel with 2-4 minute, scariose bracteoles. Tepals lanceolate. Staminate flower long pedicellate; stamens 6, with linear mucronate anthers about 10 times as long as the filaments. Pistillate flower short pedicellate; ovary on a short gynophore; style with filiform, sticky, papillose stigmas. Capsule unilocular, lifted on a gynophore at ripening. Seeds many. The name Distichia refers to the distichous arrangement of the leaves.
bibliographicCitation: Balslev, Henrik. 1996. Juncaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 68: 1-167.

description: Terrestrial shrub from a single arching stem to 4 m tall; seedlings with stems flexuous, finely short white pilose, the leaves elliptic, finely short white pilose on both surfaces; mature branches conspicuously and persistently 5-winged (wings to 3 mm broad), smooth, glabrous, reddish-brown. Leaves elliptic to ovate-elliptic, (8-)l 1 -20(-23) X (4-)7-16(-19) cm, basally cordate and clasping, apically rounded, glabrous; 5(-9)-plinerved from base, nerves red beneath when fresh, midrib and inner l(-2) pairs of lateral nerves conspicuously impressed above and raised beneath, outer 1-2 pairs of lateral nerves inconspicuously and slightly impressed to plane above but raised beneath; veinlets inconspicuous on both surfaces; petioles subterete, ovoid, rugose, 4-5 mm long and 5 mm in diam., glabrous, red when fresh. Inflorescence paniculate, to 850-flowered; primary rachis and lateral branches subterete, glabrous, green when living, primary rachis to 53 cm long and 6 mm in diam., primary lateral branches 20-28 cm long, secondary lateral branches ca. 13 cm long; floral bracts caducous, cucullate, ovate, ca. 6 X 8-9 mm, basally clasping, apically rounded, glabrous, green tinged with red when fresh; pedicels terete, striate, glabrous, 6-7 mm long at anthesis (elongating to 11-12 mm in fruit), ca. 1 mm in diam. but swollen to 1.5 mm at base, green when fresh; bracteoles caducous, similar to the floral bracts but ca. 3 X 4 mm. Flowers: calyx glabrous, 4 mm long, green when fresh; hypanthium cylindric, ca. 1.5 mm long and 4 mm in diam., basally slightly apophysate; limb slightly spreading, ca. 2-2.5 mm long; lobes ovate to hemispheric, apiculate, ca. 0.75 mm long, connivent after anthesis, marginally lacerate-glandular; sinus acute; corolla bottle-shaped, glabrous, 13-14 mm long and 7 mm in diam., purplish-green with the purple pigment restricted to inner (morphologically lower) epidermal surface, lobes triangular, acute, 1.5 mm long, flaring at anthesis, white; stamens 10-11 mm long; filaments very sparsely pilose along margins distally, alternately ca. 2 mm and 2.8-3 mm long; anthers subequal, 8.5-9 mm long; thecae ca. 3 mm long; style ca. 12 mm long. Berry ca. 13 mm in diam.

description: Tree to 15 m; young branchlets laxly and minutely tomentellous, to 2 mm diam., glabrescent; terminal bud slender, tomentellous, to 1 cm long. Leaves evenly distributed along branchlets, subcoriaceous, elliptic or (ovate-)lanceolate, 2-3 times longer than wide, 8-18 x 3-7 cm wide, obtuse or acute, sometimes angustate at base, apex acute or acuminate (acumen to 2 cm long), glabrous above, provided with simple, appressed, minute, caducous hairs along midrib and venation beneath, nerves 5-7 on each side, arcuately ascending, flat or slightly impressed above, prominulous beneath, reticulate veins perceptible above, slightly prominent beneath, margin slightly revolute at base of blade; petioles tomentellous, soon glabrescent, deeply canaliculate, 0.8-1.2 cm long. Panicles subterminal, ± solitary, in axils of deciduous bracts or of persistent leaves, slightly tomentellous, few-flowered, to 6 cm long. Flowers sparsely pubescent, 2-2.5 x 1.5 mm; floral tube sericeous inside; pedicels 1-2 mm long; tepals erect, inside at base strigulose, at margin ciliate, outer ones broadly ovate, 0.7 mm long, inner ones ovate, 0.9 mm long; stamens about 1 mm long, those of ser. I and II with broad anthers, large introrse/latrorse cells, slightly protruding, papillose connectives, and pilose filaments narrower than anthers, of ser. III with glabrous anthers and pilose, biglandulate filaments as wide as anthers; staminodes stipitiform, hairy, 0.4 mm long, or absent; pistil 2.2 mm long, glabrous; style as long as ovary; stigma oblique, minute. Berry (immature) ellipsoid, 1.2 x 1 cm; cupule cyathiform, 1 x 1.5 cm, outside verruculous.

description: Scandent herb, at least 1 m long, sometimes ascending and 0.3-1 m tall; stems and peduncles pilose or villous with white glandular hairs. Leaves with blades triangular, (3.6-)4.5-13 x 2.5-7.2 (-9) cm, acute, cordate at base, the margins ciliate, biserrate or lobulate-serrate; upper surface bright green, pilose; lower surface pale or grayish-green, pilose (at least on major veins); petioles with the margins entire or dentate and almost parallel (i.e., petiolar lamina not tapering towards the distal end), widened only just around the stem, (1.5-)2.5-7.6 cm long, 1-4 cm wide at base, 0.4-1.5 cm at the distal end. Inflorescence intercalary (rarely appearing distal due to poor development of the terminal leafy shoot), composed of 2-4 pairs of (4-)8-24-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles (2.5-)5.2-14 cm long; pedicels 0.9-2.6 cm, villous or tomentose with glandular hairs of different lengths; cyme bracts usually absent, sometimes present in the lower most cyme pair (then rudimentary and up to 2.4 x 1.2 cm), subordinate bracts always absent. Sepals ovate to lanceolate, light green to yellowish-green, acute or acuminate, 4.7-7 x 1.8-5.1 mm at anthesis, pilose or puberulous with glandular hairs on both sides, the margins entire or denticulate. Corolla type XI, bright yellow, unspotted; upper lip 3-4 x 4-5 mm; lower lip somewhat flattened, 9-12 x 6-10 mm, saccate in ca. 60% of length; elaiophore present, the elaiophore-bearing lobe straight, not infolded, protrading into the orifice, closing the orifice and exposing the elaiophore just below the anthers. Stamens type 1; anthers yellowish-white to huffish, glabrous, 1.5-2.4 mm, the thecae divaricate or slightly ascending, equal; filaments 1.3-2.2 mm. Style curved, 1.5-3.4 mm. Capsule ovoid, 4-6 mm long, shortly glandular-puberalous.

description: Herba ascendens vel scandens, caulibus 1-2 m, villosis vel hirsutis, pilis albis. Folia decussata, petiolata; lamina herbacea, ovata, 4.5-7.3 x 3.6-4.7 cm, acuta, ad basin cordata et ± dimidiata, marginibus biserratis, supra pilosa, infra reticulato-venosa, venis pilosis vel hirsutis, inter-stitiis glabris, glanduloso-papillosis; petioli villosi, 1-1.5 cm longi. Inflorescentia terminalis, singula paria cymarum 8-16 florum complectens; pedunculis primariis 3.7-12 cm longis; bracteae cymarum adsunt. Sepala ovata, acuta, 8.5-10 x 6-7.4 mm sub anthesi, extra pilosa vel villosa, intra glanduloso-puberulosa, marginibus inte-gris. Corolla vivide flava, punctis rubris in fauce obsita, labio inferiore 20-25 x 15-20 mm; elaeophorus adest. Antherae bubalinae, glabrae, 4.2-4.6 mm, distaliter dehiscentes; thecae subaequans, divaricatae vel leviter deflexae. Stylus rectus vel arcuatus, 3.9-5.5 mm. Capsula ovoides, glanduloso-puberulosa, 5-7 mm longa.

description: Ascending or scandent herb, the stems at least 1-2 m long; inflorescence and distal parts of stems villous or hirsute with white hairs. Leaves with blades herbaceous, ovate, 4.5-7.3 x 3.6-4.7 cm, acute, cordate and ± dimidiate at base, the margins deeply biserrate, the teeth somewhat rounded; upper surface bright green, pilose, slightly flexuose; lower surface slightly paler green, pinnate-venose or coarsely reticulate-venose, the veins hirsute or pilose with white hairs, interspaces glabrous, sparsely beset with minute stalked glands; petioles 1-1.5 cm, villous. Inflorescence composed of a single pair of 8-16-flow-ered cymes, the primary peduncles 3.7-12 cm, the pedicels 1.3-2.5 cm. Sepals ovate, bright green, 8.5-10 x 6-7.4 mm at anthesis, acute, externally short-pilose to villous, internally glandular-puberulous, the margins entire, densely ciliate with glandular hairs. Corolla type I, bright yellow, the throat internally deep yellow and provided with a transverse zone of red dots; upper lip 5-6 mm long and wide; lower lip 20-25 x 15-20 mm, saccate in 65-75% of length, slightly sigmoid, inflated distally; elaiophore present. Stamens type 10; anthers yellow-brown, glabrous, 4.2-4.6 mm, dehiscing distally, the thecae subequal, straight or slightly sigmoid, divaricate or somewhat ascending; filaments 2.2-2.6 mm. Style 3.9-5.5 mm, straight to arcuate, decurved at apex. Capsule ovoid, purplish, 5-7 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Erect herb, 2-20 cm tall; stems and inflorescence purple, pilose or villous with glandular hairs. Leaves short-petiolate; blades ovate, 1.2-3.2 x 0.8-1.4 cm, acute, rounded to cuneate at base, the margins entire, pilose with coarse white hairs on both sides; petioles 2-5 mm, glandular-hirsute. Inflorescence with pedicels 0.8-1.5 cm, sigmoid in late anthesis, peduncles sometimes present, up to 6.4 cm long. Sepals triangular, light green with purplish margins, 2.8-3.5 x 1.2-2.2 mm at anthesis, acute, externally glandular-hirsute, internally glabrous, the margins entire. Corolla type X, light yellow above, yellowish-white below, usually with two red dots in the throat just below the stamens; upper lip arched, 1.5-3 mm wide and long; lower lip 6-8 x 4-6 mm, saccate in 80-90% of length; elaiophore rudimentary, probably non-functional. Stamens with anthers huffish to yellowish-white, 0.5-1.2 mm long; filaments 0.8-1.2 mm. Style straight, 0.8-1.2 mm, the stigma capitate. Capsule semi-inferior, conical to ellipsoid, 6-8 mm long, glandular-hirsute.

description: Low shrubby plant, 0.2-0.5 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems reddish-brown, shortly glandular-hirsute with white hairs (seemingly farinose). Leaves decussate, shortly but distinctly petiolate; blades coriaceous, obovate to oblanceolate, 8-15 x 4-7 mm, obtuse, cuneate at base, the margins deflexed, entire in the proximal half, distally grossly serrate or few-dentate; upper surface dark green, glandular-puberulous or papillose; lower surface pale green, pinnate-venose to almost hyphodromous, glandular-puberulous; petioles 3-5 mm, glandular-puberulous, dilated at base. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 1- or 2-flowered cymes, the peduncles 0.8-2.5 cm, the pedicels 1.5-3 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals light green to yellow green, 4.5-5.5 x 3.7-4.3 mm at anthesis, acuminate, externally glandular-puberulous, internally glabrous, the margins entire. Corolla type II, bright yellow or lemon yellow, internally with red-brown spots in the throat; upper lip subglobose, 4-5 mm long and wide; lower lip 17-19 x 11-13 mm, saccate in 60-70% of length, elaiophore present. Stamens type 9; anthers yellowish-white, 4.5-4.8 mm, the thecae unequal, dehiscing distally in 70-80% of their length; filaments l.2-1.5 mm. Style curved, 2.2-2.8 mm. Capsule ovoid, 6-9 mm long, acuminate, the neck slightly curved, shortly glandular-hirsute.

description: Scandent or ascending shrub, 0.4-1.5 m tall, sometimes climbing up to 4.5 m, the branches divaricate or ascending; inflorescence and distal parts of stems puberulous. Leaves with blades lanceolate or almost linear, subcoriaceous, 3.2-8.9 x 0.4-1.2 cm, acute, cuneate or attenuate at base, the margins entire or denticulate, revolute; upper surface olive to dark green, strongly glutinous, sparsely puberulous, the midrib sunken; lower surface very pale green, hyphodromous or pinnate-venose, the veins puberulous or strigose, other tissue sparsely puberulous; petioles ill-defined, 2-4 mm long, canaliculate with the margins puberulous. Inflorescence distal, composed of 3-4 pairs of 4-8-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.5-5.1 cm, the pedicels 1.2-2.4 cm; cyme bracts present, conspicuous, the blades ovate, greenish-yellow, 0.9-2.5 x 0.5-1.2 cm, glabrous or minutely puberulous, the petioles 13 mm. Sepals somewhat unequal, greenish-yellow, ovate, acuminate or caudate, (6.5-) 1013 x (4.3-)7.5-7.9 mm at anthesis, externally minutely puberulous, internally puberulous towards the margins, otherwise glabrous. Corolla type I, bright yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 35 x 4-7 mm, the lower lip 17-25 x 12-20 mm, saccate in 50-60% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 11; anthers pale brown, glabrous, (3.7-)4.3-5.1 mm, the thecae divaricate, unequal in size; filaments 1.2-1.7 mm. Style curved distally, 3.2-5 mm. Capsule broadly ovoid, yellow-brown, 5-7 mm long, short-hirsute. 2n = 36 (Molau & Öhman 1631, new record).

description: Lax, scandent shrub, 0.7-1.5 m tall, the branches divaricate; inflorescence and distal parts of stems puberulous to tomentose with whitish hairs. Leaves with blades herbaceous, lanceolate, 2-7.8 x 0.6-3.4 cm, attenuate at apex, cuneate or rounded at base, the margins serrate; upper surface deep green, smooth or slightly rugose, puberulous; lower surface bright green, pinnate-or reticulate-venose, the veins white-tomentose, interspaces glabrous, orange-glandular; petioles short-villous, 2-8 mm. Inflorescence distal, composed of 2 or 3 pairs of 4-8(-16)-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.1-5.2 cm, the pedicels 0.6-1.9 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals unequal, ovate, acute or slightly acuminate, externally olivaceous, puberulous, internally bright yellow-green, puberulous and with a short-tomentose border along the margins; dorsal sepal 3-4.5 x 2.5-3.8 mm at anthesis. Corolla type XI, lemon-yellow, usually with reddish spots in the throat; upper lip 2-4 x 3-5 mm, subglobose; lower lip 7-12 x 5-7 mm, obovate, flattened, distally shallowly 3-lobate; elaiophore present. Stamens with anthers 3.4-5 mm, the thecae equal or subequal, 0.4-1 mm, separated by an elongated yellow or yellow-brown connective, its arms divaricate; filaments 0.5-1 mm. Style 2.8-4.1 mm, curved at apex, otherwise almost straight. Capsule narrowly conic, slightly acuminate, yellow-brown, 3-6 mm long, sparsely glandular-puberulous.

description: Ascending herb, 0.5-1 m tall; stems and peduncles glandular-puberulous, sometimes also pilose with white glandless hairs. Leaves with blades ovate-triangular, 3-6 x 2.5-4.8 cm, acute or acuminate at apex, cuneate to slightly cordate at base, the margins irregularly sharp-serrate or -biserrate with coarse teeth; upper surface deep green, pilose or villous with white hairs; lower surface paler, the veins raised, villous, the interspaces pilose to villous with white hairs, some of which are gland-tipped; petioles 1.5-2.2 cm long, 1.8-3.7 cm wide at base, 0.5-2.8 cm at the distal end, the margins regularly sharp-serrate. Inflorescence intercalary, composed of one or two pairs of 6-16-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 3.3-15 cm long; cyme bracts 1.5-3 x 0.6-1.8 cm, subordinate bracts smaller, rudimentary, or absent; pedicels 1.2-3.5 cm, glandular-puberulous and pilose to villous with white spreading hairs. Sepals lanceolate, yellow-green, acuminate, caudate, 8.5-13 x 4-7.2 mm at anthesis, externally pilose, internally puberulous, the margins ciliate, entire or sparsely denticulate. Corolla type I, light to bright yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 6-7 x 8-11 mm, the lower lip 18-25 x 11-17 mm, saccate in 65-70% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 7; anthers pale or light brown, glabrous, 3.8-4.3 mm, dehiscing throughout, the thecae divaricate, flaring at maturity, slightly arcuate, unequal; filaments 2-2.5 mm. Style 5.5-7.5 mm, curved at apex. Capsule ovoid, 5-6 mm long, villous.

description: Erect or ascending subshrub or shrub, 0.2-1 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems glandular-hirsute (glands brownish). Leaves decussate, sessile; blades herbaceous, ovate to triangular, 2.5-4.7 x 1.2-2.8 cm, acute, cordate at base, the margins sharp-serrate to deeply crenate; upper surface olive green, flexuose, shortly glandular-hirsute; lower surface pale green, pinnate-venose, glandular-hirsute. Inflorescence composed of 1-3 pairs of 4-20-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 0.9-4.4 cm; pedicels 0.5-1.6 cm; cyme bracts absent. Sepals olivaceous, 4-5.2 x 2.8-3.9 mm, acute, glandular-papillose to glandular-hirsute on both sides, most densely so externally, the margins entire. Corolla type II, unspotted; upper lip lemon yellow, 3-5 x 4-6 mm; lower lip 12-17 x 7-12 mm, lemon yellow at base, otherwise bright red to brownish-red, internally orange, saccate in 50-60% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 9; anthers 34 mm, buff or yellowish-white, the thecae equal, dehiscing to the connective, divaricate (though slightly deflexed at ends); filaments 1.5-2.2 mm. Style 1.9-2.5 mm, distally decurved. Capsule ovoid, 5-7 mm long, slightly acuminate, shortly glandular-hirsute. 2n = 36 (Srinath, 1939: 116, Straw in Löve, 1970: 268).

description: Ascending or scandent herb, 0.5-2 m tall, much branched, the stems ± woody below; inflorescence and distal parts of stems pilose or villous with white, gland-tipped hairs. Leaves with blades herbaceous, ovate, 2-7 x 1.7-6.6 cm, acute, truncate or slightly cordate at base and usually ± attenuate at end of petiole, the margins lobulate or coarsely biserrate; upper surface dull green, smooth, pilose; lower surface pale green, reticulate-venose, pilose, glandular; petioles 0.7-3 cm, glandular-villous, dilated at base and connate across the nodes with thin flaps 2-10 mm wide at each side of the stem. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 12-44-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 3.2-7.4 cm, the pedicels 0.5-1.7 cm. Sepals green, ovate or lanceolate, 3.4-4.7 x 1.6-2.5 mm at anthesis, acute, externally pilose and glandular-puberulous, internally with regularly dispersed stalked glands, the margins entire, densely glandular-puberulous. Corolla type XII, bright yellow above, whitish below, with many red spots in the throat; upper lip ca. 2 x 3 mm; lower lip 9-12 x 6-8 mm, saccate in 4050% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers pale buff to yellowish-white, glabrous, 2-2.5 mm, dehiscing throughout, the thecae equal, divaricate; filaments 1-1.6 mm. Style 1.6-2.2 mm, somewhat decurved distally. Capsule ovoid, 4-5 mm long, glandular-puberulous. 2n = 36 (Molau & Öhman 1808, new record).

description: Erect or ascending shrub, 0.5-1 (-3) m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems tomentose or short-villous with brownish hairs. Leaves with blades ovate or lanceolate, 3.5-7 x 1.2-1.8 cm, acute, cuneate at base, glabrous, the margins serrate; upper surface dark green, glutinous, slightly flexuose to almost smooth; lower surface whitish-green, pinnate-venose, completely glabrous; petioles 3-8 mm, dorsally tomentose. Inflorescence composed of 1 or 2 pairs of 4-6-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.3-4 cm, the pedicels 1.2-3 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals pale green (turning red in full exposure), ovate, acute or subacute, 4-6.2 x 2.5-3.5 mm at anthesis, externally glabrous, internally with a short-tomentose border along the margins. Corolla type XIV, bright yellow, the upper lip 5-10 mm high and 7-13 mm wide, the lower lip 11-18 x 6-14 mm, saccate in 30-40% of length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 5; anthers dark brown, 2-3.8 mm, glabrous, the thecae deflexed, equal, each one 1.5-2.5 mm long; filaments 1.5-2 mm. Style 3.8-5.2 mm, straight or slightly curved. Capsule ovoid, brown, 4-5 mm long, glabrous, glutinous. 2n = 36 (Molau & Öhman 1440, new record).

description: Herb or low subshrub, 0.2-0.6 m tall, ascending; inflorescence and distal parts of stems purplish and glandular-hirsute. Leaves with blades herbaceous, ovate or almost circular, ± aceri-form, 1.3—5(—6.9) x l-4.2(-6) cm, obtuse to acute at apex, cuneate to truncate (rarely slightly cordate) at base, deeply lobate with 2-6 lobes on each side of blade, the lobes entire to serrate; upper surface bright or deep green, glandular-pilose to glandular-hirsute, somewhat flexuose; lower surface pale green, pinnate-venose, the major veins glandular-hirsute, interspaces glandular-hirsute to sparsely glandular-pilose; petioles 1.1-3.5 cm, glandular-hirsute. Inflorescence composed of l(-2) pairs of (4-)12-3 2-flowered cymes (sometimes only one of the cymes of the terminal pair developed); primary peduncles 2.2-11(-18) cm; pedicels 1.1-4(-5.1) cm. Sepals ovate, dull green, 3.1-5.3(-7.8) x 2-4.7 mm at anthesis, obtuse (acute in dept. Cajamarca), externally hirsute or villous with glandular hairs, internally puberulous or short-hirsute with glandular hairs, the margins entire. Corolla type III; upper lip light greenish-yellow, 2-4 x 3-5 mm; lower lip pale yellow to light yellow, internally with red or purple dots in the sides of the throat (absent in shady sites), saccate in 30-40% of length, the upcurved portion 10-18 x 7-14 mm, the neck 2-4 mm wide at base; elaiophore present. Stamens close to type 5; anthers yellow-orange, minutely glandular, 1-1.6 mm across, not dehiscing through the connective, the thecae unequal, sharply deflexed, the anterior theca ± reduced, often sterile and vestigial, 1-1.8 mm long, the posterior theca normally developed, 1.7-2.7 mm long; filaments 1.7-2.8 mm. Style 2-3.2 mm, arcuate or decurved at apex. Capsule ovoid or conic, 5-7 mm long, slightly acuminate, glandular-hirsute, purplish. 2n = 36 (Molau et al. 434, new record).

description: Scandent herb, 0.5-5 m long; stems and inflorescence pilose to villous with coarse, buffish to purplish hairs. Leaves with blades triangular or triangular-ovate, 3.3-12 x 2.4-7.5 cm, acute, cordate to truncate at base (sometimes slightly cuneate in Colombian specimens), the margins biserrate with acute to obtuse teeth; upper surface deep green, white-pilose; lower surface pale green, rarely purplish tinged, pilose to villous (sometimes almost lanate) with coarse whitish hairs; petioles 1.5-5.7 cm long, 1.2-5.2 cm wide at base, 0.5-1.6(-2.8) cm wide at the distal end, the margins entire or serrate. Inflorescence intercalary, composed of 1-4 pairs of 4-24-flow-ered cymes, the primary peduncles 4.8-17 cm long, the pedicels 1-5 cm; cyme bracts 1.2-9.2 x 1.1-5.4 cm, subordinate bracts usually absent. Sepals ovate, yellow-green to almost pure yellow, 6-14 x 5.3-11 mm at anthesis, acuminate or slightly caudate, externally pilose to tomentose, internally puberulous, the margins entire or (rarely) sparsely denticulate, ciliate. Corolla type VI, bright yellow, unspotted; upper lip 5-9 x 712 mm; lower lip 11-18 x 10-18 mm, saccate in 40-60% of length; elaiophore normally absent (present but ± rudimentary in S Ecuador, see below). Stamens type 6; anthers dark brown to blackish-brown, glabrous, horseshoe-shaped, dehiscing throughout, 2.4-4 mm across, the thecae deflexed, bean-shaped, subequal, 1.9-3 mm long; filaments 1.2-2 mm. Style 5-7.2 mm, somewhat decurved at apex. Capsule ovoid, 5-7 mm long, pilose to villous. 2n = 36 (Molau & Öhman 1205, new record).

description: Chasmophyte; caespitose subshrub, forming dense carpets, the stems decumbent, woody at base, distally pilose with long, coarse, white hairs, the internodes much reduced. Leaves oblanceolate to spathulate, 5-11 x 2-5 mm, obtuse or subacute, attenuate at base, the margins entire, not revolute; upper surface deep to olive green, smooth, hirsute with long, ascending, white hairs; lower surface pale green, hyphodromous, pilose; petioles indistinct, 5-9 mm, pilose. Inflorescence reduced to 1-8 short, axillary pedicels in the shoot apex, representing ½-4 pairs of cymes; pedicels 3-7 mm, pilose. Sepals subequal, lanceolate, green, 2.5-4.7 x 1-2.2 mm, subacute, externally pilose or hispid with long, ascending, coarse, white hairs, internally glabrous. Corolla close to type VI, light yellow, unspotted, the upper lip almost white, glabrous, 2-4 x 3-4 mm, the lower lip ellipsoid, densely glandular-papillose, 6-10 x 34 mm, saccate in 50-70% of length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 1 or 5 (the thecae ± deflexed); anthers 1.2-1.8 mm, purple, glabrous; filaments 0.4-0.8 mm. Style slender, straight or slightly arcuate, glabrous, 3.5-5.8 mm. Capsule subglobose, 2-3 mm long, glandular-puberulous, few-seeded (often 4-seeded). Seeds densely tuberculate (colliculate). n = 18 (Molau et al. 1695).

description: Stout herb, usually erect, 0.4-1.5(-2) m tall; stems and peduncles densely villous or hirsute with spreading, brownish-white hairs, at least some of which are gland-tipped. Leaves with blades triangular to triangular-ovate, 7-20 x 515 cm, acute, cordate at base, the margins lobulate and irregularly biserrate; upper surface olive to dark green, pilose to hirsute with coarse brownish-white hairs; lower surface dull green, pilose to hirsute; petioles 4-13 cm long, 2-6.2 cm wide at base, 0.5-2.1 cm at the distal end, the margins irregularly dentate. Inflorescence distal, composed of 1-5 pairs of 4-20(-32)-flowered cymes on primary peduncles 3.2-19 cm long; cyme bracts 2.7-5.8 x 1-3.1 cm, subordinate bracts absent; pedicels 1.4-5 cm, hirsute or villous with glandular hairs. Sepals pale green, ovate to lanceolate, 11-17 x 5-14 mm at anthesis, acuminate and ± caudate, externally pilose or hirsute with glandular hairs, internally puberulous or pilose with glandular hairs, the margins ciliate, entire or denticulate. Corolla type I, light yellow to sulphur yellow, unspotted (Peru S of the Piura Divide) or with a broad purple crossband in the throat (Ecuador and northernmost Peru); upper lip 5-7 x 5-9 mm; lower lip lb-25 x 11—16 mm, saccate in 60-75% of its length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 10; anthers yellowish-white to brownish, glabrous, 4.8-6.8 mm, the thecae unequal, ascending; filaments 1.1-2.2 mm. Style decurved at apex, otherwise straight, 3.6-6.1 mm. Capsule ovoid, 5-9 mm long, shortly glandular-hirsute. 2n = 36 (Srinath, 1939: 106, without voucher).

description: Erect or ascending subshrub, 0.15-1 m tall, the stems and inflorescence glandular-puberulous. Leaves sessile or indistinctly petiolate with winged petioles to 0.7 cm long; blades herbaceous, ovate to lanceolate, 2.3-5.6 x 1.3-2.6 cm, acute or subacute, truncate or broadly cuneate at base, the margins bicrenate to lobulate-serrate; upper surface deep green, deeply rugose to bullate, glandular-puberulous, strongly glutinous; lower surface light green, reticulate-venose, villous or hirsute with glandular hairs. Inflorescence composed of 2-4 pairs of 6-12-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 0.6-1.5 cm long; cyme bracts small (rarely absent); pedicels 0.6-1.8 cm. Sepals yellow or greenish-yellow, obtuse, 2.7-3.8 x 2-3.1 mm at anthesis, glandular-puberulous on both sides, the margins entire. Corolla type VI, bright yellow, unspotted or with a few red spots in the throat; upper lip 2-3 mm long and wide; lower lip 8-11 x 5-7 mm, saccate in 40-50% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers tight brown to pale yellow, glabrous, 1.5-2.8 mm, the thecae divaricate; filaments 1.3-2.5 mm. Style almost straight, 1.5-2 mm. Capsule conic, 5-7 mm long, glandular-papillose, glutinous.

description: Ascending shrub, 0.3-1 m tall, much branched; stems and inflorescence glabrous. Leaves with blades ovate or lanceolate, 3.2-8 x 1.5-2.7 cm, acuminate, cuneate and ± dimidiate at base, glabrous, the upper surface dark green, glutinous, slightly flexuose, the lower surface whitish-green, pinnate-venose, the margins serrulate; petioles glabrous, 7-18 mm. Inflorescence composed of 2 or 3 pairs of 4-10-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 2-3.2 cm, the pedicels 0.9-2.8 cm; cyme bracts absent or present. Sepals light green, ovate, acute or subacute, 4.2-5.7 x 3-4.8 mm at anthesis, externally glabrous, internally with a short-tomentose border along the margins. Corolla type XIV, bright yellow, the upper lip 6-10 mm high and 8-11 mm wide, the lower lip 10-18 x 7-13 mm, saccate in 30-40% of length, elaiophore absent. Stamens type 6, the thecae slightly deflexed; anthers dark brown, 2.5-3.2 mm, glabrous, the thecae equal; filaments 1.3-2 mm. Style almost straight, 3-4.5 mm. Capsule ovoid, brown, 4-5 mm long, glabrous.

description: Erect or ascending shrub or subshrub, 0.4-1 m tall, the whole plant glabrous and strongly glutinous. Leaves subsessile or ill-defined petiolate; blades coriaceous, ± fasciculate, narrowly elliptic, 2.7-4 x 0.5-1 cm, subacute or obtuse, attenuate or cuneate at base, the margins ± entire, revolute; upper surface dark green, almost smooth; lower surface greenish-white, hypho-dromous; petioles ill-defined, 2-5 mm. Inflorescence composed of 1 or 2 pairs of 2-4-flowered cymes, often ± diffuse; peduncles 0.5-1.3 cm, pedicels 0.8-2 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals ovate, light yellow-green, 7-9 x 5.5-7 mm at anthesis, acute or slightly acuminate, glabrous. Corolla probably type VII, lemon yellow or bright yellow; upper lip arched, ca. 5 x 5 mm; lower lip projecting, distally upcurved, 16-18 x 11-13 mm, saccate in about 50% of length; elaio-phore present. Stamens type 1 or 5 (thecae slightly deflexed); anthers yellowish-white, 2.2-2.4 mm, glabrous, the thecae equal; filaments 1-1.5 mm. Style straight, ca. 2 mm. Capsule narrowly ovoid, slightly acuminate, ca. 7 mm long, glabrous.

description: Frutex erectus, 0.3-1 m altus, caulibus oliva-ceis, breviter glanduloso-tomentosis. Folia decussata, petiolata; lamina coriacea, ovata, 5.3-7.7 x 2.3-3.2 cm, acuta vel leviter acuminata, ad basin rotundata vel truncata, supra olivacea, tomentosa et glandulosa, infra pinnato-venosa, puberulosa et glandulis obsita, marginibus in-tegris vel crenulatis; Petioli glanduloso-tomen-tosi, 8-17 mm longi. Inflorescentia terminalis, singula paria cymarum (1-)6-8 florum complectens; pedunculis primariis 3.2-7 cm longis; brac-teae cymarum adsunt. Sepala ovata, acuta, 7.510 x 5.4-6.4 mm sub anthesi, extra breviter tomentosa, intra glabra praeter limbum breviter tomentosum secus margines, marginibus inte-gris. Corolla vivide flava, immaculata, labio superiore arcuato, 8-10 x 10-13 mm, labio in-feriore ascendente, 15-22 x 11-15 mm; elaeo-phorus adest. Antherae fuscae, glabrae 1.9-2.6 mm, totae dehiscentes; thecae divaricatae vel leviter deflexae. Stylus arcuatus, 2.2-2.8 mm. Capsula ovoides, glanduloso-tomentosa, 5-8 mm longa.

description: Erect shrub, 0.3-1 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems tomentose with short, glandular, olivaceous hairs. Leaves with blades coriaceous, ovate, 5.3-7.7 x 2.3-3.2 cm, acute or slightly acuminate, rounded or truncate at base, the margins entire or slightly crenulate, deflexed; upper surface bright olive green, smooth, matt, densely short-tomentose and beset with sessile orange glands; lower surface pale olivaceous, pinnate-venose, gland-dotted and glandular-puber-ulous; petioles 8-17 mm, shortly glandular-to-mentose. Inflorescence composed of a single pair of (1-)6-8-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 3.2-7 cm, the pedicels 1.3-2.8 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals yellow green, ovate, 7.510 x 5.4-6.4 mm at anthesis, acute, entire, externally densely short-tomentose, internally glabrous except for a short-tomentose border along the margins. Corolla type IV, bright yellow, fragrant, unspotted; upper lip subcircular, frontally flattened, 8-10 mm high and 10-13 mm wide; lower lip subglobose, saccate in 50-70% of length, the upcurved portion 15-22 x 11-15 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1 (or almost 5); anthers light brown, 1.9-2.6 mm, glabrous; the thecae equal, divaricate or slightly deflexed; filaments 0.6-1.0 mm. Style curved, 2.2-2.8 mm. Capsule widely ovoid, brownish, 5-8 mm long, shortly glandular-tomentose.

description: Ascending or scandent subshrub, 0.5-1.5 m tall; stems and inflorescence glabrous. Leaves sessile; blades subcoriaceous, 5-10 x 1.6-2.3 cm, acute at apex, cordate and connate at base, the margins regularly serrate with mucronulate teeth; upper surface bright green, glabrous, rugose, ± glutinous; lower surface light green, reticulate venose, the veins glandular-pilose, interspaces glabrous. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 8-20-flowered cymes on primary peduncles 1.7-6.5 cm long; cyme bracts present at least in the lower cyme pair; pedicels 0.9-1.7 cm, puberulous, glandular. Sepals green, triangular to lanceolate, 3.2-3.8 x 2-3.3 mm at anthesis, slightly acuminate, externally glabrous and glutinous. Corolla type XIV, bright yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 5-8 mm high and 7-12 mm wide, the lower lip 10-19 x 10-16 mm, saccate in 40-50% of length; elaiophore present (though probably non-functional with regard to pollination). Stamens type 1 (but with the thecae slightly deflexed); anthers 2.7-3.8 mm, chestnut to dark brown, glandular at base; filaments 1.5-2.2 mm. Style almost straight, 3.1-4.2 mm. Capsule ovoid, 4-5 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Ascending, ± densely tufted herb, 0.3-1 mtall, the stems and inflorescence villous with white hairs. Leaves with blades herbaceous, ovate to almost circular, 1-2.6 x 0.8-2.1 cm, obtuse, cordate or truncate at base, the margins crenate or 5-9-lobulate (then lobes entire), deflexed or slightly revolute; upper surface bright green, pilose to hispid, rugose; lower surface pale green or whitish-green, villous or lanate with white hairs, reticulate-venose; petioles 5-15 mm, villous. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 2-8-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles l.8-14 cm, the pedicels 0.9-4(-5.8) cm. Sepals ovate, pale green, 6.5-10 x 4.5-6 mm at anthesis, acute, externally villous, internally glandular-puberulous, the margins entire. Corolla type I, light yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 5-7 x 46 mm, the lower lip 15-23 x 11-18 mm, saccate in 50-70% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 11; anthers yellowish-white, glabrous, 4-4.5 mm, dehiscing distally, the thecae equal or subequal, divaricate or slightly ascending; filaments 1.2-1.8 mm. Style 4-5.8 mm, decurved at apex. Capsule ovoid, 6-8 mm long, glandular-pilose. 2n = 36 (Løjtnant & Molau 14914).

description: Ascending herb, 0.2-0.6 m tall; stems and inflorescence pilose to hirsute or villous with coarse, ± undulate, pale brownish hairs. Leaves sessile or indistinctly short-petiolate; blades herbaceous, ovate, 3.8-8.4 x 2.4-4.3 cm, acute or subacute, cuneate to truncate or even slightly cordate at base, the margins coarsely serrate or crenate; upper surface deep green, flexuose, pilose; lower surface pale green, predominantly pinnate-venose, the veins hirsute, interspaces sparsely pilose; petioles 0-6 mm, hirsute. Inflorescence composed of a single 6-8-flowered cyme (the other cyme of the pair inhibited); primary peduncle 4.2-15 cm long, the pedicels 0.6-1.8 cm; cyme bracts absent. Sepals olivaceous, ovate, 3.2-4.8 x 2-3.4 mm at anthesis, acute or subacute, ± mucronate, externally coarsely short-pilose, internally puberulous proximally, otherwise glabrous, the margins entire, long-ciliate. Corolla type XI, pale yellow, unspotted or with red dots in the throat, externally glandular-puberulous; upper lip arched, 3-5 x 5-9 mm; lower lip flattened, ovate, projecting, (7-) 15-21 x (5-)9-16 mm, saccate in 70-80% of length, dorsally with a glandular-tomentose area just below the orifice; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers dark brown (purplish tinged?), glabrous, 1.9-2.6 mm, the thecae equal, slightly deflexed; filaments 1-1.5 mm. Style 1.5-1.7 mm, straight, the stigma capitate. Capsule ovoid, purplish-brown, 5-6 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Erect or ascending shrub, 0.3-1.5 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems shortly white-tomentose. Leaves decussate, somewhat fasciculate; blades subcoriaceous, ovate, 6-12 x 3-7 mm, obtuse or subacute at apex, rounded or truncate at base, the margins crenate or bluntly serrate with 6-11 teeth on each side of blade, revolute; upper surface bright green, flexuose, short-hirsute; lower surface whitish-green, pinnate-venose, shortly white-tomentose and with sessile hyaline glands; petioles 1-3 mm, villous. Inflorescence composed of (2)3-5 pairs of (1-)4-8-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 0.8-2.2 cm, the pedicels 0.7-1.4 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals light greenish-yellow, 3.3-5.6 x 3-5.3 mm at anthesis, obtuse, externally short-tomentose, internally puberulous. Corolla type IX, sulphur yellow, the lower lip light yellow beneath, the throat with a distinct crossband of confluent deep purple spots inside, the upper half of the throat (i.e., above crossband) white with some purple dots, the lower half bright yellow, sometimes with a few purple dots; upper lip 23 mm long, 4-5 mm wide, and 5-6 mm high, truncate and shallowly tridentate at apex; lower lip saccate in 50-60% of length, the upeurved portion 10-12 x 8-9 mm. Stamens with anthers huffish to yellow-brown, 1.5-2.3 mm, the thecae divaricate or slightly deflexed; filaments 1-1.3 mm. Style 1.4-2.2 mm long. Capsule conic, 67 mm long, acuminate, glandular-puberulous. 2n = 36 (Molau 796).

description: Low shrubby plant, the stems erect or ascending, 0.1-0.8 m tall, tufted; inflorescence and distal parts of stems strigose or short-hirsute with white hairs. Leaves decussate (rarely ternate or alternate), fasciculate; blades coriaceous, elliptic or ovate, 4-17 x 2-8 mm, acute or subacute at apex, rounded or cuneate at base, the margins revolute, entire or somewhat crenulate; upper surface bright to dark green, strigose, glutinous, nitidous, almost smooth; lower surface pale green, predominantly hyphodromous, the veins strigose, interspaces glandular and puberulous or strigose; petioles 1-4 mm, dilated at base, strigose or short-villous with white hairs. Inflorescence resembling a raceme, composed of 3-10 pairs of reduced, 1- or 2-flowered cymes, the peduncles 4-14 mm, the pedicels 3-9 mm; cyme bracts present. Sepals light yellow-green to light olive green, 2.7-4.2 x 2.2-3.5 mm at anthesis, acute, externally shortly white-tomentose, internally glandular-puberulous (subglabrous at base), the margins densely short-ciliate. Corolla type VIII, bright yellow or lemon yellow, the throat internally with deep red spots, sometimes numerous and confluent to a crossband; upper lip 2-3 mm long and 5-6 mm wide, truncate and indistinctly lobulate at apex; lower lip saccate in 35-45% of length, the upcurved portion 10-15 x 8-14 mm, distally shallowly 5-lobulate. Stamens with anthers yellow-brown to medium brown, l.8-2.8 mm, the thecae divaricate or slightly deflexed; filaments 0.7-1.5 mm. Style 1.3-2.2 mm long. Capsule conic, 5-9 mm long, often slightly acuminate, minutely glandular-puberulous. 2n = 36 (Molau 581, new record).

description: Vine or scandent shrub, at least 1 m tall, the branches divaricate; inflorescence and distal parts of stems pilose or villous with white hairs. Leaves herbaceous, blades narrowly elliptic to lanceolate, 5.2-7.8 x 1.8-3.1 cm, acute, cuneate or attenuate at base, the margins coarsely sharp-serrate; upper surface bright green, pilose, slightly flexuose; lower surface pale green, reticulate-venose, the major veins hirsute or villous with white hairs, the interspaces pilose and beset with sessile glands; petioles 7-13 mm, white-villous. Inflorescence intercalary, composed of 1 or 2 pairs of 1-4-flowered cymes, the peduncles 2.5-1.1 cm; pedicels 3.2-4.4 cm; cyme bracts well-developed, also subordinate bracts present. Sepals ovate to cordiform, light green to yellow-green, acuminate or caudate, externally white-strigose, internally glabrous except for the short-tomentose border along the margins, unequal, the dorsal sepal broadly ovate, cordiform, 12-14 x 8.7-11 mm at anthesis. Corolla type I, bright yellow, unspotted, externally glandular; upper lip glandular-puberulent, 4-5 x 7-8 mm; lower lip 16-26 x 13-18 mm, saccate in 50-70% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1, the anthers pale brown, 3.8-4.8 mm, glandular at base, otherwise glabrous, the thecae subequal, slightly arcuate; filaments 1.3-1.6 mm. Style straight, relatively thick, 2.5-2.8 mm. Mature capsule not seen.

description: Ascending, sometimes scandent, shrub, 0.3-3 m tall, much branched, the stems glutinous, glabrous or subglabrous. Leaves with blades ovate, lanceolate, or narrowly elliptic, 3-11(-13) x 13 cm, glabrous, acute, the margins serrate with mucronulate teeth, often somewhat revolute; upper surface deep green, nitidous; lower surface whitish-green or pale grayish-green; petioles brownish-tomentose dorsally. Inflorescence glutinous; cymes 4-16-flowered. Sepals ovate, 3.26 mm long, acute or slightly acuminate, green or greenish-yellow, glutinous, internally with a short-tomentose border along the margins, otherwise glabrous. Corolla type XIV, bright yellow, the upper lip hooded or flattened and subcircular, the lower lip projecting or pendent, saccate in 30-50% of length; elaiophore present (sometimes rudimentary, made up of sparsely distributed glands on the infolded corolla lobe), non-functional in terms of pollination (cf. Breeding System). Stamens type 2; anthers yellow-brown to dark brown, 2.0-3.7 mm across, glabrous, the margins paler, the thecae equal, subglobose, about as high as long. Style arcuate. Capsule subglobose or broadly ovoid, brown, 4-8 mm long, glabrous.

description: Erect subshrub, 0.2-0.5 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems densely and shortly glandular-hirsute. Leaves decussate, short-petiolate; blades coriaceous, lanceolate, 12-19 x 37 mm, acute at apex, cuneate to truncate at base, the margins entire, revolute; upper surface light olive green, glabrous but densely pruinose-glandular, ± smooth (the midrib somewhat impressed); lower surface yellow-green to whitish-green, pinnate-venose, densely glandular (glistening in dried specimens), glabrous; petioles 1-2 mm, glandular-hirsute. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 4-8-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 0.9-1.9 cm; pedicels 0.7-1.4 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals olivaceous to yellow-green, 2.5-3.6 x 1.6-3.1 mm at anthesis, acute or subacute, glabrous and densely glandular on both sides, the margins entire. Corolla type XI, light yellow, the throat unspotted or with faint red dots, sometimes confluent to a narrow crossband; upper lip 2-3 mm long and wide; lower lip obovate, somewhat flattened, 1018 x 8-16 mm, saccate in 75-85% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 9; anthers yellowish-white, 1.8-2.3(-3.5) mm, the thecae subequal, dehiscing to the connective; filaments 0.7-1.1 mm. Style curved distally, 1.5-2.4 mm. Capsule ovoid, slightly acuminate, 3-6 mm long, glandular. 2n = 72 (Molau & Sanchez Vega 855).

description: Scandent subshrub with long internodes, 1-1.5 m tall; stems and inflorescence velutinous with huffish eglandular hairs. Leaves indistinctly short-petiolate; blades subcoriaceous, lanceolate, 6-14 x 1.2-3.2 cm, acute, cuneate at base, the margins slightly revolute or plane, serrulate or subentire; upper surface olivaceous, densely sericeous, almost smooth; lower surface light olive-green, lanate; petioles sericeous, 2-10 mm. Inflorescence composed of two pairs of 6-20-flow-ered cymes, the primary peduncles 2-7 cm, the pedicels 1.5-2 cm; cyme bracts rudimentary or absent. Sepals olivaceous, ovate, 3-4.6 x 1.8-3 mm at anthesis, slightly acuminate, entire, externally densely sericeous, internally glabrous. Corolla type VI, pale yellow or yellowish-white, unspotted, externally puberulous or finely villous; upper lip 8-13 x 10-15 mm; lower lip 13-18 x 10-15 mm; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 4; anthers light brown, glandular-puberulous at base or glabrous, 2.2-2.6 mm across, the thecae ascending, equal; filaments ca. 1.5 mm. Style 2.8-4 mm, distally curved. Capsule ovoid, 3-5 mm long, glandular-villous.

description: Erect or ascending herb, 0.4-1 m tall, the stems ± succulent. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate, 4.8-11 x 3-7.2 cm, acute, truncate or broadly cuneate at base, subentire or lobate in the proximal part with one or two pairs of lateral lobes, the margins serrate or biserrate; petioles 1-4.5 cm long, narrowly winged, connate across the nodes with wings 2-3 mm wide. Inflorescence with primary peduncles 2.5-17 cm, pedicels 1.1-8.4 cm. Sepals ovate, light green, 4.2-8.2 x 2.4-5.2 mm at anthesis, acuminate, externally shortly glandular-villous, internally glandular-puberulous, the margins entire or denticulate. Corolla type III, light to bright yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 2-4 x 3-5 mm, the lower lip 10-20 x 8-15 mm, saccate in 75-85% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens with anthers brown to orange, 3.5-5.8 mm long; upper (posterior) theca fertile, 1.2-2.2 mm long, short-stalked; lower theca sterile and vestigial; connective elongated, the lower arm sigmoid, distally ± flattened and expanded, dorsally with a sharp tooth 0.1-0.3 mm high; filaments 0.6-1.4 mm. Style arcuate, 2.4-3.8 mm. Capsule subglobose, 6-10 mm long, pale green and ± suffused with purple, pilose or villous with short glandular hairs.

description: Scandent subshrub or vine, 0.5-2 m tall, the stems brittle, red-brown, the branches divaricate; inflorescence and distal parts of stems hirsute or villous with coarse whitish hairs. Leaves decussate; blades herbaceous, ovate, 2.5-4.7 x 1.5-2.8 cm, subacute at apex, truncate or rounded at base, the margins crenate to coarsely biserrate, ± deflexed; upper surface deep green, hispid or villous with white hairs, somewhat rugose; lower surface paler green, pinnate-venose, the veins hispid, interspaces pilose or villous, glandless; petioles 6-15 mm, villous, dilated at base. Inflorescence composed of three or four pairs of 8-16-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.1-7.4 cm, the pedicels 0.9-2.4 cm; cyme bracts present in the lowermost cyme pair, otherwise mostly absent. Sepals ovate, light green to very pale green, ± suffused with purple, 5.510 x 4.6-7.3 mm at anthesis, acute or acuminate, externally hispid, internally puberulous distally and towards the margins, otherwise glabrous, the margins densely short-ciliate. Corolla type VIII; upper lip 2-4 mm long and 5-9 mm wide and about as high, pale yellow to greenish-white; lower lip proximally white or yellowish-white, otherwise pale yellow, distally red-dotted and distinctly 5-lobate, saccate in 30-40% of length, the upcurved portion 12-17 x 8-14 mm, the throat internally white in the upper half and light yellow in the lower half, the latter area often provided with red dots; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers yellow-brown to yellowish-white, glabrous, 2.1-2.8 mm, the thecae divaricate or slightly deflexed; filaments 1.2-2 mm. Style 1.7-2.7 mm, distally decurved. Capsule ovoid or conic, 6-9 mm long, glandular-puberulous, ± purplish. 2n = 36 (Molau 891, new record).

description: Scandent subshrub, 2-4 m long, the branches almost divaricate; inflorescence and distal parts of stems hirsute to villous with coarse, yellowish to whitish hairs. Leaves petiolate; blades herbaceous, ovate, 2.5-5.3 x 1.5-3 cm, acute, cuneate to almost rounded at base, the margins coarsely serrate; upper surface deep green to olivaceous, gently flexuose, pilose; lower surface grayish-green, pinnate-venose, whitish-hirsute; petioles 7-15 mm, densely huffish-white hirsute. Inflorescence composed of 2-4 (usually 3) pairs of 4-flowered cymes, the peduncles 1.7-7.6 cm long, the pedicels 1.5-3.9 cm; cyme bracts present, sometimes lacking in uppermost cymes. Sepals yellow-green to bright lemon-yellow, ovate or obovate, 9-15 x 8-12 mm at anthesis, acute or subacute, the margins denticulate or irregularly dentate, externally pilose, internally glabrous. Corolla type VII, bright yellow (sometimes cream-white), unspotted; upper lip 4-6 x 8-10 mm; lower lip 17-28 x 13-25 mm, up-curved, saccate in 40-50% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers pale bullish to light brown, glabrous, 2.7-3.5 mm, the thecae divaricate, equal, ± flaring; filaments 1.3-1.5 mm. Style arcuate, 2.5-3.6 mm. Capsule ovoid, brownish, 8-10 mm long, shortly glandular-hirsute.
