description: Ascending herb, 0.2-1 m tall, often subrosulate (lower internodes short), the stems and inflorescence pilose or sparsely villous with long hairs. Leaves with blades herbaceous, subcircular in inclusive outline, 4.8-9 x 4.5-9.1 cm, acute or subacute at apex, cordate at base, 9-13-lobate, the lobes serrate; upper surface bright green, pilose to velutinous, almost smooth; lower surface palmate-venose, pale green to purplish, the veins densely white-hispid, interspaces pilose or villous; petioles 2-6 cm, loosely long-villous. Inflorescence composed of a single pair (rarely two pairs) of 8-24-flowered cymes, often with one of the cymes inhibited; primary peduncles 6.8-13 cm; pedicels 1.8-4.7 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals ovate, dull green, often purple at base, 4.8-8 x 3.2-6.2 mm at anthesis, acute, externally hispid, internally pilose or sparsely villous with glandular hairs; margins entire or denticulate, glandular-villous. Corolla type I, bright to deep yellow above, paler below, the throat usually with purple or maroon spots inside; upper lip 3-5 x 5-7 mm; lower lip 16-30 x 10-15 mm, saccate in 50-60% of length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 9; anthers yellowish to brown, glabrous, 4.6-6.2 mm, dehiscing distally to (but not through) the connective, the thecae unequal, arcuate, divaricate; filaments 1.5-2 mm. Style curved, 3.2-4.5 mm. Capsule ovoid, often slightly acuminate, purplish, 7-10 mm long, glandular-hirsute.

description: Shrublet or subshrub, 0.2-1(-2) m tall, the stems erect or ascending, tufted; inflorescence and distal parts of stems glabrous or pilose. Leaves ternate, rarely decussate (dept. La Libertad); blades ovate, 1.9-7.5(-9) x 1.1-5.2(-6) cm, acute or slightly acuminate, rounded to cordate at base (rarely cuneate), the margins sharply serrate or biserrate with mucronulate teeth; upper surface bright to deep green, glabrous or pilose, nitidous, almost smooth; lower surface reticulate-venose (though predominantly pinnate-venose), light green, glabrous or sparsely pilose; petioles 2-10 (-15) mm, glabrous or pilose. Inflorescence composed of (3-)5-11 triplets (rarely pairs) of 2-16-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 5-24 mm, the pedicels 4-11 mm. Sepals ovate or lanceolate, 2.5-4.4 x 1.3-3.2 mm at anthesis, light green, acute, externally glabrous, internally glabrous or glandular-papillose. Corolla type XII, bright yellow to deep yellow, with red dots in the throat (rarely unspotted); upper lip 1-2 x 2-3 mm; upcurved part of lower lip 8-14 x 5-10 mm. Stamens with anthers pale buff to yellow-brown, 1.8-2.4 mm; filaments (1.3-)1.6-2.2 mm. Style 1.7-4.3 mm long. Capsule 4-7 mm long. 2n = 36 (Molau et al. 507, new record).

description: Woody vine, climbing up to 5 m, the branches divaricate; inflorescence and distal parts of stems purplish and tomentose with purplish-white septate hairs. Leaves with blades subcoriaceous or coriaceous, ovate, ± oblique, 3.8-5.8 x 1.7-2.7 cm, acuminate, rounded to cuneate at base; upper surface deep green, ± smooth, whitish tomentose on midrib and secondary veins, the interspaces short-pilose, the midrib magenta; lower surface pale green, predominantly pinnate-venose with pinkish short-tomentose veins, the interspaces sparsely short-pilose and with regularly dispersed yellow glands; margins shallowly serrate; petioles 3-10 mm, tomentose. Inflorescence distal, pendent, composed of 2-5 pairs of 4-10-flowered cymes on primary peduncles 1-8 cm long; cyme bracts present in lower cyme pairs only; pedicels 2.4-5.6 cm. Sepals pale green to yellow-green, acuminate or cuspidate, puberulous on both sides, externally also orange-glandular, internally with a distinct short-tomentose border along the margins, conspicuously unequal in width, the dorsal sepal 6.5-8.8 x 5.2-7.4 mm at anthesis, ovate. Corolla type I, sulphur yellow above, light yellow, unspotted, externally glandular, especially on the upper lip; upper lip 47 x 5-8 mm; lower lip 23-32 x 15-22 mm, saccate in 60-70% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers medium brown, 3.4-4.4 mm, with short-stalked glands at base, otherwise glabrous, the thecae somewhat unequal, divaricate or slightly deflexed; filaments glabrous, 1.2-2 mm. Style straight below, sharply bent near apex, glandular, 2.2-2.8 mm. Capsule ovoid, glandular, glutinous, brown, 4-6 mm long.

description: Tufted subshrub, 25-80 cm tall, the stems erect or ascending; inflorescence and distal parts of stems densely glandular-puberulous. Leaves ternate; blades herbaceous or subcoriaceous, lanceolate (rarely almost ovate), 1.3-4.8 x 0.5-3.3 cm, acute at apex, cuneate or rounded at base, the margins deeply serrate or dentate (sometimes biserrate in large leaves); upper surface olivaceous, slightly rugose, glandular-puberulous; lower surface grayish-green, predominantly pinnate-venose, densely glandular-puberulous and villous with white glandless hairs; petioles 2-8 mm, pilose or villous. Inflorescence composed of 5-8 triplets of 2-8-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 9-13 mm, the pedicels 5-11 mm. Sepals ovate or lanceolate, green, 2.5-3.5 x 1.4-2.1 mm at anthesis, acute or slightly acuminate, externally glandular-puberulous and white-villous, internally glandular-puberulous. Corolla type XII, bright yellow, the neck speckled with red or entirely red, sac unspotted or with some red spots; upper lip 1-2 x 2-3 mm; upcurved part of lower lip 8-13 x 5-9 mm. Stamens with anthers light brown, 1.9-2.2 mm; filaments 1.4-1.8 mm. Style 2.4-3.3 mm long. Capsule 4-7 mm long. 2n = 36 (Dillon & Dillon 3807, new record).

description: Ascending herb, at least 0.3-0.5 m tall; stems and inflorescence spreading hirsute with whitish gland-tipped hairs. Leaves petiolate; blades herbaceous, ovate to elliptic, 2-3.7 x 1.3-2.6 cm, acute or subacute, cuneate or almost truncate at base, the margins irregularly serrate with rounded teeth; upper surface bright green, somewhat flexuose, glandular-hirsute; lower surface paler, predominantly pinnate-venose, the veins glandular-hispid, interspaces pilose; petioles 3-19 mm, glandular-hirsute. Inflorescence composed of 1 or 2 pairs of 4-16-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 2.9-6.5 cm, the pedicels 0.5-1.3 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals green, elliptic to ovate, 3-3.8 x 1.7-2.6 mm at anthesis, acute or subacute, externally glandular-hirsute, internally glandular-puberulous, the margins entire, ciliate. Corolla type XV, yellow, unspotted, glandular, the upper lip ca. 3 x 3 mm, acuminate, tapering into an abruptly truncate apex, the lower lip ± pendent, 8-12 x 5-7 mm, saccate in 30-40% of length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 5; anthers brownish-yellow, glabrous, 1.1-1.4 mm, the thecae deflexed, equal, each one ca. 1.2 mm long; filaments 1.2-1.5 mm. Style straight, 2.1-4.4 mm. Capsule ovoid, 5-6 mm long, shortly glandular-hirsute.

description: Erect or ascending subshrub 0.4-1.5 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems glandular-puberulent to glandular-hirsute. Leaves herbaceous; blades lanceolate to ovate, 2.3-6.4 x 1.2-4.3 cm, acute, cordate to truncate (sometimes broadly cuneate) at base; upper surface deep green, pilose to shortly villous with white hairs and also beset with sessile hyaline glands, slightly rugose; lower surface pale green, reticulate-venose, the major veins glandular-pilose to -villous, interspaces sessile-glandular and glabrous or glandular-pilose; margins lobate with 2-4 lobes on each side of blade, the lobes entire or serrate; petioles 0.4-1.7 cm, glandular-tomentose, canaliculate, dilated at base to connate flaps 1-3 mm wide. Inflorescence distal, composed of 2-4 pairs of 12-36-flowered cymes on primary peduncles 1.5-7.8 cm long; cyme bracts present (though often absent in the upper cymes); pedicels 0.8-2.5 cm. Sepals ovate, bright green, acute or slightly acuminate, entire, 3-5.4 x 2-4.4 mm at anthesis, externally shortly glandular-hirsute, internally puberulous. Corolla deep yellow, unspotted or with brownish-red dots, glabrous, upper lip 2-lobed, the lobes 6-10 x 5-12 mm, lower lip 6-10 x 8-15 mm. Stamens with the anthers gray to deep blue (becoming whitish when dried), glabrous, dehiscing apically, thecae deflexed, 1.4-2 mm wide, thecae 1.1-1.6 mm long, equal; filaments 1.4-2.2 mm, glabrous or glandular-puber-ulous. Style yellow, straight, 5.2-7.7 mm, proximally with stalked glands. Capsule broadly ovoid, 3-6 mm long, glandular-hirsute, brown or purplish.

description: Leaves with blades rounded to truncate and ± dimidiate at base; lower surface pinnate-venose, the veins raised. Inflorescence composed of 18-36-flowered cymes. Sepals olivaceous, 3.7-4.2 x 3-3.3 mm at anthesis, acute or slightly acuminate, externally puberulous, internally glabrous, glandular. Stamens with anthers chestnut brown throughout, 2.5-3 mm long.

description: Leaf-blades 1.6-3.7 x 0.9-1.3 cm, pilose to villous above, the major veins hirsute with long hairs below, interspaces villous. Inflorescence composed of 2-4 (usually 3) pairs of (1-)4-6-flowered cymes, the front flowers present. Sepals 7.2-9.5 x 4.8-6.3 mm at anthesis, externally tomentose. Corolla with upper lip 6-8 x 10-15 mm, lower lip 23-35 x 17-23 mm. Stamens with anthers 2.8-3.5 mm, filaments 1.5-2 mm. Style 2.5-3 mm.

description: Erect or ascending subshrub, 0.5-1 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems hirsute with ascending yellowish-white hairs. Leaves sessile; blades herbaceous, ovate to lanceolate, 3-7.5 x 1-3.2 cm, obtuse and deflexed at apex, cordate and clasping at base; upper surface yellowish-green, bullate, sparsely hirsute; lower surface light green, reticulate-venose, villous; margins deflexed, crenate to serrate. Inflorescence composed of 1-3 pairs of 16-40-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 2-6 cm; pedicels 1-1.8 cm; cyme bracts usually absent (sometimes present in lowermost cymes). Sepals ovate to narrowly triangular, yellow-green, 3.5-5.5 x 1.9-3 mm at anthesis, acute or slightly acuminate, externally appressed-hirsute. Corolla type IV, deep yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 5-9 mm high and wide, the lower lip saccate in 50-70% of length, its upcurved portion 11-18 x 8-12 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers light yellow-brown, 1.5-2.3 mm, glabrous; filaments 0.5-1.1 mm. Style arcuate, 1.3-1.7 mm. Capsule ovoid, 4-5 mm long, glandular-puberulous. 2n = 36 (Løjtnant & Molau 14915).
bibliographicCitation: Molau, Ulf. 1988. Scrophulariaceae Part I. Calceolarieae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 47: 1-325.

description: Ascending or scandent herb, at least 0.5-1 m tall, the stems and inflorescence pilose or villous with white gland-tipped hairs. Leaves with blades herbaceous, ovate or triangular-ovate, 3.9-9 x 3.4-8.8 cm, acuminate, cordate at base, slightly 3-7-lobate, the lobes irregularly serrate; upper surface bright green, smooth, glandular-pilose; lower surface pale green, reticulate-venose, the veins pilose or spreading hirsute, the interspaces glabrous or sparsely glandular-pilose; petioles 1.5- 4.5 cm, villous. Inflorescence composed of 2-5 pairs of (2-)4-16-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 6.5-14 cm, the pedicels 1.4-6.8 cm. Sepals green, ovate, 8.8-10 x 5.3-6.8 mm at anthesis, acute, shortly glandular-villous on both sides, the margins entire. Corolla type I, yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 5-6 x 7-8 mm, the lower lip 12-17 x 10-12 mm, saccate in 40-60% of length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 1; anthers brown, glabrous, 3-3.4 mm, dehiscing throughout, the thecae equal or subequal, slightly arcuate, divaricate or slightly ascending; filaments 1.7-2 mm. Style curved, 4.6-5.5 mm. Capsule conic, 5-9 mm long, glandular-pilose.

description: Subshrub, 0.3-3 m tall. Leaves with blades acuminate or caudate, 4.2-12 x 3-7.4 cm, the lower surface villous or lanate. Inflorescence composed of (1-)2-3 pairs of 8-16-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 2-8.4 cm, the pedicels 1.7-3.2 cm; cyme bracts present, well-developed. Sepals bright yellow, rarely lemon yellow, 9.5-19 x 6-17 mm at anthesis. Corolla unspotted; upper lip light yellow or bright yellow; lower lip bright yellow at base, distally bright or (usually) golden yellow. Stamens with anthers 2.5-4 mm across.

description: Ascending subshrub, sometimes somewhat scandent, 0.3-1.5 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems purplish, puberulous to villous with white hairs. Leaves decussate, short-petiolate; blades subcoriaceous, rather stiff, ovate, 2-3.2 x 1.3-2.2 cm, acute at apex, rounded at base, the margins sharply serrate; upper surface dark green, ± nitidous, papillose, glandular, flexuose; lower surface contrasting grayish-green, reticulate-venose (but the tertiary veins ± faint), the major veins raised, strigose, the interspaces glabrous, glandular; petioles 1-4 mm, puberulous to villous. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of (2-)4-8-flowered cymes; primary peduncles(l-)2.7-6.1 cm; pedicels 1-2.3 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals very light yellow-green, slightly suffused with purple (increasing in fruit), 7.2-9.5 x 4.4-6.4 mm at anthesis, enlarged in fruit and up to 12 x 8.5 mm, acute or somewhat acuminate, externally glandular and pilose or puberulous, internally sparsely puberulous. Corolla type VIII, the upper lip white, the lower lip bright lemon-yellow, internally with a 4-5 mm wide wine-red crossband in the throat; upcurved portion of lower lip 13-15 x 7-9 mm. Stamens with anthers light brown, 2.8-3 mm, the thecae divaricate; filaments 1-1.6 mm. Style 1.8-2.5 mm long. Capsule conical, 6-7 mm long, slightly acuminate, glandular-papillose.

description: Vine, the stems scandent, 0.5-2 m long; inflorescence and distal parts of stems glandular-hirsute. Leaves never fasciculate; blades ovate, herbaceous, acute, cuneate to truncate at base, 2.5-5.5 x 1.3-3 cm, the margins deflexed, crenate to serrate; upper surface glandular-pilose to glandular-hirsute; lower surface glandular-pilose. Inflorescence composed of a single pair of 2-6-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 2.7-11 cm, the pedicels 0.6-1.9 cm. Corolla with lower lip 8-18 x 5-12 mm. Stamens with anthers 2.5-3.6 mm. Style 1.8-2.3 mm. 2n = 36 (Molau 906, 922).

description: Leaves with blades 2.3-11 x 1.5-7 cm, doubly pinnatisect (lateral pinnae pinnatifid) with 5-15 pairs of lateral pinnae. Inflorescence with pedicels 1.5-6.2 cm long. Sepals 4-9 x 3-6.8 mm at anthesis. Corolla bright yellow (sometimes cream yellow), the upper lip ± deep yellow, 3-5 x 49 mm, the lower lip 12-25 x 8-23 mm, saccate in 80-90% of length, unspotted or with a purple blotch in the throat; elaiophore well-developed. Stamens with anthers 3.2-5.5 mm long, the posterior theca 1.5-2.8 mm, the anterior theca 0.8-1.6 mm; filaments 1.1-2.1 mm. Style 2.2-3.5 mm. Capsule 8-11 mm long. 2n = 26 (Molau et al 506, new record).

description: Scandent herb, 1-3 m long, the stems and peduncles pilose with white or pale purplish hairs. Leaves with blades triangular or ovate-triangular, 3.3-8 x 2.4-5.6 cm, acute or slightly acuminate, cordate at base, the margins irregularly biserrate, sometimes also lobulate; upper surface bright green, pilose; lower surface purplish, pilose (at least on major veins); petioles 1.6-5.2 cm long, 2-4.5 cm wide at base, 0.4-1.1 cm wide at the distal end, the margins serrate. Inflorescence intercalary, composed of 1-4 pairs of 4-20-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 5.623 cm long; pedicels 1.5-4.5 cm, pilose to villous and also pubescent with short glanduliferous hairs; cyme bracts 2.4-4 x 1.2-2.2 cm, subordinate bracts absent. Sepals ovate, light green or yellowish-green, often suffused with purple, 6.812 x 4-8.4 mm at anthesis, acuminate, externally pilose or puberulous, internally puberulous, the margins denticulate (rarely subentire). Corolla type XV, light to bright yellow, unspotted; upper lip 4-7 x 6-9 mm, truncate to acuminate; lower lip flattened, 16-23 x 10-15 mm, saccate in 40-60% of length; elaiophore absent or present (see below). Stamens type 6; anthers dark brown, horseshoe-shaped, dehiscing throughout, glabrous, 2.6-3.4 mm across, the thecae deflexed, bean-shaped, subequal, 1.7-2.4 mm long; filaments 1.8-2.6 mm. Style 5.5-7.5 mm, arcuate or almost straight. Capsule subglobose, 5-7 mm long, short-villous.

description: Erect herb, 0.5-2 m tall; stems and inflorescence finely glandular-villous. Leaves with upper surface of blades bright green, ± densely hispid; petioles winged throughout, equally tapering, 0.30.7 cm wide at the distal end. Inflorescence composed of 2-3 pairs of cymes, the bracts 3.9-10 x 2.3-6.5 cm. Corolla bright to deep yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 12-16 x 10-14 mm, the lower lip 23-30 x 11-22 mm, saccate in 60-70% of length. Stamens with anthers brown to light yellow, 4.9-5.8 mm; filaments 3.2-4.2 mm. Style straight, 7.4-11 mm long. 2n = 36 (Molau 881, new record).

description: Lax shrub, the stems ascending or semi-scandent, 0.3-3 m long; inflorescence and distal parts of stems short-tomentose or short-sericeous, sessile-glandular, with purplish-brown hairs. Leaves with blades coriaceous, ovate or lanceolate, 3.9-8.8 x 1.2-4 cm, acuminate (sometimes acute), cuneate or rounded at base, the margins crenate, ± deflexed; upper surface deep green, matt, sparsely to densely short-pilose, beset with sessile hyaline glands, somewhat flexuose; lower surface light or greyish green, pinnate-venose, the veins raised, pilose or tomentose, the midrib purplish, interspaces glabrous, distinctly gland-dotted, the glands yellowish; petioles 5-26 mm, shortly tomentose or sericeous with brownish hairs. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of (2-)8-12-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.213 cm, the pedicels 0.8-4.5 cm; cyme bracts usually present (75% of the specimens examined). Sepals lanceolate (rarely ovate), ± fleshy, obtuse, yellowish-green, 4-7.5 x 1.5-3.8 mm at anthesis, puberulous or short-tomentose and sessile-glandular on both sides, the margins entire or sparsely crenate. Corolla type XIV, bright yellow to deep orange, unspotted, the upper lip arched, 4-8(-10) x 7-15(-17) mm, the lower lip pendent, flattened, obovate, 16-35(-58) x 10-25(-35) mm, saccate in 50-60(-70)% of length, the orifice wide open; elaiophore absent or rudimentary, rarely normally developed (though nonfunctional in terms of pollination). Stamens type 6; anthers dark brown to deep brownish-purple, glabrous, 1.8-3(-3.5) mm across, the thecae equal, reniform, each one (1.1-)1.5-2.4 mm; filaments 1.5-3 mm. Style slender, almost straight, (3-)3.6-5.8 mm. Capsule globose, yellow-brown, 46 mm long, glandular.

description: Erect or ascending, tufted herb, 0.2-1 m tall; stems and inflorescence densely cream white arachnoid-lanate. Leaves with blades ovate, 4.216 x 3.1-9 cm, acute or subacute, cordate to slightly cuneate at base, the margins serrate to bicrenate; upper surface grayish-green to olivaceous, sericeous or sparsely arachnoid-lanate; lower surface densely cream white arachoid-lanate; petioles 1.5-9 cm long, the margins entire, ± undulate, and almost parallel, widened only around the stem to a width of 0.6-3.6 cm, otherwise 0.3-1 cm wide. Inflorescence distal, composed of (1-)2-6 pairs of 6-20-flowered cymes on primary peduncles 4.2-15 cm long; cyme bracts 1.7-5.3 x 0.9-3.1 cm, subordinate bracts usually absent, sometimes present in the lowermost cymes and up to 1.5 x 0.9 cm; pedicels 1.5-4.3 cm. Sepals lanceolate (rarely ovate), 6.313 x 3.2-6 mm at anthesis, acute or acuminate, externally lanate, internally light green, short-villous (most densely so towards the margins), the margins entire or (rarely) sparsely dentate. Corolla type I; upper lip bright yellow or sulphur yellow, 3-8 x 4-8 mm; lower lip light yellow, 15-23 x 10-15 mm, saccate in 70-80% of length, the throat internally light purple; elaiophore present. Stamens type 11; anthers yellowish-white to yellow-brown, glabrous, 3.2-4.3 mm, dehiscing to the connective (i.e., the thecae dehiscing throughout); thecae unequal, slightly sigmoid and ± ascending, the margins flaring distally; filaments 0.8-1.4 mm. Style straight, 3.6-5.7 mm, slightly decurved at apex. Capsule ovoid, 5-6 mm long, shortly glandular-hirsute. 2n = 36 (Løjtnant & Molau 15187).

description: Leaves with blades lanceolate to almost linear, 6.5-11 x 1.1-1.5 cm, attenuate at both ends, pinnate-venose below; petioles 5-7 mm. Inflorescence composed of two pairs of 4-8-flowered cymes, the peduncles glabrous, 2.5-4.2 cm, the pedicels glabrous, 1-2.5 cm; cyme bracts absent. Sepals 5-6 x 3.5-4 mm at anthesis. Corolla with upper lip 8-12 mm high and 11-20 mm wide; lower lip ± pendent and somewhat upcurved at the distal end, 15-25 x 15-21 mm. Stamens with anthers 2.8-3.4 mm; filaments 2-2.2 mm. Style 3.5-4.5 mm.

description: Erect herb, 0.5-1 m tall, the stems and peduncles pilose or villous. Leaves with blades ovate or triangular-ovate, 3.7-6 x 2-4 cm, acute, truncate or cuneate at base, the margins irregularly shallowly serrate; upper surface olivaceous, short-villous with white hairs; lower surface very pale green, often purplish flushed; petioles 2-3.8 cm long, 1.7-3 cm wide at base, 0.6-1.2 cm at the distal end, the margins serrulate or subentire. Inflorescence intercalary, composed of a single pair of 8-12-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 12-16 cm long; pedicels villous, 2.2-3.3 cm; cyme bracts 3.2-3.9 x 2.0-2.3 cm, subordinate bracts absent. Sepals ovate, yellow, acuminate (but not caudate), 10-12 x 6.2-8 mm at anthesis, externally sparsely pilose, internally sparsely puberulous, the margins dentate, ciliate. Corolla type XIV, pale yellow, unspotted, the upper lip 4-5 x 7-8 mm, the lower lip somewhat flattened, 12-13 x 7-10 mm, saccate in 50-60% of length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 1; anthers medium brown, glabrous, 2.9-3.3 mm, dehiscing throughout, the thecae equal, not flaring at maturity; filaments 2-2.5 mm. Style curved, 4.2-4.5 mm. Capsule subglobose, 5-6 mm long, purplish, tomentose or villous.

description: Erect herb, 0.5-3 m tall; stems and inflorescence pilose to villous with white hairs, at least some of which are gland-tipped. Leaves with upper surface of blades olive green, pilose; petioles winged throughout, equally tapering, 0.3-2.5 cm wide at the distal end. Inflorescence composed of 2-5 pairs of cymes, the bracts 4.8-16 x 2.712 cm. Corolla bright yellow, usually unspotted, rarely red-dotted in the throat (Macbride 3124, Pasco, central Peru), the upper lip 7-10 x 9-14 mm, the lower lip 20-42 x 13-30 mm, saccate in 50-60% of length. Stamens with anthers buff or buffish-yellow, 4.5-6 mm; filaments 2.4-3.8 mm. Style straight to arcuate, 4.4-6.4 mm long. 2n = 36 (Molau 766, new record). The chromosome number 2n = 36 reported by Huynh (1965: 196) for C. tomentosa probably refers to the present taxon, which is the only taxon of sect. Perfoliatae present in the area where Huynh’s vouchers were collected, namely the Urubamba Valley in the department of Cuzco, SE Peru.

description: Erect or ascending herb, 6-45 cm tall, the stems and inflorescence puberulous to villous with at least some of the hairs gland-tipped. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate, 1.2-5.4 x 0.7-3.3 cm, acuminate to subacute at apex, rounded to truncate at base, the margins serrulate to entire; petioles 1-12 mm, pilose or villous. Inflorescence with pedicels 0.6-8.2 cm, almost straight. Sepals green, elliptic to ovate, 2.2-5.1 x 1.3-4 mm at anthesis, acute to obtuse, externally pilose, internally glabrous, the margins entire, short-ciliate. Corolla resembling type X, lemon to bright yellow, the upper lip sometimes almost white; upper lip elliptic, saccate in 50-70% of length, ascending, often red-dotted outside (many N Peruvian populations); lower lip subglobose, 8-18 x 6-17 mm, saccate in 50-70% of its length; elaiophore absent. Stamens with anthers elliptic, yellowish-white, 0.7-2.2 mm; filaments filiform, sigmoid, 3.5-18 mm long. Style filiform, ± sigmoid, 3.916 mm long. Capsule conic, slightly acuminate, 4-8 mm long, glandular-puberulous, non-translucent. 2n = 30 (Molau & Sánchez Vega 849).

description: Leaf blades 1.5-5.5 x 0.5-2.2 cm, pilose above, the major veins white-hirsute below, interspaces glabrous to tomentose. Inflorescence composed of 3-6 pairs of (1 - or) 3-flowered cymes, the front flowers absent. Sepals 4.3-8.0 x 3.0 6.5 mm at anthesis, externally glandular-puberulous. Corolla with upper lip 4-8 x 7-15 mm, lower lip 16-32 x 12-23 mm. Stamens with anthers 2.2-3.2 mm, filaments 0.8-2.2 mm. Style 1.5-3.5 mm. 2n = 36 (Molau 655, new record).

description: Subshrub or stout herb, woody below, ascending, 0.3-1 m tall; stems and inflorescence coarsely glandular-hirsute with brownish or huffish hairs, strongly viscous. Leaves petiolate; blades herbaceous, somewhat fleshy, ovate or lanceolate, 3.7-11 x 1.5-4.8 cm, acute or slightly acuminate, cuneate at base, the margins sharply serrate or biserrate; upper surface olive-green, flexuose, densely short-hirsute; lower surface somewhat paler, reticulate-venose, the major veins glandular-hirsute, interspaces glandular-pilose; petioles 0.7-2.5 cm, densely glandular-hirsute. Inflorescence composed of a single 6-18-flowered cyme (the other cyme of the pair inhibited); primary peduncle 2.6-11 cm long, the pedicels 1.5-3.5 cm; cyme bracts absent. Sepals lanceolate, olivaceous, 7.8-11 x 4-6.8 mm at anthesis, slightly acuminate and ± caudate, the margins entire, externally glandular-hirsute, internally shortly glandular pilose, especially along the margins. Corolla type I, bright yellow, unspotted (?); upper lip 4-6 x 6-10 mm; lower lip 15-30 x 10-22 mm, saccate in 60-70% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers yellowish-white, 3.4-4.4 mm, glabrous, the thecae subequal, divaricate, slightly arcuate; filaments 0.8-1.5 mm. Style decurved near apex, otherwise straight, 2.2-3 mm. Capsule ovoid, purplish, 610 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Dioecious, aromatic shrubs or small trees 2-4 m tall, ca. 4 cm dbh; bark gray; wood white, turning orange when exposed to air; young stems quadrate, purple, smooth, glabrous; large stems terete, smooth, glabrous, encircled by leaf sheath scars; internodes 1.2-3.3 cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic to narrowly obovate, (2-)2.5-4.5(-6.8) x (0.8-)l.l-2.7(-3.7) cm, with acuminate tips 2-3 mm long (these obtuse to retuse at apex), margins crenulate with teeth 1.5-2.5 mm distant beginning one-fourth to one-third distance from base, coriaceous, smooth, glabrous, shiny or dull, dark green above, light green beneath, drying coriaceous, smooth, light to dark gray or brown above and beneath; midveins impressed above, raised and glabrous beneath; lateral veins slightly obscure, 7-12, 2-5 mm distant, neither impressed above nor raised beneath, straight, leaving midveins at ca. 45° angle, with intersecondary veins obscure; free portion of petioles green or purple, 0.3-1.1 cm long, smooth to verrucose, glabrous, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths purple, smooth, glabrous, 11.7 x 0.4-0.8 cm at apex, neither inflated nor flared at apex, terete or quadrangular, caducous, each distal margin extended ca. 0.5 mm beyond free portion of petioles and with two linear stipular appendages 0.5-1 mm long. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 3-4 cm long, composed of 1-3 spikes on a short rachis 0.3-1.1 cm long; subtending bracts lanceolate to obovate, 0.3-1.7 x 0.1-0.8 cm, dentate or entire; mature spikes 1.8-2.5 x 0.5-0.6 cm, with ca. 200 stamens, sessile or borne on short peduncles 1-2 mm long; rachis ca. 1 mm broad, with a thick basal annulus; anthers ca. 2 x ca. 1 mm; connectives extended 0.2-0.5 mm beyond thecae, flattened. Pistillate inflorescence terminal or axillary, 1.7-3.2 cm long, composed of 1-3 cymules on a short rachis 0.5-1.1 cm long; bracts subetending cymules lanceolate to obovate, 0.10.6 x 0.1-0.3 cm, dentate or entire; cymules globose, with (2-)4-6 flowers, 7-10 mm in diam., borne on short peduncles 0.1-1 cm long; subtending floral bracts completely fusing into a bract matrix enclosing flowers completely except for exserted stigmas. Pistillate flowers slightly trigonous, 3-4 mm long, with an obscure pore on each face of the ovary; perianth lobes ca. 1 mm long completely united with only three sharp points along distal margin; stigmas purple, 1.53 mm long, linear, terete, persistent, with very short papillae. Fruiting cymules purple to black, globose, 0.8-1.2 cm in diam. Mature seeds not seen.

description: Dioecious, aromatic trees 3-6 m tall; young stems quadrate, purple, scurfy, extruding orange latex when cut; older stems terete, scurfy to smooth; internodes 4.5-10(-13) cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves elliptic to obovate, 10.5-25.5 x 5-12.9 cm, with acuminate tips 0.1-0.5 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, at margins serrate with teeth (3-)4-5 mm distant, subcoriaceous, smooth, glabrous, drying smooth to slightly scabrous, light brown above and beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath, with purple ramentaceous scales on dorsal proximal half; larger lateral veins 8-12, 11-20 mm distant, arcuate, impressed above, raised beneath, glabrous, with smaller intersecondary veins extending half-way to completely to margin, slightly impressed above and raised beneath; free portion of petioles 0.9-2.6 cm long, smooth, glabrous or with purple scales on dorsal surface, winged; petiolar sheaths purple, smooth to striate or verrucose, glabrous or with purple scales extending downward from free portion of petioles, 2-2.9 x 1.2-2 cm, inflated, notably flared at apex, quadrangular, with two prominent raised ciliate lines extending down sheath from stipular processes, notably laciniate down center, each distal margin with two caducous, fimbriate stipular processes 1-2 mm long, extending ca. 0.5 mm above free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 8.5-11.5 cm long, composed of 1-2 opposing pairs of spikes on a short rachis (0.6-2 cm long) terminated by a single spike; subtending bracts lanceolate to spatulate, 0.4-0.9 cm long, 1-2 mm broad, acute at apex, cucullate at base, entire; mature spikes 59 x 0.6-1 cm, with ca. 200 stamens, subsessile or borne on peduncles 0.6-2 cm long; stamens congested but becoming 0.5-2 mm distant; rachis ca. 2 mm broad with a thick, irregularly marginate, basal annulus; anthers yellowish green, 2-2.5 mm long, ca. 1 mm thick at middle; connectives extending ca. 0.2 mm beyond thecae, flat-topped or with a minute abrupt apicule. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal panicles 5.2-7(-11.1) cm long bearing 16-26 cymules; subtending inflorescence bracts 0.5-1.3 x 0.20.5 cm, entire or dentate; cymules with (3-)4-5(-6) imbricately arranged flowers, 4-6 x 4-6 mm, borne on peduncles 1-8 mm long, opposite or alternate on inflorescence axis, 2-14 mm distant; subtending floral bracts green, cucullate, connate in lower one-half to four-fifths, 3-3.5 mm long, including acuminate tips 0.5-1 cm long, ca. 2 mm broad, ciliate or entire along margin, enclosing one-half to four-fifths of flower. Pistillate flowers ellipsoidal, 2-2.5 x ca. 1.5 mm, with pores wanting; perianth lobes united to form a collar 0.7-1 mm high, with acute lobes barely visible; stigmas white, linear, 2-3 mm long, elaborated distally, papillose. Fruiting cymules white, irregularly globose, 8-10 mm in diam. (fully mature cymules not seen). Mature seeds not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Todzia, Carol A. 1988. Chloranthaceae: Hedyosmum. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 48: 1-138.

description: Dioecious trees 3-8 m tall; internodes 1.5-9.5 cm long; young stems quadrate, densely strigose or scurfy; older stems terete, smooth. Leaves narrowly elliptic to elliptic, 4.4-11.6 x 2.3-5.3 cm, terminating with acuminate to caudate tips 4-7 mm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, at margins crenulate to serrate with teeth 2-3 mm distant, glabrous, smooth, drying stiffly chartaceous to coriaceous, grayish brown above, reddish brown below, slightly scabrous above and beneath, with midveins sunken above, raised beneath, puberulent to verrucose; lateral veins 811, 4-8(-9) mm distant, straight to slightly arcuate, at a 45° angle to midvein, notably impressed above, raised and strigose beneath; free portions of petioles 0.4-1.8 cm long, smooth to verrucose, puberulent to densely strigose; petiolar sheaths 0.5-1.5 x 0.6-1 cm, densely strigose, becoming laciniate and leaving a ramentaceous edge, each distal margin with two minute, caducous, fimbriate appendages ca. 1 mm long, not extended above free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences axillary or terminal, solitary spikes or composed of a basal pair of spikes with a single terminal spike on a short rachis (0.5-2 cm long); inflorescence bracts 0.3-1 x 0.1-0.3 cm, dentate, ciliate or entire along margin, acute at apex, cucullate at base; mature spikes 3.5-7 x 3-6 mm, with 60-100 stamens, subsessile or borne on short peduncles 0.2-0.5 cm long; rachises 1-2 mm thick, with a small thickened irregular basal annulus; anthers 1.5-1.7 x 0.7-1 mm; connectives short, extended 0.1-0.2 mm beyond thecae, with a small erect apicule 0.3 mm long. Pistillate inflorescences thyrse-like panicles, 2.5-5.7 cm long, with cymules 0.5-0.9 cm distant, opposite or alternate along inflorescence axis, with dentate linear inflorescence bracts 3-7 x 13 mm; cymules 3-4 x 2-3 mm, on short peduncles ca. 1 mm long, with 2-4(-5) imbricately arranged flowers. Pistillate flowers whitish green, 1-2 x 1-1.5 mm ellipsoid to globular, without pores; perianth lobes 0.2-0.4 mm long, acute, basally united; subtending floral bracts 1-4 mm long, sometimes ciliolate on free distal margin, enclosing flower from one-half to three-quarters, adjacent bracts connate one-half to three-quarters, stigmas 2.5-3.8 mm long, linear to clavate, papillose, sometimes elaborated distally. Fruiting cymules white, 2-4 x 2-4 mm. Seeds 1-2 mm long, globose to ellipsoidal, brown, minutely papillate.

description: Arbores dioeciae 12-30 m altae, caules glabri, laminae foliorum anguste ellipticae vel ellipticae acuminatae, venae subtus prominenter strigosae, nervis lateralibus utroque latere (15-)23-35 parallelis, vaginae furfuraceae longae, inflores-centiam staminatam non vidi, inflorescentiae pistillatae ex 1-3 cymulis et rhachidi brevi con-stantes, fasciculis 5-15-floribus, monas disper-salis purpurea.

description: Dioecious, aromatic trees 12-30 m tall, 10-40 cm dbh, with prop roots; bark smooth, tan, brown, or gray; wood white, turning orange when exposed to air; young stems quadrate, green, glabrous; older stems terete, with tubular leaf sheaths disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; internodes 2.7-7 cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic to elliptic, (8-) 12-16.5(-21.9) x (3.2-)5.1-8.3(-9) cm, with acuminate serrated tips ().3-0.6 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, margins serrulate with teeth 2-3.5 mm distant, fleshy to subcoriaceous, smooth, dark green shiny above, light green dull beneath when fresh, drying chartaceous to coriaceous, smooth, dark slate brown above, light brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath, with dense white to brown branched trichomes or scales; lateral veins (15-)23-35, 37 m distant, straight, raised and strigose beneath, sometimes furcate, with obscure intersecondary veins extending one-half to three-fourths distance to margin; free portion of petioles scurfy, 0.6-1.5 cm long, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths smooth to rugose, glabrous to scurfy, (2-)2.9-3.5(-3.9) x 0.7-1.5 cm at apex, slightly inflated to not inflated, slightly flared at apex, quadrangular, disintegrating with age, each distal margin with two fimbriate stipular processes 23 mm long, extending ca. 2 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences not seen. Pistillate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 2.4-4.6 cm long, composed of (l-)3 cymules; bracts subtending cymules narrowly elliptic to elliptic, 1-4 x ca. 1 mm, acute at apex, cuneate at base, entire along margin; cymules green to purplish green, globose, borne on short peduncles 0.4-1.5 cm long; terminal cymules 1-1.3 cm in diam., 10-15-flowered; lateral cymules 0.8-1 cm in diam., 5-8-flowered; subtending floral bracts completely fused into a bract matrix enclosing flowers completely except for exserted stigmas. Pistillate flowers trigonous, 3-5 x ca. 1.5 mm, with a pore on each face of the ovary; perianth lobes 1-1.5 mm long, united almost to apex with the small free lobes acute; stigmas white to purple, 1-2 mm long, linear, terete, with very short papillae. Fruiting cymules dark purple, globose to oblong, 0.8-1.5 cm in diam. Seeds trigonous, ca. 3 mm long with apical beak ca. 0.75 mm long, smooth.

description: Dioecious, aromatic trees 3-16 m tall, 7-50 cm dbh, with prop roots; young stems quadrate, green or purple, smooth, sparsely to densely villous; older stems terete, smooth, glabrous, with leaf bases disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; internodes 2.5-5 cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves obovate to elliptic, 4.2-8.3(-l 2.8) x 2.7-5.0(-7.5) cm, with acuminate tips 2-4 mm long, narrowly to broadly to obliquely cuneate at base, margins serrulate with teeth 2-4 mm distant, fleshy to subcoriaceous, smooth, shiny, dark green above, dull, glabrous to sparsely villous beneath with fresh, drying coriaceous, smooth, light to dark brown above and beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath; larger lateral veins 8-14, 4-8 mm distant, impressed above and raised and villous beneath, arcuate, sometimes bifurcate one-fourth to three-fourths distance to margin, with smaller intersecondary veins extending one-fourth to three-fourths distance to margin; free portion of petioles 0.2-1.3 cm long, smooth to verrucose, glabrous to villous, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths green, smooth, glabrous to villous, 1-2.5 x 0.5-1.1 cm at apex, notably inflated, flared at apex, terete, caducous, each distal margin with two fimbriate stipular appendages 2-3 mm long, extending 2-3 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 2-4.6 cm long, composed of solitary spikes borne on short erect peduncles; subtending bracts ovate to elliptic, 2-7x1-2 mm, acute at apex, obtuse to cuneate at base, entire; spikes (completely mature spikes not seen) 2-3.3 x 0.6-0.9 cm, with ca. 200 stamens; rachis with an irregularly margined basal annulus; anthers usually yellowish green sometimes reddish green, 2.5-3 x ca. 1.5 mm; connectives extended ca. 0.5 mm beyond thecae, acute. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, 1.2-4.2 cm long, composed of 1-3 cymules; bracts subtending cymules 0.7-2.3 x 0.2-0.6 cm, entire or dentate along margin, acute at apex; cymules green to greenish purple, globose, sessile or borne on short peduncles 0.6-1.5 cm long; terminal cymules 10-13 mm in diam., 7-15-flowered; lateral cymules 8-11 mm in diam., 5-8-flowered. Pistillate flowers trigonous, (3.5-)4-6 x 2-3 mm, with a pore on each face of ovary; perianth lobes 1.5-2 mm long, unequally united in lower one-fourth to three-fourths, with free portions, deltate, acute; stigmas white or purple, 2-3 mm long, linear, terete, with short papillae. Fruiting cymules dark purple, globose, 1-1.5 cm in diam. Seeds trigonous, 4-5 mm long, brown, smooth, with a small beak 0.3 mm long at apex.
bibliographicCitation: Todzia, Carol A. 1988. Chloranthaceae: Hedyosmum. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 48: 1-138.

description: Dioecious, aromatic, columnar trees with narrow crowns 5-30 m tall; trunks 15-40 cm dbh, with or without prop roots; bark gray; wood weak, white but turning orange when exposed to air; young stems quadrate, purple, smooth, glabrous, exuding mucilage when cut; older stems terete, smooth, glabrous, with leaf bases disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; internodes 1.3-3.3 cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves obovate, narrowly obovate, to narrowly elliptic, (5-)8-17(-19.2) x (1.7-)3-6.5(-8) cm, with acuminate, rounded, non-dentate tips 2-3(-9) mm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, margins crenate to serrate with teeth 2-5 (-9) mm distant beginning one-fourth to one-third distance from base, fleshy to coriaceous, smooth, glabrous, shiny or dull, dark green above, pale green beneath when fresh, drying chartaceous to coriaceous, smooth, light to dark brown above and beneath; midveins impressed above, raised and glabrous beneath; larger lateral veins 11-16, 6-7 mm distant, straight, leaving midvein at a 70°-90° angle, with smaller intersecondary veins visible or obscure and extending one-half to three-fourths distance to margin; free portions of petioles 0.3-0.9 cm long, smooth, glabrous to scurfy, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths smooth to verrucose, glabrous to scurfy, 0.7-2.7 x 0.4-0.9 cm at apex, notably inflated, terete, with distal margin chartaceous and without stipular appendages, extending 1-2 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 4.3-7.5 cm long, composed of 1-3 spikes on a short rachis 1-2.2 cm long; subtending bracts linear, small, 2-4 x ca. 1 mm; mature spikes 3.3-6.5 x 6-10 mm, with ca. 150 stamens, on short peduncles 2-7 mm long; stamens congested but becoming ca. 0.5 mm distant; rachis ca. 3 mm thick, with or without an irregularly margined basal annulus; anthers yellowish green, 1.5-2.5 x ca. 1.5 mm; connectives extended 0.3-0.5 mm beyond thecae, flattened at apex. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, 1.5-3.2 cm long, composed of 1-3 cymules on a short rachis 1-2.4 cm long; bracts at base of inflorescences lanceolate, obovate to narrowly elliptic, 3-10 x 1-2 mm, entire or wanting; cymules yellowish green, globose, (3-)5-7(-10)-flowered, (0.6-)0.8-1.3 cm in diam., borne on short peduncles 0.6-1.8 cm long; subtending floral bracts fused into a bract matrix enclosing flowers completely except for exserted stigmas. Pistillate flowers trigonous, 4-4.5 x 1.5-2.5 mm, with a pore on each face of ovary; perianth lobes 1-1.5 mm long, united in ca. lower three-fourths, with free portions acute; stigmas white or brown, 1.5-3 mm long, linear, terete, persistent, with very short papillae. Fruiting cymules purplish black, globose, 1-1.5 cm in diam. Seeds trigonous, ca. 4 x ca. 2 mm, white or brown, smooth.
bibliographicCitation: Todzia, Carol A. 1988. Chloranthaceae: Hedyosmum. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 48: 1-138.

description: Dioecious (rarely monoecious), aromatic trees or shrubs 2-9 m tall, with prop roots; wood white; young stems quadrate, green, smooth, glabrous; older stems terete, encircled with tubular leaf bases that ultimately disintegrate with age leaving encircling scars; internodes 4.5-9.5 cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic to narrowly obovate, (8.5-)14-22.5(-29) x 4.9-8.2(-10) cm, with acuminate tips 0.4-0.8(-1.2) cm long, narrowly cuneate at base, at margins serrulate with teeth 1.5-3 mm distant continuing all the way up to apex, fleshy, smooth, glabrous, dull light green above, strigose, light green beneath when fresh, drying subcoriaceous, scabrous, gray to brown above, light to medium brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised and strigose beneath with straight trichomes 0.30.5 mm long; larger lateral veins 11-14, 9-15 mm distant, arcuate to straight, impressed above, raised and strigose beneath, with smaller intersecondary veins extending one-third to two-thirds way to margin, these strigose and slightly raised beneath; free portion of petioles glabrous, 1.2-2 cm long, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths smooth, glabrous, 2.2-3(-3.5) x 1-1.5 cm, notably inflated, quadrangular, with or without a triangular patch of appressed hairs below distal margin, becoming black and ultimately disintegrating with age, each distal margin with two fimbriate stipular appendages 3-4 mm long, extending ca. 0.5 mm above free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 5-10.2 cm long, composed of 1-2 opposing (to subopposing) pairs of spikes on a short (2.8-5.8 cm long) rachis terminated by a single spike; subtending bracts linear, 3-10 x ca. 1 mm; mature spikes 2.3-6 x 0.5-0.7 cm, with 120-200 stamens, sessile or on short peduncles 1-6 mm long; stamens congested but becoming 0.5-1 mm distant; rachis ca. 0.5 mm broad with a thick, irregularly marginate, basal annulus, anthers yellowish green, ca. 2 x ca. 1 mm; connectives extended ca. 0.3 mm beyond thecae, acute. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal panicles, 6.5-12 cm long bearing 19-37 cymules; subtending inflorescence bracts 0.4-3.7 cm long, 0.11.3 cm broad, linear to spatulate, dentate to entire; cymules with (3-)6-9(-10) clustered flowers, (4-)5-6(-7) cm long and broad, borne on short peduncles 1-3 mm long, alternate or opposite on inflorescence axis, 2-11 mm distant; subtending floral bracts green to purplish green, connate in ca. lower three-fourths, 3-5 mm long including acute tips 0.5-1 x 2-4 mm, smooth to verrucose, cucullate, ciliate or entire along margin, enclosing ca. three-fourths of flower. Pistillate flowers ellipsoidal, 2-3 x ca. 1.5 mm, with three pores present or pores wanting; perianth lobes triangular, acute, ca. 1 mm long, connate in lower one-half; stigmas white, 2-3 mm long, linear, irregularly dissected, papillose. Fruiting cymules white, irregularly globose, 0.9-1.5 cm in diam. Seeds trigonous, ca. 2 mm long, ca. 1 mm broad on each face, brown, smooth.
bibliographicCitation: Todzia, Carol A. 1988. Chloranthaceae: Hedyosmum. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 48: 1-138.

description: Dioecious, aromatic shrubs or small trees 212 m tall; trunks single or several, 5-12 cm dbh, with prop roots; wood white, weak; twigs exuding clear mucilage when cut; young stems quadrate, green or often purple, floccose with clusters of brown hairs; older stems terete, brown, with leaf bases disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; internodes (3.8-)5-11 cm long. Leaves narrowly elliptic to narrowly obovate, (5-)8-19.2(-22) x (2.2-)4-7(-8) cm, terminating with acuminate tips 0.5-1 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, at margins serrate with teeth 3-8 mm distant, fleshy, smooth sometimes scabrous, dull sometimes shiny green above, light green beneath when fresh, drying stiffly chartaceous, smooth to scabrous, gray-brown above, reddish brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised and floccose beneath with conspicuous clusters of brown hairs; larger lateral veins 9-12, 8-14 mm distant, arcuate, slightly impressed above, raised and floccose beneath, with smaller intersecondary veins extending half-way to margin; free portion of petioles 0.7-1.5 cm long, floccose; petiolar sheaths green to sometimes purple, drying brown, 1.3-1.8 x 0.9-1.3 cm, floccose, becoming lacerated by tearing for 0.2-0.8 cm distally, persistent but breaking down with age, each distal margin with two minute, triangular, caducous stipular processes ca. 1 mm long, extending 1.53 mm above free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 4-8 cm long, usually cymose or with two opposing pairs of subsessile spikes borne on a short rachis 0.5-3 cm long terminated by a single spike, this subsessile or borne on short peduncles 2-3 mm long; spike clusters subtended by a pair of dentate cucullate bracts, 3-7 mm long and 1-3 mm broad; mature spikes 1.2-5.5 x 0.3-0.6 cm, with stamens becoming 1-2 mm distant on rachis; anthers green, 1.5-2 x ca. 0.5 mm, with connectives flattened distally and extending ca. 0.2 mm beyond thecae. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, racemes or panicles, (3-)5-9.5(-11) cm long, with 8-25 cymules; cymules (1-)2-3-flowered, 4-5 x 3-5 mm, opposite or alternate on the inflorescence axis, (3-)7-10(-12) mm distant, subsessile or on short peduncles ca. 2 mm long. Pistillate flowers green, sharply trigonous, 3-4 x 2-2.5 mm, exserted, free; ovary with a notably large pore on each face; perianth lobes ca. 0.3 mm long, acute at tip, fused in ca. lower one-half; subtending floral bracts 4-5 x 4-5 mm, united in lower one-half to three-quarters, acuminate at tip, glabrous, verrucose, ciliate along margin; stigmas white or purple, clavate to capitate, variable in shape, angled. Fruiting cymules white, 10-12 x 8-11 mm. Seeds 3-4 mm long, sharply trigonous, tan, minutely papillate.
bibliographicCitation: Todzia, Carol A. 1988. Chloranthaceae: Hedyosmum. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 48: 1-138.

description: Monoecious, aromatic shrubs 1-5 m tall; wood soft; bark light gray-brown; young stems quadrate; older stems terete, with leaf bases disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; upper and lower internodes of equal length, l-4(-6.2) cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves lanceolate, 5.3-13.5 x 1-2.4 cm, with acuminate tips 0.51 cm long, rounded to cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, margins serrate with teeth 2.5-4 mm distant, green to yellowish green, smooth, glabrous, succulent when fresh, drying chartaceous, grayish brown above, reddish brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath; lateral veins 6-9, 3.5-5 mm distant, obscure; intersecondary veins not visible; tertiary veins drying slightly impressed above giving dry laminae a mottled appearance; free portion of petioles 0.1-0.4 cm long; petiolar sheaths 0.4-1 x 0.4-0.9 cm, inflated, flared at apex, deciduous, at distal margin with two linear or fimbriate, stipular appendages ca. 0.1 mm long; not extended beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences axillary, solitary spikes 3.2-4.8 cm long originating below pistillate inflorescences, on peduncles 1.4-4 cm long emerging from inside the leaf sheaths; mature spikes 1-3.2 x 0.3-0.6 cm, stamens ca. 60, congested along axis; anthers green to yellow, 1.7-2 x ca. 1 mm; connectives 0.7-1 mm long, acute, projecting upwards. Pistillate inflorescences 2.3-3.8 cm long, spicate, variable in organization, solitary or bifurcate or 3-branched with two opposite basal lateral branches or with 3-4 pairs of opposite lateral branches; rachises notably zigzag with (4-) 13-23 solitary flowers borne alternately or suboppositely along rachis, 1-1.5 distant, sessile; sterile inflorescence bracts basal, 1-1.5 x 12 mm, entire or sparsely denticulose along margin; subtending floral bracts 1.5-3 x ca. 1 mm, ciliolate, not enclosing flower, persistent on rachis. Pistillate flowers pale green, 2-3 x ca. 1.5 mm, ellipsoidal or slightly trigonous with a pore on each face of perianth tissue; perianth lobes ca. 0.3 mm long, rounded at tips, free at base; stigmas 1-2 mm long, linear in outline, papillose. Fruits ellipsoidal, 2-3 x ca. 2.5 mm, red to orange. Seeds ca. 2 mm long, brown, smooth, trigonous.
bibliographicCitation: Todzia, Carol A. 1988. Chloranthaceae: Hedyosmum. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 48: 1-138.

description: Dioecious, glabrous, creeping, straggling subshrubs 0.5-1 m tall; young stems quadrate, with leaves evenly distributed on branches; older stems terete with the persisting leaf bases encircling the stem; lower and upper internodes of equal length, 2-6.3 cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic to narrowly obovate, (2.3-)4.5-7.5 (-8.8) x (0.5-)l.3-2.2 cm, acute at apex or with acuminate tips 0.3-0.6 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, notably coriaceous, subcrassulate, smooth, glabrous, drying dark reddish brown above, medium reddish brown beneath; margins subentire to obscurely serrate, often revolute, with teeth 4-8 mm distant beginning one-third to half-way up margins; midveins impressed above, raised beneath; lateral veins 58, not visible to obscure on both faces, 5-8 mm distant, arcuate; intersecondary and tertiary veins not visible; free portions of petioles 0.2-0.5 cm long, smooth, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths 0.5-0.6 x 0.3-0.7 cm, slightly inflated, persistent, with two raised longitudinal lines extending down sheath, at distal margin with two narrowly triangular stipular processes 1.2-2 mm long; not extending beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, solitary spikes, 2.4-4.3 cm long; mature spikes 1-3.2 x 0.4-0.5 cm, subsessile or on peduncles 0.2-0.5 cm long; subtending bracts linear, 0.30.6 cm long; stamens ca. 300, congested but becoming ca. 1 mm distant along rachis; anthers 1-2 x ca. 0.5 mm, with acute connective tips projecting ca. 0.5 mm beyond thecae. Pistillate inflorescences axillary, solitary spikes 1-1.8 cm long, with 4-10 sessile flowers arranged oppositely along rachis; subtending floral bracts ovate, 2-3 x ca. 2 mm, with linear to spatulate tips 46 mm long, entire or slightly ciliate. Pistillate flowers ellipsoidal to globose to slightly trigonous, 2.5-3 x 2-3 mm, with a pore on each face of ovary minute or wanting; perianth lobes shallowly triangular, acute at tip, 0.2-0.7 mm long, free at base; stigmas lanceolate in outline, 3-angled, 2-3.5 mm long. Fruits yellow to red, subglobose, ca. 5 x 3-4 mm. Seeds smooth, trigonous, 3-4 x ca. 2 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Todzia, Carol A. 1988. Chloranthaceae: Hedyosmum. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 48: 1-138.

description: Dioecious, glabrous shrubs 1-2 m tall; young stems quadrate; older stems terete, with old leaf bases disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; upper and lower internodes of more or less equal length, 2.2-5.4 cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves lanceolate to oblanceolate, 7.1-13.8 x 1.9-3.1 cm, with acuminate tips 0.2-1.3 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, margins serrate, with teeth 4-6 mm apart, smooth, glabrous, drying chartaceous to subcoriaceous, dark brown above, reddish brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath; lateral veins 10-18, 4-6 mm distant, narrow, visible above, slightly raised beneath; intersecondary and tertiary veins obscure; free portions of petioles 0.2-0.7 cm long, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths 0.9-1.2 x 0.7-1 cm, slightly inflated, disintegrating with age, with two raised longitudinal lines extending down sheath, between which sometimes occurs a hirsute area on distal margin, each distal margin with two fimbriate stipular processes ca. 2 mm long, extending 0-0.5 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences 2.5-4.2 cm long, either of solitary spikes in leaf axils (two per node) or of three spikes at stem tip with the central spike slightly larger and maturing first; mature spikes 2.2-3.8 x 0.5-0.6 cm, on short peduncles 0.1-0.6 cm long; subtending bracts paired, linear, 0.5-3 x 0.1-0.9 cm, dentate; stamens ca. 200, congested but becoming ca. 1 mm distant on rachis; rachis ca. 1 mm thick persisting after stamens have fallen; anthers ca. 2 x ca. 0.5 mm, with acute connectives projecting ca. 0.5 mm beyond thecae. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, solitary or compound spikes, 1.5-3.5 cm long; compound spikes composed of a long center spike with two shorter opposite basal spikes, each spike with 3-11 sessile flowers borne oppositely or alternately along axis; subtending floral bracts ovate at base with slender acuminate tips 2-9 mm long. Pistillate flowers ellipsoidal to globose, 2-4 x 2-3 mm, with a small, round to narrowly linear, ciliate pore ca. 0.5 mm in diam. in the perianth tissue on each face of the ovary or pore wanting; perianth lobes shallowly triangular, ca. 0.5 mm long, acute at tips, free to base; stigmas lanceolate to oblanceolate in outline, 1-3 mm long, papillose. Fruits yellow, ellipsoidal to globose, 3-4 x 2.5-3 mm. Seeds ca. 3 mm long, trigonous, smooth.

description: Dioecious, glabrous herbs or shrubs 1-2 m tall, 2-15.5 cm dbh; wood soft; branches often drooping; young stems quadrate, with leaves notably congested at ends of branches; older stems terete, sometimes hollow, with old leaf bases disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; upper internodes condensed, 0.5-2 cm long, with petiolar sheaths overlapping; lower internodes elongate, 8-12.5 cm long. Leaves lanceolate to linear-oblong, (8.8-) 14.5-24.5 x 1.1-3.4 cm, with 1.2-1.8 cm long acuminate tips, narrowly cuneate at base, margins serrate with teeth 5-9 mm apart (these drying white) beginning 2.7-4.5 cm from base, smooth, glabrous, green above, light green beneath when fresh, drying chartaceous to subcoriaceous, grayish brown above, reddish brown beneath; midveins impressed above, slightly raised beneath; lateral veins 16-25, 4-9 mm distant, slightly arcuate, narrow, obscure above, slightly raised beneath; intersecondary and tertiary veins obscure; free portions of petioles 1-3.5 cm long; petiolar sheaths 0.7-1 x 0.5-1 cm, glabrous, smooth, inflated, flared at apex, drying light brown, thin and almost translucent, disintegrating with age, each distal margin entire or with two small, slightly fimbriate, caducous, stipular processes ca. 1 mm long; not extending beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences axillary or terminal, simple or compound racemes with cymose clusters of spikes borne at nodes, 2.2-4 cm long; nodes 2-4; mature spikes 5-6 mm long, 3-6 thick, borne at the tips of peduncles 2-3 cm long; subtending bract laminae ovate ca. 3 x ca. 3 mm, with long slender caudate tips (0.4-)2.7-7.5 cm long; stamens ca. 300, congested but becoming ca. 1 mm distant on rachis; rachises persisting after stamens have fallen; anthers green, 1.5-2 x ca. 0.5 mm; connectives projecting ca. 0.5 mm beyond thecae, triangular, acute at tip, with margin drying white. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, branched or unbranched spikes (1-)2-6.2 cm long, with 14-25 sessile flowers congested and alternate on rachis 1-1.5 mm distant; subtending floral bracts round to ovate, 5-6 x ca. 5 mm, partially to completely enclosing flower, with caudate tips 11-22 x 1-1.3 mm. Pistillate flowers green, trigonous, 2-3 x 1-1.5 mm, with an elliptic, irregular, ciliate pore in perianth tissue on each face of ovary; perianth lobes triangular, 0.7-1 mm long, acute at tips, free at base; stigmas greenish with red tips, 1-2.5 mm long, lanceolate in outline, irregularly lobulate, papillose. Fruits ellipsoidal, 3-4 x ca. 2 mm. Seeds ca. 3 mm long, trigonous, deeply wrinkled.

description: Dioecious, aromatic trees or shrubs 2-5 (-10) m tall, 8-18 cm dbh, with prop roots; wood white, turning orange when exposed to air, weak; young stems quadrate, green or purple, glabrous, smooth; large stems terete, encircled by gray-white persistent tubular chartaceous leaf bases; internodes unequal, upper internodes shorter, 0.9-1.5 cm long, and lower internodes longer, 2.1-2.8(-4.4) cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves ovate, obovate or elliptic, (3.3-)5-7.1(-9.3) x (1.3-)1.8-3.5(-4) cm, with acuminate dentate tips 2-4 mm long, cuneate at base, margins serrulate with teeth 1-1.5 mm distant, these beginning near base, coriaceous, smooth, glabrous, shiny dark green above, light green beneath when fresh, drying smooth, mottled grayish brown above, medium brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath, glabrous; lateral veins 5-7, 6-8 mm distant, arcuate, departing midvein at a 45° angle, slightly raised above and beneath; free portion of petioles smooth to asperous, glabrous, (0.1-)0.3-0.7(-l) cm long, narrowly winged, young petioles with white glands, petiolar sheaths smooth, glabrous, 0.7-1.1(-1.4) x 0.5-0.6(-0.9)cm, inflated, terete or quadrangular, flared at apex, with or without two parallel longitudinal raised lines running down from stipular processes, with a small striate patch at distal margin below stipular processes on outer side of longitudinal lines, persistent, becoming gray to white, each distal margin with two linear stipular appendages ca. 1.3 mm long, these caducous leaving minute deltoid projections, extending ca. 0.5 mm above free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences axillary or terminal, 2-3 cm long, composed of 1-2 opposing pairs of spikes on a short (0.3-1 cm long) rachis terminated by a single spike; inflorescence bracts 0.2-0.5(-1.7) x 0.1-0.6 cm, linear, cucullate at base, intergrading with leaves; mature spikes 1.3-2.3 cm long, 3-4 mm broad, with 4080 stamens, sessile or borne on short peduncles 1-2 mm long, subtended by a small, entire bract 0.2-0.5 cm long, ca. 1 mm broad; stamens congested but becoming 0.5 mm distant; rachis ca. 0.5 mm thick; anthers 1-1.3(-1.5) x ca. 0.5 mm; connective extended ca. 0.2 mm beyond thecae, either flattened or acute. Pistillate inflorescences of axillary or terminal, simple or basally branched racemes 1.1-2.7(-3.4) cm long bearing 5-10 cymules; subtending inflorescence bracts 0.3-1 x 0.1-0.3 cm, dentate or entire; cymules with 2-4 clustered flowers, 3-5 x 3-5 mm, opposite or alternate on inflorescence axis, 2-5 mm distant, subsessile or borne on short peduncles 0.5-1(-2) mm long; subtending floral bracts connate in lower one-third to two-thirds, 1.5-2 mm long with acuminate tips 1-1.5 mm long, 2-3 mm broad, entire along margin, enclosing ca. one-half of flower. Pistillate flowers trigonous, ca. 2 x ca. 1 mm, with a notably large pore on each face; perianth lobes triangular, 0.3-0.5 mm long, basally fused, acute at tips; stigmas white, (1-)2-2.5 mm long, 3-angled, linear to narrowly clavate, elaborated distally, papillose. Fruiting cymules irregularly globose, white, 4-7 mm in diam. Seeds trigonous, ca. 2 x ca. 1 mm, brown, papillate.

description: Small dioecious trees 3.5-10 m tall; trunks to 8-10 cm dbh, much-branched, forming a dense crown; wood white; smaller stems quadrate, green; older stems terete, glabrous, gray, encircled by leaf-sheath scars; internodes 1-3 cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves ovate to obovate, 2.5-4 x 1-1.5 cm broad, with long-acuminate to caudate apices 4-7 mm long, cuneate at base, at margin ascending serrate with 4-6 teeth on each side, these 4-8 mm distant, glabrous, smooth, aromatic, moderately succulent, drying chartaceous, dark green, shiny above, light green, dull below, drying slaty dark brown above, reddish brown beneath, with midveins impressed above, raised beneath; lateral veins six, 2.5-4 mm distant, arcuate, drying obscure above and slightly raised beneath; tertiary veins not visible; free portion of petioles 0.2-0.8 cm long, narrowly wing-margined; petiolar sheaths 0.2-0.6 cm long, flaring somewhat at apex, drying angled, persisting for a short time but disintegrating with age, each distal margin entire, with two erose persistent appendages ca. 2 mm long and with 1-3 additional much shorter appendages, not extending beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences solitary, terminal or axillary spikes; mature spikes 0.7-1.3 cm long, borne on peduncles approximately 5 mm long, subtended by a cucullate bract 4 mm long, with 40-55 stamens, these becoming 0.5-1 mm distant on rachis; anthers 1-1.5 x 0.5 mm; connectives ca. 0.2 mm long, distally flattened. Pistillate inflorescences 1-3 terminal or axillary, solitary cymules, borne on long-pendent peduncles, 1-2 mm long arising from within the leaf sheath; cymules with 2-3 imbricately arranged flowers, 0.5-0.7 x 0.6-0.9 cm, often with empty bracts included in cymule; subtending floral bracts green to greenish white, ca. 4 x 4 mm, acuminate at the apex, united in lower fourth to third. Pistillate flowers green, trigonous, 4-5 x ca. 2 mm, with a small pore on each face of the ovary; perianth lobes ca. 1 mm long, slightly retuse at apex, free to base; stigmas white, linear, 3-4 mm long, 3-angled, minutely papillose, elaborated distally. Fruiting cymules not seen.

description: Dioecious, aromatic shrubs with many stems, or small trees 3-6 m tall, 3-6 cm dbh, with or without prop roots; wood white, turning orange when exposed to air; young stems quadrate, green, purple, or brown, scurfy; older stems terete, gray to brown, glabrous to scurfy, encircled by persistent, tubular leaf bases that become fibrous with age; internodes 1.5-5.4 cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic to elliptic, (4-)5-10(-11.5) x 1.8-4.3 cm, with acuminate tips 0.50.7 cm long, obtuse to cuneate at base, coriaceous, smooth, glabrous, shiny or dull dark green above, dark reddish brown beneath; margins crenulate with teeth 2.5-3 mm distant, entire in lower one-fourth to one-third, sometimes revolute; midveins impressed above, raised beneath, glabrous or with sparse white trichomes; lateral veins obscure, 7-11, 7-9 mm distant, arcuate, leaving midveins at a 45° angle, not notably impressed above, slightly raised and glabrous beneath, with obscure intersecondary veins extending ca. half-way to margins; free portion of petioles glabrous to scurfy, 0.3-1 cm long, ca. 1.5 mm broad, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths scurfy, 1.4-1.8 x 0.7-1.2 cm, purple, terete or quadrangular, inflated, flared at apex, becoming gray and fibrous with age, with two longitudinal, parallel, raised, ciliate lines extending down from distal margins, each distal margin with two fimbriate stipular processes ca. 2 mm long, becoming laciniate down center with age, not extending above free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, (3-)4.3-6.8(-7.3) cm long, composed of 2-3 opposing nodes with 1-3 spikes per node along rachis terminated by a single spike, occasionally with two lateral, basal branches, these with a terminal cluster of three spikes; inflorescence bracts 0.5-l(-1.4) x 0.10.3 mm, dentate, leaf-like; bracts subtending spikes 1-4 mm long, entire or ciliate to fimbriate, ovate at base, acuminate at apex; mature spikes 1.5-3 x 4-6 mm, with 80-180 stamens, subsessile or borne on peduncles 0.2-0.8(-l. 1) cm long; rachis ca. 1 mm thick with a thickened, entire or dissected, basal annulus; anthers green, ca. 1.5 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm thick at middle; connectives extended ca. 0.3 mm beyond thecae, flattened, with the margin ciliate, with an abrupt apicule. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, racemes or panicles, 1.8-2.9 cm long bearing (3-)6-9(-15) cymules; subtending inflorescence bracts 0.5-1.6 x 0.2-0.4 cm, dentate, leaf-like; cymules with (2-)3-4(-5) clustered flowers, 4-5 x 4-6 mm, alternate or opposite on inflorescence axis, 3-7 mm distant, sessile or borne on short peduncles 1-2 mm long; subtending floral bracts green, connate in lower one-half to three-fourths of margin, 3.5-4.5 mm long including acuminate tips ca. 1 mm long, ca. 3 mm broad, slightly verrucose, cucullate, enclosing one-half to three-fourths of flower. Pistillate flowers trigonous, 2-3 x 1.5-2 mm, with a small pore on each face of ovary; perianth lobes shallowly triangular, 0.5-0.7 mm long, acute at tips, united at base; stigmas white to purple, 2-3 mm long, clavate, flattened to 3-angled, elaborated distally, papillose. Fruiting cymules white, globose, 7-9 mm in diam. Seeds ca. 2.5 mm long, trigonous, smooth.
bibliographicCitation: Todzia, Carol A. 1988. Chloranthaceae: Hedyosmum. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 48: 1-138.

description: Dioecious, aromatic shrubs or small trees 2-8 m tall, 3-11 cm dbh, with prop roots; bark gray, smooth; wood white, turning orange when exposed to air, exuding mucilage when cut; young stems quadrate, purple or green, glabrous; older stems terete, gray to brown, encircled by persistent, gray to white leaf bases; internodes l-3(-4) cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic to obovate, 5.5-8.8(-10.2) x 2.5-3.5(-4.8) cm, with acuminate tips 0.2-0.5 cm long, cuneate to attenuate at base, coriaceous, glabrous, smooth, shiny dark green, punctate above, dull light green beneath when fresh, drying smooth, light to dark reddish brown above and beneath; margins serrate to crenulate, with teeth ascending, 2-3 mm distant, entire in lower one-third to one-half; midveins impressed above, raised beneath, usually glabrous but occasionally sparsely strigose; lateral veins 5-8(-10), 7-9 mm distant, slightly arcuate, leaving midvein at a 45° angle, slightly raised beneath, with obscure intersecondary veins extending ca. half-way to margin; free portion of petioles smooth, glabrous, 0.6-0.9(-1 .6) cm long, ca. 2 mm broad, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths smooth, glabrous, 1.3-1.8 x 0.5-1.0 cm at apex, usually purple, sometimes green, terete or quadrangular, inflated, flared at apex, persistent and becoming grayish white with age, each distal margin with two fimbriate, caducous, stipular processes 1-2 mm long, becoming laciniate with age at distal margin, not extending beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 3-6 cm long, composed of 2-3 opposing pairs of spikes on a short rachis terminated by a single spike; bracts at base of inflorescence 0.6-1.5 x 0.1-0.6 cm; spikes (fully mature spikes not seen) 0.9-1.2 x 0.4-0.6 cm, with 80-100 stamens, with a basal ciliate annulus, subtended by one or three small entire bracts, these 0.1-0.3 mm long, ovate at base, acuminate at apex, entire; anthers green, 1-1.5 x ca. 0.5 mm; connectives extended ca. 0.5 mm beyond thecae, flattened at apex. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, pendulous, racemes or panicles, (1.1-)2-3.8(-4.3) cm long bearing 6-8(-11) cymules; subtending inflorescence bracts 0.5-1.3 x 0.1-0.8 cm, entire or dentate; cymules with 2-3(-4) imbricately arranged flowers, 5-7 x 4-7 mm, alternate or opposite on inflorescence axis, 2-9 mm distant, sessile or borne on short peduncles 1-5 mm long; subtending floral bracts green, free to base or connate in lower one-fourth, (1-)4-6 mm long including acuminate tips 1-2 mm long, 2-3 mm broad at base, with prominent medial ridge, entire or long ciliate on margin, either not enclosing the flower or enclosing lower one-fourth to one-half of flower. Pistillate flowers sharply trigonous, 3-4 x ca. 2 mm, with a pore on each face of ovary; perianth lobes fleshy, deltate, acute, 0.5-0.8 mm long, basally united; stigmas brown, clavate, ca. 3 mm long, elaborated distally, papillose. Fruiting cymules white, 0.9-1.2 x 0.7-1.1 mm. Seeds 3-4 mm long, brown, sharply trigonous, smooth.
bibliographicCitation: Todzia, Carol A. 1988. Chloranthaceae: Hedyosmum. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 48: 1-138.

description: Dioecious, aromatic trees or shrubs 2-9 m tall, 4-30 cm dbh, with prop roots; young stems quadrate, green; older stems terete, encircled by gray, persistent leaf sheaths; internodes (2.1-)3-5.6(-8.5) cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves elliptic to obovate, 6-15(-l 8.5) x 2.1-7 cm, with acuminate tips 0.3-0.9 cm long, cuneate at base, at margins bluntly serrulate with teeth 1-2 mm distant, coriaceous, dull or shiny, smooth, glabrous above, sparsely to densely strigose to glabrous beneath with trichomes 0.5-1 mm long, light green above when fresh, drying brittle, smooth, slate gray above, reddish brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised and villous beneath, with twisted trichomes 1-2 mm long; larger lateral veins 8-11, 0.6-1.3 cm distant, arcuate, often dark, raised or not, with obscure intersecondary veins extending ca. one-half way to margin; free portion of petioles glabrous, 0.4-0.8(-1.3) cm long, very narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths (0.8-) 1.7-2.5 x 0.6-0.9 cm at apex, green or purple when young, turning gray with age, drying reddish brown, terete or quadrangular, notably inflated, persistent, flared at apex, with distal margins becoming dry and membranous, glabrous or with two raised ciliate lines running down from the stipular processes, each distal margin entire, with two linear to fimbriate stipular processes 1-2 mm long, extending 0-0.5 mm beyond free portion of petiole. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, (2.1-)3.2-5.2 cm long, usually composed of an opposing pair of spikes borne on a short rachis 0.8-1.7(-2.6) cm long terminated by a single spike or sometimes consisting of a solitary spike; spikes subsessile or borne on short peduncles up to 6 mm long, subtended by dentate bracts 0.3-2 cm long, these ovate at the base, acuminate at apex, at maturity 1.6-4.5 x 0.5-0.9 cm, with 140— 200(-300) stamens, these becoming 1-2 mm distant on rachis; rachis 1-2 mm thick, persistent or caducous; anthers green, 1-2.3 x 0.5-1 mm, with connective ca. 0.5 mm thick with a black upwardly projecting apicule ca. 1 mm long. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal panicles 3-5.6(-6.5) cm long bearing 9-12 cymules; inflorescence bracts 0.5-2.2 x 0.2-1.4 cm, dentate, ovate to obovate, acute to acuminate at tip, cuneate at base; cymules (l-)2(-4)-flowered, (4-) 5-6(-8) x (3-)4-5(-7) mm, opposite or alternate on inflorescence axis, 4-8(-12) mm distant, borne on short peduncles 1-3 mm long; subtending floral bracts green to greenish purple, 2.5-4 mm long with acuminate tips 1-2 x 2-3 mm, connate with adjacent bracts in lower three-fourths, with margin entire or ciliate, enclosing the flower three-fourths to completely. Pistillate flowers green, ellipsoidal, 2.5-3 x ca. 2 mm, with three small pores forming a ring around the middle of the tissue covering the ovary; perianth lobes united forming a collar on top of ovary 0.7-1 mm long with lobes rounded and barely visible; stigmas (2-)3-4.5 mm long, linear, 3-angled, persistent or caducous. Fruiting cymules white, irregularly globose, 6-9 x 5-8 cm. Seeds ca. 3 mm long, trigonous or tetragonous, brown, smooth.

description: Dioecious, aromatic shrubs or trees 1-8 m tall, with prop roots; bark smooth, gray; wood white, weak, exuding mucilage and orange resin when cut; young stems quadrate, usually purple, sometimes green, smooth to asperous; older stems terete, smooth, with gray tubular leaf bases encircling stem; internodes 2.2-3.7(-6) cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves narrowly oblong to narrowly elliptic, 5.2-11.5(-16) x (1.8-)2.2-4. l(-5) cm, with acuminate dentate tips 0.5-1.3 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, at margins sharply serrate with teeth ascending (often white-tipped) 2.5-4 mm distant, entire in lower one-eighth to one-fourth, fleshy, brittle, smooth, glabrous, medium to dark green, shiny above, greenish yellow, dull beneath, drying subcoriaceous, smooth, reddish brown to gray above, reddish brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath, with or without purple or tan ramentaceous scales on the proximal half, distal half glabrous; lateral veins obscure, 10-13, 7-10 mm distant, arcuate; intersecondary veins not visible; free portion of petioles smooth, 0.3-0.7 cm long, with or without ramentaceous scales on dorsal surface, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths smooth or scaly, glabrous, 1.101.7(02) x (0.5-)0.7-1.1(-1.3) cm at apex, terete or quadrangular, inflated, often striate below distal margin, with or without two raised, longitudinal lines extending down length of sheath, persistent and becoming gray with age, sometimes weakly laciniate down middle, lacking stipular appendages, extending 0.5-1 mm above free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 2.2-5.1(-8.2) cm long, composed of 1-3 opposing pairs of spikes on a short (1.1-3.3 cm long) rachis terminated by a single spike; bracts subtending spikes 0.1-0.5 x ca. 1 mm, linear, entire, cucullate at base, acuminate at apex; mature spikes 1.7-2.9 x 0.3-0.6 cm, with 70-160 stamens, subsessile or borne on peduncles 0.1-0.3 cm long, stamens congested on axis but becoming ca. 0.1 mm distant; rachis ca. 3 mm thick, with a thickened, entire or lacerate, basal annulus; anthers green, 1.2-1.5 x ca. 0.75 mm, connective ca. 0.3 mm long, flattened or acute. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, erect, straight, simple or basally branched racemes, (2.8-)3.5-5 cm long bearing 6-12 cymules; subtending inflorescence bracts 0.4-1.7 x 1-3 mm, dentate or entire, cucullate at base; cymules with clusters of 4-7 flowers, 5-6 x 4-6 mm, opposite or subopposite on inflorescence axis, (4-)6-9(011) mm distant, borne on peduncles 1-5 mm long; subtending floral bracts 3-4 mm long including acuminate tips 0.5-1 mm long, ca. 2 mm broad, entire on margins, completely connate with adjacent bracts or connate in lower three-fourths. Pistillate flowers ellipsoidal, 2-2.5 x ca. 1 mm, with pores on ovary obscure or wanting; perianth lobes shallowly triangular, ca. 0.3 mm long, basally united; stigmas white, ca. 2 mm long, linear, terete. Fruiting cymules white, irregularly globose, 9-13 mm in diam. Seeds ca. 2 mm long, brown, trigonous, smooth, completely embedded in bract matrix.

description: Monoecious or dioecious, aromatic, glabrous shrubs or small trees 2-10 m tall; trunk 7-20 cm dbh, with prop roots; bark gray; wood white turning orange when exposed to air, with or without latex; twigs extruding mucilage when cut; young stems quadrate, glabrous, scabrous; older stems terete, smooth, encircled by persistent leaf sheaths; internodes 2-7.3 cm long. Leaves elliptic, narrowly elliptic, broadly oblong, or slightly obovate, (4.5-)8.5-22(-27) x (2.8-)3.5-6(-8.8) cm, terminating with acuminate tips 0.3-1.0 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, at margins serrulate with teeth 2-5 mm distant, fleshy, smooth, bright green, shiny above, grey-green beneath when fresh, drying stiffly chartaceous, scabrous, gray to brown above, often mottled, light reddish brown beneath; midveins sunken above, raised and glabrous beneath; larger lateral veins 6-10, 10-19 mm distant, sharply arcuate, with smaller intersecondary veins obscure, extending one-half distance to margin; free portion of petioles 0.4-1.4(-2.4) cm long, scabrous; petiolar sheaths 1.3-2.2 x 0.8-2 cm, scabrous, becoming lacerated by irregular tearing for 0.2-1.8 cm distally, with two distinct longitudinal raised lines extending down sheath marked with fimbriate processes that often continue on to free portion of petioles, persistent and breaking down with age, not extending beyond free portion of petioles, each distal margin with two linear to slightly fimbriate stipular appendages 2-3 mm long. Staminate inflorescences dimorphic on unisexual and bisexual plants. In unisexual plants, staminate inflorescences usually of two or three opposing pairs of subsessile spikes borne on a short rachis 2-4 cm long, terminated by a single sometimes pedunculate spike; lower spikes subtended by dentate leafy bracts 12-18 x 2-4 mm; mature spikes 1.5-5.5 x 0.5-0.7 cm, with 100-150 stamens, these becoming 1-2 mm distant on rachis; rachises 2-3 mm thick; anthers green to yellowish green, 1.8-2.8 x ca. 0.5 mm; connectives extending ca. 0.5 mm beyond the thecae as a brown, acute tip. In bisexual plants, staminate inflorescences of solitary spikes 0.3-2.2 x 0.2-0.4 cm, subsessile or borne on peduncles 2-9 mm long, with ca. 21-50 stamens; anthers 1.5-2 x ca. 0.4 mm; connectives extended ca. 0.2 mm beyond the thecae as a brown, acute tip. Pistillate and bisexual inflorescences axillary or terminal, racemes or panicles 4.3-9.5(-14) cm long, with 15-55 cymules, at base subtended by sterile dentate bracts (1-)6-14 mm long; cymules with (1-)2(-4) clustered flowers, 3- 4 x 2-3 mm, opposite or alternate on the inflorescence axis, 3-8 mm distant, borne on short peduncles 1-3 mm long. Pistillate flowers green, ellipsoidal, 3-4 mm long, 2-2.5 mm wide; perianth lobes ca. 0.3 mm long, acute or rounded at tips, fused almost to apices; subtending floral bracts 4-5 mm long, united in lower one-fourth to one-half, enclosing lower half of flower; stigmas white, papillose, 2-5 mm long, variable in shape, angled. Fruiting cymules white, 8-12 x 6-10 mm, irregularly ellipsoidal to globose. Seeds ca. 2 mm long, ellipsoidal, trigonous, light tan to brown, minutely papillate.
