description: Dioecious(?), glabrous trees 3-6(-15) m tall; internodes 1-4 cm long; young stems quadrate; older stems terete, encircled by leaf-sheath scars; internodes 1.1-5 cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 3-4.4(-6.3) x 1.8-2.5 cm, apically acute, basally obtuse to cuneate, decurrent on petiole, glabrous, smooth, coriaceous, drying slaty dark brown above, reddish brown beneath, with midvein impressed above, raised beneath; lateral veins 7-10, 4-7 mm distant, obscure or slightly raised above and beneath, forming a distinct, nearly straight submarginal vein 1-3 mm from lamina margin; margins often revolute, serrate with teeth ca. 2.5 mm apart; free portions of petioles 0.3-0.9 cm long, slightly winged on margin; petiolar sheaths 0.4-0.8 x 0.4-0.6 cm, flared at apex, each margin with two minute, ca. 0.5 mm long, persistent, narrowly triangular, stipular processes, extended ca. 0.5 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences 1.2-1.7 cm long, composed of 1-3 axillary or terminal spikes; mature spikes 0.8-1.2(-3) cm long, with 100-150 anthers; anthers 0.7-1.2 x 0.5-1 mm; connectives ca. 0.3 mm long with a short hyaline apicule. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, branched or unbranched racemes, 0.9-2.2 cm long, often pendent, with 2-6 oppositely arranged cymules; cymules 1 (-2) flowered, 4-5 x 3-4 mm; subtending sterile cymule bracts, cucullate, acuminate at apex, ciliolate on margin, subtending floral bracts 2-3, up to 3 mm long, acute at tip, uniting at base to form a cupule around lower half to three-fourths of flower. Pistillate flowers trigonous, with a pore on each face of ovary, 3-4 x 2-3 mm; perianth lobes 0.5-1 mm long, rounded at apex, free to base; stigmas 2-3 mm long, clavate to linear in outline, 3-angled, elaborated distally. Fruiting cymules purple, globose to oblong, 6-8 x 3.5-5(-8) mm. Seeds 4-5 x 2-3 mm, trigonous, smooth.

description: Arbor vel frutex 4-10 m alta, dioecia; caulibus glabris vel verrucatis, intemodiis 2-3.9 cm longis; foliorum laminis ovatis vel late ellipticis apicibus acuminatis vel acutis basibus obtusis vel truncatis, marginibus crenulatis dentibus 2-5 mm distantibus parte inferiore ¼ vel 1/3 integris, nervis secundariis subtus prominentibus utroque latere 10-13 parallelis subangulo circa 7 5°-8 5° exorien-tibus nervo fere recto submarginali circa 2 mm a margine, nervis intermediis obscuris usque 2/3 vel ommino ad margenes; petiolis verrucatis 59 mm longis, vaginis 1.2-1.9 cm longis, 0.5-1.1 cm latis apicibus prolongatis ultra petiolos 0.51 mm; stipulis parvis linearibus; inflorescentia staminata 2.6-7.4 cm longa, spicis 1.5-2.3 cm longis 0.3-0.4 cm latis; staminibus ca. 125, 1-1.3 mm longis ca. 0.5 mm latis, connectivo ca. 0.3 mm longo; inflorescentia pistillata racemosa 2.0-4.1 cm longa 4-12 cymulis munita, cymulis 2-3-floris 5-11 mm distantibus sessilibus, bracteis floralibus 3-3.5 mm longis 1.5-2 mm latis, basi liberis vel parte inferiore ¼ connatis, floribus pistillatis valde trigonis 3-4 mm longis paginis omnibus ca. 2.5 mm latis, ovario poro magno instructo, perianthii lobis deltoideis ca. 0.5 mm longis apice acutis vel rotundatis basi liberis; stig-matibus ca. 2 mm longis, cymulis fructiferis 68 mm longis, 5-6 mm latis rubris vel purpureis.

description: Dioecious shrubs or trees 4-10 m tall; young stems quadrate, smooth or verrucose, glabrous; older stems terete, glabrous, with leaf sheaths disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; internodes 2-3.9 cm long; nodes only slightly swollen. Leaves ovate to widely elliptic, (4.4-)6.1-8.5 x (3-)3.4-5.5(-6.4) cm, acute to acuminate with tips 0.1-0.3 cm long, obtuse to truncate at base, margins crenate to crenulate with teeth 2-5 mm distant, entire in lower one-fourth to one-third, glabrous, shiny, medium green above, dull pale green beneath, drying coriaceous, smooth, light to dark brown above, medium brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath, glabrous; larger lateral veins 10-13, 4-5 mm distant, straight, leaving midvein at a 75°-85° angle, raised beneath, with obscure intersecondary veins extending two-thirds to completely to margin, forming a nearly straight submarginal vein ca. 2 mm from margin; free portion of petioles verrucose, 5-9 mm long, ca. 2 mm thick, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths 1.2-1.9 x 0.5-1.1 cm at apex, only slightly inflated, flared at apex, terete, caducous, verrucose, glabrous, extending 0.5-1 mm beyond free portion of petiole, each distal margin with two minute awn-like processes or wanting. Staminate inflorescences 2.6-7.4 cm long, composed of two nodes with 1-3 spikes per node; mature spikes 1.5-2.3 x 0.30.4 cm, sessile, subtended by an entire cymbiform, acuminate bract 2-4 mm long; stamens ca. 125, congested on axis, 1-1.3 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm broad, connective ca. 0.3 mm long, flattened distally, with a minute, acute, white tip. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, simple or basally branched racemes, 2-4.1 cm long bearing 4-12 cymules, united with stem 0.1-0.4 cm above leaf sheath; subtending inflorescence bracts, 0.2-1.1 cm long, 0.1-0.6 cm broad, entire or dentate, acute at apex, cucullate at base; cymules with 23 clustered flowers, opposite on inflorescence axis, 5-11 mm distant, sessile; subtending floral bracts 3-3.5 x 1.5-2 mm, free to base or connate to lower one-fourth, acute at apex, with margin entire. Pistillate flowers strongly trigonous, 3-4 mm long, ca. 2.5 mm broad on each face, with a large pore on each face of ovary; perianth lobes deltate, ca. 0.5 mm long, acute to rounded at apex, free to base; stigmas ca. 2 mm long, obpyramidal, long-papillose. Fruiting cymules red to purple, 6-8 x 5-6 mm. Seeds ca. 4 mm long, strongly trigonous, light brown, minutely papillate.

description: Dioecious, aromatic trees or shrubs 2-10 m tall, 4-15 cm dbh, with prop roots; bark gray-brown; wood white, brittle; young stems quadrate, green or purple; older stems terete, encircled by gray to white, persistent leaf sheaths; internodes 3-5.8(-7) cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic, elliptic, to slightly obovate, (4.4-)5.2-l 1.4(-14) x 2-4.3(-5.1) cm, with acuminate tips 0.2-0.8 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, at margins crenulate to bluntly serrulate with teeth 1.5-3(-4) mm distant, coriaceous, shiny, glabrous, dark to bright green above, dull yellowish green beneath when fresh, drying smooth, light gray-brown to dark brown above, reddish brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised and ramentaceous beneath; larger lateral veins 8-9(-12), 6-9 mm distant, dark brown, arcuate, leaving at 90° angle from midvein, flush with surface, with obscure intersecondary veins extending ca. halfway to margin; free portion of petioles 0.5-0.8 cm long, smooth, glabrous or ramentaceous, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths 1-1.4(-1.6) x 0.4-0.7(-l.l) cm, slightly inflated, flared at apex, smooth or with two raised lines extending down from stipular processes 1 mm distant, persistent, becoming gray to white, each distal margin entire, with two linear to slightly fimbriate, caducous, stipular appendages 1-1.5 mm long, extending ca. 0.5 above free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 58 cm long, composed of 1-2 opposing pairs of spikes borne on a short rachis 0.9-3(-4.4) cm long terminated by a single spike; spikes on peduncles up to 9 mm long, subtended by dentate bracts (0.3-) 1.3-2.6 x 1-2 mm; mature spikes 1.7-5.7 x 0.6-0.9 cm, with 150-250 stamens, these becoming 1-2 mm distant on rachis at maturity; rachis 1-2 mm thick, caducous; anthers green, 1.5-2 x 0.5-1 mm; connectives extended 0.3-0.5(-0.8) mm beyond thecae, acute. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, simple or basally branched racemes (1.9-)3-4.2(-5.2) cm long bearing 4-12 cymules; inflorescence bracts (0.3-)l.3-2.6 cm long, 0.1-1.5 cm broad, leaflike; cymules with (l-)2-3(-4) imbricately arranged flowers, (4-)5-6 x 3-5 mm, usually opposite, sometimes alternate on inflorescence axis, 2-9 mm distant, borne on short peduncles 1-2 mm long; subtending floral bracts green, greenish purple or purple, (1-)3-4(-5) mm long including acuminate tips 0.5-1 x 2-3 mm, connate with adjacent bracts in lower one-fourth to three-fourths, with margin entire, enclosing one-fourth to three-fourths of flower. Pistillate flowers green, trigonous, 2-3 x ca. 1.5 mm, with a minute pore forming on each face of ovary or pores wanting; perianth lobes united to form a collar on top of ovary 0.4-1 mm long, with free portion of lobes ca. 0.3 mm long; stigmas 1.5-2.5 mm long, linear, 3-angled, caducous. Fruiting cymules white, 6-10 x 5-8 mm. Seeds ca. 3 x ca. 2 mm, trigonous, brown or black, smooth.

description: Monoecious or dioecious, aromatic, glabrous shrubs or small trees 3-7 m tall; bark gray, smooth; trunk with prop roots; wood white, turning orange when exposed to air; twigs extruding mucilage when cut; young stems quadrate; older stems terete, encircled by leaf-sheath scars; internodes 4.5-7(-8) cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic to elliptic, (4.3-)8-15(-20) x 2-5(-7) cm, with acuminate to caudate tips, 0.8-1.6 cm long, rounded to broadly cuneate at base, at margin serrate with teeth 5-7(-10) mm distant, glabrous, drying smooth stiffly chartaceous to coriaceous, with midveins impressed above, raised beneath and glabrous; larger lateral veins 12-26(-35), 4-7 mm distant, at 90° to midvein, impressed above and prominently raised beneath, with obscure intersecondary veins extending one-half to three-fourths distance to margin; free portion of petioles 0.8-2(-3) cm long; petiolar sheaths 0.7-1.7 cm long, slightly flared at apex, each distal margin with two minute, caducous, linear, stipular appendages 1 mm long, extending 0.5-1 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences in dioecious plants basally branched racemes, 3.5-8(-12) cm long with each branch bearing 13 nodes with each node bearing 1-3 spikes; bracts subtending each spike cucullate, ovate, 2-4 mm long, with acuminate tips 1-2 x ca. 2 mm; mature spikes 0.9-2(-2.5) cm long, sessile or with short peduncles up to 0.5 cm long; in monoecious plants single spikes usually arising from within a cluster of female flowers; spikes with 20-30 flowers in bisexual inflorescences and 40-80 in unisexual inflorescences; anthers ca. 1 x 0.5 mm; connectives ca. 0.5 mm broad, flattened distally. Pistillate and bisexual inflorescences thyrse-like panicles, 4-8 cm long with 4-12 cymules borne in opposite pairs 0.9-2 cm distant along inflorescence axis; cymules with 2-4(-5) imbricately arranged flowers, 3-8 x 3-5 mm; subtending cymule bract chartaceous, cucullate, ca. 1.3 cm long, sessile or on short peduncles 1-8 mm long; subtending floral bracts green, ca. 3 mm long, united in lower one-fourth to one-half, enclosing lower half of flower. Pistillate flowers green, 34 x 2-3 mm; perianth lobes 0.5-1 mm long, acute at tip, free; stigmas white, papillose, 2-3.5 mm long, 3-angled at base, linear. Fruiting cymules white, irregularly oblong, up to 1.8 x 0.50.6 cm. Seeds ca. 2 mm long, brown, trigonous, with a pore forming on each face.

description: Monoecious shrubs l-2.5(-5) m tall, ca. 2 cm dbh, much branched; young stems quadrate, green; older stems terete, tan, with leaf scars inconspicuous and narrow around the stem; upper and lower internodes of equal length, (l-)4-9 cm long. Leaves linear-lanceolate to very narrowly elliptic, 6-16 x 1.2-3.5 cm, terminating with very long-acuminate tips 0.7-2.3 cm long, cuneate at base, at margins serrate with teeth 3-6 mm distant, glabrous, smooth, thin, drying chartaceous, reddish brown above, light brown to gray beneath, with midveins impressed above, raised beneath; lateral veins 6-12, 4-8 mm distant, arcuate, obscure; intersecondary veins not visible; free portion of petioles 0-0.5 mm long, glabrous; petiolar sheaths 0.2-0.7 x 0.4-1 cm, with the distal margin entire or with two minute, caducous, narrowly triangular stipular processes ca. 0.5 mm long, these drying translucent; not extending beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences of pedunculate spikes, 1.4-2 cm long, borne on the pistillate axes; peduncles 0.3-0.9 cm long, subtended by an ovate sterile bract ca. 2 x ca. 1 mm, acuminate at apex; mature spikes 1-2 cm x ca. 0.3 cm, with ca. 18-54 stamens; anthers ca. 1 x 0.5 mm, becoming ca. 1 mm distant along axis; connectives extending into an acuminate, erect, white apicule ca. 0.5 mm long beyond thecae. Pistillate inflorescences short panicles resembling scorpioid cymes, 1.5-3.5 cm long; rachises slightly zigzag with (4-) 1450 flowers borne alternately on the inflorescence axes, up to 3 mm distant, sometimes subtended by a sterile dentate basal linear bract 0.5-3 x 24 cm; subtending floral bracts 2-4 x 2-3 mm, acuminate, entire along margin, green, chartaceous, persistent. Pistillate flowers green, slightly trigonous, 2-3 x 1.5-2.5 mm; perianth lobes 0.2-0.5 mm long, rounded at apex, free almost to base; stigmas very short, capitate, 0.5-1 mm long, angled, elaborated distally. Fruits purple to black, 3-4 x 2-3 mm, ellipsoidal, with a small pore on each face. Seeds ca. 3 mm long, brown.

description: Dioecious, aromatic shrubs or small trees 1.5-15 m tall, often with a narrow crown; trunk 416 cm dbh, with or without prop roots; bark light brown to light gray; wood white, soft; twigs often exuding mucilage when cut; older stems quadrate, larger stems terete, with leaf bases persisting and encircling the stem; internodes 2-8.5 cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic to elliptic to ovate, smooth to slightly scabrous above, glabrous, glossy, (5-)7.5-13(-17.2) x (1.8-) 3.5-6(-7) cm, with acuminate tips 0.5-1 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, margins serrate to serrulate with teeth 2.5-4 mm distant with teeth beginning ca. one-fourth distance to base, succulent, drying stiffly chartaceous, with midvein canaliculate on upper surface, raised on lower surface, sometimes with irregular brownish hairs 0.2-1 mm long; larger lateral veins (5-)7-8(-10), 7-12 mm distant, arcuate, slightly raised below, subopposite to alternate along midvein, with smaller intersecondary veins extending ca. halfway to margin; free portion of petioles (0.5-)0.9-2.5 cm long, green sometimes purple, glabrous or with irregular short or long hairs; petiolar sheath 0.5-1.4 x 0.4-1.4 cm, inflated, green often purple, each distal margin with two small, linear sometimes fimbriate, distal appendages 1-3 mm long, extending ca. 0.5 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences with spikes usually borne in two or three opposite pairs on a short axis (1-3 cm long) terminated by a single spike, subsessile or terminal on bracteate peduncles 2-15 mm long, united to the stem above the leaf sheath, subtended by a cucullate, subulate bract 5-9 mm long; flowering spikes to (1.1-)1.5-2.9(-3.5) cm long, 0.3-0.6 cm thick, with stamens becoming ca. 1 mm distant on rachis; anthers 1-1.7 x 0.40.6 mm; connectives extending ca. 0.2 mm beyond thecae, terminating in a short apicule 0.2 mm long. Pistillate inflorescences thyrse-like, paniculate or racemose, 2-9 cm long, terminal or axillary, usually united with stem to above the leaf sheath, with (3-)7-20 solitary flowers, alternate to subopposite, 2-12 mm distant on the rachis; sterile bracts chartaceous, 1-7 x 1-4 mm. Pistillate flowers green, ellipsoidal, 3-4 x 2-3 mm, borne on short peduncles 1-3 mm long or subsessile, with perianth lobes 0.2-0.5 mm long, acute at apex, free to base, subtended by a cupule 2-3 mm long with (2-)3 acute lobes on distal margin; stigmas white, 1.5-2.5 mm long, papillose, linear, elaborated distally, caducous. Fruiting cymules white, waxy, 3-4 x 2-3 mm, ellipsoidal. Seeds ca. 2 mm long, brown, smooth, trigonous.

description: Dioecious, aromatic, glabrous shrubs or small trees, 2.5-10 m tall, 2-10 cm dbh, with prop roots; wood weak, brittle; young stems quadrate; older stems terete, with leaf bases disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; internodes 1-6.8 cm long; nodes slightly swollen. Leaves elliptic, (3.2-)4.5-12(-17.5) x (1.7-)2.1-5.5 cm, with acuminate tips 6-12 mm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, margins serrate with teeth 4-8 mm distant, succulent to coriaceous, smooth, green above, light green beneath when fresh, drying stiffly chartaceous, slate gray to light gray-brown above, light reddish brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised and glabrous beneath; larger lateral veins 12-16, 3-9 mm distant, slightly arcuate, raised above and beneath, with smaller intersecondary veins extending halfway to margin, these prominent above and beneath, forming a nearly straight submarginal vein 1-2 mm from margin; free portion of petioles 0.5-1.3 cm long; petiolar sheaths 1-1.3 x 0.30.6 cm, slightly flared at apex, disintegrating with age, each distal margin entire, with two narrowly triangular to linear, entire or bifid stipular appendages 1-2 mm long, extending 0.5-1 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences of solitary or cymose spikes borne along a central axis, 1-9 cm long; mature spikes 1.4-3.1(-3.9) x 0.6-0.7 cm, subsessile or on short peduncles 2-3 mm long, subtended by an entire, sometimes dentate, cymbiform bracts 3-9 mm long; stamens ca. 150, congested on axis; anthers green, (1.2-)2-3 x ca. 0.5 mm; connective flattened distally, ca. 0.2 mm long, with a minute, acute, white tip. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal basally branched racemes, (2-)4-8 cm long, with (4-)6-24 cymules; cymules with (l-)2-3(-5) clustered flowers, 3-5 x 3-4 mm, oppositely arranged on inflorescence axis, 5-20 mm distant, sessile; subtending floral bracts free or connate to adjacent bracts at base, 1.5-3.5 mm long, acuminate at apex, enclosing lower one-half of flower. Pistillate flowers green, trigonous, 2.5-3.5 x 1.5-2 mm, with a pore on each face; perianth lobes ca. 0.3 mm long, rounded at apex, free to base; stigmas white, linear to clavate in outline, (1.5-)2-3 mm long, papillose, elaborated distally, caducous. Fruiting cymules white, translucent, irregularly globose, 6-7 mm in diam. Seeds 2-3 mm long, brown, smooth, trigonous.

description: Dioecious(?) shrubs 2-4 m tall; young stems quadrate, glabrous or sparsely strigose, often covered by overlapping leaf sheaths; large stems terete, glabrous, gray, with encircling scars forming from the old leaf bases; internodes 0.8-2.3 cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic to elliptic, 2-4(-7) x 1.1-1.7(-3) cm, with acuminate tips 0.1-0.2 cm long, truncate to obtuse (oblique or symmetrical) at base, at margins crenulate with teeth 1-2 mm distant these extending to near base, drying coriaceous, smooth, glabrous, waxy, light to dark brown above, reddish brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath, glabrous or strigose with branched trichomes; lateral veins 9-12, 3-4 mm distant, obscure, leaving midveins a 60°-75° angle, with obscure intersecondary veins extending one-third to one-half way to margin; free portion of petioles smooth, sparsely strigose beneath, 0.2-0.5 mm long, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths smooth, 0.7-1.3 x 0.6-1.0 cm at apex, inflated, flared at apex, quadrangular, with 2-4 raised ciliate longitudinal lines extending down length of sheath from distal margin, turning gray and breaking apart with age, each distal margin with two fimbriate stipular processes 2-3 mm long, ca. 0.5 mm broad at base, not extending above free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences not seen. Pistillate inflorescences of congested racemes, 0.8-1.9(-3) cm long bearing 2-4 cymules; subtending inflorescence bracts 0.5-1.5 x 0.2-0.5 cm, dentate or entire; cymules with 2-3 imbricately arranged flowers, 6-8 x 4-6 mm, sessile, opposite or alternate on inflorescence axis, 2-5 mm distant; subtending floral bracts green, free to base or connate in lower one-fourth to one-half, 4-8.5 mm long including acuminate tips 1-3.5 mm long, 2-3 mm broad. Pistillate flowers trigonous, ca. 4 x ca. 2 mm, with a large pore on each face of ovary; perianth lobes deltate, 0.3-0.5 mm long, acute or rounded at apex, united at base; stigmas 2-3 mm long, irregularly lobulate and dissected, papillose. Fruiting cymules not seen.

description: Dioecious, aromatic shrubs or columnar trees, 1-7 m tall, with narrow crowns; trunks gnarled, 6-8 cm dbh with prop roots; bark gray, smooth, slightly fissured; wood white, soft, turning orange when exposed to air; young stems quadrate, purple, smooth to verrucose, glabrous to scurfy or hirsute; older stems terete, smooth, glabrous, often hollow, with leaf bases disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; internodes 0.5-2.2 cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic, elliptic to obovate, 1.1-5.3 x 0.5-1.8 cm, with acuminate tips 0.1-0.2 cm long, rounded to truncate at base, at margins serrate with ascending often white-tipped teeth, these 2.5-4 mm distant and beginning one-third to one-half way up from base, crassulate-coriaceous, smooth, shiny, glabrous, dark green above, light to medium green beneath with margins white to purplish black when fresh, drying coriaceous, smooth, light to dark brown above and beneath; midveins impressed above, raised and glabrous to hirsute beneath; lateral and intersecondary veins not visible; free portions of petioles purple, 0.1-0.4 cm long, smooth to verrucose to scurfy, glabrous to hirsute, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths green to purple, smooth to verrucose to scurfy, glabrous to hirsute, 0.6-1.1 x 0.5-1 cm at apex, inflated, flared at apex, quadrangular, caducous, each distal margin with two caducous, fimbriate stipular appendages 1-2 mm long that continue down sheaths as raised ciliate to fimbriate lines, extending 0-0.5 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences green, terminal, composed of a solitary spike; subtending leafy bracts 0.1-1.1 cm long, 0.1-0.9 cm broad; mature spikes 2.1-4.4 x 0.6-1 cm, with 90-160 stamens, sessile or on short peduncles 1-2 mm long; stamens congested but becoming 0.5-1 mm distant on axis; rachis 0.5-2 mm broad, with a thick, irregularly margined, basal annulus; anthers yellowish green, 1.5-2.5(-3) mm long, ca. 1.5 mm thick; connectives extended 0.5-0.8 mm beyond thecae, acute. Pistillate inflorescences usually terminal, occasionally axillary, composed of a solitary cymule, subtended by a pair of leafy bracts 0.1-1.8 cm long, 0.1-0.9 cm broad; cymules with (2-)3-6(-8) clustered flowers, 5-10 mm long and broad; terminal cymules sessile; axillary cymules borne on short rachises 2-5 mm long; subtending floral bracts yellow, green, to purplish green, connate in lower three-fourths to four-fifths, 5-9 mm long, including acute tips 0.5-1 mm long, entire along margin, enclosing flowers completely except for exserted stigmas. Pistillate flowers trigonous, 4-6 x ca. 2 mm, with or without a pore on each face; perianth lobes 1.5-2 mm long, basally united in lower one-half to three-fourths, with free portions triangular, acute; stigmas green to purple, linear, terete, 24 mm long, with very short papillae. Fruiting cymules purple to black, globose, 0.9-1.5 cm in diam. Seeds trigonous, ca. 3 mm long, brown, smooth.

description: Dioecious, aromatic trees or erect to scandent shrubs, 2-12 m tall, with many trunks, 4-20 cm dbh, with prop roots; bark gray to white; wood white, weak; young stems quadrate, green, sometimes purple, smooth, sparsely to densely villous with stiff twisted white or brown trichomes; older stems terete, smooth, glabrous, with leaf bases disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; upper internodes elongate, 4-11 cm long; lower internodes condensed, 1.3-2 cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves narrowly elliptic, elliptic to obovate, (5.9-)7.1-12.7(-16) x (2.3-)2.8-6.1(-7.2) cm, with acuminate tips 0.5-1.4 cm long, cuneate at base, at margins deeply serrate with often reddish teeth 2-3 mm distant, fleshy to subcoriaceous, smooth, shiny or dull, glabrous, dark green above, dull, glabrous to villous, light green beneath when fresh, drying coriaceous, smooth, light gray to dark brown above, reddish to light brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised and villous to smooth beneath; larger lateral veins 11-19,3-5 mm distant, impressed above, raised and villous to smooth beneath, arcuate, sometimes bifurcate one-fourth to three-fourths distance to margin, with smaller intersecondary veins extending one-third to two-thirds way to margin, these impressed above, raised and villous beneath; tertiary veins impressed or flat above, raised, and villous to glabrous beneath, giving leaf a bullate appearance; free portion of petioles green or purple, 0.5-2 cm long, smooth, glabrous to villous, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths green or purple, smooth, glabrous to villous, 1.4-2 x 0.6-0.8(-1.5) cm, slightly inflated, flared at apex, terete or quadrangular, caducous, each distal margin with two caducous fimbriate stipular appendages 3-5 mm long, extending ca. 0.5 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 6-12.8 cm long, composed of 1-3 spikes clustered at the end of a rachis 3-8.7 cm long, with the solitary spike or cluster of spikes subtended by a pair of bracts; bracts 0.5-6.3 x 0.8-2.3 cm, dentate, leaf-like; mature spikes (3.5-)4.3-6(-7.8) x 0.6-0.9(-1.2) cm, with ca. 200 stamens, sessile or borne on short peduncles 1-3 mm long; stamens congested on axis but becoming 0.5-1 mm distant; rachis 3-5 mm broad with a thick, irregularly margined, basal annulus; anthers yellowish green, 1.7-3.5 x 1-2 mm, connectives extended 0.5-1 mm beyond thecae, acute. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, 1.7-6 cm long, composed of a pair of cymules at the apex of a long rachis; bracts subtending cymules 1.1-5.5(-8.2) x 0.3-1.9(-2.4) cm, leaf-like; cymules with (1-)3-4(-5) clustered flowers, 7-10 x 6-10 mm, sessile; subtending floral bracts green, connate in lower two-thirds to three-fourths, 8-10 x 6-8 mm, acute, ciliate or entire along free margins, enclosing flowers completely except for exserted perianth lobes and stigmas. Pistillate flowers strongly trigonous, 7-9 mm long, ca. 3 mm broad on each face, with a pore on each face, these ciliate along margin or pores wanting; perianth lobes 2.5-3 mm long, basally united in lower one-half to three-fourths, with free portions deltate, acute; stigmas white to purple, linear, 3-5 mm long, terete to tri- to quadrangular, with very short papillae. Fruiting cymules purple to black, irregularly globose to oblong, 1-1.9 cm in diam. Seeds sharply trigonous, 6-7 mm long, ca. 3 mm broad on each face, brown, smooth.

description: Shrubs 2-3 m tall; upper internodes 1.6-3.1 cm long; lower internodes 5.8-6.3 cm long. Leaves 3.8-7.8 x 1.1-1.8 cm. Staminate inflorescences 3.5-4.4 cm long; mature spikes 2-3.1 cm long, 4-5 mm thick, on peduncles 0.6-1.1 cm long; rachises ca. 1 mm thick persisting after stamens have fallen; anthers ca. 2 x 0.5 mm, with connectives projecting ca. 0.3 mm upwards beyond thecae. Pistillate inflorescences 0.6-1.4 cm long, with 5-12 flowers.

description: Dioecious, aromatic, glabrous shrubs or small trees 2.5-7 m tall, 4-15 cm dbh, with prop roots; bark light gray; wood white, turning orange when exposed to air, weak; young stems quadrate, green or purple, smooth, glabrous; older stems terete, with leaf bases disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; internodes 1.2-5.1 cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves lanceolate, narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate, (5.2-)l 1.5-14.8(-16.5) x (2-)2.7-4.1(-4.7) cm, with acuminate tips 0.7-1.6 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, margins serrate to crenate with teeth 2-3.5 mm distant, fleshy, lax, smooth, glabrous, shiny, medium to light green above, light green beneath when fresh, drying chartaceous, smooth, light gray to light to dark brown above and beneath; midveins impressed above, raised and glabrous beneath; larger lateral veins 16-21, 4-6 mm distant, arcuate, slightly raised above and beneath, with smaller intersecondary veins extending ca. one-half way to margin; free portion of petioles 0.3-1.5 cm long, smooth, glabrous, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths smooth, glabrous, 0.92 x 0.5-12 cm at apex, slightly inflated, slightly flared at apex, terete or quadrangular, caducous, only slightly extending beyond free portion of petioles (0.25 mm), each distal margin with two caducous, fimbriate stipular appendages 2-3 mm long. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 4-10.7 cm long, composed of 1-3 spikes clustered at the end of a rachis (1-4.5 cm long); cluster of spikes subtended by a pair of dentate, leafy bracts, 1-6.2 cm long, 0.1-1.9 cm broad; mature spikes 3.1-5.2(-9.2) cm long, 0.6-0.8 cm broad, with ca. 200 stamens, sessile or borne on short peduncles 1-3 mm long; stamens congested on axis but becoming 0.5-1 mm distant; rachis ca. 2 mm thick with a thin regular basal annulus; anthers yellowish green, 1.5-2.5 x ca. 1 mm; connectives extended 0.2-0.5 mm beyond thecae, acute. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, (2.3-)3.3-9(-11.2) cm long, composed of a pair of cymules at the apex of a long rachis; bracts subtending cymules l-3.5(-6.2) x 0.1-0.5(-1.9) cm, leaf-like; cymules with 1-2(-3) clustered flowers, 7-10 x 5-8 mm, sessile; subtending floral bracts green, connate in lower three-fourths to four-fifths, acute, entire along free margins, enclosing flowers completely except for exserted perianth lobes and stigmas. Pistillate flowers strongly trigonous, 5-7 mm long, ca. 3 mm broad on each face, with a glabrous pore on each face of ovary; perianth lobes 1.5-2 mm long, basally united in lower one-half to three-fourths, with free portions deltate, acute; stigmas green to white, linear, terete, with short papillae. Fruiting cymules bluish black to purple, irregularly globose to oblong, (5-)7-10 mm in diam. Seeds sharply trigonous, 3-5 mm long, ca. 3 mm broad on each face, brown, smooth.

description: Dioecious, aromatic shrubs or trees 3-12(-20) m tall; trunk 10-30 cm dbh, with or without prop roots; bark light brown to gray, smooth; wood white or pink, weak, with or without white latex; young stems quadrate, older stems terete, encircled by leaf scars at each node; internodes 0.8-1.6(-4) cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves lanceolate to oblanceolate, glabrous, smooth, 10-25 cm long, 2-6.5 cm wide, terminating with acuminate tips 1-1.5 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, margins serrate with blunt teeth 4-10 mm distant, with hydathodes often white, slightly succulent to subcoriaceous, lustrous, dark green above, light green below, drying stiffly chartaceous to subcoriaceous, dark brown above and light reddish brown beneath, with midveins impressed above, raised beneath; larger lateral veins 12-20, 5-9 mm distant, uniformly arcuate, often prominently raised beneath, with smaller intersecondary veins extending one-half to three-fourths distance to margin; free portion of petioles (0.2-)0.6-1.5(-2.3) cm long; petiolar sheaths 0.9-2.3 x 0.4-1 cm, often inflated, deciduous, each distal margin with two clawed fimbriate stipular processes 5-6 mm long; not extending above free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences composed of axillary or terminal spikes borne on short curved, lax, peduncles 3-20 mm long; mature spikes 3-13 x 0.6-1.3 cm, solitary or in groups of three, the center spike much longer than lateral spikes, with a thin lacerate basal annulus protruding ca. 0.5 mm from rachis; stamens crowded but becoming ca. 2 mm distant on axis; anthers 2-3.5 x ca. 1 mm; connectives forming a flat disc-like apex 0.5-1 mm broad with a minute acute apicule ca. 0.3 mm long. Pistillate inflorescences large cone-like strobili, terminal, sometimes also axillary (but then smaller), 1.7-4.5 x 1.2-3.5 cm, composed of 3070 groups of 3-5 flowers (total of 90-350 flowers) with subtending floral bracts fused both within and between clusters; subtending sterile inflorescence bracts linear, 5-10 x 1-2 mm. Pistillate flowers green, 3-4 x 1.5-2.5 mm, free in bract matrix; perianth lobes 0.5-1 mm long, acute a tip, irregularly fused; stigmas papillose, 3-5 mm long, linear to clavate in outline, entire or elaborated distally, persistent. Mature Infructescences 3-5 x 1.5-3 cm, light green to yellow to white, fleshy, sweet. Seeds 3-4 x ca. 2.5 mm, brown to black, asymmetrically trigonous, with perianth persisting only on the three ridges and apex of seed.

description: Dioecious, aromatic shrubs or trees 2-12(-16) m tall, 6-15(-20) cm dbh, with prop roots; bark gray or brown, smooth or striate, light pink in section, oxidizing to deep red; wood white, soft; young stems quadrate, green, sometimes purple; older stems terete, often hollow, with tubular leaf bases persisting, ultimately disintegrating and leaving encircling scars; internodes 1.1-5.6 cm long. Leaves obovate, elliptic, narrowly elliptic to ovate, 6.2-23 x 2.6-7.5 cm, with acuminate tips 0.3-1.4 cm long, cuneate to obliquely cuneate at base, at margins sharply serrate with teeth 2.5-4.5(-8) mm distant, sometimes revolute so as to appear entire or subentire, fleshy to subcoriaceous, smooth, glabrous, shiny dark green above, light green beneath when fresh, drying stiffly chartaceous, smooth, sometimes scabrous, gray to brown above, reddish brown beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath, glabrous or with very sparse or dense, branched or unbranched trichomes; larger lateral veins 9-12(-16), 0.7-1.6 cm distant, arcuate, raised beneath, with smaller intersecondary veins obscure, extending one-third to one-half way to margin; free portion of petioles glabrous, (0.3-)l-1.8(-2.4) cm long, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths 1-2(-2.6) x 0.6-1.1 cm at apex, inflated, slightly flared at apex, terete or quadrangular, smooth or with two raised ciliate lines extending down from free portion of petioles, persistent but disintegrating with age, each distal margin with two linear to slightly fimbriate, stipular appendages 1-2 mm long, extending above free portion of petioles ca. 0.5 mm. Staminate inflorescences composed of a straight or zigzag rachis 4-8.8 cm long, with 3-7 nodes; nodes usually opposite, sometimes alternate, with 1-3 spikes per node; spikes usually sessile, sometimes on short peduncles 1-2 mm long; inflorescence bracts 0.4-2.1 x 0.3-0.7 cm, dentate; mature spikes 1-2.6 x 0.2-0.6 cm, subtended by an entire, cymbiform bract 2-4 mm long; stamens 60-150, congested on axis, but becoming 0.5-1 mm distant; anthers yellowish green to green, 1-1.5 x 0.5-1 mm; connectives flattened distally, ca. 0.2 mm long. Pistillate inflorescences axillary or terminal, racemes or panicles, 2.3-12.5 cm long with 530 cymules, united with the stem 0.3-1.5 cm above leaf sheath; subtending bracts similar in size and shape to the leaves or more frequently smaller, 4-1.5 x 0.6-2.5 cm, lanceolate to narrowly obovate, acuminate, dentate; cymules 27 flowered, 3-6 x 4-6 mm, alternately or oppositely arranged on rachis, 4-15 mm distant, sessile or on short peduncles 1-2 mm long; subtending floral bracts connate in lower one-third to two-thirds, 1.7-5 x 4-5 mm, acuminate, with tips 1-2 mm long, margin entire, enclosing one-fourth to three-fourths of flower. Pistillate flowers slightly trigonous, 3-5 x 1.5-3 mm, with a small pore on each face of ovary ca. 0.3 mm in diameter; perianth lobes small, deltate, acute, ca. 0.3 mm long, free or basally united; stigmas white, brown, or purple, linear, 1-3 mm long, 3-angled, papillose. Fruiting cymules white, 0.6-1.2 x 0.50.9 cm. Seeds ca. 3 mm long, brown, smooth, trigonous.

description: Dioecious, aromatic trees ca. 5 m tall; young stems quadrate, smooth, glabrous; large stems terete, encircled by leaf sheath scars; internodes 2.1-11.7 cm long; nodes swollen. Leaves elliptic, 8-13.7 x 3.7-6.2 cm broad, with acuminate tips 0.7-1 cm long, broadly cuneate to obliquely broadly cuneate at base, margins serrulate with teeth 2-3 mm distant beginning near base, smooth, glabrous, shiny, waxy, drying smooth, coriaceous, light to dark brown above and beneath; midveins impressed above, raised beneath; larger lateral veins 11-17, 4-6 mm distant, slightly arcuate, leaving midvein at a 55°-85° angle; smaller intersecondary veins visible to obscure, extending ca. one-half distance to margin; free portions of petioles smooth, glabrous, (0.3-)0.5-0.9 cm long, narrowly winged; petiolar sheaths smooth, glabrous, (1.9-)2.4-2.6 x 1.1-1.9 cm at apex, inflated, slightly flared at apex, quadrangular, caducous, each distal margin with two linear to slightly fimbriate, caducous, stipular appendages 2-4 mm long, extending ca. 0.5 mm beyond free portion of petioles. Staminate inflorescences terminal or axillary, 7-14.8 cm long, composed of solitary spikes, borne on long (4.5-7.2 cm) rachises; subtending bracts paired, ovate, 2.5-4.3 x 1.9-2.1 cm, with acuminate tips, 0.6-0.9 cm long, truncate to cordate at base; mature spikes ca. 6.5 x ca. 1.4 cm, with ca. 200 stamens; stamens congested on rachis but becoming 0.5-1 mm distant on axis; anthers ca. 3 x ca. 1 mm; connectives extended 2.5-3 mm beyond thecae, flattened at apex. Pistillate inflorescences not seen.

description: Sprawling, decumbent, perennial herbs occasionally with branches 0.3-1.0 m long, but generally radiating from a central woody underground stem; decumbent branches up to 1 m long, green, varying from densely tomentose to sparsely strigose. Leaves simple, sessile, entire, usually linear or linear-lanceolate but occasionally spatulate near stem bases, 5-25 mm long, 0.9-4.0 mm wide, acute, mucronate, variably strigose. Flowers borne in secund racemes (-panicles) terminating every branch; flowering stalks 10-30 mm long each separated in the distal portion into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of linear bractlets 10-15 mm long, 0.5-2.0 mm wide; flowering stalks shed entirely if a flower aborts; buds obliquely lanceolate in outline, slightly expanded ventrally; sepals five, spreading, lanceolate to ovate, entire, acute, densely strigose dorsally, deep purple; uppermost sepal 8-15 mm long, 3-5 mm wide; lowermost sepal 10-16 mm long, 3-6 mm wide; lateral sepals narrower than the lowermost; glandular petals cuneate, 1.5-3.0 mm, pink, apricot-colored, or reddish with secretory blisters restricted to the upper half or quarter of the dorsal faces and to the distal, often plicate and convolute edge; petaloid petals three, clawed, 5-7 mm long, basally connate for about 4 mm with the connate portion cream-colored or pink and the terminal, free portions expanded into reniform, crenulate, purple, or pink and purple-edged, blades 1.5-2.0 long, 2-3 mm wide; stamens four, equal in length, 3-4 mm long, inserted on the connate base of the petaloid petals with lateral pairs fused for 1-2.5 mm beyond the point of insertion, pale pink; pollen 47-50 in diam., 3-porate with the pores lalongate and ca. 20 µm long; ovary ovoid, 3-4 mm long, densely strigose, surmounted by a stout, glabrous, pink style 2.5-4.0 mm long. Fruits globose or occasionally slightly cordate in outline with a short ridge extending from the tip of the fruit on each side toward the pedicel, 5.5-8.0 mm in diam. excluding spines, variously pubescent and bearing stout, blunt, scattered spines; individual spines yellow, 1.8-5.3 mm long, grading in size from larger to shorter distally, 0.3-0.8 mm wide in basal diam., bearing numerous, conspicuous, wavy, long white trichomes proximally and numerous, minute, retrorse barbs at the distal ends. Chromosome number, n = 6 (Turner, 1958).
bibliographicCitation: Simpson, Beryl B. 1989. Krameriaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 49: 1-108.

description: Sprawling, diffuse herbs with branches to 50 cm long; stems striate when dry, variably strigose. Leaves simple, sessile, entire, widely spaced, often abruptly divergent from the stems, narrowly linear, 8-21 mm long, 0.5-2.0(-3.0) mm wide, mucronate, often densely strigose when young, glabrate with age. Flowers borne in terminal racemes; flowering stalks (5-) 10-23 mm long each separated in the distal half into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of linear, mucronate bractlets 6.0-11.5 mm long and 0.5-1.5 mm wide; peduncle and bractlets persistent if a flower aborts; buds asymmetrically ovate in outline with the ventral half expanded; sepals five, connivent, lanceolate, entire, pink or purple-red, strigose dorsally; uppermost sepal 7-11 mm long, 3-6 mm wide, slightly strigose on the margins as well as on the central portion of the dorsal faces; lowermost sepal geniculate and slightly saccate, 8.5-15.0 mm long, 3-6 mm wide; lateral sepals narrower than the lowermost sepal; glandular petals more or less orbicular in outline, ca. 2 mm wide, green, with a pronounced area of glandular tissue along the distal margin and irregularly round blisters covering the dorsal surfaces; petaloid petals three, clawed, 5-7 mm long, basally connate for 3.0-4.5 mm with green claws and the terminal segments expanded into pink or red-purple, spatulate, obtuse, undulate-margined blades ca. 2.5 mm long and ca. 2 mm wide; stamens four, equal in length, 4-5 mm long, inserted on the connate bases of the petaloid petals, free beyond the point of insertion or with lateral pairs connate basally to 1 mm with green filaments and brown anthers; pollen 30-32 µm in diam., triporate with the pores expanded equatorially and up to 17-22 µm in length; ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm long, densely covered with white trichomes, bearing a thick, glabrous, arcuately curved, green style ca. 3 mm long. Fruits spherical or slightly cordate in outline with a vertical medial ridge, about 5 mm in diam. excluding spines, lanose with white or beige trichomes and bearing scattered stout spines; individual spines red or orange, 1.8-3.8 mm long and 0.25-0.75 mm in basal diam., retrorsely barbed in the distal half with minute barbs, and bearing scattered long trichomes at the base. Chromosome number. Unreported.

description: Procumbent, spreading, perennial herbs, usually with unbranched, trailing branches to 14 cm long; stems conspicuously strigose. Leaves simple, sessile, often abundant and crowded, especially at the branch tips, sometimes appearing almost two-ranked, often borne at a 90° angle with respect to the branch or even at a greater angle and pointing backward, occasionally revolute, thick, linear to ovate-lanceolate, 6-15 mm long, 1-4 mm wide, entire, mucronate with a deep-red purple spine up to 1 mm long, cuneate at the base, variously vestitured, glabrous, glabrate to densely strigose with long, white trichomes most prominent above. Flowers borne in open terminal racemes; flowering stalks 8-12 mm long, each separated in the distal third into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of bractlets 6-9 mm long and 1-2 mm wide; individual flowers borne upright on the pedicel with the uppermost sepal vertically oriented and the lowermost gibbous and extending upward and covering the petals and sexual parts; pedicel completely shed and peduncle and bractlets remaining if a flower aborts; buds unequally lanceolate, expanded ventrally; sepals five, strongly connivent, ovate to lanceolate, entire, yellow on the inner surfaces and dusky rose on portions of the dorsal surfaces, turning red-brown with age, strigose on the dorsal faces; uppermost sepal 6-11 mm long, 2-6 mm wide; lowermost sepal geniculate, 5.5-11.0 mm long, 3-6 mm wide; lateral sepals narrower than the uppermost and lowermost sepals; glandular petals irregularly orbicular in outline, yellow, 2-3 mm wide, with saccate blisters restricted primarily to the distal edge of the dorsal surfaces; petaloid petals three, clawed, 4-7 mm long, with yellow claws basally connate for 4.5-6.0 mm, free above for 1.0-1.5 mm and expanding into orbicular to reniform, serrulate margined, yellow blades 1.0-1.5 mm long, 1.5-2.0 mm wide; stamens four, equal in length, 3.04.5 mm long, inserted on the connate claws about 1-2 mm above the base, free from the point of insertion, arcuate, yellow; pollen 33-40 µm in diam., triporate with the pores broad, expanded equatorially to synorate; ovary ovoid, 4-5 mm long, surmounted by a glabrous, straight, vertically oriented green style 3-5 mm long. Fruit ovoid, 4-6 mm in diam. excluding spines, densely villous with trichomes up to 1 mm long and bearing scattered, slender spines; individual spines dark red, 1.3-4.0 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm in basal diam., bearing about 20, amber-colored retrorse barbs to 0.3 mm long in several series in the distal portion and long, crooked, trichomes at the base. Chromosome number. Unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Simpson, Beryl B. 1989. Krameriaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 49: 1-108.

description: Stiff angular, mound-forming shrubs 0.2-0.8 (-1.5) m tall; young branches canescent, rarely with scattered glandular trichomes at the apex; old stems terete, blue-green, rigid with acute spinose tips. Leaves simple, entire, usually sparse, occasionally almost completely lacking, linear, rarely linear-lanceolate, 4-20 mm long, 1-5 mm wide, sessile with abrupt bases and mucronate apices, canescent throughout. Flowers borne singly in leaf axils on canescent flowering stalks to 25 mm long, each separated medially into a peduncle and pedicel by a pair of green bractlets up to 10 mm long and 0.5-3.0 mm wide; flowering stalks entirely shed if flowers abort; flower buds elegantly and narrowly falcate, nodding; sepals five, reflexed, lanceolate, acute, purple or deep red-pink, canescent or strigose on the dorsal surfaces; uppermost sepal 7-13 mm long and 24 mm wide; lowermost sepal 9-12 mm long, 2.5-5.0 mm wide; lateral sepals narrower than the upper and lowermost sepals; glandular petals orbicular to reniform in outline, 1.5-4.5 mm long, 1.5-5.0 mm wide, deep purple, red-brown, pink or yellow, with the dorsal faces bullate and entirely covered with more or less equal-sized, round blisters; petaloid petals three, free to base, very narrowly oblanceolate, 3-6 mm long, 0.4-2.0 mm wide with the terminal expanded portion entire, minutely serrate or shallowly notched, pink or purple at the tip and green basally; stamens four, pink, didynamous with the upper pair 3.5-6.0 mm long and lower pair 5-8 mm long, inserted at the bases of the upper three petals; pollen grains 30-37 µm in diam., triporate with the pores 15-20 µm long and narrowly expanded equatorially; ovary ovoid, 3-4 mm long, tomentose, surmounted by a stout, glabrous style 3-4 mm long, red or pink. Fruits cordate to circular in outline, often with a conspicuous longitudinal median ridge, 5.5-10.0 mm in diam. excluding spines, canescent, sericeous, or strigose with white or brown trichomes and many scattered spines; individual spines (1.5-)2.5-4.5(-5.5) mm long, (0.1-)0.2-0.5 mm wide at the base, bearing a whorl of amber-colored, recurved barbs up to 1 mm long near the apex and long, unicellular trichomes along the basal portion. Chromosome number, n = 6, Turner (1958).

description: Shrubs to small trees 1 to 6 m tall; young stems, petioles and leaves strigose to tomentose with immature growth and flower buds often densely villous to sericeous, appearing orange or red due to the presence of colored resinous secretions mixed with the unicellular trichomes; old stems terete, woody with gray bark. Leaves compound, trifoliolate with a common point of leaflet attachment, 12-37 mm long including the 6-17 mm long sericeous petiole, 9-30 mm wide; leaflets oblanceolate, lanceolate, or ovate with terminal leaflets 6-20(-22) mm long, 2.5-5.0(-7.0) mm wide, acute, mucronate, narrowly cuneate at the bases, strigose to tomentose throughout. Flowers borne singly in leaf axils on strigose flowering stalks each separated into a peduncle and pedicel by a pair of lanceolate bractlets 5-10 mm long and 2-3 mm wide inserted in the distal half of stalk; flowering stalks completely shed if flowers abort; buds lanceolate in outline, nodding; sepals five, reflexed, lanceolate, acute, entire, bright pink to dusky-rose, sericeous on the outer surfaces with trichomes extending onto the inner surfaces; uppermost sepal 10-15 mm long and 1.5-5.0 mm wide; lowermost sepal 8-19(-24) mm long, 2.0-6.5 mm wide; lateral sepals narrower than the lowermost sepal; glandular petals orbicular in outline, 2-5 mm in diam., green or yellow, bullate throughout the dorsal surfaces; petaloid petals three, free to the base, clawed, narrowly oblanceolate, acute, slightly serrate apically, 4-7(-11) mm long, 0.3-1.0 mm wide at the broadest point, green with pink tips; stamens four, equal to subequal in length, free, borne above and sigmoidally curved over the ovary, 4-10 mm long, light pink or light pink distally and green below; pollen grains 28-35 ^im in diam., triporate with the pores narrow and extended equatorially; ovary pyriform, 6-8 mm long, densely sericeous, bearing a straight, green, basally sericeous style 6-8 mm long. Fruit globose, 9-12 mm in diam. excluding spines, densely white-tomentose to brown-hispid and with many, scattered, dark red to black spines; individual spines 2.2-7.0 mm long, 0.25-0.40 mm in basal diameter with scattered, white, wavy trichomes at the base and 48 conspicuous, amber-colored recurved barbs near the tip. Chromosome number. Unknown.

description: Erect, rounded, much branched, woody shrubs 0.5-1.5 m tall; young stems greenish-yellow, slightly strigose to densely tomentose; old branches dark yellow-green with fissured bark. Leaves simple, broadly lanceolate to oblanceolate, 6-18 mm long, 3-10 mm wide, decreasing in size distally, obtuse, mucronate with a dark red apicule, narrowly cuneate at the base, or sometimes narrowing into a petiole less than 1 mm long, variably villous, sometimes canescent or sericeous, the indumentum tending to render the young tissues a golden color. Flowers produced in branched racemes with villous to sericeous rachises; flowering stalks 11-22 mm long with the peduncle and pedicel separated in the distal half by a pair of mucronate leafy bractlets 6-11 mm long and about 1.5 mm wide; entire flowering stalk shed if a flower aborts; buds slightly falcate in outline; sepals five, spreading, ovate, acute, with entire, often scarious margins, rose, villous or sericeous on the dorsal faces; uppermost sepal 9-13 mm long, 3.0-5.5 mm wide; lowermost sepal 9-13 mm long, (2-)4-6 mm wide, often gibbous; lateral sepals narrower than the upper and lower sepals; glandular petals cuneate, 3 mm long, 2 mm wide, light to medium pink, covered on the dorsal faces with irregular, roundish blisters, appearing bullate; petaloid petals three, clawed to narrowly oblanceolate in outline, ca. 6 mm long, 1.5-2.0 mm wide, pink distally with the expanded tips and bases green or cream-colored; stamens four, didynamous, pink, with the shorter pair 4-7 mm long and the longer pair 7-9 mm long; pollen 26-29 µm in diam., tricolporate; ovary ovoid, ca. 5 mm long, green, covered with dense white trichomes; style curved upward, pink, ca. 5 mm long. Fruit globose, 8-10 mm in diam. excluding spines, green, sparsely strigose and bearing retrorsely barbed spines scattered over the entire surface; spines 3-5 mm long, 0.15-0.2 mm in basal diam., deep red or orange in color, bearing unicellular scattered trichomes along the basal portion and amber-colored retrorse barbs each up to 1 mm long in a subterminal ring and scattered along the distal half of the shaft. Chromosome number. Unreported.
bibliographicCitation: Simpson, Beryl B. 1989. Krameriaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 49: 1-108.

description: Short, erect, stout, wiry shrubs 20-60 cm tall; plants generally branched primarily at the base and distally along the stems; stems dull green, densely tomentose or sericeous to glabrous, striate when dry. Leaves simple, ovate, 31-35 mm long including the 4-7 mm long petiole, 10-13 mm wide, acute, mucronate with a red apicule up to 1 mm, narrowly cuneate at the bases of the blades, entire, densely golden lanose to sparsely strigose throughout with three veins conspicuous beneath. Flowers borne in variously branched, distally congested, terminal inflorescences; flowering stalks tomentose, 2-5 mm long, each separated into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of linear to lanceolate, mucronate bractlets 4-5 mm long and ca. 1 mm wide at about the midpoint; peduncle and bractlets persistent if a flower aborts; buds symmetrically ovate in outline; sepals four, strongly connivent, ovate, entire, often scarious marginally, tomentose in the central portion of the dorsal faces, deep red to crimson; uppermost sepal 5-7 mm wide, 8-9 mm long; lowermost sepal 4-8 mm wide, 8-10 mm long, slightly gibbous; lateral sepals slightly narrower than the lowermost sepals; glandular petals cuneate, ca. 4 mm long, 2.5-3.0 mm wide, deep rose-red to purple, covered on the dorsal faces with long, parallel, vertically-oriented blisters; petaloid petals (2-) 3, clawed, 4-6 mm long, free or slightly connate at the base for 2 mm, expanded apically into acute, blunt, or rounded, more or less oblanceolate blades to 1.0-1.5 mm wide, deep red distally, white or yellow-green below; stamens four, inserted on the connate portion of the petaloid petals, didynamous with the longer pair 5-10 mm long and the shorter pair 4.5-8.0 mm, pink throughout; pollen 36-38 µm in diam., 3 porate with lalongate pores up to 20 µm long and 5 µm wide; ovary ovoid, echinate, orange, yellow, green or white, ca. 3 mm long and bearing a thick, glabrous, arcuately curved, red style ca. 3 mm long. Fruits globose, 4-6 mm in diam. excluding spines, glabrous to sparsely strigose, densely spinose with spine bases touching, or almost touching, one another; individual spines deep orange-brown, 1.0-2.3 mm long, ca. 0.4 mm in basal diam., barbless, sometimes with long, wavy trichomes at the base. Chromosome number. Unknown.

description: Upright, weak, perennial herbs with erect branching stems to 50 cm, variably canescent to strigose with unicellular white trichomes 0.4-1.3 mm long often so dense that the branches appear white. Leaves simple, sessile, linear to ovate-lanceolate, 6-22 mm long, 1-3 mm wide, mucronate with a deep-purple apicule up to 1 mm long, sometimes appearing almost scale-like at the distal ends of branches, variously vestitured, glabrous, subglabrous to strigose above, consistently strigose below. Flowers borne in open terminal racemes; flowering stalks 4-6 mm long, separated in the distal third into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of bractlets 3-6 mm long and 0.5-1.0 mm wide; individual flowers borne upright on pedicel with upper sepals vertically oriented and the lowermost, gibbous sepal extending upward and covering the petals and sexual parts; peduncle and bractlets remaining on the rachis if an abortive flower is shed; sepals 4(-5), lanceolate to ovate, entire, strongly connivent, yellow on the inner surfaces and dusky rose on portions of the outer surfaces, turning red-brown with age, densely white-strigose on the outer surfaces; uppermost sepal 5.5-7.0mm long and 1.53.0 mm wide; lowermost sepal gibbous, geniculate, 8-9 mm long and 3-5 mm wide, dusky-rose; lateral sepals narrower than the lowermost sepal; glandular petals broadly ovate to irregularly orbicular in outline, thick, yellow or green, 2-3 mm wide, with saccate blisters restricted to the upper half of the dorsal faces and along the upper rim; petaloid petals three, clawed, 5-6 mm long, basally connate for 3.5-4.0 mm or about 2-3 mm above the point of stamen insertion, expanding apically into orbicular, serrulate blades 1.5-2.0 mm long and wide, yellow; stamens four, more or less equal in length, inserted about 1 mm above the base of the connate petal claws, free from the point of insertion, arcuate, 3.0-3.5 mm long, green; pollen 32-37 µm in diam., triporate with lalongate ora ca. 23 µm long and ca. 7.5 µm wide; ovary ovoid, densely strigose, 4-5 mm long, inserted latero-basally and surmounted by a thick, green, glabrous style 3-5 mm long. Fruits globose, 4-6 mm in diam. excluding spines, densely strigose with trichomes up to 1 mm long, and bearing scattered, slender spines; individual spines deep-red with yellow bases, 1.3-4.0 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm in basal diam. and bearing about 20 amber-colored retrorse barbs each 0.080.30 mm in length in several series beginning near the tip and wavy trichomes at the base. Chromosome number. Unreported.

description: Sprawling, procumbent subshrubs to 0.6 m tall, reaching 1 m in diam.; branches striate, lightly strigose with the trichome density increasing distally. Leaves simple, linear to linear-lanceolate, (11-)18-2 3(-30) mm long including the petiole, 1.5-2.0 mm wide, acute, mucronate with apicule reaching 1 mm in length, cuneate basally above a petiole about 1 mm long, variably strigose on both surfaces. Flowers borne in terminal racemes; flowering stalks 6-13 mm long each separated in the proximal half into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of linear bractlets 4.0-5.5 mm long and 0.5-1.0 mm wide; peduncle and bractlets persistent if flowers abort; buds symmetrically lanceolate to ovate in outline; sepals four, entire, connivent, lanceolate, pink-purple, strigose on the dorsal surfaces; uppermost sepals 610 mm long, 3.5-5.0 mm wide, scarious along the margins; lowermost sepals 7-10 mm long, 3.8-5.0 mm wide, slightly saccate; lateral sepals narrower than the upper and lowermost sepals; glandular petals cuneate and flaring outward from the base, about 3.5 mm long and about 1.5 mm wide, color unreported, covered on the outer surfaces with vertically oriented, saccate blisters; petaloid petals three, clawed, 6.5-8.5 mm long, connate basally for 3.4-4.5 mm and expanding terminally into triangular, minutely serrate or undulate blades about 1.2 mm long, ca. 1.2 mm wide, color unreported; stamens four, didynamous, inserted on the connate claws of the petaloid petals, free from the point of insertion with the longer pair ca. 5 mm long and the shorter pair ca. 4 mm long, yellow; pollen 30-35 µm in diam., triporate with the ora expanded equatorially into oval openings 20-22 µm long and 79 µm wide; ovary ovoid, densely pubescent, ca. 2 mm long, surmounted by a thick, glabrous, arcuately curved style ca. 2.5 mm long. Fruits globose, 4-5 mm in diam. excluding spines, la-nose, and bearing sparse, scattered spines; individual spines 1.0-3.5 mm long and 0.25-0.35 mm in basal diam., minutely barbed in the distal half and sparsely lanose at the base. Chromosome number. Unknown.

description: Prostrate to procumbent, Suffrutescent, perennial herbs with radiating, decumbent branches to 2 m long; branches green, striate when dry, variably strigose to densely hispid. Leaves simple, entire, petiolate, lanceolate to ovate, 8-19(-23) mm long including the 2-4 mm long petiole, 37 mm wide, acute to mucronate, strigose to hispid, often with one or more veins visible beneath. Flowers borne in terminal semi-secund racemes; flowering stalks 5-10 mm long, strigose to hispid, each separated into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of mucronate bractlets 1.5-7.0 mm long and 0.25-1.0 mm wide; peduncle and bractlets persistent if a flower aborts; buds asymmetrically ovate in outline, expanded ventrally; sepals 4(-5), spreading to slightly connivent, lanceolate, pink to deep rose red, covered with sericeous trichomes where exposed in the bud; uppermost sepal 8-13 mm long, 4.0-7.5 mm wide; lowermost sepal 9.0-13.5 mm long, 3.5-6.0(-8.0) mm wide, often saccate and scarious along the margins; lateral sepals noticeably wider than the upper and lowermost sepals; glandular petals oblong in outline, 3-5 mm long, 2.0-3.5 wide, pink, covered on the dorsal faces with short, parallel, vertically-oriented blisters; petaloid petals (2-)3, clawed, 6-11 mm long, connate for 2.0-4.0 mm, expanded terminally into irregular, ovate to cordate blades 3.0-3.5 mm long and 1.7-2.0 mm wide, purple or rose at the tips and with green claws; stamens four, didynamous, inserted about 1 mm above the base of the connate portion of the clawed petals, free from the point of insertion, with the longer pair 4.0-5.5 mm long and the shorter pair 2-4 mm long, green; pollen 33- 35 µm in diam., 3 porate with the ora expanded equatorially to 17-20 µm in length and 6.0-7.5 µm in width; ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm long, covered with stiff white trichomes and bearing a stout, glabrous, arcuate, green style ca. 3 mm long. Fruits circular to slightly cordate in outline 5-6 mm in diam. excluding spines, brown tomentose, and bearing few, stout, scattered spines, occasionally spineless; individual spines occasionally very short and hidden under the tomentum, but usually visible, 0.8-3.3 mm in length and 0.25-0.35 mm wide in basal diam., glochinate to almost smooth distally and usually with a few scattered trichomes near the base. Chromosome number. Unreported.

description: Erect, openly branched shrubs to 2 m tall; young branches green, increasingly tomentose distally; branches striate, tomentose or variably strigose. Leaves simple, broadly lanceolate to ovate, 20-35 mm long including the 3-7 mm petiole, 5-15 mm wide, entire, acute, mucronate, narrowing obliquely at base into petiole, slightly fleshy when fresh, usually densely tomentose on both surfaces with midvein and often two lateral veins visible beneath. Flowers borne in open lateral and terminal racemes with densely tomentose rachises; flowering stalks 2.5-5.0 mm long, each separated distally into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of linear bractlets up to 2 mm long and ca. 1 mm wide; peduncle and bractlets persisting if a flower aborts; buds asymmetrically ovoid with the ventral side expanded; sepals four, connivent, lanceolate to ovate, pink to deep crimson, turning white with age, tomentose to sericeous on the dorsal surfaces; uppermost sepal 7-9 mm long, 4-8 mm wide, broadly ovate, scarious along the margins; lowermost sepal 7-10 mm long, 2-5 mm wide, ovate, saccate; lateral sepals almost as wide as the upper and lowermost sepals; glandular petals rectangular in outline, 4.0-4.5 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, deep pink to red, flaring outward from the ovary, covered dorsally with thin, elongate, vertically oriented blisters; petaloid petals (2-)3, clawed, 5-10 mm long, variably connate at the base for 0.10-0.35 mm, expanding distally into deltate blades to ca. 1 mm wide, red at the apex, green below; stamens (3-)4, didynamous, inserted at the base of the petaloid petals, free beyond point of insertion with the longer pair 5.0-5.4 mm long and the shorter pair 4.04.5 mm long, green, white, or cream-colored throughout; pollen 26-32 µm in diam., synorate; ovary ovoid, 2-3 mm long bearing a stout, glabrous, arcuate pink style 2-3 mm long. Fruits globose, 4.5-6.5 mm in diam. excluding spines, densely tomentose and bearing numerous, scattered, thin spines; individual spines red with yellow tips, 2.5-5.0 mm long and 0.20-0.25 mm in basal diam., densely glochidiate at the distal end and bearing a few, long, unicellular trichomes at the base. Chromosome number. Unknown.

description: Sprawling, Suffrutescent subshrubs to 60 mm tall, often buried in sand; branches to 1 m long, striate, glabrate, often dark brown when dry. Leaves sparse, simple, lanceolate to oblong, 15-30(-42) mm long including the 1-8 mm long petiole, 3.5-11.0 mm wide, acute to mucronate, cuneate below blade, variably tomentose. Flowers borne in terminal racemes; flowering stalks to 5 mm long, each separated proximally into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of small bractlets; the short peduncle and bractlets remaining on the rachis if a flower aborts; buds slightly arcuate in outline; sepals four, lanceolate, entire, deep pink to violet; uppermost sepal 7-9 mm long, 4 mm wide; lowermost sepal 9-10 mm long, 4-5 mm wide, slightly saccate; lateral sepals narrower than the lowermost sepal; glandular petals cuneate, 2-3 mm long, 2.0-2.5 mm wide, dark red-purple, covered on the dorsal surfaces with irregularly-shaped blisters; petaloid petals three, (5-)7-9 mm long, narrowly lanceolate with pronounced, acuminate tips, essentially free to the base with the expanded portion 5-7 mm long to ca. 0.5 mm wide, red-purple with white bases; stamens four, all of equal length, 5-6 mm long, inserted at the base of the petaloid petals, free from the point of insertion; pollen ca. 30-32 µm in diam. with three long (almost touching) pores 4 µm wide in the center; ovary ovoid, 2.5 mm long, densely pubescent, surmounted by a glabrous, arcuate style 4 mm long. Fruits globose, 4.5-5.0 mm in diam. excluding spines, tomentose and bearing numerous scattered, reddish spines; individual spines 3.3-4.5 mm long, 0.25-0.6 mm in basal diam., with numerous minute retrorse barbs in the distal end and a few scattered sericeous trichomes at the base. Chromosome number. Unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Simpson, Beryl B. 1989. Krameriaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 49: 1-108.

description: Stiff, intricately branched, angular shrubs 0.31.0 m tall; branches dimorphic with variable proportions of long shoots and short shoots; short shoots nestled in tufts of straight, single-celled trichomes and long shoots often arising from the axil of one of the leaves in a short shoot; the long shoots branching at almost 90° angles producing a very stiff, angular network of branches; young branches strigose, most densely on young portions; old stems and branches gray. Leaves simple, linear to ovate, with those on long shoots up to 10 mm long and 2 mm wide and those on short-shoots 3-5 mm long and 0.75-1.0 mm wide, thick, slightly conduplicate with a median ridge on the upper surfaces, apically obtuse or occasionally mucronate, sessile, strigose to villous. Flowers borne singly in the axils of either long or short shoot leaves, often appearing as a cluster of two or three flowers at the end of a shoot, on flowering stalks 7-8 mm long with each separated in the proximal half of the stalk into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of small bractlets 2-3 mm long and 1 mm wide; flowering stalks completely shed if flowers abort; buds asymmetrically ovate in outline with the ventral half broader than the dorsal half; sepals five, connivent, ovate, entire, rose-pink, strigose, particularly in the central portions of the dorsal faces; uppermost sepal 7-10 mm long, 2.5-4 mm wide; lowermost sepal slightly geniculate and gibbous, 7-10 mm long, 3-3.5 mm wide; lateral sepals narrower than the uppermost or the lowermost sepals; glandular petals cuneate, deep rose to brick red, 2.2-3.0 mm wide and 2-3 mm long, with large, vertically oriented blisters on the dorsal surfaces, especially on the distal end; petaloid petals three, clawed, 5-6 mm long, connate basally for 1.0-2.7 mm with free portions of the lateral two petals irregularly cordate, shortly acuminate, 1.5-2.0 mm wide by 2 mm long and with the blade of the central petal oblanceolate, in all cases yellow or green basally, purple or deep pink tinged with lavender or purple above; stamens four, didynamous, inserted on the connate portion of the petaloid petals, free from the point of insertion, strongly arched from the point of attachment with the longer pair 4.5-5.0 mm and the shorter 3.5-4.0 mm, green to greenish-white: pollen ovoid 35-37 µm in diam., triporate with the pores greatly expanded equatorially to the point of bisecting the grain; ovary ovoid, densely strigose, 3 mm long, surmounted by a stout, glabrous, whitish-green style 2-3 mm long. Fruits circular to cordate in outline, slightly compressed laterally with vertical median ridge on both faces, about 5-6 mm across the broadest portion, sparsely to moderately strigose and bearing few, scattered, stout spines; individual spines red, 0.5-1.3(-l .5) mm long, 0.25-0.40 mm in basal diam., glabrous, or rarely with minute serrations near the tip. Chromosome number, n = 6, Turner (1958).
bibliographicCitation: Simpson, Beryl B. 1989. Krameriaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 49: 1-108.

description: Upright, slender, branched, often weak shrubs 0.3-1.5 m tall; young stems green, usually densely strigose at the tips; old stems striate, usually green, variably strigose. Leaves simple, lanceolate to narrowly elliptic, (8-) 17-3 3 mm long including a 2-9 mm petiole, 2-10 mm wide, acute, mucronate with a red-black apicule up to 1.5 mm long, basally cuneate, strigose to tomentose on both surfaces with the midvein often prominently raised below. Flowers borne in floriferous lateral and terminal racemes; flowering stalks 35 mm long, strigose, each separated medially into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of linear bractlets 3-4 mm long and 0.5-1.0 mm wide; peduncle and bractlets remaining on the rachis if a flower aborts; buds erect, congested at the inflorescence tips, unequally ovate in outline with the expanded, ventral half appearing white because of a dense sericeous covering of white trichomes; sepals four, entire, connivent, lanceolate, strigose to sericeous on the dorsal surfaces, pink or rose fading to pale pink or white with age and then appearing dichromatic pink and white; uppermost sepal ovate, scarious along the margins, 410 mm long, 4-7 mm wide; lowermost sepal broadly lanceolate, gibbous, 4.5-10.0 mm long, 3-6 mm wide; lateral sepals narrower than the uppermost sepal; glandular petals cuneate, pink or rose-colored, 2.5-4.0 mm long, 1.5-3.0 mm wide, covered on the dorsal faces with parallel, short, vertical saccate blisters; petaloid petals clawed, narrowly oblanceolate to linear, 4.5-7.0 mm long, basally connate for 2 mm, expanding apically into irregularly ovate pink blades 1.0-1.5 mm long and 1.0-1.5 mm wide; dark pink at the tip, yellow or white medially, pink at the base; stamens four (rarely three), didynamous, inserted near the base of the connate portion of the flag petals, free beyond the point of insertion, sigmoidally curved, with the longer pair 3-5 mm, and the shorter pair 2-4 mm, composed of stout, pink filaments and pink anthers; pollen 26-35 µm in diam., triporate, with the pores expanded equatorially into pores 14-23 µm long and 2.57 µm wide. Fruits globose, 4-7 mm in diam. excluding spines, variably strigose or occasionally tomentose and bearing numerous, scattered, thin spines; individual spines red or orange, (1.6-)2.8-4.6 mm long and 0.2-0.3 mm in basal diam., bearing many small retrorse barbs 0.1-0.3 mm long along the shaft, usually in the distal half, but always subterminally, glabrous at the base. Chromosome number. Unreported.
bibliographicCitation: Simpson, Beryl B. 1989. Krameriaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 49: 1-108.

description: Much branched shrub 1-2 m tall; young stems strigose, occasionally bearing multicellular capitate trichomes especially dense on the youngest branch tips and foliage; old stems with gray, striate bark, sometimes almost glaucous. Leaves borne in long and short shoots, sessile, simple, entire, linear to linear lanceolate, (0.5-)1.0-7.0(-15.0) mm long, 0.5-2.0 mm wide, acute to mucronate, variably strigose, sometimes also bearing multicellular capitate trichomes. Flowers borne singly in leaf axils of short shoots, but often appearing clustered into groups of two or three because of the compression of the shoot; flowering stalks 5-12 mm long with each separated medially into peduncle and pedicel by a pair of linear bractlets about 7 mm long, 0.5-1.0 mm wide, strigose, with the plain trichomes sometimes mixed with multicellular ones; pedicels completely abscissing if flowers abort; buds ovate in outline; sepals 4(5), connivent, entire, lanceolate to ovate, showy, bright pink, rose, or magenta, strigose and sometimes also with glandular, stipitate trichomes on the dorsal surfaces; uppermost sepal 8-11 mm long, 2-5 mm wide; lowermost sepal 8-10 mm long, 4-6 mm wide, gibbous; lateral sepals narrower than the upper and lowermost; glandular petals oblanceolate in outline, 2-3 mm long, pink, bearing vertical, saccate blisters on the outer surface which tend to be most prominent on, or restricted to, the upper portion of the dorsal face; petaloid petals three, clawed, 4-6 mm long, connate basally for ca. 13 mm with the free portions of the lateral petals expanded into acute, minutely serrate triangular blades 2.3-4.0 mm long and 1.5-3.0 mm wide with the free portion of the central petal smaller and oblanceolate, in all cases green basally and pink or pink with purple edges distally; stamens four, didynamous, inserted near the distal end of the connate portion of the petaloid petals, free from the point of insertion, strongly and unequally arcuate so that all of the anthers stand at the same height relative to the stigma, white, pink distally; pollen grains 30-43 µm in diam., triporate with the pores so expanded equatorially that some grains are synorate; ovary ovoid, about 3 mm long, densely strigose, occasionally displaying reddish protuberances that will develop into the fruit spines and bearing a stout, curved, glabrous pink style 3-4 mm long. Fruits cordate in outline, laterally compressed, about 6 mm long and 6 mm wide at the widest part excluding spines, bearing a vertical median ridge that is often slightly more pronounced on one side than the other, densely strigose to glabrous, spinose; spines ranging from long and thin to relatively short and stout, usually abundant, 2-5 mm long, 0.25-0.40 mm in basal diam., most commonly bearing few to several small retrorse barbs near, but not at, the tip, and long, curved, unicellular trichomes on the basal half, occasionally glabrous. Chromosome number, n = 6 (Ward, 1983).

description: Upright or mat forming shrubs 0.3-1 m tall; young branches dull green, striate in dry condition, strigose or sericeous with the vestiture especially dense on branch tips; old branches black, often gnarled. Leaves simple, entire, oblanceolate, ovate, or obovate, 6-15(-23) mm long, 2-6(-8) mm wide, mucronate with a red-black apicule up to 0.5 mm long, sessile, abruptly cuneate basally, sparsely strigose to densely sericeous on both surfaces with the whitish or golden-colored trichomes occasionally so dense as to form a notable marginal fringe. Flowers borne in sparse, latero-terminal racemes; flowering stalks strigose or sericeous, 7-12 mm long with peduncle and pedicel separated by a pair of leafy bractlets 49 mm long and 1-2 mm wide; entire flowering stalk abscising if a flower aborts; buds ovate in outline; sepals 4(-5), spreading or slightly connivent, lanceolate with entire margins, deep red-purple, sericeous on the dorsal surfaces; uppermost sepal 7-13 mm long, (3)4-6 mm wide; lowermost sepal 9-15 mm long, 4-8 mm wide, slightly saccate; lateral sepals narrower than the upper and lower; glandular petals cuneate to orbicular, 3-5 mm wide, red-purple, with irregularly circular blisters covering the dorsal faces; petaloid petals 2(-3), free, spatulate to clawed, 5.0-8.0 (-12.5) mm long, 1.5-2.0 mm wide, deep red with green markings at base of blade; stamens 3(-4) in two series with the single, shorter stamen, 3-6 mm long and the longer pair 4.5-7.0 mm; filaments incurved, pink; pollen grains 2629 pm in diam., tricolporate; ovaries ovoid, 34 mm long, densely sericeous, bearing stout, thick, nude styles 3-4 mm long. Fruits ovoid, 5-8 mm in diam. excluding spines, densely villous and bearing numerous, scattered spines; individual spines red-black, (1.7-)2.0-4.0 mm long, (0.10-)0.15-0.35 mm in basal diam., bearing recurved, amber-colored barbs to 1 mm long near the tip and in the distal portion of the shaft and long, unicellular trichomes around the basal portions. Chromosome number, n = 6, B. L. Turner [unpubl., voucher Dillon & Turner 1552 (TEX)].

description: Plants often glossy, in dark green to yellow-green, sometimes whitish green, thin to dense, flat mats. Stems 1-10 cm long, usually complanate-foliate, sometimes subjulaceous to junceous, often stout, simple or sparsely and irregularly branched; in cross-section with a cortex of a single row of large, thin-walled cells, subtended by smaller, thicker-walled cells, internally with large, thin-walled cells, central strand present or indistinct; pseudoparaphyllia foliose, rare; axillary hairs with a single, short, brown basal cell and three to four elongate, hyaline apical cells. Stem and branch leaves similar, ovate, ovate-lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate, or oblong-ovate, often concave, acute, acuminate or piliferous, soft, imbricate to distant, erect or spreading, sometimes secund, little altered when dry, symmetric or often asymmetric, smooth or undulate, strongly or scarcely decurrent; margins plane or recurved, entire or serrulate to serrate at extreme apex; costae short and double, one branch often reaching 1/3-½ the leaf length, rarely one branch poorly developed and costa appearing single, or costa sometimes lacking; upper cells linear, linear-flexuose or sometimes, when exceptionally broad, linear-rhomboidal, often becoming shorter near leaf apex and toward insertion, smooth or rarely with minute, granular, cuticular roughenings; alar cells often differentiated; decurrencies triangular to auriculate, in one to several vertical rows, cells elongate to rounded-quadrate. Brood-bodies often present (but not in South American taxa) from a stalked, branched base, cylindrical or fusiform, 2-7-celled, uniseriate, clustered in leaf axils on stems and branches, sometimes on dorsal leaf surfaces, hyaline to light green. Autoicous or dioicous. Perichaetia and perigonia numerous at bases of stems; perigonial bracts short, lanceolate to ovate, acuminate to filiform-acuminate; perichaetial leaves moderately enlarged, sheathing with somewhat spreading apices. Setae smooth, long, twisted, straight, curved or rarely circinate, yellow, orange to red-brown; capsules erect to cemuous, rarely pendulous, straight or arcuate, yellow, orange to red-brown, oblong to ovoid, often contracted under mouth when dry, smooth to furrowed; exothecial cells thick- or thin-walled; annulus differentiated in 1-3 rows, deciduous, sometimes tardily so; operculum conicto rostrate, shorter than the urn; exostome teeth bordered, shouldered, on outer surface cross-striolate below, sometimes with overlying papillae, coarsely papillose above, rarely papillose throughout, projecting from inner surface; en-dostome papillose, with a mostly high basal membrane, segments keeled, not or very narrowly perforate, cilia 1-3, nodulose, as long as or nearly as long as the segments, rarely rudimentary or lacking. Spores spherical to ovoid, smooth or papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, naked, fugaceous.

description: Plants medium-sized in complanate, mostly thin mats. Stems creeping or ± ascending to ca. 3 cm long, complanate-foliate. Leaves widely spaced, spreading, ovate to oblong-ovate, 1.1-1.4 mm long, gradually and broadly acute; margins recurved almost throughout, entire; cells long-hexagonal, 85-130 x (9-)14-20 µm, thin-walled; alar cells few, poorly differentiated; decurrencies stripping off with dissection, broad, 3-4 cells wide, to 10 cells long, cells rectangular to quadrate, sometimes somewhat inflated and spherical, mostly 2-4:1, 14-20 µm wide. Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves broadly oblong with cells 6-9 µm wide, thin-walled. Setae 2-2.5 cm long, reddish, twisted; capsules inclined, cylindric, ca. 2.5 mm long; exothecial cells subquadrate, firm-walled; operculum conic; exostome teeth striate-papillose below, papillose above; endostome papillose-spiculose, basal membrane high, segments keeled, strongly perforate, cilia mostly single. Spores 9-12 µm in diam., finely papillose.
bibliographicCitation: Buck, William R. & Ireland, Robert R. 1989. Plagiotheciaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 50: 1-23.
