description: Hierba anual o perenne, erguida o ascendente, 0.05-1 m de alto, tallos 1-varios, simples o ramificados, 0.8-4 mm diám., porción basal con corteza rojiza, longitudinalmente estriada o agrietada, porción apical desde completamente glabra hasta hirsuta con pelos porrecto-estrellados dorados o rojizos, radio central patente, 1.2-4.5 mm long., pelos simples cortísimos y algunos pelos estrellados; entrenudos bien desarrollados, longitud variable; ramas seriales desarrolladas o no. Yemas axilares seriales 2-3, generalmente la basal florífera. Hojas herbáceas, a veces discoloras. Estípulas nulas o reducidas a 1-2 pares de prominencias cónicas o subuladas, 0.1-0.3 mm long. Pecíolo 0-3(-11) mm long., indumento como el del tallo. Lámina elíptica, linear, ovada, a veces angustio-vada, raramente obovada, 8-80(-115) x 1.5-30(-40) mm, relación largoiancho = 1.9-4.5(-11): 1, disminuyendo de tamaño hacia el ápice, allí bracteiforme en algunos ejemplares, (1.5-)3-8 x 0.5-2.5 mm; base atenuada, cuneada o truncada; ápice obtuso o agudo; borde entero a doblemente aserrado; haz lisa, desde glabra a hirsuta, con pelos estrellados o porrecto-estrellados con el radio central poco más largo, oblicuamente dirigido hacia afuera; envés desde glabro a densamente piloso, con pelos estrellados; venas laterales 3-8, ángulo de divergencia 25-35°, prominentes en el envés, rectas o incurvas; venas terciarias a veces visibles; venación menor inconspicua. Flores axilares, solitarias. Alabastro latiovoide o romboide. Pedúnculo cilindrico, longitudinalmente estriado, erguido, 3-37 mm long., 0.2-0.3 mm diám., glabro o con pelos estrellados, simples y porrecto-estrellados. Profilos nulos generalmente, a veces presentes como prominencias 0.2-0.7 mm long., situadas en el ápice del pedúnculo, raramente desarrollados, subulados, 1-1.5 mm long. Pedicelo 2-9 mm long., diámetro ligeramente mayor, glabro a más piloso que el pedúnculo. Cáliz 3-11 mm long.; tubo calicino 1-3 mm long., cara externa glabra a hirsuta, con pelos porrecto-estrellados y estrellados, cara intema glabra, con pelos simples adpresos esparcidos o vellosa; lóbulos del cáliz ovados, ovado-lanceolados o angus-tiovados, 3-7 nervados, cara extema con indumento como el del tubo calicino, los internos, cuando pilosos, con bandas de pelos sedosos, adpresos, antes de los bordes membranáceos, cara interna glabra, ápice agudo, mucrón 0-0.4 mm long. Corola amarilla o crema, 0-10 mm más larga que el cáliz; pétalos con uña pilosa; lámina obovada 3.5-24 x 2-15 mm. Corona membranácea, borde superior fimbriado, lóbulos unidos a los pétalos ligeramente más largos que los de los sépalos. Filamentos estaminales subulados, erguidos, glabros, soldados al cáliz 0.4-0.7 mm en la porción basal; anteras elípticas o angustio-vadas, 0.4-3 x 0.3-0.8 mm, base emarginada, ápice obtuso recurvado a la dehiscencia; filamento inserto en una cavidad basidorsal 0.2-0.5 mm long.; polen amarillo. Ovario ovoide, 1.1-2.4 mm long., glabro a hirsuto, placentas 4-18 ovuladas; estilos cilindricos, frecuentemente bífidos, o 2-3 veces bifurcados, glabros o con algunos pelos simples en la porción basal; estigmas penicilados 0.3-1 mm long. Frutos ovoides o elipsoides, 3-9 x 2.5-8 mm; valvas ovadas, obtusas, cara externa lisa, amarillenta, glabra, subglabra o con pelos simples largos entremezclados con otros más cortos, vena placentaria deprimida; cara interna lisa, amarillenta, lustrosa, glabra. Semillas obovoides, 1.5-2.1 x 0.8-1.2 mm, ligeramente curvadas, un poco estrechadas por encima del exóstoma cónico o redondeado; rafe linear; cálaza redondeada o ligeramente deprimida, coloreada; episperma pilosiúsculo, reticulado, aréolas cuadranglares con depresiones punctiformes; arilo unilateral, 0.9-2 mm long., blanquecino o hialino en seco, borde entero.

description: Trees to 15 m. Branchlets slender, midway along flush 3-4 mm diam., distally weakly angular, soon terete, silvery to golden sericeous, the surface concealed by the indument cover, the hairs rather short, to 0.15 mm, straight, closely appressed to the surface; terminal buds plump, 3 × 3 mm, sericeous. Leaves alternate, widely and evenly spaced along current flush; petioles slender, to 1.5 × 0.3 cm, semi-terete, the indument as on branchlets; laminae chartaceous to coriaceous, plane, ovate, 10-20 × 5-8 cm, the base obtuse to rounded, briefly decurrent, the apex acute, acuminate for up to 2 cm, the margins minutely recurved throughout; upper surface light green to olive-brown, the midrib immersed, secondary and tertiary veins prominulous; lower surface densely silvery to golden sericeous, the hairs uniformly distributed, all vein orders raised, their prominence decreasing with rank; secondary veins 2-4 per side, the lowermost pair(s) subopposite shortly above the leaf base, ascending at 50-60°, arcuate, distal pairs loop-connected; tertiaries roughly horizontal, between secondaries straight or forked. Staminate inflorescences all evenly spaced along leafless flushes in the axils of cataphylls, or the distal ones in the axes of foliage leaves, to 10 cm long with 10 lateral branches, branch orders 3-4, the highest order dichasial, lax, the flowers distant, the axes golden sericeous; bracts and bracteoles caducous by anthesis, lanceolate, sericeous; pedicels terete, to 1 mm long, those supporting secondary flowers slightly shorter. Flowers infundibuliform, 2 mm diam., golden sericeous outside; receptacle infundibuliform, 1 × 1 mm, densely silvery pilose inside. Tepals chartaceous, ovate to ligulate, 1 × 0.5 mm (the inner whorl slightly broader), ascending, surrounding androecium at anthesis, the inner surface moderately silvery tomentose, the margins minutely papillose. Stamens of whorls I and II stipitate, 0.8 mm tall, the anthers depressed-elliptic to ovate, 0.5 × 0.5 mm, glabrous, the apex rounded to truncate, the connectives broad above the 2 locelli, these suborbiculate, introrse-latrorse, the filaments laminar, narrower than anthers, densely silvery pilose; whorl III stamens sessile, 0.8 mm tall, the anthers oblong, 0.4 × 0.3 mm, erect, locelli 2, extrorse-latrorse, the filaments broader than anthers, laminar, densely silvery pilose, the basal glands sessile, globose, apiculate; whorl IV staminodial; pistillode filiform. Pistillate inflorescence with indument and color as in staminate plants, but shorter and with fewer lateral branches, the flowers campanulate; stamens sterile, smaller; ovary glabrous; style slender, distinct from ovary; stigma tri-lobed, 0.3 mm diam. Fruits borne on narrowly claviform pedicels of up to 0.5 × 0.2 cm; cupules hemispherical, to 0.5 × 0.7 cm, glabrous outside, sericeous inside, the margins entire; drupes ellipsoid, to 1 × 0.5 cm.

description: Plants epiphytic in moss layers. Rhizomes very short, erect to ascending, 1.0 mm diam. Fronds to 30(37) cm long, pendent, inserted onto the rhizomes at acute angles, closely arranged (internodes 1 mm or less), caespitose. Rhizome scales to 2.2 x 0.4-0.5 mm, 8-10(-12) cells wide across bases, clathrate, dark brown to brown, strongly iridescent, cordate to pseudopeltate, acute to attenuate at tips; apical cells 1-4, linearly arranged. Petioles 5-20(-30) mm long, 0.4-0.5 mm thick, terete, with many, short, dark brown to brown, acicular to ciliform hairs 0.75-1.50 mm long, rarely glabrescent; simple and branched clavate hairs of crosiers and young fronds sometimes persistent on older fronds. Laminae papyraceous, 135-240(-350) x 15-20 (-30) mm, narrowly elliptic (broadest in the middle), cuneate to decurrent at bases, acute to attenuate at tips, abaxially pale green. Rachises dark brown to black, planar to protruding adaxially, hemispherically protruding abaxially, hairy on both sides, with hairs like those on the petioles. Largest segments 5.5-9.0 x 1.2-1.8 mm (4-5 times longer than broad), segments strongly ascending (45-60°), fully adnate, inequilateral and decurrent towards the bases, linear-oblong, the tips acute to obtuse; margins entire or broadly dentate in large fronds, without acicular or setiform hairs, but clavate hairs or cells present; midveins visible as dark lines, usually on both segment surfaces; basal 1—5(—8) pairs markedly smaller than the following segments, sometimes remote and auriculiform. Sori 1-6 pairs per segment, without hairs.

description: Plants minute; green or yellow green. Stem irregularly branched in one plane; central strand present, slender; pseudoparaphyllia ovate or narrow-ovate; paraphyllia absent; axillary hairs with 1-2-celled upper part, this hyaline when young. Stem leaves 0.4-0.6 mm long, erect-patent, straight or slightly homomallous, ovate or triangular-ovate, narrowing gradually from far below to apex, constricted at insertion, slightly concave, not decurrent; apex acuminate; margin entire or finely denticulate; costa single, extending 30-50% of way up leaf or sometimes less, to 21.0 µm wide at base; median laminal cells 14.5-42.0(-50.0) × 6.5-12.5 |iim, slightly incrassate, eporose; alar cells transverse-short-rectangular or quadrate or especially toward insertion short-rectangular, not inflated; alar group somewhat indistinctly delimited, triangular or ovate, extending upward along margin and inward all the way or almost to costa. Inner perichaetial leaves narrowing gradually or abruptly to acuminate apex, smooth or almost so; costa long, ending in lower acumen. Seta 5-8 mm long, smooth; capsule straight, erect or slightly inclined; operculum highly conical to short-rostrate. Exostome outside cross-striolate in lower part; border not widened at middle of teeth. Endostome cilia absent or vestigial. Spores 10.0-14.0(-16.5) µm, finely papillose.

description: Plants small or medium-sized; green, yellow green, or brownish. Stem somewhat stiff, pinnately or irregularly pinnately branched in one plane; central strand present, slender; pseudoparaphyllia triangular or irregular; paraphyllia uncommon, ovate and short-acuminate; axillary hairs with 1-2-celled upper part, this hyaline when young. Stem leaves 0.6-1.7 mm long, erect-patent to almost spreading, straight or slightly homomallous, triangular or rounded-triangular or ovate-triangular, narrowing gradually to apex, slightly concave, short-decurrent; apex acuminate; margin entire below, finely and obtusely denticulate above; costa single, ending in upper acumen or percurrent, 60.0-94.5 µm wide at base; median laminal cells 19.0-56.5(-67.0)  × 6.0-10.0(-l 1.0) µm, slightly incrassate, eporose; alar cells rectangular or short-rectangular or especially in upper part of group often quadrate, not or sometimes slightly inflated; alar group rather indistinct, triangular or ovate, along lower leaf margin. Inner perichaetial leaves narrowing slightly below and to acuminate apex, plicate. Seta 16-22 mm long, smooth; capsule curved, horizontal; operculum short-conical. Exostome outside cross-striolate in lower part, large part of surface reticulate; border widened at middle of teeth. Endostome cilia as long as segments or almost so. Spores 16.5-23.0 µm, finely papillose.

description: Autoicous. Plants 1.5-4 cm long × 1-2.5 mm wide, green, yellow brown to brown when dry. Stems about 0.1-0.2 mm in diam., in cross section composed of 9-25 epidermal cells surrounding 25-70 medullary cells. Leaves normally densely imbricate, deeply concave and squarrose when moist with the lobe subvertical in position and somewhat clasping the stem, lobe suborbicular, 0.8-2 mm long, apex broadly rounded, sometimes short apiculate, margins entire or ± crenulate, ventral margin broadly upcurved, when spread out forming an angle of ca. 140-180° with the keel; median cells 35-50 × 25-32 µm; oil bodies homogeneous, ellipsoid-fusiform, 15-25 per cell. Lobules narrow oblong to broad obovate-triangular, 0.3-0.6 × 0.2-0.35 mm, about l/3× lobe length, never reduced, inflated, apex oblique to truncate, not continuing into the ventral margin of the lobe, keel ± straight, free margin plane or incurved, sometimes waving, never undulate, in broad lobules making a sharp angle at the location of the second tooth (as in B. leiboldiana!), with 2(-3) widely spatiated teeth, teeth 1-3 cells long, ± inflexed, sometimes reduced. Underleaves imbricate, orbicular to broadly ovate, 0.3-0.6 × 0.4-0.8 mm, 3-5× stem width, apex rounded to truncate, margins narrowly recurved, rarely plane, bases decurrent and hardly folded, insertion line arched. Gynoecia with 1-2 innovations, bracts associated with innovations erect, obovate, shorter than perianth, apex acute or rounded, margins entire or weakly toothed, winged along the keel and with a large lobule ca. l/3-l/2× lobe length, bracts not associated with innovation resembling vegetative leaves, without wing; bracteole margins plane or incurved, entire or slightly toothed. Perianths obovate, up to 1.2 mm long, short exserted to 1/3 or immersed, 3-keeled, dorsal surface concave or plane, the lateral keels usually winged and with 1-5 teeth or lacinia up to 15 cells long, rarely smooth, the broad ventral keel rounded or with two sharp, diverging, smooth or denticulate ridges; beak about four cells long. Spores rectangular, 50-110 (mm long, with about eight rudimentary rosettes; elaters 220-430 µm long.

description: Plants dioicous, yellowish green to reddish brown. Stems to 6 cm long, leafy shoots 0.8-1.6 mm wide, profusely and irregularly branched. Stems 70-160 µm in diameter, medullary cells 15-24 in cross section, with two rows of ventral cells in surface view, cells quadrate to short rectangular, 15-75 × 25-80 µm, dorsal cells subquadrate to rectangular, 25-40 × 30-70 µm. Flagelliferous branches not seen. Branch leaves imbricate, lobe asymmetric-ovate, 290-690 × 400-760 µm, antical margin usually strongly toothed, with 5-20 teeth, 10-50 µm (1-4 cells) long, postical margin entire or with 0-3 teeth, apex rounded or broadly acute; median leaf lobe cells with rounded, short-elliptic or irregularly shaped lumina, 15-30 X 20^5 |Lim, marginal cells 10-20 × 12-35 )Lim, margins plane or incurved; walls thin, intermediate thickenings rare, oil bodies elliptical, 6-11 µm long (fide Thiers 4669, NY), botryoidal, 1-6 per cell, in all cells; ocelli 20-40 × 45-85 µm, basal, sometimes geminate, contiguous or isolated, 1-4 per leaf; lobules inflated or spherical forming series on lateral or main stems, reduced lobules rare, 0.2-0.4 the leaf lobe length, free margin involute or plane, apical tooth curved. Utriculi frequent, in pairs or solitary at the base of lateral branches. Underleaves distant to sub-imbricate, ovate, 140-390 × 150-400 µm, bifid to 2/3, lobes acute to short acuminate, uniseriate tip 1-2 cells long, margins entire, crenulate or with blunt projections, plane or recurved. Vegetative regeneration from leaves observed in a single case by Fulford (1944b). Androecia on lateral branches, in spikes of 4-7 bract pairs, spikes 750-1300 µm long, male bracteole ovate, 160 × 200 µm, bifid to 1/4, lobes rounded. Gynoecia lateral on main branches, with one sterile innovation; bracts obovate, 500 × 800 µm, with 3-4 geminate ocelli on the lower central lobe portion, proximal half of margin entire, distal half toothed, teeth uniseriate, to 65 µm long; bracteoles ovate to rectangular, 300-360 × 500-600 µm, bifid to 1/2, lower margins entire, apical region with 2-3 teeth (also on sinus). Perianth 330-620 × 550-950 µm, surface mammillose, horns four, compressed laterally, inflated when young, the tips collapsing after development, 110-200 µm long. Sporophyte valves elliptical-lanceolate, 185 × 345 µm. Elaters ca. 300 µm long. Spores not seen.

description: Epiphytic or terrestrial shrubs, wiry, scandent, or prostrate and decumbent. Young branchlets ridged, ± smooth, puberulous, the hairs eglandular, brown, the mature branches indumentum similar but glabrate. Leaves 4–8 per cm, apparently distichous, patent or sometimes diffuse; petiole 0.8–1.2 mm long, puberulous, the hairs eglandular; lamina ovate, elliptic, or rarely obovate, 0.5–1.3 × (0.2–)0.3–0.7 cm, basally obtuse or truncate, marginally entire, often slightly revolute, apically ciliolate with eglandular hairs, apically obtuse, adaxially glabrous or glabrate with eglandular hairs, abaxially glabrate with glandular hairs, the venation adaxially hyphodromous with the midvein impressed, abaxially hyphodromous or 3-nerved with the midvein raised. Axillary solitary flowers; bracts 4–5, chartaceous, ovate or transverse-elliptic, (0.5–)1–1.6 × 1–1.6 mm, sometimes marginally ciliolate with eglandular hairs, apically obtuse, abaxially glabrous; pedicel (0.4–)0.5 mm long, much reduced and hidden by overlapping bracts, glabrate with eglandular hairs; differentiated apical bracteoles 2, distinct, chartaceous, enveloping entire calyx tube, covering 37–60% of calyx, ovate or suborbicular, 1.6–3 × 1.6–3 mm, sometimes marginally ciliolate with eglandular hairs, rarely with glandular hairs, apically obtuse, the surface smooth, abaxially and adaxially glabrous. Flowers 4-merous (rarely 5-merous calyces or 3-merous corollas seen). Calyx aestivation valvate, campanulate, 3.2–4.8 mm long; tube slightly angled, 1.2–2.4 mm long, abaxially glabrous or glabrate with eglandular or glandular hairs; limb 2–3.3 mm long, abaxially glabrate or puberulous (apically) with eglandular or glandular hairs, adaxially glabrous; lobes triangular, 1.6–2.8 × 0.8–1.2 mm, marginally ciliolate with eglandular hairs, apically acute; sinuses rounded (U-shaped). Corolla light green (occasionally suffused with brick red), thin-fleshy, bistratose, campanulate, 4.4–6.3 mm long, 3–4 mm diam., 3–4 mm wide at throat, abaxially and adaxially glabrous; lobes 2.8–3.6 × 2.8–4 mm, strongly reflexed and curled, apically acute or obtuse, adaxially smooth. Stamens 8, 4.4–5.5 mm long, exserted about half their length; filaments distinct, straight, ± linear with parallel sides or broader at base, 1.2–2.4 mm long, abaxially glabrate, adaxially puberulous; anthers distinct, papillae on both thecae and tubules; thecae 1.6–2.5 mm long, without basal appendages; tubules 2, distinct, 0.8–1.3 mm long, dehiscing apically by terminal pores, 0.2 mm long, marginally irregular. Ovary 4-locular; style 4.8 mm long, exserted about half its length. Berry white, ± spherical, 6 mm diam., the persistent calyx lobes erect or spreading, becoming succulent (at least at base), same color as mature berry; embryo color unknown.

description: Herbs, 15-30 cm high. Rhizome creeping. Stems simple, rarely branched near the base, pale orange or yellowish to white, internodes 1-2 cm long. Leaves yellowish to white, connate in their lower half, narrowly triangular to narrowly ovate, 4-8 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, apex acute. Flowers solitary, 5-merous. Bracts and bracteoles similar to the upper leaves but smaller. Pedicels 1-3 mm long, sometimes longer. Calyx campanulate to cylindric, 4-8 mm long, tube 3-6 mm long, lobes triangular to broadly triangular, 1-2 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide, apex acute to acuminate, sinuses obtuse to acute, calyx scales present. Corolla salverform, yellow to orange, 25-65 mm long, tube cylindric, 20-50 mm long, dilated at the base by the maturing capsule, lobes narrowly ovate to narrowly obovate, 4-15 mm long, 1-5 mm wide, sometimes minutely hairy. Stamens inserted 3-5 mm below the throat, anthers subsessile, 0.3-0.8 mm long, dorsifixed, thecae tapering toward the base, apex rounded. Ovary fusiform, 5-8 x 1 mm, subsessile to stipitate, stipe 0.5-3 mm long in fruit. Style 10-30 mm long, stigma capitate-peltate, 5-lobed. Discoid glands absent. Capsule fusiform, 8-10 x 1.5-2.5 mm, medially septicidal. Seeds filiform to fusiform, with slender projections, 0.6-0.9 x 0.04-0.06 mm, paraphyses present.

description: Herbs, 7-37 cm high. Rhizome-scales narrowly ovate to ovate, 0.6-4.4 mm long, 1.6-2.3 mm wide, apex acute to acuminate. Stems purple to purplish white, relatively thick, mostly unbranched. Leaves ovate, 1.5-4 mm long, 1.2-1.9(-2.3) mm wide, apex obtuse to acute. Inflorescence a bifurcate cincinnus, each cincinnus 2.5-8 cm long and 2-17-flowered. Internodes of infructescence 3-8 mm long. Bracts narrowly ovate, 1.4-4(-5.5) mm long, 0.6-1.5 mm wide, apex obtuse to acute. Pedicels 1.3-6.7 mm long, in fruit to 6.8(-10) mm long. Flowers white, erect or nodding, 7-15 mm long. Floral tube 5.5-9.8 mm long, with six dark lines. Outer tepals 3-lobed, 3.5-5.6 mm long and wide; central lobe depressed ovate-triangular, 1.3-2.3 mm long, 2-3.3 mm wide; lateral lobes narrowly ovate-triangular, 1.2-2.1 mm long, 0.5-1.4 mm wide. Inner tepals ovate, often swollen, 1-1.5 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide. Connective with two deltate apical appendages ca. 0.2 mm long and wide. Style, including branches and stigmas, 4-6.2 mm long orange, branches 0.3-0.4 mm long, stigmas horseshoe-shaped, 0.4-1.1 mm diam., sinus ca. 0.3 mm deep, appendages to 5.5 mm long. Ovary obovoid, 1.9-4.2 x 1.1-2 mm. Capsule narrowly obovoid to obovoid, to 6.5 x 3.3 mm, the persistent part of the floral tube including the capsule (4.1-)6-9 mm long, style exceeding the floral tube by ca. 1 mm. Capsule longitudinally dehiscent, the three valves separating from base to apex, each valve split into two narrowly obovate parts cohering at the top; the three remaining ribs of the capsule and the three placentabearing ribs forming a lantern-like structure. Seeds 0.4-0.5 x 0.2-0.4 mm.

description: Shrubs or small trees, 5-9 m tall; young stems and leaves covered with a pinkish resinous secretion, this cracking and peeling as the parts expand; bark of the older stems reddish-gray, smooth, but still somewhat varnished and resinous. Sympodial units difoliate, geminate. Leaves elliptic, widest at the middle, glabrous and shiny above, drying somewhat dark, glabrous to densely pubescent beneath, the trichomes uniseriate, golden, and usually branched, either along the veins and in the primary vein axils, or covering the entire underside of the lamina; major leaves 10-25 x 5-10 cm, with 8-9 pairs of main lateral veins, these impressed above, prominent and golden below, the apex rounded to acute, the base acute, slightly decurrent on the petiole; petioles 1-1.5 cm long, caniculate above; minor leaves differing from the major ones only in size, 5-6 x 2.5-3.5 cm, the apex rounded to acute, the base acute; petioles 0.8-1.2 cm long. Inflorescences opposite the leaves, simple or occasionally furcate, 1.5-6 cm long, 5-20-flow-ered, resinous like the young stems and leaves; pedicel scars in pairs, the members of a pair closely spaced, but not overlapping, the pairs ca. 0.5 mm apart, the scars beginning about 1/2 way from the base of the inflorescence. Buds globose and completely enclosed in the calyx when young, later the corolla exserted and the buds obovoid, the entire bud resinous, otherwise glabrous. Pedicels at anthesis deflexed, 0.8-1 cm long, tapering from a base ca. 0.75 mm diam. to the abrupt widening of the calyx tube. Flowers with the calyx tube campanulate, 1.5-2 mm long, glabrous but covered with a resinous varnish, the lobes rounded-deltoid, 1-1.5 mm long, covered with the same resinous material as the tube, minutely papillose at the tips; corolla white or purplish, 1.5-2 cm diam., lobed ca. 3/4 of the way to the base, the lobes planar at anthesis, the tips and margins of the lobes minutely papillose; anthers 4.5-5 x 1-1.5 mm, poricidal at the tips, the pores teardrop shaped; free portion of the filaments 0.1-0.25 mm long, the filament tube 0.5-0.6 mm long; ovary glabrous; style straight, 6-7 mm long; stigma bilobed, the surface minutely papillose. Fruit a globose berry, apiculate with the persistent style base, green, ca. 1 cm diam,; fruiting pedicels woody, erect or slightly deflexed, ca. 2 cm long, 0.5-1 mm diam. at the base. Seeds tan, flattened-reni-form, ca. 2 x 1 mm, the surfaces minutely pitted, the margins incrassate. Chromosome number not known.

description: Shrub or small tree 2-5(-7.5) m tall with trunk 4-5(-12?) cm in diam.; branchlets 2-4 mm in diam., dark grayish-brown, grayish-green when young, glabrous but appressed-puberulous when young with hairs to 1.5 mm long. Leaves alternate or subopposite, often crowded at tips of branches, l(-3)-foliolate, with sessile leaflets; petiole ± terete, (slightly) winged, 8-40(-60) mm long, the base slightly tumid or not but rather thick in fast-grown shoots, tubercle usually absent, glabrous or puberulous with straight hairs 0.1-0.2 mm long; leaflet blade rather variable in outline, (narrowly) ellptic to (narrowly) (sub)obovate, 6-25.5 × 2.1-8 cm, (mainly shortly) attenuate or occasionally subcuneate at base, acuminate at apex with obtuse acumen 4-15(-30) mm long, or occasionally retuse, the margin subrevolute, the blade chartaceous-subcoriaceous, dull and deep green above when fresh, paler beneath, glabrous on both sides, rarely subglabrous at the basal part of the midvein, venation brochydodromous to sometimes slightly camptodromous, prominent on both sides, midvein prominent above. Inflorescences terminal or axillary near tips of the branchlets, erect, narrowly paniculate, not longer than the leaves, ca. 5-16 × 2-8 cm, densely minutely pubescent with hairs 0.10.5 mm long; side-branchlets alternate, 1-7 mm long; bracts (very broadly) ovate, concave to cucullate, 0.6-2.5 × 0.5-1.2(-2) mm, subglabrous; pedicels 1-4 mm long; bractlets 2, subopposite or alternate, one or both sometimes subtending a secondary pedicel. Flowers 5-8 mm in diam., scentless; calyx lobes quincuncial, adnate to the petals at very base, subcircular, 1.1-1.5 × 1.2-2 mm, rounded or obtuse at apex, softly coriaceous, ciliate or fimbriate, facially glabrous, with 810 parallel nerves branching here and there towards the tip; petals persistent, imbricate, mostly quincuncial, very widely spreading, elliptic to subcircular, 2.64.4 × 1.8-3.6 mm, roundish or obtuse, the margin somewhat wavy, chartaceous or subcoriaceous, pale yellow to white, papillose above, glabrous beneath, the 8-10 nerves like those of the calyx lobes but ± diverging; filaments subulate, 0.7-1.3mm, glabrous, furnished at base with an abaxial subglobular knob 0.1-0.2 mm high and sometimes protruding radially from the disc; anthers heart-shaped, ca. 0.4-0.5 mm long, including a mucronate tip 0.1 mm easily seen in bud only, papillose especially dorsally; disc annular, 5-parted by deep grooves to 1/2 of its thickness, 2-3 mm in diam., fleshy, the parts ±2-lobed, 0.4-0.5 mm high and 0.3-0.5 mm thick, charged with some glands and also sometimes with some tubercles, carpels adnate to the disc and connate in the lower half, globose in the upper half, ca. 0.3 mm high, furnished with numerous ovoid protuberances to 0.1-0.2 mm long and densely beset with spreading, thick hairs to 0.2 mm long; style inserted ca. midway on the carpels, 0.5-1 mm long (nearly completely free), 0.1-0.3 mm thick, glabrous; stigma capitate, slightly 5-lobed, 0.2-0.4 × 0.2-0.4 mm. Fruits depressed, stellately-lobed, (10-)15-20 × 20-30 mm, with glands, sparsely appressed-pubescent with hairs 0.1 mm long; loculi provided 2/3 from the base with an apophysis, muricate or sparsely muricate with tubercles or occasionally with blunt spines to 5 mm long, weakly curved and shrunken when mature, dehiscent septicidally from apex down to 3-4 mm above the base; seed 1 per loculus, obliquely tear-shaped, 8.5-11 × 5-6.5 mm, the ventral side flattened at the base, the apex with a short, curved beak, the dull brown testa linear-colliculate with interspaces of ca. 0.1-0.2 mm, but particularly near the chalaza also roundish-colliculate with interspaces of the same length, those shining and darker than the rest of the testa; chalazal area ovate, 2.5-4 × 1.8-2.2 mm, dark brown-black; hilum 0.5-1.2 mm broad; micropyle with a dark brown-black caruncle; embryo 1 or more, usually 2, 1 much taller than the other(s), cotyledons unequal, thick, with 2 ears and a conical radicle projecting beyond them, plumule very small.
bibliographicCitation: Kaastra, Roelof C. 1982. A monograph of the Pilocarpinae (Rutaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 33: 1-198.

description: Terrestrial shrub to 2 m tall; mature branches terete, glabrate, orangish-brown; twigs terete, muricate, hirsute with hairs 1.5-2 mm long, glaucous. Leaves elliptic to ovate-elliptic, 6—10 X 2.5-5 cm, basally rounded, apically abruptly short caudate-acuminate, margin somewhat revolute, glabrous above but densely strigose beneath; 3(-5)-plinerved from base, midrib and lateral nerves impressed above and raised but inconspicuous beneath, reticulate veinlets impressed and inconspicuous above and obscure beneath; petioles terete, rugose, hirsute, 4-5 mm long and 1.5-2.5 mm in diam. Inflorescence ca. 20-25-flowered, encircled at base by numerous oblong to obovate bracts 30-55 X 20-40 mm; rachis terete, somewhat fusiform, glabrous, 2-2.5 cm long and 4.5-5 mm in diam. in midportion (ca. 3 mm in basal diam.); floral bracts oblong to oblong-obovate, 50-55 X 23-26 mm, basally truncate, apically rounded, glabrous, bright glossy orangish-red when fresh; pedicels subterete, striate, glabrous, 14-15 mm long and 3.5-4 mm in diam., provided with few short-stipitate to sessile spherical glands 0.1 mm in diam. at distal tip; bracteoles oblong, obtuse, somewhat cucullate, ca. 3 X 1.5 mm, glabrous but marginally provided on each side with several subspherical or oblong callose, sessile glands to 0.75 mm long. Flowers: calyx glabrous, ca. 7 mm long, greenish-white when fresh; hypanthium subcylindric, rugose, coarsely 10-ribbed, 4-4.5 mm long, basally apophysate; limb campanulate, rugose, 2.5-3 mm long; lobes triangular, acute, 1-1.5 X 3 mm, marginally with an oblong, callose gland ca. 1.5 mm long along each side but these not contiguous at tip; sinus rounded; corolla cylindric but abruptly and sharply constricted at throat, glabrous, 38 mm long and 9 mm in diam. (ca. 4.5 mm in diam. at throat), when fresh the lower half white grading through a very dark purple in upper half with throat white, lobes deltoid obtuse spreading at anthesis, 1 X 3 mm, white with purple margins when fresh; stamens 34-35 mm long; filaments with the shorter one densely short-pilose along inner surface of distal half, the longer one moderately pilose on the medial inner surface, alternately 3.5-4 mm and 9.5-10 mm long; anthers alternately ca. 33 mm and 25-27 mm long; thecae alternately ca. 16 mm and 12.5 mm long; tubules golden-yellow tinged with purple when fresh; style 37 mm long. Berry not seen.

description: Tree, to 20 m; branchlets terete, glabrous (minutely laxly pilose, glabrescent towards apex). Leaves chartaceous, shiny green, elliptic, 6-18 x (2.5-)4.5(-6) cm, base acute or rotundate, apex acuminate, acumen to 1 cm long, margins not thickened, midrib and 3-5 pairs of lateral veins per side slightly impressed, glabrous above, prominent with few, single hairs on and along midrib, glabrescent beneath, basal pair of lateral veins departing at a more acute angle than following pairs, densely prominulously reticulate; petioles pilose, glabrescent, 1.5 cm long. Peduncles sparsely pilose; pedicels glabrous, 1 mm long. Flowers glabrous, white, 1-1.5 mm long, floral tube obconical, pilose within; tepals about as long as tube, pilose at base within; stamens of series I, II, III fertile, staminodes of series IV sub-clavate, ca. 0.5 mm long, base pilose; outer 6 stamens with introrse cells, connective hardly protruding beyond cells, filaments distinctly narrower than anthers, of about same length, pilose; stamens of series III extrorse, glands on slender, pilose stalks; ovary globose; style much shorter than ovary; stigma as big as cross-section of style. Berry 1.3 x 0.7 cm; cupule pateriform, with 6 teeth at margin formed by persistent tepals, merging into enlarged (0.5 cm long) pedicel.

description: Plants erect, yellowish green, in tufts. Stems 3-15 mm high, radiculose, equally foliate with erect patent leaves when wet or appressed leaves when dry, often with flagelliferous branches in the axils of the upper leaves. Leaves 1.8-2.3 mm long, lanceolate, gradually contracted, margins entire, only slightly denticulate at the extreme apex. Costa filling 1/2-2/3 of the leaf base, 155 µm wide, excurrent, in transverse section with large ventral and dorsal hyalocysts, a median band of stereids and 2-4 stereids ventrally. Alar cells hyaline or brownish, often bistratose, slightly inflated. Basal laminal cells in about six rows, rectangular to subquadrate, 15-40 × 10-16 µm, narrower at margins. Upper laminal cells rectangular, 13-30 × 4-12 µm. Seta ca. 10 mm long, light brown, sinuose. Capsule 1.5 mm long, light brown, slightly ribbed. Operculum as long as the capsule, obliquely rostrate. Calyptra cucullate, entire at base.
bibliographicCitation: Frahm, Jan-Peter. 1991. Dicranaceae: Campylopodioideae, Paraleucobryoideae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 54: 1-238.

description: Plants resembling much those of C. nivalis var. nivalis, to 3 cm high, in tufts, light green above, reddish tomentose below. Stems equally foliate. Leaves to 5 mm long, lanceolate. Costa filling 2/3 of the leaf width, excurrent in a serrate tip, in transverse section with ventral stereids and dorsal groups of substereids, smooth at back in the lower part and ridged in the upper part of the leaf. Alar cells lacking or scarcely developed. Basal laminal cells elongate rectangular, thin-walled, 6-12 × 12-26 µm, at margins in 5-6 rows narrower. Upper laminal cells incrassate, short rectangular to oblique, 6-10 × 10-19 µm, ca. 1:2. Sporophyte as in C. nivalis var. nivalis.

description: Shrub; young shoots pubescent at first with spreading ferruginous hairs, becoming glabrous, grey or brown, rough, without lenticels. Stipules 3-4 mm long, lanceolate, densely ferruginous-pubescent. Leaves clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 4.6-10.5 × 2.6-5.3 cm, elliptic, apex obtuse to shortly attenuate, base rounded or truncate, coriaceous, glabrous or with residual pubescence along the midrib on the lower surface, venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondaries 6-9 pairs, slightly convergent, arcuate, slightly impressed on the upper surface; tertiaries oblique, parallel, numerous, slightly impressed on the upper surface. Petiole 0.5-1 cm long, slightly channelled, ferruginous-pubescent. Fascicles 2-5-flowered, axillary and ramiflorous. Flowers bisexual (?). Sepals five, ca. 2 mm long, ovate, apex acute, ferruginous-pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Corolla ca. 3 mm long, tube ca. 1 mm long, lobes (four-)five, ca. 2 mm long, ovate, apeacute, often auriculate at base, sparsely sericeous outside on the tube, glabrous inside. Stamens (four-)five, fixed about halfway up the corolla tube, filaments ca. 1 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, broadly ovate, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, long strigose; style ca. 1.5 mm long after anthesis; style-head entire or slightly lobed. Fruit ca. 1.7 cm long, ellipsoid, apex and base rounded, thin-walled, smooth, subglabrous. Seed solitary, ca. 1.3 cm long, ellipsoid, rounded at base and apex, slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.2 mm thick; scar adaxial and extending around the base of the seed, ca. 2 mm wide. Field characters. A low shrub to 3 m high, with white flowers and a fleshy yellow fruit. Flowering and fruiting Aug.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Tree; young shoots subglabrous or with some evanescent appressed brown pubescence, becoming pale greyish, thinly scaling, sometimes with a few large lenticels. Leaves loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 7-16 × 3.4-6.5 cm, broadly oblanceolate or obovate, apex obtuse, round or truncate, base narrowly attenuate, margin revolute, coriaceous, glabrous, lower surface minutely punctate; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 7-12 pairs, parallel or convergent, arcuate, sometimes slightly impressed on the upper surface; intersecondaries shorter or absent; tertiaries obscure, horizontal to reticulate. Petiole 0.5-2.7 cm long, not channelled, broad and flattened. Fascicles 3-7-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 0.4-1.2 cm long, glabrous. Flowers unisexual (?). Sepals (four)five, ovate-lanceolate, apex acute, subglabrous. Corolla subrotate, 5-5.5 mm long, tube ca. 1.5 mm long, lobes five, 3.5-4 mm long, ovate to broadly elliptic, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube and exserted; filaments 2.5-4 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 2 mm long, broadly lanceolate to oblong, apex rounded, glabrous. Staminodes 0-2, up to 1.5 mm long, and sometimes bearing a rudimentary anther. Disk absent. Ovary ovoid, 2-3-locular, sparsely pubescent at the base; style ca. 1.5 mm long after anthesis; style-head simple. Fruit 1.8-2.5 cm long, obovoid or broadly ellipsoid, apex rounded, style persistent, base rounded or broadly tapered, smooth (shrinking when dry), glabrous. Seed solitary, 1.4-1.8 cm long, broadly ellipsoid, slightly laterally compressed, obtuse at apex and base, testa smooth or slightly wrinkled, shiny, ca. 0.3 mm thick; scar adaxial, about three quarters the length of the seed, 1-3 mm wide; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle exserted, ca. 2 mm long; thin sheath of endosperm present. Field characters. Tree to 25 m high and 30 cm diam., sometimes flowering as a small treelet, slash with copious white latex. Rowers pale green, sometimes reddish within, fruit ripening bluish or purple. Flowering recorded May, Aug-Sep, Nov-Dec, fruit maturing Feb-Mar and Jun.

description: Shrub or tree; young shoots subglabrous, pale greyish-white, becoming scaly, usually with some large elongate lenticels. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered, spirally arranged, 2-6(-9.5) × 1.2-3 cm, narrowly to broadly oblanceolate, apex obtuse, rounded or emarginate, base acute to narrowly attenuate, margin often slightly revolute, coriaceous, glabrous, upper surface often scrobiculate, lower surface often minutely punctate; venation eucamptodromous to brochidodromous, often obscure, midrib flat or slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 5-7(-9) pairs, steeply ascending, parallel or slightly convergent, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries often long; tertiaries reticulate. Petiole 1-5 mm long, not channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 1-10-flowered, mostly axillary. Pedicel 1-5 mm long, glabrous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, (1.5-)2-3 mm long, lanceolate to suborbicular, apex acute to rounded, glabrous or sometimes margin ciliate. Corolla broadly cyathiform to subrotate, 2.5-3.5(-4) mm long, tube 0.5-1 mm long, lobes five, 2-2.25 mm long, elliptic to suborbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube and exserted; filaments 0.75-1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.5-1.5 mm long, broadly lanceolate or ovate, with rounded apex, glabrous; stamens absent in female. Staminodes absent, or occasionally a minute vestige present. Disk absent. Ovary conical or ovoid, 3(-4)-locular, sparsely pubescent to subglabrous, style 0.25-1 mm long, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 1.2-1.4 cm long, broadly ellipsoid, apex rounded, base rounded to slightly tapered, soft-skinned, smooth, glabrous. Seed solitary, 0.8-1 cm long, broadly ellipsoid, rounded at both ends, sometimes with a small beak at the apex of the scar, not laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, ca. 0.5 mm thick; scar adaxial, full-length, 5-5.5 mm wide, rugose or verrucose; embryo with plano-convex, free cotyledons, radicle exserted, ca. 0.75 mm long; thin sheath of endosperm present. Field characters. Many-branched shrub or crooked tree to 8 m high, with copious white latex. Flowers pale green to white, fruit ripening purple or black. Flowering mostly Sep-Jan, fruit Mar and Aug.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Plants to 4 cm high, dark to yellowish green, often brownish below and lighter above, in loose tufts. Stems equally foliate, tomentose below; rhizoids papillose. Leaves 6-7 mm long, erect patent when wet, more or less appressed when dry, and lanceolate. Costa filling half of the leaf width, excurrent in a nearly smooth or scarcely dentate awn, which may be hyaline or (rarely) concolorous, in transverse section with ventral hyalocysts and a dorsal layer of stereids. Alar cells inflated, hyaline or reddish, usually reddish inside and hyaline outside, protruding into the costa. Inner basal laminal cells elongate, hyaline, short rectangular to oval, 6-10 × 19-54 µm, the marginal cells in 8-10 rows very narrow. Upper laminal cells incrassate, oval to shortly elongate, with thickened comers, 3-5.5 × 20-35 µm (410:1). Sporophyte not known.

description: Plants 0.5 to 5 cm high, yellowish green above, dark green to blackish below. Stems interruptedly foliate, the leaves erect patent when wet but appressed when dry. Leaves 4-5 mm long, lanceolate, subtubulose in the upper part, with entire margins. Costa filling half of the leaf width, excurrent in a serrate, sometimes at the outermost tip hyaline awn, in transverse section with ventral and dorsal stereids, smooth at back. Alar cells hyaline and thin-walled or reddish and incrassate in older leaves. Basal laminal cells rectangular, 2-6:1, incrassate and slightly porose, 6-10 × 26-42 µm, at margins in 2-8 rows elongate. Upper laminal cells irregular, short rectangular to oblique or rhomboid, 3-10 × 10-19 µm, (2-) 4(-6): 1, incrassate. Seta 1.5 mm long, curved. Capsule 1 mm long, globose.
bibliographicCitation: Frahm, Jan-Peter. 1991. Dicranaceae: Campylopodioideae, Paraleucobryoideae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 54: 1-238.

description: Shrub or small tree 1-5 m high; hairs all simple or a mixture of simple and dibrachiate, reddish-brown to yellowish; twigs densely pubescent when young, glabrescent with age, the bark remaining smooth or becoming rough with cracks, grey to reddish-brown; leaves densely pubescent when young, losing some or all pubescence with age, generally more pubescent beneath than above, elliptic to obovate or oblanceolate, 2.6-5.3 cm long, 0.9-2.3 cm wide, 2.5-3.5 times as long as wide; apex rounded to acute, the mid vein often slightly excurrent; base cuneate or acuminate; petiole 2-5 mm long, 1-1.5 mm thick, densely pubescent when young, glabrescent with age, slightly channeled; midvein impressed for entire length or only proximally above, prominent, slightly sulcate below; lateral veins indistinguishable or up to about 10 pairs faintly visible; marginal veins equalling laterals in prominence; blades light to dark grey-green above, light yellow-green to reddish-brown beneath, coriaceous; flowers often grouped together in bracteate shoots of up to ca. 12 flowers, the bracteate shoots up to ca. 3.5 cm long, axillary or terminal, terminating in a vegetative bud; peduncles solitary or in pairs, 4-12 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, densely pubescent; bracts linear, 3-4 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide, densely pubescent; bracteoles linear, 3-4 mm long, 0.5-0.7 mm wide, densely pubescent throughout or glabrous proximally within; calyx-lobes ovate, more or less concave, 2.2-3.4 mm long, 2-3.2 mm wide, 1-1.5 times as long as wide, submembranous, densely to sparsely pubescent without, densely to sparsely pubescent distally to glabrous or nearly so proximally within; hypanthium obconic, densely pubescent, 1.5-2.3 mm long; disk ca. 2 mm in diam., sparsely pubescent, sometimes becoming enlarged and convex after flowering; style 4-6 mm long, very sparsely pubescent to glabrous; stamens 80120, 3-8 mm long; anthers 0.4-0.7 mm long when dry; petals suborbicular, 3-5 mm in diam.; ovary 2-4-locular; ovules 7-12(-14) per locule; fruit subglobose, 3-5 mm in diam., blackish-purple, pubescent; seeds usually 1-2 per fruit, ca. 4 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Landrum, Leslie R. 1981. A monograph of the genus Myrceugenia (Myrtaceae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 29: 1-137.

description: Petiole 0.4-1.5(-1.8) cm long, lower leaf surface usually with closely appressed indumentum  of whitish or brown hairs, becoming glabrous with age. A tree to 40 m high and 1.5 m diam., with very thick simple or branched buttresses to 1 m high or more. Bole often slightly fluted. The bark is greyish-white to dark brown, dependent on the situation, scaling in thick narrow plates or shallowly fissured. The slash is reddish or pinkish with plentiful white watery or sticky latex. The flowers are fragrant, white or cream and the fruit ripens red to purplish-black with abundant white latex in the pericarp. Peak flowering throughout the range is from Jun to Sep, with ripe fruit recorded in Oct and Dec to Jun. The seeds (not fruit) are eaten by birds, kinkajou and paca (Wendt et al 4271, Mexico, Veracruz).
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Small tree; young branches glabrous, greyish-brown, becoming cracked and fissured with age, usually without lenticels. Without spines. Leaves usually opposite, spaced, less frequently spirally arranged, 3-7.2 × 1.2-4.3 cm, broadly oblanceolate, elliptic or orbicular, apex obtuse, rounded or truncate, base narrowly attenuate to rounded, thinly coriaceous with a slightly revolute margin, glabrous; venation brochidodromous, with a strong marginal vein, midrib flat on the upper surface; secondary veins, 4-8 pairs, ascending, straight, parallel or slightly divergent; inter-secondaries long; tertiaries descending from the margin and tending to run parallel to the secondaries. Petiole 2-5 mm long, not channelled, glabrous Flowers bisexual, axillary, 5-10 in a fascicle. Pedicel 4-8 mm long, glabrous. Sepals five, 2-2.5 mm long, ovate, apex rounded, glabrous or occasionally a few appressed hairs inside. Corolla glabrous, 3-4.5 mm long, lobes five; median segment broadly elliptic, apex rounded, lateral segments 1-1.5 mm long, lanceolate or falcate, often erose. Stamens five, glabrous; filaments 1.5-2 mm long, anthers 0.75- 1.25	mm long, lanceolate. Staminodes 1.5-2 mm long, ovate, often erose, usually slightly folded and incurved against the style, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, with some appressed pubescence, five-locular; style 2-2.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style head simple. Fruit ca. 1.3 cm long and 0.5 cm broad, narrowly ellipsoid, apex rounded, base acute, smooth, glabrous; pericarp 1-2 mm thick, fleshy. Seed solitary, 0.9-1 cm long, narrowly ovoid with acute apex and obliquely truncate base; testa hard, shining, smooth, hollowed at the base, 0.2-0.4 mm thick; scar basal, crescent shaped, ca. 1-2 mm long; embryo vertical, with plano-convex cotyledons, and slightly exserted radicle, surrounded by a thin sheath of endosperm. Field characters. A small unarmed tree to 20 m high, with pale grey fissured and grid-cracked bark. The whitish or cream-coloured scented flowers are produced from Dec to May.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Shrub or small tree; young branches golden-ferruginous to whitish sericeous-pubescent, soon glabrous, grey to greyish-brown, usually becoming cracked, fissured, lenticellate. Not spiny. Leaves spirally arranged, not clustered, 4-11 × 0.9-3 cm, narrowly elliptic or less frequently oblanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate or occasionally acute, base narrowly attenuate; chartaceous; small amount of residual golden-ferruginous indumentum along midrib below, otherwise glabrous; venation brochidodromous with a prominent and thickened marginal vein; midrib flat on the upper surface; secondary veins 10-17 (-20) pairs, ascending, straight, parallel; intersecondaries long; tertiaries descending from the margin and parallel to the secondaries. Petiole 0.5-1.2 cm long, not channelled, sericeous-pubescent at first, soon glabrous. Flowers bisexual, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves, in fascicles of 5-12 flowers. Pedicel 1.5-3(-6) mm long, golden ferruginous appressed puberulous. Sepals five, (1.5-)2-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate, obtuse or rounded, outside appressed sericeous-puberulous, often with a glabrous membranous margin, inside usually glabrous, occasionally puberulous near the margin. Corolla glabrous, 3-3.5 (-4.5) mm long, tube ca. 1 mm long, lobes five; median segment broadly elliptic to suborbicular, apex rounded, often erose, lateral segments lanceolate, erose or laciniate, 1-1.5 mm long. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube, glabrous; filaments 1.5-2 mm long, anthers 0.75-1 mm long, lanceolate, ventrifixed and extrorse in bud. Staminodes 1.5-2 mm long, lanceolate to ovate, erose to fimbriate, infolded, glabrous. Ovary slender, ovoid, tapering gradually into the style, 5-locular, glabrous; style 1.25-2.5 mm long, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 0.6-0.85 cm long, broadly ellipsoid or globose, apex obtuse to rounded, base rounded or tapered, smooth, glabrous; pericarp 0.3-1 mm thick, fleshy. Seed one(two), 4-6 mm long, broadly ellipsoid to subglobose, slightly laterally compressed or angular (plano-convex in 2-seeded fruit); testa hard, shining, sometimes with several thickened plates on the adaxial side, slightly hollowed at the base, 0.3-1 mm thick; scar basal, circular, 0.75-1 mm diam.; embryo horizontal, oblique or less frequently vertical, with thin foliaceous cotyledons and radicle exserted 1-1.5 mm, surrounded by copious endosperm. An unarmed shrub or small tree rarely reaching 20 m high, with grey to dark brown fissured and grid-cracked bark. The slash is pale cream, with some white latex. The sap-wood is cream and the heart wood rose. The greenish or yellowish-white flowers are rather strongly scented and visited by bees and other insects. The mature fruit is black or purplish.

description: Tree 8-25 m tall, sometimes with buttresses, the branchlets subterete, lepidote when young. Leaves simple, elliptic to oblong-obovate, rounded to obtuse or subcuspidate apically, rounded to cuneate at base, 6-20 cm long, 2.5-9 cm wide, entire, the margins frequently somewhat revolute, coriaceous to subcoriaceous, lepidote above and below, otherwise glabrous, conspicuously glandular at base of midvein below, drying olive to grayish; petiole lepidote, 1-3 cm long. Inflorescence a raceme or racemose panicle, densely lepidote, terminal, the bracts spathulate, to 2.5 cm long and 3 mm wide, the pedicels 1.5-2.5 cm long. Flower with the calyx tubular, (18-)25-40 mm long, 5-12 mm wide, bilabiately to subspathaceously split 3-8 mm, one of the lobes with three denticulations, the other two, weakly 5-striate with the striations ending in the teeth, densely lepidote, usually also with plate- shaped glands; corolla white, salverform, 6-9.5 cm long, 0.5- 0.7 cm wide at mouth of tube, the tube very narrowly cylindrical, 5-8 cm long, the lobes 1.7 -2cm long, mostly glabrous outside, lepidote and with patelliform glands at apex of tube and base of lobes, the tube apex densely papillose- puberulous inside, the rest of the tube glabrous; stamens didynamous, inserted 4.5 -5 cm from base of tube, the thecae more or less parallele, 4mm long; ovary oblong, densely lepidote, the ovules 2- seriate in each locule; disk short - cupular, 1mm long, 2mm wide. Fruit a linear- oblong capsule, subteret, narrowed at base and apex, 19-19 cm long, 1.1-2cm wide, densely lepidote, the calyx persistent , spathaceously split along one side; seeds flat, bialate, to 1.3 cm long, 3.5 -4cm wide, the wings hyaline - membranaceous.
bibliographicCitation: Gentry, Alwyn H. 1992. Bignoniaceae--part II (Tribe Tecomeae). Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 25: 1-370.

description: Small trees. Leaves alternate, pari-pinnately compound, distal leaflet rudimentary or wanting; leaflets 2, 4, or 6, opposite, or less often alternate; rachis winged or nearly cylindric; stipules wanting. Inflorescence of terminal or axillary panicle-shaped thyrses, panicles or racemes. Flowers 4- or 5-merous, actinomorphic, unisexual (the plants dioecious or monoecious); pedicels articulate or not articulate; sepals imbricate, connate at base, shorter or as long as the petals; corolla of distinct petals with imbricate aestivation, inserted on the base of an extrastaminal nectary disc, the petals erect or reflexed, elliptic to obovate, without appendages, the margins sometimes with an elongated projection on each side above the base; nectary disc prominent, annular or lobed; stamens 8, spreading, filaments of equal or unequal length, longer than the petals, glabrous or pubescent, the anthers dorsifixed, elliptic or ovate, retuse at apex; ovary 2 or 3 carpellate, with as many locules as carpels or unilocular, each carpel with a single campylotropous or apotropous ovule, the stigma 2 or 3-lobed to subcapitate, sessile. Fruits baccate, indehiscent, ellipsoid, ovoid, or globose, with leathery mesocarp. Seed 1(-2), with a fleshy, edible testa. Embryo fleshy, lomatorrhizal with straight erect cotyledons of similar size, or notorrhizal, with cotyledons diagonally superimposed, the radicle punctiform or elongated. Pollen colporate, nearly spherical, oblate, isopolar, trangular or trigonous with straight to convex sides.

description: Subarbusto delgado 0.5-1 m de alto, corteza rojiza. Hojas herbáceas, viscosas, patentes o recurvadas, en seco frecuentemente plegadas a lo largo de la vena media. Estípulas nulas. Pecíolo 3-20 mm long., cilindrico. Lámina foliar ovada, 18-55 x 8-37 mm, base redondeada, cordada o brevemente atenuada; ápice obtuso, subagudo o agudo; borde revoluto, simple o doblemente crenado-aserrado; haz lustrosa, glabra o con algunos pelos esparcidos, especialmente sobre las venas; envés opaco, más pálido, glabro o con algunos pelos sobre las venas. Inflorescencias cimosas, axilares, 2-6-floras. Pedúnculo 10-33 mm long con pelos estrellados cortos, pelos simples, tenues, rojizos y a veces pelos glandulares. Profilos altemos, desiguales, los fértiles 0,5-3 mm long. Ramas sucesivas 3-13 mm long. Pedicelos 2-7 mm long., ligeramente más gruesos que el pedúnculo. Flores heterostilas. Cáliz verde oscuro, 7-10 mm long., indumento ferrugíneo, pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares; lóbulos ovados o angustiovados, 3-5 nervados, los intemos con bandas de pelos más o menos adpresos antes del borde membranáceo, mucrón apical 0.4-0.5 mm long. Corola 11-16 mm long., color naranja muy vivo o amarillo-anaranjada. Corona laciniada. Filamentos estaminales glabros, 3.7-6 mm long, en flores longistilas, 7-8 mm long, en flores brevistilas, soldados 0,5 mm en la base al tubo calicino; anteras sagitadas. Ovario ovoide; estilos cilindricos, 5-6 mm long, en flores longistilas, 1.5-2 mm long, en flores brevistilas; estigma penicilado, 0.5-1 mm long. Frutos 4-9 mm long., cara externa lisa, papilosa, o apenas verrucosa, con pelos simples y glandulares, cara interna glabra, lustrosa, vena placentaria no o ligeramente prominente.

description: Hierba o subarbusto frecuentemente viscoso, 0.15-1.2 m de alto, base lignifícada, tallos 1-varios, 2-4 mm diám., corteza rojiza con grietas longitudinales; ramas jóvenes con pelos glandulares, estrellados, porrecto-estrellados y simples tenues. Yemas axilares 1-2 seriales, la basal florífera; ramas seriales desarrolladas o no. Hojas generalmente cartáceas, discoloras en seco, planas, a veces plegadas en ángulo a lo largo de la vena media. Estípulas nulas o reducidas a prominencias glandulares subuladas 0.3-0.6 mm long, escondidas entre el indumento. Pecíolo 0.5-15 mm long., cilindrico, indumento como en el tallo. Lámina foliar ovada, latiovada, a veces elíptica, angustiovada o suborbicular, raramente obovada, 14-82 x 9-59 mm; base cuneada, brevemente atenuada, redondeada, a veces ligeramente cordada; ápice agudo u obtuso; borde simple o doblemente crenado-aserrado o serrulado, plano o ligeramente revoluto; haz lustrosa en seco, pardo-rojiza, a veces castaña, con pelos estrellados o porrecto-estrellados laxamente dispuestos, frecuentemente entremezclados con pelos glandulares; envés verde-grisáceo, con pelos estrellados y algunos glandulares; 4-9 pares de venas laterales alternas u opuestas, ángulo de divergencia 30-55°; venas terciarias prominentes o inconspicuas; venación menor a veces visible en el envés. Flores axilares, solitarias, heterostilas. Pedúnculo cilindrico, 6-20 mm long., con pelos estrellados y glandulares. Profilos reducidos a un mechón de pelos porrecto-estrellados en la articulación, o a prominencias glandulares, raramente desarrollados. Pedicelo 3-11 mm long., ligeramente más grueso que el pedúnculo. Cáliz 7-16 mm long.; tubo calicino 1.5-3 mm long., con pelos estrellados y glandulares densos; lóbulos externos ovados, anchos, indumento como el del tubo, lóbulos internos triangulares, angostos, glabrescentes a ambos lados de la vena media, sin pelos sedosos antes de los bordes membranáceos, mucrón 0.1-1 mm long. Corola 12.5-30 mm long., color salmón o durazno, a veces con venas y base más coloreadas; lámina 10-27 x 8-13 mm. Corona membranácea, amarilla, color fucsia o purpúrea, lóbulos unidos a los pétalos 1-2 mm long., borde superior laciniado. Filamentos estaminales subulados, glabros, soldados 0.6-1 mm en la base al tubo calicino, 3.5-6 mm long, en flores longistilas, 6-9 mm long, en flores brevistilas; anteras angustiovadas, 1.7-2.5 x 0.5-1.2 mm, filamento inserto dorsalmente a 0,5-0,8 mm, base emarginada, ápice obtuso, recurvado en la dehiscencia. Ovario latiovoide, verde, hirsuto, 1.7-3 mm long., placentas 8-19-ovuladas; estilos cilindricos, glabros o con algunos pelos, 4-6 mm long, en flores longistilas, 1.5-2.5 mm long, en flores brevistilas; estigmas penicilados, amarillos, 0.6-1.5 mm long. Frutos subesféricos, 5.5-11 mm long.; valvas tuberculadas, pilosas, con pelos porrecto-estrellados o estrellados y glandulares, por dentro glabras, amarillentas o jaspeadas. Semillas obovoides, rectas o ligeramente curvadas, 2-3.5 x 1.1-1.5 mm; exóstoma breve, cónico; rafe linear; cálaza no prominente; episperma glabro, reticulado, aréolas transrectangulares o cuadranglares; arilo amplio, borde lacerado.

description: Subarbusto 0.3-1 m de alto; ramas viejas con corteza pardo-rojiza, longitudinalmente estriada; ramas jóvenes con pelos estrellados, porrecto-estrellados, pelos simples tenues y a veces pelos glandulares. Yemas axilares 2, la basal florífera. Hojas discoloras, cartáceas. Estípulas triangulares, rojizas, 0.2-0.5 mm long. Pecíolo cilindrico, 2-8 mm long., tomentoso. Lámina elíptica, angustielíptica o linear, 24-100 x 3-29 mm; base cuneada, a veces redondeada; ápice obtuso o agudo; borde revoluto, crenado-serrulado, a veces doblemente, dientes obtusos; haz verde-grisácea, tomentosa, con pelos estrellados y porrecto-estrellados, radio central 0.7-0.9 mm long, orientado diagonalmente, y algunos pelos glandulares cerca del borde; envés tomentoso, grisáceo o amarillento, pelos estrellados; venas laterales 5-8, ángulo de divergencia 30-40°, hundidas en la haz, prominentes en el envés, con pelos porrecto-estrellados, incurvas, perdiéndose cerca del margen, con ramas laterales hacia los dientes; venas terciarias prominentes en el envés, más o menos perpendiculares a la vena media o ligeramente recurvas. Inflorescencias cimosas, axilares, 3-20-floras. Pedúnculo cilindrico, 4-15 mm long. Ramas sucesivas 1-3 mm long. Profilos subulados, desiguales, 0.4-3 mm long., opuestos o alternos cerca del ápice de cada rama, los fértiles más desarrollados. Pedicelos 2-5 mm long., diámetro e indumento como el del pedúnculo. Flores heterostilas. Cáliz 5-9 mm long.; tubo calicino 1-2 mm long., tomentoso, pelos estrellados, sobre las venas pelos porrecto-estrellados, radio central 0.5-0.6 mm long, y pelos glandulares 0.4 mm long., por dentro glabro; lóbulos angustiovados o triangulares, 3-5 nervados, los internos con bandas de pelos sedosos, antrorsos antes de los bordes membranáceos, mucrón apical 0.5-0.6 mm long. Corola amarilla, 1-2 mm más larga que el cáliz; pétalos con uña glabra; lámina obovada, 5-8 x 2.5-6 mm; corona amarilla, laciniada, lóbulos unidos a los pétalos 0.6 mm long.; filamentos estaminales subulados en seco, glabros, 2.5-3 mm long, en flores longistilas, 5 mm long, en flores brevistilas; anteras sagitadas, 1.2-2 x 0.5-1 mm, lóbulos básales y ápice obtuso revolutos a la dehiscencia, filamento inserto a 0.5-0.7 mm de la base. Ovario elipsoide, 1.5-2 mm long., hirsuto, placentas 4-8 ovuladas; estilos cilindricos, 2.5-2.7 mm long, en flores longistilas, 1 mm long, en flores brevistilas, glabros; estigma penicilado, 0.3-1 mm long. Frutos subesféricos u ovoides, 4-6 mm long.; valvas ovadas, granulosas por fuera, pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares, por dentro lisas, lustrosas, amarillentas, vena placentaria no prominente. Semillas ob-ovoides, curvadas, 2.4-3 x 0.7-1.3 mm, un poco estrechadas por encima del exóstoma cónico; rafe linear apenas marcada; cálaza redondeada no prominente; episperma pilosiúsculo, reticulado, aréolas cuadranglares y transrectangulares, con una o dos depresiones punctiformes; arilo unilateral más largo que la semilla, lobulado.

description: Hierba erecta 30-80 cm de alto, con o sin pelos glandulares; base leñosa hasta 10 mm diám., 1-varios tallos, corteza parda con grietas longitudinales que dejan ver el súber blanquecino; ramas jóvenes con pelos porrecto-estrellados y simples, tenues, frecuentemente retrorsos, a veces con pelos estrellados y glandulares. Yemas axilares 1-2; ramas seriales desarrolladas o no. Hojas planas o plegadas a lo largo de la vena media en seco, las floríferas apicales con frecuencia de tamaño bruscamente decreciente, sésiles o subsésiles, bracteiformes, 3-5 mm long. Estípulas nulas o cónicas o subuladas, 0.2-0.6 mm long. Pecíolo 0-15 mm long., indumento como el del tallo. Lámina foliar ovada, angustiovada, elíptica o angus-tielíptica, raramente obovada, 9-58 x 3-22 mm, relación largo:ancho = 1.5-6.5:1, base cuneada o redondeada; ápice agudo u obtuso; margen plano o ligeramente revoluto, aserrado-crenado, aserrado o subentero, dientes obtusos; haz con pelos porrecto-estrellados o estrellados, a veces con pelos glandulares; envés con pelos estrellados densos y sobre las venas pelos porrecto-estrellados; 3-6 pares de venas laterales prominentes en el envés, rectas o ligeramente incurvas, divididas o no cerca del margen, ángulo de divergencia 18-45°. Flores axilares, solitarias, heterostilas. Alabastros piriformes u ovoides, ápice acuminado o agudo. Pedúnculo (7-) 10-30 mm long., indumento como el del tallo. Profilos nulos o muy pequeños. Pedicelo 3-10 mm long., indumento más denso que el del pedicelo. Cáliz 7-15 mm long., tomentoso o hirsuto; tubo calicino 1.5-3 mm long.; lóbulos triangulares o angustiovados, los internos con bandas de pelos sedosos, antrorsos, antes de los bordes membranáceos. Corola más larga que el cáliz, color salmón o anaranjada; pétalos 8-21 mm long. Corona purpúrea 0.7-1.5 mm long. Filamentos estaminales 3-4 mm long, en flores longistilas, 5-7.5 mm long, en flores brevistilas; anteras amarillas o anaranjadas, 1.3-2.5 mm long., base emarginada, ápice obtuso y recurvado a la dehiscencia. Ovario 1.5-2.3 mm long., hirsuto, placentas 13-33 ovuladas; estilo cilindrico, glabro o piloso en la mitad basal, 3-5 mm long, en flores longistilas, 1.5-2.5 mm long, en flores brevistilas; estigma penicilado; ramas 0.5-1 mm long. Frutos 4-9 mm diám., esféricos u ovoides; valvas ovadas o elípticas, por fuera granulosas o tuberculadas, con pelos simples y a veces glandulares, por dentro glabras y lisas, vena placentaria más o menos prominente. Semillas rectas o ligeramente curvadas, obovoides, 1.5-2.3 x 0.8-1.2 mm; exóstoma breve; rafe linear; cálaza redondeada, oscura; episperma pilosiúsculo, reticulado, aréolas con una depresión punctiforme en cada una; arilo angosto, unilateral, corto.

description: Hierba, subarbusto o arbusto, 0.2-2 m de alto, uni o pluricaule; ramas viejas con corteza rojiza, parda o negruzca, glabra o glabrescente, lenticelas pequeñas; ramas jóvenes cilindricas o longitudinalmente estriadas, con indumento variado, tomentosas, densamente pilosas o subglabras, pelos cortos, 0.5 mm long. Yemas axilares 1-2, la basal florífera; ramas seriales desarrolladas a veces. Hojas cartáceas o coriáceas, discoloras, abolladas. Estípulas ausentes o reducidas a prominencias subuladas rojas, glandulares, 1-2 a cada lado, 0.1-0.3 mm long. Pecíolos 0.5-30 mm long. Lámina ovada a angustiovada o elíptica, 2.8-9.7 cm long.; base obtusa, redondeada o cordada, a veces cuneada; ápice redondeado o agudo; margen plano o ligeramente revoluto, crenado desde la base, a veces aserrado o subíntegro, crenas generalmente desiguales o duplicadas; haz oscura en seco, ligeramente lustrosa, con pelos estrellados y porrecto-estrellados laxos; envés tomentoso, grisáceo; venas laterales 5-7 a cada lado, hundidas en la haz, prominentes en el envés, con algunos pelos porrecto-estrellados, ángulo de divergencia 20-35(-50)°; venas terciarias recurvas o aproximadamente perpendiculares a la vena media, hundidas en la haz, prominentes en el envés; venación menor conspicua en el envés. Inflorescencias cimosas, axilares, 2-20-floras, a veces las básales unifloras, hasta 15 cm long. Pedúnculo 4-45 mm long. Ramas sucesivas 3.5-22 mm long. Profilos opuestos, subopuestos o alternos, desiguales, filiformes, subulados o lineares, 1-5 mm long. Pedicelos inferiores 2.5-10 mm long. Flores heterostilas. Cáliz 6.5-15 mm long., tomentoso por fuera, con pelos glandulares entremezclados; tubo calicino 1,6-4 mm long., por dentro glabro; lóbulos lanceolados u oblongo-lanceolados, agudos o acuminados, los externos 5-nervados, los internos 1-3 nervados, con bandas de pelos sedosos, antrorsos antes de los bordes membranáceos. Pétalos hasta 1/2 más largos que el cáliz, amarillos; lámina 6-15 mm long., obovada u obovado-oblonga, glabra. Corona 0.8-1 mm long., laciniada en el borde superior. Filamentos estaminales soldados 0.3-1 mm en la base al tubo calicino, 3-4.5 mm long, en flores longistilas, 4.5-7 mm long, en flores brevistilas; anteras cerradas ovado-oblongas o lineares, 1.8-3.5 x 0.6-1.3 mm, obtusas o subretusas, raramente apiculadas, dorsifijas, ápice revoluto en la dehiscencia. Ovario cónico, 1.5-1.7 mm long., pelos cortos, placentas 8-14 ovu-ladas; estilos cilindricos, 3.5-6 mm long, en flores longistilas, 1.5-2.5 mm long, en flores brevistilas; estigma 0.3-0.8 mm long., varias veces dividido, multífido, a veces pocas ramas y ligeramente más largas, hasta 1 mm long. Frutos trígono-globulosos, a menudo apiculados, o trígono-subcónicos 5-11 mm diám., dorso tuberculado o verrucoso, piloso amarillenta. Semillas obovoides u oblongo-obovoides, 2.4-3.5 x 1-1.7 mm, rectas o ligeramente curvadas, atenuadas en la parte inferior, un poco estrechadas por encima del exóstoma cónico; cálaza no prominente; episperma pilosiúsculo, pardo o negruzco, reticulado; arilo 1.5-3.4 mm long.

description: Hierba o subarbusto 20-75 cm de alto, generalmente erecto, corteza rojiza, longitudinalmente agrietada; ramas jóvenes viscosas, tomentosas o hirsutas, pelos glandulares 0.3-1.2 mm long., pelos simples cortos tenues y porrecto-estrellados con el radio central 1-6 mm long. Yemas axilares 1-2, la basal florífera, a veces ramas seriales desarrolladas. Hojas patentes o recurvadas, planas o plegadas en ángulo longitudinalmente, a veces discoloras. Estípulas reducidas, 0.2-0.3 mm long. Pecíolo semicilíndrico, 2-16 mm long., indumento como el del tallo o más denso. Lámina ovada o angustiovada, a veces suborbicular, 6-55 x 5-32 mm, relación largo:ancho = 1.1-2.4:1; base redondeada, brevemente atenuada, obtusa o cuneada; ápice agudo u obtuso; borde ligeramente revoluto, aserrado-crenado o crenado, dientes generalmente asimétricos; haz con pelos porrecto-estrellados y glandulares, venas impresas; envés grisáceo, con pelos estrellados, vena principal y 4-8 pares de venas laterales prominentes, con pelos porrecto-estrellados, alternas o subopuestas, ángulo de divergencia 26-48°; venas terciarias salientes en el envés, recurvas o más o menos perpendiculares a la vena media; venación menor inconspicua. Flores axilares, solitarias, heterostilas. Pedúnculo cilindrico, 2-8(-15) mm long., indumento como el del tallo. Profilos nulos o subulados, 0.2-2 mm long., opuestos en la articulación, o alternos cerca del ápice del pedúnculo. Pedicelo 1-10 mm long., ligeramente más grueso que el pedúnculo. Cáliz 7-15 mm long.; tubo calicino 1.5-2 mm long., tomentoso o hirsuto por fuera, con pelos estrellados, porrecto-estrellados y glandulares, por dentro con pelos simples densos; lóbulos 5-9 nervados, angustiovados o triangulares, brevemente mucronados, tomentoso-hirsutos por fuera, los internos con bandas de pelos sedosos, adpresos, antes de los bordes membranáceos, glabros por dentro. Corola rosada o color salmón, con venas más oscuras, 1.4-1.8 veces más larga que el cáliz; pétalos con uña pilosa; lámina obovada, 11-20 x 714 mm. Corona del mismo color que los pétalos o purpúrea, lóbulos unidos a los pétalos 1-2 mm long., laciniados, lóbulos unidos a los sépalos 0.3-0.7 mm long. Filamentos estaminales glabros, amarillos o verdosos, soldados 0.5-1 mm en la base al tubo calicino, 3-6 mm long, en flores longistilas, 5-7 mm long, en flores brevistilas; anteras amarillas, anaranjadas u obscuras, 1.5-2 x 0.6-1 mm, base anchamente emarginada, ápice recurvado después de la dehiscencia, filamento inserto a 0.5 mm de la base. Ovario ovoide o elipsoide, 1.5-3 mm long., hirsuto, placentas 13-20 ovuladas; estilos cilindricos con pelos cortos en la base o glabros, 3.5-7 mm long, en flores longistilas, 1.5-2.5 mm long, en flores brevistilas; estigma penicilado, paucirramoso, 0.5-1 mm long. Frutos 5-9 mm long.; valvas tuberculadas por fuera, con pelos glandulares de base frecuentemente obscura y pelos estrellados o porrecto-estrellados, por dentro glabras y lustrosas, amarillentas. Semillas claviformes, a veces corta y gruesa, 2.2-3.2 x 0.8-1.2 mm, recta o ligeramente curvada; exóstoma cónico breve; rafe linear o ancha; cálaza redondeada apenas prominente; episperma generalmente pilosiúsculo, reticulado, aréolas transrectangulares o más o menos cuadrangulares; arilo reducido, unilateral, 1-2 mm long.

description: Hierba o subarbusto, 8-70 cm de alto; ramas jóvenes con pelos tenues recurvos, pelos glandulares 0.3-1 mm long, y especialmente a la altura de los nudos algunos porrecto-estrellados, radio central 1-2 mm long. Yemas axilares 1-2, la basal florífera; ramas seriales desarrolladas. Hojas herbáceas, viscosas. Estípulas nulas o reducidas a prominencias glandulares cónicas 0.3 mm long. Pecíolo semicilín-drico, indumento como el del tallo, 1-8 mm long. Lámina elíptica, angustiovada u ovada, 13-61 x 3.5-27 mm, relación largoiancho = 1.8-3.8:1; base cuneada o redondeada; ápice agudo, a veces obtuso; borde plano, simple o doblemente aserrado-crenado; haz con pelos glandulares y porrecto-estrellados laxos, paucirradiados, (2-8 radios), frecuentemente reducidos al radio central 0.4-1.8 mm long.; envés indumento igual o más corto; 5-7 pares de venas laterales salientes en el envés, ángulo de divergencia 25-40°, perdiéndose cerca del margen; venas terciarias a veces visibles en el envés; venación menor inconspicua. Flores axilares, solitarias, homostilas. Alabastro angustiovoide, mucrones muy cortos libres en el ápice. Pedúnculo 7-45 mm long., con pelos simples, tenues, retrorsos, pelos glandulares y a veces porrecto-estrellados reducidos al radio central. Profilos nulos o reducidos a prominencias glandulares cónicas 0,3 mm long., opuestas en la articulación. Pedicelo 3-6 mm long., diám. e indumento igual al pedúnculo, o ligeramente más grueso y piloso. Cáliz 3.5-7 mm long.; tubo calicino 1 mm long.; lóbulos más o menos triangulares, cara externa con pelos glandulares y simples antrorsos, a veces algunos porrecto-estrellados, cara interna glabra, lóbulos internos angostos, glabrescentes a ambos lados de la vena media, bordes membranáceos. Corola rosada, color salmón o amarillo-naranja, 1-5 mm más larga que el cáliz; pétalos obovados, 4-8 x 2-4- mm. Corona fimbriada, lóbulos unidos a los pétalos 0,3-1 mm long. Filamentos estaminales 2-4 mm long.; anteras 0.5-1 mm long., dorsifijas, a veces el ápice recurvado a la dehiscencia. Ovario elipsoide, 1.2-1.7 mm long., hirsuto, placentas 8-23 ovuladas; estilos cilindricos, 1-3 mm long.; estigmas penicilados, 0.5-1 mm long. Frutos 3.5-7 mm long.; valvas ovadas, verrucosas o granulosas por fuera, epidermis papilosa, con pelos glandulares y algunos simples, por dentro lisas, lustrosas, amarillentas, vena placentaria poco prominente. Semillas obovoides, 1.4-2.2 x 0.6-1.1 mm, ligeramente curvadas; exóstoma cónico; rafe linear; cálaza redondeada no prominente; episperma glabro, reticulado, aréolas pequeñas, transrectangulares o cuadranglares; arilo pequeño, unilateral, más corto que la semilla, lobulado.

description: Perennial herbs, 20-170 cm high. Rhizome creeping, 2.5-10 mm diam., branching but with long unbranched segments, internodes very short or more often up to 4 cm long, the insertion of the culms accordingly crowded or spaced, sometimes with a creeping part with long internodes and side branches with short internodes. Culms erect, 1-7 mm diam., smooth or slightly wrinkled to striate, but only very rarely with longitudinal ridges. Cataphylls 2-3 to each culm, lower one 1-8 cm long, distal one 3-25 cm long, usually mucronate by a = 3 mm long, acicular, rudimentary blade, yellow to light brown or stramineous. Foliar leaves absent or, in var. mexicanus, present and then 1-2 to each culm, the blade terete, laterally compressed, very short to equalling the culm. Inflorescence pseudolateral, few- to many-flowered, usually lax and then up to 15 x 7 cm, sometimes congested and only 2.5 x 2 cm, compound, cymose, consisting of several congested cymes, of which the ultimate ones are unilateral drepania. Lower inflorescence bract appearing as a continuation of the culm, (2-)5-15(-25) cm long, or usually constituting between 1/10 and 1/5 (sometimes less) of the total plant height, distal bracts progressively shorter, scariose. Each flower clasped by two 1.5-2.5 mm long, acute, scariose bracteoles. Tepals equal or outer ones longer, lanceolate, stramineous to dark brown or castaneous, sometimes lighter colored along the midrib and at least the inner ones often with scariose margins, outer tepals 3-5.5 mm long, concave, acuminate, inner tepals 3-5 mm long, flat to concave, acute. Stamens 6, 1.5-3 mm long; filaments flat, widened toward the base; anthers linear 0.7-2.5 mm long, 1-6 x the length of the filaments. Style 0.5-1.5 mm. Stigmas 1.5-3 mm. Capsule ellipsoid to ovoid, apiculate, round to trigonous or slightly 3-lobed, 2.5-4.5 x 1.5-2 mm, light to dark brown, often light-colored at the base and dark at the apex, glossy, 3-septate. Seeds ellipsoid, oblong, ovoid, or irregularly shaped, short apiculate, 0.6-0.8 x 0.2-0.5 mm, rugose, light brown to castaneous below a hyaline outer seed coat.

description: Perennial cushion-forming, glabrous herbs. Stems more or less regularly forked, the proximal parts densely covered with persisting, wilted leaves. Leaves regularly, densely and spirally inserted along the stem; blade equal to or longer than the sheath, terete, smooth with hard-pointed prickly apex. Inflorescence reduced to a single, lateral, subapical flower, clasped by 2 scariose bracteoles, perfect or imperfect; plants with unisexual flowers dioecious, but without differentiation in long pedicellate staminate flowers and short pedicellate pistillate flowers. Staminate flowers with narrowly lanceolate tepals; stamens 6, with long, linear, mucronate anthers on short filaments. Pistillate flowers with broadly lanceolate tepals; ovary sessile, with pronounced style and 3 slightly tapering, papillose stigmas. Capsule trilocular or triseptate, sessile, dehiscing or indehiscent. Seeds many.  The name Oxychloe is derived from the Greek oxys (acute) and chloe (grass), referring to the hard-pointed and prickly leaves.

description: Perennial, cushion-forming, glabrous herbs. Stems more or less regularly forked, dying back from the base, densely covered with persisting wilted leaves. Leaves regularly, densely, and alternately inserted along the stem. Blade equal to or slightly shorter than the sheath, flat or canaliculate, usually finely dentate along the margin. Inflorescence reduced to a single, lateral, subapical flower. Plants dioecious or rarely with a few perfect flowers. Tepals linear to lanceolate. Staminate flowers long pedicellate, lifted above the cushion, surrounded by one clasping bracteole at the base; stamens 6, with long, linear, mucronate anthers on short filaments. Pistillate flowers sessile in axil of a subapical leaf; ovary sessile; style long, filiform, with 3 filiform, papillose stigmas. Capsule triseptate, sessile. Seeds many. The name Patosia is derived from ‘Los Patos,’ the type locality of Rostkovia ? clandestina Philippi, which is the basionym of Patosia clandestina (Philippi) Buchenau.

description: Erect, glabrous, perennial herbs. Culms without leaves. Leaves all basal, spirally arranged, linear or with reduced blade, stomata restricted to 2 narrow bands of lighter color, one on each side of the midrib. Flower terminal, single on the culm, large, perfect. Stamens 6, with linear, mucronate anthers. Ovary sessile. Style with 3 tapering, twining stigmas. Capsule suborbicular, unilocular or slightly 3-septate, sessile. Seeds many. The name Rostkovia honours F. W. G. Rostkov (1770-1848), a student of Willdenow and a medical counsellor in Stettin, in present-day Poland, and author of a monograph of Juncus in 1801.

description: Monoecious or dioecious trees. Leaves entire, sometimes dentate or repand, with globose-capitate or oblongoid-capitate pluricellular hairs; stipules free or connate, fully amplexicaul or not. Inflorescences bisexual or unisexual, (sub) globose, hemispherical, turbinate, or convexly discoid, receptacle at first completely covered with peltate bracts; staminate flowers several to numerous, perianth well-developed and 4-3(-2)-lobed to 4-3(-2)-parted, vestigial, or lacking, stamens 4-1, anthers latrorse to extrorse, pistillode lacking; pistillate flowers one to several; testa with thickened part, sometimes vascularized, embryo transverse or oblique, cotyledons equal or unequal.
