description: Tree; young shoots sparsely golden or ferruginous sericeous, soon glabrous, greyish-brown, sometimes minutely fissured, with numerous lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 5-8.5 × 2.7-5 cm, broadly lanceolate or elliptic, apex shortly narrowly attenuate to obtuse or rounded, base shortly broad attenuate to rounded, upper surface glabrous, lower surface with scattered appressed hairs along the midrib; venation brochidodromous, sometimes with a marginal vein, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 12-16 pairs, parallel, straight; intersecondaries long; tertiaries parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin. Petiole 4-9 mm long, slightly channelled, appressed puberulous. Fascicles 3-10-flowered. Pedicel 3-5 mm long, appressed puberulous with golden or ferruginous hairs. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 4-5, ca. 2 mm long, ovate or suborbicular, apex acute or obtuse, outside appressed puberulous, sometimes with a glabrous hyaline margin, sometimes ciliate; inside appressed puberulous or glabrous. Corolla ca. 4 mm long, tube ca. 3 mm long, lobes (four-)five, ca. 1 mm long, ovate, rounded, glabrous. Stamens (four-)five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube or base of the lobes; filaments 0.4-0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.5-0.75 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, 4-5-locular, appressed puberulous; style 0.5-1 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple or slightly expanded. Fruit 1.8-2 cm long, oblanceolate or obovoid, apex rounded or obtuse, base tapered, smooth, glabrous; pericarp fleshy. Seed solitary, 1.5-1.6 cm long, narrowly obovoid, with a rounded apex and acute base, not laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, with impressions of the aborted locules on the adaxial surface above the scar, 0.3-0.75 mm thick; scar broad, basi-ventral, extending about two-thirds the length of the seed; embryo with thinly plano-convex cotyledons and exserted radicle, with a thin layer of endosperm. Field characters. Tree to 20 m high and 30 cm diam.; ultimate branchlets pendulous. The flowers are pale green, and mature fruit green. Flowering Jun to Nov, fruit maturing Jan.

description: Arbor; ramuli novelli arete adpresse puberuli, pilis aureis, demum glabri, pallide cinerascenti-bubalini, interdum leviter suberosi, elenticellati. Folia 7.5-19 × 3.2-6.5 cm, elliptica, oblonga vel oblanceolata, apice breviter et anguste attenuata, basi obtusa vel rotundata, supra glabra, infra arete sericea, pilis argentiis vel stramineis, interdum tandem subglabra; venatio eucamptodroma; costa supra leviter impressa; nervi secundarii 9-15-jugi, paralleli vel leviter convergentes, arcuati; nervi intersecundarii breves vel nulli; nervi tertiarii pauci, laxe reticulati. Petiolus 0.5-1.1 cm longus, canaliculata, breviter sericeus. Fasciculi 2-10-flori. Pedicellus 0.9-1.1 cm longus, sericeus, in fructu elongatus. Flores bisexuales. Sepala quinque, 3-4 mm longa, ovata, apice acuta vel obtusa, extus sericea, glabro margine hyalino, intus prope apicem cum indumento adpresso. Corolla 5.5-6.5 mm longa; tubus 4-4.5 mm longus; lobi quinque, 2-2.5 mm longi, oblongi, apice rotundati, glabri. Stamina quinque, medio vel indimidio inferiore tubo corollae affixa; filamenta 1.5-2.5 mm longa, glabra; antherae ca. 1.5 mm longae, lanceolatae usque ovatae, parce et longe hirsutae. Ovarium anguste pyramidale ad stylum decrescens, quinqueloculare, adpresse pubescens; stylus post anthesin ca. 3 mm longus, prope basim hirsutus; styli capitulum minute lobatum. Fructus 2-3.2 × 1-1.5 cm, ellipsoideus, apice decrescens, longo stylo persistente, basi decrescens, laevis, parce et adpresse puberulus vel glaber; pericarpium camosum. Semen solitarium, 1.5-1.8 cm longum, anguste obovoideum vel ellipsoideum, apice rotundatum, basi decrescens, lateraliter compressum, testa laevis, nitida, dimidio superiore paullum sculpturata, 0.3-0.5 mm crassa; cicatrix lata, basi-ventralis, anguste cordata, fere tertia parte semine brevior; embryo cotyledonibus crassis planis, radicula exserta, albumen cotyledones aequans.

description: Tree; young shoots closely appressed puberulous with golden hairs, becoming glabrous, pale greyish-buff, sometimes slightly suberous, without lenticels. Leaves 7.5-19 × 3.2-6.5 cm, elliptic, oblong or oblanceolate, apex shortly narrowly attenuate, base obtuse or rounded, glabrous above, closely sericeous below with silvery or straw-coloured hairs, sometimes becoming subglabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-15 pairs, parallel or slightly convergent, arcuate; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries few, forming a lax reticulum. Petiole 0.5-1.1 cm long, channelled, shortly sericeous. Fascicles 2-10-flowered. Pedicel 0.9-1.1 cm long, elongating in fruit, sericeous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, 3-4 mm long, ovate, apex acute or obtuse, outside sericeous with a hyaline glabrous margin, inside with some appressed indumentum near the apex. Corolla 5.5-6.5 mm long, tube 4-4.5 mm long, lobes five, 2-2.5 mm long, oblong, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed about one-third to one-half the way up the corolla tube, filaments 1.5-2.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.5 mm long, lanceolate to ovate, sparsely long-hairy. Ovary narrowly pyramidal tapering gradually to the style, five-locular, appressed pubescent; style ca. 3 mm long after anthesis, hairy below; style-head minutely lobed. Fruit 2-3.2 × 1-1.5 cm, ellipsoid, apex tapering, with long, persistent style, base tapered, smooth, sparsely appressed puberulous or glabrous; pericarp fleshy. Seed solitary, 1.5-1.8 cm long, narrowly obovoid or ellipsoid, apex rounded, base tapered, laterally compressed, testa smooth, shiny, with some slight sculpturing in the upper half, 0.3-0.5 mm thick; scar broad, basi-ventral, narrowly cordate, about two-thirds the length of the seed; embryo with thick flat cotyledons and exserted radicle, endosperm about as thick as the cotyledons. Field characters. Tree to 8 m high and 15 cm diam., trunk with white latex. Flowers greenish-cream, mature fruit wine-coloured. Flowering Jan to Feb, single fruiting collection Jan.

description: Tree; young shoots puberulous with appressed or slightly spreading golden to greyish hairs, soon glabrous, greyish-brown, smooth, often densely lenticellate. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 5.8-14.5 × 2.5-5.7 cm, elliptic, oblong-elliptic or lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate to acuminate, base shortly narrowly attenuate, glabrous, venation brochidodromous with a marginal vein, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 10-16 pairs, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate, not impressed on the upper surface; intersecondaries long; tertiaries parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin. Petiole 4-6 mm long, not channelled, subglabrous. Fascicles 5-20-flowered. Pedicel 5-7 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, 1.25-1.5 mm long, broadly ovate or suborbicular, apex obtuse, appressed puberulous outside, often with a broad hyaline glabrous margin, sometimes ciliate, sparsely appressed puberulous inside. Corolla 2.5-3.5 mm long, tube equalling the lobes, tube sometimes creased below the sinuses, lobes five, ovate, obtuse, glabrous or with scattered appressed hairs on the tube outside. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the tube; filaments 0.5-0.6 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.5 mm long, ovoid, glabrous. Ovary broadly ovoid, five-locular, appressed puberulous; style 0-0.1 mm long, glabrous; style-head minutely lobed. Fruit 1.5-2 cm long, broadly ellipsoid to subglobose, apex rounded, base tapered, smooth, glabrous; pericarp fleshy. Seed solitary, 1-1.5 cm long, ellipsoid, slightly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining; scar broad basi-ventral, extending to about two-thirds the length of the seed; embryo with thick, flat cotyledons and exserted radicle, endosperm about equalling the thickness of the cotyledons. Field characters. Tree to 32 m high with rough bark and reddish-brown wood. Flowers yellowish-green to greenish-white, fragrant; mature fruit black. Flowering Jul to Aug, Nov to Jan, fruiting Feb.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Shrub or small tree; young growth sericeous-tomentose with golden-ferruginous or rarely paler buff-coloured hairs, becoming greyish with age and finally glabrous, grey-brown, usually scaly, lenticellate or not. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, (1.3-)3-12 × (0.6-)1.5-4(-6.7) cm, usually elliptic, less frequently lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate or oblong, apex usually shortly narrowly attenuate, but very variable and sometimes rounded or emarginate, base narrowly attenuate, obtuse or rounded, usually coriaceous, upper surface glabrous or occasionally with residual venation along the midrib, lower surface sericeous-tomentose or less frequently sericeous, hairs golden-ferruginous or sometimes paler buff-silvery, turning greyish with age; venation brochidodromous, usually with a marginal vein, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins (11-)15-20(-25) pairs, usually straight, occasionally slightly arcuate, parallel, not sunken on the upper surface; intersecondaries long, tertiaries parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin, but usually obscured by the indumentum. Petiole (0.3-)0.5-1(-1.7) cm long, slightly channelled, tomentose with golden or greyish hairs. Fascicles 1-10-flowered. Pedicel 3-5(-8) mm long, sericeous-tomentose. Flowers bisexual. Sepals (four-)five, 1.5-2 mm long, broadly ovate or suborbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, outside sericeous to tomentose, inside appressed puberulous or glabrous, often with a hyaline margin, and sometimes ciliate. Corolla 3.5-4(-5) mm long, tube 2-3.5 mm long, sometimes slightly thickened at the throat, lobes (4-)5(-6), 1-1.5 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, usually glabrous, less frequently sparsely sericeous outside. Stamens (4-)5(-6), fixed at the top of the corolla tube or base of lobes; filaments 0.3-0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.5-0.6(-1.0) mm long, lanceolate to ovoid, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, (3-)5(-6)-locular, appressed puberulous; style (0.2-)0.5-0.75 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head minutely lobed. Fruit 1.4-3 cm long, 0.7-1 cm broad, narrowly ellipsoid to ovoid, apex and base acute to rounded, smooth, glabrous; pericarp fleshy. Seed solitary, 1.3-1.5 cm long, oblong, ellipsoid or narrowly ovoid, base obliquely truncate, not laterally compressed, testa smooth but strongly sculptured into prominent plates, 0.5-1.5 mm thick; scar broad, basi-ventral, often cordate, up to half the length of the seed; embryo vertical, with thin foliaceous cotyledons and exserted radicle, surrounded by copious endosperm.

description: Tree; young shoots minutely appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, greyish-brown, lenticellate, becoming cracked and fissured. Leaves spaced or loosely clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 5.7-24 × 2.5-8.5 cm, usually elliptic, less frequently oblanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate, acute or rounded, base narrowly attenuate, decurrent on the petiole, chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, glabrous; venation usually eucamptodromous, less frequently brochidodromous, sometimes with a marginal vein, midrib slightly raised or flat on the upper surface, secondary veins (8-) 13-20 pairs, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate, raised on both surfaces; intersecondaries usually short or absent; tertiaries oblique to horizontal, joined by a finer reticulum. Petiole 0.4-1.5 cm long, not channelled, glabrous. Fascicles 2-10-flowered, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves. Pedicel 1.5-6 mm long, sparsely appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, 1.5-3 mm long, lanceolate, ovate or elliptic, apex acute to rounded, sparsely appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside, often ciliate. Corolla 2-3 mm long, tube 0.5-1 mm long, lobes five, 1.5-2 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse, often slightly auriculate at base, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed near the top of the corolla tube; filaments 0.5-1 mm long, not geniculate, glabrous; anthers 0.6-1 mm long, lanceolate or ovate, acute, glabrous. Staminodes usually absent, occasionally present as 1-5 small vestiges to 0.5 mm long. Ovary ovoid or conical, five-locular, densely pubescent, style 0.75-1 mm long after anthesis, pubescent in lower half; style-head simple. Fruit (1.5-)3.5-5 cm long, ovoid, subglobose or obovoid, apex acute to rounded or truncate, base rounded or truncate, usually drying black, thick walled and not contracting or shrivelling on drying, smooth or irregularly and coarsely tuberulate, glabrous. Seeds several, 1.4-2.5 cm long, laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.3-1 mm thick; scar adaxial, extending most of the length of the seed and sometimes along the base, 1.5-3 mm wide; embryo vertical, with foliaceous cotyledons and long exserted radicle, surrounded by copious endosperm.

description: Arbor, ramuli novelli dense et brunneo lanato-villosi, demum glabri, cinerascenti, leviter fissurate lenticellati. Folia ad apicem ramulorum laxe congesta, spiraliter disposita, 5-11.8 × 3.26 cm, late elliptica, apice rotundata, basi obtusa usque rotundata, coriacea, supra glabra, praeter residuum indumentum secundum costam, infra dense lanato-villosa, pilis brunneis; venatio eucamptodroma; costa et nervi secundarii supra impressi; nervi secundarii 7-9-jugi, paralleli, leviter arcuati, nervi intersecundarii nulli; nervi tertiarii plerumque obliqui. Petiolus 1-1.8 cm longus, interdum leviter canaliculata, lanato-villosus. Fasciculi axillares, 1-4-flori. Pedicellus 3-5 mm longus, lanato-villosus. Flores unisex-uales (planta dioica) et (?) bisexuales. Sepala quinque, ca. 6.5 mm longa, ovata, apice acuta, extus dense lanato-villosa, intus adpresse puberula usque glabra. Corolla ca. 6 mm longa; tubus ca. 3.5 mm longus; lobi quinque, ca. 2.5 mm longi, late ovati, truncati, glabri, margine leviter ciliati. Stamina quinque, prope apicem tubo corollae affixa; filamenta ca. 0.75 mm longa, non geniculata, glabra; antherae ca. 1.25 mm longae, oblongo-lanceolatae, glabrae; antherae in flores foemineas nullae. Staminodia nulla. Ovarium anguste conicum, quinquelocular, dense villosum; stylus post anthesin 3-4 mm longus, glaber; styli capitulum simplex. Fructus ca. 2.5 × 2 cm, late ellipsoideus, apice obtusus, basi rotundatus, laevis, initio lanatus demum glaber. Semina dua, ca. 1.8 cm longa, lateraliter valde compressa, testa laevis, nitida, ca. 0.3 mm crassa; cicatrix adaxialis de prope dimidium ad prope basim extenta, ca. 2 mm lata; embryo cotyledonibus foliaceis tenuibus, radicula longe exserta, albumine copioso circumdatum.

description: Tree; young shoots densely brown lanate-villose, eventually glabrous, greyish, slightly fissured, lenticellate. Leaves loosely clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 5-11.8 × 3.2-6 cm, broadly elliptic, apex rounded, base obtuse to rounded, coriaceous, glabrous above, except for residual indumentum along the midrib, lower surface densely lanate-villose with brown hairs; venation eucamptodromous, midrib and secondaries impressed above; secondary veins 7-9 pairs, parallel, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries absent, tertiaries mostly oblique. Petiole 1-1.8 cm long, sometimes slightly channelled, lanate-villose. Fascicles axillary, 1-4-flowered. Pedicel 3-5 mm long, lanate-villose. Flowers unisexual (dioecious) and ? bisexual. Sepals five, ca. 6.5 mm long, ovate, apex acute, densely lanate-villose outside, appressed puberulous to glabrous inside. Corolla ca. 6 mm long, tube ca. 3.5 mm long, lobes five, ca. 2.5 mm long, broadly ovate, truncate, glabrous, margin slightly ciliate. Stamens five, fixed near the top of the staminal tube; filaments ca. 0.75 mm long, not geniculate, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.25 mm long, oblong-lanceolate, glabrous; anthers absent in female flowers. Staminodes absent. Ovary narrowly conical, five-locular, densely villose; style 3-4 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit ca. 2.5 × 2 cm, broadly ellipsoid, apex obtuse, base rounded, smooth, lanate at first becoming glabrous with age. Seeds two, ca. 1.8 cm long, strongly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shiny, ca. 0.3 mm thick; scar adaxial, extending from near halfway to the base of the seed, ca. 2 mm wide; embryo with thin foliaceous cotyledons and long exserted radicle, surrounded by copious endosperm. Field characters. Tree to 25 m high and 60 cm diam. with green flowers. Flowering Oct to Dec, fruit Dec.

description: Tree; young shoots shortly and densely ferrugineous-villose, eventually glabrous, greyish-straw coloured, rough and suberous, without lenticels. Leaves 6.8-11.6 × 3-5 cm, oblong-lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, apex acute or narrowly attenuate, base truncate, sub-glabrous above, lower surface with villose midrib and uniformly pubescent lamina, indumentum of erect ferruginous hairs; venation brochidodromous, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-13 pairs, parallel, straight; intersecondaries moderate to long; tertiaries forming an open reticulum. Petiole 4-6 mm long, ferruginous villose. Fascicles 2-12-flowered. Pedicel 4-5 mm long, villous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals (four-)five, 2.25-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, villose outside, glabrous inside. Corolla ca. 3.5 mm long, tube about equalling the lobes, lobes five, broadly ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed about one-third up the corolla tube; filaments ca. 1 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 1 mm long, broadly lanceolate, apiculate, sparsely villose. Ovary narrowly ovoid or conical, tapering to the style, five-locular, pubescent; style 1-1.25 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head minutely lobed. Fruit unknown. Field characters. A large tree, with russet flowers (sepals). Flowering Jan to Feb.

description: Small tree; young shoots golden sericeous-tomentose, soon glabrous, pale greyish-buff, smooth or slightly suberous, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, (2-)4- 11 × 1.2-5.5 cm, mostly elliptic, apex narrowly attenuate or acuminate, base acute, cuneate or narrowly attenuate, glabrous above, lower surface clothed in minute closely appressed whitish hairs or subglabrous; venation brochidodromous, sometimes with a marginal vein, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-20 pairs, parallel, straight; intersecondaries long; tertiaries parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin. Petiole 2-6 mm long, channelled, sericeous-tomentose, soon becoming glabrous. Fascicles 1-4-flowered. Pedicel 0.5-1 cm long, sparsely to densely sericeous-tomentose. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, (1-)1.5-2 mm long, ovate or lanceolate, apex acute, sparsely sericeous-tomentose outside, sometimes with a glabrous hyaline margin, inner face with sparse appressed pubescence. Corolla 4-5 mm long, tube 2.5-3.5 mm long, slightly expanded at apex, lobes five, 1-1.5 mm long, ovate, apex acute, obtuse or rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube or base of the lobes; filaments 0.5-1 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.5-0.75 mm long, lanceolate or oblong, glabrous. Ovary broadly ovoid or pyramidal, five-locular, puberulous; style 0.5-1 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head minutely lobed. Fruit ca. 3.7 × 1.3 cm, slender ellipsoid-lanceolate, apex long tapered, base rounded, smooth glabrous, pericarp fleshy. Seed solitary, ca. 2.3 x 0.6 × 0.5 cm, narrowly ellipsoid with a slightly rounded apex and acute base, testa smooth, shiny, ca. 0.2 mm thick; scar basi-ventral, ca. 1.1 × 0.3 cm, narrowly cordate; embryo vertical, with thin foliaceous cotyledons and long exserted radicle, surrounded by copious endosperm. Field characters. Small tree to 12 m high with a small amount of white latex in the bark. Flowers cream-coloured or greenish, fruit maturing through red to black. Flowering Dec to Feb, fruiting Jan.

description: Young shoots rather coarsely pubescent with reddish-brown hairs, becoming glabrous, pale grey or buff, roughened, lenticellate or not. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 4.4-13.2 × 2.3-5 cm, elliptic, oblong-elliptic or oblanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, upper surface scattered pubescent to glabrous, lower surface pubescent with brown hairs or glabrous; venation brochidodromous, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 12-18 pairs looping below the margin to form a prominent submarginal vein, parallel, straight or sometimes slightly arcuate; intersecondaries long; tertiaries parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin. Petiole 3-9 mm long, not or only slightly channelled, pubescent. Fascicles 2-4-flowered. Pedicel 0.5-1.8 cm long, pubescent with reddish-brown hairs. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, 3-4 mm long, lanceolate to narrowly ovate, apex acute to rounded, reddish-brown sericeous-pubescent. Corolla 4.5-6.5 mm long, tube 3.5-5 mm long, slightly thickened at the throat, lobes five, 1-1.5 mm long, ovate or triangular, apex obtuse to rounded, sparsely sericeous outside, glabrous inside. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments 0.5-0.75 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.4-0.75 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Ovary ovoid to pyramidal, five-locular, appressed puberulous; style ca. 0.5 mm long after anthesis, appressed puberulous in the lower half; style-head simple or minutely lobed. Fruit ca. 2 × 0.8 cm, narrowly ellipsoid, apex acute, base tapered, smooth, glabrous; pericarp fleshy. Seed solitary, ca. 1.5 × 0.7 cm, narrowly ellipsoid, apex acute, base tapered, not laterally compressed, testa smooth, shiny, with some inconspicuous sculpturing on the adaxial surface; scar basi-ventral, ca. 1 × 0.6 cm, cordate; embryo not seen. Field characters. Tree to 20 m high and 30 cm diam. with brown, narrowly fissured bark. Flowers pale green or cream-coloured, mature fruit greenish-red, exuding latex from cut surface. Flowering Jan to Apr, only fruiting collection Jan (Costa Rica, Alajuela).

description: Small tree, young shoots sparsely sericeous with pale or golden hairs, soon glabrous, pale brown, cracked, sometimes lenticellate. Leaves 5-15(-27) × 2-4(-9.5) cm, narrowly elliptic, oblong or lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate, base acute to narrowly attenuate, upper surface glabrous, lower surface sparsely sericeous at first with whitish hairs, becoming subglabrous; venation eucamptodromous-brochidodromous, midrib flat or slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 7-13 pairs, parallel or slightly convergent, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries short or long; tertiaries often descending from the margin and parallel to the secondaries, or reticulate. Petiole 0.5-0.9(-1.6) cm long, slightly channelled appressed puberulous to glabrous. Fascicles 2-5-flowered. Pedicel 0.5-1 (-2.2) cm long, sericeous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals (4-)5, 2-3.5 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse or rounded, sericeous outside, subglabrous inside. Corolla 4-7 mm long, tube about equalling the lobes, lobes (four-)five, ovate, apex rounded or obtuse, glabrous or with a few appressed hairs outside. Stamens (four-)five, fixed one-quarter to halfway up the corolla tube; filaments 1.5-2.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 1-2 mm long, lanceolate or ovate, glabrous or sparsely long-hairy. Ovary long-conical, tapering gradually into the style, 4-5-locular, appressed pubescent; style 2-3.5 mm long after anthesis, about equalling the corolla, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit (not seen, desc. from RB1061), ca. 2.8 × l cm, narrowly ellipsoid, acute. Seed ca. 1.9 × 0.7 cm, with a broad basi-ventral scar. Small tree to 10 m high and 15 cm diam., with widely spreading branches. Flowers pale green to yellowish green, visited by bees (Kuhlmann 3786). Fruit maturing red. Flowering Nov to Jun.

description: Tree; young shoots densely golden to ferruginous tomentose, becoming glabrous, pale greyish, rough, scaly, without lenticels. Leaves densely clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 9.5-23 × 5.5-12.7 cm, narrowly to broadly oblanceolate, broadly elliptic or obovate, apex rounded or obtuse, base narrowly cuneate, acute or rounded, margin revolute, strongly coriaceous, upper surface glabrous, or residual tomentum along the midrib, lower surface densely and persistently shortly golden to ferruginous tomentose; venation eucamptodromous, midrib broad, usually slightly raised on the upper surface, secondary veins 7-12 pairs, slightly convergent or parallel, arcuate; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries obscure, oblique to horizontal. Petiole 0.5-2(-3) cm long, flat, not channelled or winged, tomentose at first. Fascicles 5-10-flowered, borne just below the leaves. Pedicel 2-5 mm long, tomentose. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, female ca. 3 mm long, male 4-4.5 mm long, slightly accrescent in fruit, lanceolate to ovate, apex acute obtuse or rounded, golden tomentose outside, glabrous or with some appressed indumentum inside. Corolla, female ca. 3.5 mm long, tube equalling the lobes, male 5-7 mm long, tube 2-2.5 mm long, lobes five, 3-5 mm long, ovate or lanceolate, apex acute, obtuse or rounded, glabrous or sometimes pubescent outside. Stamens (absent in female) fixed in the lower half of the corolla tube; filaments 2.5-3 mm long, glabrous; anthers 1.5-2.5 mm long, lanceolate or ovate, glabrous. Staminodes usually absent, occasionally represented by five small vestiges. Ovary ovoid (expanded at base in male flowers), 2-3-locular, densely pubescent; style ca. 2 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 4.5-5 cm long, obovoid or globose, apex slightly depressed or obtusely apiculate, base broadly tapering, smooth, glabrous. Seed laterally compressed, with a narrow adaxial scar; embryo not seen. Field characters. Tree to 20 m and 35 cm diam. with white latex. Lower leaf surface golden brown. Flowers greenish white. Flowering Sep to Nov, immature fruit in Mar.

description: Arbuscula; ramuli novelli breviter tomentosi, pilis aureis usque albidis, mox glabri, cinerascenti-brunnei, laevi, lenticellis paucis numerosis muniti. Folia dissita, alternata et disticha, 3-5.4 × 2.2-3.7 cm, late elliptica, apice obtusa vel denique apice breviter late attenuata, basi rotundata vel truncata, utrinque laxo indumento arachnoideo in juventute vestita, demum subglabra; venatio eucamptodroma-brochidodroma; supra costa leviter impressa; nervi secundarii 7-8-jugi paralleli vel convergentes, leviter arcuati; nervi intersecundarii breves vel nulli; nervi tertiarii laxe reticulati. Petiolus 5-6 mm longus, leviter canaliculata, dense pubescens. Fasciculi ca. 10-flori, axillares. Pedicellus ca. 1 mm longus, aureo-tomentosus. Flores bisexuales. Sepala quinque, ca. 1.25 mm longa, ovata, apice obtusa usque rotundata, extus aureo tomentosa, intus glabra. Corolla ca. 2.5 mm longa; tubus ca 1.5 mm longus; lobi quinque, ca. 1 mm longi, ovati, apice rotundati, glabri. Stamina quinque, ad apicem tubo corollae affixa; filamenta ca. 0.3 mm longa, glabra; antherae ca. 0.4 mm longae, ovatae, glabrae. Ovarium ovoideum, quinqueloculare, adpresse puberulum; stylus post anthesin ca. 0.5 mm longus, glaber; styli capitulum leviter lobatum. Fructus ignotus.

description: Treelet; young shoots shortly tomentose with golden to whitish hairs, becoming glabrous, greyish-brown, smooth, with numerous small lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 3-5.4 × 2.2-3.7 cm, broadly elliptic, apex obtuse or ultimately shortly broadly attenuate, base rounded or truncate, both surfaces covered with loose whitish arachnoid indumentum when young, becoming subglabrous; venation eucamptodromous-brochidodromous, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 7-8 pairs, parallel or convergent, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries forming on open reticulum. Petiole 5-6 mm long, slightly channelled, densely pubescent. Fascicles ca. 10-flowered, axillary. Pedicel ca. 1 mm long, golden tomentose. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, ca. 1.25 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse to rounded, golden tomentose outside, glabrous inside. Corolla ca. 2.5 mm long, tube ca. 1.5 mm long, lobes five, ca. 1 mm long, ovate, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 0.3 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.4 mm long, ovate, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, appressed puberulous; style ca. 0.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head slightly lobed. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Straggling treelet ca. 4 m high, with fragrant greenish flowers. Flowering records Jul and Sep.

description: Tree; young growth golden or golden-ferruginous sericeous eventually glabrous, greyish-brown, smooth or cracked, lenticellate or not. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 4.5-15.5 × 2.5-6.9 cm, broadly elliptic to oblong elliptic, apex shortly broadly attenuate or cuspidate to obtuse or rounded, base narrowly or broadly attenuate or cuneate, upper surface glabrous or occasionally with some residual indumentum along the midrib, lower surface golden or golden-ferruginous sericeous; venation brochidodromous, secondary veins often looping to form a submarginal vein, marginal vein sometimes conspicuous, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondaries 14-26 pairs, arcuate, parallel; intersecondaries long; tertiaries parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin. Petiole (0.9) 1-2 cm long, channelled, sericeous. Fascicles 5-20(-30)-flowered. Pedicel 0.6-1.2 cm long, sericeous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals (4-)5(-6), 1.5-2 mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex rounded, outside sericeous, inside appressed puberulous to glabrous, margin often hyaline. Corolla 3.5-4 mm long, tube about equalling the lobes, lobes 5-6, ovate or triangular, apex acute to rounded, outside sericeous, indumentum often confined to the centre of the lobes, inside glabrous. Stamens 5-6, fixed at the top of the corolla tube or base of the lobes; filaments 0.3-0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.40.8 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Staminodes absent, or rarely present, in a single whorl alternating with the stamens, up to 1 mm long. Ovary broadly ovoid to globose, (8-)9-11-locular, appressed pubescent; style 0.1-0.3 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head (8-)9-11-lobed. Fruit 4-7 cm long, broadly ellipsoid to globose, apex and base obtuse to rounded, smooth, glabrous; pericarp fleshy. Seeds 3-10, 1-1.8 cm long, usually laterally compressed, with a smooth shining testa 0.2-1 mm thick; scar adaxial, 0.6-1.3 cm long, always more than half the length of the seed, about equalling the width of the seed, often with a small rounded beak near the apex; embryo with thick flat cotyledons and exserted radicle, endosperm equalling or slightly thicker than the cotyledons. Field characters. A tree to 25 m high, usually smaller, the bole becoming slightly fluted with age. The colour of the bark varies from pale greyish to dark brownish-black, depending on exposure, and it is deeply and narrowly fissured, often suberous. The exudate is abundant, white. The crown is characteristic and easily spotted from a distance because of the dark glossy upper leaf surface, and shining golden pubescence on the lower surface. The flowers are greenish to cream-white, fragrant, and the ripe fruit usually purple, though a yellow-skinned form is also known. Flowering in the Greater Antilles is mostly Jun to Sep, and the fruit take several months to mature.

description: Tree; young shoots closely appressed puberulous with whitish hairs, soon becoming glabrous, pale grey or buff, rough, lenticellate. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 3.2-14.5 × 1.3-4.5 cm (but up to 17 × 5 cm in immature individuals), elliptic, apex acute or narrowly attenuate, base narrowly attenuate, upper surface glabrous, lower surface closely appressed puberulous to subglabrous, hairs whitish; venation brochidodromous, marginal vein present, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 7-12 pairs (up to 20 pairs on leaves of immature specimens), straight or slightly arcuate, parallel; intersecondaries long; tertiaries few, parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin. Petiole 5-9 mm long, not or only slightly channelled, closely appressed puberulous to subglabrous. Fascicles 3-10-flowered. Pedicel 5-7 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, 1.5-2 mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside, margin ciliate. Corolla 3.25-3.5 mm long, tube 2-2.25 mm long, lobes five, 1.23-1.3 mm long narrowly ovate, apex obtuse to rounded, sparsely sericeous outside, indumentum usually present on tube and centre of lobes, glabrous inside. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments 0.5-0.8 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.5 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, 5-6-locular, appressed puberulous; style 0.5-0.75 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head with 5-6 minute recurved lobes. Fruit 1.2-1.8 cm × 0.7-1 cm, ellipsoid, apex acute, base tapered, smooth, glabrous; pericarp fleshy. Seed solitary, 0.9-1.3 cm long, ellipsoid with an oblique base, not or scarcely laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, often bearing impressions of the aborted locules on the adaxial surface, 0.5-0.8 mm thick; scar broad, cordate, basi-ventral, slightly less than half the length of the seed; embryo with thick, flat cotyledons and exserted radicle, surrounded by a layer of endosperm about as thick as the cotyledons. Field characters. A monopodial tree to 25 m high and 50 cm diam. The bole is fluted at the base, and the bark greyish-brown, scaling in thin narrow strips. The pink slash contains a small amount of white latex. The ultimate branches are pendulous, and the lower leaf surface slightly silvery-grey. Flowers greenish-white to yellowish-green, fruit maturing pale green, containing abundant white latex. The fruit are eaten by birds and monkeys and seeds dispersed after passage through the gut (Janzen, in litt., 4.2.1984).

description: Arbor; ramuli novelli crassi, pallide adpresse puberuli vel rarius villosi, demum glabri, scabri, brunnei, squamati, cicatricibus foliorum delap-sorum prominentibus, elenticellati. Folia ad apicem ramulorum congesta, spiraliter disposita, 40-65 × 15-24 cm, oblanceolata, apice obtuse cuspidata usque anguste attenuata, basi longe decrescentia, denique acuta vel rotundata, in lato petiolo leviter decurrentia, coriacea; pagina superior glabra, pagina inferior arete sericea pilis pallide bubalinis vel argenteis; venatio eucamptodroma, nervo marginali tenui; costa et nervis secundariis supeme impressis, subtus prominentibus; nervi secundarii 25-30-jugi, paralleli, arcuati vel recti; intersecundarii nulli; tertiarii numerosi, obliqui, paralleli. Petiolus 1-2.2 cm longus, latissimus, saepe anguste alatus, adpresse puberulus. Fasciculi 1-20-flori, ramiflori, in ramis vetustioribus ex pulvinatis excrescentiis persistentibus enati. Pedicellus 0.5-1 cm longus, adpresse puberulus. Flores bisexuales. Sepala quinque, 5-7 mm longa, in fructu usque ad 1-1.2 cm accrescentia, lanceolata vel oblonge ovata, apice acuta, uniformiter adpresse puberula in super-ficiebus ambabus. Corolla ca. 7.5 mm longa; tubus 2-2.5 mm longus; lobi quinque, 5-5.5 mm longi, elliptici vel late ovati, apice obtusi, glabra. Stamina quinque, tubo corollae sub apicem affixa; filamenta 3-3.5 mm longa, glabra; antherae 2-3 mm longae, lanceolatae, glabrae. Ovarium depresse globosum, quinquelocular, villosum; stylus 4.5-6.5 mm longus post anthesin, in dimidio inferiore pubescens; styli capitulum minute lobatum. Fructus sepalis accrescentibus incrassatis subtentus, ca. 4 × 3.5 cm, globosus vel obovoideus, apice truncatus vel rotundatus, basi contractus, laevis, glaber vel indumento residuali prope basim. Semina plura, ca. 2 cm longa, la-teraliter valde compressa; testa laevis, nitida, 0.3-0.5 mm crassa; cicatrix angusta, secundum plerumque latus adaxiale et circa basim extensa; embryo cotyledonibus foliaceis tenuibus, radicula longe exserta, albumine copioso circumdatum.

description: Tree; young shoots massive, with pale appressed puberulous or less frequently villous indumentum, becoming glabrous, rough, brown, scaly, with prominent leaf scars, without lenticels. Leaves tightly clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 40-65 × 15-24 cm, oblanceolate, apex obtusely cuspidate to narrowly attenuate, base long tapering, finally acute or rounded, slightly decurrent on the broad petiole, coriaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower surface closely sericeous with pale buff to silvery hairs; venation eucamptodromous with a thin marginal vein, midrib and secondaries sunken on the upper surface, prominent below; secondary veins 25-30 pairs, parallel, arcuate or straight; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries numerous, oblique, parallel. Petiole 1-2.2 cm long, very broad, often narrowly winged, appressed puberulous. Ramiflorous, fascicles 1-20-flowered, on older branches produced from persistent pulvinate excrescences. Pedicel 0.5-1 cm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, 5-7 mm long, accrescent to 1-1.2 cm long in fruit, lanceolate to oblong-ovate, apex acute, uniformly appressed puberulous on both surfaces. Corolla ca. 7.5 mm long, tube 2-2.5 mm long, lobes five, 5-5.5 mm long, elliptic to broadly ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed just below the apex of the corolla tube; filaments 3-3.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 2-3 mm long, lanceolate, glabrous. Ovary depressed globose, five-locular, villose; style 4.5-6.5 mm long after anthesis, pubescent in the lower half, style-head minutely lobed. Fruit subtended by thickened accrescent sepals, ca. 4 × 3.5 cm, globose or obovoid, apex truncate or rounded, base tapered, smooth, glabrous or some residual indumentum near the base. Seeds several, ca. 2 cm long, strongly laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, 0.3-0.5 mm thick; scar narrow, ca. 1.5 mm wide, extending most of the adaxial side and around the base; embryo with thin foliaceous cotyledons and long exserted radicle, surrounded by copious endosperm. Field characters. Unbuttressed tree to 25 m high, with cylindrical bole. Leaves conspicuously pale tan on the lower surface. Latex white. Flowers white, mature fruit yellow to orange. Flowering Jul to Aug, fruiting Jan to Mar.

description: Young shoots appressed puberulous to sericeous, with golden-brown, reddish or whitish hairs, soon glabrous, becoming rough and scaly, lenticellate. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, (4-)8-18(-23) x (1.8-)3-8(-10.5) cm, usually broadly oblong or elliptic, less frequently oblong-lanceolate, oblanceolate or obovate, apex usually narrowly attenuate, less frequently obtuse or rounded, base narrowly attenuate, cuneate, obtuse, rounded or truncate; upper surface glabrous, lower surface sericeous to sparsely appressed puberulous or glabrous, hairs golden, reddish or whitish; venation eucamptodromous or brochidodromous, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins (8-) 10-16(-25) pairs, usually parallel and slightly arcuate, or sometimes straight, not impressed on the upper surface; intersecondaries long or short; tertiaries parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin or forming an open reticulum. Petiole (0.3-)0.5-2 cm long, channelled, sericeous to sparsely appressed puberulous or glabrous. Fascicles (2-)5-15(-25)-flowered. Pedicel (2-)3-7(-10) mm long, sericeous to sparsely appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals (four-)five, 1.5 2(-2.5) mm long, broadly ovate or suborbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, outside sericeous to appressed puberulous, except for the broad hyaline margin, inside appressed puberulous to glabrous; margin sometimes ciliate. Corolla (3.5-)4-6(-7) mm long, tube (2.25-)3-4(-5) mm long, lobes (4-)5(-6), (0.5-)1-1.5(-2) mm long, ovate or triangular, apex obtuse or rounded, sparsely to densely sericeous outside, indumentum sometimes restricted to the lobes, glabrous inside. Stamens (4-)5(-6), fixed at the top of the corolla tube or base of the lobes; filaments 0.2-0.5(-0.7) mm long, glabrous, traces sometimes visible to base of tube; anthers (0.2-)0.3-0.6(-0.9) mm long, mostly lanceolate, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, 5-7(-8)-locular, appressed puberulous; style (0.3-)0.5-1 mm long after anthesis, style-head minutely 5-7(-8)-lobed. Fruit 1-4.5 cm long, 0.6-5 cm broad, narrowly ellipsoid to depressed globose, apex and base acute, obtuse, rounded or hollowed, smooth, glabrous; pericarp fleshy. Seed one-several, 1-1.6 cm long, ellipsoid, slightly to strongly laterally compressed; testa smooth, usually glossy, often bearing strong impressions of the aborted loculi on the adaxial surface, 0.2-1 mm thick; scar broad, usually heartshaped, basi-ventral but often attaining more than half the length of the seed; embryo vertical, with thick, flat cotyledons and exserted radicle, surrounded by a layer of endosperm about as thick as the cotyledons.

description: Shrub or small tree; young shoots shortly rufous or ferruginous sericeous-tomentose, soon glabrous, grey-brown, cracked and fissured, lenticellate. Leaves 1.9-5 × 1.2-2.2 cm, lanceolate, narrowly ovate or oblong-lanceolate, apex acute or shortly narrowly attenuate, base obtuse or rounded, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous-brochidodromous, with a marginal vein, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 8-14 pairs, parallel, straight; intersecondaries and tertiaries obscure. Petiole 3-4 mm long, channelled, sericeous-tomentose. Fascicles 5-10-flowered. Pedicel 2-4 mm long, sericeous-pubescent. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, 1-2 mm long, ovate to suborbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, sparsely sericeous outside, usually with a glabrous hyaline border, margin ciliate, inside appressed puberulous. Corolla 1.5-2.5 mm long, tube usually shorter than the lobes, lobes five, broadly ovate to suborbicular, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed about halfway up the corolla tube; filaments 0.3-0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.8-1 mm long, lanceolate, sparsely long-hairy. Ovary ovoid or conical, tapering gradually to the style, five-locular, pubescent; style 0.5-1 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 1-1.3 × 0.7-1 cm, ellipsoid to obovoid, apex rounded, base rounded or slightly tapered, smooth, glabrous; pericarp thin, fleshy. Seed solitary, 0.9-1.1 × 0.7-0.9 cm, obovoid, flattened on the adaxial face, not laterally compressed, testa smooth, shining, very hard and woody, ca. 1 mm thick; scar broadly adaxial or basi-ventral, 5-9 × 3.5-6 mm; embryo (young) vertical, with thin foliaceous cotyledons and exserted radicle; endosperm copious.  Field characters. Shrub or small tree to 4 m high. Flowering Feb to May (Ceará & Pernambuco), fruiting Sep (Ceará).

description: Tree; young shoots sparsely and minutely appressed puberulous, soon glabrous, becoming greyish-brown, scaly, usually lenticellate. Leaves loosely clustered at the shoot apex, spirally arranged, 9.3-17.5 × 3.3-6.5(-7.7) cm, oblanceolate, apex rounded, obtuse, or shortly cuspidate, base acute to narrowly attenuate, thinly coriaceous, glabrous or with a few minute appressed hairs near the midrib below; venation eucamptodromous, midrib slightly prominent on the upper surface, secondary veins 10-13(-16) pairs, slightly convergent or parallel, arcuate, slightly prominent on both surfaces; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique to horizontal, numerous, close, parallel; lower order reticulum sometimes visible. Petiole 1-2.2 cm long, not channelled, slightly decurrent, glabrous. Ramiflorous, fascicles five-many-flowered. Pedicel 5-8 mm long, minutely appressed puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, 2-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate or suborbicular, apex rounded or obtuse, appressed puberulous on both surfaces, inner sepals fringed ciliate. Corolla 2.5-3.5 mm long, tube 0.5-1 mm long, often carnose, lobes 1.5-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate or elliptic, apex rounded to obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at or near the top of the corolla tube; filaments 1-1.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, lanceolate or elliptic, glabrous; stamens reduced to vestigial filaments in female flower. Staminodes absent. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, densely strigose; style 0.25-0.5 mm long after anthesis, strigose; style-head minutely five-lobed. Fruit 3-4.5 cm long, ellipsoid or obovoid, apex rounded, base rounded to acute, smooth, glabrous, with conspicuous pale lenticels. Seeds one-several, 2-2.6 cm long, laterally compressed, testa not shiny, adherent to the pericarp, ca. 1 mm thick; scar narrow adaxial, extending most of the length of the seed, ca. 2 mm wide; embryo with foliaceous cotyledons and exserted radicle, surrounded by copious endosperm. Field characters. Unbuttressed tree to 35 m high and 50 cm diam. with copious white latex. Flowers greenish-yellow or green, fruit ripening through yellow to orange. Flowering Jul to Jan, fruiting Dec to May.

description: Young shoots shortly appressed pubescent with white hairs, becoming glabrous, pale grey-brown, smooth or slightly fissured, with numerous lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 5.1-9.8 × 2.2-3.8 cm, elliptic, apex acute to obtusely cuspidate, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, both surfaces with an indumentum of scattered short appressed whitish hairs; venation eucamptodromous-brochidodromous, with a marginal vein, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 8-10 pairs, slightly convergent, slightly arcuate; intersecondaries long; tertiaries forming an open reticulum. Petiole 4-5 mm long, flat or slightly channelled, with scattered appressed hairs. Fascicles 2-5-flowered. Pedicel 1.5-2 mm long, appressed puberulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals five, ca. 1.5 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse, appressed puberulous outside, margin ciliate, glabrous inside. Corolla ca. 4 mm long, tube ca. 3 mm long, lobes five(-six), 1-1.25 mm long, ovate, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens five(-6), fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.4 mm long, lanceolate-sagittate, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, shortly pubescent; style ca. 1 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head minutely 5(-6)-lobed. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Tree to 7 m high with green flowers. Flowering in May.

description: Tree; young shoots shortly hispid with rufous hairs, soon glabrous, greyish-white or buff, smooth, without lenticels. Leaves spaced, alternate and distichous, 4.8-11.4 × 1.8-3.5 cm, lanceolate or narrowly oblong-lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate, base rounded, obtuse or narrowly cuneate, margin slightly revolute, upper surface glabrous or with some residual indumentum along the midrib, lower surface with some hispid indumentum mainly confined to the midrib; venation brochidodromous, midrib sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 9-15 pairs, parallel, straight; intersecondaries long; tertiaries parallel to the secondaries and descending from the margin, lower order venation finely reticulate. Petiole 2-4 mm long, not channelled, shortly hispid. Fascicles 2-5-flowered. Pedicel 1.5-3.5 mm long, rufous-hispidulous. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 4-5, ca. 1.5 mm long, suborbicular, apex rounded, hispidulous outside with a glabrous hyaline margin, ciliate, inside glabrous. Corolla ca. 4 mm long, tube ca. 3 mm long, lobes five, ca. 1 mm long, ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at the top of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 0.3 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.6 mm long, broadly ovoid, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, four-locular, appressed pubescent; style ca. 0.5 mm long after anthesis; style-head minutely lobed. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Tree to 12 m high with pale green flowers produced Jul to Oct.

description: Tree; young shoots subglabrous, brown or greyish-brown, rough, with prominent leaf scars, often lenticellate. Stipules 2-4 cm long, narrowly lanceolate with a long tapering apex, conspicuously striate, glabrous or with a few appressed hairs on the dorsal surface. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 23-45 × 7.8-15 cm, oblanceolate, apex shortly narrowly attenuate to obtusely cuspidate, base long narrowly cuneate, chartaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat or slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 17-40 pairs, usually parallel and arcuate, often rather widely spreading; intersecondaries short or absent; tertiaries oblique, often numerous; quaternary reticulum conspicuous. Petiole 4-8 cm long, strongly channeled, glabrous. Fascicles many-flowered, below the leaves. Pedicel 1.5-3.7 cm long, slender, puberulous. Flowers unisexual (plant monoecious). Sepals five, 4.5-5 mm long, ovate to oblong, apex acute to rounded, appressed puberulous outside, glabrous inside, sometimes ciliate. Corolla cyathiform or broadly tubular, (male) ca. 5 mm long, tube ca. 2 mm long, lobes five, ca. 3 mm long, (female) tube ca. 2 mm long, lobes five, ca. 2 mm long, lobes of both sexes broadly ovate, rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed at or near the top of the corolla tube; filaments ca. 0.5 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 1.8 mm long, broadly ovate, absent in female. Staminodes five, ca. 1.25 mm long in male flowers, ca. 0.5 mm long in female flowers, lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary broadly truncate to broadly ovoid, 2-3-locular, densely pubescent; style ca. 2 mm long after anthesis, pubescent in lower half; style-head simple. Fruit 4-8 cm long, broadly ellipsoid, rounded at base and apex, smooth or rugose (when immature drying to become strongly and irregularly ribbed and furrowed), shortly velutinous, becoming subglabrous at maturity. Seed solitary, 2.5-5.5 cm long, ellipsoid, rounded at base and apex, testa rough, not shining; scar adaxial, covering two thirds of the surface; embryo with planoconvex, free cotyledons, radicle slightly exserted; endosperm absent. Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 40 cm diam., buttressed, slash with scarce yellow latex. Flowers with orange-red calyx and whitish corolla; fruit ferruginous brown. Flowering recorded Mar, Jul, Sep-Oct, fruit Jan-Feb, Jul.

description: Tree; young shoots appressed puberulous (brown) at first, becoming glabrous, very rough with scars of fallen leaves, without lenticels. Stipules 1-2.2 cm long, narrowly oblong to spathulate, not striate, appressed puberulous. Leaves clustered, spirally arranged, 11-42 × 5-19 cm, broadly oblanceolate, apex acute to rounded, base tapering, finally acute to rounded, thinly coriaceous, glabrous above, golden brown sericeous below; venation eucamptodromous, midrib flat or slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 13-26 pairs, parallel, straight or slightly arcuate; intersecondaries absent; tertiaries oblique; quaternary reticulum visible on lower surface. Petiole 1.5-7.3 cm long, strongly infolded, appressed puberulous to glabrous. Fascicles 2-6-flowered, axillary and below the leaves. Pedicel 5-9 mm long, stout, sericeous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Sepals five, 3-4.5 mm long, ovate, apex acute or obtuse, appressed puberulous outside, and near the margin inside. Corolla broadly tubular, 3-4.5 mm long, tube 1.25-3 mm long, lobes five, 1.25-1.5 mm long, oblong to ovate, obtuse to rounded, glabrous. Stamens five, fixed in the upper half of the corolla tube, absent in female; filaments ca. 0.75 mm long, glabrous; anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, ovate, apex rounded, glabrous. Staminodes five, ca. 0.3 mm long (vestigial in female), lanceolate, glabrous. Disk absent. Ovary broadly truncate or patelliform, 5-locular, densely long-pubescent; style 1.75-2.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous above; style-head simple or minutely five-lobed. Fruit unknown.  Field characters. Tree to 30 m high and 70 cm diam., buttressed to 3 m high, bole fluted, with scaling reddish bark, slash with sparse white or yellow latex. Flowers greenish-white, fruit velvety-chestnut (young). Flowering recorded May and Nov.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Young branches appressed ferruginous puberulous, becoming glabrous, grey-brown, rough, lenticellate. Unarmed. Leaves spirally arranged, not clustered, 4.5-7.5 × 1.6-2.9 cm, oblanceolate, apex acute and finally shortly attenuate, base narrowly attenuate, coriaceous, glabrous above, appressed ferruginous puberulous on the lower surface; venation brochidodromous with a marginal vein, margin revolute, midrib flat on the upper surface; secondary veins ca. seven pairs, ascending, straight, parallel, rather prominent on the lower surface; intersecondaries long; tertiaries descending from the margin and parallel to the secondaries. Petiole 3-4 mm long, not channelled, glabrous. Flowers bisexual, axillary, solitary or paired. Pedicel ca. 2.5 mm long, appressed ferruginous puberulous. Sepals five, ca. 3.5 mm long, ovate, acute, glabrous inside, appressed ferruginous puberulous outside. Corolla glabrous, ca. 5.5 mm long, tube ca. 2 mm long, lobes five; median segment elliptic, rounded, erose, lateral segments oblong-lanceolate, erose, 1.75-2 mm long. Stamens five, glabrous; filaments ca. 1.5 mm long, anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, lanceolate. Staminodes five, ca. 2.5 mm long, ovate, strongly erose, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, five-locular, glabrous; style ca. 2 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit unknown. Field characters. Habit unknown. Flowering in Jan.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Small tree; young branches shortly brown-tomentose with crisped hairs, becoming glabrous, greyish-brown, rough, wrinkled and cracked, with numerous elongate lenticels. Not spiny. Leaves spirally arranged, not clustered, 6.7-10.5 × 1.8-4 cm, oblanceolate, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, apex narrowly attenuate or acute, base narrowly attenuate or cuneate or acute, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous above, tomentose along the midrib below; venation brochidodromous to eucamptodromous with a strong thickened marginal vein, midrib slightly sunken on the upper surface; secondary veins 15-16 pairs, shallowly ascending, parallel or slightly convergent, arcuate, rather prominent on the lower surface; intersecondaries usually short, tertiaries reticulate, sometimes slightly impressed on the upper surface. Petiole 0.7-1.1 cm long, not channelled, tomentose at first, becoming glabrous. Flowers bisexual, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves, in 5-10-flowered fascicles. Pedicel 1.5-2.5 mm long, tomentose. Sepals five, 2.5-3 mm long, broadly ovate or elliptic, rounded, tomentose outside, glabrous inside. Corolla glabrous, ca. 4 mm long, tube ca. 1.5 mm long, lobes five; median segment broadly elliptic, apex rounded, erose, lateral segments narrowly triangular or irregularly acute, toothed or erose, 1-1.5 mm long. Stamens five, glabrous; filaments ca. 2 mm long; anthers 1-1.25 mm long, lanceolate-sagittate. Staminodes five, 1.5-2 mm long, broadly lanceolate or ovate, usually with a short stout stalk, margin erose or deeply cut, usually infolded, glabrous. Ovary narrowly ovoid, gradually tapering, 5-locular, glabrous; style 1.5-1.75 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 0.6-0.7 cm long, subglobose, apex and base rounded, smooth, glabrous; pericarp 0.5-1 mm thick, fleshy. Seed solitary, 0.5-0.6 mm long, broadly ovoid, rounded; testa hard, shining, with several thickened plates on the adaxial side, 0.3-1 mm thick; scar basal, circular, ca. 1 mm diam.; embryo vertical, with thin foliaceous cotyledons and radicle exserted ca. 1 mm, surrounded by copious endosperm. Field characters. A small tree to 6 m high with yellowish-white flowers. Flowering specimens are mostly from Aug and Sep, with one in Nov, mature fruit Mar-Apr.

description: Spiny shrub. Young branches densely short reddish-ferruginous tomentose to sparsely pubescent with whitish hairs or glabrous, older shoots smooth to rough, lenticellate. Axillary or lateral spines usually present. Leaves spirally arranged and spaced at first, soon becoming fascicled on short shoots, 1-5.5 × 0.4-2 cm, spatulate, oblanceolate to broadly elliptic, apex rounded to emarginate or obtuse, base narrowly attenuate or cuneate, usually chartaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower surface loosely pubescent to glabrous; venation brochidodromous without a marginal vein, midrib flat on the upper surface; secondary veins 5-9(-13) pairs, ascending, arcuate, slightly convergent or parallel; intersecondaries usually moderate to long; tertiaries reticulate, usually conspicuous on both surfaces. Petiole 1-3 (-4) mm long, slightly channelled, pubescent or glabrous. Flowers bisexual, in 5-20-flowered fascicles, axillary or on leafless shoots. Pedicel 0.4-1.2 cm long, glabrous. Sepals five(six), 1.5-2.25 mm long, ovate or oblong, rounded, glabrous or strigose outside, glabrous inside. Corolla 2.25-2.5 mm long, tube 0.5-0.75 mm long, glabrous; lobes five; median segment broadly ovate, elliptic or suborbicular, apex rounded, lateral segments lanceolate to falcate, often erose, 0.75-1 mm long; stamens five, glabrous; filaments 0.75-1 mm long, anthers 0.5-0.8 mm long, lanceolate-sagittate. Staminodes five, 1.25-1.5 mm long, broadly lanceolate; infolded, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, (4)5-locular, strigose or glabrous; style 0.75-1 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 5-7(-9) mm long, broadly ellipsoid or globose, apex and base rounded, smooth, glabrous or rarely sparsely strigose; pericarp ca. 1 mm thick, fleshy. Seed one(two), 0.4-0.7 cm long, ellipsoid or globose, with truncate base; testa hard, smooth, shining, sometimes mottled, ca. 0.2 mm thick; scar basal, in two parts, a half-moon or circular basal part, 1.5-2 mm across and a smaller, laterally elongate part on the abaxial side near the base, the two sometimes coalescing; embryo vertical or oblique, with plano-convex cotyledons and slightly exserted radicle, sometimes surrounded by a thin layer of endosperm.

description: Tree; young branches minutely appressed puberulous, soon glabrous, greyish-brown, rough and cracked, usually lenticellate. Unarmed. Leaves spirally arranged, spaced or loosely clustered at the stem apex, 6-20 × 1.8-6.7 cm, elliptic to oblanceolate or rarely obovate, apex acute, obtuse or narrowly attenuate, often finally rounded, base narrowly attenuate or cuneate, leaf margin often revolute near the base, chartaceous or coriaceous, glabrous above, lower surface with loosely appressed whitish or brown fine indumentum usually becoming glabrous with age; venation eucamptodromous with a marginal vein, midrib usually sunken on the upper surface; secondary veins (7)8-14(-l 5) pairs, ascending, usually arcuate and convergent, rarely straight and parallel; intersecondaries usually small or absent; tertiaries forming an open reticulum, sometimes tending to be oblique or horizontal. Petiole 0.43.0 cm long, slightly channelled or not, sparsely appressed puberulous to glabrous. Flowers bisexual, in 5-20-flowered fascicles in the axils of defoliated nodes. Pedicel 0.35-1 cm long, often elongating after flower fall, appressed puberulous to glabrous. Sepals (four)five, 1.5-3.5 mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, rounded, outside appressed puberulous or glabrous, margin sometimes membranous or ciliate, inside glabrous. Corolla glabrous, 4-6.5 mm long, tube 1-2 mm long, lobes five; median segment broadly ovate, obtuse or rounded, often auriculate at base, lateral segments irregularly lanceolate, often auriculate, cut or erose, 1-3 mm long. Stamens five, glabrous; filaments 2.5-4.5 mm long, anthers (1.25) 1.5-2 mm long, lanceolate. Staminodes five, (1.75)2-4 mm long, ovate or lanceolate, infolded, incurved, margin erose to deeply cut, glabrous. Ovary slender, ovoid, gradually tapering to the style, 5(6)-locular, glabrous; style 1-2(-3) mm long after anthesis, slightly tapered, glabrous; style-head rounded, simple. Fruit 1.6-2.5 cm long, ovoid, obovoid or broadly ellipsoid, apex acute, rounded or truncate, base obtuse or rounded, smooth, glabrous; pericarp 2-4 mm thick, fleshy. Seed one(two), 1.2-1.5 cm long, ellipsoid to subglobose, sometimes slightly laterally compressed, base usually truncate; testa hard, smooth, shining, (0.5) 1-3 mm thick; scar basal, 4-8 × 2.5-4 mm, elliptic or rounded; embryo oblique, with thin foliaceous cotyledons and radicle exserted 2-3 mm, surrounded by copious endosperm.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Plants yellow-green to olive brown, to 7 cm high, usually 2-4 cm high, whitish-tomentose below, with blackish stem and long, crowded, sometimes slightly curved comal leaves. Leaves to 11 mm long, lanceolate, gradually narrowed to a long, slender subula, serrate in the upper third. Costa filling 1/2 of the leaf base, smooth at back, excurrent as a long awn, in transverse section with large ventral hyalocysts and dorsal groups of 2-5 stereids. Alar cells large and inflated. Basal laminal cells short, subquadrate to short rectangular (1-2:1), thick-walled and pitted, at margins narrow and elongate (30 × 30-60 µm). Upper laminal cells irregular, subquadrate, short rectangular or obliquely, 6-9 × 10-30 µm, smaller at margins, extending in a few marginal rows nearly to the apex. Sporophyte not known.

description: Plants in loose tufts, slender, yellowish green above, blackish below. Stems 5-10(-l5) cm high, not tomentose, loosely appressed foliate. Leaves 6-8 mm long, lanceolate, canaliculate, the margins serrate in the upper third. Costa relatively narrow, filling only 1/4-1/3 of the leaf base, ending in the leaf tip or shortly excurrent, in transverse section with ventral and dorsal stereids, ridged at back. Alar cells numerous, inflated, brownish, thickened. Basal laminal cells rectangular, incrassate, pitted, 13-67 × 6-10 µm, at margins in several rows narrower. Upper laminal cells rectangular to oblique, incrassate, 10-38 × 3-10 µm. Sporophyte not known.

description: Shrub or small tree; young branches finely appressed puberulous with ferruginous or grey hairs, soon glabrous, greyish, usually longitudinally cracked, lenticellate. Spines simple, axillary, 1-2 cm long, or terminating lateral branches, or absent. Leaves spirally arranged, spaced, or clustered in small fascicles, 0.7-4.5 × 0.2-3.8 cm, broadly cuneiform to obovate or oblanceolate, apex rounded, truncate or retuse, base usually cuneate, less frequently acute, obtuse or narrowly attenuate, chartaceous or coriaceous, margin often revolute, glabrous or less frequently finely appressed puberulous on the lower surface, venation brochidodromous with a marginal vein, midrib flat on the upper surface; secondaries 4-5 pairs, usually steeply ascending, straight, slightly divergent; intersecondaries short to prominent; tertiaries descending from the margin and parallel to secondaries; venation sometimes obscure in small-leaved forms; leaves with numerous fine striations running parallel to the secondary veins, especially visible on the upper surface. Petiole 0.5-4 mm long, not channelled, appressed puberulous or glabrous. Flowers bisexual, axillary, 1-5 flowers in a fascicle. Pedicel 0.5-5 mm long, appressed puberulous or occasionally glabrous. Sepals five, 1.5-2.25 mm long, ovate, apex acute to rounded, outside glabrous or less frequently appressed ferruginous puberulous, inside glabrous. Corolla glabrous, 3-4.5 mm long, tube 1-1.5 mm long; lobes five, median segment ovate or elliptic, rounded or obtuse, lateral segments narrowly lanceolate, sometimes erose, 1-1.5 mm long. Stamens five, glabrous; filaments 1.5-2 mm long, anthers ca. 0.75 mm long, lanceolate or lanceolate-sagittate. Staminodes five, 1.25-2.5 mm long, ovate or lanceolate, sometimes erose, often folded and incurved against the style, glabrous. Ovary ovoid, 5-locular, pubescent or occasionally glabrous; style 2.5-3.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 0.4-1 cm long, ellipsoid to obovoid or globose, apex rounded to truncate, base slightly tapered, smooth, glabrous; pericarp 0.5-1 mm thick, fleshy. Seed solitary, 3.5-7 mm long, subglobose to obovoid, testa hard, shiny, smooth, usually with several thickened plates on the adaxial side, and sometimes hollowed at the base, 0.3-1 mm thick; scar basal or basi-ventral, ca. 1 mm diam.; embryo vertical, with planoconvex cotyledons and radicle exserted ca. 1 mm; surrounded by a thin sheath of endosperm. Field characters. A spiny or unarmed spreading shrub or small tree to 10 m high. Larger specimens develop greyish fissured bark which may be grid-cracked. White latex is rarely recorded from the cut bark. Flower color is recorded as white, cream, or greenish white, and many collectors comment on their strong fragrance. The ripe fruit is purple or black, containing white latex.

description: Shrub or small tree. Young branches glabrous, reddish- or grey-brown, smooth, with pale lenticels. Spines frequently present, axillary or terminating lateral branches. Leaves spirally arranged and spaced on young growth, becoming fascicled on short shoots, (2.6-)4-10(-12) × 1-3.4 cm, elliptic to oblanceolate, apex usually acute or attenuate, less frequently obtuse to rounded, base narrowly attenuate, usually chartaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower with some semi-appressed silvery indumentum, or glabrous; venation eucamptodromous to brochidodromous, marginal vein absent, midrib often slightly prominent on the upper surface; secondary veins, 8-13 pairs, ascending, usually arcuate, parallel or convergent; intersecondaries short or long; tertiaries reticulate to areolate, conspicuous on both surfaces, leaves drying pale or yellowish-green. Petiole 0.3-1.5 cm long, slightly channelled, soon glabrous. Flowers bisexual, the fascicles axillary and clustered on the short shoots. Pedicel 0.3-1 cm long, glabrous. Sepals five(six), 1.5-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate, rounded, glabrous. Corolla 3-4.5 mm long, tube 0.5-1.5 mm long, glabrous; lobes five(six); median segment elliptic, ovate or obovate, rounded, lateral segments falcate, 0.75-1.25 mm long. Stamens five(six), glabrous; filaments 1.75-2.5 mm long, anthers ca. 1.25 mm long, lanceolate or lanceolate-sagittate. Staminodes five(six), 1.5-2 mm long, lanceolate, infolded, glabrous. Ovary ovoid or globose, 4-5-locular, sparsely strigose; style 1-2 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 0.8- 1.3 cm long, globose to ellipsoid, apex rounded or occasionally acute, base rounded; smooth, glabrous; pericarp ca. 1 mm thick, fleshy. Seed 0.65-0.9 cm long, ellipsoid or globose, often with a truncate base; testa hard, smooth, shining, sometimes mottled, sometimes with several thickened plates on the adaxial side, 0.3-1 mm thick; scar basal, usually in two parts, a circular or halfmoon shaped basal part 1.5-2 mm across, and a smaller laterally elongate part on the abaxial side near the base, the two sometimes coalescing; embryo vertical or oblique, with plano-convex cotyledons and slightly exserted radicle, surrounded by a thin layer of endosperm. Relationships. Sideroxylon lycioides, S. lanuginosum, S. tenax and S. reclinatum form a closely knit group of species. They are easily distinguished from all neotropical species by the combination of fascicled leaves with conspicuous finely reticulate tertiary venation, short-styled flowers, small fruit, and the seed with a bipartite scar.

description: Small tree; young branches densely woolly tomentose-villose with whitish hairs, eventually glabrous, greyish, longitudinally cracked or fissured, without lenticels. Unarmed but sometimes with short leafless tapering axillary branches. Leaves spirally arranged, spaced or loosely clustered, occasionally fascicled, 4-10.5 × 1-3.3 cm, oblong-elliptic, lanceolate or oblanceolate, apex acute, obtuse or emarginate, base obtuse to narrowly attenuate, usually coriaceous, densely whitish tomentose with crisped hairs on both surfaces, tomentum slightly shorter on upper surface; venation eucamptodromous, marginal vein narrow or absent, midrib sometimes slightly raised on the upper surface; secondary veins 7-10 pairs, ascending, straight or slightly arcuate, parallel or slightly convergent; intersecondaries small or absent, tertiaries forming an open reticulum, obscure. Petiole 0.6-2 cm long, not channelled, tomentose. Flowers bisexual, fascicles axillary, 5-10-flowered. Pedicel 4-6 mm long, densely tomentose-villose. Sepals five, 4-5 mm long, suborbicular or much broader than long, apex rounded, densely tomentose-villose outside, crisped puberulous inside. Corolla 6-6.5 mm long, tube 1.5-3 mm long, glabrous; lobes five, broadly elliptic, apex rounded, each with two narrowly acute lateral appendages 1.5-2 mm long. Stamens five, glabrous; filaments 3.5-4 mm long, anthers 1.5-2 mm long, lanceolate-sagittate. Staminodes five, 2.5-3 mm long, lanceolate, infolded, apex erose to deeply cut, glabrous. Ovary ovoid to conical, five(-six)-locular, densely strigose; style ca. 4 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 2-2.5 cm long, ovoid, apex obtuse, base rounded, smooth, densely tomentose-villose; pericarp 1-2 mm thick, leathery-fleshy. Seed solitary 1.7-1.8 cm long, broadly ovoid with truncate base; testa smooth, shining, 0.5-1 mm thick; scar basal, ovate, ca. 7 × 5 mm; embryo not seen. Field characters. A small tree to 10 m high and 60 cm diam., with reddish-brown to grey-brown fissured shaggy bark. Latex has not been recorded in the trunk or branches but is present in the developing fruit. The cream coloured flowers are produced from Dec to May.

description: Young branches villose with white to brown hairs or glabrous, becoming smooth, usually dark brown, finally cracked or fissured, lenticellate. Spines usually present, 1-2 cm long, axillary or terminating lateral branches. Leaves spirally arranged and spaced on young growth, soon becoming fascicled on short shoots, 1.3-10.7 × 0.7-4 cm, oblanceolate, apex rounded or obtuse, rarely acute, base long narrowly attenuate, chartaceous, sometimes becoming coriaceous, loosely villous with white or brown hairs when young, soon becoming glabrous on the upper surface except for residual hairs along the midrib, lower surface remaining villose or becoming glabrous; venation eucamptodromous to brochidodromous, marginal vein absent, midrib flat or slightly sunken on the upper surface; secondary veins 5- 9(-12) pairs, ascending, usually arcuate and slightly convergent; intersecondaries usually short to moderate, occasionally long; tertiaries reticulate or reticulate-areolate, conspicuous on the upper surface. Petiole 0.2-1.1 cm long, slightly channelled, villous to glabrous. Flowers bisexual, the fascicles axillary and clustered on the short shoots. Pedicel 2-9 mm long, villous to glabrous. Sepals (four)five, 1.75-3 mm long, ovate to suborbicular, obtuse to rounded, villous, pubescent or rarely glabrous outside, glabrous inside. Corolla 3-4(-5) mm long, tube 0.75-1.5 mm long, glabrous; lobes five(six); median segment ovate, oblong or elliptic, apex rounded, often erose, often auriculate at base; lateral segments lanceolate or falcate, 0.75-1.75 mm long. Stamens five(six), glabrous; filaments 1.25-2 mm long, anthers 0.75-1.25 mm long, lanceolate. Staminodes five(six), 1.25-2(-3) mm long, lanceolate, often infolded, often erose, glabrous. Ovary globose or ovoid, 5-8-locular, strigose; style 0.75-1.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit 0.7-1.4 cm long, broadly ellipsoid to oblanceolate, apex rounded, base rounded or slightly tapered, smooth, glabrous; pericarp 0.5-2 mm thick, fleshy. Seed one(two), 0.6-1.1 cm long, ellipsoid, often with a truncate base; testa hard, smooth, shining, 0.25-2 mm thick; scar basal, nearly always in two parts, a circular or planoconvex basal part 1-2 mm across and a smaller laterally elongate part on the abaxial surface, the two sometimes coalescing; embryo vertical, with plano-convex cotyledons and slightly exserted radicle, surrounded by a thin layer of endosperm.

description: Tree, young branches appressed pubescent with golden-ferruginous hairs, soon glabrous, dark brown, becoming rough and cracked, with numerous pale lenticels. Not spiny. Leaves spirally arranged, not clustered, 7-11 × 3-4 cm, lanceolate, apex narrowly attenuate, base obtuse or rounded, decurrent into the petiole, coriaceous, glabrous or with a few residual hairs along the midrib below; venation eucamptodromous or craspedodromous, with a strong thickened marginal vein; midrib flat or slightly sunken on the upper surface, secondary veins 13-15 pairs, ascending, slightly arcuate, convergent or parallel, slightly prominent below; intersecondaries moderately long; tertiaries reticulate. Petiole 1.8-2.8 cm long, not channelled, laterally broadened by the decurrent leaf margin, short pubescent at first, soon glabrous. Flowers bisexual, axillary and in the axils of fallen leaves, in 3-10-flowered fascicles. Pedicels 3-4 mm long, with brown puberulous indumentum. Sepals five, 2-2.5 mm long, broadly ovate, elliptic, obtuse or rounded, puberulous outside, glabrous inside. Corolla glabrous, 3-3.25 mm long, tube about equalling the lobes; lobes five; median segment orbicular, lateral segments lanceolate, erose, 1-1.5 mm long. Stamens five; filaments ca. 1.5 mm long, glabrous or with sparse long appressed hairs, anthers ca. 1 mm long, lanceolate-sagittate, with scattered long appressed hairs on the back. Staminodes five, 1-1.5 mm long, broadly lanceolate or ovate, erose, infolded, with a short broad stalk, glabrous or with scattered long hairs on the back. Ovary slender ovoid, gradually tapering, 5-locular, sparsely appressed pubescent; style ca. 1.5 mm long after anthesis, glabrous; style-head simple. Fruit unknown. Field characters. A tree to 15 m high with white flowers. Flowering in Aug and Sep. The cut bark exudes white latex.
bibliographicCitation: Pennington, Terence D. 1990. Sapotaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 52: 1-750.

description: Tree; young branches finely appressed puberulous at first, soon glabrous, greyish- to reddish-brown, smooth or becoming finely cracked, lenticellate or not. Unarmed. Leaves spirally arranged, spaced or loosely clustered, 7.5-14.5 × 3.3-7.7 cm, broadly oblong-elliptic, elliptic or oblanceolate, apex shortly attenuate, acute, obtuse or rounded, base rounded, obtuse, acute or shortly narrowly attenuate, often decurrent, chartaceous, glabrous; venation eucamptodromous with a prominent marginal vein, midrib sunken on the upper surface; secondary veins 9-13 pairs, ascending, slightly arcuate, slightly convergent; intersecondaries usually moderate or long; tertiaries conspicuous, horizontal and reticulate; leaves drying pale yellow-green. Petiole (1.5-)2.5-4.5 cm long, glabrous, strongly channelled, or the decurrent marginal veins often fused near the apex of the petiole to form a pouch, the upper margin of this sometimes prolonged upwards to form a leafy projection to 1 cm long. Flowers bisexual, in 5-20-flowered fascicles in the axils of defoliated nodes. Pedicel 4-8 mm long, with scattered appressed minute hairs or glabrous. Sepals (4)5(6), 1.5-2 mm long, broadly ovate to suborbicular, rounded, glabrous or margin sometimes ciliate. Corolla glabrous, 4-4.5 (-5) mm long, tube 0.5-1.5 mm long, lobes (4)5-6, ovate to lanceolate-elliptic, apex rounded, often auriculate at base, lateral segments vestigial or absent. Stamens 5-6, glabrous; filaments 1.5-2.5 mm long, anthers 1.3-1.5 (-2) mm long, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate. Staminodes 5-6, 1-1.5(-2.5) mm long, lanceolate or irregularly shaped, toothed, cut or erose, glabrous. Ovary narrowly ovoid, (4)5(6)-locular, glabrous; style 1-2 mm long after anthesis, often ribbed, glabrous; style-head truncate or slightly hollowed, sometimes minutely five-lobed. Fruit 1.5-2.6 cm long, broadly ellipsoid, apex and base obtuse or rounded, smooth, glabrous, pericarp 1-2 mm thick, fleshy. Seed 1(2), 1.3-2 cm long, ellipsoid or obovoid, tapering at the base; testa hard, smooth and shining, sometimes with thickened plates on the adaxial surface, 0.75-3 mm thick; scar basi-ventral, 2-8 mm long, lanceolate, elliptic or suborbicular; embryo vertical, with thin foliaceous cotyledons and radicle exserted 1.5-3 mm, surrounded by copious endosperm.

description: Frutex vel arbor parva; ramuli novelli pilis crispatis brunneis tomentosi, demum glabri, valde scabri, cicatricibus foliorum et inflorescentiarum delapsorum persistentibus, elenticellati. Planta non spinosa. Folia spiraliter disposita, ad apicem ramulorum congesta, 4.2-6.2 × 1.8-2.5 cm, elliptica, apice acuta vel obtusa, basi acuta vel anguste cuneata, chartacea, supra glabra, infra indumento crispato sparsim residuo vestita; venatio eucamptodroma usque brochidodroma; nervo marginali; costa plana vel pagina superiore leviter impressa; nervi secundarii 8-9-jugi, ascendentes, paralleli et leviter arcuati; nervi in-tersecundarii breves usque modice longi; nervi tertiarii reticulati. Petiolus 5-9 mm longus, non canaliculata, initio tomentosus. Fasciculi 2-5-flori; flores bisexuales, plerumque infra folia axillis foliorum delapsorum enati. Pedicellus ca. 1.5	mm longus, breviter tomentosus. Sepala 5, ca. 2.5 mm longa, late orbiculari-ovata, apice rotundata, extra breviter tomentosa, intra glabra. Corolla glabra, ca. 4 mm longa; tubus ca. 1.5 mm longus; lobi quinque; segmentum ir edium sub-orbiculare, segmenta lateralia lanceolata vel irregularia, 1.5-1.75 mm longa. Stamina quinque, tubo corollae ad apicem affixa, glabra; filamenta ca. 1.75 mm longa, antherae 0.75-1 mm longae, lanceolatae, in alabastro ventrifixae vel extrorsae. Staminodia quinque, ca. 1.5 mm longa, triangulari-ovata, breviter petiolata, leviter ero-sa, non involuta, glabra. Ovarium glabrum, supra sensim decrescens, quinque loculare, glabrum; stylus post anthesin ca. 1.5 mm longus, glaber; styli capitulum simplex. Fructus ca. 1.2 cm longus, ca. 0.6 cm latus, ellipsoideus, apice acutus, basi decrescens, laevis, glaber; pericarpium 0.5-1 mm crassum, camosum. Semen so-litarium, ca. 7.5 mm longum, ellipsoideum, leviter lateraliter compressum; testa dura, nitida, laevis, basi excavata, 0.3-1.5 mm crassa; cicatrix basalis, rotundata, ca. 0.75 mm diam.; embryo verticalis, cotyledonibus foliaceis tenuibus, ra-dicula ca. 1 mm exserta, albumine copioso circumdatum.
