description: Hierbas de gran porte, rizomatosas. Lepidofilos ca. 30 x 0.8 cm, con vena media conspicua hasta de 6 mm ancho, apice atenuado, haz y enves glabros, enves pardo, margen cartaceo, laciniado. Peciolo desconocido; lamina 5-lobulada, base cordada, no peltada, lobulos primarios sublobulados, todos los lobulos de apice agudo, senos secundarios poco profundos, profundidad de los senos primarios igual a 1/5 de la longitud laminar, haz generalmente con parches muy escabro-sos, cada areola coronada por proyecciones espinosas, enves con venacion pilosa, provista de proyecciones vesiculosas, las venas secundarias con proyecciones espinosas purpuras hasta de 2 mm largo, margen ondulado, dentado, dientes laciniados, espinosos. Inflorescencia ca. 1.5 m largo, raquis 2.2 cm diam., pardo, bracteas espatuladas o lineares, 1.5-3 cm largo, ca. 1 mm ancho basal, en la parte media 2.2 mm ancho, glabras por ambas caras, margen laciniado; ramificaciones de la inflorescencia 20-22 cm largo, 1.2-1.5 mm diam., pilosas, lisas o levemente surcadas. Sepalos caducos, base triangular, ca. 0.75 mm largo, apice laciniado, 0.25 mm largo; péalos 2, de forma variable 1.5-1.7 x 0.4-1 mm; estambres 2, anteras orbiculate* en pre-antesis, 1.3-1.5 mm diám., a menudo subsésiles, elipsoides en post-antesis, 1.25-1.5 × 1.3 retusas, no apiculadas, conectivo ampliado, verruc ovario subcilíndrico, 1-1.3 mm diám., ligeramente pedicelado, púrpura oscuro. Fruto subgloboso, ca. 1.5 mm diám., muy cortamente pedicelado.

description: Hierbas de gran porte, rizomatosas. Lepidofilos 5-10 x 1-1.5 cm, sésiles, enteros, con costa prominente, pilosos por ambas caras, laciniados hacia el apice, atropurpúreos aunque a veces las lacinias reverdecen. Pecíolo ca. 2 cm diám, basal, 1 cm diám, distal, glabérrimo, provisto de proyecciones espinosas conspi-cuas; lámina suborbicular-reniforme, base profunda mente cordada, lóbulos primarios 2-3, sublobulados con ápice agudo, senos angostísimos, superpuestos, dt profundidad igual a 5/6 de la longitud laminar, haz muy escabrosa y con venación pilosa, envés con las venas primarias, secundarias y terciarias provistas de proyecciones espinosas, margen prominentemente dentadocrenado, espiniscente, dientes con prolongaciones de las venas. Inflorescencia con eje glabro a esparcidamente pubérulo y brácteas de 16-32 x 1.5-3 mm, glabras por ambas caras aunque el envés es rugoso, vena media visible, engrosada hacia el ápice, margen laciniado, apice generalmente emarginado; ramificaciones de la inflorescencia 3.2-4 cm largo, (1.5-)2-3 mm diám., glabras o escasamente pilosas, atropurpúreas. Sepalos 2(3), base incurvada, ca. 1.2 x 1-1.25 mm ancho, triangular o trapezoidal, crasa, margen laciniado, ápice membranoso; pétalos 2, cuculados, angos-tados hacia la base, de tamano y forma variables, 1.6-3 x (1-) 1.5-1.8 mm, glabros, apice laciniado, apicu-lado; estambres 2, filamentos en antesis hasta de 2.5 mm largo, anteras generalmente elipsoides u orbicu-lares, 0.6-1.3 x 0.4-0.9 mm, apiculadas; ovario cilíndrico. Infructescencia con ramificaciones de 9-10 cm largo, crasas. Frutos pedicelados, pedicelo ca. 0.25 mm largo, densamente dispuestos, subglobosos, 2.2—2.3 x 2-2.2 mm, constrictos hacia el ápice y coronados por la base de los sépalos.

description: Hierbas de porte mediano, hasta de 1 m alto, rizomatosas. Lepidofilos desconocidos. Pecíolo hasta de 30 cm largo y 1 cm diám, basal, surcado y con proyecciones espinosas cortas, atropurpúreo; lámina orbicular-reniforme, base cordada (no peltada), lobulada, lóbulos 2-3-sublobulados, hasta de 1/4 de la longitud laminar, todos los lóbulos de ápice agudo a mucronado, haz lisa (no escabrosa), muy densamente pilosa, verde-pálida brillante o parda opaca, envés con venación pilosa, prominente o plana, margen entero 0 con dientes finos, diminutos, espinosos. Inflorescencia 30-40 cm largo, con brácteas lineares, 4—9 x ca. 0.2 cm, carinadas, de ápice marcadamente laciniado en la región apical, pardo-pálidas; ramificaciones de la inflorescencia 5-8 cm largo. Sépalos con base rectangular, ca. 0.25 x 0.5 mm y ápice membranoso, caduco; pétalos desconocidos; estambres 2, anteras elipsoides, ca. 1 x 0.75 mm, levemente apiculadas, atropurpúreas; ovario ovoide, ca. 1 x 0.6 mm, constricto en el ápice. Infructescencia con escapo hasta de 5 cm largo y 4 mm diám., surcado, glabro, raquis terete, pubérulo, y ramificaciones más o menos engrosadas. Frutos levemente pedicelados, globosos a ligeramente trígonos, hasta de 1.5 mm diam., coronados por las bases de los sépalos rectangulares.

description: Hierbas de tamano gigante, rizomatosas, rizoma 8- 10 cm diam. Lepidofilos hasta de 60 x 15 cm, glabros a puberulos, venacion similar a las de las hojas normales, apice y margen de los lobulos laciniados, membranosos, lacinias pinnatffidas, hasta de 2 cm largo, purpura y a veces con areas verde claras. Peciolo hasta de 1.3 m largo y 3 cm diam, basal, profundamente surcado a lo largo de toda su longitud, glabro, usualmente con diminutas proyecciones espinosas; lamina suborbicular, hasta de 1.2 x 1.5 m, ligeramente 9-13 lobulada, base cordada, lobulos con apice agudo, profundidad de los senos 1/5 de la longitud laminar, ondu-lados, haz verde-oscura a rojiza (a veces con algunas areas albo-variegadas), escabrosa, areolada, rara vez lisa, hacia la parte central con proyecciones espinosas blancas diminutas dispersas, glabra o esparcidamente pubérula, envés verde-pálido, hirsuto, con venacion prominente, venas primarias frecuentemente con proyecciones espinosas diminutas, margen con dientes espiniscentes, rígidos, de tamano desigual. Inflorescencia hasta de 1.8 m largo, escapo y raquis redondeados, glabros, hasta de 2.5 cm diam, basal; bracteas de la Inflorescencia obovadas, (1—)2—3 x 0.5-1 cm, rigidas, conduplicadas en la base, haz glabra o muy esparcidamente pubérula, envés rugoso, hirsuto, margen entero, costa prominente, ápice lanceolado-acuminado; ramificaciones de la inflorescencia hasta de 5 cm largo, flores congestionadas. Sépalos con base triangular, ca. 0.20 mm largo, y ápice caduco, membranoso, laciniado; pétalos 2, levemente cuculados, 0.7-1 mm largo, base angosto-linear, limbo 0.3-0.6 mm ancho; estambres 2, subsésiles en pre-antesis, anteras suborbiculares, ca. 0.75 mm largo, ápice levemente emarginado a cortamente apiculado; ovario globoso, ca. 1 mm diám. Infructescencia con ramificaciones de 18-25 cm largo, hirsutas, arqueadas, generalmente no engrosadas. Frutos laxamente dispuestos, sesiles o cortamente pedicelados, ovoides, 1.4-1.6 x 1-1.2 mm, coronados por la base persistente de los sépalos hasta de 0.3 mm largo, blancos.

description: Hierbas de porte gigante, rizomatosas. Lepidofilos numerosos, laciniados. Pecíolo robusto, ca. 40 cm largo, piloso, ligeramente canaliculado por la haz; lámina hasta de 3 m diám., 7-lobulada, base cordada, no peltada, profundidad de los senos igual a 1/2 de la longitud laminar, lóbulos mayores 2-3-sublobulados, todos los lóbulos con ápice muy agudo, profundidad de los senos secundarios casi igual a la mitad de los senos primarios, haz con venación pubescente, areolada, areolas glabras o pubescentes, a veces con proyecciones espinosas y entonces escabrosa, envés con venación pilosa o pubescente, levemente prominente o plana, sin proyecciones espinosas, margen con dientes agudisimos en la terminatión de todos los lóbulos. Inflorescencia ca. 36 x 6.5 cm, sobre un escapo esparcidamente piloso hasta de 8 cm largo, oblongo-lanceolada, atenuada hacia el ápice, escapo y raquis surcados y con proyecciones pequeñas dispersas; brácteas de la inflorescencia lineares, 1.5-2.5 x 0.1-0.4 cm, esparcidamente pilosas, con venas casi paralelas, muy marcadas y margen entero a esparcidamente ciliado; ramificaciones de la inflorescencia (1.5-)3-7 cm largo, cortamente pediceladas (pedicelo 2-4 mm largo), engrosadas. Estambres 2, anteras ovoides o elipsoides, ca. 0.75 x 0 30 mm, atropurpúreas; ovario cortamente pedicelado, subgloboso, ca. 0.75 x 0.3 mm. Infructescencia con escapo y raquis pilosos, hasta de 40 cm largo. Frutos densamente dispuestos, subglobosos, ca. 1.5 x 1 mm, ligeramente trígonos, a veces lenticulares, blancos.

description: Deciduous shrub or small tree 2-10 m. Leaves 2-6.5(-10) × 0.8-2 cm, chartaceous, usually narrowly elliptic, sometimes oblanceolate or elliptic, acute to obtuse or rarely emarginate at apex and often mu crenate, cuneate to shortly attenuate at base, sparsely appressed-pubescent when mature but usually more densely so on main veins; domatia weak in secondary vein-axils but with dense hair-tufts. Venation brochidodromous; midvein weak to moderate, prominent; secondary veins (3-)4-7(-8) pairs, distant, originating at moderately acute angles, slightly curved, scarcely prominent; intersecondary veins usually present; tertiary veins usually not conspicuous, randomly reticulate; higher order veins sometimes distinct; areolation imperfect or incomplete, not prominent. Petiole 0.1-0.5 cm, appressed-pubescent to subglabrous, eglandular. Inflorescences 1.6-6 cm, simple, more or less capitate, with 6-12 flowers all bisexual; peduncle 1.5-5.5 cm, appressed-pubescent to sparsely so; rhachis 0.1-0.3(-0.5) cm. Flowers pentamerous, 4.5-5.5 × 3-5 mm; lower hypanthium 2-2.5 mm, densely appressed-pubescent; upper hypanthium 2-2.5 mm, infundibuliform to campanulate, appressed-pubescent; calyx lobes 0.5-1 mm, usually revolute, appressed-pubescent; disk very sparsely pilose; stamens 3-4.5 mm; style 4-5.5 mm, pubescent in proximal half. Fruits few crowded on short rhachis, 1,4-2(-2.8) × 0.8-1.5(-2) cm, flattened, ovate to elliptic in side view, acute to obtuse and shortly beaked at apex, rounded at base, pubescent to subglabrous; wings 2, stiff and narrow, equal, 0.2-0.5(-0.6) cm wide; body 0.6-1.1 cm wide, bulging and 1-2 ridged on each face. Reproductive biology. Flowers white, cream-colored, yellowish green, distinctly protogynous. Flowering October to December; fruiting November to March.

description: Deciduous shrub or tree 2-18 (rarely to 35) m. Leaves 6-12(-15.5) × 2.5-5(-6.5) cm, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, lanceolate to ovate or elliptic to narrowly elliptic, acute to acuminate at apex, attenuate-cuneate at base, usually densely sericeous-pubescent when young, remaining pubescent or becoming subglabrous at maturity; domatia absent. Venation eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 6-10 pairs, close to moderately spaced, originating at moderately acute angles, curved or curved distally; intersecondary veins often present; tertiary and higher order veins usually randomly reticulate; areolation usually imperfect or incomplete, scarcely prominent. Petiole 1.2-3.7 cm, subglabrous to pubescent, biglandular. Inflorescences 2-6 cm, simple, with all flowers bisexual; peduncle 1-2.5 cm, pubescent to densely so; rhachis 1-3.5 cm, pubescent to densely so. Flowers pentamerous, 4-5 × 3-4 mm; lower hypanthium 1.5-2.5 mm, densely pubescent; upper hypanthium 1.5-2 mm, campanulate, pubescent; calyx lobes 0.5-1 mm, pubescent to sparsely so, patent to revolute; disk glabrous; stamens 3-5 mm; style 2.5-5 mm, pilose proximally. Fruits few crowded on short rhachis, 1.5-3 × 3-6.3 cm, flattened, transversely oblong in side view, usually emarginate at apex, truncate to emarginate at base, densely silvery-sericeous at first, remaining so or becoming sparsely pubescent or rarely subglabrous at maturity; wings 2, rarely with 1 or 2 small extra wings on 1 face, fairly stiff, equal, 1.5-2.6cm wide, to 3.2 cm long at longest point, rounded laterally; body 0.7-1.5 cm wide, bulging on both faces. Reproductive biology. Flowers yellow, yellow-green or cream-colored; strongly protogynous. Flowering July to October, along with new leaves; fruiting August onwards, often until next flowering. We have not been able to confirm the statement and the drawing (see Fig. 86) of Eichler (1867) that this species is andromonoecious; all the inflorescences that we have examined have only bisexual flowers.

description: Deciduous shrub or tree 3.5-25 m. Leaves (8-)10-27 × (4-)5-14 cm, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, oblong or elliptic to obovate, rounded to acute or acuminate at apex, cuneate to attenuate at base, minutely pubescent adaxially and densely so abaxially but becoming subglabrous except on main veins and secondary vein axils abaxially; domatia present in secondary vein axils, densely pubescent. Venation eucamptodromous, sometimes eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein stout to very stout, promi- nent; secondary veins 9-14 pairs, close to moderately spaced, originating at moderately acute angles curved distally, prominent; intersecondary veins usually absent; tertiary veins usually regularly percurrent; higher order veins well developed; areolation imperfect, slightly prominent. Petiole 2-5 cm glabrous to sparsely pubescent, biglandular. Inflorescences 4-8 em, simple, with all flowers bisexual; peduncle 2-3 cm, sparsely to densely pubescent; rhachis 2-5 cm, sparsely to densely pubescent. Flowers pentamerous, 4.5-6 × 4-4.5 mm; lower hypanthium 2-3 mm, very sparsely (often on two opposite edges) to densely pubescent; upper hypanthium 2-2.5 mm, cupuliform to slightly campanulate, glabrous to pubescent; calyx lobes 0.5-1.2 mm, suberect to variously revolute, glabrous to pubescent; disk glabrous to pilose; stamens 3-7 mm; style 4-5.5 mm, sparsely pilose proximally to wholly glabrous. Fruits few crowded on short rhachis, 1-3 × 3-7 cm, flattened, transversely oblong in side view, emarginate at base and apex, glabrous to (less often) sparsely pubescent; wings 2, fairly stiff, equal, 1-2.8 cm wide, to 3.7 cm long at longest point, rounded laterally; body 0.4-1 cm wide, bulging on both faces. Reproductive biology. Flowers yellow; strongly protogynous. Flowering August to September, along with new leaves; fruiting September onwards, often until next flowering.

description: Deciduous tree or sometimes shrub 1.8-30 m. Leaves 3-12.5 × 1.5-5.5 cm, chartaceous, elliptic or elliptic-oblong (or less often obovate) to narrowly so, acute to obtuse and usually apiculate to very shortly acuminate at apex, cuneate (rarely slightly decurrent) at base, sericeous-pubescent to sparsely so adaxially, sericeous-pubescent to densely so adaxially, sometimes subglabrous when old; domatia absent or weak. Venation craspedodromous-eucamptodromous, midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 5-12 pairs, moderately spaced to distant, originating at narrowly acute angles, curved proximally, strongly curved distally and often running parallel and close to margin for short way and then often reaching margin, prominent; intersecondary veins usually absent; tertiary veins mostly closely and very regularly percurrent, prominent; higher order veins distinct; areolation imperfect, prominent. Petiole 0.1-0.8 cm, densely appressed-pubescent, eglandular. Inflorescences 2-5(-6) cm, simple, andromonoecious, the male flowers mostly apical on each inflorescence or sometimes all flowers male in one inflorescence; peduncle 1.4-2.5(-3) cm, densely pubescent; rhachis 0.5-1.5(-2.5) cm, often subcapitate, densely pubescent. Flowers pentamerous, 3-4 mm (male) or 4.5-8 × 3.5-4.5 mm (bisexual); lower hypanthium 3-5.5 mm in bisexual flowers with fruit wings often clearly developing by anthesis, 1.2-2 mm and pedicellike in male flowers, densely pubescent; upper hypanthium 1-1.5 mm, shallowly infundibuliform, densely pubescent; calyx lobes 0.5-1 mm, erect to patent, densely pubescent; disk densely pilose; stamens 4-6.5 mm; style 3-6 mm, glabrous or very sparsely pilose near base. Fruits few crowded on short rhachis, 0.5-1.1 × 1.2-3 cm, flattened, transversely elliptic-oblong in side view, strongly emarginate at base and apex, densely pubescent; wings 2, fairly stiff, equal or subequal, 0.5-1.4 cm wide, to 1.5 cm long at longest point, rounded laterally; body 0.3-0.5 cm wide, bulging on one or both faces usually with 1-2 ridges (rudimentary wings) on each. Reproductive biology. Flowers whitish, cream-colored, yellow, creamish yellow, yellowish green, green, the bisexual ones clearly protogynous. Flowering August to January (June); fruiting October to July.

description: Deciduous tree 4-20 m. Leaves 2.5-12 × 1.4-6.5 cm, chartaceous, obovate or less often elliptic, sometimes narrowly so, rounded to subacute at apex, attenuate-cuneate at base, sparsely pubescent adaxially, pubescent abaxially, becoming subglabrous at fruiting; pocket-shaped domatia often present in proximal secondary vein axils. Venation brochidodromous; midvein moderate to weak, prominent; secondary veins 5-7(-9) pairs, moderately spaced to distant, originating at moderately to widely acute angles, curved, prominent; intersecondary veins present; tertiary veins randomly reticulate to irregularly and weakly percurrent; higher order veins scarcely distinct; areolation imperfect, scarcely prominent. Petiole 0.1-1 cm, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, eglandular or biglandular. Inflorescences 3-12 cm, simple, andromonoecious, the female organs variably expressed; peduncle 0.9-4 cm, densely rufous-pubescent; rhachis 2-5.7 cm (at anthesis) to 8 cm (at fruiting), densely rufous-pubescent. Flowers pentamerous, 3-5 × 2-4.5 mm; lower hypanthium 1-3 mm, densely rufous-pubescent, not much shorter in male than in bisexual flowers; upper hypanthium 1.3-2 mm, campanulate, densely rufous-pubescent; calyx lobes 0.5-1 mm, densely rufous-pubescent, suberect to strongly reflexed; disk pilose to sparsely so; stamens 4-5.5 mm; style 3.5-4.5 mm and sparsely pilose for proximal half in bisexual flowers, very sparsely pilose to glabrous and varying down to absent in male flowers. Fruits (few to) numerous disposed along whole length of rhachis, 0.4-0.7 × 0.9-1.8 cm, usually brown or pale brown, sometimes yellowish brown, flattened or irregular, transversely elliptic to transversely narrowly oblong in side view, rounded to strongly beaked at apex, truncate to shortly pseudostipitate at base, pubescent to densely so; wings variously developed, usually 2 subequal well-developed ones often with l(-3) others partly developed or rudimentary, sometimes only 1 well-developed with 1-4 others variously developed, fairly stiff to papery, to 0.9 cm wide, rounded to narrowly rounded laterally; body ca. 0.3 cm wide, usually bulging on one face and flatter on other, but with 1-2 ridges or rudimentary wings on each. Reproductive biology. Flowers cream-colored, cream-colored with red filaments, yellow, green, melliferous. Flowering August to November; fruiting August to June.

description: Probably deciduous tree. Leaves 5-12 × 2-5 cm, chartaceous, narrowly obovate or sometimes obovate, subacute to shortly acuminate at apex, cuneate and slightly attenuate at base, sparsely appressed-pubescent when mature but usually more densely so on main veins; domatia weak in secondary vein-axils but with dense hair-tufts. Venation as in T. australis. Petiole 0.5-1 cm, appressed-pubescent to subglabrous, eglandular. Inflorescences at fruiting 1.8-3.1 cm, simple, more or less capitate, probably with all flowers bisexual (fruits to apex of rhachis); peduncle at fruiting 1.5-2.7 cm, appressed-pubescent; rhachis 0.2-0.4 cm, appressed-pubescent. Flowers unknown. Fruits single or few and crowded on short rhachis, 1.3-1.5 × (2.5-)3-4.4 cm, flattened, transversely oblong in side view, emarginate at apex, retuse at base, subglabrous; wings 2, often with rudimentary third wing, fairly stiff, equal, 1.3-2 cm wide, rounded to narrowly rounded or obtuse laterally, basiscopically curved; body 0.5-0.8 mm wide, sharply keeled on both faces.

description: Woody liana to at least 8 m (probably much more), less often shrub 1.5-4m (or rarely tree to 10 m but based on questionably accurate field observation; possibly of a liana in tree); combretaceous hairs (only inside flowers) and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite or rarely in threes, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, 3-16 × 1-10.5 cm, elliptic or elliptic-oblong to broadly or narrowly so, abruptly short- to long-acuminate at apex, rounded or broadly cuneate to cuneate at base, moderately lepidote abaxially, very sparsely to sparsely lepidote adaxially. Venation eucamptodromous to eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 4-7 pairs, usually distant, originating at moderately to widely acute angles, usually markedly curved along length, fairly prominent; intersecondary veins absent; tertiary veins usually regularly percurrent, somewhat prominent; higher order veins distinct; areolation imperfect, scarcely prominent. Petiole 0.8-1.8 cm, usually moderately lepidote. Inflorescences usually much branched, in leaf-axils or terminal on lateral branches, 4-25 cm, with ultimate branches 1-10 cm and rather slender, its axis moderately to densely lepidote. Flowers tetramerous, 1.8-2.5 mm; lower hypanthium scarcely extended beyond ovary, 1.1-1.7 mm, without pedicel-like proximal region, densely lepidote; upper hypanthium 0.7-1 × 1.8-2 mm, very shallowly cupuliform, moderately to densely lepidote on outside, pubescent inside; calyx lobes triangular, ca. half total length of upper hypanthium, erect, acute at apex; petals 4, 1.2-1.6 mm, spathulate to oblanceolate or obovate, rounded at apex, with usually strongly recurved (often appar- ently emarginate but usually not so) extreme apex well exserted and patent at anthesis, glabrous; stamens 8, scarcely or not exserted, with filaments to 1 mm; disk densely pubescent, with very narrow free margin (ca. 0.1 mm), bulging between bases of lower (inner) whorl of filaments; style much less than 1 mm, included, glabrous; ovules usually 4. Fruit 1.5-2.2 × 1.2-2.2 cm, orbicular to broadly or transversely oblong-elliptic in side view, rounded to broadly obtuse and often minutely apiculate at apex, rounded or truncate to broadly obtuse at base, with slender pseudostipe 0.25-0.45 cm, densely lepidote on body, sparsely so on wings; wings 4, fairly stiff, 0.4-0.9 cm wide. Scales ca. 110-150 µm diam., greyish brown to rufous, more or less circular but convexly scalloped at each marginal cell, divided by solely or a great predominance of radial walls into markedly radially elongated cells; marginal cells 35-60 in number, several to many reaching from center to margin. Reproductive biology. Flowers green, yellowish green, cream-colored, whitish, pinkish white. Flowering January to March; fruiting May to July.

description: Shrub, scandent shrub or liana; combretaceous hairs and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, subcoriaceous, 4-12.5 × 2.1-8.2 cm, elliptic, sometimes ovate- or obovate-elliptic, obtuse to rounded and sometimes shortly apiculate at apex, broadly cuneate, rounded or subcordate at base, more or less glabrous even when young, moderately to rather densely lepidote abaxially, sparsely or very sparsely so adaxially, the scales inconspicuous. Venation as in C. laxum. Petiole 0.4-0.8 cm, sparsely pubescent to more or less glabrous. Inflorescences sparsely branched, moderately slender, 3-10 cm, aggregated into terminal panicles to 15 cm, sparsely pubescent, inconspicuously lepidote. Flowers borne fairly densely on rhachis, tetramerous, 1.6-2.3 mm; lower hypanthium 0.7-1.2 mm, not constricted above ovary, without pedicellike proximal region, rather sparsely pubescent, densely lepidote; upper hypanthium 1-1.1 × 1.2-1.4 mm, deeply cupuliform, sparsely pubescent on outside, pubescent inside; calyx lobes 0.3-0.6 mm, erect to incurved, acute; petals absent; stamens absent; disk densely pubescent at margin, with very narrow free margin; style 2.3-2.8 mm, exserted ca. 2 mm, glabrous; ovules 0-2. Fruit not seen. Scales as in C. laxum. Reproductive biology. Flowers green, very small and inconspicuous but probably nectariferous. Flowering August to February; apparently dioecious and only the female known. The style is conspicuously exserted through the narrowly opening hypanthium.

description: Woody liana to 30 m with stems to 15 cm diam., or shrub to 2 m; combretaceous hairs (only inside flowers) and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, 1.7-10.6 × 0.9-6 cm, elliptic, usually shortly to long acuminate but sometimes acute or obtuse at apex, cuneate to rounded at base, without hairs, moderately orange-red-lepidote abaxially, sparsely or very sparsely so adaxially. Venation as in C. fruticosum but secondary veins 4-8 pairs. Petiole 0.4-1 cm, glabrous, densely to contiguously orange-red-lepidote. Inflorescences unbranched, stout, in opposite pairs in leaf-axils, 5-18 cm, usually aggregated into terminal racemes to 56 cm, at the lower nodes in axils of normal leaves (usually fallen by fruiting, often by flowering), at the upper nodes usually without or with much reduced subtending leaves, glabrous, densely to contiguously orange-red-lepidote. Flowers borne densely around rhachis but in nature all swept up to vertical position from more or less horizontal rhachis, with long exserted stamens forming bottlebrush syndrome, tetramerous, 8.5-11.5 mm, without hairs on outside; lower hypanthium 3-3.5 mm, 4-angled, with pedicel-like proximal region 0.5-1 mm, contiguously orange-red-lepidote; upper hypanthium 5.5-8 × 3.5-5 mm, with narrowly infundibuliform proximal region (below disk) 2-3 mm and abruptly demarcated distal deeply cupuliform region (above disk) 2.5-3.5 mm excl. calyx lobes, moderately to densely orange-red-lepidote; calyx lobes 1-1.6 mm, erect, acute, moderately to densely orange-red-lepidote; petals 4, l.l-1.5 × 0.7-l mm, usually falling short of calyx lobes but sometimes reaching ca. to their apex, elliptic to suborbicular, obtuse to acute, sometimes apiculate, without a basal claw, glabrous; stamens 8, far exserted, with filaments 11.5-14.5 mm; disk densely pubescent at margin with straight hairs, with distinct free margin 0.5-1 mm; style 14-19.5 mm, exserted ca. as far as stamens, glabrous; ovules 3-5. Fruit 1.2-2.8 × 1.1-2.2cm, oblong-elliptic or elliptic to broadly so, rounded to truncate or slightly retuse at base, with very distinct narrow pseudostipe 0.2-0.5 cm, rounded or retuse and sometimes apiculate at apex, moderately to densely orange-red-lepidote especially on body; wings 4, 0.4-0.7 cm wide. Scales ca. 70-175 µm diam., rather irregularly undulate in outline, convexly scalloped at each marginal cell, divided by radial and tangential walls, nearly all by the former in the peripheral zone but more equally by both in the central zone, hence with a central area of subisodiametric cells; marginal cells ca. 20-45, somewhat radially elongated but none reaching from margin to center. The smallest scales of this species have nearly equal numbers of radial and tangential walls and hence have subisodiametric cells; they contrast strongly with the extra-small scales of C. fruticosum (q.v.). Reproductive biology. The flowers pass through the same stages of color-change as in C. fruticosum (greenish yellow to yellow to orange to red), and probably all the pollination data given under that species apply equally here. The "calyx (hypanthium) is usually described as red, due to the scales. There is a note of visitation by hummingbirds. Flowering August to January; fruiting July.

description: Usually a woody liana to 20 m, in the absence of support a shrub with decumbent long branches or a shrub to 4 m, or even a tree to 15 m with trunk to 18 cm; combretaceous hairs (often very scarce) and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, coriaceous, 4-20 × 2-12.5 cm, narrowly oblong-ovate to broadly elliptic or almost orbicular, gradually or abruptly shortly to long acuminate, acute, obtuse or rounded at apex, cuneate to subcordate or sometimes cordate at base, hairless or almost so, moderately to rather densely lepidote abaxially, sparsely or very sparsely so adaxially, the scales usually inconspicuous to naked eye, dark or whitish in color according to maturity. Venation usually eucamptodromous-brochidodromous, sometimes eucamptodromous or brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent to moderately so; secondary veins 7-17 pairs, close to distant, not to slightly or sometimes moderately prominent; lesser veins not prominent. Petiole 0.3-1.4 cm, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, inconspicuously lepidote. Inflorescences sparsely to extensively branched, slender, in opposite pairs in leaf-axils, 2-7 cm, usually aggregated into terminal panicles to 27 cm, at the lower nodes in axils of normal leaves (often fallen by fruiting), at the upper nodes without subtending leaves, glabrous to densely pubescent or rarely tomentose, inconspicuously lepidote. Flowers borne densely on rhachis, tetramerous, 2.6-3.5 mm, moderately to densely but usually very inconspicuously lepidote on outside; lower hypanthium 1.1-1.3 mm, without pedicel-like proximal region, pubescent to very sparsely so; upper hypanthium 1.5-2.9 × 1.5-3.4 mm, deeply cupuliform, glabrous to sparsely pubescent outside, subglabrous to pubescent inside (degree not correlated to pubescence outside); calyx lobes 0.2-0.3 mm, erect, subacute to obtuse; petals 4, 0.7-1.5 × 1.1-1.6 mm, well exceeding calyx lobes, patent at full anthesis, broadly spathulate with limb transversely oblong-elliptic and rounded or irregular at apex, with basal claw 0.1-0.3 mm, glabrous; stamens 8, well exserted, with filaments 3.5-4.8 mm; disk glabrous to densely pubescent at margin, without or with narrow free margin to 0.15 mm; style 3.8-5.3 mm, usually exserted ca. as far as stamens, glabrous; ovules 1-2. Fruit very variable; 1.5-4.5 × 0.7-1.7 cm, ovate or elliptic to narrowly so in side view, rounded to narrowly cuneate at base, with thick to narrow pseudostipe 0-0.6 cm, rounded to acute or acuminate and sometimes minutely apiculate at apex, hairless or nearly so, moderately to densely but minutely lepidote especially on body; body much thickened with spongy tissue; ridges 4, stiff, 0-0 3 cm wide, sometimes spirally twisted undulate. Scales as in C. laxum. Reproductive biology. Flowers white cream-colored or yellow (probably progressively with age), strongly sweetly scented; no pollinators noted but surely insect pollinated. The fruits vary in morphology but always have spongy tissue rendering them buoyant in rivers and lakes. Flowering (June) August to October; fruiting August to June.

description: Woody liana to 8 m; thin stems with weak often recurved infra-axillary spines, larger branches with spines to 7.5 cm; combretaceous hairs and stalked glands present. Leaves opposite or more or less so, chartaceous, 2-13 × 1.2-8 cm, elliptic to oblong- or ovate-elliptic, obtuse to shortly acuminate or rounded-apiculate at apex, broadly cuneate to rounded or cordate at base, usually densely minutely verruculose along all veins, especially on veinlets abaxially, pubescent to tomentose abaxially, rather sparsely pubescent mainly on veins adaxially, with stalked glands rather frequent on veins abaxially and sparse adaxially but very small and inconspicuous. Venation as in C. decandrum except secondary veins 3-7 pairs. Petiole 0.3-1.5 cm, densely pubescent to tomentose, with sparse stalked glands, often disarticulating at varying distances above base which remains to become spine next season. Inflorescences simple or branched, in leaf-axils, often forming a raceme or panicle of spikes to 40 cm sometimes devoid of leaves; each spike 3-12 cm, slender to very slender, its axis densely pubescent to tomentose and with sparse to frequent stalked glands. Flowers (tetramerous to) pentamerous, 4-5 mm; lower hypanthium 1.8-2.5 mm, pedicel-like proximal region 0.3-0.6 mm, narrowed to neck distally, densely appressed-pubescent, with stalked glands absent to frequent; upper hypanthium 2-2.5 × 3-3.3 mm, campanulate to infundibuliform, pubescent to densely so outside, with very sparse stalked glands, pubescent inside; calyx lobes triangular, 0.7-1 mm, erect, subacute to obtuse at apex; petals (4-)5, 2.3-2.8 × 1.2-1.6 mm, obovate, rounded at apex, exserted and patent to reflexed at anthesis, pubescent abaxially and on margins; stamens (8-) 10, well exserted, with filaments 3.8-5.5 mm; disk small but thick, closely applied to style base, pubescent at margin, with free portion ca. 0.2 mm; style 4.5-7.3 mm, exserted ca. as far as filaments, glabrous; ovules 5. Fruit 1.3-1.9 × 1.1-1.8 cm, broadly elliptic to suborbicular in side view, more or less rounded at base, with slender short but distinct pseudostipe 0.03-0.1 cm, rounded to slightly retuse and sometimes minutely apiculate at apex, sparsely pubescent on wings, pubescent or densely so on pseudostipe and body, and with sparse stalked glands; wings (4-)5, 0.5-0.8 cm wide, papery, straw-colored when dried. Stalked glands as in C. decandrum. Reproductive biology. Flowers white, cream-colored, creamy-white (drying yellow), apparently not protogynous, no mention of scent or pollinators. Flowering August to January; fruiting October to February.

description: Shrub or tree 2-8 m, with long sometimes pendent or scandent branches; combretaceous hairs (only inside flowers), stalked glands and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, chartaceous, 1.6-10 × 0.8-5 cm, elliptic or ovate-elliptic to sometimes broadly so, sometimes obovate-elliptic, acute, obtuse, or shortly acuminate with finely acute to obtuse point at apex, rounded to cuneate at base, with sparse to moderate stalked glands on midvein and secondary veins of abaxial surface, moderately to densely lepidote abaxially, sparsely to moderately lepidote adaxially, with whitish to yellowish golden scales. Venation brochidodromous to eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein moderate, fairly prominent; secondary veins 4-8 pairs, moderately spaced or close, originating at moderately to widely acute angles, curved along length or mainly distally, fairly prominent; intersecondary veins sometimes present; tertiary veins irregularly to regularly percurrent, slightly prominent; higher order veins distinct; areolation well developed, scarcely or not prominent. Petiole 0.1-0.7 cm, densely to contiguously lepidote, with sparse to moderate stalked glands. Inflorescences simple, in leaf-axils; rhachis 0.1-0.7(-1) cm and usually subcapitate in flower; peduncle 0.3-1.5(-2.5) cm, the whole becoming to 2.5(-3) cm in fruit, the axis contiguously lepidote at least in flower and often with sparse to moderate stalked glands. Flowers tetramerous, 3.5-5(-6.7) mm; lower hypanthium 1.2-1.8 mm, without pedicel-like proximal region, densely to contiguously lepidote; upper hypanthium 2.4-4.8 × 2.5-3 mm, with proximal region infundibuliform and distal region shallowly cupuliform, the 2 regions ca. equal length or either region (mostly proximal) slightly longer, moderately to densely lepidote on outside, glabrous inside; calyx lobes triangular, 0.5-0.6 mm, erect, acute to subacute at apex; petals 4, l-l.2 × 0.5-0.6 mm, oblanceolate, rounded to truncate but often apiculate or irregular at apex, exserted and erect at anthesis, glabrous; stamens 8, well exserted, with filaments 1.5-4.1 mm; disk densely pubescent, with free portion 0.1-0.2 mm; style 3-5.5(-8.2) mm, exserted ca. as far as filaments, glabrous; ovules 3-4. Fruit 0.75-2.5 × 0.8-1.8 cm, broadly triangular-ovate or orbicular to elliptic or oblong-elliptic in side view, truncate to rounded or slightly retuse at base, with pseudostipe 0.1-0.3 cm, rounded to truncate or slightly retuse and often apiculate at apex, densely yellowish- to rufous-lepidote on body, more sparsely so on wings; wings 4, fairly stiff, 0.2-0.7 cm wide. Scales ca. 110-200 µm diam., whitish to yellowish golden, more or less circular but often slightly convexly scalloped at each marginal cell, divided by solely or a great predominance of radial walls into markedly radially elongated cells; marginal cells 30-60 in number, many reaching from center to margin. Reproductive biology. Flowers cream-colored, yellow with pink stamens becoming red when older; no pollinators noted. Flowering November to February; fruiting December to June.

description: Small shrub to 4 m, but often developing spreading, decumbent or scandent branches, or woody liana to 15 m, combretaceous hairs (only inside flowers) and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, chartaceous or subcoriaceous, 2.5-12 × 0.9-5.7 cm, usually more than twice as long as wide, ovate to elliptic or more often narrowly so, obtuse or acute to acuminate at apex, cuneate at base, densely to contiguously whitish-lepidote abaxially, moderately to densely so adaxially. Venation as in C. fruticosum. Petiole 0.4-1 cm, contiguously whitish-lepidote. Inflorescences stout, in opposite pairs in leaf-axils, 3-16.5 cm, usually aggregated into terminal racemes to 40 cm (probably more) at the lower nodes in axils of normal leaves (usually fallen by fruiting), at the upper nodes usually without or with much reduced subtending leaves, densely to (usually) contiguously whitish-lepidote. Flowers borne densely around rhachis but in nature all swept up to vertical position from more or less horizontal rhachis, with long exserted stamens forming bottlebrush syndrome, tetramerous, 14.5-18 mm; lower hypanthium 4.5-9 mm, 4-angled, with pedicel-like proximal region 0.6-3 mm, contiguously whitish-lepidote; upper hypanthium 8-8.5 × 7-10 mm, with narrowly infundibuliform proximal region (below disk) 1.5-2 mm and abruptly demarcated distal shallowly cupuliform region (above disk) 3.5-4.5 mm excl. calyx lobes, densely to contiguously whitish-lepidote, glabrous to sparsely pubescent inside; calyx lobes 2.6-4 mm, erecto-patent, subacute to obtuse, the sinus between them obtuse (>90°), densely to contiguously whitish-lepidote; petals 4, 1.7-2.3 × 1.7-2.4 mm, usually at least as wide as long, falling well short of calyx lobes, orbicular, rounded at apex, without a basal claw, glabrous, sometimes sparsely lepidote abaxially; stamens 8, far exserted, with filaments 19.5-28.5 mm; disk densely pubescent with long straight hairs, with prominent free margin 1.7-3 mm excl. apical hair-tuft, thickened and at its apex closely appressed round near base of style, deeply corrugated on its inner (adaxial) side; style 26-32.5 mm, exserted ca. as far as stamens, glabrous; ovules 5-8. Fruit 1.2-2.2 × 1-1.7 cm, elliptic to very broadly so, rounded to truncate or slightly retuse at base, with very distinct narrow pseudostipe 0.1-0.5 cm, obtuse to rounded or retuse and very shortly apiculate at apex, often vinous-red, densely whitish-lepidote, densely to contiguously so on body; wings 4, 0.2-0.5 cm wide. Scales ca. 70-175(-210) µm diam., rather irregularly undulate in outline, convexly scalloped at each marginal cell, divided as in C. rohrii. Reproductive biology. The inflorescence structure and flower presentation of Combretum lanceolatum is similar to that of other species in the section, but there are important differences in detail. The filaments do not progress through yellow-orange-red phases according to field notes, but remain green to greenish yellow (although in some dried specimens they appear red), and the disk is considerably prolonged into a thick collar above the the style-base. The upper hypanthium and petals also are greenish yellow or cream-colored. Prance (1980) reported that the inflorescences present a large mass of greenish white flowers which produce abundant nectar (jelly, see below) and "suggest" pollination by bats. However, the only visitors he reported in Mato Grosso were capuchin monkeys (Cebus), which he thought might merely be secondary pollinators. Sazima et al. (2001) made detailed studies on C. lanceolatum in Mato Grosso. The flowers are scentless and their opening follows the same pattern as observed by Schemske (1980) in C. farinosum, those in the present case lasting for five days. Instead of secreting watery nectar the disk exudes a gelatinous "pellet" which sits atop the disk and which in most cases is removed whole by the pollinator, and then is not replaced. Also, in contrast to C. fruticosum, C. lanceolatum exhibits a high (>95%) pollen viability and high fruit-set. Sazima et al. recorded 28 species of birds in eight families: Columbidae (2), Psittacidae (4), Trochilidae (1), Picidae (1), Furnariidae (1), Tyrranidae (3), Muscicapidae (incl. Turdidae) (2), and Emberizidae (incl. Thraupidae and Icteridae) (14); the last four are passerines. The birds all gathered the pellet while perched on the inflorescences, except the hummingbird which licked the pellet while hovering. Flowering April to October; fruiting June to November.

description: Woody liana to 30m, or tree to 25 m, or well-branched often scandent shrub of few meters, tree and liana forms sometimes in the same locality; combretaceous hairs (only inside flowers) and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, 2-16 × 1-7.5 cm, elliptic or oblong-elliptic to broadly or narrowly elliptic, acute or obtuse to apiculate or shortly and abruptly acuminate at apex, broadly cuneate to rounded or subcordate at base, sparsely to very densely lepidote abaxially, sparsely to very sparsely so adaxially, especially along midvein. Venation eucamptodromous to eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 4-10 pairs, moderately spaced or rarely distant, originating at moderately acute angles, curved along length or only distally, sometimes forming intramarginal vein, fairly prominent; intersecondary veins absent; tertiary veins mostly regularly percurrent, scarcely prominent; higher order veins distinct; areolation imperfect, scarcely prominent. Petiole 0.6-1.8 cm, densely lepidote and often with long-stalked scales as well as subsessile ones. Inflorescences usually much branched, in axils of old or fallen leaves, 3-10(-18) cm, with ultimate branches 1-6 cm and very slender, its axis very densely lepidote, sometimes with long-stalked scales as well as subsessile ones. Flowers tetramerous, 3.5-5.3 mm; lower hypanthium narrow and pedicel-like distally to ovary, 1.7-3.2 mm, without pedicel-like proximal region, densely lepidote; upper hypanthium 1.7-2 × 2-2.3 mm, deeply cupuliform, densely lepidote outside, glabrous or sparsely pubescent inside; calyx lobes vestigial to very short (less than 0.5 mm), broadly obtuse at apex; petals absent; stamens 4, opposite each calyx-lobe, without caruncles, slightly exserted or not so, with filaments ca. 1-1.2 mm; staminodes absent; disk moderately to densely pubescent, bulging between bases of filaments, with very narrow (ca. 0.1-0.2 mm) free margins, leaving narrow gap around style base; style 1.8-2 mm, slightly exserted or not so, glabrous-ovules 2. Fruit (1.2-) 1.5-2.6×(0.8-)l.3-2.3 cm, orbicular to broadly oblong-elliptic in side view, broadly obtuse to retuse at base, with pseudostipe 0-0 1 cm broadly obtuse to retuse and often apiculate at apex! sparsely lepidote but more densely so on body; wings 4, fairly stiff, 0.4-1 cm wide. Scales ca. 75-150 diam., rufous, the smaller ones often more or less circular but convexly scalloped at each marginal cell, the larger ones rather irregularly wavy-edged, divided by more or less equally numerous radial and tangential walls into usually only slightly radially elongated cells; marginal cells (15-)20-30 in number, none reaching from center to margin except sometimes a few in the smallest scales. Reproductive biology. Flowers greenish, yellow, cream-colored, white; purplish- or rufous-spotted in flower or rufous in bud due to scales; with a strong sweet odour. Flowering January to May; fruiting February to September.

description: Woody liana to 30 m, or (? error) tree to 5 m; combretaceous hairs and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, chartaceous, 7-21 × 3-8.3 cm, narrowly oblong-ovate, rather gradually shortly to long acuminate at apex, broadly cuneate to more or less rounded at base, hairless or almost so, moderately to rather densely lepidote abaxially, sparsely or very sparsely so adaxially, the scales usually whitish in color. Venation eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 10-20 pairs, moderately spaced, originating at moderately acute to rather wide angles, curved along length or more or less straight proximally, moderately prominent; intersecondary veins usually present; tertiary veins irregularly to regularly percurrent, slightly prominent; higher or- der veins distinct; areolation imperfect, slightly to scarcely prominent. Petiole 0.6-2 cm, glabrous, inconspicuously lepidote. Inflorescences sparsely to extensively branched, rather stout, in opposite pairs in leaf-axils, 3-15 cm, usually aggregated into terminal panicles to 33 cm, at the lower nodes in axils of normal leaves (fallen by fruiting), at the upper nodes without subtending leaves, sparsely pubescent, inconspicuously lepidote. Flowers unknown. Fruit 4-6.5 × 0.8-1.3	cm, very narrowly oblong-elliptic to oblanceolate in side view, tapering to narrow base and apex, without distinct pseudostipe, rather densely lepidote, squarish in section with thick short lateral ridges (scarcely wings) running the length of the fruit. Scales as in C. laxum. Reproductive biology. Fruiting July to April.

description: Shrub 1.5-3 m or tree 2-10 m, perhaps sometimes a woody liana; combretaceous hairs and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, chartaceous, 4-13 × 2.8-9.5 cm, ovate or ovate-elliptic to broadly so, mostly obtuse to rounded but sometimes acute or retuse at apex, very broadly cuneate to rounded or subcordate at base, usually hairless but rarely moderately pubescent abaxially, moderately yellowish-whitish- or whitish-lepidote abaxially, sparsely or very sparsely so adaxially. Venation eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 5-10 pairs, moderately spaced or some close, originating at moderately acute angles, slightly curved along length or more or less straight proximally, moderately prominent; intersecondary veins sometimes present; tertiary veins rather irregularly percurrent, slightly prominent; higher order veins distinct; areolation imperfect, slightly prominent. Petiole 0.1-0.4 cm, usually without hairs except in stipular region, contiguously to moderately lepidote. Inflorescences unbranched, axillary or terminal, or a few forming a terminal raceme of spikes, 3-14 cm with the terminal one on a peduncle (i.e., proximal flowerless region of axis) to 4cm, rather stout, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, moderately to densely lepidote. Flowers tetramerous, 8-9.2 mm, without hairs on outside; lower hypanthium 2-2.5 mm, without pedicel-like proximal region, contiguously lepidote; upper hypanthium 6-8.5 × 5-6 mm, deeply cupuliform to infundibuliform, densely to contiguously lepidote, shortly pubescent inside; calyx lobes 1.3-2 mm, erect, subacute, densely lepidote; petals 4, 3.8-4.8 × 3-5 mm, reaching much higher than calyx lobes, broadly obovate, obtrullate or obtriangular, rounded or irregular at apex, gradually narrowed proximally, sometimes with scales abaxially, without hairs; stamens 8, exserted, with filaments 10-14 mm; disk densely pubescent at margin with long straight hairs, with distinct free margin ca. 0.5 mm; style 10-13 mm, exserted ca. as far as stamens’ glabrous; ovules usually 4. Fruit 1.2-2.2 × 0.4-0.9 cm narrowly triangular or trapeziform in side view, truncate to rounded at base, without pseudostipe, narrowly rounded to truncate at apex with apiculus to 0.1 cm, moderately lepidote; wings 4, stiff, 0.1-0 15(-0 2) cm wide. Scales ca. 60-180 µm diam., whitish or yellowish-whitish, nearly circular in outline, convexly or rarely concavely scalloped at each marginal cell. divided by numerous radial and some tangential walls; marginal cells ca. 15-40, much radially elongated but very rarely reaching from center to margin. Reproductive biology. Flowers white, white fading to yellow, cream-colored, pale pink. Flowering March to June, September; fruiting May to December No mention of perfume. Fruit said to be eaten by fish.

description: Woody liana in tall trees, with trunk to 30 cm diam., or shrub to 3 m; combretaceous hairs an peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, chartaceous, 2.3-14.5 × 1.2-6 cm, elliptic or oblong-elliptic to narrowly so, obtuse to acuminate at apex, cuneate rounded or subcordate at base, rufous-tomentose when very young but the pubescence soon wearing off and usually subglabrous when full-sized, moderately to rather densely yellowish- or golden-lepidote abaxially, sparsely or very sparsely so adaxially. Venation as in C. fruticosum. Petiole 0.3-1.2 cm, densely pubescent when very young but sparsely pubescent to subglabrous at maturity, moderately to densely golden-lepidote. Inflorescences unbranched, stout, in opposite pairs in leaf-axils, 6.5-15 cm, usually aggregated into terminal racemes to 36 cm, at the lower nodes in axils of normal leaves (usually fallen by fruiting time), at the upper nodes usually without or with much reduced subtending leaves, golden- to rufous-tomentose when young, the pubescence slowly wearing off but still strongly evident at fruiting and still obscuring scales, moderately to sparsely lepidote but many scales reduced in size. Flowers borne densely around rhachis but in nature all swept up to vertical position from more or less horizontal rhachis, with long exserted stamens forming bottle-brush syndrome, tetramerous, 12-14 mm, golden- to rufous-pubescent, the tomenturn totally obscuring scales which are all reduced size; lower hypanthium ca. 3.5 mm, with pedicel-like proximal region ca. 0.6 mm; upper hypanthium 8.5 10.5 mm, with narrowly infundibuliform proxima region 2.5-3.5 mm and usually rather poorly demarcated distal deeply cupuliform to infundibuliform region 3.5-4.5 × 4.5-5.5 mm excl, calyx lobes but the two regions scarcely distinguished; calyx lobes 2-3 mm, erect, acute; petals 4, 1.8-2.5 × 1.5-2.1 mm, usually falling just short of calyx lobes, broadly elliptic to orbicular, acute to shortly acuminate, without a basal claw, glabrous; stamens 8, far exserted, with filaments 18-21 mm; disk densely pubescent at margin with straight hairs, with distinct free margin to 1 mm, style 22-26 mm, exserted ca. as far as stamens, glabrous; ovules 6-7. Fruit 1.5-2.5 × 1.3-2.1 cm, very broadly elliptic to orbicular in side view, truncate to rounded or retuse at base, with very distinct narrow pseudostipe 0.2-0.4 cm, rounded to retuse and usually very shortly apiculate at apex, moderately pubescent especially on body and pseudostipe but sometimes all pubescence gone by mature fruiting, moderately to very sparsely lepidote but all scales reduced in size; wings 4, 0.4-0.8 cm wide. Scales as in C. fruticosum, but often much reduced in size and complexity where highly obscured by hairs. Reproductive biology. Little direct information, but probably most comments concerning flower color and pollination under C. fruticosum apply equally here. A specimen from Brazil: Rondonia (Ulisees & Coelho s.n.) is labeled as having aromatic yellowish green flowers, but scent is unlikely. In Central America flowering November to January; fruiting December to March. Flowering in May in Brazil.

description: Woody liana often in tall trees, or if without support then a sprawling shrub, erect shrub to 4 m, or even tree to 5 m; combretaceous hairs (very scarce and usually only inside flowers) and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, 3.5-16 × 2.5-10 cm, elliptic or rarely narrowly or broadly so, usually obtuse to acute but sometimes shortly acuminate at apex, cuneate to rounded at base, usually without hairs even when very young, rarely very sparsely pubescent on veins, moderately to densely greyish-lepidote abaxially (contiguously so when very young), sparsely to moderately so adaxially. Venation as in C. fruticosum. Petiole 0.5-2.2 cm, glabrous, contiguously to moderately greyish-lepidote. Inflorescences unbranched, stout, in opposite pairs in leaf-axils, 4-22 cm, usually aggregated into terminal racemes to 29 cm, at the lower nodes in axils of normal leaves (usually fallen by fruiting, often by flowering), at the upper nodes usually without or with much reduced subtending leaves, glabrous or sometimes sparsely pubescent, densely to contiguously greyish-lepidote. Flowers borne densely around rhachis but in nature all swept up to vertical position from more or less horizontal rhachis, with long exserted stamens forming bottle-brush syndrome, tetramerous, 13.5-15.5 mm, without hairs on outside; lower hypanthium 5-5.5 mm, 4-angled, with pedicel-like proximal re- gion ca. 1 mm, contiguously greyish-lepidote; upper hypanthium 8.7-10x6.5-7.5 mm, with regions above and below disk scarcely differentiated externally, together infundibuliform to bucciniform, 6-7.5 mm excl. calyx lobes, moderately to densely greyish-lepidote, usually shortly pubescent inside; calyx lobes 2.2-3 mm, erect, acute to subacute, moderately to densely greyish-lepidote; petals 4 or rarely 0 (e.g Erlansen et al. 46, ex Mexico), 1.4-1.7 × 0.6-0.8 mm. falling well short of calyx lobes, elliptic, obtuse to acute, sometimes apiculate, without a basal claw glabrous or sparsely pubescent abaxially; stamens 8, far exserted, with filaments 13.5-21 mm; disk densely pubescent at margin with straight hairs, with distinct free margin ca. 0.2 mm; style 22.5-30 mm, exserted ca. as far as stamens, glabrous; ovules 5-7, Fruit 1.7-2.7 × 1-1.9 cm, oblong-elliptic or elliptic to broadly so, rounded to truncate or slightly retuse at base, with very distinct narrow pseudostipe 0.2-0.4 cm, rounded or retuse and sometimes apiculate at apex, moderately to densely greyish-lepidote especially on body; wings 4, 0.4-0.7 cm wide. Scales as in C. fruticosum except sometimes to 250(-275) µm diam. Reproductive biology. The flowers pass through the same stages of color-change as in C. fruticosum (greenish yellow to yellow to orange to red), but since the great majority of labels state that the filaments are red (not yellow as in C. fruticosum) they presumably pass to the red stage more quickly. This color is reinforced by the red petals and red tinge of the upper hypanthium frequently showing through between the greyish scales, both in pressed specimens and in vivo. In contrast, the fruits are never red-tinged as is so often the case in C. fruticosum. Schemske (1980) followed a course of development in which flowers first open in the evening and secrete their abundant nectar overnight and for part of the next (first) day, when they are greenish. On the second day the flowers are greenish orange or sometimes already orange, on the third day they are orange, and on the fourth and fifth days red. Since nectar-secretion finishes during the first day (contrast C. fruticosum above), and most pollinator visits take place then, he suggested that the red flowers act as a signal. At any one time 40% of the inflorescences are red but these attract only 2% of the visits; the green flowers attracted 61% of all visits. The flowers are homogamous, self-incompatible and scentless. Flowering August to March; fruiting November to May. Schemske (1980) made detailed pollination studies of this species in Costa Rica. The flowers are very attractive to hummingbirds (Trochilidae), of which he recorded five species; Chlorostilbon canivetii and Archilochus colubris accounted for 66% of the visits, and Amazilia saucerottei and A. rutila for most of the rest. Eight species of birds in the families Picidae, Corvidae, Troglodytidae, Turdidae, Parulidae, and Icteridae were also recorded as pollinators. Also recorded were wasps, ants, and bees. Despite much nocturnal nectar-secretion no bats or hawkmoths were seen. Schemske obtained less than 1% seed-set from selfing but 30% from crossing, yet natural fruit-set was only 7% mainly due to predation. Flower predators recorded were a parrot (Amazona), a squirrel (Sciurus), and the howler monkey (Alouatta). Arizmendi and Ornelas (1990) also recorded hummingbirds (Cynanthus latirostris, Amazilia rutila, and Chlorostilbon canivetii) as well as passerines visiting this species in Jalisco, Mexico. Observations by Gryj et al. (1990) in the same region, purporting to refer to C. fruticosum, probably refer to C. farinosum, since the two were treated as synonyms by them and their study area was in dry forest on the west coast. Thirty-one species of birds were recorded as visitors, of which 40% were nearctic migrants. They disagreed with Schemske’s idea that hummingbirds are the main pollinators, because most visits were by passerines and these were dusted with much more pollen than the former. Of the 31 species, five were hummingbirds (Trochilidae) and six other families were represented: Columbidae (1 species), Picidae (1 species), Corvidae (1 species), Vireonidae (1 species), Muscicapidae (2 species), and Emberizidae (20 species), the last four families being passerines.

description: Tree 3-10 m or shrub 0.7-6 m, sometimes with flexuous branches; combretaceous hairs (only inside flowers), stalked glands and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, chartaceous, 2.8-14.4 × 1.5-7.9 cm, elliptic, ovate or obovate, shortly acuminate to acute or subacute at apex, rounded to cuneate at base, with stalked glands absent to sparse on midvein of abaxial surface, moderately to contiguously lepidote abaxially, moderately to densely lepidote adaxially, with whitish to yellowish scales. Venation as in C. monetaria except secondary veins 6-12 pairs. Petiole 0.1-1 cm, densely to contiguously lepidote, without or with sparse stalked glands. Inflorescences simple or rarely weakly branched, in leaf-axils; rhachis 0.5-4 cm in flower; peduncle 0.5-3 cm, the whole becoming to 7 cm in fruit, the axis contiguously whitish- to orange-lepidote at least in flower and sometimes with sparse stalked glands. Flowers tetramerous, 4.8-8.5 mm; lower hypanthium 1.2-2.5 mm, with pedicel-like proximal region 0-0.5 mm, densely to contiguously lepidote; upper hypanthium 3.3-6 × 2.5-4 mm, with proximal infundibuliform region 1.8-4 mm, much longer than distal shallowly cupuliform region 1.1-2 mm excl. calyx lobes, moderately to densely lepidote on outside, glabrous inside; calyx lobes triangular, 0.8-1 mm, erect, acute at apex; petals 4, 2-3.5 × 0.7-1.2 mm, oblanceolate to narrowly obovate, rounded or truncate to retuse at apex, exserted and erect at anthesis, glabrous; stamens 8, well exserted, with filaments 4-5.5 mm; disk densely pubescent, with free portion 0.2-1 mm; style 4.5-8.5 mm, exserted ca. as far as filaments, glabrous; ovules 2-4. Fruit 1.4-4 × 0.8-2.3 cm, elliptic or obovate to narrowly so in side view, cuneate to rounded or retuse at base, with pseudostipe 0.1-0.6 cm, rounded to truncate or slightly retuse and often apiculate at apex, with contorted wings and with a series of conspicuous bulges along the juncture of the wings and body (anfractuose), moderately to densely whitish- to orange-lepidote on body, more sparsely so on wings; wings 4, fairly stiff, 0.3-0.6 cm wide. Scales as in C. monetaria except ca. 80-200 µm diam, and with 25-60 marginal cells. Reproductive biology. Flowers white, greenish, cream-colored, yellow, red, evidently starting pale and turning red with age, scented; petals and stamens cream-colored or red. Flowering September to February; fruiting most months of year, primarily December to July.

description: Woody liana to 10 m with stems to 5 cm diam., or sometimes a shrub to 3 m or a tree to 7 m; stems with strong infra-axillary spines derived from old petioles; combretaceous hairs and stalked glands present. Leaves opposite or more or less so, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, 2-15 × 1.1-8 cm, elliptic to ovate- or oblong-elliptic, rounded to acute or sometimes acuminate at apex, broadly cuneate to rounded or subcordate at base, usually densely minutely verruculose along all veins, especially minor veinlets abaxially, often hairless but sometimes sparsely pubescent especially near base of midvein and rarely moderately pubescent all over leaf, with stalked glands rather frequent on veins abaxially and sparse adaxially but very small and inconspicuous. Venation usually eucamptodromous, sometimes eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 4-9 pairs, moderately spaced to distant, originating at moderately acute angles, usually markedly curved along length, fairly prominent; intersecondary veins absent; tertiary veins rather regularly percurrent, slightly prominent; higher order veins distinct; areolation imperfect to well developed, slightly to scarcely prominent. Petiole 0.2-1.6 cm, glabrous to pubescent, with sparse stalked glands, often disarticulating at varying distances above base which remains to become spine next season. Inflorescences simple or branched, in leaf-axils, often forming a raceme or panicle of spikes to 34 cm and often devoid of leaves; each spike 1-14 cm, slender to very slender, its axis sparsely to densely pubescent and with sparse to frequent stalked glands. Flowers (tetramerous or) pentamerous, 4-5 mm; lower hypanthium 2-2.5 mm, with pedicel-like proximal region 0.2-0.6 mm and usually narrowed to neck distally, usually hairless but sometimes sparsely to densely appressed-pubescent, with stalked glands absent to frequent; upper hypanthium 2-2.5 × 3.5-3.7 mm, campanulate to infundibuliform, hairless outside, without or with very sparse stalked glands, hairless to sparsely pubescent inside; calyx lobes triangular, 0.7-1 mm, erect, subacute to obtuse at apex; petals (4-)5, 2-2.7 × 1.2-1.7 mm, obovate to narrowly so, rounded or sometimes retuse at apex, exserted and patent to reflexed at anthesis, pubescent abaxially and on margins; stamens (8-)10, well exserted, with filaments 4-4.8 mm; disk small but thick, closely applied to style base, sparsely pubescent at margin, with free portion ca. 0.2 mm; style 5.6-6.8 mm, exserted ca. as far as filaments, glabrous; ovules 7-8. Fruit 1.2-2.1 × 1-1.8 cm, broadly elliptic to suborbicular in side view, retuse, rounded or obtuse at base, with slender pseudostipe 0.05-0.3 cm, rounded to retuse at apex glabrous to sparsely pubescent and with sparse stalked glands; wings 4-5, 0.5-0.9 cm wide, papery, straw-colored when dried. Stalked glands 35-65 µm, mostly appressed to organ, with uniseriate stalk 1-3 cells long and 12-20 × ca. 15 µm, with obovoid head 25-40 × l5-25 µm composed of 3-4 biseriate rows of cells. Reproductive biology. Flowers (petals) white, with cream-colored to green hypanthium, distinctly protogynous. No mention of scent or visitors, but presumably pollinated by insects; the thick disk suggests good nectar production. Flowering and fruiting throughout most of year especially November to June, the fruits often remaining until next flowering, which sometimes commences before leaves develop.

description: Woody liana, or shrub to 1.5 m with scandent branches; combretaceous hairs and peltate scales present. Leaves opposite, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, 1.8-10 × 1.l-7 cm, elliptic to broadly so, rounded to abruptly and shortly acuminate at apex, rounded or subcordate at base, sparsely rufous-pubescent except densely so on midvein and secondary veins on both surfaces at flowering, becoming glabrous except on midvein at fruiting (Parker 328), moderately to rather densely lepidote abaxially, sparsely or very sparsely so adaxially, the scales inconspicuous. Venation brochidodromous to eucamptodromous-brochidodromous, midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 5-9 Pairs, moderately spaced, originating at moderately acute an gles, curved along length or more or less straight proximally, moderately prominent; intersecondary veins absent; tertiary veins irregularly to regularly percurrent, slightly prominent; higher order veins distinct; areolation imperfect, slightly to scarcely prominent. Petiole 0.2-1 cm, densely rufous-pubescent, even at fruiting obscuring scales. Inflorescences extensively branched, very slender, in opposite pairs in leaf-axils, 0.6-2.5 cm, usually aggregated into terminal panicles to 30 cm, at the lower nodes in axils of normal leaves (often fallen by fruiting), at the upper nodes without subtending leaves, rufous-tomentose on main branches, pubescent to sparsely so on rhachides, inconspicuously lepidote. Flowers borne densely on rhachis, tetramerous, 2.1-2.5 mm; lower hypanthium 1.1-1.5 mm, markedly constricted above ovary, without pedicel-like proximal region, densely rufous-pubescent with stiff spreading hairs on ovary-containing portion, less so on constricted portion, rather densely lepidote; upper hypanthium ca. 1 × 1.3-1.5 mm, deeply cupuliform, sparsely pubescent on outside, very sparsely so inside; calyx lobes 0.1mm, erect, obtuse; petals 4, 0.7-0.9 × 0.7-1 mm, well exceeding calyx lobes, patent to reflexed at full anthesis, broadly spathulate with limb transversely oblong-elliptic and rounded at apex, with basal claw 0.1-0.2 mm, glabrous; stamens 8, exserted, with filaments 1.5-1.7 mm and conspicuously dilated proximally; disk vestigial, without free margin; style 0.3-0.4 mm, included, glabrous; ovules 2. Fruit unknown (but see comments on Parker 328 below). Scales as in C. laxum but mostly 40-45 µm diam. Reproductive biology. Flowers white, or white in bud turning yellow, with tawny calyx. The very small disk probably produces very little nectar. Flowering July to September.

description: Shrub or tree, 2-55 m, with buttressed trunk to 1.1 m diam. Leaves (2-)3-9(-10.5) × 1.5-4.5(-5.5) cm, chartaceous to coriaceous, obovate to elliptic or narrowly so, rounded to obtusely or subacutely acuminate at apex, cuneate at base, subglabrous except sparsely pubescent on midvein, especially abaxially: domatia usually present in secondary vein-axils. Venation brochidodromous or eucamptodromous-brochidodromous: midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins (3-)4-7 pairs, moderately spaced to distant, originating at moderately to widely acute angles, curved to slightly so, prominent; intersecondary veins usually absent; tertiary veins irregularly reticulate to weakly percurrent; higher order veins distinct or not; areolation well developed to inconspicuous. Petiole 0.4-2 cm, pubescent, usually eglandular but sometimes biglandular. Inflorescences 2-7.5 cm, spicate; peduncle 0.5-2.7 cm, pubescent; rhachis 1.2-5 cm, pubescent. Flowers 3-4.5 mm; lower hypanthium 1.5-2.2 mm, glabrous to densely pubescent, with glabrous to less pubescent neck ca. half the total length; upper hypanthium 1-1.5 × 1.8-3 mm, sparsely pubescent to subglabrous. Fruits 1.3-2.4 × 0.7-1.3 cm, elliptic in side view, more or less terete, rounded to subacute or shortly apiculate at apex, rounded to obtuse at base, glabrous to densely puberulous. Reproductive biology. Flowering July to October; fruiting October to July. Flowers greenish, cream-colored, dark purplish green, reddish brown.

description: Deciduous tree, 2-40 m, often less than 10 m. Leaves 3.5-24 × 1.5-10 cm, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, narrowly elliptic or narrowly obovate to elliptic, obovate or elliptic-oblong, rounded to obtuse at apex, broadly to narrowly cuneate but not or rarely slightly decurrent at base, often revolute at margin, densely rufous-pubescent to -tomentose all over when young, the pubescence varyingly wearing off with age but usually still conspicuously pubescent at fruiting on both surfaces (especially lower), especially on venous system which is therefore usually redder than the intervenous areas; domatia usually present in secondary vein-axils but shallow and usually obscured by hairs. Venation brochidodromous to eucamptodromous-brochidodromous; midvein strong, very prominent; secondary veins 8-14 pairs, moderately spaced, arising at moderately to widely acute angles, curved, very prominent; intersecondary veins absent; tertiary veins percurrent or weakly so; higher order veins distinct; areolation well developed to imperfect, prominent, forming conspicuous raised reticulum; venation conspicuous due to both prominence and thicker rufous pubescence. Petiole 0.3-1.8 cm, densely rufous-pubescent to tomentose, usually eglandular. Inflorescences (2.5-)4-14 cm, spicate; peduncle 0.6-2 cm, densely rufous-pubescent; rhachis (1.5-)3-12 cm, densely rufous-pubescent. Flowers 3.5-5 mm; lower hypanthium 2-3 mm, abruptly narrowed into long thin glabrous neck ca. twice as long as rufous-tomentose ovary-bearing part; upper hypanthium 1.5-2 × 2.5-4.5 mm, glabrous. Fruits 2-3.5 × 1.2-2.5 cm, elliptic to broadly so in side view, more or less terete, very succulent, rounded at apex, rounded to very shortly pseudostipitate at base, sparsely pubescent to glabrous at maturity. Reproductive biology. Flowering July to October, before leaves appear; fruiting in most months. Flowers cream-colored, yellow, yellowish green or greenish; fruits yellow or sometimes green when ripe, succulent, edible, and no doubt attractive to birds and mammals too.

description: Tree, 2.5-35 m. Leaves 3-16 × 1-3.5(-4) cm, coriaceous, oblanceolate or narrowly obovate to narrowly oblong-elliptic, rounded and apiculate to acute or acuminate at apex, narrowly cuneate at base, subglabrous except sparsely pubescent on main veins when mature; domatia present in secondary vein-axils. Venation brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins 5-8 pairs, moderately spaced, originating at moderately acute angles but immediately strongly curved hence often appearing to arise narrowly acutely, strongly curved, fairly prominent; intersecondary veins usually absent; tertiary veins consistently but weakly percurrent; higher order veins distinct; areolation complete, very small. Petiole 0.5-1.5 cm, pubescent, becoming subglabrous when old, biglandular. Inflorescences 4.5-10.5 cm, spicate; peduncle 1-3.5 cm, pubescent to sparsely so; rhachis 3.5-7 cm, pubescent. Flowers 2.5-3.5 mm; lower hypanthium 1.5-2 mm, narrowed to a short neck, wholly densely pubescent; upper hypanthium 1-1.5 × 2.5-4 mm, pubescent. Fruits 1-1.7 × 0.6-1.3 cm, elliptic in side view, more or less terete, subacute to rounded at apex, rounded to truncate at base, glabrous or finely pubescent. Reproductive biology. Fruiting September to March.

description: Tree 2.5-45 m. Leaves 14-36 × 5-14 cm, chartaceous, obovate to oblanceolate, rounded and apiculate to shortly and abruptly acuminate or cuspidate at apex, narrowly cuneate and scarcely decurrent at base, glabrous except often puberulous on midvein and secondary veins especially abaxially; domatia absent or shallow except for dense hair-tufts. Venation as in B. macrophylla. Petiole 1.2-2.3 cm, puberulous, biglandular. Inflorescences 9-16 cm, spicate; peduncle 2-3 cm, densely pubescent; rhachis 7-13 cm, densely pubescent. Flowers 3-4.5 mm; lower hypanthium 2-3 mm, densely pubescent on ovary-bearing part, with less pubescent rather thick neck much less than half total length; upper hypanthium 1-2 × 2.5-4mm, glabrous or nearly so. Fruits 1.8-4.7 × l-1.4 cm, elliptic in side view, strongly 5-ridged, abruptly narrowed to usually strongly curved beak 1-2 cm at apex, rounded or obtuse and abruptly narrowed to pseudostipe 0.2-0.7 cm at base, densely fulvous-tomentellous. Reproductive biology. Flowering August to November; fruiting February to July. Flowers red.

description: Deciduous tree, 5-30 m, with trunk to 20 m, buttressed when old. Leaves 2-10 × 1.5-6 cm, subcoriaceous, broadly obovate to oblanceolate, rounded to retuse (rarely obtuse) and sometimes apiculate at apex, narrowly acute and usually decurrent at base, appressed-pubescent when young, becoming glabrous except often sparsely pubescent on midvein when mature; domatia present in secondary vein axils. Venation brochidodromous; midvein moderate, fairly prominent; secondary veins 4-8 pairs, moderately spaced, originating at moderately to widely acute angles, curved to slightly so, slightly prominent; intersecondary veins often present; tertiary veins randomly reticulate to weakly percurrent; higher order veins often distinct; areolation incomplete to complete. Petiole 0.8-3.3 cm, appressed-pubescent, eglandular but base of leaf sometimes obscurely biglandular. Inflorescences 1.2-2.5(-4) cm, more or less capitate, with many densely grouped flowers; peduncle 1-2(-3) cm, stout, rufous pubescent in flower, becoming subglabrous in fruit; rhachis 0.4-1.3 cm. Flowers 3-4 mm; lower hypanthium (1.5-)1.7-2(-3) mm, rather gradually narrowed to neck ca. half total length, densely rufous-pubescent (rarely glabrous in Espírito Santo); upper hypanthium l-2 × 2-4 mm, glabrous or subglabrous. Fruits 1.5-3 × 1-1.5 cm, elliptic to obovate in side view, more or less terete, acute to rounded and often apiculate at apex, rounded at base, densely puberulous, becoming much less so when very old. Reproductive biology. Flowers cream-colored, green. Flowering December to January, July; fruiting December to April.

description: Tree, 8-35 m, with high, long, thin buttresses. Leaves 2.5-13 × 1.5-5 cm, chartaceous or sometimes subcoriaceous, obovate or narrowly so, obtuse to rounded at apex, narrowly cuneate and decurrent at base, glabrous except pubescent on midvein and secondary veins abaxially; domatia present. Venation brochidodromous; secondary veins 5-8 pairs, arising at moderately to widely acute angles; venation otherwise as in B. oxycarpa. Petiole 1.3-3.5 cm, to half as long as leaf, slender, glabrous or sometimes sparsely pubescent, eglandular or sometimes inconspicuously biglandular when young. Inflorescences 6-12 cm, spicate; peduncle 1-2.5 cm, sparsely pubescent; rhachis 4-9.5 cm, sparsely pubescent. Flowers 4-5 mm; lower hypanthium 2.5-3 mm, with very slender glabrous neck more than half the total, puberulous in lower ovary-bearing part; upper hypanthium 1.5-2 × 4-5 mm, glabrous on outside. Fruits 2-3 × l.3-l.9 cm, oblong to elliptic in side view, more or less terete, subacute to rounded at apex, rounded to subacute and usually shortly pseudostipitate at base, glabrous. Reproductive biology. Flowering January; fruit, ing August to April. Flowers yellowish green.

description: Semi- or briefly deciduous shrub or tree 1.5-8 m, with spines on branches. Leaves coriaceous, 0.5-2.5(-3.5) × 0.3-1 (-1.7) cm, obovate to oblanceolate, obtuse or rounded to retuse at apex, cuneate to narrowly cuneate at base, usually revolute at margin, glabrous or sparsely pubescent only on midvein abaxially; domatia absent. Venation brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins (3-)4-8 pairs, moderately spaced, originating at narrowly acute angles, slightly curved, scarcely or not prominent; intersecondary veins numerous, strong; tertiary veins randomly reticulate; higher order veins usually not distinct; areolation incomplete, not prominent. Petiole 0-0.2 cm, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, often biglandular. Inflorescences 0.6-6 cm, simple, usually capitate or subcapitate with ca. 3-13 flowers all bisexual; peduncle 0.5-4 cm, glabrous to sparsely pubescent; rhachis 0.1-2 cm, almost always glabrous; bracts less than 1 mm, ovate-triangular, puberulous abaxially. Flowers pentamerous, 3-5 × 2.5-4 mm; lower hypanthium 1.5-3 mm, glabrous to sparsely pubescent; upper hypanthium 1-2 mm, widely cupuliform, glabrous to very sparsely pubescent; calyx lobes 0.2-0.5 mm, suberect, glabrous; disk pilose; stamens 3-4 mm; style 2-3 mm, pilose proximally. Fruits few clustered at end of rhachis, 0.25-0.6 × 0.17-0.35 cm (excl, upper hypanthium), terete, ovate or narrowly ovate (often asymmetrically curved) in side view, woody and achene-like, abruptly or gradually narrowed to beak 0-1-0.2 cm at apex, rounded at base, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, the upper hypanthium not or only slightly persistent on the beak. Reproductive biology. Flowers yellow, yellow-green or greenish, odourless (in Hawaii), clearly protogynous. Flowering April to July; fruiting June to August.

description: Deciduous tree 5-35 m. Leaves 5-12 × 2.5-6 cm, chartaceous, obovate, subacute to acuminate at apex, cuneate at base, subglabrous when mature; domatia absent. Venation brochidodromous; midvein moderate; secondary veins 5-8 pairs, moderately spaced to distant, originating at moderately acute angles, curved; intersecondary veins usually absent; tertiary veins randomly reticulate; higher order veins conspicuous but scarcely prominent; areolation well developed. Petiole 1-2.6 cm, glabrous to sparsely pubescent, eglandular. Inflorescences 4-8 cm, simple, with all flowers bisexual; peduncle 2-3.5 cm, pubescent; rhachis 2-4.5 cm, densely pubescent. Flowers pentamerous, 5-6 × 4.5-5.5 mm; lower hypanthium 2.8-3 mm, densely appressed-pubescent; upper hypanthium 2-2.6 mm, campanulate, appressed-pubescent; calyx lobes 1-1.6 mm, appressed-pubescent, revolute to slightly so; disk sparsely pubescent to subglabrous; stamens 3-4.5 mm; style ca. 4 mm, pubescent proximally to over half way. Fruits few crowded on short rhachis, 1.2-2.5 × 3-4.6 cm, flattened, transversely oblong or elliptic-oblong in side view, usually emarginate at apex, truncate to broadly obtuse at base, pubescent, wings 2, fairly stiff, equal, 1.4-2.1 cm wide, narrowly rounded laterally; body 0.3-0.5 cm wide, slightly to strongly keeled on one face. Reproductive biology. Flowering September to December; fruiting September to December. Flowers cream-colored, green.

description: Deciduous tree 6-50 m, with plank buttresses to 3 m high, 1.7 m wide, 0.15 m thick. Leaves 4-11 × 2-4(-5.5) cm, chartaceous, elliptic-oblong to obovate or narrowly so, long-acuminate at apex, cuneate or attenuate-cuneate at base, sericeous when young, glabrous or nearly so except sparsely pubescent on main veins abaxially at maturity; domatia absent. Venation brochidodromous; midvein moderate, prominent; secondary veins (5-)7-12 pairs, moderately spaced to distant, diverging at widely acute angles, curved, prominent; intersecondary veins often present; tertiary veins randomly reticulate or sometimes weakly percurrent; higher order veins not distinct; areolation large, imperfect, scarcely prominent. Petiole 1.2-3.5 cm, usually glabrous, biglandular. Inflorescences 1.5-5.5 cm, simple, with all flowers bisexual; peduncle 0.5-2.8 cm, pubescent; rhachis 0.8-3.5 cm, subcapitate to moderately elongated, densely pubescent at flowering. Flowers pentamerous, 3-4.6 × 2-3.8 mm; lower hypanthium 1.5-2.2 mm, pubescent to densely so; upper hypanthium 0.8-1.5 mm, deeply cupuliform to deeply campanulate, pubescent to sparsely so; calyx lobes 0.7-1 mm, pubescent to sparsely so, revolute to erect; disk sparsely pilose; stamens 3-5 mm; style 3-4 mm, pilose proximally or almost to apex. Fruits few crowded on short rhachis, 1.6-3.2 × 3.3-7.8 cm, flattened, transversely oblong in side view, rounded to emarginate at apex, obtuse (often with concave basiscopic wing margin), truncate or slightly emarginate at base, glabrous and usually shiny; wings 2, fairly stiff, equal, 1.7-3.5 cm wide, rounded to very narrowly rounded laterally, to 4 cm long at longest point; body 0.4-0.7 cm wide, usually bulging on both faces. Reproductive biology. Flowers yellow-green, with slight scent, protogynous. Flowering October to March; fruiting October to June. The large-winged fruits seem well adapted for wind dispersal.
