description: Plants stout, 2-6 m tall. Sheaths sparsely puberulous to glabrous, 1-3 cm in diam. Ligule truncate, 1-2 mm long, margins dilacerating into fibers, glabrescent with age. Petiole 2-25 mm long, sparsely to densely puberulo-sericeous. Leaves congested towards the top of the stem, narrowly ovate to narrowly obovate, cuneate at the base, ending in a 10-50 mm long acumen at the apex, 12-50 cm long, 3-12 cm wide, upper side glabrous, lower side sparsely to rather densely puberulo-sericeous or rarely glabrous. Inflorescence ovoid to cylindric, 10-40 cm long, 4-7 cm wide, often with leafy shoots arising from the base or apex. Bracts green, becoming brown in fruit, coriaceous often completely sheathing, apex obtuse or acute, 2-6 cm long, 2-4 cm wide, glabrous to rather densely puberulo-sericeous, margins dilacerating into fibers, glabrescent with age, callus 2-6 mm long. Bracteole green, becoming brown in fruit, coriaceous, (20-)25-30(-35) mm long, sparsely to rather densely puberulo-sericeous. Calyx green, becoming brown in fruit, coriaceous, (20-) 25-35 (-40) mm long, sparsely to rather densely puberulo-sericeous, lobes ovate-triangular, 3-5 mm long, callus 3-10 mm long. Corolla white or yellow, 65-80 mm long, tube 20-30 mm long, lobes narrowly obovate, obtuse or rounded at the apex, 45-60 mm long, 10-25 mm wide, glabrous or rarely sparsely sericeous towards the apex. Labellum white or yellow and occasionally somewhat tinged with orange, broadly obovate when spread out, 70-90 mm long 80-130 (!) mm wide, margins slightly crisped. Stamen white or yellow (or purple-red?), 50-60 mm long, 12-15 mm wide, obtuse at the apex, anther 11-16 mm long. Stigma 2-3 mm long, 4-4.5 mm wide. Ovary cylindric, 5-10 mm long, rather densely to sparsely puberulo-sericeous. Capsule green, turning orange and brown at maturity, coriaceous, ellipsoid-cylindric, 25-50 mm long, to 12 mm wide, sparsely to rather densely puberulo-sericeous, seeds glossy brown (rarely black), 2.5-5 mm long, 2-3 mm wide.

description: Plants stout, 2-4(-6) m tall. Sheaths sparsely to densely puberulous, 10-20 mm in diam. Ligule obliquely truncate, 5-15 mm long, hairy like the sheaths. Petiole 5-15 mm long, densely (yellowish) sericeous. Leaves narrowly elliptic, cuneate to rounded, or rarely cordate at the base, ending in a 10-30 mm long acumen at the apex, 18-60 cm long, 5-13 cm wide, upper side more or less scabrid, lower side densely sericeous. Inflorescence broadly ovoid to cylindric, obtuse, 8-18 cm long, 6-8 cm wide. Bracts dark red (5.0 R 4/12), coriaceous, broadly ovate, 2-2.5 cm long and wide, sericeous on both sides; appendages foliaceous, dark red (5.0 R 4/12, later turning 2.5 R 3/10), often with a yellow line in the middle, horizontally spreading or ascending in living plants, usually reflexed when dry, broadly to very broadly ovate, obtuse, 15-25 mm long, 10-35 mm wide (the lower ones often greenish and much longer), rather densely hirsute and scabrid to the touch, to glabrous. Bracteole reddish, 15-23 mm long, rather densely puberulous. Calyx reddish, 12-14 mm long, sparsely to rather densely puberulous, lobes deltate, 2-4 mm long. Corolla deep pink to yellow, 35-50 mm long, tube ca 10 mm long, lobes narrowly obovate, 25-40 mm long, 9-17 mm wide, densely puberulo-sericeous. Labellum pink, oblong-obovate when spread out, 25-40 mm long, 10-12 mm wide, lateral lobes rolled inwards and forming a tube ca 10 mm in diam, upper margin 5-dentate, teeth reflexed, deltate, 1-5 mm long, often with a yellow line in the middle. Stamen narrowly elliptic, yellowish red, 25-40 mm long, 2-8 mm wide, apex acute, enclosing the 8-10 mm long anther like a helmet. Ovary 4-8 mm long, densely sericeous, especially towards base and apex. Capsule ellipsoid, 10-15 mm long, sericeous to glabrous, seeds black.

description: Rather low plants, 0.3-1.5 m tall. Sheaths membranaceous and very fragile when dry, puberulous to strigose, 8-15 mm in diam. Ligule (5-)20-40 mm long, unequally two-lobed, lobes rounded, membranaceous and very fragile when dry, puberulous to strigose. Petiole 2-5 mm long, densely villose to hirsute. Leaves narrowly elliptic, narrowly obovate, or obovate, rounded at the base, shortly acuminate at the apex, 16-32 cm long, 5.5-9 cm wide, densely strigose to glabrous on both sides, costa densely strigose above. Inflorescence ovoid, 6-11 cm long, 3-5-4(-6) cm wide. Bracts bright red to orange, broadly ovate, chartaceous to coriaceous, to 2.5 cm long and 3 cm wide, glabrous to sparsely puberulous, callus 6-12 mm long; appendages foliaceous, bright red, usually reflexed when dry, very broadly ovate to deltate, acute to obtuse, 5-20 mm long and wide (the lower ones greenish to 60 mm long and 25 mm wide), rather densely puberulo-strigose. Bracteole 17 mm long, sparsely puberulous at the base, callus to 4 mm long. Calyx 10-15 mm long, glabrous to rather densely puberulous, lobes shallowly triangular to deltate, 3-5 mm long, occasionally with a 2 mm long callus. Corolla pale yellow or orange, 35-42 mm long, glabrous, tube 10 mm long, lobes narrowly obovate, 25-32 mm long, 10-12 mm wide. Labellum oblong-obovate when spread out, 25-35 mm long, 8-15 mm wide, lateral lobes rolled inwards and forming a tube, upper margin 5-dentate. Stamen narrowly elliptic, 25-30 mm long, 4-8 mm wide, apex rounded or obtuse, anther 6-8 mm long. Ovary 5 mm long, sericeous, especially at the apex. Capsule ellipsoid, 14 mm long, densely yellowish sericeous, seeds black.

description: Plants stout (o.5-)2-6 m tall. Sheaths, ligules, petioles, leaves, and bracts glabrous, puberulous, sericeous, villose, strigose or hirsute. Sheaths 10-40 mm in diam. Ligule truncate, 5-10(-15) mm long. Petiole 5-20 mm long. Leaves narrowly ovate to narrowly obovate, cuneate, rounded, or rarely cordate at the base, shortly acuminate at the apex, (13-) 20-65 cm long, 5-15 cm wide. Inflorescence ovoid, obtuse, 5-15 (-30) cm long, 4-6(-10) cm wide, terminating a leafy stem, or on a separate leafless shoot to 50 cm long, sheaths obliquely truncate, to 8.5 cm long, to 3.5 cm wide. Bracts green in the exposed part, red or rarely green in the covered part, coriaceous, broadly ovate, 2-4(-6) cm long and 1-5-5 cm wide, callus absent, or to 10 mm long; appendages rarely absent, foliaceous, rigid, green, ascending or slightly reflexed, narrowly triangular to deltate, 2-4(-10) cm long, 1.5-2 (-4) cm wide. Bracteole red, often greenish-tipped, 25-40 mm long, glabrous to densely puberulous. Calyx red, (7-) 14-18(-22) mm long, glabrous to densely puberulous, lobes triangular to shallowly triangular, (2-) 3-6 mm long. Corolla white, reddish white, or yellowish white, 70-100 mm long, glabrous to rather densely puberulous, tube ca 20 mm long, lobes narrowly obovate, (50-)60-80 mm long, 15-35 mm wide. Labellum white or yellowish white, broadly obovate when spread out, 75-110 mm long, 60-70 mm wide, lateral lobes usually striped with red, middle lobe reflexed, blotched with yellow to orange in the centre. Stamen narrowly elliptic, white to pinkish white, 40-60 mm long, 7-20 mm wide, apex obtuse or obscurely three-lobed, anther 10-14 mm long. Ovary 5-10 mm long, densely puberulo-sericeous to glabrous. Capsule ellipsoid, 12-22 mm long, densely puberulo-sericeous to glabrous, seeds black.

description: Plants 0.5-2 (-3) m tall. Sheaths densely to rather densely puberulous, villose to velutinous, rarely glabrescent, 5-12 mm in diam. Ligule truncate, 1-6 mm long, hairy like the sheaths. Petiole 2-10 mm long, densely puberulo-sericeous. Leaves narrowly elliptic to narrowly obovate, cuneate to rounded at the base, terminating in a 10-30 mm long acumen, 10-26(-37) cm long, 2.5-6.5 cm wide, upper side glabrous, strigose, puberulous, or villose, lower side puberulous, villose, sericeous, or velutinous (rarely strigose). Inflorescence ovoid to cylindric, 6-10(-12) cm long, 4.5-5.5 cm wide. Bracts reddish green to green, coriaceous, broadly ovate, 2-3 cm long and wide, rather densely (minutely) puberulous; appendages foliaceous, reddish, the lower ones tinged with green, horizontally spreading or ascending in the living plant, usually reflexed when dry, triangular, 15-40 mm long, 5-15 mm wide (the lower ones to 80 mm long and 20 mm wide), sericeous, puberulous, strigose, or glabrous. Bracteole reddish, 14-20 mm long, rather densely (minutely) puberulous. Calyx reddish, 9-12 (-15) mm long, rather densely (minutely) puberulous, lobes deltate, ca 4 mm long. Corolla yellow, sometimes tinged with orange-red at the apex, 30-35 mm long, densely puberulous, tube 10 mm long, lobes narrowly obovate, 20-25 mm long, (8-) 10-12 mm wide. Labellum yellow, often reddish at the apex, oblong-obovate when spread out, 20-25 mm long, 8-12 mm wide, lateral lobes rolled inwards and forming a tube, upper margin 5-dentate, teeth reflexed, deltate, 1-5 mm long. Stamen narrowly elliptic, 18-23 mm long, 2-8 mm wide, apex obtuse or rounded, anther 5-6 mm long. Ovary 3-8 mm long, densely puberulo-sericeous. Capsule ellipsoid, 8-12 mm long, densely puberulo-sericeous, especially at the apex, seeds black.

description: Leafy stems 1-3.5 m tall. Rhizomes densely brownish strigose. Sheaths 5-20 mm in diam, glabrescent. Ligule truncate, 2-10 mm long, glabrous or villose towards the margins. Petiole 2-17 mm long, glabrous to villose. Leaves narrowly elliptic, shortly acuminate at the apex, cuneate to rounded at the base, 8-43 cm long, 5-14 cm wide, glabrous to densely villose on both sides. Flowering stems 25-70 cm tall, sheaths truncate, 1.5-6 cm long, o.5-2.0 cm wide, glabrous. Inflorescence ovoid, obtuse, 4-11 (-22) cm long, 2-5(-8) cm wide. Bracts red (5.0 R 4/12-5/12 in the exposed part, 5.0 R 6/10 in the covered part), coriaceous, broadly ovate, obtuse (or acute) at the apex, 2-4 cm long, 2.5-4.5 cm wide, glabrous or rarely appressed puberulous, margins of the covered part often dilacerating into fibers, margins of the exposed part rarely so, callus 5-10 mm long, green to yellowish green. Bracteole purplish red, 15-29 mm long, glabrous to sparsely puberulous. Calyx purplish red (10.0 RP 5/8), 7-12 (-15) mm long, glabrous to sparsely puberulous, lobes shallowly triangular to deltate, 2-4 mm long. Corolla pinkish red to salmon-red, glabrous, 45-60 mm long, tube ca 10 mm long, lobes narrowly obovate-elliptic, 35-45 mm long, 10-20 mm wide. Labellum pinkish red to salmon-red (5.0 R 5/12 to 5/10), inner side near apex yellowish, oblong-obovate when spread out, 25-30 mm long, 20-25 mm wide, lateral lobes rolled inwards and forming a slender tube of 7-10 mm in diam, apex slightly irregularly crenulate. Stamen narrowly elliptic, 25-30 mm long, 5-10 mm wide, red (5.0 R 6/10), apex emarginate or acute, anther 7-9 mm long. Ovary 4-12 mm long, densely sericeous to glabrous. Capsule ellipsoid, 10-13 mm long, glabrous, seeds black.

description: Plants 0.4-3 m tall. Rhizomes 3-10 mm thick. Sheaths striate, 4-10 mm wide, glabrous or sometimes towards the ligule and near the margins covered with furcate and stellate prickles (to 0.1 mm long). Ligule 1-2 mm long, glabrous or covered with furcate to stellate prickles (to 0.1 mm long) and/or simple, appressed hairs (0.1-0.3 mm long). Petiole 0-12 mm long, hairy like the sheaths. Lamina narrowly elliptic, acute or shortly acuminate at the apex (acumen 5-10 mm long), cuneate at the base, 640 cm long, (1.5-) 2-7(-8) cm wide (the uppermost leaves often strongly reduced: 3-26 X 0.5-7 cm), glabrous on both sides. Inflorescence a terminal thyrse 3-17 cm long and 1-8 cm wide, with (1-) 2-4(-5)-flowered cincinni, rhachis pink to red, 1-2(-3) mm thick. Indument of inflorescence: sheaths, rhachis, peduncles, and pedicels glabrous or densely covered with furcate (and plurifurcate) hairs, and mostly much fewer simple hairs (both hair types 0.1-0.4 mm long), bracts, bracteofes, and calyx sparsely so at their base, ovary and capsule glabrous to sparsely hairy, corolla glabrous (for the exceptional indument of Ekman 214 see the discussion). Bracts red, pinkish-red, or scarlet, membranous, rather long persistent, ovate to triangular, acute to obtuse at the apex, 8-30(40) mm long, 3-10(-15) mm wide (the lower, sterile ones 40-100 X 6-15 mm). Peduncles 2-10(-12) mm long. Bracteole red 4-10 (-13) mm long. Pedicels 2-15(-20) mm long. Calyx (bright) red, tubular to slightly turbinate, 5-11 (-13) mm long, 3-6 mm wide, the lobes depressed-ovate, 1-2 mm long, 24 mm wide. Corolla white, 14-25 mm long, the tube 6-12 mm long, the lobes 6-13 mm long, 3-5 mm wide. Labellum white (according to Wright margins and lateral staminodes slightly tinged with purple), 5-8 mm long and wide when spread out, glabrous, the limb more or less transversally elliptic in outline, 3.5-6 mm long, 5-8 mm wide, the middle lobe obscurely divided into two broadly ovate-deltate to ovate-triangular lobules 0.5-1 mm long, basal claw 1-3 mm long, 1.54 mm wide, lateral staminodes 0.8-1.3 mm long, 0.3-0.5 mm wide. Anther red, 4-6 mm long, 1.5-3 mm wide, glabrous. Style (13-) 16-23 mm long. Nectarial glands multilobulate, 1-2 mm long, completely surrounding the style base. Ovary red. Capsule red, maturing black, globose to ellipsoid, 5-10 X 5-8(-10) mm, its wall ca 0.1 mm thick when dry, 5-25 seeded, seeds 1.5-3 X 2-3.5 mm.

description: Plants (0.8-)1-3(-4) m tall. Rhizomes 10-15 mm thick. Sheaths striate, 5-15 mm wide, to 30 mm at the base of the plant, glabrous. Ligule 1-2 mm long, glabrous or covered with simple, needle-like hairs (to 0.5 mm long) and furcate prickles (less than 0.1 mm long). Petiole absent or sometimes up to 10 mm long, glabrous. Lamina narrowly elliptic, acute or acuminate at the apex (acumen 10-20 mm long), cuneate at the base, 13-55 cm long, (2-)4-12 cm wide, glabrous on both sides. Scape (15-)40-65(-100) cm tall, up to 5 mm thick, beset with sheaths up to 4-15 cm long and 0.5-1.5 cm wide. Inflorescence a basal (very rarely terminal) thyrse 10-35 cm long and 2-7 cm wide, with 2-17-flowered cincinni, rhachis red. Indument of inflorescence: all parts glabrous to densely covered with simple hairs, furcate hairs rare, corolla glabrous. Bracts pale green to red, membranous and soon deciduous, narrowly triangular-ovate to triangular-ovate, acute or obtuse, often at an angle of 45°-90° with the rhachis, 6-75 mm long, 3-10 mm wide. Peduncles red, 4-20 mm long. Bracteole 7-17 mm long. Pedicels red, 3-17 mm long. Calyx red, turbinate, 4-7 mm long and wide (ca 2 mm wide at the base), the lobes depressed ovate, obtuse, 1-3 mm long, 3-5 mm wide. Corolla yellow, 13-21 mm long, the tube 6-11 mm long, the lobes 7-10 mm long, 4-7 mm wide. Labellum  yellow, 7-10 mm long and 5-9 mm wide when spread out, basal part opposite anther densely hairy (hairs to 0.5 mm long), the limb 4-7 mm long, 5-9 mm wide, lateral lobes rounded, 3-5 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, the middle lobe reflexed, rounded and entire, basal claw 3-4 mm long and 3-5 mm wide, lateral staminodes 1-1.5 mm long. Anther 5-7 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, glabrous. Style 14-19 mm long. Nectarial glands partly surrounding the excentric style base, 1-2 mm long. Ovary red. Capsule red (rarely purple-black), globose to ellipsoid, 4-18 X 4-9 mm, its wall 0.1-0.2 mm thick when dry (ca 1 mm in living material), 10-25-seeded, seeds 2-3 X 2-4 mm.

description: Plants 1-3 m tall. Rhizomes 10-20 mm thick. Sheaths striate, 8-10 mm wide, to 20 mm at the base of the plant, glabrous. Ligule 3-4 mm long, glabrous. Petiole absent. Lamina narrowly elliptic, acuminate at the apex (acumen 10-20 mm long), cuneate at the base, (15-)25-45 cm long, (5-)8-12(-15) cm wide, glabrous on both sides. Inflorescence a terminal thyrse 6-25 cm long and 4-8 cm wide, with 2-4 flowered cincinni, rhachis 2-5 mm thick. Indument of inflorescence: rhachis, peduncles, bracteoles, pedicels, calyx, ovary, and capsule sparsely to densely covered with erect, simple hairs (0.1-0.2 mm long), bracts and corolla sparsely so or glabrous. Bracts white, deciduous during fructification, narrowly triangular-ovate to triangular-ovate, acute or obtuse, 10-50 mm long, 4-10 mm wide (the lower, sterile ones 60-200 X 10-15 mm). Peduncles 5-20 mm long. Bracteole white, 13-20 m long (according to Gagnepain 6-8 mm long ??). Pedicels 5-20 mm long. Calyx white to pale green, slightly turbinate, 7-11 mm long, 5-8 mm wide, the lobes deltate to shallowly triangular, 2-4 mm long, 4-5 mm wide. Corolla white at the base, 15-19 mm long, the tube 8-10 mm long, the lobes white to pink, 7-9 mm long, 4-8 mm wide. Labellum pale pink to white, 8-10 mm long and 8-11 mm wide when spread out, glabrous, the limb horizontally spreading, ca 4 mm long, 8-11 mm wide, the lateral lobes rounded, 2-4 mm long, (3-)4-5 mm wide, the middle lobe bilobulate, the lobules triangular, 2-3 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, basal claw 4 mm long, 2-3 mm wide, lateral staminodes 1-1.5 mm long. Anther 4-6 mm long, 1-2 mm wide, glabrous. Style 15-16 mm long. Nectarial glands multilobulate, completely surrounding the style base, ca 2 mm long. Ovary green, narrowly ellipsoid. Capsule green, maturing red and finally black, ellipsoid, 10-17 X 5-10 mm, its wall ca 0.2 mm thick when dry (ca 2 mm in living material), 10-25-seeded, seeds 2-3 X 3-4 mm, aril orange.

description: Plants 0.8-5 m tall. Rhizomes 10-30 mm thick. Sheaths striate to reticulate, 5-15 mm wide, to 35 mm at the base of the plant, densely to sparsely covered with simple, furcate, and stellate prickles (less than 0.1 mm long) and towards the ligule and at the reticulations with needle-like hairs (to 1 mm long). Ligule 1-2 mm long. Petiole 0-30(-60) mm long, hairy like the sheaths. Lamina narrowly elliptic, acuminate (acumen 5-15 mm long) or rarely acute at the apex, cuneate at the base, 25-90 cm long, 5-22 cm wide, upper side glabrous or sparsely covered with sessile, furcate hairs (less than 0.1 mm long), lower side glabrous or sparsely covered with simple or sessile, furcate hairs (0.1-0.2 mm long), the marginal regions and the midrib often covered with simple hairs (to 0.5 mm long). Scape erect, 8-80 cm tall, to 6 mm thick, beset with sheaths up to 3-20 cm long and 0.8-3.5 cm wide. Inflorescence a basal, spiciform raceme 7-30 cm long and 3-6 cm wide. Indument of inflorescence: sheaths, rhachis, bracts, peduncles, bracteoles, pedicels, calyx, corolla, ovary, and capsule densely to sparsely covered with sessile, furcate (to plurifurcate) hairs (0.1-0.2 mm long) and/or with simple hairs (0.3-0.5 mm long), rarely completely glabrous. Bracts red, pink, orange-red, or yellow, rather long persistent or sometimes soon deciduous, broadly obovate to broadly ovate, obovate to ovate, or narrowly obovate to narrowly triangular, obtuse to acute, 10-50 mm long, 3-35 mm wide. Peduncles 1-2 mm long, rarely elongating to 10(-15) mm. Bracteole cup-shaped, obliquely truncate, often split on one side, 5-16(-20) mm long. Pedicels 1-3 mm long, rarely elongating to 10 mm. Calyx yellow to red, tubular, 9-23 mm long, 5-11 mm wide, the lobes deltate to shallowly triangular, 3-5 mm long, 4-10 mm wide. Corolla yellow, yellowish-orange, or orange, 19-33 mm long, the tube 6-18 mm long, the lobes 10-18 mm long, 6-14 mm wide. Labellum yellow to orange, 8-15 mm long and wide when spread out, basal part opposite the anther and middle part densely covered with simple, furcate, or plurifurcate hairs (0.2-0.5 mm long), its posterior side and the lateral staminodes less densely so, the limb erect, 4-10 mm long, 8-15 mm wide, lateral lobes involute, rounded, 3-5 mm long, 2-4 mm wide, middle lobe entire and rounded (very rarely slightly bilobulate), basal claw 4-7 mm long and wide, lateral staminodes 1-2 mm long. Anther 5-12 mm long, 3-6 mm wide, sides densely covered with the same hairs as on the labellum, back less densely so. Style 17-26 mm long. Nectarial glands multilobulate , completely surrounding the style base, 1-3 mm long. Ovary green to red, ellipsoid. Capsule (green to) red, maturing black-purple, globose to ellipsoid, 15-45 X 7-25 (-35) mm, its wall ca 1 mm thick when dry (3-7 mm in living material), 30-75-seeded, seeds 3-3.5 X 4-4.5 mm, aril yellow to red.

description: Erect, saprophytic herbs. Rhizomes cylindric, slightly tuberous, densely covered with narrowly ovate, imbricate scales. Stems unbranched. Inflorescence a terminal, contracted, bifurcate cincinnus, each cincinnus 2-9-flowered, or the plant having a solitary terminal flower only. Flowers erect, tubular, 6-7 mm long, shortly pedicellate. Floral tube measurement includes ovary. Outer tepals entire, inner tepals absent. Stamens three, inserted just below and alternating with the tepals, filaments basally decurrent into a crescent-shaped pouch, connective obtrapezi-form in outline, 0.1-0.2 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, apex acute, with a triangular, apical appendage. Style 3-branched at the apex, each branch with a peltate stigma. Ovary unilocular, with three parietal placentas and three short-stipitate, 2-lobed glands on the top of the ovary. Capsule crowned by the persistent perianth; dehiscence unknown. Seeds brown, ellipsoid to broadly ovoid.

description: Erect, saprophytic herbs. Rhizome tuberous, cylindric, apical part densely covered with stiff scale-like leaves, middle and basal part densely rooted. Stems mostly unbranched. Leaves many, more or less imbricate. Inflorescence terminal, a bifurcate cincinnus (cincinni 2-7-flowered) or the plant having a solitary terminal flower only. Flowers erect, salverform, 16-28(-36) mm long, sessile or pedicellate. Tepals 6(-8), outer ones entire, inner ones as long as the outer ones, but narrower, inserted at the same level as the outer tepals. Floral tube trigonous, narrowly 3-ribbed, ribs running from the outer tepals down to the base of the ovary. Anthers three, subsessile, inserted just below the inner tepals, connective cubical to transversely oblong, 0.2-0.4(-0.6) mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, bearing apically two and in the center one appendage; apical appendages broadly to narrowly triangular, (0.1-)0.2-0.5 mm long, 0.1-0.4 mm wide, papillate, basal appendage deltate, 0.1-0.2 mm long and wide; thecae 0.5-0.9(-1.1) mm long, 0.2-0.5 mm wide. Style 3-branched at the apex, each branch with a deeply infundibular stigma and two subglobose lateral swellings just below the funnel. Upper part of the ovary unilocular with three parietal protruding placentas, basal part trilocular with axile placentation. Septal nectaries three, situated in a longitudinal cleft in the upper part of each septum, opening at the base of the floral tube. Capsule crowned by the persistent perianth, irregularly dehiscent by withering of the membranous wall between the six ribs. Seeds brown, laterally flattened, triangular to subcircular in outline.

description: Erect, saprophytic herbs. Rhizome cylindric, slightly tuberous, densely covered with ovate-triangular, imbricate scales and filiform roots. Stems unbranched. Inflorescence a terminal cincinnus, 1-5-flowered, or the plant having a solitary terminal flower only. Flowers erect to nodding, infundibular to campanulate, 6.5-21 mm long, pedicellate. Floral tube measurement includes ovary. Tepals entire, all six inserted at the same level in the floral tube; inner ones as long as the outer ones, but somewhat narrower. Stamens three, inserted 2.2-4.8(-6.5) mm below the inner tepals, filament basally decurrent into a crescent-shaped pouch, abaxially bearing a 2-lobed wing, lobes elliptic to obovate; connective ovoid to very broadly ovoid, 0.3-0.4 mm long, 0.2-0.5 mm wide, axially bearing one basal ovoid to very broadly-ovoid swelling, 0.2-0.3 mm long, 0.2 mm wide. Style 3-branched at the apex, each branch with a funnel-shaped to sometimes horseshoe-shaped stigma. Ovary unilocular with three parietal placentas. Septal nectaries three, situated in a narrow and very short cleft in the upper part of the placenta, opening in the basal part of the floral tube. Capsule nodding, broadly ellipsoid to globose, crowned by the persistent perianth, longitudinally dehiscent by three valves separating from base to apex; after these valves and the perianth are shed, only three patent ribs are left, each bearing a placenta. Seeds brown to yellowish brown, (narrowly) ellipsoid to subglobose.

description: Erect, autotrophic or rarely saprophytic, terrestrial or rarely epiphytic herbs. Rhizome absent, roots filiform. Stems branched or not. Leaves small and scalelike, sometimes rather large especially near the base of the stem and sometimes rosulate. Inflorescence a terminal, bifurcate, lax to capitate cincinnus, or the plant having a solitary terminal flower only. Bracts sometimes imbricate. Flowers erect, rarely nodding, tubular to salverform, 2-25 mm long, sessile to shortly pedicellate. Outer tepals entire, margins often involute. Inner tepals smaller than the outer ones, sometimes incurved over the stamens, inserted at the same level as the outer ones. Floral tube cylindrical to trigonous, wingless to broadly 3-winged. Wings running from the top of the floral tube down to the apical or basal part of the ovary, sometimes continuing as a crest over the outer tepals. Anthers three, sessile, inserted just below the inner tepals; connective trapeziform to subcircular in outline (largest width above the middle), often swollen, 0.1-0.8 mm long, 0.10.5 mm wide, bearing two apical appendages and (0-)1(-2) basal one; apical appendage narrowly oblong-triangular to oblong-triangular, 0.1-0.6 mm long, 0.20.4 mm wide, often papillate; basal appendage(s) broadly oblong-triangular to oblong-triangular, 0.1-0.5 mm long and wide; thecae laterally stipitate, stipes 0.10.2 mm long; thecae 0.1-1 mm long, 0.1-0.5 mm wide. Style 3-branched at the apex, each branch with a bilabiate (to shallowly funnel-shaped) stigma, upper lip erect, club-shaped, sometimes divided into two parts, lower lip flat, thin, horizontally patent. Ovary trilocular, trigonous, with axile placentation. Septal nectaries three, sometimes present, situated in a longitudinal cleft in the upper part of each septum, opening at the base of the floral tube. Capsule crowned by the persistent perianth, transversely dehiscent by several slits in the membranous wall, or longitudinally dehiscent by three reflexed valves (see B. tenella) or irregularly dehiscent by withering of the membranous wall between the ribs. Seeds yellowish to greenish brown, (narrowly) ellipsoid, rarely narrowly fusiform (B. tenella), 0.2-1 x 0.1-0.3 mm.

description: Erect, saprophytic herbs. Rhizome cylindric, slightly tuberous, densely covered with narrowly ovate to ovate, imbricate scales and filiform roots. Stems mostly unbranched. Inflorescence a terminal, bifurcate cincinnus, each cincinnus 1-4-flowered, or the plant having a solitary, terminal flower only. Flowers erect, salverform, 6.5-10.2 mm long, shortly pedicellate. Floral tube measurement includes ovary. Outer tepals 3-lobed. Inner tepals very small, inserted in the floral tube below the insertion of the outer tepals. Anthers three, sessile, inserted in the apical part of the floral tube, connective depressed obovoid to broadly obovoid, ca. 0.2 mm long, ca. 0.4 mm wide, without appendages. Style 3-branched at the apex, each branch with a horseshoe-shaped stigma (seen from above) with two short, apical, filiform appendages. Ovary unilocular, with three parietal placentas; each septum bearing two apical globose glands, each with a secretory duct, but opening at the base of the floral tube by one common duct. Capsule ellipsoid, more or less asymmetric, due to one of the placentas being better developed than the two others, at an angle of ca. 90° with the axis of the inflorescence, crowned by the persistent part of the floral tube, the upper part of the floral tube soon caducous. Capsule longitudinally and loculicidally dehiscent by one slit in the horizontal wall between the two smallest placentas, exposing the seeds of the best developed placenta at the bottom of the boat-shaped fruit. Seeds brown, (narrowly) ellipsoid to ovoid, funicles mostly longer than the seeds.

description: Erect, saprophytic herbs. Rhizome cylindric, slightly tuberous, densely covered with narrowly ovate, imbricate, long-ciliate scales. Stems mostly unbranched. Inflorescence a terminal, bifurcate cincinnus, each cincinnus 3-16-flowered, with 1-2 bracts at the base of the inflorescence. Flowers nodding, tubular, 1.8-8.5 mm long, shortly pedicellate. Floral tube measurement includes ovary. Tepals entire, all six inserted at the same level in the floral tube, inner ones smaller than the outer ones. Anthers three, sessile, inserted in the apical part of the floral tube, connective ovoid to broadly ovoid, 0.2-0.6 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, unappendaged. Style 3-branched at the apex, each branch with a funnel-shaped stigma. Top of the ovary unilocular, with three parietal placentas; placentas protruding into the center of the ovary on the inner, separated layer of the ovary wall; base of the ovary trilocular. Septal nectaries three, situated in a furrow in the upper distal part of the placenta, opening into the cavity between the inner and outer part of the ovary wall. Capsule nodding, crowned by the persistent perianth; perianth finally deciduous; capsule longitudinally dehiscent, the three valves separating from apex to base, each bearing a parietal placenta. Seeds white, narrowly fusiform, the small ellipsoid embryo loosely surrounded by a thin transparent testa.

description: Erect, saprophytic herbs. Rhizome cylindric, slightly tuberous, densely covered with (narrowly) ovate, triangular to subulate, imbricate scales and filiform roots. Stems branched or not. Inflorescence a terminal, bifurcate, lax to capitate cincinnus, each cincinnus 1-24-flowered, or the plant having a solitary, terminal flower only. Flowers erect, rarely recurved, salverform, 3.2-15 mm long, pedicellate or sometimes sessile. Floral tube measurement includes ovary. Outer tepals mostly 3-lobed, the lateral lobes induplicate. Inner tepals very small, often somewhat swollen, inserted in the floral tube below the insertion of the outer tepals. Anthers three, sessile, inserted 0.5-1 (-1.5) mm below the inner tepals, connective broadly ovoid to broadly obovoid, 0.2-0.5 mm long, 0.1-0.6 mm wide, mostly without appendages. Style 3-branched at the apex, each branch with a horseshoe-shaped stigma (when seen from above), with or without two apical, tortuous, filiform appendages (often partly broken off). Ovary unilocular, with three parietal placentas; placentas protruding on short thick septa into the center of the ovary. Each septum laterally provided with two hollow, globose glands (0.2-0.7 mm diam.), opening at the base of the floral tube by one common duct, or, glands free from the septa, each opening by a duct of its own. Capsule erect or nodding, globose to ellipsoid, crowned by the often constricted, persistent part of the floral tube, the upper part of the floral tube soon caducous. Capsule longitudinally dehiscent either by (a) three loculicidal valves separating from apex to base, or (b) by six septicidal valves separating from base to apex, or (c) irregularly by withering of the membranous wall between the ribs. Seeds grayish-black, ellipsoid to transversely ellipsoid or fusiform, 0.2-0.9 x 0.1-0.6 mm, funicle very short.

description: Erect, saprophytic herbs. Rhizomes cylindric, slightly tuberous, densely covered with strongly recurved, filiform scales, and many, long, filiform roots. Stems mostly unbranched. Inflorescence a terminal, bifurcate cincinnus (cincinni 3-4-flowered) or the plant having a solitary terminal flower only. Flowers erect, salverform, 7.5-14 mm long, pedicellate. Outer tepals entire. Inner tepals much smaller than the outer ones, sometimes with a 3-dentate apex. Inner and outer tepals inserted at the same level in the floral tube. Floral tube cylindric to hexagonal, widened at the base, 6-ribbed to slightly 6-winged. Ribs or wings running from the widened part of the floral tube down to the ovary. Stamens three, inserted below the inner tepals, in the apical part of the floral tube, slightly exceeding it, filaments long; connective cubical to transversely oblong, 0.1-0.2 mm long, 0.1-0.2(-0.3) mm wide, bearing one apical deltate appendage 0.1-0.2(-0.3) mm long and 0.1-0.3 mm wide; thecae 0.2-0.5 mm long, 0.1-0.3 mm wide. Style as long as the stamens, 3-branched at the apex, each branch with a bilabiate stigma, upper lip deeply infundibular, lower lip flat, very small, appressed to the base of funnel. Upper part of the ovary unilocular with three 2-lobed parietal placentas, basal part trilocular; placentas protruding on long thin septa into the center of the ovary, each one only fertile in the middle part. Septal nectaries three, situated in a vertical cylindric pouch in the upper part of each septum, opening at the base of the floral tube. Capsule crowned by the persistent part of the floral tube, the upper part of the floral tube soon caducous, finally the whole perianth deciduous and only six ribs left; capsule dehiscent by withering of the membranous wall between the ribs. Seeds brown, subglobose to ovoid, funicle short.
bibliographicCitation: Maas, Paulus J. M., et al. 1986. Burmanniaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 42: 1-189.

description: Erect, saprophytic herbs. Rhizome cylindric, slightly tuberous, densely covered with roots and narrowly to broadly ovate, sometimes fimbriate, imbricate scales. Stems unbranched. Inflorescence terminal, umbelliform, 4-10(-22)-flowered, with 2-4 bracts at the base of the inflorescence. Flowers erect, tubular, 2.5-4.5 mm long, distinctly pedicellate. Floral tube measurement includes ovary. Tepals entire, inner tepals smaller, inserted at the same level in the floral tube as the outer ones. Anthers three, sessile, perpendicular or appressed to the floral tube, inserted in the apical part; connective ovoid to broadly angular-obovoid, without appendages. Style 3-branched at the apex, each branch with a funnel-shaped (to horseshoeshaped) stigma. Ovary unilocular, with three parietal placentas, and three 2-lobed glands on the top of the ovary. Capsule crowned by the persistent, finally deciduous perianth. Upper part of capsule inside the persistent perianth splitting longitudinally into three septicidal segments cohering by the persistent style (Miers 1841). Seeds brown, narrowly ellipsoid to ovoid, somewhat laterally flattened.

description: Saprophytic herbs, erect, fleshy, and hyaline. Vegetative parts of the plant of two different types: 1) a tuber bearing exogenous roots with rootcap, 1-4 longitudinally bisulcate stems and 2-4 bract-like leaves forming a rosette just below the flower, or 2) creeping, branched and cylindric roots, terete stems and scattered leaves. No scales present. Stems unbranched, endogenous. Leaves ovate. Flowers solitary, terminal, erect, 5-20 mm long. Floral tube almost cylindric to urceolate, sometimes campanulate, zygomorphic to actinomorphic (measurement includes ovary). Tepals six, entire, forming two whorls, each of different shape and size, sometimes connate into a miter, inserted at one level or at two different levels in the floral tube. Throat circular, surrounded by an annulus often ornamented by emergences, rims or lobes forming one or more rings around the throat. Stamens six, pendent, filaments short, filiform to ribbon-shaped, free, thecae separate, or united, loculi parallel, dehiscing longitudinally to the abaxial side, connectives more or less dilated, bearing 0-2 apical appendages and 0-2 basal ones, sometimes forming an anther-tube; interstaminal lobes six, triangular to linear, free, alternating with the stamens, sometimes absent. Perianth (with stamens and interstaminal lobes) circumscissile and deciduous. Style short, cylindric, 3-branched, each branch bearing a stigma, or unbranched with one capitate stigma. Ovary unilocular, with three parietal placentas or with three placental columns in the center of the ovary; funiculi long. Fruit cup-shaped, fleshy and hyaline, crowned by a rim formed by the persistent, basal part of the floral tube, and by the persistent style and stigma(s). Seeds brownish, (narrowly) ellipsoid to ovoid, 0.3-0.5 x 0.1-0.2 mm, with 10-15 darker, more or less spirally arranged, longitudinal ribs; funicle as long as or longer than the seed.
bibliographicCitation: Maas, Paulus J. M., et al. 1986. Burmanniaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 42: 1-189.

description: Herbs, 10-48 cm high. Rhizome scales narrowly ovate, 1.6-4 mm long, 0.20.8 mm wide, base rounded, apex acuminate. Stems white to purplish-white, mostly unbranched. Leaves narrowly ovate, 1.2-8.5 mm long, 0.4-2.5 mm wide, apex acute to acuminate. Inflorescence a bifurcate cincinnus, each cincinnus 3-16-flowered and 1-8 cm long. Bracts narrowly ovate, 1-3(-4) mm long, 0.3-1.1 mm wide, apex acute to acuminate. Pedicels 1-5.2 mm long. Flowers white to purplish white or pale yellow, 1.8-8.5 mm long. Floral tube 1.4-5.4 mm long, 0.7-3.6 mm diam. Outer tepals (very) broadly (angular-)ovate to narrowly ovate, 0.4-1.6 mm long, 0.5-0.6 mm wide, margins slightly involute, outer side papillate. Inner tepals broadly ovate, 0.3-1 mm long, 0.3-1(-1.2)mm wide. Anthers inserted 0.4-1.3 mm below the insertion of the inner tepals, connective 0.2-0.6 mm long, 0.2-0.3 mm wide, base truncate, apex narrowly triangular, often cut off. Style, including branches and stigmas, 0.6-3.5 mm long, branches with stigmas 0.2-0.8 mm long, stigmas funnel-shaped. Ovary obovoid, 1.1-3 mm long. Capsule broadly ellipsoid to globose, to 3.5 x 4 mm. Seeds 0.4-0.9 x 0.1-0.2 mm.

description: Shrubs or trees (very rarely lianas). Leafy twigs terete, lenticellate, densely to sparsely covered with white to ferruginous, erect to appressed, simple, sometimes furcate to stellate hairs, soon becoming glabrous in many species. Leaves distichous, simple, entire, petiolate, estipulate. Lamina most often elliptic to ovate, chartaceous, sometimes coriaceous, base acute to obtuse, apex acute to acuminate, rarely obtuse, upper side sparsely to less often densely covered with erect or appressed, frequently crisped, simple to rarely stellate hairs mainly along primary and secondary veins, commonly to 0.2-1 mm long, lower side densely to sparsely covered with erect to appressed, simple, less frequently furcate to stellate, straight to less frequently (in erect hairs) crisped, white to brown hairs commonly to 0.2-1.5 mm long; primary vein impressed above; secondary veins curved to straight, between 5-35 on either side of the primary vein, angles with primary vein generally (30-)40-70(-80)°, flat to slightly raised above, loop-forming mostly under the apex only, occasionally in the apical fourth to apical half, rarely not forming loops, the distance between loops and margin 0-3(-4) mm; tertiary veins percurrent to reticulate, prominulous to flat above; domatia occasionally present in axils between primary vein and secondary veins, as little, mostly inconspicuous pockets. Inflorescences mostly supra-axillary or leaf-opposed, occasionally sub-axillary, rarely terminal rhipidia or (in occasional floriferous specimens) pleiothyrses of 2-3 rhipidia, the rhipidia 1-4-flowered, or sometimes producing more flowers on sympodially elongating rachis. Inflorescences in foliate zone, in some species frequently at or near the base of freshly grown lateral branchlets. Indument of inflorescences (including fruits) consisting of simple, occasionally furcate to stellate hairs to l(-2) mm long; peduncles, pedicels, outer side of bracts and sepals, and outer petals densely to sparsely covered, sometimes becoming glabrous; fruit the same, but often becoming glabrous. Peduncles generally very short, rarely reaching 5 mm in length, or absent. Pedicels short, stout, to rather long and slender, with basal articulation. Bracts normally two per pedicel, the lower bract below the articulation, the upper bract above the articulation, inserted near the base to halfway up (or beyond) on the pedicel. The bracts generally small, caducous or persistent. Flowers actinomorphic, bisexual, mostly colored green, yellow, or white, rarely red in vivo. Perianth not opening widely, trimerous, with one whorl of sepals and two whorls of connate petals, the corolla tube enclosing stamens and carpels. Sepals valvate, triangular to ovate, to broadly or shallowly so, free or sometimes connate, much shorter than the petals, herbaceous, mostly appressed, persistent until after anthesis. In various species the sepals are keeled to gibbous on the dorsal side. Corolla tube globose, dark red within in vivo. Petals fleshy, valvate. Outer petals with wing-like appendage on the dorsal side, the wings generally ovate-oblong to ovate-elliptic, (mostly) ascending when young to horizontal, rarely recurved when mature, mostly strongly flattened on the sides, occasionally rather thick and humplike. Free part of the inner petals often largely hidden by the outer petals, triangular, deltate to cordate. Torus depressed ovoid to triangular-oblongoid, glabrous or hairy. Stamens oo, in spiral, free, with very short filament, anther four-celled, extrorse, connective with discoid, small apical prolongation. Carpels mostly 8, in spiral, free, glabrous or hairy, one-celled with one basal ovule, stigma sessile, ellipsoid, oblongoid or obdeltoid. Fruit syncarpous, apocarpous or partly so in few species, globose to ellipsoid, green to yellow, rarely orange or red in vivo, fleshy when mature, composed of few to ca. 300 carpels, the wall 0.2-6 mm thick, areoles (pentagonal or) hexagonal or indistinctly marked, flat to protruding, then pyramidal, pulvinate or merely mucronate, or free part of carpels (in ± apocarpous species) ellipsoid or oblongoid. Seeds often large, ellipsoid, glabrous, sometimes provided with a rudimentary aril. Chromosome numbers: 2 n = 14, 28, 42, or 56.
bibliographicCitation: Maas, Paulus J. M., et al. 1992. Rollinia. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 57: 1-188.

description: Trees or shrubs. Leafy twigs terete, covered in varying degree with stellate hairs, scales, or both, often becoming glabrous with age. Lenticels wanting or more often scarce to numerous, usually small, but larger in few species, usually round and solitary (or rarely in vertical lines). Leaves distichous, simple, entire, shortly petiolate, estipulate. Lamina mostly medium-sized, generally elliptic to ovate, leaf index (length/width ratio) varying from 1.3-6, chartaceous or coriaceous, symmetric, or in few species asymmetric and slightly falcate, base acute, attenuate, or rounded, rarely cordate or very rarely amplexicaul, sometimes oblique, apex acuminate to acute, or rarely rounded or emarginate, glabrous or sparsely hairy above, covered in varying degree with stellate hairs and/or scales below, venation brochidodromous, primary vein impressed above (very rarely flat), secondary veins curved, sometimes straight, rarely recurved, 4-23 on either side of primary vein, forming indistinct to distinct loops, or rarely a marginal vein, intersecondary veins present, distinct or indistinct, or absent, tertiary veins reticulate or percurrent. Inflorescences mostly among leaves, or also on leafless branches, leaf-opposed, supra-axillary, sub-axillary, or rarely terminal, consisting of a single rhipidium, or also aggregates of 2-several rhipidia, or rhipidia branched, rarely plant cauliflorous or flagelliflorous. Rhipidia generally 1-3-flowered, but often continuing to develop a few more to occasionally quite numerous successive flowers on an elongating sympodial rachis. The inflorescence, including the outer side of bracts, sepals, and petals covered in varying degree with stellate hairs or scales, the inner side of sepals and petals often predominantly covered with stellate hairs. Peduncle generally short. Pedicels short to rather long and slender, with basal articulation, bibracteate. Lower bract below the articulation, the upper bract mostly in the lower part of the pedicel or about halfway, amplectent, often caducous. Flowers actinomorphic, bisexual, perianth with three trimerous whorls, exceptionally in spiral. Flower buds ovoid to broadly ovoid, apex acute to obtuse, sometimes prominently ribbed by the reduplicate-valvate sepals. Sepals three (very rarely four), valvate or reduplicate-valvate, free to connate in various degrees, sometimes with distinct and prominent venation, much smaller than the petals. Petals six (or exceptionally more), free, green, cream, white to red in vivo, the inner ones often reddish at the inner base, imbricate (very rarely valvate), both whorls mostly subequal, fleshy, veins usually not prominent, inner base of inner petals often callose or grooved. Torus depressed ovoid with a concave apex. Stamens indefinite in number, many, spirally arranged, often entirely red in vivo, filament very short, anthers extrorse to latrorse, apex of connective discoid, rarely umbonate, rarely strongly reduced, glabrous, papillose, or sometimes densely-covered with simple to stellate hairs. Carpels indefinite in number, few to mostly many, spirally arranged, free, ovary hairy to glabrous, one-celled with one basal ovule, stigma usually elongate, glabrous to hairy. Fruit apocarpous with tightly-appressed carpels or less often pseudosyncarpous (aggregate), globose, sometimes broadly ellipsoid to broadly ovoid, 1-15 cm in diam., (white), green, yellow, brown, orange, to red in vivo, rarely with a glaucous cover, wall 0.3-1.5 mm thick, woody-like when dry, pulp fleshy, composed of 5-600, sessile, free to rarely far-connate carpels, carpels at the base generally sterile, often connate into a collar, the collar protruding or not, fruit covered in varying degree with stellate hairs or scales, sometimes glabrous, fruiting receptacle ellipsoid to obovoid or narrowly so, areoles often pyramidal, smooth to grooved, often distinctly 5-6-ribbed, apex obtuse to acute, rarely rounded, often distinctly apiculate. Seed one per carpel, obovoid to ellipsoid, rarely globose, glabrous, apex obtuse to rounded, rarely acute to apiculate, with mostly distinct raphe, pale to dark brown, often shiny, rudimentary aril often present. Chromosome numbers: 2n = 16, 24, 32, 48.

description: Shrub or subshrub, 1-3.5 m, with grayish brown fissured bark near base, young branches quadrangular, sometimes winged, with grayish tomentum. Leaves subsessile or with petiole to 1 cm long or connateperfoliate, stipules reduced to a line, blades ovate or oblong-lanceolate, 5-20(-28) x 3—8(—11) cm, mem-brancaceous, above tomentulose to glabrescent, below white tomentose; apex acute or acuminate, base acute, auriculate or perfoliate, margin serrate to crenulate. Inflorescence 10-30 cm long, essentially unbranched, with 4-15(-20) pairs of axillary cymes, basal pairs occasionally pedunculate, the upper pairs often borne close together and often appearing spi-cate, each pair of cymes in the axil of progressively smaller leaves. Each cyme with 9-12 sessile flowers. Calyx tubular, tomentose, tube 3-3.5 mm long, lobes acuminate, 2-2.5 mm long. Corolla greenish-yellow, yellow or light orange, tubular, tomentose outside, inside with warty hairs throughout except in region of ovary, tube 5-7 mm long, lobes erect, elliptic to ovate, 1.8-2.5 x 1-1.8 mm. Stamens sessile, inserted close to sinus, anthers 1-1.5 mm long. Ovary ellipsoid 2.5-3.5 mm long, tomentose on upper half, style 4-5.5 mm long, stigma globose, 0.5 mm long. Capsule ellipsoid 4.5-6 x 2.5-3 mm, tomentulose near apex, pericarp thin, opening only septicidally, valves not separating, rounded. Seeds type 6, oblong, truncate at apex, 0.6-0.7 mm x 0.25-0.3 mm long, lighter in color at funicular end, seed body 0.5-0.6 mm long. 2n = 38.

description: Erect or ascending shrub, 0.5-3 m tall, the stems up to 3 cm diam. below, distally quadrangular, glabrous, ± purplish. Leaves with blades ovate to elliptic, glabrous, the margins entire or shallowly serrate. Inflorescence glabrous, composed of 1 or 2 pairs of subumbellate 8-24-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 2.7-10 cm, the pedicels 1.4-5.7 cm; cyme bracts absent. Sepals ovate, bright yellow, lemon-yellow, or bright greenish-yellow, subequal (the lateral ones slightly wider), acute, 9.5-12 x 5.5-8.7 mm at anthesis, glabrous, glutinous. Corolla bright yellow (rarely white), type I (but with the upper lip not appressed against the sac of the lower one); upper lip 4-8 x 6-12 mm; lower lip 16-32 x 12-25 mm, saccate in 60-70% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 9; anthers pale buff to yellowish-white, 6-7.2 mm, dehiscing to connective or somewhat less, the connective raised, acute, the thecae ± arcuate, subequal or unequal; filaments 1.2-2.6 mm. Style arcuate, 4.5-7.2 mm. Capsule ovoid, yellow-brown, 6-9 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Erect shrub (0.3-)1-2 m high, in thickets sometimes scandent with the stems 5-8 m long; stems and inflorescence glabrous, glutinous, purple. Leaves with blades lanceolate, acute or (usually) acuminate, cuneate or rounded at base, glabrous, the margins evenly sharp-serrate or serrulate with mucronulate teeth; upper surface deep green, smooth, strongly glutinous and nitidous; lower surface pale green, reticulate-venose; petioles glabrous. Sepals subequal, lanceolate or ovate, 8.6-14 mm long, externally glabrous, internally with a shortly tomentose or strigose border along the margins. Corolla type I, bright yellow, the throat deep yellow inside, unspotted; upper lip triangular; lower lip saccate in 60-80% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers light huffish, glabrous, dehiscing throughout but somewhat constricted at the connective and with a raised septum, the thecae subequal, boatshaped, slightly arcuate, divaricate or slightly ascending. Style straight, decurved at apex. Capsule ovoid, brownish-purple, 7-10 mm long, minutely glandular.

description: Erect or ascending herb, 5-50 cm tall (rarely up to 1.2 m), the stems succulent, light green to purplish. Leaves petiolate; blades ovate to lanceolate in inclusive outline, pinnatisect (dissected to the midrib into ± remote lateral pinnae), the lateral pinnae divaricate or deflexed; petioles 0.6-4.4 cm, narrowly winged and 2-5 mm wide, connate across the nodes with wings less than 2 mm wide. Inflorescence of vigorous specimens with primary peduncles 3.7-13 cm long. Sepals pale green, ovate, ± acuminate, externally pilose, internally glandular-puberulous, the margins entire or (rarely) somewhat denticulate. Corolla type IX. Stamens with anthers orange, the thecae unequal, both fertile, the anterior one much smaller, stipitate, the connective elongated and with a short dorsal tooth at the base of the posterior theca (the tooth hardly visible in many specimens). Style arcuate or curved. Capsule ovoid, acuminate, truncate at apex, glandular-pilose or sparsely glandular-villous, whitish-green, often suffused with purple. 2n = 26.

description: Ascending or scandent herb, 0.3-2 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems white-villous with glandless hairs. Leaves decussate; blades herbaceous, ovate, 1.6-4.2 x 1.1-3 cm, acute, cordate at base, the margins bluntly serrate or bicrenate; upper surface deep green, pilose or sparsely villous, slightly rugose; lower surface paler green, reticulate-venose, completely villous when young, in older leaves with the major veins pilose or villous and the interspaces pilose or subglabrous; petioles villous, 3-21 mm. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 4-12-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.9-7 cm, the pedicels 0.8-3 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals ovate or lanceolate, green or greenish-yellow, acute, externally finely tomentose with eglandular hairs, internally glabrous and conspicuously veined. Corolla type XV, bright yellow to lemon yellow, unspotted; upper lip ± triangular; lower lip pendent, somewhat concave, saccate only in 20-40% of length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 2; anthers dark brown, glabrous, the thecae elliptic or subglobose, equal; filaments 1.2-3 mm. Style straight or somewhat arcuate, 5.2-8.3 mm long. Capsule ovoid, 4-6 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Subshrub, 0.1-1.5 m tall; inflorescence and stem white-pubescent, the internodes short. Leaves decussate; blades mostly ovate, obtuse or subacute, rounded to cordate at base, the margins serrate with rounded teeth; petioles 1-6 mm, tomentose to lanate. Inflorescence composed of 24 pairs of cymes; peduncles 1.4-4.6 cm; pedicels 0.5-1.7 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals pale green to light lemon yellow, unequal, ovate or (the dorsal sepal) broadly ovate, subacute to slightly acuminate, externally puberulous to short-villous, internally glabrous or puberulous, the margins ciliate. Corolla type IX; upper lip 2-3 mm long, 5-8 mm wide, 7-10 mm high; lower lip saccate in 45-60% of length, its upcurved portion 12-19(-25) x 8-15(-18) mm. Stamens with anthers 1.8-3.1 mm, yellow-brown to dark brown, the thecae divaricate; filaments 0.8-1.8 mm. Style 1.2-2.2 mm long. Capsule 5-8 mm long, pale to reddish brown. 2n = 36.

description: Ascending or semi-scandent shrub, 0.5-3 m tall, the whole plant strongly glutinous, much branched, stems and inflorescence glabrous. Leaves with blades glabrous, ovate or lanceolate, acute, rounded or truncate at base (rarely cuneate), the margins serrate and ± deflexed or revolute; petioles dorsally pubescent. Inflorescence composed of 1-3 (mostly 2) pairs of 4-16-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.5-9 cm, the pedicels 0.6-3 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals ovate, light green to yellow-green, acute, mucronate, 4.4-6.2(-7.2) x (2.5-)3.0-4.7 mm at anthesis, externally glabrous, internally with a short-tomentose border along the margins. Corolla type IV, bright yellow; upper lip flattened, circular, 8-15 mm high and 10-17 mm wide, lower lip saccate in 30-40% of length, the upcurved portion 13-17 x 10-16 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers buff to pale yellow-brown, 2.3-3.4 mm, the thecae equal; filaments 1-1.5 mm. Style curved, 2-3(-4.1) mm. Capsule conical, brown, 5-6 mm long, glabrous. 2n = 36.

description: Decumbent or ascending herb, 0.1-0.6(-1) m tall. Leaves petiolate or sessile; blades usually deeply pinnatifid-lobed, dissected to % of their width (but never completely dissected to the midrib) with one or two pairs of lingulate lateral lobes, sometimes entire or subentire. Inflorescence with primary peduncles 2.5-15 cm, pedicels 1.3-2.2 cm. Sepals green, ovate or lanceolate, 2.3-5.9 x 1.2-3.8 mm, acute, the margins dentate. Corolla type XI, bright or (usually) deep yellow, unspotted; upper lip 1.5-3 x 2-4 mm; lower lip 5-14 x 3-10 mm, saccate in 85-90% of length, distally shallowly 3-lobed, dorsally with a horseshoe-shaped ridge surrounding the orifice, the throat glabrous; elaiophore small or absent. Stamens with anthers 1.6-4 mm long; thecae subequal, whitish, both fertile, both stalked, 0.41 mm long; connective elongated into two yellow to brown, divaricate, subequal connective arms 0.3-1.5 mm long; filaments 0.3-0.7 mm. Style straight or somewhat curved at apex, 0.7-1.4 mm. Capsule whitish-green, subglobose, 4-7 mm long, often wider than long, glandular-pilose.

description: Plant low, shrubby, subshrub, or vine. Leaves decussate, short-petiolate; blades ovate to elliptic, deep green above, pale green below, pinnate-venose; petioles 2-6 mm, villous to hispid. Inflorescence composed of 1-3 pairs of cymes; cyme bracts present. Sepals bright to light green, externally often ± suffused with purple, acute, 3.2-5.2(-7.2) x 1.7-3.8(-4.3) mm at anthesis, externally glandular-puberulous and hispid to hirsute with glandular hairs, internally glabrous, the margins entire. Corolla type XI, light yellow to bright yellow (occasionally white), with a 3-4 mm high wine-red crossband in the throat, sometimes also with some red dots dorsally on the lower lip just below the orifice; upper lip 2-4 x 3-6 mm; lower lip saccate in 70-80% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 9; anthers yellowish-white to buff, the thecae unequal, divaricate or slightly ascending, dehiscing distally in about 80% of their length; filaments 0.4-1.3 mm. Style curved. Capsule ovoid or conical, ± acuminate, 5-7 mm long, brownish or purplish, shortly glandular-hirsute. 2n = 36.

description: Shrub with short internodes, much branched, 0.5-1.5 m tall; inflorescence and distal parts of stems densely hirsute to velutinous with coarse, glandular, huffish to brownish hairs. Leaves somewhat fasciculate; blades subcoriaceous, ovate to lanceolate or oblanceolate, obtuse or subacute and ± hamate at apex, cuneate at base, the margins revolute; upper surface olive to deep green, flexuose, densely puberulous or short-hirsute with glandular hairs; lower surface pale olivaceous, hyphodromous to almost pinnate-venose, the major veins raised, glandular-hirsute, interspaces glandular-pilose; petioles barbate with long glandular hairs. Inflorescence composed of 1-2(-3) pairs of (2-)8-16-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1-4.1 cm, the pedicels 0.7-2.8 cm. Sepals ovate, light green to pale brownish-green, 2.8-6.2 x 1.7-4 mm at anthesis, acute, externally puberulous to hirsute with glandular hairs, internally glandular-puberulous. Corolla type III (sometimes approaching type IX), light or pale yellow; upper lip 1-3 x 3-6 mm; lower lip 8-16(-19) x 5-12(-15) mm, saccate in 50-60% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers pale buff, glabrous, 1.5-2.6 mm, dehiscing throughout, the thecae equal, divaricate or slightly deflexed; filaments (0.7-)1.2-1.8 mm. Style 1.5-2.3 mm, somewhat decurved distally. Capsule ovoid, 4-7 mm, brownish, glandular-puberulous.

description: Low shrubby plant, usually tufted, 0.1-1 m tall, the stems erect or ascending, brittle; inflorescence and distal parts of stems purplish and shortly glandular-villous or -hirsute with whitish hairs of different length, rarely almost lanate. Leaves decussate, fasciculate; blades subcoriaceous, ± aceriform, ovate in inclusive outline, 3-15(-32) x 2-12(-29) mm, obtuse to acute at apex, truncate or slightly cordate at base, 3-9-lobate or deeply crenate, the margins deflexed or revolute; upper surface bright green to grayish, puberulous to hirsute with often glandular hairs, somewhat flexuose; lower surface pale green, pinnate-venose, hirsute to villous with glandular or eglandular hairs; petioles 1-4(-8) mm, conspicuously white-barbate. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of (1-)4-8-flowered cymes on primary peduncles 0.5-2.6 cm long; pedicels 0.4-1.2 cm; cyme bracts present (small, lanceolate) or absent. Sepals green, triangular to ovate, 2.5-4.4 x 1.5-2.7 mm at anthesis, acute, glandular-puberulous to glandular-hirsute on both sides. Corolla type VIII or IX, unspotted; upper lip 23 x 3-5 mm; lower lip saccate in 50-70% of length, its ± upcurved portion 8-14 x 6-10 mm. Stamens with anthers yellow or pale buff, 1.6-2.4 mm, the thecae divaricate or slightly deflexed, somewhat arcuate; filaments 0.9-1.8 mm. Style 1.4-2.2 mm long. Capsule ovoid or conic, 4-8 mm long, ± acuminate, pale brown to purplish, glandular-puberulous or glandular-hirsute.

description: Erect, ascending, or prostrate herb (rosulate in subsp, acaulis). Leaves with blades herbaceous, ovate to circular, the margins shallowly to deeply lobate with 3-9 lobes on each side of blade; upper surface olive to deep green, pilose or (usually) hispid with coarse white hairs, ± flexuose; lower surface pale green or whitish-green, pinnate-venose (sometimes almost palmate-venose), the major veins often purplish, pilose to hispid, the interspaces glabrous to villous. Inflorescence composed of 1-2 pairs of (1-)8-32-flowered cymes, often with only a single cyme of the terminal pair developed; primary peduncles 5.2-30 cm; pedicels 1.1-7 cm. Sepals ovate, green, 4.6-8.5  x 2.7-5.8 mm at anthesis, acute, externally hirsute or hispid, internally subglabrous to sparsely glandular-villous, the margins ciliate, entire or denticulate. Corolla type III, pale yellow to bright yellow, the throat internally usually with red or maroon dots in the sides; upper lip 3-5 x 4-7 mm; lower lip saccate in 50-60% of length, the upeurved portion 13-23 x 10-18 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers glabrous, dehiscing throughout, the thecae subequal, divaricate or slightly ascending. Style curved. Capsule ovoid, pilose or hirsute with glandular hairs, ± purplish.

description: Ascending, scrambling, or semi-scandent subshrub with long (10-20 cm) internodes, the branches ± divaricate; inflorescence and distal parts of stems villous or hirsute with white hairs, at least some of which are gland-tipped; older stems reddish-brown to purplish. Leaves decussate; blades herbaceous, ovate; upper surface bright to dark green, ± nitidous, short-pilose, flexuose or somewhat rugose; lower surface whitish or whitish-green, pinnate-venose, the major veins pilose or villous with white hairs, interspaces brownish gland-dotted and pilose to lanate with white hairs; petioles 3-15 mm, villous, dilated at base. Sepals ovate, acuminate, externally puberulous or short-villous, internally puberulous distally and towards the margins, otherwise glabrous, the margins densely short-ciliate. Corolla type IV; upper lip 3-6 mm long, 7-13 mm wide, and 6-10 mm high; lower lip saccate in 50-60% of length, the upcurved portion 12-18 x 9-16 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens type 5 or 7 (the thecae ± flaring); anthers yellow-brown to medium brown or grayish-brown, glabrous, the thecae deflexed, each one 1.6-2.6 mm long; filaments 1.3-2.8 mm. Style slightly curved to almost straight, 1.7-3.2 mm. Capsule ovoid, 6-10 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Erect or ascending shrub or subshrub; stems reddish-brown; inflorescence and distal parts of stems finely short-tomentose (sometimes puberulous in Bolivian material) with white or buffish-white, ascending hairs, and beset with sessile orange-yellow glands. Leaves with blades herbaceous or subcoriaceous, lanceolate (rarely ovate or narrowly elliptic), acute, cuneate or rounded at base, the margins denticulate or serrulate, often seemingly entire, revolute or deflexed; petioles 1-6 mm, tomentose. Sepals somewhat unequal, externally puberulous and glandular, internally puberulous or subglabrous and with a yellow, short-tomentose border along the margins, the margins entire. Corolla type II, the lower lip saccate in 30-40% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers yellowish-white to light buff, dehiscing throughout but with a raised septum, brownish-glandular at base, otherwise glabrous, the thecae subequal, slightly arcuate. Style straight, 2-3.2 mm, laterally flattened, decurved at apex. Capsule ovoid, brownish-yellow to purplish, 5-8 mm long, glandular.

description: Erect or ascending (sometimes scrambling) shrub, 0.4-2 m tall. Leaves with blades lanceolate, 4-9.5 (-11) x 1.1-2.8 cm, narrowly acute, the margins ± deflexed; upper surface dark green, tomentose on the proximal part of the midrib, otherwise glabrous, nitidous, flexuose; lower surface light green, reticulate-venose, glabrous; petioles canaliculate, dorsally pilose. Inflorescence composed of 2 or 3(-4) pairs of 8-16-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 1.5-6 cm, the pedicels 0.8-2 cm; cyme bracts absent, at least in uppermost cymes. Sepals green, triangular, acute, 2.7-4.2 x 1.8-3.3 mm at anthesis, externally glabrous or glandular-papillose, internally glabrous, the margins short-strigose. Corolla type IV; upper lip flattened, circular, 7-12 mm high and 9-13 mm wide; lower lip upcurved, saccate in 40-50% of length, the upcurved portion 13-21 x 9-16 mm; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1; anthers buff to medium brown, glabrous, 2-2.8 mm, the thecae equal; filaments 0.9-1.6 mm. Style 1.5-2.1 mm, slightly arcuate. Capsule ovoid, brownish, 4-6 mm long, glabrous, glutinous.

description: Low shrub, much branched, 0.2-1.2 m tall, the stems erect or ascending. Leaves decussate, ± fasciculate; blades subcoriaceous, obtuse or subacute at apex, cuneate at base, the margins serrate or deeply crenate with three or four teeth on each side of leaf, entire in the proximal third; petioles 2-4 mm, swollen at base, tomentose or hirsute. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 1-4-flowered cymes, the peduncles 0.5-1.4 cm, the pedicels 0.4-1.2 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals pale green, (3-)3.8-7 x 2.4-4.9 mm at anthesis, acute or acuminate, externally short-tomentose to villous, internally puberulous, at least toward the margins. Corolla type VIII, whitish-yellow to bright lemon yellow, the throat internally white with a pale yellow area in the middle, usually unspotted, rarely with a few tiny red dots; upper lip 2-3 x 4-6 mm; lower lip saccate in 30-40% of length, the upcurved portion 10-16 x 6-12 mm, externally sulphur yellow on top. Stamens with anthers yellow or light brown, 1.8-2.6 mm, the thecae divaricate; filaments 1-1.3 mm. Style 1.3-2.4 mm long. Capsule ovoid, 5-7 mm long, ± acuminate, glandular-puberulous, often purplish tinged.

description: Erect or ascending subshrub. Leaves decussate, petiolate; blades herbaceous, obtuse or acute, the upper surface flexuose, densely pubescent, the lower surface pinnate-venose, villous or lanate with huffish hairs ± concealing the veins; petioles 3-15 mm, densely sericeous. Inflorescence composed of two or three pairs of 4-16-flowered cymes; primary peduncles 0.5-9.3 cm; pedicels 0.7-2.0 cm. Sepals ovate or elliptic, obtuse to acute or slightly acuminate, 4-7 x 2.8-5.5 mm at anthesis, externally sericeous or lanate, internally pale green, glabrous except for a tomentose border along the margins. Corolla type VIII, pale sulphur yellow to bright yellow, internally with purple spots in the throat, often confluent to a blotch or one or several crossbands; upcurved portion of the lower lip 8-15 x 6-11 mm. Stamens with anthers yellow-brown to dark brown, 1.7-2.9 mm, the thecae divaricate or slightly deflexed. Style 1.5-2.5 mm long. Capsule ovoid, slightly acuminate, 4-6 mm long, glandular-papillose.

description: Vine, climbing 1-5 m high, the branches divaricate; inflorescence and distal parts of stems purplish-tomentose. Leaves with blades herbaceous, ovate, lanceolate, or narrowly elliptic, acute, cuneate or rounded at base, yellowish-glandular on both sides (sometimes covered by pubescence), deep green above, rugose, pale green below, reticulate-venose, the margins crenate or bluntly serrate; petioles 1-8 mm, villous. Inflorescence distal, ± pendent, composed of 2-6 pairs of cymes, the peduncles 0.8-5 cm, the pedicels 1.1-3.1 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals greenish-yellow to yellow-green, subequal, lanceolate to ovate, acute or subacute, externally glandular-puberulous to tomentose, internally glabrous except for the tomentose border along the margins. Corolla type V, above bright yellow to sulphur yellow (rarely orange yellow), below light yellow, unspotted; lower lip saccate in 50-60(-70)% of length; elaiophore present. Stamens type 1 or 2, the anthers dark brown, glabrous, the thecae equal, divaricate. Style 1.5-3.5 mm, yellow, ± arcuate. Capsule widely ovoid, yellowish, 3-6 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Ascending herb or subshrub, 0.5-1.2 m tall, inflorescence and distal parts of stems incanous or white-puberulous. Leaves decussate; blades herbaceous, ovate, 3.5-4.7 x 1.6-2.4 cm, acute or subacute, cordate to rounded at base, the margins serrate or biserrate; upper surface dull green to dark green, pubescent, rugose; lower surface whitish-green, incanous or short-villous; petioles 3-8 mm, white-tomentose. Inflorescence composed of one or two pairs of 8-36-flowered cymes, the primary peduncles 3.6-10 cm, the pedicels 1.2-3.2 cm; cyme bracts present. Sepals ovate, light green to olivaceous. Corolla bright yellow or cadmium yellow, unspotted, type XV; upper lip 3-4 x 4-7 mm; lower lip 10-16 x 8-11 mm; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 2; anthers glandular-puberulous or glandular-papillose, brown, the thecae subglobose, ± divaricate; filaments 1.3-2 mm. Style 6.3-7.6 mm long, straight or arcuate, the stigma capitate. Capsule ovoid, 4-6 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Erect ascending, or scandent herb', stems and inflorescence pilose to villous with white glandless hairs mixed with short glandular hairs. Leaves with blades ovate or ovate-triangular, acute at apex, truncate to cordate at base, the margins biserrate and ± lobulate; upper surface bright green, pilose; lower surface pale green, the veins pilose or hispid, interspaces glabrous; petioles with the margins entire (rarely sparsely dentate) and almost parallel (i.e., not tapering towards the distal end), widened only just around the stem. Sepals pale green, puberulous or pilose on both sides, the margins ciliate, entire or denticulate. Corolla type XV, yellow, unspotted, the lower lip saccate in 50-75% of length; elaiophore absent. Stamens type 11; anthers grayish-brown, glabrous, dehiscing distally, the thecae subequal; filaments 1-1.4 mm. Style 4-5 mm, somewhat decurved at apex, otherwise straight. Capsule ovoid or conic, 6-7 mm long, glandular-puberulous.

description: Medium to large trees. Leaves in apical whorls of 7-40 usually with hirsute mass in axils of secondary veins. Inflorescence cauliflorous or rarely ramiflorous on oldest branches, racemose or paniculate arrangements of racemes, growing continuously from apex, pendulous, up to 3 m long, with flowers at apex of rachises only, rarely with a few leaf clusters borne on flowering rachises. Flowers zygomorphic; sepals six, well developed, with rounded lobes; petals six, oblong and curved; androecial hood flat, the stamens extending from staminal ring to apex of hood in C. nicaraguarensis, restricted to apex of hood in C. guianensis and C. subsessilis, the hood pollen of C. guianensis physiologically and morphologically different from that of staminal ring, the apex of hood V-shaped in C. subsessilis; style very short, with 6-partite stigma; ovary 6-locular, the ovules attached to bilamellar placentae running length of locule. Fruit round or nearly round when mature, indehiscent, falling from tree at maturity, the exocarp woody, 5-10 mm thick, the mesocarp fleshy, disintegrated in dried specimens, the endocarp woody, 2-5 mm thick, harder than exocarp, the interior filled with pulp which oxidizes bluish-green when exposed to air, becoming hard and sponge-like or fibrous with age and drying, the dry pulp breaks into six crescent-shaped segments. Seeds ovate, numerous, embedded in pulp, with funicle 10-15 mm long, the testa hirsute to slightly hairy, the cotyledons foliaceous. X = 17.

description: Medium to very large trees. Leaves entire to crenulate, glabrous or with simple or stellate pubescence. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose or paniculate arrangement or racemes. Flowers 2-3.5 cm diam., appearing with or without leaves; hypanthium campanulate; Calyx-lobes six; petals six, oblong to oblong-spathulate; androecium markedly asymmetrical, extending unilaterally into large sterile hood which is spirally coiled inwards, the apical part abruptly folded back over hood to form a second hood which is either thick-fleshy, smooth to transversely  plaited, or not thickened but covered with numerous slender sterile appendages, in both types there are often a few clavate sterile appendages at the apex of the inner spiral (Fig. 50); stamens 10-75, arranged in one to many rows around staminal ring, with short thin filaments, sometimes fertile stamens extending slightly up ligule; ovary 3-locular, with numerous ovules in each loculus; the style very short. Fruits cylindrical to campanulate, woody or thin and coriaceous, always longer than broad; operculum tack-shaped, readily dehiscent from base of Pyxidium, the columella triangular, detaching from base of Pyxidium. Seeds alate, surrounded by more or less symmetrical wings; embryo with foliaceous cotyledons.

description: Large trees. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, spikes or paniculate arrangements of spikes. Flowers zygomorphic; calyx lobes two large and oblong, navicular, the apex often obscurely 3-den-tate; petals six; androecium zygomorphic, the appendages of the hood swept inwards but not forming a coil, antherless; style usually long and geniculate, rarely shorter than stamens; ovary (3-)4(-6) locular. Fruit round or almost round, falling from tree with seeds intact at maturity, with an inconspicuous calycine ring at flattened apex forming circle 3.5-4.5 cm diam., the exocarp crustaceous, the mesocarp cracking when dry, ca. 5 mm thick, easily detaching from endocarp, the endocarp very hard and woody, to 5 mm thick, the exterior with much channeled and pitted surface, the operculum very small, less than 1.5 diam., falling into fruit at dehiscence. Seeds 10-25, triangular in cross section, the testa very hard and woody, without funicle, the embryo undifferentiated, the cotyledons present only as two inconspicuous scales. X = 17.

description: Canopy trees, to 30 m tall. Twigs 2.5-4 mm diam., with horizontally oriented cracks. Bark brown, with deep vertical fissures. Leaf blades elliptic, 4-16 x 2-9 cm, glabrous, coriaceous, with 12-18 pairs of lateral veins; apex acuminate; base obtuse to rounded; margins undulate, minutely crenulate; petiole 7-19 mm long. Inflorescences terminal or in axils of uppermost leaves, with two orders of branching, 15-26 x 10-25 cm, all rachises ferrugineous, with horizontally oriented squamulae; pedicel subsessile, jointed, the lower part persisting as knob 1 mm or less long after flowers fall. Flowers ca. 2.5 cm diam.; calyx of six broadly ovate or triangular lobes, 1.5-3.5 x 1.5-3 mm, not imbricate at bases, rounded or acute at apices; petals six, ovate to suborbiculate, 5-13 x 4-8 mm, yellow or green in central Amazonia or red in French Guiana and eastern Amazonia; hood of androecium flat, only slightly expanded dorsiventrally, white to yellow, 11-12 x 10 mm, the appendages well developed, with yellow anthers; staminal ring with 50-70 stamens, the filaments 1-2.5 mm long, the anthers 0.3-0.5 mm long; hypanthium glabrous, black, truncate at base; ovary 2(-5)-locular, each locule with 4-7 ovules attached at base, the summit umbonate, ca. 1 mm high, the style not differentiated. Fruits campanulate, 8-12 x 8-11.5 cm, the pericarp 18-28 mm in diam. Seeds elongate, to 50 x 20 mm, light to dark reddish-brown, verrucose.

description: Canopy or infrequently understory, trees. Bark with or without vertical fissures. Leaves medium-sized, 8-30 x 4-11 cm, never densely congested at branch ends. Inflorescences terminal or in axils of uppermost leaves, simple racemes or paniculate arrangements of racemes with 2 to 3 orders of branching. Flowers zygomorphic, 2-4 cm diam.; calyx of six lobes, these without mucilage-bearing ducts; petals six; hood of androecium flat, slightly or markedly dorsiventrally expanded, the appendages mostly fused or free, with or without anthers; staminal ring with 40-230 stamens, the anthers 0.3-0.5 mm long, dehiscing via lateral slits; ovary 2-5-locular, each locule with 4-26 ovules attached to floor of locule or lower part of septum, the summit umbonate or truncate, the style well differentiated or not differentiated from summit, when differentiated 1.8- 5 mm long. Fruits woody, dehiscent, campanulate, cylindric or turbinate, 2.5-15 x 2.5-10 cm. Seeds elongate, with basal aril. X = 17.
