description: Dioecious shrub or small tree, rarely up to 6.0 m tall. Branchlets stoutish, ca 4.0 mm diam, rather densely and shortly pubescent at tips, glabrescent below. Leaves oblong, apex acuminate for ca 2.0 cm, subacute, base attenuate, very base truncate-obtuse, (sub)coriaceous, impunctate, glabrous on both faces except some substrigose hairs on midrib and lateral nerves beneath, subserrate-dentate to -denticulate (1.0 mm), 12.0-24.0 cm long, 5.0-9.0 cm broad, lateral nerves ca 10 pairs slightly curved, ascending, obscurely looping within the margin, prominent on both faces but especially beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather lax, a little raised beneath; petiole robust, 3.0-5.0 mm long, ca 2.0 mm diam; stipules subulate, pubescent, 3.0-5.0 mm long, [male] flowers axillary, several in a fascicle, the latter sometimes from apex of a very short peduncle; pedicels slender, puberulous, 1.0-1.3 cm long. Sepals 3, broadly elliptic to subrotund, sparsely hairy dorsally, 10.0-12.0 mm long, 12.0-16.0 mm broad. Petals ca 10, unguiculate-obovate, often erose at apex, pubescent dorsally, creamy white, 13.0-16.0 mm long, 12.0-13.0 mm broad. Stamens ca 20; filaments pubescent, 1.8-2.5 mm long; anthers narrowly ellipsoid, 2.0 mm long. [female] flowers solitary or in pairs in the upper axils. Sepals and petals similar to those of the [male]. Ovary globose, densely set with soft fleshy short aculei; styles 5, stigmas multi-lacerate. Fruit globular, (2.0-)3.0 cm diam, densely armed with stiff subuliferous laxly hairy bristles 5.0-8.0 mm long; pericarp lignescent, ca 1.0 mm thick.

description: Shrub or small tree, 2.0-6.0, rarely -12.0 m tall, with spreading crown; trunk or stem straight, 3.0-7.0(-15.0) cm diam, not branched in the lower half; bark thin, gray to dark brown or nigrescent. Branchlets slender, tips grayish-brownish-pubescent to -hirsutulous, glabrescent below, sparsely lenticellate. Leaves distantly arranged towards the end of the branchlets, oblong to obovate-oblong, apex rather gradually to more abruptly acutely acuminate, base attenuate, though the very base obtuse, membranaceous, becoming chartaceous with age, impunctate, entire or remotely denticulate to rather coarsely sinuate-dentate, especially beyond the middle of lamina, initially hirtellous on midrib and nerves of both faces, early glabrescent above, tardily so beneath, often sparsely tuberculate beneath in dry specimens, 12.0-25.0 cm long, 3.5-6.5(-8.5, rarely -10.0) cm broad, lateral nerves 7-9 pairs curved-ascending, rather faintly looping within the margin, slightly prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets close, generally obscurely raised beneath; petiole rather slender, a little swollen distally, hirtellous initially, glabrescent, 1.0-2.0 (-3.5, very rarely -4.0) cm long; stipules subulate, 1.5-2.5 mm long, persistent for some time on youngest parts of the branchlets. Flowers dioecious, the [male] in axillary 3-5, the [female] in 2-3-flowered fascicles, or the [female] sometimes solitary, all over short-pubescent on the outside; pedicels 2.0-4.0(-7.0, in the [female] up to 12.0) mm long. Sepals 3, ovate-suborbicular, 5.0-7.0 mm diam. Petals (5-)7-9, obovate, white, glabrous, 8.0-9.0(-11.0) mm long, 5.0-7.0 mm broad, slightly longer in the [male] flowers (up to 13.0 x 10.0 mm), [male] flowers: stamens (20-)30; filaments strigulose, 0.5-2.0(-3.0) mm long; anthers elongate-oblong, strigulose, 2.0-3.0(-4.0) mm long. [female] flowers: ovary ovoid, short-tomentose and generally also muriculate; styles 2 or 3, forked, stigmas lacerate. Fruit on peduncle ca 1.0 cm long, globular, pale orange, 1.5-2.0(-3.0) cm diam, subdensely (rarely very laxly) set with laxly pubescent and somewhat flattened, finally caducous bristles 4.0-10.0 mm long; pericarp coriaceous, 0.5 mm thick; seeds 4-8, polyhedric, red to orange, up to 1.0 cm long, the testa more or less deeply striate, lustrous.

description: Shrub or treelet. Branchlets slender, flexuous, glabrous. Leaves elliptic or oblong-elliptic, apex rather abruptly acuminate for 1.0-1.5 cm, base cuneate to the petiole, firmly membranaceous, laxly coarsely pellucid-punctate and -lineate, glabrous, slightly lustrous on both faces, shallowly subsinuate to entire, (8.0-)10.0-16.0 cm long, 4.0-6.0 cm broad, lateral nerves 4-5(-6) pairs moderately prominent beneath, veins laxly reticulate, veinlets rather obscure; petiole slender, glabrous, not thickened apically, 5.0-10.0 mm long. description: Dioecious tree up to 10.0 m tall. Branchlets pubescent at tips. Leaves more or less broadly oblong-lanceolate, apex shortly acutely acuminate, attenuate towards base, the very base obtuse, chartaceous, glabrous above except some puberulence on the midrib and lower part of the lateral nerves, rather densely and shortly pubescent with whitish more or less patent hairs all over the undersurface, soft to the touch there, remotely denticulate by protruding veins to almost entire, 10.0-16.0 cm long, (4.0-)5.0-7.5 cm broad, lateral nerves 9-10 pairs rather straight below, curved-ascending distally and looping within the margin, prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather lax and slightly raised beneath; petiole pubescent, 6.0-10.0 mm long; stipules lanceolate-subulate, tomentose, ca 6.0 mm long. [male] flowers 2 or 3 crowded in the upper axils; pedicels rusty-tomentose, ca 1.0 cm long. Sepals 3, ovate-oblong, tomentellous outside, 7.0-8.0 mm long, 5.0-6.0 mm broad. Petals 6-8, oblong-spathulate, thin, pinkish, sericeous in the middle outside, glabrous otherwise, ca 12.0 mm long, 5.0-6.0 mm broad. Stamens ca 20; filaments very short; anthers ca 2.0 mm long. [female] flowers (Idrobo 1502) solitary axillary on short rather robust pedicel. Sepals 3, ovate-orbicular, dorsally sericeous, 5.0-7.0 mm long, 4.0-6.0 mm broad. Petals ca 10, broadly oblong-elliptic, thin, white, as long as or slightly longer than the sepals. Ovary ellipsoid, subsericeous-tomentose; styles 4 or 5. Fruit globular, echinate, 2.0-2.5 cm diam incl aculei, yellowish-tomentose or -velutinous with soft subulate aculei 1.0-1.3 cm long, ca 1.0 diam at base; pericarp thin.

description: Dioecious tree. Branchlets slender, shortly pubescent and elongate-lenticellate at tips, older parts glabrescent. Leaves subovate- to lanceolate-oblong, apex subfalcate-acuminate for 1.0-1.5 cm and subacute, base more or less broadly cuneate, the very base acute or sometimes obtuse, subcoriaceous, glabrous, shining on both faces, impunctate, entire, 8.0-12.0(-16.0) cm long, 3.5-5.0(-6.0) cm broad, lateral nerves 8-10 pairs curved-ascending and rather obscurely inarching within the margin, slightly prominent on both faces, reticulation of veins and veinlets dense, finely though markedly raised on both faces; petiole glabrous, ca 1.0 cm long; stipules subuliform, ca 3.0 mm long, subpersistent, [male] flowers 3-6 per axillary fascicle, shortly subappressedly hairy all over; pedicels slender, 4.0-6.0 mm long. Sepals 3, oblong, 6.0-7.0 mm long, 3.0-4.0 mm broad. Petals 6-8, oblong-subspathulate, white, 11.0(-15.0) mm long, ca 5.0 mm broad. Stamens 20-25; filaments hairy, 1.5-2.0 mm long; anthers hairy, 1.5 mm long. [female] flowers axillary, solitary, their sepals and petals very similar to those of the [male] Ovary densely pilose-subsetose; styles 3; stigmas multi-lacerate. Capsule globular, pubescent, ca 1.5 cm diam, rather densely echinate with slender subuliform and densely hairy aculei ca 2.0 mm long.

description: Treelet 3.0-6.0, rarely tree up to 15.0 m high; trunk up to 15.0 cm diam. Branchlets slender, tips only tomentellous and set with 2 or 3, sometimes up to 5 leaves, lower parts leafless, early corticate, atrescent and glabrescent. Leaves obovate or elliptic-obovate, apex cuspidate-acuminate for 1.0-2.0 cm, acute, base broadly cuneate, very base obtuse, membranaceous to subchartaceous, softly pubescent to tomentulose on both faces though mainly on nerves and veins by more or less appressed pale whitish-greyish hairs, upper surface only glabrescent with age, denticulate-barbellate by veins protruding for ca 1.0 mm beyond the margin, (10.0-)15.0-24.0(-30.0) cm long, 8.0-15.0 cm broad, lateral nerves 8-10 pairs curved-ascending and indistinctly looping before the margin, prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather coarse, slightly raised beneath; petiole swollen distally, tomentose, 1.0-2.0 cm long; stipules linear-lanceolate, hairy, ca 5.0 mm long, caducous. Flowers dioecious, [male] flowers 2 or 3 in an abbreviate corymbose raceme, rarely solitary, all over yellowish-tomentulose in the outer parts, on peduncle 1.0-2.0 cm long; pedicels 1.0-2.0 mm long. Sepals 2 or 3 (rarely 4), oblong-obovate to rounded, silky-tomentose outside, subglabrous inside, 1.5-2.0 cm long, 1.2-1.5 cm broad. Petals ca 9, elongate-oblong or subspathulate, inner ones narrower, white-sericeous-tomentose on both faces, 2.5-3.0 cm long, 0.5-1.0 cm broad. Stamens (40-)50-60, densely hairy; filaments 3.0-4.0 mm long; anthers glabrous distally, 5.0-6.0(-7.0) mm long, the connective protruding for 1.5-2.0 mm beyond the cells. [female] flowers generally solitary. Sepals and petals similar to those in the [male] flowers and of the same number. Ovary narrowly ovoid, yellowish-tomentulose, with 5 plus 5 vertical slightly prominent ridges or ribs (reduced wings); styles ca 10; stigmas somewhat lacerate distally. Fruit subovoid-globose, a little apiculate, yellowish-greyish-tomentulose, in the place of wings provided with 5 stronger and 5 rather inconspicuous low vertical ribs or rows of tubercles, up to 7.0 cm long and 5.8 cm broad, finally dehiscent in 6 valves from the apex; pericarp coriaceous, not properly fibrose, almost woody, 4.0-6.0(-7.0) mm thick; peduncle ca 1.5 cm long, 3.0 mm thick. Seeds 10-25, ovoid-compressed, 0.8-1.0 cm long.

description: Shrub or generally tree 2.0-15.0(-20.0) m tall; trunk 10.0-25.0 cm diam; bark smooth, light gray. Branchlets grayish-tomentellous to -tomentose at tips, older parts glabrescent, corky and covered with small roundish lenticels. Leaves obovate- to elliptic-oblong, sometimes elongately so, apex shortly acuminate or obtuse, base attenuate to obtuse, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, pubescent initially on midrib and nerves, less densely on the intervenium beneath, gradually glabrescent, entire or dentate-subcrenulate in the upper part of the lamina, (6.0-)10.0-15.0(-22.0) cm long, 4.0-9.0 cm broad, lateral nerves 7-9 (sometimes -11) pairs rather straight below, more or less distinctly looping distally, prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather inconspicuous on both faces; petiole hardly thickened distally, 1.0-2.0 cm long; stipules linear-subulate, 5.0-10.0 mm long, rather early caducous. Flowers on usually foliate branches, axillary, polygamo-dioecious, the [male] 3-5 together collected into corymbose-contracted peduncled (1.5-4.0 cm) racemes, all over sericeous-tomentellous; pedicels 1.0(-2.0) cm long, articulate more or less at middle and provided there with several subulate rather caducous bracts and bracteoles up to 1.0 cm long. Sepals 3, obovate-elliptic, membranous, 1.2-1.4 cm long. Petals 9(-12), obovate-elliptic, white, sericeous-puberulous especially dorsally and towards the base, the outer ones slightly surpassing the sepals. Stamens 50-60, hispidulous-hairy; filaments ca 3 mm long; anthers 6.0-7.0 mm long. Flowers [male and female] generally solitary, rarely 2 or 3 in a fascicle, slightly larger than the [male] ones, on peduncle 2.0-4.0 cm long. Stamens 20(-30). Ovary sessile, ovoid-subglobose, with 10-14 thickish plicate-undulate larger and a few intermixed smaller wings, all over yellowish-tomentulose; styles 5-7, tubular, pubescent; stigmas subcapitate, cristate-lobulate, glabrous. Fruit capsular, ellipsoid-subglobular, variable in shape, size, and in form and position of the wings, (6.0-)10.0-20.0(-40.0) cm diam, with (8-)10-14 dextrorse or sinistrorse wings or crests, these papyraceous, erect and shortly wavy, sometimes reflexed, edge entire or wavy, finally more or less incised, (5.0-)10.0(-20.0, -30.0) mm high; pericarp fibrose, 2.0-4.0 mm thick. Seeds numerous, obovoid-rhomboid, striate, 15.0-20.0 mm long, in a yellowish pulp.

description: Small tree, rarely up to 15.0 m tall; trunk up to 15.0 cm diam, with grayish-blackish bark. Branchlets slender, tips densely pubescent, bearing 4 or 5 leaves, lower parts blackish-corticate and showing scars of fallen leaves. Leaves oblong-obovate, apex for ca 2.0 cm subcuspidate-acuminate, acute, base narrowly to broadly cuneate, very base maybe obtuse, membranaceous to thin-chartaceous, subsinuate-denticulate to subentire, laxly to rather densely set with longish soft subappressed whitish hairs on midrib, nerves and veins on both faces initially, finally more or less glabrescent, (8.0-)10.0-20.0(-28.0) cm long, 3.5-8.0(-11.0) cm broad, lateral nerves 8-10(-12) pairs, curved-ascending, prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather coarse, slightly raised beneath; petiole usually slender, densely hairy, 0.5-1.0(-1.5) cm long. Flowers scented, dioecious, the [male] in corymbose racemes reduced to 2 or 3 flowers, rarely solitary in the upper axils, on peduncle ca 1.0 cm long; pedicels yellowish-tomentulose, ca 1.0 cm long. Sepals 3, elliptic-suborbicular, appressed-hairy outside, almost glabrous inside, 1.0-1.5 cm diam. Petals 8 or 9, outer ones obovate-oblong, inner ones narrower, white, silky outside, less densely so except the base inside, 1.8-2.5(-3.0) cm long, 0.6-1.0(-1.5) cm broad. Stamens ca 40; filaments densely hairy, 2.0-3.0 mm long; anthers hairy, 5.0-6.0(-7.0) mm long. Flowers [female] solitary, axillary, on stoutish peduncle ca 1.0 cm long, articulate with the pedicel, ca 8.0 mm long. Sepals and petals as in [male]. Ovary subglobose, tomentulose, with 10 or 12 vertical short membranous crenate wings; styles ca 5, tomentose; stigmas short-lacerate. Fruit on peduncle 2.0-3.0 cm long, subglobular, all over yellow-green-subtomentose, (2.5-)3.0-4.0(-5.0, -7.0) cm diam, with 10 or 12 vertical membranous wings, these irregularly obtusely crisped-dentate, often more or less revolute, 3.0-8.0 (rarely -20.0) mm high, not covering each other; pericarp lignescent, not properly fibrose, 1.5-2.0 mm thick; seeds 15-30, polyhedric, white, pubescent, ca 10.0 mm long, with reddish aril.

description: Shrubs or trees. Leaves alternate, often crowded towards the end of the branchlets, persistent, or rarely periodically deciduous, subentire to dentate or serrate, penninerved; petiole short to elongate, sometimes markedly thickened distally; stipules lanceolate to subulate, early caducous. Flowers odoriferous, unisexual or polygamo-monoecious or -dioecious, pedicellate; bracts small. Inflorescences axillar, the [male] of short, generally few-flowered cymes, the [female] usually 1-flowered, sometimes on leafless branches or on old wood. Sepals (2-)3, imbricate, subpersistent. Petals (4-)6-9(-12), imbricate, more or less biseriate, generally larger than the sepals. [male]: stamens numerous, inserted on a small scarcely thickened torus; filaments rather short, hairy; anthers linear, basifixed, hairy. Rudiment of ovary 0. 9 [female]: often larger than the [male], lacking any rudiment of stamens. Ovary smooth or generally provided with short 4-8 (rarely more) vertical ridges or wings; placentas 4-8, multi-ovulate; styles 4-8 (-10), short, persistent, connate at base; stigmas capitellate or very shortly lacerate-palmatifid. Fruit large and winged in general, capsular, with a thick, often fibrous pericarp, (tardily) dehiscent by 3-5(-7) valves, provided with (4-) 6-16 distinct (or very rarely reduced and merely rim-like) vertical ridges or wings, the latter entire, crenate or lacerate. Seeds generally numerous, polyhedric, immersed in pulp; testa smooth; chalaza large; albumen copious; embryo straight; cotyledons foliaceous.

description: Shrub or treelet up to 10.0 m high. Branchlets slender, sparsely short-pubescent. Leaves elliptic-lanceolate to lanceolate, apex acutely subcaudate-acuminate for 2.0-3.0 cm, base more or less narrowly cuneate to the petiole, subcoriaceous, a little shining, very sparsely pubescent on petiole and midrib, practically glabrous, entire, (10.0-)14.0-22.0 cm long, (2.5-)3.0-6.0 cm broad, lateral nerves (10-)12-14 pairs, the lowest 3 or 4 ones rather straight, the upper ones curved, all markedly looping before the margin, prominent on both faces especially beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather dense, slightly raised beneath; petiole slender, ca 1.0 cm long; stipules linear, puberulous, ca 3. mm long. Flowers dioecious, white. Inflorescences [male] 3-6-flowered, contracted to hardly peduncled racemes or fascicles; pedicels slender, short-pubescent, up to 4.0 mm long. Sepals 2, suborbicular, membranous, (2.0-)2.5-3.0	mm diam, slightly pubescent dorsally. Petals 5 or 6, oblong, a little longer than the sepals, sericeous outside, almost glabrous inside. Stamens 20-25, subsessile; anthers pubescent, ca 2.0 mm long. Flowers 9 solitary, axillary, on short — tomentulose pedicel ca 4.0 mm long. Sepals 2, suborbicular, 2.5-3.0 mm diam. Petals 5 or 6, 3.0-4.0 mm long. Ovary obovoid — oblongoid, 6-sulcate, very shortly pubescent; styles 4, thickish, bipartite and a little lacerate distally. Fruit oblongoid-ellipsoid, subglabrous, yellow when ripe, (2.5-)3.5-4.0 cm long, 1.8-2.3 cm broad, with 6 vertical wings, these coriaceous, thin-undulate, ca 3.0 mm high; seeds few, angular, sparsely pubescent, also on chalaza, ca 1.3 cm long, 0.6-0.7 cm broad.

description: Shrub or tree (2.0-)3.0-12.0(-20.0) m high; crown spreading or conical with elongate branches; trunk straight, slender, up to 6.0 cm diam; bark thin, grayish to reddish-brownish or blackish, rather smooth. Branchlets rusty-tomentulose at tips. Leaves obovate-oblong to oblanceolate, not rarely elongately so, apex shortly subcaudate-acuminate, base long-attenuate, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, somewhat appressedly short-pubescent on both faces or rarely beneath only, generally glabrescent above, rarely more densely pubescent beneath and remaining so, remotely sinuate-dentate especially in the upper half of the lamina, rarely (sub)entire, 30.0-62.0 cm long, 10.0-22.0 cm broad, lateral nerves 15-20(-25) pairs rather straight below, arcuate and looping before the margin, prominent beneath; petiole markedly thickened and geniculate distally, 4.0-6.0(-8.0, -11.0) cm long; stipules broadly triangular, acuminate, pubescent, 6.0-10.0 mm long, caducous. Flowers polygamodioecious, with a scent of cyanide, clustered generally on defoliated parts of the branches, or on old wood respectively the trunk, rarely in the axils of lower leaves, rusty-pubescent all over in the outer parts; pedicels articulate at base, up to 6.0 mm long. Flowers [male]: sepals 2 or 3, calycoid, whitish-greenish, ovatesuborbicular, sometimes deeply lacerate, 6.0-8.0 mm long, 5.0-6.0 mm broad. Petals (5-)6-7(-10), white to almost cream, outer ones obovate and (5.0-)7.0- 8.0	mm long, 4.0-5.0 mm broad, inner ones gradually narrower, subglabrous. Stamens (20-)35-50, subsessile, hairy, 3.5-5.0 mm long. Rudiment of disk or ovary 0. Flowers 9 : sepals 3, suborbicular, 8.0-10.0 mm long. description: Dioecious tree up to 4.0 m high, with few branches; trunk ca 6.0 cm diam. Branchlets grayish-reddish-corticate, tips puberulous. Leaves obovate-lanceolate, apex subcaudate-acuminate for 2.0-3.5 cm, base long-attenuate, subcoriaceous, glabrous above, very shortly pubescent beneath, sinuate-dentate to -serrate, 34.0-50.0 cm long, 11.0-16.0 cm broad, lateral nerves 16-18(-20) pairs rather straight-ascending, looping before the margin, prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather inconspicuous beneath; petiole puberulous, 4.0-9.0 cm long; stipules caducous. Flowers [male] few, arranged in contracted racemes or subfasciculate from defoliate axils, or from trunk; pedicels pubescent, up to 7.0 mm long. Sepals 2 (rarely 3), elliptic-suborbicular, short-pubescent dorsally, 5.0-7.0 mm diam. Petals ca 7, ovate-elliptic to oblong, white, glabrous, 7.0-12.0 mm long, 5.0-6.0 mm broad. Stamens ca 30; filaments hirsute, 0.5 mm long; anthers subhirsute, ca 4.0 mm long. [female] flowers: sepals 2 or 3, ovoid-orbicular, short-pubescent dorsally, up to 10.0 mm long and 5.0 mm broad below mature fruit. Petals not known. Fruit ovoid-oblongoid, (5.0-) 6.0-8.0 cm long, 3.5-4.0 cm diam, puberulous, with (6-)10 vertical membranaceous irregularly sinuate-dentate up to 7.0 mm high wings, dehiscent with 5 valves, on thick peduncle ca 2.0 cm long; pericarp fibrose-coriaceous, 3.0-4.0 mm thick; seeds polyhedric, ca 1.0 cm long.

description: Shrub or small tree up to 6.0 m high, with few distally foliate, often simple branches; trunk up to 7.0 cm diam. Branchlets slender, furfuraceous. Leaves oblanceolate, obovate or obovate-elliptic, apex shortly cuspidate-acuminate, rarely obtuse, base long-cuneate-attenuate, very base more or less obtuse, chartaceous to rather coriaceous, glabrous above, laxly to subdensely and finely soft-hairy beneath, though glabrescent with age, or glabrous, more or less deeply and coarsely sinuate-dentate or -serrate particularly toward the apex of the lamina, 30.0-50.0(-65.0) cm long, 10.0-14.0(-20.0) cm broad, lateral nerves 10(-15) pairs rather straight from the midrib, looping before the margin, slightly impressed above, prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather coarse, slightly raised beneath; petiole swollen distally, (2.0-) 3.0-5.0 cm long; stipules triangular to lanceolate, up to 2.0 cm long and ca 0.5 cm broad, caducous. Flowers dioecious, the [male] fascicles and subsessile in the axils of the leaves, or on defoliate lower parts of the branchlets, or born at the base of the stem; pedicels pubescent, ca 4.0 mm long. Sepals 2, ovate, concave, puberulous outside, glabrous inside, 3.5-6.5 mm long, ca 5.0 mm wide. Petals 4-6, exterior ones oblong-elliptic, interior ones narrower, sparsely appressedly hairy on both sides, greenish-white, up to 6.5 mm long, 1.7-2.7 mm wide. Stamens 13-26; filaments hairy, ca 5.0 mm long; anthers appressed-pubescent, 2.5-3.5 mm long. Flowers [female] solitary and axillary. Sepals as in the [male] flowers, though somewhat larger. Petals 8, elliptic-obovate, ca 1.5 cm long. Ovary ovoid, vertically (6-)8- or 10-ribbed, densely short-hairy; styles 4 or 5, short; stigmas hardly widened at apex. Fruit subglobular, on peduncle ca 1.0 cm long, 3.5-4.0(-6.5) cm diam (or possibly larger) the wings included, reddish-purplish or creamish-greenish, sparsely pubescent, with (6-)8 or 10 rigidly chartaceous undulate-margined wings 0.8-2.0 cm broad in their middle; seeds (3-)l5-20, obovoid, flattened, up to 8.0 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Dioecious (also monoecious ?) tree, 3.0-4.0 m high, with few branches in its upper part; trunk 7.0-8.0 cm diam; bark rather smooth, brownish. Branchlets pubescent at tips. Leaves obovate-lanceolate, apex more or less long-acuminate and acute, base long-cuneate to the petiole, subcoriaceous, covered with short strigose hairs on both faces especially underneath, scabrid to the touch, glabrescent with age, subentire to obscurely sinuate-dentate, ca 50.0 cm long, 15.0-18.0 cm broad, lateral nerves 13-14 pairs, curved-ascending and looping before the edge, prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather inconspicuous; petiole somewhat pubescent, up to 10.0 cm long; stipules ovate-triangular, acute, hairy, ca 7.0 mm long, 3.0 mm broad, caducous. Flowers [male] in very short racemes or glomerules on defoliate branches or on the trunk, shortly fuscous-pubescent in all outer parts; pedicels 3.0-10.0 mm long. Sepals 3, ovate-orbicular, 3.0-4.0 mm long, 2.5-3.0 mm broad. Petals 5, elliptic-oblong, white, very laxly hairy or glabrous, 4.0-5.0 mm long, 1.2-2.0 mm broad. Stamens ca 20; filaments hispid, 1.0 mm long; anthers 2.0 mm long. [female] flowers: sepals and petals not known yet. Ovary hairy, 8-winged; styles 4. Fruit ovoid-ellipsoid, laxly hairy, ca 4.0 cm long, 3.0 cm broad, provided with 8 membranous patulous entire wings ca 1.0 cm high, on robust peduncle ca 1.2 cm long; pericarp coriaceous, 2.0-3.0 mm thick; seeds 10-20, polyhedric, reddish, 8.0-10.0 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Treelet 2.0-6.0(-8.0) m tall; trunk up to 8.0 cm diam. Branchlets rather slender, tips short-pubescent, older parts early glabrescent and covered with thin brownish cork and sparse lenticels. Leaves oblong to lanceolate, sometimes oblanceolate or even elliptic-obovate, apex more or less curved and shortly subcuspidate-acuminate, tip acute, rarely bluntish, base subinequilateral, cuneate to the petiole, very base obtuse, initially membranaceous, becoming subcoriaceous with age, flexible, shining on both faces and glabrous except for some short hairs on the midrib beneath, entire, (9.0-)13.0-30.0(-35.0) cm long, (1.5-)3.0-9.0(-12.0) cm broad, lateral nerves 9-12(-15) pairs, with shorter intercalary ones (or veins) between, curved-ascending and rather indistinctly looping before the margin, slightly prominent above, more markedly so beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets more or less distinctly raised beneath; petiole (1.0-)1.5-3.0(-4.0) cm long, generally somewhat swollen distally; stipules subulate, 2.0-3.0 mm long, in part subpersistent. Flowers dioecious. Flowers [male] in leafless axils of otherwise leafy branchlets, solitary or 2-4 in a cluster; pedicels densely short-pubescent, 5.0-10.0(-14.0) mm long. Sepals 3, calycoid, ellipsoid to suborbicular, greenish, sericeous dorsally, subglabrous internally, 6.0-8.0 mm long or diam. Petals 6-7, obovate, unguiculate, white or cream, sericeous outside, partly so inside, 8.0-12.0 mm long, 5.0-6.0 mm broad. Stamens 30-40; filaments very short; anthers laxly to subdensely hairy, 2.0-3.0 mm long. Flowers [female] solitary; pedicels hairy, 5.0-7.0 mm long. Sepals and petals as in the [male] flowers, though generally slightly longer, the petals up to 13.0 mm long. Ovary subglobose, tomentulose, 8-10-ribbed; styles 4 or 5, hairy, dilated and lacerate-palmatifid distally, 1.0-2.0 mm long. Fruit capsular, ellipsoid or subglobose, all over yellow- or orange-tomentose, 3.0-4.0(-5.0 ?) cm diam incl the 8-10 wings (the latter subentire, sometimes more or less revolute, undulate especially in the dry state, 4.0-8.0 mm high), dehiscent with 4 or 5 valves, on thick peduncle ca 1.0 cm long; pericarp fibrose-lignescent, 1.5-2.0 mm thick; seeds 10-20, flattened-polyhedric, slightly pubescent, with a red to purple sarcotesta, 8.0-12.0 mm long, 5.0-10.0 mm broad.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Slender shrubs or small trees, with simple and/or stellate (fascicled) hairs. Leaves opposite or almost so, sometimes subverticillate, becoming blackish-brownish when dry, glandular-serrate, penninerved, petiolate, exstipulate. Inflorescences (sub)erect, normally terminal, sometimes also axillary shorter ones added; racemes spiciform, elongate, many-flowered, pedunculate, the flowers hermaphrodite, yellow, solitary, or in fascicles along the rhachis, subsessile or pedicellate, subtended by small more or less caducous bracts. Calyx short-tubular, lobes or sepals 4 or 5, valvate, rather glabrous inside, reddish-brownish in dry specimens. Petals 0. Stamens (4-)16-30, 1- or 2-seriate, sub-perigynous; filaments capillary, glabrous; anthers oblong-ovate, small, erect, or finally reniform-recurved, introrse, almost basifixed; connective thickened, slightly or hardly protruding beyond the anther; thecae longitudinally dehiscent. Extra-staminal appendages (or staminodes) few to numerous, filiform, crisped, glabrous, similar to the filaments and of their length, inserted on the edge of the calyx tube. Ovary 1-celled (rarely incompletely 2-celled), with (2-)3(-4) multi-ovulate placentas; style filiform; stigma truncate. Capsule (sub)globose, subcoriaceous, loculicidally dehiscent to 2 (rarely 3 or 4) valves, subtended at the base by the remnants of the calyx; seeds few to rather numerous, small, obliquely oblongoid, dorsally

description: Shrubs or small trees; wood with a bitter taste. Leaves (sub)persistent, becoming blackish when dry, alternate, entire or glandular-dentate or -serrate, penninerved, petiolate, at the base often with 1 or 2 accessory, generally much smaller, stipule-like, sometimes caducous leaf or leaves; stipules very narrow, caducous. Flowers [male and female], or andromonoecious (possibly androdioecious), protogynous, small, sometimes fragrant, collected in axillary peduncled (sometimes spike-like) racemes, or (sometimes umbelliform) corymbs or fascicles; pedicels subtended by several small squamiform bracts. Calyx lobes or sepals 4 or 5 (rarely 6), valvate at base, subimbricate distally, persistent. Petals 0. Stamens exserted, indefinite in number (rarely 4-10, mostly 20 or more), inserted on a receptacle in several hardly distinct rows, the outer row(s) sometimes sterile (no anthers); filaments very slender; anthers small, extrorse, broadly transversely elliptic or subglobose, basifixed, longitudinally dehiscent. Disk consisting of squamular episepalous glands or lobes, of the number of the sepals or more, free, approximate or almost connate, either extra-staminal, or interstaminal, i e between the sterile and fertile stamens, or sometimes wanting. Ovary superior (much reduced in the [male] flowers), unilocular, glabrous, with 3 (rarely 2 or 4) parietal multi-ovulate placentas; ovules anatropous; style simple, filiform; stigma obtuse or sometimes 3-lobulate. Berry subglobose; pericarp thin-fleshy; seeds few to numerous, ovoid-polyhedric; testa minutely impressed-punctate; endosperm copious.

description: Shrubs or trees. Leaves alternate, more or less distichous, 3-5-nerved from base or penninerved, entire or generally glandular-serrate or -crenate, sometimes with a pair of basal glands above (these usually almost on top of the petiole), petiolate; stipules small, fugacious. Inflorescences (sub)terminal or more rarely axillary, paniculate, racemose or corymbose, rarely fasciculate. Flowers [male and female], often yellow; pedicels articulate at or above the base; bracts and bracteoles deltoid, minute, generally caducous. Sepals 3 (rarely 4), shortly united at base, valvate or rarely subimbricate distally. Petals isomerous with and similar to the sepals, persistent with these under the fruit. Disk (inter- or intra-staminal glands) 0. Stamens indefinite, free, pluriseriate, inserted on a rather flat glabrous or hairy receptacle; filaments filiform, usually glabrous; anthers very small, didymous-subglobose or very rarely oblong, basifixed, introrse, the 2 thecae dehiscent longitudinally. Ovary sessile, incompletely plurilocular by 3-8 filiform or lamelliform multi-ovulate placentas intruded far into the cavity, glabrous or rarely hairy; style simple, persistent; stigma subcapitate, minutely lobed according to the number of placentas. Fruit indehiscent, baccate, rather dry or fleshy; pericarp thin-coriaceous; seeds numerous, embedded in a fleshy pulp, oblongoid to ovoid-applanate; testa crustaceous, sometimes slightly foveolate.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Dioecious trees or shrubs. Leaves alternate, 3-5-nerved from the base, not properly pellucid-punctate, crenate-serrate, petiolate, caducously stipulate. Flowers small, (3-)4-merous, arranged in axillary solitary rather many-flowered spikes or spike-like racemes; bract and 2 bracteoles of each flower minute. Flowers [male]: sepals 4, subimbricate, almost free. Petals 4, similar to though generally longer than the sepals. Stamens 8 or rarely 10-12, inserted on an inconspicuous disk; filaments filiform, elongate; anthers minute, didymous, dehiscing lengthwise. Rudiment of ovary 0. Flowers [female]: sepals 4, subimbricate, subpersistent. Petals 0. Ovary 4-sulcate, contracted at base to a kind of stipe; placentas 4, 2-ovulate; style columnar, very short, or almost absent, with 4 subulate more or less reflexed stigmatic branches. Disk annular, depressedly cupuliform, fimbriate, surrounding the basal part of the ovary. Fruit a depressed-globose capsule, which splits halfway or to almost the base into 3 or 4 valves; seeds few, covered with longish soft cottony hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrubs or trees. Branchlets rarely thorny. Leaves alternate, distichous, penninerved, entire or glandular-crenate or -serrate, rarely spiny, membranaceous to coriaceous, generally provided with pellucid dots and/or lines, petiolate, stipulate. Flowers [male and female] , small, in axillary sessile or peduncled fascicles or glomerules, rarely in cymes, very rarely solitary; pedicels articulate; basal bracts free, scale-like, often numerous and forming a cushion rarely thick and connate to a kind of cup. Sepals (or calyx lobes) (4-)5(-6, -9), connate usually at base, rarely up to halfway, imbricate, subpersistent. Petals 0. Stamens (5-)6-10(-12, very rarely -22), more or less perigynous, uniseriate; filaments free, or rarely adnate to the disk; anthers globose to ovoid, may be apiculate by a glabrous or barbate gland-like connective. Disk lobes generally in the same row with the stamens and alternating with them, sometimes inserted inside or outside the row of stamens, very rarely fused to an almost extra-staminal corona. Ovary free, 1-locular, with usually 3 parietal multi-ovulate placentas; ovules anatropous; style simple or divided at apex into 3 branches; stigma(s) capitate. Capsule dry to succulent, often 3-angled, dehiscing to 3(-4) valves; seeds generally numerous, glabrous or pubescent, completely to partially enveloped by a soft, often coloured and fimbriate aril; testa crustaceous, foveolate; albumen fleshy; cotyledons flat.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrubs or small trees, the foliage sparse at the end of the branchlets. Leaves spiral, coriaceous, glandular-serrulate, pellucid-punctate and -lineate, penninerved, markedly reticulate, petiolate, stipulate. Inflorescences paniculate, axillary. Flowers [male and female] (or possibly sometimes polygamous ?), small, almost immersed in the rhachis with their base, sessile, the subtending bract and 2 bracteoles subpersistent. Sepals 4, slightly connate at base, imbricate. Petals 0. Stamens 8, of which 4 longer ones before the sepals, and 4 shorter ones alternating with them; filaments filiform; anthers small, bilocular, subglobose, introrse, basifixed, dehiscent lengthwise. Disk lobes 8, alternating with the stamens and connate with them at base, spathulate, barbate. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with 2 parietal placentas, each of them bearing a single ovule; style 0; stigma sessile, its 4-6 lobes radiating. Fruit baccate; seeds 1 or 2, each with a short lacerate aril.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrubs or trees. Leaves alternate, 3 (or sub-5)-nerved from base, penninerved in the upper part, with 2 basal foveolate glands on the upper face close to the petiole, entire to coarsely glandular-serrate-crenate, petiolate; stipules small, caducous. Inflorescences subterminal or axillary in compound, repeatedly 3- or 4-radiate, long-peduncled, umbel-like racemes; pedicels minutely bracteate and bibracteolate. Flowers [male and female], small, odoriferous. Sepals and petals 4 (rarely 3 or 5), valvate, persistent, reflexed after anthesis. Stamens 2040 on a densely hairy flat receptacle which bears 8-20 small glabrous subglobular or flattish glands between the base of the filaments; filaments filiform, pubescent below; anthers small, subglobose, basifixed, the 2 thecae longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary free, superior, 2 (rarely 3)-celled by an early union of the 2 (or 3) opposite parietal placentas; ovules numerous, inserted on the central pseudo-axis; style simple, entire, persistent. Fruit subtended by the remnants of the sepals and petals, baccate with a succulent, red to blackish pericarp, each cell usually with 1 (rarely 2) seed(s); testa coriaceous, glabrous; endosperm present; embryo straight; cotyledons foliaceous.

description: Shrub or tree. Leaves subdistichous, remotely glandular-subserrate, 3(-5)-nerved from base, penninerved in the upper part of the lamina, no basal glands, petiolate; stipules minute, caducous; hairs simple. Inflorescences axillary, corymbiform, rather few-flowered, shortly pedunculate. Flowers dioecious. Sepals 3, valvate, thickish, persistent. Petals 3, alternating with and slightly larger than the sepals, valvate, thin, persistent. Receptacle hairy, [male]: stamens indefinite, multi-seriate; filaments elongate, filiform, hairy below; anthers elliptic-obovoid, small. Disk-lobes 12-15, inserted between the outer row of stamens, short, thick, truncate. Rudiment of ovary 0. [female]: filaments several, without anthers, thickish, of various length between ca 15 truncate disk-lobes. Ovary superior, sessile, unilocular, with 3 or 4 parietal placentas which protrude a little as laminae into the cavity, each placenta with a few hemianatropous ovules; style 0; stigma radiate with (3-)4-5 bifurcate flattened branches. Fruit a fleshy berry, enveloped for most of its length by the persistent sepals and petals; seeds several, ovoid-angular; testa very finely impressed-punctate.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrub or tree. Leaves alternate, deciduous, subserrate, subcrenate, or subentire, penninerved, pellucid-punctate and -lineate, petiolate, caducously stipulate. Cymes axillary, contracted, short-pedunculate, rather few-flowered. Flowers [male and female], rather small, precocious. Calyx lobes 5, imbricate, persistent. Petals 0. Receptacle very shallow. Stamens indefinite, 80-100, free, arranged in 3 series, inserted at the base of the calyx outside the disk, which consists of ca 15 1-seriate free, short-clavate and flattened, distally hairy lobes or staminodes; filaments filiform, anthers oblong-elliptic, almost basifixed, dehiscing lengthwise; connective small. Ovary free, sessile, 1-locular, hairy, with 3 multi-ovulate placentas, attenuate to a rather short glabrous style; stigma small, capitate, faintly 3-lobed. Fruit capsular, obtusely 3- to sub-6-gonous, dehiscent with 3 valves; pericarp coriaceous; seeds numerous.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrubs or trees. Leaves alternate, distichous, entire or glandular-crenate or -serrate, usually with distinct pellucid dots and lines (seemingly impunctate in sp with coriaceous leaves), penninerved, petiolate, fugaciously stipulate. Inflorescences axillary (or slightly supra-axillary) or subterminal, fasciculate or cymose (corymbose). Flowers [male and female], rather small; pedicels articulate at or a little above base; bracts and bracteoles free or sometimes united into a cupule. Sepals 4 or 5, imbricate, free or a little connate at base, almost petaloid, pellucid-punctate and -lineate, often reflexed in anthesis, more or less caducous. Petals 0. Stamens 10 to numerous, inserted on an obsolete disk; filaments free, not rarely unequal in length; anthers small, elliptic to almost linear, introrse, basifixed or almost so, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary free, 1-locular, with 3(-6) parietal, few- to many-ovulate placentas; style short, simple or shortly 3-lobed, stigmas capitate or obscurely lobed. Fruit a berry-like capsule, tardily valvately dehiscent, sometimes resinous within; pericarp coriaceous. Seeds few to rather numerous, arillate; testa leathery; endosperm copious; embryo straight; cotyledons broad and foliaceous.

description: Tree. Leaves alternate, remotely thickish-glandular-subserrate, 3-5-nerved from base, no proper basal gland(s) present (sometimes seemingly glandular at or near base by the gland(s) of the lowest serration(s) on one or both sides), petiolate (petiole distinctly swollen and rugosely canaliculate distally); stipules not observed; hairs stellate. Inflorescence axillary and subterminal, laxly corymbose or paniculate. Flowers y; pedicels articulate near middle; bracteoles 2, minute, caducous. Sepals 5 or 6, valvate, thickish, caducous. Petals 0. Stamens numerous (ca 100), free, multi-seriate, inserted on a hairy receptacle and on the inner base of the sepals; filaments thick-filiform, long-hairy; anthers small, elliptic-subglobose; connective thickened, erect, surpassing the thecae as an apiculus. Free disk-glands 0. Ovary superior, sessile, 1-locular, surrounded by a small shortly 4-lobed disk, with 4 or 5 multi-ovulate placentas a little protruding into the cavity; style very short; stigma subcapitate, very shortly 4- or 5-lobed. Capsule ovoid-acuminate, dehiscent from base towards the apex by 4 valves; pericarp separating into a coriaceous early-shed exocarp, and a thin lignescent endocarp; seed 1, elongate, covered with white cottony hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrub or small tree. Leaves alternate, distichous, penninerved, densely pellucid-punctate, petiolate, caducously stipulate. Flowers dioecious, solitary or mostly a few together in axillary bracteate sessile glomerules, the latter sometimes from already defoliate branches, subtending bract and the 2 bracteoles of each flower rather large, partly enclosing the flower in bud. Calyx tube urceolate, fleshy, its 4 short lobes erect, imbricate at prefloration. [male]: Stamens 8, subsessile, inserted on a hairy disk which covers the lower part of the calyx tube, perigynous, 4 longer ones opposite the calyx lobes, 4 shorter ones alternating with them; filament fleshy, more or less adnate to the calyx tube, very short; anthers almost basifixed, introrse, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary rudimentary. [female]: Stamens much reduced in size, sterile. Ovary sessile, ovoid-pyramidate, rugose, 1-locular, with 3 or 4 multi-ovulate placentas; style short, 3-4-fid, stigmas subcapitate, reflexed. Capsule suborbicular, slightly 3-4-gonous, transversely subalate-rugose, loculicidally 3-4 valved; pericarp coriaceous, rather thick. Seeds numerous, angular by mutual compression, arillate; tests crustaceous, sericeous-puberulous; albumen fleshy; cotyledons foliaceous.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate, 3 (or faintly 5)-nerved from base, often with a pair of basal glands on the upper surface, entire or remotely glan-dular-serrate-crenate, petiolate; stipules minute, caducous. Inflorescences in axilary or subterminal lax-flowered racemes. Flowers rather large; pedicels articulate above the base. Sepals (3-)4, valvate, persistent. Petals (3-)4, similar to the sepals and alternating with them, valvate, persistent. Stamens indefinite, subperigynous, multi-seriate, on a hairy receptacle; filaments filiform, short; anthers elongate-linear, basifixed, 2-thecate, dehiscent by an oblique introrse slit at apex. Ovary superior, sessile, incompletely 5-6(-9)-locular by the intrusion of the multi-ovulate placentas; style simple. Fruit baccate, indehiscent, dry, surmounted by the persistent style and more or less included by the persistent sepals and petals; pericarp thin-coriaceous, brittle. Seeds numerous, small, subovoid-ellipsoid; testa smooth.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Dioecious tree. Leaves more or less alternate, persistent, spiny (Ilex-like), penninerved, with 2 basal glands on the upper surface, petiolate, stipulate. Flowers [male] [female], small, greenish, [male]: sepals (11-)14-15(-22) imbricate. Petals 0. Receptacle disk-shaped, glabrous, with numerous conical short and thick yellow-orange disk-lobes between the stamens. Stamens very numerous, indefinite; filaments slender; anthers ovate, small, dorsifixed, longitudinally dehiscent. Rudiment of ovary 0. [female]: sepals 7-9. Petals 0. Nectaries forming 1-2(-3) rows around the ovary, with a few staminodia between them. Ovary superior, imperfectly celled by 6-8 multi-ovulate placentas protruding far into the cavity; ovules anatropous; style very short; stigmas 6-8, radiating and reflexed, canaliculate above, thickened and papillate distally. Fruit baccate; pericarp stony. Seeds numerous, flat; testa thin, smooth; endosperm copious; cotyledons cordate, foliaceous; embryo straight.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrub. Leaves alternate, denticulate to entire, penninerved, petiolate; hairs stellate; stipules minute, caducous. Flowers [male and female] arranged in terminal and/or axillary few-flowered cymes; pedicels articulate above the base; bracts and bracteoles minute, caducous. Sepals 5 (rarely 4), valvate, connate at base. Petals 4 (rarely 4), valvate, similar to the sepals, alternating with them and persistent as these. Receptacle flat with ca 10 thick-flattish more or less marginal glands. Stamens indefinite, multi-seriate, hypogynous, only the outer ones subperigynous; filaments filiform, glabrous; anthers small, subglobose, dorsifixed, dehiscent by short slits; connective fleshy. Ovary sessile, unilocular, with 3-5 parietal thick multi-ovulate placentas protruding a little into the cavity; style short, thickish; stigma obscurely 3-5-lobulate. Capsule coriaceous, dehiscent from apex to 2 or 3 valves, crowned by the style; seeds 2-7, ovoid, with rather smooth crustaceous testa; endsperm copious.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrub or tree. Leaves alternate, entire or remotely glandular-subserrate, (3-5)-nerved from base, 2-glandular at the junction of blade and petiole, petiolate; stipules minute, caducous; hairs simple. Inflorescence a terminal panicle or several panicles both terminal and from the axils of the upper leaves, laxly many-flowered. Flowers [male and female]; pedicels articulate at base, fugaciously bracteolate. Sepals 4-6, valvate, caducous. Petals 4-6, alternating with the sepals, valvate, caducous. Stamens indefinite, multi-seriate; filaments filiform, elongate, glabrous; anthers minute, subglobose, basifixed, bilocular, longitudinally dehiscent; connective thickened, not or hardly protruding beyond the tecae. Receptacle glabrous between the base of the filaments. Interstaminal glands 6-8, small, flattish. Ovary superior, sessile, unilocular, with 3 or 4 parietal multi-ovulate placentas hardly protruding into the cavity; style slender, more or less persistent, stigma very shortly 3- or 4-lobed. Capsule dry, dehiscent irregularly from the top, or laterally; pericarp thin-crustaceous; seed 1, glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrubs or small trees. Leaves alternate, (3-5-)7-nerved from base, penninerved above, glandular-serrate, often with 2 basal glands, petiolate; stipules small to large, foliaceous, caducous or persistent. Inflorescences terminal on lateral branchlets, in short racemes, corymbs or fascicles, sometimes reduced to a solitary flower; pedicels provided with a basal linear bract, articulate and bibracteolate above the base. Flowers [male and female]. Sepals 3 (rarely 4 or 5), valvate, persistent. Petals isomerous and alternate with, and smaller than the sepals, persistent, rarely abortive. Stamens indefinite (50-70), pluri-seriate, free, inserted on the slightly elevated receptacle; filaments filiform; anthers small, didymous-subglobose, almost basifixed, 2-locular, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary free, subsessile, 3-5(-6)-locular; ovules numerous, anatropous, fixed to the inner angle on lamelliform, sometimes 2-lobed placentas; style simple, filiform; stigma small, faintly 3-lobed. Fruit baccate, dry or almost so, indehiscent, surmounted by the persistent style, 3-5(-6)-locular; seeds numerous, small, angular-ovoid, in a white pulp; testa brittle; endosperm copious; embryo straight; cotyledons thick.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrubs or slender trees up to 15.0 m tall, with simple and/or stellate hairs on branchlets, leaves, inflorescences and fruits; stem up to 20.0 cm diam; wood hard. Leaves alternate, distichous, epunctate, not rarely subasymmetrical, membranous to coriaceous, penninerved, entire to denticulate or serrate, petiolate; stipules 2, acicular to elongate-lanceolate, often caducous. Inflorescences axillary, 1-4 flowered, fasciculate or on very short rhachis. Flowers [male and female] , heterostylous, often showy, white, yellowish-greenish, pink or red, fragrant. Pedicels articulate at or above base, bracteolate at base; bracts small, caducous. Calyx tube very short, its 5 lobes or sepals quicuncial, almost free, petaloid, spreading or erect, sometimes subpersistent under the fruit. Stamens 30-70, free or almost so, inserted in 2 or 3 series at apex of calyx tube near base of sepals; filaments filiform, subequal in length, tapering to a fine point distally; anthers oblong to linear, subsagittate, attached near base, introrse, apex often conspicuously mucronate, opening their full length by 2 longitudinal slits. Disk coroniform, urceolate, villose outside, glabrous within, unequally toothed (up to 1.0 mm). Ovary superior, sessile to manifestly stipitate, 1-locular; placentas 3-9, multiovulate in many ranks; style terminal, short to elongate, entire, or at apex 3-9-fid (up to 3.0 mm); stigmas capitellate. Fruit capsular, indehiscent or ultimately valvetely dehiscent, globular to pyriform, 1.0-6.0 cm long, slightly lobulate, suberose, or with spongeous emergences, stellate-tomentose or subhirsute; exocarp up to 8.0 mm thick, endocarp crustaceous or osseous, up to 6.0 mm thick. Seeds 25-150 per fruit, globular to bluntly angular, 3.0-5.0 mm diam, hispidulous with scattered stellate, rarely also simple hairs; testa very finely pitted; aril at base of seed membranaceous, brown, resinous-punctate; endosperm copious; embryo straight; cotyledons flat and thin.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrubs or small trees. Branchlets zigzag, rarely spinose distally. Leaves alternate, distichous or spirally arranged, with pellucid dots and lines, penninerved, entire to glandular-denticulate or -serrate, petiolate, caducously to persistently stipulate. Flowers [male and female], axillary, solitary or 2-3 (rarely more) in a cluster, usually fragrant; pedicels articulate more or less halfway; bracts usually small. Calyx (4-)5(-6)-lobed, lobes fused for at least 1/3 their length into a generally white, greenish or reddish, cylindrical or campanulate tube, imbricate, more or less unequal. Stamens (6-)8-20, uniseriate, with an equal number of often obsolete staminodes, the whole connate and adnate to the calyx below the throat of the tube, free above, but stamens and staminodes planate and fused into a definite tube for at least 1/3 the length of the filaments, rarely remaining distinct above the calyx throat; anthers introrse, (sub)basifixed, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary superior, 1-locular, with 3-5 many-ovulate placentas, tapering gradually to the style; stigma capitate, occasionally obsoletely 3-4-lobed. Capsule subglobose, often a little angled, 3-5-valved from apex almost to the base; valves fleshy or coriaceous to almost woody. Seeds numerous, angular, arillate; testa coriaceous, brittle, finely textured; endosperm fleshy; cotyledons foliaceous.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrubs or generally trees. Leaves alternate, subdistichous, large, entire, to repand-serrate, penninerved, petiolate, caducously to subpersistently stipulate. Inflorescence axillary, panicles composed of spikes, elongated in fruit. Flowers [male and female], or occasionally polygamous (andromonoecious ?), small, sessile, each subtended by a bract and 2 bracteoles, these small and closely appressed to the rhachis. Calyx urceolate, thickened, 4-gibbous or -angulate (compressed by the crowding of the flowers along the rhachis), or 4-lobed, persistent, the lobes (or sepals) biseriately imbricate, small, membranous, rounded. Petals 0. Disk in form of 4 obsolete teeth between the stamens. Stamens 4, inserted within the calyx tube; filaments short, filiform, alternate with the calyx lobes; anthers ovate-cordate, introrse, longitudinally dehiscent, almost basifixed, exserted or not. Ovary sessile, 1-locular, with 4 parietal many-ovulate placentas; style very short; stigma capitate, obscurely 3- or 4-lobed. Fruit baccate, coriaceous, not or very tardily dehiscent by 3 or 4 valves; seeds numerous, exarillate, though each seed is surrounded by a thin membrane; testa foveolate-alveolate; embryo straight; endosperm copious.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrubs or trees. Leaves periodically deciduous, alternate, entire to subcrenate-serrate, pellucid-punctate and -lineate, penninerved, petiolate, fruga-ciously stipulate. Flowers [male and female], often precocious, in fascicles from defoliate axils of annotinous shoots, pedicellate, bracteolate at base. Sepals (4)-5, hardly connate at base, imbricate, persistent. Petals 0. Stamens indefinite (20-40), sub-perigynous. Disk-appendages or staminodes 15-20, clavate, more or less alternating with the stamens and united basally with them; filaments filiform; anthers small, almost basifixed, introrse, longitudinally dehiscent. Ovary free, 1-locular, with 3 many-ovulate placentas; stigma (sub)sessile, thick, peltate. Fruit a fleshy capsule, globose, opening at length by 3 valves; seeds numerous, arillate; endosperm fleshy.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrub, up to 2.0 m tall, rarely treelet. Branchlets pale rusty-tomentulose to -tomentose at tips, lower parts gradually glabrescent. Leaves oblong-lanceolate to elliptic, or ovate, apex attenuate to subacuminate, tip subacute, base cuneate to rounded, chartaceous, brownish when dry, softly rusty-strigose-tomentose on both faces initially, generally more densely so beneath, or more laxly hairy on both faces, sometimes early glabrescent, or even subglabrous, the midrib and lateral nerves excepted, rather densely glandular-dentate-serrate (the teeth thickish, often recurved), (3.5-)5.0-10.0 cm long, (1.5-)2.0-5.0 (rarely -6.0) cm broad, lateral nerves (6-)8(-10) pairs rather straight ascendent and excurrent before the edge of the lamina, slightly impressed above, prominent beneath, veins transverse, slightly raised beneath, proper reticulation of veinlets inconspicuous; petiole densely hairy, 5.0-10.0(-20.0) mm long, 1.0-2.0 mm thick. Racemes spiciform, subterminal, erect, dense-flowered, all over densely covered with pale rusty crisp hairs, (5.0-)16.0-40.0 cm long. Flowers solitary, or 2-4 in a fascicle, subtended by subuliform rather persistent bracts 5.0-7.0 mm long; pedicels slender, (2.0-)4.0 mm long. Calyx lobes or sepals 4, subovate-oblong, or lanceolate, subacuminate, deep yellow-orange, rusty-tomentulose outside, glabrous inside, (2.0-)3.0-4.0 mm long, ca 2.0 mm broad, reflexed in anthesis. Stamens (8-)12-16(-20). Ovary densely appressedly hairy; style slender, glabrous, 1.5-3.0 mm long. Capsule ovoid-subglobose, 3.5 mm diam, more or less included by the calyx lobes; seeds numerous, subovoid, apiculate, nigrescent, ca 1.0 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrub up to 2.0 m tall. Branchlets densely patently gray- or yellowish-pubescent at tips, glabrescent and covered with brownish cork below. Leaves oblong-obovate or oblong, apex shortly acuminate, base narrowed to the petiole, membranaceous, laxly to subdensely covered with simple substrigose gray or yellowish hairs on both faces, more densely so on midrib and lateral nerves beneath, glandular-serrulate-denticulate, (4.0-)7.0-9.0 cm long, (1.5-) 3.0-4.0) cm broad, lateral nerves (5-)7-8 pairs, curved-ascending, a little prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets lax, rather inconspicuous; petiole hairy, 6.0-10.0 mm long. Racemes spiciform, erect, all over densely grayish-yellowish-pubescent, terminal ones 14.0-18.0 cm long, lower axillary ones much shorter; pedicels articulate in the middle, 3.0-6.0 mm long; bracts lanceolate, acuminate, 3.0-5.0 (sometimes -12.0) mm long. Calyx lobes or sepals 4, ovate-lanceolate, yellow, glabrous inside, 3.0-4.0 mm long, 1.5 mm broad at base. Stamens ca 35. Ovary ovoid-subglobular, white-tomentose; style glabrous, 2.0-3.0 mm long. Fruit not known yet.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrub to 3.5 m high. Branchlets slender, tips grayish-whitish-stellate-tomentose, older parts glabrescent. Leaves lanceolate-ovate, apex long-acuminate and acute, base rounded, or sometimes subcordate, firmly membranaceous, sparsely stellate-hairy at midrib and lateral nerves on both faces, manifestly, or mostly more obscurely crenate-serrulate, 4.0-8.0(-12.0) cm long, 1.5-3.5(-5.0) cm broad, lateral nerves 5-6(-7) pairs, flat above, slightly raised beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather obscure beneath; petiole slender, stellate-tomentose, 6.0-9.0(-15.0, -20.0) mm long. Racemes spiciform, slender, rather dense-flowered, 5.0-9.0(-16.0) cm long incl peduncle (1.0-4.0 cm), all over yellowish-grayish-stellate-tomentose; pedicels 2.5-3.0 mm long; bracts lanceolate to subuliform, 2.0 mm long. Calyx lobes or sepals 4, triangular-ovate, acute, yellow, patent or a little reflexed in anthesis, yellowish-grayish outside, almost glabrous inside, reddish-brown in the dry state, 2.5 mm long. Stamens 8. Ovary densely covered with white hairs; style 1.0-1.5 mm long, glabrous. Capsule ovoid, subacute, white-tomentellous, 5.0-6.0 mm long; seeds 15-20, ellipsoid, striate, hardly 1.0 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrub. Branchlets slender, tips strigose, older parts glabrescent and corticate. Leaves lanceolate, or oblong-lanceolate, apex subacuminate-attenuate, acute, or mucronulate, base attenuate, thin-chartaceous, rather firm in texture, with some strigose hairs on the midrib above, glabrous otherwise, with numerous pale points beneath in the dry state, a little shining, serrulate by 3-6 remote glandular teeth on either side of the lamina, (1.0-)1.5-3.0 cm long, 0.4-1.0 cm broad, lateral nerves 5-6 pairs steeply ascending, slightly impressed above, prominent beneath, reticulation of veins obscure; petiole 1.0-1.5 mm long. Racemes spiciform, the lowest part only without flowers, erect, dense-flowered, 4.0-8.0(-11.0) cm long; rhachis ferrugineous-villous; pedicels laxly hairy, ca 2.0 mm long at anthesis, glabrescent and a little accrescent in fruit, articulate in the middle. Calyx glabrous, lobes or sepals ovate-acuminate, ca 2.0 mm long, 1.2 mm broad, granular-blackish-punctulate under a lens, finally reflexed. Stamens ca 12. Ovary laxly appressedly hairy; style glabrous, 1.5 mm long. Capsule subglobose, ca 3.0 mm diam, blackish-purplish-pubescent; seeds several, ellipsoid, black, shining, densely reticulate, sparsely pubescent, hardly 1.0 mm long.

description: Shrub or weak tree up to 1.0 m tall; stem slender, straight; bark rather smooth, brown to gray. Branchlets virgate, grayish- or whitish-stellate-tomen-tulose, or -lanuginose, striate-angled in the youngest parts. Leaves oblong, or lanceolate-oblong, or oblong-elliptic, apex shortly (sometimes narrowly) acuminate, base rather broadly attenuate, the very base generally obtuse, firmly chartaceous, becoming subcoriaceous with age, densely grayish-stellate-tomentulose initially, less densely so to glabrescent with age above, densely softly stellate-hairy to -tomentose, or lanuginose-pulverulent all over the undersurface, especially on midrib and lateral nerves, sometimes glabrescent to various degrees, serrulate-denticulate, 8.0-16.0 cm long, 3.5-6.0(-7.0) cm broad, lateral nerves (8-)10-12 pairs prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets dense and rather distinctly raised beneath; petiole thick, whitish-grayish-tomentulose, sometimes glabrescent, (1.0-)1.3-2.0 (rarely -2.5) cm long, with a small gland at the very base. Racemes spiciform, erect, densely or more loosely flowered, all over grayish-yellowish-stellate-tomentose, 15.0-20.0(-25.0) cm long incl peduncle (1.5-2.5 cm). Flowers fragrant, pale yellow, or greenish; pedicels stoutish to more slender, densely to loosely stellate-hairy, 2.0-5.0(-7.0) mm long at, slightly accrescent after anthesis. Calyx lobes or sepals ovate-oblong, acuminate, more or less reflexed at anthesis, whitish-yellowish-tomentulose outside, subglabrous inside, 4.0-5.0(-6.0) mm long, 1.5-2.0 mm broad. Stamens 20-30. Ovary gray-tomentose; style glabrous, 3.0 mm long. Capsule depressed-globose, grayish-yellowish-tomentulose, ca 5.0 mm diam; seeds numerous, ovoid-oblongoid, striate, glabrous, dark red to blackish, 1.2 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Erect shrub, ca 3 m tall. Branchlets rusty-stellate-tomentose at tips, glabrescent below. Leaves oblong, or oblong-elliptic, or lanceolate-oblong, apex acuminate, subacute or more obtuse, base broadly attenuate to the petiole, the very base being obtuse or subcordate, firmly chartaceous, sparsely floccose and strigose though finally glabrescent and rather rough to the touch above, grayish-yellowish-stellate-tomentose beneath, 8.0-12.0(-18.0) cm long, (4.0-)4.5-5.5(-8.0) cm broad, the upper leaves smaller, regularly subcrenulate-denticulate, lateral nerves ca 12 pairs, prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets rather dense and slightly impressed above, concealed by the tomentum beneath; petiole rusty-tomentose, 1.0-1.5(-2.0) cm long. Racemes spiciform, erect, terminal and solitary, dense-flowered to almost the base, 16.0-20.0(-25.0) cm long, all over rusty-stellate-tomentose at least initially, glabrescent in the lower part; pedicels rather slender, articulate in general 2.0 3.0 mm above the base, 6.0-9.0(-10.0) mm long at anthesis. Calyx lobes or sepals 4 (rarely 5), elongate-ovate, acuminate, yellow, rusty-stellate-tomentu-lose outside, glabrous and reddish when dry inside, 4.0-5.0(-6.0) mm long. Stamens ca 30. Ovary white-hirsute; style glabrous, 4.0 mm long. Capsule subglobose, hirsute, 3.0-4.0 mm diam, dehiscent with 3 valves; seeds numerous, obovoid, blackish, minutely striate, hardly 1.0 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrub, 3.0-4.0 m tall, with yellowish-ferrugineous-stellate-tomentose slender branchlets. Leaves ovate, or ovate-oblong, apex acuminate, tip acute or obtuse, base broadly cuneate-obtuse, or often rounded and more or less deeply auriculate, firmly chartaceous, laxly strigose-hairy and somewhat scabrid to the touch above, yellowish-ferrugineous-stellate-tomentose beneath initially, glabrescent with age except midrib, lateral nerves and veins beneath, subcrenate-serrate, 9.0-18.0(-22.0) cm long, (5.0-)6.0-10.0(-13.0) cm broad, lateral nerves (9-) 10-12 pairs prominent beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets not impressed above, a little raised beneath; petiole rusty-stellate-tomentose, (2.0-)2.5-3.5(-5.0) cm long. Racemes spiciform, terminal, showy, many- and dense-flowered, all over rusty-stellate-tomentose, 20.0-25.0 cm long incl peduncle; rhachis robust; pedicels slender, articulate near the middle, (1.0-)1.5-2.0 cm long. Calyx lobes or sepals 4, narrowly lanceolate, tip subulate, tomentose outside, glabrous inside, greenish when fresh, becoming reddish when dry, 7.0-8.0 mm long, 2.5-3.0 mm broad at base. Stamens 30-35. Ovary tomentulose; style glabrous, 7.0-8.0 mm long. Capsule globose, tomentose, 5.0-6.0 mm diam; seeds numerous, narrowly oblongoid, black, 1.5 mm long.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Erect shrub, straggling or loosely branched, 1.0-1.5 m tall. Branchlets very slender, recent parts densely covered with gray scurfy-stellate hairs, older parts glabrescent. Leaves narrowly ovate to lanceolate, apex acuminate, acute, based rounded to subcordate, membranaceous to thin-chartaceous, nigrescent in the dry state, initially densely covered on both faces with stellate or fascicled and simple gray to yellowish hairs, glabrescent above, rarely so beneath, midrib and nerves excepted, rather irregularly glandular-serrate-dentate, (3.0-)6.0-9.0 (-10.0) cm long, (2.0-)3.0-5.0 cm broad, lateral nerves 4-6 pairs rather straight ascendent, a little raised beneath, reticulation of veins and veinlets obscure; petiole slender, hairy, (2.0-)3.0-5.0 mm long. Racemes spiciform, terminal, rarely also from the upper leaf-axils, dense-flowered, erect in anthesis, rather decurved in fruit, all over grayish scurfy-stellate-tomentulose, (4.0-)5.0-7.0(-12.0) cm long incl peduncle (2.0-4.0 cm), a little accrescent towards fructification. Flowers in general solitary, subsessile, or pedicelled up to 1 mm, subtended by a linear-lanceolate bract 3.0-4.0 mm long. Calyx lobes or sepals 4 or 5, ovate-deltoid, yellow, gray-tomentulose outside, almost glabrous inside, 1.5-1.8 mm long. Stamens 4-6. Ovary tomentose; style curved, base hairy, glabrous distally, 1.5 mm long. Capsule ovoid-oblongoid, apiculate, tomentellous, 5.0-6.0 mm long, included halfway by the calyx lobes, dehiscent with 2 (sometimes bifid) valves; seeds 10-20, oblongoid, blackish, shining, ca 1.0 mm long, testa puncticulate.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Tree or treelet, 2.0-8.0(-10.0) m tall; trunk 10.0-25.0 cm diam. Branchlets brownish, glabrous. Leaves subpersistent, oblong-lanceolate, apex rather long acuminate, acute, ending in a very small gland, base cuneate and mostly a little inequilateral, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, shining above, dull and paler beneath, initially laxly set with short hairs, early glabrescent, quite glabrous with age, regularly serrate-dentate (teeth spinuliferous, acute, ending in a minute stipitate gland), (4.0-)6.0-8.0(-10.0) cm long, 1.5-2.5(-3.0, very rarely -4.0) cm broad, lateral nerves 5-7 pairs discolorous, somewhat raised on both faces, veins more or less transverse, forming with the veinlets a close reticulation which is more distinctly prominent beneath; petiole 0.8-2.0 cm long. Accessory stipule-like leaves 1 per axil, ovate to oblong, similar to the normal ones, 1.0-2.5 cm long, 0.4-1.0 cm broad, rather early caducous. Flowers [male and female], greenish-yellowish, 4 or 5 per abbreviated corymb, usually from defoliate axils of the annotinous branchlets, on peduncle 2.0-4.0 mm long; pedicels stoutish, puberulous, 2.0-3.0 mm long, the basal bract ovate-acuminate, densely hairy, ca 5.0 mm long. Sepals 4 or 5, ovate-acuminate, bluntish, sericeous outside, subglabrous inside, 1.5-2.0 mm long. Receptacle densely long-hairy. Disk consisting of 2 rather small thickish glands before each sepal, which are hidden between the base of the outer sterile (filament-like) and the inner fertile stamens. Stamens 20-25. Ovary subglobose; style ca 2.5 mm long; stigma very shortly 3-lobed. Berry subglobose, somewhat fleshy, reddish-blackish, 5.0-6.0 mm diam; seeds 6-10, ovoid-angular, 1.5-2.0 mm long, ca 1.5 mm broad.
bibliographicCitation: Sleumer, Hermann O. 1980. Flacourtiaceae. Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 22: 1-499.

description: Shrub or small tree up to 6 m tall, andromonoecious or possibly androdioecious. Branchlets rather slender, tips glabrous or pubescent, rarely yellow-ish-tomentose. Ovary subglobose; style 2.0 mm long; stigma truncate. Berry globose, a little fleshy, sordidly pinkish-blue, pruinose, (5.0-)6.0-8.0 mm diam; seeds (4-)6-20(-25), ovoid-angular, 1.5-2.0 mm long.

description: Shrub, treelet or tree, 2.0-6.0, rarely up to 40.0 m tall. description: Shrub or generally small tree up to 7.0 m high. Branchlets fugaciously puberulent at tips, older parts grayish-corticate and very densely minutely lenticellate. description: Slender shrub, up to 4.0 m tall. Branchlets very shortly gray-pubescent at tips, otherwise glabrous, lenticels obscure. description: Much branched shrub or small tree, 2.0-3.0(-6.0) m tall. Branchlets yellowish-grayish-pubescent at tips, glabrescent below, older parts laxly set with elliptic lenticels. description: Shrub or tree up to 8.0 m tall; bark gray, fissured, peeling off. description: Shrub or small tree, 1.0-3.0, rarely -8.0 m high. Branchlets slender, tips patently puberulous, older parts covered with a gray or brownish cork and suborbicular lenticels. description: Tree 10.0-15.0(-30.0) m tall, with flattish crown; trunk up to 60.0 cm diam, clear of branches up to halfway; bark brown. Branchlets rather slender, young parts shortly patently pubescent, older ones covered with grayish-brownish cork; lenticels flat, rather inconspicuous. Leaves oblong to ovate-oblong, apex short- to long-attentuate or subacuminate, tip obtuse, base markedly inequilateral, one side cuneate, the other one rounded, with 1 (rarely 2) small cupular gland(s) at the very base of lamina or on top of the petiole, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, shining and (sub)glabrous above, dull and short-pubescent mainly on midrib and nerves beneath, glabrescent, rather coarsely and remotely glandular-serrate-crenate (1.0-2.0 mm), 9.0-15.0(-20.0) cm long, 4.0-6.0(-9.0) cm broad, lateral nerves (7-)9-12 pairs prominent beneath, veins more or less transverse, close to each other, a little raised on both faces, reticulation of veinlets rather obscure; petiole pubescent initially, 6.0-10.0 mm long; stipules lanceolate, pubescent, ca 2.0 mm long, subpersistent. Panicles terminal, pyramidate, widely divaricate, slender, laxly many-flowered, all over appressedly gray-puberulous, 7.0-12.0 cm long, lower branches up to 6.0 cm long; pedicels slender, articulate a little above base, 4.0-5.0 mm long. Flowers yellowish-greenish, with red hue in bud. Sepals 3, ovate-oblong, puberulous dorsally, glabrous internally, ca 3.0 mm long, 2.0 mm broad. Petals 3, similar to the sepals, ca 4.0 mm long. Receptacle glabrous. Ovary ovoid, glabrous; style ca 2.5 mm long. Fruit capsular, dry, globose, 10.0(-15.0) mm diam; pericarp coriaceous; seeds (10-)15-30, flattened-ovoid, blackish, finely striate, ca 2.0 mm long.

description: Tree or treelet, 4.0-8.0 m tall. Branchlets slender, tips shortly brownish-tomentulose, older parts glabrescent with thin longitudinally fissured brownish cork, lenticels rather inconspicuous. Leaves lanceolate-oblong or sometimes elliptic-oblong, apex gradually attenuate or subacuminate, tip subacute or obtuse with a minute gland, base more or less unequal, one side cuneate, the other rounded, very base often contracted and provided with a pair of rather small glands, chartaceous, subglabrous and a little shining above, the substrigose midrib and lateral nerves excepted, grayish-tomentellous to -tomentulose (simple more or less appressed hairs) and soft to the touch all over the undersurface, densely glandular-serr(ul)ate or -denticulate (0.5-1.0 mm), 8.0-12.0(-15.0) cm long, (3.0-)4.5-6 cm broad, lateral nerves 7-8 pairs steeply arcuate-ascending and obscurely looping before the margin, prominent beneath, veins more or less transverse, slightly raised beneath, reticulation of veinlets much less visible; petiole tomentulose, (6.0-)8.0-12.0 mm long; stipules subulate, ca 2.0 mm long, persistent for some time. Panicles terminal, pyramidate, rather few-flowered, slender, all over yellowish-tomentulose, (6.0-)8.0-12.0 cm long, lower branches up to 5.0 cm long; pedicels slender, (4.0-)6.0-12.0 mm long; bracts minute. Flowers yellowish. Sepals 3, ovate to ovate-oblong, subacute, densely appressed-hairy outside, much less so inside, 5.0-6.0(-9.0) mm long, (2.5-)3.5-5.0(-6.0) mm broad, slightly accrescent in fruit. Petals 3, similar to the sepals, often a little narrower and longer. Receptacle subdensely long-hairy between bases of filaments. Ovary ovoid, glabrous; style 3.0-4.0(-5.0) mm long. Fruit unknown.

description: Treelet or tree 3.0-8.0 (rarely -20.0) m tall; trunk up to 50.0 cm diam; bark grayish-brown. Branches virgate, pendent. Branchlets slender, glabrous, minutely lenticellate. Leaves lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, rarely oblong, apex subacutely acuminate, base slightly or hardly unequal, cuneate, or rounded on one side, chartaceous, glabrous, shining on both faces, 5.0-8.0(-11.0) cm long, 2.0-3.0(-3.5) cm broad, rather regularly glandular-subcrenate-serrate (1.0-1.5 mm), 3- or faintly 5-nerved from base, with 4-6 pairs of upper lateral nerves, all nerves prominent beneath, veins more or less transverse, rather densely reticulate with the veinlets and but slightly raised beneath; petiole slender, 6.0-10.0 mm long; stipules subulate, 1.5 mm long, tardily caducous. Panicles terminal, pyramidate, composed of simple racemes in the upper, shortly branched ones in the lower part, slender, very many-flowered, all over puberulous or glabrescent, up to 6.0 cm long and wide below; pedicels slender, glabrous, 2.0-4.0 mm long; bracts lanceolate-subulate, bearded distally, ca 1.5 mm long. Flowers small, yellow. Sepals 3, ovate, obtuse, (sub)glabrous on both faces, 1.5-2.0 mm long. Petals 3, broad-oblong, to subobovate, obtuse, ciliate, otherwise glabrous, ca 2.0 mm long. Receptacle glabrous. Ovary ovoid, glabrous; style hardly 1.0 mm long. Fruit baccate, reddish or orange, ca 5.0 mm diam; seeds few, compressed-ovoid, blackish, 1.5 mm long.

description: Shrub or tree, sometimes up to 8.0 m tall, little branched. Branchlets glabrous even at tips, densely minutely lenticellate. Leaves ovate to elliptic, rarely lanceolate, apex shortly (sub)acutely acuminate, base slightly unequal, broadly cuneate or sometimes obtuse, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous except some scattered hairs on midrib beneath, shining on both faces, glandular-serrate or -serrulate (0.5-1.0 mm) along the whole margin, (5.0-)7.0-12.5 cm long, (2.0-)3.5-6.0 cm broad, basal nerves 3-5 pairs ascending to the lower 1/3 of the lamina (the outer pair faint or shorter), upper lateral nerves 4-6 pairs from the upper 2/3 of the midrib, markedly raised beneath, less so above, reticulation of the more or less transverse veins and the veinlets dense, finely prominent on both faces; petiole 6.0-12.0 mm long; stipules lanceolate-subulate, somewhat pubescent, 1.0-1.5 mm long, subpersistent. Inflorescences racemose, simple or branched at base, laxly 5-10-flowered, glabrous; rhachis 3.0-5.0 cm long; pedicels slender, articulate 2.0-4.0 mm above the thickened base, 1.5-2.5 cm long; bracts lanceolate or linear-subulate, 1.5-3.0 mm long. Sepals 3, ovate, obtuse or acutish, firm, glabrous outside, appressed-pubescent at edge and inside, 5.0 mm long, 4.0 mm broad. Petals 3, ovate-orbicular, obtuse, edge thin, otherwise as sepals. Receptacle glabrous. Ovary ovoid, glabrous, attenuate to the style hardly 2.0 mm long. Fruit subglobose, 6.5 mm long, 7.0 mm broad; seeds numerous, ovoid, 1.2-1.5 mm long; testa smooth, shining.

description: Small tree. Branchlets covered with slender, more or less spreading short hairs, brownish; lenticels small. Leaves ovate or narrowly so, apex obtuse or rounded but the very apex acutely protracted, base truncate to subcordate, coriaceous, shining on both faces, glabrous above, very shortly pubescent at midrib and nerves beneath, glandular-denticulate, 5.0-7.0 cm long, 3.0-4.0 cm broad, 5-nerved from base (the outer pair of nerves shorter than the inner, high-ascending one), with 3-4 pairs of upper lateral nerves, all nerves prominent on both faces as is the reticulation of veins and veinlets; petiole 4.0-6.0 mm long; stipules linear-filiform, 3.0 mm long, caducous. Otherwise unknown.

description: Tree up to 20.0 m tall, with elongate, pendent branches; trunk up to 40.0 cm diam, sometimes with low tableroots; bark gray, smooth. Branchlets angular, purplish when dry, glabrous, up to 7.0 mm diam. Leaves almost distichous, oblong-lanceolate, oblanceolate or elliptic-oblong, apex obtuse though apiculate with a mucro i e produced midrib 1.0 mm long, sometimes a little emarginate, base very unequal, one side cordate-auriculate, the other rounded, no basal glands, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, minutely hairy on midrib and lateral nerves beneath, practically glabrous, somewhat shining on both face, 26.0-49.0 cm long, (8.0-)10.0-18.0 cm broad, glandular-crenate or -dentate (ca 2.5 mm), lateral nerves up to 22 on one, and up to 16 pairs on the other side, arcuate, prominent mainly beneath, veins and veinlets slightly raised beneath; petiole subglabrous, 1.0-1.3 cm long; stipules not observed. Panicles terminal, pyramidate, pendent, glabrous, many-flowered, 16.0-25.0 cm long, lower branches up to 11.0 cm long; rhachis robust, angular; pedicels stoutish, articulate above base, 2.0-4.0(-7.0) mm long. Flowers yellowish or pale green, fragrant. Sepals 3 (rarely 4), ovate-acuminate, tomentellous mainly in the upper part outside and more densely so inside, (4.0-)5.0-8.0 mm long, 3.0-4.0 mm broad. Petals 3 (rarely 4), ovate to broad-oblong, apex rounded, gray-tomentellous on both faces, sometimes glabrescent inside, ca 5.0 mm long, 4.0 mm broad, reflexed as are the sepals in late anthesis. Receptacle glabrous. Ovary ovoid, base substipitate, apex gradually tapering to the thick style (2.0 mm). Fruit not known.

description: Shrub. Branchlets covered with slender spreading short hairs; lenticels scarce. Leaves elliptic to oblong, apex attenuate or short-acuminate, acute, base narrowed, very base obtuse, chartaceous, glossy on both faces, glabrous above, minutely hairy at midrib and nerves beneath, glandular-dentate, 4.0-7.0 cm long, 1.5-3.5 cm broad, 3-nerved from base (the pair of lateral nerves ascending to or beyond the middle of the lamina parallel to the edge), upper nerves 3-4 pairs from the midrib, all nerves impressed above, prominent beneath, reticulation more or less prominent; petiole patently hairy, 2.0-4.0 mm long; stipules linear or filiform, 0.5-1.0 mm long, caducous. Otherwise unknown.
